audits.t: P001 An audit to assess whether patients who had a delayed or missed denosumab dose during the covid-19 pandemic came to any harm or suffered a subsequent fracture
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: E051 Audit of the management of patients over 75 with osteoporotic fragility fractures in primary care

audits.c: Dedicated clinics (telephone or face to face) to discuss management and start medication
audits.r2: 49% started on medication; 9% refused; 17% deemed inappropriate; 25% had died or left the practice.

audits.t: P058 Anabolic treatment of osteoporosis: an audit on safety events from a teaching hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Teriparatide (n=24): 17 (70%) had a documented post-teriparatide plan, 2 adverse events, no fractures after cessation. Romosozumab (n=26): 7 adverse events including heart failure and hypocalcaemia, no fractures after cessation. All met NICE criteria.

audits.t: E050 Parathyroidectomy vs pharmacological strategies in the management of bone health in patients with primary hyperparathyroidism: a service improvement audit
audits.tp: Bone health management in primary hyperparathyroidism

audits.f: Parathyroidectomy in 21 (32.8%); cinacalcet 10 (15.6%); alendronic acid 37 (68.5%), denosumab 24 (37.5%), zoledronic acid 10 (18.5%), risedronate 2 (3.7%); fragility fractures in 41 (64%).

audits.t: E051 Diagnosis and monitoring of Paget’s disease of bone: an audit across hospital departments in secondary care
audits.tp: Paget's disease of bone investigation and treatment

audits.t: Independent sector and peri‐operative cardiac arrest as reported to the 7th National Audit Project of the Royal College of Anaesthetists

audits.t: Data quality audit of a clinical quality registry: a generic framework and case study of the Australian and New Zealand Hip Fracture Registry.

audits.t: THROMBOPROPHYLAXIS FOR AMBULATORY PATIENTS WITH IMMOBILISED LOWER LIMB TRAUMA: A CLOSED AUDIT LOOP
audits.st: NICE recommendation for VTE risk assessment in lower limb immobilisation, RCEM GEMNet guidance and local policy

audits.t: Introduction of clerking pro forma for surgical spinal patients at the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust (London): an audit cycle.

audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Vitamin D deficiency in a high secure forensic psychiatry hospital: A clinical audit and service evaluation
audits.st: Local trust guideline: vitamin D checked within one month of admission and then three-monthly, with dosing by level

audits.t: An audit cycle of physical health monitoring and record keeping of long term in-patients at male and female psychiatric rehabilitation wards using QI approach

audits.t: When Psychosis is Not Psychosis: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Delirium Misdiagnosis Across Hospital Departments

audits.t: DELIVERING SUSTAINABLE CHANGE OF POSTOPERATIVE CARE DOCUMENTATION PRACTICES IN SPINAL SURGERY THROUGH QUALITY IMPROVEMENT FRAMEWORKS

audits.t: A VIRTUAL FRACTURE CLINIC AUDIT: ARE WALES MATCHING THE OUTCOMES IN ENGLAND?

audits.t: A RETROSPECTIVE ANALYSIS OF THE DEFINITIVE MANAGEMENT OF OPEN TALUS FRACTURES, COMPARING ORIF AND TIBIOCALCANEAL FUSIONS, AT A MAJOR TRAUMA CENTRE: COHORT STUDY AND AUDIT OF BOAST 4 GUIDELINES

audits.t: COMPLIANCE WITH THE SUSPECTED CAUDA EQUINA SYNDROME (CES) PATHWAY IN BETSI CADWALADR UNIVERSITY HEALTH BOARD (BCUHB) WEST: A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT AGAINST NATIONAL STANDARDS

audits.t: STANDARDIZATION OF URINARY CATHETERIZATION GUIDELINES TO REDUCE PAEDIATRIC PERIOPERATIVE URINARY TRACT INFECTION RATES: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVE

audits.t: THE CHILDREN'S URGENT REDUCTION OF FOREARM FRACTURES IN THE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT (CURFFED) PROJECT: A NATIONAL PROSPECTIVE TRAINEE-LED COLLABORATIVE AUDIT OF PRACTICE AND PERCEIVED BARRIERS TO CHANGE

audits.t: A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT OF PAIN MANAGEMENT IN PATIENTS PRESENTING WITH HIP FRACTURE

audits.r2: 76% of hip fracture and 81% of distal radius fracture patients investigated, treated or referred (both p < 0.00001).

audits.t: Quality improvement for patients with hip fracture: experience from a multi-site audit.
audits.tp: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
audits.st: Indicator standards for re-audit circulated after the 1992 audit
audits.f: Pharmaceutical thromboembolic prophylaxis 45%; early mobilisation 56%.
audits.c: Results of the 1992 audit and indicator standards circulated to orthopaedic and care of the elderly consultants and audit leads at each hospital.
audits.r2: Pharmaceutical thromboembolic prophylaxis 81%; early mobilisation 70%; reduced pneumonia, wound infection, pressure sores and fatal PE.

audits.t: Improvements in pain relief, handling time and pressure ulcers through internal audits of hip fracture patients.
audits.tp: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
audits.st: Aims: optimise preoperative pain relief, reduce time from admission to operation and reduce pressure ulcers; no target stated
audits.f: Close to half waited more than 24 hours for operation; 11% operated within 12 hours; 19% had pressure ulcers at discharge
audits.c: Quality improvements with attention from all staff (details not given)
audits.r2: 34% waited more than 24 hours; 24% operated within 12 hours; 4.5% had pressure ulcers at discharge

audits.t: A unitary patient record improves admission documentation in a medical assessment unit in a major teaching hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Standard documentation before the unitary patient record (random sample of 100 admissions across both groups).
audits.c: Introduction of a multidisciplinary unitary patient record (UPR) for emergency medical admissions.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in documentation of function before episode, ethnic origin, chest pain, breathlessness, ankle oedema, cough, bowel habit, locomotor symptoms, blood pressure and peripheral pulses; no items worse.

audits.t: A strategy for reducing blood-transfusion requirements in elective orthopaedic surgery. Audit of an algorithm for arthroplasty of the lower limb.
audits.tp: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 66% transfused at least one unit (58% of knees, 73% of hips); mean transfusion requirement given as 13 units per patient (1.1 knees, 1.5 hips).
audits.c: New transfusion protocol based on maximum allowable blood loss, colloid replacement, bedside haematocrit and transfusion thresholds, with Hb checks on days 1-3.
audits.r2: 24% required blood (11% of knees, 34% of hips); mean 0.56 units per patient (0.26 knees, 0.79 hips).

audits.t: Audit of antibiotic prophylaxis for surgical patients in three hospital trusts in Tayside. Tayside Area Clinical Audit Commitee.
audits.st: Previously agreed standards for administration of antibiotic prophylaxis (three general standards)
audits.f: Prophylaxis given to 82% of eligible orthopaedic patients; rate for indicated operations 84% to 93% across trusts; continued <24 h in 78% to 97%; given within two hours in >95%; second doses in 5/44 (11%) of operations >2 h.

audits.t: Clinical effectiveness of high tibial osteotomy for osteoarthritis of the knee.
audits.st: Standard 5-year result from the literature: 85% satisfactory
audits.f: 71% satisfactory and good results (96 knees, 81 patients, mean follow-up 4.5 years).
audits.c: Procedure restricted to patients under 65 years with routine pre-osteotomy arthroscopy.

audits.t: Closing the audit loop--prevention of perioperative hypothermia: audit and reaudit of perioperative hypothermia.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean core temperature on arrival in recovery 35.5 degrees C (range 32.2-37.2, SD +/- 0.74).
audits.c: Simple but consistently implemented changes in practice to prevent hypothermia (details not given in the supplied text).
audits.r2: Mean core temperature on arrival in recovery 36.6 degrees C (33.6-38.2, +/- 0.72); difference reached significance.

audits.t: Use of an integrated care pathway: a third round audit of the management of shoulder pain in neurological conditions.
audits.tp: Shoulder pain management in neurological conditions
audits.st: Pre-determined standards for assessment, documentation and management of shoulder pain within an integrated care pathway
audits.f: Second round audit figures not given in abstract.
audits.c: Integrated care pathway with pro forma documentation.
audits.r2: Third round: 5 of 9 initial assessment and documentation standards improved, ranging 56% to 94%; 9 continued-management standards achieved 44% to 97%.

audits.t: Pelvic and acetabular fractures in the United Kingdom: a continued public health emergency.
audits.tp: Early management of pelvic and acetabular fractures
audits.st: Guidelines laid down for early management in four specific areas
audits.f: 56% did not meet standards; 34% had deficiencies in more than one area
audits.r2: 57% did not meet guideline standards; 20% had problems in more than one area

audits.t: Regional audit: perioperative management of MRSA orthopaedic patients in the Oxford region.
audits.st: Local MRSA guidelines and policies
audits.f: 78% knew of a pre-admission screening policy; 15% unaware of any MRSA policy; teicoplanin 44% and vancomycin 44% for prophylaxis; 18% believed cefuroxime used; 48% of hospitals had an MRSA-free zone.

audits.t: Improvement in the treatment of stable ankle fractures: an audit based approach.
audits.st: Departmental evidence-based guidelines on recognition and functional treatment of stable ankle fractures
audits.f: Recognition and functional treatment of stable ankle fractures was rarely followed.
audits.c: Introduction of formal departmental evidence-based guidelines.
audits.r2: Subsequent audits showed progressive improvement with significant reductions in time immobilised in plaster, time non-weight bearing and number of routine check radiographs, without compromising safety.

audits.t: Reduction of nosocomial pressure ulcers in patients with hip fractures: a quality improvement program.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Incidence of nosocomial pressure ulcers in hip fracture patients 12.9%.
audits.c: Visco-elastic mattress and a specially designed limb-elevation cushion for each patient on the orthopaedic ward; pressure-relieving practices introduced in the recovery room.

audits.t: Quality of post-anesthetic care in a hospital without a Post-Anesthetic Care Unit. A clinical audit.
audits.st: Defined discharge criteria: modified Aldrete score ≥7, systolic BP within 20% of pre-operative value, no nausea/vomiting or shivering, pain absent or mild
audits.f: Discharge criteria observed in 74%; not fully met in 26% (69/261): 14 unstable vital signs, 46 uncontrolled pain, 6 nausea/vomiting, 3 shivering.

audits.t: Human skeletal allograft collection--room for improvement?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Allograft not collected from 22/70 suitable patients; 68.6% of suitable bone collected. 29% of donated allograft rejected due to poor patient selection.
audits.c: Procedural changes to improve the efficiency of allograft collection (not detailed).
audits.r2: 8/70 allografts discarded due to logistical problems; 88.9% of suitable allograft collected (p = 0.001). Rejection for poor selection fell to 9.4% (p = 0.05).

audits.t: The effect of a fracture protocol on hospital prescriptions after minimal trauma fractured neck of the femur: a retrospective audit.
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: Fracture protocol based on Australian Fracture Prevention Summit recommendations for in-hospital calcium, vitamin D, SERMs and bisphosphonates
audits.f: In-hospital prescription: any treatment 36%, calcium 26%, vitamin D 29%, oral bisphosphonates 5%, SERMs 1%.
audits.r2: Any treatment 58%, calcium 51%, vitamin D 48%, oral bisphosphonates 24% (all P <0.01); SERMs 1% (P =0.70).

audits.t: A clinical audit of patients on an orthopaedic waiting list for greater than two years.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 134 of 142 replied and 103 attended clinic; 34 removed after reassessment; only 69 (49%) remained on the waiting list.

audits.t: Audit on radiographs in anterior shoulder dislocations.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 88 patients (88%) had AP view only; 10 had two views and 2 had three views (115 dislocations).

audits.t: Audit on the efficient use of cross-matched blood in elective total hip and total knee replacement.
audits.tp: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
audits.st: Maximum Surgical Blood Ordering Schedule (MSBOS) and national guidelines
audits.f: High level of unnecessary cross-matched blood; THR cross-match transfusion (C:T) ratio 3.21
audits.c: Ceased routine cross-matching for THR; check full blood count on day 2 after surgery for all patients; Hb-based criteria (detail truncated)
audits.r2: Units cross-matched but not transfused fell by 96% for THR; C:T ratio reduced to 1.62

audits.t: A prospective audit of blood usage post primary total knee arthroplasty.
audits.tp: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
audits.st: National Blood Users Group guidelines (haemovigilance nurse employed in compliance)
audits.f: 11% of patients undergoing primary TKA required post-operative transfusion.
audits.c: Routine cross-matching stopped for primary TKA, a Haemovigilance Nurse was employed, and post-operative cell salvage introduced for patients with preoperative haemoglobin below 12 g/dl.
audits.r2: 17 of 233 patients (7%) received allogeneic blood, average two units; no statistically significant difference from the first audit.

audits.t: Blood audit evidenced-based cross-match requesting for lumbar spine surgery.
audits.tp: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
audits.st: Evidence-based cross-match tariff (cross-match to transfusion ratio and transfusion index)
audits.f: 664 cross-match requests, 40 units transfused; C:T ratio 16.6:1.
audits.c: New evidence-based cross-match tariff agreed between surgeons, anaesthetists and transfusion department.

audits.t: [The quality of care in shoulder pain. A medical audit].
audits.st: Quality indicators developed from systematic reviews, guidelines and expert criteria (history, examination, diagnosis, treatment)
audits.f: 76.3% of records did not meet at least 4 of 10 history criteria; 61.6% did not meet at least 3 of 10 examination criteria; 7.7% had no diagnosis. 96.9% of 98 impingement patients did not meet anti-inflammatory/injection timing criteria; 95.8% of 24 rotator cuff tears not proposed for early surgical evaluation; 86.7% of 15 adhesive capsulitis cases lacked timely exercise instructions.

audits.t: Using clinical audit to improve the quality of obstetric care at the Tibetan Delek Hospital in North India: a longitudinal study.
audits.st: Hospital policy of active management of the third stage of labour; WHO partogram use for labour management and transfer decisions
audits.f: Postpartum haemorrhage 7 (12%); retained placenta 3 (5%); 11 (19%) transferred, 8 (75%) for 'failure to progress' in uncomplicated primiparous women; no partograms used.
audits.c: Staff retraining in active management of the third stage with intramuscular Syntometrine at delivery of the anterior shoulder, introduction of the WHO partogram with training, and feedback seminars, one-to-one sessions and newsletter reports after each cycle.
audits.r2: PPH 5 (6%); retained placenta 0; 6 (7%) transferred, 1 (17%) for failure to progress; partograms used in 77 (86%), complete and accurate in 13 (17%).

audits.t: Secondary prevention of fragility fractures: are we following the guidelines? Closing the audit loop.
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: British Orthopaedic Association guidelines for secondary prevention of fragility fractures
audits.f: FBC 26 (96%); LFT and bone profile 18 (66%); calcium and vitamin D 9 (30%); 1 patient referred for DEXA.
audits.c: Awareness raised among junior doctors and nurse practitioners; AMTS above 7 used as DEXA criterion in over-80s; hospital protocol based on BOA guidelines.
audits.r2: FBC and renal profile 100%; bone profile 28 (75.7%); LFT 34 (91.9%); treatment 24 (65%); DEXA referral 9/23 eligible (40%) (P = 0.03).

audits.t: Does it matter whom you see? - a fracture clinic audit.
audits.tp: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall discharge rate 38%, differing significantly between consultants

audits.t: The extended scope physiotherapist in orthopaedic out-patients - an audit.
audits.st: Independent management of 85% of patients by ESPs; no re-referral with the same problem; patient satisfaction 89%
audits.f: 82/150 (55%) managed independently; 4/150 (3%) re-referred by GPs; 97/126 (77%) satisfied.

audits.t: Broken bones and fractures - an audit of patients' perceptions.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 84% thought a 'fracture' and a 'break' differ; 68% believed a 'break' is worse.
audits.c: Patient information leaflet on fractures/broken bones introduced.
audits.r2: 67% thought there was a difference; 65% believed a 'break' is worse.

audits.t: Rate of referral of breech infants for hip ultrasound: an audit cycle.
audits.st: Infants with risk factors for DDH, including breech presentation, should have hip ultrasound shortly after birth
audits.f: 56% of breech infants referred for hip ultrasound.
audits.c: New pro-forma encouraging recognition of breech presentation at the routine neonatal examination.

audits.t: The detection of patients with 'fragility fractures' in fracture clinic - an audit of practice with reference to recent British Orthopaedic Association guidelines.
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: British Orthopaedic Association 2003 guidelines on care of fragility fracture patients (secondary prevention of osteoporotic fractures)
audits.f: Only 5 of 38 patients who should have been assessed and investigated for osteoporosis were referred or offered referral.
audits.c: Steps to improve awareness among orthopaedic staff and prompt referral.
audits.r2: 23 of 43 patients referred or offered referral.

audits.t: The ANKLe score: an audit of otolaryngology emergency clinic record keeping.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England record-keeping guidelines plus legibility, scored with the ANKLe score
audits.f: Baseline ANKLe scores for content and legibility (figures not given in abstract); 20 notes from each of 7 SHOs.
audits.c: Documentation proforma introduced and handwriting advice given.
audits.r2: Significant increase in content, legibility and overall ANKLe score.

audits.t: Clinical audit of the management of stable ankle fractures.
audits.st: Local evidence-based guidelines for diagnosis, functional brace treatment and follow-up of stable ankle fractures
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Guidelines with diagnostic criteria, brace management protocol and outpatient follow-up algorithm widely distributed, with persistent education of colleagues.
audits.r2: 91% managed in a functional brace; mean outpatient appointments, weeks to discharge and repeat radiographs fell significantly.

audits.t: Standardised proformas improve patient handover: Audit of trauma handover practice.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England 'Safe Handover' minimum dataset and BMA guidance; gold standard 100% data transmission and 100% proforma compliance
audits.f: Handwritten plain paper sheets: patient labels used 73% (35/48); side of injury handed over in 28/49; tasks performed or outstanding 31% (15); relevant blood results 19% (6/32); overall data handed over 72.6%.
audits.c: Standardised handover proforma based on the RCS dataset, piloted (version 1, 78% compliance), revised after junior doctor feedback and implemented as version 2.
audits.r2: 100% proforma compliance; labels 96% (53/55); side of injury 98% (54/55); tasks 100% (55/55); relevant blood results 20% (6/29); overall data handed over 93.2% (p<0.01).

audits.t: Audit of ankle injuries in an accident and emergency department.
audits.st: Locally developed ankle injury protocol based on published reports
audits.f: 205 (80%) had radiography; 20 ligamentous injuries reviewed; 13 inappropriate fracture clinic referrals.
audits.c: Introduction of an ankle injury management protocol.
audits.r2: 186 (70%) had radiography; 66 ligamentous injuries reviewed; 9 inappropriate referrals (53% reduction); protocol completed in 87% of notes.

audits.t: National audit of provision of MRI services 2006/07.
audits.st: RCR standards for MRI provision: request-to-report times and recommended waiting times for cancer staging and routine orthopaedic examinations
audits.f: Request-to-report time did not meet the standard for cancer staging but was within target for routine orthopaedic examinations nationally; mean waiting times longer than recommended for both.
audits.c: Major investment in MRI capacity: new NHS scanners and, in England, outsourcing of routine MRI to an independent provider.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in waiting times for routine orthopaedic examinations; cancer staging examinations deteriorated.

audits.t: Clinical audit of foot problems in patients with rheumatoid arthritis treated at Counties Manukau District Health Board, Auckland, New Zealand.
audits.tp: Foot care provision in rheumatoid arthritis
audits.st: Arthritis and Musculoskeletal Alliance (ARMA) Standards of Care for People with Foot Health Problems and Inflammatory Arthritis
audits.f: 77% reported no previous formal foot assessment; 76% had not seen a podiatrist; 40% had used the orthotic centre; 27% had previous foot surgery; over 85% had foot lesions.

audits.t: Pain management practices in paediatric emergency departments in Australia and New Zealand: a clinical and organizational audit by National Health and Medical Research Council's National Institute of Clinical Studies and Paediatric Research in Emergency Departments International Collaborative.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 196 migraine, 197 abdominal pain, 177 femur fracture cases. Less than half had pain score at triage. Femur fractures: analgesia 78% (opioids 49%, femoral nerve blocks 40%); median 75 min to enteral and 26 min to parenteral medication.

audits.t: An audit of hip fracture services in the Mater Hospital Dublin 2001 compared with 2006.
audits.tp: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Inpatient mortality 20%; discharge home 8%; discharge to nursing home 25%.
audits.r2: Inpatient mortality 8%; discharge home 18%; discharge to nursing home 21%; prescription of perioperative antibiotics, DVT prophylaxis and osteoporosis medication improved.

audits.t: The national clinical audit of falls and bone health: the clinical management of hip fracture patients.
audits.tp: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
audits.st: Published national guidelines for hip fracture care in older people
audits.f: A&E stay under 2h 20% (640/3133) and over 240 min 23%; surgery within 24h 35% (1080/3088); sat out of bed within 24h 48% (1480/2998); orthogeriatric care 35% (1115/3184); median stay 16 days.

audits.t: National comparative audit of blood use in elective primary unilateral total hip replacement surgery in the UK.
audits.tp: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
audits.st: National comparative audit indicators and standards for transfusion practice
audits.f: 47% of hospitals had a transfusion policy; 73% did group-and-save rather than cross-match; of patients transfused, 7% had a single unit and 67% two units; 65% of those given two or more units had post-transfusion Hb 10 g/dl or more.

audits.t: Low rates of treatment in postmenopausal women with a history of low trauma fractures: results of audit in a Fracture Liaison Service.
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: National guidance recommending treatment in the majority of postmenopausal women with a history of low trauma fracture
audits.f: Of 1641 women, 526 (31%) had a past low trauma fracture; only 27.6% of these were receiving bone protective therapy (bisphosphonate 89%) and 35.6% calcium and vitamin D. Only 45.1% of women aged 75 and over with a previous fracture were treated.

audits.t: Improving the quality of procedure-specific operation reports in orthopaedic surgery.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidelines on surgical documentation (33 parameters)
audits.f: Handwritten operation reports scored an average of 58.7%.
audits.c: Procedure-specific computerised operation report proforma for hip hemi-arthroplasty.
audits.r2: Scores rose significantly (exact figure truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Retrospective audit of triage of acute traumatic shoulder dislocation by emergency nurses.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Nurses less likely than physicians to identify dislocation at triage (OR 0.06; 99% CI 0.014-0.272).
audits.c: Integrated care pathway for acute traumatic shoulder dislocation developed.

audits.t: The national clinical audit of falls and bone health-secondary prevention of falls and fractures: a physiotherapy perspective.
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: National guidance and professional standards on secondary management of falls and fragility fractures
audits.f: Non-hip fragility fractures (n=5642): 28% gait and balance assessment, 22% exercise programme, 3% shown how to get up from the floor. Hip fracture (n=3184): 68%, 44% and 7% respectively.

audits.t: Assessing the adequacy of procedure-specific consent forms in orthopaedic surgery against current methods of operative consent.
audits.st: Information on BOA-endorsed Orthoconsent forms as the set standard for patient understanding at confirmation of consent
audits.f: Patients consented with standard yellow generic forms scored an average of 56.7% (knee arthroscopy) and 57.6% (total knee replacement) on questionnaires.
audits.c: Patients additionally given the procedure-specific Orthoconsent form to read at home and sign on the morning of surgery.
audits.r2: Average scores rose to 80.5% (knee arthroscopy) and 81.6% (total knee replacement).

audits.t: An audit of the role of vitamin K in the reversal of International Normalised Ratio (INR) in patients undergoing surgery for hip fracture.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Current practice (stopping warfarin) analysed for days from admission to surgery, reasons for delay and time for INR to fall to 1.5 or below; figures not given in abstract.
audits.c: Single dose of vitamin K 1 mg intravenously on admission in addition to stopping warfarin for patients with INR above 1.5.
audits.r2: Vitamin K significantly reduced the time for INR reversal and the pre-operative delay to surgery (numbers not given in abstract).

audits.t: Postoperative infection rates in foot and ankle surgery: a clinical audit of Australian podiatric surgeons, January to December 2007.
audits.st: Australian Council on Health Care Standards (ACHS) infection definitions; literature benchmark of 0.5-6.5%
audits.f: Overall infection rate 3.1%; infection resulting in re-admission 0.25% (1339 admissions, 2387 procedures)

audits.t: Audit of the utilization of time in an orthopaedic trauma theatre.
audits.st: Institutional standards: end utilisation 77%; operating theatre utilisation 85-90%; changeover and start times
audits.f: End utilisation 78.8% and operating theatre utilisation 81%; changeover and start times sub-standard

audits.t: Audit-induced change reduces complications of the Ganz trochanteric flip approach.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Non-union 6.2%; screw irritation and removal 20.7%.
audits.c: Selection criteria modified with age limit of 50 years recommended for the trochanteric flip approach.
audits.r2: Non-union 1.3%; no non-unions under age 50; screw irritation and removal 28.3%.

audits.t: Is there adequate provision of venous thromboembolism prophylaxis following hip arthroplasty? An audit and international survey.
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines recommending VTE prophylaxis for 4 weeks after hip arthroplasty
audits.f: Enoxaparin 40 mg once daily: mean duration of prophylaxis 5.4 days.
audits.c: Switch to oral rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily.
audits.r2: Rivaroxaban: mean duration of prophylaxis 35 days.

audits.t: The impact of an Acute Knee Clinic.
audits.tp: Time to specialist review for acute knee injury
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average of five visits of any sort before specialist review.
audits.c: Introduction of a weekly open-access Acute Knee Clinic.
audits.r2: 89% reduction in time to diagnosis for A&E referrals and 32% reduction for GP referrals; average one visit before specialist review.

audits.t: Audit of orthopaedic audits in an english teaching hospital: are we closing the loop?
audits.st: NICE principles for best practice in clinical audit: every audit should complete the cycle with re-audit (100%)
audits.f: Of 61 audits, 12 (19.7%) abandoned, 44 (72.1%) presented and 5 (8.2%) ongoing; audit cycle completed by re-audit in only 13 (29%).
audits.c: Recommendations only (signed undertaking by audit lead, reallocation to a new trainee, email reminders of re-audit dates, consultant supervision); no re-audit reported.

audits.t: Low back pain and physiotherapy use of red flags: the evidence from Scotland.
audits.tp: Red flag documentation in low back pain
audits.st: Evidence- and consensus-based guideline recommendations on red flag assessment in low back pain
audits.f: Documentation of all red flags 33% (n=709); cauda equina syndrome 60% (n=1288).
audits.c: Improvement phase between cycles (details not given in the abstract).
audits.r2: Documentation of all red flags 65% (n=1396); cauda equina syndrome 84% (n=1804).

audits.t: Assessing and improving the knowledge of orthopaedic foundation-year doctors.
audits.st: Orthopaedic consultants' expectations of basic knowledge, assessed by a test; no target stated
audits.f: Knowledge was inadequate against consultants' basic expectations (no figures in abstract).
audits.c: A focused 2-week teaching programme at the start of the orthopaedic job.
audits.r2: Standards improved significantly on a different retest (no figures in abstract).

audits.t: [Clinical audits of the procedure of the total hip arthroplasty and its impact on the improvement of the quality care].
audits.tp: Primary total hip arthroplasty quality indicators
audits.st: Management indicators (hospital stay, readmission rate) and clinical practice indicators (dislocation rate, infection rate) for non-traumatic primary THA; no target stated
audits.f: Median (range) hospital stay 8 (7-78) days

audits.t: Improving prescribing of antiosteoporosis discharge medication in fractured neck of femur patients: a completed audit cycle.
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: Discharge prescription should include the secondary prevention medication recommended by the fracture liaison specialist nurse
audits.f: Recommended secondary prevention medications included in discharge prescriptions in 50.9%
audits.c: Fluorescent drug kardex stickers detailing simple treatment recommendations
audits.r2: Recommended medications prescribed on discharge in 84.6%

audits.t: Is urinary continence considered in the assessment of older people after a fall in England and Wales? Cross-sectional clinical audit results.
audits.st: National falls guidelines for England and Wales: assessment of urinary function including continence
audits.f: Hip fracture: 63% (2009) of 3184 assessed for continence; 41% (817) of these had a problem. Non-hip fragility fracture: 21% (1187) of 5642 assessed; problem found in 27% (316).

audits.t: An audit of current practice and management of metastatic spinal cord compression at a regional cancer centre.
audits.st: NICE guidance on metastatic spinal cord compression
audits.f: 5 (50%) had MRI within 24 hours; 6 (60%) had full MRI scan; 8 (80%) had corticosteroids before MRI; 6 (60%) had radiotherapy within 24 hours; 4 (40%) referred to orthopaedics

audits.t: Iron studies and red cell transfusion in cardiothoracic and orthopaedic surgical patients: a retrospective audit at a tertiary hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 36.5% had preoperative iron studies; of those, 38.5% had anaemia of inflammation, 21.5% IDA, 23.1% normal. 51.5% of patients transfused post-surgery had a discharge Hb ≥110 g/l.

audits.t: Auckland City Hospital's Ortho-Geriatric Service: an audit of patients aged over 65 with fractured neck of femur.
audits.tp: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
audits.st: ANZHFR Minimum Data Set and NICE hip fracture guidelines; national health target of ED admission within 6 hours
audits.f: 76% admitted from ED within 6 hours; 86% had surgery within 48 hours; 82% had rehabilitation by Older People's Health; bisphosphonates prescribed for 56%.

audits.t: The role of a multidisciplinary pre-assessment clinic in reducing mortality after complex orthopaedic surgery.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: PACU admissions 22%, mortality 6.1%, HDU length of stay 2.1 days, ICU unplanned admissions 1.3%, ICU length of stay 2.3 days.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary anaesthetic-led preoperative assessment clinic started in April 2006.
audits.r2: PACU admissions 10%, mortality 1.2% (p = 0.001); HDU length of stay 1.6 days, ICU unplanned admissions 0.4%, ICU length of stay 1.9 days (p = 0.01).

audits.t: The National Falls and Bone Health Audit: implications for UK emergency care.
audits.st: National standards/indicators for integrated falls services developed by a multidisciplinary group
audits.f: Management of falls and bone health in older people remained suboptimal in emergency departments and minor injury units; opportunities for evidence-based risk assessment and management were missed (no figures in abstract).

audits.t: Imaging the spine for tumour and trauma--a national audit of practice in Irish hospitals.
audits.tp: Spinal imaging provision for trauma and tumour
audits.st: International best practice (not specified)
audits.f: 67.64% of centres routinely used a spinal clearance protocol; ED cleared the spine in 87%; CT available in hours in 85.3%, out of hours 47%; MRI available in 50%, out of hours in only two centres.

audits.t: The appropriateness of blood transfusion following primary total hip replacement.
audits.tp: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
audits.st: British Orthopaedic Association guidelines on blood conservation in elective orthopaedic surgery
audits.f: 39/143 (27%) transfused; 18/39 (46%) inappropriate, 9/39 (23%) appropriate, 5/39 (13%) over-transfused, 7/39 (18%) not assessable.
audits.c: Staff education and amendments to local transfusion policy.

audits.t: Enhancing patient recovery following lower limb arthroplasty with a modern wound dressing: a prospective, comparative audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Traditional dressing (Mepore) wear time 2 days.
audits.c: Change from traditional dressing to a modern dressing (Aquacel Surgical).
audits.r2: Modern dressing wear time 7 days, significantly longer.

audits.t: Effect of a patient blood management programme on preoperative anaemia, transfusion rate, and outcome after primary hip or knee arthroplasty: a quality improvement cycle.
audits.st: National agency instruction to implement blood conservation measures including preoperative anaemia management
audits.f: Preoperative Hb predicted allogeneic blood transfusion (odds ratio 0.25 per 1 g/dl)
audits.c: Patient blood management algorithm adapted for UK practice to optimise Hb before arthroplasty and limit perioperative Hb loss
audits.r2: Associated with improved outcome up to 90 days after discharge; figures not given in the supplied text

audits.t: Transition to total one-stop wide-awake hand surgery service-audit: a retrospective review.
audits.tp: One-stop wide-awake hand surgery service outcomes
audits.st: Service targets: one-stop care, wide-awake care, 0% referral to hospital, low DNA rate, 0% litigation, patient satisfaction >99%, 0% deferral for investigation (locally set)
audits.f: Last 1000 consecutive cases: one-stop and wide-awake care achieved in 1000 cases; referral to hospital 0%; DNA rate 0.2%; litigation 0%; patient satisfaction >99%; deferral for investigation 0%; all cases managed within 45 minutes (median 30 minutes); 3 superficial surgical site infections and 15 delayed wound healing cases.
audits.c: Absorbable skin sutures (introduced early 2011) replaced by non-absorbable silk sutures after audit linked them to infection and delayed wound healing.

audits.t: Systems-based safety intervention: reducing falls with injury and total falls on an orthopaedic ward.

audits.c: Four systems-based fall-prevention interventions targeting high-risk situations
audits.r2: Falls with injury 0.41 (p = 0.036) and total falls 2.53 (p = 0.024) per 1000 patient days (12,267 patient days).

audits.t: The use of enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) principles in Scottish orthopaedic units--an implementation and follow-up at 1 year, 2010-2011: a report from the Musculoskeletal Audit, Scotland.

audits.r2: 86 consent forms used the sticker; significant improvement in documentation of fracture, neurovascular damage, leg length discrepancy, failure, loosening, death, medical complications, pain, stiffness, wound problems and other (P<0.0001).

audits.t: Implementing the National Hip Fracture Database: An audit of care.

audits.st: BOA-BGS 'Blue Book' hip fracture guidelines

audits.c: A series of procedural and logistical measures (details not given in abstract).

audits.t: Early MRI diagnostics for suspected scaphoid fractures subsequent to initial plain radiography.

audits.r2: 7 of 77 (9%) diagnosed with scaphoid fracture; mean time to MRI 14 days.

audits.t: A multi-centred audit of secondary spinal assessments in a trauma setting: are we ATLS compliant?
audits.st: ATLS guidelines for secondary survey
audits.f: 29% received digital rectal examination; paralysis level not documented in 20.4%; MRC grade documented in only 24.5% though assessed in 73.5%; secondary survey after 2 h in 54.6%.

audits.t: Primary elective spine arthrodesis: Audit of institutional cross matched to transfused (C/T) ratio to develop blood product ordering guidelines.
audits.tp: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
audits.st: Cross-matched to transfused (C/T) ratio compared with the optimal 2:1 reported in the literature
audits.f: 292 units of packed red cells cross-matched, 66 transfused (C/T ratio 4.4:1); 39 of 85 patients (45.88%) transfused. C/T 6.9:1 for degenerative disease and 23:1 for cervical spine.
audits.c: Recommended a blood ordering schedule: two units for preoperative haemoglobin <9 g/dl, trauma, adult idiopathic scoliosis or more than two levels; group and hold for the rest. Not re-audited.

audits.t: Improving the management of tibia stress fractures: a collaborative, outpatient clinic-based quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Tibial stress fracture screening and management
audits.st: Leg Pain Screening and Referral Tool (LPS&RT) algorithm
audits.f: 16 tibial stress fractures diagnosed.
audits.c: Implementation of the Leg Pain Screening and Referral Tool (LPS&RT) algorithm for lower leg pain.
audits.r2: 30 tibial stress fractures diagnosed (87.5% increase); provider adherence to LPS&RT 93.3% on chart audit.

audits.t: [Implementation of the EndoCert system for certification of arthroplasty centers. Experiences from the pilot phase].
audits.st: EndoCert certification requirements for structural and process quality
audits.f: 172 nonconformities found in 23 pilot clinics.
audits.c: Rectification of nonconformities found at audit.

audits.t: Evaluating the Use of a Negative D-Dimer and Modified Low Wells Score in Excluding above Knee Deep Venous Thrombosis in an Outpatient Population, Assessing Need for Diagnostic Ultrasound.
audits.tp: DVT diagnostic pathway (D-dimer and Wells score)
audits.st: Modified Wells rule (low Wells score with negative D-dimer to avoid ultrasound); re-audit against the local revised diagnostic algorithm; no target stated
audits.f: 510 (96.9%) had D-dimer and ultrasound results; 265 (51.9%) negative D-dimer, of whom 143 (53.9%) had a low Wells score. 7 of 143 with negative D-dimer and low Wells score had a DVT, all with a risk factor not in the Wells score; none without risk factors had a DVT (NPV 100%).
audits.c: Revised clinical diagnostic algorithm adding assessment of extra risk factors to the Wells score; ultrasound omitted in patients with negative D-dimer, low Wells score and no risk factors.
audits.r2: All 290 (100%) had complete results; 94 (32.4%) negative D-dimer, 43 with low Wells score, of whom 30 had risk factors and were scanned. 1/94 (1%) with negative D-dimer had a DVT (on OCP). 13 of 290 (4.5%) not scanned under the algorithm; all negative D-dimer patients had probability score and risk factors recorded.

audits.t: Improving emergency department management of paediatric clavicle fractures: a complete audit cycle.
audits.st: Protocol: uncomplicated minimally displaced middle clavicle fractures discharged without fracture clinic follow-up
audits.f: Unnecessary fracture clinic attendance 85% (47/55).
audits.c: Protocol dividing the clavicle into three zones; minimally displaced middle-third fractures discharged with parental advice.

audits.t: Rapid access imaging for occult fractured neck of femur.
audits.tp: MRI for suspected occult hip fracture
audits.st: NICE hip fracture guidance (June 2011): MRI within 24 hours for suspected occult femoral neck fracture
audits.f: Mean wait for MRI 2,025.4 min (SD 2,406.4).
audits.c: Strategies addressing correctable delays: clinicians not contacting duty radiologist directly, slow vetting and protocoling of electronic requests, resistance to weekend scanning, and delay in MRI safety questionnaire completion; results presented at directorate audit meetings
audits.r2: 16% improvement in patients scanned within 24 h; mean wait 1,374 min (SD 1,635.7); mean difference 651.4 min (95% CI 85.21, 1,217.5; p = 0.0243).

audits.t: Audit improves emergency department triage, assessment, multi-modal analgesia and nerve block use in the management of pain in older people with neck of femur fracture.
audits.tp: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block
audits.st: Evidence-based use of nerve blocks and multimodal analgesia for older patients with neck of femur fracture (no target stated)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Educational and awareness strategies on pain management for emergency department clinical staff.
audits.r2: Significant increase in nerve block use and multimodal analgesia and a reduction in average milligrams of morphine given (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Audit of operation notes in an orthopaedic unit.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons guidelines on operation notes
audits.f: Good documentation of date and time (100%), surgeon (100%), procedure (100%), duration (94%), diagnosis (92%), incision (84%), signature (84%); poor for tourniquet time (32%; 8 of 25), closure details (16%) and postoperative instructions (24%).

audits.t: Data quality audit of the arthroplasty clinical outcomes registry NSW.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Benchmark of 95.0% for data completeness and accuracy against reabstracted medical record data
audits.f: Completeness 99.0% (1259/1272) Hospital A and 99.3% (1589/1600) Hospital B; accuracy 94.0% (2159/2296) Hospital A and 96.1% (2444/2542) Hospital B. 57.1% (28/49) of variables met the 95% accuracy benchmark in A and 74.5% (38/51) in B. Registry captured 93.5% (660/706) of eligible patients.

audits.t: An audit of fresh frozen plasma usage in a tertiary trauma care centre in north India.
audits.st: College of American Pathologists guidelines for FFP transfusion
audits.f: Appropriate FFP use 49.5%

audits.t: Weber C ankle fractures: a retrospective audit of screw number, size, complications, and retrieval rates.
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Minimally invasive surgery for pedal digital deformity: an audit of complications using national benchmark indicators.
audits.tp: Complications of minimally invasive lesser toe surgery
audits.st: Australasian College of Podiatric Surgeons surgical audit clinical indicators (developed from the ACHS clinical indicator program); compared with published complication rates for open digital surgery
audits.f: 299 digits operated on; 1 superficial infection (0.56%), 2 under-corrections needing revision (0.67%); no other ACPS indicator events, no neurovascular or medical complications

audits.t: Enhanced recovery from surgery in the UK: an audit of the enhanced recovery partnership programme 2009-2012.
audits.st: Enhanced Recovery protocol elements; good compliance defined as 80% or more
audits.f: Compliance weakly associated with shorter stay (r -0.18 colorectal, -0.14 orthopaedics, -0.25 gynaecology); 80% compliance linked to 2, 1 and 3 day shorter median stay in colorectal, orthopaedic and urological surgery

audits.t: Improving the care of patients with a hip fracture: a quality improvement report.
audits.st: Operative intervention within 36 h of admission (Best Practice Tariff / National Hip Fracture Database)
audits.f: Mean time to theatre 49±39 h

audits.t: Hospital audit of delayed transfusion after orthopaedic surgery.
audits.tp: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Delayed transfusion (>12 hours after threshold reached) in 57% of severely anaemic patients.

audits.t: The impact of a national clinician-led audit initiative on care and mortality after hip fracture in England: an external evaluation using time trends in non-audit data.
audits.tp: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
audits.st: BOA/BGS six national hip fracture standards (including surgery within 48 hours); outcome measures were early surgery (day of or day after admission) and 30-day mortality
audits.f: Whole 2003-2011 cohort n=471,590. Before NHFD: early surgery fairly stable (annual RR 0.987, 1.3% relative decrease per year); 30-day mortality fell from 11.5% to 10.9% (1.8% relative reduction per year).
audits.c: Launch of the National Hip Fracture Database in 2007: national clinical standards, continuous web-based audit feedback, helpline, website and regional meetings
audits.r2: Early surgery rose from 54.5% to 71.3% (annual RR 1.080); 30-day mortality fell from 10.9% to 8.5% (7.6% relative reduction per year; P<0.001 for difference in trend).

audits.t: Management of hip fractures in older people in Beijing: a retrospective audit and comparison with evidence-based guidelines and practice in the UK.
audits.tp: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
audits.st: UK Blue Book standards, compared with National Hip Fracture Database 2012 (180 UK hospitals)
audits.f: 66% admitted to orthopaedic ward within 24 h; 8% surgery within 48 h (UK 83%); 10% no surgery; 27% orthogeriatric assessment (UK 70%); 0.3% osteoporosis assessment (UK 94%); 3.8% falls assessment (UK 92%)

audits.t: Trimodal venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in total knee replacement: A quality improvement project for best care practices.
audits.st: National guidelines for risk stratification and trimodal VTE prophylaxis (chemical, mechanical, early ambulation)
audits.f: Frontline staff negligence identified as the main cause of nonadherence in the mechanical arm (figures not given in the supplied text).

audits.t: Improving Osteoporosis Management in Primary Care: An Audit of the Impact of a Community Based Fracture Liaison Nurse.
audits.tp: Bone protection and secondary fracture prevention
audits.st: Anticipated pay-for-performance (QOF/Directed Enhanced Service) osteoporosis indicators: register of patients with fragility fracture, and treatment with a bone-sparing agent in those aged 50–74 with confirmed osteoporosis and in those aged 75 and over with a fragility fracture
audits.f: Females 50–74 (n=13,519) and ≥75 (n=4,883). Bone-sparing agent in those aged 50–74 with fragility fracture and confirmed osteoporosis 47.9% (23/48); in those ≥75 with fragility fracture 39.5% (118/181). Fragility fracture recorded 8.8% (15/171) aged 50–74 and 0.8% (65/8110) aged ≥75.
audits.c: Introduction of a community-based fracture liaison nurse who reviewed the practice population meeting the inclusion criteria.
audits.r2: Bone-sparing agent 84.0% (42/50) aged 50–74 and 70.5% (222/316) aged ≥75 (p<0.001). Fragility fracture recorded 14% (25/178) aged 50–74 (p=0.168) and 2.3% (199/8702) aged ≥75 (p<0.001).

audits.t: Accurate falls risk assessment and interventions for preventing falls in patients in the acute care setting within a private hospital in a large capital city: a best practice implementation project.
audits.st: Hospital Falls Minimization Program and National Safety and Quality Health Service Standard 10 (Preventing Falls and Harm from Falls); eight JBI audit criteria
audits.f: Baseline audit showed significant opportunity for improvement in all criteria (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Corrective action plan after the baseline audit (details not given in abstract).
audits.r2: Results were maintained and consistent with the first follow-up audit (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: "Early Trigger" Intravenous Vitamin K: Optimizing Target-Driven Care in Warfarinised Patients With Hip Fracture.
audits.st: Hip fracture best practice tariff: surgery within 36 hours of admission
audits.f: Warfarinised patients on oral vitamin K protocol: mean time to theatre 53.71 hours; 79% breached BPT due to anticoagulation.
audits.c: Nurse-led 'early trigger' protocol giving 2 mg intravenous vitamin K in the emergency department before the INR result, added to the fast-track pathway.
audits.r2: Mean time to theatre 37.61 hours (p<0.0001); 34% breached BPT due to anticoagulation; 21 (50%) operated within 36 hours and 33 (79%) within 48 hours.

audits.t: National audits of hip fractures: Are yearly audits required?
audits.tp: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
audits.st: Scottish hip fracture clinical standards including discharge from A&E within 4 h and surgery within 48 h of admission
audits.f: Discharge from A&E within 4 h improved from 80.5% (2003) to 96% (2008); surgery within 48 h improved from 89.9% to 98.4%.
audits.c: Continuous annual audit discontinued in 2008, then re-introduced in 2014
audits.r2: A&E 4 h improvement not maintained; surgery within 48 h fell to 91.8%.

audits.t: Venous thromboembolism rates in patients with lower limb immobilization after Achilles tendon injury are unchanged after the introduction of prophylactic aspirin: audit.
audits.st: Local policy to routinely prescribe aspirin 100 mg daily for Achilles tendon injury requiring lower limb immobilisation
audits.f: Aspirin prescribed in 0.5%; symptomatic VTE incidence 6.3%.
audits.c: Introduction of a policy to routinely prescribe aspirin 100 mg daily
audits.r2: Aspirin prescribed to 189/218 (93%); symptomatic VTE in 14 (6.4%, 95% CI 3.6-10.5%), unchanged.

audits.t: Blood tests: One too many? Evaluating blood requesting guidance developed for acute patients admitted to trauma and orthopaedic units.
audits.tp: Blood test requesting in acute admissions
audits.st: Locally developed multidisciplinary blood requesting guidelines
audits.f: LFTs 895, coagulation/INR 307, CRP 894; mean 4.81 requests per patient (SD 4.75); cost £2674.14.
audits.c: Clinical guidelines for blood requesting developed with multidisciplinary input and implemented in the department.

audits.t: Improving spinal trauma management in non-specialist centres.
audits.st: Local standards of 95% for neurological examination, management plan, stability, permitted mobility and precautions documentation
audits.f: No criterion met the standard; hospital 1: neurological examination 74%, stability 44%, precautions 53%, permitted mobility 26%, delay in treatment 59%, serious medical concern 37% (7/19)
audits.c: Spinal injuries proforma and ASIA chart placed on trust computers, introduced via M&M presentations, email and face-to-face; desktop icon added
audits.r2: Hospital 1: neurological examination 100%, stability 95%, precautions 100%, permitted mobility 95%, delay in treatment 11%, serious medical concern 6% (1/18)

audits.t: Using a proforma to improve standards of documentation of an orthopaedic post-take ward round.
audits.st: GMC and Royal College of Physicians documentation recommendations: clearly documented PTWR, date/time, consultant on take, clinician leading and documenting, presenting complaint and management plan
audits.f: 72% seen on PTWR, 47% of these clearly labelled; 64% of those not seen were weekend admissions; no consultant on take identifiable in 19%, presenting complaint missing in 78%, no plan in 3%, not timed in 17%, no name 19%, no signature 14%, no grade 50%, no contact details 25%.
audits.c: Trauma Meeting/Post-Take Ward Round proforma on yellow paper, designed with the team (PDSA cycles), results presented at departmental teaching, and weekend surgical juniors briefed to attend the trauma meeting and complete it.
audits.r2: Not seen on PTWR fell from 28% to 18% (4% weekend admissions); 88% of those seen had a proforma; 18% of all cases had no proforma; consultant unidentifiable in 4%; all entries signed and dated; no name 12%, no contact details 15%, no grade 10%.

audits.t: Medical rota changes and venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in orthopaedic patients.
audits.st: SIGN guideline 122 VTE prophylaxis; seven-item checklist (weight/BMI and eGFR recorded, correct LMWH dose, timely administration, AES prescribed and worn, early mobilisation, hydration), 100% target
audits.f: 71% of patients compliant with all measures; errors mainly medical (failure to prescribe LMWH or stockings, incorrect dosing), plus nursing and patient errors; about 30% of surveyed patients (n=47) understood aims of VTE prophylaxis.
audits.c: Policy of prophylaxis unless contraindicated, summarised guidelines displayed on wards, MDT teaching for doctors and nurses, patient education, VTE added to handover and radiology meeting, teaching after rota change, and VTE education added to junior doctor induction.
audits.r2: Re-audit 4: 100% compliance; 80% of patients understood aims of VTE prophylaxis.

audits.t: Continuity of care for orthopaedic patients in a district general hospital.
audits.st: Local standard from patient survey: a patient should be seen by the same surgeon from preoperative clinic to surgery and postoperative follow-up
audits.f: Same surgeon throughout 23%; same team 43%; operated on by clinic surgeon 50%; followed up by operating surgeon 40%; trauma continuity 10%.
audits.c: Trauma on-call rota reorganised to weekly consultant 'on take' so the admitting team operates, and ward clerk booked follow-up into the operating surgeon's clinic.
audits.r2: Same surgeon throughout 24%; same team 56%; operated on by clinic surgeon 60%; followed up by operating surgeon 43%; trauma same team 75%.

audits.t: Improving inpatient care with the introduction of a hip fracture pathway.
audits.tp: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
audits.st: National Hip Fracture Database best practice tariff criteria (surgery within 36 h, orthogeriatric review within 72 h, pre- and post-operative AMT, etc.)
audits.f: BPT achieved in 8/18 (44.4%); 4 waited >36 h for surgery, 7 >72 h for orthogeriatric review, 9 lacked both AMT scores; FI block in ED 3/18 (16.7%)
audits.c: Eight-page multidisciplinary clerking booklet, hip fracture care group, twice-weekly consultant orthogeriatric ward rounds, and booklet in local induction
audits.r2: BPT achieved in 22/24 (91.7%); all had both AMT scores; FI block in ED in 6

audits.t: Improving the availability of intra-operative images created during trauma operations - a multidisciplinary team collaboration.
audits.st: All intraoperative images available on PACS within 72 hours of being taken (local target)
audits.f: 9/27 (33%) images available within 72 hours; 4 (15%) delayed by failure to request, 14 (52%) requested but not processed
audits.c: Radiographers told not to screen without a valid request; tick box added to trauma list submission template; agreement with radiology to upload within 72 hours; radiographers invited to trauma meeting; changes communicated by email and governance meetings
audits.r2: 90% of images processed within 72 hours; delays from failure to request eliminated

audits.t: Improving handover of acute orthopaedic admissions.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England handover guidance (2007) plus local orthopaedic-specific criteria
audits.f: Poor handover: patient location 57%, responsible consultant 14%, results of significant/pending investigations 29%, co-morbidities 38%, outstanding tasks 38%; one patient not handed over and one nerve injury not handed over.
audits.c: Trauma-specific paper handover proforma (SHOs informed by email and verbally), then an electronic proforma accessible from any hospital computer, created with IT.
audits.r2: With the electronic proforma only one criterion fell below 95% (results of pending investigations 82%); no patient safety issues; proforma uptake 100%.

audits.t: Postoperative analgesia for Enhanced recovery in Joint replacement: Audit of a new electronic prescribing order set.

audits.f: 0/27 patients received all medications according to the protocol
audits.c: Electronic prescribing order set (JAC) for the analgesia protocol introduced in August 2014; results presented, re-education of rotating junior staff and protocol added to induction documentation
audits.r2: Total compliance 58%; gabapentin 96%, modified-release morphine 96%, weak opioid 100%, conversion to PRN analgesia 100%, ibuprofen 58%

audits.t: Are patients with newly diagnosed breast cancer getting appropriate DEXA scans? A District General Hospital experience.

audits.f: 100 patients sampled, 66 with early/locally invasive cancer, 42 with an indication; 16/42 (38%) had a DEXA scan. Of those scanned 8/16 (50%) osteopaenic and 1/16 (6%) osteoporotic.
audits.c: Results presented to surgical and oncology departments and the breast MDT, posters summarising the guideline in breast clinics and MDT areas, and MDT discussion of the need for DEXA.
audits.r2: 11/11 (100%) indicated patients received a DEXA scan (17 early breast cancers).

audits.t: Audit of Atypical Femoral Fractures and a Description of Some of Their Features.

audits.t: An audit of consent for allograft use in elective orthopaedic surgery.

audits.t: Discontinuation of peri-operative gentamicin use for indwelling urinary catheter manipulation in orthopaedic surgery.

audits.t: Reducing mortality from hip fractures: a systematic quality improvement programme.

audits.t: Virtual fracture clinic delivers British Orthopaedic Association compliance.

audits.t: Reducing time to surgery after anterior cruciate ligament injury.
audits.st: ACL reconstruction within 12 months of injury
audits.f: Mean time from injury to surgery 14 months (range 3-56).
audits.c: Acute Knee Clinic established in December 2004.
audits.r2: 21 Acute Knee Clinic patients: mean 6 months to surgery, 95% within 12 months; 28 elective clinic patients: mean 25 months, 53% within 12 months.

audits.t: Audit of geriatric hip fracture care - a Slovenian trauma center analysis.
audits.tp: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 20% seen preoperatively by a physician or geriatrician; 93.1% had surgical repair, 58.5% of them within 48 h of admission.

audits.t: Change the habit to change the practice: Do audits really ever change anything?
audits.st: Local MRSA guidelines: eradication therapy and correct induction antibiotics for MRSA-unknown patients
audits.f: Eradication therapy prescribed 1%; correct antibiotic choice 18%. Operation median 24.05 h from admission but MRSA swab results at median 48 h.
audits.c: Posters on induction antibiotics in anaesthetic rooms and stickers on MRSA eradication therapy on nursing care bundles.
audits.r2: Eradication therapy prescribed 8%; correct antibiotic choice 94%.

audits.t: An Audit to Evaluate the Image Quality of Magnetic Resonance of Knee at Radiology Department of a Tertiary Care Hospital.
audits.st: American College of Radiology (ACR) recommendations for knee MRI image acquisition
audits.f: All three planes acquired; sagittal and coronal slice thickness, gap and coverage appropriate in all. FOV appropriate in 66% axial, 5% sagittal, 0% coronal; adequate axial superior coverage in 13 (66%) and inferior coverage in 16 (80%).
audits.c: Recommendations (decrease FOV in all planes, increase axial anatomical coverage) presented in departmental meetings.

audits.t: The Introduction of a Multidisciplinary Hip Fracture Pathway to Optimise Patient Care and Reduce Mortality: A Prospective Audit of 161 Patients.
audits.tp: Hip fracture care standards (national audit and best practice tariff)
audits.st: Cycle 1: Best Practice Tariff time to orthogeriatric assessment <72 hours and time to surgery <36 hours. Cycle 2: 100% preoperative medical assessment, orthogeriatric assessment <24 hours, time to surgery <36 hours
audits.f: Preoperative medical assessment 19%; mean time to orthogeriatric assessment 91 hours; mean time to surgery 37 hours; mean length of stay 24.8 days; inpatient mortality 14%.
audits.c: New multidisciplinary hip fracture pathway from 1 June 2011: direct admission to the acute medical ward under joint named medical and orthopaedic consultants, anaesthetic assessment within 12 hours, consultant orthopaedic and orthogeriatric review within 24 hours; seminars and laminated posters for staff.
audits.r2: Preoperative medical assessment 85% (p=0.0001); mean time to orthogeriatric assessment 19 hours (p=0.0001); mean time to surgery 31 hours (p=0.0663); length of stay 19.5 days (p=0.029); mortality 4% (p=0.0336).

audits.t: Improving time to surgery for hip fracture patients. Impact of the introduction of an emergency theatre.
audits.st: Surgery on the day of or after admission; delay over 36 hours measured
audits.f: 49% delayed over 36 hours; lack of theatre space caused 28.6% (9 of 32) of delays.
audits.r2: 26% delayed over 36 hours; lack of theatre space caused 23% (3 of 13) of delays.

audits.t: A representative assessment of the management of open fractures of the lower limb within UK orthoplastic centres: A two-centre audit of compliance with national standards.
audits.st: BOAST 4 (BAPRAS/BOA) and NICE guidance: debridement within 24h, soft tissue cover within 72h and 7 days
audits.f: Debridement within 24h 83 (98.8%); plastic surgeon at 33.3% of initial operations; soft tissue cover within 72h 56.4% and within 7 days 78.2% (of 78).

audits.t: Upcoming strategies in obstetrics: how the technology of clinical audit may reduce cesarean birth.
audits.st: Five literature-derived quality criteria for elective caesarean section, each with a standard; repeat caesarean rate standard ≤30%
audits.f: Most indicators met the standard; caesarean rate for previous caesarean was 84% (73/86) against a standard of ≤30%.

audits.t: An audit of clinical training exposure amongst junior doctors working in Trauma & Orthopaedic Surgery in 101 hospitals in the United Kingdom.
audits.st: JCST Core Quality Indicators 10 (minimum 5 consultant-supervised sessions per week) and 16 (2 trauma and 1 elective operating sessions and at least 1 fracture clinic per week)
audits.f: QI 10 met by 51/200 (25.5%) CSTs; QI 16 met by 11/200 (5.5%); both standards met by 10/200 (5%)

audits.t: Improving Management of Paediatric Buckle Fracture in Orthopaedic Outpatients: A Completed Audit Loop.
audits.tp: Paediatric buckle and forearm fracture management
audits.st: NICE NG38: buckle fractures treated with non-rigid cast or splint without routine follow-up
audits.f: 59 fracture clinic visits; mean 1.9 visits per child
audits.c: Parents taught about fracture type and soft cast removal and offered no further visits; information leaflet designed with plaster technicians and nurses

audits.t: A service evaluation and improvement project: a three year systematic audit cycle of the physiotherapy treatment for Lateral Epicondylalgia.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Phase two: strengthening as core treatment; phase three: standardised protocol of high load isometric exercise progressing to concentric and eccentric strengthening.
audits.r2: Average number of treatments reduced by 42% and responders increased by 8% compared with phase one.

audits.t: An Orthopaedic Fracture Clinic Service Audit: A Complete Loop.
audits.tp: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
audits.st: BOAST Guideline 7 (fracture clinic services), assessed with a patient questionnaire adapted from the RCSI SWOPS questionnaire; no target stated
audits.f: Average wait for appointment 3.55 days (85 hours); wait to see doctor in clinic 56.81 minutes; doctors rated excellent 75%; X-ray facilities inadequate 34.7%; waiting area inadequate 44.93%; overall experience excellent 50.72%.
audits.c: Changed fracture clinic appointment rotation, increased doctors on site, ensured patients returning from X-ray saw the same doctor, optimised follow-up X-ray process and increased waiting area seating from about 40 to 50; findings on X-ray location passed to management.
audits.r2: Average wait for appointment 3.21 days (77.04 hours); wait to see doctor 52.55 minutes; doctors rated excellent 73.9%; X-ray facilities inadequate 32.79%; waiting area inadequate 41.49%; overall experience excellent 53.55%.

audits.t: Customizable pre-printed consent forms: a solution in light of the Montgomery ruling.
audits.st: Montgomery ruling standard for consent (material risks); legibility and completeness
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: New pre-printed but customisable consent form.
audits.r2: Improved legibility, reduced error variation and abolished abbreviations and jargon (no numbers given).

audits.t: Developing and Testing an International Audit of Nursing Quality Indicators for Older Adults With Fragility Hip Fracture.
audits.tp: Nursing quality indicators in hip fracture
audits.st: 12 internationally accepted nursing quality care indicators for older adults with fragility hip fracture
audits.f: 35 hospitals (100%) completed the audit; quality indicators were reflected in the majority of policies, protocols or processes, with variable timing and frequency

audits.t: Improving consent in patients undergoing surgery for fractured neck of femur.
audits.st: British Orthopaedic Association-endorsed consent guidance (12 potential risks)
audits.f: 4/12 risks documented in <50% of intracapsular fractures (n=35) and 7/12 in <50% of extracapsular fractures (n=35)
audits.c: Raising awareness and attaching consent guidance; neck of femur fracture-specific consent form then implemented
audits.r2: 100% documentation of potential risks in intracapsular and extracapsular fractures

audits.t: Prevention of Glucocorticoid-Induced Osteoporosis: Clinical audit to evaluate the implementation of National Osteoporosis Guideline Group 2017 guidelines in a primary care setting.
audits.st: NOGG 2017 guidelines for patients on long-term glucocorticoids; target 90% investigated and treated appropriately
audits.f: Only 25% of patients recommended bisphosphonates were taking them.
audits.c: GP education on FRAX and NOGG; COPD annual template amended with glucocorticoid course alerts and prompts for alendronate and lifestyle leaflet; 2-monthly RAIDR searches by practice pharmacist

audits.t: Supracondylar Humeral Fractures: An Audit of the Frequency of Bi-columnar Fixation and Intra-articular Wire Placement.
audits.st: UK national guidelines: displaced supracondylar fractures treated by early surgical stabilisation with bicortical wire fixation; bi-columnar fixation assessed on intra-operative AP radiograph
audits.f: Bi-columnar fixation achieved in 41/49 (84%): 7/7 (100%) cross-wire cases and 34/42 (81%) lateral-entry-only cases. Intra-articular wire in 44/49 (90%). Loss of fixation needing revision 1/49 (2%), in a case without bi-columnar fixation (1/8, 13%).

audits.t: Making the weekend work: a local quality improvement project to establish and improve the quality of weekend handover.
audits.st: 10 handover components derived from RCS, RCP and BMA handover guidelines, each with a set standard (some patient identifiers at 100%); aim to raise compliance to 90–100%
audits.f: Baseline (247 handovers over nine weeks): patient name 99%, hospital number 94%, admission reason 91%, other categories 12% to 84% (date of birth 54%, location 84%, frequency of review 70%, TTO 12%); only admission reason met its standard.
audits.c: Two-step change: extra columns (TTO, day to be seen, DNAR) added to the Word handover table, then a new intranet handover tool with drop-down boxes, date selector and multiuser access; instruction document given at induction.
audits.r2: Sustainability re-audit of intranet tool (201 handovers, new cohort of doctors): patient name 100%, hospital number 98%, date of birth 85%; five of 10 categories met their standard (patient name, location, consultant, admission reason, frequency of review); all except TTO were above 50%.

audits.t: Addressing Hand Hygiene Compliance in a Low-Resource Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: a Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Hand hygiene protocols
audits.f: Of 1227 planned contacts: hand-washing 707 (58.6%), hand rub 442 (36%), missed 78 (6.4%); missed rate 20% during resuscitation.
audits.c: Hand rubs placed at each bassinet after departmental review.

audits.t: Benzodiazepine and Z-drug Prescribing for Elderly People in a General Hospital: A Complete Audit Cycle.
audits.tp: Benzodiazepine and Z-drug prescribing in older inpatients
audits.st: Evidence-based consensus guidelines on benzodiazepine and Z-drug prescribing in older adults
audits.f: Prevalence of benzodiazepine/Z-drug use 54% (38/70); 36% (25/70) started before admission.
audits.c: Audit results and consensus guidelines sent to all GPs in County Sligo; educational sessions for doctors and nurses.
audits.r2: Prevalence 46% (32/70), not statistically significant; started before admission 23% (16/70).

audits.t: Enhanced Recovery in Orthopedics: A Prospective Audit of an Enhanced Recovery Program for Patients Undergoing Hip or Knee Arthroplasty.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Improved pain management, reduced nausea and vomiting and quicker recovery reported (no numbers in abstract).

audits.t: Opioid prescribing in orthopaedic and neurosurgical specialties in a tertiary hospital: a retrospective audit of hospital discharge data.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: About 82% discharged on opioids; combination opioids in 71.4% (orthopaedic) and 73.8% (neurosurgical); only 6.9% and 11.5% of discharge summaries referred to opioid management.

audits.t: Weight-bearing in ankle fractures: An audit of UK practice.
audits.st: NICE: early (within 3 weeks) unrestricted weight-bearing
audits.f: 81% of 531 non-operatively managed patients instructed for early weight-bearing; only 21% of 276 operatively managed patients.

audits.t: Current imaging practice for suspected scaphoid fracture in patients with normal initial radiographs: UK-wide national audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 74 of 140 trusts responded (53%). 38 offered MRI first line for radiographically occult scaphoid injury (51% of trusts), 25 preferred CT and 11 repeat plain radiographs. Of the 38 offering MRI, 26 provided it within 1 week and the rest within 2 weeks.

audits.t: Improving Orthopedic-Related Postoperative Edema Management in a Rehabilitative Nursing Setting.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 96% had oedema on admission; length of stay 19.2 days.
audits.c: Standardised staff and patient oedema education, including an educational video.
audits.r2: 97% had oedema on admission; length of stay 16.3 days.

audits.t: Are we neglecting sexual function assessment in suspected cauda equina syndrome?
audits.tp: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Lower limb neurology, urinary function and saddle sensation were almost universally documented; sexual function poorly documented.
audits.c: Results presented locally to increase awareness.
audits.r2: Significant increase in documentation of certain features (p value not given in abstract); sexual function still poorly documented.

audits.t: Can we reduce the number of MRSA screening site swabs in elective orthopedic patients?
audits.st: Trust four-site MRSA screening policy (nose, throat, axilla, groin)
audits.f: Positive sites: nose 69.60% (n=96), groin 26.10% (n=36), throat 25.30% (n=35), axilla 8.70% (n=12); a nose, groin and throat three-swab policy would miss 2.2%.
audits.c: Screening policy changed from four-swab to three-swab (nose, throat, groin)
audits.r2: Audited four times after the change; all were negative (no figures given).

audits.t: Perioperative Blood Management, Red Cell Recovery (Cell Salvage) Practice in an Australian Tertiary Hospital: A Hospital District Clinical Audit.
audits.tp: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
audits.st: Australian national cell salvage guidelines
audits.f: 79% compliance with national guidelines; orthopaedics used most cases (22.9%, n = 108).

audits.t: Fracture clinic service redesign: an audit evaluating clinic waiting times and compliance to British Orthopaedic Association standards.
audits.tp: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
audits.st: British Orthopaedic Association standards for fracture clinics
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Fracture clinic service redesign (details not reported).

audits.t: Fixation of ankle fractures - a major trauma centre's experience in improving quality.
audits.st: Reduction criteria published by Pettrone et al.
audits.f: Malreduction rate 33%.
audits.c: Education and reflection between 2013 and 2015; then a change in process in ankle fracture management supported by education between 2015 and 2017.

audits.t: Opioid prescribing improvement in orthopaedic specialty unit in a tertiary hospital: a retrospective audit of hospital discharge data pre- and post-intervention for better opioid prescribing practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 82.2% (n = 231) discharged on opioids; 71.4% discharged on combination opioids.
audits.c: Expert Advisory Group oversight of opioid prescribing, a prescription opioid guideline and a series of education sessions.
audits.r2: 79.6% (n = 230) discharged on opioids; combination opioids fell to 45.7%.

audits.t: Shoulder Reduction Bench Project: improving care for patients with shoulder dislocations.
audits.st: Royal College of Emergency Medicine guidelines on time to shoulder dislocation reduction (2-hour RCEM clinical standard of 75% for initial attempt at reduction)
audits.f: Average triage to confirmed shoulder reduction X-ray 2 hours 25 min (range 1 h 14 min to 5 h 3 min); triage to discharge 3 hours 22 min (range 1 h 46 min to 6 h 39 min); 57% (17/30) sedated for reduction.
audits.c: Shoulder Reduction Bench (modified Oxford Chair) introduced with three PDSA cycles: training of emergency nurse practitioners, written protocol and flowchart on the intranet, and an online training video.
audits.r2: Average triage to confirmed reduction X-ray 1 hour 54 min (31 min, 21% reduction); triage to discharge 2 hours 30 min (52 min, 26% reduction); 18% (7) sedated, a 68% reduction.

audits.t: Trust compliance with best practice tariff criteria for total hip and knee replacement.
audits.tp: Best practice tariff compliance for hip and knee replacement
audits.st: Best practice tariff criteria: NJR compliance at least 85%, NJR unknown consent below 15%, PROMs participation ≥50%, average health gain not significantly below national average
audits.f: PROMs participation rate 31% due to a systematic error in submitting preoperative PROM scores.
audits.c: PROM data resubmitted under the trust's correct organisation data service code.
audits.r2: PROMs compliance 90% and all criteria satisfied.

audits.t: Effects of protocol on prevention of delirium in hospitalized hip fracture patients: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Hip fracture delirium and cognitive assessment
audits.st: Evidence-based delirium prevention protocol; records audited with the CHART-DEL instrument
audits.f: Delirium incidence 11.1% (pre-implementation).
audits.c: Evidence-based hip fracture delirium prevention protocol introduced.
audits.r2: Delirium incidence 15.6% (not statistically significant); protocol used by admitting physicians in 31% of admissions; prevention interventions documented by nurses in 75.6% of records.

audits.t: The effect of a multidisciplinary care bundle on the incidence of delirium after hip fracture surgery: a quality improvement study.
audits.tp: Hip fracture delirium and cognitive assessment
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Delirium on day 3: 49 (33%); bundle compliance ED 49 (33%), anaesthesia 40 (27%), orthogeriatrics 140 (93%).
audits.c: Perioperative care bundle: fascia iliaca blocks, rationalised analgesia, avoidance of deliriogenic drugs, regular staff education and continuous compliance audit.
audits.r2: Delirium on day 3: 33 (22%) (p = 0.04); bundle compliance ED 85 (59%), anaesthesia 104 (69%), orthogeriatrics 143 (95%).

audits.t: Pain relief during wound care for patients with a deep open wound in an orthopedic trauma department: a best practice implementation project.
audits.st: JBI best practice recommendations for pain relief during wound care
audits.f: Poor compliance with best practice (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Recommended changes implemented using the Getting Research into Practice barriers and strategies (details not given).
audits.r2: Significant improvements after implementation, but not adequately maintained at the second follow-up audit.

audits.t: Injury coding in a national trauma registry: a one-year validation audit in a level 1 trauma centre.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Expert coder group consensus reference standard using the AIS 2005 Update 2008 manual (review of all EHR data and reinterpretation of all imaging); no target stated
audits.f: 582 AIS codes in the registry vs 766 in the reference standard. All injuries concordantly coded in 62 (43.1%) patients. 166 missing codes in 71 (49.3%) patients, mostly AIS 1, chiefly EHR information overlooked by coders. 157 discordant codes in 74 (51.4%) patients, mainly head injuries and extremity fractures. Median ISS (9) and NISS (12) identical in registry and reference standard; ISS changed in 52 (36.1%) patients; no significant difference on Bland–Altman regression (ISS p = 0.078, NISS p = 0.656).

audits.t: Enhancing the verbal handover process for nurses in inpatient orthopedic wards: a best practice implementation project.
audits.st: JBI evidence-based best practice criteria for handover (PACES)
audits.f: Poor compliance in handover of essential patient information (figures not given in the supplied text).
audits.c: Handover guide for registered nurse to enrolled nurse handovers, using the GRiP approach.
audits.r2: Significant increase in compliance (figures not given in the supplied text).

audits.t: Fracture clinic referrals: the need for self audit.
audits.tp: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
audits.st: not reported
