audits.c: Findings presented and physical health equipment boxes placed in ward clinic rooms
audits.r2: Mean availability 73.5% (range 72.2%-77.8%); mean percentage increase 12.5% (range -12.5% to 41.8%)

audits.t: An audit of admission clerking of patients in Heddfan, Adult Mental Health Unit in BCUHB - north Wales
audits.st: Standard based on RCPsych core training intended learning outcomes and textbooks; target 100% compliance
audits.f: GMC number documented 30%, route of admission 4%, consultant name 8%, nursing observation level 20%; no personal history or formulation documented; risk assessment, mental state and physical examination often incomplete.

audits.t: Junior doctor daytime bleep audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 249 daytime bleeps; about 70% (East) and 90% (West) judged appropriate versus 15% (Central); 70% (East) and about 95% (Central) deferrable.

audits.t: Audit on use of PRN (pro re nata) psychotropic medication for behavioural disturbance in individuals with intellectual disability in the community
audits.st: Standards for PRN psychotropic protocols for behavioural disturbance (protocol accessible, indications, de-escalation, maximum dose, recording)
audits.f: Medical file standards 100% achieved; PRN protocol standards achieved in only 53% of cases.

audits.t: Audit of the quality and content of discharge summaries from mental health inpatient units across Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
audits.st: RCPsych Standards for Inpatient Mental Health Services (2014) and PRSB Mental Health Discharge guidelines (2018)
audits.f: Allergy status not mentioned in 96% of Hergest summaries; summary reached GP on day of discharge in 13% Ablett, 0% Hergest, 100% Heddfan; risk history 0% Hergest and Heddfan, 12% Ablett; crisis contacts 0% across the Health Board.

audits.t: VTE prophylaxis admission assessment full cycle audit and QI project
audits.st: Completion of VTE prophylaxis admission assessment
audits.f: Overall compliance 35%; VTE risk assessment 50%, active VTE on admission 30%, active VTE at 72 hours 20%, risk assessment form 40%.
audits.r2: Overall compliance 50%; VTE risk assessment 60%, active VTE on admission 40%, active VTE at 72 hours 40%, risk assessment form 60%.

audits.t: An audit of Individual Care Plan (ICP) in Dublin North City and County (DNCC) child and adolescent mental health service (CAMHS)
audits.tp: Care plan documentation in mental health
audits.st: Established service policy on individual care plans (ICP): every patient should have a care plan with key worker, formulation, goals, action plan, copy to young person/parents, review date and projected discharge date
audits.f: Overall compliance with ICP components 62%
audits.c: Findings and intervention discussed at the multidisciplinary team meeting and wider DNCC CAMHS academic meeting; intervention not otherwise described

audits.t: Audit on availability, quality and frequency of clincal and educational supervision
audits.st: Severn deanery and trust recommendation of one hour of supervision per week
audits.f: 17/27 (63%) responded; over half had no time set aside for e-portfolio; 4/7 core trainees discussed audit/QI with supervisors most/always; 100% found supervisors supportive; WPBA and portfolio review completion suboptimal.
audits.c: Supervision template created; extension to a regional quality improvement project underway.

audits.t: Assessing the quality of risk assessment conducted for new psychiatry inpatients
audits.tp: Risk assessment documentation in mental health
audits.st: Junior doctors document risk assessment in admission clerking
audits.f: 12/30 (40%) had a junior doctor risk assessment in clerking; 14 (47%) had none on admission.
audits.c: Teaching on risk assessment and a risk assessment template.

audits.t: Dementia screening: an audit of screening for reversible causes of dementia
audits.tp: Memory service referral quality and dementia screening bloods
audits.st: NICE-recommended eight blood tests for memory assessment; agreed standard 95%
audits.f: 15/31 (48%) had all 8 tests; 13 (42%) some; 3 (10%) none; mean 76.6% of tests done.
audits.c: Business-card aide-memoires and a letter with audit findings sent to all local GPs.
audits.r2: 10/20 (50%) had all 8 tests; 8 (40%) some; 2 (10%) none; mean 76% of tests done.

audits.t: An audit of ECG monitoring in patients admitted to the general adult wards at clock view hospital
audits.st: Mersey Care physical health policy: ECG within 24 hours of admission (also NICE and RCP recommendations)
audits.f: 31/60 had an ECG within 24 hours of admission; reason for no ECG documented in 16 of 29; only 3 of 13 abnormal ECGs referred for further investigation.

audits.t: An audit of high-dose and combination antipsychotic prescribing across the general adult inpatient wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.st: Trust recommendations for high-dose antipsychotic therapy (HDAT) monitoring and clozapine consideration
audits.f: 21/121 on combination therapy, 11 on HDAT (9%); clozapine considered in 9 of 11 HDAT patients; ECG before HDAT 100% but after dose increase only 36%; baseline prolactin 46%, HbA1c 91%.

audits.t: An audit to assess the measurement of Body Mass Index (BMI) and referral to the dietetics service following admission to the general adult inpatient wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.tp: BMI measurement and dietetics referral on psychiatric wards
audits.st: Referral to dietetics service for BMI >30 kg/m2 (or >28 kg/m2 with weight-related comorbidities)
audits.f: BMI not measured in 14/148; of 134 with BMI measured, 74 were overweight/obese categories; 34 met referral criteria, of whom 4 were not referred, 5 declined referral, 17 referred for other reasons

audits.t: An audit to assess physical health monitoring of patients following their admission to the general adult psychiatric inpatient wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.tp: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
audits.st: Trust policy: physical health monitoring within 24 hours of admission
audits.f: Within 24 hours: BMI 91%, blood pressure 62%, serum cholesterol 59%, HbA1c 58%; QRISK calculated in 78%.

audits.t: Off-label prescribing of quetiapine in HMP Elmley, a Category B remand prison: a re-audit
audits.st: RCPsych 'Use of licensed medicines for unlicensed applications in psychiatric practice' (2nd edition)
audits.f: 82 residents on off-label quetiapine; 28.1% (23/82) initiated by the inreach psychiatrists.
audits.r2: 60 residents on off-label quetiapine; 8.3% (5/60) initiated by inreach psychiatrists; licensed medication considered first, risks documented, and consent documented in 80.0%; low-dose start 100%.

audits.t: An audit during COVID-19: monitoring of CMHT-patient contact and physical health assessments in a rural Welsh setting
audits.st: 10 standards derived from NICE guidelines (NICE QS80, Quality Standard 6)
audits.f: Average compliance across the three previous cycles used as comparator (figures not reported).
audits.r2: Compliance increased in 2/10 standards and decreased in 8/10 compared with the average of the previous three cycles.

audits.t: Improving venous thromboembolism risk assessments on an older age psychiatric ward – a complete audit cycle
audits.st: VTE risk assessment on admission (Department of Health tool)
audits.f: 3/23 (13%) had VTE and bleeding risk assessed on admission.
audits.c: Paper VTE risk assessment proforma attached to drug charts, education of ward doctors, and VTE review in weekly MDT meetings.

audits.t: Clinical audit of the inclusion of the Lester Tool details in discharge documents at Foss Park Hospital, York
audits.tp: Physical health information in psychiatric discharge summaries
audits.st: Lester Tool: 100% of required data included in discharge documents
audits.f: None of 40 discharges fully compliant; on average 23% of Lester Tool information included; no cholesterol ratio recorded, BMI 50%, smoking status 27%.

audits.t: Clinical audit of cardio-metabolic monitoring in people with intellectual disability (PWID) taking antipsychotic medication
audits.st: NICE CG11 and physical health CQUIN targets (Lester adaptation tool): cardiometabolic monitoring for people with intellectual disability on antipsychotics
audits.f: Baseline cardiometabolic assessment in 50–65%; less than 15% at 3–6 months. Weight and blood pressure recorded in 15% and 2.5% at 3–6 months. GP collaboration for annual health check 78–100%.

audits.t: An audit of risk assessments and management for self-harm and suicide in patients with depressive symptoms at a primary care practice in the UK
audits.tp: Suicide and self-harm risk assessment in depression
audits.st: NICE guideline for adults with depression: 100% asked direct questions about suicidal ideation and intent; 100% at significant risk referred to specialist mental health services same day
audits.f: 42/62 patients asked direct questions about self-harm and suicide; 2 patients at immediate risk were urgently referred.

audits.t: An audit to assess whether patients under the care of a community mental health team who are taking clozapine are having their lipid profile checked annually and are given lifestyle advice and have had a QRISK3 assessment
audits.st: NICE: lipids at baseline, 3 months after starting a new antipsychotic, then annually; lifestyle advice and QRISK3 assessment
audits.f: 36/39 (92%) had lipids checked in 12 months; 21/39 (54%) cholesterol over 5.0; 9/39 (23%) documented lifestyle discussion; 0/39 (0%) QRISK3 assessment.

audits.t: Audit on clozapine dose and plasma level correlation for patients with chronic treatment-resistant psychosis
audits.st: MHRA guidance: clozapine levels monitored in situations with suspected toxicity
audits.f: 273 levels taken; average interval 10 months 2 weeks (range 2 days to 13 years); 88 levels over 600 ug/L; 32% of levels above the recommended level.

audits.t: You have to acknowledge the problem before you can address the problem: Audit looking at identification of co-existing substance misuse in a Liaison Psychiatry patient population
audits.tp: Substance misuse screening in mental health patients
audits.st: NICE: all patients asked about substance use
audits.f: 69% asked about substance use; none aged over 80, 55% of females and 33.3% of ward referrals asked.
audits.c: Training session highlighting results and NICE recommendations.
audits.r2: 93% asked about substance use; 60% of over-80s, 96% of females and 85% of ward referrals.

audits.t: Audit of inpatient smoking cessation advice
audits.tp: Smoking cessation in mental health inpatients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Smoking status asked in 68%; 32% not asked; cessation advice or NRT given in 14% of potential smokers (4 smokers advised, 13 not advised).

audits.t: An audit to review the extent to which appropriate preconception advice is given to women being discharged from mental health wards on psychotropic medication, in line with NICE guidelines
audits.tp: Preconception and contraception advice on psychotropics
audits.st: NICE guideline 192 (Antenatal and Postnatal Mental Health), sections 1.2 and 1.4
audits.f: 4 women received contraception advice; fertility impact of antipsychotics discussed with none; preconception counselling advised to none; pregnancy impact of medication discussed with one.
audits.c: Planned: teaching, ward posters, information leaflet and doctors' office reminder posters.

audits.t: Audit of patients absent without leave from a psychiatric intensive care unit
audits.tp: Absent without leave and missing person management
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists Quality Network for PICUs standards (eight criteria on leave plans, AWOL actions and carer involvement)
audits.f: Six of eight criteria met in all cases; carers involved in 5 of 6; no patient had documented crisis numbers provided before leave.

audits.t: Audit of section 2 and section 3 mental health act paperwork in Derby inpatient psychiatric units using an audit tool by Mason et al. (2012)
audits.st: Mental Health Act 1983 criteria, using the Mason et al. (2012) audit tool
audits.f: Mental disorder and nature or degree well documented; why informal admission was inappropriate reasonable; poor compliance for justification of risk to health, safety or others, lowest for health (figures not reported).

audits.t: An audit of liaison service provision in Aneurin Bevan University Health Board
audits.st: RCPsych Psychiatric Liaison Accreditation Network (PLAN) quality standards (essential standards target 100%, expected 80%, desirable 60%)
audits.f: 30% of essential standards not met and 21% only somewhat met, particularly in policies/procedures and urgent/emergency mental healthcare; 36% of expected standards met and 41% not met, with poor performance in governance, induction and support/teaching to acute colleagues; 89% of desirable standards not met

audits.t: A clinical audit to investigate polypharmacy and interactions in inpatients in an old age psychiatric ward
audits.st: King's Fund report criteria for problematic polypharmacy; Medscape and BNF interaction tools
audits.f: 69.7% (30 patients) at higher risk of polypharmacy on discharge; 31 of 43 had at least one interaction; 18.6% (8) had at least one potentially severe interaction.

audits.t: A closed loop audit of clerking psychiatric histories in an acute psychiatric inpatient unit
audits.st: New Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry history components
audits.f: Only ID and presenting complaint present in 100%; medical history 72%, forensic history 44%, social history 39%, premorbid personality 44%.
audits.c: Clerking proforma distributed to junior doctors.
audits.r2: ID, PC, HPC, psychiatric history and MSE 100%; forensic history 73% (p = 0.015); social history 78% (p = 0.018); premorbid personality 89% (p = 0.005); medical history 94%.

audits.t: Investigation and management of vitamin D insufficiency and deficiency in acute adult psychiatric admissions: a clinical audit
audits.st: Trust policy: vitamin D checked in all inpatients and supplementation started where appropriate; target 90% for both
audits.f: Vitamin D checked in 79 (56.4%); colecalciferol started in 61 (83.6%) of those insufficient or deficient. Target not met.

audits.t: Clinical audit investigating the recognition of tardive dyskinesia in an acute inpatient setting
audits.st: AIMS assessment every 3–6 months for patients on antipsychotics
audits.f: 3/33 (9.1%) on antipsychotics over three months had an AIMS assessment; 14 (28.0%) given verbal information on EPSEs; 19 (38.0%) had documented side-effect assessment.

audits.t: Audit on the documentation of ethnicity within CAMHS
audits.st: Mental Health Services Data Set: ethnicity documented for 100% of patients
audits.f: 823 (20%) ethnicity recorded as 'unknown'; 49 (1.2%) missing.
audits.c: Recommended: refined search, emailing care coordinators, questionnaire, process review and staff training.

audits.t: Implementation of physical examination pro forma – a complete audit cycle
audits.tp: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
audits.st: Mental Health Commission Judgment Support Framework version 5; target 100% physical examination on admission
audits.f: 3/13 had physical examination on admission (23%); 6 had examination in ED.
audits.c: Colour-coded physical examination proforma developed and implemented, with MDT and NCHD briefing.

audits.t: Audit on monitoring physical health of patients on mood stabilisers following NICE guidelines
audits.st: NICE guidelines on physical health monitoring for mood stabilisers
audits.f: Monitoring was almost consistent with guidelines; gaps included thyroid function not checked 6-monthly on lithium and carbamazepine levels not monitored (one patient had no bloods).
audits.c: Monitoring proforma attached to case notes and an online database with reminders

audits.t: Audit of physical health monitoring in a forensic psychiatric community caseload
audits.st: CNTW Trust physical health monitoring guidelines; target 100%
audits.f: Bloods 80% and ECG 50% compliance.
audits.c: Routine bloods and ECGs to be requested two months before annual due dates.

audits.t: Re-audit of use of seclusion in a tier 4 adolescent psychiatric intensive care unit
audits.st: Trust seclusion guidelines
audits.f: Average seclusion 30h; consultant review within 24h under 70%; care plan modification 63%.
audits.c: Daily nursing safety huddles, weekly incident reduction meetings and an ongoing QI project on restrictive practice.
audits.r2: Average seclusion 20h; consultant review within 24h over 90%; care plan modification over 95%; 46 incidents.

audits.t: Audit of antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring for the management of behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia
audits.st: NICE guideline on antipsychotics for behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia; local CAIR form
audits.f: CAIR form present in 73% (new shorter version 37%); 63% of forms fully completed. 100% had assessment of causes, non-drug measures first, target symptoms and risk-benefit discussion; all reviewed within three months.
audits.c: Teaching session at team meeting, health board leaflet for patients and carers, and reversion to the original CAIR form.

audits.t: An audit of lithium prescribing practices in an old age psychiatry service highlighting renal impairment in this cohort
audits.st: NICE 2014, BNF 2019 and Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines 2018: 3-monthly serum lithium and renal tests
audits.f: 78% (n = 14) on track for 3-monthly lithium level; 83% (n = 15) met 3-monthly renal tests; thyroid function 89% (n = 16); serum calcium 63%; 39% (n = 7) lithium level in therapeutic range 0.6-0.8mmol/L.

audits.t: Improving the patient involvement in research and development on acute psychiatric wards – an audit and quality improvement project
audits.st: Local and national research and development standards
audits.f: 13 of 14 marked as approached; only 3 remembered a research leaflet and none were verbally informed; documentation in 9 cases and nonspecific.

audits.t: Old age liaison psychiatry: audit assessing adherence to referral pathway and referral characteristics including indications, interventions and outcomes
audits.st: Existing referral pathway using a Microsoft Word referral template
audits.f: 114 referrals (82%) adhered to the referral template; 72 (52%) contained adequate information.

audits.t: An audit of waiting times in the outpatient clinic in Inverness Sector A NHS Highland during the COVID-19 pandemic
audits.tp: Outpatient referral to first appointment waiting times
audits.st: 12-week waiting time from referral to first offered outpatient appointment
audits.f: 87.5% (140) given an appointment; mean wait 12 weeks for 64% (103), with 36% (57) waiting longer than 13 weeks; 12.5% (20) referrals deemed inadequate

audits.t: An audit on prescribing practice and risk of serotonin syndrome among patients with chronic pain
audits.tp: Serotonin syndrome risk from drug combinations
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 28 patients (28.8%) had at-risk medication combinations: 11 on two antidepressants, 3 on fentanyl patches plus an antidepressant, 14 on an antidepressant plus tramadol.

audits.t: Co-morbid gambling disorder in a local drug and alcohol service: an audit to determine prevalence
audits.tp: Recording of comorbid gambling disorder in substance misuse services
audits.st: not reported (local recording process; comparison against expected screening practice)
audits.f: 0% of patients had gambling activity noted in initial screening; only 3.5% (99) had ever discussed gambling with a worker in any of the services

audits.t: Audit of baseline cardiometabolic monitoring for patients prescribed or advised dose increase of antipsychotic medication by the knowsley assessment team
audits.st: Baseline cardiometabolic monitoring before antipsychotic prescription or dose increase
audits.f: 50% (20) attended physical health review; 35% (14) not offered one; BP documented in 1 and BMI in 2; HbA1c within 12 months 67.5% (27), lipids 62.5% (25).

audits.t: Audit on High Dose Antipsychotic Treatment (HDAT) Monitoring at Rampton Hospital
audits.st: HDAT monitoring guidelines (MHRA/Committee on Safety of Medicines): bloods, ECG and observations after each dose escalation and 6-monthly; consent documentation
audits.f: Blood and ECG monitoring 8% to 23%; yearly TFT 88% and prolactin 72%; quarterly observations 77%.
audits.r2: 6% of patients on HDAT (18); quarterly bloods about 50-60%, quarterly ECG about 40%; yearly TFT 100%, prolactin 71%; quarterly observations 100% (regular HDAT), 81% (including PRN); consent forms 100%.

audits.t: A quality improvement (QI) project to ensure females on valproate in a CMHT outpatient clinic, eput are registered on the valproate pregnancy prevention programme
audits.st: MHRA guidance: valproate not used in women of childbearing potential unless a Pregnancy Prevention Programme is in place; target 50% reduction in prescriptions
audits.f: 4 of 25 female patients on valproate registered on the Pregnancy Prevention Programme; non-compliance 86%.

audits.t: Audit on nursing notes in a psychiatry in-patient setting
audits.st: MDT-agreed standard for daily nursing notes (clear language; mental state, medication, meals, physical health, personal care, activities, risks, leave)
audits.f: Average accessibility score 1 and language score 2 (Likert +3 to -3); personal care information present in 17%.
audits.c: Standards and a suggested note format emailed to staff, with follow-up meetings with individual staff and the MDT.
audits.r2: Accessibility score 3 and language score 2; meals, medication and physical health information present 100%; personal care 89%.

audits.t: A quality improvement project to improve the number of section 136 GP discharge summaries from the place of safety
audits.st: Aim to increase GP discharge summaries by 50% over 12 months
audits.f: 2 of 89 patients (stated as 0.02%) had a completed GP summary emailed to the practice.
audits.c: New protocol: nursing staff copy the discharging doctor's entry into the S136 discharge template and email it to the GP; all doctors emailed the protocol and told what to include.
audits.r2: 33 of 60 patients (55%) had a completed GP summary emailed to the practice.

audits.t: Hyperprolactinaemia: audit of practice and new guidance
audits.st: Locally agreed audit standards (95%) on frequency of prolactin monitoring, time to review and referral
audits.f: Only 7/30 (23.33%) tested within the last year; no audit standards met. 2 (6.667%) had new hyperprolactinaemia, both reviewed and treated within one month.
audits.c: New risk-stratified hyperprolactinaemia guidance developed (awaiting ratification).

audits.t: An audit: fitness to drive assessment in inpatients of general adult and old age psychiatry
audits.st: Assessment and documentation of fitness to drive at admission and discharge, patient education and awareness of duty to inform the DVLA
audits.f: 18/49 patients had physical health screening prior to medication initiation (only result reported).

audits.t: Improving quality and assessment of referrals to the Enfield Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team (ECRHTT)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 46.9% of inappropriate referrals were accepted; 38% of all referrals were inappropriate; 71% of GP referrals and 55.5% of CMHT referrals were inappropriate.
audits.c: Consultant psychiatrist based in the assessment team, then teaching for GPs and the crisis telephone service and weekly meetings with liaison and community teams.
audits.r2: Inappropriate referrals fell to 27.4% overall (difference 10.6%, 95% CI 1.3-19.8%, p < 0.05); GP inappropriate referrals 36%; CMHT 12%.

audits.t: A community service review of the quality of inpatient discharge summaries from six inpatient wards at St Charles Hospital: an initial audit and quality improvement recommendations
audits.st: Ten items considered useful to community teams (locally agreed with community psychiatric colleagues)
audits.f: Only 3.3% (1/30) complete for all items; 23.3% (7/30) missing a single item; 7/30 provided no information; reason for admission recorded in 2/30.

audits.t: Improving attendance in addictions - do quality improvement plans work?
audits.st: Attendance at an addictions prescriber review in the last 3 months
audits.c: New appointment letter, text confirmation and reminder, keyworker verbal reminder, prescriber calls to persistent non-attenders, and medication safety review for non-attenders (enhanced QIP).
audits.r2: 86% (78/91) attended; all 13 non-attenders had a medication review.

audits.t: A quality improvement project on the discharge summary completion process in an addictions service
audits.st: Target to increase discharge summary completion from 57.7% to 80% by June 2019
audits.f: Discharge summary completion rate 57.7%.
audits.c: PDSA cycles with process mapping, root cause analysis, education, communication and a checklist.
audits.r2: Completion rose to 100% before tapering to 85% by the end of the project.

audits.t: A quality improvement project on nicotine replacement therapy in Shannon Clinic (Northern Ireland)
audits.tp: Smoking cessation in mental health inpatients
audits.st: Correct prescribing of nicotine replacement therapy
audits.f: 22% of drug charts had NRT prescribed incorrectly.
audits.c: Poster on correct NRT prescribing placed on each ward.
audits.r2: 0% of drug charts had NRT prescribed incorrectly.

audits.t: Bridging the gap: improving liaison psychiatry documentation quality to meet the National Confidential Enquiry into Patient Outcome and Death (NCEPOD) treat as one recommendations at newcastle hospitals
audits.st: NCEPOD 'Treat as One' seven documentation elements
audits.f: 58% of documentation had ≥50% of NCEPOD elements; formulation 0%, legal status and capacity 47%, risk assessment 2%, risk management 18%, discharge plan 2%; acute trust documentation completed 74%.
audits.c: Streamlined e-template in the acute hospital eRecord, structured clinician training and 'Treat as One Guardians' in the team.
audits.r2: 98% had ≥50% of NCEPOD elements; formulation 8%, legal status and capacity 79%, risk assessment 28%, risk management 53%, discharge plan 29%; acute trust documentation 96%.

audits.t: An audit into the monitoring of off-label antipsychotics in primary care
audits.st: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (12th edition) monitoring recommendations
audits.f: 0% completely monitored as per standard; basic bloods 54% (n = 13); glucose 38% (n = 9); prolactin 13% (n = 3); creatine kinase 0%.

audits.t: Audit of documentation of observations on mental health services for older people (MHSOP) wards following implementation of nervecentre
audits.st: Local and national guidance on documentation of NEWS and psychiatric observations
audits.f: Paper documentation: NEWS correctly documented 87%; raised NEWS escalated and reviewed 0%.

audits.r2: NEWS correctly documented 100%; raised NEWS escalated and reviewed 80%.

audits.t: QI project: Improvement in quality of Seclusion Medical Review
audits.st: Mental Health Act Code of Practice, NICE and Trust seclusion policy
audits.f: Above 90% for time of review, record keeping, management plan, risk, mental state and physical health; prescribed medications 60%, medication side effects 40%, physical observations 40%.
audits.c: Seclusion medical review template incorporated into the existing documentation template, with teaching for doctors.
audits.r2: Quality of seclusion medical review between 95% and 100%; no major concerns.

audits.t: Quality of seclusion medical review according to trust guidelines
audits.st: Trust seclusion policy based on Mental Health Act Code of Practice (review within first hour then every 4 hours until MDT, then twice daily)
audits.f: Above 80% for time of review, record keeping, plan for continuing seclusion, risk and mental state; less than 60% for prescribed medications, medication side effects and physical observations.
audits.c: Seclusion medical review template developed, with teaching and example documentation for doctors.

audits.t: Audit for prescription and administration of PRN buccal midazolam for people with learning disabilities and epilepsy in the Hertfordshire & Essex
audits.st: ESNA and ILAE guidelines for PRN buccal midazolam
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: PLAN standards and writing to patients: quality improvement by audit
audits.st: Psychiatric Liaison Accreditation Network (PLAN) standards
audits.f: Collateral history 23%; past medical history 30%; patient/carer perspective 46%; written correspondence offered 0%.
audits.c: Results presented to the team, emailed instructions to create a PLAN-based assessment template, and lobbying for Cerner access in the team office.
audits.r2: Collateral history 67%; past medical history 70%; patient/carer perspective 74%; written correspondence offered 20%.

audits.t: A quality improvement project: documentation of liaison psychiatry patient reviews in the John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford
audits.st: NCEPOD Treat as One (2017) recommendations on content of liaison psychiatry documentation
audits.f: Primary diagnosis 77.9%, reason for referral 66.3%, mental capacity 19.8%, need for DOLS 2.3%, risks 27.9%, risk management 7%; clear plan 61.6%, medication changes 51.4%, useful plan 73%, answered referral question 69.8%, action points assigned 47.7%, non-medical MDT advice 18.6%.
audits.c: Electronic documentation template developed from the report recommendations and implemented for all initial reviews.

audits.t: Improving patient access to medication information: a quality improvement project on patient-centred prescribing
audits.st: Local target: 100% of patients meet 'Patient-Centred Prescribing' criteria (ward round discussion, written leaflets, discussion groups) by March 2021
audits.f: 30% of clients answered passively to 'Do you feel involved in your care?'
audits.c: Weekly MDT-led medication discussion groups (week 1), rolling rota and posters (week 6), 1:1 offer of patient information leaflets (week 14)
audits.r2: Median 92.86% of patients fulfilled Patient-Centred Prescribing criteria

audits.t: Audit of follow-up within 7 days on discharge from the mental health unit, Forth Valley Royal Hospital
audits.st: NICE 2016 guidance and local discharge policy (April 2019): follow-up within 7 days of discharge for all patients
audits.f: 26/41 (64%) followed up within 7 days
audits.c: New discharge policy (April 2019) with a 'Discharge Pause' sticker (later electronic form) completed at decision to discharge, reminders to Community Mental Health Teams, and a flowchart (May 2019) on who provides follow-up

audits.t: Physical health audit of gwent specialist substance misuse services (North Team)

audits.st: Completion of physical examination, 12-lead ECG and blood-borne virus screening
audits.f: Physical examination 60/121 (50%); ECG 37/121 (31%); BBV test in last 6 months 62/121.

audits.t: Audit of the use of the physical health improvement (PHIT) to document physical health examination on an electronic health record at a mental health trust in Manchester
audits.tp: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
audits.st: Local expectation that initial physical examination, admission bloods and ECG are completed and recorded on the PHIT electronic tool
audits.f: IPE 73%, admission bloods 84%, ECG 74%; recorded on PHIT in 33-42%; valid refusal reason documented in 63-91%
audits.c: Interventions to increase completion and documentation, with regular monitoring of PHIT completion (details not reported)

audits.t: Targeting Overtreatment of Asymptomatic Bacteriuria in the Emergency Department: Results from a Quasi-Experimental Intervention Programme based on Education and Audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Pre-intervention 30-day UTI return with same isolate 6.2%; overall UTI return 8.5%; 30-day mortality 6.2%.
audits.c: Targeted education for ED staff and daily audit-feedback on antibiotic prescriptions for suspected ASB.
audits.r2: Discontinuation recommended in 96 (75.6%); acceptance 29.2%. Cephalosporins reduced by 21%, carbapenems by 24%; urine culture requests fell by 16.1%. Same-isolate UTI return 1.6% (p=0.103); overall UTI return 4.7%; mortality 3.9%.

audits.t: Translating Guidelines into Practice: A Multicentre Audit of the Implementation of ERC Survivorship and Follow-Up Recommendations After Cardiac Arrest.
audits.st: European Resuscitation Council guidelines: functional assessment before discharge and systematic review within three months covering cognition, mood, fatigue and family support (five operational criteria)
audits.f: Pre-discharge assessment offered to 116/143 (81%), completed in 81 (57%). Of 132 eligible for follow-up, 108 (82%) contacted and 87 (66%) attended; only 25% seen within 3 months (median 185 days, IQR 81-225). Cognition assessed in 44%, mood 52%, fatigue 51%; family attended in 45%.

audits.t: Evaluating Standards-Based Audit for Quality Improvement in Maternal and Newborn Care: Evidence from a multi-country implementation study
audits.st: Facility-selected standards for maternal and newborn care, with local improvement targets
audits.f: Average baseline audit score 38.8%
audits.c: Quality improvement training in standards-based audit (traditional and blended learning), appointment of a QI champion and facility-specific targeted interventions
audits.r2: Average follow-up score 77.4% (mean improvement 38.2%); 54% of facilities met or exceeded their improvement targets

audits.t: Audit of antibiotic prescribing practices for pediatric pneumonia in the outpatient department: focus on amoxicillin and azithromycin.
audits.st: WHO AWaRe and IMNCI guidance on antibiotic choice, dose and duration
audits.f: Antibiotics prescribed 116/132 (87.9%); amoxicillin 26/132 (19.7%), appropriate 1/26 (3.8%); azithromycin 66/132 (50.0%), appropriate 20/66 (30.3%).

audits.t: PDCA Cycle-Driven Whole-Chain Optimization of the Pre-Prescription Audit System: A Multidimensional Approach from Pharmacist Competency Development to Dynamic Rule Database Management
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Proportion of irrational prescriptions identified by window pharmacists 0.11%.
audits.c: PDCA cycle: centralised rule database management, pharmacist competency development, documentation of irrational prescriptions at dispensing windows, and workflow optimisation.
audits.r2: Proportion of irrational prescriptions identified by window pharmacists dropped to 0.008% (χ² = 249.019).

audits.t: Evaluation of Pre-Analytical, Analytical, and Post-Analytical Quality Indicators Before and After Laboratory Audit in a Tertiary Care Hospital
audits.st: Laboratory quality indicators: sample rejection, re-testing, turnaround time compliance, alerts, EQA performance
audits.f: Sample rejection rate 0.14%; re-test rate 0.04%.

audits.t: In-hospital malaria mortality and time to death in Mozambique: a national clinical audit and survival analysis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1,926 in-hospital deaths among 735,580 malaria cases (case fatality 2.61 per 1,000); 57.4% of deaths within 48 hours of admission; 55.3% in children.

audits.t: Inadequate postpartum screening for type 2 diabetes in women with previous gestation diabetes mellitus: A retrospective audit of practice over 17 years.
audits.st: UK guidance: screening for type 2 diabetes around 6 weeks postpartum and annually thereafter
audits.f: 59.8% of women had the recommended postpartum testing.
audits.r2: 35.0% of women had the recommended postpartum testing.

audits.t: Unfolding possible non-medically indicated caesarean sections in five high-volume urban maternity units in Tanzania: A criterion-based clinical audit (a PartoMa sub-study)
audits.st: Evidence-based locally co-created guidelines; pre-defined localised audit criteria for CS indications
audits.f: CS rate 31% (2949/9364). 1061/2674 (40%) did not comply with audit criteria: one previous CS with no trial of labour (50%), reported prolonged labour without slow progress (23%), fetal distress with normal FHR (21%).

audits.t: Scan length as a major driver of CT radiation dose: a diagnostic reference level audit from Kosovo
audits.tp: Diagnostic reference levels for radiation dose
audits.st: German BfS 2022 diagnostic reference levels and Turkish reference values; local DRLs as 75th percentile
audits.f: 1,535 acquisitions analysed. Head CT (n = 590) CTDIvol 4.7% below BfS DRL but scan length 98.5% above orientation value (median 25.8 vs 13 cm); abdomen-pelvis scan length exceeded reference by 28%; coronary CTA CTDIvol +377%.
audits.c: Recommended: technologist landmarking training, protocol review and enabling iterative reconstruction.

audits.t: A Retrospective Audit of Compliance with International Standards in Colorectal Cancer Pathology Reporting in a National Referral Hospital in Tanzania
audits.st: International Collaboration on Cancer Reporting (ICCR) colorectal cancer reporting checklist
audits.f: Clinical impression 83.6%, type of colectomy 91.3%, neoadjuvant history 57.4%, intraoperative tumour extent 50.8%. Lymph node harvesting adequate in 44.8%, radial margin sampling 45.9%. Reports: histologic subtype and extension 92.3%, lymph node status 67.2%, pathological staging 71%, radial margin status 45.9%.
audits.c: Recommended adoption of ICCR synoptic reporting and stronger multidisciplinary communication.

audits.t: Two-Year Evolution of a Prospective Audit and Feedback Antimicrobial Stewardship Program in a Quaternary Intensive Care Unit in Ghana
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Biomarker-guided prescribing 86.3%; culture and sensitivity testing 74.5%; targeted therapy 23.5%; antibiotic use 96.1%; meropenem 42.9%; clinician acceptance of AMS recommendations 40.6%.
audits.c: Ongoing prospective audit and feedback antimicrobial stewardship programme.
audits.r2: Biomarker-guided prescribing 100% (p=0.005); culture and sensitivity 90.5% (p=0.02); targeted therapy 41.7% (p=0.03); antibiotic use 95.2%; meropenem 56.7% (p=0.13); acceptance 67.5% (p=0.01).

audits.t: Prescribing Trends of Antimicrobials in Obstetric and Gynaecological Inpatients: A Prospective Drug Utilization Study with Concurrent Antimicrobial Stewardship Audit from a Tertiary Care Hospital in Karachi, Pakistan
audits.st: Antimicrobial stewardship programme compliance; WHO AWaRe 2023
audits.f: AMS compliance 0%; 65.1% of prescriptions had no documented indication; Access 53.6%, Watch 46.1%.

audits.t: Implementation of an Anaesthesia Quality Improvement Programme to Reduce Fibreoptic Bronchoscope Repair Incidents.
audits.st: Practice guidelines and policy on fibreoptic bronchoscope use
audits.f: Annual repair rate 1%, repair cost 18,757 USD, FOB unavailability at induction 1.4%.
audits.c: Quality improvement campaign based on the baseline audit, then regular internal audits of compliance with FOB policy.
audits.r2: Repair rate fell by 81% to 0.19% in 2013 (p value truncated).

audits.t: Improving meropenem prescribing through antimicrobial stewardship interventions: a prospective clinical audit in a UK district general hospital
audits.st: Local antimicrobial guidelines; documentation of indication, duration and penicillin allergy status
audits.f: Guideline compliance 50% (50/100); indication documented 86% (86/100); duration 94% (94/100); penicillin-allergy label 69% (69/100).
audits.c: Daily multidisciplinary antimicrobial stewardship ward rounds, prospective audit with real-time feedback and focused prescriber education.
audits.r2: Guideline compliance 74% (74/100); indication and duration documented 100% (100/100); penicillin-allergy label 53% (53/100).

audits.t: Interrupting source-dependent verification cascades after a near-miss wrong-side surgery event: a pre-post quality-improvement study of closed-loop imaging-based laterality verification
audits.tp: Surgical site marking and laterality verification
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist process compliance
audits.f: Checklist process compliance 85.0%; checklist quality pass rate 40.0%; item completion 91.9%; site marking accuracy 73.1%; preparation-area verification 89.6%; theatre entry verification 91.2%.
audits.c: Standardised site marking with mandatory original-imaging review, revised challenge-response laterality checklist items, three-stage closed-loop digital verification workflow and HIS/EMR/PACS integration with forced constraints.
audits.r2: Checklist process compliance 100.0%; quality pass rate 90.0%; item completion 99.0%; site marking accuracy 97.7%; preparation-area verification 95.0%; theatre entry verification 98.0%.

audits.t: An audit assessing data quality, viral suppression, and transition to dolutegravir among children and adolescents with HIV in care at eThekwini Municipality, South Africa
audits.tp: Paediatric HIV treatment and viral load monitoring
audits.st: 2023 South African ART guidelines: dolutegravir-based ART for children and adolescents; viral load in last 12 months
audits.f: 3379 (100%) on dolutegravir-based ART; 193 (6%) had no recent viral load; 303 (10%) had last viral load ≥1000 copies/mL.

audits.t: The Infection Prevention and Biosafety Assessment Initiative: Impact of a Structured Multimodal Training Intervention on Infection Prevention and Biosafety Compliance in a Resource-Limited Setting
audits.st: IPBAI tool of ten domains aligned with WHO IPC core components
audits.f: General indicator score 72.5%; standard and transmission-based precautions 20%; environmental cleaning 0%; spill response 20%; antimicrobial stewardship 20%.
audits.c: Structured multimodal IPC training module delivered in two cycles to 607 healthcare workers.
audits.r2: General indicator score 94%; all ten domains 100%.

audits.t: Improving rational medicine prescribing at a public district hospital in southwestern Uganda, January–November 2021: a quality improvement initiative
audits.tp: Prescription quality and WHO prescribing indicators
audits.st: Uganda Clinical Guidelines (UCG) prescribing concordance and rational medicine use indicators
audits.f: Guideline-concordant prescribing 43.7%; antibiotic prescribing 83.4%; mean 3.35 medicines per encounter; generic-only prescriptions 78.6%.
audits.c: Prescriber education, soft-copy UCG and essential medicines lists, prescribing restricted to recognised clinicians with signature verification, and periodic prescription audit and feedback.
audits.r2: Guideline-concordant prescribing 76.2% (aPR=1.82); antibiotic prescribing 65.3%; 2.66 medicines per encounter; generic-only 94.1%.

audits.t: Improving the quality of dementia care through establishing a quality improvement collaborative of Agents of Change: an interrupted time series study
audits.tp: Management of behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia
audits.st: Three dementia guideline recommendations on non-pharmacological care, measured by checklists
audits.f: Baseline adherence measured by monthly checklists; figures not reported.
audits.c: Quality improvement collaborative: start-up meeting, online learning course, expert-reviewed QI plan, audit feedback and peer sharing.
audits.r2: 42.1% immediate increase in adherence (IRR 1.42; 95% CI 1.08-1.87; p=0.012); 1,717 checklists analysed.

audits.t: Clinical audit in the Pediatric primary care office and overweight prevention in toddlers.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overweight/obesity 26.3%.
audits.c: Revised weaning and feeding protocol up to 36 months, mainly reducing excess protein and sugar.

audits.t: Evaluating documentation of social history in paediatric medical notes at a regional paediatric centre - a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Full compliance with comprehensive biopsychosocial history documentation for all medical admissions
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Teaching interventions, educational sessions and a survey of NCHDs

audits.t: Differences in rates of uptake of NICE clinical guidelines between Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) as evidenced by National Diabetes Audit of England and Wales
audits.st: NICE targets: HbA1c =<7.5% (58.5 mmol/mol), blood pressure <140/80mmHg, cholesterol <5mmol/l; at least annual monitoring of HbA1c, blood pressure, cholesterol, albumin:creatinine ratio, smoking status and BMI
audits.f: T2DM patients had higher odds of meeting clinical targets than T1DM in all five years except cholesterol <5mmol/l; largest difference for HbA1c =<7.5% in 2015-16 (OR 3.43, 95% CI 3.39 to 3.47)

audits.t: Evaluation of demographic, clinical characteristics, and the prescribing practice of guideline-directed medical therapy among chronic heart failure outpatients in multidisciplinary clinics in a large tertiary hospital: a retrospective audit of 1186 patients from 12 years
audits.st: Guideline-directed medical therapy for chronic heart failure
audits.f: Similar GDMT prescribing in both clinics for HFrEF; ACEI/ARB prescription in HFpEF 70.5% (pharmacist clinic) vs 56.2%; low β-blocker and MRA prescription in both clinics.

audits.t: Establishment of National DRL for CT in Hybrid Imaging Studies (The Second Phase of the National NM CT (PET) Dose Audit for Kuwait Population -2019)
audits.tp: Diagnostic reference levels for radiation dose
audits.st: National diagnostic reference levels compared with UK, Swiss and French NDRLs
audits.f: First-phase national DRLs; figures not reported in this abstract.
audits.c: Not reported; second phase aimed to support optimisation and dose reduction.
audits.r2: Head-body third quartile DLP 537 mGy·cm and CTDIvol 5 mGy (higher than UK NDRL 400, 4.3); whole-body proposed NDRLs 684, 4.1. Mean ED 6.9 mSv (HB) and 4.6 mSv (WB), lower than the first phase; 9.1% improvement in NDRL.

audits.t: Quality Improvement Implementation and Maintenance of a Paediatric Early Warning System
audits.st: Local observation and monitoring policy
audits.f: Timely PIC admissions 39%; observation accuracy 66%; chart completion 87%; cardiac arrest 0.36 per 1000 admissions; mortality 3.46 per 1000 admissions.
audits.c: PEW system: observation and monitoring policy, standardised charting with embedded PEW score, clinical skills training, process audit and feedback, and outcome surveillance (implemented 2008).
audits.r2: Timely PIC admissions 92%; observation accuracy 82%; chart completion 99%; cardiac arrest 0.16 per 1000 admissions; mortality 2.24 per 1000 admissions.

audits.t: Improving the quality of nursing documentation at a residential care home: a clinical audit.
audits.st: N-Catch II audit instrument: complete documentation (score 3) for admission assessment, nursing diagnoses, aims, interventions and evaluation
audits.f: No records met standards; mean scores from 0.4 (aims for nursing care) to 1.1 (nursing diagnoses).
audits.c: Tailored multifaceted implementation strategy addressing local barriers.
audits.r2: Improvement reported but standards not yet met (figures truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Radiotherapy Dosimetry Audits in Taiwan Hospitals
audits.st: Standards for Medical Exposure Quality Assurance (SMEQA) acceptance criteria
audits.f: Over 78% of photon and 75% of electron beams within 1.0% of reference-point dose; all measurements within SMEQA acceptance criteria.

audits.t: The role of screening, SIRS and qSOFA in Head and Neck Sepsis: An Audit of 104 Patients
audits.tp: Sepsis recognition and treatment on wards
audits.st: Sepsis screening on admission
audits.f: Sepsis screening was poor; figures not reported.
audits.c: Suggested education and visual reminders such as posters or a clerking proforma.

audits.t: Clinic audit on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) management in public primary care setting: Hong Kong experience
audits.st: Evidence-based audit criteria and performance standards for COPD care
audits.f: Smokers referred to cessation service 57.6%, attended 50.9%; influenza vaccine 46.9%; pneumococcal vaccine 40.7%; spirometry 19.1%; AECOPD admission 12.8%.
audits.c: One-year implementation phase with a series of improvement strategies (not detailed).
audits.r2: Significant improvement in all criteria; AECOPD admission rate reduced to 9.6%.

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative: Improving Time-to-Antibiotics for Pediatric Oncology Patients with Fever and Suspected Neutropenia
audits.st: Antibiotics within 60 minutes of arrival
audits.f: 51% met target; mean time to antibiotics 58 minutes.
audits.c: Ceftriaxone for all suspected neutropenic fever; pharmacist-driven verbal antibiotic ordering; nurse-driven order set by triage category allowing line access, bloods and IV antibiotics before provider review.
audits.r2: 96% met target; mean time to antibiotics 28 minutes.

audits.t: The implementation and outcome of a 2-year prospective audit and feedback based antimicrobial stewardship program at a private tertiary care hospital.
audits.st: Justification of restricted antimicrobials against guidelines, reviewed at 48-72 h
audits.f: 12.5% of prescriptions unjustified; de-escalation recommendations accepted in 89%; restricted antimicrobial use 41 DOT/1000 patient days.

audits.t: Impact of the Audit and Intervention of Infectologists in the Use of Antimicrobials in Intensive Care Units
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 91.4% received at least one antimicrobial; 727 LOT/1000pd; glycopeptides 284 DOT/1000pd; polymyxin B 121 DOT/1000pd.
audits.r2: 90.0% received antimicrobials; 680 LOT/1000pd (p=0.028); glycopeptides 234 DOT/1000pd (p=0.014); polymyxin B 88 DOT/1000pd (p=0.029).

audits.t: Deviation from delivery of radiation therapy to childhood cancer patients: A retrospective audit.
audits.st: Accepted norms for time to start, duration and completion of radiotherapy
audits.f: Deviation in time to start 23.6%, duration 6.0%, completion 24.7%; 43.4% had at least one deviation.

audits.t: An Audit of Use and Monitoring of ACE-inhibitors in General Practice
audits.st: Guidelines on monitoring renal function during ACE inhibitor treatment; target 100%
audits.f: Within 3 months of initiation: blood pressure 94.8%, electrolytes 37.1%, renal function 51%, GFR 31%. During January 2010 to June 2011: blood pressure 91.2%, electrolytes 73%, renal function 80.4%, GFR 54.7%.

audits.t: Assessment of Malnutrition in Emergency Laparotomy Patients. A QIP Highlights Simple Measures To Improve Early Recognition and Optimisation of High-Risk Patients.
audits.st: NICE guidelines on nutritional assessment; accurate MUST scoring
audits.f: MUST accurate in 27 (54%); 23 (46%) inaccurate.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary approach and a standard online MUST calculator.

audits.t: Cesarean section rate changes after audit and feedback with the Ten Group Classification System in a French perinatal network: A retrospective pre-post study.
audits.st: Robson Ten Group Classification System audit and feedback of caesarean section rates
audits.f: Overall caesarean section rate 24.5% (audit feedback of overall rates only).
audits.c: Audit and feedback providing caesarean section rates for each Robson group.
audits.r2: Overall caesarean section rate 25.1%; no significant difference in any Robson group after adjustment.

audits.t: Reducing thoracic and lumbar radiographs in an urban emergency department through a clinical champion led quality improvement intervention.
audits.tp: Low back pain management in the emergency department
audits.st: Choosing Wisely and American College of Radiology recommendations for thoracic and lumbar radiographs
audits.f: Appropriately ordered radiographs 5.8%; 86 radiographs ordered per month.
audits.c: Clinician champion-led staff and patient education, EMR modification, audit and peer feedback, and clinical decision support tools.
audits.r2: Appropriately ordered radiographs rose to 53.9%; monthly radiographs fell to 47.

audits.t: The quality of palliative sedation in end-stage disease: audit from a department of oncology and haematology.
audits.st: International palliative sedation guidelines
audits.f: Midazolam was the drug of choice; most patients had Rudkin score 5 after 24 h; 33% died within 24 h of starting sedation.

audits.t: Online prescribing for sexually transmitted infections – what’s on offer? An evaluation of internet pharmacies based in the United Kingdom
audits.st: British Association of Sexual Health and HIV (BASHH) guidelines
audits.f: Gonorrhoea: 3 of 5 (60%) sold BASHH-approved antibiotics; chlamydia first-line options 22 of 25 (88%); herpes simplex 13 of 22 (59%); trichomonas 4 in line with BASHH.
audits.c: Results fed back to each provider.
audits.r2: Improvement in standards (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Impact of the Canadian CT head rule supplemented by the original published minimum inclusion criteria to assist emergency department clinicians' assessment of patients presenting post fall from residential aged care: a retrospective audit.
audits.tp: CT head justification in head injury
audits.st: Canadian CT Head Rule supplemented by minimum inclusion criteria for minor head injury
audits.f: 134 (57.0%) had CT brain.
audits.c: Decision support tool integrating the Canadian CT Head Rule with simplified minimum inclusion criteria.

audits.t: Audit of transvaginal sonography of normal postmenopausal ovaries by sonographers from the United Kingdom Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening (UKCTOCS).
audits.st: Expert confirmation of self-reported visualisation of both postmenopausal ovaries
audits.f: Mean confirmed visualisation of both ovaries 67.2% (range 47.6-86.5%) against self-reported rates >89%.

audits.t: The Role of Assistant Psychologists within Inpatient Units: A Clinical Audit
audits.tp: Assistant psychologist role in inpatient units
audits.st: Current guidelines for employment of assistant psychologists
audits.f: All standards unmet.

audits.t: Developing and Implementing a Quality Assurance Strategy for Electroconvulsive Therapy
audits.st: Electroconvulsive Therapy Accreditation Service (ECTAS) standards
audits.f: ECT prescription completed by consultant in 100%; administering doctor's signature missing in 40%.
audits.r2: ECT prescription completed in 100%; administering doctor's signature missing in 21%.

audits.t: An Assessment of the Management of Dizzy Patients in a Specialist Multi-Disciplinary Clinic; The Impact of Effective Telephone Triage
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 40% of patients referred with dizziness did not require a face-to-face appointment.
audits.c: Telephone triage to a rapid access BPPV clinic or a multidisciplinary complex balance clinic with audiologists, physiotherapists and ENT surgeons.
audits.r2: Only 35.8% streamed to face-to-face appointment; 90% of face-to-face appointments by non-ENT surgeons; 60% discharged after first assessment (61% previously).

audits.t: An audit of antibiotic prescriptions at the Base Hospital of Wathupitiwala in Sri Lanka
audits.st: Appropriate antibiotic choice, documentation of indication, dosing and microbiological cultures
audits.f: 95 (45.23%) patients on antibiotics; 33.68% wrong choices; indication not documented in 11 (11.58%); sub-therapeutic dose in 4 (4.21%); cultures not sent in 71.87%.

audits.t: Insulin prescribing, administration, and glucose monitoring trends in Irish hospitals: scope for improvement?
audits.st: Local insulin prescribing, administration and glucose monitoring standards
audits.f: 90% [37] of insulin-prescribed inpatients had one or more errors; 95% brand names and 89% dose units clearly prescribed; 87% orders signed; 70% administrations double checked; 26% [10] given insulin when not prescribed.

audits.t: A National Audit of Pancreatic Enzyme Prescribing in Pancreatic Cancer from 2015 to 2023 in England Using OpenSAFELY-TPP.
audits.tp: Pancreatic enzyme replacement in pancreatic cancer
audits.st: UK guidelines: pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy for all people with unresectable pancreatic cancer (100% standard)
audits.f: National PERT prescribing rates ranged from 41% in 2015 to 48% in early 2023, rising about 1% per year; highest regional rates 50% to 60% in West Midlands.

audits.t: An Audit of Referrals to the Minor Operating Theater of the Patient Presenting in Otolaryngology OPD with Ear Discharge
audits.st: Hospital OPD guidelines enacted by the Pakistan Otolaryngology Association
audits.f: 52.5% of patients with ear discharge required referral to ENT theatre/emergency for suctioning.
audits.c: Changes in practice and simple protocols to allow ear suction in the outpatient clinic.
audits.r2: Referrals to ENT theatre fell to 9.5%.

audits.t: Developing a Tool for Auditing the Quality of Antibiotic Dispensing in Community Pharmacies: A Pilot Study.
audits.tp: Antibiotic dispensing quality in community pharmacy
audits.st: EU guidelines for antibiotic dispensing (Audit Project Odense methodology)
audits.f: Checks for allergies, contraindications and interactions varied widely between countries; little patient advice given and prescribers rarely contacted.

audits.t: Pre-biologic screening and biologic monitoring in a tertiary dermatology department in Ireland
audits.st: British Association of Dermatologists guidelines for biologic therapy
audits.f: Baseline disease severity scores documented in 68%; full viral screen 87%; vaccination status 80%.
audits.c: Screening and monitoring checklists created and being implemented.

audits.t: Retrospective audit in documentation practice in surgical inpatients records, a two cycles audit.
audits.st: Hospital documentation policy and standard hospital guidelines (37 audit standards)
audits.f: Retrospective analysis of 120 case files against 37 standards; baseline figures not reported in abstract.
audits.c: Results presented at clinical governance; incorporated into the documentation protocol with instructions to all surgical staff on appropriate documentation.
audits.r2: Compliance increased in 35 of 37 standards and no standard fell; average compliance rose by 32% across all criteria.

audits.t: Prevalence of inadequate completion of computed tomography request forms submitted to public and private medical imaging centres in Ashanti Region of Ghana: a retrospective audit
audits.st: Complete documentation of demographic, clinical, referrer and procedure information on CT request forms
audits.f: Overall prevalence of inadequate completion 0.752 (95% CI 0.719-0.787); reason for referral documented on 391 (81.5%), highest in the private centre (96.7%).

audits.t: Outcomes of newly referred patients with suspected angle closure: do we need to redefine the clinical pathways?
audits.st: Gonioscopy as reference standard for occludable angle
audits.f: 431/1754 (24.6%) were PACS referrals; only 42/393 (10.7%) had an occludable angle on gonioscopy
audits.c: Virtual clinic triaging criterion changed using AS-OCT

audits.t: Application of the Robson classification in assessing cesarean section rates: an audit of a tertiary care hospital's gynecology department in Karachi, Pakistan.
audits.st: WHO recommendation that caesarean rates not exceed 10-15%; Robson Ten Group Classification
audits.f: 507 caesarean sections among 1464 deliveries; main contributors group 5 (51.9%), group 2 (18.5%) and group 10 (14.4%).

audits.t: An audit to assess and improve the quality of referrals received by Community Dental Services from General Dental Practitioners for the one-off treatments of patients under 18 years, with inhalation sedation and general anaesthesia, in Salford
audits.st: Referral quality/acceptance for inhalation sedation and general anaesthesia; no numeric target stated
audits.f: 48% acceptance rate; most referrals had 2 errors; almost 2 in 5 inhalation sedation referrals not justified appropriately or lacked a diagnosis.
audits.c: Contacted the triaging hub and local GDPs and created local triaging guidance.

audits.t: A national audit of facilities, human and material resources for the comprehensive management of diabetes in Ghana-A 2023 update.
audits.st: Resources required for comprehensive diabetes care (personnel, medicines, laboratory services, guidelines)
audits.f: 85 (69.7%) had a dedicated diabetes service; 28 (23%) had trained diabetes specialists; 13.9% had monofilaments; about 50% could measure HbA1c

audits.t: Auditing cesarean section indications in women of Groups 1 to 4 of Robson's Ten-Group Classification System: A descriptive study at a university hospital in Thailand
audits.st: Institutional criteria for appropriate caesarean section indications in Robson groups 1-4
audits.f: Overall appropriate rate of caesarean section indications 32.5% (95% CI 26.8%-38.7%).

audits.t: WHO Surgical Checklist in Transplant Surgery: Still another tick box exercise? Results from a Closed Loop Audit at a Medium-Sized Transplant Centre
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (Sign in, Time out, Sign out)
audits.f: Adherence to the WHO Surgical Checklist was less than optimal (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Recommendations from the 2014 audit (details not reported).
audits.r2: Checklist adhered to in 100% of operations (N=54) across all phases; statistically significant improvement in recall of patient ID and primary surgeon's name.

audits.t: Retrospective audit compares screening and treatment of pregnancy-related anaemia in regional New South Wales with Australian guidelines.
audits.st: Australian Red Cross Guidelines for anaemia in pregnancy
audits.f: Of 103 with screening data, only 5.3% completed full recommended screening; Hb measured in T1 56.7%, T2 44.7%, T3 36.6%; IV iron given to 14.0%, about 1.75 times the recommended rate.

audits.t: The correlation between a healthy lifestyle among pregnant women and their compliance with educational guidelines in Iran's health system using best-evidence audit criteria
audits.st: Best-Evidence Audit Criteria Checklist for healthy lifestyle education in pregnancy
audits.f: No compliance with the first six criteria; Criterion VII (opportunity to ask questions) met, highest score 17.32 ± 6.79; Criterion II (written information) lowest at 5.17 ± 5.31.

audits.t: A clinical audit on longer-term stroke management as a specific service in a primary care setting: Assessing adherence of service and clinical parameters.
audits.tp: Long-term stroke care in primary care
audits.st: 11 service criteria adapted from the Canadian Post-Stroke Checklist; clinical targets from Malaysian CPG on Cardiovascular Disease 2017 and CPG on Ischaemic Stroke 2020
audits.f: 9 of 11 service criteria met the standard; not met were asking about fatigue (43.4%) and access to community resources (26.5%). BP and HbA1c target attainment met the standards.

audits.t: Addressing the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic: A quality improvement collaborative to optimize the use of antibacterials in Argentine Intensive Care Units
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Quality improvement collaborative: audit and feedback on antibacterial use, facility-specific treatment guidelines, antibacterial timeouts, pharmacy-based interventions, education, learning sessions and coaching.
audits.r2: Authors report improved antibacterial utilisation and fewer healthcare-associated infections related to multidrug-resistant organisms (figures truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Antimicrobial Use for Urinary Tract Infection in Long-Term Care Facilities in Spain: Baseline Results from a Registration Audit
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for urinary tract infection
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 6% of asymptomatic bacteriuria cases treated; dipstick used in 83%, including 46 asymptomatic cases.

audits.t: Adequate Completion of Radiology Request Forms: A clinical Audit at Managil Teaching Hospital, Sudan
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists standard structured request form
audits.f: Many request forms incomplete; patient's age written in 13% of forms.
audits.c: A ready (pre-designed) request form was introduced.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in most areas; patient's age written in 92% of forms.

audits.t: Discharge summaries: One size does not fit all
audits.st: Essential discharge summary elements agreed with departmental clinicians
audits.f: Poor documentation, especially of medical issues during admission, clinical condition on discharge and safety-netting.
audits.c: Visual aid of key components placed above computer stations in junior doctors' offices and formal departmental teaching sessions.
audits.r2: Documentation in all key components improved dramatically (figures not given).

audits.t: Improving delirium assessments in acute senior health: A quality improvement project for care of the older person.
audits.st: NICE delirium guidelines
audits.f: Full delirium assessment 1.9%; formal diagnosis 5.8%.
audits.c: Posters and education-based multidisciplinary team interventions developed after literature analysis and ward discussion.

audits.t: Emergency paediatric bronchoscopy: A freely available, durable, effective training resource.
audits.st: Naming, function and assembly tasks for the paediatric bronchoscope; no external standard stated
audits.f: Baseline naming, function and assembly time scores recorded (figures not given).
audits.r2: Average improvements of 29% in naming and 15% in function scores; assembly time improved by an average of 49 seconds.

audits.t: An Audit of Perioperative VTE Risk Assessment and Prophylactic Anticoagulation
audits.st: Caprini risk assessment model for VTE risk assessment and prophylaxis
audits.f: 71 (36.6%) of 194 patients at risk of DVT on Caprini; 123 (63.4%) had no risk score evaluation because staff were unaware of VTE risk assessment.

audits.t: Optimizing SGLT2 inhibitor and GLP-1 RA prescribing in high-risk patients with diabetes: a Department of Veterans Affairs quality improvement intervention.
audits.tp: SGLT2 inhibitor and GLP-1 RA prescribing
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Prescribing rate 22.7% in VAAAHS (20.3% VISN 10, 18.7% VA nationally).
audits.c: Education, pharmacist academic detailing, audit and feedback, and patient outreach and inreach.
audits.r2: Prescribing rate 42.4% in VAAAHS (32.2% VISN 10, 30.2% VA nationally); 37.9% at end of the 12-month intervention.

audits.t: Clinical control in COPD and therapeutic implications: The EPOCONSUL audit.
audits.st: Spanish COPD Guidelines (GesEPOC) control criteria
audits.f: Control analysed in 1804 (42.7%); 49.1% uncontrolled; therapeutic inertia in 68.4% of uncontrolled patients.

audits.t: Evaluation of criterion-based audit in improving quality of neonatal birth asphyxia care at Balaka district hospital in Malawi.
audits.st: Locally established criteria based on Malawi guidelines on care of the infant and newborn and WHO documents
audits.f: Vital signs checked 80%; laboratory investigations 0.9%; thermal support 82.7%; correct diagnosis 60%; correct treatment 18.7%; correct feeding 12.7%; clinical officer ward rounds 0%; daily weight check 49.1%.
audits.c: Gaps discussed by a multidisciplinary team and recommendations implemented (details not reported in abstract).
audits.r2: Vital signs 98.2% (p = 0.000); laboratory investigations 74%; thermal support 91.8% (p = 0.041); correct diagnosis 81% (p = 0.001); correct treatment 81%; correct feeding 56.4%; clinical officer ward rounds 72%; daily weight check 93%.

audits.t: Evaluating acute medical service performance against assessment time metrics: the Society for Acute Medicine Benchmarking Audit 2023 (SAMBA23).
audits.st: Society for Acute Medicine clinical quality indicators, including consultant review within target times
audits.f: Only 29% of daytime arrivals assessed in the Emergency Department received consultant review within target times; 29% of patients needing admission were not admitted to the AMU

audits.t: Prolonged labour as a driver of the ”caesarean section pandemic”: A criterion-based audit of caesarean sections in the five highest volume maternity units in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
audits.st: Audit criteria for prolonged labour as a caesarean section indication
audits.f: 243/456 (53.3%) caesareans for prolonged labour were in uncomplicated labour: no trial of labour 78/243 (32.1%), partograph action line not crossed 145/243 (59.7%), second stage under 1 hour 20/243 (8.2%).

audits.t: Retrospective study on pain management pathway for patients with suspected renal/ ureteric colic in a U.K. accidents and emergency department: A quality improvement project.
audits.st: NICE guideline for pain management in suspected renal/ureteric colic: NSAIDs first line, IV paracetamol second, opioids third, no antispasmodics
audits.f: Full compliance with NICE pain management guidance in 23%; unsatisfactory in 78%.

audits.t: Prescription Audit in Outpatient Pharmacy of a Tertiary Care Referral Hospital in Haryana Using Who/ Inrud Core Prescribing Indicators: A Step Towards Refining Drug Use and Patient Care
audits.tp: Prescription quality and WHO prescribing indicators
audits.st: WHO/INRUD core prescribing indicators
audits.f: Mean 3.03 drugs per prescription; 75% generic names; antibiotic in 20.59%; injectables in 1.15%; 55.4% from the National List of Essential Medicines; IRDP 3.86.

audits.t: Timely identification of deteriorating patients from acute respiratory infections at the primary care level in the COVID-19 era: quality improvement collaborative.
audits.tp: Recognition of deterioration in primary care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: NEWS2-based triage, portable oximeters, telehealth, reminders, audits, feedback and direct observation.

audits.t: Clinical audit on laboratory diagnosis of malaria parasites at Jimma University Medical Center laboratory, Southwest Ethiopia
audits.st: 26 established quality standards for malaria diagnosis (pre-analytic, analytic and post-analytic)
audits.f: 78% of samples from properly rubbed fingers; all anticoagulated samples mixed properly (n=35); 78.8% of slides first viewed with 100x objective and only 17.5% with 10x

audits.t: Clinical audit of the process of referral to genitourinary medicine of patients found to be chlamydia positive in a family planning service.
audits.st: All women having termination of pregnancy or IUD fitting offered chlamydia screening, informed of positive results and referred to GUM
audits.f: 999 offered a test and 988 tested; 38 positive (3.8%); result documented as given in 27/38 (74%); 24 (63%) seen in GUM.

audits.t: Waterbirths: regional audit of infection control practices.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 14 (88%) centres responded, 11 did waterbirths; all 8 with on-site pools had infection control policies; 6 used detergent and disinfectant, 2 detergent alone; no centre tested mothers for blood-borne viruses; 2 did regular microbiological testing of pools

audits.t: Discordance between uterine cervical cytology and biopsy: results and etiologies of a one-year audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Discrepancy of at least two grades in 49/427 (11.5%); of 39 reviewed, 30 (77%) cytologic and 9 (23%) histologic errors

audits.t: Children presenting with convulsions (including status epilepticus) to a paediatric accident and emergency department: an audit of a treatment protocol.
audits.tp: Acute convulsion and status epilepticus management
audits.st: Local convulsion protocol: diazepam 0.4 mg/kg up to two doses, then phenytoin 18 mg/kg with rectal paraldehyde 0.4 mL/kg
audits.f: Convulsion terminated in ED in 76 (94%); 69 (85%) after a single diazepam dose; 5/10 (50%) stopped with phenytoin plus paraldehyde; 9 (11%) needed ICU.

audits.t: Quality assurance of data collection in an aminoglycoside dosing service.
audits.st: Complete documentation of data needed to interpret serum aminoglycoside levels
audits.f: Complete documentation in 75% of pre-dose and 63% of post-dose levels.
audits.c: Education via Pharmacy Bulletin, revision of Laboratory and IV Medication Manuals, communication with head nurses and active pharmacist follow-up of missing information.
audits.r2: Complete documentation 93% for pre-dose and 84% for post-dose levels (p < 0.001).

audits.t: Do we measure up? The development of a multidisciplinary quality assurance and audit system in a psychiatric rehabilitation setting.
audits.st: Criteria for assessing performance in a long-term and rehabilitation setting (developed by the team)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Renal disease audit and drug usage evaluation for all patients.
audits.st: Dose or interval adjustment of renally excreted drugs in patients with GFR less than 50 mL per minute
audits.f: 70 pharmacy-initiated interventions made for patients with calculated GFR less than 50 mL per minute

audits.t: A multicentre audit of hospital referral for radiological investigation in England and Wales. Royal College of Radiologists Working Party.
audits.st: Baseline for guidelines of good radiology referral practice
audits.f: X ray referral rates varied between firms in the same specialty up to eightfold for inpatients and 13-fold for outpatients; chest x ray up to ninefold and 25-fold.

audits.t: Audit of thrombolysis initiated in an accident and emergency department.
audits.st: Early thrombolysis after acute myocardial infarction; door to needle and pain to needle times
audits.f: Group 1 (thrombolysis in CCU): geometric mean door to needle 128 min, pain to needle 242 min.
audits.c: Selected patients given thrombolysis in the A and E department before transfer, after oral confirmation of myocardial infarction by the CCU admitting officer on receipt of a faxed ECG.
audits.r2: Group 2b (thrombolysis in A and E): geometric mean door to needle 38 min and pain to needle 141 min, v 121 min and 237 min in ineligible patients treated in CCU (group 2a, n=30); both p < 0.0001.

audits.t: Improving information given to patients before endoscopy: a regional audit.
audits.st: Regionally agreed 12-item standard for endoscopy information leaflets
audits.f: Leaflets included 35% (range 8-67%) of standard items.
audits.c: Each unit given a comparison of its leaflet with the standard.
audits.r2: All 11 units with new leaflets had made changes; 80% of items included overall.

audits.t: Audit of coding in gastrointestinal endoscopy.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Accurate and complete coding of gastrointestinal endoscopic procedures
audits.f: Staff unaware of the coding system; typed discharge summaries usually inadequate for coding; considerable variation in proportion of procedures coded.
audits.c: Changes made to improve accuracy and completeness of coding (details not reported).
audits.r2: Follow-up study showed the changes were effective (no figures in abstract).

audits.t: Improving management of asthma: closing the loop or progressing along the audit spiral?
audits.st: Checklist of important aspects of acute asthma management
audits.f: Oral corticosteroids 69 (68%); oxygen 62 (61%).

audits.t: Audit of bronchial artery embolisation in a specialist respiratory centre.
audits.st: Appropriateness of bronchial arteriography and embolisation for haemoptysis (retrospective assessment)
audits.f: 58 procedures in 35 patients; embolisation technically successful in 33/40 procedures for major haemoptysis, but haemoptysis recurred within 10 days in 17; overall success rate 40% (16/40).

audits.t: Audit of the use of doctors' holding power under Section 5(2) of the Mental Health Act 1983.
audits.st: Mental Health Act 1983 Section 5(2)
audits.f: 80 of 146 Section 5(2) orders converted to Section 2 or 3; Section 5(2) may have been used inappropriately in up to 45% of cases.

audits.t: Completing the clinical audit cycle: discharge medication.
audits.st: Three indicators: personal visits to pharmacy by ward staff and patients; nurse telephone calls chasing prescriptions; written patient complaints
audits.f: All three measures increased substantially compared with the previous four-month period.
audits.c: Action plan to change behaviour of consultants, junior doctors, ward and nursing staff, patients and pharmacy staff by raising awareness of the consequences of their actions.
audits.r2: Substantial reductions in all three measures.

audits.t: National audit of acute severe asthma in adults admitted to hospital. Standards of Care Committee, British Thoracic Society.
audits.tp: Acute severe asthma management in adults
audits.st: British Thoracic Society national guidelines for hospital management of acute severe asthma
audits.f: Peak flow measured initially in 661/766 (86%); arterial blood gases ever assessed in 534 (70%); 65 (8%) had no steroid in first 24 hours; peak flow variability measured before discharge in 597/759 (78%), of whom 334 (56%) had good control. Only 237 (31%) prescribed oral steroids before admission despite 429 (56%) having treatment increased.

audits.t: Education and audit can improve the identification of excessive drinkers among medical inpatients.
audits.st: Recording of quantitative alcohol history, CAGE questionnaire use and alcohol notification in discharge summaries
audits.f: Quantitative alcohol history in medical notes 175/792 (22%) and nursing notes 31/792 (4%); excessive drinkers identified 40/792 (5.1%).
audits.c: Training of junior medical and nursing staff, then feedback of results at a clinical audit meeting.
audits.r2: After audit feedback: quantitative history in medical notes 241/497 (48%) and nursing notes 237/497 (48%); excessive drinkers identified 45/497 (9.1%); chi 2 for trend p < 0.0001 for notes.

audits.t: Managing meningitis in children: audit of notifications, rifampicin chemoprophylaxis, and audiological referrals.
audits.st: Statutory notification, nationally agreed chemoprophylaxis and hearing assessment for all survivors
audits.f: Notified 20/36 (56%); chemoprophylaxis to 5/23 (22%) index cases; audiology arranged for 19/32 (59%) survivors.
audits.c: Written information for all doctors including each junior intake, and guidelines displayed on wards.

audits.t: Continuity of care on admission to hospital: an audit of Airedale NHS Trust's transfer policy.
audits.tp: Care transfer communication on hospital admission
audits.st: Airedale NHS Trust transfer policy
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Recommendations: pre-admission checklist, changes to nursing documentation, faster information transfer and clearer responsibility for contact across the hospital-community interface.

audits.t: Transfusion practice in a Canadian hospital. Use of a major European study of transfusion practice for comparison as a form of audit.
audits.st: Comparison with a multi-hospital European study of transfusion practice
audits.f: Red cell use lower than most European centres for all four procedures and plasma lower for CABG and AAA; platelet use for CABG and AAA higher than most European centres.

audits.t: Comparison of appropriateness of cholesterol testing in general practice with the recommendations of national guidelines: an audit of patient records in 20 general practices.
audits.st: Dutch College of General Practitioners national guidelines on opportunistic cholesterol testing
audits.f: Cholesterol tested in 415 (11.7%); only 31% of 668 patients with a positive cardiovascular risk profile tested, versus 8% of those without.

audits.t: Does medical audit lead to explicit standards? Experience with thrombolysis in four UK hospitals.
audits.tp: Thrombolysis use in acute myocardial infarction
audits.st: Locally set explicit standards for proportion of patients with definite and probable AMI given intravenous thrombolysis (technical standards in two hospitals, population standards in two)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Peer review meetings of baseline results, with standard setting requested by letter and telephone.
