audits.r2: Six of the eight standards set were achieved in at least one of four audits in each hospital.

audits.t: Why is evaluation of the cost effectiveness of audit so difficult? The example of thrombolysis for suspected acute myocardial infarction.
audits.tp: Thrombolysis use in acute myocardial infarction
audits.st: Proportion of patients with suspected acute myocardial infarction given thrombolysis
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Repeated audits with a series of four audit meetings and subsequent actions.
audits.r2: Thrombolysis rose by 20% to 37% in three auditing hospitals and fell by 6% in the fourth (baseline over 90%); control rose 15%. Only one hospital differed significantly from control (51 extra treatments per year, 95% CI 0.5 to 61).

audits.t: How to improve low lymph node recovery rates from axillary clearance specimens of breast cancer. A short-term audit.
audits.tp: Lymph node yield in axillary clearance
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median 10 lymph nodes recovered per specimen.
audits.c: Audit scheme with specimen weighing and a second pathologist cutting up each specimen, recording node numbers and sizes.
audits.r2: Median 22 lymph nodes recovered per specimen.

audits.t: Inadequate cervical cytology--the need to audit individual smear takers' inadequate rates.
audits.st: Acceptable inadequate smear rates per smear taker
audits.f: Yearly average clinic inadequate rates were acceptable, but individual smear takers ranged from 0% to 19.5%.
audits.c: Smear takers with unacceptably high inadequate rates underwent further training.

audits.t: Chlamydia in a district general hospital: an audit of treatment and contact tracing.
audits.st: Central audit group guidelines on chlamydia management
audits.f: Contact tracing of current and recent partners was more successful than of previous partners; women treated before attending were more likely to need retreatment.

audits.t: An audit of the quality of operation notes in an otolaryngology unit.
audits.st: Operation notes should record accurate data, ward, department and name of surgeon, and avoid unacceptable abbreviations
audits.f: Clear identification of operating surgeon 74%; avoidance of unacceptable abbreviations 53%.
audits.c: Aide-memoire attached to the front of the operation sheet.
audits.r2: Clear identification of operating surgeon 93%; avoidance of unacceptable abbreviations 84%; all criteria improved.

audits.t: A multihospital medication allergy audit: a means to quality assurance.
audits.st: Allergy information for penicillin- or aspirin-sensitive patients appropriately communicated to the pharmacist
audits.f: Overall acceptance rate 62.3%.
audits.c: Corrective follow-up measures at each hospital (details not reported).

audits.t: A multidisciplinary audit of diabetic care using criteria mapping.
audits.st: Criteria Map of 23 criteria (18 medical, three dietetic, one nursing); score above 75% indicates adequate care
audits.f: Medical compliance 78.46%, dietetic 79.17%, nursing 85.71%; mean dossier score 80.62%

audits.t: Audit of digoxin prescribing in ambulatory patients.
audits.st: A priori criteria for digoxin discontinuance and monitoring in uncomplicated heart failure in sinus rhythm
audits.f: 23 (68%) met criteria for discontinuance but only three stopped, none with proper follow-up; CHF status and toxicity assessed at fewer than half of visits.

audits.t: Quality of care of patients with diabetes: collation of data from multi-practice audits of diabetes in primary care.
audits.st: Annual key process measures for diabetes care
audits.f: Annual mean compliance: HbA1c or fructosamine 72.5%, fundi 67.5%, urine 65.8%, blood pressure 87.6%, smoking 71.4%, feet 67.7%, BMI 52.5%, with wide ranges between groups.

audits.t: Implementing evidence based medicine in general practice: audit and qualitative study of antithrombotic treatment for atrial fibrillation.
audits.st: Evidence-based antithrombotic (warfarin) treatment for patients with atrial fibrillation at risk of thromboembolism
audits.f: 132 of 13 239 patients had a history of atrial fibrillation, 100 of them at risk of thromboembolism.
audits.c: Assessment and educational interview with eligible patients about antithrombotic treatment.
audits.r2: After the study 52 patients were taking warfarin; of the other 48 (41 on aspirin), eight too ill, 16 unable to consent, four refused interview and 20 declined warfarin.

audits.t: Can audit improve antibiotic prescribing in general dental practice?
audits.st: Antibiotic prescribing guidelines issued as part of the audit
audits.f: 2316 antibiotic prescriptions issued; 81% for therapeutic reasons; amoxycillin most commonly prescribed (57.6% overall).
audits.c: Audit with an educational component and issuing of guidelines.
audits.r2: Prescriptions reduced by 42.5% to 1330; antibiotic regimens significantly changed.

audits.t: Clinical audit of emergency out-of-hours service in general practice in Sefton.
audits.st: Criteria agreed at the inception of the new General Dental Services contract in 1990
audits.f: Management of all cases was within the standards set, with one exception.

audits.t: Cooperation between general practitioners and diabetologists and clinical audit improve the management of type 2 diabetic patients.
audits.st: Consensus guidelines based on French St Vincent recommendations
audits.f: Standards not met for several criteria; lack of HbA1c standardisation and delayed intervention for inadequate glucose control.
audits.c: Cooperative protocols for foot care, nephropathy and retinopathy prevention, HbA1c standardisation and a primary care educational programme.
audits.r2: Improvement in foot care (+33.6%), quality (+39.9%), HbA1c prescription (+11.9%), blood pressure control (+11.9%), lipids (+12.8%); early interventions for poor glucose control +10.5%.

audits.t: Diabetes complication screening in general practice: a two pass audit with benchmarking.
audits.st: Agreed key complication screening tasks and maximum screening intervals
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Benchmarking feedback with optional group feedback sessions for general practitioners between passes.
audits.r2: Screening rates improved or remained unchanged; small improvement in total cholesterol and glycated haemoglobin.

audits.t: An audit of measuring equipment in elderly care.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An audit of the investigation and treatment of localised prostatic cancer in the south west region.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean referral to clinic interval 67 days (54 days if GP PSA > 10 ng/ml, 104 days if < 10 ng/ml); 34% had radical treatment (10% prostatectomy, 24% radiotherapy); 27% hormone treatment; all had histological diagnosis and 84% were staged before treatment.

audits.t: Audit of the effect of introducing local guidelines for referral for carotid duplex scanning.
audits.st: Local referral guidelines: scans indicated only for hemispheric localising symptoms or asymptomatic bruits
audits.f: 27.6% of requests inappropriate
audits.c: Introduction of local referral guidelines for carotid duplex scanning
audits.r2: 12.8% of requests inappropriate; 19% reduction in referral rate for new scans

audits.t: Better by half: hypertension in the elderly and the 'rule of halves': a primary care audit of the clinical computer record as a springboard to improving care.
audits.st: 'Rule of halves' for hypertension; locally agreed guidelines and targets
audits.f: Using strict definitions the rule of halves still applied; using looser definitions three-quarters of hypertensives known, two-thirds treated and just under two-thirds controlled.
audits.c: Feedback of results to practices, agreed management guidelines, standardised computer recording, targets and review dates.

audits.t: External audit on the clinical practice and medical decision-making at the departments of radiotherapy in Budapest and Vienna.
audits.st: Institutional protocols and EORTC quality assurance deviation scoring (Horiot et al.) for six qualifying parameters
audits.f: Adequate values for the six parameters in Department B: 85.3%, 94%, 83.4%, 28.3%, 41.9% and 81.1%; in Department A: 67%, 83.4%, 87.8%, 26.1%, 33.2% and 17.7%.

audits.t: An audit of primary surgical treatment for women with ovarian cancer referred to a cancer centre.
audits.st: National and international guidelines for initial surgery and staging of ovarian cancer
audits.f: 92% presented via outpatient clinic (elective surgery); up to seven consultants per hospital operated; less than half underwent the recommended surgical procedure

audits.t: An audit of breast cancer pathology reporting in Australia in 1995.
audits.st: Recommended items in breast cancer pathology reports (before Australian Cancer Network recommendations)
audits.f: Only 28% of invasive cancer reports had all recommended information; histological type 99.6%, tumour size 94%, margins 87%, grade 84%, DCIS 79%, vessel invasion 61%.

audits.t: An audit of waiting times in a haematology clinic before and after the introduction of point-of-care testing.
audits.st: Patient-set maximum clinic waiting time of 30 min (longer-term target 20 min)
audits.f: Patient survey of 50 consecutive patients set the standard; air-tube sample transport with electronic results did not achieve it despite repeated audits.
audits.c: Point-of-care testing in the clinic, with the backup analyser moved weekly and tests done by trained nurse specialists.
audits.r2: Clinic waiting times consistently achieved the standard.

audits.t: Audit and quality control in angioplasty in Europe: procedural results of the AQUA Study 1997: assessment of 250 randomly selected coronary interventions performed in 25 centres of five European countries. AQUA Study Group, Nucleus Clinical Issues, Working Group Coronary Circulation, of the European Society of Cardiology.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 98% had justifiable indications; procedural success 92%; major complications 4.8%.
audits.co: Germany, France, UK, Belgium and Italy

audits.t: Are doctors still failing to assess and treat asthma attacks? An audit of the management of acute attacks in a health district.
audits.st: British Thoracic Society asthma guidelines
audits.f: Peak flow recorded in 234 (76% of those aged 6 or over); emergency bronchodilation in 114 (30%); systemic steroids in 204 (54%); oxygen not used in primary care.

audits.t: An audit of diagnostic coding in genitourinary medicine clinics. Trent Region Genitourinary Medicine Audit Group.
audits.st: Correct KC60 diagnostic coding
audits.f: Correct STI coding ranged from 59.4% to 100% across scenarios; HIV pre-test counselling without testing coded by only 57.8%; 21% failed to code hepatitis B vaccine course once only.
audits.c: Regional discussions led to more training and new coding guidelines.

audits.t: Audit of resuscitation decisions has little impact on clinical practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Recording of resuscitation decisions 50% before the audit cycle.
audits.c: Clinical audit feedback and a resuscitation proforma.
audits.r2: Recording rose to 73% (p = 0.02) over a two-month audit cycle but was not maintained.

audits.t: Auditing complementary therapies in palliative care: the experience of the day-care massage service at Mount Edgcumbe Hospice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Community nephrology: audit of screening for renal insufficiency in a high risk population.
audits.tp: CKD detection and management in primary care
audits.st: Blood pressure and urine protein within 12 months and plasma creatinine within 24 months in patients aged 50-75 with hypertension or diabetes
audits.f: Creatinine measured within 24 months in 1359 (53.1%); blood pressure recorded in 73% and proteinuria tested in 29% within 12 months.

audits.t: Hepatitis B vaccination for occupational risk: an audit in general practice.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B vaccination of healthcare staff
audits.st: Full course of hepatitis B vaccine for patients at occupational risk
audits.f: Coverage with a full course of hepatitis B vaccine 46%.

audits.t: Radioisotope laboratory audits.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Introducing and auditing a nurse-led leg ulcer service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Introduction of a nurse-led leg ulcer clinic.

audits.t: Medical audit changes physicians' prescribing of antibiotics for respiratory tract infections.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection
audits.st: Audit Project Odense model for respiratory tract infection prescribing
audits.f: 45% of patients did not receive an antibiotic in the intervention group.
audits.c: Active intervention between registrations (feedback and follow-up discussion).
audits.r2: 55% did not receive an antibiotic in the intervention group.

audits.t: Long-lasting improvement in general practitioners' prescribing of antibiotics by means of medical audit.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection
audits.st: Recommendations on diagnosis and treatment of respiratory infections (APO method)
audits.f: Penicillin/broad-spectrum antibiotic ratio 1.33.
audits.c: Courses, visits to the laboratory and distribution of recommendations on diagnosis and treatment of respiratory infections.
audits.r2: Penicillin/broad-spectrum ratio 2.70 (1.94 in 1993), significantly higher increase than in controls.

audits.t: Prospective audit of cytomegalovirus-negative blood product utilization in haematology/oncology patients.
audits.st: Appropriate use of CMV-negative blood products according to CMV serostatus
audits.f: Inappropriate transfusions: packed red cells 73.2%, platelets 68.1%.
audits.c: Concurrent prospective audit of all orders with cancellation of inappropriate CMV-negative orders once serostatus known.
audits.r2: Inappropriate transfusions: packed red cells 14.3%, platelets 10.6% (P<0.001).

audits.t: An audit of error rates in a UK district hospital transfusion laboratory.
audits.st: Error rates reported in the transfusion literature
audits.f: Most errors were preanalytical (incomplete sample or request form data) and corrected before action; main analytical errors were transcription of patient identification and incorrect blood group testing; main postanalytical error was nurses not following blood component collection procedures.

audits.t: Improving the repeat prescribing process in a busy general practice. A study using continuous quality improvement methodology.
audits.st: 48 hour target for processing repeat prescription requests
audits.f: Turnaround within 48 hours 95%; prescriptions needing records checked 18%.
audits.c: PDSA cycles: synchronising repeat medications and recording drugs prescribed on visits, prioritising prescription signing at an agreed time, and moving prescription printing to reception.
audits.r2: Turnaround within 48 hours 99%; prescriptions needing records checked 8.6%.

audits.t: Oesophageal and gastric cancer pathology reporting: a regional audit.
audits.st: Minimum dataset (tumour type, depth of invasion, lymph node involvement, completeness of excision) and best practice reporting
audits.f: Minimum standards met in 77% of gastric (156/203) and 53% of oesophageal (42/79) resection reports; best practice in 20% of gastric and 18% of oesophageal reports.

audits.t: Audit of cervical screening and colposcopy in HIV-positive women at a central London teaching hospital.
audits.tp: Cervical screening in women living with HIV
audits.st: Local guideline: annual cervical cytology and baseline colposcopy for HIV-positive women
audits.f: Cytology undocumented in 72 (32.4%); colposcopy offered to 93 (42%), attended by 71 (32%); 49.7% had management not complying with the guidelines.

audits.t: Audit of condom issuing in eastbourne sexual health clinic.
audits.st: Locally developed standards for issuing condoms
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Health Promotion Department training on sexual history taking, including asking about frequency of intercourse.

audits.t: The investigation of iron deficiency anemia--a hospital based audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 94% had upper GI endoscopy (yield 54%, including 4 malignancies); 84% had lower GI investigation by colonoscopy or barium enema (yield 37%). Combined endoscopic and barium examinations gave a diagnosis in 69%; overall an underlying diagnosis was made in 92%.

audits.t: Prospective audits of quality of PEM recognition and nutritional support in critically ill elderly patients.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Audit A: misclassification of malnutrition in 54.0%

audits.t: An audit of mastitis in the emergency department.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 39% afebrile and only 27% had temperature of 38.5C or higher; most prescribed flucloxacillin; milk culture obtained in only 15 cases.

audits.t: An audit of positive findings in flexible and rigid check cystoscopy.
audits.st: Positive findings at flexible cystoscopy no more than 10%; negative findings at rigid cystoscopy no more than 50% (local standards)
audits.f: Positive finding rate 8.3% with flexible and 48.1% with rigid cystoscopy.

audits.t: Quality assurance in myocardial perfusion tomography: a collaborative BNCS/BNMS audit programme. British Nuclear Cardiology Society/British nuclear Medicine Society.
audits.st: Expert panel scoring of six parameters (stress technique, radiopharmaceutical usage, image acquisition, processing, report images, report text) as good (2), adequate (1) or poor (0)
audits.f: Stress technique inadequate in 10 (11%) studies; radiopharmaceutical usage and acquisition inadequate in 5 (6%); processing inadequate in 8 (10%); report images inadequate in 2 (3%); report text inadequate in 21 of 66 (32%). Mean quality score 1.3 (range 0.5-2.0); 17 of 88 (19%) scored below 1.0.

audits.t: The British Association of Dermatologists audit of atopic eczema management in secondary care. Phase 3: audit of service outcome.
audits.st: Eight working standards for service outcome (e.g. 60% relative DLQI improvement, 70% improvement in sleep loss, 80% improvement in worst aspect, 80% return to work or school)
audits.f: Mean DLQI 12.5 falling to 9.7 at 6 weeks (P = 0.001); mean CDLQI 10.5 falling to 8.7. Sleep loss improved in 44% of adults and 47% of children (standard 70%); worst aspect improved in 61% of adults and 59% of children (standard 80%). Return to work/school 70% of adults and 87.5% of children (standard 80%). Only one of eight standards met nationally.

audits.t: [Audit on the quality of medical records in oncology at the Lyon civic hospices].
audits.st: Consensus standards set by the care teams for medical record content
audits.f: Significant deviations for postal code of birth, pTNM classification, presence of pathology report and coded performance status.

audits.t: The national sentinel audit for stroke: a tool for raising standards of care.
audits.st: Intercollegiate Stroke Audit
audits.f: Swallow screening 55%, cognitive testing 23%, visual field examination 44%; MDT rehabilitation goals 55%; GP contact within 3 days of discharge 41%; 64% of trusts had a stroke physician and 50% a stroke team.

audits.t: The care of patients with diabetic nephropathy: audit, feedback, and improvement.
audits.st: St Vincent Declaration criteria for hypertension and good practice in diabetic nephropathy care
audits.f: 63% hypertensive at referral, untreated in 25%; ACE inhibitors not prescribed in 48% without contraindication; HbA1c > 9.1% in 29%; referral too late for RRT preparation in 33%.
audits.c: Education and feedback of results to referring practitioners.
audits.r2: Timing of referral improved (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: A completed audit to reduce hospital outpatients non-attendance rates.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Non-attendance 34% (32.5% Europeans, 50% Asian patients).

audits.t: The effect of a multifaceted physician office-based intervention on older women's mammography use.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mammography rate 62.7% in intervention sample
audits.c: Multifaceted intervention with physician opinion leaders, academic detailing, patient education, physician reminders and audit with feedback

audits.t: Informed choice in genetic screening for thalassaemia during pregnancy: audit from a national confidential inquiry.
audits.tp: Antenatal thalassaemia screening and informed choice
audits.st: Antenatal screening and counselling for haemoglobin disorders as standard UK practice; offer of prenatal diagnosis
audits.f: Risk detected by screening before or during first pregnancy in 49% (68/138) of couples. Prenatal diagnosis offered in 69% (274/400) of pregnancies; uptake 80% (216/274). Demonstrable service failure in 28% (110/400) of pregnancies.

audits.t: An audit of the use of manual handling equipment and their microbiological flora--implications for infection control.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Equipment used on multiple patients with inadequate cleaning; fabric aids frequently contaminated with MRSA and Clostridium difficile.

audits.t: An audit of long-stay patients in an inner city palliative care centre.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: A prospective audit of hospital-acquired deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
audits.st: THRIFT risk assessment criteria
audits.f: Overall rate of clinically apparent hospital-acquired thromboembolic complications 0.4% (n = 35); 2.1% (n = 17) in the high-risk group. Prophylaxis did not appear to reduce incidence, even when stratified by risk.

audits.t: Prospective 5-year audit for day-case laparoscopic cholecystectomy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Day-case rate 16%; successful day-case allocation 56%.
audits.c: 23-hour stay ward established, adding a third option.

audits.t: Management of acute pancreatitis: a comparative audit of clinical practice against the recommendations of the british society of gastroenterology
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology 1998 acute pancreatitis guidelines (e.g. mortality <10%, <30% in severe AP)
audits.f: Mortality 17% (standard <10%), 56% in severe AP (<30%); diagnosis within 48 h 100%; severity stratification about 80%; CRP measured in 51%; aetiology found in 77% (75-80%).
audits.c: None yet; prospective re-audit of 1999 admissions planned.

audits.t: Auditing the process of care in a new geriatric unit.
audits.st: Unit objectives expressed as individual audit criteria and a composite audit score
audits.f: Audit revealed the extent to which the Unit's goals were reflected in the care process; no significant correlation between recorded care processes and outcomes

audits.t: Audit and recurrence rates after hernia surgery.
audits.st: Recurrence rate and reoperation rate for recurrence after inguinal or femoral hernia repair; no target stated
audits.f: Recurrence rate 18% in 1984 and 1986; reoperation rate for recurrence at three years 10.8% (95% CI 9.3 to 12.2%) for 1986-1988.
audits.c: Recording recurrence rate, reoperation rate, hospital stay and day cases, and presenting these results to participating surgeons.
audits.r2: Recurrence rate 3% in 1993 and 1994; reoperation rate for recurrence at three years 2.2% (1.7 to 2.7%) for 1992-1997.

audits.t: An audit of antiretroviral medication offered to patients with HIV attending a district general hospital for outpatient care.
audits.st: British HIV Association (BHIVA) antiretroviral guidelines
audits.f: All patients eligible under BHIVA guidelines were being offered triple therapy. Viral load undetectable in 75% of 20 patients on their first established regimen and 36% of 14 patients who had failed at least one drug.

audits.t: [Auditing of drug use practices in anesthesia].
audits.st: Internal departmental pharmaceutical practice guidelines for anaesthetic agents and fresh gas flows
audits.f: Guidelines followed in more than 90% of cases for all agents except non-depolarising relaxants; intermediate-duration relaxants used in 52% of cases with expected surgery over 90 min against guidance to use pancuronium.
audits.c: Results presented and discussed; slight changes to the guidelines, especially on monitoring of neuromuscular blockade.
audits.r2: Use of propofol in non-approved situations fell from 5% to 0% (P = 0.03); pancuronium in surgery expected over 90 min 47% vs 52%, NS.

audits.t: Diabetic retinal photographic screening: a model for introducing audit and improving general practitioner care of diabetic patients in a rural setting.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Nurse-facilitator employed to visit practices, set up diabetic registers and audit referral for retinal photography.

audits.t: Evaluating the effect of assessment education with community psychiatric nurses using a file audit tool.
audits.st: File audit tool based on Present State Examination-9 for initial assessment documentation
audits.f: Documentation of initial assessments audited; baseline figures not given.
audits.c: Educational package on assessment based on Present State Examination-9 for community psychiatric nurses.
audits.r2: Documentation improved in all aspects, most significantly in recording history, mental state and treatment plan.

audits.t: Improved clinical practice but continuing service deficiencies following a regional audit of childhood diabetes mellitus.
audits.st: British Paediatric Association definition of a specialist and national recommendations for childhood diabetes services
audits.f: 7 of 21 consultant paediatricians met the specialist definition; many children seen in general paediatric clinics; 16 of 21 consultants used glycated haemoglobin.
audits.c: Wide distribution of the 1994 audit report to those in a position of influence.
audits.r2: 12 of 14 consultants met the specialist definition; all centres used designated diabetes clinics; all consultants used glycated haemoglobin.

audits.t: The surgical management of cervical carcinoma within the South West of England: progress through an audit loop. Gynaecology Tumour Panel.
audits.st: Minimum clinical dataset; proposed targets 100% FIGO staging and 95% appropriate radical surgery
audits.f: Retrospective audit; results not reported in abstract.
audits.c: Prospective collection of a defined minimum dataset on paper forms.
audits.r2: FIGO staging 92% (98% for cases above Stage Ia); tumour diameter not measured in 20% and thickness in 28%.

audits.t: Methodological issues in the use of guidelines and audit to improve clinical effectiveness in breast cancer in one United Kingdom health region.
audits.st: Regional evidence-based breast cancer clinical guidelines and guideline targets
audits.f: Chemotherapy use 17% and axillary surgery 46% (previous studies in this population).
audits.c: Regional guidelines, senior clinicians as local leads, audit of quality, clinician ownership of data, confidential feedback to participants and education.
audits.r2: Chemotherapy use rose to 23% and axillary surgery to 76%.

audits.t: The role of staging CT scans in the treatment of prostate cancer: a retrospective audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: All 97 had a planning CT; 85 also had a diagnostic staging CT, 51 (60%) with pelvic and abdominal imaging. 20 abnormalities were found in 19 patients; 13 were considered metastatic but only 4 altered treatment intent. Overall 4% were denied radical treatment on CT findings.

audits.t: Can district-wide audits improve primary care epilepsy management? An audit of seizure frequency recording.
audits.st: Recording of seizure frequency
audits.f: Seizure frequency recorded in 54.7%.
audits.r2: Seizure frequency recorded in 68% (improvement 13.2%, CI 8.9 to 17.6).

audits.t: An audit of the management of uterine malignancy within the West Midlands. West Midlands Gynaecological Oncology Group.
audits.st: 15 regional standards for uterine malignancy management
audits.f: Of 15 standards, 11 were met by at least one hospital; no hospital met all standards. Standards on initial referral and diagnostic intervals were universally failed. Outpatient diagnosis in only 30%. Surgery was usually within six weeks of diagnosis.

audits.t: Audit of time to emergency trauma laparotomy.
audits.tp: Major trauma time to CT and theatre
audits.st: Audit filter set at the upper quartile of emergency call to operating room time; comparison with national trauma database
audits.f: Median emergency call to operation 127 min (140 blunt, 86 penetrating); emergency department arrival to theatre 54 min. Audit filter selected 21 patients, with five correctable delays identified.

audits.t: The rate of breast-conserving surgery in early breast cancer: an audit of surgical practice at St Vincent's campus, NSW in 1990 and 1994.
audits.tp: Breast-conserving surgery rate in early breast cancer
audits.st: Comparison with published Australian breast-conserving surgery rates
audits.f: Breast-conserving surgery rate 33% in 1990 and 36% in 1994, lower than expected.

audits.t: A quality assurance audit: phase III trial of maximal androgen deprivation in prostate cancer (TROG 96.01).
audits.st: Technical adherence to the trial protocol
audits.f: Unacceptable protocol violation rate 10%.
audits.c: Improved audit design, staff education and increased data management resources.
audits.r2: Unacceptable protocol violation rate fell to 4%, with improved data quality and quantity.

audits.t: [Auditorship and errors: emphasis on nursing records].
audits.tp: Nursing record errors in billing reports
audits.st: Standard note-taking procedures (8 criteria)
audits.f: 491 errors in 34 procedure billing reports: 198 (40.6%) administrative, 121 (24.6%) doctors, 99 (20.2%) nurses, 51 (10.2%) accounting.

audits.t: Implementing clinical practice guidelines: a community-based audit of breast cancer treatment. Australian Capital Territory and South Eastern New South Wales Breast Cancer Treatment Group.
audits.st: Four locally agreed guidelines based on 1995 NHMRC breast cancer guidelines
audits.f: 85/87 (98%) had radiotherapy after breast-conserving surgery; 95/99 (96%) indicated received systemic adjuvant therapy; all 27 women under 50 with node-positive disease received chemotherapy; axillary surgery in 173 (91%).

audits.t: A regional collaborative audit of the practice and outcome of carotid endarterectomy in the United Kingdom. Northern Regional Carotid Endarterectomy Audit Group.
audits.st: Audit standards agreed from national guidelines
audits.f: Standards generally achieved: 114 (82%) had symptomatic 70-99% stenosis, 14 (10%) asymptomatic; 30-day disabling stroke or death 2.2% (95% CI 0.4-6.4%).

audits.t: Comparative audit of tonsillectomy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Two-thirds had tonsillectomy for recurrent acute tonsillitis; 3% were day cases. Return to theatre for haemorrhage 0.75%; readmission almost 7%. 92% felt their throat was better and 88% were pleased they had the operation.

audits.t: Brain attack!--How good is the early management of subarachnoid haemorrhage in accident and emergency departments? South Thames A&E Specialty Sub Committee Audit Group.
audits.st: Established guidelines for A&E management of subarachnoid haemorrhage
audits.f: CT within two hours in 18.8% and within six hours in 66.3%; 49.2% seen by a doctor within 30 minutes; nimodipine 18%, IV fluids 26%, analgesia 32%.

audits.t: Use of a computerised maternity information system to improve clinical effectiveness: thromboprophylaxis at caesarean section.
audits.st: Local thromboprophylaxis protocol for caesarean section
audits.f: Overtreatment of low-risk and undertreatment of high-risk women.
audits.c: Routine computer-generated risk assessment profile added to the maternity information system.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in protocol adherence in all risk groups.

audits.t: An audit of basic life support skills amongst general practitioner principals: is there a need for regular training?
audits.st: 1997 UK Resuscitation Council BLS guidelines in checklist form
audits.f: 48 (90.6%) unable to perform BLS according to guidelines.

audits.t: Monitoring quality of audit in obstetrics and gynaecology.
audits.st: Seven RCOG Clinical Audit Unit quality criteria for audit
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Significant improvement in audit quality over time.

audits.t: Carotid endarterectomy for carotid stenosis: audit at a tertiary referral centre.
audits.st: Criteria advised by the Stroke Council of the American Heart Association in 1995
audits.f: 36 carotid endarterectomies; all patients recovered without neurological complications or mortality; results fulfilled the AHA criteria

audits.t: Coding plastic surgery operations: an audit of performance using OPCS-4.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Gold standard OPCS-4 coding
audits.f: Coding office vs theatre staff overall accuracy 78% vs 43%; procedural codes 98% vs 42%; primary codes 62% vs 74%.
audits.c: Results discussed with all relevant staff
audits.r2: Only significant improvement was in overall accuracy of coding office records; coders better than theatre staff for primary codes (76% vs 56%).

audits.t: A clinical audit on the practice of platelet transfusions at a tertiary paediatric referral centre.
audits.st: Criteria agreed by the audit committee
audits.f: 22 of 119 (18.5%) platelet transfusions inappropriate.

audits.t: Integrated care pathways: an audit tool in paediatric oncology.
audits.st: Local standards set from neutropenia guidelines
audits.f: Retrospective notes review of care before the pathway; results not given in the abstract.
audits.c: Integrated care pathway for fever and neutropenia introduced to all members of the oncology unit.

audits.t: Audit of rheumatology services for adolescents and young adults in the UK. British Paediatric Rheumatology Group.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 18% of units (n = 9) had a dedicated adolescent clinic. Seven clinics had a standardised transfer process, first discussed at a median age of 13 years, but none provided literature or pre-visits. Generic health issues were addressed by only two clinics.

audits.t: An audit of phase II cardiac rehabilitation at Auckland hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 113 (39%) suitable for rehabilitation; 50 (44%) attended one or more sessions, 22 (19%) completed the six-week programme; 63 (56%) attended none.

audits.t: Quality assurance audit in an Australasian phase III trial of accelerated radiotherapy for head and neck cancer (TROG 91.01). Trans-Tasman Radiation Oncology Group.
audits.st: Technical adherence to the trial protocol
audits.f: Unacceptable protocol violation rate 10%.

audits.t: The 1998 Australian external beam radiotherapy survey and IAEA/WHO TLD postal dose quality audit.
audits.st: IAEA/WHO TLD postal dose quality audit; combined standard uncertainty 1.8%
audits.f: Dose quoted by centres was in nearly every case within 1.5% of the IAEA-assessed dose.

audits.t: An audit of MRI for bone and soft-tissue tumours performed at referral centres.
audits.tp: MRI staging of bone and soft-tissue tumours
audits.st: MR imaging and reporting requirements for staging musculoskeletal tumours (e.g. whole-bone imaging for skip metastases)
audits.f: Mean 4 sequences (range 2-8); enhancement used in 19. Whole bone not imaged for skip metastases in 50% of appropriate cases. Reports (available in 40) commonly omitted intraosseous and extraosseous extent and relation to the neurovascular bundle and joint.

audits.t: An audit of indications and techniques for supraclavicular fossa irradiation in early breast cancer in the United Kingdom.
audits.tp: Supraclavicular fossa irradiation in early breast cancer
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Significant variation in indications for supraclavicular fossa irradiation and in target volume definition; broad agreement on technique, including matching tangential and SCF fields.

audits.t: Performance and standards for the process of head and neck cancer care: South and West audit of head and neck cancer 1996-1997 (SWAHN I). South and West Regional Cancer Organisation Tumour Panel for Head and Neck Cancer.
audits.tp: Head and neck cancer care standards
audits.st: Established standards for head and neck cancer care, e.g. pretreatment chest X-ray 95%, multidisciplinary clinic pretreatment 95%
audits.f: 59% had pretreatment chest X-ray (standard 95%); 45% seen in multidisciplinary clinic pretreatment (standard 95%); median cases per surgeon 4 (1-26), per radiotherapist 10 (1-51)

audits.t: Cost-effective prescribing of proton pump inhibitor therapy: an audit in general practice.
audits.st: Practice policy to step PPI therapy down to low-dose cost-effective therapy, or to antacids, H2 receptor antagonists or no treatment where PPI not needed
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Patients on PPI were identified and switched to low-dose therapy or alternatives where PPI was not required.

audits.t: An audit on the assessment and management of acute bronchial asthma in the accident and emergency department of a district hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Severity recording: cyanosis 8%, inability to speak 2%, chest auscultation 64%, heart rate 10%, blood pressure 6%, respiratory rate 4%; no discharged patients given oral steroids.

audits.t: Audit of diabetes in Perak outpatient departments.
audits.st: Adequacy of diabetic management
audits.f: Overall control and monitoring of diabetes inadequate; most records had insufficient data on early detection; 55% of doctors had adequate knowledge; patient knowledge adequacy 13% to 80%

audits.t: Impact of quality improvement activities on care for acute myocardial infarction.
audits.st: Eight explicit process quality indicators for AMI care
audits.f: Pre-intervention chart audit; figures not given in abstract.
audits.c: Hospital-specific performance data, statewide data and peer comparisons fed back; hospitals asked to submit an improvement plan.
audits.r2: Statewide care improved on five of eight indicators; 44 (38%) hospitals with own measurement or system changes improved more on aspirin in hospital, aspirin at discharge and beta blockers at discharge.

audits.t: Audit in forensic pathology.
audits.st: Minimum standard for a routine, sudden, presumed natural death autopsy
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Improvement in intraoperative fresh frozen plasma transfusion practice--impact of medical audits and provider education.
audits.st: British Committee for Standards in Haematology FFP recommendations
audits.f: 14.6% definitely indicated, 40.2% conditionally indicated, 45.1% unjustified.
audits.c: Results presented at departmental meeting and guidelines circulated.
audits.r2: Unjustified FFP transfusions fell to 23.3%; conditional use rose to 69.1%.

audits.t: Rationalised prescribing for community acquired pneumonia: a closed loop audit.
audits.st: Local management protocol for community acquired pneumonia
audits.f: 26% received intravenous penicillin or erythromycin.

audits.t: Incidence of incomplete excision in surgically treated basal cell carcinoma: a retrospective clinical audit.
audits.tp: Basal cell carcinoma management and histology reporting
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 41 of 879 lesions (4.7%) were incompletely excised in 754 patients; 16 were re-excised and the rest followed up.

audits.t: Reducing red blood cell transfusion in elective surgical patients: the role of audit and practice guidelines.
audits.st: Transfusion guidelines requiring haemoglobin measurement immediately before transfusion
audits.f: Two-unit transfusions were 60% of all transfusions; haemoglobin was rarely measured before transfusion and the main trigger was estimated blood loss over 500 ml. Mean blood loss with a 2-unit transfusion 608 (373) ml; post-transfusion haemoglobin 12.4 (1.8) g/dl.
audits.c: Transfusion guidelines introduced requiring haemoglobin measurement immediately before transfusion.
audits.r2: Total transfusions fell by 43%. Mean blood loss with a 2-unit transfusion rose to 1320 (644) ml (p < 0.01) and post-transfusion haemoglobin fell to 9.9 (2.4) g/dl (p < 0.01).

audits.t: One stop breast clinics--victims of their own success? A prospective audit of referrals to a specialist breast clinic.
audits.st: Published referral guidelines (NHS, SIGN, BASO)
audits.f: 35% of referrals urgent; 28% of urgent and 37% of non-urgent referrals inappropriate according to guidelines.

audits.t: Audit of a one-stop breast clinic--revisited.
audits.st: Complete triple assessment at the one-stop visit
audits.f: Original audit found time constraints meant many patients with carcinoma had to return for further investigations.
audits.c: Booking only new patients at the start of clinic; greater GP access to referral
audits.r2: 36 of 40 (90%) had a definitive management decision at the first visit; 4 (10%) equivocal; mean wait to consultation 36.7 minutes, unchanged.

audits.t: Has the breast cancer 'two week wait' guarantee for assessment made any difference?
audits.st: Two-week wait guarantee for suspected breast cancer
audits.f: Cancer detection 22%; all cancers seen within 1 week; GP referral accuracy 42%; routine wait 4 weeks.
audits.r2: Cancer detection 19%; 85% seen within 2 weeks; GP accuracy 49%; routine wait at least 8 weeks.

audits.t: Who should manage primary retinal detachments?
audits.st: not reported (authors suggest 85-90% single-procedure reattachment)
audits.f: Single-procedure reattachment 76.1%.
audits.c: Primary retinal reattachment surgery centralised in the specialist vitreoretinal unit.

audits.t: Audit of small-incision cataract surgery using an anterior chamber maintainer.
audits.st: Comparison with the National Cataract Surgery Survey (RCO 1993)
audits.f: 90% gained visual acuity at 3 months. Posterior capsule opacification 13%, comparable to the national survey; corneal endothelial decompensation and endophthalmitis marginally higher.

audits.t: Using a national guideline: an audit of the management of gonorrhoea in Newcastle upon Tyne.
audits.st: National gonorrhoea guideline with auditable targets
audits.f: Chlamydia screening or presumptive treatment 98%; effective first-line therapy 95.4%; test of cure within one month 68.2%; partner notification discussion documented 94.3%; partner attendance 65%.

audits.t: Radiological review of accident and emergency radiographs: a 1-year audit.
audits.tp: Radiology reporting of emergency department radiographs
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 684 actual or suspected A&E interpretation errors flagged; 351 missed or strongly suspected fractures (mainly ankle, finger and elbow), 11 missed chest abnormalities and 24 A&E false positives. Further A&E action was taken in 286 (42.6%).

audits.t: Surgical management of intractable epistaxis: audit of results.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 8 patients had surgery (septoplasty, nasal packing, external carotid ligation); mean post-operative stay 3.9 days (range 3-6).
audits.c: Endoscopic sphenopalatine artery diathermy, with or without anterior ethmoid artery diathermy, offered instead of conventional surgery.
audits.r2: 10 patients (7%) needed surgery, all endoscopic sphenopalatine artery diathermy; mean post-operative stay 2.1 days (range 1-3); one recurrence managed conservatively and no surgical complications.

audits.t: Dementia care mapping: an approach to quality audit of services for people with dementia in two health districts.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline mapping highlighted limited staff-client interaction and a need for a wider range of activities to promote person-centred care.

audits.t: An audit of asthma care in minor injury units.
audits.st: BTS asthma guidelines and local protocols
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of thromboprophylaxis following caesarean section.
audits.st: RCOG 1995 guidelines for thromboprophylaxis following caesarean section
audits.f: 62.9% were moderate and 20.4% high risk. Overall 34 (17%) of 200 eligible women received thromboprophylaxis.

audits.t: Use and accuracy of fine-needle aspiration cytology in histologically proven thyroid carcinoma: an audit using a national nathology database.
audits.st: Guideline recommendation that FNAC is the first diagnostic step in nodular thyroid disease
audits.f: FNAC-t used in 591/890 (66%); overall sensitivity 57%, 70% for the most recent aspiration; only 47% of malignancies detected by FNAC-t

audits.t: How are abnormal results for liver function tests dealt with in primary care? Audit of yield and impact.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Follow-up data in 873 (94%); 531 already under hospital review. Of 157 suitable for investigation, no further tests were requested in 91 (58%); in seven, results suggesting treatable chronic liver disease had not been followed up. On investigation 97 (62%) had a diagnosis needing hospital intervention or follow-up.

audits.t: Effect of audit on door-to-inflation times in primary angioplasty/stenting for acute myocardial infarction.
audits.st: Door-to-inflation time; no target stated
audits.f: Pre-audit mean door-to-inflation time similar to the national average (figure not given).
audits.r2: Door-to-inflation times markedly reduced (figures not given).

audits.t: National breast surgery audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Data on 3000 breast cancer patients collected in the first 6 months; describes development and implementation of the audit.

audits.t: Culturally sensitive mental health services through quality improvement.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Clinical file audits showed non-English-speaking patients received more pharmacological treatment and less cognitive behavioural therapy than English-speaking patients.
audits.c: Planned cross-cultural training, revised policies and procedures, and revised roles for bilingual counsellors as cultural consultants.

audits.t: A national audit to monitor and promote the uptake of clinical guidelines on the management of diabetes in pregnancy.
audits.st: National clinical guideline on management of diabetes in pregnancy (criterion-based audit)
audits.f: Antenatal care was organised in line with guideline recommendations, but formal prepregnancy care provision was lower and pregnancy planning and periconceptual care fell short of recommendations; care during pregnancy was meticulous.

audits.t: An audit of psychiatric case notes in relation to antipsychotic medication and information giving.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Case notes were examined for the type, nature and frequency of information given to patients on depot neuroleptics; results not given in the abstract.

audits.t: [Quality of medical records in oncology: results of an audit of the Lyon Civil Hospices].
audits.st: Consensus standards agreed by the health care teams
audits.f: Significant deviations for pTNM classification and postal code of birth place.
audits.c: Guidelines proposed and a manual of procedures distributed in the unit during the second audit.

audits.t: An audit of clinical nurse practitioner led thrombolysis to improve the treatment of acute myocardial infarction.
audits.st: Acceptable door to needle times for thrombolysis in AMI
audits.f: Median door to needle time 60 min (range 42-110 min).
audits.c: Cardiac nurse practitioner led intravenous thrombolysis.
audits.r2: Median door to needle time 30 min (range 20-61 min).

audits.t: Applying the diabetes quality improvement project indicators in the Indian Health Service primary care setting.
audits.st: Diabetes Quality Improvement Project (DQIP) measures
audits.f: 55% had more than one HbA1c test during the year.
audits.r2: 80% had more than one HbA1c test during the year.

audits.t: Drugs for dementia: the first year. An audit of prescribing practice.
audits.tp: Dementia diagnosis and treatment in memory services
audits.st: Department of Health and Social Services (March 1998) prescribing guidelines for drugs for dementia
audits.f: Guidelines generally followed; 3 patients prescribed drugs outside the guidelines; most failures (10) were due to poor recording of data in the clinical record.
audits.c: Changes made to documentation of patient assessments; suggestions made to review CREST guidelines.

audits.t: Neonatal cranial ultrasound interpretation: a clinical audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 42 of 59 questionnaires returned (71%); mean accurate identification of cerebral abnormalities 59% (range 45-71%); only 44% of neonatal registrars had formal training in cranial ultrasonography.

audits.t: Audit of referral practice to a fast-access breast clinic before the guaranteed 2-week wait.
audits.st: Referral guidelines and 2-week wait
audits.f: 80% of referrals adhered to guidelines; 73% deemed urgent and seen within 2 weeks; all patients later diagnosed with breast cancer seen within 2 weeks.

audits.t: An audit of general dental practitioners' referral practice following the distribution of third molar guidelines.
audits.st: Local guidelines for management of impacted third molars issued to general dental practitioners (April 1998)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Distribution of third molar referral guidelines to local general dental practitioners in April 1998.

audits.t: Medical audit of diagnostic mammography examinations: comparison with screening outcomes obtained concurrently.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Diagnostic mammography had more positive biopsies, higher cancer detection rates and larger, more advanced cancers than screening

audits.t: Audit of pain management at home following tonsillectomy in children.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 36 responders; 50% consulted their GP for pain; many had moderately severe to severe pain.
audits.c: Five days of discharge analgesia and improved written discharge advice.
audits.r2: 56 responders; GP consultation 27%; moderately severe to severe pain not reduced.

audits.t: Factors influencing the use of thoracic radiotherapy in lung cancer--an analysis of the 1995 Scottish lung cancer audit.
