audits.st: Published guidelines on compensation for treatment gaps and national waiting time targets
audits.f: 55 of 56 centres returned data. 1467 (55%) had one or more interruptions; of these 56% still completed on time but 32% had no attempted compensation. Seven centres had no interruption policy. Mean time from first clinic visit to radiotherapy 40 days; six centres averaged under 28 days.

audits.t: An audit of delays before and during radical radiotherapy for cervical cancer--effect on tumour cure probability.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 22% completed EBRT without interruption; median overall treatment time 49 days; median wait to start radiotherapy 14 days.
audits.r2: 94% completed EBRT without interruption (P = 0.0009); median overall treatment time 39 days (P = 0.001); median wait increased to 35 days (P = 0.007).

audits.t: Audit of transfusion procedures in 660 hospitals. A College of American Pathologists Q-Probes study of patient identification and vital sign monitoring frequencies in 16494 transfusions.
audits.st: Laboratory and blood bank accreditation requirements for patient identification (4 components) and vital sign monitoring (3 intervals)
audits.f: First study: all identification components performed in 62.3% and all vital sign monitoring in 81.6% of transfusions (institution medians 69.0% and 90.2%).
audits.r2: Second study: all identification performed in 25.4% and all monitoring in 88.3% (institution medians 10.0% and 95.0%).

audits.t: Management of colorectal cancer: variations in practice in one hospital.
audits.st: RCS England and ACPGBI 1996 guidelines for colorectal cancer management
audits.f: Marked variation; colorectal specialists more likely to meet guidelines, performed fewer APRs and more extensive lymphadenectomy.
audits.r2: Compliance with guidelines markedly improved and fewer rectal procedures done by non-colorectal surgeons.

audits.t: Reducing antibiotic use on the neonatal unit by improving communication of blood culture results: a completed audit cycle.
audits.tp: Antibiotic use for suspected early onset neonatal infection
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Improved communication of blood culture results.

audits.t: Patients presenting with acute myocardial infarction to a district general hospital: baseline results and effect of audit.
audits.tp: Reperfusion times in acute myocardial infarction
audits.st: Cardiovascular Health Strategy: thrombolysis within ninety minutes of alerting medical or ambulance services
audits.f: Thrombolysis given in 31%; median call to needle time 200 minutes (rural median 227.5 minutes, n = 64; urban median 175 minutes, n = 37). Median arrival to CCU 90 minutes.

audits.t: Itemized bill: novel method to audit the process of laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
audits.st: Recommendations developed from itemised bill review of in-hospital process
audits.f: 8 of 23 charge categories accounted for 95% of total charge; surgeon and anaesthetist fees 34%, supplies 20%, theatre time 17%; areas for change identified in 6 categories.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary clinical pathway developed and implemented from recommendations.
audits.r2: A large number of recommendations were in place.

audits.t: Hepatitis A virus infection control: an audit of practice in England and Wales prior to guidelines being published.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Response rate about 44%; 31% of CsCDC were not notified of index cases within a week of onset; 95% were informed within two weeks; 5% to 28% did not recommend active prevention for close family contacts.

audits.t: Screening for gestational diabetes: a retrospective audit.
audits.st: Diabetic Pregnancy Study Group timed random blood sugar thresholds (fasting >6.1 mmol/l, non-fasting >7.0 mmol/l) compared with local thresholds
audits.f: Among women with t-RBS between local and proposed thresholds, 257 (97.7%) had a normal GTT and 6 (2.30%) abnormal; 4 (1.52%) were labelled gestational diabetic, all diet-managed with no adverse outcome.

audits.t: Adherence to local hospital guidelines for surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis: a multicentre audit in Dutch hospitals.
audits.st: Local hospital guidelines for surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis (choice, duration, dose, dosing interval, timing)
audits.f: Concordance: choice 92%, duration 82%, dose 89%, dosing interval 43%, timing of first dose 50%; overall adherence to all aspects 28%.

audits.t: National audit of emergency department child protection procedures.
audits.tp: Child protection in the emergency department
audits.st: Two official 1999 documents on child protection procedures and staffing in emergency departments
audits.f: Many standards met; figures not given in abstract.

audits.t: Clinical outcome monitoring program (COMP): a new application for use in orthodontic audits and research.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average PAR improvement 77.5% for the unit; clinician A marginally better than clinician B.

audits.t: Introducing practice-based learning and improvement ACGME core competencies into a family medicine residency curriculum.
audits.tp: Resident doctor engagement in quality improvement
audits.st: ACGME practice-based learning and improvement competencies
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Resident, faculty and staff teams completed clinical improvement projects with PDSA cycles over 6 months.
audits.r2: Chart audits indicated improvement in clinical projects (no figures given).

audits.t: Prescribing and administration of nebulized bronchodilators: a prospective audit in a university hospital.
audits.st: Complete and accurate prescription in five aspects; optimal administration
audits.f: No prescription was correct in all five aspects; driving gas type and flow omitted in 100%; recommended dose not prescribed in 46%; unclear frequency in 39%; administration optimal in 21.5%.

audits.t: Conventional antipsychotic prescription in unipolar depression, I: an audit and recommendations for practice.
audits.st: Recognised indications for antipsychotics in unipolar depression
audits.f: 138 of 494 were prescribed an antipsychotic; 40% of these had no recognised indication; mean time on antipsychotic 3 years.

audits.t: Reasons for increased postnatal length of stay & women's perceptions of length of stay.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Reasons for increased postnatal length of stay were varied.
audits.r2: By the second audit there was a demonstrated reduction in length of stay (no figures given).

audits.t: An audit of anaesthetic fresh-gas flow rates and volatile anaesthetic use in a teaching hospital.
audits.tp: Low-flow anaesthesia and volatile agent use
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average fresh-gas flow 2.0 l/min.
audits.c: Widespread discussion of first-period results; second period was clearly advised.
audits.r2: Average fresh-gas flow 2.1 l/min; sevoflurane use increased but its gas flows decreased.

audits.t: Evaluation of a quality improvement intervention for diabetes management.
audits.st: Diabetes management guidelines
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Diabetes management flowsheet in patient charts, with or without quarterly provider feedback on compliance.
audits.r2: Flowsheet associated with improved compliance only for foot examinations.

audits.t: The evolution of clinical audit as a tool for quality improvement.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 57 recommendations: 35% without action, 28% implemented, 33.3% pending or in progress.

audits.t: An audit of out of hours interventional vascular radiology.
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists 1996 guidelines that units should regularly assess their out of hours workload
audits.f: 1093 (57%) under vascular surgeons; only 17 (1.6%) of these investigated out of hours; 13/17 (76%) had intervention within 24 h.

audits.t: Adjuvant systemic therapies in women with breast cancer: an audit of clinical practice in Italy.
audits.st: International Consensus Panel recommendations for adjuvant systemic therapy
audits.f: Endocrine therapy not given to 102/541 (19%) endocrine-responsive patients; given to 22/182 (12%) endocrine-unresponsive patients; chemotherapy prescribed for 98%.

audits.t: Reduction of mechanical heart valve thrombosis through a clinical audit.
audits.st: Target INR 2.5-3.9 (thrombotic and bleeding complications under 2 per 100 patient-years)
audits.f: Under-anticoagulation in most patients; thrombosis risk 8.68 per 100 patient-years; fatal events 3.8 per 100 patient-years.
audits.c: INR reporting introduced, patient and doctor education on drug and diet interactions and valve thrombosis signs, treatment protocols.
audits.r2: Thrombosis 5.12 per 100 patient-years; non-fatal bleeding rose from 0.28 to 1.96 per 100 patient-years; no fatal events for four years.

audits.t: An audit of the laboratory interpretation of growth hormone response to insulin-induced hypoglycaemia in the assessment of short stature in children.
audits.st: Consensus cut-off concentrations for GH response in insulin stress test
audits.f: A number of laboratories used out-of-consensus cut-offs; five laboratories (9.6%) reported equivocal results for specimens not indicative of GH deficiency.

audits.t: National guidance on gynaecological cancer management: an audit of gynaecological cancer services and management in the South East of England.
audits.st: National guidance on gynaecological cancer management (centre/unit requirements, FIGO stage-based management)
audits.f: Ovarian cancer: stage recorded in 53% (262/492); 81% (169/209) managed per guidelines. Cervical cancer: stage recorded in 60% (188/315); 76% (142/188) managed per guidelines; 40% (127/315) not assessable.

audits.t: Use of collaborative audit to assist local implementation of the SIGN guideline for prevention of visual impairment in diabetes.
audits.st: SIGN guideline for prevention of visual impairment in diabetes (annual eye review and risk factor monitoring)
audits.f: Dilated fundoscopy within one year 72%; visual acuity 69%; HbA1c recorded 85% (65% of these 8% or less); BP recorded 88% (52% at or below 140/90); smoking status 89%.

audits.t: Using audit to monitor and improve the quality of anaesthesia for caesarean section.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: General anaesthesia in 58.0% of emergency and 45.5% of elective sections (53.0% overall); 25.3% had anaesthetic complications or side-effects; 90.3% satisfied.
audits.c: Findings presented to the multidisciplinary team and changes to anaesthetic practice introduced
audits.r2: General anaesthesia fell to 23.8% (P < 0.05); complications or side-effects 17.2%; satisfaction maintained.

audits.t: Audit of chest X-rays in general practice--a case for local guidelines?
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists referral guidelines, including six weeks' delay after onset of chest wall pain
audits.f: 569 CXRs in 482 patients; 30% assessed as not indicated.

audits.t: Breast cancer audit: adapting national audit frameworks for local review of clinical practice.
audits.st: Scottish Cancer Therapy Network (SCTN) minimum data set for breast cancer
audits.f: Minimum data set identified outliers from the normal range of process indicators; no figures given in abstract.

audits.t: An audit of the vaccination and antibiotic prophylaxis practices amongst patients splenectomised in Lothian.
audits.st: Department of Health guidelines on post-splenectomy vaccination and antibiotic prophylaxis
audits.f: Vaccinated against S. pneumoniae 80.6%, H. influenzae 65.9%, N. meningitidis 48.2%; 74.8% on long-term prophylaxis; only 37.4% both vaccinated and on prophylaxis as recommended.

audits.t: Audit can ensure the safe and effective introduction of seizure prophylaxis with magnesium sulphate in obstetric practice.
audits.st: Local magnesium sulphate protocol compliance and achievement of therapeutic magnesium levels
audits.f: Protocol violations caused delayed therapeutic levels or high magnesium concentrations in 5 of 8 cases.
audits.c: Circulation of results and staff education
audits.r2: Near complete protocol compliance and more consistent time to therapeutic magnesium concentration.

audits.t: Organisation of services for acute stroke in Scotland--report of the Scottish stroke services audit.
audits.st: Key recommendations of the four SIGN stroke guidelines (14 key components of an integrated stroke service)
audits.f: No Trust provided all 14 key components; lack of provision was widespread for fast-track TIA/minor stroke clinics and CT scanning within 48 hours.

audits.t: An audit of the implementation of guidelines to reduce wound infection following caesarean section.
audits.st: National guidelines on antibiotic prophylaxis at caesarean section; wound infection rate <5%
audits.f: Wound infection rate 10%; failure to give antibiotics, especially at elective caesarean section.
audits.c: Local protocol for antibiotics at all caesarean sections introduced.

audits.t: [Documentation of the care process for prevention and treatment of decubitus lesions: the audit method].
audits.st: Local pressure lesion prevention and treatment protocol
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Quality control of the European Liver Transplant Registry: results of audit visits to the contributing centers.
audits.st: Agreement between registry data and hospital charts
audits.f: Registry completeness 95%; consistency between charts and registry 98%.

audits.t: Reducing unnecessary blood work in the neurosurgical ICU.
audits.st: Blood work should match physicians' orders
audits.f: Blood drawn without orders, duplicate tests and blood work continuing long past medical need.
audits.c: In-service training, reminder posters, protocol reference sheets and medical staff memoranda; further measures after repeat audits.
audits.r2: Project goals were met; unordered blood work reduced (no figures given).

audits.t: Nursing home physician educational intervention improves end-of-life outcomes.
audits.st: End-of-life care indicators (recognition of dying, advance directives, pain and dyspnoea control, hygiene, bereavement support, comfort)
audits.f: Terminal care by 61 physicians for 203 dying residents reviewed.
audits.c: Half-day educational outreach for key physicians with audit and feedback and quality improvement suggestions.
audits.r2: All four facilities completing the intervention had significant improvements in end-of-life outcomes.

audits.t: Sexual health care of HIV-positive patients: an audit of a local service.
audits.tp: Sexual health screening in people with HIV
audits.st: 100% of HIV-positive patients should have a sexual health screen within six months of their first HIV out-patient appointment
audits.f: 44.5% had a sexual health screen; 46 (60.5%) of those screened had a sexually transmitted infection.
audits.c: A number of recommendations were implemented to improve uptake of sexual health screening (details not reported)

audits.t: Significant improvement in quality of caesarean section documentation with dedicated operative proforma--completion of the audit cycle.
audits.st: CNST documentation guidelines
audits.f: Under 80% documented several key items; only 41% had complete signature with printed name and 35% correct time and date.
audits.c: Dedicated caesarean 'operative delivery note' proforma designed to CNST guidelines
audits.r2: Significant improvement in almost all items assessed.

audits.t: Audit of primary care and initial secondary care investigations set against RCOG guidelines as standard in cases of subfertility.
audits.st: RCOG evidence-based guidelines on initial investigation of the infertile couple
audits.f: Mid-luteal progesterone and semen analysis performed correctly with results available in only 33% and 2% of occasions; many patients lacked clearly documented advice.

audits.t: A prospective clinical audit of neonatal resuscitation practices in Canada.
audits.st: Neonatal Resuscitation Program (NRP) and Canadian National Guidelines for Neonatal Resuscitation
audits.f: Resuscitation unanticipated in 76% (596/783); sequencing errors reported; chest compressions 8% (65/783); medications 14% (113/783); 52% out of neutral temperature range (27% hypothermic, 25% hyperthermic).

audits.t: An audit of interventions for dual diagnosis in a psychiatric unit.
audits.tp: Substance misuse screening in mental health patients
audits.st: Key standards for dual diagnosis care based on national and local recommendations
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Training programme on dual diagnosis for mental health nurses.
audits.r2: Improvement observed in standards of care; figures not given in abstract.

audits.t: Assessment of the accuracy of cytology in women referred for colposcopy and biopsy: the results of a 1 year audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 80% of 326 women referred for moderate or severe dyskaryosis had CIN II/III or invasive carcinoma; of 20 with glandular changes, 5 had adenocarcinoma in situ, 8 CIN and 7 negative biopsies.

audits.t: Pressure ulcer risk: audit findings.
audits.st: Guideline recommendations for reducing pressure ulcer development
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Pathology reporting of rectal cancer: a national audit.
audits.st: Predefined proforma for rectal cancer histopathology reports
audits.f: Multiple staging systems in 40% of reports; no stage in 31%; circumferential margin involvement recorded in 63%.

audits.t: [Audit of prescribing practices in nursing homes. Many preparations but few serious interactions].
audits.st: Swedish Drug Compendium (FASS) interactions
audits.f: Mean 9.6 drugs per patient; 74 potential interactions, four clinically important; 28% on neuroleptics at moderate doses.

audits.t: Genital herpes: audit of cases referred by general practitioners to a department of genito-urinary medicine.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: GPs correctly diagnosed herpes in 32/78 (41%) men and 56/118 (47%) women.

audits.t: Prospective audit of diabetes care and outcomes in a group of geriatric French care homes.
audits.st: French diabetes guideline end-points
audits.f: HbA1c in keeping with guidelines in 23.3%; never performed in 26%; above 8% in 20.5%; guideline items never addressed in 2 to 80%.

audits.t: Total mesorectal excision for rectal cancer--what can be achieved by a national audit?
audits.st: Total mesorectal excision (TME) standard
audits.f: Local recurrence 28%; 5-year overall survival 55% for under 75s.
audits.c: National TME training courses, pathologist training, a rectal cancer registry and regular feedback of departmental results.
audits.r2: TME rose from 78% (1994) to 96% (1998); local recurrence 8% at 39 months; 5-year overall survival 71% for under 75s.

audits.t: Monitoring blood transfusion in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting: an audit methodology.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 47.4% of patients received red blood cell transfusion.
audits.c: Transfusion database built from patient administration system and blood transfusion service data allowing continuous audit.
audits.r2: 31.6% of patients received red blood cell transfusion.

audits.t: Comparative audit of abdominal aortic aneurysm repairs using POSSUM scores.
audits.st: P-POSSUM predicted mortality
audits.f: Observed mortality 5% elective, 18% urgent, 30% emergency rupture; no significant difference from P-POSSUM predicted deaths.

audits.t: New method to evaluate the practice of positive pressure ventilation in intensive care units.
audits.st: Protective ventilation strategy; proportion of data points with unnecessary hyperventilation
audits.f: Clear differences in practice between teaching and district hospitals.
audits.c: Intensive education programme with nurse-run simple ventilation protocols
audits.r2: District hospital practice closely mirrored the teaching centre.

audits.t: Improving the effectiveness of the emergency management of renal colic in a district general hospital: a completed audit cycle.
audits.st: New local guidelines based on literature (diclofenac analgesia, prompt IVU)
audits.f: 7 of 14 admitted, 5 to wait for IVU; mean IVU wait 12.3 (SD 2.2) hours; mainly intramuscular opioids.
audits.c: New interdepartmental guidelines, junior doctor training, ED staff performing 3-film IVUs
audits.r2: 5 of 19 admitted, 1 waiting for IVU; mean IVU wait 4.1 (SD 0.96) hours; rectal diclofenac the drug of choice.

audits.t: Sterilisation at caesarean section--an audit from a district general hospital.
audits.st: RCOG Clinical Audit and Effectiveness Support Unit guidelines on female sterilisation
audits.f: Gaps between rhetoric and reality in many standards; figures not given in abstract.

audits.t: Clinical audit: obstetric performance after caesarean section.
audits.st: Two RCOG Clinical Audit Unit auditable standards for women labouring with a previous caesarean section
audits.f: Documented discussion of delivery options in 98% of notes; successful vaginal delivery 36/60 (60%) excluding those declining trial of labour.

audits.t: Audit of referrals to a hospital palliative care team: role of the bilingual health-care worker.
audits.tp: Palliative care access for ethnic minority patients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Bilingual health-care worker involved in 41% of referrals from ethnic minorities.
audits.c: Appointment of a bilingual health-care worker in May 2000.

audits.t: An audit of resuscitation and anaesthesia during Operation 'Safe Haven'.
audits.st: Advanced Trauma Life Support principles
audits.f: 18 casualties resuscitated, 3 died; 71 anaesthetics in 52 patients audited; isoflurane with controlled ventilation gave higher systolic BP and faster recovery than halothane/trichloroethylene.

audits.t: A criterion based audit of inpatient asthma care. Closing the feedback loop.
audits.st: Hospital asthma management protocol: PEF variability 20% or less before discharge and written check of inhaler technique
audits.f: PEF variability criterion met in 30/55 (54%); written inhaler technique check 32/55.
audits.c: PEF discharge criterion relaxed in line with national guidelines, a stamp introduced to record inhaler technique checks, and encouragement from senior staff.
audits.r2: PEF variability criterion met in 17/23 (74%); written inhaler technique check 22/23 (96%).

audits.t: An audit of cardiac arrest management by extended trained ambulance crew.
audits.st: Agreed resuscitation protocols for ventricular fibrillation and asystole/EMD
audits.f: Deviations from the VF protocol in 27 cases (27.5%) and from the asystole protocol in 27 cases (16.0%). VF: 26 admitted, 17 discharged; asystole/EMD: 11 admitted, 1 discharged.

audits.t: The use of intradepartmental audit to contain cesarean section rate.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Caesarean section rate 12.3%; perinatal mortality 8.25 per 1000.
audits.c: Intradepartmental critical review of caesarean indications.
audits.r2: Caesarean section rate 11.4%; 26.8% fall in caesareans for cephalopelvic disproportion (P = 0.0013); perinatal mortality 5.83 per 1000.

audits.t: Cervical cytology: an audit in a Singapore teaching hospital.
audits.st: International data on cervical cytology diagnoses and cytohistological correlation
audits.f: 96% negative, under 1% inadequate, 1% atypia, 1% dysplasia or malignancy; 97% concordance for biopsied high-grade dysplasia.

audits.t: Time delays in provision of thrombolytic treatment in six district hospitals. Joint Audit Committee of the British Cardiac Society and a Cardiology Committee of Royal College of Physicians of London.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median arrival to thrombolysis 80 minutes in the cardiac care unit vs 31 minutes in A&E; call to arrival 41 minutes by ambulance vs 90 minutes via GP.

audits.t: An audit of the management and outcome of hospital inpatients with diabetes: resource planning implications for the diabetes care team.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 23% had documented screening for diabetic complications; discharge diagnoses omitted diabetes in 54 cases; only 10% had formal diabetes team advice; median stay 22 days.

audits.t: An audit of acute asthma admissions to a respiratory unit.
audits.st: British Thoracic Society acute asthma guidelines
audits.f: PEFR recorded 52%, blood gases 72%, speech 27%, air entry 58%, exhaustion 4%; 93% of severe cases given corticosteroids but none given more than 35% oxygen; chest radiograph 87%, serum potassium 56%.
audits.c: Severity marker stamp for case notes and treatment guidelines implemented.

audits.t: A simple and direct method of turnround time audit in a microbiology laboratory.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Minimal reorganisation to address administrative and technical delays
audits.r2: Mean turnround time improved (figures not reported).

audits.t: Towards the audit of geriatric day hospitals: a pilot project in west Surrey/north east Hampshire.
audits.tp: Geriatric long-term and day hospital care standards
audits.st: Individual patient targets measured with the Patient Achievement Inventory
audits.f: Data form completion 90% and 81%; PAI kappa 0.72.

audits.t: Comparative audit: an experimental study of 147,882 general surgical admissions during 1990.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 160 surgeons returned data; mortality 0 to 5 per cent and morbidity 0 to 22 per cent; laparoscopic cholecystectomy had one-quarter the mortality and two-thirds the morbidity of open.
audits.c: Confidential feedback of comparative results to surgeons.

audits.t: An audit of the use of platelet concentrates in the prophylaxis of thrombocytopenic haemorrhage in a large haematology unit.
audits.st: Threshold platelet count for prophylactic transfusion of 20 x 10(9)/l
audits.f: Lack of adherence to the threshold, with transfusions at higher platelet counts; major bleeding occurred above threshold when additional clinical factors present.
audits.c: A lower transfusion threshold was recommended and instituted.
audits.r2: 20% reduction in use of platelet concentrates with no increase in major bleeding episodes.

audits.t: [Audit on antibiotic prescriptions in a department of infectious diseases].
audits.st: SPILF consensus conferences and bacteriology results
audits.f: 35% of prescriptions inadequate: 22 excessive, 8 unjustified, 5 inappropriate.

audits.t: Audit of gonorrhoea test of cure at the genitourinary medicine department in Newcastle upon Tyne, UK.
audits.st: National guidelines stating that test of cure is usually performed
audits.f: Of 126 cases with test of cure after a sensitive antibiotic, none were positive.

audits.t: The quality and value of sudden infant death necropsy reporting in Ireland.
audits.st: Modified Rushton scoring; minimum accepted standard of necropsy per recent guidelines
audits.f: Of 245 reports overall, 55.5% below the minimum accepted standard.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in necropsy quality after guidelines.

audits.t: The need for radio-opaque side markers on CT of the paranasal sinuses.
audits.st: Radio-opaque side marker on the right side of the face for all paranasal sinus CT
audits.f: Marker identified in 85% of scans; 30% of clinical staff aware of it.
audits.c: Changes indicated by the first cycle (details not stated)
audits.r2: Marker identified in 100% of scans; staff awareness 90%.

audits.t: The health needs of children in public care: the results of an audit of immunizations of children in care.
audits.st: Local population immunisation rates / national immunisation schedule
audits.f: Children in public care had lower immunisation rates and more incomplete schedules than the local population (no figures given in abstract).

audits.t: [Assessment of the habits of physicians involved in the management of HIV-infected patients. A clinical audit on the biological follow-up].
audits.st: 1998 Dormont report guidelines
audits.f: 45% had initial tests conforming to recommendations (hospital 57%, GP 23%).

audits.t: A prospective audit of the implementation of the 2-week rule for assessment of suspected urological cancers.
audits.st: UK Government 2-week rule for suspected cancer referrals (seen within 2 weeks); regional tumour working group referral criteria
audits.f: 82/234 GP referrals met regional suspected cancer criteria; 13% clearly marked urgent/cancer; 23% had no implication of cancer; 72% seen in haematuria clinic with median 56.5 days and none within 2 weeks; others median 21 days with 34% compliance.

audits.t: Chlamydia trachomatis infection in a colposcopy unit: an audit of a fast track referral system for infected patients to a genitourinary medicine department and a survey of patients' demography, clinical findings and partner details.
audits.st: Adequate treatment and partner notification for all chlamydia-positive patients
audits.f: Not reported; need for a formal protocol became apparent.
audits.c: Interdepartmental fast-track referral protocol to the GUM health adviser for immediate treatment and partner notification
audits.r2: All infected patients received adequate treatment and partner notification.

audits.t: The IAEA/WHO TLD postal dose quality audits for radiotherapy: a perspective of dosimetry practices at hospitals in developing countries.
audits.st: 5% acceptance limit for TLD dose
audits.f: 84% of participants within the 5% acceptance limit.

audits.t: Audit of 'crash' emergency caesarean sections due to cord prolapse in terms of response time and perinatal outcome.
audits.st: Delivery within 30 minutes of diagnosis for crash caesarean section
audits.f: Median diagnosis to delivery 20 minutes (range 10 to 40); 76% (19/30) delivered within 30 minutes; time of diagnosis not recorded in 5 cases.

audits.t: Completion of the audit cycle: standardised nurse-led information for patients.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Previous audit found differences between standard-treatment and clinical-trial patients in information and involvement.
audits.c: Routine nurse appointment at least one day before consent with standardised written chemotherapy information
audits.r2: Of 160 questionnaires, 131 replies; significantly more standard-chemotherapy patients remembered written nurse information and signing a consent form.

audits.t: Introducing criteria based audit into Ugandan maternity units.
audits.st: Criteria based audit standards of maternity care set locally
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Didactic teaching on criteria based audit, practical work in own units, ongoing support and follow-up workshops
audits.r2: Improvements were seen in many standards of care (no figures in abstract).

audits.t: Audit of compliance to adjuvant chemotherapy and radiotherapy guidelines in breast cancer in a cancer network.
audits.st: North Trent Cancer Network Breast Group adjuvant chemotherapy and radiotherapy guidelines (revised 1998)
audits.f: Overall compliance 82% (chemotherapy 90%, radiotherapy 74%), similar across the network; compliance undetermined in 5%.

audits.t: Audit of an antibiotic policy and microbiological investigations for treating bacteraemia in a large teaching hospital.
audits.st: Hospital antibiotic policy for empirical therapy
audits.f: Poor use of the antibiotic policy, with inadequate (P=0.005) or excessive (P<0.00001) antibiotic treatment and a trend to increased mortality.

audits.t: Exploring the links between quality assurance and laboratory resources. An audit-based study.
audits.st: Quality assurance of smear selection for Ziehl-Neelsen staining
audits.f: Overall acid-fast bacillus positivity 42%.
audits.c: Two-step corrective measure in smear selection based on audit results.

audits.t: Effect of a new guideline on outcome following third-degree perineal tears: results of a 3-year audit.
audits.st: New local guideline for repair of obstetric anal sphincter tears
audits.f: Repairs in theatre 70%; Prolene used 64%; adequate anaesthesia 70%; complete follow-up 66%.
audits.r2: Repairs in theatre 82% then 97%; Prolene 76% then 93%; adequate anaesthesia 82% then 97% (P<0.05); complete follow-up 86% then 80%.

audits.t: Audit of compliance with antenatal protocols.
audits.st: Departmental antenatal action protocols triggered by booking risk factors
audits.f: 3673 of 15,658 protocol-dictated actions (23.5%) performed; actions rated clinically important by consultants 28.3% vs 18.6% for less important.

audits.t: Audit of HIV partner notification in a district general hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: The majority of current partners were notified and 60% were HIV-positive; no previous partners were successfully notified.

audits.t: Obstetric audit in resource-poor settings: lessons from a multi-country project auditing 'near miss' obstetrical emergencies.
audits.tp: Maternal death and severe morbidity review
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Non-attendance at clinic: cycles of audit of a consultant based gastroenterology outpatient department.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Non-attendance rate for new appointments remained unsatisfactory and comparable to the NHS average.
audits.c: Optimising the operation of the clinic (details not reported); several audit cycles.
audits.r2: Short-term improvements in defaulting rates appeared to result from extraneous factors (a general election and moving to new buildings); no numbers reported.

audits.t: Increased prescription of thrombolytic treatment to elderly patients with suspected acute myocardial infarction associated with audit.
audits.tp: Reperfusion times in acute myocardial infarction
audits.st: Prescription of thrombolytic treatment to elderly patients with acute myocardial infarction
audits.f: Thrombolysis prescribed to 13/110 (12%) patients aged 65 or over with confirmed myocardial infarction; no patients with angina received it.
audits.c: Interventions in clinical management (details not specified in abstract).
audits.r2: Thrombolysis prescribed to 55/119 (46%) (p less than 0.01); 13/79 (16%) with angina treated.

audits.t: Delivering a selective neonatal BCG vaccination programme in a multi-ethnic community: an audit of the neonatal BCG immunisation programme in Birmingham and Solihull.
audits.st: National guidelines on selective neonatal BCG vaccination of eligible (high-risk) infants
audits.f: BCG indicated for 41% of newborns; 74% of eligible infants vaccinated (range 36-83% across five maternity units).

audits.t: Towards evidence-based use of serum tumour marker requests: an audit of use in a tertiary hospital.
audits.st: Predefined criteria for appropriate and useful tumour marker requests
audits.f: 476 tumour markers ordered; 69% deemed appropriately ordered; 29% helpful in management; 22% abnormal.

audits.t: Introduction of nurse led DC cardioversion service in day surgery unit: prospective audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Waiting time 27 weeks before the new service.
audits.c: Introduction of a collaborative nurse-led DC cardioversion service in a day surgery unit, with a nurse consultant coordinating.
audits.r2: Waiting times reduced to 8 weeks; sinus rhythm restored in 131 of first 143 patients (92%); 3 needed admission, no important complications.

audits.t: Re-audit of radiotherapy waiting times 2003.
audits.st: Joint Collegiate Council for Oncology (JCCO) waiting time guidelines
audits.f: Not reported in detail.
audits.r2: Waiting times lengthened in most centres; fewer patients in all categories treated within JCCO guidelines; no further rise in median palliative wait.

audits.t: Inter-observer agreement in audit of quality of radiology requests and reports.
audits.st: Standardised scoring system for request and report quality items
audits.f: Acceptable item scores above 70% for all items except requester bleep/extension, legibility of physician's name and previous investigation details.

audits.t: Audit of infective morbidity following caesarean section at a district general hospital.
audits.st: Local guideline: single intraoperative IV antibiotic dose after delivery; target 90% coverage
audits.f: 14% received prophylactic antibiotics; infection-related morbidity 28.5%; wound infection 17.5%.
audits.c: New guidelines requiring a single intraoperative IV antibiotic dose
audits.r2: 81% received prophylaxis (difference 67%, 95% CI 60-74%); infective morbidity 16%; wound infection 9%.

audits.t: Towards the modern management of ectopic pregnancy: a complete audit cycle of practice in a London teaching hospital.
audits.st: Local targets: low rupture rates, high sonographic diagnosis, acceptable tubal conservation and laparoscopic surgery rates
audits.f: Not reported in detail.
audits.r2: Substantial improvement, mainly in ultrasound diagnosis, with fewer ruptured ectopics; laparoscopic rate stable.

audits.t: Audit of anti-D immunoglobulin administration to pregnant Rhesus D negative women following sensitising events.
audits.st: National Blood Transfusion Service Immunoglobulin Working Party guidelines (1991) on anti-D prophylaxis
audits.f: All patients received appropriate postpartum management; more than half of antepartum sensitising events beyond 20 weeks were not managed according to the guidelines.

audits.t: An audit of trial of labour after previous caesarean section.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 51% of women with a previous caesarean were allowed a trial of labour; vaginal delivery success 70% in those, 36% if elective repeat caesareans included.

audits.t: Audit of the management of convulsive status epilepticus in children: the need for a uniform treatment strategy.
audits.tp: Acute convulsion and status epilepticus management
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Considerable variability in the management of convulsive status epilepticus.

audits.t: Findings from the British HIV Association's national clinical audit of first-line antiretroviral therapy and survey of treatment practice and maternity care, 2002.
audits.st: British HIV Association (BHIVA) antiretroviral therapy guidelines; government target of >90% antenatal HIV testing
audits.f: 844 (90%) started recommended first-line therapy; 98 (10%) nonstandard regimens; 3 did not strictly meet starting criteria; shortfalls in pretreatment testing of glucose, lipids and hepatitis C.

audits.t: An audit of paediatric audits.
audits.st: Criteria for a full audit
audits.f: 27.8% met criteria for a full audit; 22.2% were re-audited.

audits.t: Audit of antibiotic use in a Brazilian University Hospital.
audits.st: Appropriate therapeutic antibiotic use and surgical prophylaxis choice, timing and duration
audits.f: Antibiotics prescribed for 55.4%; therapeutic use inadequate in 27%; prophylaxis correctly chosen in 78.9%, correctly timed in 15.9%, and postoperative use appropriate in 29.8%.

audits.t: Prospective audit of quality of colonoscopy in a surgical coloproctology unit.
audits.st: Compared with published results (no named standard)
audits.f: Bowel preparation success 94%; completion 90% for consultant and registrars, 74% for junior grades (overall 86%).

audits.t: Auditing a new lung cancer service.
audits.st: Compared with national figures (no named standard)
audits.f: Mean time to tissue diagnosis 14.8 days (range 2-46); no tissue diagnosis in 6 (5.1%); 47.8% of NSCLC stage 4.

audits.t: Caesarean section in term nulliparous women at Wellington Hospital in 2001: a regional audit.
audits.st: Standards from the literature for caesarean section indications and care
audits.f: Corrected CS rate 27%; elective 36/743 (5%), emergency 165/743 (22%); a significant proportion of CS did not meet the standards.

audits.t: An audit of the implementation of guidelines in relation to the prevention of dental caries.
audits.st: SIGN guidelines on targeted prevention of dental caries in 6-16-year-olds
audits.f: Caries risk assessment recorded 13%; radiographic reporting 53%; dietary advice 36%; toothbrushing instruction 41%.
audits.c: Dissemination of results and reinforcement of key guideline points.
audits.r2: Caries risk assessment 17%; radiographic reporting 80% (P = 0.001); dietary advice 68%; toothbrushing instruction 92% (both P = 0.001); fissure sealant prescription improved significantly.

audits.t: Vaccination levels and missed opportunities for measles vaccination: a record audit in a public pediatric clinic.
audits.st: Age-appropriate vaccination
audits.f: Coverage with all age-appropriate vaccines fell from 67% at 3 months to 25% at 19 months; a missed MMR opportunity in one third of children.

audits.t: Accelerating the audit cycle: data gathering, analysis and dissemination of results by electronic methods. The third Yorkshire audit of genital chlamydial management.
audits.st: National standards and guidelines for management of genital chlamydial infection
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Feedback and discussion with clinics to identify interventions to improve practice

audits.t: Sphygmomanometers--an audit in general practice.
audits.st: Accuracy against a gold standard sphygmomanometer (within 4 mmHg)
audits.f: Over 95% of sphygmomanometers were within 4 mmHg of the gold standard across the clinical pressure range.

audits.t: [Structure and content of the radiological report: an audit of 94 reports from a university education center].
audits.st: Five report criteria: comprehensible, problem-oriented, correct Dutch, concise and direct
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: [Efficacy of auditing in improving a Control Program of Pregnancy].
audits.st: 20 antenatal care markers with defined quality criteria
audits.f: Baseline quality index for 20 markers (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Audit feedback (quality control) between cycles; details not specified.
audits.r2: Quality index improved in 9 markers, worsened in 1 and was unchanged in the rest.

audits.t: Record keeping by undergraduate dental students: a clinical audit.
audits.st: Modified CRABEL scoring system
audits.f: Department where patient was seen most often missing, followed by illegible demonstrator and student signatures.
audits.c: Tutorial presentation of results and teaching session on good record keeping to 20 students
audits.r2: Almost all elements improved, most reaching 100%, except updated medical history and most recent complaint.

audits.t: An audit of appropriate tests in renal biopsy coagulation screens.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 30 of 147 coagulation screens abnormal, most commonly prolonged bleeding time (58.6%); 21 of 30 biopsies delayed by 1 hour to 14 days.
audits.c: Clotting screen modified as a result of the audit

audits.t: Antibiotic prescription practice in an intensive care unit using twice-weekly collection of screening specimens: a prospective audit in a large UK teaching hospital.
audits.st: Current evidence-based practice (clinician consensus); no named standard
audits.f: 77% received at least one antibiotic; of 183 sepsis prescriptions 108 (59%) were empirical and only 21% of these were changed; 28% of 75 organism-specific prescriptions targeted organisms isolated at least 4 days earlier.
audits.c: Regular twice-weekly screening samples stopped in favour of targeted, invasive sampling guided by clinical suspicion.

audits.t: An audit of assessment procedures in women who develop breast cancer after a negative result.
audits.tp: Interval cancer review in breast screening
audits.st: UK National Breast Screening Programme assessment guidelines (2001)
audits.f: 139 of 194 cancers were judged inadequately assessed; missed biopsy or false-negative biopsy was the recurring cause.

audits.t: Audit of therapeutic interventions in inpatient children using two scores: are they evidence-based in developing countries?
audits.st: Level of evidence (Ellis score and Oxford Centre for Evidence Based Medicine levels)
audits.f: Ellis level I evidence in 21%, level II 73%, level III 6%; Oxford grades A 16%, B 8%, C 1%, D 75%.

audits.t: Management of children with cerebral malaria in Lagos - a medical audit.
audits.st: Standard management of cerebral malaria in children
audits.f: Critical information missing in 50-60% of records; appropriate IV quinine in 54 (94.7%); mannitol or dexamethasone given to 12 (21.1%); transfusion ordered in 60% though severe anaemia present in only 30%.

audits.t: Assessment of dizziness among older patients at a family practice clinic: a chart audit study.
audits.st: Quality indicators for dizziness assessment (onset, own words, medications, postural BP, mood, falls, syncope, diagnosis, referrals)
audits.f: Documentation of key quality indicators was sub-optimal (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Women who decline antenatal screening for HIV infection in the era of universal testing: results of an audit of uptake in three London hospitals.
audits.st: UK universal antenatal HIV screening policy, target 90% uptake
audits.f: 401 of 2,710 women (15%) declined an HIV test.

audits.t: An audit of first seizures presenting to an Accident and Emergency department.
audits.tp: First seizure clinic referral and follow-up
audits.st: Consensus recommendations for management of first seizure, including recommended time to specialist review
audits.f: 83% of patients discharged with a GP letter were lost to follow-up versus 20% referred directly to neurology clinic; median wait to neurology clinic 22 weeks, 18 weeks longer than recommended.

audits.t: Diagnosis of Chlamydia trachomatis in North Thames region 2003.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Previous audit of chlamydia tests used (figures not given).
audits.r2: Significant increase in the proportion of clinics using nucleic acid amplification tests and non-invasive testing.

audits.t: Treatment of Chlamydia trachomatis in North Thames region 2003.
audits.st: National guidelines for antibiotic treatment of chlamydia and test of cure
audits.f: Previous audit; figures not reported.
audits.r2: Significant increase in centres following national antibiotic prescribing guidelines and offering test of cure when indicated.

audits.t: Quality assurance and gastrointestinal endoscopy: an audit of 500 colonoscopic procedures.
audits.st: 62 colonoscopy process and outcome quality indicators with standard limits
audits.f: Within standards: caecal intubation 92%, inadequate preparation 24%, inappropriate procedures 9.7%, morbidity 0.4%, satisfaction 95.8%; outside standards: withdrawal time under 6 minutes 78%, forceps polyp removal 31%, polyps not recovered 12%.

audits.t: IAEA/WHO postal dose audits for radiotherapy hospitals in Eastern and South-Eastern Europe.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Results very good for most countries but a few struggle with basic dosimetry; only about 2/3 of participants had appropriate dosimetry equipment.

audits.t: Stroke units: research and reality. Results from the National Sentinel Audit of Stroke.
audits.st: Five key organisational characteristics of stroke units from research literature; National Service Framework for Older People target of a stroke unit in all hospitals by April 2004
audits.f: 73% of hospitals had a stroke unit but only 36% of admissions spent any time on one; 46% of stroke units had all five key characteristics, 26% had four and 28% three or fewer.

audits.t: Video-EEG recording: a four-year clinical audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: High rate of negative studies with no attacks recorded; about 50% of positive studies showed non-epileptic attacks.

audits.t: Audit of operating theatre time utilization in neurosurgery.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Actual operating time was only 56% of available time; mean interval between end of one procedure and start of the next 101 minutes.

audits.t: Audit of the management of victims of sexual assault in a city centre genitourinary medicine clinic.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 60 seen at a dedicated sexual assault clinic and 53 at the routine walk-in service; drug-facilitated rape reported in 20%.

audits.t: Setting up and auditing guideline- and evidence-based cardiac rehabilitation.
audits.st: Guideline-based individualised cardiac rehabilitation
audits.f: Individualised plans negotiated for all patients; the rehabilitation team achieved high delivery of agreed interventions, better than primary care.

audits.t: Quality of stroke care within a hospital: effects of a mobile stroke service.
audits.st: SCOPES stroke care quality indicators, with localised stroke units as the gold standard
audits.f: Historical controls before the mobile stroke service: severe complications 24%; median length of stay 18.5 days; 9% independent at discharge.
audits.r2: Significant improvements in DVT prophylaxis, incontinence management, premorbid function documentation, frequent neurological observations and early occupational therapy; severe complications 9% (P = 0.004); median stay 12.0 days (P = 0.003); 32% independent at discharge.

audits.t: Documentation of preoperative counselling for female sterilisation: a complete audit cycle.
audits.st: Auditable standards from published guidelines on counselling for female sterilisation
audits.f: Long-term alternatives 33%; irreversibility 94%; failure rate 96%; ectopic risk 48%; intended method 39%; operative risks 67%; continuing contraception 37%.
audits.r2: Proforma used in 62% (100% compliant when used); long-term alternatives 68%; irreversibility 78%; failure rate 78%; ectopic risk 66%; intended method 66%; operative risks 66%; continuing contraception 64%.

audits.t: Audit of diabetes mellitus in general practice.
audits.st: Eleven diabetes process and outcome criteria
audits.f: Inadequacies in nine of eleven criteria; diabetic register in 28.6% of clinics; reminder mechanism in 0%; blood sugar control 21.8%.
audits.c: Remedial measures implemented, including diabetic registers and reminder mechanisms.
audits.r2: Improvements in all criteria; all clinics had a diabetic register; 57.1% had a reminder mechanism; blood sugar control 31.3%.

audits.t: An audit of the management of acute asthma in accident and emergency.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Respiratory tract infections in Greenland: results of an audit project.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection
audits.st: Audit Project Odense (APO) method, compared with Danish practice
audits.f: Lung infections 26%, throat 22%, otitis media 16%; paraclinical tests in 32%; antibiotics in 47%, two-thirds penicillin V.

audits.t: Systematic follow-up after curative surgery for colorectal cancer in Norway: a population-based audit of effectiveness, costs, and compliance.
audits.st: Norwegian guidelines for follow-up after curative colorectal cancer surgery
audits.f: Follow-up per guidelines in 194 (62%); overall compliance 66%, lowest for colonoscopy (55%) and highest for liver ultrasonography (85%).

audits.t: An audit of drug prescribing practices of dentists.
audits.st: WHO prescribing guidelines
audits.f: Mean 2.03 drugs per prescription; 66% contained antimicrobials; 21% prescribed by generic name; 38% fixed dose combinations.

audits.t: Improving secondary prevention in coronary bypass patients: closing the audit loop.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean systolic BP 142.5 (19.2) mm Hg.
audits.c: Lists of CABG patients and first survey results sent to practices; Lothian Health recall project for cardiac patients (65 of 128 practices)
audits.r2: 918 questionnaires (92%) on 875 patients: 17% smoked, 86% took aspirin; mean systolic BP 139.4 (19.1) mm Hg.

audits.t: Audit of bloodborne virus prevention activity with drug users seen in primary care.
audits.tp: Bloodborne virus testing and hepatitis B immunisation in injecting drug users
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 4% (54/1278) completed hepatitis B immunisation; HCV tested 28% (354/1278), HBV 33% (416/1278), HIV 36% (454/1278); BBV discussion recorded in 41% (523/1278).
audits.c: Audit feedback, training and advice offered to practices (baseline audit only reported).

audits.t: Replacement of routine liver biopsy by procollagen III aminopeptide for monitoring patients with psoriasis receiving long-term methotrexate: a multicentre audit and health economic analysis.
audits.st: Manchester PIIINP monitoring protocol compared with American Academy of Dermatology guidelines (routine liver biopsy)
audits.f: Intervention (PIIINP) groups (n = 166) had 0.04 and 0.02 biopsies/patient/year versus 0.26 and 0.30 in control groups (n = 87), a sevenfold reduction.

audits.t: A regional audit of the use of COX-2 selective non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) in rheumatology clinics in the West Midlands, in relation to NICE guidelines.
audits.st: NICE 2001 guidance on COX-2 selective inhibitors for rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis
audits.f: 1164 (41%) taking NSAIDs; 37% of NSAID prescriptions appropriate; 92% of non-selective NSAID users had a GI risk factor (inappropriate) and 97% of COX-2 users were appropriately treated.

audits.t: Failure of Internet-based audit and feedback to improve quality of care delivered by primary care residents.
audits.st: National guidelines: HbA1c testing in previous 6 months for diabetes; beta-blocker or diuretic for hypertension
audits.f: Pre-intervention cohort: 76 diabetes and 329 hypertension patients (adherence figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Internet-based audit and feedback: residents given access to their practice profiles on a secure website.
audits.r2: No discernible effect on adherence to diabetes or hypertension guidelines.

audits.t: The consent and counselling of patients for cataract surgery: a prospective audit.
audits.st: Ideal informed consent (patient knowledge assessed by interview)
audits.f: 37% understood what a cataract was; 48% understood surgery; 48% thought surgery risk-free; mean anxiety VAS 2.89.
audits.c: Non-paternalistic consent approach with new patient consent forms
audits.r2: 39% understood a cataract; 28% understood surgery; 43% thought surgery risk-free; mean anxiety VAS 5.00.

audits.t: Availability, distribution and use of emergency obstetric care in northern Tanzania.
audits.st: UNICEF/UNFPA/WHO guidelines for emergency obstetric care (minimum 15% of expected deliveries in EmOC facilities)
audits.f: Basic EmOC units 1.6 per 500,000 and comprehensive units 4.6 per 500,000; 36% of expected deliveries in EmOC facilities.

audits.t: Referral patterns: an audit into referral practice among doctors in emergency medicine.
audits.tp: Emergency department referral to inpatient specialties
audits.st: Locally developed standard for safe referral from emergency medicine to inpatient specialties
audits.f: Many problems at referral were identified (no figures reported).
audits.c: Recommendations implemented at the base hospital (details not reported).

audits.t: Clinical audit of the use of fresh-frozen plasma and platelets in a tertiary teaching hospital and the impact of a new transfusion request form.
audits.st: NHMRC/ASBT Clinical Practice Guidelines for FFP and platelet transfusion
audits.f: More than 72% of FFP and 88% of platelets prescribed appropriately (figures reported across the audit).
audits.r2: Appropriate use further improved with the new request form, with satisfactory compliance (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: National audit of the sensitivity of double-contrast barium enema for colorectal carcinoma, using control charts For the Royal College of Radiologists Clinical Radiology Audit Sub-Committee.
audits.tp: Barium enema detection of colorectal cancer
audits.st: RCR targets: lesion demonstration >=95%; correct identification as carcinoma >=90%
audits.f: Mean demonstration rate 92.9% and diagnosis rate 85.9%, slightly below targets.

audits.t: Diabetes care provision and glycaemic control in Northern Ireland: a UK regional audit.
audits.st: National guidelines, including HbA1c below 7.5%
audits.f: Mean HbA1c 8.8% (SD 1.5%); 20% achieved HbA1c below 7.5%; 76% reviewed by a diabetes specialist nurse and 42% tested for microalbuminuria in the previous year.

audits.t: Are we good at thromboembolic disease prophylaxis - an audit of the use of risk assessment forms in emergency medical admissions.
audits.st: Thromboembolic Risk Factors Consensus Group recommendations
audits.f: Initial audit showed poor adherence to recommendations (no figures reported).
audits.c: Introduction of a VTE risk assessment form.
audits.r2: Repeated audits assessed form uptake and its effect on thromboprophylaxis; no figures in abstract.

audits.t: A survey and audit of the first 'Guides to Local Health Services' produced by Primary Care Trusts in England.
audits.st: Central guidance on structure and content of Guides to Local Health Services
audits.f: Most PCTs complied with central guidance on structure and content, but Guides lost clarity of purpose.

audits.t: A comparison of quality of care using Phaneuf's Nursing Audit.
audits.st: Phaneuf's Nursing Audit
audits.f: Professional Nursing Unit mean scores were 26.4% higher than those of general hospital wards.

audits.t: Blood transfusion prescribing in the ACT: an insight into clinical decision making.
audits.st: Transfusion appropriateness criteria
audits.f: Prescriber identifiable in 78% of transfusion episodes, mostly specialists; registrars and after-hours staff prescribed significantly fewer inappropriate transfusions.

audits.t: Management of suspected venous thromboembolism: the impact of a multifaceted intervention.
audits.tp: DVT diagnostic pathway (D-dimer and Wells score)
audits.st: Five local criteria for management of suspected VTE
audits.f: Diagnostic procedure >48 h in 27.2%; no anticoagulation at suspicion in 27.7%; inconclusive lung scan without further testing in 14%.
audits.c: Local guidelines for suspected pulmonary embolism formulated by a working group and implemented.

audits.t: Guideline recommendations for the management of patients admitted with acute stroke: implications of a local audit.
audits.st: New Zealand guideline for management of stroke
audits.f: Brain imaging 100% (86% within 48 hours); aspirin or documented contraindication within 48 hours 62%; swallowing and mobility assessment within 48 hours 88%; driving advice documented in only 19%.

audits.t: Audits in general practice by medical students.
audits.st: Target standards set for each audited indicator of care
audits.f: The majority of indicators audited did not meet target standards; 28 students completed audits (50% hypertension, 36% diabetes).

audits.t: Audit of antibiotic policies in the South East of England, 2004.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average policy age 12 months, 13 more than 2 years old; 38 (79%) made few or no cautionary points; only 10 used plain English for dosages.

audits.t: Management of preterm prelabour rupture of membranes: an audit. How do the results compare with clinical practice guidelines?
audits.tp: Preterm prelabour rupture of membranes management
audits.st: Royal Women's Hospital clinical practice guideline for preterm prelabour rupture of membranes
audits.f: All 56 women received antibiotics; over two-thirds had antibiotics changed; 10 given IV antibiotics without clear indication; 64% received steroids; 30% nifedipine tocolysis.

audits.t: Teaching and improving quality of care in a primary care internal medicine residency clinic.
audits.tp: Resident doctor engagement in quality improvement
audits.st: Patient-level diabetes quality of care measures (e.g. monofilament foot examination, baseline ECG, HbA1c, LDL, Pneumovax)
audits.f: Baseline medical record audits of residents' diabetic patients; figures not reported in abstract.
audits.c: Self-directed quality curriculum for 13 second-year residents: readings, weekly self-reflection with faculty, commitment to change survey and medical record audits; 13 third-year residents as comparison.
audits.r2: Intervention group patients significantly more likely to have monofilament foot examination and baseline ECG; significantly more improvement in HbA1c, LDL and Pneumovax than comparison group.

audits.t: Does dedicated pre-abortion contraception counselling help to improve post-abortion contraception uptake?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Initial audit figures not given in abstract.
audits.c: Dedicated, targeted contraception counselling at the pre-abortion assessment visit
audits.r2: 96% received post-abortion contraception; 73% chose less user-dependent methods (IUD, IUS, injectable, implant).

audits.t: Urine cytology: appropriate usage maximizes sensitivity and reduces cost.
audits.st: Departmental guidelines for requesting urine cytology
audits.f: 33% of requests inappropriate; cost of unnecessary samples £2418.
audits.c: Departmental request guidelines circulated with staff education

audits.t: Changing occupational therapy and physiotherapy practice through guidelines and audit in the United Kingdom.
audits.st: National Clinical Guidelines for Stroke occupational therapy and physiotherapy recommendations
audits.f: Low rates of compliance with national standards across all domains.

audits.t: Audit cycle of documentation in laser hair removal.
audits.st: Documentation of six criteria: consent, Fitzpatrick skin type, appropriate laser, appropriate fluence, patient satisfaction, objective assessment
audits.f: Median 100% for consent, laser and fluence; skin type 90%; patient satisfaction 67%; objective assessment 53% (772 treatments overall).
audits.r2: Nine clinics: significant improvement in patient satisfaction (OR 0.38, 95% CI 0.15-0.78, P=0.01) and objective assessment (OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.07-0.50, P=0.0003).

audits.t: Medication errors in intravenous drug preparation and administration: a multicentre audit in the UK, Germany and France.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Product not labelled or incorrectly labelled in 43%, 99% and 20% of doses (UK, Germany, France); wrong administration rate in 49%, 21% and 5%; at least one aseptic technique deviation in 100%, 58% and 19%.

audits.t: Improvement in neonatal intensive care in Northern Ireland through sharing of audit data.
audits.st: Agreed regional quality indicators on transfer patterns, thermoregulation, antenatal steroids and surfactant timing
audits.f: In utero transfers 26%; antenatal steroids 68%; normothermia on first admission (inborn) 66%; surfactant first dose within 1 hour 13%.
audits.c: Centralised data collection with annual confidential feedback and anonymised unit comparisons; regional consensus guidelines adopted locally.
audits.r2: In utero transfers 42%; antenatal steroids 82%; normothermia 71%; surfactant within 1 hour 66%.

audits.t: Audit of correction of high INR in an anticoagulation clinic.
audits.st: Target: safely correct INR above 4.5 to a maximum of 8.0 within 7 days
audits.f: Unacceptable variation in dosage change for high INR results not dosed by the computer programme.
audits.c: Development of a dosing protocol for INR up to 7.0 (to be tested); patients with higher results to be contacted.

audits.t: Clinical audit of linezolid use in a large teaching hospital.
audits.st: Hospital antibiotic committee indications for linezolid use, including prior infection specialist approval
audits.f: Overall compliance with local recommendations very good; only 34 of 77 had documented prior approval by an infection specialist.
audits.c: Mandatory linezolid order form to be completed by the prescriber (future evaluation planned).

audits.t: An audit of informed consent in gastroscopy: investigation of a hospital's informed consent procedure in endoscopy by assessing current practice.
audits.st: Hospital informed consent procedure for endoscopy (NHS consent form plus departmental leaflet)
audits.f: All 67 records had a signed NHS consent form; departmental leaflet present in only 31, patient-signed in 20; multiple choice test full marks in 17 of 28.

audits.t: Audit on the management of epididymo-orchitis by the Department of Urology in Edinburgh.
audits.st: National guidelines for management of epididymo-orchitis (chlamydia testing and appropriate treatment in men under 35)
audits.f: Patients were not routinely tested for chlamydia and most men under 35 were treated inappropriately with ciprofloxacin; diagnosis by ultrasound in 94%.
audits.c: All patients to be tested for chlamydia, men under 35 treated with ofloxacin, and partners treated by genitourinary medicine.

audits.t: Improving the quality of child health services: participatory action by providers.
audits.st: Over 65 quality indicators for child health services (IMCI-linked)
audits.f: Pre-intervention observations, facility audits and surveys; figures not reported.
audits.c: COPE (Client-Oriented, Provider-Efficient services) exercises four times over 15 months, supervisor training in quality management and minimal staff-selected training.
audits.r2: Intervention sites performed significantly better than controls on almost every indicator.

audits.t: Managing diabetes mellitus in patients with advanced cancer: a case note audit and guidelines.
audits.tp: Diabetes management at end of life
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Management and monitoring of diabetes was variable; 32 of 42 had blood sugar monitoring up to and including the day of death.
audits.c: Guidelines for managing diabetes in the palliative setting proposed.

audits.t: Prospective audit of the quality of ENT emergency clinic notes before and after introduction of a computerized template.
audits.st: Trust standard for note keeping
audits.f: Notes initially failed to meet the set standard.
audits.c: Introduction of a computerised template for data entry.
audits.r2: Notes accurate and contained relevant demographic data in more than 90% of cases.

audits.t: Improving end-of-life care: development and pilot-test of a clinical pathway.
audits.st: Chart audit tool indices: symptoms assessed, problematic symptoms, interventions consistent with PCAD pathway, consultations
audits.f: Baseline chart audit of patients who died; figures not reported.
audits.c: Palliative Care for Advanced Disease (PCAD) pathway: carepath, daily flowsheet and physician order sheet with standard symptom orders.
audits.r2: Mean symptoms assessed increased on all units (P < 0.001); problematic symptoms (P=0.014) and PCAD-consistent interventions (P=0.021) increased only on palliative care unit.

audits.t: Audit of general practitioner referrals to an acute surgical unit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 78 admissions considered inappropriate, 23 needing neither surgical admission nor opinion; estimated cost 25,000 pounds.

audits.t: Medical audit of mammography: a simplified alternative.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: PPV of mammography for nonpalpable lesions 20%; ROC area 0.84 to 0.89 across four radiologists.

audits.t: Clinical audit: adherence to sexually transmitted infection screening guidelines for men who have sex with men.
audits.tp: HIV and STI testing in men who have sex with men
audits.st: Australian guidelines for regular STI screening of MSM
audits.f: Testing rates before guideline development; figures not reported.
audits.c: Development of Australian STI screening guidelines for MSM.
audits.r2: 61% of MSM had all recommended tests within the past year; significant increase for most tests.

audits.t: Audit of offering HIV testing in the genitourinary medicine clinic in Aberystwyth in 2003.
audits.tp: HIV testing uptake in STI patients
audits.st: GU Medicine Good Clinical Care Standard 2: offering HIV testing
audits.f: 97.5% of new patients screened for STIs were offered HIV testing; uptake 70.3%.

audits.t: Indications and efficacy of continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) therapy in Type 1 diabetes mellitus: a clinical audit in a specialist service.
audits.tp: Insulin pump therapy in type 1 diabetes
audits.st: Current guidelines on indications and contraindications for continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion
audits.f: 25 of 40 started for reasons other than severe hypoglycaemia and 15 of 40 had contraindications; HbA1c fell from 9.6% to 8.3% (P = 0.011), severe hypoglycaemia from 6.45 to 0.34 per year and DKA from 1.83 to 0.27 per year.

audits.t: Safe storage of methadone in the home--an audit of the effectiveness of safety information giving.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Advice on safe storage recalled by 30% and on measuring by 28%; 126 (78%) given a measuring container on first visit, 24 (15%) on every visit; 95 (60.1%) had children living in or visiting the home

audits.t: Local audit of surgical pathology. 18 month's experience of peer review-based quality assessment in an English teaching hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Microscopic report unsatisfactory in 20 of 518 cases (3.9%), six of which could have affected management; in 13 of 18 months more than 10% of reports were delayed by pathologist reporting time.

audits.t: Growing up and moving on. A multicentre UK audit of the transfer of adolescents with juvenile idiopathic arthritis from paediatric to adult centred care.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean age at which independent clinic visit introduced 16.8 years (SD 1.06).
audits.r2: Improved documentation of transitional issues, educational needs, readiness and parental needs; independent visit introduced at 15.8 years (SD 1.46), p = 0.01; more preparatory adult clinic visits and transition plans.

audits.t: The management of Chlamydia trachomatis in genitourinary medicine clinics: a national audit in 2004.
audits.st: National outcome standards for chlamydia management
audits.f: 99% (1647) treated appropriately; 76% (1261) followed up, of whom 12% needed re-treatment; 71% (1186) managed appropriately within four weeks; 942 partners (0.56 per index case) managed within four weeks.

audits.t: The diabetes annual review as an educational tool: assessment and learning integrated with care, screening, and audit. The North Tyneside Diabetes Team.
audits.st: Standards set by the diabetes team; HbA1c target range per treatment group
audits.f: 34% of patients had HbA1c outside target range in year one.
audits.c: Integrated structured annual review with education and goal setting; team changed working practices and documentation and developed in-service training.
audits.r2: 46% outside HbA1c target in year two; 18% outside in both years; knowledge scores improved by 44%.

audits.t: Improving clinical practice in stroke through audit: results of three rounds of National Stroke Audit.
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians national stroke audit process standards
audits.f: 48% of hospitals had a stroke unit; 17% of patients spent most of their stay on a stroke unit.
audits.c: Repeated national audit rounds (specific changes not reported)
audits.r2: 77% of hospitals had a stroke unit; 29% spent most of their stay on a stroke unit; process standards showed no further median gain after 1999 (median change 0%).

audits.t: Implementing clinical protocols in oncology: quality gaps and the learning curve phenomenon.
audits.st: Internally developed clinical protocol quality indicators
audits.f: Retrospective audit of clinical practice; figures not reported.
audits.c: Internally developed clinical protocol applied prospectively with specific tools to increase conformance.
audits.r2: All indicators improved, many significantly; further improvement in the second part of the prospective study.

audits.t: Audit of the use of psoralen photochemotherapy (PUVA) and narrowband UVB phototherapy in the treatment of psoriasis.
audits.st: British Photodermatology Group PUVA guidelines and unit narrowband UVB guidelines
audits.f: Guidelines followed relatively closely; exceptions were one high cumulative PUVA exposure, failure to measure minimal phototoxic doses in some PUVA patients, and slightly prolonged referral delays.

audits.t: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV). An audit across the North Central London Critical Care Network (NCLCCN).
audits.tp: NIV in acute hypercapnic respiratory failure
audits.st: British Thoracic Society guideline on NIV in acute respiratory failure (2002) and NHS Modernisation Agency weaning and long term ventilation document (2002)
audits.f: Results discussed against BTS guidelines; figures not given in the abstract.

audits.t: An audit of the standard of response letters sent by hospital specialists to general dental practitioners following a referred patient's first appointment.
audits.st: Dentists' requirements for response letter content as determined in a previous questionnaire study
audits.f: Almost all departments achieved a minimum total score of 80%; over 90% across departments for all items except those relating to time. Most letters written within 18 days of the appointment.

audits.t: Pap smear taking in a general practice. Outcomes of a quality assurance audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Real time patient safety audits: improving safety every day.
audits.st: 36-item patient safety checklist (delays, equipment, diagnostics, information transfer, hospital policy)
audits.f: 338 errors detected; 27 (75%) of 36 items detected at least one error; ID band missing or misplaced n = 70, unlabelled bedside medication n = 31, inappropriate oximeter alarm n = 22.

audits.t: Oro-nasal fistula development and velopharyngeal insufficiency following primary cleft palate surgery--an audit of 148 children born between 1985 and 1997.
audits.tp: Cleft lip and palate care standards
audits.st: Comparison with Clinical Standards Advisory Group (CSAG) report and other recent studies
audits.f: Oro-nasal fistula requiring closure 4.7%; velopharyngeal insufficiency requiring pharyngoplasty 26.4%; hypernasality in 14.9% on CAPS assessment.

audits.t: Improvement in mammography interpretation skills in a community radiology practice after dedicated teaching courses: 2-year medical audit of 38,633 cases.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 121 cancers diagnosed; sensitivity 80%; PPV 32%.

audits.t: An audit of clinical resources available for the care of head and neck cancer patients in England.
audits.tp: Head and neck cancer care standards
audits.st: National targets for time to diagnosis and treatment
audits.f: MDT working in all centres but often not fully staffed (pathology, radiology, dietetics, speech therapy); clinically significant delays in complex investigations, ICU beds and oncology, especially radiotherapy.

audits.t: Medical audit in general practice. I: Effects on doctors' clinical behaviour for common childhood conditions. North of England Study of Standards and Performance in General Practice.
audits.tp: Management of common childhood conditions in general practice
audits.st: Clinical standards set by general practitioner trainer groups for five childhood conditions
audits.f: Figures not reported in abstract.
audits.c: Standard setting by trainer groups and different forms of audit feedback (standards, comparative data, own data, control).
audits.r2: Increased bronchodilators for acute cough, oral rehydration for vomiting; reduced antibiotics for cough and wheezy chest and tricyclics for bedwetting.

audits.t: Medical audit in general practice. II: Effects on health of patients with common childhood conditions. North of England Study of Standards and Performance in General Practice.
audits.tp: Management of common childhood conditions in general practice
audits.st: Clinical standards set by general practitioner trainer groups for five childhood conditions
audits.f: Recurrent wheezy chest: drug compliance 79%; breathlessness 3.8 days; wheeziness 4.7 days.
audits.c: Standard setting by trainer groups and different forms of audit feedback.
audits.r2: Drug compliance 93%; breathlessness 1.7 days; wheeziness 1.8 days.

audits.t: Computed tomography in abdominal trauma: an audit of usage and image quality.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 52% (64/122) unsatisfactory images, mainly inadequate IV contrast; 60% out of hours vs 45% in hours.
audits.c: New dedicated CT system for all abdominal work and technique guidelines issued to radiographers and radiologists

audits.t: Prospective multidisciplinary audit of obstetric general anaesthesia in a district general hospital.
audits.st: Royal College of Anaesthetists recommended general anaesthesia rate for caesarean section
audits.f: Potential serious shortfalls in communication and teamworking; insufficient information to assess appropriateness of indication for general anaesthesia.
audits.c: Recommendations to improve communication channels between labour ward personnel.

audits.t: Audit of nutritional guidelines for head and neck cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy.
audits.tp: Nutritional support in head and neck cancer
audits.st: Locally produced nutritional guidelines for head and neck cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy
audits.f: Previous audits used as comparison; figures not given in the abstract.
audits.c: Implementation of local nutritional guidelines, including prophylactic gastrostomy, and a dietitian present at the multidisciplinary head and neck clinic.
audits.r2: Fewer patients lost weight over radiotherapy and there were no admissions for feeding.

audits.t: Audit of the radiotherapy in the DBCG 82 b&c trials--a validation study of the 1,538 patients randomised to postmastectomy radiotherapy.
audits.st: DBCG radiotherapy guidelines for target coverage, dose and fractionation
audits.f: Megavoltage RT compliance for target coverage: axillary/periclavicular 88%, internal mammary 79%, chest wall 85%; dose and fractionation 96%.

audits.t: Sore throat in adults--does the introduction of a clinical scoring system improve the management of these patients in a secondary care setting?
audits.st: Guidelines using a clinical scoring system for sore throat
audits.f: Inappropriate antibiotic prescribing 44%; correct antibiotic 60%; supportive advice documented 67.8%.
audits.c: Proforma-based guidelines with clinical scoring system and staff education
audits.r2: Inappropriate prescribing 11%; correct antibiotic 100%; supportive advice 58%.

audits.t: Audit of outcome of super-accelerated hepatitis B vaccination schedule in a genitourinary medicine clinic.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B vaccination in sexual health clinics
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 61.5% completed three vaccinations.
audits.c: Introduction of a super-accelerated hepatitis B vaccination schedule
audits.r2: 72.4% completed three vaccinations; of 39 tested at about 12 weeks, 69.2% had some serological response and 48.7% a good response.

audits.t: Using quality improvement to address pain management practices in nursing homes.
audits.st: Pain quality indicators for assessment and treatment
audits.f: 8% of residents in pain had pain assessments; 31% received non-pharmacological treatment.
audits.c: Feedback on pain quality indicator data, pain management education and technical assistance with Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles.

audits.t: Advice given to patients with epistaxis by A&E doctors.
audits.st: All patients discharged from A&E with epistaxis given verbal and written advice
audits.f: Verbal advice 19%; written advice 2%; 11 (17%) re-attenders.
audits.c: Presentation to A&E doctors on epistaxis management and advice leaflets placed in the department

audits.t: An audit of study casts used to monitor tooth wear in general practice.
audits.st: Consultant advice to monitor tooth wear with study casts
audits.f: Replies from 60 dentists (87%) and 53 patients (75%); study casts taken reported by 23 dentists (38%) and 18 patients (34%).

audits.t: Internal quality audit and quality standards as a method of quality improvement at the Department of Ophthalmology, University Hospital.
audits.st: Hospital quality standards (ideal result 100%)
audits.f: Baseline figures not reported.
audits.c: Pilot quality programme with seven internal audit teams evaluating standards every three months.
