audits.t: Utility of urine drug screening: a clinical audit.
audits.st: International guidelines on urine drug screening in overdose (no target stated)
audits.f: Clinical utility identified in only 85 of 171 UDS; 61% of AEC requests had no clinical utility vs 24% from other specialties.

audits.t: Is the faculty of family planning and reproductive health care guidance on emergency contraception being followed in general practice? An audit in the West Midlands, UK.
audits.st: FFPRHC (RCOG) 2003 guidance on emergency contraception
audits.f: No evidence of future contraceptive needs being discussed in 40%; STIs discussed in 20 (2.8%); chlamydia tests in 15/718 (1.7%); IUD discussed in 10 (1.4%).

audits.t: Counselling of complications of termination of pregnancy within a single Trust setting.
audits.st: National guidelines on counselling about complications and sequelae before induced abortion
audits.f: Adequate counselling documented in 98% of nurse-led and 43% of consultant-led clinics.
audits.c: Integrated care pathway altered to list potential complications and sequelae
audits.r2: Adequate counselling 100% in nurse-led and 64% in consultant-led clinics.

audits.t: An audit of influenza and pneumococcal vaccination in rheumatology outpatients.
audits.tp: Vaccination uptake in immunosuppressed rheumatology patients
audits.st: Influenza and pneumococcal vaccination recommendations for patients on immunosuppressant DMARDs
audits.f: Fewer patients on major immunosuppressants were vaccinated against influenza than those with additional clinical risk factors (53% vs 93%).

audits.t: General practitioner notifications of gastroenteritis and food poisoning: cause for concern.
audits.st: Public Health (Infectious Diseases) Regulations 1988: all doctors must notify suspected gastrointestinal infection and food poisoning
audits.f: Considerable variation in GP reporting behaviour and timeliness of notification of suspected gastroenteritis and food poisoning.
audits.c: A series of local interventions to improve notification (not described in detail).
audits.r2: Notification rates and timeliness had not improved; they had deteriorated.

audits.t: Prospective peer-review audit of paediatric upper gastrointestinal endoscopy.
audits.tp: Paediatric upper GI endoscopy diagnostic yield
audits.st: Aim to reduce the rate of normal findings at diagnostic upper GI endoscopy (no target stated)
audits.f: Over 3 years, 90% of 1172 UGE were diagnostic, of which 48% were normal, 16% oesophagitis, 11% coeliac disease, 6% gastritis, 3% H. pylori, 1% peptic ulcer disease.
audits.c: After year 1 each endoscopist was appraised of their practice and strategies introduced to reduce normal UGE; monthly peer-review audit in years 2 and 3.
audits.r2: Peer-review audit significantly reduced normal findings in coeliac disease, RAP and overall (p value truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Intravenous fluid administration in elderly patients at a London hospital: a two-part audit encompassing ward-based fluid monitoring and prescribing practice by doctors.
audits.st: NPSA guidelines for fluid management in children, applied to elderly patients; NCEPOD
audits.f: Daily urea, creatinine and sodium monitored in 65.1% of patients on IV fluids; initial weight measured in one quarter; daily weight monitored in 9.4%.

audits.t: An audit of the quality of root canal treatments performed by undergraduate dental students on single-rooted teeth in Glasgow dental hospital and school.
audits.st: Predetermined radiographic criteria for acceptable root canal filling
audits.f: Of 100 teeth, 20 had voids and one was perforated; of the remaining 79, 80% (n=63) acceptable, 5% (n=4) under-filled and 15% (n=12) over-filled.

audits.t: Current management of acute coronary syndromes in Australia: observations from the acute coronary syndromes prospective audit.
audits.st: Guideline evidence-based therapies and invasive management for ACS
audits.f: Angiography use: STEMI 89%, high-risk NSTEACS 54%, intermediate-risk NSTEACS 34%; an evidence-practice gap was described.

audits.t: Inadequate analgesic prescription increases secondary post-tonsillectomy bleed rates: a completed audit loop.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Secondary haemorrhage rate 17.8% in waiting list initiative cases at the alternative provider vs 3.9% in the primary healthcare trust (p 0.1).

audits.t: Transfusion practice in coronary artery bypass surgery in Denmark: a multicenter audit.
audits.st: Guidelines for allogeneic transfusion (discharge haemoglobin >7 mmol/l taken as indicating inappropriate transfusion)
audits.f: Red cell transfusion rates ranged from 30.0% to 64.2%; 12.1-42.7% of transfused patients were discharged with haemoglobin >7 mmol/l, indicating inappropriate transfusion.

audits.t: Quality improvement programme for diabetes care in family practice settings in Dubai.
audits.st: Key clinical indicators for diabetes care (HbA1c <7%, LDL <100 mg/dL, blood pressure)
audits.f: HbA1c <7% in 20.6%; LDL cholesterol <100 mg/dL in 20.8%; mean systolic BP 135.3 mmHg.
audits.c: Quality improvement teams, clinical guidelines, information systems, diabetes nurse practitioners and a team approach
audits.r2: HbA1c <7% in 31.7%; LDL cholesterol <100 mg/dL in 33.6%; mean systolic BP 133.2 mmHg.

audits.t: Management of spontaneous pneumothorax compared to British Thoracic Society (BTS) 2003 guidelines: a district general hospital audit.
audits.st: British Thoracic Society 2003 spontaneous pneumothorax guidelines
audits.f: Deviation rate from BTS guidelines 26.9%.
audits.c: Junior doctor educational update on guidelines and audit results, and an online guideline hyperlink
audits.r2: Deviation rate 32.1%; persisting failures included no chest drain after failed aspiration and aspiration of symptomatic secondary pneumothorax.

audits.t: Audit on inpatient prescription writing guidelines.
audits.st: Trust guidelines on prescription writing
audits.f: Allergy information absent in 40% of drug cards.
audits.c: Refresher on the trust prescription writing guidelines after the initial survey.
audits.r2: Absence of allergy information improved slightly (figure not given).

audits.t: Evidence-based emergency medicine. Creating a system to facilitate translation of evidence into standardized clinical practice: a preliminary report.
audits.st: Departmental evidence-based guidelines and quality measures (e.g. asthma care)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Evidence-based guidelines with provider-specific peer-matched scorecards and feedback
audits.r2: For asthma, time to first nebuliser and time to disposition decreased, initial agent changed and documentation improved (no figures given).

audits.t: Audit of healthcare provision for UK prisoners with suspected epilepsy.
audits.st: NICE epilepsy guidelines
audits.f: 61.5% of diagnoses not made by specialists; 73.1% uncontrolled seizures; 19.2% had CT, none MRI; 53.8% with confirmed epilepsy had no review in 12 months; 63.2% needed AED change.

audits.t: An audit of the management of ectopic pregnancy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 19 (13%) women with ectopic pregnancy were sent home with an incorrect diagnosis; 8 recalled, 8 needed emergency admission and one died at home.

audits.t: UK national audit of sexual health care for people with HIV infection: clinic policies.
audits.tp: STI care pathways for people with HIV
audits.st: 100% of service providers able to document local care pathways for STIs in people with HIV
audits.f: Only 38 clinics (30%, regional range 0-60%) had written local care pathways; 73 (58%, 20-100%) had unwritten policies.

audits.t: Introduction of an early pregnancy assessment unit: audit on the first 6 months of service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 83.4% self-referred; all seen within 1 to 3 h; miscarriage managed surgically in 218/278 (78.4%) and conservatively or medically in 60/278 (21.6%); 5/13 (39%) ectopics managed laparoscopically.

audits.t: A 10-year retrospective audit of penile cancer management in the UK.
audits.st: BAUS National Cancer Registry data, NICE and European Association of Urology guidelines
audits.f: 61 (94%) had SCC (about 0.6 cases per 100 000 per year); 36 had conservative primary therapy; 5-year relapse-free survival after radiotherapy 63%; 5-year overall survival 71%.

audits.t: A repeat audit of spinal board usage in the emergency department.
audits.st: Spinal boards should be used for extrication and transport, with usual removal after the primary survey
audits.f: Previous audit: 5% removed patients immediately; 52% removed after senior log roll clearance; 43% left patients on boards until radiological clearance; 48% placed patients on boards after arrival.
audits.r2: 21% removed patients immediately; 58% removed after senior clinician clearance following log roll; 21% still left patients on boards routinely until radiological clearance; 45% placed patients on boards after arrival even if not on one pre-hospital.

audits.t: An audit of ward nurses' knowledge of sepsis.
audits.tp: Sepsis recognition and treatment on wards
audits.st: Standard sepsis definitions and Surviving Sepsis Campaign management guidelines
audits.f: Some ward nurses appeared to have poor knowledge of the signs and symptoms of sepsis, severe sepsis/septic shock and some aspects of initial management (no figures in abstract).
audits.c: Educational initiatives introduced to raise awareness of sepsis definitions and Surviving Sepsis guidelines.

audits.t: Review of ICU nutrition support practices: implementing the nurse-led enteral feeding algorithm.
audits.st: ICU nurse-led enteral feeding algorithm (feed type, target volume by body weight, dietetic referral criteria)
audits.f: 90% (n = 43) of dietetic referrals met referral criteria; absolute compliance (correct feed type and volume, correct prescription and accurate documented weight) was 2% (n = 1); 60% of patients were receiving the correct feed regimen.

audits.t: A criteria-based clinical audit on the case-management of children presenting with malaria at Mangochi District Hospital, Malawi.
audits.st: Criteria for diagnosis, medical treatment and nursing care of children with malaria
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of deaths less than a week after admission through an emergency department: how accurate was the ED diagnosis and were any deaths preventable?
audits.tp: Early deaths after emergency department attendance
audits.st: Local preventability criteria (no external standard)
audits.f: Of 3521 ED admissions, 95 (2.69%) died within 7 days; 78 (82.1%) appropriately diagnosed and managed; 17 (17.87%) had deficiencies; 3 (3.15%) definitely, 3 (3.15%) probably and 6 (6.31%) possibly preventable deaths.

audits.t: An interdistrict audit of vascular surgery.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 28% of initial assessment patients had an arteriogram, 9% were admitted immediately and 7% discharged to the GP; at follow-up main symptom cured in 38%, unchanged in 27%, worse in 5%.

audits.t: Improving correspondence to general practitioners regarding patients attending the ENT emergency clinic: a regional general practitioner survey and audit.
audits.st: All ENT emergency clinic patients should have a summary letter sent to their GP
audits.f: Only 7% of responding GPs had previously received regular correspondence from the clinic.
audits.r2: Letter sent to 100% of patients' GPs; 97% of GPs valued it (mean satisfaction 8.4/10); 86% would not prefer a dictated letter.

audits.t: Audit of elective paediatric clinic referrals from primary care February 2002-September 2006.
audits.st: Local protocols guiding primary care referral of common paediatric orthopaedic problems
audits.f: Few examples of inappropriate referrals; variations of normal development were the commonest complaint, with most discharged after the first consultation.

audits.t: The impact of a citywide audit with educational intervention on the care of patients with epilepsy.
audits.st: New GP Contract epilepsy quality indicators (from April 2004)
audits.f: Overall review rate 41%; documented remission rate 29%.
audits.c: Comprehensive template, individualised categorisation for each patient and a neurologist-led educational session
audits.r2: Review rate rose to 49% at 1 year and 63% at 2 years (p<0.0001); documented remission rose from 29% to 43% (p<0.0001); A&E admissions fell (p=0.0026).

audits.t: UK national audit of sexual health care for people with HIV infection: case-notes audit.
audits.tp: Sexual health screening in people with HIV
audits.st: National standards for sexual health care of people with HIV
audits.f: Sexual history documented around diagnosis in 69% (45-84%) and in prior 6 months in 34%; STI tests offered around diagnosis in 58% and prior 6 months in 28%; hepatitis B testing 98%, hepatitis C 91%; cervical cytology documented in 73% of eligible women.

audits.t: Successful blind placement of nasojejunal tubes in paediatric intensive care: impact of training and audit.
audits.st: Previously achieved blind bedside placement success of 96%
audits.f: Nasojejunal route used in 19%; placement success 94.5-95%.
audits.c: Training programme: one-to-one training of key nurses and supervised placement with senior nurse or dietitian.

audits.t: Introduction and audit of intravenous paracetamol at a tertiary paediatric teaching hospital.
audits.st: Restricted indications and dosing guideline for IV paracetamol
audits.f: 121 children and 5 neonates received 1216 doses; indications appropriate (97% nil oral, 41% vomiting); only 5 patients had incorrect dosing (3 prescription errors, 2 guideline deviations).

audits.t: Use of an electronic record audit to enhance mental health training for pediatric residents.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Audit measured detected mental health problems, screening instrument use and interventions/referrals (no figures given).
audits.c: Feedback to preceptors, curriculum changes and improved access to mental health referrals

audits.t: Delivery of preventive health services to Indigenous adults: response to a systems-oriented primary care quality improvement intervention.
audits.tp: Preventive care delivery in primary care
audits.st: Guideline-scheduled preventive services (measurements, investigations, lifestyle counselling, pneumococcal vaccination)
audits.f: Baseline counselling: diet 3%, physical activity 2%, smoking 2%, alcohol 2%.
audits.c: Two annual cycles of system assessment, feedback workshops, action planning and system changes
audits.r2: Counselling on diet 8% (P=0.018), physical activity 8% (P=0.006), smoking 11% (P=0.003), alcohol 10% (P=0.007); 4 of 12 services improved.

audits.t: The management of first episode genital herpes in genitourinary medicine clinics: a national audit in 2006.
audits.st: National guidelines for genital herpes management; target 100% for counselling, written information and syphilis testing
audits.f: No evidence of counselling in 243 (15%); 1355 (84%) screened for other STIs; syphilis serology in 72%.

audits.t: An audit on the management of pelvic inflammatory disease in the West Midlands, UK.
audits.tp: Outpatient management of pelvic inflammatory disease
audits.st: National PID management guidelines
audits.f: Ofloxacin-based regimen in 91 (65%); doxycycline plus metronidazole in 44 (32%) but cephalosporin added in only 3; partner notification in 101 (73%); 58 of 130 male contacts (45%) traced and 51 (39%) treated; standard not met for regimen choice or partners traced.

audits.t: Audit of patient experience of day-case inguinal hernia repair.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 10% of patients had poor understanding of postoperative complications; 38% had early postoperative pain.
audits.c: Patient information leaflets introduced and intraoperative and postoperative analgesia standardised, including wound infiltration of local anaesthetic at the end of surgery.
audits.r2: Early postoperative pain fell to 23% with wound infiltration of local anaesthetic.

audits.t: Treatment planning and delivery of involved field radiotherapy in advanced Hodgkin's disease: results from a questionnaire-based audit for the UK Stanford V regimen vs ABVD clinical trial quality assurance programme (ISRCTN 64141244).
audits.st: Trial quality assurance programme (no target stated)
audits.f: One-third plan with CT alone, one-third with simulator only; 11 centres calculate a dose distribution per patient; in vivo dosimetry in 7 centres; treatment verification in 24.

audits.t: An audit of the use of definitions of sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS).
audits.st: Use of a standard published SIDS definition
audits.f: 58% of reports did not specify a definition or used non-standard ones; 30% used the 1989 NICHD, 10% the 2004 San Diego and 2% the 1969 Seattle definition.

audits.t: Evidence-based medicine audit as a tool for improving emergency ophthalmology.
audits.st: Published evidence level (Medline, Cochrane) for each diagnosis-intervention pair
audits.f: 71% of interventions evidence based; 36% at evidence levels 1-3; 29% no or contrary evidence.
audits.r2: 82% evidence based (P=0.04); levels 1-3 in 60% (P=0.02); no or contrary evidence fell to 18% (P=0.04).

audits.t: Development and implementation of a medical oncology quality improvement tool for a regional community oncology network: the Fox Chase Cancer Center Partners initiative.
audits.st: NCCN-derived quality indicators; 20 charts per practice
audits.f: Stage II/III breast cancer: mean compliance per parameter 88%; 15 of 16 practices achieved mean compliance above 80%.
audits.c: Education and documentation tools provided to physicians and nurses

audits.t: Mammography rates for 20 community-based family practices in Ontario: a full practice audit.
audits.st: Mammogram every two years for women aged 50 to 69
audits.f: Two-year time-appropriate mammography rate 58.8% (range 25% to 76%); four practices reached 70% or more.

audits.t: Auditing and benchmarking of azithromycin utilization in primary care military clinics.
audits.st: Local guideline on indications for azithromycin
audits.f: Azithromycin appropriately chosen in 5.7%; unnecessary in 90.5%.
audits.c: Dissemination of local guideline on azithromycin indications

audits.t: Ambiguous abbreviations: an audit of abbreviations in paediatric note keeping.
audits.st: Trust Intranet Medical Dictionary (TID) and Mosby's Medical Dictionary (MMD)
audits.f: 25 handover sheets: 2286 abbreviations (221 different), 14% recognised by TID and 20% by MMD; 168 sets of notes: 3668 abbreviations (479 different), 15% TID and 17% MMD.

audits.t: Audits can improve neurosurgical practice--illustrated by endoscopic third ventriculostomy.
audits.st: ETV success rate (no formal standard; no consensus selection criteria at the time)
audits.f: 1-year ETV success rate 53%; review in August 2001 showed significantly lower success in some patient groups.
audits.c: Change in patient selection criteria for ETV after the audit
audits.r2: 1-year ETV success rate 65%, significantly higher than group 1.

audits.t: An audit of 24-hour creatinine clearance measurements at Tygerberg Hospital and comparison with prediction equations.
audits.st: Clinical guidelines recommending creatinine-based eGFR equations instead of routine 24-hour creatinine clearance
audits.f: Problems with urine collection or data supplied in one third of creatinine clearance requests, giving unreliable results.

audits.t: Airway management equipment in a metropolitan region: an audit.
audits.st: Difficult Airway Society (UK) and ASA difficult airway guidelines
audits.f: 18 of 42 sites had an airway container; equipment for unexpected difficult intubation deficient at all sites; half of containers with checklists had items missing; one third of dated items expired.

audits.t: The Cataract National Dataset electronic multi-centre audit of 55,567 operations: updating benchmark standards of care in the United Kingdom and internationally.
audits.st: Benchmark standards from the 1997-1998 UK National Cataract Survey
audits.f: Posterior capsule rupture and/or vitreous loss 1.92%; zonule dialysis 0.46%; retained lens fragments 0.18%; postoperative VA 6/12 or better in 91.0% (6/6 or better 45.9%).

audits.t: A quality audit of the service delivered by the NSW Neonatal and Paediatric Transport Service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Referring doctors (288): over 90% positive about communication; parents (152): over 98% found team helpful; receiving doctors (218): 93% thought referral appropriate, 98% advice carried out correctly, 90% needs reported accurately.

audits.t: An audit of the NICE self-harm guidelines at a local Accident and Emergency department in North Wales.
audits.tp: Self-harm care in the emergency department
audits.st: NICE 2004 self-harm guideline audit criteria (psychosocial assessment, staff training, patient satisfaction)
audits.f: Generally high standards of psychosocial assessment; ambulance involvement information often unclear; staff training questionnaire response 44% with wide variation between staff groups.

audits.t: Six year audit of cardiac arrests and medical emergency team calls in an Australian outer metropolitan teaching hospital.
audits.tp: Early warning score response and escalation
audits.st: Criteria for calling the medical emergency team; incidence of cardiac arrests
audits.f: Cardiac arrest incidence 2.4/1000 admissions; failure to call the team when criteria were met was a problem.
audits.c: Orientation programme for first year doctors, professional development course for medical registrars and liaison ICU nurse role
audits.r2: Cardiac arrest incidence 0.66/1000 admissions (24% decrease per year).

audits.t: Preventable deaths after head injury: a clinical audit of performance.
audits.st: TRISS predicted survival and peer review
audits.f: Mortality 33%; 18 (51%) of 35 deaths were unexpected by TRISS (Z = 5.74, P < 0.001); peer review judged 11 deaths preventable.

audits.t: Red cell transfusion for iron-deficiency anaemia: a retrospective audit at a tertiary hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 39.2% of iron-deficient patients were transfused; transfused patients were older (mean 73 vs 53 years).

audits.t: A clinical audit of neurosurgical bed usage.
audits.st: Inappropriate delay defined as an action taking more than 24 h from initiation to completion
audits.f: 482 of 1665 bed days (29%) due to delays; 92.5% of wasted days in emergency admissions; delays due to transfer back (46%), operative (26%), radiological (19%).

audits.t: An audit of perioperative cardiac arrest at Lagos University Teaching Hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 13 cardiac arrests in 2147 cases (6 per 1000); drug and defibrillator therapy were inadequate; immediate survival in 5 (38.46%).

audits.t: A comprehensive audit of nursing record keeping practice.
audits.st: Record keeping standards (not specified)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Audit recommendations and action plans with stakeholder involvement and senior nurse support.
audits.r2: Improving audit data reported (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: An audit of oxygen therapy on a respiratory ward.
audits.st: Oxygen should be prescribed like any other drug
audits.f: Only 5% of patients had an oxygen prescription; 14 issues with oxygen delivery.
audits.c: Education sessions on oxygen prescribing and oxygen therapy
audits.r2: 20% had a prescription (P=0.042); oxygen delivery issues fell to one.

audits.t: An audit of intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) in the prophylaxis of asymptomatic deep vein thrombosis (DVT).
audits.st: Existing baseline standard for IPC use in DVT prophylaxis (not detailed)
audits.f: Performance against the standard good: IPC is the perioperative DVT prophylaxis of choice and is used frequently on most patients.

audits.t: Uptake of influenza vaccination among children with diabetes--a re-audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Contact tracing in a regional sexual health clinic: audit outcomes and implications for sexually transmissible infection control.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Ratio of index cases to contacts known treated 1:0.71 and seen at clinic 1:0.26; total index cases to clients seen as contacts 1:0.52.

audits.t: Endoscopic 'cold steel' versus laser dacryocystorhinostomy: completing the audit cycle.
audits.st: External dacryocystorhinostomy by a consultant ophthalmologist as gold standard (success rate 94%); success defined as watering 'better' or 'cured'
audits.f: Laser-assisted endonasal dacryocystorhinostomy success rate 64%, significantly worse than external dacryocystorhinostomy.
audits.c: Changed technique of choice from laser-assisted to cold steel endonasal dacryocystorhinostomy.
audits.r2: Cold steel endonasal success rate 79% (45/57); no difference from external dacryocystorhinostomy (p = 0.55).

audits.t: Clinical outcome assessment in mammography: an audit of 7,506 screening and diagnostic mammography examinations.
audits.st: Performance benchmarks for screening mammography (BI-RADS)
audits.f: Recall rate 10.9%; screening sensitivity 100% and specificity 88%; screening cancer detection rate 6.1 per thousand; screening PPV1 4.9%.

audits.t: [Transfusion evaluation measured by a retrospective audit].
audits.st: Appropriate transfusion criteria
audits.f: Inappropriate transfusion in 25.8% of requests, 23.3% of units and 39.3% of patients.

audits.t: Quality improvement of diabetes care using flow sheets in family health practice.
audits.st: Canadian clinical practice guidelines for type 2 diabetes (9 quality indicators)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Diabetic flow sheet based on Canadian guidelines
audits.r2: Significant improvement in BMI, HbA1c, microalbuminuria, lipid profile, retinoscopy, foot examination and neuropathy examination indicators (figures not given).

audits.t: An audit on diabetes management in Asian patients treated by specialists: the Diabcare-Asia 1998 and 2003 studies.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean HbA1c approximately 8%; lipids well controlled but hypertension not.
audits.r2: Similar profile: mean HbA1c approximately 8%; about 71% on oral monotherapy and 24% on insulin.

audits.t: Application of quality audit tools to evaluate care quality received by terminal cancer patients admitted to a palliative care unit.
audits.st: Lai's modified support team assessment schedule (17 audit criteria scored 0-4)
audits.f: Average audit scores 10.05 at admission, 8.85 at week 1 and 8.49 at week 2.

audits.t: A multicentre audit of single-use surgical instruments (SUSI) for tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Postoperative haemorrhage rate well within acceptable range; Draffin rods, Boyle-Davis gag and bipolar diathermy forceps found poor quality and difficult to use.
audits.c: Manufacturer redesigned the criticised single-use instruments.
audits.r2: Haemorrhage rate within acceptable range; redesigned instruments judged as good as, or better than, re-usable instruments.

audits.t: The national inpatient medication chart: critical audit of design and performance at a tertiary hospital.
audits.st: Chart field completion criteria required by the WA Office of Safety and Quality in Health Care
audits.f: Average compliance with national inpatient medication chart fields 56% (95% CI 43%-67%).
audits.c: Introduction of the national inpatient medication chart replacing the previous hospital chart

audits.t: Audit of quality in a radiological department--a pilot study.
audits.st: 26-item quality score across request card, films, report and film packets with a predetermined acceptable range
audits.f: Several problem areas identified (no figures in abstract).
audits.c: Steps taken to improve items with scores outside the predetermined range.

audits.t: Suboptimal asthma care for immigrant children: results of an audit study.
audits.st: Review criteria derived from clinical asthma guidelines
audits.f: Ethnic differences in suboptimal care were not significant; 'other non-Western' children more often received suboptimal care.

audits.t: Analysis of blood transfusion predictors in patients undergoing elective oesophagectomy for cancer.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: The cohort was over-crossmatched; mean preoperative Hb 13.0 g/dl
audits.c: Maximum surgical blood-ordering schedule for oesophagectomy reduced to 2 units

audits.t: Audit of symptoms and prescribing in patients with the anorexia-cachexia syndrome.
audits.st: Evidence-based or best-practice standardised management strategies
audits.f: 119 active symptoms in 23 patients; median eight drugs prescribed; dry mouth in 21 (91%) and constipation in 12 (52%); many symptoms unmanaged by medication.

audits.t: Effect of standard treatment guidelines with or without prescription audit on prescribing for acute respiratory tract infection (ARI) and diarrhoea in some thana health complexes (THCs) of Bangladesh.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection
audits.st: Standard treatment guidelines for acute respiratory infection
audits.f: 38 of 60 health complexes did not comply with STG for ARI (unnecessary antibiotics in >50% of encounters); 26 prescribed antibiotics in >=72% of encounters.
audits.c: Standard treatment guidelines with prescription audit (group I) or guidelines alone (group II), with a control group
audits.r2: Antibiotic use fell by 23.7% of encounters with STG plus audit and 15.2% with STG alone; 15.2% and 6.9% after adjusting for control.

audits.t: [Audit of general hospitals and private surgical clinics in Israel].
audits.st: Ministry of Health checklists for 20 areas of activity
audits.f: Most general hospitals met required standards; standards lower in private surgical clinics.

audits.t: Use of antibiotics in a haematology ward--an audit.
audits.st: Departmental 2002 consensus guidelines for antibiotic use in febrile neutropenia (cefepime first line)
audits.f: Compliance with first-line agent 31% (31 of 100 episodes); valid clinical reasons existed in all non-compliant cases.

audits.t: Informed consent for vascular intervention: completing one audit loop.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Surgical consent forms signed by a consultant in 2 (4%).
audits.r2: Surgical consent forms signed by a consultant in 16 (32%) (p = 0.013).

audits.t: The North West Diabetic Pregnancy Audit: a practical system for multi-centre diabetic pregnancy audit.
audits.st: Regionally agreed standards (1999) in line with the St Vincent Declaration and Diabetes National Service Framework
audits.f: Funnel plots and tables highlight large differences between hospitals in booking and outcome measures (no figures in abstract).

audits.t: Implementation, reliability testing, and compliance monitoring of the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit in trauma patients.
audits.st: Daily delirium assessment with CAM-ICU by bedside nurses
audits.f: Nurses completed CAM-ICU in 84% of evaluations; agreement with expert kappa 0.77.
audits.c: Web-based teaching modules and group in-services before implementation

audits.t: Access to specialist gastroenterology care in Canada: the Practice Audit in Gastroenterology (PAGE) Wait Times Program.
audits.st: Clinically reasonable wait times for specialist care
audits.f: Median/75th percentile wait from referral to procedure 91/203 days, ranging from 42/84 days in Nova Scotia to 134/284 days in Alberta.

audits.t: Antipsychotics for BPSD: an audit of prescribing practice in a specialist psychiatric inpatient unit.
audits.st: Standards derived from two UK dementia guidelines
audits.f: Of 60 patients with dementia, 50 (83%) had BPSD and 28 (56%) of these received antipsychotics; results generally satisfactory.

audits.t: Introducing caesarean section audit in a regional teaching hospital in The Netherlands.
audits.st: Caesarean section necessity and rate
audits.f: 284 caesarean sections in 1216 deliveries (23.4%).
audits.c: Caesarean section audit introduced into daily report meetings
audits.r2: 228 caesarean sections in 1221 deliveries (18.7%), significantly lower; consensus on lack of necessity in 6.7%.

audits.t: Could clinical audit improve the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis in Cuba, Peru and Bolivia?
audits.st: WHO and national TB programme guidelines on use of microscopy, culture and radiology
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Introduction of clinical audit with at least two audit cycles over 2 years.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in 11 of 13 criteria in Cuba, 2 of 6 in Bolivia and 2 of 5 in Peru; 12 of 24 criteria reached the agreed standards.

audits.t: Audit of internal quality control practice and processes in the south-east of England and suggested regional standards.
audits.st: Best practice for internal quality control (no agreed standard before audit)
audits.f: Significant variability in IQC frequency, use of appropriate material, statistical processing and grades of staff involved.

audits.t: Written consent - a prospective audit of practices for ENT patients.
audits.st: Current recommendations that patients have time to consider surgery before giving written consent
audits.f: 15% of patients gave written consent on the day of their operation.
audits.c: Simple change in departmental consent policy.

audits.t: Impact of the Singapore National Asthma Program (SNAP) on preventor-reliever prescription ratio in polyclinics.
audits.st: Preventor-reliever prescription ratio as key performance indicator (Singapore National Asthma Program)
audits.f: Average preventor-reliever ratio 0.68.
audits.c: Audit and positive feedback on PR ratio plus local initiatives (chronic care models, multidisciplinary teams, decision support tools, self-management support, patient information system, community education)

audits.t: Quality improvement program in an emergency department.
audits.st: ED quality indicators (length of stay, left against medical advice, left without being seen, 48-hour returns, complaints)
audits.f: Unscheduled returns 2%; left against advice 1.5%; left without being seen 1.6%; complaints 1.3 per 1000 patients.
audits.c: Monthly data collection and analysis, data-driven process change and staff education in quality concepts
audits.r2: Unscheduled returns 1%; left against advice 1.2%; left without being seen 0.8%; complaints 0.25 per 1000 patients.

audits.t: An institutional quality improvement initiative for pain management for pediatric cancer inpatients.
audits.st: Institutional pain standard of care (pain assessment; effective treatment to <=4/10 within one hour)
audits.f: Compliance with pain assessment guidelines 77%.
audits.c: Institutional quality improvement initiative with repeated chart audits and comprehensive pain management guidelines
audits.r2: Compliance consistently greater than 90%; 66% of patients with significant pain treated effectively within one hour.

audits.t: An audit of the interval to treatment of anogenital Chlamydia trachomatis at Scottish genitourinary medicine clinics.
audits.st: National standard and local best practice target for interval to chlamydia treatment
audits.f: Three clinics treated 95% within two weeks and 10 clinics treated 95% within four weeks; all clinics treated 60% within four weeks.

audits.t: An audit of completeness of HIV clinical histories: before and after introduction of an HIV proforma.
audits.st: Twenty key variables considered essential in a first consultation HIV history
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Introduction of a structured HIV first consultation proforma
audits.r2: Significant improvement in 14 of 18 items for men and 14 of 20 items for women, with no deterioration in any variable.

audits.t: Section 5(2) MHA 1983: results of a three-year rapid cycle clinical audit.
audits.st: Appropriate use of section 5(2) Mental Health Act 1983 and review within 72 hours
audits.f: Section 5(4) before 5(2) in 2%.
audits.r2: 98% of uses appropriate overall; section 5(4) before 5(2) rose to 12%; review within 24 hours nearly doubled.

audits.t: Dosimetry quality audit of high energy photon beams in greek radiotherapy centers.
audits.st: IAEA TRS 398 dosimetry code of practice; tolerance limits and +/-3% dose deviation
audits.f: 28% of units exceeded the acceptance limit in at least one mechanical parameter; 61% of Co-60 units and 24% of linacs deviated beyond +/-3%.

audits.t: Continence care for older people in England and Wales: data from a national audit.
audits.tp: Continence assessment and care in older inpatients
audits.st: Policy requirement for integrated continence services
audits.f: Returns from 141/326 (43%) PCTs, 159/196 (81%) acute trusts and 29/309 (9%) care homes; integrated services reported by 58% of PCTs, 48% of hospitals and 74% of care homes.

audits.t: A prospective audit program to determine blood component transfusion appropriateness at a large university hospital: a 5-year experience.
audits.st: Predetermined institutional transfusion guidelines with mandatory prospective audit
audits.f: Fresh frozen plasma was the component most often denied or changed; denial rarely caused harm; components released against blood bank advice were mostly inappropriate.

audits.t: Palliative Care Integration Project (PCIP) quality improvement strategy evaluation.
audits.st: Documentation of pain in charts
audits.f: Pain documented in 24.5% of charts.
audits.c: Common assessment tools, collaborative care plans and symptom management guidelines across organisations.

audits.t: The use of Lee and co-workers' index to assist a risk adjusted audit of perioperative cardiac outcome.
audits.st: Lee revised cardiac risk index predicted event rates (1.3%, 3.6% and 9% for one, two and three or more risk factors)
audits.f: Observed cardiac event rates 0.8%, 6.7% and 2% for one, two and three or more risk factors.

audits.t: Adverse physiological events under anaesthesia and sedation: a pilot audit of electronic patient records.
audits.tp: Adverse events during anaesthesia and sedation
audits.st: In-house guidelines for colonoscopy sedation and desflurane anaesthesia
audits.f: Overall adverse event incidence 3.3% (138 events); colonoscopy adverse events 6.3%; laryngospasm/hypoxia with desflurane 1.3%.
audits.c: In-house guidelines for colonoscopy sedation and desflurane anaesthesia plus feedback on adverse event patterns to anaesthetic staff

audits.t: Falls education for practitioners: auditing a three-tier learning approach.
audits.st: NICE 2004 falls guideline recommendation on education and information-giving
audits.f: Staff are beginning to meet the NICE education recommendation (no figures in abstract).
audits.c: Local falls champions and a three-tier education approach.

audits.t: Prenatal Screening for HIV in Nova Scotia: Survey of Postpartum Women and Audit of Current Prenatal Screening Practices.
audits.st: Nova Scotia guideline: opt-in HIV screening with counselling and consent
audits.f: HIV screening rate 72% (rubella 95%, hepatitis B 89%, GBS 24%); 17% received pretest counselling and 3.8% post-test counselling.

audits.t: Challenges and choices: an audit of the management of nausea, vomiting and bowel obstruction in metastatic ovarian cancer.
audits.st: Best practice guidelines for nausea, vomiting and bowel obstruction
audits.f: Many areas were in line with evidence-based practice but use of non-pharmaceutical interventions was limited.

audits.t: Prospective audit of colonoscopy quality in Kent and Medway, UK.
audits.st: National standards: total colonoscopy in at least 90%; BSG sedation guidelines; more than 100 colonoscopies per year
audits.f: 39 of 55 colonoscopists (71%) achieved total colonoscopy in at least 90%; 12 (22%) in 80-89%; 4 (7%) in 79% or less; 79% sedated per BSG guidelines; 22 of 55 (40%) performed more than 100 colonoscopies.

audits.t: Tracking quality over time: what do pressure ulcer data show?
audits.st: Pressure ulcer prevalence and prevention measures as quality markers
audits.f: Pressure ulcer prevalence 23.9% (8.0% excluding non-blanchable erythema).
audits.c: Comprehensive quality improvement programme (details not stated)
audits.r2: Pressure ulcer prevalence 22.9% (12.0% excluding non-blanchable erythema).

audits.t: Management of suspected ectopic pregnancy: An audit from East Kent NHS Hospital Trust.
audits.st: RCOG ectopic pregnancy guidelines, local guidelines and NCEPOD recommendations
audits.f: 90.19% of procedures in working hours; 86.7% of non-sensitised Rhesus negative women received anti-D; 96% diagnosed within 96 h; betahCG available within 24 h in 80%.

audits.t: Infection control audit and potential sources of infection of a Nigerian eye unit.
audits.st: Infection control procedures and practices (pre-designed questionnaire)
audits.f: No post-operative infections in 207 procedures; deficiencies in hand drying and washing, steriliser training, undated packs, waste segregation and equipment disinfection.

audits.t: Audit on cardiovascular disease preventive care in general practice.
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk assessment in primary care
audits.st: Agreed criteria and standards for cardiovascular disease preventive care (ten indicators)
audits.f: Targets achieved in 3 of 10 indicators: blood pressure recording 92.4%, blood sugar screening 72.7%, latest BP ≤140/90 mmHg in hypertensives 71.3%. Other indicators ranged from 11.1% to 66.7% (hypertension and diabetes registers, smoking status, height and weight, lipid screening, glycaemic targets in diabetics).

audits.t: The management of renal failure in patients with liver disease. Experiences from a district general hospital.
audits.st: Published evidence-based management of hepatorenal syndrome
audits.f: All 11 patients with hepatorenal syndrome died.
audits.c: Evidence-based protocol for diagnosis and management of hepatorenal syndrome introduced.
audits.r2: Second group received more appropriate and aggressive therapy; 2 had renal function corrected and 1 was discharged.

audits.t: A significant reduction in paediatric post-tonsillectomy vomiting through audit.
audits.tp: Postoperative nausea and vomiting prevention in tonsillectomy
audits.st: Gold standard for postoperative vomiting (not specified)
audits.f: Postoperative vomiting 27%.

audits.t: Innovative approaches to increase deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis rate resulting in a decrease in hospital-acquired deep vein thrombosis at a tertiary-care teaching hospital.
audits.st: DVT prophylaxis guidelines
audits.f: DVT prophylaxis rate on the general medicine house-staff service 63%; 14 hospital-acquired DVTs (2.6 per 1000 discharges, 95% CI 1.5-4.4).
audits.c: Layered, multifaceted programme from November 2002: provider education, provider reminders with decision support, and audit with feedback.
audits.r2: DVT prophylaxis rate 96%; 1 hospital-acquired DVT (0.2 per 1000 discharges, 95% CI 0.0-1.1), P = .007.

audits.t: Epilepsy clinic services, NICE guidelines and patient satisfaction--an audit.
audits.st: NICE epilepsy audit criteria; parent satisfaction standards of Webb et al.
audits.f: Service achieved almost all key NICE targets.

audits.t: An audit of skeletal surveys for suspected non-accidental injury following publication of the British Society of Paediatric Radiology guidelines.
audits.tp: Skeletal survey quality in suspected physical abuse
audits.st: British Society of Paediatric Radiology guidelines: 20 recommended views per skeletal survey; technical quality score out of 11
audits.f: Mean 16.5 (range 5-20) of 20 recommended views covered per survey; 15% of surveys included all 20 views (previously 0% in an earlier study before the guideline). Mean technical score 9.7/11 (88%).

audits.t: Achieving changes in practice from national audit: national audit of the organization of services for falls and bone health in older people.
audits.tp: Falls and bone health service organisation
audits.st: Requirement to implement an integrated falls service for older people by April 2005
audits.f: Each site received a report of local results against the national picture with an organisational score and section scores; numbers not reported in abstract.
audits.c: Site reports with scoring, action planning workshops learning from high performers, and chief executives asked to provide action plans.

audits.t: Decreasing delays in urgent and expedited surgery in a university teaching hospital through audit and communication between peri-operative and surgical directorates.
audits.tp: Emergency theatre delays and NCEPOD timing
audits.st: NCEPOD guidelines for urgent surgery: fully staffed emergency theatre and after-midnight operating restricted to immediate life-, limb- or organ-threatening conditions; classification of delays developed from existing guidelines
audits.f: Urgent cases continued to be delayed unnecessarily; incidence of delays audited (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Audit results disseminated to the involved perioperative and surgical directorates.
audits.r2: Significant decrease in delays (p = 0.001), significant increase in surgeon availability (p = 0.001) and significant decrease in median waiting time for urgent surgery compared with the first cycle and a previous standard (p < 0.01).

audits.t: Paediatric day-case surgery: an audit of unplanned hospital admission Royal Hospital for Sick Children, Glasgow.
audits.tp: Unplanned overnight stay after day case surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Unplanned admission rate 3.7%.

audits.t: Evidence-based algorithms and the management of falls and syncope presenting to acute medical services.
audits.st: Evidence-based falls and syncope algorithms
audits.f: 10.6% admitted with falls and syncope; readmission 12%; mortality 12%.
audits.c: Evidence-based management algorithms for falls and syncope introduced.
audits.r2: 8.2% admitted with falls and syncope; readmission 0%; mortality 12%.

audits.t: Delivery of child health services in Indigenous communities: implications for the federal government's emergency intervention in the Northern Territory.
audits.st: Guideline-scheduled child health services (examinations, brief interventions, social enquiry, follow-up of identified problems)
audits.f: Documentation of specific clinical examinations 26%-80%; brief interventions or advice on health behaviour and risks 5%-36%; enquiry about social conditions 3%-11%.

audits.t: Children admitted with acute wheeze/asthma during November 1998-2005: a national UK audit.
audits.st: British Thoracic Society asthma guidelines
audits.f: In 1998, 7% of admitted children received bronchodilators exclusively by spacer and 24% were discharged with a written asthma plan.
audits.r2: By 2005, 44% received bronchodilators exclusively by spacer and 41% were discharged with a written asthma plan.

audits.t: An audit of pregnant women with severe mental illness referred during the first 2 years of a new perinatal mental health service.
audits.st: Recommendation that high-risk pregnant women are referred to perinatal mental health services with individualised care plans before delivery
audits.f: 39 women (87%) were seen for assessment; all women seen antenatally had care plans written addressing the high risk of postpartum relapse.

audits.t: Selecting appropriate recall intervals for patients in general dental practice--an audit project to categorize patients according to risk.
audits.st: NICE guidance on dental recall intervals based on risk from oral disease, with oral health assessment before recall categorisation
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: High-dose and combination antipsychotic prescribing in acute adult wards in the UK: the challenges posed by p.r.n. prescribing.
audits.st: Clinical guidelines: single antipsychotic at standard dose
audits.f: High-dose prescribing 36%; combined antipsychotic prescribing 43%.
audits.c: Feedback of benchmarked data and bespoke change interventions.

audits.t: Reperfusion times for ST elevation myocardial infarction: a prospective audit.
audits.st: Guidelines: first medical contact to thrombolysis within 30 minutes and to primary PCI within 90 minutes
audits.f: 41 (70.7%) received reperfusion; for thrombolysis median first contact to reperfusion 54 [37-72] minutes, with 12.0% (remainder of result truncated in abstract).
audits.c: Results conveyed to emergency room staff and a dedicated EKG machine placed in the ER.

audits.t: Quality audit of radiotherapy with EORTC mailed in water TL-dosimetry.
audits.st: Absorbed dose within acceptable variation (≤4%) of the stated 2 Gy
audits.f: 89% of 178 photon beams within acceptable levels (≤4%); mean ratio 1.012, SD 0.025.

audits.t: A system for the quality audit of treatment dose delivery in radiotherapy.
audits.st: Calculated delivered dose compared with prescribed dose; errors greater than 5% flagged
audits.f: 14 errors in excess of 5% discovered and corrected, approximately 0.5% of all plans checked.

audits.t: The use of section 5(2) of the Mental Health Act 1983: an audit.
audits.st: Mental Health Act 1983 Code of Practice standards for section 5(2)
audits.f: 75% of patients were assessed by the RMO within 48 hours; 41% regraded to informal, 32% placed on section 3 and 27% on section 2.

audits.t: An audit of basic record keeping standards: lessons learnt from the Royal College of Physicians.
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians inpatient record keeping standards 6 and 7
audits.f: Time recorded 19%; author name 60%; patient location 58%; most senior doctor present 68%.
audits.c: Adoption of RCP record keeping standards 6 and 7
audits.r2: Time recorded 82%; author name 89%; patient location 94%; most senior doctor present 89% (p<0.001).

audits.t: Safeguarding children: audit of staff knowledge.
audits.st: Working together to safeguard children (HM Government 2006)
audits.f: Knowledge about information sharing was good; only 41% of staff gave an acceptable response on parental responsibility.

audits.t: A prospective audit of regional anaesthesia failure in 5080 Caesarean sections.
audits.st: Royal College of Anaesthetists targets for conversion of regional to general anaesthesia: 1% for elective and 3% for emergency Caesarean section
audits.f: Conversion of regional to general anaesthesia 0.8% for elective and 4.9% for emergency Caesarean section; 20% in category 1 Caesarean section. 8% of women had general anaesthesia overall (primary plus conversion).

audits.t: Closing the audit loop is necessary to achieve compliance with evidence-based guidelines in the management of acute pancreatitis.
audits.st: Evidence-based acute pancreatitis guidelines (Pancreatitis Proforma)
audits.f: Diagnosis within 48 hours in 135/168 (80.4%).
audits.c: Evidence-based Pancreatitis Proforma and audit feedback to surgeons at 9 months.

audits.t: Audit of perioperative blood transfusion.
audits.st: Appropriate transfusion triggers (haemoglobin-based; Hb target of 8 gm% considered safe for patients with good cardiovascular reserve)
audits.f: Transfusion trigger was clinical anaemia on conjunctival examination in 40.7% and estimated blood loss >20% of blood volume in 29.3%; theatre Hb not measured in 45.9%; only 7.8% transfused on Hb criteria; 96 patients (7.8%) transfused for hypovolaemia.

audits.t: Developing evidence-based maternity care in Iran: a quality improvement study.
audits.st: Ten selected evidence-based clinical recommendations
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: New care model redesigned around evidence-based recommendations and women's needs and preferences.
audits.r2: Satisfaction improved on 16 of 20 items; compliance with guidelines improved and caesarean rates fell (figures not given).

audits.t: The management of interruptions to radiotherapy in head and neck cancer: an audit of the effectiveness of national guidelines.
audits.tp: Radiotherapy interruptions in head and neck cancer
audits.st: National guidelines on managing radiotherapy interruptions; completion within target; start within 4 weeks
audits.f: 62% of interrupted cases completed within 1 day of target; 41% started treatment within 4 weeks.
audits.c: New national guidelines on management of interruptions.
audits.r2: 397/631 (63%) had interruptions; 88% of interrupted cases completed within 1 day of target; 92% of all cases within 1 day and 95% within 2 days; 52% started within 4 weeks.

audits.t: [Evaluation of clinical practice: audit of prophylactic antibiotics in urology].
audits.st: CHU de Toulouse and SFAR prophylactic antibiotic guidelines (indication, antibiotic, timing, duration), CCLIN Ouest method
audits.f: Compliance with indication 88.1%; type of antibiotic 91.9%; time of administration 72.9%; duration excessive in one case; overall compliance 58.3%.

audits.t: Audit of antibiotic prescribing in two governmental teaching hospitals in Indonesia.
audits.st: Standardised criteria for appropriateness of antibiotic prescribing
audits.f: 84% received an antibiotic; only 21% of prescriptions definitely appropriate, 15% inappropriate in choice, dose or duration, 42% unnecessary; indication unclear in 32%; use 39 DDD/100 patient-days.

audits.t: How good are we at advising appropriate patients with glaucoma to inform the DVLA? A closed audit loop.
audits.st: Glaucoma patients with bilateral field defects should be advised to inform the DVLA
audits.f: Driving status documented in 9%; 20% of drivers with bilateral field defects advised to inform DVLA, with 11.4% documentation.
audits.c: 'Driver sticker' placed in notes at visual field testing.
audits.r2: Driving status documented in 99%; advice given and documented in 97% of drivers with bilateral field defects.

audits.t: A complete audit cycle of management of third/fourth degree perineal tears.
audits.st: RCOG Guideline No. 29
audits.f: Shortcomings in practice identified.
audits.c: Findings circulated and an operative proforma introduced.

audits.t: UK National Audit of chlamydial infection management in sexual health clinics. case notes audit: demography, diagnosis and treatment.
audits.st: UK National Guideline for chlamydial infection
audits.f: 93% of cases had genital NAATs; azithromycin used more than doxycycline (54% vs 37%); 93% of women with genital NAATs sampled from cervix or vulvovaginal area.

audits.t: UK National Audit of chlamydial infection management in sexual health clinics. case notes audit: information-giving, partner notification and follow-up.
audits.st: UK National Guideline for chlamydial infection
audits.f: Partner notification advice given to 91%, method documented in 92%; outcome not documented in about 25%; contacts screened per index 0.52 outside London and 0.29 in London, below guideline levels.

audits.t: UK National Audit of chlamydial infection management in sexual health clinics. clinic policies audit.
audits.st: UK National Guideline for chlamydial infection
audits.f: 92% had nucleic acid tests; 97% had leaflets, 30% lacking antibiotic and contraception information; about two-thirds followed recommended test of cure interval.

audits.t: The ENT emergency clinic: a prospective audit to improve effectiveness of an established service.
audits.st: No gold standard for service
audits.f: Mean waiting time 70 minutes.
audits.c: Verbal referral and appointment-based system introduced.

audits.t: Screening for the metabolic syndrome in community psychiatric patients prescribed antipsychotics: a quality improvement programme.
audits.st: Evidence-based standards for screening for the metabolic syndrome (blood pressure, obesity, glucose, lipids)
audits.f: Baseline screening rates for all four aspects (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Benchmarked data feedback and bespoke change interventions.
audits.r2: Screening for all four aspects increased significantly (35 teams).

audits.t: Dental audit (I): Exact criteria of dental records; results of a Phase-III study.
audits.st: 46 explicit criteria for completion of dental records
audits.f: No record free from errors; maximum 36 of 46 criteria fulfilled (mean 20.8); the standard of appropriate completion was met in only 12 criteria (75%).
audits.c: Remedial action proposed (Phase IV): new model of dental record with re-evaluation (Phase V) in a second paper.

audits.t: Quality improvement program to reduce the prevalence of pressure ulcers in an intensive care unit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline pressure ulcer prevalence 50%; appropriate allocation of pressure-relieving devices 75%.
audits.c: One-on-one clinical instruction to bedside nurses during skin surveys and display of pressure ulcer data in the clinical area.
audits.r2: Prevalence fell to 8%; appropriate allocation of pressure-relieving devices rose to 95% to 100%.

audits.t: Audit of the management of antiretroviral treatment-naïve HIV patients in Greater Manchester, UK.
audits.st: BHIVA 2005 guidelines
audits.f: Baseline laboratory tests in 96%, blood pressure in 53%, urinalysis in 25%; 2 NRTI plus NNRTI in 76%; 82% reviewed with bloods within five weeks.

audits.t: An audit of baseline HIV-1 genotypic resistance testing in a UK provincial city.
audits.st: BHIVA 2005 guidelines: baseline HIV-1 resistance testing
audits.f: 93% of newly diagnosed patients had a baseline genotypic resistance test.

audits.t: Cutaneous malignant melanoma: audit of the diagnostic process.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Patient delay over 3 months in at least 60%; delay after presentation in 21%; missed opportunity for earlier diagnosis in 12%.

audits.t: Non-attendance at the colorectal clinic: a prospective audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Did-not-attend rate 21% (males 28.6%, females 16.9%; P = 0.001).

audits.t: Closing the knowledge-performance gap: an audit of medical management for severe paediatric trauma in Flanders (Belgium).
audits.st: Available evidence and existing universal guidelines for early trauma care, judged by expert panel
audits.f: 264 defaults identified in 92 cases; 25.4% judged to affect outcome. Problems with cervical spine management (18/82), pCO2 and respiratory management (38/92), fluid management (29/92) and analgesia (27/89).

audits.t: Discussing withholding and withdrawing of life-sustaining medical treatment in paediatric inpatients: audit of current practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Life-sustaining treatment withdrawn or limited before death in 84%; family involvement documented in 98%; 83% of discussions first occurred on the day of death or in the preceding week.

audits.t: An audit of carotid endarterectomy for internal carotid artery disease at Dunedin Hospital.
audits.st: NASCET and ECST trial results; estimated upper limit of 5.5% for 30-day perioperative morbidity and mortality
audits.f: 30-day perioperative morbidity and mortality 4.3% (1.2% 7.4%), within the 5.5% upper limit.

audits.t: An audit of intravenous fluid prescribing and plasma electrolyte monitoring; a comparison with guidelines from the National Patient Safety Agency.
audits.st: National Patient Safety Agency guidance NPSA/2007/22 (March 2007) on intravenous fluids in children
audits.f: Hypotonic maintenance fluid prescribed for 94% before surgery and 92% after surgery; all maintenance volumes correctly calculated by weight; boluses isotonic on 128/129 occasions; no patient had daily plasma electrolytes while on i.v. fluids; 27 patients had recorded hyponatraemia.

audits.t: Value of emergency cardiac enzymes: audit in a coronary care unit.
audits.tp: Thrombolysis use in acute myocardial infarction
audits.st: Eligible patients should receive thrombolysis
audits.f: 73.7% of patients eligible for thrombolysis received it.
audits.c: Introduction of an emergency cardiac enzyme service.

audits.t: Audit of dental reports (II): first Phase-II study in a Spanish Faculty of Dentistry.
audits.st: 46 quality criteria for dental records; standard 75% completion per criterion
audits.f: Standard of 75% reached in 12 criteria.
audits.r2: Standard of 75% reached in 29 criteria; fulfilment improved in 41 criteria, significantly in 25.

audits.t: Audit of motor weakness and premature catheter dislodgement after epidural analgesia in major abdominal surgery.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Lower leg motor weakness 14.7%; premature catheter dislodgement 14.5%; weakness in more than half of patients with lumbar epidurals.
audits.c: Lumbar insertion abandoned in favour of thoracic placement only; catheters inserted deeper into the epidural space (5.2 vs 4.6 cm).
audits.r2: Motor weakness 5.1% (OR 0.35; 95% CI 0.16-0.74); premature dislodgement 5.7% (OR 0.35; 95% CI 0.17-0.72).

audits.t: Random safety audits in the neonatal unit.
audits.tp: Infection prevention and control in neonatal units
audits.st: 11 infection control and four routine care standards (random safety audits based on a Vermont-Oxford Network concept)
audits.f: Median compliance with infection control standards 70% (range 20%-100%).
audits.c: Random safety audits during the weekly grand round with immediate feedback.
audits.r2: Median compliance with infection control standards 95% (range 66%-100%).

audits.t: Improving the translation of research into primary care practice: results of a national quality improvement demonstration project.
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines across eight clinical areas: 31 process and 5 outcome quality measures, Summary Quality Index
audits.f: Baseline quality measures from EMRs of 847,073 patients (baseline values not reported in abstract).
audits.c: Practice performance reports (audit and feedback), site visits for academic detailing and participatory planning, and network meetings sharing best practice.
audits.r2: Yearly adjusted absolute improvement in Summary Quality Index 2.43% (95% CI 2.24%-2.63%); significant improvement in 29 of 36 measures, including all 5 outcome measures.

audits.t: A 12-month audit of laryngeal mask airway (LMA) use in a South Australian ambulance service.
audits.tp: Prehospital airway management in cardiac arrest
audits.st: Comparison with success rates of comparable groups
audits.f: Success after one or two attempts 65% (107/164); overall success 74% (121/164).

audits.t: Local audit of diagnostic surgical pathology as a tool for quality assurance.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Concordance 94.8% between original and review diagnoses; defects from missing request form demographics (22.8%), poor slide quality (18.4%) and typing errors (12.3%); turnaround 2-16 days (mean 6.2), 75.8% within 7 days.

audits.t: Urinary incontinence in stroke: results from the UK National Sentinel Audits of Stroke 1998-2004.
audits.st: National Sentinel Stroke Audit organisational and process standards for continence care
audits.f: Urinary incontinence rates changed little over the four audit cycles.

audits.t: Improving door-to-balloon times in primary percutaneous coronary intervention for acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction: the value of an audit-driven quality initiative.
audits.st: Door-to-balloon time for primary PCI (target not reported)
audits.f: Median door-to-balloon time 130.5 minutes.
audits.c: Guideline-based, institution-specific written protocol for triage and management of suspected STEMI, with process and workflow changes.

audits.t: Improved survival of diabetic foot ulcer patients 1995-2008: possible impact of aggressive cardiovascular risk management.
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk management in diabetic foot ulcer
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 5-year mortality 48.0% in cohort 1.
audits.c: Aggressive cardiovascular risk management policy introduced as standard practice in 2001

audits.t: A tale of two audits: statistical process control for improving diabetes care in primary care settings.
audits.st: Appropriateness of diabetes management against locally agreed guideline criteria
audits.f: Random samples of 30 files every two weeks plotted on p charts; mean non-conformities 5.0 at the start.
audits.c: Periodic process audits with statistical process control charts displayed for all staff (feedback).
audits.r2: Process-measure series: mean non-conformities fell from 5.0 to 1.4; proportion non-conforming fell by 10% within 3 months.

audits.t: The difficulty with audit of high grade cervical cytology in the absence of a national screening programme.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 74% of returned questionnaires contained insufficient data, with a 'don't know' result rate over 50%.

audits.t: Accuracy of diagnostic registers and management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: the Devon primary care audit.
audits.st: NICE COPD guidelines for diagnosis and treatment
audits.f: 580 had spirometry; COPD confirmed in 422 (73%); LAMA/SAMA and LABA under-prescribed (indicated but not received in 15-18%); inhaled steroids recommended in 17% but taken by 60%.

audits.t: An audit of diabetes care at 3 centres in Alexandria.
audits.st: Selected indicators for structure, process and outcome of diabetes care
audits.f: Structure poor (no appointment and recall system, limited laboratory resources, no educational material); process of care poor for 69.2% of patients; control poor for 49.2%; only 30.6% free of complications; appointment compliance about 80%.

audits.t: A district-wide anaesthetic audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Reducing pain in patients undergoing cardiac surgery after implementation of a quality improvement postoperative pain treatment program.
audits.st: Acute pain management algorithm; implementation complete when adherence to 2 of 3 process indicators reached at least 70% over 2 months
audits.f: Pain at rest VAS 2.7 +/- 1.4 cm; no pain or often without pain 11%; sleep disturbance 68%.
audits.c: Pain management algorithm implemented with training, pocket guidelines, regular audits and feedback.
audits.r2: Pain at rest VAS 2.2 +/- 1.4 cm (P = .008); no pain or often without pain 37% (P = .005); sleep disturbance 35% (P = .012).

audits.t: Audit of acute hypoglycaemia in children: re-audit of procedures for diagnosis.
audits.st: Hypopack protocol for investigation of unexplained hypoglycaemia
audits.f: Problems: samples taken during dextrose, incomplete history, insufficient and haemolysed samples, poor filing of reports.
audits.c: Request form redesigned, protocol updated and summative report introduced (April 2006).
audits.r2: 49% of patients were hypoglycaemic; more appropriately performed investigations.

audits.t: An audit of the quality of reports to Mental Health Review Tribunals.
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists framework of 18 criteria for tribunal reports
audits.f: Current practice assessed against the 18 criteria (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Guidelines circulated in the form of a template.
audits.r2: Significant improvements in quality of reports.

audits.t: Adjusting mammography--audit recommendations in a lower-incidence Taiwanese population.
audits.st: ACR BI-RADS medical audit recommendations, with adjusted targets for Taiwan (PPV1 1.7%-3.4%; cancer detection 0.7-3.4 per 1,000)
audits.f: 89 biopsies, 22 cancers; PPV1 3.1%, PPV2 16.2%, PPV3 24.7%; cancer detection 2.7 per 1,000; minimal cancer 50%; node-negative 71.4%; recall rate 8.5%.

audits.t: A criterion-based obstetric morbidity audit in southern Thailand.
audits.tp: Maternal death and severe morbidity review
audits.st: Criterion-based clinical audit standards for severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, obstructed labour and postpartum haemorrhage
audits.f: 515 severe morbid conditions in 486 women (13.2%). Substandard care: no record of respiratory rate and tendon reflex in severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia (35%); no antibiotic prophylaxis for obstructed labour (28%); no urine output record in postpartum haemorrhage (32%).

audits.t: Audit of blood transfusion in elective breast cancer surgery--do we need to group and save pre-operatively?
audits.st: Hospital blood ordering guidelines requiring group, screen and save for all elective breast cancer surgery
audits.f: 438 (88.1%) had group-and-save; only 19 (3.82%) received a transfusion: 9 (1.81%) of 447 mastectomy or wide local excision patients and 10 (20%) of 50 immediate reconstructions.

audits.t: Audit system on Quality of breast cancer diagnosis and Treatment (QT): results of quality indicators on screen-detected lesions in Italy for 2006 and preliminary results for 2007.
audits.st: Breast screening quality indicators and recommendations
audits.f: Overall good quality; preoperative diagnosis reached acceptable target with regional variation; sentinel node used in over 70% of invasive cancers.

audits.t: Effectiveness of home detoxification: a clinical audit.
audits.st: Suitability criteria for home detoxification
audits.f: Of 154 referrals, 59 commenced home detoxification and 95 did not; 96.6% of those who commenced completed the programme.

audits.t: A criterion based audit of the management of obstructed labour in Malawi.
audits.st: Local standards based on Malawi Ministry of Health guidelines and WHO manuals
audits.f: Bladder drained 70.5%; broad-spectrum antibiotics 72.7%; caesarean within 1 hour or delivery within 2 hours of diagnosis 38.6%; observation chart maintained 45.5%.
audits.c: Gaps discussed with staff; recommendations made and implemented.
audits.r2: Bladder drained 90.2% (P = 0.022); antibiotics 90.2% (P = 0.039); caesarean within 1 hour or delivery within 2 hours 61.0% (P = 0.023); observation chart 61.0%.

audits.t: Using criteria-based audit to improve the management of postpartum haemorrhage in resource limited countries: a case study of Malawi.
audits.st: Standards for PPH management based on WHO manuals
audits.f: Typing and cross-match 65.0%; haematocrit or haemoglobin established 67.5%; fluid intake/output chart 0.0%.
audits.c: Audit results presented to providers, who made and implemented recommendations.
audits.r2: Typing and cross-match 84.4% (P = 0.034); haematocrit or haemoglobin 86.7% (P = 0.029); fluid chart 33.3%.

audits.t: Audit of diagnostic accuracy of FNA cytology specimens taken by the histopathologist in a symptomatic breast clinic.
audits.tp: Breast fine needle aspiration cytology accuracy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: FNA complete sensitivity 95.7%, specificity 100%; combined sensitivity with mammography and clinical assessment 99.7%.

audits.t: Improving the quality of surgical pathology reports for breast cancer: a centralized audit with feedback.
audits.st: 7 diagnostic elements chosen by a pathologist committee as essential in the surgical pathology report
audits.f: Overall conformity 85.0% (51 hospitals).
audits.c: Centralised surveillance with feedback of results to hospitals.

audits.t: Implementing online medication reconciliation at a large academic medical center.
audits.st: Completion of admission and discharge medication reconciliation
audits.f: Compliance 20% of patients.
audits.c: Online medication reconciliation made mandatory at admission with an EHR blocking function (April 2007), then mandatory discharge reconciliation (November 2007).

audits.t: A data collection system to audit post-newborn hearing surveillance programme: problems and possibilities.
audits.st: Locally endorsed benchmark of 80% minimum coverage

audits.t: Effect of a vascular access nurse coordinator to reduce central venous catheter use in incident hemodialysis patients: a quality improvement report.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 56% of patients started haemodialysis with an AVF (earlier audit showed less than 50%).
audits.c: Vascular access nurse coordinator and an algorithm to prioritise access surgery on the waiting list.
audits.r2: 75% started with an AVF (P = 0.007); adjusted OR 2.85; catheter-days 2,833 vs 4,685.

audits.t: Audit of provincial gastroenterology services in the Western Cape.
audits.st: Internationally accepted standards for endoscope maintenance, disinfection and staffing
audits.f: 89 endoscopes (mean age 6.1 years); 26,434 procedures; mean delay to gastroscopy 9.25 weeks and colonoscopy 8 weeks; most units did not meet international standards for maintenance and disinfection; only 2 hospitals employed fully trained nurses.

audits.t: Criteria-based audit to improve a district referral system in Malawi: a pilot study.
audits.st: Prior established standards for optimal referral of obstetric emergencies (7 standards)
audits.f: Adequate resuscitation before referral 33.3%; ambulance delay under 2 hours 42.8%; clinician attends within 30 minutes 30.8%; feedback to referring centre 1.7%
audits.c: Recommendations made and implemented (details not stated)
audits.r2: Adequate resuscitation 88.7% (p = 0.001); ambulance delay under 2 hours 88.3% (p = 0.014); clinician within 30 minutes 92.6% (p = 0.001); feedback 91.9%

audits.t: An infective endocarditis audit illustrates why dental guidelines in general need to be kept clear, simple and unambiguous.
audits.st: British Cardiac Society and Royal College of Physicians 2004 infective endocarditis prophylaxis guidelines; standards agreed at a regional audit meeting
audits.f: Significant deficiencies in knowledge of which dental procedures did or did not need antibiotic prophylaxis (14 consultants and 9 trainees).
audits.c: Survey results discussed at a regional audit meeting and standards agreed.
audits.r2: Knowledge improved to a variable extent (13 consultants and 8 trainees), with persistent confusion about multiple conflicting guidelines.

audits.t: Reducing the rate of primary caesarean sections--an audit.
audits.st: Universally acceptable labour management standards
audits.f: Primary emergency caesarean section rate 16%.

audits.t: An audit of dentine hypersensitivity treatments in six general dental practices in Scotland.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Four agents routinely used (Duraphat, Duraphat and Sensodyne, Sensodyne, Seal and Protect); all produced statistically significant improvement (details truncated in abstract).
audits.c: The most successful treatment (Seal and Protect) was adopted by all participating dentists.
audits.r2: Seal and Protect was found to be reliable and predictable when used by all dentists (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Effect of audit and feedback on the availability, utilisation and quality of emergency obstetric care in three districts in Malawi.
audits.st: Criterion-based clinical audit of emergency obstetric care
audits.f: Baseline emergency obstetric care availability, utilisation and quality (details not given in abstract).
audits.c: Facility-based maternal death reviews and criterion-based clinical audit with feedback introduced in 2006.
audits.r2: Number of comprehensive and basic EmOC facilities did not change over 3 years (p for trend=1.000); institutional delivery rate increased overall over 3 years.

audits.t: An educational and audit tool to reduce prescribing error in intensive care.
audits.st: Correct prescribing (error-free prescriptions)
audits.f: Pretraining prescriptions with errors: 25%, 19% (one missing data point) across 3-month cycles.
audits.c: Prescriber education in tutorials and ward-based teaching with feedback of individual and anonymised peer error rates, in 3-monthly cycles for each new trainee group.
audits.r2: Final audit after 6 weeks: prescriptions with errors 7%, 3%, 5% across cycles.

audits.t: Exposure reduction through quality assurance for diagnostic x-ray procedures.
audits.tp: Diagnostic reference levels for radiation dose
audits.st: New Jersey regulation 'Quality Assurance Programs for Medical Diagnostic X-ray Installations' (quality control tests, frequencies and standards)
audits.f: Traditional machine-parameter inspections (baseline values not reported).
audits.c: Outcome-based inspection of image quality and entrance skin exposure, credentialing of medical physicists and a mandatory facility quality assurance programme (regulation adopted 16 January 2001).
audits.r2: Entrance skin exposure reduced by 34% for lumbar spine, 46% for chest and 66% for foot x-rays; image quality improved by 22%.

audits.t: An audit of compliance with the sepsis resuscitation care bundle in patients admitted to A&E with severe sepsis or septic shock.
audits.st: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 6-hour resuscitation care bundle
audits.f: Overall compliance with the 6-hour bundle 19%; arterial lactate done 100% of the time; only just over half received an appropriate fluid challenge; antibiotic administration very slow.

audits.t: Titanium clip placement to allow accurate tumour bed localisation following breast conserving surgery: audit on behalf of the IMPORT Trial Management Group.
audits.tp: Tumour bed clip placement after breast conserving surgery
audits.st: 5/6 pairs of clips identified on RT planning CT - 100%; possible clip migration: 50%
audits.f: Five or six pairs of clips identified in all 30 cases (100%); no evidence of clip migration. Tumour bed identifiable by seroma alone in only 8/30 (27%); clips essential in 22/30 (73%).

audits.t: Systematic services audit of consecutive suicides in New Brunswick: the case for coordinating specialist mental health and addiction services.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: More than half had contact with a mental health specialist in the last year but under 5% with addiction services; in one-third, service gaps called for better coordination of mental health and addiction services.

audits.t: Pediatric urodynamics: baseline audit and effect on management.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Successful videocystometry in 39 (81%); 97% of written reports contained adequate information. Of 33 returned questionnaires (85%), 30 (91%) said the result directly influenced management.

audits.t: Audit of oxygen use in emergency ambulances and in a hospital emergency department.
audits.st: Joint Royal Colleges Ambulance Liaison Committee (JRCALC) guidance on oxygen use
audits.f: SpO2 recorded for 90% of patients (remainder of results truncated in abstract).

audits.t: MEASURE IT, IMPROVE IT: the Safer Patients Initiative and quality improvement in subcutaneous insulin therapy for hospital in-patients.
audits.st: Evidence-based care cluster for subcutaneous insulin therapy
audits.f: Baseline: patient identification 97%; insulin device identification 11%; insulin administration 75%; hypoglycaemic control 85%.
audits.c: New insulin prescribing chart based on an evidence-based care cluster, refined through PDSA cycles, with run charts fed back to staff
audits.r2: Patient identification 100%; insulin device identification 100%; insulin administration 95%; hypoglycaemic control 94%.

audits.t: The impact of a GP clinical audit on the provision of smoking cessation advice.
audits.tp: Smoking status documentation and cessation support
audits.st: Evidence-based smoking cessation management practices
audits.f: Baseline GP self-audit of smoking cessation management (figures not given).
audits.c: 2.5-hour education session about GP management of smoking cessation.
audits.r2: Significant increases in evidence-based cessation practices; 57% of 28 GPs said they had changed their approach.

audits.t: An audit of the first year of screening for depression in patients with diabetes and ischaemic heart disease under the Quality and Outcomes Framework.
audits.st: Quality and Outcomes Framework (2006) depression screening in patients with diabetes and ischaemic heart disease
audits.f: 365 of 435 (84%) screened; only 3 (1%) of those not already depressed screened positive, none diagnosed with depression.

audits.t: Copying letters to children and parents: audit and survey of nurses' views.
audits.st: Department of Health 'copying letters' initiative
audits.f: 70% of letters from medical staff copied; community children's nurses copied 19%.
audits.c: Implementation of the national copying-letters initiative.
audits.r2: 74% of medical letters copied; community children's nurses copied 47%.
