audits.t: Audit of referrals for cataract extraction: are they appropriate?
audits.st: Agreement of community referral data with hospital ophthalmic opinion at first outpatient assessment
audits.f: 23 (76.7%) of patients referred with cataract were listed for surgery; 86% (n = 7) of those not listed were not listed for lifestyle reasons; no association between lifestyle compromise on the referral and listing (P = 0.62).

audits.t: Use of antipsychotic medications for the management of delirium: an audit of current practice in the acute care setting.
audits.st: Best practice recommendations for pharmacological management of delirium (baseline before new Australian guidelines)
audits.f: Antipsychotics used for most patients with severe behavioural or emotional disturbance; less than a quarter started on a low dose; very few reviewed regularly; prescribing and documentation of management plans varied.

audits.t: Audit of laboratory diagnostic methods for syphilis in England and Wales.
audits.st: Health Protection Agency standard operating procedure for serological diagnosis of syphilis
audits.f: Response rate 76%; EIA performed by 94%, TPPA/TPHA 34%, RPR/VDRL 41%, EIA IgM 10%; 57% performed a single screening assay; negative results within 1 week in 84%.

audits.t: Suprapubic catheter insertion is an outpatient procedure: cost savings resultant on closing an audit loop.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 66 local SPC insertions (49 elective, 17 emergency); median stay 3.5 (1-85) days. Regionally 480 inserted in theatre: 52% elective inpatient, 11% day case, 37% emergency.
audits.c: New outpatient SPC clinic using a new kit and Seldinger technique.
audits.r2: 50 of 54 patients had SPC inserted successfully in clinic; no major complications.

audits.t: An audit of transfers for neonatal surgical care in England in 2007.
audits.st: National Audit Office recommended maximum of 5% of transfers out of network
audits.f: 91 infants (18.8%) were transferred out of network or to a more distant centre than appropriate, compared with 3.6% for all network patients.

audits.t: Urinary incontinence management in women: audit in general practice.
audits.st: NICE guideline on urinary incontinence
audits.f: Gynaecological examination in 51%; urine dipstick in 40%; follow-up in 34% of 65 women with newly reported incontinence.
audits.c: Results fed back to GPs in a feedback session.

audits.t: Audit in general practice by a receptionist: a feasibility study.
audits.st: Practice-set goals for immunisation, abnormal smear follow-up, blood pressure and smoking recording, over-75 screening, diabetes and serious mental illness care, antenatal care, workload and appointment availability
audits.f: The receptionist audited all these tasks in four hours a week; attainment figures not given in abstract.

audits.t: Prevention of venous thromboembolism: improving practice in surgical patients.
audits.st: Local guidelines derived from American College of Chest Physicians (ACCP) criteria for VTE prophylaxis
audits.f: Only 19/51 (37%) received appropriate VTE prophylaxis; 18/29 high risk and 4/10 medium risk patients were not adequately protected.
audits.c: VTE prevention protocol with risk assessment and decision support nested within a new clerking proforma for acute surgical admissions.

audits.t: An audit of cancer diagnosis in a Canadian children's hospital: Quality, timing and efficiency.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 10 (19%) had an outpatient diagnostic procedure; 50% of 117 inpatient procedures within working hours; 31% needed two or more general anaesthetics; mean lag to biopsy 2.6 days and to diagnosis 1.2 days.

audits.t: Audit of quality of perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis.
audits.st: Appropriate perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis (indication, agent, timing, duration under 24 h)
audits.f: 331 of 391 (84.7%) received prophylaxis; not indicated in 15.1% of those given it; only 18.4% lasted less than 24 h; timing inappropriate in 135 (40.8%); all steps correct in only 44 (13.3%).

audits.t: Surveillance colonoscopies for colorectal polyps--too often, too many! An Audit at a Large District General Hospital.
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for adenoma surveillance
audits.f: Guidelines followed in 16% (4/25).
audits.c: BSG guidelines printed, laminated and displayed in colorectal clinics.

audits.t: [Clinical audit on the use of expensive systemic antifungals in the Besançon University Hospital].
audits.st: Local antifungal prescribing guidelines (2003, updated 2005 and 2006): indication, absence of better alternative, dosage, loading dose and timing
audits.f: Overall conformity 54%; therapy justified in 113 prescriptions (96%); a better alternative existed in 30%; dosage correct in 92% and loading dose in 80%.

audits.t: Children and young people with diabetes in Yorkshire: a population-based clinical audit of patient data 2005/2006.
audits.st: NICE-recommended HbA1c target level
audits.f: An HbA1c measure was recorded for 91.6% of patients (proportion meeting target truncated in abstract).

audits.t: An audit of letters of referral to a prosthodontic department in a dental teaching hospital.
audits.st: Five criteria: dental history, medical history, teeth present, diagnosis, treatment plan
audits.f: 8% of letters met all five criteria; 11% met none.
audits.c: Letters sent to referring practitioners requesting better information.
audits.r2: 9% met all five criteria; 15% met none.

audits.t: Automated versus manual audit in the emergency department.
audits.tp: Automated versus manual clinical audit methods
audits.st: 16 clinical indicators for croup, asthma, bronchiolitis, head injury and gastroenteritis
audits.f: Manual audit showed overall agreement with clinical indicators of 73.5%, versus 90.6% from automated TELEform data (available for only 24 patients), an overestimate of 17%.

audits.t: Quality improvement in radiography in a neonatal intensive care unit.
audits.st: Standards defined a priori for radiographic technique and essential clinical information on X-ray requisitions
audits.f: Baseline review of all neonatal X-rays and requisitions identified areas of suboptimal image quality and documentation (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Brief educational sessions and printed pamphlets targeting suboptimal areas, delivered jointly by radiology and neonatology staff.
audits.r2: Improvements in requisition completion and image quality, including legibility (P = 0.019) and completeness of medical history.

audits.t: [In-hospital stroke care in Catalonia [Spain]. Results of the "First Clinical Audit of Stroke. Catalonia, 2005/2006"].
audits.st: Indicators from the stroke clinical practice guideline (six dimensions of care)
audits.f: Compliance: medical records 78.5%; initial interventions 92.4%; neurological assessment 38.3%; assessment of rehabilitation needs 44.9%; prevention and management of complications 68.4%; initial preventive measures 78.9%.

audits.t: An audit of ambulatory laparoscopic cholecystectomy in a Singapore institution: are we ready for day-case laparoscopic cholecystectomy?
audits.st: Proposed same-day discharge criteria (minimal pain, tolerating feeds, independent walking, spontaneous voiding after 6-8 hours)
audits.f: 84% of patients listed for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy were admitted to the 23-hour ward; 66 admitted as inpatients (41 due to conversion). Projected day-case success rate at least 50%.

audits.t: Medical audit of diabetes mellitus in primary care setting in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
audits.st: Pre-determined explicit criteria for long-term diabetes management
audits.f: Poor compliance overall; metabolic control acceptable in 69.5%; foot examination 53.4% and fundus examination 53%.

audits.t: An audit of immunisation status of sickle cell patients in Coventry, UK.
audits.st: UK national immunisation guidance (2006)
audits.f: Children (n=25): 14 (56%) completely immunised against pneumococcus, Hib and MenC, 8 (32%) partial, 3 (12%) none. Adults (n=33): 4 (12%) complete; pneumococcus 21%, Hib 18%, MenC 15%. Influenza within last year 12% of adults and 8% of children.

audits.t: Anglian Genitourinary Medicine Audit Group -- cervical cytology screening in HIV-positive women.
audits.st: NHS Cervical Screening Programme: annual cervical cytology in HIV-positive women
audits.f: Only 55.5% of clinics met NHSCSP standards; mean smears performed 1.9 versus 3.29 expected (P = 0.0001).

audits.t: Inequalities in child health up to five years: a supradistrict audit.
audits.st: Seven standards for evidence-based interventions to reduce child health inequalities (postnatal depression, breastfeeding, parental support, looked-after children, nutrition, day care, smoking in pregnancy)
audits.f: Recommendations not implemented consistently across areas, services or populations, particularly smoking cessation, postnatal depression management and breastfeeding.

audits.t: [Prophylactic antibiotic use in gastro-intestinal surgery: an audit of current practice].
audits.st: Toulouse teaching hospital and SFAR prophylactic antibiotic guidelines; Haute Autorité de Santé criteria (indication, antibiotic, timing, duration)
audits.f: Prophylaxis prescribed in 58%; compliance with indication 85%; antibiotic choice 82.8%; timing 39.7%; duration excessive in 5 cases; overall compliance 42%.

audits.t: Care of patients with psoriasis: an audit of U.K. services in secondary care.
audits.st: British Association of Dermatologists guidelines and standards for psoriasis care
audits.f: 18% (18/98) of units had fewer than 2.0 WTE consultants and 20% had no specialist nurse; only 21% had dedicated psoriasis clinics; 55% had no systemic drug monitoring clinic. Of 73 units prescribing biologics, 88% (64/73) followed BAD biologics guidelines. Quality-of-life score inadequately or never recorded in 81% of units' outpatient records; PASI inadequately or never recorded in 79% of outpatient records.

audits.t: Audit of quality of diagnostic procedures for occupational asthma.
audits.st: Quality indicators with criteria for sufficient care: exposure assessment, spirometry, bronchodilator response, serial workplace PEF, time to diagnosis
audits.f: Exposure assessment 92%, spirometry 87%, bronchodilator response 79%; workplace PEF in 51% (sufficient quality in 52%); median time from symptoms to diagnosis 3.2 years.

audits.t: Emergency management of children with severe sepsis in the United Kingdom: the results of the Paediatric Intensive Care Society sepsis audit.
audits.tp: Paediatric sepsis management in the emergency department
audits.st: 2002 American College of Critical Care Medicine/Pediatric Advanced Life Support (ACCM-PALS) guideline
audits.f: 34/200 (17%) children died after referral; most children received inadequate fluid resuscitation and inotropic support in the first hours after presentation.

audits.t: Clinical audit and peer review scheme for the South West post-new 2006 dental contract: a report on progress so far.
audits.tp: Dental practice audit and peer review scheme
audits.st: 'Cookbook' audits devised by the Local Assessment Panel
audits.f: First-cycle patient satisfaction averaged 99%; other first-cycle results not reported.
audits.r2: All audits showed improvement except patient satisfaction; improvement in clinical record keeping was particularly marked.

audits.t: A perinatal audit of neonatal deaths in three Danish counties.
audits.st: Generally accepted standards of satisfactory perinatal and neonatal care
audits.f: County without a neonatal intensive care unit had significantly more potentially avoidable deaths than the county with a fully staffed NICU; suboptimal care in another county linked to inadequate staffing and inexperienced junior doctors.

audits.t: Safer sedation practice may not translate into improvements in endoscopic outcomes.
audits.st: Guidelines on sedation in endoscopy
audits.f: Mean midazolam dose 4.9 mg (SD 2.5).
audits.c: Unit sedation policy, 5 mg midazolam syringes replacing 10 mg vials, adverse event recording for doses over 5 mg and reversal agents, stricter monitoring, and endoscopist education and feedback.

audits.t: Improving blood-borne viral diagnosis; clinical audit of the uptake of dried blood spot testing offered by a substance misuse service.
audits.tp: Bloodborne virus testing and hepatitis B immunisation in injecting drug users
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Venepuncture testing uptake among clients (figures not given).
audits.c: Routine offer of dried blood spot testing for hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV
audits.r2: Uptake of DBS testing almost six times greater than previous venepuncture uptake.

audits.t: Implementation of patient safety strategies in European hospitals.
audits.st: Basic patient safety strategies
audits.f: Considerable proportion of audited hospitals did not comply with basic strategies such as adult identification bracelets and medication labelling.

audits.t: Does a dedicated nurse practitioner improve thromboprophylaxis use in acutely ill medical patients in Australia? The methodology for a multicentre VTE Task Force Audit.
audits.st: Current guidelines for thromboprophylaxis in high-risk acutely ill medical patients
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: 4-month programme led by a VTE nurse educator raising awareness of VTE risk, risk assessment and prophylaxis, with feedback of local audit results.

audits.t: A national audit of the secondary care of "acute" asthma in Wales--February 2006.
audits.tp: Acute severe asthma management in adults
audits.st: British Thoracic Society/SIGN asthma guidelines
audits.f: BTS/SIGN severity assessment rarely performed; monitoring of progress and discharge process disappointing. 30% of patients appeared mild and 19% severe/acute severe.

audits.t: Audit of the consultation process on general internal medicine services.
audits.st: A clear clinical question posed to the subspecialist
audits.f: Clear clinical question in 69.7% (131/188); MTU member contacted the subspecialist in 74.2%; urgent consultations had a clear question in 63.3%.

audits.t: A model for increasing patient safety in the intensive care unit: increasing the implementation rates of proven safety measures.
audits.st: Evidence-based prophylaxis against venous thromboembolism, ventilator-associated pneumonia and stress ulcers
audits.f: Baseline implementation rates measured per patient-shift (values not given in abstract).
audits.c: Systematic approach to delivering safety measures, team communication tools, daily prompts in the ICU progress note and a data wall for real-time feedback.
audits.r2: Mean implementation rose for each measure, with reduced variation and narrower control limits.

audits.t: Quality of in-hospital stroke care according to evidence-based performance measures: results from the first audit of stroke, Catalonia, Spain.
audits.st: 13 evidence-based performance measures of in-hospital stroke process of care
audits.f: Eight performance measures achieved compliance >=75%, 4 of which were more than 90%; the remaining showed lower adherence.

audits.t: Management of patients on warfarin by general dental practitioners in South West Wales: continuing the audit cycle.
audits.st: Current guidelines, including new recommendations produced in 2001, on dental management of patients on warfarin
audits.f: Results of the first audit not given in abstract.
audits.r2: 332/447 (74%) returned; 278 (84%) would check INR before treatment, 214 (65%) within 24 hours; none would advise reducing warfarin dose and 1% would stop warfarin without medical opinion; 206 (63%) would seek medical advice for high risk procedures.

audits.t: Audit of anticoagulant thromboprophylaxis in hospitalized oncology patients.
audits.st: 2004 American College of Chest Physicians consensus guidelines on VTE prophylaxis
audits.f: 38/113 (33.6%) had indications for prophylactic anticoagulation; 23 of these had contraindications, leaving 15 (13%) appropriate; only one was appropriately given prophylaxis.

audits.t: Audit of clinical coding of major head and neck operations.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Correct OPCS procedure coding reflective of work undertaken
audits.f: 47 of 99 (47.4%) original procedure codes were incorrect (revised coding generated 146 codes); HRG unchanged in 19 of 34 cases (55.9%); six cases never coded, equating to a 15,300 pound loss.

audits.t: Audit of two-week rule referrals for suspected testicular cancer in Cornwall, 2003-2005.
audits.tp: Suspected testicular cancer referral pathway timeliness
audits.st: Two-week wait referral guidelines for suspected testicular cancer
audits.f: Referral-to-treatment journey for 42 testicular tumour cases before the two-week wait system (interval figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Introduction of the two-week wait referral system.
audits.r2: Testicular cancer found in only 8% of two-week wait referrals; 48% of referrals judged inappropriate; 78% required no surgery. Average GP referral to urology clinic time improved by 9 days; other intervals unchanged.

audits.t: An audit of percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy insertion in patients undergoing treatment for head and neck cancer: reducing the incidence of peri-operative airway events by the introduction of a tumour assessment protocol.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 2 (6%) of 33 PEGs under sedation had major airway complications, one fatal.
audits.r2: No airway complications or abdominal wall metastases; 16 (13%) under general anaesthetic and 5 (4.5%) under radiological guidance.

audits.t: Effect of clinical audits of radiation use in one hospital district in Finland.
audits.tp: Diagnostic reference levels for radiation dose
audits.st: Generally accepted standards for good medical radiological procedures (audit criteria list)
audits.f: All units used radiation in accordance with requirements; 80 recommendations made, most (22/80) on instructions for the fundamental practice of examining a patient.
audits.c: Recommendations from the first audit implemented by units.
audits.r2: Audit criteria fulfilled clearly better; 53 recommendations made, most in the category of radiation doses.

audits.t: Standard of care for type 2 diabetic patients in a public hospital general medical clinic: report of a self-audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Annual testing: blood pressure 100%, lipids 91.8%, HbA1c 69%; screening: eye 69%, albuminuria 51%, foot 22.4%; BMI documented 38.3%, smoking 46%.

audits.t: Internal audit of a comprehensive IMRT program for prostate cancer: a model for centers in developing countries?
audits.st: Departmental prostate IMRT protocol with 18 dose objectives to target and critical organs
audits.f: 39/1140 (3.3%) dosimetric end points did not meet protocol criteria; no plans required revision at QA rounds; one major protocol violation.

audits.t: Intraoperative consultation in gynecologic pathology: a 6-year audit at a tertiary care medical center.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Patient care potentially negatively impacted in 14 IOCs (2 by gynaecologic pathologists, 12 by surgical pathologists); gross inspection only had accuracy of 94.7%.

audits.t: A multidisciplinary audit of clinical coding accuracy in otolaryngology: financial, managerial and clinical governance considerations under payment-by-results.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: National standard clinical coding audit methodology
audits.f: Coding errors in 24.1% (301/1250); 48 primary diagnoses and 186 primary procedures reassigned; 209 missed secondary codes; HRG changed in 203 cases.

audits.t: A prospective audit to investigate the level of consciousness of children requiring conscious sedation using an 'alternative technique'.
audits.st: Contemporary standards and guidance for alternative conscious sedation (no loss of consciousness)
audits.f: 11 children (1.9%) scored level 5 on modified Wilson scale, mostly for under a minute and no more than five minutes; no children became unresponsive.

audits.t: Setting up clinical audit in Gondar Hospital, Ethiopia.
audits.st: Agreed local clinical guidelines by topic
audits.f: 20 audits commenced: 7 completed, 11 in progress, 2 awaiting analysis; good practice in treating common paediatric emergencies and record documentation; glucose testing on the children's ward needed improvement.
audits.c: Lead clinician nominated, audit clerk appointed, staff training and local guidelines written.

audits.t: Analysis of the use of imipenem at a university hospital following the restructuring of an antimicrobial audit system.
audits.st: Criteria for rational use of imipenem from a literature review
audits.f: Baseline appropriateness of indication, consumption and outcomes reported; 4 associations with spectrum superposition; 4 therapy changes.
audits.c: Restructuring of the hospital antimicrobial audit system.
audits.r2: No difference in appropriate indication, consumption or outcomes; associations with spectrum superposition fell from 4 to 1; therapy changes rose from 4 to 8.

audits.t: Success and failure of fast track extubation in cardiac surgery patients of tertiary care hospital: one year audit.
audits.st: Fast-track extubation within six hours of arrival in cardiac ICU
audits.f: 196 (49.5%) of patients planned for fast-track were extubated within six hours.

audits.t: Audit of dermatological content of U.K. undergraduate curricula.
audits.st: British Association of Dermatologists recommendations for a core undergraduate dermatology curriculum; all curricula should include the essential clinical skills learning outcomes
audits.f: Replies from 29 of 30 schools; dermatological history taking and skin examination were included in most but not all curricula; some omissions such as diagnosis of meningococcaemia.

audits.t: Measuring success in asthma care: a repeat audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline asthma care measures (figures not given).
audits.c: Minimal intervention programme using checklists, booklets and repeated audit.
audits.r2: Significant increase in peak flow meter ownership and use and improved inhaler technique; inadequate control in 22%.

audits.t: An audit of rectal examination on general/geriatric wards in a district general hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Rectal examination performed in 25% overall and 36% of 118 elderly patients.

audits.t: An audit of rejected repeated x-ray films as a quality assurance element in a radiology department.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1338 of 15,095 films (8.86%) rejected (range 7.69% to 13.82%); causes: radiographer faults 547 (40.88%), equipment faults 255 (19.06%), patient faults 250 (18.90%).

audits.t: Promoting accountability in obstetric care: use of criteria-based audit in Viet Nam.
audits.st: National guidelines for major obstetric complications (2002) via criteria-based audit
audits.f: Clinical protocols for major obstetric complications were not followed; obstacles to timely treatment out of hours.
audits.c: Teams devised action plans to correct identified problems.
audits.r2: Significant improvements when audit cycle repeated (no figures given).

audits.t: Adolescent self harm patients: audit of assessment in an accident and emergency department.
audits.tp: Self-harm care in the emergency department
audits.st: Adequacy of psychiatric and social assessment by the A&E doctor, scored over 10 headings (no named guideline or target)
audits.f: 210 adolescents attended after deliberate self poisoning; records available for 200. 89 admitted (mean score 5.1), 80 discharged without psychiatric consultation or follow up (mean score 5.4), 31 discharged with consultation or follow up (mean score 9.1). Adequate or better assessment across 10 headings ranged 0%-40%, 0%-50% and 0%-61% by group. Documentation of suicidal state inadequate in 49% (54/111) of those discharged.

audits.t: Nasal injury management: an audit of accident and emergency practice.
audits.st: Local nasal injury management guideline (refer only patients with deformity after swelling subsides)
audits.f: Nasal injury referrals seen in ENT outpatients before the guideline, including those not requiring ENT treatment (figures not reported in abstract).
audits.c: Introduction of a nasal injury management guideline for A&E
audits.r2: Proportion of patients seen in ENT outpatients not requiring any ENT treatment was reduced (figures not reported in abstract).

audits.t: An audit of urology two-week wait referrals in a large teaching hospital in England.
audits.st: Department of Health two-week wait referral guidelines for suspected urological cancer
audits.f: 42 (11%) referrals were inappropriate. Cancer found in 90 of 400 (23%); detection ranged from 50 of 122 (41%) for elevated PSA to 2 of 56 (4%) for scrotal lumps.

audits.t: Chart audit: strategies to improve quality of nursing documentation.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Strategies implemented to improve nursing documentation.

audits.t: Impact of audit of routine second-trimester cardiac images using a novel image-scoring method.
audits.tp: Fetal cardiac anomaly scan image quality
audits.st: Novel image-scoring method for four-chamber and outflow tract views (maximum patient score 15)
audits.f: Baseline audit scores for 8 sonographers (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Feedback from the primary audit to sonographers.

audits.t: Impact of audit and feedback on antipsychotic prescribing in schizophrenia.
audits.st: Practice recommendations for antipsychotic monotherapy, second-generation antipsychotic and clozapine use
audits.f: Baseline variation between services in antipsychotic combinations and SGA prescribing, especially clozapine.
audits.c: Audit and feedback to all services; two services had continued feedback, interim reviews and clozapine-targeted interventions.
audits.r2: Monotherapy 85.7%, SGA 82.7%, clozapine 34.5%; all changed in the desired direction in all three services.

audits.t: [Impact of a new regional management for postpartum hemorrhages by an audit of severe cases: a before and after study (2002-2005)].
audits.st: Regional PPH management guidelines (2004)
audits.f: Inadequate management in 32% of severe PPH cases.
audits.c: Regional guidelines for PPH management diffused to all birthplaces in 2004.

audits.t: Evaluation of clinical practice improvement programs for nurses for the management of alcohol withdrawal in hospitals.
audits.st: Nine clinical standards derived from CIWA-Ar and NSW drug and alcohol withdrawal clinical practice guidelines
audits.f: Baseline compliance with the nine standards measured (figures not given).
audits.c: Nurse education: self-directed competency training package (70 nurses, 3 hospitals) or traditional in-service programme (238 nurses, 8 hospitals).
audits.r2: Hospitals using self-directed competency training had higher total compliance score across the nine standards than in-service hospitals (figures not given).

audits.t: A prospective audit to look at the number of plain sinus x-rays requested via the radiology department.
audits.st: Current best practice guidelines (chronic rhinosinusitis diagnosed on history and nasendoscopy; sinus x-rays not indicated)
audits.f: Sinus x-rays still being requested, particularly by primary care physicians (figures not reported).
audits.c: Informing GPs of current best practice guidelines

audits.t: Out of hours work in primary care: audit of an urban co-operative deputising service.
audits.st: Diagnosis-based classification of calls as emergency, reasonable or unnecessary
audits.f: 6834 calls from 37,300 population (183 per 1000 patients per year). In a sample of 468 (7%) calls, 23% were unnecessary, 65% reasonable and 12% emergencies. Only 1% ended with telephone advice; 5% waited more than two hours.

audits.t: An audit of the quality of care indicators for the management of diabetes in family practice clinics in Karachi, Pakistan.
audits.st: Diabetes quality of care indicator recommendations
audits.f: Only one quarter qualified as excellent or good care; body weight monitored at every visit in 100%; blood glucose advice 79.5%; physical activity advice 27.3%; blood sugar control in 23.9%.

audits.t: Audit of newborn screening programme for congenital hypothyroidism.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Coverage 98.8%; mean recall rate 0.32%; only 79.5% of recalled babies retested; sample rejection rate 2.2%.

audits.t: An audit of tumour marker utilization in Greece.
audits.st: International guidelines on correct use of tumour markers
audits.f: 9782 inappropriate tumour marker orders; appropriate requests below 10% for CA 125, AFP, CA 19-9, CYFRA 21-1 and NSE; 5.6 requests per patient.

audits.t: Analgesics administered during minor painful procedures in a cohort of hospitalized infants: a prospective clinical audit.
audits.st: Evidence-based consensus statements on pain management during painful procedures in infants
audits.f: Oral sucrose or background opioid given during 85% of 3605 minor painful procedures; 15% had no analgesia.

audits.t: Evaluation of criteria-based clinical audit in improving quality of obstetric care in a developing country hospital.
audits.st: Standard criteria for management of obstetric haemorrhage, eclampsia, genital tract infection, obstructed labour and uterine rupture
audits.f: Overall care: obstetric haemorrhage 61%, eclampsia 54.3%, obstructed labour 81.7%, genital tract sepsis 66%.
audits.c: Mechanisms for improving care identified and implemented after Phase I.
audits.r2: Obstetric haemorrhage 81% (p = 0.000), eclampsia 90% (p = 0.00), obstructed labour 93.5% (p < 0.001), genital tract sepsis 85.2% (p < 0.01).

audits.t: Impact of an audit program and other factors on door-to-balloon times in acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction patients destined for primary coronary intervention.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Geometric mean door-to-balloon time 164.9 minutes; median 147.5 minutes.
audits.c: Audit programme collecting time data for essential intervals with feedback to Emergency Medicine and Cardiology departments.
audits.r2: Geometric mean 141.9 minutes (p = 0.039); median 136.0 minutes (p = 0.09); adjusted reduction 35.5 minutes (p = 0.004).

audits.t: Failure of a poster-based educational programme to improve compliance with peripheral venous catheter care in a tertiary hospital. A clinical audit.
audits.st: In-house infection control recommendation to record date and time of PVC insertion
audits.f: Any dating of PVC insertion recorded in 13.4%.
audits.r2: Any dating recorded in 16.1% (P = 0.27, not significant).

audits.t: Microcytosis and possible early iron deficiency in paediatric inpatients: a retrospective audit.
audits.tp: Blood test result actioning and communication
audits.st: Identification, documentation as abnormal, and follow-up or treatment of abnormally low MCV results (no numeric target stated)
audits.f: Of 701 inpatients with full blood counts across both periods, 61 (8.7%) had low MCV. Among the 85% without an identifiable explanation, 25% had the result documented as abnormal.
audits.c: Results of the first audit presented to medical staff with suggestions for improving documentation and follow-up of abnormal results.
audits.r2: Documentation of results as abnormal rose to 91% (p = 0.00, z-test); no increase in the proportion receiving follow-up or treatment.

audits.t: The impact of national guidelines on the waiting list for colonoscopy: a quantitative clinical audit.
audits.st: ACPGBI/BSG 2002 guidelines for colonoscopic surveillance
audits.f: Around 22% (n = 664) of surveillance referrals were in line with guidelines, 51% (n = 1540) could be cancelled and 27% (n = 816) could be given a new date. Average wait for diagnostic colonoscopy 76.8 days.
audits.c: Non-compliant surveillance referrals adjusted (cancelled or re-dated) to match the guidelines
audits.r2: Average wait for diagnostic colonoscopy fell from 76.8 to 56.0 days (P = 0.0022).

audits.t: British HIV Association (BHIVA) national cohort outcomes audit of patients commencing antiretrovirals from naïve.
audits.st: BHIVA guidelines: viral load below 50 copies/mL within 6 months of starting HAART
audits.f: Majority managed within BHIVA guidelines and achieved viral suppression below 50 copies/mL around 6 months.

audits.t: An audit of prophylactic antibiotic use in laryngeal reconstruction surgery.
audits.st: Departmental antibiotic prophylaxis protocol
audits.f: 32 of 36 children received appropriate antibiotic prophylaxis.
audits.c: Revised antibiotic protocol presented; no re-audit reported

audits.t: Combined audit of hospital antibiotic use and a prevalence survey of healthcare-associated infection.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 7.18% of patients had a healthcare-associated infection and 36.8% were on antibiotics.

audits.t: Quality assurance audit: a prospective non-randomised trial of chemotherapy and radiotherapy for osteolymphoma (TROG 99.04/ALLG LY02).
audits.st: Trial protocol (consent, eligibility, chemotherapy and radiotherapy)
audits.f: Overall rate of major protocol variations 3.6%.

audits.t: Criteria-based audit to improve women-friendly care in maternity units in Malawi.
audits.st: Local standards for women-friendly care based on WHO manuals
audits.f: Greeting clients 74.6%.
audits.c: Audit results presented; recommendations made and implemented.

audits.t: Audit of an inpatient liaison psychiatry consultation service.
audits.st: Published international standards for timeliness of response to referrals
audits.f: 40.1% of referrals seen the same day, 75.4% by the end of the next day and 93.4% by the end of the following day.

audits.t: Why are HIV-positive mothers refusing to have their children screened for vertically transmitted HIV infection?
audits.tp: HIV testing of children of HIV-positive mothers
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: HIV status unknown in 73% of children of HIV-positive mothers.
audits.c: The audit process itself (no specific intervention described).
audits.r2: 13/92 (14%) of previously untested children had HIV status established.

audits.t: UK Renal Registry 12th Annual Report (December 2009): chapter 10: biochemistry profile of patients receiving dialysis in the UK in 2008: national and centre-specific analyses.
audits.st: UK Renal Association clinical performance measures for biochemical parameters
audits.f: Phosphate 1.1-1.8 mmol/L in 55% HD and 64% PD; revised calcium target 2.2-2.5 mmol/L met by 63% HD and 65% PD.

audits.t: Improved oxygen prescribing using a nurse-facilitated reminder.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Oxygen prescribed in 0%; appropriate oxygen therapy 70.6%; type 1 respiratory failure errors 18.4%; type 2 errors 61.3%.
audits.c: MAU nurse education and a nurse-facilitated oxygen prescribing reminder to junior doctors.
audits.r2: Oxygen prescribed in 49% (p < 0.0001); appropriate therapy 76.5% (p = 0.65); type 1 errors 3.8% (p = 0.13); type 2 errors 44.0% (p = 0.49).

audits.t: Audit of anticoagulation after embolectomy for acute ischaemia.
audits.st: APTT in therapeutic range (50-90 s)
audits.f: Of 389 APTT tests, 146 (37.6%) were in the therapeutic range (50-90 s); 40.4% were 90 s (text truncated in abstract).
audits.c: New UFH protocol being developed; no re-audit reported

audits.t: Audit of dental practice record-keeping: a PCT-coordinated clinical audit by Worcestershire dentists.
audits.st: Common framework of eight record-keeping domains; standard of grade 1 (good) or 2 (adequate)
audits.f: 161 of 184 dentists (87.5%) each audited 30 records. Proportion below standard: soft tissues 36%, periodontal status 30%, radiographic review 27%, note-taking 25%.
audits.c: PCT arranged postgraduate education on record keeping and raised awareness; individual anonymised peer comparison fed back

audits.t: Three consecutive audits to achieve acceptable colonoscopy completion rates.
audits.st: Acceptable colonoscopy completion (caecal intubation) rates
audits.f: Crude caecal intubation rate 55%; adjusted rate not calculable due to inadequate documentation.
audits.c: Proforma introduced for prospective data collection and further improvements in methodology after each audit.

audits.t: Audit of frequent attendees to an ENT emergency clinic.
audits.st: Patients should not attend the ENT emergency clinic more than twice in the same episode
audits.f: 38 patients seen more than twice, generating 81 excess appointments.
audits.c: Senior review for patients seen more than twice and a management guideline for acute otitis externa.
audits.r2: 19 patients seen more than twice, generating 24 excess appointments (70% reduction).

audits.t: Dosimetry audit for a multi-centre IMRT head and neck trial.
audits.st: Gamma criteria 3%/3mm (individual fields) and 4%/3mm (combined fields)
audits.f: Mean PTV dose differences -0.6% (IMRT) and 0.7% (CRT) at six centres; 94% of individual IMRT fluence films passed 3%/3mm and 75% of combined field films passed 4%/3mm.

audits.t: Evaluating changes in gastrointestinal endoscopy training over 5 years: closing the audit loop.
audits.st: Recommended standards for colonoscopy training supervision
audits.f: Formal teaching of colonoscopy principles 65%, polypectomy 52%, extubation 56%; course attendance 48%; training adequate or better 25%.
audits.c: National Endoscopy Training Programme accredited courses and new assessment tools (2004).
audits.r2: Principles 91% (P = 0.02); polypectomy 81% (P = 0.02); extubation 88% (P = 0.01); course attendance 84% (P = 0.003); training adequate or better 87%.

audits.t: Bacterial contamination of PCA and epidural infusion devices.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 45% of handset swabs and 46% of keypad swabs grew bacteria, mostly coagulase-negative staphylococcus.
audits.c: Additional cleaning step with 70% isopropyl alcohol wipes.
audits.r2: 6% of handset swabs and 4% of keypad swabs grew bacteria.

audits.t: Audit of hepatitis B vaccination of men who have sex with men attending Scottish genitourinary medicine clinics.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B vaccination in sexual health clinics
audits.st: BASHH targets for offer and completion of hepatitis B vaccination
audits.f: 215 (41%) eligible; 175 (81%) offered vaccination; 144 (82%) accepted; overall completion 31%.

audits.t: Long-term indwelling silastic central venous catheters: clinical audit leading to improved surgical technique.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 23 (58%) of 40 lines had complications, many related to surgical technique.
audits.c: Dedicated surgical team using a standardised technique: all catheters via the right internal jugular vein with on-table radiographic confirmation of position
audits.r2: 26 catheters in 24 patients; significant improvement in results (figures not reported in abstract).

audits.t: Radiotherapy in England in 2007: modelled demand and audited activity.
audits.st: National Radiotherapy Advisory Group model; 50% radiotherapy access rate accepted in the literature
audits.f: 2114 patients prescribed 27,420 fractions. Access rate 37% versus 50% expected; shortfall due to lack of access (67%) and reduced fractionation (33%).

audits.t: An audit of thiopurine methyltransferase genotyping and phenotyping before intended azathioprine treatment for dermatological conditions.
audits.st: Recommended azathioprine dosing guidelines
audits.f: 90.6% TPMT wild type, 9.4% heterozygous; 103/192 (53.6%) wild-type and 7/20 (35%) heterozygotes started azathioprine; mean dose 84.1 mg/day vs 64.3 mg/day.

audits.t: An audit of NICE guidelines on antenatal pelvic floor exercises.
audits.st: NICE: antenatal pelvic floor exercises during first pregnancy
audits.f: 95% were aware of the importance of pelvic floor exercises, but only a limited proportion had the right information and a minority practised them.

audits.t: Audit of transfer of unconscious head-injured patients to a neurosurgical unit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 42% of comatose patients had been intubated; half of those without airway were transported supine.

audits.t: Opportunistic immunisation of paediatric inpatients at Rotorua Hospital: audit and discussion.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 84% had immunisation status documented; only 60% of these were up to date; no follow-up action in 79% of under-immunised; 4% received catch-up on the unit.

audits.t: Triggers and appropriateness of red blood cell transfusions in the postpartum patient--a retrospective audit.
audits.st: National transfusion guidelines: Hb threshold 6.4 g/dl (non-massive) and 8.1 g/dl (massive blood loss)
audits.f: 68% (n = 61) may have received one or more units inappropriately; 143 of 311 units (46%) possibly inappropriate.

audits.t: Impact of a real-time peer review audit on patient management in a radiation oncology department.
audits.st: RANZCR modified Peer Review Audit Tool (PRAT) criteria
audits.f: Behaviour criteria well documented; histology and imaging reports not scanned into the EMR in up to a third of cases; prescription errors rare. 8 (3.8%) of 208 had a change to management recommended.

audits.t: Effect of an audit and feedback intervention on hospitalized oncology patients' perception of nurse practitioner care.
audits.tp: Patient perception of nurse practitioner care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Nurse practitioner audit and feedback intervention.

audits.t: Postoperative hyperglycaemia of diabetic patients undergoing cardiac surgery - a clinical audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Wide variation in blood glucose levels and inconsistent testing; mean levels 'borderline'. 52% (n = 78) developed 114 complications, including 21.4% (n = 32) wound infections.

audits.t: Interobserver agreement between primary graders and an expert grader in the Bristol and Weston diabetic retinopathy screening programme: a quality assurance audit.
audits.st: Interobserver agreement of 80% with Kappa coefficient 0.7
audits.f: Agreement bettered 80% in all categories; Kappa 0.7 overall and 0.59-0.65 for referable, non-referable and ungradable disease.

audits.t: Audit of early syphilis: Teesside experience 2005-2007.
audits.st: National standards for syphilis treatment, follow-up and partner notification
audits.f: Treatment rate 100%; 75 of 80 had benzathine penicillin; 87 of 115 contactable partners (75.7%) screened and/or treated; satisfactory titre decline in 56 of 59 (94.9%).

audits.t: Renal biopsies in children: current practice and audit of outcomes.
audits.st: Nationally agreed standards for number of needle passes, adequacy of biopsy material and complication rates
audits.f: 531 biopsies (352 native); 31% day case and 49% under GA. Major complication rate was higher than the standard (exact figures truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Auditing the nursing standard for weighing patients on an acute medical unit.
audits.st: Nursing standard for observations and assessments on the AMU (patient weight)
audits.f: Only 50% of nurses routinely weighed patients on admission and/or as part of nutritional screening.
audits.c: Revisions made to the existing nursing standard; no re-audit reported

audits.t: Immunisation practices in infants born prematurely: neonatologists' survey and clinical audit.
audits.st: Australian immunisation guidelines
audits.f: Coverage 90% at 12 months; only 20% (10/50) with chronic lung disease had influenza vaccine; DTPa delayed >1 month in 15% at 2 months and 43% at 6 months.

audits.t: Improving diabetes care using a multitiered quality improvement model.
audits.st: Diabetes mellitus guideline recommended annual tests and examinations
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Changed office visit structure, protocol-driven electronic prompts, clinical decision support in new EMR form, and audit with feedback.
audits.r2: Significant improvements in 5 process and 2 outcome measures; quality summary measure improved 8%.

audits.t: Current standards for infection control: audit assures compliance.
audits.st: Health and Social Care Act 2008 Code of Practice for prevention and control of healthcare-associated infections
audits.f: Audit identified shortfalls in infection control compliance (figures not given); staff had assumed compliance near 100%.
audits.r2: Re-audit showed the effectiveness of the action plan (figures not given).

audits.t: Medical audit on children with asthma in an Emergency Department.
audits.st: 17 explicit indicators from international guides
audits.f: Cause of crisis recorded 32%; severity 18%; supportive treatment 24%; respiratory rate 49%; peak flow 0%; auscultation 100%; treatment result 69%.

audits.t: Perioperative management of anticoagulated patients having cataract surgery: National audit of current practice of members of the Royal College of Ophthalmologists.
audits.tp: Perioperative anticoagulation management in cataract surgery
audits.st: RCOphth guidelines on perioperative management of anticoagulated patients having cataract surgery
audits.f: 29.5% of respondents adhered to all aspects of the guidelines (check INR, continue warfarin, operate within therapeutic INR, consider sub-Tenon or topical anaesthesia).

audits.t: Survivors of childhood cancer: an Australian audit of vaccination status after treatment.
audits.st: Australian guidelines for post-chemotherapy revaccination
audits.f: 39% (35/89) had no evidence of booster vaccination after therapy; 47% (42/89) had at least one influenza vaccination.

audits.t: A prospective audit of postoperative pain control in pediatric patients.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) in the clinical management of acute COPD in 233 UK hospitals: results from the RCP/BTS 2003 National COPD Audit.
audits.tp: NIV in acute hypercapnic respiratory failure
audits.st: NICE and BTS guidelines on NIV for acidotic exacerbations of COPD
audits.f: 19 hospitals (8%) did not offer NIV; NIV available on all three sites in 74 (30%). pH <7.35 in 26% (1714/6544) and NIV given to 31% of these.

audits.t: Emergency department management of exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: audit of compliance with evidence-based guidelines.
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines (Level A and B) for COPD exacerbation: bronchodilators, methylxanthines, steroids and NIPPV
audits.f: 72.4% received short-acting beta-agonist, 37.8% inhaled anticholinergic, 56.6% systemic steroids; NIPPV in 21 patients, 15 with documented acidosis or hypercapnia.

audits.t: An audit of the use of breakaway techniques in a large psychiatric hospital: a replication study.
audits.st: Break away from simulated scenario within 10 s using taught techniques
audits.f: Only 14% (21/147) correctly used taught techniques to break away within 10 s; 80% broke away within 10 s without using taught techniques.

audits.t: An audit of first-aid treatment of pediatric burns patients and their clinical outcome.
audits.st: Recommended first aid: cold water for 20 minutes or longer
audits.f: 86.1% received first aid, 80.2% cold water, but only 12.1% applied cold water for the recommended 20 minutes or longer.

audits.t: A prospective audit on the validity of written informed consent prior to glaucoma surgery: an Asian perspective.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 50 (68.5%) felt given enough time; 69 (94.5%) reported adequate information on risks. Only 13 (17.8%) showed good overall understanding and 57.5% moderate understanding.

audits.t: The impact of rational pharmacotherapy training reinforced via prescription audit on the prescribing skills of fifth-year medical students.
audits.st: Prescription audit criteria for standardised hypertension patients
audits.f: Baseline prescription audit scores recorded (figures not given).
audits.c: Five-day rational pharmacotherapy training by pharmacologists and clinicians.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in prescription audit scores in all parts of the prescription (figures not given).

audits.t: Introduction of the Liverpool Care Pathway for end of life care to emergency medicine.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline 2001 study and 2003 audit showed an increasing role in care of the acutely dying with inconsistent approach (figures not reported).
audits.c: Modified Liverpool Care Pathway launched November 2005, with meetings and a pilot
audits.r2: Care of the dying described as more consistent and positive; nursing staff very satisfied (no figures reported).

audits.t: Maintaining over time clinical performance targets on anaemia correction in unselected population on chronic dialysis at 20 Italian centres. Data from a retrospective study for a clinical audit.
audits.st: Italian and European Best Practice Guidelines: Hb 11-12 g/dl; iron 60-160 mcg/dl; ferritin 30-400 mcg/l; transferrin 200-360 mg/dl; TSAT >25%
audits.f: Targets maintained over time: Hb 4.3% (mean 11.43 g/dl); ferritin 71.1%; iron 95.0%; transferrin 44.8%; TSAT 8.4%; HD KT/V 61.0%; PD KT/V 31.4%. Mean Hb 11.3 g/dl (SD 0.91).

audits.t: Exploring the outcomes and implications of the latest national COPD audit.
audits.st: not reported

audits.f: 43% met the criterion for appropriate number of screening episodes; 100% met visual acuity and optic disc criteria; 84% met pupil-testing criterion.

audits.t: Audit of referral of obstetric emergencies in Angola: a tool for assessing quality of care.
audits.st: Process indicators: waiting time, partogramme quality, caesarean section rate
audits.f: Maternal mortality 17.8%; mean waiting time 13.7 hours; caesarean rate 13%.
audits.c: Change in routines at hospital admission and further partogramme education.
audits.r2: Maternal mortality nil; mean waiting time 1.2 hours; partogramme quality significantly improved; caesarean rate 30%.

audits.t: More allopurinol is needed to get gout patients < 0.36 mmol/l: a gout audit in the form of a before-after trial.
audits.st: Serum uric acid < 0.36 mmol/l
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Mail and phone intervention to improve gout control (two interventions in two practices).
audits.r2: No significant change after intervention 1 at three months; intervention 2 improved SUA levels with a greater proportion below target.

audits.t: Cardiovascular risk assessment: audit findings from a nurse clinic--a quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk assessment in primary care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 430 (69.2%) had 5-year risk < 15%; 84 (13.5%) > 15%; anti-platelet prescribing for risk > 15% 71%, lipid lowering 65%.
audits.r2: Anti-platelet prescribing rose to 86% and lipid lowering to 72%; 34 showed improved CVD risk.

audits.t: Use of the inhaled corticosteroid to bronchodilator ratio in an audit of the treatment of asthma in an academic family medicine residency programme.
audits.st: Asthma guidelines
audits.f: Inhaled corticosteroid to bronchodilator ratio related to asthma step and inversely to prednisone courses (R2 = .30, p = 0.0012).

audits.t: Audit of protocols for treatment of paediatric burns in emergency departments in the Île de France.
audits.st: International recommendations for paediatric burns management
audits.f: 48% of responding EDs had specific written burns protocols; 65% had a paediatric pain protocol; morphine used by 43%.

audits.t: Still sad after successful renal transplantation: are we failing to recognise depression? An audit of depression screening in renal graft recipients.
audits.st: NICE guidance advocating depression screening in chronic physical illness
audits.f: Screening rate for depression was poor, particularly by nephrologists (n = 8, 13.8%).

audits.t: Why do patients with complex palliative care needs experience delayed hospital discharge?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Reasons for delayed discharge examined (findings not reported).
audits.c: Recommendations made and implemented (details not reported).

audits.t: Use of a guideline based questionnaire to audit hospital care of acute asthma.
audits.st: Hospital guidelines on management of acute asthma
audits.f: Overall deviations from guidelines in severity recording, emergency beta 2 agonists (60/76, 79%), steroids (43/76, 57%) and antibiotics per guideline (29/45, 64%).
audits.r2: Recording of arterial blood gas tensions improved (chi 2 = 7.0, p = 0.08); few other standards improved.

audits.t: Do differences in dialysis prescription impact on KDOQI bone mineral targets? The Pan Thames Renal Audit.
audits.tp: CKD-mineral bone disorder management in dialysis
audits.st: KDOQI bone mineral clinical practice guideline targets (calcium, phosphate, calcium-phosphate product, PTH)
audits.f: Patients achieving KDOQI targets varied between centres: 23.4-60% for calcium, 31.7-56.7% for phosphate, 60-87.3% for calcium-phosphate product, 17.1-46.8% for PTH and 1.8-10.8% for all 4 targets.

audits.t: An audit on assessment and management of pain at the time of acute hospital admission in older people.
audits.st: All patients admitted with an acute condition should be assessed for pain and managed appropriately at admission (within first 24 h)
audits.f: Pain management may be sub-optimal in older people in acute medical settings (detailed figures truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Implementing the national invasive cervical cancer audit: a local perspective.
audits.st: Invasive Cervical Cancer Audit classification (national)
audits.f: Lapsed attenders 30%, screen detected 26%, interval 13%, never attended 12%, lost to follow-up 10%, never invited 9%.

audits.t: Audit of severe acute maternal morbidity describing reasons for transfer and potential preventability of admissions to ICU.
audits.tp: Maternal death and severe morbidity review
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 10 (35%) of cases deemed preventable; all five septicaemia cases preventable.

audits.t: Patients admitted with an acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in New Zealand in 2007: results of a second comprehensive nationwide audit and a comparison with the first audit from 2002.
audits.st: Guideline recommended risk stratification after ACS
audits.f: Risk stratification by treadmill test or angiogram in 48%; exercise tests 21%, echocardiograms 19%, angiography 32%; PCI 19%, CABG 2.8%.

audits.t: ACS patients in New Zealand experience significant delays to access cardiac investigations and revascularisation treatment especially when admitted to non-interventional centres: results of the second comprehensive national audit of ACS patients.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Patients at non-intervention centres (n=556) older (median 70 vs 66 years) and faced longer delays to investigation and revascularisation.

audits.t: Audit of cervical screening in women with HIV infection in the Auckland and Northland regions of New Zealand.
audits.tp: Cervical screening in women living with HIV
audits.st: Yearly cervical smear for women with HIV infection
audits.f: 69 of 123 (56%) met the definition for yearly cervical smears.
audits.c: Informing GPs, flagging women to the National Cervical Screening Unit for yearly recall, and informing women of low-cost smear options.

audits.t: Retrospective audit of the investigation of patients with suspected acute subarachnoid haemorrhage.
audits.st: Recommended investigational care: lumbar puncture for xanthochromia after negative CT
audits.f: 36/91 (39.6%) with negative CT had LP (recommended care); 55/91 (60.4%) did not, 15 of them with no documented reason.

audits.t: [Interest of evaluation of professional practice for the improvement of the management of postoperative pain with patient controlled analgesia (PCA)].
audits.st: Criteria for hospital means (8) and medical and nursing practice (16) in PCA management
audits.f: POP evaluation 73%; advance PCA adjustment prescription 56%; nurse PCA adaptation 15%; pre-filled prescription form use 59%.
audits.c: Pre-filled prescription form, posters and pocket guides, and training of PCA adviser nurses.
audits.r2: POP evaluation 87%; PCA adjustment prescription 68%; adverse effect treatment 68%; nurse PCA adaptation 43%; administration of adverse effect treatment 64%; form use 70%.

audits.t: Obstetric care of new European migrants in Scotland: an audit of antenatal care, obstetric outcomes and communication.
audits.st: Care standards for antenatal booking, antenatal attendance and interpretation
audits.f: 55% booked by end of week 14; interpretation services used infrequently; full compliance not achieved.

audits.t: Improving diabetes care in a public hospital medical clinic: report of a completed audit cycle.
audits.st: Diabetes-related process and intermediate outcome measures
audits.f: Annual HbA1c testing 68.4%.
audits.c: Results fed back to doctors and measures implemented to improve care.

audits.t: Audit and improve! Evaluation of a real-time probe-based PCR assay with internal control for the direct detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Commercial kit sensitivity unacceptably low at 69% (52/75).
audits.c: In-house probe-based real-time PCR assay with internal control developed.
audits.r2: In-house end-point PCR sensitivity 90% (66/73); real-time assay sensitivity 84%, specificity 97%, DOR 207.

audits.t: Quality of pathology reports for advanced ovarian cancer: are we missing essential information? An audit of 479 pathology reports from the EORTC-GCG 55971/NCIC-CTG OV13 neoadjuvant trial.
audits.st: Quality indicators: macroscopic description, measuring and weighing, tumour origin and differentiation
audits.f: All specimens described in 92.3%; major samples measured and weighed in 59.9%; tumour origin missing in 20.5% (primary) and 23.4% (interval debulking).

audits.t: National audit of asymptomatic screening in UK genitourinary medicine clinics: case-notes audit.
audits.st: BASHH national guidelines for screening asymptomatic patients
audits.f: Performance was over 80% for screening asymptomatic heterosexual men, MSM and women for chlamydia, gonorrhoea, syphilis and HIV; recommended endocervical culture for gonorrhoea performed in only 65% of women.

audits.t: National audit of asymptomatic screening in UK genitourinary medicine clinics: clinic policies audit.
audits.st: BASHH National Guidelines for testing of asymptomatic men and women
audits.f: 99% and 97% of responding clinics had policies compliant for HIV and syphilis testing respectively; one-third offered men urine or urethral NAATs and one quarter offered women NAATs rather than endocervical culture for gonorrhoea (non-compliant).

audits.t: Audit of partner notification for chlamydia infection in the genitourinary medicine clinic at the University Hospital of Hartlepool: 2004-2008.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1.37 partners declared per index patient; 0.52 partners screened per index patient (38% of declared partners); 57% of screened partners positive.

audits.t: An audit of fresh frozen plasma usage and effect of fresh frozen plasma on the pre-transfusion international normalized ratio.
audits.st: National Health and Medical Research Council and Australasian Society for Blood Transfusion guidelines for FFP use
audits.f: Of 325 units, 197 (60.6%) in 67 patients were appropriate and 128 (39.4%) in 33 patients inappropriate.

audits.t: Acne - best practice management.
audits.st: Preset best-practice standards for acne management
audits.f: Some treatment inconsistent with best practice, especially undertreatment or suboptimal antibiotic therapy in moderate and moderate to severe acne.
audits.c: Educational material sent to GPs between cycles.

audits.t: How clean is your scope? A completed audit cycle of the disinfection of nasendoscopes.
audits.st: ENT UK guidelines for disinfection of nasendoscopes
audits.f: Expiry date checked 5/10 sessions; discard date recorded 0/10; dirty bag transport 0/31; scope washed 0/31; adequate disinfection time 16/31; rinse and alcohol dry 0/31; clean bag storage 0/31.
audits.c: Instructional poster and staff training session.
audits.r2: Expiry date checked 10/12; discard date 10/12; dirty bag 19/36; washed 36/36; adequate disinfection time 33/36; rinse and dry 35/36; clean bag 35/36 (all P ≤ 0.048 or better).

audits.t: An audit improves the quality of water within the dental unit water lines of general dental practices across the East of England.
audits.st: CDC guideline/EPA drinking water standard (no more than 5% coliform contaminated, at most 500 cfu/ml); EU potable standard (under 100 cfu/ml, no faecal coliforms) encouraged
audits.f: 25% met EU potable standard; 3% met only CDC/EPA; 72% failed minimum standard; coliforms in 5 (7%).
audits.c: All practices used a suitable disinfectant (mainly Alpron or Sterilox) for at least a month.
audits.r2: Nearly 81% met EU standard (54% zero planktonic bacteria); nearly 6% more met CDC/EPA; 13% failed; coliforms in 1 (1.5%).

audits.t: General pain assessment among patients with cancer in an acute care setting: a best practice implementation project.
audits.st: NHS Quality Improvement Scotland pain criteria (3 of 10), Joanna Briggs Institute best practice
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Education of registered nurses on pain assessment, champions and performance feedback.
audits.r2: Pain assessment tool use improved by 33%; nurses educated increased by 75%; accurate assessment and documentation increased by 46%.

audits.t: Patient information about options for treatment: Methods of a national audit of information provision in chronic kidney disease.
audits.st: CARI guidelines: referral at eGFR < 30 with 3-6 months for pre-dialysis education
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of an automated checklist for quality control of radiotherapy treatment plans.
audits.st: Plan acceptance at radiation oncologist and physicist review
audits.f: Without the checklist 5.9% of plans rejected.
audits.c: Automated checklist of more than twenty planning parameters added to treatment planning.
audits.r2: Rejection rate reduced to 3.1%; checklist used for 64.7% of plans; causes of rejection fell from twelve to seven.

audits.t: The Nursing and Midwifery Content Audit Tool (NMCAT): a short nursing documentation audit tool.
audits.st: Nursing and Midwifery Content Audit Tool criteria
audits.f: Health status, objective information and logical presentation met to a high level; response to treatment and timely recording poor.

audits.t: Medical audit using the Ten Group Classification System and its impact on the cesarean section rate.
audits.st: Ten Group Classification System
audits.f: Caesarean section rate 36.8%.
audits.c: Audit and report of caesarean rates by TGCS group to medical and midwifery staff (6 months).

audits.t: An audit of the impact of a stroke unit in an acute teaching hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline audit of 55 consecutive stroke patients in 2005; mean length of stay 29.3 ± 28 days.
audits.c: Acute stroke unit established in June 2008.
audits.r2: Marked improvements in time to CT brain, aspirin administration and multidisciplinary involvement; mean length of stay fell to 19.6 ± 20 days (p = 0.018).

audits.t: Non-clinical errors using voice recognition dictation software for radiology reports: a retrospective audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 11% of plain film reports had errors (2% nonsense phrases); 36% of non-CR reports had errors (5% nonsense phrases).

audits.t: A prospective audit of patient experiences in colonoscopy using the Global Rating Scale: a cohort of 1,187 patients.
audits.st: Global Rating Scale
audits.f: Indication explained to 85%; risks explained to 65%; 21% left without knowing how to get final results; 10% rated it (very) uncomfortable.

audits.t: Auditing ultrasound assessment of fetal nuchal translucency thickness: a review of Australian National Data 2002-2008.
audits.st: 40-60% of NT measurements above the median for gestational age
audits.f: 40% of certified operators met the international standard in 2002.
audits.c: National NT ultrasound education and monitoring programme.
audits.r2: 55% of certified operators met the standard in 2008.

audits.t: Improving transfusion practice: ongoing education and audit at two tertiary speciality hospitals in Western Australia.
audits.st: National transfusion guidelines
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Transfusion coordinator employed; education, protocols rewritten and published electronically, positive patient identification promoted.
audits.r2: Baseline, hourly and completion observations recorded in >94% (KEMH) and >96% (PMH); 15 min observations up 23% and 36%; consent up 20% and 31%.

audits.t: An audit of platelet transfusion within the Wellington Cancer Centre.
audits.st: Local prophylactic platelet transfusion policy and international recommendations
audits.f: Decisions to withhold prophylactic platelets adhered to policy in 99%.

audits.t: [Cardiovascular risk factors. An audit of their detection in primary care].
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk assessment in primary care
audits.st: Recording of preventive cardiovascular activities (target not reported)
audits.f: Blood pressure measurement 45%, cholesterol 23%, height and weight 8%, smoking enquiry 40%; risk factors recorded in clinical history 87%, age and sex card 72%.
audits.c: Corrective measures following medical audit methodology (details not reported).
audits.r2: Blood pressure 79%, cholesterol 76%, height and weight 71%, smoking enquiry 56%; recording 98% in clinical history and 91% in age and sex card.

audits.t: An eight year audit before and after the introduction of modified early warning score (MEWS) charts, of patients admitted to a tertiary referral intensive care unit after CPR.
audits.tp: Early warning score response and escalation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Cardiac arrest calls 0.4% of adult hospital admissions.
audits.c: Introduction of a 24/7 Critical Care Outreach Service and MEWS charts.
audits.r2: Cardiac arrest calls 0.2% of adult hospital admissions (significant decrease).

audits.t: A computerized audit of 15,009 emergency department records.
audits.st: Inclusion of critical pertinent positives and negatives for trigger diagnoses (extremity laceration, epiglottitis, abdominal pain, meningitis, myocardial infarction)
audits.f: Records created by a voice-activated word processor with real-time risk management prompts were superior to handwritten and dictated records (figures not reported).

audits.t: Screening for depression in post stroke patients.
audits.st: NICE guidance: formal screening for depression after stroke
audits.f: No formal screening tool in use; depression identified in 28%; in 9 cases no record of mood assessment; 13 of 60 prescribed psychotropics.
audits.c: Introduction of the PHQ-9 screening tool two weeks after admission
audits.r2: 10 of 18 screened (56%) scored 5 or above, indicating depression.

audits.t: Delays in recognition and management of giant cell arteritis: results from a retrospective audit.
audits.st: Guidelines on managing GCA (early recognition and prompt treatment)
audits.f: Mean time from symptom onset to diagnosis 35 days; corticosteroids not delayed once diagnosed; recognition of ischaemic symptoms was slow.

audits.t: Are primary care practitioners in Barbados following hypertension guidelines? - a chart audit.
audits.st: Hypertension practice guidelines
audits.f: not reported (abstract says improvements needed in BMI assessment, accurate BP measurement, thiazide use and lifestyle advice; BP control inadequate)

audits.t: Completion of a British Association for Sexual Health and HIV regional audit loop: HIV testing in genitourinary medicine clinics in Scotland in 2004 and 2008.
audits.tp: HIV testing uptake in STI patients
audits.st: Recommended HIV test offer and uptake in new attendees diagnosed with an STI
audits.f: Baseline test offer and uptake rates (figures not given in abstract).
audits.r2: Large increases in rates of test offer and uptake, especially in boards with low baseline testing; overall rates remain below recommended levels.

audits.t: The value of audit and feedback reports in improving nutrition therapy in the intensive care unit: a multicenter observational study.
audits.st: Canadian Critical Care Nutrition guidelines
audits.f: EN adequacy 45.1% (calories) and 44.8% (protein); EN without PN 71.9%; EN started within 48 h 60.3%.
audits.c: Individualised benchmarked performance reports e-mailed to each ICU.
audits.r2: EN adequacy 51.9% (calories) and 51.5% (protein); EN without PN 81.3%; EN within 48 h 66.8%.

audits.t: The role of education in the promotion of red reflex assessments.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: No referrals for abnormal red reflex
audits.c: Information posters sent to 200 GP practices and the local hospital, with referral pathways
audits.r2: 21 abnormal red reflex referrals over 18 months (18 GP, 3 neonatologists); 3 had a positive finding

audits.t: An audit of two methods of anticoagulation monitoring in a general practice.
audits.st: Not reported; measures were testing frequency, time in therapeutic range and mean INR
audits.f: Ad hoc GP-led warfarin adjustment; figures not reported.
audits.c: Change from ad hoc GP dose adjustment to a standardised nurse-led protocol.
audits.r2: Improved practice efficiency while maintaining anticoagulation control, with no significant increase in venesection frequency (figures not reported).

audits.t: Auditing psychiatric out-patient records.
audits.st: Letters to GPs inserted into the chart within one month
audits.f: 15% of charts had no letter; only 11% had the letter inserted within one month; electronic data also missing.

audits.t: A quality improvement initiative to improve adherence to national guidelines for empiric management of community-acquired pneumonia in emergency departments.
audits.st: Australian national guidelines for empiric community-acquired pneumonia management; documented pneumonia severity index use and concordant antibiotic prescribing
audits.f: Documented PSI use 30/518 (6%, 95% CI 4-8); practice varied and mostly discordant with guidelines.
audits.c: Drug use evaluation with academic detailing, group feedback presentations and prescribing prompts, in two intervention phases.

audits.t: A single-centre audit of junior doctors' diagnostic activity in medical admissions.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: In A&E 53% given a symptom as diagnosis, 18% wrong domain, 22% concordant with consultant; in AMU 20% symptom, 11% wrong domain, 45% concordant.

audits.t: Analysis of regional radiotherapy dosimetry audit data and recommendations for future audits.
audits.st: Audit protocol dosimetric tolerances
audits.f: Apart from minor resolved systematic errors, all audit results within protocol tolerances.

audits.t: Management of patients with diabetes mellitus referred for elective surgery from primary care: the challenge of the 18 weeks pathway.
audits.st: Glycaemic control optimisation before elective surgery (target not reported)
audits.f: Only 46 had HbA1c measured preoperatively and only 8 had a practice nurse review to optimise control.

audits.t: Radiological safety status and quality assurance audit of medical X-ray diagnostic installations in India.
audits.st: National regulatory safety code requirements (Atomic Energy Regulatory Board)
audits.f: Non-compliance: kVp inaccuracy 23%, radiation/optical field incongruence 23%, mA non-linearity 16%, timer 9%, improper collimator 19.6%, no warning light 29%, barriers without lead glass 14%.

audits.t: The national heart failure audit for England and Wales 2008-2009.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Echocardiograms in 75%; at discharge >90% loop diuretics, 80% ACE inhibitors or ARBs, 50% beta-blockers, 30% aldosterone antagonists; natriuretic peptides rarely measured.

audits.t: Determining the appropriate sleeve lobectomy versus pneumonectomy ratio in central non-small cell lung cancer patients: an audit of an aggressive policy of pneumonectomy avoidance.
audits.st: Proposed quality standard: pneumonectomy to sleeve lobectomy ratio below 1:1.5
audits.f: 21 (4%) pneumonectomies and 55 (11%) sleeve lobectomies; 5-year PN:SL ratio 1:2.6.

audits.t: An audit on the management of lymphogranuloma venereum in a sexual health clinic in London, UK.
audits.st: BASHH guidelines for LGV
audits.f: 56/63 (89%) episodes treated in accordance with guidelines; all eligible patients offered HIV test, but 10% and 29% not offered syphilis and hepatitis C tests respectively.

audits.t: An audit of the quality of referral letters received by the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Dublin Dental School and Hospital.
audits.st: SIGN 1998 recommendations for referral letters
audits.f: Referral letters in general required modification and did not give the required information.

audits.t: The impact of audit and feedback on nodal harvest in colorectal cancer.
audits.tp: Lymph node yield in colorectal cancer resection
audits.st: Adequate nodal harvest of 12 or more lymph nodes (quality indicator)
audits.f: Median nodal harvest 8; 719 (31%) had adequate harvest. Earlier audit (published 2002) found 22% adequate.
audits.c: Dissemination (presentation and publication) of a previous audit with feedback.
audits.r2: not reported separately (improvement over time, greater in the audited district)

audits.t: Improving the quality of general surgical operation notes in accordance with the Royal College of Surgeons guidelines: a prospective completed audit loop study.
audits.st: RCS England Good Surgical Practice 2008 (18 operation note items)
audits.f: Poor documentation of emergency/elective (36%), time (36%), date (87%), assistant (87%) and postoperative management (88%).
audits.c: Findings presented at clinical governance, surgeon education and theatre aide-memoires.
audits.r2: Clear improvement in four of five deficient areas, with compliance reaching almost 100%.

audits.t: Nursing monitoring and management of free and pedicled flaps--outcomes of teaching sessions on flap care.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Observational audit showed shortcomings in flap monitoring.
audits.c: Nursing teaching session, a universal flap monitoring chart and protocol, and a cartoon poster on the ward.

audits.t: Audit system on Quality of breast cancer diagnosis and Treatment (QT): results of quality indicators on screen-detected lesions in Italy, 2011-2012.
audits.st: Quality indicators for diagnosis and treatment of screen-detected breast lesions
audits.f: Good overall quality; sentinel node biopsy in almost 90% of screen-detected invasive cancers; waiting times worsening

audits.t: Chart Audit of Mammography in a Family Practice: How to improve screening rates with a chart audit and outreach.
audits.st: Mammography within 2 years for women aged 50 to 69
audits.f: Screening rate 49.2%.
audits.c: Outreach by mail and telephone to women without a mammogram.

audits.t: Optimization and audit of radiation dose during percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean dose area product before optimisation 66.16 Gy cm2 (single stent) and 122.68 Gy cm2 (multiple stents).
audits.c: Copper filters and optimal exposure parameters.
audits.r2: Mean DAP after optimisation 48.67 Gy cm2 (single) and 65.44 Gy cm2 (multiple); dose reduction 27-47%.

audits.t: Audit of budesonide/formoterol prescribing for asthma in community pharmacy in the U.K.
audits.tp: SABA overuse and MART in asthma
audits.st: UK product licence (summary of product characteristics) for Symbicort SMART
audits.f: 2.81% (70/2484) prescribed SMART as licensed; 7.44% (27/363) of 18-35 year olds.

audits.t: Audit and feedback: an intervention to improve discharge summary completion.
audits.st: 21-item discharge summary checklist
audits.f: All required data completed in 71%; admission section 70%, duration of hospitalisation 78%, discharge planning 18%, post-discharge care 57%.
audits.c: Individual 30-minute audit and feedback sessions with each fellow.
audits.r2: All required data completed in 91% (P < 0.001); admission 93%, duration 93%, discharge planning 93%, post-discharge care 83%.

audits.t: Audit of cases with uterine rupture: a process indicator of quality of obstetric care in Angola.
audits.st: Clinical estimation of avoidability of uterine rupture (criterion-based review)
audits.f: Prevalence of uterine rupture 4.9%; maternal case fatality 14%; early perinatal mortality 71%; uterotonic treatment in 36%; avoidability estimated at 65%.

audits.t: Use and wear of anti-embolism stockings: a clinical audit of surgical patients.
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines for fitting and wearing anti-embolism stockings
audits.f: 38.75% incorrect presentation; 29% wrong size; 70% received no information; 100% no written information; DVT risk not recorded in 82.5%; size not recorded in 100%; daily skin inspection 29%.

audits.t: Implementing the national invasive cervical cancer audit: correlation between local and regional classification.
audits.st: National invasive cervical cancer audit categories
audits.f: Agreement between local and regional classification in 52 cases (59.7%), kappa 0.51 (95% CI 0.39-0.63).

audits.t: Point-of-care, peer-comparator colonoscopy practice audit: The Canadian Association of Gastroenterology Quality Program--Endoscopy.
audits.st: Colonoscopy quality indicators including caecal intubation over 90% and withdrawal time at least 6 min
audits.f: Mean caecal intubation 94.9%; mean withdrawal time 8.8 min, but 41.9% of colonoscopists had mean withdrawal under 6 min; polypectomy in 37%.

audits.t: Medication prescribing errors pertaining to cardiovascular/antidiabetic medications: a prescription audit in primary care.
audits.st: Not stated; prescribing errors against accepted prescribing practice
audits.f: About one-quarter of prescriptions had errors; commonest was beta-blocker or thiazide with lipid-lowering drugs (8.0%); duplicate antihypertensives 2.2%; high-dose metformin in about 4% of diabetic hypertensives.

audits.t: Targeted thyroid testing in acute illness: achieving success through audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 53.8% of admissions had thyroid tests; appropriate indications documented in 43.9% of those with abnormal results; intervention documented in 25.5% and follow-up in 45.5%.
audits.c: Guidelines on indications for thyroid testing were issued.
audits.r2: Thyroid testing fell to 21.7% (p<0.001); appropriate indications documented in 73.7% of abnormal results (p=0.004); intervention documentation 92.9% and follow-up 85.7% (p=0.001).

audits.t: Lack of improvement after audit assessing the management of voiding dysfunction in patients with spinal cord injury: necessity for institutional guidelines.
audits.tp: Voiding dysfunction management in spinal cord injury
audits.st: Institutional practice; no standard guidelines exist
audits.f: Urodynamic studies 11%; urological consultation 26%; spontaneous voiding at follow-up 19.1%.
audits.r2: Urodynamic studies 1.75% (p = 0.045); urological consultation 31.58% (p = 0.452); spontaneous voiding 10.5%.

audits.t: Best medical therapy or wishful thinking in carotid disease? A single-centre audit in Germany.
audits.tp: Best medical therapy in carotid stenosis
audits.st: Best medical therapy for risk factors (lipids, diabetes, antithrombotics, blood pressure)
audits.f: 54% on statins, of whom 45% had LDL >100 mg/dl; other results truncated in abstract.

audits.t: Variability in the quality of rectal cancer care in public hospitals in Catalonia (Spain): clinical audit as a basis for action.
audits.st: Catalonian colorectal cancer guideline recommendations
audits.f: TME reported by surgeons in 46.4% and pathologists in 36.2%; preoperative radiotherapy in 52% of stage II and III patients.
