audits.t: Clinical audit of children with permanent tooth injuries treated at a dental hospital in Ireland.
audits.st: Published dental trauma guidelines on splinting duration and pulp extirpation
audits.f: Tendency to splint for longer than recommended in some avulsion, lateral luxation, subluxation and extrusion injuries; pulp extirpation for replanted teeth in keeping with recommendations.

audits.t: Postgraduate multidisciplinary development program: impact on the interpretation of pelvic MRI in patients with rectal cancer: a clinical audit in West Denmark.
audits.tp: Rectal cancer MRI staging report quality
audits.st: Expert reviewer reference standard for technical quality, reporting and interpretation
audits.f: 18% of scans of satisfactory technical quality before the course.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team course with on-site visits.
audits.r2: 74% of scans of satisfactory technical quality after the course.

audits.t: Multidisciplinary cancer care in Australia: a national audit highlights gaps in care and medico-legal risk for clinicians.
audits.st: Best practice and national recommendations for multidisciplinary cancer care
audits.f: Two-thirds of hospitals had no multidisciplinary team; of those with a team, one-third did not inform patients of discussion, half did not seek consent for all cases, one-quarter did not record the recommended plan in the notes.

audits.t: Implementation of best practice for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in an acute care setting.
audits.st: Four Joanna Briggs Institute best practice criteria
audits.f: Pre-implementation compliance gaps (figures not given).
audits.c: Audit-feedback-re-audit using JBI-PACES and GRiP to facilitate evidence-based nursing practice.
audits.r2: All four criteria 100% compliance at second follow-up audit.

audits.t: An audit of diagnostic reference levels in interventional cardiology and radiology: are there differences between academic and non-academic centres?
audits.tp: Diagnostic reference levels for radiation dose
audits.st: Diagnostic reference levels (dose-area product, fluoroscopy time, number of images)
audits.f: No difference for cardiology procedures; lower doses for lower-limb procedures in non-academic centres, with wide variation.

audits.t: Ten-year audit of melanoma in a central England population.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Incidence of melanoma more than doubled over 10 years and nearly tripled in thin melanomas (1 mm or less); thin melanomas diagnosed at a significantly younger age.

audits.t: Audit of emergency department assessment and management of patients presenting with community-acquired needle stick injuries.
audits.st: Appropriate assessment, prophylaxis and documentation after needlestick injury (standard not named)
audits.f: Source serology in 5 (12.82%); of 31 not immune to hepatitis B only 4 (12.90%) got vaccine plus immunoglobulin; 6 got HIV prophylaxis, 2 of them without baseline HIV test; 2 of 10 attended immunology follow-up.

audits.t: Privacy and dignity in a hospice environment-the development of a clinical audit.
audits.tp: Privacy and dignity in inpatient care
audits.st: Standards set from key documents on privacy and dignity
audits.f: 70% of patients rated privacy and dignity 'excellent' and 30% 'very good'; staff and patient ratings largely agreed and indicated achievement of the expected standard.

audits.t: Delivery of maternal health care in Indigenous primary care services: baseline data for an ongoing quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Maternal and child health care quality in primary care
audits.st: Recommended antenatal and postnatal protocols and procedures (investigations, gestational diabetes and GBS screening, brief interventions, follow-up)
audits.f: First antenatal visit in first trimester 34% to 49% by region; 46% of known smokers received cessation advice; 52% received antenatal education; 51% investigated for gestational diabetes.

audits.t: Effective quality improvement of thromboprophylaxis in acute medicine.
audits.st: Trust guideline on VTE in adult medical inpatients (2007)
audits.f: Guideline adherence 56%; lack of VTE risk assessment documentation.
audits.c: Guideline launched with education and feedback, IT intervention, verbal and written reminders, regular audit and process redesign.
audits.r2: Most patients received appropriate thromboprophylaxis but risk assessment documentation was poor.

audits.t: Laboratory quality improvement in Thailand's northernmost provinces.
audits.st: Thailand Medical Technology Council certification checklist (ten laboratory management areas)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Training and workshops, self-assessment against a standard checklist, distribution of quality documents, equipment calibration and peer internal audit.

audits.t: Current application of National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidance in the management of patients with severe psoriasis: a clinical audit against NICE guidance in seven National Health Service specialist dermatology units in England.
audits.st: NICE guidance on biological agents for psoriasis
audits.f: Biologics started for appropriately severe disease in 85% (n = 180) and after failure of standard systemics in 97% (n = 206) of 212 episodes; etanercept discontinued appropriately in responders before week 24 in 12% (5 of 60).

audits.t: Multicentre audit of inpatient management of acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: comparison with clinical guidelines.
audits.st: Clinical guidelines for COPD exacerbation management
audits.f: Spirometry performed in 34% of admissions (inter-hospital range 4-58%).

audits.t: A clinical audit of congenital thrombophilia investigation in tertiary practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: About 36% of APCR tests done while on anticoagulants; about 80% of low PC, PS or AT results likely from patients on anticoagulants; FVL heterozygote detection about 10%.

audits.t: A PCT-wide collaborative clinical audit selecting recall intervals for patients according to risk.
audits.st: Risk-based selection of recall intervals
audits.f: Retrospective audit of risk categorisation, appropriate recall and recall discussion (figures not stated).
audits.r2: Marked increase in risk assessments for caries, periodontal disease, oral cancer and NCTSL; recall more often based on risk and discussed with patient.

audits.t: Heparin infusion and haemorrhagic complications in patients treated with modified Blalock-Taussig shunt: significance of a nurse and medical audit.
audits.st: Institutional postoperative anticoagulation protocol
audits.f: Four patients (8.1%) had a haemorrhagic event, linked to heparin resistance treated with antithrombin III and increased heparin.
audits.c: Revised institutional anticoagulation protocol and combined medical and nursing screening protocol with a bleeding risk score.
audits.r2: Haemorrhagic complications reduced significantly (figures not reported).

audits.t: Ensuring evidence-based practices for falls prevention in a nursing home setting.
audits.st: Locally built evidence-based criteria (4 structure, 9 process)
audits.f: Baseline structure and falls prevention practices poor; 32 falls in 6 months before intervention.
audits.c: Audit and feedback, education and sensitisation, and changes in process and recording systems.
audits.r2: All structure criteria present and 8 of 9 process criteria improved significantly; 21 falls after intervention.

audits.t: An audit of the use of intra-septal local anaesthesia in a dental practice in the South of England.
audits.st: At least 70% find injection pain-free and at least 80% no pain during cavity preparation
audits.f: 69 (62%) pain-free injection (plus 23 (20%) very minor pain); 80 (71%) pain-free treatment (plus 18 (16%) very minor pain).

audits.t: Enhancing the quality of care for patients with breast cancer: seven years of experience with a Dutch auditing system.
audits.st: Dutch National Guideline for breast cancer; nine quality indicators including maximum waiting times
audits.f: Preoperative MDT discussion 56%, postoperative 70%; outpatient waiting time met 61%, diagnosis 82%, surgery 34%; successful sentinel node 69%.
audits.c: Intervention project in 2004 and 2005 to improve efficiency of diagnosis and surgical treatment.
audits.r2: Preoperative MDT 83%, postoperative 98%; waiting times 74%, 92% and 52%; sentinel node 92%; >10 nodes in ALND 85%; single operation 87%; discharge within 7 days 98%.

audits.t: The British HIV Association national audit on the management of subjects co-infected with HIV and hepatitis B/C.
audits.tp: HIV and hepatitis C coinfection management
audits.st: BHIVA guidelines for management of HIV and hepatitis B/C co-infection
audits.f: About a third of sites did not re-check hepatitis serology or vaccination titres annually; 122 (13%) patients neither vaccinated nor immune to hepatitis A; 26 (5%) with hepatitis C not immune to hepatitis B; 25 (6%) HBsAg-positive on lamivudine as sole anti-HBV drug.

audits.t: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis guideline implementation is improved by nurse directed feedback and audit.
audits.st: Australian and New Zealand Working Party on the Management and Prevention of VTE recommendations
audits.f: 37.9% of high-risk patients received appropriate thromboprophylaxis (82.2% were high risk).
audits.r2: 54.1% of high-risk patients received appropriate prophylaxis (absolute improvement 16%; 95% CI 11.7%, 20.5%; OR 1.96, 1.62-2.37).

audits.t: Multiple sclerosis, from referral to confirmed diagnosis: an audit of clinical practice.
audits.st: NICE: 6 weeks from referral to neurology consultation, then 6 weeks to diagnosis of MS
audits.f: 93 (78%) seen within 6 weeks of referral; 63 (53%) received final diagnosis within 6 weeks of first visit, 57 (48%) delayed.

audits.t: Clinical audit of antenatal service provision in Nigeria.
audits.st: Recommended antenatal care components (standard not named)
audits.f: Weight checked 97.3%, blood pressure 95.1%, urine 86.3%; haemoglobin 19.2%; two tetanus toxoid doses 34.8%; malaria prophylaxis 72.1%; iron and folate 80.3%.

audits.t: Feasibility of audit and feedback to reduce postoperative urinary catheter duration.
audits.st: Not stated; mean postoperative catheter duration
audits.f: Mean catheter duration 1.7 days (orthopaedic surgery) and 2.6 days (general surgery).
audits.c: Audit and feedback of catheter duration to nurses during an educational session.

audits.t: Seeking solutions: scaling-up audit as a quality improvement tool for infection control in Gujarat, India.
audits.st: CDC guidelines for surgical site infection prevention
audits.f: Baseline surgical site infection rate 30%.
audits.c: Surveillance and hospital epidemiology, practice reforms and monthly and annual review meetings.
audits.r2: 88% decrease in infection rate in the surgical unit; 67% reduction after department-wide roll-out.

audits.t: British Thoracic Society adult community acquired pneumonia audit 2009/10.
audits.st: BTS Guidelines for the management of community acquired pneumonia in adults (2009) and local CAP guidelines
audits.f: Initial empirical antibiotics in accordance with local guidelines in 1478 (55.5%); chest x-ray within 4 hours in 83% and first antibiotic dose within 4 hours in 58%.

audits.t: Compliance of antithrombotic management at a tertiary paediatric hospital with international guidelines: a 100-Day audit.
audits.st: ACCP paediatric antithrombotic therapy guidelines
audits.f: 5885 administrations; complete adherence to ACCP indication and dosing in 2915 (49.5%).

audits.t: A hospital-site controlled intervention using audit and feedback to implement guidelines concerning inappropriate treatment of catheter-associated asymptomatic bacteriuria.
audits.st: Guidelines recommending neither screening for nor treating asymptomatic bacteriuria in most catheterised patients
audits.f: not reported (protocol)
audits.c: 12 months of individualised audit and feedback plus guideline distribution, then 12 months of unit-level feedback.

audits.t: Impact of a care pathway in acute pancreatitis.
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for management of acute pancreatitis
audits.f: Previous region-wide audit: abdominal imaging within 24 h 35.2%, severity stratification within 48 h 28.7%, critical care admission for severe cases 39.3%, definitive treatment during index admission 22.2%.
audits.c: Simple written care pathway for acute pancreatitis introduced.
audits.r2: Imaging within 24 h 47.7%, severity stratification within 48 h 75%, critical care admission for severe 63.6%, definitive treatment during index admission 38.5%.

audits.t: Diabetes care: is it adequate?--An audit of diabetes care in a hospital.
audits.st: Adequate diabetes care (standard not named)
audits.f: Only 9% had good glycaemic control; 39% hypertriglyceridaemia; 65% undesirable weight gain; 12% retinopathy; 61% had weekly hypoglycaemia.

audits.t: Antibiotic screening of urine culture as a useful quality audit.
audits.st: Accurate antibiotic history on urine culture request forms
audits.f: Antibiotic assay: 97.32% true-negative, 0.04% false-negative, 1.51% true-positive, 1.13% false-positive; sensitivity 97.37%, specificity 98.85%.

audits.t: An Australian audit of ED pain management patterns.
audits.tp: Time to analgesia in the emergency department
audits.st: Timely and appropriate pain management as an ED quality indicator
audits.f: Triage pain score documented in 547 (56.4%); 1473 (74.9%) of those in pain received analgesia; 644 (32.7%) opioid; median time to analgesia 70 minutes (IQR 58 to 92).

audits.t: Improving influenza vaccination of healthcare workers by means of quality improvement tools.
audits.st: Target not stated; authors note a rate above 80% was not achieved
audits.f: Vaccination rate 58.8%.
audits.c: Leadership support, vaccine kits, grand rounds, influenza website, screensaver, e-mails, phone messages and audit feedback.

audits.t: An audit of the contraception service offered to teenagers attending Scottish genitourinary medicine clinics in 2007.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 553 assessable women, 280 (50.6%) needed contraceptive advice and 156 (56%) of these received it.

audits.t: Effective use of an audit tool devised to optimize the management of syphilis in an integrated sexual health clinic.
audits.st: BASHH syphilis guideline auditable outcomes (baseline VDRL 100%; treatment completion 95%; contacts attending 60%)
audits.f: All patients had baseline VDRL (target 100%); 97% completed treatment (target 95%); 100% of contactable partners attended (target 60%); 50 (60%) showed response to treatment.

audits.t: An analysis of the regulatory program of quality audits in radiotherapy in Brazil from 1995 to 2007.
audits.st: IAEA dosimetry protocols TRS 277 and TRS 398; national radiological protection requirements
audits.f: Dose deviation within ±3% for 67.6% of Co-60 units and 79.6% of linear accelerators; above 5% in 13.9% of Co-60 and 10.8% of linac facilities.

audits.t: Improving the interaction between the ophthalmology and histopathology departments.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Request form completion reviewed (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Redesigned ophthalmic histopathology request form circulated.
audits.r2: Improved completion of important sections of the form.

audits.t: [Assessment of targeted clinical audit in suicide attempt].
audits.st: Anaes 16 criteria for care after suicide attempt; 100% target
audits.f: Patient assessment, somatic examination and coordination met 100% in more than half of wards; sociofamily evaluation, after-care and follow-up monitoring below 50% in more than half of wards.
audits.c: 29 interventions including better coordination and communication, protocol design, reminders and information tools.
audits.r2: Modest, mixed changes: only one criterion reached 100% in one ward; conformity fell in nine cases (mean -23%) and rose in 16 (+19%).

audits.t: Safety and efficacy of warfarin in paediatric patients with prosthetic cardiac valves: a retrospective audit.
audits.st: INR within target therapeutic range
audits.f: 44.0% of INR tests within target range; out-of-range tests twice as likely to be subtherapeutic; no thrombotic events and 3 major bleeds.

audits.t: Changes in NHS organization of care and management of hospital admissions with COPD exacerbations between the national COPD audits of 2003 and 2008.
audits.st: National COPD audit processes of care and organisation of care
audits.f: 2003 national COPD audit baseline (up to 60 consecutive admissions per unit); detailed figures not stated in abstract.
audits.c: Improvements in resources and organisation of care between audit rounds
audits.r2: Adjusted inpatient mortality (P = 0.05) and 90-day mortality (P = 0.001) reduced; more patients discharged under a respiratory specialist.

audits.t: Rate of postdates induction using first-trimester ultrasound to determine estimated due date: Wellington Regional Hospital audit.
audits.st: Postdates induction only at 41 weeks or more
audits.f: 50 (15.2%) induced for postdates were not 41 weeks or more by PIMS due date; 43 of 158 (27%) with first-trimester scans had revised dating (text truncated).

audits.t: The prevention and management of constipation in older adults in a residential aged care facility.
audits.st: Evidence-based standards of care for constipation (Joanna Briggs Institute PACES)
audits.f: Baseline audit (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Action plan implemented through audit and feedback
audits.r2: Real improvement in practice relating to constipation (figures not given).

audits.t: Improving the oral health of older adults with dementia/cognitive impairment living in a residential aged care facility.
audits.st: JBI best practice criteria for oral hygiene care
audits.f: Baseline compliance (figures not given).
audits.c: Strategic change-management plan by a project team targeting specific criteria.
audits.r2: Denture marking compliance increased significantly; documentation of denture cleaning and night-time removal increased slightly (not significant).

audits.t: Advance care planning for residents in aged care facilities: what is best practice and how can evidence-based guidelines be implemented?
audits.st: Five JBI audit criteria based on 'Guidelines for a Palliative Approach in Residential Aged Care'
audits.f: Compliance 0% for all five criteria.
audits.c: Programme to implement advance care planning via audit, feedback and JBI-PACES; staff preparation and resident support to discuss and document wishes.

audits.t: Are we providing the best possible pain management for our elderly patients in the acute-care setting?
audits.st: Relevant pain management standards of practice (not specified)
audits.f: 78% had a documented pain assessment in previous 24 h, but 83% of these were only a general comment; 62% had no analgesia 1 h before mobilising or significant dressing.
audits.c: Education sessions and introduction of the Abbey Pain Scale.
audits.r2: Increased staff awareness; Abbey Pain Scale used well and prompted pain assessment (figures not given).

audits.t: Benefits of implementing an interdisciplinary and multifactorial strategy to falls prevention in a rural, residential aged-care facility.
audits.st: JBI best practice criteria for interdisciplinary multifactorial falls prevention
audits.f: Baseline compliance (figures not given).
audits.r2: Positive effect on audit criteria (figures not given).

audits.t: Improving the fundamentals of care for older people in the acute hospital setting: facilitating practice improvement using a Knowledge Translation Toolkit.
audits.tp: Fundamentals of nursing care for older inpatients
audits.st: Specific evidence-based guidelines for care of older people; locally developed standards
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Structured facilitation programme (Knowledge Translation Toolkit) with education, support and quality improvement tools.
audits.r2: Small improvements in care were shown; results varied from clarifying issues to reducing functional decline.

audits.t: Clinical audit on documentation of anticipatory "not for resuscitation" orders in a tertiary Australian teaching hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Prognosis documented in 40%; palliative care offered to two-thirds with NFR; CPR process and outcomes mostly undocumented; under 50% showed the NFR reason matched patient choices.

audits.t: Patient information in otorhinolaryngology: a prospective audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Written patient information not routine; recall of majority of complications 24%
audits.c: Departmental drive towards provision of written patient information leaflets
audits.r2: 64% received written information; recall of majority of complications 52%

audits.t: Aseptic insertion of central venous lines to reduce bacteraemia.
audits.st: Aseptic central line insertion bundle (clinician and patient bundles) recorded on a checklist
audits.f: Compliance with aseptic insertion improved significantly (figures truncated in abstract).
audits.c: Collaborative quality improvement with a central line insertion checklist and bundles.

audits.t: Sedation in a radiology department--do radiologists follow their own guidelines?
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists 2003 sedation guidelines
audits.f: Low awareness of guidelines and variable practice on fasting and drug order.
audits.r2: Some improvements; persisting deviation on fasting and giving opiate before benzodiazepine; trend towards shorter acting benzodiazepines.

audits.t: Bile vomiting in paediatrics: what do we really know?
audits.st: Correct identification of bile vomit (dark green) and its significance (intestinal obstruction)
audits.f: 41% of nurses selected yellow as the colour of bile; 33% identified intestinal obstruction as the cause of bile vomiting.
audits.r2: 18% of nurses selected yellow, approximately 70% selected dark green; 64% identified intestinal obstruction as the cause.

audits.t: Surgical margin status among men with organ-confined (pT2) prostate cancer: a population-based study.
audits.tp: Positive surgical margins after radical prostatectomy
audits.st: Not stated; province-wide positive margin rate for pT2 disease
audits.f: Median positive surgical margin rate 33% (range 0-100%); no significant volume-margin association.

audits.t: Introducing random safety audits (RSA) in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).
audits.tp: Infection prevention and control in neonatal units
audits.st: Unit guidelines on hygiene, safe prescribing and oxygen saturation limits; Medical Practitioners Act 2007 documentation requirements
audits.f: Oxygen pulse oximetry guideline compliance 4/27 (15%); hygiene 80%-100% and prescribing 86%-100%.
audits.r2: Oxygen monitoring compliance improved to 9/16 (56%); hygiene and prescribing reached 25/25 (100%).

audits.t: Are primary care practitioners in Barbados following diabetes guidelines? - a chart audit with comparison between public and private care sectors.
audits.st: Diabetes guideline processes of care and quality targets for BP, fasting blood glucose and HbA1c
audits.f: not reported in full (125 public and 127 private charts; metformin 66%, sulphonylurea 68%, statin 25%, insulin 21%, aspirin 15%)

audits.t: Factors associated with a clinician's offer of screening HIV-positive patients for sexually transmitted infections, including syphilis.
audits.tp: Sexual health care for people living with HIV
audits.st: Quality Improvement Scotland standards: HIV-positive patients offered annual STI screen and six-monthly syphilis testing
audits.f: 64% offered STI screens and 69% offered syphilis testing.

audits.t: Health Alliance for prudent antibiotic prescribing in patients with respiratory tract infections (HAPPY AUDIT) -impact of a non-randomised multifaceted intervention programme.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported as baseline rates in abstract (440 GPs registered consultations)
audits.c: Individual prescriber feedback, training courses, clinical guidelines, waiting-room posters, patient brochures and point-of-care tests (Strep A and CRP).
audits.r2: Lower RTI prescribing fell by 42% in Lithuania, 25% in Russia, 25% in Spain, 9% in Argentina; upper RTI by 20%, 15%, 9% and 5%.
audits.co: Denmark, Sweden, Lithuania, Russia, Spain, Argentina

audits.t: Difficulties for the detection of positive signs of sacroiliitis in spondyloarthritides by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in everyday clinical practice. Results from an audit circle (audit and re-audit).
audits.tp: MRI requesting and reporting in axial spondyloarthritis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of handover in an ENT unit.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidance on handover
audits.f: Morning handover present and complete on 77% of days (absent 17%); evening handover present and complete on 30% of days (absent 67%).
audits.c: Team emphasis on handover, RCS guidance reminder placed in handover book, regular feedback to junior doctors
audits.r2: Substantial improvement in quality and completeness of written handover (figures not stated in abstract).

audits.t: Vaccination against hepatitis B in an HIV outpatients' department: an audit against national vaccination guidelines.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B vaccination in sexual health and HIV
audits.st: BHIVA immunisation guidelines 2004 and 2008; target 95% completing hepatitis B vaccination
audits.f: 67% of patients needing vaccination received a full course; 33% managed according to BHIVA guidelines overall.
audits.c: Hepatitis B vaccination record sheet in the notes
audits.r2: Completion rate 79%; 61% managed according to BHIVA guidelines overall.

audits.t: Clinical audit: a useful tool for reducing severe postpartum haemorrhages?
audits.st: Explicit criteria for recommended procedures in severe postpartum haemorrhage
audits.f: Severe PPH prevalence 1.52% of deliveries (level III) and 2.08% (level II).
audits.c: Quarterly criteria-based clinical audit meetings reviewing all severe PPH cases with feedback to all staff.

audits.t: Chronic hepatitis B - a clinical audit of GP management.
audits.st: Prevailing guidelines for chronic hepatitis B management and monitoring
audits.f: HBV DNA results recorded in 24%.
audits.c: Education of GPs on the guidelines.
audits.r2: HBV DNA recorded in 63%; 29% monitored at recommended intervals and 47% managed according to guidelines.

audits.t: Improving recording of capacity to consent and explanation of medication side effects in a psychiatric service for people with learning disability: audit findings.
audits.st: Recording of capacity to consent to treatment and documentation of side-effect explanation
audits.f: Capacity recorded in 30% of case notes.
audits.c: Rubber stamp in case notes introduced in 2008 as a visual prompt
audits.r2: Capacity recorded in 51% (P = 0.000006); capacity more likely recorded when stamp present (OR 13.5, p < 0.0001).

audits.t: A national audit of pollen immunotherapy for children in the United Kingdom: patient selection and programme safety.
audits.st: National guidelines on patient selection for specific immunotherapy (exclusion of asthmatic children)
audits.f: 55% of patients had asthma; 75.6% of asthmatics on SCIT were at BTS/SIGN step 2 or above; national guidance to exclude asthmatic children not followed by most centres.

audits.t: Post-operative nausea and vomiting following paediatric day-case tonsillectomy: audit of the Epsom protocol.
audits.tp: Postoperative nausea and vomiting prevention in tonsillectomy
audits.st: Epsom protocol previously reported PONV rate 2% and same-day discharge 100%
audits.f: No post-operative nausea or vomiting on day of surgery and no delayed discharges.

audits.t: An Australian audit of vaccination status in children and adolescents with inflammatory bowel disease.
audits.st: Current Australian vaccination guidelines for children with IBD (routine plus pneumococcal and influenza)
audits.f: Routine immunisations up to date in 90% (38/42); pneumococcal booster 5% (5/101); ever had influenza vaccine 10% (10/101).

audits.t: Use of audit and feedback with fluorescent targeting to achieve rapid improvements in room cleaning in the intensive care unit and ward settings.
audits.st: Thorough cleaning of high-touch surfaces measured by fluorescent targeting
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Audit and feedback to cleaning staff using fluorescent targeting.
audits.r2: Rapid improvements in cleaning thoroughness (figures not reported).

audits.t: Remifentanil patient-controlled analgesia for labour: a complete audit cycle.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: A prospective audit of the quality of documentation of gynaecological operations.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidelines on operation note documentation
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Standardised operation note proforma based on RCS England guidelines.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in documentation with the proforma (no figures given in abstract).

audits.t: An audit of the caries status of patients about to start orthodontic treatment.
audits.st: HSE guidelines that all caries needs are addressed before orthodontic treatment; gold standard adopted from a similar UK audit
audits.f: 42% of patients had caries in permanent teeth requiring restoration (48.9% of males, 35.3% of females), failing the gold standard.

audits.t: An audit of dental prescriptions between clinics and dental laboratories.
audits.st: Ethical and legal guidelines for dental laboratory prescriptions
audits.f: Two-thirds of prescriptions were non-compliant.

audits.t: Diagnostic workup of paediatric patients with inflammatory bowel disease in Europe: results of a 5-year audit of the EUROKIDS registry.
audits.st: ESPGHAN Porto criteria: OGD, ileocolonoscopy and small-bowel imaging
audits.f: Both OGD and ileocolonoscopy in 64% overall, rising from 52% in year 1 to 71% in year 5.

audits.t: UK Renal Registry 13th Annual Report (December 2010): Chapter 10: calcium, phosphate, parathyroid hormone, bicarbonate and total cholesterol concentrations amongst patients receiving haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis in England, Wales and Northern Ireland in 2009: national and centre-specific analyses.
audits.tp: CKD-mineral bone disorder management in dialysis
audits.st: UK Renal Association clinical performance measures: phosphate 1.1-1.8 mmol/L, adjusted calcium 2.2-2.5 mmol/L, PTH 16-32 pmol/L, bicarbonate
audits.f: Phosphate in range: 61% HD, 70% PD; calcium in range: 74% HD, 75% PD; PTH in range: 28% HD, 32% PD; bicarbonate measure met: 72% HD, 83% PD.

audits.t: POMHS 9b - antipsychotic prescribing in people with a learning disability.
audits.st: POMH-UK 9b: indication documented (Deb 2006); continuing need reviewed at least annually (Deb 2006); annual side-effect review including EPS and 4 aspects of metabolic syndrome (NICE CG82, 2009)
audits.f: Standard 1 100%; Standard 2 over 90%; Standard 3 lower than at re-audit (figures not given).
audits.r2: Standard 1 maintained 100%; Standard 2 over 90%; Standard 3 improved from baseline.

audits.t: Re-audit of physical examination on admission.
audits.tp: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
audits.st: 90% of patients to have a full physical examination within 72 hours of admission
audits.f: Previous audit: results slightly worse than re-audit (figures not given).
audits.r2: 58% had a brief physical examination and 43% a full physical examination on admission; 65% had a full examination by 72 hours.

audits.t: Compliance with ECT NICE guidance by the John Connolly ECT clinic: January 2010 - July 2010.
audits.st: NICE ECT TA59 (2003) and depression guidance CG90 (2009)
audits.f: Good compliance on indications for ECT and prior adequate treatment trial; poor documentation of risk-benefit discussion and poor post-ECT and ongoing cognitive assessment. No reason for stopping ECT documented in 3 patients.
audits.c: ECT Care Pathway document produced and introduced; re-audit planned.

audits.t: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) treatment experience in Bedford East - audit and reaudit.
audits.st: NICE guidelines for PTSD treatment
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Increase in identification of PTSD patients; many drug treatments used were outside NICE guidelines; less availability of psychological therapy than expected.

audits.t: Audit of antipsychotic prescribing in dementia: Cambridgeshire results and lessons learnt.
audits.st: NICE recommendations on antipsychotics for BPSD (severe symptoms, counselling, risk-benefit analysis, regular review)
audits.f: 9 (13.4%) prescribed antipsychotics for BPSD; risk-benefit analysis recorded in 6 and discussion with family or carers in 5; 3 of 4 on treatment over 3 months had two or more reviews.

audits.t: Unmet needs in patients with epilepsy, following audit, educational intervention and the introduction of the New General Practice Contract.
audits.st: New General Practice Contract epilepsy quality indicators (annual review, seizure frequency documentation)
audits.f: Baseline annual review and seizure frequency documentation (figures not stated); 22% under shared care.
audits.c: Letter summarising findings, comprehensive template, individual patient categorisation, neurologist-led educational session (March 2004) and New Contract (April 2004)
audits.r2: Significant, sustained increase in annual review rate and documentation of seizure frequency; shared care fell to 16%.

audits.t: British HIV Association national audit on the management of patients co-infected with tuberculosis and HIV.
audits.st: BHIVA recommended practice; chief medical officer targets of 85% TB therapy completion and 65% culture confirmation
audits.f: TB therapy completion fell short of the 85% CMO target; culture confirmation of pulmonary TB met the 65% target; many positive smear results unacceptably delayed.

audits.t: Audit of antibiotic therapy used in 66 cases of endocarditis.
audits.st: 2004 European Society of Cardiology endocarditis guidelines (drug, dose, route, interval and duration)
audits.f: Antibiotic therapy complied with guidelines in 14%; single daily gentamicin in 55% (27/49); unnecessary rifampicin in 72% (18/25); excess gentamicin duration in 32% (9/28).

audits.t: A clinical audit of the management of patients with a tracheostomy in an Australian tertiary hospital intensive care unit: Focus on speech-language pathology.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Speech-language pathology involved in 78%, initial assessment mean 14 days after tracheostomy; median time to phonation 12 days, to oral intake 15 days; 20% spoke within 1 week.

audits.t: An audit of cervicovaginal cytology in a teaching hospital: Are atypical glandular cells under-recognised on cytological screening?
audits.st: Accepted cervical cytology quality indices and cytohistological correlation
audits.f: 98.14% negative, 1.36% unsatisfactory; ASCUS:SIL ratio 0.5; ten significant cytohistological discrepancies.

audits.t: A prospective audit of transfusion requests in a tertiary care hospital for the use of fresh frozen plasma.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 573 (69.8%) requests (2,202 units, 75.54%) appropriate; 248 (30.2%) inappropriate.

audits.t: Surgical cancellations: a review of elective surgery cancellations in a tertiary care pediatric institution.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Illness was the leading cause of cancellation; otolaryngology had most cancellations.
audits.c: Nursing practice changes in the preoperative assessment clinic (details not reported).
audits.r2: Illness remained the leading cause of cancellation.

audits.t: [Lessons and impact of two audits on postpartum hemorrhages in 24 maternity hospitals of the network "Sécurité Naissance - Naître Ensemble" in "Pays-de-la-Loire" area].
audits.st: CNGOF guidelines and HAS 2004 criteria for postpartum haemorrhage
audits.f: Time of PPH noted 66%; specific monitoring sheet 0%; blood loss noted 51%; sulprostone within 30 minutes 53%; decision within 2 hours 47%.
audits.c: Corrective actions: specific monitoring sheet, recording blood loss, transfusion on clinical criteria, earlier sulprostone, agreements with visceral surgery and avoiding maternal transfers.
audits.r2: Management compliance 81%; time of PPH noted 85%; monitoring sheet 87%; blood loss noted 67%; sulprostone within 30 minutes 58%; decision within 2 hours 69%.

audits.t: Hip resurfacing revision rates: radiological audit of risk factors.
audits.st: Cup inclination angle of 60 degrees or more and varus stem shaft angle as revision risk thresholds
audits.f: Mean CIA 47.6 degrees; 34% had CIA over 50 degrees and 13% over 60 degrees; mean SSA 1.4 degrees varus with 67% varus.

audits.t: An audit of the variability of diagnosis and management of gout in the rheumatology setting: the gout evaluation and management study.
audits.st: EULAR recommendations for gout diagnosis and management
audits.f: Diagnostic recommendations adherence 26.0% (crystal-proven diagnosis 26%); comorbidity evaluation 50.6%; acute flare management 100%; lifestyle 71.4%; urate-lowering therapy 52.1%.

audits.t: New Zealand National Acute Stroke Services Audit 2009: organisation of acute stroke services in New Zealand.
audits.st: Organised acute stroke unit care (international benchmarks, compared with Australia)
audits.f: Only 8 DHBs had stroke units; 39% of patients managed in a stroke unit on audit day (Australia 51%); 64% in DHBs with stroke units.

audits.t: Towards the development of integrated epilepsy services: an audit of documented epilepsy care.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Neurologist confirmation of diagnosis documented in 132 (35%); 282 (75%) had no documented specialist review; 149 (40%) not reviewed by GP for epilepsy in previous two years.

audits.t: The Second Stroke Audit of Catalonia shows improvements in many, but not all quality indicators.
audits.st: 13 evidence-based stroke performance measures (Catalan stroke guidelines)
audits.f: tPA 2.8%; stroke unit admission 16.6%; seven-day mortality 9.5%.
audits.c: Delivery of stroke guidelines between audits.
audits.r2: tPA 5.9%; stroke unit admission 22.6%; seven-day mortality 6.8%; seven measures improved.

audits.t: Preventing perioperative complications in the patient with a high body mass index.
audits.tp: Perioperative care of patients with obesity
audits.st: Local policy: BMI documented on surgery schedule and preoperative checklist
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Task force developed policies and procedures for morbidly obese patients after two sentinel events.
audits.r2: BMI on surgery schedule in 92% and on preoperative checklist in 94%.

audits.t: Co-cyprindiol prescribing in a large, rural general practice in England.
audits.st: MHRA guidelines and licence for co-cyprindiol use
audits.f: 26 individuals prescribed co-cyprindiol; 30.7% of prescriptions met MHRA guidelines. Acne was the most common indication (69%).
audits.c: Prescribers contacted and sent the MHRA guideline; all patients invited for review.
audits.r2: 12 individuals prescribed co-cyprindiol; 75% of prescriptions met guidelines.

audits.t: Measuring the quality of end of life management in patients with advanced kidney disease: results from the pan-Thames renal audit group.
audits.st: Quality markers of good end of life management
audits.f: Many aspects of good end of life care under-achieved; 69% of deaths were inpatient, 36% of these 'unexpected', with quality markers significantly less likely to be achieved in unexpected deaths.

audits.t: Do GP referral guidelines really work? Audit of an electronic urgent referral system for suspected head and neck cancer.
audits.tp: Head and neck cancer two-week-wait pathway
audits.st: 2002 Scottish Referral Guidelines for suspected head and neck cancer (alarm symptoms)
audits.f: Overall poor compliance with referral guidelines; 15 of 190 (8%) diagnosed with SCCHN.

audits.t: From prevention to nursing home care: a comprehensive national audit of stroke care.
audits.st: Stroke care from prevention to long-term care
audits.f: Substantial deficits in primary prevention, emergency assessment and treatment, discharge planning, rehabilitation, secondary prevention and communication.

audits.t: Improving the rate of preschool vision screening: an interrupted time-series analysis.
audits.st: Vision screening for children aged 3 to 5 (distance vision and stereopsis testing)
audits.f: Distance vision testing 92%; stereopsis testing 80%.
audits.c: Clinic training in vision screening and clinic champions giving feedback from monthly chart audits.
audits.r2: Distance vision testing 97% (other results truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Managing chlamydia infections in young men: results from an audit of a public men's clinic in New York City.
audits.st: Not stated; timely treatment, partner management and retesting for reinfection
audits.f: 99% treated, 81% within 14 days; 65% had no documented partner management; of 34% with a later visit only 36% retested.

audits.t: Developing quality indicators for genitourinary medicine services with patient and public involvement: an audit of performance against proposed local measures.
audits.st: Local service quality indicators developed with patient and public involvement
audits.f: All measures were achieved, almost achieved or probably achieved.

audits.t: Paediatric day-case tonsillectomy: a three-year prospective audit spiral in a district hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Haemorrhage rate 2.6% over three years; nausea and vomiting in 5.3%.

audits.t: Implementation of new recommendations for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes: a 5-month audit.
audits.st: International recommendations for gestational diabetes diagnosis (75 g OGTT, fasting glucose threshold 5.1 mmol/L)
audits.f: 98.3% performed the correct (two-step) protocol.
audits.c: Implementation of new diagnostic criteria (one-step 75 g OGTT).
audits.r2: 77.0% performed the correct protocol; 38 (15.1%) 75 g OGTTs positive.

audits.t: Improving utilization of antimicrobial drugs among physician assistants in the ED.
audits.st: Current guidelines for antimicrobial prescribing
audits.f: Appropriate prescriptions 64% (95% CI 58-72); inappropriate 36%.
audits.c: One-hour academic detailing with audit and feedback for each physician assistant.

audits.t: Ensuring successful admission to hospital for young people with learning difficulties, autism and challenging behaviour: a continuous quality improvement and change management programme.
audits.tp: Hospital admission for children with autism
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Audit of family and staff experiences of admission (no figures given).
audits.c: Checklist on behaviour and communication incorporated into pre-admission planning, with a team member allocated to ensure the care plan is followed.
audits.r2: Vastly improved patient experience from family and staff perspective (no figures given).

audits.t: Audit of informed consent practice within a Community Mental Health Team.
audits.st: Expected standards for informed consent documentation
audits.f: Baseline standard of informed consent documentation in letters to GPs (figures not stated).
audits.r2: Documentation of risks increased by 36% (P 0.0017), benefits by 56%, risks and benefits of no treatment by 52%, side-effects by 25% and written material by 28%.

audits.t: Explicit review of risperidone long-acting injection prescribing practice.
audits.st: Best practice recommendations for RLAI (indication, initiation, dose, co-prescribing)
audits.f: 72% had prior oral risperidone; 81.9% started on 25 mg/2 weeks; 93.3% had crossover; antipsychotic co-prescribing ongoing at 12 months in 12.3%.

audits.t: Psoriasis consultation audit: a two-centre study.
audits.st: Record-keeping criteria defined with a peer group of 60 British dermatologists
audits.f: Similar record keeping at both centres; non-consultant staff completed records more fully; poor communication to GPs after clinic default at both centres.

audits.t: Putting guidelines into practice: a tailored multi-modal approach to improve post-operative assessments.
audits.st: SIGN Postoperative Management in Adults (2004)
audits.f: 27 (37%) assessed within 4 hours; 15 (21%) individual reviews; 23 (32%) reviewed due to nursing concerns. Documentation of PMH 2 (3%), medications 1 (1%), allergies 0, complications 8 (11%), post-operative instructions 26 (36%).
audits.c: Staff education, designated HDU bleeps and a post-operative assessment proforma.
audits.r2: 46 (74%) assessed within 4 hours; 38 (61%) individual reviews; 1 (2%) due to nursing concerns. Documentation of PMH 18 (29%), medications 28 (45%), allergies 20 (32%), complications 18 (29%), instructions 55 (89%).

audits.t: Guidelines reduce time to consultation for a liaison psychiatry service in an Irish teaching hospital.
audits.st: Locally introduced guidelines for time from referral to consultation
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Introduction of guidelines for time to consultation.
audits.r2: Significant reduction in time to consultation (chi-squared = 43.84).

audits.t: An audit of hypertension at university health center in oman.
audits.st: Recording of care items in a pre-designed structured form
audits.f: Age, gender, blood pressure, renal function and lipids recorded in >75%; pertinent symptoms and smoking history poorly recorded.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in documentation of pertinent symptoms.

audits.t: Implementation and evaluation of a network-based pilot program to improve palliative care in the intensive care unit.
audits.st: Time-triggered processes: decision maker, advance directive and CPR preferences by Day 1; social work and spiritual support by Day 3; family meeting by Day 5
audits.f: Pre-intervention rates not reported.
audits.c: Auditing, performance feedback, improvement tools, education and monthly nurse team meetings.
audits.r2: Social work and spiritual support offers, identification of medical decision maker and family meeting documentation improved significantly (figures not reported).

audits.t: Urgent suspected cancer referrals from general practice: audit of compliance with guidelines and referral outcomes.
audits.st: Agreed national urgent suspected cancer referral guidelines
audits.f: Compliance with referral guidelines was 90.9%.

audits.t: Management of acute coronary syndromes at hospital discharge: do targeted educational interventions improve practice quality?
audits.tp: Secondary prevention after acute coronary syndrome
audits.st: Evidence-based ACS guidelines (discharge medications, cardiac rehabilitation referral, communication)
audits.f: All four recommended medications 57%; short-acting nitrates 56%; cardiac rehabilitation referral 57%.
audits.c: Educational meetings, academic detailing, point-of-care reminders and feedback of baseline results.
audits.r2: All four medications 69%; nitrates 68%; cardiac rehabilitation referral 68% (all p<.0001).

audits.t: Non-medical prescribing: audit, practice and views.
audits.st: UK Standards for non-medical prescribing adopted by the mental health service
audits.f: 83% of non-medical prescribers responded; UK Standards were met by the majority, but there was a shortfall in uptake of training and supervision.

audits.t: Monitoring and documentation of side effects from depot antipsychotic medication: an interdisciplinary audit of practice in a regional mental health service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Most had an annual documented medical review and prescription; injection site condition documented in 5 (8%); site alternation in 28 (47%); no written consent to treatment in any; no information on depot and side effects documented in 57 (95%).
audits.c: A standardised checklist was developed to be introduced by all teams (not yet re-audited).

audits.t: Province wide clinical governance network for clinical audit for quality improvement in endometrial cancer management.
audits.st: Common shared evidence-based provincial guidelines; process indicators
audits.f: Pre-guideline: diagnostic hysteroscopy 53%; MRI use 8.1%, MRI accuracy 37.3%; laparoscopy 1.6%; early surgical complications 16%; radiotherapy 14.%.
audits.c: Inter-hospital multidisciplinary oncology group wrote common evidence-based guidelines via clinical audit.
audits.r2: Post-guideline: hysteroscopy 74%; MRI use 35.3%, accuracy 74.7%; laparoscopy 18.6; early surgical complications 9%; radiotherapy 32.3%.

audits.t: Using audit to enhance quality of maternity care in resource limited countries: lessons learnt from rural Tanzania.
audits.tp: Maternal death and severe morbidity review
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 341 of 363 severe maternal morbidities (94%) had at least one area of substandard care; 36 deaths (case fatality 10%).
audits.c: Improved responsiveness to obstetric emergencies, workforce capacity building, referral system improvement and upgrading of hard-to-reach health centres to provide comprehensive emergency obstetric care.

audits.t: Preliminary audit on early identification and management of chronic kidney disease in adults in an acute general medical unit in Sri Lanka.
audits.tp: CKD detection and management in primary care
audits.st: NICE guidelines on early identification and management of chronic kidney disease in adults
audits.f: Target BP achieved in 66%; urine test 58%; UTI investigations 12%; serum creatinine 40%; eGFR, ACR and PCR in none; ACEI 47%, ARB 9%, statins 64%; follow-up arranged 17%. Concurrence with NICE poor.

audits.t: Successful implementation of a perioperative glycemic control protocol in cardiac surgery: barrier analysis and intervention using lean six sigma.
audits.st: Admission to CSICU with glucose <200 mg/dL (perioperative insulin protocol)
audits.f: Fewer than 10% of patients admitted to the CSICU with glucose <200 mg/dL.
audits.c: Perioperative insulin protocol implemented using Lean Six Sigma, with barrier analysis, provider education and extension to the intraoperative period.
audits.r2: More than 90% of patients admitted with glucose <200 mg/dL.

audits.t: Audit of pain management in the emergency department.
audits.tp: Time to analgesia in the emergency department
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Analgesia prescribed to 178 (44.3%); median arrival pain score 7. Pain found to be inadequately treated.

audits.t: A point prevalence survey of antibiotic use in four acute-care teaching hospitals utilizing the European Surveillance of Antimicrobial Consumption (ESAC) audit tool.
audits.st: Hospital antibiotic guidelines; ESAC quality indicators (indication recorded, surgical prophylaxis duration)
audits.f: 52.4% of antibiotics compliant with hospital guidelines; indication recorded in 84.3% of prescribing episodes; 3.9% of surgical prophylaxis prescriptions were for >24 h.

audits.t: Service innovation: a comparison of two approaches for physical screening of psychiatric inpatients.
audits.tp: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Screening performed inconsistently and infrequently.
audits.c: One ward modified the admission proforma; the other set up a discharge screening clinic.
audits.r2: Modified admission proforma raised screening rates by 4.7% on average versus 30.7% for the discharge screening clinic.

audits.t: Increased length of inpatient stay and poor clinical coding: audit of patients with diabetes.
audits.st: National average length of stay; accuracy of clinical coding
audits.f: 110 inpatients with diabetes identified, but discharge coding recorded 119; length of stay 22.39 (22.26) days with diabetes vs 11.68 (6.46) without.

audits.t: Secondary prevention of stroke: an evidence-based clinical audit in the primary care.
audits.tp: Secondary prevention after stroke or TIA
audits.st: Evidence-based audit criteria and performance standards from literature review
audits.f: Marked deficiencies in cardiovascular risk assessment; satisfactory control in 47% of hypertensive (BP), 45% of diabetic (glucose) and 37% of dyslipidaemic (lipids) patients.
audits.r2: BP control 73% of hypertensive patients; adequate metabolic control 62% of diabetic patients; significant improvements.

audits.t: [Factors associated with non-compliance to surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis guidelines during a prospective audit].
audits.st: Guidelines for surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis (indication, choice, dose, timing, duration)
audits.f: Appropriate indication 83%, administration 56%; overall compliance 37%.

audits.t: Audit on quality of breast cancer diagnosis and treatment in Italy, 2008-2009.
audits.st: Screening quality indicators and recommendations (e.g. acceptable target for pre-operative diagnosis)
audits.f: Good overall quality; pre-operative diagnosis reached acceptable target with regional variation; SLN performed in almost 90% of screen-detected invasive cancers.

audits.t: An outcome audit of three day antimicrobial prescribing for the acute dentoalveolar abscess.
audits.st: Departmental guidelines: drainage plus three-day standard-dose antibiotic course
audits.f: Review obtained for 80.3%; when departmental guidelines were followed all reviewed patients had a successful outcome; overall antibiotic prescribing rate 2.9% for adults attending emergency department in pain.

audits.t: Readability and content of postoperative tonsillectomy instructions given to patients in Scotland, a completed audit cycle.
audits.st: Recommended reading level set by patient education experts
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Original audit results mailed to all ENT wards, presented at a national meeting and published.
audits.r2: 61% of information sheets had changed; 6 of 31 (19%) written at or below the recommended reading level; average reading grade still above recommendation.

audits.t: Cataract surgery at Marie Adelaide Leprosy Centre Karachi: an audit.
audits.st: CBM guidelines based on WHO monitoring for quality monitoring
audits.f: Good visual acuity at discharge in 962 (66%); best corrected acuity good in 97.2%. Posterior capsular rent with vitreous loss 70 (4.8%).

audits.t: Surgical time out checklist with debriefing and multidisciplinary feedback improves venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in thoracic surgery: a prospective audit.
audits.st: Extended surgical time out checklist including VTE prophylaxis
audits.f: Time out performed in 959 of 990 (96.8%); errors captured: VTE prophylaxis n=53 (6%), blood products n=11, clerical n=5, imaging n=2, miscellaneous n=2.
audits.c: Human factors training, introduction of debriefing and escalation of VTE prophylaxis to regular departmental meetings.
audits.r2: VTE prophylaxis errors substantially reduced (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Improved guideline compliance after a 3-year audit of multidisciplinary colorectal cancer care in the western part of the Netherlands.
audits.st: Nine quality indicators derived from evidence-based colorectal cancer guidelines
audits.f: Examination of 10 or more lymph nodes in colon cancer 53%.
audits.c: Feedback of casemix-adjusted benchmark information to hospitals over a 3-year audit.
audits.r2: Examination of 10 or more lymph nodes rose to 78%; compliance improved and inter-hospital differences decreased.

audits.t: Current practice of antiplatelet and anticoagulation management in post-cardiac surgery patients: a national audit.
audits.st: EACTS guideline on antiplatelet and anticoagulation management in cardiac surgery (aspirin 150-300 mg, loading within 24 h)
audits.f: 20 (54%) hospitals had a unit protocol; 23 (62.2%) registrars aware of EACTS guidelines; aspirin loading within 24 h followed by 60.7% of surgeons; low-dose aspirin commonly used.

audits.t: Audit of physicians' adherence to the antibiotic policy guidelines in Kuwait.
audits.st: Local hospital antibiotic policy guidelines
audits.f: 1,112 (49.8%) patients received 1,528 antibiotic prescriptions; adherence to local policy was low.

audits.t: Identifying, documenting, and reviewing preferred place of death: an audit of one UK hospice.
audits.tp: Achievement of preferred place of death
audits.st: UK health-care policy that good end-of-life care includes choosing a place of death
audits.f: Preferred place of death documented in 28 (18.6%); conversations about end-of-life preferences documented in 16 (10.6%); preferences reviewed in 6 (4%).

audits.t: Review of cytology and histopathology as part of the NHS Cervical Screening Programme audit of invasive cervical cancers.
audits.tp: Invasive cervical cancer screening history review
audits.st: Nationally agreed review protocol for slides from women diagnosed with invasive cervical cancer
audits.f: Of 3759 originally normal cytology slides, only 45% were normal on review (11% inadequate, 21% low grade, 23% high grade); 94% of reviewed histology samples retained the original diagnosis.

audits.t: Accuracy in documentation of peripheral venous catheters in paediatric care: an intervention study in electronic patient records.
audits.st: Complete and accurate recording of peripheral venous catheters in the electronic patient record
audits.f: Recording of any kind in 85-93%; 1 of 22 observed complications documented.
audits.c: Structured standardised template for recording peripheral venous catheters in the electronic record.
audits.r2: Significant increase in complete recording; side and size recording improved; none of the complications (n = 17 and n = 9) documented.

audits.t: A baseline audit of referral and treatment delivered to patients in the intermediate minor oral surgery service in Croydon PCT.
audits.st: Local referral guidelines
audits.f: 99% treated in IMOS practices, only three (<1%) referred on to hospital; 72 (13%) teeth removed were simple extractions without medical complications.

audits.t: National audit of supported discharge programmes for management of acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease 2008.
audits.st: British Thoracic Society guidelines on supported discharge programmes
audits.f: SDPs available in 142 of 239 (59%) units; 1630 of 8971 (18%) patients treated within SDPs.

audits.t: An audit of pressure sores caused by intermittent compression devices used to prevent venous thromboembolism.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Intermittent compression devices caused pressure sores in selected women undergoing long operations.
audits.r2: Reduced risk of pressure sores without increased VTE risk (figures not given).

audits.t: Developing best practice for fungal specimen management: audit of UK microbiology laboratories.
audits.st: HPA National Standard Methods SOP for investigation of dermatological specimens for superficial mycoses (e.g. 14-day incubation of microscopy-negative specimens)
audits.f: NSM SOP followed by 92% for microscopy; only 34% incubated microscopy-negative specimens for the recommended 14 days; about 60% incubated microscopy-positive specimens for 21 days; recommended culture medium used by 82%.

audits.t: Adapting the World Federation for Medical Education standards for use in a self-audit of an eye care training programme.
audits.st: World Federation for Medical Education (WFME) standards adapted (9 areas, 38 subareas)
audits.f: All nine areas completely attained at least basic level; two attained quality development level; 26 (68%) subareas completely attained quality development level.

audits.t: Assessing care for patients with TB/HIV/STI infections in a rural district in KwaZulu-Natal.
audits.tp: TB, HIV and STI care in primary care
audits.st: Adapted TB/HIV/STI audit tool and programme targets
audits.f: 71% of clinical staff untrained in TB; 46% of facilities visited monthly by supervisor; 80% had drug or supply stock-outs; PCR results undocumented for 54%; mean 47 days from ART eligibility to start.

audits.t: Educating surgical patients to reduce the risk of venous thromboembolism: an audit of an effective strategy.
audits.st: NICE guidance on VTE risk and prophylaxis (patient understanding of its components)
audits.f: Baseline questionnaire of patient awareness of VTE, risk factors and prophylaxis (figures not reported in abstract).
audits.c: Patient leaflets addressing gaps in understanding and guidance for junior doctors on patient education at pre-assessment and discharge.
audits.r2: Awareness of VTE improved significantly to 90%.

audits.t: Oxygen therapy multicentric study--a nationwide audit to oxygen therapy procedures in internal medicine wards.
audits.st: BTS guideline for emergency oxygen use in adult patients
audits.f: Oxygen prescribed in 93.4%; 82.4% fixed dose but only 11.6% of those complete; oxygen given to only 77.0% with fixed-dose prescriptions; FiO2/flow and device matched in 70.9% and 89.2%; 82.7% of 127 target-range prescriptions within range.

audits.t: Improving serological test ordering patterns for the diagnosis of celiac disease through clinical laboratory audit of practice.
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines recommending tTG to screen for coeliac disease
audits.f: Coeliac panel ordered in 48.4% of children and 72.3% of adults; tTG alone in 7.2% of adults.
audits.c: Interaction with physicians, revised test menu and changed test ordering policy.
audits.r2: Coeliac panel 3.6% in children and 28.1% in adults; tTG alone over 90% in children and 61.3% in adults.

audits.t: Using electronic clinical practice audits as needs assessment to produce effective continuing medical education programming.
audits.tp: Chronic disease management in primary care
audits.st: 10 preventive care and 10 chronic disease interventions
audits.f: Documented completion ranged from 13% (tetanus vaccine current) to 97% (prenatal vitamins in pregnancy).
audits.c: Personalised learning needs translated into CME programming.

audits.t: Hospital management and outcomes of stroke in Indigenous Australians: evidence from the 2009 Acute Care National Stroke Audit.
audits.st: National Stroke Audit clinical processes of care (e.g. stroke unit care, timely allied health assessment)
audits.f: 7% Indigenous; Indigenous patients less likely to receive stroke unit care and timely allied health assessment.

audits.t: Audit of extrapleural local anaesthetic infusion in neonates following repair of tracheo-oesophageal fistulae and oesophageal atresia via thoracotomy.
audits.st: Institutional extrapleural infusion dosing recommendations and catheter insertion guideline
audits.f: 90% received 300 µg/kg/hour or less; 36% needed morphine infusion; 39% ventilated. Group 1 (term): 24% morphine, 77% extubated immediately; group 2: 64% morphine, 82% ventilated.
audits.c: Guideline revised to restrict use to term neonates of 2.5 kg or more expected to be extubated early.

audits.t: Auditing resuscitation of preterm infants at birth by recording video and physiological parameters.
audits.tp: Neonatal resuscitation guideline compliance and documentation
audits.st: Local neonatal resuscitation guidelines
audits.f: Interventions per guidelines in 7/34 (21%); respiratory deviations in 25/34 (74%); non-respiratory deviations in 10/34 (29%); time to initial evaluation 65 s.

audits.t: Compliance with pre-operative instructions for procedures with conscious sedation: a complete audit cycle.
audits.st: Pre-operative instructions for conscious sedation with midazolam
audits.f: Over 55% of patients non-compliant; no competent escort 17%, alcohol within 24 hours 17%.
audits.c: Patient information leaflet revised; given at listing and with appointment letter, plus verbal reminder before attending.
audits.r2: 22% increase in compliance across all instructions; all patients brought competent escorts.

audits.t: Clinical audits: A practical strategy for reducing cesarean section rates in a general hospital in Tehran, Iran.
audits.st: Reduction of unnecessary caesarean sections (Safe Motherhood Committee audits)
audits.f: Overall caesarean section rate 40%.
audits.c: Clinical audits introduced by the Safe Motherhood Committee.

audits.t: Clinical audit of stroke thrombolysis in Wellington, New Zealand: disparity between in-hours and out-of-hours treatment time.
audits.st: Agreed clinical eligibility criteria for rt-PA
audits.f: All treated within eligibility criteria; mean onset-to-treatment 168 minutes; out-of-hours added 33 minutes (p=0.03).

audits.t: Prolonged labour as indication for emergency caesarean section: a quality assurance analysis by criterion-based audit at two Tanzanian rural hospitals.
audits.st: Criteria of realistic best practice
audits.f: Suboptimal management in most cases; labour not prolonged in 26%, membranes intact in 16%; 36% of genuine prolonged labour sectioned at full dilatation.

audits.t: Audit about Medical Decision: Data Transmission Concerning Patients with Dementia Entering French Nursing Homes Does Not Confirm the Diagnosis.
audits.tp: Dementia diagnosis data in nursing home admission letters
audits.st: 25 diagnostic criteria from French guidelines for dementia and Alzheimer disease diagnosis
audits.f: Median number of diagnostic criteria in admission letters 1 (IQR 0-4, maximum 12).

audits.t: An audit of amputation levels in patients referred for prosthetic rehabilitation.
audits.st: National figures for other DSCs (39-48% below-knee, 1981-1988)
audits.f: Final healed level was below the knee in 55% of cases; 11 vascular surgeons (28%) referred 64% of patients.

audits.t: A national audit on the management of pelvic inflammatory disease in UK genitourinary medicine clinics.
audits.tp: Outpatient management of pelvic inflammatory disease
audits.st: BASHH 2005 national guideline on PID treatment and partner notification
audits.f: 504 (44.5%) received a recommended treatment regimen; 447 (39%) of named male contacts were treated.

audits.t: Exploring variations in lung cancer care across the UK--the 'story so far' for the National Lung Cancer Audit.
audits.st: National Lung Cancer Audit process and outcome measures
audits.f: Histological confirmation 64%; MDT discussion 78%; anti-cancer treatment 43%; surgical resection 9%; small cell chemotherapy 58%.
audits.c: Continuous national audit with feedback over five years.
audits.r2: Histological confirmation 76%; MDT discussion 94%; anti-cancer treatment 59%; surgical resection 14%; small cell chemotherapy 66%.

audits.t: Auditing urinary catheter care.
audits.st: Evidence-based catheter care and prompt removal
audits.f: Poor documented evidence that best practice was carried out.
audits.c: Urinary catheter assessment and monitoring tool designed.

audits.t: [Quality of nursing care in intensive therapy: evaluation through operational auditing].
audits.st: Operational Auditing Plan; quality defined as at least 70% positive answers
audits.f: Physical safety 71% and equipment use 72% met standard; physical activity 28% and oxygenation/ventilation 29% lowest.

audits.t: Staging cancer of the uterus: a national audit of MRI accuracy.
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists target accuracies: myometrial invasion 85%, cervical extension 86%, nodal spread 70%
audits.f: National accuracy: myometrial invasion 82%, cervical extension 90%, pelvic nodes 94%; centres meeting target: 13/37 (35%) myometrial invasion, 31/36 (86%) cervical extension, 31/34 (91%) nodes.

audits.t: Do psychiatric inpatients know their rights? A re-audit on information given to inpatients at a London mental health trust about their rights and admission to hospital.
audits.tp: Informing detained patients of their rights
audits.st: Agreed trust standards on informing inpatients about legal status and rights (Mental Health Act 1983, revised 2007)
audits.f: 54.2% of informal inpatients aware of their legal status; 37.5% knew they could refuse treatment.
audits.r2: Wards A-C: 81.3% aware of legal status (P = 0.101), 68.8% knew they could refuse treatment (P = 0.105). All 10 wards: 90.2% knew status (P = 0.0002), 65.6% knew they could refuse treatment (P = 0.0184).

audits.t: Improving the safety of patient transfer from AMU using a written checklist.
audits.st: NHS Litigation Authority criteria for safe transfer
audits.f: Extremely poor uptake of the transfer checklist.
audits.c: Education of nursing staff and raising awareness at regular staff meetings, following introduction of a redesigned checklist.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in completion rate; subsequent monitoring showed compliance up to 95%.

audits.t: A clinical audit of the number of vaginal examinations in labor: a NOVEL idea.
audits.st: WHO recommendation of one vaginal examination every 4 hours in the first stage
audits.f: Average 4 vaginal examinations per woman, above WHO recommendation; presumed chorioamnionitis 6% (these women averaged 7 examinations).
audits.c: Presentation and discussion of audit findings with midwives.

audits.t: The Nelson general practice prescribing project. Part I: A pilot audit of the regional prescribing profile.
audits.st: Current guidelines on benzodiazepine prescribing
audits.f: Marked variation between GPs; prescription cost $2.20 to $127.70 (median $10.77); benzodiazepines mean 6.7% of prescribing, not in line with guidelines.

audits.t: Clinical audit of health promotion of vitamin D in one general practice.
audits.tp: Vitamin D health promotion in general practice
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 486 (51%) had a Medicare-funded Health Assessment; women 54% vs men 46% (p = 0.010); mean 25-OHD men 70.0 nmol/l, women 60.3 nmol/l.
audits.c: Vitamin D health promotion information provided to the target group.
audits.r2: not reported (information given to 50% of the target group; no effect on uptake of health assessment invitation)

audits.t: Addressing long-term physical healthcare needs in a forensic mental health inpatient population using the UK primary care Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF): an audit.
audits.tp: Physical health monitoring of psychiatric inpatients
audits.st: UK primary care Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF) local and national benchmarks (2005-2006)
audits.f: QOF was a useful assessment tool; increased prevalence of all QOF-assessed long-term conditions compared with local and national populations (figures not given).

audits.t: Depression case management by practice nurses in primary care: an audit.
audits.st: Benchmarked against randomised trial data
audits.f: Mean PHQ9 change 9.07 (SD 6.67, 95% CI 7.93-10.22, P < 0.001); shift from moderate-severe to mild depression.

audits.t: Physical healthcare of people with severe mental illness: everybody's business!
audits.st: Annual physical health monitoring for people with severe mental illness
audits.f: 20% had at least one annual physical health check.
audits.c: Raised awareness in the multidisciplinary team and liaison with primary care.
audits.r2: 58% had at least one annual physical health check; a record was in the notes for 75% of those checked.

audits.t: Use of evidence-based therapy at discharge for patients with acute myocardial infarction: retrospective audit of medical records.
audits.tp: Secondary prevention after acute coronary syndrome
audits.st: Canadian benchmarks: ASA at least 90%, beta-blockers and ACE inhibitors at least 85%, statins at least 70%
audits.f: In ideal patients: ASA 99.0% (308/311), beta-blockers 96.3% (310/322), ACE inhibitors 90.4% (264/292), statins 88.8% (278/313); all exceeded benchmarks.

audits.t: Audit of physicians' adherence to a preprinted order set for community-acquired pneumonia.
audits.st: Institutional preprinted order set for community-acquired pneumonia; IDSA-ATS guidelines
audits.f: Preprinted order used for 25/58 (43%); all sections used correctly in 4 (7%).

audits.t: Retrospective audit of medication order turnaround time after implementation of standardized definitions.
audits.st: Target dispensary turnaround time under 15 min
audits.f: 76/84 (90%) met target; median dispensary time 10 min for stat/emergent and 10 min for urgent/now.
audits.c: Standardised definitions for stat, emergent, urgent and now implemented through education of pharmacy staff.
audits.r2: 129/142 (91%) met target (p=0.80); median dispensary time 9 and 12 min.

audits.t: Adherence to clinical guidelines improves patient outcomes in Australian audit of stroke rehabilitation practice.
audits.st: Australian Clinical Guidelines for Stroke Rehabilitation and Recovery
audits.f: Evidence-based management delivered: treatment for sensorimotor impairment 38%, hypertonicity 56%, mobility 94%, home assessments 71%.

audits.t: Two audits of the diagnosis of oral cancer and the two-week rule following referrals from primary care practitioners in Newcastle.
audits.st: Department of Health two-week rule referral guidelines
audits.f: 57 (90%) seen within time; 60 (95%) conformed to guidelines; cancer detection rate 11% (7/63).
audits.c: Repeat identical audit in a different department; no intervention described.
audits.r2: 43/49 (88%) seen within time; 39 (80%) compliant with guidelines; detection rate 7%.

audits.t: Use of trastuzumab in Australia and New Zealand: results from the National Breast Cancer Audit.
audits.st: National Breast and Ovarian Cancer Centre 2007 recommendation to offer adjuvant trastuzumab for HER-2 positive cancers
audits.f: HER-2 testing rose from 77% to 91%; trastuzumab in HER-2 positive cancers 50% (2006), 66% (2007), 74% (2008).

audits.t: The effectiveness of local child weight management programmes: an audit study.
audits.st: Standard Evaluation Framework
audits.f: None of the programmes provided all essential measures; weight change from +0.4 kg to -0.9 kg; BMI SD fell 0.1-0.2 in four programmes and was unchanged in two.

audits.t: [Prevalence and control of hypertension in chronic hemodialysis patients: results of a single-centre clinical audit].
audits.st: Current guidelines: pre-dialysis BP 140/90 or less and post-dialysis BP 130/80 mmHg or less
audits.f: 49 (55%) hypertensive; only 14.3% achieved both pre- and post-dialysis BP targets.

audits.t: Anti-malarial chemoprophylaxis following evacuation from Afghanistan.
audits.st: Prescription of post-deployment anti-malarial chemoprophylaxis
audits.f: Prescription rate of 50%; poor pre-injury compliance.
audits.r2: 5 of 305 (1.64%) inpatients prescribed appropriate post-deployment chemoprophylaxis.

audits.t: Outpatient clinic letters in ENT. Is there any margin of improvement?
audits.st: Structured format for outpatient clinic letters (readability score 0-4)
audits.f: SpR letters 71.91% structured, mean readability 2.87/4; consultant letters 46.58% structured, mean 1.25/4.
audits.c: First audit results presented to participating doctors.
audits.r2: SpR letters 84.72% structured, mean readability 3.41/4; consultant letters 52.56% structured, mean 2.04/4.

audits.t: Reduction in pediatric identification band errors: a quality collaborative.
audits.st: Aim to halve ID band error rate (absent, illegible or inaccurate band) in 1 year
audits.f: ID band failure rate 17%.
audits.c: Frontline staff education, softer and luggage-tag ID bands, and education of families and patients.
audits.r2: ID band failure rate 4.1% (77% relative reduction).

audits.t: Inpatient care for children with diabetes: are standards being met?
audits.st: Department of Health Children's Diabetes Working Group care standards
audits.f: 70% of wards had all four protocols (52% of EDs); trained children's nurses every shift on wards 100% vs EDs 33%; dietetic advice on wards 37%; diabetes team informed within 2 h in daytime 26%.

audits.t: UK national re-audit of sexual history-taking.
audits.st: BASHH sexual history-taking standards
audits.f: Baseline national audit identified several areas of under-performance.
audits.r2: Documentation increased for all measures except legibility; chaperone offer, condom usage and four of five HIV risk assessment aspects remained below target.

audits.t: Management of Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection over 12 months in a genitourinary medicine setting against British Association for Sexual Health and HIV auditable outcome measures.
audits.st: BASHH auditable outcome measures for gonorrhoea management
audits.f: Audit identified the need to change the clinic protocol for first-line antibiotic therapy (no figures given).
audits.c: Clinic protocol for first-line antibiotic therapy changed.
audits.r2: Improvements reported in recording of written information given to patients and outcome of contact tracing (no figures given).

audits.t: Did an acute medical assessment unit improve the initial assessment and treatment of community acquired pneumonia--a retrospective audit.
audits.st: Evidence-based CAP guidelines; timeliness of assessment
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Opening of a Medical Assessment and Planning Unit.
audits.r2: Times to doctor and X-ray longer in MAPU than ED; time to physician review unchanged; guideline compliance patchy with no improvement.

audits.t: Clinical audit on diagnostic accuracy and management of respiratory failure in COPD.
audits.st: GOLD 2008 guidelines; accuracy of respiratory failure diagnosis and LTOT prescription
audits.f: ABG performed in 118 (90.8%); diagnosis of respiratory failure agreed with ABG in only about half.

audits.t: Audit of major colorectal and biliary surgery to reduce rates of wound infection.
audits.st: Annual review of wound infection rate
audits.f: Wound infection 43% in colorectal surgery in 1976 with no prophylaxis; 12% in biliary surgery 1981-7 with no prophylaxis.
audits.c: Serial changes in prophylaxis: single intravenous metronidazole and cefuroxime intraoperatively plus peritoneal and wound lavage with 0.1% tetracycline.
audits.r2: Colorectal wound infection 1%; biliary 2% after tetracycline lavage.

audits.t: Brain death and organ donation in a neurosurgical unit: audit of recent practice.
audits.st: Comparison with 1981 unit data and a recent national audit
audits.f: 35% (191) died on a ventilator; consent sought in 88% (96) of 109 medically suitable brain dead patients and granted in 70% (67).

audits.t: Surgical handover in an era of reduced working hours: an audit of current practice.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons handover guidelines (satisfactory compliance >80% of sessions)
audits.f: Satisfactory compliance for only five of nine components; 95% at a designated place; none had formal handover training; 48% (n=20) aware of guidelines.

audits.t: An audit of inpatient management of community-acquired pneumonia in Oman: a comparison with regional clinical guidelines.
audits.st: Gulf Cooperation Council CAP guidelines
audits.f: CURB-65 documented in 4 (2.3%); smoking history 56 (32.6%); standard co-amoxiclav and clarithromycin in 115 (67%); antibiotics within 4 hours in 139 (81%).

audits.t: Variation in clinical practice in carotid surgery in nine countries 2005-2010. Lessons from VASCUNET and recommendations for the future of national clinical audit.
audits.st: Current European recommendations on CEA indications
audits.f: 92.6% of CEAs met inclusion criteria; stroke and death 2.3% symptomatic and 0.9% asymptomatic.

audits.t: Disclosing doubtful indications for emergency cesarean sections in rural hospitals in Tanzania: a retrospective criterion-based audit.
audits.st: Evidence-based audit criteria for realistic best practice
audits.f: 26% of emergency sections on inappropriate indications and 38% unclear; in prolonged labour 36% had timely progress and/or intact membranes.

audits.t: Tonsillectomy under threat: auditing the indications for performing tonsillectomy.
audits.st: ENTUK and SIGN criteria: five or more disabling sore throat episodes per year for at least a year
