audits.f: All 17 tonsillectomies justified but only two (11.8 per cent) had documented indications.
audits.c: Surgeons agreed to list specified criteria when scheduling; pro forma reminder distributed to all clinics.
audits.r2: 85 per cent had all essential criteria documented in the listing letter.

audits.t: Performance against local service quality indicators: re-setting the indicators.
audits.st: Local service quality indicators for GUM and HIV
audits.f: Performance audited against local SQIs (figures not given in abstract).
audits.r2: Re-audited in 2010 and 2011; SQIs were revised based on the three audits (figures not given).

audits.t: Surgeons' Evaluation of Colorectal Cancer Resections Against Standard HPE Protocol-Auditing the Surgeons.
audits.st: Standard HPE reporting protocol using a formulated standard proforma
audits.f: Surgeons claimed curative resection in 40 (90%), only 1 (2.5%) had positive margin; 4 surgeon-reported margin involvements all disputed by HPE; 7 of 31 (22.5%) without obvious nodes were node positive.

audits.t: Management of microinvasive cervical cancer: a British Society for Colposcopy and Cervical Pathology audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 110 of 210 (52%) responded; all discuss stage IA cancer at gynaecological MDT; conservatively managed women followed up for at least 5 years.

audits.t: The national colonoscopy audit: a nationwide assessment of the quality and safety of colonoscopy in the UK.
audits.st: National colonoscopy standards (caecal intubation, polyp detection, retrieval, comfort)
audits.f: Unadjusted caecal intubation rate 92.3% (adjusted 95.8%); polyp detection rate 32.1%; 92.3% of resected polyps retrieved; 90.2% acceptable comfort.

audits.t: Diabetic retinopathy screening in New Zealand requires improvement: results from a multi-centre audit.
audits.st: National diabetes retinal screening guidelines (referral and review within six months)
audits.f: 75 (48%) referred to ophthalmologist as recommended; 45 (60% of referred) seen within six months.

audits.t: Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy in a district general hospital: is it safe and feasible?
audits.tp: Index admission cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 10.42% of emergency gallstone admissions had early laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
audits.c: Departmental education on early cholecystectomy and altered management guidelines to consider it for all suitable patients.
audits.r2: 21 of 36 suitable patients (58%) had early laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

audits.t: Medication Safety in Primary Care Practice: results from a PPRNet quality improvement intervention.
audits.tp: High-risk prescribing and monitoring in primary care
audits.st: Five categories of preventable prescribing and monitoring errors
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Multimethod quality improvement intervention including EHR-based audit and feedback, medication reconciliation, decision support and refill protocols.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in avoiding inappropriate therapy, drug-disease interactions and monitoring; inappropriate dosages and drug-drug interactions unchanged.

audits.t: Improving dosing of gentamicin in the obese patient: a 3-cycle drug chart and case note audit.
audits.st: Trust once daily gentamicin dosing protocol
audits.f: Dose prescribing errors in obese patients 43%; frequency errors 12.8%.
audits.c: Introduction of an online electronic gentamicin dose calculator.
audits.r2: Dose errors in obese patients fell to 20% (similar to non-obese patients); frequency errors fell to 4%.

audits.t: Comparison of achievement of NICE targets in type 2 diabetes in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia and Grimsby, United Kingdom: an audit.
audits.st: NICE standards of diabetic care (yearly BP, HbA1c, lipid profile, urine dipstick; NICE targets for BP, HbA1c, cholesterol)
audits.f: Yearly BP, HbA1c, lipid profile and urine dipstick testing done in 95, 89, 84, 51% (Riyadh) and 100, 81, 92, 95% (Grimsby). NICE targets for overall, systolic, diastolic BP and HbA1c achieved in 53, 55, 18 and 46, 39, 35% respectively. Total cholesterol and LDL-C targets met in 54, 51% and 71, 75%.

audits.t: Validating dose rate calibration of radiotherapy photon beams through IAEA/WHO postal audit dosimetry service.
audits.st: IAEA/WHO postal audit dosimetry service (agreement of stated dose with IAEA measurement)
audits.f: Agreement between stated doses and IAEA results within 1% for the two 6 MV beams and within 2% for the 18 MV beam.

audits.t: Clinical audit of emergency unit before and after establishment of the emergency medicine department.
audits.st: Ward-based international standards checklist (staffing, education/CPD, facility, equipment, records, disaster planning and other domains)
audits.f: Deficiencies found across domains before establishment of emergency medicine departments (figures not given in abstract).
audits.r2: Education and CPD (p = 0.042), design and facility (p = 0.027), equipment (p = 0.028) and disaster planning (p = 0.026) significantly improved; nearly all domains showed a positive change.

audits.t: Physical health of patients with severe mental illness: an intervention on medium secure forensic unit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 80% smokers, 80% raised BMI, 87% raised 10-year cardiovascular risk.
audits.c: Physical health monitoring sheet introduced in all patient records.
audits.r2: Monitoring sheets up to date in 100% of records; serum lipids and 10-year cardiovascular risk reduced.

audits.t: Using pathology-specific laboratory profiles in clinical pathology to reduce inappropriate test requesting: two completed audit cycles.
audits.st: Jointly developed pathology-specific laboratory profiles and inclusion of provisional diagnosis on request forms
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Seven pathology-specific laboratory profiles developed by a multidisciplinary team, with 8 training sessions for the 23 trial GPs.
audits.r2: Number of tests requested in the trial district fell by about 5% (remainder truncated in abstract).

audits.t: False-positive coding for acute myocardial infarction on hospital discharge records: chart audit results from a tertiary centre.
audits.st: Documentation criteria for acute myocardial infarction (symptomatic, ECG and enzymatic elements) in charts coded ICD-9-CM AMI
audits.f: 43 (21%) false-positives (95% CI 15 to 26%), i.e. charts coded AMI where criteria were not met.

audits.t: Recording a history of alcohol use in pregnancy: an audit of knowledge, attitudes and practice at a child development service.
audits.st: Documentation of alcohol use in pregnancy in medical records and correspondence
audits.f: Only three letters recorded alcohol use in pregnancy across a random sample of 40 medical records and all 210 paediatric letters for 2006.

audits.t: Adherence to national guidelines for gastric cancer in the Netherlands: a retrospective population-based audit.
audits.st: Dutch national gastric cancer guideline (May 2009): perioperative chemotherapy, adequate lymphadenectomy (≥10 lymph nodes), non-curative resections
audits.f: Adequate lymphadenectomy (≥10 lymph nodes) 49%.
audits.c: Release of new national clinical practice guideline in May 2009
audits.r2: Adequate lymphadenectomy increased to 58% (p = 0.005); other indicators showed no major change.

audits.t: [An audit of perioperative fluid management and electrolyte monitoring in children undergoing surgery for scoliosis].
audits.st: 2009 guideline on perioperative intravenous fluids and electrolyte and glucose monitoring in children
audits.f: Preoperative electrolytes checked in 82.3%; postoperative electrolytes unavailable in 27/122; electrolytes monitored only once in 82.3%; Day 1 hyponatraemia 23.6%.
audits.r2: Preoperative electrolytes checked in 94.3%; postoperative electrolytes unavailable in 13/113; monitored only once in 70.5%; Day 1 hyponatraemia 26.2% (P = 0.044).

audits.t: A simple approach to improve recording of concerns about child maltreatment in primary care records: developing a quality improvement intervention.
audits.tp: Child maltreatment recording in primary care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 8.4 children per 1000 child years with at least one maltreatment-related code (8.0/1000 in THIN); of 25 patients with known maltreatment, six had no maltreatment codes.
audits.c: Consensus recommendations to code 'child is cause for concern' and use a code list around four clinical concepts with an optional templated form (not re-audited).

audits.t: Antipsychotics in dementia: prevalence and quality of antipsychotic drug prescribing in UK mental health services.
audits.st: POMH-UK practice standards for antipsychotic prescribing in dementia (including 6-monthly review)
audits.f: 1620 (16%) without psychotic illness prescribed an antipsychotic; of 1001 (62%) treated >6 months, only three-quarters had a documented review in the previous 6 months.

audits.t: Quality of care in palliative sedation: audit and compliance monitoring of a clinical protocol.
audits.st: Local clinical protocol for palliative sedation (ethical sedation checklist, justification, patient/family agreement, appropriate treatment)
audits.f: Concordance of procedures with the sedation guideline 100%; patient/family agreement recorded in 100%; 63% sedated.
audits.c: Educational programme and results feedback meetings
audits.r2: Concordance with the sedation guideline 100%; 57% sedated.

audits.t: BASHH Scotland/Scottish HIV and AIDS group national audit 2009-2010: sexual health care for people living with HIV.
audits.tp: Sexual health care for people living with HIV
audits.st: Quality Improvement Scotland Sexual Health Services Standards
audits.f: Syphilis serology offered in previous six months to 55% (range 12-97%); sexual history within four weeks of HIV diagnosis in 67% (12-100%); STI tests offered within four weeks in 45% (4-96%).

audits.t: Innovation in hospital quality improvement activities--acute postoperative pain management (APOP) self-help toolkit audits as an example.
audits.st: Key indicators of acute postoperative pain management (pain and sedation scores measured, documented pain management plans at discharge)
audits.f: Earlier APOP project audits (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Downloadable APOP toolkit with data collection and educational tools and automated feedback report, used in two facilitated snapshot audits
audits.r2: Continued improvement in the percentage of patients with measured pain and sedation scores and with documented discharge pain plans (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: An audit of inhaler technique among asthma patients of 34 general practitioners.
audits.st: Inhaler technique scoring system (good 4/4, adequate 3-4, inadequate 2 or less)
audits.f: 25% had inadequate technique; good technique 78% with Turbohaler and 45% with metered dose inhalers.

audits.t: Quality audit of colonoscopy reports amongst patients screened or surveilled for colorectal neoplasia.
audits.st: National Colorectal Cancer Roundtable Quality Assurance Task Group colonoscopy reporting criteria
audits.f: Indication and consent always documented; previous colonoscopy date 14%; caecum reached 94.4% with landmarks 78.8% and photodocumentation 67.2%; no procedural times recorded; polyp size 65.8%, morphology 62.2%, removal method unrecorded 20.7%.

audits.t: Auditing a court assessment and advice service for defendants with mental health difficulties: utilizing electronic patient records.
audits.st: Six objectives in the Service Level Agreement
audits.f: Service met all six Service Level Agreement objectives.

audits.t: Audit of the recording of occupational asthma in primary care.
audits.st: National guidelines (2008): ask two screening questions about work effect
audits.f: Occupation recorded in 55/396 (14%); 9 (2%) had any work-effect enquiry; 4 had enquiry at diagnosis among 117 with traceable notes.
audits.c: Suggested modifying asthma review electronic templates (not implemented).

audits.t: New Zealand National Acute Stroke Services Audit: acute stroke care delivery in New Zealand.
audits.st: Acute stroke care quality indicators (stroke unit care, thrombolysis, anticoagulation in AF, aspirin, therapy assessments)
audits.f: Only 28% managed in a stroke unit; 38% arrived within 4.5 hours but only 3% thrombolysed; of 40% with known AF, only 24% were taking anticoagulants.

audits.t: Improving newborn screening follow-up in pediatric practices: quality improvement innovation network.
audits.st: Newborn screening follow-up processes: assessment of all infants, documentation and sharing of in-range results, use of ACMG ACTion sheets
audits.f: Almost half of practices completed assessment of infants for NBS; only 2 practices documented all in-range results and shared them with parents; 1 of 15 used ACTion sheets.
audits.c: Information about NBS, training in QI methods, practice-led changes with monthly chart audits over 6 months
audits.r2: 80% of practices assessed all infants; 10 of 15 practices documented and shared in-range results for ≥70% of infants; 7 of 15 used ACTion sheets.

audits.t: Structured airway intervention improves safety of endotracheal intubation in an intensive care unit.
audits.st: Royal College of Anaesthetists NAP4 recommendations for advanced airway management
audits.f: Local practice benchmarked against NAP4 national standards (figures not given).
audits.c: Multidisciplinary training, improved resources, new working practices and a new departmental training programme.
audits.r2: Improved endotracheal intubation technique and embedded new practice (figures not given).

audits.t: Washing and changing uniforms:  is guidance being adhered to?
audits.st: Local infection prevention and control standard on uniform use, laundry and storage
audits.f: Staff generally adhered: uniforms changed daily and immediately on soiling, aprons worn where indicated, machine-washed and ironed hot; few placed laundered uniforms in protective covers.

audits.t: Measuring surgical outcomes in neurosurgery: implementation, analysis, and auditing a prospective series of more than 5000 procedures.
audits.st: Institution-wide compliance with reporting of complications in the EMR
audits.f: Compliance with major complication reporting 80.7%; unreported complications 11%.
audits.c: Staged implementation with physician pilots, nurse participation, point-of-service data capture, EMR form modification, data auditing and confidential surgeon reports
audits.r2: Compliance with major complication reporting 90.3%; unreported complications 4%.

audits.t: Radiographic evaluation of the technical quality of undergraduate endodontic 'competence' cases in the Dublin Dental University Hospital: an audit.
audits.st: European guidelines for technical quality of root canal treatment (obturation within 2 mm of apex, no voids or errors)
audits.f: Acceptable: 49% of single-rooted and 17% of multi-rooted teeth; voids in 36% (single) and 38% (multi); within 2 mm of apex 69% and 60%.

audits.t: Achieving flying colours in surgical safety: audit of World Health Organization 'Surgical Safety Checklist' compliance.
audits.st: Local version of the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (National Patient Safety Agency guidance)
audits.f: Overall compliance 63.7% (SEM 8.9%). 44% undocumented at Sign in; Time out interrupted in 39%; procedure started before completion in 33%; Sign out not read out in 94% and not fully documented in 42%.

audits.t: Prospective audit of post-chemotherapy febrile neutropenia in patients with solid cancer and lymphoma in two Singaporean cancer centres.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 3.7% of FN episodes managed as outpatients, none with complications; 30-day mortality 6.6%; median length of stay 7 days (IQR 4 to 11).

audits.t: Medication Error Minimization Scheme (MEMS) in an adult tertiary intensive care unit (ICU) 2009-2011.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Intravenous infusion error rate 38/331 (11.5%); incorrect documentation of omitted medications 105/347 (30.3%); 6.2 reported medication incidents per 1000 patient days.
audits.c: Multifaceted PDSA programme: education sessions, meeting and bedside discussions, promotion with logo and displays, staff incentives, surveys and focus groups
audits.r2: Intravenous infusion error rate 15/468 (3.2%); incorrect documentation of omitted medications 104/486 (21.4%); reported incidents rose to 14.9 per 1000 patient days.

audits.t: Testing for heritable thrombophilia in children at Starship Children's Hospital: an audit of requests between 2004 and 2009.
audits.st: BCSH criteria for heritable thrombophilia testing
audits.f: The large majority of 379 requests did not satisfy BCSH criteria; 34% of tests abnormal but only 36% of abnormal tests repeated; 34 tests done on patients on anticoagulation.

audits.t: A clinical audit of the nutritional status and need for nutrition support amongst head and neck cancer patients treated with radiotherapy.
audits.tp: Nutritional support in head and neck cancer
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 28 (77.8%) well nourished on PG-SGA at initial assessment; mean weight loss during radiotherapy 5.74%.

audits.t: Clinical audit of COPD patients requiring hospital admissions in Spain: AUDIPOC study.
audits.st: Current international COPD guidelines
audits.f: Median inpatient mortality 5% (range 0-35%); 37% readmitted and 6.5% died after discharge; overall mortality 11.6%. Management mostly complied with diagnosis and treatment recommendations.

audits.t: Audit of renal drug dosing: comparison of 2 methods and evaluation of pharmacists' knowledge, attitudes, and behaviour.
audits.st: Renal dosing directive: dose adjusted, or rationale documented if not adjusted
audits.f: 86 (22%) orders needed dose adjustment consideration; 78 (91%) followed renal dosing guidelines; 6 (7%) manual and 8 (9%) pharmacy system orders were non-compliant.

audits.t: An audit of chaperone use for intimate examinations in an integrated sexual health clinic.
audits.st: GMC guidance on chaperones for intimate examinations
audits.f: 20 of 104 genital examinations recorded as chaperoned; chaperone declined documented in 5; 24% had documentation of chaperone presence or offer.

audits.t: National Breast Cancer Audit: overview of invasive breast cancer in New Zealand.
audits.st: National Breast Cancer Audit performance indicators and clinical guidelines
audits.f: 3% involved margins; 72% of screening and 86% of symptomatic high-risk patients did not receive post-mastectomy radiotherapy; endocrine therapy prescribed to 81% of hormone receptor positive patients.

audits.t: Therapeutic hypothermia following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA): an audit of compliance at a large Australian hospital.
audits.tp: Targeted temperature management after cardiac arrest
audits.st: Therapeutic hypothermia as standard of care after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest due to ventricular arrhythmias
audits.f: Only 20% had TH commenced in the emergency department; mean time to goal temperature 595 minutes, not reached at all in 13%.

audits.t: Improving the Standard of Operative Notes within an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Department, using an Operative Note Proforma.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidelines on operative notes
audits.f: Mean data point inclusion 76.1%.
audits.c: Paper-based operative note proforma designed and piloted.
audits.r2: Mean data point inclusion 98.3%; all criteria improved.

audits.t: Impacts and outcomes of diabetes care in a high risk remote Indigenous community over time: implications for practice.
audits.tp: Diabetes care processes in primary care
audits.st: National optimal diabetes management guidelines (regular monitoring of care processes)
audits.f: Earlier audit of diabetes care processes and outcomes (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Intravenous fluid use in the acutely unwell adult medical inpatient: improving practice through a clinical audit process.
audits.st: Trust IV fluid guideline based on British consensus guidelines; seven local standards forming a prescribing bundle

audits.t: Avoiding never events: improving nasogastric intubation practice and standards.

audits.r2: Interpretation errors reduced from seven to one; documentation improved by 22%.

audits.t: Chapter 9 Biochemical variables amongst UK adult dialysis patients in 2010: national and centre-specific analyses.

audits.st: UK Renal Association clinical performance measures: phosphate in range, adjusted calcium 2.2-2.5 mmol/L, PTH 16-32 pmol/L, bicarbonate

audits.t: Chapter 14 Comparative audit of peritoneal dialysis catheter placement in England, Northern Ireland and Wales in 2011: a summary of progress to July 2012.
audits.st: 2009 Renal Association working party recommended PD access outcome measures
audits.f: 43 of 63 centres returned data on 863 PD catheter placements, 225 with missing insertion date; outcome results not yet available.

audits.t: Dosimetric verification of radiotherapy treatment planning systems in Serbia: national audit.
audits.st: IAEA recommendations and agreement criteria for measured vs calculated doses
audits.f: All test cases with advanced algorithms were within agreement criteria; larger deviations with simpler algorithms and higher beam energies.

audits.t: An audit of influenza vaccination status in adults with inflammatory bowel disease.
audits.st: Guidelines recommending influenza vaccination for high-risk patients including those on immunosuppressants
audits.f: 104 (41.6%) immunised against H1N1 and 62 (24.8%) against seasonal influenza; 158 (63.2%) on immunosuppressants.

audits.t: The care for chronic heart failure by general practitioners. Results from a clinical audit in Italy.
audits.tp: Chronic heart failure management in primary care
audits.st: Standards of care for chronic heart failure (diagnosis, medication, follow-up)
audits.f: Echocardiography used in 57%; diuretics 88%, ACE inhibitors or ARB 77%, beta-blockers 46%, anti-aldosterone agents 32%.
audits.r2: ACE inhibitor/ARB use increased to 80% and beta-blocker use to 56%.

audits.t: A clinical audit in a multidisciplinary care path for thoracic surgery: an instrument for continuous quality improvement.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline data showed age, indication and postoperative pain were associated with outcomes (full figures truncated in abstract).
audits.c: New multidisciplinary care path developed from baseline data in consensus meetings, introduced January 2008
audits.r2: Significant reduction in length of hospital stay, postoperative pain and loss of quality of life.

audits.t: Audit of diabetic care in a saudi primary care setting.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported (care relatively inappropriate and important parameters under-recorded)

audits.t: Audit of structure, process, and outcome of diabetic care at Al asyah primary health care centre, qassim region, saudi arabia.
audits.st: National Quality Assurance protocol for chronic diseases; ADA 2002 recommendations
audits.f: Process items covered in 73% and above except fundus examination and triglycerides; 21.4% good and 42.8% poor diabetic control.

audits.t: Variable compliance with clinical practice guidelines identified in a 1-day audit at 66 French adult intensive care units.
audits.st: Bundle of 13 clinical practice guidelines for ICU care
audits.f: Median compliance 75% (60-100), from 24% (sedation monitoring) to 96% (identified closest relative, bacteriological sampling before antibiotics); only 24% (20-27) of patients received fully compliant care.

audits.t: Secondary prevention therapies for coronary heart disease in patients with type 2 diabetes: an audit.
audits.tp: Secondary prevention in coronary heart disease
audits.st: Evidence-based secondary prevention pharmacotherapy (aspirin, beta-blockers, ACEI/ARB, lipid-lowering drugs)
audits.f: In CHD with vs without diabetes: beta-blockers 59.4% vs 69.2%, ACEI/ARB 86.5% vs 82.1%, statins 67.1% vs 59.7%, aspirin 88.7% vs 88.3%.

audits.t: Interventional cardiology audit report for 2011.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Procedural success 93.3%; major adverse cardiac events 3.6%, including mortality 0.5%; 93% drug-eluting stents.

audits.t: Epworth HealthCare cardiac surgery audit report 2011.
audits.st: Benchmarking against the Australian and New Zealand Society of Cardiac and Thoracic Surgeons database
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Prospective clinical audit of chloral hydrate administration practices in a neonatal unit.
audits.st: Study site's recommended chloral hydrate dosing range
audits.f: 238 doses to 32 patients; 84% ordered as repeating doses; median repetitive dose above the recommended range; distress assessment accompanied about half of doses.

audits.t: Auditing national HIV guidelines and policies: The United Kingdom CD4 Surveillance Scheme.
audits.st: National target of a CD4 count within 14 days of HIV diagnosis; national guidance on ARV for CD4 <350 cells/mm3
audits.f: CD4 count within 14 days of diagnosis met for 61% (2008); 83% of patients with CD4 <350 cells/mm3 received ARV; 52% diagnosed late (2009).

audits.t: A computer-aided audit system for respiratory therapy consult evaluations: description of a method and early results.
audits.st: Concordance of respiratory therapist care plans with gold standard care plans under RT-guided protocols
audits.f: Live audit system: 6.1 audits per month.
audits.c: New computer-aided audit system using the electronic medical record and an electronic respiratory therapy management system
audits.r2: 11 audits per month; concordance with gold standard care plans similar to the old system.

audits.t: Diagnosis and rehabilitation of visual field defects in stroke patients: a retrospective audit.
audits.tp: Visual field defect assessment after stroke
audits.st: Referral to perimetry and visual rehabilitation within one year (no explicit target)
audits.f: 34 (9.6%) referred to perimetry and 8 (2.3%) to visual rehabilitation.

audits.t: An audit of pain management following pediatric day surgery at British Columbia Children's Hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Pain reports and scores significantly higher at home than in hospital (P<0.01); good pain control commonly achieved after surgery.

audits.t: Myelosuppression monitoring after immunomodulator initiation in veterans with inflammatory bowel disease: a national practice audit.
audits.st: IBD guideline: white blood cell test within 90 days of immunomodulator initiation
audits.f: Only 57% had a WBC test within 90 days; monitoring rose from 48% in 2003 to 75% in 2009; facility rates ranged 0 to 83%.

audits.t: Translating obstetrics and gynaecology undergraduate experience into career aspiration: an audit of Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG) medical student placement standards.
audits.st: RCOG undergraduate placement standards (2006)
audits.f: Students rated the RCOG standards as highly appropriate.

audits.t: A re-audit of the use of definitions of sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS) in peer-reviewed literature.
audits.st: Use of one of three internationally accepted SIDS definitions
audits.f: 42% of papers quoted or referenced a standard definition.
audits.r2: 68% quoted or referenced a standard definition.

audits.t: Improving the quality of oral surgery referrals.
audits.st: Set standard for oral surgery referral content
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Redesigned referral proforma, guidance and feedback questionnaires distributed to referrers.
audits.r2: Increases of 52% in stating anaesthesia type, 48% medical history, 38% referral date, 35% symptom duration, 31% treatment provided, 18% reason for referral, 14% diagnosis, 10% radiograph inclusion.

audits.t: HIV diagnoses and missed opportunities. Results of the British HIV Association (BHIVA) National Audit 2010.
audits.st: 2008 UK HIV testing guidelines
audits.f: 52.2% had a late HIV diagnosis (CD4 <350 cells/mm3); a quarter had a missed opportunity for earlier diagnosis.

audits.t: UK national audit against the key performance indicators in the British Association for Sexual Health and HIV Medical Foundation for AIDS and Sexual Health Sexually Transmitted Infections Management Standards.

audits.f: Lowest-performing areas for level 3 clinics were STI/HIV risk assessment, care pathways, HIV test offer, information governance and receipt of chlamydia results within seven working days (worst); no figures given in abstract.

audits.t: Chlamydial partner notification in the British Association for Sexual Health and HIV (BASHH) 2011 UK national audit against the BASHH Medical Foundation for AIDS and Sexual Health Sexually Transmitted Infections Management Standards.
audits.st: BASHH/MedFASH STI Management Standards: ≥0.6 contacts seen per index case outside London, ≥0.4 in London
audits.f: Level 3: 43% (regional range 0-80%) of clinics outside London met ≥0.6 and 85% (82-88%) in London met ≥0.4; level 2: 39% outside London and 43% in London met the standards.

audits.t: Clinical audit of diabetes management can improve the quality of care in a resource-limited primary care setting.
audits.tp: Diabetes care processes in primary care
audits.st: Nine diabetic clinical processes
audits.f: Baseline medians for six of nine processes were below 50%.
audits.c: Clinical audit and feedback, with co-interventions after the baseline audit
audits.r2: Statistically significant improvement in seven of nine clinical processes (annual audits 2005, 2007, 2008 and 2009).

audits.t: Audit of audit: review of a clinical audit programme in a teaching hospital intensive care unit.
audits.st: National guidelines for clinical audit; UK Clinical Governance Support Team Audit Project Assessment Tool
audits.f: 22 of 25 projects were true audits; all retrospective; 4 were re-audits (3 showed improvement, 1 deterioration); 11 of 22 rated good quality.
audits.c: Series of improvements to the audit programme after the review.

audits.t: Audit of blood transfusion policy in head and neck surgery.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Retrospective review of 100 records found transfusion practice lacked standardisation on a scientific basis and represented resource over-utilisation.
audits.c: A new transfusion policy for head and neck surgery was proposed; no re-audit reported.

audits.t: An audit of prophylactic surgical antibiotic use in a Sudanese Teaching Hospital.
audits.st: International standards for surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (choice, dose, timing, duration)
audits.f: 99.4% (1,758) received prophylactic antibiotics; prophylaxis was recommended in 74.5% (1,288) of cases. Among recommended cases, 56.3% received a broad-spectrum antibiotic or unnecessary combination, 70.9% a sub-therapeutic dose, 9.3% (120) the first dose within the proper time window, and 97% (1,250) an extended duration. Compliance with all criteria was 2.7% (47).
audits.c: Development and implementation of local guidelines recommended; no re-audit reported.

audits.t: A clinical audit on diabetes care in patients with type 2 diabetes in Al-ain, United arab emirates.
audits.st: ICSI guidelines and international targets for glucose, BP and LDL-C
audits.f: 45.7% at target fasting glucose and 40.1% at target HbA1c; mean HbA1c 8.7%.
audits.c: Implementation of ICSI guidelines with an individualised structured approach.
audits.r2: 81.1% at target fasting glucose and 73.6% at target HbA1c; mean HbA1c 8.1%; BP improved.

audits.t: Re: Adult and paediatric tonsillectomy: a two-cycle audit of Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network 117 in a total of one hundred and sixty-nine patients.
audits.st: Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN) 117
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Findings of the UK national audit evaluating image-guided or image-assisted liver biopsy. Part II. Minor and major complications and procedure-related mortality.

audits.f: Standards met for pain, hypotension, haemorrhage, haemobilia and organ puncture; haemorrhage-related death target narrowly missed (0.11%, 4 of 3486). INR absent in 3% (97/2951), platelets absent in 1% (32/2986), INR over 1 week old in 8% (229/2888), platelets over 1 week old in 10% (291/2955).

audits.t: An audit of partner notification for syphilis and HIV.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Follow-up testing information available for 58% of traceable syphilis contacts and 59% of traceable HIV contacts; 78% and 90% respectively were informed of exposure; screening verification in 78% of syphilis and 94% of HIV contacts.

audits.t: An audit of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in children.
audits.st: Anti-emetic prescribing proportional to emetogenic potential of chemotherapy (evidence-based practice)
audits.f: Anti-emetic prescription was unrelated to the emetogenic potential of chemotherapy; dexamethasone was used in only 1 case; 20 children took no anti-emetics after discharge, of whom 11 had delayed vomiting.
audits.c: Evidence-based guidelines established with anti-emetic prescription proportional to emetogenic potential; education of staff, patients and families recommended. No re-audit reported.

audits.t: Improving quality of care among COPD outpatients in Denmark 2008-2011.
audits.st: Recommended processes of COPD care (annual FEV1, BMI, MRC dyspnoea, smoking status, cessation advice, pulmonary rehabilitation)
audits.f: Baseline process indicator fulfilment (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: National multidisciplinary quality improvement programme with register monitoring and audit
audits.r2: Registration fulfilment above 85% for all indicators; RR vs 2008: FEV1 2.14, BMI 2.24, MRC dyspnoea 2.25, smoking status 2.41, cessation advice 3.40, pulmonary rehabilitation offer 2.78.

audits.t: [Impact of quality improvement process upon the state of nutritional support in a critical care unit].
audits.st: Local nutritional support protocol (fulfilment of prescribed nutritional support, ≥80% of prescribed energy)
audits.f: Phase 1 (previous audit): overall mortality 40.0%; mean energy intake 574.7 ± 395.3 kcal/24 h.
audits.c: Presentation and publication of audit results, a new nutritional support protocol, and continuous education (expert talks, courses, protocol training)
audits.r2: Higher fulfilment of prescribed nutritional support, more patients receiving ≥80% of prescribed energy and fewer lost days; mortality 20.5% (p = 0.054); mean energy intake 591.1 ± 315.3 kcal/24 h (p > 0.05).

audits.t: Improved quality of management of eclampsia patients through criteria based audit at Muhimbili National Hospital, Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Bridging the quality gap.
audits.st: Evidence-based criteria from Ministry of Health guidelines, local guidelines, WHO manual and other sources
audits.f: Senior review of plan 76%; urine albumin 61%; partogram 75%; steroids 2.0%; Caesarean within 2 hours of decision 33%; FBC 28%; urea and creatinine 44%; liver enzymes 4.0%; specialist review within 2 hours 25%; maternal deaths 7.7%
audits.c: Implementation of recommendations from the initial audit
audits.r2: Senior review 99%; urine albumin 99%; partogram 95%; steroids 24%; Caesarean within 2 hours 61%; FBC 93%; urea and creatinine 86%; liver enzymes 86%; specialist review within 2 hours 39%; maternal deaths 0% (P=0.001)

audits.t: Nutritional screening among patients with cancer in an acute care hospital: a best practice implementation project.
audits.st: Three JBI criteria for nutritional screening
audits.f: Validated tool used 100%; screening on admission 96%; action plan for at-risk patients 46%.
audits.c: Simplified nutritional screening tool and empowering nurses to refer to the dietician.

audits.t: An audit of prescribing for type 2 diabetes in primary care: optimising the role of the community pharmacist in the primary healthcare team.
audits.tp: Type 2 diabetes care in primary care
audits.st: NICE type 2 diabetes guidelines
audits.f: All anti-hyperglycaemic prescribing was within guidance; 87.4% of patients on an anti-hypertensive were prescribed an ACE inhibitor or equivalent.

audits.t: Findings of the UK national audit evaluating image-guided or image-assisted liver biopsy. Part I. Procedural aspects, diagnostic adequacy, and accuracy.
audits.st: Sample adequacy 98%; diagnostic accuracy 90%
audits.f: Sample adequacy 97.96% (3401/3472), narrowly missing the standard; diagnostic accuracy 98.55% (3187/3234), meeting the standard.

audits.t: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis audit in two Queensland hospitals.
audits.st: Recommended VTE prophylaxis guidelines by risk stratification
audits.f: Appropriate prophylaxis in 235/372 (63%) medical, 273/326 (84%) surgical and 168/215 (78%) orthopaedic patients.

audits.t: Clinical audit: recent practice in caring for patients with acute severe colitis compared with published guidelines--is there a problem?
audits.st: Published guidelines for acute severe colitis (blood tests, C. difficile test, abdominal X-ray, colonic examination, VTE prophylaxis, severity scoring on days 1 and 3)
audits.f: Only 8 (26%) had all major management details; formal severity scoring on admission in one patient, descriptive severity in 7 (24%); some day 3 severity assessment in 9 (30%) without formal criteria.

audits.t: Audit of CT scanning of paranasal sinuses in patients referred with facial pain.
audits.tp: CT sinus imaging for facial pain
audits.st: EPOS 2007 guideline and International Headache Society criteria for investigating rhinosinusitis
audits.f: 16% had positive nasal endoscopic findings; 30 patients had Lund-Mackay score 0 and only 9 had significant changes (LMS 8 or more).
audits.c: Implementation of IHS and EPOS criteria.
audits.r2: Only 10 patients had CT per EPOS guideline, 4 with significant changes; 80% diagnosed and treated for non-sinogenic causes.

audits.t: Clinical audit of postpartum hemorrhage at district-level and referral-level hospitals in southern Thailand.
audits.st: Evidence-based checklist for immediate postpartum haemorrhage management
audits.f: District level: retained Foley catheter 44%, close haemodynamic monitoring 67%. Referral level: retained Foley catheter 76%, uterine massage documented 67%.

audits.t: An audit of level two and level three checks of anaesthesia delivery systems performed at three hospitals in South Australia.
audits.st: Australian and New Zealand College of Anaesthetists and manufacturer recommendations for level two and three anaesthetic machine checks
audits.f: Backup oxygen cylinder not checked in 45% of observations; emergency ventilation device not checked in 67%; breathing circuit not tested between patients in 79%; no documentation of checks in any case; no staff assessment or accreditation.

audits.t: Audit of decision-making regarding female genitourinary infections in outpatient practice.
audits.st: Panel of 9 specialist physicians' recommendations
audits.f: Panel supported 81% of prescribing decisions (14% not supported, 5% undecided) and 62% of diagnoses (13% not supported, 25% undecided); history and examination unsatisfactory in 22% of consultations.

audits.t: Four-week nutritional audit of preterm infants born <33 weeks gestation.

audits.f: Milk composition varied (protein 16.6 (13.4-27.6) g/L, energy 3074 (2631-3761) kJ/L); intakes based on measured composition differed from assumed; protein intake associated with weight gain.

audits.t: Medical audit of a rapid-throughput mammography screening practice: methodology and results of 27,114 examinations.
audits.st: Medical audit of screening mammography performance measures
audits.f: Sensitivity 93.1%, specificity 94.2%, positive predictive value 10.0%; biopsy malignancy yield 32.1%; 170 cancers, 76.5% stage 0 or 1.

audits.t: Management of anaphylaxis in the ED: a clinical audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Widespread inconsistencies in diagnosis and treatment of anaphylaxis (no figures given in abstract).

audits.t: Diabetes management in Australian rural aged care facilities: A cross--sectional audit.
audits.st: Current Australian diabetes management guidelines (antihypertensive, lipid-lowering and antiplatelet therapy)
audits.f: Only 41% of medication-managed residents were treated according to guidelines; of those with CVD, all on antihypertensives, 71% not managed for lipids and 20% not on antiplatelet therapy.

audits.t: Using a combined nursing and medical approach to reduce the incidence of central line associated bacteraemia in a New Zealand critical care unit: a clinical audit.
audits.st: Median central line associated bacteraemia rate of zero
audits.f: Mean CLAB rate 6.43 per 1000 catheter days (range 0-12.30, median 6.3).

audits.r2: Insertion bundle reduced mean CLAB rate to 1.50 per 1000 catheter days (median 0, p=.02); maintenance and high-risk bundles sustained median of zero over 12 months.

audits.t: Allied health services to nephrology: an audit of current workforce and meeting future challenges.
audits.tp: Allied health workforce in renal services

audits.f: All services provided dietetics, nine meeting benchmark (median 1:127); pharmacy in 10 (1:245), social work in 12 (1:191), psychology in 7 (1:396); podiatry in one-third (1:1077), none meeting benchmark.

audits.t: Audit of HIV testing frequency and behavioural interventions for men who have sex with men: policy and practice in sexual health clinics in England.
audits.tp: HIV and STI testing in men who have sex with men
audits.st: National guidance recommending frequent HIV testing and structured one-to-one behavioural interventions for MSM
audits.f: 92% (552/598) had one or more HIV test in a year, meeting the national minimum standard; only 52/251 (21%) accepted a structured one-to-one behavioural intervention (29/107, 27% among higher-risk MSM).

audits.t: Should prophylactic antibiotics be used routinely in epistaxis patients with nasal packs?
audits.tp: Antibiotic prophylaxis for nasal packing in epistaxis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: New treatment algorithm/guideline favouring topical antibiotics over systemic antibiotics
audits.r2: Systemic antibiotic prescribing in anterior nasal packing fell by 58.2% between cycles

audits.t: An audit of generic prescribing in a general surgical department.
audits.st: Health Service Executive generic prescription policy
audits.f: 51% of prescriptions were trade-name where an appropriate generic equivalent existed.

audits.t: Audit of complications in post-operative epidural analgesia and adherence to acute pain service protocols at an Indian cancer center.
audits.st: Established Acute Pain Service epidural protocols
audits.f: Variances from protocols were noted (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Antibiotic timing in neonates with suspected hospital-acquired infections.

audits.r2: Median antibiotic delivery time 75 minutes, with reduced variation (P < .001).

audits.t: Antimicrobial prophylaxis in open reduction and internal fixation of compound mandibular fractures: a collaborative regional audit of outcome.
audits.st: Infection rate after ORIF of mandibular fractures compared with other centres
audits.f: Wide range of antimicrobial prophylaxis used across units; infection rate 10.3%.

audits.r2: Infection rate 8.9% (vs 10.3%; χ2=0.051, df=1, p=0.83, not significant).

audits.t: Health equity audits in general practice: a strategy to reduce health inequalities.
audits.tp: Health equity in chronic disease management
audits.st: Key process and outcome indicators for CHD, type 2 diabetes and COPD by ethnicity, age and gender
audits.f: Baseline inequalities were found in each condition across the three east London PCTs.
audits.c: Practice-level health equity audit reports disseminated to practices with facilitation sessions.
audits.r2: Performance on physician-driven indicators (cholesterol in CHD, blood pressure and HbA1c in diabetes) improved, but smoking rates in COPD remained static; all ethnic groups improved without reduction in differences between them.

audits.t: An Australian secondary standard dosimetry laboratory participation in IAEA postal dose audits.
audits.st: IAEA/WHO postal dose audits
audits.f: Consistent absorbed dose to water measurements (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Management of uncomplicated malaria in underfives in private and public health facilities in South-eastern Nigeria: a clinical audit of current practices.
audits.st: WHO-recommended case management of uncomplicated malaria

audits.t: Auditing of medical chart among type 2 diabetic patient done by primary care physicians.
audits.tp: Type 2 diabetes care in primary care

audits.f: FMT vs PAT recorded: blood glucose 58% vs 30%; BP 70% vs 33%; total cholesterol 35% vs 22%; BMI 48% vs 28%; HbA1c 41% vs 75%; foot exam 26% vs 78%.

audits.t: Preoperative fasting: a clinical audit.
audits.st: Royal College of Nursing (2005) preoperative fasting guidelines
audits.f: Results upheld previous studies showing prolonged preoperative starving periods (no figures given in abstract).

audits.t: General practice theophylline audit in the Exeter Health District.
audits.st: Theophylline therapeutic range
audits.f: Serum theophylline below the therapeutic range in 75% of patients.

audits.t: Prospective audit of vitamin D levels of women presenting for their first antenatal visit at a tertiary centre.
audits.st: Hospital risk-based vitamin D screening guideline in pregnancy
audits.f: 318/472 (67.4%) were low-risk under the guideline; 46.2% of low-risk and 78.6% of high-risk women were vitamin D deficient.

audits.t: Audit of terminal care in a general practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Relatives dissatisfied in six cases, mainly due to poor communication; doctors dissatisfied in eight cases (communication, poor symptom control, inadequate care).

audits.t: Maintenance of patency of central venous access devices by registered nurses in an acute ambulatory setting: an evidence utilisation project.

audits.t: Measuring and improving the quality of postoperative epidural analgesia for major abdominal surgery using statistical process control charts.

audits.t: Replicating changes in hand hygiene in a surgical intensive care unit with remote video auditing and feedback.
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Implementing Quality Oncology Practice Initiative (QOPI) participation in a community oncology practice.
audits.st: ASCO Quality Oncology Practice Initiative (QOPI) documentation and certification measures
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Preoperative fasting in children: An audit and its implications in a tertiary care hospital.

audits.f: BMI z-score calculable for 3436 (62.9%); of the 12.6% obese children only one-third received an overweight/obese diagnosis.

audits.f: 684 incidents in 457 DAAs (11.5%); blister packs 10.5%, sachets 14.5%; unsuitable re-packing 50.1%, added medicine 9.8%, incorrect quantity 5.4%, omitted medicine 5.3%.

audits.t: Clinical audit improves hypertension control in hemodialysis patients.

audits.r2: Hypertension prevalence 51.1% at month 1 and 47.6% at month 6.

audits.t: Chlorhexidine to maintain cleanliness of laryngoscope handles: an audit and laboratory study.
audits.st: not reported

audits.r2: Significant improvement in incidence and extent of contamination compared with previous practice (p value truncated).

audits.t: Seven years' experience of Mohs micrographic surgery in a UK centre, and development of a UK minimum dataset and audit standards.

audits.t: Quality improvement in documentation of postoperative care nursing using computer-based medical records.

audits.r2: Quality of documentation improved (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: The effect of a resident-led quality improvement project on improving communication between hospital-based and outpatient physicians.

audits.t: Improving management of type 2 diabetes - findings of the Type2Care clinical audit.
audits.st: Annual cycle of care and diabetes targets (e.g. microalbumin)
audits.f: Mean HbA1c 6.9%.
audits.c: Feedback to GPs and a decision support tool.
audits.r2: Use of annual cycle of care plans increased by 12%; performance improved on all measures; mean HbA1c 6.9%.

audits.t: Colonoscopy practice in lagos, Nigeria: a report of an audit.
audits.st: Guideline standard colonoscopy quality indices
audits.f: Caecal intubation rate 81.2%; bowel preparation good in 81.4%; polyp detection 6.8%.

audits.t: A multidisciplinary audit of head and neck referrals: considerations for patients' timelines and outcomes.
audits.tp: Head and neck cancer two-week-wait pathway
audits.st: NICE 2004 Improving outcomes in head and neck cancer; 2-week wait referrals
audits.f: Mean time from referral to being seen 11 days for 2-week wait referrals and 34 days for other referrals.
audits.c: One-stop Rapid Diagnostic Clinic with on-site ultrasound and cytology.
audits.r2: Mean waiting time 9 days for 2-week wait and 23 days for other referrals; most reached a definitive outcome at first consultation.

audits.t: A completed audit cycle of the lateral scan projection radiograph in CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA); the impact on scan length and radiation dose.
audits.st: Optimal scan length from lung apex to lung base

audits.r2: Mean excess scan length 19.5 mm (SD 17.4), significantly lower.

audits.t: Treatment algorithm for oral anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy in epistaxis patients.
audits.st: Joint otolaryngology and haematology treatment algorithm for anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy
audits.f: 58% of patients were taking anticoagulant or antiplatelet medication on admission (across the study).
audits.r2: Significant decrease in withholding of aspirin, clopidogrel and warfarin.

audits.t: Clinical governance network for clinical audit to improve quality in epithelial ovarian cancer management.
audits.st: Evidence-based quality indicators for ovarian cancer workup and treatment
audits.f: Histological diagnosis in 222 (76.3%); FIGO surgical staging reported in 206 (70.9%); residual disease not always reported.
audits.c: Identification of reference centres and promotion of centralisation; new region-wide audit planned.

audits.t: Head injury: audit of a clinical guideline to justify head CT.
audits.tp: CT head justification in head injury
audits.st: NICE CG56 head injury guideline criteria for head CT
audits.f: 73% of CG56 criteria were documented; 32% of patients had head CT, 24% (37) of these with pathology; 24 patients (5%) had CT without documented clinical justification, none with pathology.
audits.c: Further education and awareness of head injury guidelines suggested; no re-audit reported.

audits.t: Compliance with the minimum dataset of the British Orthodontic Society/British Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons for record keeping for orthognathic patients: retrospective comparative multicentre audit.
audits.st: BOS/BAOMS minimum dataset for orthognathic clinical records
audits.f: Compliance varied between units; documentation of altered sensation was consistently poor and too many unnecessary radiographs were taken.
audits.c: Recirculation of the guidelines suggested; no re-audit reported.

audits.t: [Evaluation of the management of COPD exacerbations: an audit in French emergency services].
audits.st: French national guidelines for management of COPD exacerbations
audits.f: Respiratory rate and sputum description recorded in 99 (45%) records; oxygen given to 215 (97%), beta-2-agonist aerosols 209 (95%), anticholinergic aerosols 176 (80%); systemic corticosteroid 116 (52%), antibiotics 123 (56%); NIV used in only 59% of eligible acidotic patients.

audits.t: The diagnostic value of clinical examination and imaging used as part of an age-related protocol when diagnosing male breast disease: an audit of 1141 cases from a single centre.
audits.st: Local age-related triple assessment protocol (mammography in men 35 years or older)
audits.f: Sensitivity was 64.0% for clinical examination, 77.8% for mammography and 92.0% for ultrasound; 25 cancers were diagnosed, 24 in men over 40.

audits.t: Improving the quality of lung cancer care in Ontario: the lung cancer disease pathway initiative.
audits.st: Evidence-based lung cancer disease pathways and provincial quality metrics
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Multidisciplinary working groups, standardised diagnostic and treatment pathways, regional roadshows sharing performance data, funding for regional improvement, diagnostic assessment units and dyspnoea education materials.
audits.r2: Proportion of lung cancer patients with symptoms assessed at least monthly using ESAS improved (no figures given).

audits.t: Is point of care testing in Irish hospitals ready for the laboratory modernisation process? An audit against the current national Irish guidelines.
audits.st: 15 recommendations of the 2007 Irish National Guidelines for point of care testing
audits.f: Only a quarter of hospitals had POCT committees; staff allocation to POCT had doubled since the baseline survey.

audits.t: Introduction of the I-gel supraglottic airway device for prehospital airway management in a UK ambulance service.
audits.tp: Prehospital airway management in cardiac arrest
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: i-gel insertion success 94% versus endotracheal tube 90%; airway management method poorly documented in 11% of records.
audits.c: Individual feedback from Quality Improvement Officers on documentation.
audits.r2: i-gel insertion success 92% versus endotracheal tube 86%; upward trend in i-gel use.

audits.t: A prospective audit of a nurse independent prescribing within critical care.
audits.st: Prescription accuracy (patient data, dose, concentration, rate, frequency, legibility, signature)
audits.f: 40 errors in 1418 prescriptions (2.8%): advanced nurse practitioners 2 in 388 (0.6%), trainee medical staff 33 in 984 (3.4%), consultants 5 in 73 (6.8%).

audits.t: FIASCO II failure to achieve a satisfactory cardiac outcome study: the elimination of system errors.
audits.st: not reported

audits.r2: 7 deaths (0.27%) in low-risk patients, 3 preventable and 4 non-preventable; none from inadequate myocardial protection or communication failure.

audits.t: Decreasing severe pain and serious adverse events while moving intensive care unit patients: a prospective interventional study (the NURSE-DO project).
audits.tp: Pain and adverse events when moving ICU patients

audits.r2: Severe pain 2% (OR 0.30 (0.12; 0.95), P = 0.02); serious adverse events 21%.

audits.t: Completing the audit cycle improves surgical standards in lung cancer. Why do some patients still not receive the best care?

audits.f: Non-anatomical resections 12%; excision of at least 1, 2 and 3 N2 stations 86%, 63% and 40%.

audits.r2: Non-anatomical resections 6% (not significant); at least 1, 2 and 3 N2 stations 91%, 77% and 63% (p = 0.003).

audits.t: Surgical hospital audit of record keeping (SHARK)--a new audit tool for the improvement in surgical record keeping.

audits.t: Venous thromboembolism in ENT surgery: a review of the literature and completed audit cycle of adherence to national guidance.

audits.r2: 42 violations per 100 doses; absolute risk reduction 42 per 100 doses (95% CI 35-48).

audits.t: An identification and brief advice programme for low-risk alcohol consumption in an acute medical setting: an implementation study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean 67.3% of admitted patients screened in the earlier period.

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Medical audit of the quality of diabetes care: is primary care more successful than hospitals?
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Trichomonas vaginalis: an audit of clinical practice and the demography of infected patients at three London genitourinary medicine clinics.
audits.st: BASHH guidelines for Trichomonas vaginalis
audits.f: Contact tracing occurred in 87%; 56% of these confirmed at least one contact treated in the last month.

audits.t: A survey of HIV care in the UK: results of British HIV association (BHIVA) national audit 2010.
audits.st: 2008 UK HIV testing guidelines, including non-urgent results within 72 hours
audits.f: HIV testing routine in GU medicine and antenatal services but selective elsewhere; non-urgent results took over 72 hours in 29% of sites.

audits.t: An audit of pharyngeal gonorrhoea treatment in a public sexual health clinic in Adelaide, South Australia.
audits.st: Local protocol of ceftriaxone 250 mg with test of cure; CDC 2010 and BASHH 2011 gonorrhoea guidelines
audits.f: Six test-of-cure failures over 11 years among 215 patients treated for pharyngeal gonorrhoea.

audits.t: Delay prior to expedited carotid endarterectomy: a prospective audit of practice.

audits.st: Carotid endarterectomy within 14 days of index symptom
audits.f: 74/87 (85%) underwent CEA within 14 days; median delay 8 days; 10 (11%) had recurrent symptoms before surgery.

audits.t: Quality improvement in colorectal cancer in local health integration network 4 (LHIN 4) project (QICC-L4): integrated knowledge translation in a large geographic region.
audits.st: Surgeon-selected quality markers: preoperative imaging, reporting of rectal radial margin, positive radial margin rate

audits.t: Improving access and satisfaction with spiritual care in the hospice setting.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Spiritual care referrals falling while hospice census rose (no figures given).
audits.c: Staff survey, education on spirituality and the chaplain's role, and an audit of chaplain time allocation.
audits.r2: Increased use of spiritual care by patients and staff and two new full-time chaplain posts (no figures given).

audits.t: Formative assessment based on an audit and feedback improves nuchal translucency ultrasound image quality.
audits.st: CFEF/CNRS nuchal translucency image-scoring method
audits.f: Low scorers who later received feedback had a mean score of 11.1 +/- 1.3.
audits.c: Individual audit feedback report on the first series of 30 images (73 sonographers; 15 received no feedback).
audits.r2: Low scorers with feedback improved to 13.4 +/- 1.4 (significant).

audits.t: Medicines Reconciliation on Admission to Inpatient Psychiatric Care: Findings from a UK Quality Improvement Programme.
audits.st: Two or more sources of information consulted about current medicines (proxy for medicines reconciliation)
audits.f: Medicines reconciliation possible in 71%; discrepancies found in 25% of these.
audits.r2: Medicines reconciliation possible in 79%; discrepancies found in 31%.

audits.t: National audit of bedside transfusion practice.
audits.st: Best practice for patient identification and monitoring during transfusion
audits.f: Most patients received safe transfusion with adequate identity checks and monitoring, but some lacked an identity wristband or monitoring (no figures given in abstract).

audits.t: Variability of hospital resources for acute care of COPD patients: the European COPD Audit.
audits.st: COPD guidelines
audits.f: Larger hospitals had more resources and staff; guideline adherence varied with hospital size but differences were small and inconsistent.

audits.t: Multidetector CT radiation dose optimisation in adults: short- and long-term effects of a clinical audit.
audits.st: Diagnostic reference levels (75th percentile doses) for common CT examinations
audits.f: Baseline survey of CTDIvol and DLP for head, sinus, cervical spine, thorax, abdomen and lumbar spine (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: External clinical audit in each department in 2008 to optimise default CT parameters.
audits.r2: DLP per examination fell 32-69% for all regions between 2007 and 2009; DRLs reduced by 20-78%, mean DLP per examination by 18-75% and collective dose by 30%.

audits.t: Can we prevent under-diagnosis and misdiagnosis of bipolar affective disorder? Repeat audits to assess the epidemiological change in the caseload of a community mental health team when bipolar disorder is accurately assessed and diagnosed.
audits.st: Team standards based on DSM-IV criteria for bipolar I and II
audits.f: Bipolar I 10.5%, bipolar II 0%; recurrent depressive disorder 16.1%, other unipolar depression 18.7%.
audits.c: Patients reassessed against DSM-IV based standards.
audits.r2: Bipolar I 11.0%, bipolar II 9.7%; recurrent depressive disorder 4.8%, other unipolar depression 8.0%.

audits.t: Audit to identify the number of patients with multiple diagnoses in a community mental health team in Bedford, England.
audits.st: Every patient should have only one mental health diagnosis where possible
audits.f: 23.2% of patients had multiple diagnoses.
audits.c: No intervention; repeated measurements in June 2011 and February 2013.

audits.t: The incidence of Parkinson's disease in a Bedford Community "Adult Working Age" Mental Health Team and its relationship with the use of atypical antipsychotics: an audit and description of current practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Case descriptions of patients assessed for Parkinson's disease; many were started on Parkinson's medication (no figures given in abstract).

audits.t: Acute quadriceps tendon rupture: a pragmatic approach to diagnostic imaging.
audits.tp: Imaging for suspected quadriceps tendon rupture
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: MRI used in 4%; misdiagnosis 4/47 (9%) leading to exploration of an intact tendon.
audits.c: Recommendation to increase the use of MRI.

audits.t: External validation of the Society of Thoracic Surgeons General Thoracic Surgery Database.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 28 omissions among 559 lobectomy cases, 94.6% agreement with operative logs; overall data accuracy 94.9%; all category agreement rates above 90%.

audits.t: Impact of national guidelines on reporting anaphylaxis during anaesthesia -- an outcome audit.
audits.st: AAGBI 2008 guideline on suspected anaphylaxis during anaesthesia
audits.f: 12 patients referred for suspected anaphylaxis before the guideline.
audits.c: Local implementation of the 2008 AAGBI guideline and Anaphylaxis Referral Form.
audits.r2: 53 patients referred; improved documentation of referral to local and national databases.

audits.t: [An audit of type 2 diabetes management in a diabetes center in Marrakech].
audits.st: Current type 2 diabetes management recommendations
audits.f: HbA1c every six months recorded in 59%; haemodynamic status, weight and height in 30%; complication screening in half; adherence assessed in 97% of 27 consultations; foot examination in 18%.

audits.t: Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA) utilisation by rural clinicians in acute ischaemic stroke: an audit of current practice and clinical outcomes.
audits.st: rt-PA implementation guidelines and treatment protocol
audits.f: 20 (3.3%) received rt-PA; median onset-to-needle 2 h 34 min and door-to-needle 1 h 40 min; no protocol violations; 2 (10%) symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage; one death within 6 months.

audits.t: Completing the audit cycle: the impact of an electronic reporting system on the feedback loop in surgical specialties.
audits.st: Reported incidents should be evaluated and acted upon
audits.f: 43% of reported incidents evaluated and 40% acted upon.

audits.t: Audit of acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease at Waitemata District Health Board, New Zealand.
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines for acute exacerbations of COPD
audits.f: Good adherence in several areas; room for improvement in NIV use, ABG and spirometry measurement and pulmonary rehabilitation referral (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Improved sexual history taking in the 2012 BASHH asymptomatic screening re-audit.
audits.st: BASHH guidelines for asymptomatic screening (documentation of oral and anal sex, gonorrhoea NAAT, hepatitis B screening in MSM, HIV screening)
audits.f: 2009 audit led to recommendations on documentation, NAAT use, hepatitis B and HIV screening.
audits.r2: Improvement in all areas measured; gonorrhoea NAAT testing doubled, but 10% still had microscopy not recommended by BASHH.

audits.t: The national one week prevalence audit of universal meticillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) admission screening 2012.
audits.st: Department of Health universal MRSA admission screening policy
audits.f: Screened: 61% of emergency admissions, 81% electives, 47% day-cases; 37% (219/596) of new MRSA patients discharged before result; 55% (205/376) of the rest isolated post-result.

audits.t: Audit of maternal mortality ratio and causes of maternal deaths in the largest maternity hospital in Cairo, Egypt (Kasr Al Aini) in 2008 and 2009: lessons learned.
audits.tp: Maternal death and severe morbidity review
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Cutting cancer waiting times: streamlining cervical lymph node biopsy.

audits.st: National cancer services guidelines for waiting times
audits.f: Guidelines not met; median wait from referral to biopsy 74 days (IQR 47-113).
audits.c: Referral proforma and a co-ordinator arranging biopsy appointments.

audits.t: A national audit of the management of young people in genitourinary medicine clinics (level 3 services) in the United Kingdom.
audits.tp: Sexual health care for young people
audits.st: BASHH 2010 guideline on STIs in children and young people: offer of screen 90%, acceptance 90%, risk assessment proforma completed 100%, following a guideline 100%
audits.f: Of 1946 at risk, 1871 (96%) offered tests and 1692 (90%) accepted (standards met); 1732/2108 (82%) assessed with a proforma (standard 100% not met); 68 (93%) clinics follow BASHH guidelines.

audits.t: Chronic kidney disease and diabetes in the national health service: a cross-sectional survey of the U.K. national diabetes audit.
audits.tp: Diabetes management in chronic kidney disease
audits.st: Therapeutic targets for HbA1c and systolic blood pressure
audits.f: Achievement of systolic blood pressure and HbA1c targets was poor; 67.8% of people with type 1 diabetes failed to achieve the HbA1c target (threshold truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Identification of important and potentially avoidable risk factors in a prospective audit study of neonatal deaths in a paediatric hospital in Vietnam.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 235 deaths and 67 expected deaths among 5763 admissions; six potentially avoidable risk factors identified in 85% (60/71) of neonates with relatively good prognosis.

audits.t: Management program decreases postoperative nausea and vomiting in high-risk and in general surgical patients: a quality improvement cycle.
audits.st: Institutional multimodal PONV protocol using Apfel risk score
audits.f: PONV in PACU in 37/395 (9.4%).
audits.c: Multimodal PONV protocol (anaesthetic technique and antiemetics) with quarterly audit feedback and teaching sessions.

audits.t: Deployed antimicrobial stewardship: an audit of antimicrobial use at Role 3.

audits.f: 84.8% (212/250) were prescribed antimicrobials in line with the formulary: 93.5% (130/139) in battle injury versus 73.9% (82/111) in disease and non-battle injury.

audits.t: Safety and predictability of conscious sedation in dentistry -- a multi-centre regional audit: South and West Wales experience.
audits.st: Locally agreed standards: completion rate of 90% and adverse incident rate of 2% or less
audits.f: Completion rate 92%; minor adverse incident rate 2.6%.

audits.t: National sentinel stroke audit 1998-2011.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Monitoring lithium therapy: the impact of a quality improvement programme in the UK.

audits.t: Convergence of HbA1c values towards target in 272 primary care patients following nine years of target-driven care.

audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Can we improve the prevention and detection of congenital abnormalities? An audit of early pregnancy care in New Zealand.

audits.t: An audit of eye dryness and corneal abrasion in ICU patients in Iran.
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Audit of referral pathways in the diagnosis of lung cancer: a pilot study.

audits.t: A 5-year audit of cataract surgery outcomes after posterior capsule rupture and risk factors affecting visual acuity.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 887 capsule ruptures (rate 1.8%); visual success 93.9% after rupture versus 98.5% in uneventful cases.

audits.t: Inpatient hypoglycaemia: a study of nursing management.

audits.f: 117 hypoglycaemic episodes in 32 patients; initial glucose treatment in 46 (40.4%); repeat capillary glucose at 10-15 minutes in 35 (30.7%); only 36.7% of episodes corrected within 30 minutes.

audits.st: National nursing documentation model
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Results of a mixed-methods evaluation of partnerships for health: a quality improvement initiative for diabetes care.

audits.r2: Significant improvement (P ≤ .005) in documented A1c, cholesterol, ACR, creatinine, eGFR, ECG, foot/eye/neuropathy examination, BMI, waist circumference and depression screening; more patients at LDL and BP targets (P ≤ .001).

audits.t: Bridging efforts to longitudinally improve and evaluate VEnous thromboembolism prophylaxis uptake in hospitalized cancer patients through Interprofessional Teamwork (BELIEVE IT): a study by Princess Margaret Cancer Centre.

audits.t: Cystogram use and outcomes in colorectal surgery involving bladder repair: a clinical audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: All patients had at least one postoperative cystogram; only 46% had cystogram instructions documented in the operation note; 4 (7%) showed a leak.

audits.t: Improvement in the management of gout is vital and overdue: an audit from a UK primary care medical practice.

audits.f: 74% (226) had serum uric acid recorded, 11% (34) eGFR ever, 53% (162) glucose; 34% (105) ever and 25% (77) currently on urate-lowering therapy.

audits.t: Comparative audit of oxygen use in the prehospital setting in acute COPD exacerbation over 5 years.

audits.r2: HIGH 80 (44.0%), NEB 61 (33.5%), LOW 41 (22.5%); distribution significantly different from 2005.

audits.st: Current best practice recommendations for plasma exchange prescription
audits.f: 135 PE treatments using 156 membranes; premature circuit clotting 15.5%; TTP the commonest indication (37%); regimens not always prescribed per best practice; no patient complications.

audits.t: A multifaceted intervention  to improve sepsis management  in general hospital wards with  evaluation using segmented  regression of interrupted time series.

audits.r2: All outcome measures improved but differences were small and interrupted time series analysis did not attribute change to the intervention.

audits.t: A re-audit of paediatric ENT services in England and Wales.

audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: 56% response from 164 departments; children's ward facilities remained high; more staff qualified in paediatric life support; anaesthetic supervision and post-operative management improved.

audits.t: Clinical audit of diabetes care in the bahrain defence forces hospital.
audits.st: Recognised standards for diabetes process and outcome measures

audits.t: [Romanian echoes of European COPD audit].
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in acute medical admissions to a university teaching hospital.
audits.st: Appropriate thromboprophylaxis for at-risk patients
