audits.r2: Costs fell to $80,319 (46% reduction, $69,424 saved, 78% from carbapenems); audit adherence 80%; moxifloxacin use fell by -1.9 DDDs per 1000 patient-days per month (P = 0.048); C. difficile 19.6 per 10,000 patient-days (IRR 0.8).

audits.t: Improvements in newborn care and newborn resuscitation following a quality improvement program at scale: results from a before and after study in Tanzania.
audits.tp: Newborn resuscitation and essential newborn care
audits.st: Essential newborn care quality index
audits.f: Observed essential newborn care quality index 39%.

audits.t: Duration of participation in continuous quality improvement: a key factor explaining improved delivery of Type 2 diabetes services.
audits.st: Best practice guideline scheduled services for type 2 diabetes
audits.f: Over 10,000 audit records analysed; longer CQI participation, remoteness and regular attendance associated with greater adherence.

audits.t: Challenges of audit of care on clinical quality indicators for hypertension and type 2 diabetes across four European countries.
audits.tp: Chronic disease monitoring in primary care
audits.st: Clinical quality indicators for hypertension and type 2 diabetes from OECD, WHO and ECHI sources
audits.f: Huge variability across countries in compliance with indicators (figures not given).

audits.t: An Audit Of Obsessive Compulsive Disorder in A Bedford (UK) Community Mental Health Team.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Many OCD patients were complex, had not responded to first-line treatment such as SSRIs or basic psychology, and had comorbidities (no figures given).

audits.t: Nosocomial bacteriuria in elderly inpatients may be leading to considerable antibiotic overuse: an audit of current management practice in a secondary level care hospital in New Zealand.
audits.st: No treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria
audits.f: Significant bacteriuria in 30% of patients; 54% of episodes were ASB/CA-ASB without inflammatory response; treatment of ASB and CA-ASB accounted for 43% of antibiotic courses; 55% of antibiotic treatment days unnecessary.

audits.t: A complete audit cycle to assess adherence to a lung protective ventilation strategy.
audits.st: ARDS network mechanical ventilation protocol: tidal volume 6 ml/kg ideal body weight and plateau pressure 30 cm H2O or less
audits.f: Tidal volume 9.5 ml/kg IBW; standard not met
audits.c: Implementation of a protective ventilation strategy and an educational programme
audits.r2: Tidal volume 6.6 ml/kg IBW; significant improvement

audits.t: Implementation of a new tool to improve the efficacy and safety of surgical handovers.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England (2007) minimum data-set for safe handover
audits.f: Name and responsible consultant recorded in all cases; age recorded in 52%.
audits.c: New detailed electronic handover proforma and training.
audits.r2: Age recorded in 85%; significant improvement in completeness of handover information.

audits.t: Clinical audit of patients hospitalized due to COPD exacerbation. MAG-1 Study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Smoking habit recorded in only 45%; no previous lung function data in 31%; median stay 7 days; 90-day mortality 12.4%; readmission 49%.

audits.t: The long-term effects of training interventions on transfusion practice: a follow-up audit of red cell concentrate utilisation at Kimberley Hospital, South Africa.
audits.st: Transfusion guidelines for red cell concentrate in chronically anaemic adults (appropriateness, anaemia investigation, threshold, wastage, consent)
audits.f: 25 transfusion episodes audited retrospectively (figures not given).
audits.r2: No statistically significant impact of current training; but significant improvement compared with a 2010 audit.

audits.t: A multi-institutional dosimetry audit of rotational intensity-modulated radiotherapy.
audits.st: Gamma index pass criterion: >95% of pixels passing in all measured planes
audits.f: Point dose differences mean 0.1±2.6% (3DTPS test) and 0.2±2.0% (clinical trial plans); 34/43 planning and delivery combinations achieved >95% pixels passing gamma in all measured planes.

audits.t: Improving the quality of documentation of paediatric post-take ward rounds: the impact of an acrostic.
audits.st: Documentation of nine aspects of the post-take ward round (acrostic items)
audits.f: Problem 84%, investigations 26%, fluids 16%, drugs 26%, patient/parental concerns 16%, nursing concerns 4%.
audits.c: Acrostic mnemonic introduced at a teaching session and in mandatory induction for new doctors.
audits.r2: Problem 94%, investigations 72%, fluids 74%, drugs 76%, patient/parental concerns 72%, nursing concerns 48%.

audits.t: The quality of treatment of hyperacute ischemic stroke in Canada: a retrospective chart audit.
audits.st: Thrombolysis rate as key quality indicator of hyperacute stroke care
audits.f: 5.4% of stroke and 6.1% of ischaemic stroke patients received thrombolysis; comprehensive stroke centres treated about one-third of ischaemic cases.

audits.t: The effects of audit and feedback and electronic referrals on the quality of primary care referral letters.
audits.st: Nine-point referral letter checklist
audits.f: Average referral letter score 81.4%.
audits.c: Written feedback on referral letter quality; later introduction of electronic referrals
audits.r2: Average score improved to 86.9% after feedback.

audits.t: Improving pressure ulcer risk assessment and management using the Waterlow scale at a London teaching hospital.
audits.st: Waterlow pressure ulcer risk assessment scale
audits.f: Nursing Waterlow score recorded for 81% of patients; nursing scores were lower than study scores.
audits.c: Staff questionnaires, educational sessions, presentations and posters on risk stratification.
audits.r2: Nursing Waterlow score recorded for 100% of patients (p value truncated in abstract); differences between nursing and study scores reduced.

audits.t: Discharge communication from inpatient care: an audit of written medical discharge summary procedure against the new National Health Service Standard for clinical handover.
audits.st: Standard Six (clinical handover) of the Australian National Safety and Quality Health Service Standards
audits.f: 26% of departments had a documented procedure; 52% monitored completion; 48% monitored timeliness; 22% gave patients a copy; 26% trained staff.

audits.t: Deployed communication between the Role 3 and Role 1.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1/40 (2.5%) discharge summaries arrived from Role 3 to Role 1.
audits.c: Implementation of a system to transfer discharge information from Role 3 to Role 1.

audits.t: Audit of lymphadenectomy in lung cancer resections using a specimen collection kit and checklist.
audits.tp: Intraoperative lymph node staging in lung cancer surgery
audits.st: Mediastinal lymph node dissection or systematic sampling in lung cancer resection; concordance of surgeon claims, pathology and operation notes
audits.f: With pre-labelled specimen kit and checklist, 73% had mediastinal dissection or systematic sampling; surgeon claims concordant with pathology in 80% (kappa 0.69); operation note audit concordance poor (kappa 0.14 vs pathology, 0.09 vs surgeon claims).

audits.t: Implementation of an Evidence Based Guideline for Assessment and Documentation of the Civil Commitment Process.
audits.st: American Psychiatric Association recommended 11 domains of assessment
audits.f: 25.5% of evaluations contained all 11 APA domains.
audits.c: Evidence-based documentation form for civil commitment evaluations plus one-to-one education session for each examiner

audits.t: Multicentre study to develop a medication safety package for decreasing inpatient harm from omission of time-critical medications.
audits.st: Critical medication list and omitted dose audit tool
audits.f: Audit tool tested in 321 patients receiving 17,361 doses (omission rates not given).
audits.c: Medication safety package: critical medication list, audit tool, user guide and nursing education presentation

audits.t: Improving operative flow during pediatric airway evaluation: a quality-improvement initiative.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Personnel exited the OR in 55% of MLBs (n = 22); surgical technologist 20%, circulator 38%, surgeon 25% (10/40); equipment retrieval in 40%.
audits.c: Pre-case huddles on equipment, improved case ordering and preference cards, OR door sign to limit traffic, and discouraging breaks during airway procedures
audits.r2: Surgical technologist exiting fell to 8% (n = 5), circulator 27% (n = 17), surgeon 9% (6/66, P = .03).

audits.t: Piloting laboratory quality system management in six health facilities in Nigeria.
audits.st: WHO/AFRO SLIPTA checklist star rating
audits.f: Baseline: two labs 1-star, four 0-star; internal audit 4%, occurrence management 15%.
audits.c: Advocacy, capacity building, mentorship and quality improvement projects.
audits.r2: Exit: four labs 4-star, one 3-star, one 2-star; internal audit 76%, occurrence management 81%.

audits.t: Optimising stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation: application of the GRASP-AF audit tool in a UK general practice cohort.
audits.st: Oral anticoagulation for AF patients at high stroke risk (CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2 or CHADS2 ≥1), using the GRASP-AF tool
audits.f: Of those with CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2, 39.7% were not receiving appropriate OAC; of those with CHADS2 ≥1, 39.5% were not.

audits.t: Pressure injury prevention success in a regional hospital.
audits.st: State average pressure injury prevalence and best practice guidelines
audits.f: Pressure injury prevalence significantly above the State average (figures not given).
audits.c: Quality improvement strategies addressing accountability, documentation, education and risk assessment
audits.r2: Authors report significantly decreased hospital-acquired pressure injuries (figures not given).

audits.t: Variations in acute hospital stroke care and factors influencing adherence to quality indicators in 6 European audits.
audits.st: Predefined acute stroke care quality indicators (thrombolysis, anticoagulation, stroke unit care, dysphagia testing, antiplatelets)
audits.f: Substantial variation in adherence to quality indicators; older age associated with lower probability of thrombolysis, anticoagulation or stroke unit care and higher probability of dysphagia testing; women less likely to receive anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy or stroke unit care.

audits.t: Diabetic hypertensive control and treatment: a descriptive report from the audit diabetes control and management (adcm) registry.
audits.st: Target BP of 130/80 mmHg or less in diabetes
audits.f: 65% had hypertension; BP recorded in 94.4%, of whom 58.5% had BP >130/80 mmHg; 65.9% on antihypertensives; about 40% had hypertension well controlled.

audits.t: An audit of sputum smear negative pulmonary tuberculosis cases in kinta district, perak, in 2011.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 47 (81%) true smear-negative; 6 (10.3%) were actually smear positive; 5 (8.6%) misdiagnosed as TB.

audits.t: Diagnostic miss rate for colorectal cancer: an audit.
audits.st: Counselling about a 5% colonoscopy miss rate recommended by most societies
audits.f: 17% (26/150) investigated in prior 3 years; 8% (12/150) false negatives; false negative rate colonoscopy 3.5% (3/85), CTC 6.7% (1/17), CT 9.4% (5/53), barium enema 26.7% (4/15).

audits.t: Thyroid cytopathology with an emphasis on the 'atypical cells of uncertain significance' category: a 3-year audit with cytohistologic correlation.
audits.st: Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology (AUS/FLUS malignancy rate 5-15%)
audits.f: Inadequate 23%, benign 60%, AUS/FLUS 8%, suspicious for follicular neoplasm 4%, suspicious for malignancy 2%, malignant 2%.

audits.t: Childhood extravasation injuries: improved outcome following the introduction of hospital-wide guidelines.
audits.st: Hospital-wide guidelines (2005): early referral to plastic surgeons and washout of high-risk cases
audits.f: Earlier review: favourable outcome in 86%.
audits.r2: 82 injuries in 78 patients; 60% referred within 6 h, 30% in 6-12 h, 10% after 12 h; mean time to referral 8 h; 26% needed washout; tissue necrosis in 3 (4%), none needing surgery.

audits.t: Evaluation of a consultant audit and feedback programme to improve the quality of antimicrobial prescribing in acute medical admissions.
audits.st: Four quality indicators: documented indication; guideline choice or justified deviation; documented stop/review prompt; antimicrobial not deemed unnecessary by specialists
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Pharmacist-led consultant performance audit and feedback at quarterly intervals
audits.r2: Documented indication improved by 6.0% (95% CI 2.5, 9.6) and guideline adherence by 8.7% (95% CI 3.7, 13.7), significant in all follow-up periods; stop/review prompt improved in all but the first period.

audits.t: Improving maternal and child health systems in Fiji through a perinatal mortality audit.
audits.st: Current guidelines for investigating stillbirths and neonatal deaths
audits.f: 141 stillbirths and neonatal deaths analysed (57 hospital A, 84 hospital B); stillbirths were 28 (49%) in hospital A and 53 (63%) in hospital B.
audits.c: Training of clinicians and managers in perinatal mortality audit and a refined audit datasheet

audits.t: An audit and feedback system for effective quality improvement in head and neck surgery: Can we become better surgeons?
audits.st: Negative performance measures: length of stay (2 days or longer for low-acuity, 11 days or longer for high-acuity procedures), transfusion, return to theatre within 7 days, 30-day readmission, SSI and mortality
audits.f: Mean length of stay 2.1 days for low-acuity and 10.5 days for high-acuity procedures; 39.1% of low-acuity procedures had one or more negative indicators.
audits.c: Risk-adjusted individual performance feedback to surgeons
audits.r2: Length of stay fell to 1.5 days (P = .005) for low-acuity and 7 days (P = .003) for high-acuity procedures; negative indicators in low-acuity procedures fell to 28.6%.

audits.t: Relationship between input and output in acute medicine - secondary analysis of the Society for Acute Medicine's benchmarking audit 2013 (SAMBA '13).
audits.tp: Acute medical unit function and flow
audits.st: Society for Acute Medicine published quality indicators for timely assessment and discharge
audits.f: Performance against quality indicators was worst in the early evening; units admitting fewer than 40 patients performed better.

audits.t: Microbiology and audit of vascular access-associated bloodstream infections in multi-ethnic Asian hemodialysis patients in a tertiary hospital.
audits.st: In-house antibiotic guidelines for empirical therapy of vascular access-associated bloodstream infection
audits.f: In-house guideline used as empirical therapy in 24 episodes (16.7%); MRSA/MSSA 64.2% (68/106) of gram-positive infections; gram-negatives in 26.4% (38/144).

audits.t: An audit of antimicrobial prescribing in an acute dental care department.
audits.st: FGDP(UK) and Scottish Dental Clinical Effectiveness guidelines on antimicrobial prescribing; target 100% compliance
audits.f: 30% of prescriptions appropriate; 62% of practitioners recorded a diagnosis.
audits.c: Two-month intervention of extensive training and education of staff and students.
audits.r2: 80% of prescriptions appropriate; 100% recorded a diagnosis.

audits.t: Evaluation of a minimal sedation protocol using ICU sedative consumption as a monitoring tool: a quality improvement multicenter project.
audits.st: Guideline-based minimal sedation practice
audits.f: Length of mechanical ventilation 3.91 ± 6.2 days.
audits.c: Multifaceted minimal sedation programme with multidisciplinary daily rounds and monthly audits of sedative consumption with feedback and benchmarking.
audits.r2: Length of mechanical ventilation 3.15 ± 4.6 days; mean difference -0.76 (95% CI -1.10 to -0.43).

audits.t: Documentation of medication changes in inpatient clinical notes: an audit to support quality improvement.
audits.st: Seven quality criteria for documenting medication changes in progress notes
audits.f: 519 medication changes on NIMCs; just over half documented in progress notes; documentation seldom comprehensive.

audits.t: Assessing the use of initial oxygen therapy in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients: a retrospective audit of pre-hospital and hospital emergency management.
audits.st: Recommended controlled inspired oxygen (FiO2 ≤0.28) in COPD exacerbations
audits.f: COPD recognised in 53%; SpO2 recorded in 124; FiO2 >0.28 given in 54 patients in ambulances and 35 in the ED.

audits.t: Comparison of Quality Oncology Practice Initiative (QOPI) Measure Adherence Between Oncology Fellows, Advanced Practice Providers, and Attending Physicians.
audits.st: Quality Oncology Practice Initiative (QOPI) measures
audits.f: Fellows and attendings similar on 90 of 94 metrics; APPs and attendings similar on 88 of 90; oral chemotherapy plan documented 92% attendings vs 63% fellows (88% on re-review).

audits.t: Institutional review of compliance with NCCN guidelines for breast cancer: lessons learned from real-time multidimensional synoptic reporting.
audits.st: NCCN Guidelines for breast cancer
audits.f: Compliance: staging 94%, surgery 97%, chemotherapy 91%, hormone therapy 89%, radiotherapy 91%, follow-up 85%, ER/PR and HER2 100%.

audits.t: A 3 year audit of adult epilepsy care in a Nigerian tertiary hospital (2011-2013).
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 41% had good seizure control (no seizure in preceding year); 76% on monotherapy; 21% non-compliant with AEDs.

audits.t: Red blood cell transfusion practices: a College of American Pathologists Q-Probes study of compliance with audit criteria in 128 hospitals.
audits.st: Institutional RBC transfusion audit criteria
audits.f: Median pretransfusion haemoglobin 8.1 g/dL; median compliance with institutional guidelines 69% (range 0%-100%); 60% (2063/6518) single-unit transfusions.

audits.t: Professional responsibility in maternity care: role of medical audit.
audits.tp: Maternal death and severe morbidity review
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Medical audit of maternal and perinatal deaths and consultation in peripheral facilities
audits.r2: By 1984 maternal and perinatal mortality had declined and clinical judgement improved.

audits.t: Measuring antimicrobial prescribing quality in Australian hospitals: development and evaluation of a national antimicrobial prescribing survey tool.
audits.st: Antimicrobial prescribing survey criteria (indication documented, surgical prophylaxis not over 24 h, guideline compliance, appropriateness)
audits.f: Pilot across 32 hospitals (results not given).
audits.c: Audit tool revised after participant feedback
audits.r2: Second pilot across 85 hospitals identified targets: indication documentation, surgical prophylaxis over 24 h, guideline compliance and appropriateness.

audits.t: Risk stratification and stroke prevention therapy care gaps in Canadian atrial fibrillation patients (from the Co-ordinated National Network to Engage Physicians in the Care and Treatment of Patients With Atrial Fibrillation chart audit).
audits.st: Formal stroke (CHADS2) and bleeding (HAS-BLED) risk assessment; suggested warfarin time in therapeutic range target of ≥70%
audits.f: No annual stroke risk assessment in 15% and no formal tool in 33%; bleeding risk not assessed in 25% and no formal tool in 47%. Warfarin TTR ≥70% in 1,827 (55%), 50-69% in 674 (20%) and <50% in 845 (25%); median TTR 73%.

audits.t: The Royal College of Radiologists' audit of prostate brachytherapy in the year 2012.
audits.st: Standards from guidelines in use at the start of 2012 covering case mix and dosimetry
audits.f: 49 of 59 centres submitted data; 29 performed prostate brachytherapy and 25 (86%) gave full data. Compliance was excellent in most areas but low for post-implant dosimetry and post-implant scanning at 30 days.

audits.t: Audit of radiation dose delivered in time-resolved four-dimensional computed tomography in a radiotherapy department.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 444 4D CT scans; CTDIvol about 20 mGy for adults; lung 4D CT 19.6 mGy, 63% higher than conventional CT (12 mGy).

audits.t: Complete internal audit of a mammography service in a reference institution for breast imaging.
audits.st: BI-RADS recommended complete audit and literature benchmarks
audits.f: Cancer detection 4.8 per 1,000 mammograms; PPV for BI-RADS 3, 4 and 5 were 1.3%, 41.3% and 100%; sensitivity 97.1%, specificity 97.4%.

audits.t: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis   and urological pelvic cancer surgery: a UK   national audit.
audits.st: NICE guidance on VTE prophylaxis (including post-discharge LMWH) after pelvic and abdominal cancer surgery
audits.f: All centres use perioperative LMWH after radical cystectomy, 67% post-discharge; after radical prostatectomy 98% perioperative and 61% always post-discharge.

audits.t: Cognitive assessment of elderly inpatients: a clinical audit.
audits.st: Guidance that cognitive assessment should be performed on admission
audits.f: Cognitive assessment documented on admission in 22%, rising to 56% by discharge.

audits.t: An audit of histopathology reports of carcinoma endometrium: experience from a tertiary referral center.
audits.st: Minimum data set for endometrial carcinoma reports
audits.f: Compliance generally good; pTNM stage not mentioned in 71.9% of reports; median lymph node yield 15.
audits.c: Recommended use of proformas or checklists.

audits.t: Drug therapy in patients with diabetes mellitus: an audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Over 90% prescribed at least one drug; oral hypoglycaemics for 86% of non-insulin requiring diabetics; 19% prescribed more than three drugs; 63% of those on glibenclamide or chlorpropamide aged 65 or older; diuretics and beta-blockers commonly prescribed.

audits.t: Implementation of a surgical handover tool in a busy tertiary referral centre: a complete audit cycle.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean 294 patients per month; baseline weekend discharges, length of stay and emergency response team calls measured.
audits.c: Standardised weekend handover using an electronic tool supplemented by verbal handover.
audits.r2: 40% increase in weekend discharges, consistent at subsequent time-points.

audits.t: Compliance with published recommendations for postoperative antibiotic management of children with appendicitis: A chart audit.
audits.st: American Pediatric Surgical Association (APSA) 2010 recommendations for postoperative antibiotics in appendicitis
audits.f: Antibiotics in excess of recommendations in 62/119 (52%) non-perforated and 52/84 (62%) uncomplicated perforated appendicitis.

audits.t: Audit of transoral laser-assisted microsurgical resection of early laryngeal cancer.
audits.st: ENT UK Head and Neck Group standards
audits.f: 84% discussed at MDT before surgery; complete circumferential excision in 77%; 65% of specimens had histological analysis complying with standard margin reporting.

audits.t: Variation in health care for children and young people with cerebral palsies: a retrospective multicentre audit study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Significant variation between districts in access to MRI (other figures not given in the abstract).

audits.t: Automatic patient dose registry and clinical audit on line for mammography.
audits.tp: Diagnostic reference levels for radiation dose
audits.st: European Directives and international recommendations on patient dose
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Geriatric assessment of older patients with cancer in Australia--a multicentre audit.
audits.tp: Geriatric assessment in older patients with cancer
audits.st: Geriatric assessment domains in patients aged over 70
audits.f: At initial consultation: comorbidities 92%, social situation 80%, social supports 63%, at least one ADL 50%, performance status 49%, IADL 26%, geriatric syndrome 24%, polypharmacy 29%, creatinine clearance 11%; only one patient had all ADLs and IADLs assessed.

audits.t: EULAR task force recommendations on annual cardiovascular risk assessment for patients with rheumatoid arthritis: an audit of the success of implementation in a rheumatology outpatient clinic.
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk factor control in rheumatoid arthritis
audits.st: EULAR recommendation of annual CVD risk assessment in RA
audits.f: Overall CVD risk factor recording 40.1%; 59.1% in structured arthritis clinic vs 23.6% in regular clinic.

audits.t: A multi-centre audit of epistaxis management in England: is there a case for a national review of practice?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Variance between the six units in key outcome areas; 28% of patients were eligible for operative intervention in one unit compared with 12.5% in another.

audits.t: Monitoring Compliance to Promote Quality Assurance: Development of a Mental Health Clinical Chart Audit Tool in Belize, 2013.
audits.st: 20 essential components of initial assessment notes; benchmark 70% compliance (score 14 or higher)
audits.f: Mean chart score 9.57 (range 3-15); 23 charts (17.2%) met the 70% benchmark; labs named in 15.7%, psychiatric diagnosis in 21.6%, medication dose and frequency in 47.0%.

audits.t: National Audit of Seizure management in Hospitals (NASH): results of the national audit of adult epilepsy in the UK.
audits.tp: Seizure care in the emergency department
audits.st: National Audit of Seizure management in Hospitals (NASH) standards
audits.f: Witness history sought in 759 (75%) first seizure patients; 58% seen by a senior doctor; 27% of first seizure patients given advice; 55% referred to a neurologist or epilepsy specialist.

audits.t: Conducting an audit to improve the facilitation of emergency maternal and newborn referral in northern Ghana.
audits.st: Referral guidelines and facilitating mechanisms (transport, escort, referral slips, calling ahead, feedback)
audits.f: 446 referred women tracked across two cycles (baseline figures not given).
audits.c: Teams identified and implemented fixes: regional managers resolved staffing shortages, districts addressed transport cost and availability and improved communication with women and drivers
audits.r2: Less reliance on taxis in favour of ambulances/vehicles, more health worker escorts, greater use of referral slips and calling ahead, higher feedback rates.

audits.t: Back to basics: an audit of measurement of infant growth at presentation to hospital.
audits.st: Documentation of anthropometric measurements in infants presenting to hospital
audits.f: Birthweight 103 (22%), presentation weight 275 (59%), length 8 (2%), head circumference 15 (3%), percentiles 27 (6%), BMI 1 (0%).

audits.t: Dosimetry audit of radiotherapy treatment planning systems.
audits.st: 5% dose tolerance between TPS calculation and measurement
audits.f: Most TLD results within 5%; bone and polystyrene differences did not exceed 4%; inside lung-equivalent material off axis up to about 7%.

audits.t: Audit of cervical cancer screening and colposcopy attendance in rural South Africa.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 54% of 928 patients attended colposcopy after an abnormal Pap smear.

audits.t: Practices of end-of-life decisions in 66 southern French ICUs 4 years after an official legal framework: A 1-day audit.
audits.st: French EoL legislation (2002, 2005) and professional guidelines on end-of-life decisions
audits.f: Written surrogate designation in 87 (15%); advance directives 4%; multidisciplinary decision process in 99 (47%), recorded in chart in 63 (64%); families informed in 58%.

audits.t: Feasibility and utility of the use of real time random safety audits in adult ICU patients: a multicentre study.
audits.st: 37 safety measures in ten blocks based on good clinical practice guidelines
audits.f: 87.6% of scheduled audits completed; mean 34.5 min per audit; changes in the care process in 5.4% of measures analysed.

audits.t: Clinical audit results in earlier nutritional intervention in malnourished children with cystic fibrosis with improved outcome.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Earlier cohort: weight-for-age z -2.67, FEV1 52%, Pseudomonas colonisation 100%, 2-year survival post-gastrostomy 70%.
audits.c: Qualitative changes to the CF service leading to earlier referral for nutritional intervention
audits.r2: Weight-for-age z -1.5 (P = 0.0001), FEV1 68% (P = 0.006), Pseudomonas colonisation 41%, 2-year survival 100% (P = 0.004).

audits.t: Inpatient management of gout in a New Zealand hospital: a retrospective audit.
audits.st: Published gout protocols including treat-to-target urate management
audits.f: 50% of known gout patients on urate-lowering therapy; serum urate measured in 60%; treat-to-target mentioned in only 9%.

audits.t: An audit of prescribing practices for benzodiazepines and Z-drugs.
audits.st: Benzodiazepine and Z-drug prescribing guidelines (Benzodiazepine Committee report)
audits.f: 18.8% of prescriptions fully compliant; 53.7% had multiple discrepancies.

audits.t: Use of prothrombin complex concentrate in warfarin anticoagulation reversal in the emergency department: a quality improvement study of administration delays.
audits.st: Timely administration of PCC for warfarin reversal (target not stated)
audits.f: Mean administration delay 73.6 minutes (SD 34.1), median 70.0 minutes (IQR 45.0-95.0).
audits.c: Action plan developed with ED and blood bank stakeholders: a flowchart reminding clinicians how to order PCC and a new blood bank to ED delivery method.

audits.t: UK service level audit of insulin pump therapy in paediatrics.
audits.tp: Insulin pump therapy in type 1 diabetes
audits.st: NICE Technology Appraisal 151 (2008) on continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion
audits.f: 166/176 centres (94.3%) participated; 5094 children on CSII (19% of paediatric type 1 diabetes); 24-h support in 83% of units; structured CSII education in 53%; written inpatient CSII guidelines in 56%; 9% had funding refusal for a NICE-eligible patient.

audits.t: Operative blood transfusion quality improvement audit.
audits.st: Internal policies and procedures for blood transfusion to anaesthetised patients (KPIs)
audits.f: High compliance with transfusion phases by anaesthesia staff (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Pre-use anesthesia machine check; certified anesthesia technician based quality improvement audit.
audits.st: Daily and between-case anaesthetic machine inspection and manufacturer self-check (KPIs)
audits.f: Highest compliance percentage and low rate of machine replacement (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: The effectiveness of prophylactic proton pump inhibitors for prevention of non-steroidal anti inflammatory drugs associated gastric and duodenal ulcers in elderly.
audits.st: eMC guidance: proton pump inhibitor prescribed alongside NSAIDs in elderly patients
audits.f: 23 (6%) patients were not prescribed PPIs with NSAIDs and were eligible.
audits.c: Eligible patients contacted by post, offered an appointment and prescribed PPIs
audits.r2: 100% of patients prescribed NSAIDs were prescribed prophylactic PPIs.

audits.t: Using multifaceted education to improve management in acute viral bronchiolitis.
audits.st: SIGN bronchiolitis guidelines and local hospital guidelines
audits.f: Compliance: investigations 50% (46% to 53%), management 65% (61% to 68%), overall 38% (37% to 39%).
audits.c: Nationwide multifaceted education bundle after dissemination of first audit results.
audits.r2: Compliance: investigations 71% (68% to 74%), management 74% (71% to 77%), overall 59% (56% to 62%).

audits.t: Management of BK virus nephropathy in kidney transplant recipients at the Royal Hospital - Clinical Audit - Oman.
audits.tp: BK virus management after kidney transplant
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Stepwise treatment options applied in all 19 patients with success rate over 70%.
audits.c: Pharmacist-developed treatment protocol for BK virus nephropathy

audits.t: An audit into the reasons why treatment was not completed as planned under intravenous sedation in an adult oral surgery department, and the cost implications.
audits.st: Departmental acceptable sedation failure rate of 10%
audits.f: 83 of 109 sedation appointments successful (76%); failure rate 24% vs 10% target; causes: cancellation 8 (30.8%), non-attendance 6 (23.1%), late arrival 4 (15.4%), failure to cannulate 3 (11.6%).

audits.t: Value of audits in breast cancer screening quality assurance programmes.
audits.st: Screening outcome indicators (recall rate, detection rate, sensitivity) with radiological review
audits.f: Recall rate 0.66%, detection rate 3.3 per 1000, sensitivity 64.5%.
audits.c: Repeated triennial audits with radiological review and feedback
audits.r2: Recall rate 1.58%, detection rate 5.4 per 1000, sensitivity 71.6%.

audits.t: Antibiotic Prescription for COPD Exacerbations Admitted to Hospital: European COPD Audit.
audits.st: GOLD 2010 recommendations for antibiotic use in COPD exacerbations
audits.f: 86% of admissions received antibiotics but only 61.4% of cases met the GOLD recommendations.

audits.t: Targeted clinical audits immediately following the establishment of clinical practice guidelines for multiple sclerosis in 17 neurology departments: A pragmatic and collaborative study.
audits.st: GRESEP clinical practice guidelines for multiple sclerosis (targeted clinical audit criteria)
audits.f: Compliance with criteria ranged from 8% to 98% (240 files) for the diagnostic audit (TCA-DIAG) and from 15% to 99% (221 files) for the disease-course audit (TCA-EVOL), with wide disparity between sites.

audits.t: Risk of antenatal psychosocial distress in indigenous women and its management at primary health care centres in Australia.
audits.tp: Antenatal psychosocial and mental health screening
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: About 18% (n=141) at risk of antenatal psychosocial distress; of these 16% (n=22) prescribed antidepressants, brief intervention 61%, counselling 57%, CBT 5%, external referral 39% (n=55).

audits.t: Criteria-based audit of quality of care to women with severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia in a referral hospital in Accra, Ghana.
audits.st: Nine key clinical care protocols for severe pre-eclampsia, hypertensive emergency and eclampsia
audits.f: Mean adherence 15-85%: plan for delivery and magnesium sulphate 85%, eclampsia 64%, severe pre-eclampsia at admission 60%, ward follow-up 53%, hypertensive emergency 53%, monitoring 15%.

audits.t: A simple clinical coding strategy to improve recording of child maltreatment concerns: an audit study.
audits.tp: Child maltreatment recording in primary care
audits.st: GMC and NICE recommendation to record concerns about child maltreatment, including minor concerns
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Simple coding strategy encouraging GPs always to use, as a minimum, the Read code 'Child is cause for concern'
audits.r2: Increased recording of any maltreatment-related code (rate ratio 1.4; 95% CI 1.1-1.6), child protection procedures (RR 1.4; 95% CI 1.1-1.6) and cause for concern (RR 2.5; 95% CI 1.8-3.4).

audits.t: Contemporary Management and Control of Uncomplicated Hypertension in Canada: Insight From the Primary Care Audit of Global Risk Management (PARADIGM) Study.
audits.st: Blood pressure control per Canadian hypertension guidelines
audits.f: BP control rate 57.4%; mean treated BP 134/82 mm Hg; of treated patients 46.9% on 1 drug, 38.7% on 2, 14.3% on 3 or more.

audits.t: Enhancing the Quality of Prescribing Practices for Older Veterans Discharged from the Emergency Department (EQUiPPED): Preliminary Results from Enhancing Quality of Prescribing Practices for Older Veterans Discharged from the Emergency Department, a Novel Multicomponent Interdisciplinary Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Beers criteria for potentially inappropriate medications in patients aged 65 and older
audits.f: Average monthly proportion of PIMs prescribed by staff providers 9.4±1.5% before the intervention.
audits.c: Provider education, EMR-embedded geriatric pharmacy order sets and decision support, academic detailing, audit and feedback, and peer benchmarking
audits.r2: Average monthly proportion of PIMs 4.6±1.0% after EQUiPPED (relative risk 0.48, 95% CI 0.40-0.59, P<.001).

audits.t: An audit of epilepsy in general practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Records audit revealed deficiencies in care and inadequate regular follow-up.

audits.t: Clinical audit of ultrasound guided fine needle aspiration in a general cytopathology service.
audits.st: Literature inadequacy rates
audits.f: Inadequate 33 (29.46%), nondiagnostic descriptive 35 (31.25%), diagnostic 44 (39.28%); inadequacy thyroid 30.56%, breast 18.18%, intra-abdominal 28.88%.

audits.t: Use of psychotropics among looked after children: an audit in the Borough of Lambeth.
audits.tp: Psychotropic prescribing in children and young people
audits.st: NICE: psychological therapies as first-line treatment before medication; looked after children on psychotropics should have mental health service input
audits.f: Responses from 63 of 67 GP surgeries covering 145 children (87.34%); no looked after children were prescribed psychotropic medication without CAMHS involvement.

audits.t: Making audit actionable: an example algorithm for blood pressure management in chronic kidney disease.
audits.tp: Blood pressure control in chronic kidney disease
audits.st: UK clinical guidelines for blood pressure management in CKD
audits.f: Of 11,097 CKD patients identified from 532,409 records, 3,766 (34%) showed room for improvement through medication optimisation or better BP monitoring.

audits.t: PA1 An internal audit into the adequacy of pain assessment in a hospice setting.
audits.st: SOCRATES mnemonic pain assessment; target 100% fully assessed with all eight elements; regular and breakthrough analgesia prescribed
audits.f: 0% fully assessed with all SOCRATES elements; 66.7% partially assessed; mean 3.3 elements used; regular and breakthrough analgesia prescribed for 100%

audits.t: Paediatric ENT standards in London: are we delivering a first-class service? a repeat audit.
audits.st: Paediatric ENT standards
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Identifying targets for quality improvement in hospital antibiotic prescribing.
audits.st: Local antibiotic guidelines in place; documentation of reason for prescription
audits.f: 40.9% of 428 inpatients received antibiotics; 75.7% of prescriptions guideline-compliant; reason documented for 87.8%

audits.t: Post to predialysis plasma urea nitrogen ratio, ultrafiltration and weight to estimate K.t/V. Use in auditing the amount of dialysis being administered.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: R:UF:W-derived Kt/V averaged 0.91 +/- 0.19; 9 of 40 patients had Kt/V below 0.8 and 13 others between 0.8 and 0.9; KT still below 0.9 in 19 patients after residual renal function

audits.t: An audit of the laboratory diagnosis of cryptosporidiosis in England and Wales.
audits.st: UK national standards for Cryptosporidium testing
audits.f: 85/156 (54%) laboratories responded; first-line methods microscopy 68/85 (80%), EIA 16/85 (19%), PCR 1/85 (1%); 28/85 (33%) routinely tested all stools; 16 (19%) used stool consistency to select samples.

audits.t: An audit of the use of intravenous ketamine for paediatric dental conscious sedation.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 76% accepted all treatment with no problems and 19% had a small amount of resistance; no adverse reactions.

audits.t: Structured Handover in General Surgery: An Audit of Current Practice.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons guidelines on minimum dataset for safe handover
audits.f: Patient location documented 56%, outstanding tasks 45%, senior review 28% (18).
audits.c: Standardised computer-generated handover proforma based on RCS guidelines circulated and made available on wards
audits.r2: Patient location 87% (P < 0.0001), outstanding tasks 89% (P = 0.004), senior review 85% (45) (P < 0.0001); blood results documentation also increased (P < 0.0001).

audits.t: Antibiotic prophylaxis audit and questionnaire study: Traffic Light Poster improves adherence to protocol in gastrointestinal surgery.
audits.st: Local antibiotic prophylaxis protocol
audits.f: 31% of procedures followed the protocol; 73% of clean procedures received prophylaxis inappropriately.
audits.r2: 73% followed the protocol; inappropriate prophylaxis in clean procedures fell to 20%.

audits.t: The quality of paper-based versus electronic nursing care plan in Australian aged care homes: A documentation audit study.
audits.st: 16-question documentation quality instrument developed for the study
audits.f: 111 paper-based and 194 electronic care plans reviewed; electronic plans documented more signs, symptoms and evaluation (48.30 vs 47.34 out of 60); overall quality no better in electronic system

audits.t: An audit of nursing reports for First-Tier Tribunals in a secure inpatient service.
audits.st: October 2013 Tribunals Judiciary practice direction (24 key items)
audits.f: Average 36.3% of key items present; mean length 2.9 pages.
audits.c: New practice direction and a local report-writing template.
audits.r2: Average 51.3% of key items present; mean length 4.0 pages.

audits.t: Do we practise low tidal-volume ventilation in the intensive care unit? a 14-year audit.
audits.st: Low tidal volume ventilation, 6.5 mL/kg predicted body weight or less
audits.f: Median tidal volume 8.15 mL/kg PBW (IQR 7.15-9.34), adherence 13.4%

audits.t: Auditing an intensive care unit recycling program.
audits.st: Hospital protocol and local recycling programmes (potential recycling)
audits.f: Total waste 505 kg; 145 kg (28%) potentially recyclable, of which 70 kg (49%) recycled (14% of total); 82% of infectious bin waste truly infectious

audits.t: An audit of doctor's management of patients with chest pain in the accident and emergency department.
audits.tp: Chest pain assessment in the emergency department
audits.st: Retrospective opinion of experienced clinical assessors on need for coronary care unit admission
audits.f: Of 119 patients who should have been admitted to CCU, 14 (11.8%) were discharged in error; of 485 who should not, 32 (16%) were advised admission unnecessarily.

audits.t: Variation in lung cancer resources and workload: results from the first national lung cancer organisational audit.
audits.st: Recommended clinical nurse specialist case volumes and access to key treatments
audits.f: Over half of clinical nurse specialists reported case volumes above recommended numbers; some trusts had no access to VAT lobectomy or stereotactic radiotherapy.

audits.t: A retrospective audit of antibiotic prescriptions in primary health-care facilities in Eastern Region, Ghana.
audits.st: WHO/International Network for the Rational Use of Drugs rational drug use indicators
audits.f: Mean 4.01 medicines per encounter; 59.9% of prescriptions had antibiotics and 24.2% injections; 79.2% of medicines were generics and 88.1% from the national essential medicines list.

audits.t: Diabetic foot complications in a secondary foot hospital: A clinical audit.
audits.st: Best practice guidelines for diabetic foot complications
audits.f: 24 admissions (19 patients); clinical data poorly recorded, especially neuropathy, HbA1c and examination; 12% no follow-up; half not seen by endocrinology; mean stay 12 days

audits.t: Symptom Assessment for a Palliative Care Approach in People With Dementia Admitted to Acute Hospitals: Results From a National Audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Among 76 patients who died, received EOL care or were referred to palliative care: no pain assessment in 27%, no delirium screening in 68%, no mood or BPSD assessment in 93%.

audits.t: Emergency department management of falls in the elderly: A clinical audit and suggestions for improvement.
audits.tp: Falls risk screening and multifactorial assessment
audits.st: Institutionally approved optimum care for falls in patients aged 60 and over
audits.f: Most common omissions: Romberg test not done (92.75%) and no physiotherapy consultation (82.75%)
audits.c: Educational programme based on Delphi expert panel suggestions
audits.r2: Educational programme had a modest effect on improving care (beta = 3.79)

audits.t: A prospective audit of the impact of additional staff on the care of diabetic patients in a community podiatry service.
audits.st: NICE guidelines on foot problems in type 2 diabetes (emergency foot seen within 24 hours)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Two additional podiatry staff and internal service reorganisation.
audits.r2: More patients treated in all risk categories and waiting times fell, but targets not met; emergency diabetic foot waited on average 37 weeks.

audits.t: Neonatal admissions, quality of care and outcome: 4 years of inpatient audit data from The Gambia's teaching hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1734 of 4944 admissions (35%) died; 57% of deaths within first 48 hours of admission; 1267 early neonatal deaths

audits.t: Improvement in Perinatal HIV Status Documentation in a Massachusetts Birth Hospital, 2009-2013.
audits.st: Universal prenatal HIV testing; aim to improve documentation from 50% to 100%
audits.f: HIV status documented in 55.5%
audits.c: Three-pronged intervention: switch to verbal-only consent, rapid HIV testing protocol, simplified newborn admission document

audits.t: [Audit as a tool to assess and promote the quality of medical records and hospital appropriateness: metodology and preliminary results].
audits.st: 48-item grid modified from Lombardy Region medical record manual; Italian Appropriateness Evaluation Protocol (AEP) 2002
audits.f: 40% did not fully meet the minimum level of acceptability; 30% of hospital days inappropriate
audits.c: Departmental audit meetings sharing results with staff and implementing improvement strategies (34 editions, 480 professionals)

audits.t: Video Surveillance Audit of Hand-washing Practices in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
audits.st: WHO hand hygiene technique with soap and water (steps 2 to 7)
audits.f: Of 1081 video recordings: 403 (37.3%) excellent, 521 (48.2%) acceptable, 157 (14.5%) unacceptable

audits.t: Contraception post severe maternal morbidity: a retrospective audit.
audits.st: Effective postpartum contraception should be offered to all women
audits.f: 84 of 98 (85.7%) left hospital without contraception prescription; all 7 with severe pre-existing comorbidity left without contraception

audits.t: A multicentre audit of GDPs knowledge of orthodontic retention.
audits.st: 100% of GDPs should be aware of commonly used retainers and able to provide replacements
audits.f: 502 of 1,053 questionnaires returned (48%); awareness of vacuum-formed, Hawley and fixed retainers was generally high but significantly fewer GDPs were willing to prescribe, fit or review retainers.

audits.t: The Disconnect Between Novel Oral Anticoagulant Eligibility and Provincial Drug Coverage: An Albertan Anticoagulation Clinic Audit.
audits.st: Canadian guidelines recommending NOAC in preference to warfarin in nonvalvular AF
audits.f: 89%-95% eligible for NOAC but only 39%-41% qualified for provincial drug coverage

audits.t: A multicentre, multicycle audit of the prescribing practices of three paediatric dental departments in the North of England.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 28% of prescriptions appropriate.
audits.c: Education and provision of an aide-memoire.
audits.r2: 71% of prescriptions appropriate in the third cycle.

audits.t: Thrombolysis in acute stroke: ongoing challenges based on a tertiary hospital audit and comparisons with other Australian studies.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 57 of 490 ischaemic strokes (11.6%) received tPA; median onset to treatment 175 min; median door to needle 97 min; protocol deviations 21.1%

audits.t: An audit of general practitioner involvement in public community mental health care.
audits.st: Guidelines suggesting collaboration between GPs and mental health services for physical health in serious mental illness
audits.f: 98 of 191 (51%) patients had a GP documented in their records; no significant difference in metabolic screening rates between those with and without a GP.

audits.t: 'True Blood' The Critical Care Story: An audit of blood sampling practice across three adult, paediatric and neonatal intensive care settings.
audits.tp: Laboratory test utilisation in intensive care
audits.st: Seven evidence-based blood conservation recommendations
audits.f: 940 sampling episodes from 96 patients; arterial blood gas accounted for 82% of adult, 80% of paediatric and 47% of neonatal samples

audits.t: Vaccinations in sickle cell disease: An audit of vaccination uptake in sickle cell patients attending Newham University Hospital.
audits.st: Sickle Cell Society guidelines on vaccination
audits.f: 2 fully up to date; influenza 24 (30%); pneumococcal 33 (41%); MenC, HiB and HBV under 31%.
audits.c: New database of vaccination history, raising GP awareness and patient education seminars.
audits.r2: 7 fully up to date; influenza 43 (50%, P=0.0062); pneumococcal 38 (44%, P=0.7874); MenC, HiB and HBV under 31%.

audits.t: Time trends, improvements and national auditing of rectal cancer management over an 18-year period.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 30- and 90-day postoperative mortality fell to 1.7% and 2.9%; 5-year local recurrence fell to 5.0%; more preoperative radiotherapy and MDT conferences

audits.t: Pediatric IBD-unclassified Is Less Common than Previously Reported; Results of an 8-Year Audit of the EUROKIDS Registry.
audits.st: Complete diagnostic workup defined as full endoscopy plus small bowel radiology
audits.f: IBD-U was the provisional diagnosis in 265 of 3461 children (7.7%); only 48% had complete diagnostic workup, mainly lacking small bowel radiology.

audits.t: Glycaemic control and lipid concentrations in a cohort of people with diabetes over 7 years of follow-up: a regional audit of diabetes care in the UK.
audits.st: Quality and Outcomes Framework targets for cholesterol
audits.f: Mean HbA1c 62.1 ± 16.1 mmol/mol in those with follow-up.
audits.r2: Mean HbA1c 61.7 ± 17.3 mmol/mol; more patients achieved lipid targets in 2013 than 2006.

audits.t: The importance of a medical chaperone: a quality improvement study exploring the use of a note stamp in a tertiary breast surgery unit.
audits.st: Professional guidelines on medical chaperones (documentation of chaperone offer, patient preference, chaperone identity and clinician gender)
audits.f: not reported (baseline figures not given in the abstract).
audits.c: Cycle 1: presentation and discussion of chaperone guidelines, reminder posters and introduction of a note stamp; cycle 2: note stamp alone.
audits.r2: After first intervention (November 2013) documentation of chaperone offer was 69.95%; final cycle result not given in the abstract.

audits.t: Histopathological correlations of appendectomies: a clinical audit of a single center.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 211 of 238 (88.7%) specimens showed appendicitis; negative appendicectomy rate 11.3%; 1.7% had other abnormal pathology.

audits.t: Use of a capacity audit tool in a mental health setting.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 100% completion of capacity audit tool; 25 of 153 beds (16%) occupied by patients not needing the bed or vacant

audits.t: A template for a clinico-pathological audit of medical liver biopsies.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Hepatologists rated 96% of reports clinically useful; 56% confirmed diagnoses, 46% differentiated between and 42% excluded diagnoses; 74% changed management; 27% gave an unsuspected diagnosis.

audits.t: Piloting a Structured Practice Audit to Assess ACGME Milestones in Written Handoff Communication in Internal Medicine.
audits.st: UPDATED tool scoring 7 aspects of written sign-out linked to ACGME milestones
audits.f: 14 of 45 interns (31%) satisfactory; 5 (11%) critical deficiencies
audits.c: Immediate feedback and repeat audits for unsatisfactory interns; results fed into performance reviews
audits.r2: Second trimester 21 interns (68%) satisfactory; final trimester 9 of 10 remaining interns satisfactory

audits.t: Audit of preoperative localisation of tumor with tattoo for patients undergoing laparoscopic colorectal surgery.
audits.st: Recommendation of at least three tattoo spots one mucosal fold distal to the lesion, with tattoo site documented in the endoscopy report
audits.f: Only 59% had a visible and accurate tattoo; 17% documented but not visible, 4% visible but inaccurate, 20% had no tattoo.
audits.c: Standardised departmental tattooing protocol recommended (not re-audited)

audits.t: [Prenatal screening for anueploidies in the first trimester: Audit to a Fetal Medicine Centre with specialized Laboratory in Mexico].
audits.st: Qualification requirements for first trimester ultrasound and biochemical screening
audits.f: 1020 pregnancies; 1009 valid nuchal translucency measurements, 7.3% >p95; qualification requirements fulfilled for nuchal translucency, ductus venosus and combined test; estimated false positive rate 3.9%

audits.t: Improving the quality of care for patients with hypertension in Moshupa District, Botswana: quality improvement cycle.
audits.st: Target standards for structure, process and outcome of hypertension care
audits.f: None of the target standards met.
audits.c: Simple interventions designed and implemented to improve care (details not reported).
audits.r2: Six of nine structural, five of 11 process and one of two outcome target standards achieved.

audits.t: An audit of diagnosis and treatment of tuberculosis in Ethiopia.
audits.st: Ethiopian national tuberculosis guidelines
audits.f: Guidelines implemented at diagnosis for 60.9% (n = 67) of women and 56.1% (n = 69) of men; correct pill numbers for 91.8% (n = 101) of women and 90.2% (n = 111) of men; only 2.6% (2/76) of smear-negative pulmonary TB correctly diagnosed.

audits.t: Prevention of mother-to-child transmission in HIV audit in Xhosa clinic, Mahalapye, Botswana.
audits.st: Botswana PMTCT national guidelines
audits.f: 19% knew HIV-positive status; 69% seen at 14-28 weeks' gestation; 67% took antiretrovirals; 39/44 (89%) infants HIV DNA PCR negative at 6 weeks; 32 (73%) given cotrimoxazole prophylaxis at 6-8 weeks.

audits.t: Management of cryptococcal meningitis in a district hospital in KwaZulu-Natal: a clinical audit.
audits.st: Context-specific guidelines for cryptococcal meningitis (selected process criteria, including 14-day amphotericin B course)
audits.f: Opening pressure rarely measured; therapeutic LPs in 23.4%; 117/127 (92.1%) received amphotericin B but only 19/117 (16.2%) completed 14 days.

audits.t: Audit on management of eclampsia at Sultan Abdul Halim Hospital.
audits.st: 12 standardised criteria for eclampsia management; local KPI on recurrence of eclamptic fits
audits.f: Incidence 9.17 per 10,000 deliveries; suboptimal care mainly delayed Red Alert activation and untreated uncontrolled blood pressure
audits.c: Staff education to improve working knowledge and re-engineering of the hospital Red Alert system
audits.r2: Reduction in recurrent eclamptic fits and perinatal mortality rate (figures not given)

audits.t: Audit of Endotracheal Tube Suction in a Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.
audits.st: Endotracheal Suction Assessment Tool (ESAT) criteria
audits.f: Median 2 documented criteria per suction event matched ESAT (IQR 1-6); all ESAT criteria appeared in notes

audits.t: The quality of cardiovascular disease prevention in rural primary care.
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk assessment in primary care
audits.st: Recording of cardiovascular risk factors and lifestyle advice for high-risk patients and those with cardiovascular disease
audits.f: High-risk vs diagnosed: blood pressure recorded 94% vs 99% (P = 0.019); physical activity 24% vs 56%; dietary advice 32% vs 51% (P = 0.001); physical activity advice 34% vs 56%.

audits.t: Improving Compliance with Statins in Patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.tp: Best medical therapy in peripheral arterial disease
audits.st: Vascular Society of Great Britain and Ireland and draft NICE guidance: all patients undergoing major vascular procedures should be prescribed a statin
audits.f: Statins not prescribed in 30.1% of discharge letters (113 admissions, 96 patients)
audits.c: Several junior doctor-led interventions monitored through weekly PDSA cycles (details not stated)
audits.r2: Statins not prescribed in 24.4% (86 admissions, 76 patients), an 18.9% decrease

audits.t: Improving Compliance with NICE Guidelines on Parkinson's isease: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.st: NICE Parkinson's disease guideline audit criteria (diagnosis, follow-up, multidisciplinary referral)
audits.f: First and second audits: high compliance for initial diagnosis and referral criteria but poor for multidisciplinary referral criteria.
audits.c: Pro forma stamp placed in the notes at each regular Parkinson's outpatient review (by October 2009)
audits.r2: Compliance improved to 100% on all criteria measured.

audits.t: Audit of primary care electrocardiograms sent as emergency to a telehealth service - the Telehealth Network of Minas Gerais, Brazil.
audits.st: Proper definition of emergency ECG
audits.f: 28% of ECGs sent as emergency; 63 cities with units sending >70% as emergency selected; 50% of practitioners did not know the definition of emergency
audits.r2: 67% of cities had significant reduction in emergency ECGs in month 1 and 17% in month 2

audits.t: Implications of miscoding urological procedures in an era of financial austerity - 'Every Penny Counts'.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Correct OPCS coding for final HRG payment
audits.f: 20% of cases miscoded; revised codes recovered £10,716
audits.c: Review of coding deficiencies with the head of professional coders and revised OPCS codes; surgeon involvement with the coding department

audits.t: Quality audits of radiotherapy centres in Latin America: a pilot experience of the International Atomic Energy Agency.
audits.st: IAEA QUATRO audit guidelines (2007)
audits.f: All 12 centres audited; three lacked minimum infrastructure, three did not perform gynaecological brachytherapy and one delivered around 900 teletherapy treatments a year without simulation, planning or dosimetry equipment.

audits.t: An audit of the completion of radiology request forms and the request practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Most complete form 86.67% filled and least 26.67%; requested examination field filled in 99.66%; 28% of clinicians did not use the request form; 7.37% illegible handwriting.

audits.t: Documentation of Pregnancy Status, Gynaecological History, Date of Last Menstrual Period and Contraception Use in Emergency Surgical Admissions: Time for a Change in Practice?
audits.st: Documented pregnancy status within 24 h of admission and before any surgical intervention
audits.f: 30 (30%) documented pregnancy status; gynaecological history 32%, contraception 25%, LMP 29%; 6/24 (25%) surgical patients had status before surgery.
audits.c: Prompt added to the medical clerk-in document.

audits.t: Do English NHS Microbiology laboratories offer adequate services for the diagnosis of UTI in children? Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership (HQIP) Audit of Standard Operational Procedures.
audits.st: NICE CG54 (2007) urinary tract infection in children: urgent microscopy and culture, reporting of non-E. coli infections
audits.f: 73% of laboratories (110/150) participated; 61% (67/110) reported non-E. coli Enterobacteriaceae only as coliforms; 88% (97/110) provided urgent microscopy for hospital and 54% for GP urines; only 22% (24/110) reported non-E. coli coliforms and provided urgent microscopy for both.

audits.t: Audit of practice in sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP) post mortems and neuropathological findings.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Whole fixed brain examined in 76.6% of post mortems; macroscopic brain abnormalities in 52%; relevant microscopic pathology in 89%.

audits.t: Closing the audit cycle: improving short-term outcomes of oesophagectomy in a provincial hospital.
audits.st: Previously published unit audit of oesophagectomy outcomes (Al-Herz et al 2012)
audits.f: Before the unit audit: intraoperative IV fluid 6.6 L, first 24 h 9.2 L; tracheostomy 26.7%; hospital stay 15 days
audits.c: Changes in perioperative management following publication of the unit audit (details not given)
audits.r2: Intraoperative IV fluid 3.3 L (P < 0.0001), first 24 h 5.5 L; extubation three days earlier; tracheostomy 0% (P = 0.003); stay 13 days (P = 0.035)

audits.t: An Audit of 204 Histopathology Reports Over Three Years of Carcinoma of Cervix: Experience from a Tertiary Referral Centre.
audits.st: Minimum data set for carcinoma cervix histopathology reports
audits.f: Minimum dataset compliance generally good; pTNM stage not mentioned in 65.06%; mean pelvic lymph node yield 16.6

audits.t: Clinical radiotherapy audits in Belgium, 2011-2014.
audits.st: IAEA manual for comprehensive clinical radiotherapy audits; Euratom 97/43 directive article 11
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Doctors learn new tricks, but do they remember them? Lack of effect of an educational intervention in improving Oxygen prescribing.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Oxygen prescribed in 24.5%.
audits.r2: Oxygen prescription rate 13.9% four years on, a significant deterioration from 58.8% at the second audit (P = 0.01).

audits.t: Four-Stage Audit Demonstrating Increased Uptake of HIV Testing in Acute Neurology Admissions Using Staged Practical Interventions.
audits.st: UK National Guidelines on HIV testing in clinically indicated neurological presentations
audits.f: Pre-protocol testing rate 21.9%.
audits.c: HIV testing protocol, then a tailored clerking proforma prompting testing and consent plus regular focused tutorials.

audits.t: Perineal wound infections: an audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Higher than average perineal wound infection rate among women with an instrumental birth.
audits.c: Delivery packs separated into a birth pack and a suturing pack, plus a back-to-basics update session for maternity staff.
audits.r2: Overall perineal wound infection rate in the trust reduced.

audits.t: Prescription audit of under six children living in periurban areas.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 212 illness episodes in 172 children: antimicrobials 28.4%; tetracyclines 7.1% of chemotherapeutic exposures; ORS used in only 13.9% of diarrhoea episodes; weight not recorded before prescribing

audits.t: British Orthodontic Society national audit of temporary anchorage devices (TADs): report of the first thousand TADs placed.
audits.st: Audit standards set from NICE recommendations with BOS Development and Standards Committee
audits.f: Written information and risk discussion in over 90%; 17.4% placed without signed consent form; failure rate 24.2%; infection or inflammation causing loss in 6%

audits.t: [Clinical audit on drug prescriptions for elderly patients hospitalized in a unit of psychiatry].

audits.f: 18.1% of prescriptions had at least two neuroleptics; 30% of patients not taking anticholinergic drugs; mean 3.3 psychotropics per patient
