audits.f: Appointment system did not meet standards and visual outcomes were poorer than trial standards.
audits.c: Changes to the appointment system, expansion of the treatment facility and employment of additional staff.
audits.r2: Appointment standards reached Royal College recommendations; visual outcomes approached landmark study standards.

audits.t: Successful implementation of strategies to transform Emergency Department transfusion practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 3209 units ordered; 39.5% transfused; 9.5% (289 units) unaccounted for.
audits.c: Staff education, monthly traceability reports, ED transfusion guideline, blood fridge moved to resuscitation room, named transfusion consultant and link nurse, and hospital transfusion group representation.
audits.r2: 1034 units ordered (64% reduction); 687 transfused (39% reduction); 68% increase in proportion transfused; 9 units unaccounted for (96% reduction).

audits.t: Introduction of 'Anaphylaxis Packs' to improve patient safety in a hospital setting.
audits.st: Immediate availability of 1:1000 adrenaline for anaphylaxis
audits.f: Adrenaline unavailable on 50% of audited wards; staff lacked knowledge of anaphylaxis management and drug location.
audits.c: Anaphylaxis packs (adrenaline, chlorphenamine, hydrocortisone, algorithm) added to crash trolleys and checklist, piloted on four wards via PDSA then trust-wide.
audits.r2: 100% ward stock of anaphylaxis packs, more consistent drug location and improved staff knowledge.

audits.t: Improving documentation and use of ultrasound for suprapubic catheter insertions.
audits.st: British Association of Urological Surgeons (BAUS) recommendations for safe insertion of suprapubic catheters (2011), including ultrasound use if available and appropriate
audits.f: Ultrasound used in 17/36 (47%) SPC insertions, up from 0/19 in 2009; documentation of insertion technique and indication needed improving.
audits.c: A proforma was designed for every SPC insertion and is now mandatory Trust practice.

audits.t: Can a multi-factorial assessment and interventional programme decrease inpatient falls in an elderly care ward?
audits.st: Target 20% reduction in inpatient falls rate
audits.f: 14.70 falls per 1000 bed days.
audits.c: Falls risk care plan, 'walking-stick' incentive poster for nurses and post-fall guidelines, with staff feedback sessions.
audits.r2: 12.44 falls per 1000 bed days, a 15.4% reduction.

audits.t: Delivering preference for place of death in a specialist palliative care setting.
audits.tp: Achievement of preferred place of death
audits.st: Public policy goal of achieving choice in place of death
audits.f: 18% died at home; 31% of those preferring home died at home; 91% of those preferring elsewhere achieved it; overall achievement 56%; 29% had no recorded preference.
audits.c: Seven-year QI programme: documentation changes, clinical system changes to support documentation, staff support and skills development, and a new early discharge service for those wishing to die at home.
audits.r2: All patients had a recorded preference or documented reason; one third died at home; 71% of those wishing to die at home did so; 88% achievement for those preferring hospice.

audits.t: Warfarin Management Pathway: A clear and safe algorithm, from admission to discharge.
audits.st: NPSA safer practice for anticoagulant therapy
audits.f: Errors on warfarin charts audited (numbers not stated)
audits.c: Warfarin management algorithm emailed to all doctors and laminated copies attached to pneumatic tube system machines
audits.r2: Marked decrease in chart errors and incomplete anticoagulation referrals (numbers not stated)

audits.t: Improving the investigation of suspected deep vein thrombosis in the Emergency Department.
audits.tp: DVT diagnostic pathway (D-dimer and Wells score)
audits.st: NICE guidance on DVT diagnosis (June 2012)
audits.f: Suspected DVT often over- and inadequately investigated (numbers not stated)
audits.c: New investigation pathway and proforma, placed on Trust website and included in departmental induction
audits.r2: Significant improvement in adherence and documentation; 21% reduction in ultrasound scans

audits.t: Improving adherence to guidelines for extended venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in patients with colorectal cancer.
audits.tp: Extended VTE prophylaxis after abdominal cancer surgery
audits.st: Local EVTEP guidelines based on NICE (28 days LMWH after colorectal cancer surgery)
audits.f: 11% of at-risk patients identified in pre-operative assessment clinic; 44% prescribed EVTEP at discharge
audits.c: Education of the multidisciplinary team and presentation of audit results after each cycle

audits.t: The management of ureteric stones in the Accident and Emergency department.
audits.st: Appropriate admission or discharge of patients with radiologically proven ureteric stones (no specific criteria existed at baseline)
audits.f: No easily accessible, specific criteria were used to guide which patients were admitted and which discharged.
audits.c: Admission criteria and a discharge proforma were developed and implemented in A&E.
audits.r2: Fewer unnecessary admissions and fewer inappropriate discharges (no figures given in abstract).

audits.t: Electronic prescribing: Reducing delay to first dose of antibiotics for patients in intensive care.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Delays in antibiotic administration quantified (numbers not stated)
audits.c: Electronic prescribing system modified to remove default dose times so doses scheduled within an hour of prescription, plus enhanced training for clinicians and nurses
audits.r2: Significant reduction in delays (p=0.002, Mann-Whitney U test)

audits.t: Investigating the bundle compliance of IVIG delivery in the Greater Manchester Neuroscience centre.
audits.st: Local IVIG care bundle (17 areas of care)
audits.f: Nine areas delivered to all 75 patients; no patient received the complete bundle
audits.c: Electronic treatment dashboard for chronic IVIG therapy
audits.r2: Individual areas of care delivered markedly more often; overall compliance only slightly increased

audits.t: Pre-operative fasting - a patient centered approach.
audits.st: Royal College of Nursing guidelines: minimum fasting of six hours for food and two hours for clear fluids before elective anaesthesia or sedation
audits.f: Policy stated nothing to eat or drink from midnight/7AM; patients not encouraged to drink clear fluids up to two hours before surgery; 70% subjective dehydration, 40% clinical evidence of dehydration; longest fast 17 hours.
audits.c: Staff teaching session on current fasting guidelines, a corrected patient information leaflet, and reminder posters of the updated policy.
audits.r2: All patients encouraged to drink clear fluids until two hours before surgery; 25% subjective dehydration, 25% clinical evidence of dehydration; longest fast eight hours.

audits.t: Tonsillectomy discharge information - An improvement in both patient safety and satisfaction.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England standards for tonsillectomy discharge information
audits.f: 35% had post-operative bleeding information on discharge summary; 51% received no written information; 66% recalled verbal explanation; 54% knew to go to A&E if bleeding; 40% not satisfied (35 telephone questionnaire respondents).
audits.c: Focus group; tonsillectomy patient leaflet produced with bleeding instructions and nearest A&E contact details, revised after patient feedback.
audits.r2: 83% received an information leaflet, 100% a verbal explanation, 100% satisfied and 100% knew what to do if they bled.

audits.t: Improving the management of Acute Kidney Injury in a District General Hospital: Introduction of the DONUT bundle.
audits.tp: Acute kidney injury recognition and management
audits.st: DONUT care bundle of six interventions for AKI (NCEPOD 2009 context)
audits.f: Only 8% of stage 1 AKI cases had all components of the care bundle completed at 24 hours.
audits.c: DONUT sticker for the notes, Foundation Programme teaching and summary flash cards
audits.r2: Full compliance rose to 17%. The sticker was used in only 7% of cases, but where used there was 100% compliance.

audits.t: Weight a minute - iatrogenic paracetamol toxicity is preventable by utilisation of well-designed drug charts.
audits.st: BNF: IV paracetamol 15mg/kg every 4-6 hours for adults 10-50kg
audits.f: 37% weighed on admission; 27% had weight on drug chart; 18 (25% of patients on paracetamol) inappropriately dosed
audits.c: 3 months of awareness-raising on recording weights and dose adjustment
audits.r2: 68% weighed (p<0.0001); 53% had weight on drug chart (p=0.0003); 5 (5.75%) inappropriately dosed (p=0.0013)

audits.t: Management of anaemia and blood transfusion in critical care - implementing national guidelines in ICU.
audits.st: British Committee for Standards in Haematology 2012 guidelines: transfuse at haemoglobin below 70 g/L unless bleeding, sepsis, neurological injury or acute coronary syndrome
audits.f: Before intervention, of 10 transfusions 2 appropriate (green), 1 inappropriate (red) and 7 unclear (amber).
audits.c: Local transfusion guideline with posters in the ICU, then guidance attached to transfusion prescriptions.
audits.r2: After both interventions 7 green and 3 amber transfusions, none inappropriate; total ICU transfusions fell by about 50% (41 to 18) after the first intervention.

audits.t: Improving the accessibility of trust guidelines for junior doctors at North Bristol NHS Trust.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 48% unable to locate UGIB or VTE guidelines within 5 min; mean 111 sec and 17 clicks; antibiotic guideline found by 100% in 12 sec and two clicks
audits.c: Redesign of the Trust intranet homepage
audits.r2: 100% located all three guidelines in mean 7.2 sec and 2.1 clicks (p=0.001)

audits.t: Starting early: integration of self-management support into an acute stroke service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Optimum washing and dressing practice supporting independence on 54% of occasions at baseline.
audits.c: Bridges stroke self-management training for 46 multidisciplinary staff, using PDSA cycles.

audits.t: Service improvement system to enhance the safety of patients admitted on long-term warfarin.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Poor completion rate of warfarin prescriptions and poor junior doctor knowledge and confidence (numbers not stated)
audits.c: Warfarin administration time changed from 6 pm to 2 pm, supported by a poster campaign
audits.r2: Third cycle showed the changes were not sustained (numbers not stated)

audits.t: A persuasive intervention: improving the compliance of extended venous thromboembolism prophylaxis following cancer resections in a tertiary colorectal and hepatobiliary unit.
audits.tp: Extended VTE prophylaxis after abdominal cancer surgery
audits.st: Extended VTE prophylaxis prescribed on discharge after cancer resection
audits.f: Compliance 79% colorectal and 48% HPB
audits.c: Education and visual reminders for junior doctors

audits.t: Management of transient ischaemic attacks in the emergency department: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: Local guideline for management of TIA (including antiplatelet prescription)
audits.f: 31% of TIA patients received antiplatelets.
audits.c: Teaching session for new FY2 doctors on initial TIA management and the local guideline.
audits.r2: First improvement cycle: 86% received antiplatelets, with significant improvement (P = 0.05) in documentation of symptoms in the prior week; similar results in the second improvement cycle.

audits.t: Improving Sepsis Management in the Acute Admissions Unit.
audits.tp: Sepsis recognition and treatment on wards
audits.st: College of Emergency Medicine sepsis standards (e.g. high-flow oxygen 95%, crystalloid bolus 100%, lactate 95%, blood cultures 95%)
audits.f: High-flow oxygen documented 24%; crystalloid boluses 52%; lactate 66%; blood cultures 52%; only 3% received all six parts of the bundle.
audits.c: Sepsis proforma based on Sepsis Six; sepsis working group educating junior doctors and nurses with posters, pocket cards and teaching sessions.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in all parts of the Sepsis Six bundle and an 8% improvement in patients receiving all six.

audits.t: Improving Patient Safety of Acute Care Lumbar Punctures.
audits.st: 15 key documentation parameters from literature review and national guidelines
audits.f: Overall documentation 44%
audits.c: Presentation of results with departmental education session and introduction of an LP documentation proforma
audits.r2: Overall documentation 95%; new proforma used in 85% of cases

audits.t: Anticoagulation service: improving the referral process.
audits.st: Patients discharged on warfarin should be referred to the anticoagulation service
audits.f: 66% of patients successfully referred on discharge.
audits.c: Electronic referral form within the existing computer ordering system, with mandatory key fields, replacing faxed paper forms.
audits.r2: 84% of patients discharged on warfarin referred (increase of 18%).

audits.t: Improving the management of patients with acute red eyes in a large London Emergency Department.
audits.tp: Red eye assessment in the emergency department
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Contact lens status documented in 63% and visual acuity in 77%
audits.c: Eye examination proforma with integrated clinical guidelines and a new referral pathway to ophthalmology
audits.r2: Proforma completed for only 28% of patients, but its use was associated with higher documentation of all parameters

audits.t: Improving the accuracy and turn-around time of controlled drug prescribing for patients being discharged home for end-of-life care.
audits.st: Legal requirements for controlled drug prescriptions
audits.f: 89% error rate in end-of-life discharge prescriptions
audits.c: Single standardised pre-written dispensing chart for Just in Case and syringe driver medications with flow-chart guidance
audits.r2: Error rate 11%; improved dispensing turnaround time

audits.t: Improving acute eye consultations in general practice: a practical approach.
audits.tp: Red eye assessment in primary care
audits.st: Documentation of four red flag findings in acute eye consultations
audits.f: All four red flag findings documented in 2.8%; pain 26%; visual acuity 35%; photophobia 6%; laterality 88%
audits.c: Education with memory aids and an eye examination kit in each consultation room
audits.r2: All four findings documented in 50% (p < 0.01); pain 63%; visual acuity 69%; photophobia 63%; laterality 94%

audits.t: Improving management of severe sepsis and uptake of sepsis resuscitation bundle in an acute setting.
audits.tp: Sepsis recognition and treatment on wards
audits.st: Best practice guidelines for severe sepsis resuscitation bundle (oxygen, IV fluids, antibiotics, blood cultures, lactate, urine output)
audits.f: Lactate measured 15/32 (47%); fluids within an hour 10/22 (45%); blood cultures taken after antibiotics 12/22 (55%); antibiotics within an hour 12/22 (55%).
audits.c: A set of interventions including a 'sepsis box'.
audits.r2: Antibiotics within an hour up by 22%; lactate performed in 26/30 (87%); improved identification of severe sepsis and IV fluid administration.

audits.t: A new oxygen prescription produces real improvements in therapeutic oxygen use.
audits.st: British Thoracic Society oxygen audit standards (four key standards)
audits.f: 55% had a valid oxygen prescription; 50% had a documented target saturation range; 84% had saturations on the MEWS chart; 0% had oxygen signed for at drug rounds.
audits.c: New oxygen prescription chart, oxygen alert stickers for drug and MEWS charts, point-of-care resources and senior-led education, over three PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: After PDSA cycle three: valid prescription 94%, target range documented 94%, saturations on MEWS chart 100%, oxygen signed for at drug rounds 18%.

audits.t: Quality improvement project using a care bundle approach on the management of the immediate discharge document (IDD) within a single general practice.
audits.tp: Immediate discharge document processing in general practice
audits.st: Scottish Patient Safety Programme in Primary Care care bundle for immediate discharge documents (medicines reconciled, follow-up documented, diagnosis coded, all actions completed)
audits.f: 20% compliance with the care bundle.
audits.c: Education at each cycle, all doctors using the Medicines Reconciliation Polypharmacy LES template, and an electronic checklist for the care bundle.
audits.r2: 100% compliance in PDSA cycles two and three.

audits.t: Improving venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis in acute urological admissions during out of hours through the introduction of a urological admission proforma.
audits.st: NICE: all urgently admitted patients to have a completed VTE assessment within 24 hours and appropriate prophylaxis
audits.f: Completed VTE form 56%; LMWH appropriately prescribed 65%; TEDS 35%; 3 VTE-related complications
audits.c: Urological admissions proforma and teaching sessions for junior doctors
audits.r2: Completed VTE form 92%; LMWH prescribed 84%; TEDS 76%; 1 VTE-related complication

audits.t: Improving the handover and care of acute urological admissions.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Rates of handover and registrar involvement audited (numbers not stated)
audits.c: Foundation doctor induction training in acute urology, explanation of importance of handover, and review of team approachability
audits.r2: Significant improvements in early registrar involvement and successful handover (numbers not stated)

audits.t: Giving ourselves a head start: improving the quality of documentation of referrals to neurosurgery.
audits.st: Gold standard referral documentation parameters from national guidelines and literature review
audits.f: Referral documentation adequacy assessed (numbers not stated)
audits.c: Educational meeting with results and case studies, and a 'record of telephone referral to neurosurgery' (RTRN) form
audits.r2: Significant improvement in documentation with use of the RTRN form (numbers not stated)

audits.t: Improving management of gout in primary care using a customised electronic records template.
audits.st: Current gout guidance: serum uric acid (SUA) checked in past 12 months, SUA below target, lifestyle advice in past 12 months; audit standard 60% at 2 months and 80% at 4 months
audits.f: 51 (40%) had SUA checked in past 12 months; 88 (25%) had SUA below target; lifestyle advice not recorded.
audits.c: Custom electronic EMIS template displaying gout guidance and allowing data entry, with education of GPs and administrative staff.
audits.r2: 112 (84%) had SUA checked; 79 (51%) had SUA below target; 76 (57%) received lifestyle advice.

audits.t: Epilepsy emergency rescue training.
audits.st: Joint Epilepsy Council training guidelines backed by NICE
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Web-based epilepsy emergency rescue training resource piloted using QI methodology.

audits.t: Nutritional assessment in elderly care: a MUST!
audits.st: Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST) documented, correctly calculated and acted on
audits.f: MUST scores calculated in 73%; dietitian referral 62%
audits.c: Liaison with hospital teams, encouraging regular nurse training, and weekly dietitian ward rounds to screen for malnutrition
audits.r2: MUST scores calculated in 97%; dietitian referral 86% (second cycle)

audits.t: Improving feedback from outpatient medical appointments attended by escorted psychiatric patients in the North London Forensic Service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Appointment details (date, time, hospital, specialty) documented in 54.5% of cases; content documented in fewer; 68.43% of staff unsatisfied with feedback.
audits.c: A six-question outpatient appointment feedback form designed by junior doctors.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in feedback quality at 3 and 6 months (figures not given); 70% of staff aware of form; 40% still unsatisfied.

audits.t: Promoting vision and hearing aids use in an intensive care unit.
audits.st: UK Clinical Pharmacy Association guidance on minimising delirium risk factors
audits.f: High prevalence of vision/hearing aid need and low availability (numbers not stated)
audits.c: Changes to the ICU Innovian assessment system to prompt nurses' daily delirium reduction checks
audits.r2: Rate of assessment 100% and vision aid use near 100% after further amendments

audits.t: CQUIN audit for prescription of antibiotics for urinary tract infections in an acute medical assessment unit.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for urinary tract infection
audits.st: Local hospital antibiotic guidelines for UTI (CQUIN)
audits.f: 20% with culture-confirmed UTI not given antibiotics; 25% of prescriptions non-compliant; stop dates missing on 77%; duration 1 to 11 days
audits.c: Group teaching sessions, proactive pharmacist checks and widely distributed posters
audits.r2: Compliance with local policy 100%; stop/review date on 100%; duration 1 to 7 days; 35% not prescribed antibiotics

audits.t: The psychiatric inpatient physical health assessment sheet (PIPHAS): a useful tool to improve the speed, efficiency, and documentation of physical examination in new psychiatric inpatients.
audits.tp: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists: full physical examination on admission or within 24 hours; Trust guidelines
audits.f: 78/111 (70.3%) had a physical examination during admission; documentation often poor and incomplete across domains.
audits.c: Introduction of a psychiatric inpatient physical health assessment sheet (PIPHAS).
audits.r2: 75/100 (75%) examined on admission, with more thorough documentation of all examination domains when a PIPHAS form was used.

audits.t: Improving handover from intensive care to ward medical teams with simple changes to paperwork.
audits.st: General Medical Council guidance on medical handover
audits.f: Handover present only in a minority of patients and documented in none (0%).
audits.c: Handover prompt and documentation of recipient on discharge paperwork, space in daily review sheets for outstanding handover, and presentation of findings at a local meeting.
audits.r2: Handover rate 100% (n=12) and documentation of handover 100%.

audits.t: Improving critical care discharge summaries: a collaborative quality improvement project using PDSA.
audits.st: Guidelines and evidence identified by scoping review for critical care discharge summaries
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Regular audit and feedback of discharge summary quality, feedback of patient experience, and championing and education by local opinion leaders over three PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: Audit results were mixed across the project, showing difficulty sustaining positive change.

audits.t: Developing a ward round checklist to improve patient safety.
audits.st: Predefined patient safety outcome measures documented on ward round
audits.f: Overall documentation compliance 45%.
audits.c: Ward round checklist introduced and developed through PDSA cycles over nine months.

audits.t: Improving paediatric prescribing practice in a district general hospital through implementation of a quality improvement programme.
audits.st: Error-free prescribing on drug charts (predesigned proforma)
audits.f: 32 errors across 12 drug charts.
audits.c: Seven sequential interventions over six months covering education and communication, practical prescribing changes and medicine reconciliation.
audits.r2: After intervention 7: 10 errors (-63%); lowest after intervention 6: 7 errors (-74%).

audits.t: Evaluation of an evidence based quality improvement innovation for patients with musculoskeletal low back pain in an accident and emergency setting.
audits.tp: Low back pain management in the emergency department
audits.st: Locally developed evidence-based low back pain pathway and medico-legal documentation standards
audits.f: Initial review of 75 case notes showed inconsistent assessment, incomplete documentation and a biomedical approach.
audits.c: Evidence-based low back pain pathway, staff education programme and patient education booklet.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in all areas: red flag screening up 22%, biopsychosocial screening 29%, previous symptoms 44%, observation 57%, classification 59%; analgesic ladder adherence up 45%, reassurance 23%, GP referral 44%.

audits.t: Mind the gap: Improving discharge communication between secondary and primary care.
audits.st: Locally developed 'golden rules' for discharge communication
audits.f: One third missing discharging doctor details; medication changes unclear in 68%; follow-up not completed in 40%
audits.c: Interactive teaching for foundation doctors, an e-learning module and suggested software changes to the electronic discharge proforma

audits.t: Improving the acute care of COPD patients across Gloucestershire: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: BTS COPD admission care bundle and local CQUIN target
audits.f: 63% received all bundle elements (up from 10% before bundle paperwork was introduced in June 2014)
audits.c: Focus group of junior medical staff to raise awareness, following introduction of bundle paperwork with training
audits.r2: 73% received all elements of the bundle; steroids and antibiotics within four hours 96%; appropriate oxygen prescription 87% (from 97%)

audits.t: Improving reporting of critical incidents through education and involvement.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 11 incident reports submitted (1.8 per month).
audits.c: Agreed definition of a critical incident, presentation of staff questionnaire findings on barriers to senior management, and feedback to staff after critical incident presentations.
audits.r2: 22 incident reports (3.7 per month), an increase of 100%.

audits.t: Improving documentation of physical health investigations in an adolescent mental health inpatient unit.
audits.tp: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
audits.st: Documentation of five investigations (blood tests, ECG, MRI head, DEXA, ovarian ultrasound) in ward round entries
audits.f: Blood tests documented in 2/22 (9.1%); ECG, MRI head, DEXA and ovarian ultrasound 0/22 (0%)
audits.c: Electronic ward round template modified with headings, free-text and drop-down boxes for each investigation
audits.r2: Blood tests 21/22 (95.5%); ECG, MRI head, DEXA and pelvic ultrasound 22/22 (100%)

audits.t: Alcohol detoxification in Ysbyty Gwynedd: Two small sips or one big gulp? Two-step screening more reliable for identification of alcohol dependency syndrome at risk of delirium tremens for routine care.
audits.st: Local pathway for recognition and treatment of alcohol dependency
audits.f: Over-prescription of chlordiazepoxide with average length of stay 5.5 days (2012/2013); compliance with screening tools in random samples over three months was persistently low (exact figure unclear in abstract).
audits.c: Redesigned pathway with an abbreviated two-question AUDIT screening tool and threshold, implemented over several PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: 86 patients screened with the two-question tool, 18 at possible risk, 16 had full AUDIT and 8 started detoxification; overall pathway compliance 84%.

audits.t: Improving induction of labour - a quality improvement project addressing Caesarean section rates and length of process in women undergoing induction of labour.
audits.tp: Induction of labour process and outcomes
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Caesarean section rate after induction 29%; time to administer induction medication 6.3 h; outpatient induction 3%.
audits.c: Dedicated induction of labour suite, promotion of outpatient induction, single-administration prostaglandin, staff engagement and rolling audit.
audits.r2: Caesarean section rate 22% (p=0.05); time to induction medication 2.7 h (p=0.0001); outpatient induction 33% (p=0.001); reduced inpatient length of stay.

audits.t: Inpatient Falls: Improving assessment, documentation, and management.
audits.st: National Patient Safety Agency (NPSA) guidance on post-fall medical assessment
audits.f: Pilot audit: 50% of expected data points not recorded; thorough musculoskeletal examination documented in 54%
audits.c: Teaching session for new junior doctors, then a falls proforma
audits.r2: Fall history documented in 100% (improved by nearly 30%); musculoskeletal examination 77% (100% where proforma used)

audits.t: Improving documentation within the acute stroke unit: Introducing a stroke specific clerking proforma.
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians acute stroke guidelines; recommended clerking categories
audits.f: Only half of the recommended categories were being completed; junior doctors lacked confidence.
audits.c: Stroke specific admission clerking proforma piloted on the ward
audits.r2: Significant improvement in the quality of clerkings (no figures given in abstract).

audits.t: Four Simple Ward Based Initiatives to Reduce Unnecessary In-Hospital Patient Stay: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean time from medically fit for discharge to discharge with care package 25 days; total LoS 46 days; admission to MFFD 21 days.
audits.c: Four daily ward initiatives: morning nurse-doctor board round, post-ward-round MDT meeting, evening board round for next-day discharge paperwork, and computer on wheels on ward rounds.
audits.r2: MFFD to discharge fell to 1 day; total LoS 16 days; admission to MFFD 15 days.

audits.t: Applying Quality Improvement into Systems-based Learning to Improve Diabetes Outcomes in Primary Care.
audits.st: National patient-centred diabetes quality measures (Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Shared Savings Program)
audits.f: Baseline chart audit of documented counselling, side-effect assessment, adherence, A1C and BMI (baseline figures not given).
audits.c: Accredited CME: private performance improvement internet course, small-group internet courses and enduring materials.
audits.r2: Documented side-effect assessment +11%, counselling on risks/benefits +28%, medication adherence +13%, lifestyle modification +8%; documented adherence +24%; A1C -0.16%, BMI -2.1.

audits.t: Hypokalaemia: Improving the investigation, management and therapeutic monitoring of hypokalaemic medical inpatients at a district general hospital.
audits.st: Trust guidelines for treatment of hypokalaemia (serum potassium <3.5 mmol/L)
audits.f: 7/32 (22%) received adequate treatment
audits.c: Set of interventions including a hypokalaemia treatment algorithm
audits.r2: 19/30 (63%) correctly prescribed appropriate doses consistent with the algorithm

audits.t: Simple interventions can greatly improve clinical documentation: a quality improvement project of record keeping on the surgical wards at a district general hospital.
audits.st: Record keeping standards for documentation, labelling and filing
audits.f: Only 12% (4/33) of notes free of loose pages; designation recorded in 11/33 and printed name in 21/33 (65%); labelling 16%.
audits.c: PDSA over 10 months: education, single admission folders, and an educational poster on patient identification stickers.
audits.r2: Sustained improvement of over 80% compliance; labelling rose from 16% to 68%.

audits.t: A multi-faceted approach to increase appropriate analgesia prescribing in the emergency department.
audits.tp: Time to analgesia in the emergency department
audits.st: RCEM analgesia guidelines, including analgesia within 20 minutes for severe pain
audits.f: Guideline-compliant analgesia 29%; pain score at triage 38%; rechecked 19%; severe pain treated within 20 minutes 22%
audits.c: Locally adapted RCEM guidelines, monthly doctor and nurse teaching, and a nurse prescriber champion
audits.r2: Pain score at triage 87%; guideline-concordant analgesia 52%; severe pain acted on in time 40%

audits.t: Monitoring of physical health parameters for inpatients on a child and adolescent mental health unit receiving regular antipsychotic therapy.
audits.st: Local trust guidelines, NICE schizophrenia guidance and Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines: baseline and 12-week physical health checks
audits.f: Overall monitoring of physical health parameters poor (numbers not stated)
audits.c: Prompting tool filed in physical health files and education of staff
audits.r2: Significant improvement for the majority of parameters (numbers not stated)

audits.t: Perioperative dexamethasone administration in tonsillectomy patients: A three-cycle audit showing improvement using printed theatre lists.
audits.tp: Postoperative nausea and vomiting prevention in tonsillectomy
audits.st: SIGN guideline 117: dexamethasone before tonsillectomy
audits.f: 73% compliance.
audits.c: ENT secretaries added 'Dex Please' to tonsillectomy theatre lists; after cycle 2, a reminding tool for secretarial staff.
audits.r2: Third cycle: all lists had 'Dex Please' and compliance was 100%.

audits.t: An audit of hepatitis B vaccination for men who have sex with men before and after sexual health service integration.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B vaccination in sexual health clinics
audits.st: Scottish Government sexual health standard: hepatitis B vaccination for MSM
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Integration of genitourinary medicine and sexual and reproductive health services (service redesign).
audits.r2: No significant difference in proportion receiving at least one dose (p = 0.64); significant drop in proportion receiving three doses (p = 0.0157).

audits.t: A re-audit of the management of gonorrhoea.
audits.st: Auditable outcomes for gonorrhoea management (national guideline outcomes)
audits.f: Three of eight auditable outcomes met.
audits.c: New measures introduced after the first audit; electronic patient records with patient record templates introduced December 2012
audits.r2: Six of nine auditable outcomes met.

audits.t: Audit of radiology communication systems for critical, urgent, and unexpected significant findings.
audits.st: National Patient Safety Agency and Royal College of Radiologists guidance on communication of critical, urgent and unexpected significant radiological findings
audits.f: 154 of 229 departments (67%) responded; 88% had a policy, 34% had an automated electronic alert system and 17% had service-wide electronic tracking of reports.

audits.t: Improving clinical outcomes through centralization of rectal cancer surgery and clinical audit: a mixed-methods assessment.
audits.st: Clinical guidelines for rectal cancer care (quality indicators)
audits.f: 51 hospitals performed rectal cancer surgery; 37.5% of patients operated in high-volume centres; total mesorectal excision reported 36.2; emergency surgery 5.6%; median lymph nodes examined 14.1.
audits.c: Centralisation of rectal cancer surgery to fewer hospitals.
audits.r2: 32 hospitals; 52.8% in high-volume centres; total mesorectal excision reported 85.7; emergency surgery 3.6%; median lymph nodes 16.

audits.t: Laboratory audit as part of the quality assessment of a primary HPV-screening program.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: High-risk HPV positivity 97% (148/154) in prediagnostic samples of women with CIN3+, versus cytological abnormality in 143/154 (94%).

audits.t: Laboratory system strengthening and quality improvement in Ethiopia.
audits.st: WHO AFRO SLIPTA checklist star rating
audits.f: Baseline audit compliance (figures not legible in abstract).
audits.c: SLMTA training, improvement projects and supportive supervision.
audits.r2: At exit, 61% of cohort I and 48% of cohort II laboratories increased their star rating.

audits.t: An Audit of Diabetes Self-Management Education Programs in South Africa.
audits.st: International Standards for Diabetes Education (International Diabetes Federation)
audits.f: No guideline dedicated to DSME; five structured programmes and 22 ad hoc interventions identified; materials mainly in English.

audits.t: New patient assessment in old age psychiatry: the importance of risk assessment.
audits.tp: Old age psychiatry new patient assessment quality
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 72.4% of new assessments done by non-medical clinicians; the majority missed important information, especially medications and risk assessment.
audits.c: Assessment form, training seminars and supervision for CMHT clinicians.

audits.t: The Team at Work--The Society for Acute Medicine's Benchmarking Audit 2014 (SAMBA'14).
audits.tp: Acute medical unit function and flow
audits.st: Society for Acute Medicine clinical quality indicators and Royal College of Physicians standards (early warning score within 30 minutes, competent decision maker within 4 hours, timely consultant review)
audits.f: 84% had an early warning score within 30 minutes, 81% were seen by a competent decision maker within 4 hours and 73% saw a consultant in time; only 56% met all three standards.

audits.t: Audits show that specialist paediatric training programmes are sensitive to medical, staffing and economic changes.
audits.st: Modified European Union of Medical Specialists 1997 protocol
audits.f: Key areas performing poorly were identified for follow-up; figures not reported.
audits.c: Follow-up of poorly performing key areas; increase in paediatric specialist resources.
audits.r2: Most key follow-up issues had improved, but educational objectives needed clarifying and following up, and trainees needed more outpatient time.

audits.t: Pressure ulcer and wounds reporting in NHS hospitals in England part 1: Audit of monitoring systems.
audits.st: Gold-standard pressure ulcer prevalence methods used to assess Safety Thermometer, incident reporting and STEIS
audits.f: Wound audit found 160 (7.1%) patients with an existing pressure ulcer versus 105 (4.7%) on Safety Thermometer (sensitivity 48.2%); incident reporting sensitivity 53.4%.

audits.t: [Evaluation of therapeutical appropriateness in psychiatric treatment of schizophrenia, by integrating computer data records with clinical audit results].
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Schizophrenia was the most frequent diagnosis (31.1%); olanzapine most used (29.1%); about 70% on monotherapy, 23.6% on polytherapy, 7.9% switched.

audits.t: Internal Audit of Compliance with a Perioperative Checklist in a Tertiary Care Neurosurgical Unit.
audits.st: Perioperative checklist adapted from WHO Surgical Safety Checklist
audits.f: Compliance with Sign-in 82%, Time-out 99%, Sign-out 93%; on average 92% of Time-out elements verified.

audits.t: Time for a culture change? Suboptimal compliance with blood culture standards at a district hospital in Cape Town.
audits.st: 2010 South African guideline for blood cultures (22 standards); contamination benchmark 3%
audits.f: Contamination 4.5%; 33% of bottles had the recommended 8-10 mL fill; 96.9% of patients had a single culture in 24 hours; 7.8% had a combined volume of at least 20 mL; median needle-to-incubator time 11 hours 25 minutes.

audits.t: Tuberculosis screening in patients with HIV: An audit against UK national guidelines to assess current practice and the effectiveness of an electronic tuberculosis-screening prompt.
audits.st: British HIV Association 2011 guidelines on routine tuberculosis screening in HIV
audits.f: Of 165 new attendees in whom screening was recommended, 6.1% had a completed electronic TB screening prompt and 12.1% underwent routine TB screening.

audits.t: Improving the Medical Assessment of Patients Before Electroconvulsive Therapy: An Audit Across Two Sites.
audits.st: Scottish ECT Accreditation Network standards
audits.f: Site A: repeat examination in 30 (100%), incomplete in 47%, histories accurate in 20%. Site B: repeat in 6/26 (23%), incomplete in 100%, histories accurate in 38%.
audits.c: Amended examination sheet and prompts to use multiple sources for medical history (site A).
audits.r2: Site A: all 12 had complete repeat examination; histories accurate in 8 (67%); multiple sources used in 11 (92%).

audits.t: Assessment of rehabilitation needs in colorectal cancer treatment: Results from a mixed audit and qualitative study in Denmark.
audits.st: National rehabilitation policy for needs assessment
audits.f: Physical, psychological and social needs documented at start and end of treatment in 10% (n=2) of surgical and 35% (n=7) of oncology trajectories; physical needs documented in 90% (n=36); referral to municipal rehabilitation in 5% (n=2).

audits.t: An Innovative Approach to Improving the Accuracy of Delirium Assessments Using the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit.
audits.st: At least 1 CAM-ICU delirium assessment every shift; assessment accuracy
audits.f: Compliance with at least 1 assessment per shift 85%; accuracy 70.31% overall and 53.49% in sedate or agitated patients.
audits.c: Programme to improve delirium assessment accuracy (details not stated).
audits.r2: Compliance 99%; accuracy 95.51% overall and 89.23% in sedate or agitated patients.

audits.t: Anaphylaxis audit in a busy metropolitan Emergency Department: a review of real life management compared to best practice.
audits.st: Established anaphylaxis treatment guidelines (Brown grading, adrenaline use, observation at least 4 hours, immunologist referral)
audits.f: Anaphylaxis not always recognised or graded; adrenaline often withheld; parenteral promethazine frequently given; observation often inadequate; referral to immunologist not universal.
audits.c: Targeted educational programme for emergency department staff at 5 months.
audits.r2: Appropriate adrenaline use up 21%; sedating antihistamine use down 16%; immunologist referrals up 24%; 11% reduction in patients observed at least 4 hours.

audits.t: A quality improvement project using a problem based post take ward round proforma based on the SOAP acronym to improve documentation in acute surgical receiving.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England record keeping guidelines
audits.f: Name/ID 96%; subjective 84%; objective 48%; impression/diagnosis 30%; plan 98%; diet status 16%; discharge decision 16%; discharge planning 20%; signature 96%; grade 62%
audits.c: Problem-based SOAP post-take ward round proforma
audits.r2: Name/ID, subjective, objective, plan, signature and grade 100%; impression/diagnosis 98%; diet status 83%; discharge decision 66%; discharge planning 40%

audits.t: AUDIT OF BLOOD TRANSFUSION PRACTICES IN THE PAEDIATRIC MEDICAL WARD OF A TERTIARY HOSPITAL IN SOUTHEAST NIGERIA.
audits.st: Recommended transfusion duration of four hours
audits.f: 238 transfusions in 95 patients; 96.4% received appropriate volume; 59.7% of transfusions exceeded the recommended four hours (mean 4.6 hours); mean Hb rise 3.1 g/dl.

audits.t: Perioperative management of diabetes in elective patients: a region-wide audit.
audits.st: National guidance on management of adults with diabetes undergoing surgery (2011)
audits.f: HbA1c recorded preoperatively in 71%; VRIII not used when indicated in 11%; only 8% received recommended substrate fluid; hourly intra-operative CBG in 56%; CBG in recovery in 73%.

audits.t: A retrospective review of the type of anaesthesia used for LLETZ: proposal for a categorisation audit tool.
audits.st: Majority of LLETZ procedures should be performed under local anaesthesia in an outpatient setting
audits.f: 829 (85.5%) under local anaesthesia and 141 (14.5%) under general anaesthesia; GA indications: associated pathology 33.8%, anticipated difficulty 41.2%, patient request 25%.

audits.t: An audit of consenting practices in a district general hospital. Can we improve?
audits.st: GMC consent guidance and local policy
audits.f: All criteria met in 12 (5%); form secured in records 87 (34%); grade recorded 211 (83%); legible 191 (75%); copy given 48 (19%); additional written information 24 (9%); abbreviations used 68 (27%).
audits.c: Interventions to improve adherence to consent guidance (details not given in abstract)
audits.r2: Form secured 52 (47%); grade recorded 94 (85%); legible 101 (75%); copy given 42 (38%); additional written information 41 (37%).

audits.t: Clinical audit of genetic testing and referral patterns for fragile X and associated conditions.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Expanded allele found in 3.7% of tests; paediatricians requested about 70%; median age at full mutation diagnosis 4.3 years (males) and 9.4 years (females); about 25% of full mutation or premutation carriers may not have attended genetic counselling or multidisciplinary services.

audits.t: Criteria-based audit of caesarean section in a referral hospital in rural Tanzania.
audits.st: Audit criteria for caesarean section based on literature and national/international guidelines
audits.f: Of 82 CS among women with severe maternal morbidity or death, 36 (44.0%) met criteria without delay, 20 (24.4%) had correct indication but significant delay, and 16 (19.5%) did not meet criteria.

audits.t: Improving the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism in the emergency department.
audits.st: NICE guidelines for diagnosis of PE, with PERC allowed where appropriate
audits.f: Inappropriate d-dimers 36%; inappropriate CTPAs 34%; inappropriate V/Q scans 42%.
audits.c: Flowchart encouraging correct use of Wells score and PERC, after PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: Inappropriate d-dimers 24%; inappropriate CTPAs 10%; inappropriate V/Q scans 14%; documentation of pre-test probability increased.

audits.t: Improvement of fluid balance monitoring through education and rationalisation.
audits.st: Fluid balance monitoring only when clinically indicated, with complete and accurate charts
audits.f: Only 53% of input/output monitoring was clinically indicated; average chart completion 50%.
audits.c: E-learning and verbal presentations on fluid balance, plus daily medical review of charts to rationalise monitoring.
audits.r2: 93% reduction in unnecessary monitoring, with increases in completion (40%) and accuracy (48%) of remaining charts.

audits.t: Reduction of referral to assessment time for an older adults community mental health team.
audits.tp: Community mental health referral to assessment time
audits.st: Previously set waiting time standards for routine and urgent assessment
audits.f: Mean time to assessment 15.89 days routine, 9.81 days urgent (2011: 12 and 3.6 days)
audits.c: Duty worker role for triage and allocation of referrals
audits.r2: Mean time to assessment 10.68 days routine, 6.8 days urgent

audits.t: Antimicrobial stewardship: Improving antibiotic prescribing practice in a respiratory ward.
audits.tp: Antibiotic indication and review date documentation
audits.st: Local antimicrobial guidelines: indication and intended duration documented on drug chart
audits.f: Indication documented 24%; duration 39%
audits.c: Antibiotic guardian pocket cards with a three-point checklist, mini-posters, MDT feedback and certificates, then an MDT awareness session

audits.t: Standards in Operation Notes--Is It Time to Re-Emphasise Their Importance?
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England operation note guidelines
audits.f: Time recorded in 12 (40%), emergency/elective status in none (0%), operative diagnosis in 7 (23%), surgeon's name in 30 (100%), findings in 27 (90%), tissue altered in 27 (90%).
audits.c: Educational intervention to increase awareness of the RCS guidelines.
audits.r2: Time 16 (53%), emergency/elective status 11 (36%), operative diagnosis 21 (70%); surgeon's name fell to 26 (86%), findings to 21 (53%) and tissue altered to 20 (66%).

audits.t: Management of non ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome patients in New Zealand: a longitudinal analysis. Results from the New Zealand Acute Coronary Syndrome national audits of 2002, 2007 and 2012.
audits.st: Evidence-based care for NSTEACS
audits.f: Important limitations to NSTEACS care demonstrated (no figures given in abstract).
audits.c: National audit and feedback creating momentum for change (repeated audits).
audits.r2: More patients had echocardiography and coronary angiography; evidence-based in-hospital medical treatment and revascularisation increased (no figures given).

audits.t: Audit of cytology of upper urinary tract.
audits.st: Diagnostic performance compared with histology
audits.f: Sensitivity 73%, specificity 86%, PPV 84.6%.
audits.c: New terminology with two-tiered atypia grading, a new request form and better communication with clinicians.

audits.t: An audit and feedback intervention study increased adherence to antibiotic prescribing guidelines at a Norwegian hospital.
audits.st: National clinical practice guideline for antibiotic use in community-acquired pneumonia and acute exacerbations of COPD
audits.f: Appropriate empirical antibiotics prescribed in 61.7%.
audits.c: Audit and feedback at an internal educational meeting plus distribution of a pocket version of the national guideline.

audits.t: Surveillance of Antibiotic Consumption Point Prevalence Survey 2014: Antimicrobial Prescribing in Pediatrics Wards of 16 Iranian Hospitals.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 571 of 858 children (66.6%) received one or more antimicrobials; 60.6% therapeutic; parenteral route in 92.5% of therapeutic use; ceftriaxone most prescribed (32.4%).

audits.t: Lessons learned from transfusion audits.
audits.st: Self-inspection forms approved by the hospital transfusion committee (indication, consent, immunohaematology tests, documentation)
audits.f: Adequate documentation in 5 (10.6%), intermediate 51.1%, inadequate 38.3%.

audits.t: Does periodical department audit really works to make things fall in place: A Geriatric/General Oral Health Assessment Index based audit in prosthodontics.
audits.st: Patient satisfaction graded with the Geriatric/General Oral Health Assessment Index
audits.f: Satisfaction with complete dentures delivered by clinical students (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Corrective measures and strict staff supervision of students
audits.r2: Patient satisfaction increased significantly (figures not given).

audits.t: Early management of traumatic brain injury in a Tertiary hospital in Central Kenya: A clinical audit.
audits.st: Seventeen audit criteria in five clinical domains
audits.f: Only 3/17 criteria met in under-13s and 4/17 in over-13s; cervical radiograph assessment 7.1% and 8.8%; oxygen administration 21.4% and 20.6%.

audits.t: Implementation and evaluation of a quality improvement project: carepaths for Early Psychosis Intervention Programmes in Northeastern Ontario.
audits.tp: Early intervention in psychosis care standards
audits.st: 12 EPI best practices specified in the Carepath
audits.f: Pre-Carepath chart audit of 110 client files; figures not reported.
audits.c: Implementation of an early psychosis intervention Carepath outlining best practice care pathways.
audits.r2: Significantly higher frequencies for 2 of 12 best practices (assessing impact on family and assessing substance use); standardisation of documentation did not improve significantly.

audits.t: Audit of emergent and urgent surgery for acutely ill pediatric patients: is access timely?
audits.st: Surgical urgency class target times: class 1 1 h, 2A 6 h, 2B 24 h, 3 72 h
audits.f: Performed within target: class 1 59.2%, 2A 81.9%, 2B 81.2%, 3 74.4%; out of hours for 73.2%, 71.5%, 54.7% and 27.7% respectively.

audits.t: Audit of paediatric residents' medical records.
audits.st: 15-component audit form; more than two 'not met' items = not acceptable
audits.f: Highest 'not acceptable' rates: initial investigations 5.3%, summary of investigations 4.5%, progression of clinical conditions 4.3%.

audits.t: Safety of community-based minor surgery performed by GPs: an audit in different settings.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 6138 procedures; 88.8% of samples expected to go to histology were sent; malignant diagnosis correct in 69% (ESGPs), 93% (GPwSIs) and 91% (Model 2 GPs).

audits.t: Improving Compliance With a Single Post-Operative Dose of Intravesical Chemotherapy After Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumour.
audits.st: European Association of Urology guidelines on single post-operative dose of intravesical chemotherapy
audits.f: 15 (28% of NMIBC) given PSDIVC; 23 (36%) given PSDIVC or had documented contraindication
audits.c: Intervention bundle: pre-operative delivery of mitomycin C to theatre, proforma in operative notes and designated roles
audits.r2: 12 (50% of NMIBC) given PSDIVC; 28 (90%) given PSDIVC or documented contraindication

audits.t: Using a community of practice to evaluate falls prevention activity in a residential aged care organisation: a clinical audit.
audits.st: Evidence-based falls prevention practice guidelines
audits.f: All 13 sites completed the audit; vitamin D supplementation mean 41.5% (s.d. 23.7); no site had mandatory falls education or a falls prevention policy.
audits.c: Community of practice actions: letter to GPs about vitamin D, staff and resident surveys to shape education, falls definition and a falls prevention policy.

audits.t: Guideline Adherence in Outpatient Clinics for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Results from a Clinical Audit.
audits.st: Three COPD guidance documents; performance graded excellent (>80%), good (60-80%), adequate (40-59%), inadequate (20-39%)
audits.f: Excellent or good adherence for symptom recording, MRC or CAT use, smoking status, spirometry and bronchodilator therapy.

audits.t: Audit of anesthetic trainees' 'hands-on' operating room experience in an Australian tertiary children's hospital.
audits.st: New ANZCA curriculum training requirements
audits.f: Trainees would comfortably achieve new ANZCA training standards for volume and breadth of exposure (no figures given).

audits.t: Audit of Turnaround Time for a Training Oral Histopathology Laboratory in Malaysia.
audits.st: Turnaround time goals
audits.f: Mean turnaround time acceptable for most specimens but turnaround time goals were less than satisfactory; surgical and decalcified specimens took significantly longer than biopsies.

audits.t: Determinants and Gaps in Preventive Care Delivery for Indigenous Australians: A Cross-sectional Analysis.
audits.tp: Preventive care delivery in primary care
audits.st: Best practice guidelines: 26 recommended preventive services
audits.f: Good delivery of most basic measurements but poor follow-up of abnormal findings.

audits.t: Wide Variation in Absolute Cardiovascular Risk Assessment in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People with Type 2 Diabetes.
audits.st: Documented absolute cardiovascular risk assessment in eligible patients with diabetes
audits.f: 33% (574/1728) had documented CVRA; 95% of assessments were in the Northern Territory.

audits.t: Implementing Laboratory Quality Management Systems in Mozambique: The Becton Dickinson-US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief Public-Private Partnership Initiative.
audits.st: WHO AFRO SLIPTA checklist (13 quality system essentials)
audits.f: Baseline SLIPTA audits (figures not given).
audits.c: SLMTA curriculum, training and mentorship of local auditors and managers.
audits.r2: Final audits showed improvement across the 13 quality system essentials compared with baseline (figures not given).

audits.t: A quality improvement project to reduce hypothermia in infants undergoing MRI scanning.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Post-scan hypothermia associated with younger age (P = 0.002), lower weight (P = 0.005) and lower pre-scan temperature.
audits.c: Protocol development, risk factor identification, vigilance and use of a vacuum immobiliser.
audits.r2: Re-audit of NICU infants; authors report the problem was minimised (figures not given).

audits.t: The impact of SLMTA in improving laboratory quality systems in the Caribbean Region.
audits.st: SLIPTA checklist star rating
audits.f: Baseline scores 19% to 52% (0 stars).
audits.c: SLMTA training, improvement projects, mentorship and implementation plans after each audit.
audits.r2: One laboratory reached four stars, two three stars and two two stars.

audits.t: [Clinical audit of screening for gestational diabetes among 848 pregnant women in 23 maternity units of the Pays de la Loire, 2014].
audits.st: 2010 national guidelines for gestational diabetes screening
audits.f: Adherence to screening guidelines 45.5%, non-adherence 27.6%, over-screening 26.9%; OGTT performed per guidelines in 95.9%; specialist follow-up of GDM 84.6%.

audits.t: Management of ADHD in children and adolescents: clinical audit in a South African setting.
audits.st: 17 audit standards from NICE ADHD guidelines; good compliance ≥80%, fair 50-79%
audits.f: Compliance low, with only four of 17 standards rated good; physical monitoring especially poor.

audits.t: Screening for diabetic kidney disease in primary care for the underinsured: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines for diabetic kidney disease screening (urine microalbumin)
audits.f: Microalbumin ordered in 50.3%; DKD diagnosed in 3.3% (n=10).
audits.c: Chart audit with feedback, provider education on guidelines and TeamSTEPPS teamwork strategies.
audits.r2: Microalbumin ordered in 75%; DKD diagnosed in 10.7% (n=21) over three months (P=.000).

audits.t: An audit of the quality of inpatient care for adults with learning disability in the UK.
audits.tp: Inpatient care for adults with learning disability
audits.st: Seven key indicators of high-quality inpatient care for people with learning disability
audits.f: Only 34 (19.3%) had any swallowing assessment and 12 of 57 with epilepsy (21.1%) had an epilepsy risk assessment; BMI poorly recorded.

audits.t: Use of an electronic metabolic monitoring form in a mental health service - a retrospective file audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Metabolic monitoring forms of 36% of consumers contained data; weight 87.4%, height 85.4%, BP 83.5%, BMI 73.6%, cholesterol 56.3%, fasting glucose 60.2%, waist circumference 54.4%.

audits.t: Clinical Practice Audit: Perioperative Antibiotic Prophylaxis in Paediatric Cancer Patients with Broviac Catheter Implantation.
audits.st: Internal perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis guideline (January 2014), including duration of 24 h or less
audits.f: Prophylaxis given for 24 h or less in 22%.
audits.c: Introduction of an internal perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis guideline.
audits.r2: Prophylaxis given for 24 h or less in 91%.

audits.t: Prescription errors in the National Health Services, time to change practice.
audits.st: Standard hospital prescription charts per local pharmacy guidance
audits.f: DGH: allergy 31%, weight 5%, capital letters 40%; discontinued prescriptions properly deleted 49%. Teaching hospital: age 82%, generic name 63%, capital letters 65%.
audits.c: Recommendations and changes in prescribing practice.
audits.r2: DGH: name 100%, gender 54%, allergy 51%, generic name 71%. Teaching hospital: significant improvement in unit number, generic name, insulin prescription and ward.

audits.t: Simplifying the audit of risk factor recording and control: A report from an international study in 11 countries.
audits.tp: Secondary prevention in coronary heart disease
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Smoking was recorded in over 98%, but about 20% lacked relevant laboratory measurements; 16% smoked, 29% were obese and 46% had abdominal obesity.

audits.t: Low-dose intensive insulin therapy in patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome accompanied by Left Ventricular Failure: audit of two UK hospitals.
audits.st: Normoglycaemia (4-8 mmol/l) for a consecutive six-hour period with a low-dose insulin regimen
audits.f: Normoglycaemia for six consecutive hours achieved in 72% of patients within a median of 13 hours.
audits.c: New low-dose intravenous insulin regimen for ACS with left ventricular failure, introduced after local audit showed more hypoglycaemia in this group.

audits.t: Audit of Use and Overuse of Serum Protein Immunofixation Electrophoresis and Serum Free Light Chain Assay in Tertiary Health Care: A Case for Algorithmic Testing to Optimize Laboratory Utilization.
audits.st: Authors' criteria for warranted serum immunofixation and free light chain testing
audits.f: Only 46% of serum immunofixation and 42% of serum free light chain assays were warranted.

audits.t: DEMAT: A multi-institutional dosimetry audit of rotational and static intensity-modulated radiotherapy.
audits.st: Gamma criteria 5%/3 mm and 3%/3 mm
audits.f: Point measurement mean errors -0.18±1.54% (prostate) and 0.00±1.58% (head and neck); gamma pass rate above 95% with 5%/3 mm.

audits.t: Which patients are assessed by lung cancer nurse specialists? A national lung cancer audit study of over 128,000 patients across england.
audits.st: NICE recommendation that all lung cancer patients have access to a lung cancer nurse specialist
audits.f: LCNS assessment recorded as yes in 62%, no in 6% and missing in 32%.

audits.t: A Clinical Audit of Escorts' Awareness And Patients' Safety Following Intravenous Sedation In Adult Oral Surgery.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Safety scores correlated with instruction source; reliability correlated with gender, age and information source (no figures given).

audits.t: Short Report. Audit of Conscious Sedation Provision in a Salaried Dental Service.
audits.st: Safety and effectiveness of standard conscious sedation techniques
audits.f: Care judged to be delivered satisfactorily (no figures given).

audits.t: An audit of HIV treatment outcomes in a UK inner city cohort.
audits.st: Compared with Public Health England 2014 data and British HIV Association audit
audits.f: 98.6% viral load <100 copies/ml; 99.0% <200 copies/ml.

audits.t: An audit of CT chest surveillance following oral cancer treatment.
audits.tp: Imaging surveillance after head and neck cancer
audits.st: Recommended follow-up interval CT for indeterminate chest nodules
audits.f: Of 49 patients recommended interval scans, only 20 (41%) had them; 11 had further pathological findings (5 metastatic disease, 4 primary lung tumours).
audits.c: Changed the process for booking CT surveillance scans with periodic checks that they are done.

audits.t: Can the incidence of obstetric anal sphincter injury be reduced? The STOMP experience.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Incidence of third/fourth degree tears 4.7%.
audits.c: STOMP (Stop Traumatic OASIS Morbidity Project): a series of clinical measures adopted by all staff with workshops and a publicity campaign.
audits.r2: Incidence of third/fourth degree tears fell to 2.2% (significant decrease).

audits.t: Prospective audit of postoperative instructions to patients undergoing root canal treatment in the DDUH and re-audit following introduction of a written patient information sheet.
audits.tp: Postoperative instructions after root canal treatment
audits.st: Proposed benchmarks for delivery of postoperative advice (six categories)
audits.f: 56% of charts documented that postoperative advice was given; patient questionnaire showed key messages were not consistently given.
audits.c: Introduction of a written postoperative advice sheet.
audits.r2: Benchmarks met in four of six categories.

audits.t: Audit of compliance with the British Committee for Standards in Haematology (BCSH) revised guidelines for the diagnosis and assessment of treatment response of hairy cell leukemia in University Hospital Galway.
audits.st: British Committee for Standards in Haematology revised guidelines for hairy cell leukaemia
audits.f: Blood film in 100%; flow cytometry in 89% (16), of which only 31% (5) included all four markers; no trephine analysed DBA44; post-treatment bone marrow biopsy in 65% (11) of treated patients.

audits.t: A retrospective audit of referral letter quality from general practice to an inner-city emergency department.
audits.tp: GP referrals to community mental health teams
audits.st: Authors' nine-item checklist and NSW Agency for Clinical Innovation referral template (2013)
audits.f: Over 60% completion in 80.9% of letters against the authors' checklist and 6.3% against the ACI checklist.

audits.t: Micturating cystourethrogram as a tool for investigating UTI in children - An institutional audit.
audits.tp: Imaging after childhood urinary tract infection
audits.st: Local WCH guidelines for micturating cystourethrogram after UTI, compared with RCH, NICE and AAP
audits.f: 82% conformance with WCH guidelines; 67/168 MCUGs abnormal (62 with VUR).

audits.t: Misuse of antibiotics reserved for hospital settings in outpatients: a prospective clinical audit in a university hospital in Southern France.
audits.st: Guidelines for hospital-reserved antibiotics
audits.f: Only 40% of prescriptions were appropriate; 22 of 32 inappropriate were not recommended.

audits.t: Suboptimal bone protection in geriatric inpatients and effect of a simple educational and mnemonic strategy.
audits.tp: Bone health assessment in older inpatients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Vitamin D measured in 57.4%.
audits.c: Education and a bone health mnemonic introduced into discharge summaries.
audits.r2: Vitamin D measured in 86.6% (P value truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Care of elderly patients: a prospective audit of the prevalence of hypotension and the use of BIS intraoperatively in 25 hospitals in London.
audits.st: National guidelines on intraoperative blood pressure (AAGBI standard) and depth of anaesthesia monitoring
audits.f: Hypotension by AAGBI standard in 400 patients (83.3%).

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Project to Assess Timing of Initial Investigations in Stroke Medicine.
audits.st: National guideline CT head within 12 hours; trust guideline CT head within four hours and a specified stroke blood panel

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Road map for improvement: Point prevalence audit and survey of central venous access devices in paediatric acute care.

audits.f: 13.5% of dressings not clean, dry and intact; 26.4% reinforced with non-sterile dressings; 49.4% had no site assessment documented in previous 4 h; 13.4% had no planned use in next 24 h.

audits.t: Improvement in delivery of type 2 diabetes services differs by mode of care: a retrospective longitudinal analysis in the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Primary Health Care setting.
audits.tp: Type 2 diabetes care in primary care
audits.st: 15 service items recommended in clinical guidelines for type 2 diabetes
audits.f: Clients received on average 43 to 60% of recommended care.
audits.c: Wide-scale continuous quality improvement programme with repeated clinical audits.
audits.r2: Generalist physical checks improved year on year, laboratory tests only in later years, and education/counselling improved early then plateaued; CQI participation increased odds of top-quartile delivery for all modes.

audits.t: Prostate intensity-modulated radiotherapy planning in seven mouse clicks: Development of a class solution for cancer.
audits.st: Departmental protocol criteria for target and organ-at-risk doses
audits.f: Stage 2 template refinement and clinical audit in 20 patients (results not stated).
audits.c: Stepwise refinement and review of a Monaco treatment planning template.
audits.r2: Stage 4 template met clinical criteria in 82% of patients; minor changes in 13%, major changes in 4%, one not assessable; mean calculation time 13 minutes with seven mouse clicks.

audits.t: Exploring the third delay: an audit evaluating obstetric triage at Mulago National Referral Hospital.
audits.st: Traffic Light System for obstetric triage
audits.f: Informal triage occurred 46% of the time at the first checkpoint, but the Traffic Light System was not being used and many vital signs were not recorded.

audits.t: Full Implementation of Screening for Nutritional Risk and Dysphagia in an Acute Stroke Unit: A Clinical Audit.
audits.tp: Swallow screening within 4 hours of stroke
audits.st: National guideline for nutritional risk and dysphagia screening in acute stroke (introduced 1 June 2012)
audits.f: Nutritional risk screening performed in 65% and swallow testing in 91% of eligible patients.
audits.c: Clinical microsystems approach with rapid improvement cycles and audits over 6 months.

audits.t: Influence of Continuing Medical Education on Rheumatologists' Performance on National Quality Measures for Rheumatoid Arthritis.
audits.st: Six PQRS national quality measures for rheumatoid arthritis
audits.f: Baseline chart performance on PQRS measures (figures not given).
audits.c: QI education with private audit feedback, small-group webinars and online print and video activities.
audits.r2: Four of six PQRS measures significantly higher (absolute increases 9 to 24%); counselling and adherence assessment increased 9 to 40%.

audits.t: Improving the Quality of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgical Notes in an Indian Public Sector Hospital in Accordance with the Royal College of Surgeons Guidelines: A Completed Audit Loop Study.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidelines on operation notes, plus OMFS-specific criteria
audits.f: Mean data point inclusion 84.6%; 94-100% documentation for 9 essential criteria; assistant name and date of surgery poorly documented; OMFS-specific criteria scored poorly.
audits.c: OMFS-specific consent forms, diagram sheets and a computerised operation note proforma with a prefilled operative findings template.
audits.r2: Mean data point inclusion 98.4% (P 0.001); excellent documentation in almost all essential and additional criteria.

audits.t: Is parenteral chemotherapy safe in rural hospitals? A prospective audit of neutropenic fever in Albany Hospital, a regional West Australian cancer centre.
audits.st: Guidelines: antibiotics within 60 minutes of arrival for neutropenic fever
audits.f: Antibiotics within 60 minutes in 73.68% of cases (14/19); neutropenic fever in 16/192 patients (8.33%) and 1.47% of cycles (19/1294); no deaths.

audits.t: The management of epilepsy in pregnancy at the Whittington Hospital: a retrospective audit 2004-2006 and 2007-2010.
audits.st: Scottish Obstetric Group and Audit Project recommendations
audits.f: Obstetric medicine clinic: 14% documented preconception counselling, 58% on anti-epileptic drugs; antenatal clinic: 0% preconception counselling, 34% on anti-epileptic drugs.
audits.r2: Obstetric medicine clinic: 37.5% preconception counselling, 84% on anti-epileptic drugs; antenatal clinic: 4.2% preconception counselling, 31% on anti-epileptic drugs.

audits.t: [Real-time safety audits in a neonatal unit].
audits.st: All written resuscitation information and material (endotracheal tube information, mask and bag, laryngoscopes) correctly available
audits.f: Appropriate overall use in 62.50% (185/296) of audits; mask and bag prepared in 97.3%.

audits.t: Hospital-wide implementation of an electronic-workflow solution aiming to make surgical practice improvement easy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 5785 of 7179 (80%) general surgical operations had an operation note created in the new system; theatre-booking compliance approached 90% (44,953 bookings); synoptic reporting uptake for laparoscopic cholecystectomy 81%.
audits.c: Hospital-wide integrated electronic workflow system introduced in 2013 managing the perioperative journey and facilitating audit.

audits.t: [Dental and oral surgical treatment of medication-induced bleeding patients: Audit of the national guideline in Hungary].
audits.st: 2015 Hungarian national guideline on dental treatment of anticoagulated patients
audits.f: Six patients (2.3%) had minor postoperative bleeding after the one-hour check and one (0.5%) needed night duty support.

audits.t: Is Ovarian Cancer Being Managed According to Clinical Guidelines? Evidence From a Population-Based Clinical Audit.
audits.st: Clinical guidelines for ovarian cancer surgery and chemotherapy
audits.f: 215 (62.5%) had care with curative intent; surgery adherent to guidelines in 35.2% and chemotherapy in 87.8%.

audits.t: Predictors of Cardiac Rehabilitation Utilization in England: Results From the National Audit.
audits.st: English NHS targets for cardiac rehabilitation enrolment (target not stated)
audits.f: Of 234,736 (81.5%) referred, 141,648 enrolled and 97,406 initiated CR; 37.2% of initiators completed a programme of 8 weeks or more.

audits.t: A prospective audit of complications in 100 consecutive pediatric percutaneous renal biopsies done under real-time ultrasound guidance.
audits.st: British Association of Paediatric Nephrologists standards for paediatric percutaneous renal biopsy
audits.f: BAPN standards achieved; gross haematuria in 6 cases; major complication in 1.

audits.t: Gynaecological cancer pathway for faster cancer treatment: a repeat clinical audit.
audits.st: Ministry of Health Faster Cancer Treatment targets (31 days from decision, 62 days from referral)
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: 89.2% treated within 31 days of decision and 66.9% within 62 days of referral.

audits.t: Initial Results from the Royal College of Radiologists' UK National Audit of Anal Cancer Radiotherapy 2015.
audits.st: UK guidance for intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) in anal cancer
audits.f: 231 (95%) had full dose radiotherapy with prophylactic nodal irradiation; 180 (78%) received IMRT and 52 (22%) two-phase conformal; interruptions 4% with IMRT vs 7% conformal.

audits.t: Orthodontic referrals: why do GDPs get it wrong?
audits.st: Orthodontic referral standards (IOTN-based referral guidelines)
audits.f: 37.2% of patients met the standards.
audits.c: Referral guidelines and pathway sent back to referring practitioners.

audits.t: Auditing an Online Self-reported Interventional Radiology Adverse Event Database for Compliance and Accuracy.
audits.st: Complete record entry and accurate adverse event reporting and grading in the IR quality assurance database
audits.f: Compliance with record entry and AE reporting measured; figures not reported.
audits.c: Physicians informed of the audit process, with reminders.
audits.r2: Compliance with record entry improved, but reminders were needed for 100%; AE self-reporting and grading accuracy did not improve significantly.

audits.t: Clinical practice audit concerning antimicrobial prophylaxis in paediatric neurosurgery: results from a German paediatric oncology unit.
audits.st: Internal perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis guideline (January 2014)
audits.f: Cefotaxime used instead of cefuroxime in 23%; prophylaxis over 3 doses (>24 h) in 66%.
audits.r2: Cefotaxime in 18%; prophylaxis over 24 h in 60% (p = n.s.).

audits.t: Criteria-based audit to improve quality of care of foetal distress: standardising obstetric care at a national referral hospital in a low resource setting, Tanzania.
audits.st: Criteria for diagnosis and management of foetal distress based on international and national guidelines
audits.f: Standard diagnosis 52%.
audits.c: Recommendations for improving care implemented with feedback.

audits.t: Audit of Helicobacter pylori Testing in Microbiology Laboratories in England: To Inform Compliance with NICE Guidance and the Feasibility of Routine Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance.
audits.st: NICE guidance: test dyspeptic patients for H. pylori by urea breath test, stool antigen or serology
audits.f: 121/170 (71%) responded; 96% provided H. pylori testing and 94% used stool antigen; only five laboratories did not comply with NICE guidance.

audits.t: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis risk assessment in a general surgery cohort: a closed-loop audit.
audits.st: NICE and SIGN VTE prophylaxis guidelines; kardex-based risk assessment tool
audits.f: Risk assessment tool completed in 2.7%; AES correctly prescribed in 75% and LMWH in 97%.
audits.c: Audit results and risk assessment tool information presented at two departmental teaching sessions.
audits.r2: 66% had a risk assessment performed (statistically significant improvement).

audits.t: An Audit of the Effectiveness of Large Group Neurology Tutorials for Irish Undergraduate Medical Students.
audits.st: Association of British Neurologists undergraduate education guidelines
audits.f: No students rated confidence 9 or 10/10 in history taking, examination or differential diagnosis.
audits.c: Series of interactive large group tutorials.
audits.r2: Confidence 9–10/10: history taking 6%, examination 12%, differential diagnosis 25%.

audits.t: Improving the use and timeliness of anticoagulation reversal for warfarin related intracranial haemorrhage.
audits.tp: Warfarin reversal with prothrombin complex concentrate
audits.st: Anticoagulation reversal protocol including prothrombin complex concentrate
audits.f: PCC used in 15% of eligible patients.
audits.c: Introduction and later revisions of an anticoagulation reversal protocol.
audits.r2: PCC used in 100% of eligible patients.

audits.t: Pain assessment and management in paediatric oncology: a cross-sectional audit.
audits.st: International recommendations for paediatric pain management
audits.f: Pain present in 146/258 (57%); pain recorded by health professionals in 75/146 (51%); non-drug methods in 38/146 (26%); pain appropriately managed in 65/76 (87%) by the Pain Management Index.

audits.t: An audit of coagulation screening in patients presenting to the emergency department for potential stroke thrombolysis.
audits.tp: Admission blood tests in acute stroke
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: No coagulation sample sent in 11 of 99 (11%) episodes; sample unsuitable in 16 (18%); median time to laboratory report 61 (53-77) min in hours and 64 (50-90) min out of hours.

audits.t: What are the critical steps in processing blood cultures? A prospective audit evaluating current practice of reporting blood cultures in a centralised laboratory serving secondary care hospitals.
audits.st: National standards for processing positive blood cultures
audits.f: 211 flagged positive; 69 (3.1%) contaminated; 50% of positive cultures had Gram stain reported within 2 hours; 30-day mortality 10.9% (23/211).

audits.t: Adequacy of physician documentation and correlation with assessment of transfusion appropriateness: a follow-up study in the setting of prospective audits and patient blood management.
audits.st: Hospital transfusion guidelines
audits.f: Suboptimal documentation in 46.8% of reviewed transfusion events; 81.8% of these could not be justified, versus 18.0% of adequately documented events.

audits.t: Clinical auditing as an instrument for quality improvement in breast cancer care in the Netherlands: The national NABON Breast Cancer Audit.
audits.st: 32 national breast cancer quality indicators
audits.f: Pre- and post-operative MDT discussion in 83% and 91%.
audits.c: Nationwide clinical audit with hospital benchmarking.
audits.r2: Pre- and post-operative MDT discussion in 98% and 99%.

audits.t: The challenges of implementing a multi-centre audit of end-of-life care in care homes.
audits.st: Family Perception of Care Scale (validated questionnaire of bereaved relatives)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Management of Older Inpatients Who Refuse Nonpsychiatric Medication Within Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust: Audit.
audits.st: National guidelines: duty doctor consultation when a competent patient refuses medication
audits.f: Discussion with the duty doctor occurred in 75% of cases (27/36).

audits.t: Improving Standards of Care in Obstructed Labour: A Criteria-Based Audit at a Referral Hospital in a Low-Resource Setting in Tanzania.
audits.st: Criteria for diagnosis and management of obstructed labour
audits.f: Diagnosis to standard 74%; management to standard 4.2%.
