audits.t: Rheumatologists fail to advise people with RA to get immunised, which matters if you are under 65: An audit in a New Zealand rheumatology service.
audits.tp: Vaccination uptake in immunosuppressed rheumatology patients
audits.st: Guidelines for yearly influenza and five-yearly pneumococcal vaccination in rheumatoid arthritis
audits.f: Documented immunisation advice was infrequent; exact figures not reported in the abstract.

audits.t: A re-audit of the technical quality of undergraduate root canal treatment after the introduction of new technology and teaching practices.

audits.f: Acceptable fillings in 48% of single-rooted and 38% of multirooted canals; 18.8% of multirooted teeth acceptable as a unit.
audits.c: Educational changes and mandatory new technologies (nickel-titanium files, apex locators, greater taper gutta-percha).
audits.r2: Acceptable in 23/40 (57.5%) single-rooted and 68/129 (52.7%) multirooted canals; 45.2% of multirooted teeth acceptable (P = 0.042).

audits.t: Clinical audit and national survey on the assessment of collateral circulation before radial forearm free flap harvest.
audits.tp: Collateral circulation assessment before radial forearm free flap
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Routine MAT and DUS: 6 abnormal DUS, 1 abnormal MAT; no ischaemic complications.
audits.c: Duplex ultrasound no longer requested; Modified Allen's Test alone.
audits.r2: 2 abnormal MAT had contralateral flap; no ischaemic complications.

audits.t: Quality of prescribing of antipsychotic medication for people with intellectual disability under the care of UK mental health services: a cross-sectional audit of clinical practice.
audits.st: Practice standards derived from evidence-based guidelines including NICE (indications and annual side-effect screening)
audits.f: 64% prescribed antipsychotics; annual screening documented for body weight 41%, blood pressure 32%, and blood glucose and lipids 37%.

audits.t: Methodological issues associated with an audit of stillbirth in a family medicine practice in Israel.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Methodological description of a deficient-outcome audit of five stillbirths.

audits.t: The accuracy of interpretation of emergency abdominal CT in adult patients who present with non-traumatic abdominal pain: results of a UK national audit.

audits.f: 109/188 (58%) departments supplied data on 4,931 patients; the standard for provisional report major discrepancy was achieved for registrars (remaining figures truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Improving multidisciplinary severe sepsis management using the Sepsis Six .
audits.tp: Sepsis recognition and treatment on wards
audits.st: Sepsis Six protocol and national severe sepsis guidelines
audits.f: 1% appropriately managed; 19% admitted to ITU (6% died); length of stay 10 days.
audits.c: Active promotion of teamwork to initiate the protocol; trust-wide updated protocols.
audits.r2: 67% adhered to the protocol (p<0.0001); 7% admitted to ITU (no deaths); length of stay 7 days (p<0.0001).

audits.t: Convex stoma appliances: an audit of stoma care nurses.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Results not reported in the abstract.

audits.t: Clinical audit and effective change in leg ulcer services.
audits.st: Adaptation of the Riverside model (Doppler ABPI assessment and four-layer high compression)
audits.f: Average consumable cost per patient £8.53.
audits.c: Research-based implementation: community clinics, Doppler assessment, compression by ABPI and staff training.
audits.r2: Average consumable cost £10.14; 111 patients (134 limbs) in high compression had 54% healing at 12 weeks and 68% at 24 weeks.

audits.t: Necropsies in clinical audit.
audits.st: CEPOD experience range; Royal College of Pathologists recommended pathologist staffing levels
audits.f: Overall necropsy rate 180/600 (30%); perioperative deaths 26/74 (35%), other surgical 16/72 (22%), medical 89/386 (23%); Northern Ireland overall 11.7%, and 8.2% outside Belfast teaching hospitals.

audits.t: Quality of acute asthma care in two tertiary hospitals in a state in South Western Nigeria: A report of clinical audit.
audits.st: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) guideline
audits.f: Low compliance with most guideline recommendations (figures not given in text supplied).

audits.t: Over-imaging in uncomplicated low back pain: a 12-month audit of a general medical unit.
audits.st: Appropriate indications for imaging in uncomplicated low back pain
audits.f: Imaging ordered unnecessarily in 40% of patients with no indication.

audits.f: FiO2 1.0 and hyperoxia common; delays to cardiac catheterisation; frequent hyperglycaemia; therapeutic hypothermia not given in almost 50% of patients.

audits.t: The evaluation of the audit of Fresh-Frozen Plasma (FFP) usage in emergency department.
audits.st: British Committee for Standards in Haematology guideline 2004
audits.f: 59.6% of FFP use improper; 40.2% improper in bleeding patients, 90.7% in those without active bleeding or given prophylactically.

audits.t: From guidelines to practice: a pharmacist-driven prospective audit and feedback improvement model for peri-operative antibiotic prophylaxis in 34 South African hospitals.
audits.st: Peri-operative antibiotic prophylaxis guideline: antibiotic choice, dose, timing and duration
audits.f: Composite compliance with all four process measures 66.8% (95% CI 64.8-68.7).
audits.c: Pharmacist-driven prospective audit and feedback with a PAP guideline and toolkit, change management and monthly feedback over 70 weeks.

audits.t: Assessment of bone health in breast cancer patients starting adjuvant aromatase inhibitors: A quality improvement clinical audit.
audits.tp: Baseline DEXA scanning in breast cancer
audits.st: Baseline DEXA scan requested within 3 months of starting adjuvant aromatase inhibitors; target 90% or more
audits.f: Baseline DEXA in 188 (51.2%).
audits.c: Four educational and awareness sessions over two weeks.

audits.t: Solitary thyroid nodule: audit shows improved care requires cytological diagnosis.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 118 (46%) had a solitary nodule removed; only 12.7% were carcinomas; FNAC diagnostic accuracy 82.6% and sensitivity for carcinoma 87.5%.

audits.t: British Association of Dermatologists' national audit on nonmelanoma skin cancer excision, 2014.
audits.st: Complete excision as the required surgical standard for nonmelanoma skin cancer
audits.f: Lateral and deep margins clear in 98.3% and 99.2% of BCCs and 98.4% and 97.1% of SCCs; clinical diagnosis confirmed in 94.4% of suspected BCCs and 66.8% of suspected SCCs; complication rate 3.4%.

audits.t: Impact of a peri-operative quality improvement programme on postoperative pulmonary complications.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Postoperative pulmonary complication rate 16/83 (19.3%).
audits.c: ERAS+ peri-operative care model combining enhanced recovery with measures to reduce pulmonary complications, introduced June 2014 and fully implemented September 2014.
audits.r2: Pulmonary complication rate 16/183 (8.7%); median length of stay improved from 12 to 9 days.

audits.t: Impact of personalized report cards on nurses managing central lines.
audits.st: Established guidelines for central line management (visual and documentation audits)
audits.f: 113 lines (19.2%) failed the visual audit; 628 CLABSI contributing factors identified.

audits.r2: Frequency of CLABSI contributing factors decreased over time (ρ = -0.12, P = .003).

audits.t: Optimizing postoperative handover to the intensive care unit at a tertiary centre.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Need for improvement across all domains.

audits.r2: Overall improvement from baseline but decreased performance in just under half of domains compared with PDSA cycle 1.

audits.t: The impact of evidence-based sepsis guidelines on emergency department clinical practice: a pre-post medical record audit.
audits.tp: Sepsis six in the emergency department
audits.st: New South Wales sepsis guidelines
audits.f: Baseline time to antibiotics not reported.
audits.c: Implementation of state sepsis guidelines in the emergency department.
audits.r2: Time to antibiotics reduced by 230 minutes; 81 (49.1%) received more urgent triage; lactate collected in 112 (67.9%); time to second litre of fluid reduced by 758 minutes.

audits.t: Addressing Opioid-Associated Constipation Using Quality Oncology Practice Initiative Scores and Plan-Do-Study-Act Cycles.
audits.tp: Opioid co-prescribing of laxatives, antiemetics and naloxone
audits.st: ASCO Quality Oncology Practice Initiative measure for assessing opioid-associated constipation
audits.f: Constipation assessed in 52%.
audits.c: Mandatory check boxes in EMR templates prompting assessment of constipation in patients on opioids, with monthly PDSA meetings.

audits.t: Assessment of quality of care among in-patients with postpartum haemorrhage and severe pre-eclampsia at st. Francis hospital nsambya: a criteria-based audit.
audits.st: Criteria-based standards of care for PPH (4 standards) and severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia (10 standards)
audits.f: Adherence rates to standards assessed (numbers not stated in abstract)
audits.c: Feedback, continuing medical education, drills and display of guidelines
audits.r2: 7 of 10 pre-eclampsia/eclampsia standards and 3 of 4 PPH standards significantly higher

audits.t: Improving capacity and consent to treatment recording in psychiatric inpatient wards: A multi-centre quality improvement project.

audits.c: Teaching sessions on mental capacity, then an admission clerking proforma with a capacity prompt
audits.r2: Sustained improvement of 26% from baseline across all measures

audits.t: An audit of referral and treatment patterns of high-risk prostate cancer patients in Alberta.
audits.st: Provincial clinical practice guidelines for high-risk prostate cancer (created 2005)
audits.f: Referral and treatment rates not given in the abstract.
audits.r2: Radiation oncologist referral and ADT plus radiotherapy use declined and radical prostatectomy increased.

audits.t: Patient dosimetry audit for establishing local diagnostic reference levels for nuclear medicine CT.
audits.tp: Diagnostic reference levels for radiation dose
audits.st: Proposed National Diagnostic Reference Levels for nuclear medicine CT
audits.f: For most examinations mean dose-length products did not exceed proposed national reference levels; bone SPECT/CT lumbar spine DLPs ranged from 51 ± 5 mGy cm (low dose) to 1086 ± 124 mGy cm (metal dose).

audits.t: Data-driven management using quantitative metric and automatic auditing program (QMAP) improves consistency of radiation oncology processes.

audits.f: Late treatment plan completion 18.2%; late weekly physics check 8.9%.

audits.r2: Late plan completion 4.2%; late weekly physics check 0.1%.

audits.t: Impact of Pharmacists' audit on improving the quality of prescription of dabigatran etexilate methanesulfonate: a retrospective study.
audits.tp: DOAC renal function monitoring and dosing
audits.st: Approved prescribing information for dabigatran (contraindications and dose reduction)
audits.f: 33% of ambulant patient prescriptions and 11% of inpatient prescriptions had at least one violation.

audits.t: A national dosimetry audit for stereotactic ablative radiotherapy in lung.
audits.st: Planned and delivered dose agreement within ±3.0%
audits.f: Mean measured versus calculated dose difference 0.4±1.4% (alanine) and 1.4±3.4% (film) excluding pencil-beam; 25/27 SABR plans within ±3.0%.

audits.t: Improving the antenatal and post-partum management of women presenting to Sexual Health Services with positive syphilis serology through audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Large proportion of referred women never attended; recorded partner notification was poor.

audits.t: Improving visual assessment documentation in patients with periorbital trauma through an eye assessment teaching session and a proforma sticker.

audits.st: Present HIQA guidelines for tonsillectomy

audits.t: Development and evaluation of a centralised computerised registry for ureteric stents: completing the audit cycle.

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Audit of anticholinergic medication changes in older hospitalised patients using the Anticholinergic Drug Scale.
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Reducing Unnecessary Postoperative Complete Blood Count Testing in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Good to Great: Quality-Improvement Initiative Increases and Sustains Pediatric Health Care Worker Hand Hygiene Compliance.

audits.r2: Compliance ≥95%, sustained for more than 2 years.

audits.t: Provision of an emergency theatre in tertiary hospitals is cost-effective: Audit and cost of cancelled planned elective general surgical operations at Pietersburg Hospital, Limpopo Province, South Africa.
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Improving the quality of endodontic record keeping through clinical audit.

audits.t: Protocol Adherence for Severe Sepsis and Septic Shock Management in the Emergency Department; a Clinical Audit.

audits.t: Doing Pre-operative Investigations in Emergency Department; a Clinical Audit.

audits.t: Comparing electronic recording with a diagrammatic template versus traditional handwritten recording of tympanomastoid procedures: third audit cycle of 95 cases.

audits.t: Using the Nippita classification system for women undergoing induction of labour in a large metropolitan maternity service: Bringing simplicity and certainty to an important quality improvement process.

audits.f: Overall induction rate 24.7% (New South Wales comparison 25.4%).

audits.t: Management of thyroid eye disease in the United Kingdom: A multi-centre thyroid eye disease audit.
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: An Audit of Second-Trimester Fetal Anomaly Scans Based on a Novel Image-Scoring Method in the Southwest Region of the Netherlands.

audits.t: Can trainees design and deliver a national audit of epistaxis management? A pilot of a secure web-based audit tool and research trainee collaboratives.

audits.t: Reducing socioeconomic inequalities in COPD care in the hospital outpatient setting - A nationwide initiative.

audits.t: The assessment of headaches on the acute medical unit: is it adequate and how could it be improved? .
audits.st: Appropriate management as judged by a consultant neurologist
audits.f: 14/27 (51.9%) appropriately managed.

audits.t: Results of a Regional Effort to Improve Warfarin Management.

audits.t: A decade of improvement in the management of New Zealand ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients: results from the New Zealand Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) Audit Group national audits of 2002, 2007 and 2012.

audits.t: Antimicrobial prophylaxis outside the operating theatre, an audit in a university hospital.

audits.tp: Antenatal care access for women with social complexity
audits.st: NICE guidelines, local trust policy and national statistics (booking by 12 weeks; recommended number of antenatal appointments)
audits.f: Over 70% of non-English speaking women not booked by 12 weeks; on average 89% of primiparous women had fewer than the recommended antenatal appointments; no sample met the appointment criteria.

audits.t: [Mobile emergency care medical records audit: the need for Tunisian guidelines].
audits.st: 56 criteria based on SMUR guidelines and the 2013 French Society of Emergency Medicine evaluation guide
audits.f: Overall non-conformance score 24%; highest non-conformance 48.5% in the specificities of the emergency medical record section, lowest 23.4% in surveillance data.

audits.t: An Interprofessional Quality Improvement Initiative to Standardize Pediatric Extubation Readiness Assessment.
audits.st: Respiratory therapist-led daily spontaneous breathing trial screening protocol
audits.f: Extubation failure 7.8% before the protocol.
audits.c: Respiratory therapist-led daily spontaneous breathing trial protocol, standardised EMR documentation, education and daily audits.
audits.r2: Daily screening occurred in 92% of patients; extubation failure 4.5%.

audits.t: Benchmarked performance charts using principal components analysis to improve the effectiveness of feedback for audit data in HIV care.
audits.st: BHIVA 2011 guidelines for routine investigation and monitoring of adults with HIV-1
audits.f: HIV treatment monitoring was high across sites; hepatitis testing, cardiovascular and smoking risk assessment, flu vaccination, sexual health screening and cervical cytology varied widely.

audits.t: Quality of care in gout: a clinical audit on treating to the target with urate lowering therapy in real-world gout patients.
audits.st: EULAR serum urate targets (<360 and <300 micromol/L)
audits.f: 146 (82.5%) had serum urate <360 micromol/L; 104 (58.8%) <300 micromol/L.

audits.t: Patient-driven hand hygiene audit process at a regional cancer center.
audits.st: Hand hygiene compliance (patient-driven audit)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Nationwide prospective audit of pancreatic surgery: design, accuracy, and outcomes of the Dutch Pancreatic Cancer Audit.
audits.st: Sixteen performance indicators and 20 case-mix factors
audits.f: Overall in-hospital mortality 3.6%; after pancreatoduodenectomy (n=1345) mortality 4.1%, Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher morbidity 29.9%, median length of stay 12 (IQR 9-18) days, readmission 16.0%.

audits.t: Duodenal biopsies for the diagnosis of coeliac disease: are we adhering to current guidance?
audits.tp: Duodenal biopsies for suspected coeliac disease
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology: at least four duodenal biopsy specimens when coeliac disease suspected
audits.f: 21.9% had at least 4 biopsy specimens
audits.c: Measures to raise awareness among endoscopy users

audits.t: WHO Safer Surgery checklist compliance amongst paediatric emergency plastic surgery patients in an UK hospital.
audits.st: WHO Safer Surgery checklist completion
audits.f: Overall compliance 88%; sign-in 85%, time-out 92%, sign-out 86%
audits.c: Raised awareness at an audit meeting

audits.t: Benchmarking quality for renal cancer surgery: Canadian Kidney Cancer information system (CKCis) perspective.
audits.st: Kidney Cancer Research Network of Canada quality indicators (laparoscopic approach, partial nephrectomy, partial nephrectomy in CKD, positive margins, complications, warm ischaemia time)
audits.f: National averages 74% laparoscopic approach, 73% partial nephrectomy and 70% partial nephrectomy in CKD; 3 (23%), 2 (15%) and 2 (15%) hospitals performed below expected.

audits.t: Reducing inappropriate non-steroidal anti-inflammatory prescription in primary care patients with chronic kidney disease.
audits.tp: NSAID prescribing in chronic kidney disease
audits.st: Nephrology consensus: avoid NSAIDs in CKD
audits.f: 10.2% of at-risk patients had received an NSAID prescription in the preceding three months; 6.2% had NSAIDs on repeat prescription.
audits.c: Automated alert on at-risk patient records when NSAIDs prescribed, plus discussion of the rationale with practice staff.
audits.r2: 75% reduction in total NSAIDs prescribed and 90% reduction in repeat NSAID prescriptions in those with CKD.

audits.t: What follows diagnosis by computed tomography of solitary brain tumour? Audit of one year's experience in South East Scotland.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Histological confirmation sought in only 67 of 142; CT diagnosis of glioma wrong in 3 of 44 and of solitary metastasis in 4 of 8.

audits.t: Implementing an Inpatient Pediatric Prospective Audit and Feedback Antimicrobial Stewardship Program Within a Larger Medical Center.
audits.st: Institutional evidence-based ASP guidelines for common inpatient paediatric infections
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Formal paediatric antimicrobial stewardship programme with prospective audit and feedback, guidelines and meetings with staff (January 2013).
audits.r2: Guidelines applicable to 44% of antimicrobial orders; interventions on 30% of orders, 89% accepted; days of therapy and length of therapy fell significantly.

audits.t: Using Practice Facilitation to Increase Rates of Colorectal Cancer Screening in Community Health Centers, North Carolina, 2012-2013: Feasibility, Facilitators, and Barriers.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 15% of eligible patients had a documented colorectal cancer screening recommendation.
audits.c: 12 months of practice facilitation to implement office systems

audits.t: Improving patient blood management in obstetrics: snapshots of a practice improvement partnership.
audits.st: Australian Patient Blood Management Module 5 Obstetrics guidelines
audits.f: 22% of women with postpartum haemorrhage were transfused, a third of whom were anaemic on admission; anaemia on admission intrapartum 12.2%.
audits.c: Education for maternity staff, standardised algorithms, oral iron prescription handout and unselective ferritin screening
audits.r2: Anaemia on admission intrapartum 3.6%; single unit transfusions rose from 35.4% to 50% (p=0.037).

audits.t: Sustained participation in annual continuous quality improvement activities improves quality of care for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children.
audits.st: Audit and Best Practice for Chronic Disease programme care items for children under 2 years
audits.f: Recall recorded in 84%; hearing assessment in 52%.
audits.c: Participation in annual continuous quality improvement audit cycles.
audits.r2: Recall recorded in 95% (OR 2.44); hearing assessment in 89% (OR 1.37).

audits.t: Proposed biopsy performance benchmarks for MRI based on an audit of a large academic center.
audits.st: BI-RADS 5 Atlas MRI screening benchmarks and ACR desirable goals for diagnostic mammography
audits.f: PPVs met for screening and diagnostic MRIs against BI-RADS 5 MRI screening benchmarks, except PPV2 for screening MRIs (1563 screening, 892 diagnostic).

audits.t: The Perth Emergency Laparotomy Audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Data recorded for 198 (76.2%) of 260; 30-day mortality 6.5% (17/260). In 48 patients with documented risk of 10% or more, consultant surgeon and anaesthetist present in 68.8%, 62.8% admitted to critical care and 45.8% started surgery within 2 h.

audits.t: Inflammatory bowel disease in the UK: is quality of care improving?
audits.st: National IBD service standards (mortality, medical and surgical treatment, specialist nursing and dietetic care)
audits.f: 2005/6: UC mortality 1.7%, CD mortality 1.3%; review by IBD specialist nurse 23.7% in UC and 18.1% in CD (1953 UC and 2074 CD patients).
audits.c: Wide dissemination of results, selected site visits, development of national service standards and an online document repository.
audits.r2: 2010/11: UC mortality 0.8% (p=0.034), CD mortality 0.8% (p=0.226); IBD specialist nurse review 44.9% in UC and 39.9% in CD (1948 UC and 1900 CD patients).

audits.t: Quality Improvement Initiatives to Optimize the Management of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease in Patients With Lung Cancer.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: DMAIC cycles: cycle 1 engaged stakeholders and prioritised COPD management by respirologists; cycle 2 restructured physicians and introduced a standard work protocol.
audits.r2: No change in PFT completion over time; abstract reports significantly improved COPD management, figures truncated.

audits.t: RCR audit of compliance with UK guidelines for the prevention and detection of acute kidney injury in adult patients undergoing iodinated contrast media injections for CT.
audits.st: Current UK guidelines for prevention, recognition and management of contrast-induced AKI
audits.f: Compliance with guidelines was poor with wide variation; clinically significant post-contrast AKI 0/3590 outpatients and 14/3569 (0.4%) inpatients; overall AKI incidence 0.9%.

audits.t: Quality indicators of psychotropic prescribing to people with dementia in aged psychiatry inpatient units.
audits.st: Indicators derived from three Australian health care quality and safety standards or guidelines
audits.f: Most problematic areas were psychotropic history taking on admission and discharge handover of new treatments and reasons for stopping medications, including adverse reactions.

audits.t: Acute oxygen therapy: an audit of prescribing and delivery practices in a tertiary hospital in Perth, Western Australia.
audits.st: Oxygen prescription guidelines with appropriate medically indicated target saturations
audits.f: 36 of 65 (55.4%) had target oxygen saturations prescribed and 25% of prescribed targets were inappropriate; 49 (75.4%) exposed to potential risk from prescription and/or delivery error.

audits.t: Implementation of the World Health Organization Regional Office for Africa Stepwise Laboratory Quality Improvement Process Towards Accreditation.
audits.st: WHO AFRO SLIPTA checklist (1-5 stars)
audits.f: Mean score 69%; 70% achieved at least 2 stars (55% compliance) and 1% achieved 5 stars.

audits.t: Prescription audit of NSAIDs and gastroprotective strategy in elderly in primary care.
audits.st: Guideline recommendations for NSAID choice and gastroprotective agents
audits.f: 45.9% on low-dose aspirin and 13.5% on other NSAIDs; gastroprotective agent prescription rate 29.2% for aspirin and 33.3% for other NSAIDs.

audits.t: An Internal Audit of Diabetes Care for Type 2 Diabetic Patients in a Public Hospital Diabetes Clinic in Malaysia.
audits.st: Diabetes care guidelines
audits.f: Fasting glucose, BP, BMI and lipids recorded in 99.1%, 99.6%, 92.6% and 99.6%; HbA1c in previous six months 79.7%; annual foot screening 25.8%, eye screening 71.2%, albuminuria screening 93.6%.

audits.t: Routine monitoring and assessment of adults living with HIV: results of the British HIV Association (BHIVA) national audit 2015.
audits.st: BHIVA guidelines for routine investigation and monitoring of adults with HIV-1 (22 audited outcomes)
audits.f: Only 44.9% on ART had a documented 10-year CVD risk in the past three years and 16.7% over 50 had fracture risk assessed; sexual health screening provided in 96.4% of services.

audits.t: Benchmarking against the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit recommendations.
audits.st: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) recommendations and outcomes (11.1% 30-day mortality)
audits.f: Total 30-day mortality 9.7% vs 11.1% reported by NELA.

audits.t: Psychotropic drug utilization and audit in two Italian psychiatric services.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Almost all patients received one or more psychotropic drugs, with substantial polypharmacy; women were prescribed more than men.
audits.c: Medical staff made aware that their prescribing was being monitored.
audits.r2: Awareness of monitoring had little effect on prescribing patterns.

audits.t: Cutaneous melanoma: an audit of management timeliness against New Zealand guidelines.
audits.st: New Zealand melanoma care guideline timeliness standards (Faster Cancer Treatment programme)
audits.f: Suspicious lesions: referral to first treatment (Standard 2.1) 0%, referral to biopsy 17.6%, biopsy report to first treatment 21.7%, referral to first treatment 9.3%, biopsy to first treatment 21.7% compliance. Biopsy-confirmed melanoma: referral to first treatment 42.2%, biopsy to first treatment 42.9%.

audits.t: Variation in use of neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with stage III breast cancer: Results of the Dutch national breast cancer audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1230 of 1556 (79%) received neoadjuvant chemotherapy; variation between hospitals 0-100%.

audits.t: An audit comparing the reporting of staging MRI scans for rectal cancer with the London Cancer Alliance (LCA) guidelines.
audits.tp: Rectal cancer MRI staging report quality
audits.st: London Cancer Alliance MRI reporting guidelines (standardised proforma)
audits.f: Key MRI metric completion 98% in proforma vs 73% in prose reports.
audits.c: Incorporation of standardised proforma-based reporting into LCA guidelines.
audits.r2: Uptake of proforma-based reporting improved and proforma reports captured more items than prose (figures truncated in abstract).

audits.t: A multi-centre audit of excess steroid use in 1176 patients with inflammatory bowel disease.
audits.tp: Steroid use in inflammatory bowel disease
audits.st: Steroid dependency or excess criteria
audits.f: 30% received steroids; 14.9% had steroid dependency or excess, avoidable in 49.1%; annual incidence of inappropriate steroid excess 7.1%.

audits.t: HIV testing in dermatology - a national audit.
audits.st: British HIV Association guidelines on HIV testing in dermatology indicator diseases
audits.f: HIV testing in key indicator diseases remained below the national standard (figures not stated).

audits.t: A National Audit of Smoking Cessation Services in Irish Maternity Units.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: All units recorded smoking at booking and gave verbal advice; 1 validated with CO breath test; 12 (63%) recorded cessation timing and gave written advice; 6 (32%) had all midwives trained; 5 (26%) revisited smoking status later.

audits.t: Audit: Prescribing PRN medication.
audits.st: Local trust medicine policy standards for PRN prescribing, based on good clinical practice
audits.f: 36% of PRN medications were not cancelled despite not being used for >1 month; 23% did not have clear indications for use. Most other standards showed full compliance.

audits.t: Re-Audit of the Contents of GP Referral letters to General Adult Community Psychiatrists.
audits.tp: GP referrals to community mental health teams
audits.st: Checklist of most important referral letter items agreed by GPs and psychiatrists (items scoring 8 or more)
audits.f: Reason for referral in 95%; current physical health 24%; risk concerns 47%; treatment provided by GP 50%.
audits.c: Standardised approach to referral letters devised with involvement of GPs and psychiatrists.
audits.r2: Current physical health 59%; risk concerns 79%; treatment provided by GP 71%.

audits.t: Audit: Monitoring of side effects using GASS (Glasgow Antipsychotic Side-Effect Scale).
audits.st: Hospital policy requiring completion of Glasgow Antipsychotic Side-Effect Scale (GASS) forms
audits.f: Only 31% of patients had completed GASS forms.
audits.c: Remaining patients were supported to complete the forms.
audits.r2: 92% of patients compliant with the policy.

audits.t: A quality improvement approach to cognitive assessment on hospice admission: could we use the 4AT or Short CAM?
audits.st: Cognitive assessment on admission to hospice
audits.f: Cognitive assessment performed in 50% after an initial drop in sustainability.
audits.c: 4AT embedded in the admission process over five PDSA cycles, then staff education and changes to admission documentation plus a delirium checklist.

audits.t: An audit of the management of nicotine withdrawal in an Australian inpatient unit: are we there yet?
audits.st: Smoke-free policy and Smoking Assessment and Management Form (SAMF)
audits.f: SAMF implemented for 76.1%, 64.71% completed within 24 hours; nicotine dependence not properly assessed in 42.3% of smokers; 69.23% prescribed NRT.

audits.t: Regular and frequent feedback of specific clinical criteria delivers a sustained improvement in the management of diabetic ketoacidosis .
audits.st: Five specific targets: fluid prescription, fixed rate intravenous insulin infusion, glucose measurement, ketone measurement and specialist referral
audits.f: Baseline audit; mean average duration of DKA 22.0 hours.
audits.c: Quality improvement using PDSA cycles, with interventions including monthly feedback of specific clinical criteria to emergency medicine, acute medicine and diabetes departments.
audits.r2: Mean average duration of DKA reduced to 10.2 hours.

audits.t: Renal replacement therapy in Scottish critical care units: A national audit of practices.
audits.tp: Renal replacement therapy in critical care
audits.st: Intensity of renal replacement therapy compared with evidence from large randomised trials showing no benefit of high intensity
audits.f: Mean delivered effluent flow for CVVH 29.1 (SD 8.1) ml/kg/h (89% of prescribed); CVVHDF mean delivered dose 41.3 (7.9) ml/kg/h (88.4% of prescribed). Of 8 intermittent haemodialysis patients, 7 had daily treatments.

audits.t: Peri-procedural management of bleeding risks in critical care patients: A local audit and national survey.
audits.st: Transfusion thresholds: prothrombin time 22 s for fresh frozen plasma; platelet count 50 × 10^9/l
audits.f: 8 (12.3%) patients received fresh frozen plasma before drain insertion despite prothrombin time below 22 s; one patient above the threshold received FFP; one received a double-dose platelet transfusion despite platelets above 50 × 10^9/l.

audits.t: Time for change? A national audit on bereavement care in intensive care units.
audits.st: Intensive Care Society 1998 bereavement care recommendations (nine recommendations)
audits.f: 113 responses (78% of Trusts, 63% of ICUs). 96% had an information booklet; training (53%), auditing (19%) and adequate facilities (27%) did not meet the recommended standards.

audits.t: Introduction of the identification, situation, background, assessment, recommendations tool to improve the quality of information transfer during medical handover in intensive care.
audits.st: ISBAR (Identification, Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendations) handover tool
audits.f: Total handover score 263/500.

audits.t: Protective mechanical ventilation in United Kingdom critical care units: A multicentre audit.
audits.st: Low tidal volume ventilation ≤6.5 ml/kg predicted body weight; recommended PEEP levels
audits.f: Mean tidal volume 7.2 (±1.4) ml/kg PBW; compliance with low tidal volume ventilation 34%. Compliance with recommended PEEP 72%.

audits.t: The application of a "6S Lean" initiative to improve workflow for emergency eye examination rooms.
audits.st: 5S audit checklist
audits.f: 5S audit checklist score 44.
audits.c: 6S Lean changes to room setup, supply organisation, inventory control, maintenance and workplace protocols.
audits.r2: 5S audit checklist score 77 (increase of 33 points); all targets achieved.

audits.t: Improving the quality of radiation oncology: 10years' experience of QUATRO audits in the IAEA Europe Region.
audits.st: IAEA QUATRO comprehensive quality audit methodology
audits.f: 759 recommendations and 600 commendations were given across 31 audit reports; 8 centres of competence had complete quality management systems and adequate staffing.

audits.t: An evidence-based medicine audit of the ophthalmic emergency services unit of King Abdulaziz University Hospital (KAUH).
audits.st: Best available evidence (Medline and Cochrane) for interventions
audits.f: 73.2% of 355 interventions were evidence based.
audits.c: Results of the first phase disseminated to ophthalmology staff.

audits.t: The Chronic Care Model to Improve Management of Childhood Obesity.
audits.st: 20 assessment measures from expert guidelines on childhood overweight and obesity
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Chronic care model applied to primary care provider identification, prevention and management of childhood obesity.
audits.r2: Statistically significant improvement in documentation of parental obesity, family history, sleep assessment, endocrine assessment and weight classification as a diagnosis.

audits.t: Patient outcome of emergency laparotomy improved with increasing "number of surgeons on-call" in a university hospital: Audit loop.
audits.st: NELA average mortality 11.1% and median length of stay 16.3 days (comparison benchmark)
audits.f: 30-day mortality 21%; median length of stay 16 days; anastomotic leak rate 16.6%
audits.c: Addition of a second consultant to the daily general surgery on-call rota
audits.r2: 30-day mortality 10.50%; median length of stay 11 days; anastomotic leak rate 4.2%

audits.t: Compliance with the guide for commissioning oral surgery: an audit and discussion.
audits.st: NHS England Guide for commissioning oral surgery: 100% of Level 1 procedures performed by dental undergraduates or discharged to the referring GDP
audits.f: 25% of Level 1 procedures met the gold standard; Level 2 practitioners performed most Level 1 and Level 2 procedures.
audits.c: Results presented at a departmental meeting, recommendations made and an action plan implemented.
audits.r2: 66% of Level 1 procedures met the gold standard.

audits.t: Screening for Oral Cancer in a Mixed General Dental Practice.
audits.st: 100% soft tissue examination and 100% social history recording (alcohol and smoking)
audits.f: 100% had soft tissue examination; 99% had social history recorded.
audits.c: Medical history form changed to include social history; re-audit planned in six months.

audits.t: TodaysBaby Quality Improvement: Safe Sleep Teaching and Role Modeling in 8 US Maternity Units.
audits.st: At least 90% of mothers reporting safe sleep information from nurses and at least 90% of infants observed supine in a safe sleep environment
audits.f: not reported (reported as increases over baseline)
audits.c: Safe sleep QI toolkit with educational curriculum and staff and parent education tools, implemented as PDSA cycles with audits after each cycle.
audits.r2: Mothers reported receiving information on 4 primary safe sleep topics 72% to 95% of the time (24%-57% increase); 93% of infants supine and 88% in a safe sleep environment (24% and 33% increases).

audits.t: A multicentre 'end to end' dosimetry audit of motion management (4DCT-defined motion envelope) in radiotherapy.
audits.st: Gamma analysis at 3%/2 mm against planned dose distributions
audits.f: Mean gamma pass 98.7% (3% 2 mm) with static phantom; 88.2% with moving phantom.

audits.t: An audit of immunofixation requesting practices at a South African referral laboratory.
audits.st: IFE to follow pathologist suggestion after suspicious SPEP
audits.f: 304 IFEs suggested; only 45 (15%) requested by clinicians; 20 (46.5%) of those performed showed a paraprotein.
audits.c: Recommended reflective IFE testing by the laboratory.

audits.t: Creating a sustainable culture of quality through the SLMTA programme in a district hospital laboratory in Kenya.
audits.st: SLIPTA checklist star rating
audits.f: Zero stars (38%).
audits.c: SLMTA workshops, mentorship, audits and integration of quality improvement into daily operations.
audits.r2: Four stars (89%); three stars (81%) at external KENAS audit 12 months later.

audits.t: One laboratory's progress toward accreditation in Tanzania.
audits.st: SLIPTA checklist star rating
audits.f: Zero stars (36%).
audits.c: SLMTA training, improvement projects, supervisory visits and a mentor.

audits.t: From grass to grace: How SLMTA revolutionised the Bamenda Regional Hospital Laboratory in Cameroon.
audits.st: SLIPTA checklist star rating
audits.f: 18%, lowest in the cohort of five laboratories.
audits.c: SLMTA workshops, improvement projects and intensive on-site mentorship.
audits.r2: 81% at official SLIPTA audit, highest in the cohort.

audits.t: Accelerating the spread of laboratory quality improvement efforts in Botswana.
audits.st: SLIPTA checklist score
audits.f: Median baseline score 53%.
audits.c: SLMTA workshops and improvement projects over nine months; four laboratories also had extra training and mentorship from the Botswana Bureau of Standards.

audits.t: Translating a National Laboratory Strategic Plan into action through SLMTA in a district hospital laboratory in Botswana.
audits.st: SLIPTA checklist star rating
audits.f: 53% (zero stars).
audits.c: SLMTA training, improvement projects, site visits and focused mentorship.
audits.r2: 80% (three stars); 85% (four stars) at official audit nearly three years later.

audits.t: Working toward a sustainable laboratory quality improvement programme through country ownership: Mozambique's SLMTA story.
audits.st: SLIPTA checklist score
audits.f: Median score 35%.
audits.c: SLMTA embedded in Ministry of Health structure with national coordinator, workshops, mentorship and site visits.

audits.t: How do primary care doctors in England and Wales code and manage people with chronic kidney disease? Results from the National Chronic Kidney Disease Audit.
audits.tp: Chronic kidney disease coding and management
audits.st: Recommended CKD interventions: blood pressure targets, proteinuria testing, statin prescription, flu and pneumococcal vaccination
audits.f: 30% of patients with biochemical CKD did not have a GP CKD code.

audits.t: Atypia of Undetermined Significance in Thyroid Fine Needle Aspirates: a 4-Year Audit of Thy3a Reporting.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Thy3a used in 1.2% (n = 16) with malignancy rate 7%; overall false-positive rate 1.9% and false-negative rate 0.3%.

audits.t: Deceased donor kidney transplantation in New Zealand: use and audit of a survival prediction tool.
audits.st: Guideline that only patients with projected five-year survival of 80% are listed for deceased donor kidney transplantation
audits.f: 325 of 420 (77%) accepted onto the list; mean estimated five-year survival 89.4% in listed vs 79.8% in not-accepted patients.

audits.t: Reducing unnecessary chest X-rays, antibiotics and bronchodilators through implementation of the NICE bronchiolitis guideline.
audits.st: NICE bronchiolitis guideline
audits.f: Chest X-ray 20%, antibiotics 22%, inhaled/nebulised treatment 30%; overall NICE compliance 28%.
audits.c: Educational sessions for clinicians and nurses on appropriate and inappropriate bronchiolitis management with NICE guideline implementation.
audits.r2: Chest X-ray 4%, antibiotics 6%, inhaled/nebulised treatment 16%; overall NICE compliance 63%.

audits.t: Prescription practice of anti-tuberculosis drugs in Yunnan, China: A clinical audit.
audits.st: Correct regimen and adequate dosing of anti-TB drugs
audits.f: 24.4% prescribed second-line drugs and 15.2% a fluoroquinolone; correct dosing: isoniazid 88.2%, rifampicin 50.2%, pyrazinamide 67.6%, ethambutol 41.4%.
audits.c: Training activity in late 2012 at the Tuberculosis Clinical Centre
audits.r2: Fluoroquinolone use at the TCC fell from 41.4% before 2013 to 13.5% after 2013 (adjOR 0.19).

audits.t: Surgical assessment clinic - One stop emergency out-patient clinic for rapid assessment, reduced admissions and improved acute surgical service: A quality improvement study.
audits.st: Clinic referral criteria (new referral guidelines)
audits.f: 42.9% of referrals appropriate
audits.c: New referral guidelines distributed to the local Care Coordination Centre handling GP referrals

audits.t: Audit on the Use of Dangerous Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations in Paper Compared to Electronic Medication Orders: A Multicenter Study.
audits.st: Institute for Safe Medication Practices Canada 'Do Not Use' list
audits.f: Dangerous abbreviations in 172/714 (24.1%) paper orders vs 9/2207 (0.4%) electronic orders.

audits.t: Auditing The Completeness and Legibility of Computerized Radiological Request Forms.
audits.st: Completeness and legibility of radiological request forms
audits.f: Electronic forms were significantly more complete and legible than paper forms, with fewer entry errors.

audits.t: Quality of medication information in discharge summaries from hospitals: an audit of electronic patient records.
audits.st: Eight Norwegian quality criteria for medication information (score 0-16)
audits.f: Mean score 7.4 (SD 2.8; range 0-14); 7.80 for regular vs 6.52 for as-needed medicines (p < 0.001).

audits.t: What the FLOQ? A quality improvement project to reduce unnecessary paediatric respiratory viral swabs in a peripheral metropolitan hospital.
audits.st: Target to reduce paediatric respiratory viral swabs by 25% over 4 months
audits.f: 336 FLOQ swabs (ED 237); ED-discharged patients under 2 years with a swab 40% on monthly audit.
audits.c: Staff education, targeted feedback to frequent requesters, rationalising patients appropriate for testing, stakeholder engagement and monthly audit with feedback.
audits.r2: 151 swabs (55% reduction); ED 82 (66% reduction); ED-discharged under 2s with a swab 3%.

audits.t: Audit on first seizure presentation to Taranaki Base Hospital: a secondary centre experience.
audits.tp: First seizure and suspected epilepsy assessment
audits.st: International guidelines for first seizure management
audits.f: Only 14% received formal neurology follow-up, only 8% had EEG and only 43% had documented driving advice; 52% had an abnormality on neuroimaging.

audits.t: Optimal Line and Tube Placement in Very Preterm Neonates: An Audit of Practice.
audits.tp: Endotracheal tube and umbilical catheter position
audits.st: Optimal radiological position of ETTs and umbilical catheters
audits.f: Accurate placement: ETT depth 50%, UAC 40%, UVC 14%.
audits.c: Educational sessions for staff on insertion length methods.
audits.r2: ETT depth 47%, UAC 43%, UVC 23%; no significant difference.

audits.t: Using the Evidence-Based Practice Service Nursing Bundle to Increase Patient Satisfaction.
audits.st: At least a 5% increase in overall quality-of-care ranking and ratings
audits.f: 50% of patients rated overall quality of care as excellent (42.5 percentile); staff bundle compliance 65% in week 1.
audits.c: 1-hour service nursing bundle class (AIDET, hourly rounding and bedside shift report) with observational audits.
audits.r2: 60% rated care as excellent (85.5 percentile); staff compliance 100% by week 8 (1,104 audits).

audits.t: Inaccurate Dental Charting in an Audit of 1128 General Dental Practice Records.
audits.st: GDC requirement for complete and accurate dental records
audits.f: 44% of dental charts were inaccurate (range 16% to 83% between practices); 13% missed amalgam and 18% missed tooth-coloured restorations.

audits.t: National Comparative Audit of Blood Transfusion: report on the 2014 audit of patient information and consent.
audits.tp: Blood transfusion consent and patient information
audits.st: SaBTO (2011) recommendations: valid consent for transfusion documented in clinical records and a standardised source of patient information
audits.f: Consent documented in 43% of case notes; 85% of sites had a consent policy. 68% of patients recalled information on benefits, 38% on risks, 8% on alternatives; 28% received a leaflet.

audits.t: An audit of change in clinical practice: from oxygen-driven to air-driven nebulisers for prehospital patients with acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD).
audits.st: Target oxygen saturation 88-92%
audits.f: Median final oxygen saturation 96%; air nebuliser use 0%.
audits.r2: Median final oxygen saturation 94%; air nebuliser use 56%.

audits.t: Mystery shopping and coaching as a form of audit and feedback to improve community pharmacy management of non-prescription medicine requests: an intervention study.

audits.t: The Prevalence and Management of Dehydration amongst Neonatal Admissions to General Paediatric Wards in Kenya-A Clinical Audit.
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Predictive factors for pharyngocutaneous fistulization after total laryngectomy: a Dutch Head and Neck Society audit.
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Optimisation of intravenous fluid prescribing: framework for changing practice through education and audits.

audits.t: Preventing cerebral palsy in preterm labour: a multiorganisational quality improvement approach to the adoption and spread of magnesium sulphate for neuroprotection.
