audits.t: Audit of prevention of mother-to-child transmission programme interventions in HIV-Exposed children at national hospital, Abuja, Nigeria.
audits.st: 2010 Nigerian national guideline on prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV
audits.f: MTCT in 22 (3.2%); PCR testing in 445 (64.7%); breastfeeding 402 (58.2%); post-exposure ARV prophylaxis about 88.0%; co-trimoxazole prophylaxis only 226 (34.6%).

audits.t: Histopathological report of colorectal carcinoma resections: A 5-year audit in Lagos.
audits.st: Society for Gastroenterology and Hepatology in Nigeria pro forma dataset
audits.f: Completeness: differentiation 96.7%, extent of tumour 91.3%, total nodes 83.7%, node involvement 92.4%, perforation 73.9%, venous involvement 21.7%; TNM staging complete in 87%, Dukes 8.7%.

audits.t: Dutch Lung Surgery Audit: A National Audit Comprising Lung and Thoracic Surgery Patients.
audits.st: Dutch lung cancer guideline adherence
audits.f: Guideline adherence increased over the years; 96.5% of lung cancer patients discussed at preoperative MDT; complications 15.5% and mortality 2.0% after NSCLC surgery.

audits.t: Clinical Audit of the Radiotherapy Process in Rectal Cancer: Clinical Practice Guidelines and Quality Certification Do Not Avert Variability in Clinical Practice.
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines and agreed protocols, using a set of radiotherapy process indicators
audits.f: MRI reports lacked distance to mesorectal fascia in 38.3%; 96.7% received planned dose and 57.4% at the planned time; postoperative CRM recorded in 65.5%; 40 records per centre.

audits.t: Major obstetric haemorrhage of 2000 ml or greater: a clinical audit.
audits.st: Local major obstetric haemorrhage guideline
audits.f: Poor compliance (<75%) with MOH call activation (52%), anaesthetic consultant presence (63%) and tranexamic acid (46%); 30/56 (54%) acutely transfused.
audits.c: Guideline revised and staff training including simulation held after the audit.

audits.t: Treatment of Hyperkalemia With a Low-Dose Insulin Protocol Is Effective and Results in Reduced Hypoglycemia.
audits.st: Hyperkalaemia protocol via CPOE with 5 units insulin for CKD/ESRD
audits.f: Protocol ordering 62/99 (62%); 5 units in CKD/ESRD 32/43 (75%); hypoglycaemia 22/76 (28%).
audits.c: Education encouraging use of the CPOE hyperkalaemia protocol.
audits.r2: Protocol ordering 58/78 (74%); 5 units in CKD/ESRD 30/32 (93%, P = .03); hypoglycaemia 7/63 (11%, P = .03).

audits.t: Addressing prescription discrepancies in renal patients: a prospective audit.
audits.st: Hospital medication record matches current prescription (patients bring a medication list)
audits.f: Median proportion failing to bring a list or recall medications 0.45; significant discrepancies in 10.9% of those forgetting a list.
audits.r2: Median proportion 0.30 (0.36 in 2015; Chi-sq = 46.94, p < 0.001); significant discrepancies fell to 3.9%.

audits.t: BASHH 2016 UK national audit and survey of HIV testing, risk assessment and follow-up: case note audit.
audits.tp: HIV testing uptake in STI patients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Discrepancies between practice and clinic policies on enquiry about alcohol, recreational drugs and chemsex; previous testing commonest reason for refusing HIV test, though 33% of MSM had last tested over three months ago.

audits.t: The British Association for Sexual Health and HIV 2016 UK national audit and survey of clinic policies in relation to risk assessment, HIV testing and follow-up.
audits.tp: HIV testing uptake in STI patients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: No policy or agreed practice for alcohol enquiry in 24%, recreational drugs 21%, chemsex 43%; no policy on HIV test refusal in 13% for MSM and 18% for heterosexuals; 70% had HIV point-of-care tests.

audits.t: Managing antibiotics wisely: a quality improvement programme in a tertiary neonatal unit in the UK.
audits.st: Reduce antibiotic usage rate by 20% of baseline by 31 December 2016
audits.f: Baseline median antibiotic usage rate 347 per 1000 patient-days; antibiotics stopped within 36-48 hours in 32.5% of culture-negative sepsis screens.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary quality improvement programme with Vermont Oxford Network, shared strategies and PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: Antibiotic usage rate reduced to 198 per 1000 patient-days (43% reduction); stopping within 36-48 hours rose to 91%; antibiotic days per patient fell from median 3 to 2.

audits.t: Multidisciplinary team meetings appear to be effective in inflammatory bowel disease management: an audit of process and outcomes.
audits.st: MDT considered successful when at least top-level recommendations were implemented within 6 months
audits.f: Electronic reports filed for all patients, hard copies in 84%; all (n = 127) or top-line (n = 24) recommendations implemented in 151/166, with delay beyond 6 months in 5.

audits.t: Caesarean section audit to improve quality of care in a rural referral hospital in Tanzania.
audits.st: Appropriateness of Caesarean section indications judged by local audit panel and external auditor
audits.f: Unjustified Caesarean sections 34% (local panel) and 75% (external auditor).
audits.c: Introduction of a focused Caesarean section audit system with local panel and external auditor review.
audits.r2: Unjustified Caesarean sections fell to 23% (p = 0.29) and 52% (p = 0.01) by local panel and external auditor respectively.

audits.t: Evaluating the implementation of confusion assessment method-intensive care unit using a quality improvement approach.
audits.st: Timely delirium assessment with CAM-ICU per new local guidelines
audits.f: 134/202 assessment points appropriately assessed (60%); 18% identified as delirious.
audits.c: CAM-ICU tool introduced via educational initiatives and new local guidelines using the Model for Improvement.

audits.t: Telemedicine-based system for quality management and peer review in radiology.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Clinically significant discrepancies in 6% and clinically insignificant in 19% of CT and MRI cases; 80% of musculoskeletal examinations had diagnostic or technical imperfections.
audits.c: Routine telemedicine support and personalised e-learning
audits.r2: Level of discrepancies decreased significantly (p value not given in abstract).

audits.t: [Proper use of fluoroquinolones in hospitalized elderly patients: Realisation of a clinical audit in geriatric hospitals of Lyon University Hospital].
audits.st: SPILF recommendations (2015)
audits.f: Overall compliance of fluoroquinolone prescriptions 56% before pharmaceutical intervention; 28% should not have been prescribed.
audits.c: Pharmacist interventions on prescriptions (33 made, 72% accepted)

audits.t: Management of children and young people (CYP) with asthma: a clinical audit report.
audits.st: National Review of Asthma Deaths (NRAD) recommendations
audits.f: Risks for future attacks not recognised, few assessed objectively during attacks and only 10% of attacks followed up within 2 days.

audits.t: Hidden care: Revelations of a case-note audit of physical health care in a community mental health service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Physical health care was evident in case notes but buried in entries; under-reporting, gaps and inconsistencies in systematic recording of physical health information.

audits.t: Barriers to improving tracheostomy care in low- and middle-income countries: Our experience of a 23 patient closed loop audit cycle.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Strategies for improving outcomes in the acute management of ischemic stroke in rural emergency departments: a quality improvement initiative in the Stroke Belt.
audits.st: Guideline door-to-needle time of 60 minutes for alteplase
audits.f: 1.9% of patients treated with alteplase within 60 minutes of arrival.
audits.c: Repeat audit-and-feedback cycles, CME grand rounds at each site and targeted reinforcement of best practice

audits.t: Contact tracing for chronic hepatitis B in primary care? A 'snapshot' audit in Grampian, Northeast Scotland.
audits.st: Green Book: all sexual and household contacts of chronic hepatitis B should be tested and vaccinated if required
audits.f: Only 4/20 (20%) close contacts tested; no eligible contact vaccinated.

audits.t: From Inpatient to Ambulatory Care: The Introduction of a Rapid Access Transient Ischaemic Attack Service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median referral to consultation 10 days; brain imaging 10.5 days; carotid ultrasound 10 days.
audits.c: Daily weekday rapid access TIA clinic set up.
audits.r2: Median referral to consultation 1 day; imaging 1 day; carotid ultrasound same day.

audits.t: Preventing and managing constipation in older inpatients.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Multidisciplinary war on constipation (WOC) algorithm for prevention, detection and treatment, developed through PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: 14 per cent reduction in constipation incidence.

audits.t: Orbital infections: a complete cycle 7-year audit and a management guideline.
audits.st: not reported (new local multidisciplinary guideline developed)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Evidence review and new local multidisciplinary guideline on management of orbital infections.
audits.r2: Standardising management proved achievable through the guideline (no figures given).

audits.t: Bedside paediatric HIV testing in Malawi: Impact on testing rates.
audits.st: Provider initiated testing and counselling for all inpatients not tested in previous 3 months
audits.f: 85 (63%) of 135 children had documented HIV tests
audits.c: Bedside diagnostic HIV testing service with counsellors, supervision and remuneration
audits.r2: 110 (94.8%) of 116 children had documented HIV tests

audits.t: Audit of healthcare professionals' attitudes towards patients who self-harm and adherence to national guidance in a UK burns and plastic surgery department.
audits.st: National guidance on care of patients who self-harm
audits.f: Awareness of national guidance in 12% (7/59); training completed by 34% (20/59); 20% (12) reported conservative management offered more often for self-harm injuries, contrary to guidance.

audits.t: Pharmacoclinical audit on the use of digitalis in patients aged over 75 years hospitalized in an acute geriatric unit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 7 (35%) had high serum digoxin concentrations, 4 of whom had renal failure; 3 had ECG signs of digoxin effect.

audits.t: Programmatic Comparison and Dissemination of an Audit of Single-fraction Radiation Therapy Prescribing Practices for Bone Metastases is Associated with a Meaningful and Lasting Change in Practice on a Population Level.
audits.st: Benchmark single-fraction radiotherapy rate of 60%
audits.f: Single-fraction radiotherapy used in 49.2%.
audits.c: 2012 audit of individual physicians' prescribing presented to leaders and oncologists

audits.t: An audit of chronic oedema within the care home setting.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Establishing a Multidisciplinary Head and Neck Clinical Pathway: An Implementation Evaluation and Audit of Dysphagia-Related Services and Outcomes.
audits.tp: Head and neck cancer dysphagia pathway
audits.st: Head and neck cancer guidelines recommending regular MDT monitoring and early dysphagia intervention
audits.f: Attendance was excellent during treatment with non-compliance below 15% to 24 months; outcome tool collection good during treatment but lower afterwards.

audits.t: Faster Cancer Treatment pathway in gynaecological malignancy: a repeat clinical audit.
audits.st: Ministry of Health Faster Cancer Treatment targets: first treatment within 31 days of decision and within 62 days of referral
audits.f: 31-day target met in 73%; 62-day target met in 39%.
audits.r2: 31-day target met in 85%; 62-day target met in 45%.

audits.t: Anaesthesia, surgery, and life-threatening allergic reactions: management and outcomes in the 6th National Audit Project (NAP6).
audits.st: Published anaphylaxis management guidelines
audits.f: Immediate management good in 46%, poor in 15%; recognition prompt in 97%, treatment in 83%; epinephrine not given in 11%; fluids inadequate in 19%.

audits.t: Evaluating Neonates With Antenatal Hyderonephrosis Using a Standard Protocol: An Audit of Hospital Records.
audits.st: Standard protocol for evaluation of neonates with antenatal hydronephrosis
audits.f: 93 (32%) had abnormalities on voiding cystourethrogram; with hydroureter 65% were abnormal vs 11% without; pelvis 20 mm or more had abnormal diuretic renogram in 93%.

audits.t: Piloting online self-audit of methadone treatment in Irish general practice: results, reflections and educational outcomes.
audits.st: 25 essential national criteria for methadone maintenance treatment provision
audits.f: The majority of GPs scored 80% or over on the 25 essential criteria.

audits.t: Cost-effectiveness of Screening and Confirmatory Tests for Multiple Myeloma in Pakistani Population: An Audit Report.
audits.st: Justified use of screening and confirmatory tests for multiple myeloma
audits.f: Only 17.1% of serum protein electrophoresis tests justified (13% fully, 4.1% partially); 82.8% unjustified; 26.6% of immunoelectrophoresis/immunofixation tests properly used.

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF ORAL AND MAXILLOFACIAL PROCEDURES UNDER GENERAL ANAESTHESIA AT THE UNIVERSITY COLLEGE HOSPITAL IBADAN, NIGERIA.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Main delays were patient waits at theatre reception and in the operating suite before intubation; mandibulectomy took about 5 hours, maxillectomy 4 hours and trauma 3.5 hours.

audits.t: Implementing a standardised discharge analgesia guideline to reduce paediatric post tonsillectomy pain.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 25 (16.6%) readmitted; 13 (8.6%) readmitted for pain control; 12 (7.9%) postoperative haemorrhage; discharge analgesia varied widely.
audits.c: Standardised weight-based algorithm for regular paracetamol for 2 weeks (standardised discharge analgesia protocol).
audits.r2: 17 (14.4%) readmitted; 0 readmitted for pain control (reduction from 7.3% to 0%, p = 0.0027); 12 (10.2%) postoperative haemorrhage.

audits.t: Prescription audit in a paediatric sickle cell clinic in South-West Nigeria: A cross-sectional retrospective study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1015 medications prescribed (mean 5.02 +/- 1.9); vitamins 41.4%, antimalarials 29.0%, antibiotics 15.7%, analgesics 13.9%.

audits.t: Analyzing Volatile Anesthetic Consumption by Auditing Fresh Gas Flow: An Observational Study at an Academic Hospital.
audits.tp: Low-flow anaesthesia and volatile agent use
audits.st: Manufacturer recommendations: sevoflurane fresh gas flow 1-2 L/min; isoflurane above 1 L/min
audits.f: Sevoflurane mean fresh gas flow 2.55 L/min (95% CI 2.45-2.66); flows at least 28% higher than necessary for sevoflurane and at least 130% higher for isoflurane.

audits.t: A clinical audit of an office-based anaesthesia service for dental procedures in Victoria.
audits.st: ANZCA day surgery policy documents
audits.f: 93% were ASA 1 or 2 and demographics were within ANZCA day surgery policy; TIVA in 1,054 of 1,096 documented general anaesthetics; three unplanned hospital transfers (annual incidence 0.07%).

audits.t: Community Assessment of COPD Health Care (COACH) study: a clinical audit on primary care performance variability in COPD care.
audits.st: Two national COPD guidelines used as benchmark; adequacy graded excellent (over 80%) to highly inadequate
audits.f: Correct diagnosis with spirometric obstruction in 17.6% (9.8 to 23.3% by region); dyspnoea evaluated in 11.1%; 33.6% received no maintenance inhaled therapy.

audits.t: Otitis Externa in Secondary Care: A Change in Our Practice Following a Full Cycle Audit.
audits.tp: Otitis externa management in emergency clinic
audits.st: NICE guideline for otitis externa
audits.f: Ear swabs sent in 14 of 19 cases; Sofradex most popular empirical eardrop
audits.c: Recommendation of Betnesol-N and swabs only for refractory cases, disseminated by posters and email reminders
audits.r2: Ear swabs sent in 3 of 25 cases; Betnesol-N used in 24 of 25 cases

audits.t: Audit of ophthalmology discharge summaries in a Nigerian Teaching Hospital.
audits.st: Hospital discharge summary template and Joint Commission International content recommendations
audits.f: Traditional fields were largely complete, but medication changes were missing in 368/420 (87.6%) and test results in 334/420 (79.5%).

audits.t: A clinical audit of combined first trimester screening and non-invasive prenatal testing offered to pregnant women in a regional Australian hospital.
audits.st: Offer of first trimester screening for fetal abnormalities to pregnant women
audits.f: 609 (54%) of 1114 women had undergone or been offered screening.

audits.t: Audit of antenatal steroid use in mothers of preterms admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit in Ghana.
audits.st: Local recommendation: a course of antenatal corticosteroids for delivery between 24 and 34 weeks
audits.f: Mothers of 65 of 93 (70%) babies received at least one dose of dexamethasone; 17 (18%) only one dose.

audits.t: Use of an educational, audiovisual podcast to maximise safety with variable rate intravenous insulin infusions.
audits.tp: Variable rate intravenous insulin infusion use
audits.st: Joint British Diabetes Societies guidance and Trust VRIII chart: correct substrate fluid prescribed
audits.f: 48% of patients on VRIII were prescribed the correct fluid.
audits.c: Educational audiovisual podcast on fluid prescription with VRIII shown to prescribers
audits.r2: 63% of patients on VRIII were prescribed correct fluids.

audits.t: Quality improvement of delirium status communication and documentation for intensive care unit patients during daily multidisciplinary rounds.
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines: ICU patients assessed for delirium at least once per shift
audits.f: Delirium assessments performed 31% of the time; documentation 40% (12/30) dayshift and 27% (8/30) nightshift.
audits.c: Simulation-based nurse education with screening videos, then a standardised delirium screening tool and critical care progress note with a delirium section discussed on rounds

audits.t: An audit of discharge summaries from secondary to primary care.
audits.st: HIQA National Standard for Patient Discharge Summary 2013
audits.f: Name and date of birth present in 100%; gender missing 82%, method of admission missing 70%, medication missing 30%, medication changes missing 39%, specialty of author missing 85%.

audits.t: Anticoagulation management services in community pharmacy: Feasibility of implementing a quality improvement programme through a practice-based research network.
audits.st: Quality indicators for anticoagulation management services
audits.f: Mean global QI score 39.1% for VKAs and 12.3% for DOACs.
audits.c: Audit and feedback on quality indicators plus a personalised training programme with online videos
audits.r2: QI scores rose by 12.5 percentage points for VKAs and 9.9 points for DOACs.

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Bundle to Improve Informed Choice for Children With Typical, Newly Diagnosed Immune Thrombocytopenia.
audits.st: Current guidelines supporting conservative management of newly diagnosed ITP
audits.f: IVIG used in 88%; corticosteroids 6%; observation 6%; length of stay 47 hours.
audits.c: QI bundle: patient information sheet, evidence-informed protocol and shared decision-making through stakeholder engagement and education
audits.r2: IVIG 55%; corticosteroids 15%; observation 30%; length of stay 36 hours.

audits.t: Early decision-making in acute pulmonary embolism: a retrospective clinical audit.
audits.st: 2014 European Society of Cardiology guidelines (sPESI risk stratification)
audits.f: 52 (65%) non-low risk; 12 (23%) of these discharged home, 11 of 12 with unrecognised sPESI history components.
audits.r2: 122 (63.5%) non-low risk; 20 (16.4%) of these discharged home, 18 of 20 (90%) with unrecognised sPESI history components.

audits.t: Improving quality of clinical coding of post-partum haemorrhage: the process and its effects on reported incidence rates in a New Zealand hospital maternity service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Clinician-coder collaboration, redesigned birth documentation form, audit and follow-up by a quality midwife, a designated senior coder and ongoing education
audits.r2: Coded PPH rate rose dramatically to expected Australasian levels.

audits.t: Editor's Choice - Effect of More Expedited Carotid Intervention on Recurrent Ischaemic Event Rate: A National Audit.
audits.tp: Carotid endarterectomy symptom to surgery time
audits.st: Guidelines recommend a short delay to carotid intervention
audits.f: Recurrent ischaemic events 31%.

audits.t: Use of a safe procedure checklist in the cardiac catheterisation laboratory.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Reported complication rate 2.0% (95% CI 1.6% to 2.4%).
audits.c: WHO-derived safe procedure checklist refined by weekly PDSA cycles, with team briefing before each procedure list.
audits.r2: Complication rate fell to 0.8% (95% CI 0.6% to 1.1%, p≤0.001); average turnaround time reduced by 3 min (p=0.027); dose area product reduced by 641.5 cGy/cm2 (p=0.002).

audits.t: Making surgical wards safer for patients with diabetes: reducing hypoglycaemia and insulin errors.
audits.st: National perioperative diabetes guidelines; aim to reduce hypoglycaemia, insulin errors and harm events by 50%
audits.f: Poor glycaemic control in 90% of amputation patients; hypoglycaemia and insulin management errors in 75%; less than 15% had specialist diabetes input; 20% needed third-party help for hypoglycaemia.
audits.c: Education and guidelines (2015), diabetes in-reach service (2016) and whiteboard sugar cube alert system for poor glycaemic control (2017) over three PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: Hypoglycaemia reduced by more than 50%, insulin management errors by 70% and patient harm events by 75%.

audits.t: Do ward round stickers improve surgical ward round? A quality improvement project in a high-volume general surgery department.
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians, General Medical Council and Imperial College London standards (16 items)
audits.f: Checking of drug chart, IV fluid chart, analgesia, antiemetic, enoxaparin and TEDs ranged from 0% to 6%
audits.c: Ward round sticker introduced, then redesigned after questionnaire feedback
audits.r2: Noticeable improvement from baseline in all items when stickers used; entries without stickers similar to baseline

audits.t: Quality Improvement Bedside Rounding Audits Enhance Protein Provision for Pediatric Patients Receiving Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy.
audits.tp: Nutrition delivery in paediatric intensive care
audits.st: Protein goals met in the first 5 days of continuous renal replacement therapy
audits.f: Group 1: protein goals met 22% of time by day 5 and 35% throughout (cohort n = 55 across groups).
audits.c: PDSA cycles: interdisciplinary QI group with thrice weekly bedside rounds and protein prescriptions in nephrology notes; education of intensivists; monthly QI meetings reviewing nutrition goals.
audits.r2: Group 3: protein goals met 71% of time by day 5 and 75% throughout; significant improvement after PDSA 3 (p value truncated).

audits.t: A nurse-led audit on the incidence and management of inadvertent hypothermia in an operating theatre department of an Irish hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: The prescription of lidocaine patches in osteoarthritis-a complete audit cycle.
audits.st: Licensed indication for topical lidocaine patches: post-herpetic neuralgia
audits.f: 52 inpatients (17.1%) on topical lidocaine patches; most common indication musculoskeletal pain (75%).
audits.c: Education on indications and licensed use of topical lidocaine patches.
audits.r2: 18 inpatients (6%) on topical lidocaine patches; musculoskeletal pain 77.78% of indications.

audits.t: A repeat audit of primary care management of group A streptococcal pharyngitis in Northland, New Zealand 2016.
audits.st: National guidelines for management of GAS pharyngitis
audits.f: Audit suggested adherence to national guidelines needed improvement.
audits.r2: Throat swabs more than doubled and amoxicillin more commonly prescribed, but the proportion not receiving recommended antibiotics, or given inadequate length or no prescription, had not reduced.

audits.t: Nerve root injection cancellations because of incomplete anticoagulation management.
audits.tp: Peri-procedural anticoagulation plans for spinal injections
audits.st: 100% of outpatients attending CT-guided nerve root and facet injections should have an appropriate anticoagulation plan
audits.f: 3/55 (5%) cancelled because of incorrect anticoagulation management.
audits.c: Revised electronic request form with new compulsory fields on antiplatelets and anticoagulants.

audits.t: Identifying antibiotic stewardship interventions to meet the NHS England CQUIN: an evaluation of antibiotic -prescribing against published evidence-based antibiotic audit tools .
audits.st: Published evidence-based antibiotic audit tools, local prescribing guidelines, NICE UTI Quality Standard and NHS England CQUIN targets
audits.f: Only 38% treated for UTI met the UTI definition; courses 19% longer than recommended on average; 17% eligible for IV to oral switch at 72 h not switched; 96% of non-severe CAP started on IV.

audits.t: The Dutch Audit of Carotid Interventions: Transparency in Quality of Carotid Endarterectomy in Symptomatic Patients in the Netherlands.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Low overall mortality and stroke/death rates; time to intervention varied between hospitals.

audits.t: Nursing and medical contribution to Defence Healthcare Engagement: initial experiences of the UK Defence Medical Services.
audits.st: Best practice and DMS care standards for hand hygiene before and after patient contact and VIP scoring for peripheral cannulas
audits.f: Hand hygiene compliance poor on induction; no cannula surveillance (VIP scoring) in place.
audits.c: Intensive education, training, demonstrations and coworking; introduction of peripheral cannula care and VIP scoring.
audits.r2: Second cycle: hand hygiene compliance 69% and VIP scoring compliance 99%. Final cycle: nurses' hand hygiene 75/98 (77%) vs doctors' 76/200 (38%).

audits.t: Improving developmental care in primary practice for disadvantaged children.
audits.st: Delivery of basic developmental care (continuous quality improvement audit)
audits.f: Basic developmental care items delivered ranged from 55% (advice on stimulation, 1279, 55.1%) to 74% (developmental milestone assessment, 1510, 73.7%); 92.6% (88) received follow-up care.
audits.c: Sustained participation in continuous quality improvement audit cycles (compared, not introduced as a change).

audits.t: Audit cycle of the provision of compression garments on prescription.
audits.st: Patients obtain the correct compression garment on an NHS prescription from their GP (target not reported)
audits.f: The audit standard was not met.
audits.c: Necessary changes in clinical practice identified and introduced through the audit cycle (details not reported).
audits.r2: The audit standard was not met in any of the audits.

audits.t: Nurse-led active surveillance for prostate cancer is safe, effective and associated with high rates of patient satisfaction-results of an audit in the East of England.
audits.st: Trust and national guidelines for active surveillance
audits.f: Compliance with aspects of local guidelines ranged from 88.8% to 100%.

audits.t: Auditing and Improving Surgical Antibiotic Prophylaxis.
audits.st: Hospital surgical antibiotic prophylaxis protocols; six process quality indicators
audits.f: High compliance for indication, choice of agent, dose and route, and intra-operative redosing; worse compliance for timing of first dose and duration of prophylaxis (figures not reported in abstract).
audits.c: Annual audit with feedback of results to surgical services, whose management contracts include protocol compliance; use of prophylaxis kits.

audits.t: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) in gynecologic oncology: System-wide implementation and audit leads to improved value and patient outcomes.
audits.st: ERAS gynaecologic oncology guidelines (ERAS Interactive Audit System compliance)
audits.f: Mean compliance with ERAS care elements 56%.
audits.c: System-wide implementation of ERAS gynaecologic oncology guidelines.
audits.r2: Mean compliance with ERAS care elements 77.0%.

audits.t: Determinants of medical prescriptions for COPD care: an analysis of the EPOCONSUL clinical audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Triple therapy in 2,428 (53.9%); incorrect inhaled therapy prescriptions in 261 (5.9%); 3,494 (77.5%) had no change in prescription.

audits.t: An antibiotic audit of the surgical department at a rural hospital in Western Kenya.
audits.st: Criteria for appropriate antibiotic choice, duration and indication (no named guideline)
audits.f: Inappropriate prescriptions in 45.4% of prophylactic, 33.4% of treatment and 52.6% of discharge antibiotics; duration indicated in only 11% of treatment sheets; most common reason inappropriate duration (45.9%).

audits.t: Documenting Goals of Care Among Patients With Advanced Cancer: Results of a Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Guidelines recommending goals of care discussion and early palliative care referral for patients with advanced cancer
audits.f: Goals of care documentation 0% at baseline; palliative care referral 36%.
audits.c: Drafted guideline for goals of care documentation and palliative care referral, standardised documentation system, e-mail reminders and a QI scorecard of overall and individual physician rates (DMAIC methodology).
audits.r2: Goals of care documentation 31% (passive phase 3%); palliative care referral 48% (passive phase 35%).

audits.t: A pre and post intervention study to reduce unnecessary urinary catheter use on general internal medicine wards of a large academic health science center.
audits.st: SafetyLEAP programme; primary outcome urinary catheter prevalence (no target stated)
audits.f: Initial audit and feedback of 534 patients; pre-intervention daily catheter point prevalence 22%; catheter utilisation ratio 0.14.
audits.c: SafetyLEAP programme (systematic detection and reduction of safety incidents) with audit and feedback; programme adherence 97.4%.
audits.r2: Daily catheter point prevalence fell to 13%; catheter utilisation ratio 0.12.

audits.t: Monitoring of prolactin levels in children and adolescents prescribed antipsychotic medication: a complete audit cycle.
audits.st: NICE guidelines on monitoring and managing hyperprolactinaemia with antipsychotics
audits.f: Baseline serum prolactin 28.6%; six-monthly repeat prolactin 28.6%; management of hyperprolactinaemia 0%.
audits.c: Recommended guidelines and changes implemented (details not stated).
audits.r2: Baseline prolactin 57%; six-monthly repeat prolactin 39.1%; management of hyperprolactinaemia 12.5%.

audits.t: Psychiatric illness, medication and driving: an audit of documentation.
audits.st: Road Safety Authority and Royal College of Physicians of Ireland guidelines on fitness to drive
audits.f: None of 100 patients had specific documentation about driving.
audits.c: Presentation at an academic meeting and education of team members on the guidelines.
audits.r2: Minor improvement of 7% in documentation (not significant).

audits.t: Monitoring of extrapyramidal side effects in patients on antipsychotic treatment: a completed audit cycle.
audits.st: Clinical guidelines recommending regular monitoring of extrapyramidal side effects
audits.f: EPSE documented in 14% of records.

audits.t: Nutrition of Preterm Infants and Raw Breast Milk-Acquired Cytomegalovirus Infection: French National Audit of Clinical Practices and Diagnostic Approach.
audits.tp: Raw breast milk feeding and CMV in preterm infants
audits.st: French national recommendations (2005) on raw breast milk for preterm infants of CMV-positive mothers
audits.f: 75% of units responded; 24% complied with recommendations, 20% contraindicated raw milk for all under 32 weeks, 25% fed raw milk unconditionally.

audits.t: Reducing Trainee Service Provision Burden: An Audit of Cardiac Surgical Follow-Up.
audits.st: Departmentally agreed guideline on discharge from postoperative follow-up
audits.f: Inappropriate recalls at first postoperative appointment 17.6%.
audits.c: Introduction of departmentally agreed guidelines on discharge from follow-up.
audits.r2: Inappropriate recalls at first postoperative appointment 4.6% (p value truncated in abstract); n = 250 in 2016 and n = 324 in 2017.

audits.t: Audit of Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: Impact of Procedure Recording on Clinical Practice.
audits.tp: Critical view of safety in laparoscopic cholecystectomy
audits.st: Recommendations from published literature: establish critical view of safety, divide cystic artery before duct, avoid gallbladder perforation, avoid diathermy for cystic artery
audits.f: Critical view of safety established in 91; optimisation of view in 54; gallbladder perforation in 32; diathermy routinely used for cystic artery.
audits.c: Recommendations from published literature implemented in practice after video review.
audits.r2: Critical view of safety in 99 (p=0.009); optimisation in 83 (p<0.001); perforation in 19 (p=0.035); diathermy for cystic artery stopped completely.

audits.t: An Audit of Thrombophilia Testing in Patients with Ischemic Stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack: The Futility of Testing.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 44 (31%) had at least one positive result; testing altered management in only 1 patient (1%); 33 (75%) of positives risked misdiagnosis because tests were not repeated or repeated too soon.
audits.c: Thrombophilia testing in inpatients with stroke discontinued.

audits.t: Audit of Mental Capacity Assessment by Primary Care Physicians Versus Consultation-liaison Psychiatrists.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Assessments by primary care physicians were suboptimal; consultation-liaison psychiatrists documented mental capacity in 93.7% and psychiatric diagnosis in 88.9%.

audits.t: Clinical audit to assess delays in chemotherapy administration at daycare oncology center at a tertiary care hospital in Karachi, Pakistan.
audits.st: Initial nursing assessment within 15 min of arrival in daycare
audits.f: 72% of patients had initial assessment within 15 min of arrival.
audits.c: After review I, number of nurses increased (review II); then initial assessment process divided between two different areas (review III).
audits.r2: 75% had initial assessment within 15 min after separating the initial assessment into two areas.

audits.t: Revisiting the Pain Resource Nurse Role in Sustaining Evidence-Based Practice Changes for Pain Assessment and Management.
audits.st: Three key evidence-based practice targets for pain assessment and management, including documentation of pain scores on admission and each nursing shift
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Ward-based pain resource nurses introduced in 2007 to facilitate evidence-based practice change.
audits.r2: Significant improvements in documentation of pain scores on admission and for each nursing shift (figures not reported in abstract).

audits.t: Safety Stop: A Valuable Addition to the Pediatric Universal Protocol.
audits.st: WHO guidelines and Joint Commission Universal Protocol: time-out performed just prior to incision
audits.f: Mock Joint Commission survey found time-out was performed before preparation and draping, not just before incision.
audits.c: Enhanced paediatric Universal Protocol adding a safety stop before preparation and draping, with the time-out moved to just before incision; introduced after electronic correspondence and leadership meetings.

audits.t: Audit of defibrillators at an urban public sector hospital.
audits.st: Availability of checklist books, daily documented checks, service in last 12 months and absence of critical problems
audits.f: Checklist books available for 101 (72.7%) manual defibrillators; 26 (18.7%) had at least daily documented checks over 5 days; 57 (41.0%) serviced in last 12 months.

audits.t: Knowledge translation and process improvement interventions increased pain assessment documentation in a large quaternary paediatric post-anaesthesia care unit.
audits.st: Documented pain assessment (pain intensity score with validated measure) during PACU stay; no target stated
audits.f: 69% of charts had at least one documented pain assessment.
audits.c: PDSA: PACU flowsheets modified; knowledge translation strategy with educational meetings, huddle discussions, reminders (screensavers, posters, emails) and audit feedback.
audits.r2: >90% at 4 and 5 months and 100% at 6 months.

audits.t: Standards of prescription writing in a long-term psychogeriatric unit: a series of clinical audits.
audits.st: Irish and UK best practice guidelines for prescription writing
audits.f: Drug sensitivity box completed in 25% at audit one.
audits.c: Prescribing guidelines introduced after audit one; new prescription sheet developed after audit two.
audits.r2: Drug sensitivity box completion 100% at audit three; generic psychotropic prescribing increased by 69%; Medical Council Registration Number inclusion increased by 78%.

audits.t: Are there missed opportunities for occupational therapy for people with dementia? An audit of practice in Australia.
audits.st: Criteria including duration of service, assessments conducted and interventions used
audits.f: Average 2.1 consultations per referral; commonest assessments were home safety, falls risk and function; commonest interventions were referrals, environmental modification advice and assistive devices.

audits.t: Compliance with the Data Protection Acts in a psychiatric department: a complete audit cycle.
audits.st: Data Protection Acts and hospital data protection policy
audits.f: Significant lack of compliance with the DPA among staff and lack of staff training on the DPA.
audits.c: Educational interventions including DPA training and practical solutions.
audits.r2: Staff awareness and adherence to data handling practices improved and mean default points dropped significantly.

audits.t: Audit of community pharmacists' prescribing interventions: Quality assessment of a newly reimbursed service.
audits.st: Reimbursement criteria requiring a drug-related problem and a prescriber recommendation to be stated; quality rated by clinical pharmacists
audits.f: 261 (46%) met reimbursement criteria; recommendation quality good to excellent in 70% of the 261 eligible opinions.

audits.t: An audit of the screen-and-treat intervention to reduce cryptococcal meningitis in HIV-positive patients with low CD4 count.
audits.st: Screen-and-treat intervention: CrAg-positive patients with CD4 100 cells/mm3 or less to have lumbar puncture
audits.f: 190 (5.1%) CrAg positive; only 5/190 (2.6%) referred for lumbar puncture; 43 (22.6%) admitted with CCM.
audits.c: Recommended systems to ensure all CrAg-positive patients have an LP.

audits.t: Audit of documentation of allergies in a psychiatric inpatient unit.
audits.st: Gold standard guidelines on allergy documentation
audits.f: Allergy section completed in 25% of medication charts; 12% of current case notes; 65% of original admission notes.
audits.c: Formal initial assessment proforma with a designated allergy section and promotion of awareness among NCHDs.
audits.r2: Medication charts 58.1%; current case notes 19.1%; original admission notes 80.9%.

audits.t: Improving the practice of handover for psychiatric inpatient nursing staff.
audits.st: SBAR communication framework for nursing handover
audits.f: SBAR used in 4% of handovers; satisfaction with handover information 34%.
audits.c: PDSA cycles: psychiatry-relevant SBAR resources developed, staff education, audits and survey.

audits.t: Prevention of venous thromboembolism in postoperative abdominal patients: a best practice implementation project.
audits.st: JBI evidence-based audit criteria for VTE prevention
audits.f: Four audit criteria had compliance under 30% (21 nurses and 30 patients).
audits.c: VTE education including a VTE video, clinical practice and prophylaxis measures.

audits.t: Effect of Audit and Feedback on Physician Adherence to Clinical Practice Guidelines for Pneumonia and Sepsis.
audits.st: Guidelines for antibiotic administration in inpatient pneumonia and 3-hour Surviving Sepsis Bundle
audits.f: Guideline adherence 52% without feedback.
audits.c: Detailed individual feedback with blinded peer comparison to attending emergency physicians (stepped wedge, 6 clusters).
audits.r2: Guideline adherence 65% with feedback (difference 13%, 95% CI 4% to 22%); adjusted OR 1.8.

audits.t: Evidence-based patient/public voice: a patient and public involvement audit in the field of sexual health.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Wide variability; lack of PPI goals, reliance on focus groups, poor resourcing, late PPI in research and poor lay summaries.

audits.t: Noncompliance to a Postoperative Algorithm Using Feeding Readiness Assessments Prolonged Length of Stay at a Pediatric Heart Institute.
audits.st: Postoperative feeding algorithm: pursue gastrostomy or oral-only feeds within 3 days once indicated by sentinel feeding readiness assessment
audits.f: 49/69 (71%) complied with the algorithm; noncompliers had longer length of stay (34 v 25 days; P = 0.01).

audits.t: Reducing Antibiotic Use in Respiratory Syncytial Virus-A Quality Improvement Approach to Antimicrobial Stewardship.
audits.st: Aim: reduce antibiotic exposure and DOT/1000 patient days in hospitalised RSV-positive patients by 25%
audits.f: 56.2% of RSV-positive patients received antibiotics.
audits.c: Antimicrobial stewardship programme: education, prospective audit and feedback, emergency department engagement and performance dashboards.
audits.r2: Antibiotic exposure fell to 30.9%; DOT/1000PD fell by 164.6 from baseline (P = 0.017).

audits.t: 'CPR for Feet' care bundle to improve foot assessment in inpatient diabetes.
audits.st: 'CPR for Feet' (Check, Protect and Refer) campaign guidelines
audits.f: 28% had evidence of foot assessment; 13% of staff aware of the campaign
audits.c: Staff education and 'CPR for Feet' assessment checklist, then a 'CPR for Feet' care bundle after staff feedback (four PDSA cycles)
audits.r2: 72% had feet assessed and managed correctly; all staff aware of the campaign

audits.t: Optimisation of hyperemesis gravidarum management through an emergency department setting.
audits.tp: Hyperemesis gravidarum management in the emergency department
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Admissions to O&G reduced by 68.7% compared with before the proforma
audits.c: ED clinical pathway and treatment protocol proforma for hyperemesis gravidarum
audits.r2: Admissions to O&G reduced by 70.5% compared with before the proforma

audits.t: An end-to-end postal audit test to examine the coincidence between the imaging isocenter and treatment beam isocenter of the IGRT linac system for Japan Clinical Oncology Group (JCOG) clinical trials.
audits.st: Radiation positional error within acceptance levels (1 mm/1°)
audits.f: 42 IGRT devices (89.4%) within acceptance levels at first check.

audits.t: Community mental health services in Southern Gauteng: An audit using Gauteng District Health Information Systems data.
audits.st: National Mental Health Policy Framework norms: minimum coverage 2.7% of adults and 1.5% of children and adolescents
audits.f: Coverage approximately 0.3% of adults and 0.02% of children and adolescents; only 2.23% of clinic visits were for mental health; no norms met.

audits.t: Peri-Operative Anaesthetic Documentation: A Report of Three Sequential Audits on the Quality of Outcomes, with an Insight Into Surrounding Legal Issues.
audits.st: Selected Royal College of Anaesthetists and ANZCA criteria for adequacy of peri-operative anaesthetic documentation
audits.f: Pre-operative records appropriately documented 16.3%; intra-operative records adequately documented 25.5%.
audits.c: Repeated audits (regular audit of anaesthetic record keeping); no specific change described.
audits.r2: Pre-operative records appropriately documented 43.8%; intra-operative adequately documented 35.1%.

audits.t: Successful use of "Choice Architecture" and "Nudge Theory" in a quality improvement initiative of analgesia administration after Caesarean section.
audits.st: Local prescribing guidelines for regular multimodal postoperative analgesia after Caesarean section
audits.f: Analgesic medications administered in compliance with guidelines in 39.6%.
audits.c: Education sessions for recovery and ward staff and a new preprinted, highlighted medication chart (nudge theory).

audits.t: An audit of completion of diaries for rehabilitation in an intensive care unit.
audits.st: NICE recommendation that services meet psychological needs after critical illness
audits.f: Compliance with completing ICU diaries was poor.

audits.t: An audit of incomplete involuntary admissions to an approved Irish centre.
audits.st: Mental Health Act 2001 and recommendations of Audit 2003
audits.f: Audit 2003 analysed all Temporary Patient Reception Orders whose admission orders were not completed by the consultant psychiatrist.
audits.c: Implementation of the Mental Health Act 2001 (November 2006) and Audit 2003 recommendations.
audits.r2: No change in involuntary referral rate; consultant psychiatrist refused to make an order in one in three cases; increased rate of incorrectly filled GP forms.

audits.t: Internal audit of attendances at a psychiatry outpatient clinic.
audits.st: Locally set standards for patterns of attendance at the outpatient clinic
audits.f: Non-attendance 13.9%; 30.1% attended without an appointment; 20.4% inappropriate attendances; 2.2% outside catchment.
audits.c: Protocols for attenders without appointment and for streamlining prescriptions, plus renewed emphasis on transferring out-of-catchment patients.
audits.r2: Non-attendance unchanged; without appointment 9.3% (significant decrease); inappropriate attendances 9.3% (not significant); outside catchment 2.3%.

audits.t: Use of tranexamic acid in trauma patients requiring massive transfusion protocol activation: an audit in a major trauma centre in New Zealand.
audits.st: International best practice for TXA in severe trauma: initial dose within three hours of injury and second dose
audits.f: 76.2% of indicated patients received an initial TXA dose and 19.0% both doses; 21.1% dosed within one hour, 52.6% between one and three hours, 26.3% after three hours.

audits.t: RCPAQAP audit of antimicrobial reporting in Australian and New Zealand laboratories: opportunities for laboratory contribution to antimicrobial stewardship.
audits.tp: Laboratory quality management for antimicrobial resistance testing
audits.st: Selective reporting: no broad-spectrum agents on isolates susceptible to narrow-spectrum agents and no agents inappropriate for the site
audits.f: 82% (77/94) of laboratories over-reported or inappropriately reported at least one antimicrobial; 65% (55/84) over-reported for fully susceptible E. coli in blood culture.

audits.t: Audit of COPD exacerbations in secondary care.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Quality-improvement program for ultrasound-based fetal anatomy screening using large-scale clinical audit.
audits.st: Recommended clinical image-acquisition standards: scan completeness and objective image quality scoring
audits.f: 103 501 images from 6257 examinations by 22 sonographers; departmental median scan completeness 72%
audits.c: Targeted actions in response to audit findings (not detailed in abstract)
audits.r2: 153 557 images from 6406 scans by 25 sonographers; departmental median scan completeness 78%

audits.t: Understanding changes in the standardized antimicrobial administration ratio for total antimicrobial use after implementation of prospective audit and feedback.
audits.st: Standardised antimicrobial administration ratio (SAAR)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Stewardship intervention with prospective audit and feedback.
audits.r2: SAAR for total antimicrobial use decreased; prescribing and clinical outcomes stable or improved.

audits.t: Delirium in the hospitalised elderly: An audit of NCHD prescribing practice.
audits.st: Best practice guidelines for psychotropic prescribing in delirium
audits.f: 55% response rate (n = 52); haloperidol and lorazepam most used; substantial proportion used higher than recommended starting doses; intramuscular route commonest.

audits.t: Electronic Audit and Feedback With Positive Rewards Improve Anesthesia Provider Compliance With a Barcode-Based Drug Safety System.
audits.st: Scanning syringe barcodes before drug administration (barcode-based drug safety system)
audits.f: 8.7% of syringe barcodes scanned.
audits.c: Monthly individual email performance reports with rank relative to peers, plus public coffee gift card awards for top performers in the first 2 months.

audits.t: Minimizing central line-associated bloodstream infections in a high-acuity liver transplant intensive care unit.
audits.st: Central venous catheter care process measures (complete compliance) and CLABSI rate per 1,000 CVC days
audits.f: Complete compliance with process measures 25%; CLABSI rate 4.2 per 1,000 CVC days.
audits.c: 14 interventions via Lean and PDSA cycles: infection prevention, care standardisation, team-based monitoring, audit and feedback and education.
audits.r2: Complete compliance 67%; CLABSI rate 1.8 per 1,000 CVC days (61.2% annual reduction).

audits.t: Diagnosis and management of otitis media with effusion in a tertiary hospital in Kano: a best practice implementation project.
audits.st: Eleven evidence-based JBI audit criteria for OME diagnosis and management
audits.f: Compliance for criteria 1, 6, 9 and 10 was 0-25%.
audits.c: Introduction of pneumatic otoscope use and education sessions for clinicians and caregivers.
audits.r2: Compliance for criteria 1, 6, 9 and 10 rose to 70-100%.

audits.t: Reducing night-time discharge from intensive care. A nationwide improvement project with public display of ICU outcomes.
audits.st: Night-time discharge as a national quality indicator
audits.f: Night-time discharge prevalence 7.0% (95% CI 5.2 to 8.7%) in 2006.
audits.c: Night-time discharge appointed as a national quality indicator with public internet display of discharge proportions and outcomes.
audits.r2: Night-time discharge prevalence 4.9% (95% CI 4.3 to 5.5%) (P = .035 for trend).

audits.t: Major lower limb amputation audit - introduction and implementation of a multimodal perioperative pain management guideline.
audits.st: Local multimodal perioperative pain management guideline (no national guideline)
audits.f: 61% of pain scores reported as 0; 26% needed opioid PCA.
audits.c: Multimodal perioperative pain guideline introduced, including a local anaesthetic perineural catheter.
audits.r2: 78% of pain scores reported as 0; 4% needed opioid PCA; pain scores significantly lower (p < 0.05) on ward admission, 6, 12, 24 hours and 2 days.

audits.t: Auditing the appropriateness of cesarean delivery using the Robson classification among women experiencing a maternal near miss.
audits.st: Swedish obstetric guidelines for Caesarean delivery indication, reported by Robson ten-group classification
audits.f: Caesarean deliveries were more likely judged appropriate by local than Swedish auditors (OR 2.7, 95% CI 1.3-5.7).

audits.t: Improving out-of-hours surgical patient care.
audits.st: Seven electronic handover criteria (layout, location, clinical priority, active issues, resuscitation status, test results, weekend plan)
audits.f: Handover entry scores averaged from 42.2% at the start.
audits.c: New electronic handover tool, regular handover meetings, 50% more weekend staff, staff training and audit feedback.
audits.r2: Handover scores improved progressively to 92.9%; handover meeting attendance consistently above 80%.

audits.t: Antimicrobial prescription patterns and ventilator associated pneumonia: findings from a 10-site prospective audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: About 75% received an antimicrobial; no clinical justification documented for 20% of prescriptions.

audits.t: The World Health Organization Surgical Safety Checklist: An audit of quality of implementation at a tertiary care high volume cancer institution.
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (modified version)
audits.f: Compliance 100%, 78% and 76.5% for the first, second and third parts; interaction of all three team representatives in 265/509 (52%).

audits.t: Wrong-Patient Blood Transfusion Error: Leveraging Technology to Overcome Human Error in Intraoperative Blood Component Administration.
audits.st: Documentation of patient identification: two electronic signatures, transfusion start and stop times and volume transfused
audits.f: Mean compliance 86%.
audits.c: Bedside barcode transfusion verification in four phases and Epic anaesthesia information management system documentation with automated audit reports.

audits.t: Multidisciplinary quality improvement initiative to standardize reporting of lung cancer screening.
audits.st: Documented Lung-RADS category in screening low-dose CT reports
audits.f: No screening LDCT reports contained a Lung-RADS assessment (0%).
audits.c: Revised radiology reporting template and monthly audit reports to thoracic radiologists.
audits.r2: 94% of screening LDCTs contained a Lung-RADS assessment with a recommended follow-up action.

audits.t: Are there patients missing from community heart failure registers? An audit of clinical practice.
audits.st: Quality Outcomes Framework heart failure register
audits.f: Recorded heart failure prevalence 0.63% at baseline.
audits.c: Audit software (ENHANCE-HF) searches with specialist nurse review, and patients added to the register.
audits.r2: Heart failure prevalence 1.12% after the audit.

audits.t: Improving communication of patient issues on transfer out of intensive care.
audits.st: Number of current problems listed in medical ICU transfer documents (no target stated)
audits.f: Average 1.8 current problems listed per patient.
audits.c: PDSA cycles: paper problem list at the bedside with supporting education, then a checklist of common patient problems.
audits.r2: Average rose to 2.7 after the problem list and education, then 3.85 after adding the checklist.

audits.t: Improving the personalisation of care in a district nursing team: a service improvement project.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: PDSA project focusing on personalisation of care.
audits.r2: Patient and staff satisfaction improved and documentation audit showed increased focus on personalisation (figures not reported).

audits.t: Importance of Compliance Audits for a Pediatric Complicated Appendicitis Clinical Practice Guideline.
audits.st: Institutional complicated appendicitis clinical practice guideline (full compliance)
audits.f: Only 15% (9/60) had full guideline compliance and 49% (29/60) received recommended antibiotic durations; compliance 7% at start.
audits.c: Feedback to care providers throughout the audit (audit cycles).
audits.r2: Full compliance increased from 7% to 23% with audit-derived feedback.

audits.t: A longitudinal chart audit of hypertension in a family practice center.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Diagnosis properly made in all patients and evaluation and therapy appropriate; family and past medical history poorly recorded.
audits.c: New history database sheet and chronic disease flow sheet designed.

audits.t: Assessing antibiotic stewardship using the surgical site infection prevention bundle.
audits.st: SIGN guidance: discontinue broad-spectrum prophylactic antibiotics after 24 hours
audits.f: 88% of patients received antibiotics beyond 24 hours.
audits.c: Updated Trust guideline with poster campaign; head and neck prophylaxis bundle on electronic prescribing; updated Microguide.
audits.r2: 25% of patients received antibiotics beyond 24 hours.

audits.t: Medical practice assessment during the phlebotomy: clinical audit of blood sampling.
audits.st: Recommendations for the phlebotomy procedure
audits.f: Overall phlebotomy compliance 57.7%; collection procedure 45.1% (hand hygiene 28%, gloves 20%, antiseptics 44.4%); sample identification 61.3%; transport 49.4%.

audits.t: Testing a novel audit and feedback method for hand hygiene compliance: A multicenter quality improvement study.
audits.st: Hand hygiene compliance on room entry and exit
audits.f: Standard overt audit estimates were about 30% higher than covert secret-shopper estimates (OR 9.83).
audits.c: Monthly feedback tool reporting compliance from the covert audit method.
audits.r2: No significant change in compliance between baseline and feedback phases (OR 0.92; 95% CI 0.84-1.01).

audits.t: Self Harm and Suicidality: an audit of follow-up in primary care.
audits.st: NICE guidelines on prevalence, timing and content of follow-up after self-harm or suicidality
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An audit of psychotropic prescribing practice of general adult psychiatrists in elderly demented patients.
audits.st: American Psychiatric Association 1997 guidelines and UK old age psychiatrist practice
audits.f: Median doses in keeping with APA guidelines; 10% specified at least one dosage regime grossly outside recommended ranges.

audits.t: Effectiveness of standard fasting guidelines as assessed by gastric ultrasound examination: A clinical audit.
audits.st: ASA preoperative fasting guidelines
audits.f: 69/246 (28.04%) had high residual gastric volume on ultrasound despite ASA fasting.

audits.t: Screening and Audit as Service-Level Strategies to Support Implementation of Australian Guidelines for Cancer Pain Management in Adults: A Feasibility Study.
audits.st: Australian guidelines for cancer pain management; feasibility thresholds of 75% screening and median 30 minutes per audit
audits.f: 95% (n = 429) of 452 visits screened; median audit time 37.5 minutes (31 records); adherence to indicators ranged from 63% (pain assessment at first presentation) to 94% (regular pain assessment and regular medication).

audits.t: GooD4Mum: A general practice-based quality improvement collaborative for diabetes prevention in women with previous gestational diabetes.
audits.st: Women on GDM registers completing a diabetes screening test and prevention planning consultation within 15 months (guideline-led)
audits.f: Diabetes screening 26%; postpartum screening 43%; prevention planning consultations 0%; BMI recorded 51%.
audits.c: 12-month quality improvement collaborative with quarterly audits, guideline-led workshops and PDSA feedback cycles.
audits.r2: Diabetes screening 61%; postpartum screening 60%; prevention planning consultations 10%; BMI recorded 69%.

audits.t: Non-indicated acid-suppression prescribing in a tertiary paediatric hospital: An audit and costing study.
audits.st: Indicated prescribing of proton pump inhibitors and H2 receptor antagonists
audits.f: 238 (78.5%) of prescriptions were non-indicated.

audits.t: UK national audit of safety checks for radiology interventions.
audits.st: Use of safety checklists for radiological interventions (RCR)
audits.f: 94% used safety checklists in 2012.
audits.r2: 109/177 (62%) trusts responded; 98% used checklists (48% for all procedures in all modalities, 50% for some, 2% none).

audits.t: Use of a criteria-based audit to optimize uptake of cesarean delivery in a low-resource setting.
audits.st: Criteria-based audit checklist for obstructed labour and fetal distress
audits.f: Perinatal morbidity and mortality with obstructed labour 42/260 (16.2%); fetal distress baseline n=248.
audits.r2: Perinatal morbidity and mortality with obstructed labour 22/250 (8.8%) (P=0.012); fetal distress re-audit n=251.

audits.t: How do we compare with best practice? A completed audit of benzodiazepine and z-hypnotic prescribing.
audits.st: Best practice standards for benzodiazepine and z-hypnotic prescribing (including regular hospital-initiated courses not exceeding 4 weeks; PRN indication, time limit and maximum dose documented)
audits.f: At least 50% of regular z-hypnotics and benzodiazepines were initiated before admission; lorazepam most prescribed (other figures not reported).
audits.c: Feedback to medical practitioners through a presentation and email.
audits.r2: Total benzodiazepine and z-hypnotic prescribing increased; mean regular benzodiazepine dose fell by 2 mg; 14% increase in hospital-initiated regular benzodiazepines exceeding 4 weeks.

audits.t: Balancing quality improvement and unintended effects: The impact of implementing admission order sets for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and heart failure at two teaching hospitals.
audits.tp: Admission order sets for COPD and heart failure
audits.st: 14 guideline elements for heart failure (nine) and COPD (five)
audits.f: Order set use significantly increased adherence to 4 of the 10 guideline elements included in the order sets.
audits.c: COPD and heart failure admission order sets.

audits.t: Use of preventive home visits by general practitioners in patients diagnosed with dementia.
audits.tp: Preventive home visits for older people
audits.st: Danish guideline: annual preventive home visit for frail elderly patients with dementia
audits.f: More than 60% of patients with dementia had not received the recommended preventive home visit within the past year.

audits.t: Using the Model for Improvement to implement the Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool in an adult intensive care unit.
audits.st: Pain assessed and documented at least every four hours and CPOT score ≥3 treated with rescue opioid bolus
audits.f: Only 30% of Scottish ICUs using validated behavioural pain tools (April 2017 telephone audit).
audits.c: Implementation of the Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool using the Model for Improvement over six months.
audits.r2: Four-hourly pain assessments increased to 89% and treatment of CPOT scores ≥3 to 100%.

audits.t: The Victorian Comprehensive Cancer Centre lung cancer clinical audit: collecting the UK National Lung Cancer Audit data from hospitals in Australia.
audits.st: UK National Lung Cancer Audit headline indicators (adapted data set)
audits.f: Headline indicators of care were comparable with NLCA data where data completeness was higher; completeness varied significantly between fields.

audits.t: Retrospective audit of neutropenic fever after chemotherapy: how many patients could benefit from oral antibiotic management?
audits.st: Guidelines suggesting selected patients with neutropenic fever may be discharged early on oral antibiotics
audits.f: 12 of 40 (30%) patients were eligible for early discharge on oral antibiotics and ambulatory care.

audits.t: Quality Improvement of Clinical Handover in a Liaison Psychiatry Department: A Three-Phase Audit
audits.st: 11-item Handover Checklist including SBAR components
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Checklist posters, an electronic database and staff training.
audits.r2: Immediate and sustained improvement in most areas including demographics and SBAR components; baseline vs delayed re-audit P=0.007.

audits.t: Red blood cell transfusion in southern Finland from 2011 to 2016: a quality audit.
audits.st: Evidence-based transfusion guidelines: lower Hb thresholds and single-unit transfusion
audits.f: RBC usage 34.9 units per 1000 population; a measure reported as 29.5% in 2011 (details truncated in abstract).
audits.r2: RBC usage 27.5 units per 1000 population; same measure 25.2%.

audits.t: Crohn's & Colitis Australia inflammatory bowel disease audit: measuring the quality of care in Australia.
audits.st: National IBD standards
audits.f: Care was inconsistent and documentation poor; only one hospital had a complete multidisciplinary IBD service.

audits.t: An audit of antimicrobial prescribing by dental practitioners in the north east of England and Cumbria.
audits.st: Faculty of General Dental Practitioners UK antimicrobial prescribing guidelines
audits.f: Systemic spread documented in 18%; amoxicillin 61.2% and metronidazole 29.9% of prescriptions; most amoxicillin courses 5 days (66.8%) or 7 days (29.6%).

audits.t: Anti-IgE therapy for asthma: an audit at atertiary care centre in Saudi Arabia.
audits.st: Current guideline criteria for prescribing omalizumab
audits.f: 28/50 (56%) met all guideline prescribing criteria; 18 (64%) by pulmonary and 10 (36%) by allergy physicians (P < .05).

audits.t: The Physical Examination on Admission to the Acute Psychiatric Unit -complete Audit cycle
audits.tp: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists: every new psychiatric admission should have a thorough physical examination within 24 hours
audits.f: 32 (64%) complete physical examination, 16 (32%) partial, 2 (4%) none.

audits.t: Exploring patient-reported outcomes of home-based cardiac rehabilitation in relation to Scottish, UK and European guidelines: an audit using qualitative methods.

audits.t: Resolution of adhesive small bowel obstruction with a protocol based on Gastrografin administration.

audits.r2: More patients managed conservatively, fewer had first-line surgery or surgery after 72 h conservative management, shorter length of stay, marked improvement in appropriate blood tests and CT use (figures not reported)

audits.t: SAMBA18 Report - A National Audit of Acute Medical Care in the UK.
audits.tp: Acute medical unit function and flow
audits.st: Clinical quality indicators and NHS Improvement standards
audits.f: not reported

audits.st: Transplant eligibility guidelines (medical and behavioural criteria)

audits.t: Automated data extraction and report analysis in computer-aided radiology audit: practice implications from post-mortem paediatric imaging.

audits.t: Improving coding and primary care management for patients with chronic kidney disease: an observational controlled study in East London.

audits.f: not reported

audits.r2: Three intervention CCGs showed significant coding improvement (p values truncated in abstract).

audits.t: A brief intervention to improve rates and quality of physical examinations for admissions to acute adult psychiatry units.

audits.t: Prescribing of proton-pump inhibitors: auditing the management and reasons for prescribing in Danish general practice.
audits.st: Appropriate reason for PPI prescribing
audits.f: PPIs taken >2 years in 58% and daily in 64%; appropriate reason in three of four patients; no gastroscopy in 46%; 25% had a PPI consultation within the last year.

audits.t: A Project to Increase Nurses' Comfort in Offering Bedpans to Women Laboring With Epidural Analgesia.
audits.tp: Bladder care in labour with epidural

audits.f: Postepidural bedpan use 5.5% (n = 12); nurse comfort mean 5.7/10.
audits.c: 20-minute educational presentation to all labour ward nurses on catheter evidence, bedpan use and voiding techniques.
audits.r2: Postepidural bedpan use 19% (n = 20); nurse comfort mean 7.2/10 (p = .067).

audits.t: The Veracity of Troponin Test Requests for Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department with Chest Pain; a Clinical Audit.
audits.st: Appropriate timing of troponin request relative to admission and pain onset
audits.f: Veracity of troponin requests assessed before training (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: Educational Intervention Effect on Pain Management Quality in Emergency Department; a Clinical Audit.
audits.tp: Time to analgesia in the emergency department

audits.t: Audit of Antibiotic Prescribing Practices for Neonatal Sepsis and Measurement of Outcome in New Born Unit at Kenyatta National Hospital.
audits.st: Kenyan guidelines for neonatal sepsis
audits.f: Appropriate antibiotics on admission in 313 (97.8%); not stopped at 48-72 hours in 148 (53.62%) who improved; blood cultures in 13 (4%).

audits.t: How do I audit intraoperative blood component utilization in cardiac surgery?

audits.f: Mean intraoperative RBC 1.9, plasma 1.8 and platelets 0.7 units/patient.
audits.c: Provider-specific audit with feedback using rank-order bar graphs displayed on the anaesthesiology office door.

audits.t: Improving patient portal enrolment in an academic resident continuity clinic: quality improvement made simple.
audits.st: Aim to increase patient portal enrolment significantly (no numeric target)
audits.f: 35% of patients enrolled in the patient portal.

audits.t: Observational study evaluating the effectiveness of physician-targeted education for improving glycemic management of patients with type 2 diabetes (BEYOND II).

audits.f: Each hospital enrolled 100 patients with type 2 diabetes on basal insulin (proportion at HbA1c target not given in abstract)

audits.r2: Individual improvement goal achieved by 35 centres (49%); higher proportion of patients achieved HbA1c target

audits.t: The Dutch Acute Stroke Audit: Benchmarking acute stroke care in the Netherlands.
audits.st: National acute stroke quality indicators (time to IVT and IAT, outcome registration)

audits.st: Correct diagnosis based on exposure and airway obstruction

audits.st: Consensus guideline on indications for PPI use (Scarpignato et al, 2016)

audits.t: Use of Auditing and Feedback in an Outpatient Hospice Setting: Quality and Pharmacoeconomic Oversight.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.r2: Medication costs reduced by over $1.00 per patient-day while pain relief improved or was maintained.

audits.t: Implementing a quality improvement initiative for the management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in rural Nepal.

audits.f: not reported

audits.r2: Number of patients with inappropriately suspended VTE prophylaxis significantly reduced (figures not reported)

audits.t: Reducing the rare event: lessons from the implementation of a ventilator bundle.

audits.t: Institutional tuberculosis infection control in a rural sub-district in South Africa: A quality improvement study.
audits.st: National TB infection control draft guideline
audits.f: Time from TB symptoms to diagnosis 4 days.

audits.t: Audit of a multidisciplinary approach to improve management of community-acquired pneumonia.

audits.t: Delivery of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child in an acute paediatric setting: an audit of information available and service gap analysis.
