audits.st: Guidelines on reviewing and deactivating ICDs towards end of life
audits.f: Audit showed inadequate patient communication and documentation around deactivation.
audits.c: Electronic records, clinical review of comorbid patients before elective battery change and patient and carer education forum
audits.r2: Increased numbers of timely deactivations with improved documented patient discussion and consent (no figures in abstract).

audits.t: Audit of eliminating biopsy for presumed fibroadenomas with benign ultrasound greyscale and shear-wave elastography findings in women aged 25-39 years.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 3 (4%) recalled after second radiologist review; 5 (7%) re-presented with same lump; 2 developed ipsilateral cancer at a different site.

audits.t: New Zealand National Audit of Outpatient Inflammatory Bowel Disease Standards of Care.
audits.st: International standards of IBD care (including MDT staffing and minimum IBD nurse FTE per 250 000 population)
audits.f: No service met international MDT FTE standards; 62.5% held regular MDT meetings; nurses were more likely than doctors to document weight, smoking status and arrange colonoscopic surveillance (492 doctor-led and 196 nurse-led visits).

audits.t: An audit of local discrepancy rates in acute abdominal CT: does subspecialist reporting reduce discrepancy rates?
audits.st: National audit standard for major discrepancy rates
audits.f: Major discrepancy rate 6.86% for registrars versus 2.77% for consultants; both below the national audit standard.

audits.t: Massive blood loss protocol 'Code Red' at Papworth Hospital: A closed loop audit.
audits.st: British Committee for Standards in Haematology; ten standards in local Protocol for the Management of Massive Blood Loss in Adults
audits.f: 'Code Red' activated 18 times (0.83% of emergency surgeries)
audits.r2: Activated 9 times (0.26%); 6% increase in appropriate activation, 26% increase in prompt haematology notification, 30% increase in timely blood product delivery, 25% decrease in blood transfused before activation

audits.t: Antibiotic Prescribing in Primary Care for Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs) in Pregnancy: An Audit Study.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for UTI in pregnancy
audits.st: NICE guideline NG109
audits.f: Mid-stream urine sample collected in 77.6%; first-choice antibiotic 44%; second-line or non-recommended antibiotic 56%; self-care advice documented 16%.

audits.t: Results of the Austrian National Lung Cancer Audit.
audits.st: International lung cancer guidelines
audits.f: Median time presentation to diagnosis 8 days; diagnosis to treatment 15 days (chemotherapy), 21 days (radiotherapy), 24 days (surgery); unjustified surgery in 3 of 147 (2.0%).

audits.t: Audit of electronic operative documentation in interventional radiology: the value of standardised proformas.
audits.st: Locally developed minimum criteria for angiographic procedure documentation (14 parameters; targets 80% and 100% completeness)
audits.f: Paper records: 8 of 14 parameters over 80% complete; 2 parameters at 100%
audits.c: Conversion to electronic records, then a standardised procedure-specific electronic proforma
audits.r2: After electronic proforma: 12 of 14 parameters met 80% threshold; 6 of 14 at 100%

audits.t: Reducing caesarean section rate in an urban hospital serving women attending privately in India - a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: CS rate 79% in 2001.
audits.c: Full-time salaried consultants, regular CS audit, joining an improvement collaborative in 2011, practice guidelines, monitoring by consultant, labour ward support, antenatal preparation and group practice.
audits.r2: CS for foetal heart rate abnormalities fell from 23 to 5%.

audits.t: Impact of an extended audit on identifying heart failure patients in general practice: baseline results of the OSCAR-HF pilot study.
audits.st: Heart failure quality indicators (echocardiography, natriuretic peptides, RAAS blockers and beta-blockers at target dose)
audits.f: Extended EHR audit increased identified HF patients by 74% (310 to 538); echocardiography in 86%, natriuretic peptides in 19%; in HFrEF RAAS blockers 84% and beta-blockers 86%, but target doses reached in 34% and 14%.

audits.t: Audit of routine preoperative blood test requests for patients undergoing elective breast surgery: Less is more.
audits.st: NICE 2016 guideline on routine preoperative tests for elective surgery
audits.f: Unacceptable quantity of inappropriate blood tests (figures not given)
audits.c: Education of pre-assessment clinic staff on the guideline and a poster to guide ordering
audits.r2: Significant reduction in blood tests requested with a 71% reduction in financial expenditure

audits.t: A Retrospective Audit of Pharmacologic and Non-Pharmacologic Management of Childhood Acute Asthma Exacerbation at Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital, Sokoto: Adherence to Global Treatment Guidelines.
audits.st: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) guidelines (17 major recommendations)
audits.f: Of 17 GINA recommendations, adherence was good for 5 (29.4%), moderate for 7 (41.2%) and poor for 5 (29.4%); moderate adherence in 61 (96.8%) and poor in 2 (3.2%) patients.

audits.t: Blood Component Transfusion in Tertiary Care Neonatal Intensive Care Unit and Neonatal Intermediate Care Unit: An Audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: FFP 37.82%, red cell concentrate 31.34%, platelets 28.14% and whole blood 2.70% of transfusions; 277 (81.5%) transfused in the first week.

audits.t: Audit of diabetic care in family practice center in Abha City, Aseer region: CBAHI standards application.
audits.st: CBAHI standards for diabetes care (structure, process and outcome)
audits.f: Processes satisfactory except laboratory investigations and eye examination (partially met); good glycaemic control 28%, BP control 71%, lipid control 54%, appointment compliance 85%.

audits.t: National clinical audit for hospitalised exacerbations of COPD.
audits.st: National COPD process indicators and standards
audits.f: Length of stay halved from 8 to 4 days between 1997 and 2014; process indicators did not generally improve with sequential cross-sectional audit.
audits.c: Continuous audit from 2017 with quality improvement support and financial incentives for some indicators.
audits.r2: Early specialist review 55-66% and discharge bundle 53-74% (incentivised) improved faster than spirometry availability 40-46% and timely NIV 21-24%.

audits.t: Improving adherence to guideline recommendations in dementia care through establishing a quality improvement collaborative of agents of change: an interrupted time series study.
audits.tp: Management of behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia
audits.st: Dementia guideline recommendations on non-pharmacological care (self-reported adherence by checklist)
audits.f: Baseline audit of current practice with feedback (figures not reported).
audits.c: Quality improvement collaborative: start-up meeting, online learning course, expert-reviewed QI plans, audit feedback and peer sharing.
audits.r2: 42.1% immediate increase in self-reported adherence (IRR 1.42; 95% CI 1.08-1.87; p = 0.012).

audits.t: Implementation and Evaluation of Audit and Feedback for Monitoring Treat-to-Target (T2T) Strategies in Rheumatoid Arthritis Using Performance Measures.
audits.st: Five treat-to-target performance measures from an established Canadian quality framework
audits.f: Yearly follow-up >85% (PM1); disease activity documented at 50% or more of visits 100% (PM2); only 34% seen within 3 months if not in remission (PM3); 62% (2017) and 69% (2018) achieved low disease activity within 6 months (PM4); about 70% in remission (PM5)
audits.c: Individualised physician practice reports and facilitated group feedback session

audits.t: Impact of clinical audits on cesarean section rate in a Spanish hospital: Analysis of 6 year data according to the Robson classification.
audits.st: Robson Ten Group Classification System
audits.f: Overall CS rate 20.27%.
audits.c: Internal clinical audit committee established in 2014 with audit, feedback and modified clinical management protocols.
audits.r2: Overall CS rate 14.82% (p value truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Achieving Perfect Hand Washing: an Audit Cycle with Surgical Internees.
audits.st: Ideal surgical hand washing technique; target 100% compliance
audits.f: Baseline compliance 33.59%.
audits.c: Video demonstration, personal demonstration by a consultant and individual instruction over repeated attempts.

audits.t: Preparedness of the Healthcare Personnel Against the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) Outbreak: An Audit Cycle.
audits.st: CDC checklist for healthcare personnel preparedness for patients with confirmed or possible COVID-19
audits.f: Doctors and nurses had higher knowledge scores than non-clinical staff (p ≤ 0.05).
audits.c: Informative document based on WHO, CDC and Government of Pakistan guidance distributed through social media.
audits.r2: Statistically significant improvement after the educational intervention (p ≤ 0.05).

audits.t: Evaluation of a pharmacist-led actionable audit and feedback intervention for improving medication safety in UK primary care: An interrupted time series analysis.
audits.tp: High-risk prescribing and monitoring in primary care
audits.st: 10 indicators of potentially hazardous prescribing and inadequate blood-test monitoring
audits.f: At baseline 95% of practices had potentially hazardous prescribing rates between 0.88% and 6.19%.
audits.c: Pharmacist-led SMASH intervention: pharmacist training, web-based dashboard with patient-level feedback, pharmacist review of at-risk patients.
audits.r2: Potentially hazardous prescribing prevalence reduced by 27.9% (95% CI 20.3% to 36.8%).

audits.t: The impact of language and ethnicity on preparation for endoscopy: A prospective audit of an East London Hospital Ward.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: A little more than 20% of participants were inadequately prepared; no relationship with language proficiency or ethnicity.

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Improve Perioperative Hypothermia Rates in the NICU Utilizing Checklists.
audits.st: Target incidence of perioperative hypothermia less than 25%
audits.f: Incidence of perioperative hypothermia 44.4%.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team, staff education and a 9-task checklist, with quarterly PDSA cycles and monthly audit of checklist compliance.

audits.t: An audit of assessment rooms for mental health assessments in Ireland's emergency departments.
audits.st: Psychiatric Liaison Accreditation Network (PLAN) standards; target 100% compliance
audits.f: 100% response; full or substantial compliance with PLAN standards in 73% of services; rooms unsuitable in seven services; ligature points identified in some.
audits.c: Recommendations (ligature and room risk assessments) sent to hospital group chief executives

audits.t: Mixed methods evaluation of a computerised audit and feedback dashboard to improve patient safety through targeting acute kidney injury (AKI) in primary care.
audits.tp: Post-discharge care after acute kidney injury
audits.st: Six quality indicators from national guidance on post-discharge AKI care
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Electronic audit and feedback dashboard (PINGR) for six months
audits.r2: Improvement in medication review (+9.01%) and blood pressure measurement (+5.20%); no clear change in AKI coding (+0.39%), serum creatinine (-3.40%), proteinuria (-1.08%) or patient information (+0.16%).

audits.t: Survey on the Quality of Care Standards in a Nursing/Midwifery Training Hospital at Tikur Anbessa Specialized Hospital in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, 2019.
audits.st: Ethiopian Federal Ministry of Health nursing and midwifery quality standards (Quality Audit tool)
audits.f: 83% of nursing assessments not completed within eight hours of arrival; 58% of charts lacked data compilation based on Gordon's functional model; only two wards met Standard 1.

audits.t: Development and implementation of a national antimicrobial stewardship surveillance system, with open access data sharing.
audits.tp: Antibiotic indication and review date documentation
audits.st: NHS AMR CQUIN: documentation of indication and 48-72 hour review
audits.f: 33 trusts: on average 83% of patients had an indication documented and 71% had formal 48-72 h review documented.
audits.c: Refined national surveillance system linked to AMR CQUIN financial incentive
audits.r2: About 92% of prescriptions had an indication documented and 87.5% had review within 72 h, rising by 7 and 10 percentage points between first and final quarters.

audits.t: Effectiveness of Pediatric Asthma Pathways in Community Hospitals: A Multisite Quality Improvement Study.
audits.st: Evidence-based asthma pathway measures (e.g. systemic corticosteroids within 60 mins, tobacco smoke screening)
audits.f: Pre-pathway: timely steroids 32% (Site 1) and 62% (Site 2); tobacco screening 82% and 54%; CXR use 44% (Site 1); antibiotics 23% (Site 2); ED LOS 230 mins (Site 1).
audits.c: Asthma pathway implementation with local champions, educational meetings, audit and feedback and EHR integration.
audits.r2: Post-pathway: timely steroids 57% and 75%; tobacco screening 100% and 89%; CXR 29%; antibiotics 3%; ED LOS 197 mins.

audits.t: Clinical audit as an educative tool for optometrists: an intervention study in age-related macular degeneration.
audits.st: AMD audit tool
audits.f: 20 optometrists; median 15 records audited each; AMD family history asked 94%; smoking status 21%.
audits.c: Analytical performance feedback with optometrists identifying areas for improvement.
audits.r2: Median 12 records each; AMD family history 100% (p = 0.03); smoking status 58% (p value truncated).

audits.t: Quality of English inpatient mental health services for people with anxiety or depressive disorders: Findings and recommendations from the core audit of the National Clinical Audit of Anxiety and Depression.
audits.tp: Inpatient mental health care for anxiety and depression
audits.st: Thirteen standards based on NICE guidelines, literature review and steering committee feedback
audits.f: 39% referred for psychological therapy; care plan review date documented in only two-thirds; almost half had not received a copy of their care plan; frequent gaps in initial assessment documentation

audits.t: Administration of intravenous iron and tranexamic acid in the management of postoperative iron deficiency anaemia following free flap reconstruction: re-audit.
audits.st: Early correction of postoperative anaemia with intravenous iron; intraoperative tranexamic acid (no target stated)
audits.f: Initial audit: TXA intraoperatively 4%, RBC transfusion 26%, intravenous iron 0
audits.r2: TXA intraoperatively 30%, RBC transfusion 20%, intravenous iron 55 patients (37%)

audits.t: Not yet 90-90-90: A quality improvement approach to human immunodeficiency virus viral suppression in paediatric patients in the rural Eastern Cape, South Africa.
audits.tp: Paediatric HIV treatment and viral load monitoring
audits.st: UNAIDS target of 90% viral suppression
audits.f: Viral suppression 55.3%; prescription accuracy, scheduled viral loads and response to high viral loads were also poor.
audits.c: Clinical mentorship through dedicated doctor outreach to clinics.
audits.r2: Viral suppression 67.4%; most other process measures also improved.

audits.t: Improving Quality of Care Through a Mandatory Provincial Audit Program: Ontario's Emergency Department Return Visit Quality Program.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 125 698 return visits with admission (0.93% of visits); 12 852 chart audits found 3010 (23.4%) adverse events or quality issues.

audits.t: Society for Acute Medicine Benchmarking Audit 2019 (SAMBA19): Trends in Acute Medical Care.
audits.st: Society for Acute Medicine Clinical Quality Indicators
audits.f: EWS within 30 minutes 84.5% (SAMBA18 84.1%); seen by competent decision maker within 4 hours 90.4% (91.4%); consultant review within standard 68.6% (62.7%).

audits.t: Positive Impact of Clinical Audit on Appropriateness of Laboratory Investigations for Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase-Deficient Patients in the Emergency Department.
audits.tp: Appropriate investigations in G6PD haemolytic crisis
audits.st: Local haematology unit guidelines
audits.f: Non-indicated chemistry labs requested in 74%; Coombs test and liver enzymes most common non-indicated tests.
audits.c: Basic training and guideline dissemination to residents.

audits.t: Monitoring photographic proof of cecal intubation: A closed-loop audit of best practice colonoscopy.
audits.st: UK best practice: photographic evidence of caecal intubation for all complete colonoscopies (90% caecal intubation rate)
audits.f: 70% provided sufficient proof of caecal intubation; 50% labelled as proof of intubation; 30% insufficient proof
audits.c: Results shared at departmental governance meetings
audits.r2: 71% met best practice standards; 29% insufficient evidence

audits.t: A psychoeducational intervention increases use of a delirium protocol by Neurologists and Neurosurgeons in patients with brain disorders.
audits.st: Use of the hospital delirium protocol
audits.f: Delirium protocol used in 12% (n = 3); 4% (n = 3) referred with specific delirium query; delirium diagnosed in 33% (n = 25)
audits.c: Psychoeducational intervention to raise awareness of delirium diagnosis and management
audits.r2: Delirium protocol used in 47% (n = 15), significant increase; 2% (n = 2) referred for possible delirium; delirium diagnosed in 38% (n = 32)

audits.t: A clinical audit of anatomical side marker use in a pediatric medical imaging department: A quantitative and qualitative investigation.
audits.tp: Anatomical side marker use in radiography
audits.st: Anatomical side marker on every radiographic image (best practice)
audits.f: ASMs present on 99 per cent of radiographs; digital 78.8 per cent, radiopaque 20.2 per cent; 4 images had no marker.

audits.t: An audit of radiation doses received by paediatric patients undergoing computed tomography investigations at academic hospitals in South Africa.
audits.st: International paediatric CT diagnostic reference levels (CTDIvol and DLP)
audits.f: Most local DRLs compared favourably with international standards, except CT chest and CT abdomen in the 0-1 year age group.

audits.t: Breast imaging at Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital: A clinically relevant audit.
audits.st: ACR BI-RADS audit definitions compared with RSNA benchmark values
audits.f: Screening (n = 808): cancer detection rate 13.6 per 1000, recall rate 5.94; diagnostic (n = 741): CDR 175.4 and abnormal interpretation rate 39 per 100, significantly above RSNA benchmarks.

audits.t: Lung volume reduction eligibility in patients with COPD completing pulmonary rehabilitation: results from the UK National Asthma and COPD Audit Programme.
audits.tp: Lung volume reduction eligibility in COPD
audits.st: NICE COPD guideline NG115 (2018) criteria for respiratory review for lung volume reduction
audits.f: Between 4.9% and 18.1% of PR completers met NICE criteria for a lung volume reduction-focused respiratory review, depending on ISWT (≥140 m or ≥80 m) and MRC score (≥3 or ≥4) thresholds.

audits.t: Is medullary carcinoma of the colon underdiagnosed? An audit of poorly differentiated colorectal carcinomas in a large national health service teaching hospital.
audits.st: WHO criteria for medullary carcinoma
audits.f: Only one-third of medullary carcinomas were correctly identified; two-thirds reported as poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma NOS.

audits.t: An audit of COPD: diagnosis and management in general practice.
audits.st: Locally agreed COPD guidelines
audits.f: 388 (36%) of 1088 patients on the COPD register had an FEV1/FVC ratio of ≥0.7 (outside the diagnostic range).

audits.t: Improving prescribing of extended prophylaxis for venous thromboembolism at discharge in patients who underwent surgery for colorectal cancer.
audits.tp: Extended VTE prophylaxis after abdominal cancer surgery
audits.st: NICE guidance on extended VTE prophylaxis at discharge after colorectal cancer surgery
audits.f: Cyclical 4-monthly decline in compliance coinciding with foundation doctor rotations
audits.c: Six multidisciplinary interventions including education of health professionals
audits.r2: 100% compliance with prescribing extended VTE prophylaxis at discharge

audits.t: Standardised management of atraumatic epistaxis for improved outcomes in an emergency department with off-site ear, nose and throat cover - A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Epistaxis management in the emergency department
audits.st: Project measures: reduced re-bleed after nasal packing, longer packing duration, 100% ENT trolley stock
audits.f: Minimal vasoconstrictor use; mean nasal pack duration 7 hours; re-bleed rate after packing 39%
audits.c: Stocked ENT trolley, atraumatic epistaxis ED pathway and staff education (repeated PDSA cycles)
audits.r2: Re-bleed rate 14%; mean packing duration 8 hours; full trolley stocking achieved

audits.t: Newborn screening for congenital hypothyroidism: improvement in short-term follow-up by audit and monitoring.
audits.st: All serum TSH results ≥ 20 µIU/ml reported urgently to physicians
audits.f: 0.7% of tests ≥ 20 µIU/ml; only 62% reported to the paediatrician or neonatologist.
audits.c: Corrective measures addressing missing contact information, technologist policy awareness, critical results not highlighted on the computer display and lack of monitoring.

audits.t: Introduction of Criterion-Based Audit of Postpartum Hemorrhage in a University Hospital in Eastern Ethiopia: Implementation and Considerations.
audits.st: Eight standard criteria for PPH management adapted to the local setting
audits.f: All eight criteria met in 3 of 45 women (6.7%); low criteria: IV line set-up 71.1%, vital sign monitoring 51.1%, typing and cross-matching 48.9%, fluid chart 13.3%.

audits.t: Post-discharge care following acute kidney injury: quality improvement in primary care.
audits.tp: Post-discharge care after acute kidney injury
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: AKI coding in general practice 28% of cases.
audits.c: Locally commissioned incentivised service: audit and feedback, education and training, and a practice action plan to improve AKI management.

audits.t: A clinical audit of the electronic data capture of dementia in ambulance service patient records.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Dementia recorded in 13.5% of attended calls aged 65+ and 16.5% aged 75+; 15.2% of conveyed patients aged 75+.

audits.t: Postpartum hemorrhage in Suriname: A national descriptive study of hospital births and an audit of case management.
audits.st: National PPH guideline (criteria-based audit)
audits.f: In severe PPH: prophylactic oxytocin 61.3% (95/155), oxytocin treatment 68.8% (106/154), tranexamic acid 4.9% (5/103).

audits.t: Evaluating the impact of a pharmacist-led prescribing feedback intervention on prescribing errors in a hospital setting.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean prescribing error rate 25.0% intervention group and 19.7% control group (prescribed medications audited)
audits.c: Pharmacist-led individualised constructive prescribing feedback for 36 prescribers (41 controls)
audits.r2: Mean error rate 6.7% intervention group and 25.1% control group; overall change between groups 23.7%

audits.t: Advance Care Planning for Adolescents and Young Adults with Cancer: A Retrospective Case Note Audit from a Regional Specialist Center in the United Kingdom.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: ACP identified for 67%; 64% expressed a preferred place of death, achieved in 65%.

audits.t: The proportion of computed tomography kidneys, ureters and bladder (CTKUB) scans that comply with scan extent protocol in an emergency department: a clinical audit and dose ramification study.
audits.st: Departmental CTKUB scan extent protocol (kidneys to pubic symphysis)
audits.f: Overall compliance in 8 cases (5.3%); 142 (94.7%) non-compliant, commonly over-scanning at the kidneys by 4-5 cm and at the pubic symphysis by 1-2 cm.

audits.t: Effect of a quality improvement intervention for acute heart failure in South India: An interrupted time series study.
audits.st: Guideline-directed medical therapy at discharge for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
audits.f: Guideline-directed therapy at discharge 28.1% in the control period.
audits.c: Quality improvement toolkit: checklists, audit and feedback reports and patient education materials
audits.r2: 41.3% in the intervention period (difference 13.2%, adjusted OR 1.70).

audits.t: Remote Mentorship Using Video Conferencing as an Effective Tool to Strengthen Laboratory Quality Management in Clinical Laboratories: Lessons From Cambodia.
audits.st: ISO 15189 laboratory quality management system standard
audits.f: Pre-implementation audit scores (figures not given in abstract)
audits.c: Laboratory quality management training with in-person and remote video-conference mentorship
audits.r2: Significant improvement in audit scores across all sections of ISO 15189

audits.t: Restructuring emergency eye services during COVID-19 in a tertiary referral centre.
audits.st: Audit criteria: discharge rates, subspecialty referral and reattendance
audits.f: All appointments face-to-face; discharge rate 55.3%
audits.c: Walk-in attendance replaced by telephone triage with digital imaging via NHS email for remote review during COVID-19
audits.r2: All telephone consults, resulting in 2639 (54.2%) face-to-face appointments; discharge rate 76.9%

audits.t: Feasibility of a quality improvement project to increase adherence to evidence-based pulmonary embolism diagnosis in the emergency department.
audits.st: Evidence-based PE diagnosis protocol; feasibility criteria including data capture on at least 80% of CTPAs
audits.f: 5094 patients tested for PE before the intervention (adherence figures not reported).
audits.c: Clinical leadership endorsement, new PE testing pathway, physician education, personalised confidential audit and feedback, and patient outcome collection (November 2019).
audits.r2: Implemented in 2 of 3 sites; data captured on 90% of CTPAs; feedback finalised before month end; extraction time 14 h per week or less.

audits.t: Quality Assurance Audit of Digital Intraoral Periapical Radiographs at the Undergraduate Dental Clinics.
audits.st: Health Protection Agency radiograph quality standards
audits.f: Grade 1 231 (45.7%), Grade 2 190 (37.6%), Grade 3 85 (16.7%); standards not met.

audits.t: A mixed methods multiple case study to evaluate the implementation of a care pathway for colorectal cancer surgery using extended normalization process theory.
audits.st: Colorectal cancer surgery care pathway protocol adherence
audits.f: Mean protocol adherence 56% before implementation.
audits.c: Implementation of a care pathway for colorectal cancer surgery.
audits.r2: Mean protocol adherence 62%; mean LOS fell by 2.1 days.

audits.t: Inadequate completion of advance care directives by individuals with dementia: national audit of health and aged care facilities.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 60.8% (n=844) had ACP documentation; 31.6% (n=438) had a self-completed advance care directive; 29.3% (n=406) had ACP completed by someone else.

audits.t: Developmentally Supportive Positioning Policy for Preterm Low Birth Weight Infants in a Tertiary Care Neonatal Unit: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Developmentally supportive positioning of preterm infants
audits.st: Optimum positioning defined as Infant Position Assessment Tool (IPAT) score of 8 or more; aim to improve positioning by 50%
audits.f: 16.6% of infants had optimum position at baseline; mean IPAT 3.4 (1.4).
audits.c: PDSA cycles of educational sessions, positioning audits, low-cost nesting aids and training of mothers.
audits.r2: Mean IPAT score improved to 9.2 (2.8); optimum positioning maintained in 83.3% during sustenance phase.

audits.t: Audit of Anesthetic Equipment in Veterinary Clinics in Spain and Portugal.
audits.st: Modified human anaesthetic machine check system; vaporiser error 20% or less
audits.f: 42.7% of machines non-conforming, 26.4% conforming and 30.9% repaired in situ; 27.1% of isoflurane and 35.9% of sevoflurane vaporisers incorrect.

audits.t: Using Lean Six Sigma techniques to improve efficiency in outpatient ophthalmology clinics.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 19.4 patients per 240-minute session; median in-clinic time 131 minutes (IQR 133, 84-217 minutes).
audits.c: Lean Six Sigma: clinic schedule amendments, dedicated postoperative clinics and clear documentation templates.
audits.r2: Patients per session increased 9% to 21.1 (p = 0.016); significant reduction in in-clinic duration.

audits.t: Improving SCD compliance in trauma patients at Kings County Hospital Center: a quality improvement report.
audits.st: Mechanical VTE prophylaxis (SCD) as standard of care; aim to increase SCD compliance by 30% in 4 weeks
audits.f: Baseline SCD compliance 45% (morning 45%, afternoon 48.5%).
audits.c: Patient education flyer and short educational sessions on VTE risk and SCD use over three PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: Overall compliance 60% (morning 45%, afternoon 53%); aim not achieved.

audits.t: A student and staff collaborative audit exploring the food and drinks available from a dental teaching hospital outlet.
audits.tp: Healthy food and drink availability in hospitals
audits.st: NHS England CQUIN 1b (e.g. 80% of drinks under 5 g sugar/100 ml)
audits.f: Only cold and hot drinks met the 80% sugar target; a third of packaged biscuits and 50% of cakes and pastries exceeded 250 kcal per portion.

audits.t: Outcome of audit and education on blood transfusion practice in obstetrics setting.
audits.st: RCOG blood transfusion in obstetrics guidance (Green-top Guideline no. 47)
audits.f: 214 transfusion episodes in 51 patients; FFP was the most misused component, then whole blood; whole blood 34.5%, single unit transfusion 23.3%.
audits.c: Targeted education on blood transfusion practice.
audits.r2: 181 episodes in 43 patients; whole blood fell to 14.4%, single unit transfusion 18.2%, cryoprecipitate use 6.6%; inappropriate PRBC and FFP use fell significantly.

audits.t: An audit of the cervical screening programme in the National Drug Treatment Centre (NDTC).
audits.st: NDTC Cervical Screening guidelines (derived from CervicalCheck)
audits.f: Adherence 33% (14/43)

audits.t: Writing's on the wall: improving the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist.
audits.st: Adapted WHO Surgical Safety Checklist; target 90% compliance and engagement by April 2019
audits.f: 'Sign In' compliance 55%; 'Time Out' compliance 91%; whole-team engagement 58%
audits.c: Wall-mounted checklist replacing paper checklist, refined items, and 'Time Out' moved to immediately before knife to skin

audits.t: The assessment and management of thermal burn injuries in a UK ambulance service: a clinical audit.
audits.st: Evidence-based prehospital thermal burn management (cooling, pain assessment, analgesia, reassessment, dressings)
audits.f: Adequate cooling 35%; pain assessed 87%; analgesia given 75%; pain reassessed after analgesia 54%; near 100% avoided hydrogel dressings and topical medicines.

audits.t: Auditing local methods for quality assurance in radiotherapy using the same set of predefined treatment plans.
audits.st: Independent audit measurements of predefined IMRT and VMAT plans
audits.f: Audit agreed with local QA in 92% (ionisation chamber), 88% (array) and 76% (film) of measurements.

audits.t: A multinational audit of small field output factors calculated by treatment planning systems used in radiotherapy.
audits.st: Action limit ±3% for 2 × 2 cm² field and ±2% for other fields versus reference output factors
audits.f: 30% and 31% of calculated 2 × 2 cm² output factors exceeded the 3% action limit for 6 MV and higher than 6 MV beams; over 200 beams collected.

audits.t: Dosimetric end-to-end tests in a national audit of 3D conformal radiotherapy.
