audits.t: A Quality Improvement Approach to Reduce 30-day Readmissions and Mortality in Patients with Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
audits.st: Heart failure guideline compliance
audits.f: 30-day readmissions 36.0%; mortality 4.0%.

audits.t: A multimodal quality improvement approach to promote normothermia in very preterm infants.
audits.st: National Neonatal Audit Programme: 90% normothermia on admission in infants born under 30 weeks
audits.f: Normothermia 58%.
audits.c: Phase 1 (2011-2016) low-fidelity simulation; phase 2 (2017) in situ simulation, videos, allocated thermal care team member, thermal care protocol, 'lollipop man' coordinator, monthly feedback and servo-controlled continuous temperature monitoring.
audits.r2: 90% normothermia standard achieved in 2018, just short in 2019 due to more hyperthermia.

audits.t: Clinical Audit on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Management in Primary Care: A Quality Improvement Project from Hong Kong.
audits.st: Six evidence-based audit criteria for COPD care
audits.f: Of 3102 active smokers, 1788 (57.6%) referred for smoking cessation and 1578 (50.9%) attended; influenza vaccine 4866 (46.9%); pneumococcal vaccine 4227 (40.7%); spirometry 1983 (19.1%); AECOPD admission 1327 (12.8%).
audits.c: Series of quality improvement strategies in a one-year implementation phase (systematic team approach)
audits.r2: All criteria significantly improved, with marked rises in vaccine uptake and spirometry; AECOPD admission rate fell to 9.6%.

audits.t: An Audit of CT Chest Reports and Their Potential Impact on the Workup of Patients with Suspected Lung Cancer.
audits.st: Current guidelines for lung cancer diagnosis and staging
audits.f: Only 12% of CT reports had guideline-concordant imaging recommendations (PET suggested in 6%); invasive procedures suggested in one fifth, 58% of these guideline-concordant.

audits.t: Clinical audit on assessment of non-glycemic parameters in diabetic patients by physicians.
audits.st: RSSDI (Research Society for the Study of Diabetes in India) screening criteria (9 recommended)
audits.f: Blood pressure at every visit about 95%; smoking cessation counselling 90%; microalbuminuria, retinopathy and neuropathy screening about 60% or less; 90% had only 4 of 9 recommended screens.

audits.t: Improving Vascular Access Dressing Integrity in the Acute Care Setting: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Target of 80% of dressings with all 4 corners intact without reinforcement at day 7
audits.f: Existing dressing with education did not achieve the 80% goal.
audits.c: Sequential 2-week trials of updated and new dressings with education, then addition of a liquid gum mastic adhesive
audits.r2: Dressings with added gum mastic adhesive exceeded the 80% goal; no exposed insertion sites and no MARSI in any protocol.

audits.t: Use of a Clinical Audit System in Implementing Surviving Sepsis Campaign Guidelines in Patients With Peritonitis.
audits.st: Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines
audits.f: Overall bundle compliance 9.2%; IV bolus, CVP-guided fluids and inotropes 100%.
audits.c: Audit-based feedback in PDSA cycles with multidepartment input to modify practice
audits.r2: Overall bundle compliance 64.7%; significant improvement in blood cultures before antibiotics, antibiotics within three hours and serum lactate.

audits.t: Measuring antimicrobial prescribing quality in outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT) services: development and evaluation of a dedicated national antimicrobial prescribing survey.
audits.st: National Antimicrobial Prescribing Survey (NAPS) appropriateness criteria
audits.f: 87% of 1154 prescriptions appropriate, 11% inappropriate, 2% not assessable.

audits.t: Feasibility study of hospital antimicrobial stewardship analytics using electronic health records.
audits.st: AMS standards of care and prescribing guidelines
audits.f: 22% of low-severity community-acquired pneumonia therapy episodes were guideline-congruent; IV to oral switch delayed by an average 3.6 days; cultures taken before treatment in 22% of antibacterial prescriptions.

audits.t: Nationwide audit and feedback on implementation of antibiotic stewardship programmes in Norwegian hospitals.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: ASP structures established in most trusts but leadership commitment and implementation of interventions often lacking; 446 people interviewed.

audits.t: Antibiotic use in acute upper respiratory tract infections and uncomplicated lacerations in the Gaza Strip: clinical audit and re-audit.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing in upper respiratory tract infection
audits.st: Best international standards of antibiotic prescribing: no antibiotics for acute upper respiratory tract infections or uncomplicated lacerations
audits.f: Antibiotics prescribed to 52 (87%) of 60 patients with acute URTI and to all 59 patients whose lacerations were sutured (98% of 60).
audits.c: One-year action plan focusing on education of health-care providers and patients.
audits.r2: Antibiotics prescribed to 43 (71%) patients with acute URTI (p=0.002) and to 50 (84%) with uncomplicated lacerations.

audits.t: An international audit of the management of dyslipidaemia and hypertension in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: results from 19 countries.
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk factor control in rheumatoid arthritis
audits.st: 2016 European guidelines for CVD risk and lipid goals; BP goal <140/90 mmHg
audits.f: 44% of those with indication used lipid-lowering treatment; lipid goal attainment 45% (high risk) and 18% (very high risk); about half of 62% with hypertension at BP goal.

audits.t: Case-based audit and feedback around a decision aid improved antibiotic choice and duration for uncomplicated cystitis in primary care clinics.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for urinary tract infection
audits.st: Evidence-based guideline for antibiotic choice and duration in uncomplicated cystitis
audits.f: Guideline-adherent regimens 33.2% at intervention site (control 5.3%).
audits.c: Didactic lecture, decision algorithm and case-based audit and feedback
audits.r2: Guideline-adherent regimens 66.9% at intervention site (control 17.0%); difference-in-differences 22 percentage points, p=0.001.

audits.t: An audit of the British Thoracic Society asthma discharge care bundle in a teaching hospital.
audits.st: British Thoracic Society Asthma Discharge Care Bundle
audits.f: Hospital complied with the bundle overall; 85% had inhaler technique checked but 62% were given no written inhaler instructions.

audits.t: An audit of follow-up services for stroke patients after discharge from hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: A quarter unable to perform some everyday activities at 6 months; 18% received outpatient occupational therapy and 42% physiotherapy; a third had not seen their GP since discharge.

audits.t: The effect of hand hygiene audit in COVID intensive care units in a tertiary care hospital in South India.
audits.st: WHO five moments of hand hygiene
audits.f: Monthly total adherence 26.7%.
audits.c: Hand hygiene auditing with timely feedback
audits.r2: Monthly total adherence rose to 68.4%; overall complete 30.8%, partial 34.5%, total 65.3%.

audits.t: Criterion-Based Audit of Hand Hygiene Performance During Caesarean Section at a Referral Hospital in Northern Tanzania: An Uncontrolled Interventional Study.
audits.st: Criterion-based hand hygiene checklist
audits.f: Long nails 15 (25%); polished nails 11 (18%); hand wash with water 73%; correct glove removal 20 (33%); alcohol rub use 2 (3%); no hand wash after procedure 35 (58%).
audits.c: Feedback, discussion of findings, training, visual reminders and distribution of alcohol-based hand rub
audits.r2: Long nails 3 (5%); polished nails 1 (2%); hand wash with water 100%; correct glove removal 66%; alcohol rub use 21 (35%); no hand wash after procedure 10 (17%).

audits.t: Clinical coding of ICD-10 and OPCS in elective local anaesthetic and IV sedation cases.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: 100% coding information recorded and accurate
audits.f: ICD-10 primary diagnosis accuracy 65%; coding accuracy 62%; OPCS accuracy 80%; secondary or bilateral procedures 83%
audits.r2: ICD-10 primary diagnosis accuracy 72%; coding accuracy 78%; OPCS accuracy 90%; secondary or bilateral procedures 89%

audits.t: Auditing use of antibiotics in Zimbabwean neonates.
audits.st: Local WHO-derived guidelines for antibiotic use in neonatal sepsis
audits.f: Sepsis was the admitting diagnosis in 81%
audits.c: Intern training programme on antimicrobial stewardship and distinguishing 'at risk of' from clinically suspected sepsis, with performance feedback
audits.r2: Sepsis admitting diagnosis 59%; substantial decrease in antibiotic use (figures not reported)

audits.t: National audit of seven-day working care in radiology.
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists guidance on providing seven-day acute care
audits.f: 96% have a diagnostic radiologist rota for acute cases; 48% lack a fully staffed 24/7 consultant interventional radiology rota; MRI radiographer availability 18.8% to 63.9%.

audits.t: Examining the frequency and concomitant dose of geometric verification imaging for patients undergoing proton beam therapy for ocular tumours; an audit of current clinical practice.
audits.tp: Imaging dose in ocular proton beam therapy
audits.st: Ionising Radiation (Medical Exposure) Regulations audit context
audits.f: Patients with no clips visible needed mean 14.6 vs 9.6 image pairs (p = 2.74 × 10^-6), an additional 1.5 mGy.

audits.t: Provision of acute medicine services for pregnant women in UK hospitals: Data from the Society for Acute Medicine Benchmarking Audit 2019.
audits.tp: Acute medical care of pregnant women
audits.st: National recommendations for acute medical care in pregnancy
audits.f: 5.5% had an acute medicine consultant trained in obstetric medicine; 38% had a named maternal medicine lead; 64 units had local guidelines; 43% had a VTE in pregnancy guideline.

audits.t: An audit of gynae-oncology practices in ovarian cancer treatment based on enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocol amongst two gynae-oncology units, in UK and in Pakistan.
audits.st: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocol
audits.f: 50 patients per centre; mechanical bowel preparation in 47 (94%) of Pakistani patients vs 1 (2%) in the ERAS unit; nil-by-mouth duration, nasogastric tube and drain use differed significantly.

audits.t: Implementation of an acute tonsillitis management protocol within a clinical decisions unit.
audits.st: Standardised acute tonsillitis management protocol (five initial treatments)
audits.f: Median two of five initial treatments; admission rate 0.79
audits.c: Acute tonsillitis management protocol within a formal clinical decisions unit pathway
audits.r2: Second cycle: median three of five initial treatments (z = 2.959, p = 0.003); admission rate 0.48, relative risk reduction 39.2% (95% CI 0.380-0.972; p = 0.038)

audits.t: An audit of Zimbabwean public sector diagnostic ultrasound services.
audits.st: WHO recommendation of 20 ultrasound units per million people
audits.f: 66 of 1798 facilities (3.67%) have ultrasound; 99 units (8 per million); 97% offer obstetrics and gynaecology, 33% general abdominal scanning.

audits.t: Therapeutic duplication on the general surgical wards.
audits.st: Target 0% therapeutic duplication
audits.f: Baseline therapeutic duplication 9%
audits.c: Presentation of data and education at surgical meeting, with repeated reminders

audits.t: An audit of the effect of case selection on compliance with a 30-minute audit standard for decision-to-delivery interval at category 1 caesarean section.
audits.st: Local audit standard: 90% or more of category 1 caesarean sections with decision-to-delivery interval 30 minutes or less
audits.f: Proportion with DDI >30 min ranged from 8.3% (30/362) to 21.9% (54/247) depending on case inclusion; 18.5% (42/227) when decided in labour room excluding failed operative vaginal delivery.

audits.t: Evaluating the Need for Integrated Pediatric Palliative Care Services in a Pediatric Oncology Setting: A Retrospective Audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 27 (21.4%) children referred to palliative care; 21 (77%) inpatient consults; symptom management the commonest trigger.

audits.t: Implementation and 1-year follow-up of the cardiovascular ICU standardised handover.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Standardised operating room to CVICU handover process
audits.r2: Odds of greater provider satisfaction 18 times higher post implementation; more team members participated and information transfer increased at 1 year.

audits.t: Antibiotic prescribing practices in general surgery: a mixed methods quality improvement project.
audits.st: Single pre-operative antibiotic dose prophylaxis guidelines
audits.f: 100/205 (48.8%) received extended antibiotics beyond single-dose prophylaxis
audits.c: Daily ward round 'ABBDDOMM' checklist, antimicrobial stewardship education and better guideline accessibility

audits.t: Evaluating the Effectiveness of a Clinical Practice Intervention in Increasing Obesity Data Recording at a Western Australian Country Health Service Hospital: A Quasi-Experimental Controlled Trial.
audits.st: Complete and accurate recording and coding of obesity (weight, height, BMI)
audits.f: Obesity data accuracy assessed as poor (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: 12-month programme of staff education, tape measures, obesity decision tools, recording volunteered height, reinforcement and enhanced clinical coding
audits.r2: Improved recording of height, weight and BMI and improved obesity recording accuracy (higher sensitivity and fewer false negatives).

audits.t: Improving stroke care in Nova Scotia, Canada: a population-based project spanning 14 years.
audits.st: National stroke best practice recommendations
audits.f: Multidisciplinary stroke unit care 22.4%; alteplase 3.2%; median door-to-needle 102 min; dysphagia screening 41.4%
audits.c: Provincial stroke network, stroke coordinator and stroke physician champion roles, and a stroke registry; focus on stroke unit care, thrombolysis and dysphagia assessment
audits.r2: Stroke unit care 74.0%; alteplase 18.5%; median door-to-needle 56 min; dysphagia screening 77.4%

audits.t: Dropping risk stratification with subsequent treatment-risk paradox in non ST elevation acute coronary syndromes: a clinical audit in Iraq.
audits.st: Guideline-recommended risk stratification with TIMI and GRACE scores to guide invasive strategy
audits.f: TIMI score calculated in 5.3% and GRACE in none; invasive strategy in 85.24% and 82.7% of low GRACE and TIMI risk vs 42.85% and 40% of high-risk patients.

audits.t: Prevention of needle-stick injury among nurses in an acute ward of a hospital: a best practice implementation project.
audits.st: Five JBI audit criteria for best practice in prevention of needle-stick injuries (JBI PACES and GRiP)
audits.f: Compliance 14-15% for use of safety-engineered devices and safe use and disposal of needles; safety needle use 16%, procedure awareness 14%, no recapping 47%, disposal in sharps box 75%.
audits.c: Multiple strategies over 20 weeks, including standardised education and training on safe use and disposal of sharps.
audits.r2: Compliance ranged from 40 to 96.6%; safety needle use 95.5%, procedure awareness 96%, no recapping 85%, disposal in sharps box 80%.

audits.t: A QI Partnership to Decrease CT Use for Pediatric Appendicitis in the Community Hospital Setting.
audits.st: Aim to reduce CT use by 50% (from 32% to 16%) in 1 year
audits.f: CT rate 32%; ultrasound rate 63%; nondiagnostic ultrasound 77%; transfer 23.5%.
audits.c: Paediatric appendicitis clinical pathway, ultrasound report templates, and case audit and feedback

audits.t: A UK national audit of the laboratory investigation of phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma.
audits.st: Endocrine Society guidelines on investigation and management of PPGL
audits.f: Most laboratories used urine or plasma metanephrines first line; all in-house assays used LC or LC-MS/MS; marked variation in reference ranges and sample requirements.

audits.t: Cross-sectional study of pediatric pain prevalence, assessment, and treatment at a Canadian tertiary hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Pain prevalence 75% to 88%; moderate to severe pain 78% ward, 65% ED, 55% maternal services; pain assessment documented 93% ward, 13% ED, 0% maternal services.

audits.t: The current status of uptake of European Basic Safety Standard (2013/59/Euratom) requirements: results of a follow-up survey in European radiology departments.
audits.st: European Council Basic Safety Standards Directive 2013/59/Euratom
audits.f: Variable compliance in initial survey.
audits.r2: Mixed picture with both improvement and deterioration; 61% (78/128) participated.

audits.t: A retrospective audit of pain assessment and management post-caesarean section at New Somerset Hospital in Cape Town, South Africa.
audits.st: Perioperative pain management guidelines for caesarean section (multimodal analgesia)
audits.f: Pain assessed on the day of operation in 55 (18%); analgesia prescribed in over 98% but given as prescribed in 32.6%; NSAIDs prescribed in 5%.

audits.t: An Audit of Opportunistic Lung Cancer Screening in a Canadian Province.
audits.st: Canadian Task Force on Preventive Health Care: screen ages 55 to 74 with 30+ pack-years using low-dose CT
audits.f: Under 6.0% of eligible population screened; only 28.13% met age and smoking criteria and were screened with low-dose CT.

audits.t: A delirium prevalence audit and a pre and post evaluation of an interprofessional education intervention to increase staff knowledge about delirium in older adults.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Cognitive assessment tool used in 8.5% of case notes.
audits.c: Interprofessional delirium education and implementation of a delirium screening tool

audits.t: Data Quality Improvement and Internal Data Audit of the Chinese Neonatal Network Data Collection System.
audits.st: Predefined agreement rates for critical, important and less important data elements
audits.f: Agreement 96.1% overall; 97.2% critical, 94.3% important, 96.6% less important (24,904 fields).

audits.t: Necrotising otitis externa and how to reduce length of hospital stay: a complete audit cycle of 77 hospital admissions.
audits.st: National length of stay figures
audits.f: 66 admissions for 48 patients; mean length of stay 12.4 days
audits.r2: Mean length of stay reduced to 7.1 days

audits.t: Implementation of a pediatric early warning score tool in a pediatric oncology Ward in Palestine.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: 16-hour paediatric resuscitation programme with PEWS training; four PDSA cycles including EMR integration, escalation algorithm, job aid, data audits and ward feedback.
audits.r2: Complete PEWS vital sign documentation mean 89.9%; frequency and accuracy consistently above 89% from data audit four.

audits.t: Appropriate use criteria in myocardial perfusion imaging in a tertiary care hospital in South India: An audit.
audits.st: ACCF/ASNC appropriate use criteria for cardiac radionuclide imaging (2009)
audits.f: Appropriate 784 (77.2%); inappropriate 121 (12%); uncertain 110 (10.8%).

audits.t: Pressure injury prevention practices among medical surgical nurses in a tertiary hospital: An observational and chart audit study.
audits.st: Pressure injury prevention guideline recommendations
audits.f: Risk assessment on admission 100%; regular repositioning about 84% (n = 486); patient education documented in 75% (n = 433); skin care, nutritional screening and support surfaces suboptimal.

audits.t: Surgical safety checklist audits may be misleading! Improving the implementation and adherence of the surgical safety checklist: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: Surgical safety checklist compliance on direct observation
audits.f: Observed compliance 3.5% despite documented compliance of 100%.
audits.c: Paper checklist replaced with reusable laminated form, multidisciplinary education and marketing campaign, targeted coaching and changes after staff feedback, over four PDSA cycles.

audits.t: Selective versus universal third trimester ultrasound: Time for a rethink? An audit of current practices at a metropolitan Sydney hospital.
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines not recommending routine third-trimester ultrasound
audits.f: 560 (54%) had at least one third-trimester scan; 463/560 (83%) initial scans had valid indications; 162/560 (29%) were not normal.

audits.t: Analysis and results from a UK national dose audit of paediatric CT examinations.
audits.st: International Commission on Radiological Protection methods; existing UK national diagnostic reference levels
audits.f: Data supported proposing updated national DRLs for paediatric CT head and chest examinations.

audits.t: Improving accessibility to outpatient clinics for adults with suspected seizures from the emergency department: A quality improvement project.
audits.st: Streamlined referral from ED to first seizure clinic (national NASH audits cited); outcome measure waiting time
audits.f: Median waiting time to first seizure clinic 65.0 days (range 37 to 163).
audits.c: Streamlined ED referral pathway to first seizure clinic via three PDSA cycles, with new protocols and patient advice leaflets
audits.r2: Median waiting time 31.0 days (range 8 to 175); reduction in mean daily waiting time statistically significant (t 30.9 = 9.42).

audits.t: Implementing a quality framework for storing emergency department point-of-care ultrasound examinations on a picture archiving and communication system.
audits.st: National standards for storing point-of-care ultrasound examinations on PACS
audits.f: None of the consecutive baseline PoCUS examinations were stored on PACS.
audits.c: PoCUS machine connected to network for PACS transfer, specific electronic requests created akin to radiology codes, reporting proforma introduced
audits.r2: Up to 90% of examinations stored on PACS, mean 63%, over three PDSA cycles.

audits.t: Vitamin D levels in hospice in-patients.
audits.st: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D in all suitable admissions, with supplementation below 50 nmol/L
audits.f: 79.73% of patients assessed had 25-hydroxyvitamin D below 50 nmol/L
audits.c: Results discussed with the team and guidance changed to test all suitable patients
audits.r2: Some patients were missed from testing (no figures given)

audits.t: Quality improvement project to decrease unnecessary investigations in infants with bronchiolitis in Cork University Hospital.
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines recommending against routine radiological and laboratory investigations in bronchiolitis
audits.f: Infants under 12 months with bronchiolitis were receiving unnecessary investigations; mean average weekly CXR rate 25%.
audits.c: Locally agreed flowchart with regular performance feedback using run charts and in-person sessions.
audits.r2: Mean average weekly CXR rate fell to 11% (57% reduction, p = 0.009974).

audits.t: Audit of the appropriateness of the indication for obstetric sonography in a tertiary facility in Ghana.
audits.st: Appropriate clinical indications for obstetric ultrasound
audits.f: 314 of 527 request forms stated a clinical indication; 76 (68.5%) first-trimester scans had no indication; only 29 requests with history were inappropriate.

audits.t: The integration of mental health care act in primary care: an audit of the use of mental health care act forms for patients´ admission and the effect of continuing medical education on health professionals´ performance of usage, based on Letsholathebe II Memorial Hospital´s experience, in Maun, Botswana.
audits.st: Mental health care act requirement for required admission forms
audits.f: Required admission MHCA forms used in nil cases.
audits.c: Continuing medical education session on MHCA forms

audits.t: Senior triaging of ENT emergency clinic referrals alleviates pressures on the outpatient department.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Clinic session overbookings 85%; inappropriate referral appointments 22%
audits.c: GP telephone referrals directed to the on-call ENT registrar 8am-1pm Monday to Friday for senior triage

audits.t: Surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis in open reduction internal fixation procedures at a metropolitan hospital in Australia: a retrospective audit.
audits.st: Australian Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic v15 (2018) and v16 (2019), v16 advocating single-dose prophylaxis
audits.f: Overall guideline adherence 63.2%; 78.3% received prophylaxis for the correct duration.
audits.c: No local intervention; national guideline updated to single-dose prophylaxis between audit periods
audits.r2: Overall adherence 18.0%; only 20.4% received single-dose prophylaxis.

audits.t: National audit to assess standards of care for deliberate self-harm patients presenting to trauma centres with penetrating wounds and recommendations for action.
audits.st: NICE guidance on self-harm management
audits.f: 15 responses (14 English MTCs, 1 Scottish hospital) of 31 contacted; clear deficit in practice, with patients transferred without clear review of physical, psychological and social needs.

audits.t: A Culture Change: Impact of a Pediatric Antimicrobial Stewardship Program Based on Guideline Implementation and Prospective Audit with Feedback.
audits.st: Locally developed antibiotic guidelines
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Antimicrobial stewardship programme: guideline development, provider education and prospective audit with feedback (no formulary restriction)
audits.r2: Overall antibiotic use fell 32%; antibiotics under audit fell 51%; meropenem and similar broad-spectrum use fell 72%.

audits.t: An Audit of Pre-Pregnancy Maternal Obesity and Diabetes Screening in Rural Regional Tasmania and Its Impact on Pregnancy and Neonatal Outcomes.
audits.st: Recommended gestational weight gain standards and oral glucose tolerance test screening
audits.f: 55% overweight or obese; 43.6% gained above recommended weight; 35.8% did not have an oral glucose tolerance test.

audits.t: Peri-operative red blood cell transfusion in neonates and infants: NEonate and Children audiT of Anaesthesia pRactice IN Europe: A prospective European multicentre observational study.
audits.st: Guideline haemoglobin transfusion thresholds of 8.5 to 12 g dl-1 by postnatal week
audits.f: Transfusion in 447 procedures (6.9%); median triggering haemoglobin 9.6 g dl-1 week 1, 9.6 week 2 and 8.0 week 3.

audits.t: National Diagnostic Reference Level (DRL) for nuclear medicine computed tomography-positron emission tomography hybrid imaging studies for kuwait population: second phase dose audit-2019.
audits.tp: Diagnostic reference levels for radiation dose
audits.st: UK IPEM methodology; comparison with UK, Swiss and French national DRLs
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Half body third-quartile DLP 537 mGy x cm and CTDIvol 5 mGy, above UK NDRL (400, 4.3); whole body 684 and 4.1.

audits.t: Impact of a multifaceted and multidisciplinary intervention on pain, agitation and delirium management in an intensive care unit: an experience of a Canadian community hospital in conducting a quality improvement project.
audits.st: PAD clinical guidelines for routine assessment
audits.f: Guideline-compliant assessment by nurses: pain 23.4%, agitation 42.9%, delirium 35.2% of patient-days.
audits.c: 4-week multifaceted intervention: rounds script, posters, visual reminders, education modules, pamphlet and video

audits.t: Increasing use of an endotracheal intubation safety checklist in the emergency department.
audits.st: NAP4 recommendation to use a safety checklist for intubation; aim 90% checklist use within 6 months
audits.f: Checklist used in 16.7% of applicable cases.
audits.c: Interventions to raise awareness and expectation of checklist use, build a favourable view of its benefits and prompt its use at the right moment.

audits.t: Documentation of Assessment of Spiritual Concerns of Adult Advanced Cancer Patients: An Audit in a Hospital-based Specialist Palliative Care Service.
audits.tp: Spiritual concerns documentation in palliative care
audits.st: At least 60% of patient assessment forms document spiritual concerns (90% after practice change)
audits.f: 70.8% documented.
audits.c: Team discussions on practice and a structured 2-hour training module on spiritual assessment and documentation.

audits.t: Geriatric Choosing Wisely choice of recommendations in France: a pragmatic approach based on clinical audits.
audits.st: French Society of Geriatrics and Gerontology Choosing Wisely recommendations (urinary tract infection management, prolonged anxiolytics, neuroleptics in dementia, statins in primary prevention, dialogue on level of care)
audits.f: Important variability in practice between institutions and a significant percentage of inappropriate prescriptions, notably of psychotropic medication (figures not given in abstract).

audits.t: An Audit of the Provisional Date of Elective Surgery Allotted to Pediatric Surgery Outpatients of a Tertiary care, Public-funded Teaching Hospital of North India.
audits.st: Compliance with provisional date of admission for elective surgery (DAES) allotted in outpatients
audits.f: 12% (288/2409) defaulted on the allotted date; >49% of defaulters were day-care surgery cases, 32% simple reconstructive, 18% major reconstructive (P = 0.0001).

audits.t: Mental health diagnoses in adults with phenylketonuria: a retrospective systematic audit in a large UK single centre.
audits.tp: Phenylalanine control and mental health in phenylketonuria
audits.st: ESPKU guidelines: lifelong phenylalanine control of 600 micromol/L or less
audits.f: 220 of 244 patients had a recorded Phe level; approximately 75% did not meet the ESPKU guideline for Phe control.

audits.t: Assessing data accuracy in a large multi-institutional quality improvement registry: an update from the Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium (PC4).
audits.st: Passing score: overall accuracy >97% and low major discrepancy rate
audits.f: 39 audits of 2219 encounters (mean 57 per site); overall accuracy 99.4%, major discrepancy rate 0.52%; all sites achieved >97% accuracy.

audits.t: Widespread gaps in the quality of care for primary biliary cholangitis in UK.
audits.tp: Primary biliary cholangitis quality of care
audits.st: EASL 2017 PBC management guidelines
audits.f: Majority of hospitals did not meet all EASL standards; lowest achievement for optimal UDCA dosing, bone density assessment and symptom assessment

audits.t: Analysis of neurosurgical procedures with unplanned reoperation for quality improvement: A 5-year single hospital study.
audits.st: Unplanned return to the operating room within 30 days as a quality metric
audits.f: 93 (2%) unplanned returns within 30 days; haemorrhage 49.5% (46/93) of cranial returns; median interval 3 days (IQR 1-9)

audits.t: Response to winter pressures in acute services: analysis from the Winter Society for Acute Medicine Benchmarking Audit.
audits.st: Survey questions derived from national guidance
audits.f: All services had taken measures for increased demand; 81.7% had expanded medical inpatient beds and 80.4% had added extra clinical staff.

audits.t: Outcomes of removal of peritoneal dialysis catheter at the time of renal transplant.
audits.tp: Peritoneal dialysis catheter removal at transplant
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean time to PD catheter removal after transplant 84 days; 4 (10%) exit-site infection
audits.c: Practice changed to remove all PD catheters at the time of transplant
audits.r2: 19 of 20 had PD catheter removed at transplant; one required re-insertion

audits.t: Implementation of clinical audit to improve adherence to guideline-recommended therapy in acute coronary syndrome.
audits.tp: Secondary prevention after acute coronary syndrome
audits.st: Guideline-directed medical therapy at discharge (statins, dual antiplatelet therapy, beta-blockers, ACE-I/ARB) with no unjustifiable omissions
audits.f: Unreasonable omissions in first month: DAPT 1%, statin 0%, ACE-I/ARB 14%, beta-blockers 11%.
audits.c: Clinical pharmacist-led monthly audit with feedback report presented to cardiologists.
audits.r2: Unreasonable omissions reduced to nil by the end of the 11th month and stayed nil to the 12th month.

audits.t: An audit of dental assessments including orthopantomography and timing of dental extractions before radiotherapy for head and neck cancer.
audits.st: National guidelines for pre-radiotherapy dental assessment including OPG and extraction timing
audits.f: 89% (129) had an OPG and 72% (104) had a pre-radiotherapy dental assessment; 47 had extractions a median 13 days before radiotherapy.

audits.t: Better opioid prescribing in an inpatient oncology unit: quality improvement project.
audits.st: Safe prescribing and best practice opioid prescribing standards
audits.f: 76% met safe prescribing and 68% best practice.
audits.c: Quality improvement project from September 2020 with several interventions including opioid prescribing guidelines
audits.r2: 87% met safe prescribing and 56% best practice.

audits.t: Is it True Hypoparathyroidism? A Root Cause Analysis of Unusually Low Intact Parathyroid Hormone (iPTH) at a Clinical Laboratory.
audits.st: Pre-analytical steps for intact PTH samples (prompt separation, cold chain)
audits.f: 110 (4.3%) apparently falsely low; 60 (2.4%) normal or raised on recollection.
audits.c: Online meetings with staff country-wide and flyers on pre-analytical steps by email and hard copy
audits.r2: 30 apparently falsely low; 14 (0.96%) confirmed falsely low.

audits.t: Care of Transgender Patients: A General Practice Quality Improvement Approach.
audits.tp: Transgender patient care in primary care
audits.st: International secondary care evidence-informed guideline (no primary care standard found)
audits.f: Up to two-thirds of patients did not receive all recommended monitoring standards.

audits.t: Postcode Lottery in Healthcare? Findings from the Scottish National Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment in Secondary Care Audit 2019.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 26 of 28 hospitals responded (92.9%); significant variation in frailty units, admission routes, staffing, liaison and rehabilitation.

audits.t: Improving critical care patients' sleep quality in a surgical high-dependency unit: An evidence-based practice project.
audits.tp: Night-time noise and light in critical care
audits.st: JBI-based audit of nurses' adherence to sleep promotion activities, threshold 80%
audits.f: Sleep quality (Richards-Campbell) mean 53 (SD 19.89); adherence figures not reported.
audits.c: Evidence-based sleep promotion practice, including grouping nursing activities and reducing light and noise at night.
audits.r2: Sleep quality mean 64 (SD 19.4), effect size 0.56; nurses' adherence exceeded the 80% thresholds by month 12.

audits.t: A human factors approach to quality improvement in oxygen prescribing.
audits.st: Oxygen prescribing quality standard of the National Asthma and COPD Audit Programme COPD Clinical Audit
audits.f: Oxygen prescription within the hospital electronic prescribing system showed poor compliance despite previous QI interventions (no figures given).
audits.c: Functional resonance analysis method (FRAM), a human factors approach, used alongside QI methods to capture work-as-done and identify new potential interventions.

audits.t: Reducing omission of eye drops during hospital admission.
audits.st: NICE guideline on prescribing of eye drops during hospital admission
audits.f: Documentation of ocular diagnosis and eye drops in clerking 41%; eye drop reconciliation within 24 hours 45%; correct prescription 100%
audits.c: Clinician education in mandatory induction sessions and ward posters as prompts
audits.r2: Documentation 65% (P = 0.008); reconciliation within 24 hours 75% (P = 0.0008); correct prescription 100%

audits.t: The Value of Auditing Surgical Records in a Tertiary Hospital Setting.
audits.st: Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (STAR)
audits.f: Baseline STAR scores in 2016 (figures not given in abstract); 488 records evaluated across 2016 to 2021.
audits.c: Electronic record entry system, personnel education and systematic auditing.
audits.r2: Total STAR scores improved steadily each year versus 2016 baseline, reaching the highest in 2021; all domains improved except anaesthesia records, which were already high.

audits.t: Audits of Antimicrobial Usage in a Tertiary Care Center in Hyderabad.
audits.st: Standard prescribing protocols and hospital antibiogram
audits.f: 95.45% of doctors attended sensitisation; 74.24% aware of prescription audits; 72.27% favoured antibiogram-based selection; 77.10% recommended sample collection before antibiotics; 63% of patients improved on antibiotics prescribed before culture report.

audits.t: Image and report quality in non-obstetric ultrasound examinations undertaken by sonographers: Results of an audit of 3731 cases.
audits.st: Internal audit standard and externally set audit standards for sonographer non-obstetric ultrasound image and report quality
audits.f: Rolling audit: image and report quality exceeded externally set standards in all nine years (3186 patients); internal quality standard just failed to be met in the first five years but was achieved in all subsequent six years.

audits.t: Using electronic medical record data to assess chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease testing, recognition and management as documented in Australian general practice: a cross-sectional analysis.
audits.tp: Chronic disease monitoring in primary care
audits.st: Australian guidelines (or US guidelines if none) for risk factor assessment, diagnostic testing, monitoring and pharmacotherapy for CKD, type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease
audits.f: BMI within timeframe 30%, blood pressure 46%; diagnostic testing as recommended 17% for CKD and 37% for T2D; guideline-recommended medications ranged from 44% (beta blockers in IHD) to 78% (antiplatelets/anticoagulants after ischaemic stroke).

audits.t: Assessing the quality of cardiac rehabilitation programs by measuring adherence to the Australian quality indicators.
audits.st: Australian Cardiovascular and Rehabilitation Association and Heart Foundation Cardiac Rehabilitation Quality Indicators
audits.f: Variable adherence to quality indicator measurement; median wait from discharge 27.0 days (IQR 19.3-46.0); completion of enrolled 76.9% country vs 56.5% metropolitan.

audits.t: An audit into the timing of dental extractions pre-head and neck radiotherapy and the prevalence of osteoradionecrosis.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons guidelines: radiotherapy to commence ten days after dental extractions
audits.f: 125 assessed before radiotherapy, 102 (81.2%) needed extractions; 98.7% treated as per guidelines, 1.3% breached the ten-day protocol; ORN prevalence 1.3%.

audits.t: Rates and Outcomes of Breast Lesions of Uncertain Malignant Potential (B3) benchmarked against the National Breast Screening Pathology Audit; Improving Performance in a High Volume Screening Unit.
audits.st: National Breast Screening Pathology Audit benchmark B3 rate
audits.f: B3 rate 12.4% (30% above national average); PPV 7.7% (9.7% with atypia).
audits.c: Consensus microscopic review of AIDEP cases against published criteria
audits.r2: B3 rate 9.11%, more in line with national standards.

audits.t: Delayed antibiotic prescribing to reduce antibiotic use: an urgent care practice change.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing in upper respiratory tract infection
audits.st: CDC adult URI treatment guidelines for antibiotic use
audits.f: Chart audits showed antibiotics routinely prescribed for URI without patient instruction; comparative group n = 598.
audits.c: Implementation of CDC URI guidelines with delayed antibiotic prescribing and follow-up phone calls 10 days after discharge.
audits.r2: Antibiotic usage rates decreased by 12% in 30 days (U = 247, p = 0.023).

audits.t: Review DebrIeF: a collaborative distributed leadership approach to "hot debrief" after cardiac arrest in the emergency department - a quality improvement project.
audits.st: Hot debrief after cardiac arrest (American Heart Association recommendation; Royal College QI requirements)
audits.f: Audit identified zero hot debriefs occurring in 2019 (0%).
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles (March 2020 to September 2021) using staff surveys and interviews to co-design and implement an ED hot debrief tool with a nurse-led distributed leadership approach.
audits.r2: 5 of 12 cardiac arrests had a hot debrief (42% increase from 0%).

audits.t: Evaluating peripheral intravascular catheter insertion, maintenance and removal practices in small hospitals using a standardized audit tool.
audits.st: Standardised PIVC audit tool for insertion, maintenance and removal practices
audits.f: 22.6% did not report a visual infusion phlebitis score at least daily; 48% did not document daily dressing assessment.

audits.t: Quality Improvement Within a Mental Health Setting: Alcohol Detoxification.
audits.st: NICE guidelines on alcohol detoxification (history, physical examination including Wernicke's screening, vital signs, liver tests, breath alcohol, standardised withdrawal assessment, chlordiazepoxide and thiamine prescribing); POMH-UK audit
audits.f: First cycle as part of POMH-UK audit showed greater compliance than other services; breath alcohol level documented in 79% and CIWA in 39% (before final cycle).
audits.c: Electronic patient records; third cycle focused on breath alcohol level and CIWA documentation.
audits.r2: Breath alcohol level documentation improved from 79% to 85% and CIWA from 39% to 91% in the final (third) audit cycle.

audits.t: An Audit of the Technical Quality and Iatrogenic Errors of Root Canal Treatment by Undergraduate Dental Students at the University of Sharjah.
audits.st: Acceptable root filling: adequate length, density and taper with no iatrogenic errors
audits.f: Acceptable quality in 183/480 teeth (38.1%); 4th-year students 41.9% vs 5th-year 27.4% (p = 0.004).

audits.t: Audit of documentation accompanying referred maternity cases to a referral hospital in northern Ghana: a mixed-methods study.
audits.st: Completion of maternity referral forms
audits.f: Completion rates of referral forms reported (figures not given in abstract); 83.9% referred for advanced care, 8.3% for lack of logistics.

audits.t: Evaluating Quality Indicators of Glioblastoma Care: Audit Results From an Indian Tertiary Care Cancer Center.
audits.st: PRIME Quality Improvement study quality indicators for glioblastoma
audits.f: Concurrent RT-TMZ planned in 104 (98.1%), median time to RT-TMZ 36 days (IQR 30-44); 81 (76%) completed adjuvant TMZ, 63 (59%) six cycles.

audits.t: Improving dementia care: insights from audit and feedback in interdisciplinary primary care sites.
audits.st: Canadian guideline-based dementia care quality indicators
audits.f: Chart review of dementia care indicators fed back to 63 participants (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Audit feedback via graphic and oral presentations and focus groups.

audits.t: An audit of patients admitted to hospital in Nepal for COPD exacerbation.
audits.st: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) guidelines
audits.f: All received oxygen; 103 (95.4%) short-acting beta2 agonists; 105 (97.2%) antibiotics; 80 (74.5%) systemic corticosteroids; 72 (75.8%) discharged on long-term oxygen.

audits.t: Care in Europe after presenting to the emergency department with a seizure; position paper and insights from the European Audit of Seizure Management in Hospitals.
audits.tp: Seizure care in the emergency department
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of those with known epilepsy, 41.2% had attended ED in the previous 12 months and only 64.7% had seen an epilepsy specialist; only 37.5% of first seizure patients were given driving advice.

audits.t: Society for Acute Medicine Benchmarking Audit 2021 (SAMBA21): assessing national performance of acute medicine services.
audits.st: Society for Acute Medicine Clinical Quality Indicators (CQIs)
audits.f: Performance against the CQIs was maintained compared with previous SAMBA rounds despite increased admissions per unit (detailed figures truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Evaluation and optimization of antibiotic usage in upper respiratory tract infections in children at a tertiary care outpatient department: A clinical audit.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing in upper respiratory tract infection
audits.st: Benchmark antibiotic prescription rate for URTI; Indian Ministry of Health URTI guidelines
audits.f: Baseline antibiotic prescription rate 14.7%, ranging 4.1% to 53.1% between consultants.
audits.c: Discussions, presentations, posters, guidelines on URTI aetiology and antibiotic indications, with monitoring and feedback to consultants.
audits.r2: Average antibiotic prescription rate fell to 8.7% (40.8% reduction); azithromycin use fell from 21.2% to 14.4%.

audits.t: 2019 British Association of Sexual Health and HIV National Clinical Audit of timelines to be seen, test results and treatment for Chlamydia trachomatis.
audits.st: BASHH/MEDFASH Standards for the Management of Sexual Health Services 2014: seen within 2 working days, results within 10 working days, lab report within 5 working days, treatment within 3 weeks
audits.f: 92.1% had attempted notification within 10 working days of a positive test; 94.0% treated within 15 working days of result; GUM/level 3 attenders seen within 2 working days, results within 10 working days and treatment within 3 weeks met the standard; offer of being seen within 2 working days and lab report within 5 working days did not.

audits.t: Retrospective audit of midazolam dose and intravenous sedation record keeping in a primary care oral surgery service.
audits.st: IACSD standards for conscious sedation in dentistry
audits.f: Missing elements in sedation record keeping identified (no figures given); midazolam within recommended dose range
audits.r2: All clinicians aware of missing elements and able to complete accurate contemporaneous sedation records (no figures given)

audits.t: A quality improvement project reducing adverse events and improving adherence to guidelines surrounding VRIII usage.
audits.tp: Variable rate intravenous insulin infusion use
audits.st: Joint British Diabetes Societies 2014 VRIII guidelines, including use of balanced substrate fluid
audits.f: Hypoglycaemic events per VRIII 0.73 (±1.78); hypokalaemic events per VRIII 0.15 (±0.54); VRIII episodes with hyponatraemia 26%.
audits.c: Balanced fluid procured and VRIII guideline rewritten, with trust-wide education programmes and posters.
audits.r2: Hypoglycaemic events per VRIII 0.28 (±0.84) (p<0.05); hypokalaemic events 0.05 (±0.25); hyponatraemia 12% (p<0.01).

audits.t: An audit of the adequacy of contrast enhancement in CT pulmonary angiograms in a South African tertiary academic hospital setting.
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists guideline: ≤11% of CTPAs inadequately enhanced
audits.f: Inadequate enhancement in 19% (12/63) of retrospective and 20.8% (27/130) of prospective studies.

audits.t: Implementing primary care diabetes prevention for women with previous gestational diabetes: a mixed-methods study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Diabetes screening rate 26% before the intervention.
audits.c: 12-month quality improvement collaborative with audit feedback, reminder systems and practice-led care strategies.
audits.r2: Screening rate 61%; 1 in 10 women received a diabetes prevention planning consultation.

audits.t: Invasive cervical cancer audit: What lessons can we learn locally and where would we stand with regard to duty of candour?
audits.st: Invasive cervical cancer audit categorisation (satisfactory, satisfactory with learning points, unsatisfactory)
audits.f: Satisfactory management in 301 (87.5%), satisfactory with learning points 26 (7.5%), unsatisfactory 17 (5%).

audits.t: Cesarean Audit Using Robson Classification at a Tertiary Care Center in Bihar: A Retrospective Study.
audits.st: Ideal caesarean section rate 10% to 15%; Robson Ten Group Classification System
audits.f: Caesarean section rate 38.16% (812/2128); Robson group 5 contributed 34.97%, group 2 26.35%, group 1 15.51%, group 10 7.14%.

audits.t: Physical assessment competencies for nurses: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Complete nursing physical assessment documented accurately within 4 hours of shift start
audits.f: Complete physical assessments 78%, timely documentation within 4 h 64%, accurate documentation 67%.
audits.c: Methodist Proficient Assessment Competency (MPAC) quality improvement initiative.

audits.t: Characteristics, treatment and outcomes of 589 melanoma patients documented by 27 general practitioners on the Skin Cancer Audit Research Database.
audits.st: Current melanoma guidelines
audits.f: Diagnostic and therapeutic management was closely aligned with current guidelines; most melanomas were in situ or thin invasive.

audits.t: Promoting Progress and Learning from Mistakes: Results of a Radiology Department LGBTQ Inclusion Audit.
audits.st: Locally developed LGBTQ inclusion index (five milestones, total score 10)
audits.f: Inclusion index score 4 of 10.
audits.c: Formation of an LGBTQ inclusion task force by the diversity and inclusion committee, and proposals to address gaps in policy, facilities and culture.
audits.r2: Inclusion index score 9 of 10 (7 of 10 in 2020).

audits.t: A preclinical radiotherapy dosimetry audit using a realistic 3D printed murine phantom.
audits.st: Agreement between planned and measured dose
audits.f: Static fields: difference between planned dose and alanine measurement 4.1 ± 4.3% (range -2.3 to 10.5%); arc fields -1.2% ± 6.1% (range -13.1 to 7.7%).

audits.t: Evaluation of Urgent Retinal Practice and Safety Measures for Physicians and Patients During COVID-19 Pandemic.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 161 urgent vitreoretinal cases vs 302 before the pandemic (p = 0.022); residents and fellows less compliant with safety measures.
audits.c: Recommendations to hospital administration and specific corrective measures.
audits.r2: 391 urgent cases (p = 0.006), with more complex cases.

audits.t: Audit of epilepsy healthcare provision in a large UK category B prison.
audits.st: Standards of epilepsy healthcare provision (not named in abstract)
audits.f: Only 38.2% had a specialist review in the last 12 months; 67.3% needed further optimisation of anti-seizure medication; 12.7% seizure-free for 12 months; 76.4% did not recall guidance on precautions for duties or cell arrangements.

audits.t: Improving the Quality of Paediatric ECG Interpretation.
audits.st: Documentation of 10 ECG interpretation items (8 relating to the waveform)
audits.f: Recording of the documentation items ranged from 0-65%
audits.c: Paediatric ECG interpretation checklist with education proforma incorporated into daily practice
audits.r2: Recording of the documentation items ranged from 95-100%

audits.t: Genesis of improved quality in imaging through a national Australian echocardiography registry.
audits.st: Key data elements benchmarked against the aggregated cohort and international standards (ACC data standardisation)
audits.f: Data completeness 72.0% +/- 26.8% in 2010.
audits.c: Real-time auditing of key data elements, quality improvement pathways and benchmarked performance reports to sites.

audits.t: The effect of a mobile-learning curriculum on improving compliance to quality management guidelines for HIV rapid testing services in rural primary healthcare clinics, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa: a quasi-experimental study.
audits.st: WHO On-site Monitoring Checklist - Assessment of Quality System for HIV rapid testing
audits.f: Compliance with quality HIV rapid testing guidelines ranged from poor to moderate.
audits.r2: No statistically significant effect on quality of point-of-care testing services.

audits.t: Applying evidence to practice by increasing intensity of intervention for children with severe speech sound disorder: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: Research-recommended intervention intensity: dose of 70 or more targets per session, twice weekly
audits.f: Baseline about 30 target sounds per session, once weekly over a 6-week block.
audits.c: Intensive intervention model over 12 weeks using QI methods.
audits.r2: Sustainable increase in dose to 70 or more targets per session; twice-weekly frequency was hard to sustain.

audits.t: Initiative to improve quality of paediatric ward-round documentation by application of 'SOAP' format.
audits.st: Ward-round notes structured in SOAP format
audits.f: 13% compliance with SOAP format despite education and training.
audits.c: PDSA cycles testing verbal reminders, individual feedback, SOAP acronym display, and visual reminders at the handover site during COVID-19.
audits.r2: Acronym display raised compliance to 90%, falling to 45% during COVID-19; visual reminders restored a median of 84%.

audits.t: Paediatric minor head injury applied to Paediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network CT recommendations: An audit.
audits.tp: CT head justification in head injury
audits.st: PECARN clinical decision rule for CT in paediatric minor blunt head injury
audits.f: 20 patients were very low risk under PECARN and none had CT evidence of TBI or clinically important TBI.

audits.t: Implementing a Multifaceted Intervention among Internal Medicine Residents with Audit and Educative Data Feedback Significantly Reduces Low-Value Care in Hospitalized Patients.
audits.st: Choosing Wisely-style low-value care recommendations (blood tests per patient day, benzodiazepine and PPI prescribing)
audits.f: Blood tests 0.54 ± 0.43 per patient day; benzodiazepine prescription at discharge 4.2%.
audits.c: Three-month multifaceted informational intervention for internal medicine residents with audits and educative data feedback.
audits.r2: Blood tests 0.49 ± 0.60 per patient day (p ≤ 0.001); benzodiazepine prescription at discharge 1.7% (p = 0.003).

audits.t: Hand Hygiene Compliance in Pediatric Emergency of a Lower-Middle Income Country: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.st: Hand hygiene compliance at hand hygiene opportunities
audits.f: Overall hand hygiene compliance 31.8%.
audits.c: Structural changes to the environment, administrative changes, education and training.

audits.t: Obstetric triage improvement process using the Donabedian model of quality care: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Waiting time of 5 minutes from arrival to initial assessment, triage length of stay 120 minutes, and acuity-based care for at least 50% of patients (Angelini best practice)
audits.f: Triage length of stay 240 min; wait of 5 min achieved in 6% of patients under traditional order-of-arrival triage.
audits.c: Redesign of obstetric triage from time-based to priority (acuity-based) care over six PDSA cycles using the Donabedian model.
audits.r2: Triage length of stay reduced to 60 min; wait of 5 min achieved in 65% of patients.

audits.t: Retrospective audit for quality assessment of root fillings performed by undergraduate dental students in clinics.
audits.st: Standardised criteria for obturation length, density and taper
audits.f: 80.2% of 653 canals (397 teeth, 347 patients) acceptable on all three criteria.

audits.t: Improving the uptake of cervical screening in pregnant and recently postnatal women: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Cervical screening in pregnant and postnatal women
audits.st: Cervical screening up to date
audits.f: 47.3% (n=123/260) overdue for screening by delivery, of whom 74% (n=91/123) remained overdue at 6 months postnatal.
audits.c: Evidence-based guidelines, flow charts, multiprofessional teaching, information for women (app, social media, adapted letters), extended primary care hours and midwife letters.
audits.r2: Percentage of women overdue at 6 months postnatal improved by 8.0%, compared with a 1.6% national change.

audits.t: Patient safety during anesthesia in Ukraine: national audit results.
audits.st: Helsinki Declaration on Patient Safety in Anaesthesiology; WHO Safe Surgery checklist; minimum monitoring standards
audits.f: 40.3% reported Helsinki Declaration principles implemented; 17% of hospitals lack pulse oximetry for all patients; equipment checklists used in 27.8%; complication records kept in 72.8%.

audits.t: Drowning in antibiotics.
audits.st: NICE IV fluid therapy guidelines (fluid and electrolyte requirements)
audits.f: 10.4% met daily fluid requirement accurately; mean additional antibiotic fluid over 3 days 1,572.73 ml
audits.c: Potassium chloride with sodium chloride and glucose introduced as maintenance fluid alternative, and mandatory bolusing of IV antibiotics
audits.r2: 7.45% met daily fluid requirement accurately; mean additional antibiotic fluid over 3 days 469.44 ml

audits.t: National Emergency Resuscitation Airway Audit (NERAA): a pilot multicentre analysis of emergency intubations in Irish emergency departments.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 131 intubation attempts; first pass success 89%; checklists, video laryngoscopy and bougie used in 55%, 53% and 64% of first attempts.

audits.t: The effect of clinician education on blood transfusion practice in obstetrics: completing the audit cycle.
audits.st: Contemporary society recommendations on restrictive red cell transfusion
audits.f: 426 RCC units transfused; single-unit transfusion in stable patients 6.9%
audits.c: Educational programme for clinical and laboratory staff
audits.r2: 218 RCC units transfused (49% reduction); single-unit transfusion in stable patients 53.9%

audits.t: Managing dental unit waterlines: a quality improvement programme.
audits.st: Centers for Disease Control guidelines for dental unit waterline bacterial counts
audits.f: High bacterial counts in dental unit waterlines (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Daily flushing of waterlines and shock treatment with A-dec ICX capsules.
audits.r2: Marked reduction in bacterial counts with compliance with CDC guidelines in all units.

audits.t: Carbon monoxide: raising awareness of the silent killer in the emergency department.
audits.st: Target: CO exposure considered in 50% of non-traumatic headache presentations
audits.f: CO considered in 0.8% of non-traumatic headache presentations
audits.c: Verbal reminders, then CO posters, then CO COMA sticker placed in patient notes (three 2-week PDSA cycles)
audits.r2: CO considered in 42.1% after sticker cycle

audits.t: Prescribing clozapine in the UK: Quality improvement issues identified by clinical audit.
audits.st: POMH clozapine practice standards (smoking status in care plan, clozapine in Summary Care Record)
audits.f: Smoking status change considered in care plans of just under one-third of relevant patients; clozapine in Summary Care Record in 58% of community patients.
audits.c: POMH quality improvement programme between audits.
audits.r2: Smoking status change considered in just over a half; clozapine in Summary Care Record in 72%.

audits.t: Dosimetry audits in Taiwan radiotherapy departments.
audits.st: Standards for Medical Exposure Quality Assurance (SMEQA) acceptance criteria
audits.f: All measurements within SMEQA acceptance criteria; >78% of photon and >75% of electron beams within ±1.0% output deviation.

audits.t: Reducing Antibiotic Use in a Level III and Two Level II Neonatal Intensive Care Units Targeting Prescribing Practices for Both Early and Late-onset Sepsis: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Reduce antibiotics on admission, continuation beyond 72 hours and antibiotic utilisation rate by 28% each
audits.f: Internal audit found antibiotics started in over 50% of admitted neonates, with variation in prescribing.
audits.c: Antibiotic stewardship programme with multidisciplinary team, sepsis evaluation tools and guidelines, universal early-onset sepsis calculator for ≥34 weeks, education and 48-hour discontinuation for culture-negative asymptomatic neonates.
audits.r2: Antibiotics on admission fell 34.1%, continuation beyond 72 hours 45.3% and utilisation rate 34.9%.

audits.t: The Blunt Liver and Spleen Trauma (BLAST) audit: national survey and prospective audit of children with blunt liver and spleen trauma in major trauma centres.
audits.tp: Paediatric blunt liver and spleen injury management
audits.st: American Pediatric Surgical Association 2019 blunt liver and spleen injury guidance
audits.f: ICU care determined by haemodynamic status or concomitant injuries in line with APSA; contrary to APSA, follow-up imaging was done in 44% before and 32% after discharge.

audits.t: A Single-Center Audit of Symptomatic Breast Cancer Patient Referrals During COVID-19 Pandemic Restrictions.
audits.st: Two-week wait specialist consultation for suspected breast cancer
audits.f: 2019 cohort: 1564 referrals; breast cancer diagnosis rate 4.9%.
audits.c: COVID-19 service restrictions including telephone consultations (not a planned improvement).
audits.r2: Referrals fell by 442 (28.3%); higher rate of two-week specialist consultation (p < 0.05); cancer diagnosis 6.9%.

audits.t: Retrospective audit of CT scans performed at a hospital for surgical patients.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 51 (50%) of 102 CT scans were unremarkable.

audits.t: An Audit and Survey of Informal Use of Instant Messaging for Dermatology in District Hospitals in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
audits.st: South African ethical guidelines for telemedicine (consent, privacy and record keeping)
audits.f: Instant messaging use for teledermatology almost universal; few referrers aware of or following ethical guidelines; no secure record keeping or data storage.

audits.t: Management of hyperlipidaemia following acute coronary syndrome: a retrospective audit.
audits.tp: Secondary prevention after acute coronary syndrome
audits.st: NICE recommendations on PCSK9 inhibitor eligibility after ACS and repeat lipid measurement
audits.f: LDL measured on admission in 93 and repeated within three months in 20 (13%); 48 (30%) had any repeat LDL; 10 met NICE criteria for PCSK9i.

audits.t: Enhancing accreditation outcomes for medical laboratories on the Strengthening Laboratory Management Toward Accreditation programme in Kenya via a rapid results initiative.
audits.st: SLIPTA checklist toward ISO 15189 accreditation (star rating)
audits.f: 15 (38%) laboratories achieved greater than 2-star rating
audits.c: Rapid results initiative: high-level management stakeholder engagement, needs-based expedited SLIPTA mentorship and on-site support

audits.t: Liver function monitoring in Fontan-procedure patients: audit of current practice across South Wales.
audits.st: International guidance: yearly liver blood tests and liver imaging for end-organ surveillance
audits.f: In 2018, LFTs in 57%, alpha-fetoprotein in 8% and liver imaging in 9%; lifetime LFTs 97%, AFP 17%, imaging 49%.

audits.t: An audit to estimate the quality of practices followed during bedside blood transfusion in a tertiary care hospital and role of continuous medical education in it.
audits.st: Compliance with bedside blood transfusion practices, including documented consent
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Continuing medical education sessions for doctors and nurses.
audits.r2: Statistically significant differences between pre-CME and post-CME bedside transfusion practices (figures not given).

audits.t: Implementing delirium screening in the emergency department: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines: all older patients in acute care screened for delirium with standardised measures
audits.f: 16% of older adults screened for delirium.
audits.c: Lean Six Sigma project with education, audit and feedback, documentation changes and team huddles.
audits.r2: Screening rose to 82% at 5 weeks and 92% at 17 weeks post intervention.

audits.t: Evaluation of antibiotic prescribing for ambulatory patients seeking primary dental care services in a public hospital in Ghana: a clinical audit study.
audits.st: Ghana Standard Treatment Guidelines
audits.f: 88.6% (n = 1269) received antibiotics and 87.5% (n = 1254) of antibiotics prescribed were non-compliant with the guidelines.

audits.t: The Preoperative Fasting Conundrum: An Audit of Practice in a Tertiary Care Children's Hospital.
audits.st: Current preoperative fasting guidelines
audits.f: Mean fasting time 9.43 hours for solids and 6.64 hours for water; 43.6% of staff believed fasting from midnight best.
audits.c: Awareness interventions on recent fasting guidelines and multidisciplinary teamwork.
audits.r2: Mean fasting 7.7 hours for solids and 2.6 hours for water.

audits.t: An audit of HIV testing practice in people aged 50 years and over presenting with a known clinical indicator condition in secondary care.
