audits.f: A range of antibiotics was used with no apparent rationale.
audits.c: Protocol for antibiotic treatment of tonsillar and peritonsillar sepsis drawn up
audits.r2: Substantial savings in cost of prescribed antibiotics without compromising patient care (no figures in abstract).

audits.t: Internal audit in a microbiology laboratory.
audits.st: Laboratory standard operating procedures
audits.f: Process audit by specimen type (figures not given in abstract).
audits.c: Review of performance at laboratory audit meetings
audits.r2: Improvements in performance scores and staff morale (figures not given).

audits.t: Audit: the use of radiotherapy for NSCLC in the UK.
audits.st: Recommendations in the published literature
audits.f: 121 responses from 54 units; aims, selection criteria and schedules consistent with published recommendations; more than 90% of treatments palliative.

audits.t: Audit of antibiotic policy and wound infection in neck surgery.
audits.st: Local antibiotic policy (none for clean benign, cefuroxime for clean malignant, cefuroxime plus metronidazole for clean contaminated)
audits.f: Wound infection rate 3%, comparing well with published studies; no major sequelae.

audits.t: Indications, methods, and outcomes of percutaneous liver biopsy in England and Wales: an audit by the British Society of Gastroenterology and the Royal College of Physicians of London.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Samples excellent or satisfactory in 83%, inadequate in 5%; bleeding in 26 (1.7%); mortality 0.13-0.33%; 34% performed by radiologists under ultrasound.

audits.t: An audit of the management of acute otitis externa in an ENT casualty clinic.
audits.tp: Otitis externa management in emergency clinic
audits.st: Locally developed guidelines for management and follow-up of otitis externa
audits.f: Retrospective pilot showed lack of uniformity in management and follow-up.
audits.c: Guidelines developed for management and follow-up of otitis externa
audits.r2: Improvement in overall management and rationalisation of follow-up (no figures in abstract).

audits.t: Improving the selection of children for health assessment at secondary transfer age: completing the audit cycle.
audits.st: Locally introduced protocols for selecting children for medical review
audits.f: 9.5% of children selected for medical review.
audits.c: Differences in practice discussed and protocols introduced
audits.r2: 9.6% selected; no overall change but significant changes at individual schools.

audits.t: Third molar surgery: an audit of the indications for surgery, post-operative complaints and patient satisfaction.
audits.st: Clinically sound indications for third molar surgery
audits.f: Over half of patients did not have clinically sound indications for surgery.

audits.t: A general practitioner's audit of paediatric secondary care of asthma.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Auditing the quality of care in emergency departments.
audits.st: Physician panel criteria for management of six chief complaints (provisional standards)
audits.f: Cases not meeting standards: chest pain 51% (36), abdominal pain 35% (35), wounds 51% (51), sore throat 43% (22).
audits.r2: Being tabulated; preliminary findings indicate an improvement in cases meeting criteria.

audits.t: Audit on myocardial infarction in a district general hospital: is there room for improvement in diagnostic accuracy?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 26% of patients with final diagnosis of MI were not correctly diagnosed on admission; 51% did not receive thrombolysis, mainly because diagnosis was missed.

audits.t: Audit of guidelines for effective control of chemotherapy and radiotherapy induced emesis.
audits.st: Audit criteria: 80% control with first courses; 85% control with subsequent courses; 90% lack of anticipatory nausea
audits.f: Criteria met in two of three: 82% control for first courses, 83% for subsequent courses, 90% lack of anticipatory nausea.
audits.c: Minor modifications made to the guidelines after the audit (not re-audited)

audits.t: Written information for transurethral resection of the prostate--a national audit.
audits.st: Nominally comprehensive list of topics for TURP information sheets
audits.f: 111 replies (34%); only 56 used information sheets; 12% omitted retrograde ejaculation and 19% did not discuss the need for a catheter.

audits.t: Duplex ultrasound surveillance of infrainguinal bypass grafts: auditing the process.
audits.st: Surveillance protocol: duplex scans at 6 weeks, 3, 6, 9 and 12 months
audits.f: 208 (94.5%) grafts available for surveillance; 57 (27%) had V1/V2 ratio of 1.5 or more, 25 of which occluded; 18 interventions; median 2 months from positive duplex to investigation.

audits.t: Audit of the management of patients with refractory epilepsy.
audits.st: Rational antiepileptic drug therapy (monotherapy where possible)
audits.f: 22% on monotherapy and 43% on three or more AEDs.
audits.c: Attempts to rationalise antiepileptic drug therapy.
audits.r2: 16% on monotherapy and 28% on three or more AEDs; 22 patients had significant seizure deterioration.

audits.t: PUVA and methotrexate therapy of psoriasis: how closely do dermatology departments follow treatment guidelines? Psoriasis Audit Workgroup of the British Association of Dermatologists.
audits.st: Published BAD treatment guidelines for psoriasis
audits.f: 108 PUVA and 118 methotrexate casenotes. Well documented: psoralen dose 91%, cumulative UVA 81%, pretreatment FBC 91%, LFT 84%. Poor: skin cancer history 66% undocumented, photoactive drugs 32%, liver disease history 36%; no contraception advice noted in 29/32 PUVA and 52/63 methotrexate females.

audits.t: The effect of audit and feedback on data recording in the accident and emergency department.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: GCS recorded for head injuries in 162/401 (40%); diagnostic coding (Hospital A) 1335/4406 (30%).
audits.c: Active feedback (data presentation and discussion) at 6 and 11 weeks
audits.r2: GCS recorded in 220/244 (90%); coding 2712/3530 (77%) after second feedback.

audits.t: Changing physicians' behavior using combined strategies and an evidence-based protocol.
audits.st: Evidence-based hospital protocol to discontinue superficial cultures in neonatal infection assessment
audits.f: Superficial cultures performed in 50.5%.
audits.c: Evidence-based protocol, opinion leader, CME rounds, immediate feedback to physicians and barriers to accessing microbiological tests.

audits.t: Reproducibility of bone ages when performed by radiology registrars: an audit of Tanner and Whitehouse II versus Greulich and Pyle methods.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average interobserver spread 0.74 years for TW2 v 0.96 years for Greulich and Pyle (not significant at 5%); TW2 intraobserver variation 0.33 years (95% limits -0.87 to +1.53); mean time 7.9 min for TW2 v 1.4 min for GP.
audits.c: Routine departmental bone age method changed from TW2 to Greulich and Pyle after clinical discussion.

audits.t: An audit of the factors involved in new patient non-attendance in a dermatology out-patient department.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall new patient non-attendance rate 19%; no significant differences between attenders and non-attenders.

audits.t: An audit of the role of the sonographer in non-obstetric ultrasound.
audits.st: Local agreed standards for sonographer involvement in non-obstetric ultrasound
audits.f: Sonographer report accurate in 94% of cases; radiologist added comments in 6.3% and significantly altered the report in 0.7%; agreed standards met.

audits.t: Appropriate use of upper gastrointestinal endoscopy--a prospective audit. Steering Group of the Upper Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Audit Committee.
audits.st: Appropriateness judged by a panel of seven British gastroenterologists and by the American Rand criteria
audits.f: 45/400 (11%) cases inappropriate by British panel v 120 (31%) by Rand criteria software.

audits.t: Audit of transfer of head-injured patients to a stand-alone neurosurgical unit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 89% were intubated; hypoxia 9.7%, hypercarbia 25.9%; arterial pressure monitored in only 50% of transfers; 28.9% of intubated patients got no sedation.

audits.t: Audit of emergency throughput in a regional plastic surgery unit.
audits.tp: Emergency theatre delays and NCEPOD timing
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean delay from injury to operation was 16.9 h; 38% of operations took place after 2300 hours.

audits.t: Asthma: audit of peak flow rate guidelines for admission and discharge.
audits.st: Admission and discharge guidelines based on peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR)
audits.f: Children admitted with PEFR >= 40% expected after treatment: 43% (44/101); with PEFR > 60%: 23% (12/52).
audits.c: Introduction of PEFR-based admission and discharge guidelines.
audits.r2: Children admitted with PEFR >= 40% expected: 26% (38/145); with PEFR > 60%: 5% (4/80).

audits.t: An audit of the insulin tolerance test in adult subjects in an acute investigation unit over one year.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: The test was technically successful in all but 5; one significant adverse event with full recovery.

audits.t: An audit of a radiographer based ultrasound service.
audits.st: Independent radiologist examination and report as comparator
audits.f: 42 patients normal; 75 diagnoses in 58 patients; discrepancies in 20 observations; one relevant error by the auditing radiologist and three by the standard service.

audits.t: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy in England and Wales: results of an audit by the Royal College of Surgeons of England.
audits.st: Comparison with world literature (9322 laparoscopic cases) and other national audits
audits.f: Laparoscopic: conversion 175/3319 (5.2%), mortality 0.15% (5/3319), major complications 2.1%, minor 5.9%, bile duct injury 11/3319 (0.33%) v 0.06% (4/8035) after open.

audits.t: Emerging standards for diabetes care from a city-wide primary care audit.
audits.tp: Diabetes care processes in primary care
audits.st: Peer group standards of mean performance and of excellence derived from aggregated practice data
audits.f: Checks in preceding year: HbA1c 56.8%, weight or BMI 67.8%, foot pulses 37.3%, ankle reflexes 31.3%, proteinuria 60%, fundoscopy 48.2%, blood pressure 81.1%, cholesterol or lipids 34%.
audits.c: Standards fed back to practices so they could compare with the city mean and best performers and set their own targets.

audits.t: A clinical infection control audit programme: evaluation of an audit tool used by infection control nurses to monitor standards and assess effective staff training.
audits.st: Infection control standards measured with a modified Derbyshire audit tool
audits.f: Audit tool could be used effectively in any district but needed modifying for psychiatric departments; wards with link nurses in Stafford scored significantly higher.
audits.c: Results fed back to wards and managers with an action plan and review date.

audits.t: Audit of complete axillary dissection in early breast cancer.
audits.tp: Axillary staging in early breast cancer
audits.st: Completeness of axillary dissection assessed by independent second surgeon (residual level IV nodes)
audits.f: Residual level IV nodes retrieved in 38% of dissections; tumour in level IV nodes in 5% (2/38) without change in staging.

audits.t: Audit of patients with chest pain presenting to an accident and emergency department over a 6-month period.
audits.tp: Chest pain assessment in the emergency department
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 61% of chest pain patients were discharged by A&E doctors without second opinion; 88% of those referred as possible cardiac pain were admitted.
audits.c: Policy of more open referral for second opinion and early teaching of new senior house officers on acute MI and unstable angina.

audits.t: Audit of a system for dealing with a practice's laboratory test results.
audits.tp: Blood test result actioning and communication
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Practice team questionnaire, postal questionnaire to 36 patients and workload analysis of doctors and receptionists handling results.
audits.c: New system with two receptionists logging investigations into a newly designed results book and date/process stamping of results.
audits.r2: New system as effective as the old but less time consuming; all team members more satisfied.

audits.t: Role of pre-admission clinics in a general surgical unit: a 6-month audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 91.4% of patients attended fit and ready for surgery on admission day; 79.5% of clinic attenders underwent surgery as planned.

audits.t: A prospective audit of asthma management following emergency asthma treatment at a teaching hospital.
audits.st: Published guidelines for acute and ongoing asthma management (Australian Asthma Management Plan)
audits.f: Lung function measured in 95% of acute presentations; history and examination fully documented in 28%; corticosteroids underused and ipratropium used inappropriately.

audits.t: Departmental audit in histopathology.
audits.st: Random consultant review of 4% of specimens
audits.f: High accuracy with no serious diagnostic disagreements, though some errors were detected.

audits.t: An audit of the activities of the paediatric oncology unit in Edinburgh, 1982-1991.
audits.st: Treatment according to national or international protocols, compared with national averages
audits.f: 92% of patients treated according to national or international protocols in the last five years; 158/240 (66%) children with cancer in clinical remission.

audits.t: Influence of audit and feedback on use of caesarean section in a geographically-defined population.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Caesarean section rate 15.9%.
audits.c: Three main reasons for the rising caesarean rate were fed back non-directively to resident obstetricians throughout 1986.
audits.r2: Caesarean section rate 12.7% (P < 0.005); 12.2% in the informed hospital v 15.6% in other hospitals.

audits.t: Diabetes care in general practice: an approach to audit of process and outcome.
audits.tp: Diabetes care processes in primary care
audits.st: Published protocols for diabetes care processes
audits.f: Recommended processes completed in a high percentage of patients; adverse outcomes limited and metabolic measures not unsatisfactory.

audits.t: Assessment and communication of conscious level: an audit of neurosurgical referrals.
audits.st: Glasgow Coma Scale description of conscious level
audits.f: Only 30% of referring doctors were fully conversant with the Glasgow Coma Scale and 18% could not describe altered consciousness.

audits.t: A clinical audit of cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
audits.st: Published survival data used as a benchmark
audits.f: Immediate survival 43% of cardiorespiratory arrests; 70% of immediate survivors alive at 24 h and 69% at six weeks or beyond; survival 71% from VF, 20% asystole, 9% EMD.

audits.t: Thrombolysis in acute myocardial infarction: an audit of practice.
audits.tp: Reperfusion times in acute myocardial infarction
audits.st: Local thrombolysis guidelines (appropriate use)
audits.f: 212/335 (63%) received thrombolysis; withheld inappropriately in 8 cases and given inappropriately in 2; inpatient mortality 12% with vs 26% without thrombolysis (p < 0.005).

audits.t: Audit of start of anticoagulation treatment in inpatients.
audits.st: Local guidelines in accordance with British Society for Haematology recommendations
audits.f: Confirmatory investigations in 93% (DVT) and 79% (PE); baseline coagulation screen 52%, platelets 95%, LFT 70%, renal 87%; 33% of APTT and 58% of INR subtherapeutic; 72% of 62 discharged with therapeutic INR; 74% had anticoagulant clinic appointments

audits.t: Medical audit--need for a positive commitment.
audits.st: Criteria set of 18 questions devised by 66 dermatologists
audits.f: Centre B 60% satisfactory completion of the criteria set
audits.c: Policy decisions and protocols established at centre B only; no changes at centre A
audits.r2: Centre B 74% satisfactory completion (P < 0.0001); no improvement at centre A

audits.t: An audit of hypertensive care in general practice.
audits.st: WHO diagnostic criteria and standards of hypertension care
audits.f: Use of WHO criteria for diagnosis rose from 38.6% to 59% over five years; 78.9% had BP checked in the previous year; history taking and investigations suboptimal.

audits.t: Caesarean section audit by peer review.
audits.st: Peer review of whether each caesarean section was reasonable (four consultants and four registrars)
audits.f: At least one auditor disagreed with the decision in 24 (48%) cases; complete agreement in 6/18 (33%) elective and 20/32 (63%) emergency sections.

audits.t: Specialist practice for minor oral surgery: a comparative audit of third molar surgery.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Patients treated more promptly and at lower cost in the specialist practice with no adverse effect on complications or satisfaction.

audits.t: Criterion based audit in prosthetic dentistry.
audits.st: Established criteria for complete denture treatment and patient satisfaction
audits.f: Audit showed where treatment met the established criteria and where patient management could improve.

audits.t: The first 100 cases: a personal audit of orthodontic treatment assessed by the PAR (peer assessment rating) index.
audits.st: PAR index improvement (at least 30% drop in score)
audits.f: Of 92 with post-treatment records, 38 (41%) greatly improved, 43 (47%) improved and 11 (12%) worse or no different.

audits.t: Audit of catheter management provided by District Nurses and Continence Advisors.
audits.st: Previously formulated criteria grading management strategies A (best) to E (worst)
audits.f: Continence Advisors had more A or B graded responses in all areas; with marked bacteriuria 60% of Continence Advisors but 11% of District Nurses would assess whether the patient was ill; 53% of District Nurses would give antibiotics without assessment.

audits.t: Economic impact of inappropriate blood transfusions in coronary artery bypass graft surgery.
audits.st: Appropriateness of blood component transfusion
audits.f: 27% of blood units transfused were unnecessary (range 7% to 43%); inappropriate transfusions were 47% of platelet, 32% of plasma and 15% of red cell units.

audits.t: Using the medical audit cycle to reduce cesarean section rates.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline caesarean section rate 12%; dystocia identified as the main primary indication (21,125 deliveries across both periods).
audits.c: Labour management strategies directed at dystocia were developed and introduced.
audits.r2: Overall caesarean section rate fell to 9.5% vs 12% (p value truncated in abstract).

audits.t: An audit of the use of agreed treatment protocols at a major centre for cancer treatment.
audits.st: Agreed departmental treatment protocols
audits.f: Complete adherence to protocol in 84/100; of 16 deviations, 3 unavoidable, 5 minor, and 8 serious departures.

audits.t: Evaluation of the objectivity of an infection control audit tool.
audits.st: Infection control audit tool standards
audits.f: A few districts had problems meeting some standards, particularly on sharps and waste.

audits.t: A prospective laboratory-based audit of gentamicin use and therapeutic monitoring.
audits.st: Therapeutic serum gentamicin levels (peak above 5 mg/L; trough below 2 mg/L)
audits.f: First monitored peaks were subtherapeutic in 58 (78%) courses; initial troughs above 2 mg/L in nine (12%).

audits.t: Audit of antibiotic usage in medium-sized general hospital over an 11-year period. The impact of antibiotic policies.
audits.st: Hospital antibiotic policies (1985, not intensively monitored; 1989, intensively monitored)
audits.f: 1985 policy showed no benefit: 45 antibiotic entities stocked before and after, dosage units issued up 9.3%, expenditure up 33.3%.
audits.c: Second antibiotic policy introduced in 1989 with intensive monitoring.
audits.r2: Significant reductions in antibiotic entities stocked (28.9%), antibiotics issued (11.9%) and expenditure (6.1%).

audits.t: An audit of aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage: earlier resuscitation and surgery reduces inpatient stay and deaths from rebleeding.
audits.tp: Timing of aneurysm surgery after subarachnoid haemorrhage
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 75 of 92 patients had surgery on median day 12.
audits.c: Protocol of immediate intravenous fluid resuscitation and earlier surgery.
audits.r2: 109 of 129 had surgery on median day 4 (58 within 4 days); early surgery cut rebleeding and inpatient stay.

audits.t: A three centre audit of IVU referrals in patients with asymptomatic microscopic haematuria.
audits.st: Consensus that urine microscopy should confirm haematuria before IVU is requested
audits.f: Only 37 had significant haematuria on microscopy, 32 (31.4% of all cases) available before the IVU request; 8 had no evidence of microscopy.

audits.t: Minimum standards for the management of cleft lip and palate: efforts to close the audit loop. Royal College of Surgeons of England.
audits.tp: Cleft lip and palate care standards
audits.st: Recommended minimum standards of care for cleft lip and palate produced by a multidisciplinary steering group
audits.f: Widespread involvement of low-volume operators, incomplete networks of associated professionals and non-standardised record keeping

audits.t: Stroke audit in a New Zealand hospital.
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians Stroke Audit Package
audits.f: Documentation: heart rate and rhythm 58%, blood pressure 74%, visual fields 33%, swallow 2%, conscious level 68%.

audits.t: An audit of anterior periapical radiographs taken in a paediatric dentistry unit.
audits.st: Locally developed criteria for radiographs and records during endodontic treatment of traumatised incisors
audits.f: Less than half of films and their accompanying records were completely satisfactory; permanent staff performed no better than juniors and postgraduates.

audits.t: Prospective audit of discharge summary errors.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 63/637 (10%) summaries contained 94 errors: 21 (22%) diagnostic, 19 (20%) operative data, 19 (20%) clinical text, 14 (15%) missed complications, 10 (11%) follow-up, 11 (12%) general.

audits.t: An audit of sickle cell screening in a paediatric hospital population.
audits.st: UK guidelines recommending preoperative sickle screening of patients of African, Afro-Caribbean, Middle Eastern, South Italian, Greek and Indian descent
audits.f: 955 (73%) tested were of Asian descent and 350 (27%) African or Afro-Caribbean; only 4 (0.3%) positive, all sickle cell trait.

audits.t: Auditing ophthalmology audits.
audits.st: Criteria for a complete audit (level, objectives, beneficial effects, effect on practice)
audits.f: 1 audit met criteria for a full audit; 11 (60%) partial or potential; 6 (30%) only planning attempts; most omitted plans for change or targets for reassessment.

audits.t: Indicator-based audit of cataract surgery in four neighbouring hospitals in East Anglia.
audits.st: VA 6/60 or worse wait under 3 months; VA 6/18 or worse wait under 12 months; 6/12 or better corrected VA at 3 months; under 2% sight-threatening complications; no life-threatening complications
audits.f: 69.5% met 3-month wait standard; 85.8% met 12-month standard; 88.6% achieved 6/12 or better; 4.2% sight-threatening complications (target under 2%); 100% free of life-threatening complications.

audits.t: An audit of the 1995 Royal College of Ophthalmologists guidelines for screening for retinopathy of prematurity applied retrospectively in one regional neonatal intensive care unit.
audits.st: 1995 Royal College of Ophthalmologists ROP screening guidelines (applied retrospectively)
audits.f: Guidelines would have required 448 examinations vs 764 performed under existing protocol; all 36 threshold ROP cases would have been detected promptly.

audits.t: Audit of maternal serum screening: strategies to augment counselling in response to women's views.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1,774/2,633 women responded; general acceptance but 722/1,774 (40%) wanted more information and a third more explanation.
audits.c: Gold standard protocol, video and revised patient information, and a coordinator for interdisciplinary communication and training with midwife support.
audits.r2: Repeat survey of 2,489 postnatal women (67.3% response) showed improved satisfaction and a reduced, but not eradicated, need for more information and explanation.

audits.t: Audit of the investigation and outcome of iron-deficiency anaemia in one health district.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 109 incident cases without non-GI cause, 19% had upper and lower GI investigation, 21% upper only, 7% lower only; 55 had no investigation or only faecal occult blood tests.

audits.t: Audit of medical students' experiences of paediatric teaching: a tool to monitor and improve clinical teaching.
audits.st: Departmental aims and objectives for the child health attachment
audits.f: 45.4% of students completed the questionnaire; 32% received less than 1 hour per week of protected teaching; 54% did not visit casualty.

audits.t: An audit of treated epilepsy in Glasgow. West of Scotland Epilepsy Research Group.
audits.st: Documentation of epilepsy diagnosis, seizure control and history in treated epilepsy
audits.f: Current seizure control documented in only 39% of records; in 24% no record of who made the diagnosis; birth injury, febrile convulsions and family history not mentioned in over 80%.

audits.t: An audit of film reject and repeat rates in a department of dental radiology.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Earlier audit reject rate not stated in abstract (the re-audit rate was 1.84% lower).
audits.c: Changes implemented after the previous audit (not described).
audits.r2: Overall reject rate 3.06% (1.84% less than the earlier study); repeat rate 0.93%.

audits.t: Success of audit in reducing the time taken to administer thrombolysis and aspirin in patients with acute myocardial infarction.
audits.st: Local guidelines aimed at eliminating delays in thrombolysis and aspirin
audits.f: Median time to thrombolysis 55 min (21-148); time to ECG 14 min (4-34); time to start thrombolysis in CCU 15 min (0-110); time to aspirin 58 min (15-400).
audits.c: Sources of delay presented to clinical staff with guidelines aimed at eliminating delays.
audits.r2: Median time to thrombolysis 38 min (15-155), a 31% reduction (P = 0.013); ECG 6 min (1-19) (P < 0.0001); CCU 10 min (5-70) (P = 0.047); aspirin 15 min (3-235) (P = 0.001).

audits.t: The use of continuous quality improvement methods to implement practice guidelines in asthma.
audits.st: National asthma management guidelines
audits.f: Satisfactory emergency assessment and treatment but poor compliance with patient education aspects of the asthma management plan
audits.c: Asthma education and management service developed
audits.r2: Improvements in asthma control and management skills for attenders and reduced re-admission rates for referred patients (no figures reported)

audits.t: An audit of waiting times in the diabetic outpatient clinic: role of patients' punctuality and level of medical staffing.
audits.st: Being seen within 30 minutes of appointment time
audits.f: 18.8% seen by the doctor and 86% by the nurse within 30 minutes of appointment time.
audits.c: Strict adherence to appointment times (no effect), then combined with more doctors, lowering the patient:doctor ratio from 11.1:1 to 7.7:1.
audits.r2: With both changes, 31% were seen by the doctor and 100% by the nurse within 30 minutes.

audits.t: Clinical audit of ciprofloxacin use in adults admitted to hospital with gastroenteritis.
audits.st: Simple local clinical guidelines for ciprofloxacin use
audits.f: 64% with gastroenteritis received ciprofloxacin, 54% of these culture positive; 20% received IV ciprofloxacin; 1027 doses.
audits.c: Simple clinical guidelines for ciprofloxacin use introduced.
audits.r2: 67% received ciprofloxacin, 68% of these culture positive; 10% IV; 768 doses, saving £1465 over 6 months.

audits.t: Can audit improve the quality of care for routine tonsillectomy?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Post-operative questionnaire audited (results not given in abstract).
audits.r2: Significant improvement in care on the same questionnaire.

audits.t: Royal College of Surgeons comparative ENT audit 1990.
audits.st: Pooled comparative data used as 'standards'
audits.f: 65 of 405 consultants returned data on 52208 admissions and 31240 procedures; mean complication rate 1.39%; myringoplasty success 65%, hearing improved in 53%.

audits.t: Auditing palliative care in one general practice over eight years.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 75% were cared for by the practice GPs at the time of death; detailed data on 64 showed generally satisfactory care.

audits.t: Evaluation of the effectiveness of guidelines, audit and feedback: improving the use of intravenous thrombolysis in patients with suspected acute myocardial infarction.
audits.tp: Reperfusion times in acute myocardial infarction
audits.st: Guideline-based use of intravenous thrombolysis in eligible patients with suspected acute MI
audits.f: Eligible cases receiving thrombolysis: 94%, 60%, 58% and 57% in the four study hospitals; 53% in the control hospital (2593 patients overall).
audits.c: Guidelines with repeated audit and feedback (three further audits over a year).
audits.r2: 88%, 92% (+32%), 95% (+37%) and 77% (+20%, printed as 7796); control rose to 68% (+15%); trend significant in the second and third hospitals only.

audits.t: An audit of peripheral catheter care in a teaching hospital.
audits.st: Correct attachment and dressing of peripheral venous catheters (no named guideline or target)
audits.f: 68 PVCs incorrectly attached, 49 (71%) of these with inflammation vs 5/32 (16%) correctly attached (P < 0.01).

audits.t: The Scottish tonsillectomy audit. Audit Sub-Committee of the Scottish Otolaryngological Society.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Recurrent tonsillitis was the commonest reason to operate; rates varied between Health Boards; 98% of questionnaire responders were glad to have had the operation.

audits.t: An audit of lipid screening and management in patients undergoing diagnostic cardiac catheterization. Brompton House Officer Audit Group.
audits.tp: Secondary prevention after acute coronary syndrome
audits.st: Target lipid levels in coronary artery disease
audits.f: Lipid result documented in 46/206 (22%); 169/206 (82%) total cholesterol > 5.2; only 22 (11%) on drug therapy; most treated patients not at target.

audits.t: An audit of meal provision in an elderly care hospital.
audits.st: UK Government dietary reference values (estimated average requirement)
audits.f: Mean energy provision 1472 kcal, below the estimated average requirement; niacin, folate, vitamin D and fibre below recommendations.
audits.c: Dietary supplementation with energy-rich foods and high-fibre cakes.
audits.r2: Energy provision reached the EAR target and fibre the reference nutrient intake.

audits.t: Permanent pacemaker use after cardiac transplantation: completing the audit cycle.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 16/152 (10.5%) received permanent pacemakers; pacing on ECG at 3 months in 37.5%.
audits.c: Policy change delaying permanent pacemaker implantation to three weeks or more after transplantation, prompted by earlier audit.
audits.r2: 14/180 (7.8%) received pacemakers (P = NS); pacing at 3 months in 78.6% (P = 0.03).

audits.t: A general practice records audit of the process of care for people with epilepsy.
audits.st: Recommendations on provision of care for epilepsy
audits.f: Recording generally good but poor for key items; EEG and CT often poorly directed, therapy not always optimal, little GP review and inadequate counselling.

audits.t: Asthma management in accident and emergency and the BTS guidelines--a study of the impact of clinical audit.
audits.st: British Thoracic Society asthma guidelines
audits.f: Ability to complete a sentence recorded in 63%; nebuliser given when indicated in 97%; chest x ray when indicated in 73%; blood gases in 73%.
audits.c: Continuous audit programme ended and most medical staff changed.
audits.r2: Sentence recorded in 33%; nebuliser 88%; chest x ray 43%; blood gases 33%.

audits.t: Acute medical admissions: results of a national audit.
audits.st: Guidelines and standards suggested by a multidisciplinary working group on communication, referral appropriateness, finding beds, waiting and organisation of clinical care
audits.f: Main problems: suboptimal consultant involvement in acute care, frequent mismatch of admitting specialty to condition, and confusion about admission policies for elderly patients.

audits.t: Laparoscopic sterilisation: opinion and practice among gynaecologists in Scotland.
audits.st: 15 evidence-based criteria for good quality care in female laparoscopic sterilisation
audits.f: 6% of women under 25; over 85% documented counselling on failure and permanency; 88% by consultant or senior registrar; only 22% mentioned vasectomy discussion; 30% of gynaecologists provided local leaflets; day-case use 19% to 99%

audits.t: Audit on the use of prophylactic parenteral antimicrobial agents and the use of co-amoxiclav and metronidazole.
audits.st: Agreed written protocols for prophylactic antimicrobials and parenteral co-amoxiclav and metronidazole
audits.f: 65% of courses appropriate; 16% of courses too long; co-amoxiclav appropriateness 30%
audits.c: Agreed protocols distributed and explained to each resident; automatic stopping system
audits.r2: 72% of 226 courses appropriate; 9% too long; co-amoxiclav appropriateness 68% and use 33% lower

audits.t: An audit of pain management in acute sickle cell crisis.
audits.tp: Analgesia in sickle cell pain crisis
audits.st: Practice guidelines generated from the first audit
audits.f: Pain in sickle cell crisis not always managed effectively (no figures given).
audits.c: Practice guidelines for pain management were developed.
audits.r2: Re-audit showed improvements in quality of care (no figures given).

audits.t: Clinical audit and standard setting for symptomatic breast imaging in South Thames region.
audits.st: Standards set by the Regional Radiology Audit Committee at the end of the first cycle
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Standards set after the first cycle
audits.r2: No significant difference in accuracy or false negative and false positive rates between screening and non-screening units; non-screening units more likely to issue equivocal reports (P = 0.000001)

audits.t: The relationship between audit, research and policy: lessons from a community paediatric audiology service.
audits.st: Agreed goals and standards of the service
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Series of changes to the children's audiological service informed by audits and literature.

audits.t: Audit of postoperative pain control. Influence of a dedicated acute pain nurse.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Before the Acute Pain Nurse: unacceptable side effects with ward epidural analgesia and low PCA efficacy (no figures given).
audits.c: Appointment of a dedicated Acute Pain Nurse with frequent patient review and regular ward staff education.
audits.r2: Substantial reduction in epidural side effects and improved PCA efficacy (no figures given).

audits.t: The RCP stroke audit package in practice.
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians stroke audit package standards
audits.f: Recording of history and management compared favourably with the RCP database
audits.c: Locally developed checklist based on RCP standards used by trainee medical staff
audits.r2: For a number of items, recording was significantly improved when the checklist was used

audits.t: Managing epilepsy in general practice: the dissemination and uptake of a free audit package, and collated results from 12 practices in England and Wales.
audits.st: Epilepsy audit protocol for general practice
audits.f: 60% seizure free, 11% more than one seizure per month; 71% on monotherapy; 88% with ongoing seizures seen by GP in last 12 months; lifestyle information given and noted in 18%.

audits.t: Interpractice audit of diagnosis and management of hypertension in primary care: educational intervention and review of medical records.
audits.st: At least three blood pressure readings before treatment; recording of BMI, lipids and urea and electrolytes; blood pressure control
audits.f: Pre-education levels of care not given in figures.
audits.c: Peer review audit with educational intervention.
audits.r2: Improved recording of BMI, total lipids and urea and electrolytes; no improvement in diagnosis or blood pressure control.

audits.t: An audit of inadequate cervical cytology in a genitourinary medicine clinic.
audits.st: Proportion of inadequate cervical smears
audits.f: The largest single factor in inadequate smears was the individual taking the test (rate not given).
audits.c: Retraining of the staff concerned and an ongoing training and evaluation programme for all staff.

audits.t: Indications for arterial reconstruction and major amputation in the management of chronic critical lower limb ischaemia. The Scottish and Northern Vascular Audit Groups.
audits.tp: Indications for amputation and arterial reconstruction
audits.st: Delphi-agreed indications for arterial reconstruction and primary major amputation
audits.f: 7 (4%) arterial reconstructions and 48 (24%) major amputations did not conform to agreed indications.

audits.t: An audit of antibiotic prescribing in third molar surgery.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prophylaxis in third molar surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Audit of antibiotic prescribing showed potential for large savings with no apparent clinical disadvantage (no figures given).

audits.t: Colorectal cancer pathology reporting: a regional audit.
audits.st: Items previously agreed as desirable by pathologists in Wales, and minimum standards for patient management
audits.f: Minimum standards met in 78% (969/1242) of colonic and 46.6% (579/1242) of rectal reports; all agreed items in 11.3% (140/1242) colonic and 4.0% (40/1242) rectal reports; circumferential margin stated in 51.5% (640/1242) of rectal reports; number of involved nodes in 30% (373/1242).

audits.t: A 3 year audit of fine needle aspirates from a symptomatic breast clinic.
audits.st: Recommended standards for breast FNA diagnostic accuracy
audits.f: Diagnostic accuracy within recommended standards but the insufficient rate was high at 31.8%; positive predictive value for malignancy 99%.

audits.t: Cardioversion of atrial arrhythmias: audit of anticoagulation management.
audits.st: Anticoagulation for three weeks before and four weeks after cardioversion
audits.f: Acute AF: 15/18 heparinised but only 7 had warfarin after; acute flutter: 8/18 no anticoagulation; elective AF: 5/10 had 3 weeks of warfarin before and 5 after; elective flutter: none had warfarin after
audits.c: Formal anticoagulation policy for cardioversion adopted

audits.t: The development and testing of a cardiac rehabilitation audit tool.
audits.st: Published cardiac rehabilitation guidelines
audits.f: Proformas were clear and easy to use and identified current practice and pointers for improvement

audits.t: An audit of discharge medication for secondary prophylaxis post-myocardial infarction.
audits.tp: Secondary prevention after acute coronary syndrome
audits.st: Discharge standard for secondary prophylaxis post-MI
audits.f: 39 of 60 (65%) met the discharge standard; no significant difference between cardiologist-led and general medical teams.
audits.c: Guidelines developed feeding into the cardiac rehabilitation programme; follow-up audit planned.

audits.t: A repeat audit of hospital discharge letters in patients admitted with acute asthma.
audits.st: Recommendations from a previous audit of acute asthma discharge letters
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Implementation of recommendations from the previous audit.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in documentation of precipitating factors (p<0.001), previous admissions (p<0.01), admission ABG (p<0.001), admission peak flow (p<0.05), discharge peak flow (p<0.001), corticosteroid and beta-2 agonist prescription (p<0.01) and inhaler device (p<0.001).

audits.t: Patient dose reduction by audit of grid usage in barium enemas.
audits.st: Removal of antiscatter grid during filling phase of barium enemas
audits.f: Grid removed in 6 of 100 examinations
audits.c: Data presented at local audit meeting; departmental policy changed to recommend routine grid removal
audits.r2: Grid removed in 96 of 100 enemas; 46.5% dose reduction for filling phase (95% CI 38-61%)

audits.t: Factors influencing blood loss in transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP): auditing TURP.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Blood loss equivalent to Hb fall of 10-15 g/L (8-11%); overall transfusion rate 10.8%
audits.r2: Overall transfusion rate 8.2%; 4.4% to 1% in smaller resections

audits.t: Length of postoperative hospital stay after transurethral resection of the prostate.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean length of stay 6.4 nights, median 5 nights.
audits.c: Increased regional anaesthesia, earlier catheter removal and pre-planned discharge.

audits.t: Audit of 6 years' experience of breast fine needle aspiration (FNA) cytology using the cytospin method; improvement through multidisciplinary clinical audit.
audits.st: Complete sensitivity of breast FNA cytology (cytospin method); no explicit target stated
audits.f: Complete sensitivity 79% at the first audit (2314 aspirates in total over 6 years).
audits.c: Multidisciplinary clinical audit meetings after each cycle with agreed practice changes.
audits.r2: Complete sensitivity 96% at the final audit.

audits.t: Routine audit of breast fine needle aspiration (FNA) cytology specimens and aspirator inadequate rates.
audits.st: Inadequate aspiration rate (IR) of FNAs in final diagnosis of cancer (FDC) and category A patients; no explicit target stated
audits.f: Over 1990-1995, IR 16.0% for category A and 18.1% for FDC cases; unit FDC IR 15.5% in 1990.
audits.c: Annual review of each aspirator's performance with individual feedback; counselling and further training for poor performers.
audits.r2: Unit FDC IR 15.1% in 1995 (stable); junior aspirators improved significantly from first to last year.

audits.t: Audit of opioid prescribing: the effect of hospital guidelines.
audits.st: British National Formulary recommendations and Acute Pain Service guidelines for dose and frequency
audits.f: Correct for dose and frequency: 40% (BNF) and 16% (APS); inadequate: 18% (BNF) and 36% (APS).
audits.r2: Correct: 61% BNF (p < 0.001) and 26% APS (p < 0.05); inadequate: 3% BNF (p < 0.001) and 17% APS (p = 0.001).

audits.t: A chart audit reviewing the prescription and administration trends of analgesia and the documentation of pain, after surgery.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England 'Pain after Surgery' report
audits.f: Documentation of pain after surgery was poor; PRN prescribing trends may hinder pre-emptive analgesia (no figures given).

audits.t: New long-stay patients on acute psychiatric units: does audit change practice?
audits.tp: Long-stay patients on acute psychiatric wards
audits.st: Audit standards of care for long-stay patients
audits.f: Not reported in figures.
audits.c: Presentation and feedback to clinicians on their patients' care.
audits.r2: Improvement in many audit standards; little change in the proportion of acute beds occupied by patients staying over six months.

audits.t: The development of regional nuclear medicine audit in south Thames.
audits.st: Guidelines set for ventilation-perfusion, bone, liver, thyroid and renal DMSA imaging
audits.f: Organisational audits in 10 departments found lack of facilities and space; high patient satisfaction in nine departments

audits.t: Audit of care of newly diagnosed children with diabetes mellitus in East Anglia.
audits.tp: Care of newly diagnosed childhood diabetes
audits.st: Agreed indicators of good practice
audits.f: Good education on injection, blood testing and diet; variable home visits; poor school contact and support group introduction; only three units had adolescent joint clinics; 75% questionnaire return
audits.c: Peer review and implementation of an action plan
audits.r2: Modest improvements in problem areas (no figures reported)

audits.t: Auditing paediatric diabetes care and the impact of a specialist nurse trained in paediatric diabetes.
audits.st: Defined outcome measures for paediatric diabetes care (glycaemic control, growth, annual review, education)
audits.f: Only 16% had acceptable glycated haemoglobin; 85% had an annual review (16% background retinopathy, 20% microalbuminuria); before PDSN median stay for new diagnoses 5 days and clinic non-attendance 19%.
audits.c: Appointment of a paediatric diabetes specialist nurse.
audits.r2: Median stay for newly diagnosed patients fell to one day (10 of 24 not admitted); clinic non-attendance fell to 10%.

audits.t: The use of histopathology in the practice of necropsy.
audits.st: Local guidelines for use of histopathology in necropsy
audits.f: Tissue retained in 25% of necropsies, and 72% of these had a histopathology report; histopathology might have been valuable in a further 19%.

audits.t: COVERS for anaesthetic machines: an audit and standard.
audits.st: Extended checklist based on Association of Anaesthetists of Great Britain and Ireland checklist
audits.f: 236 faults found by 24 tests (range 1.1-64%); 65 (27.5%) day to day, 171 (72.5%) non-recurring
audits.r2: Faults on 59 occasions by 20 tests (range 1.0-11.6%); 16 (27%) day to day, 43 (73%) non-recurring

audits.t: Audit of practice in platelet refractoriness.
audits.st: Guidelines on management of platelet refractoriness produced by a working group
audits.f: Clinicians differed on the definition of platelet refractoriness; non-immune causes considered less important
audits.c: Guidelines on recommended practice produced and implemented
audits.r2: More patients receiving HLA-compatible platelets tested for HLA antibodies; mean 50.9% reduction in HLA-compatible platelet use

audits.t: Audit of the implementation of selective neonatal BCG immunisation in south east London.
audits.st: Selective neonatal BCG immunisation policy (1992)
audits.f: Only 11% of eligible infants immunised.
audits.c: Results fed back to neonatal units, encouraged to improve access to BCG.

audits.t: Evaluating the introduction of primary nursing: the use of a care plan audit.
audits.st: Roper, Logan and Tierney Activities of Living model and the nursing process
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Few changes in care plan documentation; increased communication largely not documented.

audits.t: The use of hormone replacement therapy in women with acute myocardial infarction: an audit of current practice.
audits.st: All postmenopausal women with acute MI, barring contraindication, prescribed HRT before discharge
audits.f: 4.7% were current HRT users; standard met in only 3% of eligible non-users.

audits.t: Multi-disciplinary audit and the mental health nurse.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of neonatal intensive care transport--closing the loop.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Three serious deteriorations in transit
audits.c: Nine-person nursing transport team formed, improved training and upgraded monitoring
audits.r2: Improved temperature and pH transport scores on completion; no serious deteriorations in transit

audits.t: Influencing the practice and outcome in acute upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage. Steering Committee of the National Audit of Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Haemorrhage.
audits.st: National guidelines for upper GI haemorrhage management
audits.f: Local guidelines in 71% (32/45) of hospitals; endoscopy 81%; endoscopy within 24 hours 50%; CVP monitoring in high-risk cases 30%; mortality 13.4%.
audits.c: Feedback of phase I data, re-emphasis of national guidelines and specific recommendations.
audits.r2: Local guidelines 91% (41/45); endoscopy 86%; within 24 hours 56%; CVP monitoring 43%; mortality 14.4% (no significant change).

audits.t: A regional audit of perinatal and infant autopsies in Northern Ireland.
audits.st: CESDI Pathology Audit Form 93; recommended autopsy rate 75%
audits.f: Autopsy rate 47.4%; 46.6% of autopsies failed to reach an adequate standard (only 4.9% of inadequate ones from the Regional Centre).

audits.t: Audit of neonatal screening programme for phenylketonuria and congenital hypothyroidism.
audits.st: Locally agreed clinical standards, including treatment of congenital hypothyroidism or phenylketonuria by 28 days
audits.f: All eligible babies offered screening; affected babies treated by the 28-day standard.
audits.c: Annual reports with recommendations communicated to service representatives.

audits.t: Using audit to improve senior house officer training.
audits.st: British Geriatrics Society 16 training objectives for SHOs
audits.f: Adequacy of training over 16 objectives 59%; three target objectives 38%.
audits.c: Teaching programme modified after results presented at an audit meeting
audits.r2: Adequacy 73%; target objectives 69% (p<0.05). Control hospitals unchanged.

audits.t: Reaudit of acute asthma admissions using a severity marker stamp and determinants of an outcome measure.
audits.st: Documentation of acute asthma severity markers
audits.f: PEFR 52%, respiratory rate 44%, ABG 72%, air entry 58%, speech 27%, exhaustion 4%; no patient received FiO2 >0.35.
audits.c: Severity marker stamp in case notes.
audits.r2: PEFR 83%, respiratory rate 81%, ABG 80%, air entry 86%, speech 86%, exhaustion 86% (p = 0.001 to 0.04); 66% received FiO2 0.60.

audits.t: The quality of assessment of patients with chest pain: the development of a questionnaire to audit the nursing assessment record of patients with chest pain.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Nursing assessment generally superficial; questionnaire showed good inter-rater reliability.

audits.t: An audit of emergency contraception: a look at patient characteristics and the effects of a consultation proforma.
audits.st: Quality of information recorded in emergency contraception consultations; no explicit standard stated
audits.f: Consultation information quality before proforma not quantified in abstract.
audits.r2: Proforma significantly improved certain areas of the consultation (figures not given).

audits.t: The use of clinical audit in evaluating maternity services reform: a critical reflection.
audits.st: Changing Childbirth recommendations (Department of Health 1993)
audits.f: No evidence of lower clinical standards in the study group.

audits.t: Getting a validated guideline into local practice: implementation and audit of the SIGN guideline on the prevention of deep vein thrombosis in a district general hospital.
audits.st: SIGN guideline on prevention of deep vein thrombosis; target 90% of at-risk patients prescribed prophylaxis
audits.f: 72.8% (n = 163) prescribed prophylaxis; 54% (n = 122) prescribed correct prophylaxis
audits.c: Local prevention protocols developed or upgraded in line with SIGN guideline; seconded clinician coordinated implementation

audits.t: Screening for diabetes on a vascular ward: lessons from an audit.
audits.tp: HbA1c monitoring in vascular surgery inpatients
audits.st: Random plasma glucose on every admission, with abnormal results (>6.0 mmol/L) acted on
audits.f: 36% had an abnormal random glucose that was not acted on; 19% had no result recorded.
audits.c: New protocol: RPG for all with arterial disease, fasting glucose if RPG >6.0 mmol/L, referral to diabetic clinic if abnormal fasting glucose.

audits.t: Evidence of effectiveness of clinical audit in improving histopathology reporting standards of mastectomy specimens.
audits.st: Agreed written departmental guidelines with six essential pieces of information in mastectomy reports
audits.f: 0 of 10 reports included all six mandatory items.
audits.c: Written reporting guidelines (audited 1992 and 1994), then a reporting proforma introduced before 1996.
audits.r2: All 10 reports contained all mandatory information.

audits.t: A 'fail-safe' screening programme for diabetic retinopathy.
audits.st: Gold standard retinal classification by diabetes physicians (and ophthalmologist) using European criteria
audits.f: Ophthalmoscopy only: sensitivity 71.4% for sight-threatening retinopathy, 33% for retinopathy needing six-month review, 40.3% for any retinopathy.
audits.c: Retinal Polaroid photography through dilated pupils plus ophthalmoscopy, with diabetologist back-up for uncertain cases
audits.r2: Sensitivity 100% for sight-threatening retinopathy, 100% for six-month review retinopathy, 97.2% for any retinopathy (p=0.002).

audits.t: Integrated care pathways in multiple sclerosis rehabilitation: completing the audit cycle.
audits.tp: Integrated care pathway in MS rehabilitation
audits.st: Integrated care pathway expected interventions (variance recording)
audits.f: First cohort: length of stay 28 days; goal achievement 79%.
audits.c: Integrated care pathway monitoring over successive cohorts
audits.r2: Third cohort: length of stay 18 days; goal achievement 87%.

audits.t: A detailed baseline audit of radiotherapy for primary breast cancer: old habits, new principles.
audits.st: Current agreed guideline recommendations for radiotherapy of primary breast cancer
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: The National Diabetic Retinopathy Laser Treatment Audit. I. Maculopathy.
audits.st: Laser treatment within 8 weeks of listing (implied waiting time standard; target not stated)
audits.f: 83.1% treated within 8 weeks of listing; 7% waited more than 12 weeks; 65.2% detected by systematic screening.

audits.t: The National Diabetic Retinopathy Laser Treatment Audit. II. Proliferative retinopathy.
audits.st: DRS and ETDRS treatment recommendations; laser within 8 weeks of listing
audits.f: 95.3% treated within 8 weeks of listing; 28.4% waited more than 12 weeks from referral; at least 32.5-40.2% of eyes may be undertreated initially.

audits.t: An audit of the management of thyroid cancer in a district general hospital.
audits.st: Standards of care based on long-term outcome data and published USA guidelines
audits.f: Of 31 well-differentiated cancers, 13 (42%) had preoperative FNA; of 22 tumours >1.5 cm, 5 (27%) had total thyroidectomy and 2 (9%) radioiodine ablation; inadequate TSH suppression in 12 (39%); only 5 (16%) monitored with thyroglobulin.
audits.c: An agreed interspecialty management protocol was developed.

audits.t: A collaborative audit of the management of hypertension in general practice.
audits.st: Standards based on current hypertension guidelines
audits.f: Pretreatment BP measured on 3 or more occasions in 87%; BP measured in the preceding year in 90%; current BP <150/95 mmHg in 82.5% and <140/90 mmHg in 44%; thiazide first line in 30%.

audits.t: The effect of education, assessment and a standardised prescription on postoperative pain management. The value of clinical audit in the establishment of acute pain services.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 32% of patients had moderate to severe pain at rest; 37% severe pain on movement; 41% moderate to severe pain on deep inspiration.
audits.c: Staff and patient education, formal pain assessment and recording, and a standardised algorithm for intermittent intramuscular opioid prescription.
audits.r2: Moderate to severe pain at rest fell to 12%; severe pain on movement to 13%; moderate to severe pain on deep inspiration to 22%.

audits.t: Current practice in neonatal exchange transfusions: a retrospective audit based at one transfusion centre.
audits.st: Published guidelines for blood products for neonatal exchange transfusion
audits.f: Only 42% of blood issued for exchange transfusion was used for that purpose; guidelines on blood specification were not adhered to.

audits.t: An audit of anthropometric measurements by medical and physiotherapy staff in patients with ankylosing spondylitis.
audits.st: Agreed minimum data set of anthropometric measurements for AS monitoring
audits.f: Medical notes: chest expansion 58%, Schober's flexion 48%, tragus to wall 47%; physiotherapy notes (n=52): Schober's and lumbar side flexion 96%, height 87%, cervical rotation 83%.
audits.c: Physiotherapy-led clinics started in one hospital; others reviewing arrangements.

audits.t: Developing the Cambridge palliative audit schedule (CAMPAS): a palliative care audit for primary health care teams.
audits.st: Palliative care standards developed with primary health care teams (Cambridge palliative audit schedule, CAMPAS)
audits.f: 876 contacts with 29 patients recorded; considerable inter- and intra-team variation in achievement of the standards.

audits.t: Auditing the introduction of a new product to a family planning service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of barium enema examinations in the diagnosis of colorectal carcinoma.
audits.tp: Barium enema detection of colorectal cancer
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Is audit a task for nurses?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An audit of paediatric epilepsy care.
audits.st: Agreed basic standards for correspondence quality, prescribing, drug monitoring, neuroimaging use and EEG requests
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Findings of the first audit were presented to staff.
audits.r2: Prescribing practice and appropriateness of drug monitoring improved; quality of patient correspondence and EEG requests were unchanged.

audits.t: An audit of antiemetic use with CMF chemotherapy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Metoclopramide and dexamethasone policy: 9 of 21 patients (43%) switched for nausea or vomiting; emesis in 15 of 66 (23%) CMF cycles.
audits.c: Policy changed so that granisetron and dexamethasone were used for all patients.
audits.r2: Granisetron and dexamethasone: 8 of 43 patients (19%) had emesis; emesis in 16 of 206 (8%) CMF cycles.

audits.t: The use of audit to improve clinical effectiveness in an infrequent obstetric therapy: magnesium sulphate in severe pre-eclampsia.
audits.st: Local protocol for magnesium sulphate in eclampsia and severe pre-eclampsia
audits.f: Problems with time to therapeutic levels and clinical monitoring of magnesium levels
audits.c: Protocol changes and introduction of an administration and monitoring chart
audits.r2: Significant improvement in monitoring and adequacy of prophylaxis (no figures reported)

audits.t: A comparison audit of a genitourinary medicine colposcopy service against nationally agreed quality standards.
audits.st: NHSCSP Standards and Quality in Colposcopy
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Making decisions about dialysis options: an audit of patients' views.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 50-50 split between haemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis (80-20 favouring haemodialysis in late presenters); over 75% satisfied with information.

audits.t: Audit of prehospital thrombolysis by general practitioners in peripheral practices in Grampian.
audits.tp: Reperfusion times in acute myocardial infarction
audits.st: BHF call-to-needle time of 90 minutes
audits.f: 146 (35%) of 414 thrombolytic administrations given by GPs and 268 (65%) deferred to hospital; standard readily achieved when GPs gave treatment, not otherwise.
audits.c: Periodic feedback of audit findings to GPs with practice case reviews.

audits.t: Sequential audits of geriatric care: measuring change in structure and process and the contribution of clinical audit.
audits.tp: Geriatric long-term and day hospital care standards
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians CARE scheme (long-term care) and RCP geriatric day hospital audit scheme
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Improvement outweighed deterioration in all domains of geriatric care.

audits.t: A re-audit of pulmonary function laboratories in the West Midlands.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Significant inter-laboratory variability.
audits.c: Recommendations to improve consistency and national and regional training workshops for laboratory staff.
audits.r2: Most variables had a coefficient of variation under 5%; improvements for predicted FEV1, TLC, TLCO, FVC, FRC and RV and measured FEV1 and FVC.

audits.t: A repeated criterion-based audit of radiographic usage by a paediatric dentistry unit.
audits.st: Agreed good-practice criteria for radiographic usage (pre-planned checklist)
audits.f: Clinical note-keeping to accompany radiographic examinations was the least satisfactory area of practice.
audits.c: Areas for improvement identified in the initial audit were addressed before re-audit.

audits.t: The challenges of managing gout in primary care: Results of a best-practice audit.
audits.st: Gout management guidelines (package of care)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Introduction of a package of care reflecting gout management guidelines.
audits.r2: Statistically significant increase in number commenced on allopurinol ≤100 mg/d and decrease in number commenced on allopurinol ≥200 mg/d (p value truncated in abstract).

audits.t: Implementation Science: Incorporating Obstructive Sleep Apnea Screening and Capnography Into Everyday Practice.
audits.st: STOP-Bang screening (5 or more positive = high risk) and capnography monitoring
audits.f: Among 314 OSA patients 36% were high risk; capnography used in 76% of OSA patients; respiratory complications in 10.8% (n = 34).
audits.c: Staff education by a multidisciplinary team and a PACU audit tool.

audits.t: Promoting effective care: Reducing primary cesarean births through team engagement and standardization of care at a community hospital.
audits.st: Healthy People 2020 NTSV caesarean birth target of 23.9%
audits.f: NTSV caesarean birth rate 32.3% in 2017.
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles: team huddles using a best practices checklist for labour dystocia and abnormal fetal tracings, and audits of unplanned caesarean births.
audits.r2: 13 of 55 NTSV patients had caesarean birth; rate 23.6%.

audits.t: Successful implementation of evidence-based guidelines in a regional emergency department for children presenting with acute asthma.
audits.st: National Asthma Council of Australia and Global Initiative for Asthma guidelines
audits.f: Severity recorded in 21.4% pre-intervention at the intervention hospital.
audits.c: Implementation of evidence-based guidelines at the intervention hospital.
audits.r2: Severity recorded in 45.7% post-intervention (P value truncated).

audits.t: Over-ordering of ultrasound and pre-operative investigations for inguinal hernia repair at Northern Health: a Choosing Wisely audit.
audits.st: Choosing Wisely Australia: avoid routine preoperative investigations; do not order ultrasound for clinically apparent inguinal hernia
audits.f: 34% had coagulation studies (86% unindicated); FBE 38% (42% unindicated); UEC 38% (14% unindicated); HbA1c 7% (0% unindicated); ECG 38% (11% unindicated); 70% (n = 186) had ultrasound, 25% (n = 46) with documented indication.

audits.t: The "CHROME criteria": Tool to optimize and audit prescription quality of psychotropic medications in institutionalized people with dementia.
audits.st: CHROME criteria
audits.f: Completers: atypical neuroleptics 42.7%, long half-life benzodiazepines 25.2%, hypnotics 47.7%.
audits.c: Multicomponent training and consultancy programme to eliminate physical and chemical restraints, with training in diagnostic criteria and prescribing.
