audits.f: Median targeted CMV screening rate 22%.
audits.c: Formal teaching with an algorithm and nurse educator, electronic order sets, huddle board reminders and regular audits.

audits.t: Post-Treatment Head and Neck Cancer Care: National Audit and Analysis of Current Practice in the United Kingdom.
audits.st: UK multidisciplinary guidelines for head and neck cancer surveillance
audits.f: 30% of consultations in dedicated multidisciplinary clinics; allied health input on the day in 23%; suspected recurrence investigated with MRI in 29.6% (n = 102) and PET-CT in 14.2% (n = 49); recurrence symptom education 20.4%, smoking advice 6.2%, alcohol advice 5.3%.

audits.t: Monitoring for intradialytic hypotension: An audit of nursing practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 876 of 1584 sessions audited (452 usable); 74 episodes of intradialytic hypotension; most nurses assessed before HD and as required (n = 85; 63%), with few hourly assessments.

audits.t: Reducing Unnecessary Chest X-Ray Films After Thoracic Surgery: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Routine chest radiography after thoracic surgery
audits.st: Adapted evidence-based guidelines; aim to reduce empiric post-thoracic surgery chest X-ray use by 25% over 1 year
audits.f: 99% (69/70) received a post-anaesthesia care unit chest X-ray; daily rate of other chest X-rays 1.6.
audits.c: Three 3-month PDSA cycles: education with literature and baseline data, EMR order-set modification, and audit and feedback with monthly reports.
audits.r2: Significant reduction in chest X-ray use (figures not given in the abstract).

audits.t: Effect of prospective audit and feedback on inpatient fluoroquinolone use and appropriateness of prescribing.
audits.st: Appropriate inpatient fluoroquinolone prescribing
audits.f: Fluoroquinolone use 39.19 days of therapy per 1,000 patient days; appropriateness 68%.
audits.c: Prospective audit and feedback by the antimicrobial stewardship team.
audits.r2: Fluoroquinolone use 29.58 days of therapy per 1,000 patient days (P < .001); appropriateness 88% (P < .001).

audits.t: A syndrome-based approach to antimicrobial stewardship in an Arizona skilled nursing facility-Moving the needle through quality improvement.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for urinary tract infection
audits.st: Facility antibiotic stewardship protocol for suspected urinary tract infection
audits.f: Baseline urine culturing, antibiotic days and C. difficile rates (figures not reported).
audits.c: Stewardship protocol with auditing of culturing and prescribing, prescriber feedback, staff engagement and educational in-services.
audits.r2: Urine culturing, antibiotic days for suspected UTI and C. difficile infections per 1,000 resident-days each fell by more than 50%.

audits.t: Trends in Attaining Mammography Quality Benchmarks With Repeated Participation in a Quality Measurement Program: Going Beyond the Mammography Quality Standards Act to Address Breast Cancer Disparities.
audits.st: 13 mammography quality measures and benchmarks (tracking, callback, cancer detection, loss to follow-up, timeliness)
audits.f: Baseline benchmark attainment (figures not reported in abstract).
audits.c: Repeated participation in a quality measurement programme with benchmark reporting.
audits.r2: Number of facilities meeting benchmarks increased with length of participation for many measures, including cancer detection, timely imaging and not lost at biopsy.

audits.t: Nutrition During Critical Care: An Audit on Actual Energy and Protein Intakes.
audits.st: Weight-based energy and protein targets; receiving at least 80% of targets
audits.f: Fed patients received 14.3 kcal/kg/day and 0.53 g/kg/day protein; orally fed patients 9.7 kcal/kg/day and 0.35 g/kg/day; of orally fed patients staying 7 days or more, 51% and 94% never received 80% of energy and protein targets.

audits.t: An audit of physiotherapists' documentation on physical activity assessment, promotion and prescription to older adults attending out-patient rehabilitation.
audits.st: Evidence-based assessment, promotion and prescription of physical activity for older adults
audits.f: No use of validated physical activity assessment tools; prescription documented in 55/56 (98%); goal setting 7 (12.5%); post-discharge advice 28/56 (50%); community referral 4/56 (7%).

audits.t: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in traumatic brain injury patients: An audit of clinical practice in AlRass General Hospital, Saudi Arabia and proposal for future clinical practice.
audits.st: Best clinical evidence from literature review (no local guideline)
audits.f: 8 (30.8%) had mechanical VTE prophylaxis and 1 (3.8%) received enoxaparin.

audits.t: Improving Timely Annual Ocular Examinations for Patients With Diabetes Mellitus in a Primary Care Office.
audits.st: American Diabetes Association guideline for annual ocular examination; target 85% within 90 days
audits.f: 48% of patients with diabetes had an annual ocular examination.
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles: team huddles and training, diabetes education checklist, EMR checklist and logbook referral tracking.
audits.r2: 86% had annual ocular examinations; 87% of referred patients completed the appointment.

audits.t: Implementing outpatient antimicrobial stewardship in a primary care office through ambulatory care pharmacist-led audit and feedback.
audits.st: Guideline-concordant antibiotic agent and duration for upper respiratory and urinary tract infections
audits.f: Guideline-concordant agent for UTI 20% and duration 55%; guideline-concordant agent for URI 43.3%; median URI duration 10 days.
audits.c: Education and guidelines followed by bi-weekly pharmacist audit of all URI and UTI prescriptions with written feedback to prescribers.
audits.r2: Guideline-concordant agent for UTI median 69.2% and duration 70.4%; URI agent 86.8%; median URI duration 7 days.

audits.t: Improving Timeliness of Internal Medicine Consults in the Emergency Department: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Emergency department waiting times and flow
audits.st: Consult to decision time; proportion of admitted patients under 3 hours
audits.f: Mean consult to decision time 4.61 hours.
audits.c: Sequential PDSA cycles: process mapping, resident education, audit and feedback of consult times, and a swing shift at peak consult volume.
audits.r2: Mean consult to decision time 4.18 hours.

audits.t: Audit of paediatrician recognition of children's vulnerability to harm at the Royal Children's Hospital, Melbourne.
audits.st: Documentation of adverse childhood experiences, risk and resilience factors and vulnerable child alerts
audits.f: 8% documented as vulnerable, 21% referred for intervention and 2% had a vulnerable child alert; adverse childhood experiences infrequently documented.

audits.t: Real-Time Safety Audits of Neonatal Delivery Room Resuscitation Areas: Are We Sufficiently Prepared?
audits.st: Resuscitation area set-up of radiant warmer, materials and medication without defect
audits.f: No defects in 534 (62.7%) audits; slight defects in 98 (11.5%); serious defects in 220 (25.8%).

audits.t: A quality improvement project to improve the identification and management of delirium.
audits.st: Unit standard of four to six hourly CAM-ICU assessments; critical care guidelines on light sedation
audits.f: 45% of charts met the CAM-ICU standard; light sedation RASS scores mean 31%.
audits.c: Delirium clinical pathway, sedation algorithm, delirium resource book, online education module and teaching during delirium month.
audits.r2: 84% of 145 charts met the CAM-ICU standard; light sedation RASS scores 41% (41 charts).

audits.t: Using Lean-Facilitation to Improve Quality of Hepatitis C Testing in Primary Care.
audits.tp: Hepatitis C screening in primary care
audits.st: Guideline-concordant HCV screening for persons born 1945 to 1965
audits.f: Baseline new HCV screening rate among previously untested patients (figures not reported).
audits.c: Lean-Facilitation intervention: external facilitation, stakeholder engagement, champions, rapid process improvement, PDSA cycles and audit-feedback.
audits.r2: Significant, immediate and sustained increases in HCV testing (figures not reported); no change at comparison clinics.

audits.t: Service evaluation and retrospective audit of electronic HEEADSSS (e-HEEADSSS) screening device in paediatric inpatient service in Western Australia.
audits.st: HEEADSSS psychosocial screening for inpatients aged 12-16 years
audits.f: Conventional HEEADSSS screening uptake 12%.
audits.c: Introduction of an electronic HEEADSSS (e-HEEADSSS) screening device.
audits.r2: e-HEEADSSS uptake 54% (p = 0.005); 86% of flagged concerns acted on before discharge.

audits.t: The Dutch Lung Cancer Audit: Nationwide quality of care evaluation of lung cancer patients.
audits.st: 15 DLCA-L quality indicators, e.g. brain imaging at diagnosis of stage III NSCLC
audits.f: Brain imaging at diagnosis of stage III NSCLC 80%.
audits.c: National clinical audit with quality indicator feedback to hospitals.
audits.r2: Brain imaging at diagnosis of stage III NSCLC 90%, with reduced hospital variation.

audits.t: Facilitators and Barriers to Implementing a Patient-Centered Oncology Care Model.
audits.st: Oncology medical home standards for accessible, continuous, coordinated, team-based care
audits.f: Baseline self-assessment and independent audit of standards (figures not reported).
audits.c: Implementation of the standards with training webinars and technical assistance.
audits.r2: Implementation of standards increased, largest in continuous QI; achievement on access and evidence-based decision support declined (figures not reported).

audits.t: Prospective audit of blood transfusion request forms and continuing medical education to optimise compliance of clinicians in a hospital setting.
audits.st: Complete and correct entries on blood requisition forms
audits.f: 45.77% of blood requisition form entries were complete and correct; 23.45% of incomplete entries came from emergency and trauma.
audits.c: Continuing medical education for clinicians on transfusion request details.
audits.r2: 76.75% of entries were complete and correct; cumulative mean score rose from 20687 to 30870.

audits.t: Comparison of procalcitonin testing to a targeted audit-and-feedback strategy on prescribed durations of therapy for community-acquired pneumonia.
audits.st: 5 days of therapy for uncomplicated community-acquired pneumonia
audits.f: Average duration of therapy 7.0 days (TAF site) and 7.8 days (PCT site).
audits.c: Targeted audit and feedback recommending 5 days at one site; procalcitonin testing with routine audit and feedback at the other.
audits.r2: Average duration of therapy 5.5 days (TAF) and 5.4 days (PCT), p = 0.8.

audits.t: Reducing Catheter-associated Urinary Tract Infections via Cost-saving Diagnostic Stewardship.
audits.st: Standardised infection ratio for hospital-acquired catheter-associated UTI
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Diagnostic stewardship programme with education and audit and feedback.
audits.r2: Significant reduction in inpatient urine culture orders and CAUTI standardised infection ratio (figures not reported).

audits.t: A French audit of maternity unit protocols for immediate postpartum hemorrhage: A cross-sectional study (HERA).
audits.st: 2004 French guidelines for prevention and management of postpartum haemorrhage (16 criteria)
audits.f: 97.1% had a written protocol but only 67.0% (159/237) a local protocol; blood loss quantification 83.5%; PPH defined in 25.3%; recording time of diagnosis 53.2% and blood loss volume 55.7%.

audits.t: Audit of antibiotic prophylaxis and adherence of surgeons to standard guidelines in common abdominal surgical procedures.
audits.st: Evidence-based surgical antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines (optimal 100%)
audits.f: Prophylaxis given in 97.5%; correct choice 9.5%, correct timing 40%, correct dose and route 100%; ceftriaxone most used (59.5%).

audits.t: N1c colon cancer and the use of adjuvant chemotherapy: a current audit of the National Cancer Database.
audits.st: Recommended adjuvant chemotherapy for stage III (N1c) colon cancer
audits.f: 55% (n = 3071) received adjuvant chemotherapy.

audits.t: How to minimize central line-associated bloodstream infections in a neonatal intensive care unit: a quality improvement intervention based on a retrospective analysis and the adoption of an evidence-based bundle.
audits.st: Evidence-based central line insertion, dressing and maintenance bundles; CLABSI rate per 1000 CVC days
audits.f: CLABSI rate 8.4 per 1000 CVC days; 47 catheter-related complications.
audits.c: New central line insertion, dressing and maintenance bundles and changes to materials used (PDSA approach).
audits.r2: CLABSI rate 1.8 per 1000 CVC days (p = 0.02); 10 catheter-related complications (p < 0.007).

audits.t: Hand Hygiene Compliance at a Canadian provincial cancer centre - the complementary roles of nurse auditor-driven and patient auditor-driven audit processes and impact upon practice in ambulatory cancer care.
audits.st: Hand hygiene compliance before entering and after exiting examination rooms (nurse audit) and within the room (patient audit)
audits.f: Nurse audit compliance ranged from 84% to 96% (7,213 opportunities); patient audit compliance ranged from 57% to 82% (23,402 opportunities); overall 89.2% vs 73.6%.

audits.t: Thyroid cytology in Pakistan: An institutional audit of the atypia of undetermined significance/follicular lesion of undetermined significance category.
audits.st: Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology category III (AUS/FLUS), expected risk of malignancy 5% to 15%
audits.f: 256 (10.9%) of 2342 thyroid FNACs were AUS/FLUS; of 104 resections 32 (30.7%) malignant; upper-bound ROM 30.7%, lower-bound ROM 12.5%.

audits.t: [Optimising drug dispensation by pharmacy technicians: A quality approach].
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Tools used in 52% of introductions and 11% of renewals; administration explained in all introductions but 57% of renewals; adverse events explained in 47%, storage in 9.5%, tolerance in 34%, compliance in 19%.

audits.t: Surveillance Colonoscopy after Appendicectomy in Patients over the Age of 40: Targeted Audit of Outcomes and Variability in Practice.
audits.tp: Colonic evaluation after appendicectomy in over-40s
audits.st: Recommendation for surveillance colonoscopy in patients over 40 after appendicectomy for acute appendicitis
audits.f: More than 80% of patients did not have endoscopic follow-up.

audits.t: Diagnosis and management of paediatric Clostridioides difficile infection in a tertiary centre: A prospective audit.
audits.st: Australasian Society for Infectious Diseases 2016 C. difficile guidelines
audits.f: 44 (63%) of 70 test requests were inappropriate; 17 (38%) of 45 positive tests were appropriately requested; 13 (46%) of 28 inappropriate positives were treated.

audits.t: GRASP Workload Nursing Measurement System at end of life.
audits.st: GRASP workload tool completion after every shift and agreement with the Comfort Measures Order Set documentation; target 90%
audits.f: GRASP compliance 66.6%; GRASP-documentation accuracy 60-70% (4 patient records, 15 shifts), below the 90% target.

audits.t: An audit of platelet transfusion indications in acute leukaemia patients: six-year experience at an Academic Centre.
audits.st: British Society for Haematology platelet transfusion guidelines
audits.f: 75.3% of 745 platelet transfusion episodes in 154 patients were appropriate; Paediatrics 63.9% and Internal Medicine 86.8%; wards 82.3%.

audits.t: Perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis in adult patients: The first multicenter clinical practice audit with intervention in Greek surgical departments.
audits.st: International and local guidelines for perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis: agent, timing and duration
audits.f: Overall compliance with all 3 parameters 28.2%; guideline-compliant agent 89.6%; SSI rate 6.9%.
audits.c: Multimodal intervention of education, audit and feedback.
audits.r2: Overall compliance 43.9% (P = .001); compliant agent 96.3%; SSI rate 4% (P = .026).

audits.t: A prospective clinical audit to evaluate postoperative quality of recovery in adults at New Somerset Hospital, Cape Town, South Africa.
audits.st: QoR-15 score; patient acceptable symptom state score ≥118
audits.f: Median QoR-15 score 123/150; 35% in the moderate category; 59% achieved the patient acceptable symptom state.

audits.t: An audit of ventilation and perfusion SPECT reporting for the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism in a tertiary cardiothoracic centre.
audits.tp: V/Q scan reporting in pulmonary embolism
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 173 (97.2%) had a definitive report and 2.8% an equivocal report.

audits.t: Use of Prospective Audit and Feedback to Reduce Antibiotic Exposure in a Pediatric Cardiac ICU.
audits.st: Antibiotic days of therapy per 1000 patient days
audits.f: Mean IV antibiotic use 880 days of therapy per 1000 patient days.
audits.c: Prospective audit and feedback programme by the antimicrobial stewardship team from December 7, 2015.
audits.r2: Mean IV antibiotic use 701 days of therapy per 1000 patient days (20% decrease, p = 0.001).

audits.t: Development of an Interdisciplinary Healthcare Team for Pressure Injury Management: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Staff adherence to plan of care (audit tool) and hospital-acquired pressure injury rate
audits.f: HAPI rate 5.9%.
audits.c: Interdisciplinary pressure injury team formed, unit-based education sessions and quarterly prevalence surveys (February 21 to May 23, 2017).
audits.r2: HAPI rate 5%; 100% staff adherence to the plan of care.

audits.t: Is Hospital Autopsy Auditing Suitable for Clinical Risk Manage ment? Actualities and Perspectives of Auditing in the Autopsy Room Following Italian Law 24/2017 on Patient Safety.
audits.st: Goldman criteria for class I and class II discrepancies
audits.f: Major discrepancies in 71.3%; class I error 22.7%; class II error 48.6%.

audits.t: Audit of international intraoperative hemotherapy and blood loss documentation on anesthetic records.
audits.st: 20 defined fields for haemotherapy, haemostatic and fluid therapy and diagnostics; anaesthesia society guidelines
audits.f: Fields for red cell transfusion in 29.3%, ABO testing in 6.1% and transfusion indication in 2.0% of records; blood loss 94.4%, diuresis 87.9%.

audits.t: Accuracy of SNOMED-CT Chief Presenting Complaint Codes: an audit of 1,000 cases.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Real-time SNOMED-CT chief presenting complaint agreed with clinical notes in 514/852 (60.3%); 732/852 (85.9%) with free text included.

audits.t: End-of-life care and intensive care unit clinician involvement in a private acute care hospital: A retrospective descriptive medical record audit.
audits.st: Australian National Standard for end-of-life care; 20 Processes of Care
audits.f: Median 16 (IQR 13-17) of 20 care processes met; ICU clinicians involved in 65.7%; specialist palliative care in 53%.

audits.t: The 'ins and outs' of colonoscopy at Wits Donald Gordon Medical Centre, South Africa: A practice audit of the outpatient endoscopy unit.
audits.st: ASGE/ACG benchmarks: adequate bowel preparation ≥85%; caecal intubation ≥90% overall and ≥95% screening; withdrawal time ≥6 minutes; ADR ≥25%
audits.f: Adequate bowel preparation 77.6%; caecal intubation 97.0% overall and 96.3% screening; median withdrawal time 5.7 minutes; PDR 27.6%, ADR 15.6%.

audits.t: Reducing Peripheral Intravenous Catheter Extravasation in Neonates: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Reduce total and severe peripheral IV extravasation by 40%
audits.f: 73 extravasations; 38/73 (52%) severe.
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles: dressing protocol with standardised securement and safer equipment; education on hourly assessment and documentation; extravasation identification and treatment algorithm; escalation policy limiting attempts and using a superuser team.

audits.t: Audit in surgical histopathology at a tertiary healthcare center: Study of preanalytical and analytical phase.
audits.st: International quality indicators for adequacy of clinical information, grossing, turnaround time and section quality
audits.f: Mean turnaround time 3.6 ± 1.8 days for fixed tissue and 26.6 ± 11.2 min for frozen sections; quality indicators achieved as per international norms.

audits.t: Real World Implementation of the Serious Illness Care Program in Cancer Care: Results of a Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Guidelines for early goals-of-care discussions; target at least 24 serious illness conversations with at least 95% documented
audits.f: Documentation rates 4.2% for clinician A and 0% for clinician B.
audits.c: Serious Illness Care Program, a systematic multicomponent intervention for conducting and documenting conversations.
audits.r2: 15 conversations held, 14 (93%) documented in the EMR; documentation rates 5.4% (clinician A) and 7.3% (clinician B).

audits.t: Intermittent Education and Audit and Feedback Reduce Inappropriate Prescribing of Oral Third-Generation Cephalosporins for Pediatric Upper Respiratory Tract Infections.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing in upper respiratory tract infection
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics guidelines for bacterial upper respiratory tract infections; aim to reduce inappropriate oral third-generation cephalosporins by 15% in one year
audits.f: 72% (231/322) of oral third-generation cephalosporin prescriptions did not align with AAP guidelines.
audits.c: PDSA cycles over one year: one educational session, three individual audit and feedback sessions and one group feedback session.
audits.r2: Mean inappropriate prescribing fell from 72% to 45% (absolute reduction 27%).

audits.t: Admission avoidance in acute epistaxis: A prospective national audit during the initial peak of the COVID-19 pandemic.
audits.st: New COVID-19 epistaxis guidelines; re-presentation within 10 days after ED discharge
audits.f: 54.6% (1267/2322) discharged from ED after ENT review; 19.5% (245/1259) re-presented within 10 days and 6.8% (86/1259) were admitted.

audits.t: Initiative to Increase Skin-to-Skin Contact in the Operating Room After Cesarean.
audits.st: Skin-to-skin contact for at least 15 minutes within the first hour of life in the operating room; target 50%
audits.f: SSC for 15 minutes completed in 20.3% (16/79); any SSC 30.4% (24/79).
audits.c: Nurse education, SSC added to the team time-out before procedures and a new practice guideline.
audits.r2: SSC for 15 minutes 24.7% (23/93); any SSC 61.3% (57/93); SSC verbalised in 75.3% (70/93) of time-outs.

audits.t: Implementing Continuous Quality Improvement in an Integrated Community Urology Practice: Lessons Learned.
audits.st: Clinical guidelines on active surveillance for low-risk prostate cancer; EMR prostate biopsy time-out template
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Continuous audited physician feedback with education; EMR-embedded biopsy time-out template.
audits.r2: Active surveillance adoption consistently increased with continuous audited feedback.

audits.t: Outpatient prescribing trends, rational use of medicine and impact of prescription audit with feedback at a tertiary care centre in India.
audits.tp: Prescription quality and WHO prescribing indicators
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators: drugs per prescription ≤2; antibiotics ≤30%; injections ≤10%; generic and NLEM prescribing 100%
audits.f: Mean 2.53 ± 1.23 drugs per prescription; antibiotics 19.82%; injections 1.98%; generic prescribing 15.96%; NLEM prescribing 37.37%.
audits.r2: Improvement in generic prescribing and prescribing from NLEM; other trends similar.

audits.t: An audit of disseminated intravascular coagulation screen requests at an academic hospital laboratory in central South Africa.
audits.st: ISTH DIC score
audits.f: 183 requests excluded; of 595 complete requests, 283 (47.7%) were overt DIC.

audits.t: Potentially inappropriate medicines for older adults with intellectual disability: Clinical implications from a medication audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 95% were prescribed five or more medicines and 7% ten or more.

audits.t: A pneumococcal pneumonia and influenza vaccination quality improvement program for women receiving chemotherapy for gynecologic cancers at a major tertiary cancer Centre.
audits.st: International guidelines recommending pneumococcal and influenza vaccination before chemotherapy; target 80% by March 2020
audits.f: Baseline vaccination rates: pneumococcal 8% (5% in study) and influenza 40% (36% in study).
audits.c: In-house vaccination programme, staff education campaign and a patient care bundle (pre-printed prescription, information brochure, vaccine record booklet).
audits.r2: Pneumococcal vaccination rose to a monthly mean of 61% and influenza to a monthly mean of 67%; 80% target reached in one or more months.

audits.t: Assessment of the practice of pediatrics procedural sedation and analgesia for magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography scan at a teaching hospital, Ethiopia, 2020: A clinical audit.
audits.st: 20 standards from procedural sedation practice guidelines for MRI and CT
audits.f: 6 of 20 standards had 100% compliance, 3 had 0% and 11 were between 0 and 100%.

audits.t: Clinical auditing as an instrument to improve care for patients with ovarian cancer: The Dutch Gynecological Oncology Audit (DGOA).
audits.st: Predefined DGOA quality indicators, including start of therapy within 28 days
audits.f: Start of therapy within 28 days fell from 68.7% in 2014 to 62.7% in 2018; case ascertainment 98.3% in 2016.

audits.t: [Prospektives Audit des Gentamicin Drug Monitorings in einem Kinderkrebszentrum].
audits.st: German guideline once-daily gentamicin 250 mg/m² BSA (max 10 mg/kg, max 400 mg); Cmax target 10-20 µg/ml
audits.f: Adherence to the dosing regimen 89%; Cmax reached target in 64% of cycles.

audits.t: Does Evaluation and Management of COPD Follow Therapeutic Strategy Recommendations?
audits.st: COPD therapeutic strategy recommendations for symptom and exacerbation risk assessment
audits.f: Clinicians felt 33% of patients had at least 2 exacerbations in the past year versus 56% reported by patients.
audits.c: Focused educational peer-to-peer small group webinars based on audit and feedback.
audits.r2: Improvements in processes of care and outcomes were noted in the year after the intervention.

audits.t: A clinical audit of pneumococcal vaccination among patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases living in Greece: The power of awareness.
audits.tp: Vaccination uptake in immunosuppressed rheumatology patients
audits.st: National guidelines for pneumococcal vaccination in autoimmune rheumatic diseases
audits.f: Pneumococcal vaccination rate 49.37%; 45.06% vaccinated in last five years; only 8.21% had a second vaccine as per national guidelines.

audits.t: An audit of restricted antibiotic use in a general hospital.
audits.st: Hospital formulary restricted antibiotics; appropriate vs inappropriate use
audits.f: Inappropriate use in 22 of 73 cases at excess cost of $3828; 13 inappropriate prescriptions were prophylactic, mostly excessive duration.

audits.t: Use of prescription drug monitoring program to audit opioid prescribing patterns for patients with symptomatic nephrolithiasis.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 249 (83%) prescribed narcotics, mean 226.8 +/- 232.2 MME; 19% had additional opioids not in the EMR identified via PDMP.

audits.t: Improving influenza and pneumococcal vaccination uptake among incident peritoneal dialysis patients: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Health recommendations for influenza and pneumococcal vaccination; target 80%
audits.f: Influenza 63%, PCV13 54%, PPSV23 14%.
audits.c: PDSA cycles: vaccination in non-traditional clinical settings, physician audit and feedback and reminder tools.

audits.t: Procedural Analgesia in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Unit pain protocol; SMART aim to increase procedural analgesia from 11.5% to 75% in 6 months
audits.f: 11% of procedures done after analgesia.
audits.c: PDSA cycles: posters, displayed pain protocol, analgesia orders, written test, short presentations and reminders on procedure trays.
audits.r2: 81% after third PDSA (40% after first); sustained at 75% over the next 2 months.

audits.t: A Chart Audit Study of Clozapine Utilization in Early Psychosis.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 19.7% exposed to clozapine after a mean 2.4 antipsychotic trials and mean delay of 470.8 days; 69.0% achieved full remission on clozapine.

audits.t: Reducing Cardiac Telemetry Nuisance Alarms Through Evidence-Based Interventions.
audits.st: Evidence-based daily care protocol for patients on cardiac telemetry monitoring
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Nursing education module on evidence-based practice for reducing nuisance alarms, a daily care protocol and daily audits of protocol adherence.
audits.r2: Average staff adherence to the protocol 58.46%; telemetry technician call volume fell 16%; nuisance alarms not significantly reduced.

audits.t: An Audit of Orthodontic Retention Protocol in a Tertiary Health Institution: A 3-Year Retrospective Study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Removable retainers used in 85.3%; Hawley retainer most used in the upper arch (79.4%); no lower arch retention in 86.8%.

audits.t: Impact of pharmacist-led selective audit and feedback on outpatient antibiotic prescribing for UTIs and SSTIs.
audits.st: Institutional outpatient empiric therapy guidelines for antibiotic selection, dose, duration and indication
audits.f: Total regimen appropriateness 27.5%.
audits.c: Pharmacist-led selective audit and feedback of antibiotics prescribed for UTIs and SSTIs.

audits.t: Valproate usage in pregnancy: An audit from the Kerala Registry of Epilepsy and Pregnancy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 221 pregnancies (17.75%) exposed to valproate; major malformation rate 10.36% vs 4.96% unexposed (RR 2.1).

audits.t: Decreasing Complete Blood Count Clotting Rates: An Improvement Project in an Academic Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
audits.st: Standardised capillary blood sampling protocol; rate of clotted CBC samples
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Staff education, randomised audits of heel-stick technique and a standardised capillary blood sampling protocol.
audits.r2: Clotted CBC sample rate decreased by 27%; overall CBC rejection rate decreased by 23%; cost saving $1136.

audits.t: One institution's experience with self-audit of opioid prescribing practices for common cervical procedures.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median discharge prescription 112.5 MME (IQR 75-150), 28 times the daily in-hospital MME (median 4); 3/472 received NSAIDs.

audits.t: Topical antimicrobial prescribing patterns in residents of Australian aged-care facilities: use of a national point prevalence survey to identify opportunities for quality improvement.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 2.9% of residents prescribed one or more topical antimicrobials; 33.0% of antimicrobials were topical; review or stop date not documented in 38.7%.

audits.t: Implementation of a Pharmacist-Led Antimicrobial Time-Out for Medical-Surgery Services in an Academic Pediatric Hospital.
audits.st: Pharmacist-led antimicrobial time-out on or before day 5 of therapy; target 90% completion and documentation
audits.f: Mean monthly documentation rate 54.6%.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team developed an ATO process and electronic documentation tool, educated pharmacists and physicians, and gave audit and feedback to pharmacists.
audits.r2: Mean monthly documentation rate 83.5% (647 eligible courses over 19 months).

audits.t: Sharing and Teaching Electrocardiograms to Minimize Infarction (STEMI): reducing diagnostic time for acute coronary occlusion in the emergency department.
audits.st: ECG-to-Activation time for acute coronary occlusion; balancing measure Code STEMIs without culprit lesions
audits.f: Median ECG-to-Activation time 28.0 min (95% CI 15.0-45.0); 28.2% of Code STEMIs without culprit lesions.
audits.c: Grand rounds presentation and an internal website with weekly challenging ECG cases and literature on STEMI-equivalents (audit and feedback).
audits.r2: Median ECG-to-Activation time 8.0 min (95% CI 6.0-15.0); 20.0% of Code STEMIs without culprit lesions.

audits.t: Antibiotic audit in medicine intensive care unit of tertiary care centre: A must do exercise.
audits.st: National Centre for Disease Control national treatment guidelines for infectious disease
audits.f: Rational combinations per antibiotic policy in 73.7%; appropriate doses in 89.5%; two-antibiotic combinations in 53%.

audits.t: Reducing the Risk of Postoperative Complications After Robot-assisted Radical Prostatectomy in Prostate Cancer Patients: Results of an Audit and Feedback Intervention Following the Implementation of Prospective Data Collection.
audits.st: European Association of Urology recommendations for reporting 30-day complications
audits.f: Anastomotic leak rate 9.6%.
audits.c: Audit and feedback from January 2018 identified anastomotic leak as the commonest complication; a new posterior reconstruction and urethrovesical anastomosis technique was introduced.

audits.t: Audit and Feedback to Surgery Interns and Residents on Prescribing Risk-Appropriate Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis.
audits.st: Risk-appropriate VTE prophylaxis prescription
audits.f: Among residents, risk-appropriate prophylaxis 95.6% vs 98.4% in the wash-in period.
audits.c: Monthly emailed individual scorecard, then a web-based dashboard with peer comparison and patient details.
audits.r2: Dashboard feedback improved risk-appropriate prophylaxis prescribing to near-perfect performance (4088 orders over the study).

audits.t: Staff awareness and bundling reduce skin breaks and blood tests in neonatal intensive care.
audits.tp: Skin breaks and blood sampling in neonatal intensive care
audits.st: Frequency of skin breaks and blood tests (local improvement aim)
audits.f: Baseline frequency of skin breaks and blood tests recorded (52 admissions, 34 audit sheets).
audits.c: Results disseminated to staff at unit meetings, shift handover and email (education and awareness).
audits.r2: Mean total blood tests reduced 36.3%, skin breaks per admitted baby day reduced 60% and blood volume sampled reduced 37.7%.

audits.t: The Queensland Inpatient Diabetes Survey (QuIDS) 2019: the bedside audit of practice.
audits.st: Quality of inpatient diabetes care: good diabetes days, medication errors, hospital-acquired harm, specialist review, foot and perioperative care
audits.f: Good diabetes days 22.1 per 100 patient-days (type 1) and 40.1 (insulin-treated type 2); medication errors in 201 (32%), insulin prescribing errors in 127 (39%); 121 (14%) eligible for specialist review not reviewed.

audits.t: An audit of transfusion reaction monitoring and reporting at a cancer hospital in Pakistan - a step towards haemovigilance.
audits.st: Hospital transfusion reaction procedure: complete reaction form and return of blood bag and post-transfusion EDTA sample within 2 hours
audits.f: Reaction forms completely filled in 58 (95%); blood bags returned within 2 hours in 36 (59%) and EDTA samples in 35 (57.3%).

audits.t: Quality assurance audit in adult cardiac anaesthesia.
audits.st: Anaesthesia-related quality indicators during adult cardiac surgery
audits.f: Difficult line access in 42 (19.3%); inappropriate preoperative form information in 6 (2.8%); abnormal activated clotting time post-surgery in 17 (7.8%); monitoring problems on transfer in 7 (3.2%).

audits.t: A quality improvement programme in radiotherapy using workflow audits.
audits.st: Documentation of 64 scored radiotherapy workflow task items in electronic patient folders
audits.f: Scores around 60% in some units.
audits.c: Twice-yearly peer workflow audit by an auditor from another facility, with feedback.
audits.r2: Scores above 90% in all units for at least 2 years.

audits.t: Success Factors for and Barriers to Integration of Electronic Mental Health Screening in Primary Care.
audits.tp: Substance use screening in primary care

audits.r2: Completed screenings 30% (P < .001); provider intervention for positive screens 55% (P = .1081).

audits.st: National Cervical Screening Program 2020 monitoring report PPV for CIN2+ of 57.8%

audits.st: Guideline-recommended risk assessment, safeguards and patient education at opioid initiation
audits.f: No documented opioid education in 137 (66.8%); GP letter at initiation 62 (30%); laxative co-prescription 55 (26.8%); clinic follow-up 186 (91%).

audits.t: When can I hold my baby? An audit of time to first cuddle for preterm babies (<32 weeks) pre introduction and post introduction of a Family-Integrated Care model.
audits.tp: Developmental care in neonatal and paediatric intensive care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Babies born ≤27+6 weeks first cuddled at median 157 hours.
audits.r2: Babies born ≤27+6 weeks first cuddled at median 141 hours; time to full feeds fell from 288 h to 207.5 h.

audits.t: Routine T4 No More? Reducing Excess Thyroid Hormone Testing at a Pediatric Tertiary Care Hospital.
audits.st: Resource stewardship in thyroid hormone testing (fT4 and T3 tests per week)

audits.c: EMR changes: reflex free T4, forced selection of indication for fT4/T3 orders and a clinical decision support message.
audits.r2: Mean 107 ± 12 fT4 (30% reduction) and 4 ± 3 T3 (66% reduction) tests per week.

audits.t: Analysis of Suicides Reported as Adverse Events in Psychiatry Resulted in Nine Quality Improvement Initiatives.
audits.tp: Risk assessment documentation in mental health

audits.f: Suicide risk assessments adequately documented in 6 of 35 cases; relatives involved in 4 of 35 risk assessments.

audits.t: Improving Pediatric Delirium Assessment Documentation and Implementation of a Nonpharmacologic Delirium Management Bundle in the Cardiovascular Intensive Care Unit.
audits.tp: Paediatric delirium screening in intensive care
audits.st: Delirium assessment documentation for each assessment opportunity
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Nurse education on delirium and assessment, weekly emails with documentation rates and targeted education, then a nurse-driven Bundle to Eliminate Delirium (BED) with completion feedback and observational audits.

audits.t: Improving Documentation Using a Real-Time Location System in a Pediatric Emergency Department.

audits.f: Baseline 76% of eligible encounters had appropriate documentation.

audits.r2: Documentation improved from 76% to 85%, not directly attributable to the interventions.

audits.t: Improving the Accuracy of Sepsis Screening by Nurses in Hospitalized Older Adults: A Pilot Interventional Study.
audits.st: Evidence-based sepsis screening practice

audits.r2: Mean increase of 22.06% in screening accuracy (p = 0.007).

audits.t: A clinical audit of management of third and fourth degree perineal tears.
audits.st: Established standards for management of third and fourth degree perineal tears (compared with previous 2008 audit)
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Significant increase versus previous audit in documentation of repair method, use of delayed absorbable suture for external anal sphincter and 6-week follow-up.

audits.t: Do upper GI bleed guidelines reach patient care: effect of a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Consensus upper GI bleeding guidelines: OGD within 24 hours, dual endotherapy, transfusion trigger Hb 7 g/dL

audits.r2: OGD within 24 hours 81.0%; 6 (10.3%) transfused above Hb 7 g/dL (p = 0.047); dual endotherapy improved (p = 0.02).

audits.t: Prospective audit on fasting status of elective ambulatory surgery patients, correlated to gastric ultrasound.
audits.st: Fasting guidelines: 6 h for solid food, 4 h for breast milk, 2 h for clear fluids
audits.f: Mean fasting 13h29 for solid food and 9h51 for clear fluids; 48% of patients aware of correct guidelines.

audits.t: Using Audit and Feedback to Improve Antimicrobial Prescribing in Emergency Departments: A Multicenter Quasi-Experimental Study in the Veterans Health Administration.

audits.t: Informed consent practices in oral and maxillofacial surgery setups - an audit report.
audits.st: Informed consent practice
audits.f: Consent signed by patient in 42%, by relative in 38%, verbal only in 20%; informed of alternatives 38%, surgical complications 51%, anaesthetic complications 26%.

audits.t: Audit of empirical antibiotic therapy for sepsis and the impact of early multidisciplinary consultation on patient outcomes.
audits.st: Eight inpatient quality indicators for responsible antibiotic use and local guideline
audits.f: Full guideline adherence (choice and dosing) 45.9%; choice alone 68.1%; therapy active against likely pathogens in 665/787 (84.5%).

audits.t: Two-year outcomes from the Australian and New Zealand Emergency Laparotomy Audit-Quality Improvement pilot study.
audits.st: Eight evidence-based emergency laparotomy care standards (e.g. preoperative risk score, consultant presence, timely theatre and critical care access); green 80% or more

audits.c: Monthly QI run charts with traffic light feedback to participating hospitals.
audits.r2: Preoperative risk assessment improved almost three-fold; in-hospital mortality 7.1% and length of stay both declined significantly.

audits.t: Management of cut wounds and lacerations in the Gaza Strip: a prospective clinical audit.
audits.st: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne international guidelines on laceration management
audits.f: No hand washing in 72/84 (86%) and 82/100 (82%); antibiotics given to 77% and 72%; lidocaine before suturing in 96% and 65%.

audits.t: Debriefing immediately after intubation in a children's emergency department is feasible and contributes to measurable improvements in patient safety.

audits.t: Meropenem Use in Pediatric Oncology - Audit on Indication, Appropriateness and Consumption Comparing Patient Derived and Pharmacy Dispensing Data.

audits.f: Mean unplanned extubation rate 1.78/100 ventilation days.
audits.c: Clinical guideline on best practice with key interventions introduced sequentially.
audits.r2: Mean unplanned extubation rate 0.8/100 ventilation days (55% reduction), meeting the standard.

audits.t: The resuscitation of the severely injured in the accident and emergency department--a medical audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Errors of management occurred in 21 of 36 patients with Injury Severity Score 16 or over; 78% arrived outside normal office hours.

audits.t: Antimicrobial stewardship in the Federal Bureau of Prisons: Combining prospective audit and feedback with formulary changes to reduce inappropriate fluoroquinolone use.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Prospective audit and feedback targeted at fluoroquinolones plus exclusionary formulary restrictions on ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin.
audits.r2: Overall fluoroquinolone orders per 1,000 adults in custody fell by 46.4%.

audits.t: Audit of a Novel Nurse-Led Program for Nonantibiotic Management of Acute Uncomplicated Diverticulitis.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 41 (48.8%) completed the nonantibiotic protocol with a 97.6% success rate; ED visits within 60 days 8.3% (programme) vs 12.3% (ED group); admission 2.3% vs 3.2%.

audits.t: Perioperative emergency laparotomy pathway for patients undergoing emergency laparotomy: A propensity score matched study.
audits.st: 8-item EMergency Laparotomy Audit (EMLA) perioperative care bundle
audits.f: Surgical complications 34.8%; hospitalisation cost SGD 40,160.
audits.c: Interdisciplinary perioperative pathway with an 8-item bundle, involving specialist clinicians, administrators and a quality improvement team.
audits.r2: Surgical complications 20.6%; hospitalisation cost SGD 30,948 (P=0.04); compliance with key interventions improved.

audits.t: Implementation of O-RADS Ultrasound Reporting System: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Structured ultrasound reporting of adnexal masses
audits.st: Reporting of an O-RADS risk category on pelvic ultrasound reports
audits.f: O-RADS risk category reported in <5% of reports.
audits.c: PDSA cycles: engagement of interested parties, targeted educational sessions, reporting templates and weekly audit-feedback.
audits.r2: Weekly O-RADS reporting rate reached 88%; overall 489/635 (77%) of ultrasounds July 2022 to April 2023 had a risk category.

audits.t: Documentation of International Staging System (ISS) and Revised International Staging System (R-ISS) for Multiple Myeloma at a Tertiary Care Center: A Clinical Audit.
audits.st: ISS and R-ISS staging documentation for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma
audits.f: Time-based improvement in both ISS and R-ISS documentation (figures not reported).

audits.t: The Effectiveness of Pressure Injury Prevention Education for Patient Care Technicians in an Adult Acute Care Setting: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: National Database of Nursing Quality Indicators (NDNQI) pressure injury prevention audit
audits.f: Mean NDNQI audit score 1.40 (SD 0.82).
audits.c: Pressure injury prevention educational tool kit for patient care technicians.

audits.t: Peer Audit and Feedback: A Documentation-Focused Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Nursing critical laboratory result documentation requirements
audits.f: Compliance 6.4%.
audits.c: 5-month timely peer audit and feedback of critical laboratory result events.

audits.t: Why the Delay? A Quality Improvement Initiative for Delayed Cord Clamping in Preterm Infants.
audits.tp: Delayed cord clamping in preterm births
audits.st: Delayed cord clamping as standard practice for preterm infants at or before 34+0 weeks
audits.f: Delayed cord clamping rate 12%; cord clamp time documentation 16%; admission hypothermia 76%.
audits.c: Targeted QI interventions addressing barriers (documentation of cord clamp time and admission hypothermia) identified through audit and multidisciplinary meetings.
audits.r2: Delayed cord clamping rate 70%; documentation 92.6%; admission hypothermia 43.2%.

audits.t: Epidemiology of paediatric intensive care unit admissions, deaths and organ donation candidacy: A single-centre audit.
audits.st: Singapore National Organ Transplant Unit criteria for organ donation candidacy
audits.f: Mortality 99/1766 (5.6%); among non-survivors, organ donor candidacy 21/99 (21.2%) but successful donation in only 2/99 (2.0%).

audits.t: Evaluation of Melanoma and Bladder Cancers in New Hampshire to Identify Registrar Training Needs.
audits.st: National Program of Cancer Registries data quality evaluation framework
audits.f: Accuracy rates calculated for melanoma and bladder cancer data items (figures not reported).

audits.t: Implementing Communication Boards at the Bedside to Improve Patient-Centered Care in an Inpatient Obstetric Unit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Whiteboards were underused (figures not reported).
audits.c: Custom communication boards redesigned for postpartum and antepartum patients using PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: New boards encouraged more complete information and better bedside communication (figures not reported).

audits.t: Evaluating the effectiveness of a vancomycin stewardship programme in a level IV neonatal intensive care unit.
audits.st: Recommendations to limit vancomycin to known resistant infections
audits.f: Vancomycin initiated 166 times; 113 days of therapy per 1000 patient days.
audits.c: Education of the NICU team, standardisation of vancomycin therapy, and prospective audit and feedback.
audits.r2: Vancomycin initiated 71 times (57.2% reduction); 45 days of therapy per 1000 patient days (60.2% reduction).

audits.t: A Comparison of Prescribing Guideline-Advocated Treatment for Heart Failure at Discharge from Cardiology and Non-Cardiology Wards.
audits.st: Heart failure management guidelines (guideline-advocated pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatment)
audits.f: Prescription of ACEI/ARB/ARNI and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists lower in non-cardiology vs cardiology wards (52% vs 80%).

audits.t: Assessing the appropriateness of antifungal prescribing: key results from the implementation of a novel audit tool in Australian hospitals.
audits.st: International consensus antifungal stewardship metrics and prescribing guidelines
audits.f: 77.1% of prescriptions appropriate; guideline compliance 73.6%; fluconazole appropriateness 132/209 (63.2%).

audits.t: Improving quality of physical function assessment in intensive care units through routine use of the Danish Chelsea Critical Care Physical Assessment Tool (CPAx-D).
audits.st: Routine use of the Danish Chelsea Critical Care Physical Assessment Tool (CPAx-D)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles over two years using the Model for Improvement, with questionnaires, observations, continuous feedback and status meetings.
audits.r2: CPAx-D successfully implemented into routine practice (figures not reported).

audits.t: Evaluating a collaborative paediatric eye-care model between optometry and ophthalmology: a clinical audit.
audits.st: Co-developed collaborative care model protocol
audits.f: Protocol compliance 95%; 209 patients removed or prevented from being added to the hospital waiting list; 29 re-referred.

audits.t: Reducing Antibiotic Use for Culture-Negative Sepsis in a Level IV Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
audits.st: Unit Antibiotic Guidelines to reduce treatment of culture-negative sepsis
audits.f: Early-onset sepsis antibiotic DOTs 18.3/1000 patient days; overall unit DOTs 232.5/1000 patient days.
audits.c: Antibiotic guidelines, case audits, weekly antibiotic stewardship rounds and biweekly review of culture-negative sepsis cases at staff meetings (sequential PDSA cycles).
audits.r2: Antibiotic DOTs for culture-negative sepsis fell 81%; early-onset sepsis DOTs 3.9/1000 patient days; overall unit DOTs 176.7/1000 patient days.

audits.t: Audit of Adherence to Best Practice Guidelines for Children born with Down Syndrome.
audits.st: Down Syndrome Medical Interest Group (DSMIG) Neonatal Best Practice Guideline
audits.f: ECHO performed in 66 (90%); all screened for haematological and thyroid abnormalities; growth parameters documented in 8 (11%); audiology referral 60 (82.2%), ophthalmology 17 (23.3%).

audits.t: Do the American Academy of Paediatrics Guidelines for Managing Febrile Infants Aged 22 to 28 Days Work for a Suburban Australian Emergency Department? A Retrospective Audit.
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics 2021 febrile infant guideline (22-28 days) and Australian guidelines recommending LP and empiric antibiotics in all febrile neonates
audits.f: 31% had no LP and 18% were observed without antibiotics (48% and 27% with normal inflammatory markers); 51% would have been eligible for observation without LP or antibiotics under the AAP algorithm.

audits.t: Improving cervical cancer screening rates at a Federally Qualified Health Center.
audits.st: Uniform Data System cervical cancer screening measure; target 79.2% by July 2024
audits.f: Cervical cancer screening 46.3%; outside-facility results accounted for 27% of underperformance.
audits.c: Chart auditing and reconciliation from Epic reports with tip sheets, modifying or discontinuing Pap smears, updating hysterectomy history, and scheduling outreach messages.
audits.r2: 2023 quarterly screening rates rose by 9% or more each quarter and 8.7% year-to-date; 2024 quarters 1 and 2 rose by 4% and 3%; target not reached.

audits.t: Do Adolescents Living With HIV in Kenya Know Their Viral Load Results? Record Audit and Adolescent Exit Surveys in Kiambu and Nakuru Counties: A Cross-Sectional Study.
audits.tp: Paediatric HIV treatment and viral load monitoring
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 86% (179) of charts matched the national database; 7% (14) of results missing from clinic EMR; 8% (17) incongruent.

audits.t: Swallow evaluation tool to reduce aspiration among acute stroke patients: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Swallow screening within 4 hours of stroke
audits.st: Dysphagia screening with a validated tool (Yale Swallow Protocol) within 24 hours of admission
audits.f: Aspiration incidence 42.5% among acute stroke patients; existing screening tool not validated.
audits.c: Yale Swallow Protocol added to the nurses' admission bundle with SLP referral on failure, plus nurse education and weekly audits.
audits.r2: 37 of 63 (59%) screened within 24 h of admission; 3 of 37 screened had aspiration pneumonia.

audits.t: Using a standardized pain management approach through regional anesthesia for major limb amputation patients.
audits.st: Evidence-based regional anaesthesia for all eligible major limb amputation patients
audits.f: Average 2,352.2 total MME per admission; mean length of stay 21 days.
audits.c: Formalised pain pathway: pain score at consent with pain team referral for regional anaesthesia if score 4 or higher, and an embedded checklist in the daily progress note.
audits.r2: Checklist compliance 64%; 57% of those with pain score 4 or higher received regional anaesthesia; average 842.5 MME (about 65% reduction); length of stay 28.4 days.

audits.t: Unplanned extubation prevention in the neuroscience ICU at a High Reliability Organization.
audits.st: Unit-based practice standard (sedation targeting RASS -1 or lower, soft wrist restraints, continuous observation)
audits.f: 9 unplanned extubations (0.93/100 ventilator days).
audits.c: Multidisciplinary unit-based practice standard on communication, escalation, sedation/analgesia targeting RASS -1 or lower, soft wrist restraints and continuous observation.
audits.r2: 6 unplanned extubations (0.22/100 ventilator days); all 6 had RASS goal -1 or lower and restraints.

audits.t: Perioperative Health Education for Patients With Daytime Anorectal Surgery: An Evidence-based Practice Change.
audits.st: 17 JBI evidence-based audit criteria
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Evidence-based perioperative health education programme for patients, following the JBI model.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in execution rates of audit indicators 1, 2, 5, 6, 8 and 10 to 17 (figures not reported).

audits.t: Leveraging a criteria-based audit approach to identify challenges and develop strategies to improve management of postpartum hemorrhage: A case study from the Dominican Republic.
audits.st: Eight evidence-based criteria for postpartum haemorrhage management
audits.f: 25% compliance with evidence-based criteria; gaps in maternal risk assessment, provider training and protocol use.
audits.c: PPH toolkit, protocol and simulation-based training.

audits.t: Improving Safe Thermoregulation Practices in an Urban Outpatient Surgery Center Through a Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Clinical practice recommendations for safe thermoregulation; target 80% over 8 weeks
audits.f: Safe thermoregulation 62%.
audits.c: PreOp and PACU warming bundle introduced through biweekly PDSA tests of change.

audits.t: A single centre audit of genetic testing in early-onset breast cancer.
audits.tp: Mainstream genetic testing in breast cancer
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 5 of 196 women diagnosed with breast cancer at 35 years or younger received BRCA1/2 genetic testing.

audits.t: Smoking Cessation Screening and Treatment Among Veterans With Multiple Sclerosis.
audits.tp: Smoking status documentation and cessation support
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 122 current or former smokers, only 71 (58%) had a current screen; 66 offered behavioural interventions but only 2 referred to cessation clinic; 68 offered pharmacotherapy and 8 prescribed.

audits.t: Phenobarbital for inpatient palliative sedation-a clinical audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Most common indication was agitation; common loading dose 200 mg and starting CSCI 800 mg/24 hours; 22 patients comfortable at death.

audits.t: Audit of screening for hypertension in general practice.
audits.st: Blood pressure screening within the last five years for patients born 1930-44
audits.f: 80% had been screened in the last five years.
audits.c: Patients not screened were identified and contacted.

audits.t: A retrospective medical record audit of the management of cannabis-related emergency department presentations, hospital admissions and hyperemesis of pregnant women who self-reported non-medicinal cannabis use to a substance use in parenting and pregnancy service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Cannabis history documented in 34% of 232 ED presentations and 53% of 183 admissions; substance use screening in 45% and 53%; referral to SUPPS in 7% of admissions and none from ED.

audits.t: An Audit of Narrative Reports Compared to Structured Pathology Reporting for Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
audits.st: Australian structured pathology reporting guidelines for non-melanoma skin cancer (2023)
audits.f: Macroscopic criteria reported in 95%-100%; most microscopic criteria 94%-100%; lymphovascular invasion 80%, depth of invasion 33%, satellitosis/in-transit metastasis 0%.

audits.t: Reducing Nuisance Telemetry Alarms in the Adult Inpatient Setting.
audits.st: Evidence-based alarm bundle workflow
audits.f: Average of 19.44 alarms/patient/hour.
audits.c: Evidence-based alarm bundle (daily electrode changes, parameter customisation and documentation, use of standby) with weekly audits.
audits.r2: Adherence: daily electrode change 80% (n=118), EMR documentation 75% (n=110), shift parameter documentation 75% (n=194), customised parameter documentation 86% (n=117), standby use 75% (n=166).

audits.t: Reducing Pediatric Unplanned Extubation: A National Quality Improvement Collaborative.
audits.st: Unplanned extubation prevention bundle reliability
audits.f: 0.662 unplanned extubations per 100 ventilator days.
audits.c: Spread of the UE bundle using workgroups for peer discussion and sharing of resources, tools and ideas.
audits.r2: 0.53 unplanned extubations per 100 ventilator days (19.9% reduction); 53 hospitals (74%) had significant rate reductions or increased bundle reliability.

audits.t: 3D HDR brachytherapy for cervical cancer in LMIC: Audit of a single institution experience in Lagos, Nigeria.
audits.st: American Brachytherapy Society guidelines
audits.f: Group A mean HR-CTV D90 77.48 ± 6.95 Gy.

audits.t: A systematic, standards-based, participatory assessment of a continuous quality improvement project in Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan: results for neonatal care.
audits.st: WHO neonatal care quality assessment tool (scores 0 to 3)
audits.f: Neonatal care quality suboptimal (scores 1.0-1.9) in all areas.
audits.c: Two-year QI project: QI teams, action plans, provider capacity building, supportive supervision and policy changes, with semi-annual collaborative meetings.
audits.r2: Improvements in routine care (+0.4 Kyrgyzstan, +0.5 Tajikistan), sick newborn care (+0.6 both), accessibility (+0.5, +0.8) and monitoring/follow-up (+0.3, +0.9).

audits.t: Audit of the drug treatment of Parkinson's disease in general practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 26 received L-dopa and 10 an anticholinergic; three quarters of Sinemet patients received less than 75 mg carbidopa per day; average L-dopa 468 mg per day.

audits.t: Role of Prospective Audit in Antimicrobial Stewardship at the Surgery Department of a Tertiary Hospital in Lagos.
audits.st: Consensual hospital antibiotic guidelines
audits.f: Appropriate prescribing in 323/655 (49%); reason documented in 522 (80%); stop/review dates in 77 (15%) of treatment prescriptions.
audits.c: Recommendations based on guidelines fed back to prescribers through the head of the antimicrobial stewardship committee.

audits.t: Reducing peripheral intravenous catheter related blood stream infections: findings from a quality improvement audit of taskforce strategies.
audits.st: Clinical care standards and expected benchmark for PIVC-related bloodstream infection per 10,000 occupied bed days
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Hospital-wide taskforce evidence-based practice strategies aligned with clinical care standards (details not reported).
audits.r2: PIVC-related bloodstream infection rate fell below the expected benchmark; 7 of 12 months (58.3%) had no infections.

audits.t: Quality of the antibiotic advice provided by referral centres in France: a prospective audit.
audits.st: Existing guidelines for urinary tract and respiratory infections, scored out of 5 by three senior infectious disease specialists
audits.f: Mean score 2.7 ± 1.9 out of 5; seniors scored 2.9 vs residents 2.0 (p = 0.019).

audits.t: Photodocumentation of Large Colorectal Polyps: An Audit of Image Quality.
audits.st: Guideline recommendations for pre-resection photodocumentation relative to an open snare or forceps and post-resection photodocumentation of a clear base
audits.f: High-quality pre-resection images 49% to 82% and post-resection 51% to 70% by reviewer; only 1% of pre-resection images showed an open snare or forceps.

audits.t: Impact of Prospective Audit and Feedback by Transitions of Care Pharmacists on the Management of Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
audits.st: CDC Core Elements of Hospital Antibiotic Stewardship (appropriate total days of therapy)
audits.f: Appropriate total DOT 59.5% without vs 66.3% with transitions of care pharmacist intervention (P = 0.337); discharge DOT 3.8 vs 3.4 days.
audits.c: Prospective audit and feedback by transitions of care pharmacists at discharge.

audits.t: Reducing Computed Tomography in Pediatric Cervical Spine Clearance: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.tp: Cervical spine CT imaging in children
audits.st: Paediatric guidelines reserving cervical spine CT for GCS less than 14; aim 15% reduction in 8 months
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Cervical spine clearance pathway, clinical decision support, education, and provider audit and feedback.
audits.r2: Cervical spine CT rate in trauma activations with GCS 14 or more fell by 20%.

audits.t: Targeting discrepancies in linear growth measurements in the neonatal intensive care unit through nursing interventions: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Gold standard two-person length board measurement; discrepancy of 1 cm or less between nurse and audit measurements
audits.f: Desired minimal difference in 38%.
audits.c: Nursing interventions over two PDSA cycles, including more length boards and education.
audits.r2: Desired minimal difference 74% after PDSA 2 (p = 0.003) and 71% in sustainability cycle (p = 0.007).

audits.t: Adequacy of the Diagnostic Workup of Suspected Physical Abuse in Young Children: An Audit in the Paris Metropolitan Area.
audits.st: Clinical guidelines for diagnostic workup of suspected child physical abuse (skeletal survey, eye fundus examination, head CT or MRI)
audits.f: At least one key diagnostic test not performed in 14 (14%); bone metabolism investigation in 33% of 43 with unexplained fractures; haemostasis tests in 82% of 76 with bruises or bleeding.

audits.t: Audit and Feedback Supporting New Guideline Implementation in Chronic Kidney Disease.
audits.tp: SGLT2 inhibitor and GLP-1 RA prescribing
audits.st: Clinical practice guideline recommending SGLT-2 inhibitors in adults with type 2 diabetes and CKD
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Audit and feedback delivered to providers every 3 weeks with a clinical decision guide and structured interviews.
audits.r2: Significant increase in SGLT-2 inhibitor prescribing (figures not reported).

audits.t: Sweat testing and cystic fibrosis - Test performance before and after a quality improvement project in a South African tertiary hospital laboratory.
audits.st: Acceptable quantity not sufficient (QNS) rate for sweat tests
audits.f: QNS rate 30% for sweat chloride and 12% for sweat conductivity.
audits.c: Technologist training, clinician education, patient preparation protocols and revised testing procedures.
audits.r2: QNS rate 25% for sweat chloride; 12% unchanged for sweat conductivity.

audits.t: Implementing Customized Electronic Quality Checklists to Reduce Errors and Improve Workflow in Radiotherapy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Planning delays in 42 (8.3%) of 503 cases.
audits.c: Automated customised electronic quality checklists in MOSAIQ assigned to radiotherapy staff.
audits.r2: Planning delays in 25 (4.2%) of 590 cases; errors from verification checks reduced by 50%.

audits.t: Cervical cancer screening in women with HIV: an audit of clinical care.
audits.tp: Cervical screening in women living with HIV
audits.st: National cervical screening guidelines: three-yearly screening for women with HIV
audits.f: 57/115 (49.6%) up to date with screening; 58 (50.4%) overdue, of whom 52 (89.7%) more than 6 months and 45 (76.3%) more than 12 months overdue.

audits.t: Optimizing Medication Safety Review and Adverse Drug Events: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.tp: High-alert and look-alike sound-alike medication safety
audits.st: Aim to increase days between medication safety events by 5% over 28 months; high-alert and nephrotoxic medication bundles
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Targeted medication list, rounding script modifications, provider education, review of medication orders and rounding audits.
audits.r2: Days between high-alert medication events increased by 10 days with a centreline shift; no shift for nephrotoxic medications. Mean bundle compliance 90% (monthly range 67%-100%) high-alert and 76% (25%-100%) nephrotoxic.

audits.t: Early palliative care integration in advanced cancer: two institutional quality improvement projects.
audits.st: Guideline recommendation for early palliative care integration in advanced cancer; timely referral
audits.f: Timely palliative care referral 37% at Centre A and 30% at Centre B.
audits.c: A3 methodology: raising oncologists' awareness, holistic symptom assessment and an established referral process.
audits.r2: Timely palliative care referral rose to 66% at Centre A and 60% at Centre B.

audits.t: Adherence to the febrile neutropenia protocol in pediatric leukemia patients at a Brazilian Cancer Center-A retrospective audit.
audits.st: Institutional febrile neutropenia protocol
audits.f: 329 febrile neutropenia episodes in 84 patients; inappropriate empirical antibiotic treatment 40%: inadequate Gram-positive cover 2%, failure to de-escalate 78%, maintenance of antibiotics despite negative cultures 62%.

audits.t: A collaborative approach to improving prostate magnetic resonance image quality.
audits.st: PI-QUAL v1: exams scoring 4 or more and at least one DWI sequence rated optimal
audits.f: PI-QUAL score 4 or more in 90% (95% CI 87-94%); DWI criteria met in 77% (95% CI 74-79%).
audits.c: Standardised pre-MRI patient instructions and documentation on nil by mouth and bladder emptying, technologist image quality education and weekly PI-QUAL scoring embedded in the reporting system (May-September 2023).
audits.r2: PI-QUAL score 4 or more in 97% (95% CI 95-99%); DWI criteria met in 83% (95% CI 78-88%).

audits.t: A Multiphase Quality Improvement Project to Increase Relative Value Unit Generation Through Documentation Practices in a Pediatric Emergency Department.
audits.st: Aim: 10% increase in RVU per encounter over 2 years; 20% reduction in LOS 99282 billing; 90% of admitted patients billed at LOS 99285
audits.f: LOS 99285 billing 9% overall and 50% among admitted patients.
audits.c: PDSA cycles: billing dot phrase, revised note templates, billing reference sheets and a level of service calculator.
audits.r2: RVU per encounter up 11%; LOS 99282 billing down 25%; LOS 99285 billing 13% overall and 70% among admitted patients.

audits.t: Quality and Outcomes of Acute Stroke Care for People With and Without Aphasia.
audits.st: Quality of care indicators aligned with national evidence-based stroke guidelines
audits.f: Patients with aphasia less often assessed for mood (23% vs 30%), given risk factor education (59% vs 70%) or involved in care planning (83% vs 95%).

audits.t: Improving Screening for Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency in Adults with COPD.
audits.tp: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency testing in COPD
audits.st: Evidence-based standard of care: AATD testing in adults with COPD; target 75% in eight weeks
audits.f: 2.0% of patients with COPD tested for AATD.
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles over eight weeks: shared decision-making checklist and standard of care log.

audits.t: Optimizing z-axis coverage in computed tomography scans of the kidney, ureters, and bladder via standard operating procedures: a clinical audit report.
audits.st: Departmental standard operating procedure: scan from T10 vertebra endplate to inferior margin of pubic symphysis
audits.f: Internal audit identified variability in CT KUB doses and over-scanning.
audits.c: Phase 1: new SOP with osseous anatomical landmarks; phase 2: SOP amended to use a sagittal scout view to identify the T10 endplate.
audits.r2: Phase 1 reduced scan length by 14% and DLP by 32%; phase 2 reduced scan length by a further 7%; overall scan length down 20% and DLP down 55%.

audits.t: Implementation of Team Communication and Nurse Feedback to Reduce Cesarean Rates.
audits.st: Use of an interprofessional communication tool before non-emergent caesareans
audits.f: Tool compliance averaged 62%, peaking at 77% during active education and declining to 33% after implementation.
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles: adapted communication tool and addition of individual nurse NTSV caesarean rates to audit and feedback.

audits.t: Audit: a project on peer review in general practice.
audits.st: Predefined criteria developed by experts
audits.f: 253 general practitioners took part (about 30% of area GPs; 72% of those approached).

audits.t: Epilepsy: a disease audit.
audits.st: Audit objectives: case finding against community prevalence, classification, investigation, seizure freedom in 12 months, monotherapy
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Pilot to Implement an Inpatient Opioid Withdrawal Screening Pathway.
audits.st: Evidence-based Opioid Withdrawal Screening Pathway using COWS
audits.f: Baseline screening of illicit drug use was low.
audits.c: 2-week education programme for nurses and providers, then 12-week screening pathway with COWS assessments and chart audits.
audits.r2: Screening rates increased significantly; discharge against medical advice and length of stay significantly reduced (figures not stated in abstract).

audits.t: Care for peripheral intravenous catheter: an audit in two French university hospitals.
audits.st: French Society of Hospital Hygiene recommendations for PIVC care
audits.f: Patient identity checked in 50%; hand hygiene 82.5% before insertion, 54% before infusion and 13% before removal; flushing in 82.5% of insertions and 66% post-infusion; gloves at insertion 47%.

audits.t: An audit of asthma in a Belfast practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Regular peak expiratory flow monitoring in just 14%; 13 diagnostic labels used; inadequate treatment in a small number of patients.

audits.t: Increasing Dental Varnish Rates in a Large Pediatric Care Network: A Quality Improvement Effort.
audits.st: Target: dental varnish at 20% of eligible preventive visits (6 months to 5.99 years)
audits.f: Varnish applied at 3.7% of eligible visits; 6 practices applying varnish.
audits.c: EHR prompts, practice-level education, maintenance of certification credit with monthly audit and feedback, and financial incentives.
audits.r2: Varnish application 30.5%; all 33 practices adopting; more than 50% of children received varnish annually (vs 25%).

audits.t: Improving Antibiotic Administration Time in At-Risk Pediatric Populations: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: At least 80% receive antibiotics within 60 minutes of registration
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: PDSA cycles with enhanced nursing autonomy and team-based strategies.

audits.t: Medical oxygen service readiness and service coverage in seven countries in Africa and Asia: a cross-sectional survey and clinical audit.
audits.st: Predefined minimum standards for pulse oximeter and oxygen availability; documented oximetry on admission and oxygen for hypoxaemia
audits.f: Pulse oximetry documented on admission for 79% of neonates, 61% of children and 55% of adults; oxygen documented for hypoxaemia in 88%, 68% and 65% respectively. Functional oximeter in 24% primary, 74% secondary and 83% tertiary facilities.
audits.co: Multinational (Cambodia, Ethiopia, Laos, Liberia, Nigeria, Rwanda, Uganda)

audits.t: Impact of a Resident-Driven Quality Improvement Project on Incidental Thyroid Nodule Follow-up-A Single Center Study.
audits.st: American College of Radiology guidelines for incidental thyroid nodule characterisation and follow-up
audits.f: Primary care provider awareness of nodules 75%; recommended follow-up ultrasound 40%.
audits.c: Phase 1 (2022-23) standardised dictation templates; phase 2 (2023-24) monthly chart audits and secure messaging to primary care providers.
audits.r2: Primary care provider awareness 98% (p=0.0005); recommended follow-up ultrasound 59% (p=0.04).

audits.t: Variable Adherence to Australian Clinical Care Standard: An Audit of Patients With Acute Low Back Pain Attending a Tertiary Emergency Department.
audits.tp: Low back pain management in the emergency department
audits.st: ACSQHC Low Back Pain Clinical Care Standard (2022); 80% adherence threshold per item
audits.f: Screening for serious spinal pathology and appropriate review had the highest adherence; imaging rates close to the 80% threshold; no patients screened for psychosocial factors; other items low.

audits.t: Feasibility of Auditing Preoperative Breast MRI for Extent-of-Disease Evaluation Using the BI-RADS v2025 Manual.

audits.t: Transforming an antimicrobial stewardship program at a tertiary military medical center in Saudi Arabia: An institutional quality improvement report.

audits.t: Neuraxial labor analgesia outcomes in a referral center in Vietnam: a quality improvement program incorporating Statistical Process Control methodology (2022-2024).

audits.r2: All three quality driver scores improved significantly across the three periods.

audits.t: Faster administration of antimicrobials in sepsis team quality improvement initiative in the intensive care unit: a retrospective audit (FAAST-R).
audits.st: Guideline first-dose antimicrobial timeframes: ≤60 min for sepsis or septic shock, ≤180 min without sepsis

audits.t: Time to Management of Colorectal Cancer: Audit of the Gastroenterology Department at Mongi Slim Hospital.
audits.st: Diagnosis-to-treatment interval of 30 days or less

audits.t: From Paper to Proactive Safety: Digitalising Shift Checklists in a Paediatric Cardiac ICU.
audits.st: Completion of shift safety checks

audits.st: Definitive radiotherapy discontinuation rate as a key performance indicator
audits.f: 279 definitive discontinuations (1.71%); palliative 3.49% vs curative 1.08%.

audits.t: Concordance of surveillance colonoscopy recommended intervals with Australian guidelines: a clinical audit in six Victorian public hospitals.
audits.st: 2018 Australian Cancer Council surveillance colonoscopy guidelines
audits.f: 25.4% (63/248) of recommended intervals were guideline-concordant; of discordant, 74.6% early, 20.5% not indicated, 4.9% late.

audits.t: Current Diagnostic Pathways for Rheumatoid Arthritis-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease Result in Substantial Underdiagnosis and Excess Mortality: A Multicenter Norwegian Quality Assurance Audit.
audits.tp: Interstitial lung disease screening in rheumatoid arthritis

audits.t: Decreasing contamination rates in blood cultures: A plan-do-study-act approach.
audits.st: Aseptic blood culture collection standard operating procedure
audits.f: Contamination rate 10.7%.

audits.t: <b>Monitoring the Impact of Quality Interventions to Improve Bedside Transfusion Practices at a Quaternary Care Hospital in South India</b>.
audits.st: Transfusion guidelines (bedside transfusion practices)

audits.t: Medication for Opioid Use Disorder in recovery housing: A statewide secret shopper audit of Florida Certified Recovery Residences.

audits.t: Utilizing a Standardized Bundle of Care to Improve Outcomes for Perinatal Patients with Substance Use Disorder: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Perinatal substance use screening and care

audits.t: Preventability and contributing factors in neonatal deaths in protracted refugee camp settings: A five-year audit among Syrian refugees in Jordan.

audits.t: [A quality improvement project on urinary catheter management in a medical ward of the Turin local health authority].

audits.t: Evaluating discharge opioid prescribing practices in elective surgical patients: a retrospective audit from a tertiary surgical and rehabilitation centre.

audits.t: An audit of the assessment and management of patients admitted to Christchurch Hospital with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
audits.st: Consensus local COPD management guidelines
audits.f: Level of consciousness not commented on in 50% and hyperinflation in 40%; oxygen given in 87% but not prescribed in one third; peak flow on admission 74%; arterial blood gas 81%; no discharge summary in 29%.
audits.c: Hospital-wide COPD guidelines to be developed

audits.t: Are general practitioners really prepared? An audit of emergency equipment in general practice.
audits.st: Items the authors considered essential emergency equipment
audits.f: 63% of practices did not have all required items.

audits.t: Unplanned extubation in the intensive care unit: a quality-of-care concern.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Seven unplanned extubations in six of 121 patients; one per 136 patient-ventilator days.
audits.c: Education of nurses and house staff, daily risk assessment on rounds and documentation of episodes
audits.r2: 12 unplanned extubations in 11 patients; one per 455 patient-ventilator days.

audits.t: The scope and place of ultrasound-monitored extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy in a multimodality setting and the effects of experiential, audit-evoked changes on the management of ureteric calculi.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: ESWL stone-free rate 84%; 44% needed more than one treatment; post-ESWL procedures 8%.

audits.r2: ESWL stone-free rate 92%; 14% needed more than one treatment; post-ESWL procedures 6%.

audits.t: Clinical audit of anaesthesia practice and adverse peri-operative events at Parkland Memorial Hospital, Dallas, Texas.
audits.tp: Adverse events during anaesthesia and sedation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Adverse event data collected sporadically; critical incidents not specifically identified.
audits.c: New detailed data collection form and formal presentation at clinical education sessions

audits.t: Syphilis in pregnancy: a medical audit in a rural district.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1433 (66%) had an RPR result; 197 (14%) positive; 111 (67%) of 165 adequately treated.

audits.t: An audit of X-ray investigations in patients attending a neuropsychiatric hospital.
audits.st: X-ray investigation should be requested in neuropsychiatric patients where indicated for concomitant physical problems
audits.f: 14.2% of patients meeting the criterion had X-ray investigation.

audits.t: Depth of central venous catheterization: an audit of practice in a cardiac surgical unit.
audits.st: not reported
