audits.t: Audit of deaths from cervical cancer: proposal for an essential component of the National Screening Programme.
audits.st: National Cervical Screening Programme
audits.f: Only 6% presented via a smear; 47% no record of smear invitation; 22% non-response; inappropriate laboratory diagnosis 17%; inappropriate clinical management 19%.

audits.t: The influence of medical audit on the management of epistaxis in three district general Hospitals.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Treatment and discharge protocol established, nasal pack duration reduced and pack material changed after subregional audit meetings

audits.t: Sample survey methods as a quality assurance tool in a general practice immunisation audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 22.5% of under 2 year olds recorded as not overdue for any immunisation.
audits.c: Standard telephone and letter catch-up campaign
audits.r2: Only a modest improvement; figure not given.

audits.t: The Scottish Otolaryngology Audit--laryngeal cancer audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Umbilical arterial catheter use: report of an audit conducted by the Study Group for Complications of Perinatal Care.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 582 (30%) had a UAC for a mean of 4.9 days; wide variation in tip position, heparin use and infusates.

audits.t: Diagnostic accuracy in head-injured patients: an emergency department audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: ISS discrepancies in 56 patients (29%).

audits.t: Audit strategies to reduce hospital admissions for acute asthma.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Experienced registrar sent home 53 of 158 children versus six of 39 seen by SHOs.
audits.c: SHO training programme and home treatment package
audits.r2: 229 (43.5%) deemed fit to go home; seven readmitted within one week.

audits.t: Improving nursing records with audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Audit tool introduced to measure nursing documentation
audits.r2: Quality of documentation significantly better; figures not given.

audits.t: Quality audit of megavoltage radiotherapy units: intercomparison of dose at a reference point using a mailed TL-dosimetry system.
audits.st: Dosimetry discrepancy within +/- 3%
audits.f: Majority of beams within 2%; two electron beams at 6% of reference value.

audits.t: An audit of hospital discharge letters in patients admitted with acute asthma. Tayside Asthma Audit Group.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Precipitating factor 54%; smoking history 57%; inhaler device 40%; inhaler technique assessed 17%; self-management plan 66%.

audits.t: Audit of theophylline plasma level monitoring in a pediatric hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Recommendations on 48.5% of results; physician compliance with dose changes 75.9% and with extra samples 75%.
audits.r2: Recommendations on 37.9% of results; compliance with dose changes 73.3% and with extra samples 87.2%.

audits.t: Accuracy of a computer-based anaesthetic audit system.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 50% of notes found and 40% of these lacked an anaesthetic chart; computer output accurate in 52% retrospectively and 33% prospectively.

audits.t: Congestive heart failure with sinus rhythm. Audit of digoxin therapy in a family medicine teaching unit.
audits.st: Literature-derived indicators of positive digoxin response
audits.f: Most treated appropriately; 22% to 36% treated incorrectly with digoxin.

audits.t: Value of perinatal audit in obstetric care in the developing world: a ten-year experience of the Maputo model.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Intrapartum fetal mortality 10.9 per thousand.
audits.c: Regular feedback of perinatal data on wall charts and weekly conferences

audits.t: An audit and international comparison of asthma management in the emergency department.
audits.st: Asthma management guidelines operative at the time
audits.f: Peak flow at presentation 79% and after treatment 67%; nebulised bronchodilators 88%; parenteral steroids 22%; 28% of those discharged received oral prednisone.

audits.t: A successful system of scientific data audits for clinical trials. A report from the Cancer and Leukemia Group B.
audits.st: Federal regulations on institutional review board oversight, consent and protocol compliance
audits.f: IRB deficiency rate 28.0% at main and 49.6% at affiliate institutions; consent form deficiencies 18.5%.
audits.c: Repeated on-site peer review audits of source documents
audits.r2: IRB deficiency 13.3% main and 28.2% affiliate; consent form deficiencies 3.9%; eligibility verified 94.5%; tumour response verified 96.4%.

audits.t: Audit filters in quality assurance in pediatric trauma care.
audits.st: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma audit filters
audits.f: 13 (1.5%) died; 35 (4.1%) had a complication; 90 (10.6%) failed one of the 12 minimum filters; 104 (12.3%) failed a local filter.

audits.t: Audit of intensive care unit admissions from the operating room.
audits.tp: Unplanned critical care admission after surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 34 unanticipated ICU admissions; 16 predictable, seven preventable; 36% needed no ICU-specific intervention.
audits.c: Education programme changes and reorganisation with an intermediate care area

audits.t: A private breast imaging practice: medical audit of 25,788 screening and 1,077 diagnostic examinations.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Screening recall 5.9%; sensitivity 91%; positive predictive value 11%; 119 of 188 (63%) cancers stage 0 or 1.

audits.t: National asthma attack audit 1991-2. General Practitioners in Asthma Group.
audits.st: Recommended asthma guidelines
audits.f: 1546 (86%) managed in general practice, 225 (12%) admitted; underuse of nebulised bronchodilators and systemic steroids at all severities.

audits.t: A continuous quality improvement cycle for teaching the identification of psychosocial problems to general internal medicine residents.
audits.tp: Psychosocial problem identification in primary care
audits.st: Accepted predefined specifications
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: CQI cycle with case-finding instruments, flow sheets and real-time social worker feedback
audits.r2: Statistically significant improvement; figures not given.

audits.t: An audit of comfort and convenience. Comparison of oxygen mask and nasal catheter in the provision of postoperative oxygen therapy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of inhaled asthma therapy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: More than half did not use their inhaler devices properly.

audits.t: Auditing quality of nursing care.
audits.st: Commercially produced nursing care quality audit tool
audits.f: Results of a part pilot study are discussed; figures not given in abstract.

audits.t: Audit of the support for breastfeeding mothers in Fife maternity hospitals using adapted 'Baby Friendly Hospital' materials.
audits.st: Ten WHO-UNICEF Baby Friendly Hospital standards (adapted external evaluation instruments)
audits.f: Several practices fell below WHO-UNICEF standards, including supplementary feeding of breastfed babies (especially overnight) and discharge bounty packs advertising formula. Sample: 10 staff, 12 antenatal and 21 postnatal women.
audits.c: Supplementary feeding reduced, bounty packs discontinued, hospital breastfeeding support group set up, hypoglycaemia policy revised, orientation on breastfeeding policy for medical staff identified as a need.

audits.t: Trends and variations in use of antenatal corticosteroids to prevent neonatal respiratory distress syndrome: recommendations for national and international comparative audit. Scottish Neonatal Consultants' Collaborative Study Group, International Neonatal Network.
audits.st: Antenatal corticosteroids for 24 h or more before delivery below 31 weeks; proposed targets >70% treated for 24 h or more and >90% treated at all
audits.f: Corticosteroids for 24 h or more: 16% (range 0-43) in 1988-89 and 29% (0-36) in 1990-93; data obtained in 1579 (99%).

audits.t: An emergency department radiology audit procedure.
audits.tp: Radiology reporting of emergency department radiographs
audits.st: Concordance of emergency physician and radiologist interpretation
audits.f: Concordance 97.6%. Chest radiographs for inflammatory processes: agreement in 10 of 45 (22%); 40 of 45 (89%) still received proper therapy.

audits.t: Mortality risk and patterns of practice in 4606 acute care patients with congestive heart failure. The relative importance of age, sex, and medical therapy. Clinical Quality Improvement Network Investigators.
audits.st: Use of proven efficacious therapy for congestive heart failure
audits.f: Diuretics 82%, ACE inhibitors 53%, nitrates 49%, digoxin 46%, aspirin 36%, warfarin 17%, beta-blockers 15%. ACE inhibitors used less in women and patients aged 70 or over.

audits.t: Quality assurance of clinical transfusion practice by implementation of the privilege of blood prescription and computerized prospective audit of blood requests.
audits.st: Hospital guidelines for the proper use of blood
audits.f: Perioperative patients given both red cells and plasma: 47.6% (320/672). Inappropriate plasma requests for elective general surgery 39% at programme onset.
audits.c: Non-urgent blood prescription restricted to a limited group of trained physicians, plus computerised prospective audit of all blood requests against guidelines.
audits.r2: Red cells plus plasma: 37.8% (244/646), difference -9.8% (95% CI -4.5% to -15.1%), P<0.005. Inappropriate plasma requests fell to 14% in last trimester. 7884 requests audited: 96.8% red cell and 98.1% platelet requests appropriate.

audits.t: Morbidity of varicose vein surgery: auditing the benefit of changing clinical practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Thromboembolic complication rate 0.7%. Overall 997 patients (1322 legs) across both periods; 95.5% stayed under 2 days.
audits.c: Change in bandaging policy and use of postoperative antiembolic stockings.

audits.t: An audit of palliative care in dementia.
audits.st: Current accepted palliative care practice
audits.f: Pain and dyspnoea most common. Constipation and oral candidiasis managed within accepted practice; palliation of other symptoms inadequate.

audits.t: Chart audit using the American Nurses Association standards of practice.
audits.st: American Nurses Association Standards of Home Health Nursing Practice
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An audit of the women who died during 1994 from cancer of the cervix in Victoria, Australia.
audits.tp: Cervical screening history in invasive cervical cancer
audits.st: Adequate cervical screening
audits.f: Only 10% of deaths were in adequately screened women; 70% of deaths in women aged 50 or over at diagnosis.

audits.t: An audit of third generation cephalosporin prescribing in a tertiary care hospital.
audits.st: Australian Antibiotic Guidelines handbook 1994-95 criteria for appropriate prescribing
audits.f: 65% of prescriptions appropriate, 31% inappropriate, 4% doubtful.

audits.t: The use of audit to set up a thrombolysis programme in the accident and emergency department.
audits.st: Door-to-needle time 30 min; 70% of acute myocardial infarction patients thrombolysed
audits.f: Median door-to-needle time 110 min; 58% of acute myocardial infarctions thrombolysed (thrombolysis run from coronary care unit).
audits.c: Thrombolysis programme moved from the coronary care unit to A&E, with funding for staffing and staff education.
audits.r2: 266 (28%) had acute myocardial infarction; 182 (68%) received thrombolysis (vs 58% previously). Door-to-needle result truncated in abstract.

audits.t: An audit of general practitioner referrals for pelvic ultrasound.
audits.st: Appropriate use judged by diagnostic yield and onward referral rates compared with other studies
audits.f: Diagnostic yields and referral rates were similar to other studies.

audits.t: Audit of unbooked paediatric post-anaesthesia admissions to intensive care.
audits.tp: Unplanned critical care admission after surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 35 (5%) admissions from theatre were unbooked; 71% of these were predictable and 20% had preventable features. PICU-specific therapy used in 77% of unbooked vs 88% of booked admissions.

audits.t: An audit of the organisation of neonatal screening for phenylketonuria and congenital hypothyroidism in the Northern Region.
audits.st: Fail-safe system to ensure every resident baby is screened for phenylketonuria and congenital hypothyroidism with a result before 28 days of age
audits.f: Three districts did not match results to birth notifications; of 13 that did, two did no further checks and five checked only monthly. Only six districts had a timely fail-safe system.
audits.c: Recommendations made to each district to improve timeliness and completeness of screening.
audits.r2: All districts except two had improved their fail-safe systems.

audits.t: Clinical audit of malaria diagnosis in urban primary curative care clinics, Zimbabwe.
audits.st: Diagnosis by doctors as reference standard; ZEDAP manual diagnostic criteria
audits.f: Accuracy of nurse malaria diagnosis about 10%, based on symptoms. ZEDAP criteria not being used; pyrexia absent in 40% of patients.

audits.t: An audit on hospital management of bronchial asthma.
audits.st: Accepted international asthma management standards
audits.f: Poor documentation of severity signs and peak flow; no documentation of inhaler technique checks.

audits.t: An audit into the use of intravascular contrast media in Scotland. The Audit Committee of the Scottish Radiological Society and the Scottish Standing Committee of the Royal College of Radiologists.
audits.tp: Contrast media reaction prevention and management
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists guidelines on low and high osmolar contrast media
audits.f: 100% response; all users adhered to RCR guidelines, but only 87% recorded adverse reactions.

audits.t: Administrative aspects of a general surgical firm: an audit of accuracy of operation lists and timeliness of discharge summaries.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1.4% of operation lists had errors or omissions, 5% had abbreviations. 74.2% of discharge summaries dictated within one week; 44.7% on day of operation.

audits.t: Audit of introduction of hand-held Doppler and duplex ultrasound in the management of varicose veins.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Secondary investigations 16%; 47% listed directly for surgery; long saphenous surgery 84%, short saphenous 6%.
audits.c: Introduction of hand-held Doppler and availability of duplex ultrasound.
audits.r2: Secondary investigations 41%; 29% listed directly for surgery; long saphenous surgery 76%, short saphenous 21%.

audits.t: Changing patterns of diagnosis and treatment of infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis: a clinical audit of 303 patients.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mucosal perforation 7/151 (4.6%); clinical diagnosis alone 74%, ultrasound 16%, barium meal 12%; wound infection 9%; mean stay 3.7 days.
audits.c: Ongoing clinical audit with a review after 8.5 years recommending fewer diagnostic tests.
audits.r2: Mucosal perforation 0/152; wound dehiscence 3 to 0; clinical diagnosis alone 28%, ultrasound 65%, barium meal 28%; wound infection 4%; mean stay 3.2 days.

audits.t: [Application of clinical audit to the evaluation of prescription of interferon-alpha in a teaching hospital].
audits.st: Accepted therapeutic indications, dosing schedules and discontinuation criteria (peer review panel)
audits.f: No patient treated outside established indications (85.6%) or a trial protocol (14.4%); all indications approved by the panel.

audits.t: Audit of the care of patients with epilepsy in general practice.
audits.st: 75% seen yearly; 75% seizure frequency documented; 75% on antiepileptic drugs no more than twice daily
audits.f: 83% seen in past year; seizure frequency documented 51%; 63% taking treatment no more than twice daily.
audits.c: Changes to documentation and advice on treatment.
audits.r2: 95% seen in past year; seizure frequency documented 93%; 66% taking treatment twice daily or less.

audits.t: A pilot study of the introduction of audit into nursing homes.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean short Geriatric Depression Scale score 4.73.
audits.c: Nurse audit facilitator visited homes for a year to teach staff and help with audit projects; 13 of 16 homes did at least one audit and 10 made a major procedural change.
audits.r2: Mean score fell to 4.25 (p=0.02); satisfaction improved in 6 of 11 aspects of care.

audits.t: Prescribing practice and policy for hypnotics: a model of pharmacy audit.
audits.tp: Benzodiazepine and Z-drug prescribing in older inpatients
audits.st: Appropriate hypnotic prescribing (departmental policy)
audits.f: 60% prescribed a hypnotic during stay; 12% prescribed as required on admission but never took it. Mean 2392 sleeping tablets prescribed a month.
audits.c: Departmental prescribing policy introduced as part of ongoing pharmacy audit.
audits.r2: Overall hypnotic prescribing 25%; 2% prescribed on admission but never took it. Mean 734 tablets a month.

audits.t: [Medical records audit in primary care clinics of the Israel Navy].
audits.st: Fixed criteria scoring SOAP components of the record (0-100)
audits.f: Therapeutic and evaluative plan scored 80% vs 55-59% for other parts (p<0.001). Regular primary care physicians 73% vs reserve physicians 63%.

audits.t: [Audit of histopathology activities at the pathology departments of 7 general hospitals. 2. Response time].
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1,000 consecutive cases per lab. Mean receipt-to-report 3.1-6.1 days; reported within 3 days mean 37% (range 5-64%); all labs but one reported 95-100% within 10 days.

audits.t: Redesigning the care of carotid endarterectomy patients.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline figures not given.
audits.c: Routine discharge on first postoperative day, critical pathway with computerised order set, regional block instead of general anaesthesia, and a postoperative hypertension algorithm.
audits.r2: Length of stay fell by 1.15 days and cost by $1900 per case, with no change in morbidity or mortality.

audits.t: The quality of histopathology data in a computerised cancer registration system: implications for future audit of care.
audits.st: Accurate histopathology coding
audits.f: 38% of pathology reports coded accurately; 25% of incorrectly coded reports could distort published cancer incidence.

audits.t: Breast cancer audit--the Isle of Wight experience.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: The timing of computed tomography in acute stroke: a practice audit.
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: [A multicenter primary care study on alcohol consumption].
audits.st: Recording of alcohol consumption in the last two years
audits.f: Only 24.8% of records documented alcohol consumption; 11 (2.8%) met criteria for at-risk drinking.

audits.t: Audit of waste collected over one week from ten dental practices. A pilot study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Cross-infection items made up to 91% of waste; 3 of 10 practices disposed of radiographic fixer and developer into sewerage despite Australian Dental Association advice.

audits.t: Comprehensive audit of quality-of-care and quality-of-life for patients with diabetes.
audits.st: Diabetes Australia and New South Wales Health guidelines
audits.f: Poor control and monitoring; frequent attenders no more likely to have HbA1c done (P=0.72).

audits.t: Histopathology services in a rural African hospital: how audit can improve service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean 26 days from biopsy to result reaching the clinician; only 22% of patients were ever told their result.
audits.c: Results reported and action taken against the problems found.

audits.t: Does reduced length of stay decrease the number of emergency department patients who leave without seeing a physician?
audits.tp: Emergency department waiting times and flow
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 2.4% (110/4553) left without being seen; 82 nonurgent, 28 urgent.
audits.c: Five changes from a continuous quality improvement process to speed patient flow through triage and fast-track.
audits.r2: 1.1% (51/4514) left without being seen; 35 nonurgent, 16 urgent; significant decrease.

audits.t: Computer-based audit to detect and correct overutilization of laboratory tests.
audits.st: Explicit criteria justifying three or more LDH or calcium tests in seven days
audits.f: 51% of charts with repeated LDH showed overutilisation.
audits.c: Physicians notified of overutilisation found by computer-based audit, with education.
audits.r2: 65% of charts showed overutilisation (not significant); undisclosed calcium audit also unchanged.

audits.t: Prospective population based survey of outcome of pregnancy in diabetic women: results of the Northern Diabetic Pregnancy Audit, 1994.
audits.st: St Vincent declaration target: diabetic pregnancy outcome approximating non-diabetic outcome
audits.f: Perinatal mortality 48/1000 vs 8.9/1000 background (OR 5.38); neonatal mortality 59/1000 vs 3.9/1000; congenital malformation 83/1000 vs 21.3/1000.

audits.t: CASES--clinical audit; scenarios for evaluation and study.
audits.tp: Dental practice audit and peer review scheme
audits.st: Regional and national results
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Delays in thrombolytic therapy in acute myocardial infarction: an audit from the east coast of peninsular Malaysia.
audits.tp: Thrombolysis use in acute myocardial infarction
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 70% arrived within 6 hours; median door-to-needle 85 minutes. 46 of 67 thrombolysed within 6 hours of onset; 59 of 81 confirmed infarctions thrombolysed.

audits.t: Audit of diabetes care by caseload.
audits.st: British Paediatric Association 1990 recommendation of specialist care with caseload over 40 in a designated clinic
audits.f: 701 seen in a designated clinic; 7 of 21 consultants met BPA specialist criteria. Children under non-specialists had more admissions and lower microalbuminuria screening.

audits.t: Audit of percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy in long-term enteral feeding in a nursing home.
audits.st: Eight quality-of-care criteria covering pre-insertion, early and long-term follow-up
audits.f: Early mortality 13.8%, mid-term 12.1%, late 19.0%. Only 20% free of skin complications at the insertion site; pulmonary complications 39%; 15 (25.8%) tried to remove the tube.

audits.t: Bile duct imaging and injury: a regional audit of laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Completed laparoscopically in 832 (89.6%). Cholangiography rose from 5.9% (1991) to 32.2% (1995); 15.4% with clinical indicators of stones had no bile duct imaging. Main bile duct injury 0.86%; total injury rate 2.8%.

audits.t: An audit of hospital mortality after urgent and emergency surgery in the elderly.
audits.tp: Perioperative care of older emergency surgical patients
audits.st: NCEPOD recommendations on senior involvement, night-time operating and futile surgery
audits.f: In-hospital deaths 13/49 after general surgery vs 2/53 after orthopaedic surgery (P<0.05); 12 of 25 laparotomies died.

audits.t: An audit of structure, process and outcome of care of the diabetic clinic, National Hospital of Sri Lanka.
audits.st: Standards expected of a tertiary referral centre diabetes clinic (validated audit case record forms)
audits.f: Average 186 patients a day; 2.1 minutes per patient; no screening; mean knowledge score 15.1/40; 43% bypassed a local institution; mean wait 1.56 hours to see doctor.

audits.t: Does participation in distance learning and audit improve the care of patients with acute asthma attacks? The General Practitioners in Asthma Group.
audits.st: Recommended asthma management guidelines
audits.f: Nebulised bronchodilators 272 (35%); systemic steroids 563 (72%); step-up in preventive therapy 402 (51%).
audits.c: Distance learning programme and personalised audit feedback.

audits.t: An audit of in-patients aged 18-65 in acute psychiatric wards who are inappropriately placed three months after admission.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean inpatient weeks for inappropriately placed patients 41.8.
audits.c: Named social worker for each ward and a monthly contact sheet tracking progress.
audits.r2: Mean inpatient weeks for inappropriately placed patients rose to 64.7 (p=0.05).

audits.t: An audit of the assessment and management of adults admitted to Christchurch Hospital with community acquired pneumonia.
audits.st: Management guidelines and modified British Thoracic Society severity criteria
audits.f: Guidelines followed without exception in 15%; only 33% of severe cases correctly identified; 71% of severe cases given one antibiotic; first dose delayed in 44%.

audits.t: Emergency department triage: a program assessment using the tools of continuous quality improvement.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Chart audit of 100 triage notes plus interviews and observation; emergency medical attendants judged to function well as triage staff.

audits.t: [Examination and treatment of musculoskeletal diseases in general practice investigated by medical audit].
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Frequent plain X-rays for osteoarthritis; NSAIDs prescribed at one in four musculoskeletal contacts.

audits.t: Departmental audit in surgical anatomical pathology.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Peer review of 10% of accessions: about 2% significant error rate in descriptions; good technical quality; generally satisfactory turnaround.

audits.t: Reliability audit of a regional cardiac surgery registry.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Consistency between charts and registry 86.4%; inconsistency 9.9%; rejection 3.7%.

audits.t: Pharmacy audit: an aid to continuing education.
audits.st: Drug usage review criteria adapted from Joint Commission on Accreditation of Hospitals audit procedures
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Drug-specific protocol for a continuing education seminar recommended.

audits.t: Information sharing can reduce laboratory use by emergency physicians.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean 2.36 laboratory studies per patient; mean laboratory cost $32,415 per month.
audits.c: Physician profiling: each physician's laboratory use presented and discussed at monthly meetings over 15 months.
audits.r2: Mean 1.94 studies per patient (17.8% decrease); cost $26,687 per month (17.7% decrease).

audits.t: Audit of public sector primary diabetes care in Cape Town, South Africa: high prevalence of complications, uncontrolled hyperglycaemia, and hypertension.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Acceptable glycaemic control 49.4%; acceptable blood pressure control in 38.5% of hypertensive patients; complications largely undocumented in the preceding year's records (only 1 patient with absent foot pulses and 12 with proteinuria recorded).

audits.t: Depth of central venous catheter insertion in adults: an audit and assessment of a technique to improve tip position.

audits.f: Standard technique inserted all CVCs to 15 cm; tip location assessed retrospectively (figures not reported).
audits.c: New tailored insertion technique using the skin-to-venepuncture distance to set insertion depth.
audits.r2: Tailored technique significantly reduced CVC tips entering the right atrium (P < 0.001).

audits.t: [Can medical files be used to audit hospital health care? Results of a regional audit of hospital file quality].
audits.st: Simplified ANDEM/ANAES medical file audit form
audits.f: Reason for hospitalisation recorded in 74.1% of files; operation report present in 83.2%; discharge summary present in 66.6%.

audits.t: Evaluation of orthodontic treatment outcome: a personal clinical audit using the PAR index (peer assessment rating).
audits.st: PAR index assessment of treatment standard
audits.f: Mean PAR score reduction 82.6%; 92.3% of cases improved; 4 (7.7%) worse or no different.

audits.t: Thromboembolic prophylaxis in 3575 hospitalized patients with atrial fibrillation. The Clinical Quality Improvement Network (CQIN) Investigators.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 33% received no prophylaxis, 24% warfarin alone, 35% aspirin alone, 8% both; in nonvalvular AF without contraindications 37% received neither and 23% warfarin alone.

audits.t: Palliative care of cancer patients: audit of current hospital procedures.
audits.st: Appropriateness of procedures judged by two external auditors
audits.f: 56 symptoms reviewed; 72 diagnostic procedures necessary for only 50% of symptoms; 130 therapeutic interventions necessary for 55% of symptoms.

audits.t: Implementation and evaluation of a quality improvement process to improve pain management in a hospice setting.
audits.st: Five aspects of pain management documentation
audits.f: Pre-implementation chart audit of 702 patient visits (figures not reported).

audits.t: Palliative care at home: an audit of cancer deaths in Grampian region.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Pain poorly controlled in 15.7%; other symptoms poorly controlled in 13.8% to 21%; 26% of district nurse referrals late; patients fully informed of diagnosis in 66.3% and prognosis in 55.4%.

audits.t: A clinical audit project. Record-keeping of patient status and monitoring.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: [Preventive treatment of thrombosis: audit on heparin prescription].

audits.r2: 81% of doses adapted to thrombotic risk, 2% too low, 17% too high.

audits.t: The national asthma audit. Bridging the gap between guidelines and practice.

audits.t: Auditing outcomes from a medicine for the elderly service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Assessment of GP management of symptoms of dying patients in an Australian community hospice by chart audit.

audits.f: Attempt to find a direct cause shown for 87/125 symptoms (70%); 107/114 treatments (90%) conformed to guidelines.

audits.t: [Compliance with regulations for medical records in 15 Aquitaine public health facilities. Aquitaine DIM Physician's Group].
audits.st: 18 ANDEM (1992) criteria updated to national regulations

audits.t: Audit of antihypertensive treatment in patients with renal failure.

audits.st: Target blood pressure 125/75 mmHg

audits.t: Medical audit after 26,711 breast imaging studies: improved rate of detection of small breast carcinomas (classified as Tis or T1a,b)

audits.c: Mammography reporting by a single dedicated radiologist instead of several general radiologists.

audits.t: An audit of children referred with suspected epilepsy.

audits.st: 30-question audit standard (history, examination, investigation, treatment and communication)
audits.f: Standard met for most questions; provoking factor recorded in 32/50 (64%); family told of voluntary epilepsy organisation in 0 to 48%.

audits.t: Questionnaire study and audit of use of angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor and monitoring in general practice: the need for guidelines to prevent renal failure.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Renal function checked before treatment in 55 (45%) and after starting in 35 (29%) of 122 practice patients; ACE inhibitors implicated in 9 (7%) of 135 uraemia admissions.

audits.t: Assessment of deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis in surgical patients: a study conducted at Nancy University Hospital, France.
audits.st: Criteria based on published thromboprophylaxis guidelines
audits.f: Prophylaxis documented in 86; indications appropriate in 90.7% and dosage in 75.2%; platelet count before treatment 73.8% and during 23.10%.

audits.t: Population-based audit of non-insulin-dependent diabetic patients aged under 65 years in primary health care.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Diagnosis made in 63% with two raised fasting glucose values; 87% had annual check-up; 36% satisfactory metabolic control.

audits.t: [Poor leadership behind poor pain relief. Medical audit of cancer-related pain treatment].
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 93 (61%) reported pain; 9 had undetected neuropathic pain; 18 had significant pain and were dissatisfied.

audits.t: A real-time audit of radiation therapy in a regional cancer center.
audits.st: Peer review approval of radiotherapy plans and treatment policies
audits.f: 124 (4.1%) plans not approved for planning errors, 79% of which were modified before treatment; 110 (3.6%) not approved for policy deviations.

audits.t: X-RAY AUDIT AT PRINCESS ALICE HOSPICE: IS THERE A ROLE FOR ON-SITE X-RAY IMAGING AT HOSPICES?
audits.st: If X-ray imaging is needed, it is performed where necessary and appropriate
audits.f: 18 occasions when X-ray was considered (11 chest, 3 pelvic, 1 shoulder, 3 abdominal); 4 of 18 (22%) deemed crucial and all transferred; 14 managed clinically; 7 of 18 appropriate to transfer.

audits.t: Radiation exposure of patients during mini C-arm use: an audit in 2032 procedures.

audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median screening time 11 seconds, median dose area product 0.75 cGycm2 overall; open surgery median 23 seconds/1.45 cGycm2, closed procedures 7 seconds/0.57 cGycm2, steroid injections 7 seconds/0.45 cGycm2; no significant difference between wrist/forearm and hand/digit procedures

audits.t: Self-reported and actual adherence to the Tokyo guidelines in the European snapshot audit of complicated calculous biliary disease.
audits.tp: Adherence to Tokyo Guidelines in complicated biliary calculous disease
audits.st: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 (TG18) for management of acute cholecystitis/cholangitis
audits.f: 152/338 (45.0%) index admission cholecystectomy, 17 (5.0%) interval cholecystectomy, 169 (50.0%) no surgery by 60 days; acute care surgery model more likely to do index cholecystectomy (57% vs 38%, OR 2.14, 95% CI 1.37-3.35)

audits.t: Dizziness, driving, and the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency: audit of advice given to patients, and design of a patient information leaflet.
audits.st: DVLA driving rules advice documented

audits.t: An audit of UK audiological practice in specialist paediatric oncology centres regarding hearing assessment of children at risk of ototoxicity due to chemotherapy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 17/19 centres (89%) responded; all offered audiometric monitoring; extended high-frequency testing used by 7 services (29%); only 4 (23%) kept all children with normal hearing under review after treatment.

audits.t: P51 External Ventricular Drainage Insertion Audit
audits.st: National EVD infection rate (9.3%) and national average sampling time
audits.f: Catheter-associated infection 12%; mean EVD duration 18 days; leaks 11 (26%)

audits.t: P73 LEARN: uroLogical tEAching in bRitish medical schools Nationally - a national retrospective multi-centre audit of urology teaching across British medical schools
audits.st: BAUS Undergraduate Syllabus for Urology (2012)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Admission avoidance in tonsillitis and peritonsillar abscess: A prospective national audit during the initial peak of the COVID-19 pandemic.
audits.st: New guidelines for the management of tonsillitis and peritonsillar abscess during COVID-19
audits.f: 54.4% of tonsillitis and 45.3% of PTA discharged from ED; re-presentation within 10 days 9.6% (39/408) and 10.3% (19/184).

audits.t: An audit to determine how teratogenic risks of carbimazole are considered for patients of child-bearing potential in an acute hospital setting
audits.st: MHRA 2019 guidance: acknowledgement of risk documented (70%); pregnancy or contraception status (80%); patient information provided (70%)
audits.f: No documented acknowledgement of risk in 44 (56%); pregnancy or contraception status documented in 29 (36%); specific risk consideration documented in 15 (19%).
audits.c: Recommended: upskill pharmacists and use electronic prescribing to mandate contraception status.

audits.t: An audit of high oral broad-spectrum antibiotic prescribing within a Bristol-based general practice
audits.st: 0% of oral broad-spectrum antibiotics prescribed inappropriately (outside regional guidance without specialist input or evidence of infection)
audits.f: 107 (51%) prescriptions inappropriate: 63 (30%) wrong antibiotic choice, 44 (21%) no evidence of infection.
audits.c: Planned: clinical governance meeting, updated EMIS alerts and antimicrobial stewardship protocols, re-audit 7 months later.

audits.t: An audit of discharge medicines counselling on an acute elderly admissions unit
audits.st: Trust standard: all patients with medication changes receive verbal discharge counselling and are offered a MaPPs leaflet/chart
audits.f: 11 received verbal counselling; none offered a MaPPs leaflet; 8 (40%) received no written information; none told about side-effects.
audits.c: Recommended: MaPPs leaflets and verbal counselling for all, pharmacy-led MaPPs training for nurses, handover reminders and documentation on e-prescribing.

audits.t: An audit of the pharmacological management of patients experiencing acute alcohol withdrawal at a large tertiary centre
audits.st: Local and NICE CG100 guidance: 100% AUDIT-C on admission; 100% CIWA-Ar 4-hourly on day one; 100% benzodiazepine reducing regimen; 100% discharged on thiamine 200-300mg daily where indicated
audits.f: AUDIT-C completed 2% (n=1); CIWA-Ar 4-hourly 14% (n=6); correct reducing regimen 23% (n=10); thiamine on discharge 34% (n=15). No standards met.

audits.t: An audit on patient safety in a community pharmacy using DATIX: reporting near misses
audits.st: 100% of near misses logged on paper entered onto DATIX
audits.f: 72% of near misses entered on DATIX (33 vs 46 on paper log); standard not met.

audits.t: An audit to review high risk asthma patients with over-use of short-acting beta-agonist inhalers
audits.tp: SABA overuse and MART in asthma
audits.st: NICE NG80 and BTS/SIGN 158: 100% of patients with 12 or more SABA inhalers in 12 months have a completed annual asthma review
audits.f: 16 of 41 had an up-to-date annual asthma review.
audits.c: Patients contacted and referred to pharmacist or asthma nurse for review, with inhaler technique checks and education; quarterly safety searches introduced.
audits.r2: 29 of 41 had an asthma review; 12 could not be contacted.

audits.t: 476 Prescribing of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) following a venous thromboembolism: a retrospective audit study
audits.st: Appropriate DOAC dose for renal function and appropriate treatment duration
audits.f: 98% (328/334) had appropriate doses for renal function; duration documented in 81% (n=406); 23% (n=113) continued treatment dose after completing the treatment period without indication.

audits.t: An audit of a general practices compliance with national recommendations for the avoidance of complications for type 2 diabetic patients
audits.tp: Type 2 diabetes care in primary care
audits.st: NICE NG28 and Quality and Outcomes Framework: six standards on nephropathy, hypertension, statins, QRISK2 and SGLT2 inhibitors
audits.f: ACEi/ARB for nephropathy 76% (19/25); hypertensive readings 50% (153/304); QRISK2 documented 7% (28/374); SGLT2 inhibitor 9% (32/374); statin primary prevention 73% (122), secondary 87% (89). No standards met.

audits.t: Audit of ‘true’ penicillin allergies and their documentation in Milton Keynes University Hospital (MKUH)
audits.st: ≥70% nature of allergy documented on eCare; ≥90% of eCare allergies also on Summary Care Record; 100% not given penicillin; ≥90% allergy label justified by nature of allergy
audits.f: Nature of allergy documented in 63.3% (n=57); also on SCR 85.6% (n=77); 93.3% (28/30) on antibiotics not given penicillin; justified allergy 50% (n=45). None of the four standards met.
audits.c: Planned: clinician training, new hospital guideline for a penicillin allergy de-labelling service, re-audit after 6 months.

audits.t: An audit of oral antimicrobial therapy against acne vulgaris NICE guidelines
audits.st: NICE acne guidance: 100% appropriate therapy; 100% under 6 months of antibiotics; 100% of women of childbearing age considered for contraception
audits.f: 9.8% (10) on correct oral and topical therapy; 90.2% (92) had antibiotics longer than 6 months; contraception not prescribed in 30.4% (17) of women of childbearing age.

audits.t: An audit of adherence to National Cancer Care Programme chemotherapy regimens and prescribing standards in systemic anti-cancer therapy prescriptions in an Irish hospital
audits.st: National Cancer Care Programme (NCCP) SACT regimens and 24 prescribing standards
audits.f: 86.3% adhered to NCCP regimens (oncology 89.2%, haematology 82.3%); over 98% compliance for 11 of 24 prescribing standards; only 7% on pre-printed forms.

audits.t: A prospective audit on adult thromboprophylaxis and therapeutic anticoagulation prescribing and administration practices in Galway University Hospitals
audits.st: Local anticoagulation guidelines and national HSE recommendations
audits.f: 92% (216/234) had no thromboprophylaxis risk assessment form completed; 35% (19 of 54) not on anticoagulants should have been; high compliance (>80%) for correct section, agent, dose and frequency; low compliance (<35%) for height and weight documentation and administration times.
audits.c: Targeted education and training plus a new eLearning module for high-alert medications; electronic prescribing under consideration; re-audit planned for 2024.

audits.t: A prospective re-audit on insulin prescribing and administration practices in a university teaching hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Prescribing errors in 78% (32/41); administration errors 88% (36/41); unsigned orders 12% (5/41); administration times not documented 46% (19/41); no second check 29% (12/41).
audits.c: Senior diabetes pharmacist appointed, updated insulin record, eLearning module for high-alert medications and continuous education.
audits.r2: Prescribing errors 63% (24/38); administration errors 84% (32/38); unsigned orders 21% (8/38); administration times not documented 42% (16/38); no second check 21% (8/38); contact details documented 71% (27/38) vs 59% (24/41).

audits.t: An audit to review the prescribing and monitoring of high-intensity statin therapy in acute coronary syndrome patients
audits.st: Local, NICE CG181 and ESC guidance: baseline and 3-month LFT and lipid profile; high-intensity statin
audits.f: Atorvastatin 80mg started in 84.2%; LFTs 96.5% on admission and 84.2% at follow-up; lipid profile 73.7% baseline and 47.4% follow-up; 78.9% achieved 40% non-HDL reduction; 63% reached LDL-C <1.8mmol/L.

audits.t: An audit of the continuation and review of intensive care unit (ICU)-initiated medications post ICU discharge
audits.tp: Medication discrepancies at transitions of care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 51 of 53 had ICU-initiated medications continued; stress ulcer prophylaxis continued in 52.9%, opioids 39.2%, anti-delirium medications 33.3%; no class reviewed for all patients.

audits.t: A national audit of prescribing in Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS)
audits.tp: Psychotropic prescribing in children and young people
audits.st: Six standards (consultant involvement, consent, baseline physical assessment, ongoing monitoring, GP communication, follow-up) each with 95% target
audits.f: Consultant supervision 95%; consent documented 89%; baseline monitoring 90%; ongoing monitoring 92%; GP communication 90%; follow-up arranged 98%.

audits.t: Audit project on the appropriateness of teicoplanin prescribing in Milton Keynes University Hospital (MKUH)
audits.st: Trust teicoplanin guideline; 100% for approved indication, loading dose prescribed, correct loading dose, correct maintenance dose to Day 4, correct maintenance dose from Day 5
audits.f: Approved indication 90% (n=79); loading dose prescribed 82% (n=71); correct loading dose 46% (n=40); correct maintenance to Day 4 60% (34/57); correct maintenance after Day 4 56% (22/39). None of the 5 standards met.
audits.c: Recommended: prescriber training on the EPMA pre-populated teicoplanin dose function and Antibiotic Guardian pledges at induction; re-audit in 1 year.

audits.t: An audit of the adherence to dosing and therapeutic monitoring of intravenous vancomycin in accordance with the trust’s antimicrobial guidelines
audits.st: Trust antimicrobial guidelines: seven standards on indication, loading and maintenance dose, trough timing, dose adjustment, missed doses and pharmacist screening
audits.f: Indication documented 96%; correct loading dose 65.3%; correct maintenance dose 64.7%; initial trough on time 32.23%; subsequent troughs 35%; correct dose adjustments 44%; pharmacist screened 57.33%. No targets met.
audits.c: Findings shared, TDM education for junior pharmacists and digital prompts on EPMA.

audits.t: An audit to evaluate the prescribing of antibiotics for acne against NICE guidelines in a digital setting
audits.st: NICE NG198: 100% oral antibiotics ≤6 months, with non-antibiotic topical, and no topical plus oral antibiotic
audits.f: 99% did not exceed six months of oral antibiotics; 99% had non-antibiotic topical alongside oral antibiotic.

audits.t: An audit to review compliance to cisplatin hydration guidelines within the royal Marsden NHS hospital
audits.st: Local cisplatin hydration policy: 100% weighed before and after cisplatin
audits.f: 72% of administration episodes had weight recorded before and after treatment; of the 28% missing, 4 had a documented AKI and 3 needed admission.

audits.t: eHospitals and Parkinson’s disease care: audit insights from an EPIC-integrated Hospital

audits.f: Only 29% received PD medications on time for every dose; 76% no missed doses or valid reason; medicines reconciliation within 24 hours 83%; SAM assessment 5%; PD specialist review 76%.

audits.t: (ID: 16) An audit to evaluate the prescribing of high-cost drugs for atopic dermatitis in one district general hospital
audits.st: NICE: 100% tried at least one systemic immunosuppressant (or unsuitable) and drug stopped at 16 weeks without EASI 50 and 4-point DLQI reduction
audits.f: 2/30 had not tried an immunosuppressant; 7/30 did not meet NICE response at 16 weeks but continued; mean EASI fell from 22.1 to 5 and DLQI from 18 to 7.
audits.c: More robust initiation process and MDT discussion for those not meeting 16-week response criteria.

audits.t: (ID: 54) Transforming gentamicin prescribing: an audit on safety and compliance
audits.st: Local TDM guideline (Urban & Craig nomogram): 90% correct dose ±10%; 90% levels at correct time; 90% levels correctly interpreted and redosed
audits.f: Correct dose 61.2% (82/134); levels at the right time 44% (59/134); correct redosing 41.6% (32/77).
audits.c: Gentamicin calculator, ward education, maximum dose warning and aligned pathology warning flag.

audits.t: (ID: 100) Integration of genomics into medicines optimisation governance processes and formularies: a retrospective audit
audits.st: NHS England plan to integrate genomics into medicines optimisation
audits.f: 228 of 506 drugs (45%) had actionable genes; 62 of 135 high-cost drugs (46%) had testing requirements in Blueteq forms; 90 of 93 commonly prescribed drugs had no pharmacogenomic reference in formularies.

audits.t: Severe group A streptococcal infections in mothers and their newborns in London and the South East, 2010-2016: assessment of risk and audit of public health management.

audits.st: National guidelines recommending antibiotics for both mother and neonate if either develops invasive group A Streptococcus within 28 days of birth, and investigation of maternity unit clusters
audits.f: All eligible mothers and 109/122 (89%) eligible neonates received chemoprophylaxis; in 6 of 15 clusters, GAS isolates were not saved for comparison even after relevant guidance was issued.

audits.t: Audit of provincial IVIG Request Forms and efficacy documentation in four Ontario tertiary care centres.

audits.st: IVIG Request Form requirements: verification of diagnostic and utilisation criteria per current guidelines, and documentation of clinical efficacy
audits.f: Most common indications were immune thrombocytopenia (24.2%) and secondary immune deficiency (20.2%); 24.2% were for conditions not listed on the form, mostly not indicated in current guidelines; 32.6% lacked verification of diagnostic criteria and 51.7% lacked verification of utilisation criteria (better documentation at the active surveillance site, P=0.005); 19.1% had a discrepancy between the form indication and documented diagnosis; 18.7% of follow-up notes had no mention of efficacy

audits.t: Audit of thromboprophylaxis decision-making at three independent hospice inpatient units
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Audit of delayed discharges from a specialist palliative care unit
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: An audit of the prescribing, administering and monitoring of oxygen therapy within a hospice

audits.f: Indication documented in 82%; previous steroid use in 18%; drug interactions considered in 4/21 (19%); blood sugar monitoring instructions in 24%; gastroprotection with aspirin or NSAID in 36/41 (87%).

audits.t: A REGIONAL RE-AUDIT OF THE SYMPTOMATIC MANAGEMENT OF NAUSEA & VOMITING IN THE MEDICAL MANAGEMENT OF MALIGNANT BOWEL OBSTRUCTION

audits.t: The management of malignant ascites in Palliative care: An audit of clinical practice and development of standards and guidelines

audits.t: An audit of opioid prescribing at a teaching hospital

audits.st: Recommendations from 2007 audit: indication, dose, response and planned duration documented; PPI for patients on steroids and NSAIDs; management plan on discharge
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Merseyside and Cheshire palliative care network audit and guidelines for managing breathlessness

audits.t: Audit of the use of ‘just-in case’ boxes as part of a local enhanced service agreement for end of life care

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Audit of minority ethnic group referrals to the specialist pyschological service for oncology and palliative care in East Berkshire
audits.tp: Ethnic equity in mental health service access

audits.t: Facilities offered to families and carers of patients at the end of life: audit of current practice
audits.tp: Facilities for relatives of dying patients
audits.st: End of life care strategy guidance supporting King's Fund recommendations for carer facilities
audits.f: Drinks offered in 93%; concessionary parking permits in only 23%; no concessionary dining room use; purpose-built wards offered more facilities.

audits.t: Audit of assessment of anxiety and depression in older inpatients with end stage COPD
audits.st: NICE guidelines on assessing anxiety and depression in COPD
audits.f: None of 18 patients had a recorded mental health assessment or screening tool, despite notes suggesting possible anxiety or depression in 7.

audits.t: Improving awareness of corneal donation: audit of practice and intervention in two clinical settings
audits.st: Current guidance: 100% identification of potential donors and 100% referral
audits.f: No documented assessment of eligibility, patient preference, family discussion or referral at either site; 55% (hospice) and 54% (hospital) had no contraindications.
audits.c: At Kingston General Hospital: new Liverpool Care Pathway documentation with assessment fields and a teaching session.
audits.r2: Kingston: three documented eligibility assessments and three documented family discussions (none before).

audits.t: Sustainable impact through a network audit programme
audits.st: Network-developed palliative care standards and guidelines
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: National primary care audit in end of life care and ACP and recommendations for improvement
audits.st: GSF After Death Analysis Audit Tool compared with recommended best practice standards
audits.f: Only 27% of patients who died were on the palliative care register (23% of these non-cancer); patients on the register received better coordinated care and were more likely to be offered ACP discussions.

audits.t: AUDIT OF RESUSCITATION PLANNING AND DOCUMENTATION AT A TERTIARY CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL OVER A 12 MONTH PERIOD
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Discussion about end of life care documented in 24 of 28 (85.6%) charts of children with life limiting conditions, but only two (8.3%) were readily identifiable; documentation dated on average 35.6 days before death.

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF THE PREVALENCE AND CHARACTERISTICS OF ADVANCE CARE PLANNING FOR PATIENTS FROM RESIDENTIAL AGED CARE FACILITIES (RACFS) REFERRED TO THE MOBILE ASSESSMENT AND TREATMENT SERVICE (MATS)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Prevalence of ACP 38%, Medical Enduring Power of Attorney 37% and Not for Resuscitation form 35%; ACP and NFR forms more likely in high care than low care facilities (79% vs 21%, p=0.049; 80% vs 20%, p=0.032).

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF CURRENT PRACTICE OF DOCUMENTATION AND IDENTIFICATION OF SUBSTITUTE DECISION-MAKERS/PERSONS RESPONSIBLE IN AUSTRALIAN RESIDENTIAL AGED CARE FACILITIES
audits.st: Victorian Guardianship and Administration Act 1986
audits.f: First next-of-kin documented more consistently than second (75% vs 33%); POA-MT or guardianship noted in about 15% of admission forms with only 15.4% having valid documents; admission forms unclear in 26.1%; first NOK was a potential person responsible in 71.8% of those without POA-MT, of whom 49% were confirmed.

audits.t: REVIEW OF THE INTRODUCTION AND AUDIT OF THE USE OF THEACUTE RESUSCITATION PLANAND RELATED DOCUMENTS TO ENHANCE END-OF-LIFE CARE ACROSS THE TOWNSVILLE HOSPITAL, A LARGE TERTIARY HOSPITAL IN PROVINCIAL QUEENSLAND
audits.st: Use of the Acute Resuscitation Plan (ARP) or satisfactory equivalent documentation
audits.f: About 80% of dying patients had a resuscitation plan in place when they died.
audits.c: Introduction of the Acute Resuscitation Plan (2009) and Paediatric ARP (2012) forms (before the audit period)

audits.t: A BROADER APPROACH TO LIMITATION OF MEDICAL TREATMENT: AUDIT OF COMPLIANCE AFTER CHANGING FROM ‘NFR’ TO ‘GOALS OF CARE’ IN AN ACUTE HOSPITAL
audits.st: Completion of the Goals of Care form documenting limitation of medical treatment
audits.f: NFR form uptake by medical teams 34%.
audits.c: 'Not For Resuscitation' forms replaced with a 'Goals of Care' form (curative, palliative, terminal categories) in March 2010
audits.r2: 52% of patients had a GOC form completed; uptake by medical teams 84% (vs 34% for NFR form).

audits.t: P87 May I?: Audit of documentation of consent for care
audits.st: Hospice policy: consent status documented for all personal and invasive procedures
audits.f: 74% of care plans had consent status recorded; only 37% of registered nurses recorded it.
audits.c: Training on consent, Mental Capacity Act (2005) and record keeping.
audits.r2: 93% of care plans had consent status recorded; registered nurses 77%.

audits.t: P154 Food and nutrition in a hospice: From audit to action
audits.tp: Nutrition and hydration in palliative care
audits.st: Help the Hospices Food and Nutrition Group / National Audit Tools Group Nutrition and Hydration Audit tool standards
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Nutrition Requirements Tool introduced on the ward; regular teaching and training for staff and volunteers; eight-week patient and carer support and education programme; Nutrition Steering Group

audits.t: P14 The impact of audit on CNS team development
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Low levels of referral information causing delayed contact, difficulty assessing urgency, unclear other service involvement and unnecessary home visits.
audits.c: New streamlined referral process, full-time specialist triage nurse, helpline for patients and professionals, electronic notes and enhanced documentation

audits.t: NUTRITIONAL ASSESSMENT AND MANAGEMENT — AN AUDIT OF CURRENT PRACTICE
audits.tp: Nutrition and hydration in palliative care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 64% did not use any nutritional screening assessment; 69% of MDTs had access to specialist nutrition advice; 58% in SPCS inpatient units aware of a protected mealtime policy; 44% had no nutritional training.
audits.c: MCCN guidelines for nutritional assessment and care subsequently published

audits.t: MANAGEMENT OF METASTATIC SPINAL CORD COMPRESSION: AUDIT
audits.st: NICE guidance on MSCC (MRI within 24 hours target 100%)
audits.f: Only 53% of suspected MSCC patients had MRI within 24 hours; two thirds had radiotherapy within one day; LMWH and analgesia given in 96%; all received steroids but dexamethasone prescribing inconsistent.

audits.t: THINK DELIRIUM! AN AUDIT OF ASSESSMENT OF COGNITION DURING ADMISSION TO A SCOTTISH PALLIATIVE CARE UNIT
audits.st: Assessment of cognition on admission or within 48 hours (Healthcare Improvement Scotland priority)
audits.f: 7 of 100 had cognitive assessment within 48 hours; of 34 with an indicator of cognitive impairment/delirium, 14.7% (n=5) assessed and none had a delirium screen; 68% (21/31) had the most obvious cause addressed; none had full assessment of causes.
audits.c: Planned education and a delirium screening and cause assessment tool; re-audit after implementation.

audits.t: AN AUDIT TO EVALUATE THE ASSESSMENT OF SPIRITUALITY FOR PATIENTS ADMITTED TO WILLOW WOOD HOSPICE INPATIENT UNIT
audits.tp: Spiritual concerns documentation in palliative care
audits.st: Spirituality section of admission pro forma completed; target 80%
audits.f: 73.30% (n=22) had documented spirituality conversation; females 89.47% (n=17), males 45.45% (n=5); standard not achieved.

audits.t: AN AUDIT TO IDENTIFY PATIENTS AT RISK OF SEROTONIN SYNDROME AT TIME OF ADMISSION TO A SPECIALIST PALLIATIVE CARE UNIT
audits.tp: Serotonin syndrome risk from drug combinations
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 68 of 100 took at least one implicated drug (34 on two or more); 59 of 68 had at least one symptom of serotonin toxicity; no patient met diagnostic criteria; no documentation that serotonin syndrome was considered in any patient.

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF THE INITIATION, PRESCRIPTION AND ADMINISTRATION OF OPIOID ANALGESIA TO ADULT PALLIATIVE CANCER PATIENTS IN AN ACUTE HOSPITAL
audits.st: NICE (2012) opioid guidance, NPSA (2010), NMC (2010) and local hospital standards; 15 standards
audits.f: Only a third of the 15 standards showed compliance (±10%); high rate of PRN-only prescribing, only 45 started on regular opioids.

audits.t: AUDIT OF PRESCRIBING OF OPIATES AND SEDATIVES AT END OF LIFE IN A LARGE DISTRICT GENERAL HOSPITAL
audits.tp: Opioid and sedative use in the last days of life
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Opioids given to 73.3% (46.7% via CSCI); mean daily morphine equivalent doses 20.8 to 23.7 mg over last 7 days; sedation in 70% (43% via CSCI) with mean CSCI midazolam 3.8 to 11.3 mg/day.

audits.t: PREDICTING WHEN THE LCP MIGHT NOT BE USED?: AN AUDIT OF COMMUNICATION WITH SECONDARY, CONTENT ANALYSIS OF LANGUAGE
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 56 expected deaths, relatives were informed that the patient was dying in 100% of LCP-supported and 93% of non-LCP deaths.

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF PALLIATIVE CARE PRACTICES IN THE BRISTOL ROYAL INFIRMARY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
audits.st: College of Emergency Medicine (2012) end of life care guidelines (nine criteria)
audits.f: Died in ED: families involved 19/25, ceilings of treatment 23/25, DNAR forms 14/25, organ donation considered 23/25, bereavement services 20/25, end of life pathway 0/25. Died within 24 hours: families involved 13/25, ceilings in ED 10/25, DNAR 6/25, pathway 0/25.

audits.t: THE USE OF QTC PROLONGING MEDICATIONS & DRUG INTERACTIONS IN PALLIATIVE CARE PATIENTS: AUDIT OF PRESCRIBING IN A TERTIARY CANCER CENTRE
audits.tp: QTc-prolonging drug prescribing and ECG monitoring
audits.st: Prescribing guidance recommending risk assessment when using QTc prolonging medications
audits.f: 27 patients had QTc risk factors (21 with two or more); 12 received at least one QTc prolonging drug; 3 co-prescribed QTc prolonging and CYP450 inhibiting drugs; risk assessment documented in one case only.
audits.c: Interventions with the HSPCT, other prescribers and ward pharmacists to improve awareness, risk assessment and prescribing

audits.t: TO ESCALATE OR TO PALLIATE? AN AUDIT OF PATIENTS AT RISK OF DETERIORATION ON MEDICAL WARDS
audits.st: Modified tool based on NICE CG50: doctor/outreach contacted and patient reviewed after EWS >5 (100%)
audits.f: Doctor or outreach contacted in 70% with EWS >5; a third not reviewed; only 5 of 30 had a clear escalation plan.
audits.c: Results presented and published in hospital newsletter; escalation plan form and sticker being piloted.

audits.t: AN AUDIT INTO ADVANCED CARE PLANNING FOR END OF LIFE CARE PATIENTS AT KINGSTON HOSPITAL
audits.st: Local targets: resuscitation status 100%; prognosis, ceiling of care, readmission plans, patient/family awareness 95% in notes; 100% on discharge documentation
audits.f: Notes: resuscitation status 82%, prognosis 55%, ceiling of care 41%, readmission plans 14%, awareness 77%. Discharge: resuscitation status 6%, ceiling of care 56%, readmission plans 33%, awareness 59%.
audits.c: Advance care planning summary proforma, introduced at a department meeting with teaching for junior doctors.
audits.r2: Notes: resuscitation status 97%, prognosis 95%, ceiling of care 100%, readmission plans 100%, awareness 100%. Discharge: resuscitation status 89%, others 100%.

audits.t: AUDIT OF AVERAGE LENGTH OF STAY IN MARIE CURIE HOSPICE BELFAST
audits.st: Average length of stay 14 days or less
audits.f: 48.3% of patients had a length of stay of 14 days or less; average length of stay 19 days (18.9 days for those who died, 19.2 days for those discharged).

audits.t: AUDIT OF PALLIATIVE CARE PATIENT IDENTIFICATION IN GENERAL PRACTICE
audits.st: Gold Standards Framework early identification; Dying Matters guidance that about 25% of the palliative register should have cancer
audits.f: 12 of 33 deaths were on the palliative care register; 10 expected deaths were not registered (9 of 10 non-cancer); 66% of the register had cancer.

audits.t: AUDIT OF END OF LIFE DISCUSSIONS IN PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE
audits.st: NHS End of Life Care Council advice that end of life discussions be offered to COPD patients with poor prognostic markers
audits.f: Of 48 admissions with COPD exacerbation, 20 met criteria; 3 (15%) had documented end of life conversations; 17 of 20 made DNACPR but only 4 communicated to the GP.

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF REPORTED OPIATE ERRORS IN NORTHUMBRIA HEALTHCARE TRUST, 2012
audits.st: National Patient Safety Agency recommendations
audits.f: Morphine 50%, oxycodone 23% and fentanyl 18% of errors; administration errors 56% (n=19), prescribing 23% (n=8), both 21% (n=7).
audits.c: Transdermal patch administration and removal chart, educational opiate wall chart, alert sticker for high concentration opiate solutions

audits.t: AN INTERIM AUDIT USING THE NCDAH PROFORMA OF 30 CASE NOTES OF PATIENTS WHO HAVE DIED UTILISING THE LIVERPOOL CARE PATHWAY
audits.st: National Care of the Dying Audit in Hospitals key performance indicators
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Compared with last year: 4-hourly assessments increased by 1%, spirituality discussions by 9% and PRN medication prescribing by 9%.

audits.t: BASELINE AUDIT OF SUPPORTIVE CARE PROVISION FOR PATIENTS WHO DIED IN 2010 AND HAD LUNG TRANSPLANTS OR WERE ON THE WAITING LIST AT HAREFIELD HOSPITAL
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 50% of post-transplant deaths occurred in Harefield Hospital; most had late specialist palliative care involvement; one died in a hospice and none known to die at home; GP communication rarely mentioned SPC.
audits.c: Weekly transplant and SPC meetings, supportive care access for all waiting list patients, place of death added to hospital systems

audits.t: AN AUDIT OF DOCUMENTED REFERRAL INFORMATION FOR CHILDREN REFERRED TO A UK PAEDIATRIC AND YOUNG PERSON'S HOSPICE
audits.st: SIGN 31 minimum essential referral information
audits.f: Incomplete and inconsistent documentation of referrer contact details, reason for referral and child's location; not in line with SIGN 31.

audits.t: DNA CPR SCOTLAND POLICY: AN AUDIT OF THE SUCCESS OF IMPLEMENTATION IN NHS TAYSIDE
audits.st: Scottish Government National DNACPR Integrated Adult Policy (2010)
audits.f: DNACPR form present or completed during admission: Cornhill 92% (25/27), oncology 78% (23/30), cardiology 19% (10/52), MFE 29% (7/24); form went with patient on discharge/transfer in 100% Cornhill, 4% oncology, none cardiology or MFE.

audits.t: A SUMMARY OF THE NATIONAL CARE OF THE DYING AUDIT FOR HOSPITALS, ENGLAND (NCDAH) 2013/14 AUDIT RESULTS
audits.st: National Care of the Dying Audit for Hospitals standards
audits.f: Recognition of dying recorded in 87%; clinically assisted nutrition 45% and hydration 59%; spiritual needs assessment 21% (capable patients) and 25% (relatives); care after death 46%; 7-day SPCS access in 21% of hospitals; no audit in 44%.

audits.t: Are subcutaneous palliative medicines available and accessible: an out of hours (OOH) audit in sheffield
audits.tp: Out-of-hours access to palliative care medicines
audits.st: NICE Quality Standard 13 (2011): palliative care drugs accessible 24/7; locally derived standards set at 100%
audits.f: 100% of core subcutaneous medicines were available 24/7 (n=68 hospital supplies, n=21 community pharmacy supplies).

audits.t: Screening for Lynch syndrome and referral to clinical genetics by selective mismatch repair protein immunohistochemistry testing: an audit and cost analysis.
audits.st: Selective mismatch repair (MMR) immunohistochemistry (IHC) screening pathway (with BRAF V600E testing) for colorectal cancers to identify Lynch syndrome for clinical genetics referral
audits.f: 47/209 (21%) tumours showed IHC loss of expression in at least one MMR protein, at a cost of GBP 12,540 for MMR IHC; 28/44 cases with MLH1 loss had additional BRAF V600E testing (GBP 5040); this reduced potential clinical genetics referrals from 209 to 47, and further to 21 after BRAF testing; cost per referral GBP 1340, with potential savings of GBP 234,340.

audits.t: Family voices from the bedside: National Audit of Care at the End of Life (England and Wales)
audits.tp: Bereaved relatives' experience of end of life care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: More than 70% rated care of the dying person good, excellent or outstanding; at least 66% rated care to themselves as good or better; at least 76% felt staff communicated sensitively.

audits.t: An audit of the management of heart murmurs on the postnatal wards.
audits.st: Local guideline for management of neonatal heart murmurs based on clinical examination with selective cardiology review
audits.f: Guideline generally well adhered to; 51/89 (57%) babies referred for cardiology assessment, 40 of these had an echocardiogram; 30/89 (34%) had an underlying cardiac malformation, 25 identified before discharge; 15/30 (50%) of babies with cardiac malformation remained under cardiology follow-up at 1 year; no baby discharged without cardiology review subsequently presented with a cardiac problem.

audits.t: Current process and outcomes of the surgical management of LUTS due to benign prostatic enlargement: how consistent are we? - results from the multi-institutional audit of surgical management of BPE (AuSuM BPE) in the United Kingdom.
audits.tp: Surgical management of benign prostatic enlargement (BPE)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median age 73 years; indications were acute retention (47%) and LUTS (45%); 80% had prior medical therapy; monopolar TURP was the commonest procedure

audits.t: The London memory service audit and quality improvement programme.
audits.tp: Dementia diagnosis and treatment in memory services
audits.st: NICE dementia guideline
audits.f: Variation in neuroimaging practice, neuropsychology referrals, diagnosis subtype, non-dementia diagnoses, waiting times and post-diagnostic support.
audits.c: Four service improvement projects initiated from audit findings.

audits.t: Differences in care between younger and older patients in the 2019 English national memory service audit.
audits.tp: Memory service care variation by age
audits.st: 2019 English national memory service audit
audits.f: Care varied by age group; younger patients more likely to have MRI and less likely to be offered cognitive stimulation therapy; biomarker use low in both groups

audits.t: Natural language processing application to identify covert administration of medicines: development and pilot audit.
audits.st: Covert administration should have a completed mental capacity assessment and best interests meeting, with pharmacy consulted (source not named)
audits.f: 95% of patients receiving covert administration (41/43) had a completed mental capacity assessment and best interests meeting; pharmacy was contacted for 77%.

audits.t: Specialist adult ADHD clinics in East Anglia: service evaluation and audit of NICE guideline compliance
audits.st: NICE adult ADHD recommendations (adapted ADHD audit support tool)
audits.f: Good compliance for diagnosis, assessment and drug treatment; poor transition from CAMHS, underdeveloped comprehensive treatment programmes and deficient physical examinations.

audits.t: ECT practices in Iraq: a national audit
audits.st: Local ECT standards
audits.f: Only 2 clinics had at least 2 rooms and none had EEG monitoring; bilateral ECT in all cases; general anaesthesia in 77.15%.

audits.t: Adherence to medication in the community: Audit cycle of interventions to improve the assessment of adherence
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Adherence discussed 50%; side-effects discussed 30%; response to medication discussed 46%.
audits.c: Text messages to clinicians and prompt sheets in the out-patient department.
audits.r2: Adherence discussed 62%; side-effects discussed 60%; response to medication discussed 60%.

audits.t: CT Guided Lung Biopsies: An Audit Cycle
audits.st: British Thoracic Society guidelines
audits.f: Diagnostic rate 81%.
audits.c: Changes in practice after the initial audit, mainly core biopsy instead of fine needle aspiration.
audits.r2: Diagnostic rate 85.6% (within BTS standard); pneumothorax 28.9% (above BTS standard); chest drain 6.2%.

audits.t: Oxygen therapy in patients with chest pain of acute onset: single centre audit experience.
audits.tp: Oxygen therapy prescribing in acute chest pain
audits.st: national/international guidelines restricting oxygen therapy to hypoxic patients only
audits.f: Only 71% of patients were correctly assessed for requiring oxygen therapy.
audits.c: introduction of local guidelines and a series of educational lectures
audits.r2: Rose to 94% correctly assessed after the intervention; a third audit showed sustained change with 96% appropriately assessed.

audits.t: Quality of patient information in the acute surgical admission: a prospective audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Six weeks' notice of the on-call roster: fact or fantasy? An audit study.
audits.tp: Rota notice for doctors in training
audits.st: Code of Practice: duty roster available 6 weeks before start of post
audits.f: 4/48 (8%) received roster per standard; 9/48 (19%) received no roster before starting
audits.c: Shared spreadsheet of roster coordinator contacts, reminder emails to coordinators, results sent to NHS Improvement
audits.r2: 23/133 (17%) received roster per standard; 25/133 (19%) received no roster

audits.t: Assessing critical medication prescribing in the acute assessment unit: second cycle
audits.st: 100% of critical medications prescribed within 24 hours of admission (NICE medicines reconciliation)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Posters in medical areas of AAU and A&E.
audits.r2: 63 (74.1%) had critical medications prescribed by a doctor within 24 hours; 13 of the remaining 22 prescribed by pharmacy; overall compliance 89.4%, a decrease of 5.4%.

audits.t: Assessing Clinician Compliance With DVLA Guidelines for Psychiatric Inpatients
audits.st: DVLA and GMC guidance on fitness to drive
audits.f: Driving status established 73% (n = 22); 90% (n = 9) of drivers advised to tell DVLA; 9% (n = 1) advised to tell insurer.
audits.c: Results presented at Trust-wide teaching and driving status added to the MDT template.
audits.r2: Driving status established 67% (n = 20); 100% (n = 11) of drivers advised to tell DVLA; 64% (n = 7) advised to tell insurer.

audits.t: Early Intervention in Psychosis in Southwark – Bringing Antipsychotic Prescribing Closer to the Gold Standard
audits.st: RCPsych gold standard for treatment of first episode psychosis
audits.f: 33% (N = 172) of those on medication not in remission; 85% (N = 68) of these below licensed maximum; 50% (N = 52) treatment resistant; 3.8% (N = 26) of treatment-resistant on clozapine.
audits.c: One-page flowchart for the multidisciplinary team with an education session.
audits.r2: 37% (N = 147) not in remission; 76% (N = 55) below licensed maximum; 56% (N = 55) treatment resistant; 9.7% (N = 31) of treatment-resistant on clozapine.

audits.t: Management of Clozapine Induced Hypersalivation on Slow Stream Rehabilitation Ward
audits.st: Practical and pharmacological management options for clozapine-induced hypersalivation from the literature
audits.f: All six had hypersalivation; five tried hyoscine tablets first; practical measures such as raising the pillow and chewing gum were not routinely tried.

audits.t: Evaluation of Carer Contact Practices for Junction 17 CAMHS Inpatient Unit
audits.st: Trust policies on carer contact
audits.f: Assigned staff member 58% (7/12); consent documented 8% (1/12); contact within 72 hours 100%; after medication changes 66% (2/3); after incidents 73% (132/180); after home leave 87%; after ward round 47% (51/108).

audits.t: Improving the Management of Diabetes in a Secure Forensic Psychiatric Setting in the UK
audits.tp: Diabetes care in severe mental illness
audits.st: NICE NG28, European Association for the Study of Diabetes and Southern Health NHS Foundation Trust guidelines (e.g. 2.31 CBG measurements per day; 70% of CBG readings in target range; ketone test after hyperglycaemia 100%)
audits.f: Non-compliance with diabetic monitoring 19%; 1.17 CBG measurements per day; 39% of CBG readings in target range; novorapid after hyperglycaemia 67%; ketone test offered 7%
audits.c: Feedback sessions of audit findings with the MDT, information sessions on monitoring guidelines and dietary posters in patient areas
audits.r2: Non-compliance with monitoring 9%; 1.32 CBG measurements per day; 31% of CBG readings in target range; novorapid after hyperglycaemia 68%; ketone test offered 37%

audits.t: To Determine if Patients on Birkdale Ward Are Assessed for Risk of Venous Thromboembolism in Compliance With the Trust’s Standard Operating Procedure
audits.tp: VTE risk assessment in psychiatric inpatients
audits.st: Trust standard operating procedure for prevention and management of VTE (August 2023) and NICE guidance that all admitted patients have a VTE risk assessment
audits.f: Overall compliance 0%; 68% appropriately assessed at all trigger points, 38% required an up-to-date VTE assessment
audits.c: All patients needing an assessment received one and the SOP was disseminated to ward staff; SOP to be amended before re-audit

audits.t: Physical Health Monitoring for Children and Young People on Antipsychotic Medications in Salford CAMHS
audits.st: NICE CG155: height, weight, waist circumference, pulse, blood pressure, blood tests and ECG at baseline, 12 weeks and 6 months; 100% compliance expected
audits.f: Compliance below 50% for all standards; weight at baseline and 12 weeks 47.8%; blood tests 26% and ECG 35% at baseline; waist circumference 0% at any time point
audits.c: Planned antipsychotic monitoring checklist with consent form and a running tab for physical health parameters in the electronic notes; re-audit planned in 12 months

audits.t: Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Risk Assessment in Acute Inpatient Mental Health Wards in Sherwood Oaks and Millbrook Unit (now Blossomwood Unit), Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
audits.tp: VTE risk assessment in psychiatric inpatients
audits.st: Trust policy 02.21: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours of admission; NICE NG89 (stated as NG82) 2019: assess all acute psychiatric patients as soon as possible after admission or by first consultant review
audits.f: 69.3% assessed on admission (50% within 24 hours); 30.7% not assessed during admission

audits.t: Investigating Adherence to the 2022 NICE Vitamin D Management Guidelines on MHSOP (Mental Health Services for Older People) Wards
audits.st: NICE 2022 vitamin D guidance: all patients tested on admission; all with level 50 or below prescribed vitamin D; calcium replaced if also deficient; specialist referral if eGFR <30, hypercalcaemia or granulomatous conditions
audits.f: 30/34 (88%) tested on admission or had a recent level; 9 of 15 (60%) with insufficient or deficient levels prescribed vitamin D; 1 patient needing specialist referral not referred
audits.c: Vitamin D awareness poster on wards, meetings with the ward pharmacist and presentation at the local MHSOP clinical effectiveness meeting
audits.r2: 31/33 (94%) tested on admission; 9 of 12 (75%) requiring prescription were prescribed vitamin D

audits.t: Improving Carers’ Engagement in Patient Care During Psychiatric Admissions
audits.st: Five key carer engagement domains agreed with patient groups and carer representatives (carer notified of admission, carer care plan, collateral history from carer, carer notified of discharge)
audits.f: Carer notified of admission 30%; documented carer care plan 50%; collateral information from carer 30%; carer notified of discharge 40%
audits.c: Standardised Carer Contact Form introduced over several PDSA cycles, with staff training and competency assessments for nursing assistants
audits.r2: Carer notified of admission 87%; documented carer care plan 60%; collateral information 87%; carer notified of discharge 80%

audits.t: Evaluation of Suicide Risk Assessment Documentation Standards in Psychiatric Outpatient Clinics
audits.tp: Risk assessment documentation in mental health
audits.st: NICE NG225 and local trust standards for suicide risk assessment documentation
audits.f: Consent and confidentiality 4%; history of self-harm 28%; protective factors 52%; risk formulation 62%; plan and intent in those with suicidal ideation 0%; access to means 6%; shared decision-making 98%
audits.c: Audit findings summarised and fed back to clinicians
audits.r2: Consent and confidentiality 76%; history of self-harm 76%; protective factors 78%; risk formulation 82%; plan and intent 84%; access to means 14%; shared decision-making 84%

audits.t: Monitoring Matters: Physical Health Monitoring for Children and Young People Prescribed Antipsychotics in Community CAMHS
audits.st: Community CAMHS Physical Health Standard Operating Procedure for antipsychotic monitoring
audits.f: Blood tests 77% (10/13); ECG 85% (11/13); height and weight 62% (8/13); blood pressure and heart rate 62% (8/13); allergy status 62% (8/13); neurological examination for EPSEs 0%; only 6 patients had all parameters documented
audits.c: Proposed electronic reminders, structured antipsychotic monitoring template, teaching for medical staff and re-audit in 6 to 12 months

audits.t: Falls Risk Assessment Compliance and Outcomes in Psychiatry of Old Age Inpatient Department
audits.tp: Falls risk screening and multifactorial assessment
audits.st: NICE CG161: falls risk assessment within 24 hours of admission with interventions for identified risks
