audits.f: 4 of 5 patients (80%) assessed within 24 hours with risks addressed within 48 hours; clinical documentation present for all (100%); 4 falls recorded, all documented (100%)
audits.c: Education for team members on timely and accurate falls risk assessment

audits.t: Monitoring Troponin I and CRP During Clozapine Titration: Assessing Adherence to Myocarditis Protocols
audits.st: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines and Ronaldson algorithm: baseline and weekly troponin and CRP during the first four weeks of clozapine titration
audits.f: Baseline troponin and CRP documented in 80%, baseline ECG in 90%; 5 (50%) had mildly raised troponin (>3 but <13 ng/L), 80% of these had repeat troponin testing; no suspected myocarditis
audits.c: Recommendations to align local practice with Ronaldson and Maudsley protocols using locally agreed reference ranges, to be added to local policy; re-audit planned

audits.t: Pregnancy Testing and Gynaecological History in Female Admissions to an Acute Psychiatric Unit
audits.st: Pregnancy test and gynaecological history for female admissions of reproductive age within the first 2 weeks of admission
audits.f: Pregnancy test within 2 weeks 14.3% (4/28); asked about chance of pregnancy 7.14% (1/28); last menstrual period asked in 1 patient; contraception and sexual activity asked in none; cervical screening up to date 53.57% (15/28)
audits.c: Proposed posters, presentations and changes to prescribing software; re-audit planned

audits.t: Managing Memory - Optimising Anti-Dementia Medication Prescribing in an Inpatient Setting
audits.st: Trust and Maudsley prescribing guidelines for indication, dose titration and physical health monitoring; target at least 90% adherence per domain
audits.f: 7/20 (35%) candidates for inpatient-initiated anti-dementia medication; of 6 offered, 5 clearly indicated (83%); all titrated per guideline; physical health monitoring completed in 5 (83%)
audits.c: Raising staff awareness, disseminating results and visible audit reminders on ward lists
audits.r2: 6 (30%) candidates, only 4 prescribed an indicated drug (67%); all inpatient-initiated medications titrated and monitored to standard

audits.t: Screening for the impact of social media use on self-harm crisis presentations in children and adolescents - are we adhering to NICE guidelines?
audits.st: NICE 2022 self-harm guideline: psychosocial assessment includes enquiry about social media, its use to connect with others and its effect on mental health
audits.f: Social media enquiry 72%; social media used to connect with others 14%; impact on mental health 8%
audits.c: Planned presentation of results, training and re-audit

audits.t: Improving the management of Insomnia in Community General Adult Mental Health Care
audits.st: National guidance on insomnia management (Donaldson et al. 2009; NICE CKS 2025): sleep hygiene, CBT-i and appropriate hypnotic use
audits.f: Insomnia prevalence 58%; sleep hygiene advice 36% of relevant patients; CBT-i strategies 11%; combination hypnotics 15%
audits.c: Education programme for the clinical team on sleep physiology, guidelines and CBT-i, plus a simplified sleep management algorithm
audits.r2: Insomnia prevalence 63%; sleep hygiene advice 45%; CBT-i strategies 27%; combination hypnotics 8%

audits.t: Out of Town Meeting of the Ulster Paediatric Society, Friday 8th and Saturday 9th May 2009
audits.st: Regional hypopack protocol: samples analysed and reported, taken while the patient is hypoglycaemic and before dextrose, and reports filed in charts
audits.f: 35% of patients hypoglycaemic (<2.6 mmol/L) when sampled; 54% sampled before dextrose; 35% of laboratory reports missing from charts
audits.c: Redesigned request form, updated protocol and a summative report, introduced April 2006 with presentations to regional centres
audits.r2: 49% hypoglycaemic when sampled; 64% sampled before dextrose; 21% of insulin samples rejected as haemolysed; 35% of reports still missing from charts

audits.t: Awareness of difficult airway equipment on the ICU
audits.st: 100% of clinicians aware of location and contents of the difficult airway trolley; 100% of anaesthetists trained in difficult airway equipment
audits.f: 100% aware of the trolley; 35% had read the contents folder; 90% could name the equipment; 70% confident to use it unaided; 28% not airway trained
audits.c: Designated consultant teaching at quarterly induction, simulation and mannequin training, case-based teaching and airway proficiency assessments at induction
audits.r2: 100% aware of the equipment; 60% confident in its use; 100% airway trained

audits.t: Introduction of an external noninvasive cooling device for effective implementation of Intensive Care Society standards post cardiac arrest
audits.tp: Targeted temperature management after cardiac arrest
audits.st: Intensive Care Society standards: cooling to 32 to 34°C for 12 to 24 hours after ROSC
audits.f: Effectively cooled within 4 hours 33%; maintained in target range over 24 hours 57%; mean CPC at ICU discharge 3.4
audits.c: Introduction of an external noninvasive cooling device (CritiCool)
audits.r2: Effectively cooled within 4 hours 57%; maintained in target range 70%; mean CPC 2.3

audits.t: Impact of introducing guidelines for thrombolysis of submassive pulmonary embolism at a large UK teaching hospital
audits.st: New local guideline allowing thrombolysis for massive and submassive PE
audits.f: Previous guidelines suggested considering thrombolysis in only seven patients in 6 months
audits.c: New local guideline for thrombolysis of submassive and massive PE introduced March 2013
audits.r2: 46 patients with massive or submassive PE (32% of all PEs); thrombolysis given to 2, but 6 had no contraindications

audits.t: Written communication for itu discharges: a quality improvement project
audits.st: NICE clinical guidelines 50 and 83 domains for discharge summaries
audits.f: Frequent omissions: patient demographics (10%), doctor's designation (8%), bleep number (68%), plain-English summary for relatives (18%), relevant investigations (35%), monitoring plan on the ward (45%)
audits.c: Electronic discharge summary template with mandatory NICE-based headings and prompts
audits.r2: Legal aspects almost 100% compliant; reason for admission 99%; diagnosis 85%

audits.t: Histopathological diagnostic discrepancies in soft tissue tumours referred to a specialist centre: reassessment in the era of ancillary molecular diagnosis.
audits.tp: Soft tissue tumour referral and diagnosis
audits.st: NICE and RCPath recommendation that suspected soft tissue sarcomas are referred for specialist pathology review; discrepancy rates compared with the unit's 2005 audit
audits.f: Diagnostic agreement 73.4%; discrepancy 27.5% (15.7% minor, 10.9% major); 5% of discrepant cases benign-malignant discordances
audits.c: No local intervention; in the interval referral guidance was widely adopted and ancillary molecular testing became routine
audits.r2: Diagnostic agreement 250 (71.8%); 57 (16.4%) major and 41 (11.8%) minor discrepancies; 23 benign-malignant discrepancies (23.5% of discrepancies)

audits.t: An implementation program targeted at non-physician, anaesthesia assistants improves the quality of laryngeal mask anaesthesia.
audits.st: LMA cuff pressure within the manufacturers' recommended limit of <60 cmH2O, measured by manometer
audits.f: Only 4 (5%) cuff pressures were within the recommended <60 cmH2O; 57 (63%) exceeded the manometer scale (>120 cmH2O); 25 (27%) reported sore throat.
audits.c: Results presented to anaesthetists and anaesthetic assistants; manometers bought for every theatre; education and in-theatre demonstration for anaesthetic assistants on measuring and adjusting cuff pressure.
audits.r2: LMA pressures within recommended limits rose to 43%; pressures exceeding the manometer fell to 16%; pharyngolaryngeal morbidity 11% in the 45 patients whose pressure was reduced to normal (P=0.001).

audits.t: Improving hospital weekend handover: a user-centered, standardised approach.
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians handover guidance (minimum of 3 patient identifiers, ceiling of care, task urgency, assigned team member)
audits.f: 12 different pro formas in use; 87% had 3 patient identifiers; 1% documented ceiling of care; 0% documented task urgency; 63% had a named team member for the task
audits.c: Standardised weekend handover pro forma based on RCP guidance, launched with a teaching session, trust email and ward visits
audits.r2: 100% uptake of the single pro forma; 98% had 3 patient identifiers; 60% documented ceiling of care; 88% documented task urgency; 100% had a named team member

audits.t: Improving the quality of patient handover on a surgical ward.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidelines on surgical patient handover (minimum data set)
audits.f: 15% of patients handed over from CAU to ward FY1; 0% of handovers included the full RCSEng minimum data set
audits.c: Handover tool based on RCSEng guidance attached to the notes and signed by both FY1s, policy that handover occurs after senior review, a named ward FY1 for new admissions, and teaching
audits.r2: 45% of patients handed over; 100% of handovers contained all recommended information

audits.t: Evaluating the Quality of Medical Documentation at a University Teaching Hospital.
audits.st: NHS Litigation Authority record keeping standards, CQC essential standards and Oxford University Hospitals documentation guidelines (VTE assessment within 6 hours, clear plan, postoperative instructions, senior present documented, contemporaneous entries)
audits.f: VTE assessment within 6 hours 80% (available in 100%); plan and postoperative instructions 100%; contemporaneous entries 75%; consultant presence documented 80%
audits.c: Findings presented at the departmental audit meeting to raise awareness of contemporaneous documentation and recording the most senior person present

audits.t: Improving medical handover at the weekend: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians medical handover guidelines
audits.f: Doctor survey: 12% used the electronic system for weekend handover; 89% found sorting jobs time consuming; 67% handed jobs meant for another grade; 41% knew who to hand weekend discharges to; safety score 3.18/5
audits.c: New dedicated electronic handover database with a proforma, earlier structured Friday handover meeting chaired by a registrar with SBAR and a register, plus teaching, grand round and email from the medical director
audits.r2: 100% used the electronic system; 47% found sorting jobs time consuming; 37% handed jobs for another grade; 89% knew who to hand discharges to; safety score 3.84/5

audits.t: A multifaceted approach to prevention of delirium on intensive care.
audits.st: NICE CG103 delirium guidance; delirium rate compared with PRE-DELIRIC predicted rate (39%)
audits.f: Level 3 ICU patients: delirium at first assessment 65%, at any time 70% (16/23); 87% exposed to deliriogenic drugs
audits.c: Two PDSA programmes: delirium teaching, lighter sedation with short-acting agents and daily sedation breaks, redesigned drug booklets and charts, then unit refurbishment with more natural light and clocks, dexmedetomidine and chart prompts for delirium assessment
audits.r2: Delirium at first assessment 15%, at any time 29% (predicted 39%); 70% exposed to deliriogenic drugs

audits.t: Are we meeting current standards in medicines reconciliation? A study in a District General Hospital.
audits.st: NICE and Scottish Patient Safety Programme: 95% of patients to have medicines reconciliation within 24 hours of admission
audits.f: 46% reconciled on admission and 77% within 24 hours (abstract states 49% and 75%)
audits.c: Emergency Care Summary access for junior doctors plus lunchtime teaching and email reinforcement
audits.r2: Third cycle: 57% completed on admission and 84% at 24 hours; 89% had a complete medication history

audits.t: Improving the management of sepsis in a district general hospital by implementing the 'Sepsis Six' recommendations.
audits.st: Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines and Sepsis Six bundle; antibiotics, IV fluids and oxygen within one hour of initial assessment
audits.f: 16 of 55 (29%) had antibiotics, IV fluids with or without oxygen within 1 hour; lactate measured in 10 (18%); blood cultures in 18 (33%); urine output monitoring in 15 (27%); 35% received 4-6 bundle elements.
audits.c: Sepsis Six pathway and posters; education workshops for ED staff, junior doctors and ward nurses; designated sepsis assistants; laminated Sepsis Six photo on ED phlebotomy trolleys; request for an extra ED consultant.
audits.r2: 25 of 40 (63%) had antibiotics, fluids with or without oxygen within 1 hour; lactate 10 (25%); blood cultures 25 (63%), 96% before antibiotics; urine output monitoring 17 (43%); 66% received 4-6 bundle elements.

audits.t: A simple prioritisation system to improve the electronic handover.
audits.st: GMC and BMA/NPSA safe handover guidance: unstable patients known to seniors, tasks prioritised and unstable patients reviewed
audits.f: FY1 questionnaire: 38.5% felt handover was safe; 7.1% had sufficient time to complete the ward round; 15.4% could identify and prioritise unwell patients; 30.8% could identify outstanding jobs
audits.c: Traffic light prioritisation categories (including weekend discharge and weekend admissions) added to the electronic weekend handover on EPR, publicised by posters, email and FY1 induction
audits.r2: Improvement sustained across all parameters but smaller than immediately after the change (detailed figures only in supplementary table)

audits.t: Improving cranial ultrasound scanning strategy in neonates.
audits.st: Consultant-agreed scanning schedule and local documentation standards; 100% of infants scanned to schedule and 100% of key documentation fields completed
audits.f: 52% of preterm (93 scans) and 44% of term (9 scans) scans performed to schedule; preterm reports with time documented 75% and scanning doctor's name 92%; no comment on IVH in 16% of preterm scans
audits.c: Departmental audit meeting education (PDSA 1, no real improvement), then a local cranial ultrasound guideline, a documentation template in every set of notes, posters, email and a one-minute-wonder board (PDSA 2)
audits.r2: 74% of preterm and 100% of term scans performed to schedule; 100% had doctor's name and time of scan documented; 100% of preterm reports documented IVH

audits.t: Improving the provision of pregnancy care for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander women: a continuous quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Australian Clinical Practice Guidelines for Antenatal Care: screening and counselling for smoking, alcohol, nutrition, physical activity and food security, and folate before 20 weeks
audits.f: Screened for cigarette use 73%; cessation advice 52%; screened for alcohol 65%; brief alcohol counselling 51%; nutrition counselling 41%; food security counselling 4.8%; physical activity counselling 20%; folate before 20 weeks 28%.
audits.c: Continuous quality improvement cycles: systems assessment and health record audits, with each centre setting priorities and developing its own system improvement strategies, supported by One21seventy tools and facilitators.
audits.r2: Screened for cigarette use 95% (OR 11); cessation advice 73%; screened for alcohol 83%; brief alcohol counselling 71%; nutrition counselling 65%; food security counselling 9.1%; physical activity counselling 15%; folate before 20 weeks 34%.

audits.t: Improving the quality of handover in a liaison psychiatry team.
audits.st: Locally agreed minimum handover data set (patient identifiers, location, referrer, reason for referral, priority, risk, pending tasks, clinician name and signature)
audits.f: Overall completeness 40%; hospital number 2%; risk 22%; priority of task 13%; clinician name 29%; signature 15%
audits.c: Education and a written handout at induction (no consistent improvement), then a handover proforma sticker, later a printed handover book
audits.r2: Overall completeness 78%; hospital number 48%; risk 53%; priority 59%; pending tasks 100%; clinician name 97%; signature 97%

audits.t: The use of a pro forma to improve quality in clerking vascular surgery patients.
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians 2009 standards for admission clerking documentation
audits.f: Presenting complaint absent in 19%; past surgical history absent in 45%; drug history 72%, doses and frequency 41%, allergy status 75%; family history 19%; systems enquiry 12%; vascular examination 59%, pulses 46%; observations 31%; VTE assessment 73%
audits.c: Clerking pro forma based on RCP guidance (with AMTS, VTE, ABPI, investigations and nil-by-mouth sections), junior doctor education and a named FY1 lead per cohort
audits.r2: Sustained improvement in record keeping; observations recorded in 62% (significant increase); non-significant improvements in nil-by-mouth status and prior investigations

audits.t: Improving Mental Status Questionnaire (MSQ) completion on admission to the Acute Surgical Receiving Unit (ASRU), Ninewells Hospital, Dundee.
audits.st: Mental Status Questionnaire completed on admission for 95% of patients aged 75 or over (project target)
audits.f: MSQ completion 14.99% (16.6% and 13.3% in the two five-day periods); no patient had a formal delirium diagnosis despite a mean of 5.4 of 12 risk factors
audits.c: Sticker listing all 10 MSQ questions in the admission document, with signage, email to junior doctors and advanced nurse practitioners briefing new staff
audits.r2: Average MSQ completion 81.33%; 100% on two days; 40% on the first day

audits.t: Improving bowel preparation for colonoscopy in a cost effective manner.
audits.st: JAG/BCSP: excellent or adequate bowel preparation in more than 90% of colonoscopies
audits.f: 490 (80%) adequate preparation; 118 (19%) inadequate; 14 (2.24%) needed repeat investigation; 100% PEG preparations
audits.c: Patient information leaflets with diet and medication advice, algorithm-based choice of bowel preparation triaged by consultants, and cheaper postage in padded envelopes
audits.r2: 93 (93%) adequate preparation; 7% inadequate; no repeat investigations; PEG use 58.82%

audits.t: Prevention of acute kidney injury through accurate fluid balance monitoring.
audits.st: Completion of six key fluid balance chart components (patient details, weight, running hourly input, 6-hourly input and output subtotals, 24-hour total); project aim of a 50% reduction in monthly AKI alerts
audits.f: Patient details 100%; weight 8%; running 1-hour input 80%; 6-hour input 83%; 6-hour urine output 36%; 24-hour balance 12%; mean 47 AKI alerts per month (October 2015 to January 2016)
audits.c: Redesigned fluid balance chart, posters of correct and incorrect charts, handover scenario training, three-level e-learning modules, patient leaflets and regular feedback of AKI rates to junior doctors
audits.r2: Running 1-hour total 96%; 6-hourly output 68%; weight 16% (after peaking at 80%); 24-hour running total 32% (after peaking at 72%); monthly AKI alerts fell from 50 (January 2016) to 19 (November 2016), mean down 33% to 31 (P<0.001)

audits.t: A quality improvement project to improve the Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) sepsis bundle compliance rate in a large healthcare system.
audits.st: CMS sepsis bundle (SEP-1) compliance; aim to improve from 30% to 40% within 1 year
audits.f: Mean compliance 25.8% (monthly range 16-31%); baseline rate for SPC 28.5%.
audits.c: Revised sepsis standardised clinical practice and system-wide education; computerised decision support to reflex-order repeat lactate and prompt lactate and blood cultures when antibiotics ordered; pharmacy made first-time IV antibiotic orders stat.
audits.r2: Mean compliance 34.6% in the second 6 months (p<0.0001), peaking at 42%; 31.8% after CMS changed specifications in July 2016 (p<0.019 vs baseline).

audits.t: Improving anticoagulation of patients with an implantable left ventricular assist device.
audits.st: Warfarin with target INR 2.5 (acceptable range 2.0 to 3.0); time in therapeutic range by Rosendaal method
audits.f: 0.38 INR measurements per patient-week; mean INR 2.46±0.59; time in therapeutic range 67.96%; 36 episodes out of range
audits.c: Home point-of-care INR testing for all patients with results by email, a networked electronic INR and dosing database, and a dedicated daily VAD coordinator session for anticoagulation
audits.r2: 1.24 INR measurements per patient-week; mean INR 2.48±0.6; time in therapeutic range 76.56% (not significant)

audits.t: Improving patient flow in a regional anaesthesia block room.
audits.st: Locally set targets: 90% of patients in block room 60 min before OR start; 90% arrive within 15 min of calling the surgical preparation unit; 90% enter OR within 10 min of scheduled start
audits.f: 31% arrived in the block room 60 min before OR start; 69% arrived within 15 min of the call; 52% entered OR within 10 min of scheduled start
audits.c: Audit feedback to stakeholders, preparing flagged patients in the block room with a dedicated prep nurse, a structured OR-block room communication loop and consistent block room nursing staff
audits.r2: 53% arrived 60 min before OR start (p=0.04); 98% within 15 min of the call (p<0.001); 65% entered OR on time (p=0.03)

audits.t: Quality improvement project aimed at improving the reliability of spontaneous awakening trials in a district general intensive care unit.
audits.st: Critical care guidelines recommending light sedation with a daily sedation hold (spontaneous awakening trial); project target 80% of eligible patients
audits.f: Median 47% of SAT-eligible patients received a sedation hold; mean RASS -2.3; 7 ventilated days and 10 unit days on average
audits.c: Multidisciplinary sedation hold protocol based on the 'Wake up and breathe' guidelines, tested in PDSA cycles, with staff education, consultant prompting and a daily audit form
audits.r2: 96% of SAT-eligible patients received a sedation break; ventilation 5.5 days and unit stay 8 days; no adverse events

audits.t: Optimizing Time to Antibiotic Administration in Children with Possible Febrile Neutropenia through Quality Improvement Methodologies.
audits.st: Time to antibiotic administration <60 minutes; aim >80% of eligible patients within 60 minutes
audits.f: Mean time to antibiotics 64 minutes; 59% received antibiotics in <60 minutes.
audits.c: PDSA cycles: target of antibiotic order within 13 minutes with abnormality tracker, emails and audit and feedback; revised order set with antibiotic flagged urgent and pharmacy prioritisation; EHR change allowing antibiotic ordering before patient arrival using most recent weight.
audits.r2: Mean time to antibiotics 53 minutes; 84% received antibiotics in <60 minutes.

audits.t: Improving Accuracy of Handoff by Implementing an Electronic Health Record-generated Tool: An Improvement Project in an Academic Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
audits.st: Targets: handoff data accuracy 80%, incorrectly listed medications reduced (0% target), verbal handoff time reduced by 20%, user satisfaction up 1 point on a 5-point Likert scale
audits.f: Composite accuracy of 16 patient data points 51% (demographics 37%, medical data 66%); patients with incorrect or incomplete medication lists 51%.
audits.c: EHR-generated structured handoff tool with autopopulated fields (Epic SmartPhrases), developed through PDSA cycles with stakeholder feedback, tutorials and a pilot; went live February 2019.
audits.r2: Composite accuracy 97% (demographics 100%, medical data 94%); incorrect medication lists 0%.

audits.t: Reducing redundant creatine kinase testing in cardiac injury.
audits.st: Choosing Wisely and cardiology society guidance that troponin alone is the biomarker of choice for cardiac injury; target 50% reduction in CK tests and CK-to-troponin ratio of one-third or less
audits.f: 47,556 CK tests (mean 3963 per month); CK-to-troponin ratio 0.91; 72.8% of CK tests coupled with troponin.
audits.c: Revised institutional testing guidelines; CK removed from ED triage, cardiology admission, cardiovascular surgery and ICU order sets; academic detailing and education; unit-level comparative feedback by email; reduced default intervals for recurring CK tests.
audits.r2: 25,332 CK tests (mean 2111 per month), a 46.7% reduction (p<0.001); CK-to-troponin ratio 0.49; coupled tests 58.3% of CK orders.

audits.t: Implementation of a nutrition screening tool to improve nutritional status of children with cancer in Singapore's largest paediatric hospital.
audits.st: Universal nutrition screening within 24 hours of admission (JCI accreditation); aim for timely dietitian referral of high-risk children within 48 hours of admission
audits.f: 4 of 11 (36.4%) high-risk patients referred to the dietitian; 16 of 30 (53.3%) seen within 48 hours; median time to dietitian 3 days (IQR 1-14); malnutrition at admission 45 of 258 (17.4%).
audits.c: Validated cancer-specific screening tool (SCAN) with nurse champion training; mandatory SCAN template in the EMR with auto-populated weights; direct dietitian self-referral from a work board flag.
audits.r2: 42 of 49 (85.7%) high-risk patients seen by the dietitian (p=0.005); 40 of 41 (97.6%) seen within 48 hours; median time to dietitian 1 day (p=0.010); malnutrition 17 of 260 (6.5%).

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Blood Culture Contamination in the Neonatal Unit.
audits.st: Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute benchmark of 3% blood culture contamination; project aim to reduce contamination from 2.0% to 1.0% by March 2020
audits.f: 39 contaminants (2.0%); monthly rates varied 0.0-5.7%; compliance with standard bottle inoculation and skin preparation steps 50% each (observational audits, n = 20).
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles: standardised bottle inoculation with a transfer device; standardised skin preparation for cannulation; aseptic technique education package; minimum 1 mL blood volume with a blood culture sticker and record book.
audits.r2: 10 contaminants (0.90%); compliance with inoculation process 100% and skin preparation 95%; at least 1 mL collected in 94% of 450 collections.

audits.t: Operationalising outpatient antimicrobial stewardship to reduce system-wide antibiotics for acute bronchitis.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection
audits.st: Guidelines recommending no antibiotics for acute uncomplicated bronchitis; aim to reduce antibiotic prescribing from 65% to <32% by April 2020
audits.f: Antibiotics prescribed in 314 of 486 (64.6%) acute bronchitis/URI encounters; 667 of 1054 (63%) over January to December 2018.
audits.c: Seven PDSA cycles: provider needs-assessment interviews; CDC patient education materials and supportive care prescription pads; individual comparative feedback emails; individualised focused case reviews with high prescribers; primary care grand rounds.
audits.r2: Antibiotics prescribed in 154 of 418 (36.8%) encounters (p=0.002 across periods).

audits.t: Checklist to aid young physicians managing obstetric emergencies in rural India: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Completeness of 31 agreed data points on first information sheets (items based on hospital policy and Ministry of Health guidelines); aim >90% completeness
audits.f: Mean first information sheet completeness 73.95%; 1 of 12 (8.33%) fully complete.
audits.c: PDSA cycles: education session for interns; wall notes of required data points; a printed antenatal care (ANC) admission checklist, then implemented with shift-wise training and nursing officers printing it each shift.
audits.r2: Mean completeness 86.34% (p<0.001); 16 of 65 (24.62%) fully complete (p=0.2); ANC checklist used in 69.72% of sheets.

audits.t: Improving Clinical Handover on an Electronic Communication Platform: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: National handover guidance (RCP Acute Care Toolkit) SBAR components on a local proforma: admission date, estimated discharge date, presenting complaint, past medical and social history, escalation status, issues, updates and plans
audits.f: Admission date 51%; estimated discharge date 60%; presenting complaint 100%; social history 82%; escalation status 20%; issues 12%; important updates 71%; plans 100%
audits.c: Teaching for foundation doctors, posters of the proforma, ward 'Careflow champions' and re-education at mandatory teaching
audits.r2: Admission date 58% (+13.7%); estimated discharge date 80% (+33.3%); social history 92%; escalation status 67% (+335%); issues 29% (+242%); important updates 96%; plans 100%

audits.t: Improving paediatric flow in an UK Paediatric Assessment Unit.
audits.tp: Time to senior review in paediatrics
audits.st: RCPCH Facing the Future: tier two doctor review within 4 hours and consultant review within 14 hours of admission
audits.f: 92% (24/26) seen by a registrar or above within 4 hours; mean wait 104.2 min; consultant review not measured
audits.c: Extended weekend consultant on-site cover, flagging patients awaiting consultant review on the handover sheet, and a tier two roster with at least two doctors on at all times
audits.r2: 96.2% seen by a tier two doctor within 4 hours (from 82.9% in cycle 3, p=0.028)

audits.t: A quality improvement project: Reducing the number of unnecessary plain abdominal radiographs performed in the emergency department of a London district general hospital.
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists iRefer guidelines (2017) for plain abdominal radiography
audits.f: 79% of requests had at least one indication meeting iRefer guidance; 27% of radiographs diagnostic; 50% aided clinical management
audits.c: Teaching session for ED clinicians on iRefer guidance and radiation dose, plus posters in the department and on the shared drive
audits.r2: 87% met iRefer guidance; 47% diagnostic; 70% aided clinical management; 15% fewer radiographs

audits.t: Quality improvement initiative to improve infant safe sleep practices in the newborn nursery.
audits.st: AAP Infant Safe Sleep guidelines; composite 'perfect sleep' measure; aim 70% within 1 year
audits.f: 41.9% of sleeping infants met 'perfect sleep'; 38.0% of sleep areas had extra items; 15.3% inappropriately bundled; 87.0% in a safe location; 90.3% on their back; 3.8% raised bassinette head.
audits.c: Seven PDSA cycles: nursing education module; parent education with door hangers then crib cards; temporary then permanent supply of wearable blankets (sleep sacks) with laundering; reminder to labour ward nurses to give empty bassinettes; gifting sleep sacks to take home.
audits.r2: 'Perfect sleep' rose to 67.3% (goal of 70% not met); extra items 20.2%; inappropriate bundling 3.8%; safe location 92.0%; back sleeping 98.1%.

audits.t: Improving the Acceptance Rate of Centchroman As a Postpartum Contraceptive Through a Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: SMART aim to increase centchroman acceptance as a postpartum contraceptive to at least 50%
audits.f: Baseline centchroman acceptance rate 2.9%.
audits.c: Staff seminar, then three PDSA cycles: information charts in postnatal clinics; awareness sessions by nursing staff; counselling by resident doctors.
audits.r2: Acceptance rose to 15.3%, 56.3% and 78.2% after PDSA cycles 1-3; overall acceptance 81.7% during 12-week follow-up.

audits.t: A Prospective Quality Improvement Initiative to Address the Barriers to Postpartum Tubal Ligation Among Multiparous Women.
audits.st: Aim to increase postpartum tubal ligation among multiparous women by 50% from baseline
audits.f: Baseline prevalence of postpartum tubal ligation 30.2%.
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles: modified consent form with a PPTL column and red sticker on antenatal cards plus provider counselling; group antenatal education for women; counselling of partners and birth attendants.
audits.r2: PPTL rose to 49.5% after cycle 1, 68.8% after cycle 2 and 74.4% after cycle 3; continuation rate 72% at the end of follow-up.

audits.t: Incidental lymphadenopathy in renal transplantation.
audits.st: No published standard; unit guideline introduced after cycle 1 that all incidentally enlarged iliac lymph nodes are biopsied
audits.f: 11 (14.47%) had incidentally enlarged iliac lymph nodes biopsied at the surgeon's discretion; all showed reactive changes only
audits.c: Unit guideline that all incidentally enlarged iliac lymph nodes at transplantation undergo histological assessment regardless of size
audits.r2: 8 (4.85%) had enlarged nodes, all biopsied: 5 reactive, 2 with no nodal tissue, 1 chronic lymphocytic leukaemia

audits.t: Improving the Quality of Operative Notes in Vascular Surgery: A Retrospective Analysis.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland Code of Practice for Surgeons (2018) operative note content
audits.f: Time of procedure 0%; elective/emergency 9.4%; anaesthetist 59%; complications 25%; additional procedures 12.5%; blood loss 0%; antibiotic prophylaxis 0%; closure technique 59.4%; uploaded to EVOLVE 28.1%
audits.c: Theatre checklist poster, scanner in theatre with instruction poster and video for uploading notes, individual scanner accounts and staff education at M&M meetings
audits.r2: Time 6.25%; elective/emergency 50%; anaesthetist 90.6%; complications 90.6%; additional procedures 75%; blood loss 9.3%; antibiotics 28.1%; closure technique 100%; uploaded to EVOLVE 90.6%

audits.t: Improving the Diagnosis of Rib Fractures in the Emergency Department: A Quality Improvement Project in a District General Hospital in the United Kingdom.
audits.tp: Chest trauma and rib fracture management
audits.st: Project SMART aim: 90% of chest wall injuries diagnosed at the initial ED assessment (informed by London Major Trauma System 2018 guidance on elderly trauma)
audits.f: 61% of chest wall injuries diagnosed at the initial ED encounter (30 of 77 missed; text also reports 61% missed); mean time from attendance to first CT 477 minutes
audits.c: Thoracic trauma proforma with a modified PIC score and CT criteria, updated trust chest trauma pathway allowing contrast CT, a resus drawer for the proforma, and teaching, posters and email reminders
audits.r2: 91% diagnosed at initial ED assessment (3 missed); time to first CT 169 minutes; proforma completed in 9 cases

audits.t: Adherence to Preoperative Fasting Guidelines in Elective Surgical Patients.
audits.st: International (ASA/European Society of Anaesthesiology) and Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh fasting guidance: clear fluids until 2 hours and solids until 6 hours before surgery (morning list: solids to midnight, clear fluids to 06:30; afternoon list: breakfast before 07:00, clear fluids to 11:00)
audits.f: 86 (95.6%) fasted >2 hours from clear fluids and 90 (100%) >6 hours from solid food; 18 (20.0%) fasted >12 hours from clear fluids; 48 (53.3%) received both verbal and written instructions.
audits.c: Institutional action plan: explicit morning and afternoon fasting rules, fasting information at pre-hospitalisation and preoperative clinic visits, and explanatory leaflets for patients.
audits.r2: 33 of 57 (57.9%) fasted >2 hours from clear fluids (p=0.021); 27 (47.4%) fasted >6-12 hours from solid food (p=0.005); 3 (5.3%) fasted >12 hours from clear fluids.

audits.t: Striving for excellence in ventilator bundle compliance through continuous quality improvement initiative in the intensive care unit of a tertiary care hospital in India.
audits.st: Ventilator bundle compliance (all five components documented); aim >90% within 6 months
audits.f: Ventilator bundle compliance 40.7%, lowest for daily sedation vacation with SBT and thromboprophylaxis; VAP 62.4 per 1,000 ventilator days.
audits.c: PDSA cycles: multidisciplinary educational boot camp with WhatsApp group; bundle checklist in ICU progress chart signed by nurses and residents and countersigned by consultants, random inspections and a placard; simulation and micro-scenarios to standardise technique, with coloured bed marks for head elevation.
audits.r2: Compliance >70% after cycle 1 and >90% after cycle 2; VAP fell to 25.7 per 1,000 ventilator days (P=0.004; incidence rate ratio 2.34).

audits.t: Prevention and Control of Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infection (CAUTI): A Patient Safety and Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: CDC CAUTI prevention guidance, HOUDINI nurse-driven catheter removal protocol and CAUTI care bundle
audits.f: Mean CAUTI rate 1.28 per 1000 catheter days.
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles: staff education, HOUDINI nurse-driven removal protocol with posters and a campaign; monitored HOUDINI and care bundle compliance; closed urinary drainage system introduced; external catheters as alternatives; internal audits with feedback; patient and family education and a urinary catheter passport.
audits.r2: Mean CAUTI rate 0.42 per 1000 catheter days (p=0.04); eight consecutive points below the centre line from July 2023 to May 2024.

audits.t: Standardized CT KUB Protocols for Nephrolithiasis: A Retrospective Analysis of Radiation Exposure and Cranial Extent Guidelines.
audits.st: IR(ME)R principle of minimising radiation; local protocol to start CT KUB at the T10-T12 vertebral level (no formal national guideline)
audits.f: 48% (n=49) of scans started above T10, 51% (n=52) from T10-T12 and 1% below T12; mean effective dose 6.37 mSv above T10 vs 4.56 mSv from T10-T12.
audits.c: Findings presented to urology and radiology departments and a new protocol to commence CT KUB from T10-T12 devised.
audits.r2: 21.9% (n=23) started above T10, 75.2% (n=79) from T10-T12 and 2.9% below T12; mean dose 6.76 mSv above T10 vs 4.12 mSv from T10-T12.

audits.t: Feasibility of a Standardised Mid-Trimester Ultrasound Protocol: A National Multicenter Study.
audits.tp: Second-trimester fetal anomaly scan image quality
audits.st: CNEOF 2022 national mid-trimester ultrasound protocol (21 recommended and 3 additional standardised views) with a 73-criterion consensus quality assessment score
audits.f: 9028 of 9240 (97.8%) recommended images recorded; feasibility of recommended views 88.5-100% (>95% for 20 of 21); 319 of 440 (72.5%) scans had no recommended view missing; 64 of 73 (88%) conformity criteria met in over 90% of cases.

audits.t: Improving drug charting practices and documentation among nurses in emergency department at a regional hospital, Bhutan: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Hospital transcription protocol; complete drug chart documentation to be maintained above 90%
audits.f: 44.9% (45%) of drug charts complete; adherence to standard charting practice 51%; transcriber signature/name recorded in 45%.
audits.c: Four 2-week PDSA cycles: sensitisation teaching on medication errors and the transcription protocol; standardisation to a single drug chart; red pens at the nursing station for antibiotic charting; daily drug chart monitoring and feedback by pharmacy.
audits.r2: 98% of drug charts complete; adherence to standard charting practice 98%; transcriber signature 95%.

audits.t: Improving capacity and flow in a children and young people's Community Eating Disorder Service (CEDS): how a quality improvement initiative led to a reduction in waiting times in the service.
audits.st: Commissioned target of routine assessment within 2 weeks (urgent within 5 days); national standards 1 week urgent and 4 weeks routine. Aim: reduce routine referral wait from 17 weeks to 2 weeks in 12 months.
audits.f: Average wait from routine referral to assessment 17 weeks; 73 patients on psychiatry wait list; 50 families on therapy wait list; 65 inactive cases.
audits.c: QI with PDSA cycles: weekly referral meeting with referral tracker and 2-week deadline for referrers; single-clinician triage and assessment; revised co-designed referral form; psychiatry wait list review, clinics three mornings a week, joint reviews and medication/prescription clinics; therapy wait list review and capacity planning; monthly caseload audit; shorter 2-page discharge letter; staff recruitment campaign.
audits.r2: Average routine wait fell to 2 weeks (88% reduction), sustained; psychiatry wait list 73 to 0 by December 2022; therapy wait list 50 to 0 by April 2023; inactive cases 65 to 0.

audits.t: Developing an online educational platform to expedite ADHD medication initiation in child and adolescent mental health services: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: Project aims: reduce time-to-treatment initiation (TTI) for ADHD medication by 10% and increase proportion initiated on medication by 5% by February 2024; NICE NG87 recommends medication as part of a treatment plan.
audits.f: Mean TTI 86 days; 64% (n=76) of young people started on ADHD medication; satisfaction 4.13/5 (n=13).
audits.c: Online post-diagnostic psychoeducation platform (videos, Q&A, e-form medication decision portal with physical health e-form, useful links), emailed to families; QR code posters; text message prompts (PDSA 2); patient experience video (PDSA 3).
audits.r2: Mean TTI fell to 43 days (n=82) after PDSA 3 (reported elsewhere as 51 days, 41% reduction); 70% (n=52) started on medication; satisfaction 4.37/5 (n=21).

audits.t: Identifying frail patients at the front door: a quality improvement project on improving identifying frailty and accuracy of Clinical Frailty Scale in the emergency department in an acute general hospital.
audits.st: NHS England CQUIN 05 (2023/24): identify frailty in ED patients aged 65+ using the Clinical Frailty Scale, CGA if CFS 6 or above. SMART target 70% correct identification of CFS 6+ by November 2024; ED nurse scores compared with frailty intervention team scores.
audits.f: Correct identification of moderate frailty (CFS 6+) 45–51%; exact CFS accuracy 17%.
audits.c: Two PDSA cycles of ED nurse training: CFS lanyard card to standardise scoring, 1:1 brief teaching (135 sessions), group/virtual sessions, posters, newsletter and emails (cycle 1, November 2023); plus quizzes, scenarios and individual feedback (cycle 2, September to October 2024).
audits.r2: Correct identification of CFS 6+ rose to 74–78% (78% at 9–13 October 2024); exact CFS accuracy up to 42%.

audits.t: Implementation of the bedside paediatric early warning system, its sustainability in clinical practice and patient outcomes: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Bedside PEWS protocol for scores of 5 and above: targets 95% for timely reassessment and rescoring, 100% for nurse escalation and 100% for timely physician review
audits.f: Compliance 84% in the pilot unit; in the first year compliance was below target for reassessment, escalation and physician review.
audits.c: Electronic PEWS integrated into the EMR with an action plan; training of about 600 staff and at orientation; modified action plan with observation frequency; staged roll-out to wards, ER and PICU; unit-specific action plans; quarterly compliance audits with feedback.
audits.r2: Reassessment and rescoring 95-100%, escalation 100% and physician review 100% over the past 6 years; pilot compliance rose to 96% after the action plan change.

audits.t: Improving initial vital signs assessment and documentation in the emergency department of regional hospital, Bhutan: quality improvement project.
audits.st: Complete documentation of all five initial vital signs; aim to improve from 40% to over 80% in 10 weeks
audits.f: 40% of records had all five vital signs documented; temperature 42%, respiratory rate 50%, SpO2 85%, pulse and BP 96% each.
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles: sensitisation teaching on vital signs and triage; procurement of working monitors, BP cuffs and thermometers; a designated assessment area with redesigned patient flow; a vital signs stamp on walk-in and OPD records.
audits.r2: 97% of records had complete vital signs; respiratory rate and temperature 97% each; SpO2 100%.

audits.t: Restoring antenatal health services in a war-affected hospital: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: Ethiopian Ministry of Health clinical quality audit guideline seven-element first-visit ANC bundle; aim 0% to 100%
audits.f: 0% of pregnant mothers received all ANC bundle elements at first visit (378 attended; nothing beyond counselling).
audits.c: ANC first-visit bundle checklist, client exit interviews, weekly laboratory test availability checks, backup generator funded by the community, respectful care training and psychosocial support for staff.
audits.r2: 94.5% of mothers received all ANC bundle elements at first visit (monthly sample of 19 charts); checklist use 100%.

audits.t: Beyond Pneumonia: A Dual-Cycle Initiative to Improve Imaging Compliance and Uncover Early Malignancy.
audits.tp: Follow-up chest imaging after community-acquired pneumonia
audits.st: BTS and NICE guidance: follow-up chest imaging within six weeks of diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia (patients aged 50 and over and higher-risk patients) to exclude malignancy.
audits.f: 22/42 had repeat imaging (X-ray or CT) within six weeks; 16 had none and 4 died before six weeks; 2 cancers found.
audits.c: Emails to medical and nursing staff summarising audit results and guidelines, posters and banners in clinical areas, patient leaflets in discharge folders, and standardised discharge summary templates with a follow-up imaging prompt.
audits.r2: 37/50 had repeat imaging; 13 did not; 3 cancers found (all in men).

audits.t: Improving Intensive Care Unit Nurses' Delirium Assessment Performance Through a Multimodal Educational Intervention.
audits.st: Agreement of bedside nurse ICDSC assessments with an expert nurse (kappa >0.8 benchmark)
audits.c: Three-month multimodal education: didactic lectures, case discussions of difficult scenarios and one-to-one bedside mentoring by an expert nurse.

audits.t: Compliance with NICE, BAUS, RCR, and RCEM Guidelines for Acute Renal Colic: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Study at Lister Hospital Emergency Department, United Kingdom.
audits.st: NICE NG118/QS195 (CT-KUB within 24 h, serum calcium), BAUS (CT-KUB within 14 h, calcium and urate, avoid repeat CT within 3 months), RCR iRefer and RCEM four-hour standard. Local targets: four-hour compliance ≥90%; CT-KUB request and report ≤90 min each; >90% scans within imaging windows; STONE score documentation ≥75%; calcium ≥65%, urate ≥20%; ≥30% reduction in repeat CT.
audits.f: Median urine dip turnaround 144 min, CT-KUB request 166 min, CT report 124 min; RCEM four-hour compliance 16.7% (19/114); calcium tested 50.9% (58/114); urate 0% (0/114); STONE score 5.3% (6/114); repeat CT within 3 months 19.3%; median ED stay 7.5 h.
audits.c: 'Straight to CT' pathway with registrar-requested scans, mandatory STONE score prompts in ICE/iRefer requests, three staff training sessions with prompt cards and intranet guides, dedicated porter slots and fast-track radiology queue with hot reporting, early SAU/CDU transfers.
audits.r2: Urine dip 68 min, CT request 75 min, CT report 70 min (all p<0.001); four-hour compliance 57.0% (65/114; p<0.001); calcium 65.8% (75/114; p=0.022); urate 25.4% (29/114); STONE score 78.9% (90/114); repeat CT 9.6% (p=0.038); ED stay 3.9 h.

audits.t: Investigating the Sustainability of Urological Surgery: A Retrospective Analysis.
audits.st: Trust waste management guidelines (in line with Department of Health guidance), assessed by a pictographic staff question sheet.
audits.f: No staff member placed all waste items correctly; commonest score 5/9 (32%); most common error was putting all items in the yellow clinical bin. Of 39 general anaesthetics, sevoflurane used in 30 and desflurane in 7.
audits.c: 20-minute in-person educational update on waste disposal and the new waste stream during audit days and drop-in sessions, plus wall signage; planned switch from yellow clinical to orange waste stream.
audits.r2: After education 81% of staff scored 80% or higher (8/10: 24%, 9/10: 36%, 10/10: 21%).

audits.t: Improving the safety of outpatient to Emergency Department transfers: A quality improvement study in a tertiary hospital in Pakistan.
audits.tp: Outpatient transfer to the emergency department
audits.st: Locally developed early warning criteria, transfer process and SBAR handoff tool; compliance defined as all SBAR components documented
audits.f: No baseline transfer data (inconsistent documentation and no tracking before the project).
audits.c: Revised outpatient early warning signs, structured five-step transfer process with defined roles, SBAR handoff tool, emergency transfer kits and equipment checks, hospital-wide webinar and in-person training.
audits.r2: Handoff tool completed for more than 70% of items in 65.67% (176/268) of transfers; ED stay >7 hours in 45.52%; in-hospital mortality 5.22% (14/268).

audits.t: Evaluating Adherence to 2023 National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for Computed Tomography (CT) Scans in Head Injury Presentations at University Hospital of North Durham in England, UK: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: CT head justification in head injury
audits.st: NICE 2023 head injury guideline: CT within 1 hour for high-risk features and within 8 hours for others; target 100%
audits.f: Overall compliance 29/37 (78.4%); one-hour CT completed 4/10 (40%); anticoagulated 19/19 (100%); amnesia/LOC within 8 hours 6/9 (66.7%).
audits.c: Structured teaching for doctors and nurses, NICE summary posters in triage, ambulance handover and staff base, and a rapid assessment senior clinician overseeing injury presentations.
audits.r2: Overall compliance 46/52 (88.5%) (p = 0.32); one-hour CT completed 11/18 (61.1%); anticoagulated 22/22 (100%); amnesia/LOC 22/28 (78.6%).

audits.t: Assessing and Enhancing Adherence to the Standard Aseptic Non-touch Technique in Peripheral Intravenous Cannulation: A Quality Improvement Project in a Resource-Constrained Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
audits.st: ANTT guidelines (six key actions); aim 80% adherence over 12 weeks
audits.f: Median ANTT adherence 66%; initial handwashing 50%; hand wash before unpacking 0%; before gloves 21%; tray cleaning before use 64%, after use 36%.
audits.c: Education (presentations, video, hands-on training), posters and handouts, bedside printed checklists, ANTT link nurse cascade training, then targeted feedback and supervised morning cannulations.
audits.r2: Median adherence 94% (89% after first PDSA cycle, n=15).

audits.t: Improving CT Sinus Reporting for Endoscopic Sinus Surgery Using the CLOSE Criteria: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: CT sinus reporting for endoscopic sinus surgery (CLOSE criteria)
audits.st: CLOSE criteria (Cribriform plate, Lamina papyracea, Onodi cell, Sphenoid sinus pneumatisation, anterior Ethmoidal artery) for pre-FESS CT sinus reports; RCR principle that reports be accurate and complete.
audits.f: Full documentation of all CLOSE components 8/51 (15.7%); full compliance in reports with surgically relevant high-risk variants 5/51 (9.8%).
audits.c: Educational CLOSE poster emailed and displayed in radiology reporting areas (after cycle 1); presentation at departmental radiology meeting and wider poster circulation including to a teleradiology company (after cycle 2).
audits.r2: Full documentation of all CLOSE components 11/21 (52.4%); high-risk variant compliance 9/21 (42.9%) (χ2=10.375, p<0.01).

audits.t: Evaluation of readmissions following elective colorectal surgery: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Readmission after elective colorectal cancer surgery
audits.st: GIRFT national 30-day readmission benchmarks: 6.1% for elective colonic resections and 8.8% for elective rectal cancer resections.
audits.f: 30-day readmission rate 14.2% (4/28), above GIRFT benchmarks; median length of stay 6 days. Causes: blocked catheter/urinary retention, port-site hernia, collection near anastomosis, gastrointestinal symptoms.
audits.c: Proposed/initiated: ERAS refresher training with quarterly compliance audits, pilot prehabilitation pathway for high-risk patients, virtual telephone follow-up within 7 days of discharge, revised discharge checklists and updated patient leaflets.

audits.t: Decreasing Seven-Day Revisits After Pediatric Tonsillectomy: A Multidisciplinary and Comprehensive Unit-Based Safety Program (CUSP)-Driven Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Vizient national top-quartile benchmark seven-day revisit rate 2.17%; aim to reduce revisit rate by at least 1% by December 31, 2025
audits.f: Seven-day revisit rate 3.75% (39/1041); pain and dehydration main drivers.
audits.c: Perioperative bundle: intraoperative crystalloid >=30 ml/kg, acetaminophen and dexamethasone; scheduled PACU ibuprofen; tolerance-based hydration readiness; standardised discharge packet with hydration checklist and dye-free medication calendar; surgical team PACU check-ins (three PDSA cycles).
audits.r2: Seven-day revisit rate 2.16% (n = 15); by cycle: PDSA 1 2.83% (7/247), PDSA 2 1.65% (7/423), PDSA 3 0.75% (1/133).

audits.t: Improving Documentation of Bowel Movements Using the Bristol Stool Chart: A Quality Improvement Project in a District General Hospital in the United Kingdom.
audits.st: Nursing documentation standards for daily bowel movement recording using the Bristol Stool Chart (frequency, consistency, correct chart format, escalation/clinical action).
audits.f: Daily bowel documentation 8/30 (27%); Bristol Stool Chart used 17 (57%); stool frequency 9 (30%); correct chart format 14 (47%); consistency 15 (50%); clinical action taken 15 (50%).
audits.c: 'Bowel Matters' reminder posters at workstations, ward areas and toilets; summary to ward manager to cascade; staff advised to add bowel documentation to shift handover checklist and daily nursing care bundles.
audits.r2: Daily documentation 18 (73%) (χ2 p=0.0092); Bristol Stool Chart 27 (87%) (p=0.0035); frequency 16 (60%); correct chart format 21 (70%, reported elsewhere as 87%); consistency 23 (87%) (p=0.0321); clinical action taken 15 (50%).

audits.t: Adapting <i>PICU UP!</i> to Enhance Early Mobility in a Level IV Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Developmental care in neonatal and paediatric intensive care
audits.st: Aim: >75% of eligible surgical infants (>=34 weeks PMA) receive PT and OT consults within 24 months (adapted PICU Up! programme)
audits.f: PT consults 25% (24.7%) and OT consults 22% (21.6%); mean time to consult 23 days for both.
audits.c: Adapted PICU Up! guideline for infants, one-to-one education by champions, PICU Up! level field added to the EMR and nursing handoff sheet, prompts on rounds, monthly audit feedback emails.
audits.r2: PT consults 95% (95.3%) and OT consults 95% (94.7%); time to PT consult 8 days and OT consult 9 days.

audits.t: Quality improvement: enhancing antibiotic stewardship for suspected early onset neonatal infection by refining use of the Kaiser Permanente screening tool and using a CRP threshold of 20 mg/L.
audits.tp: Antibiotic use for suspected early onset neonatal infection
audits.st: NICE NG195 neonatal infection guideline and Kaiser Permanente Neonatal Infection Calculator (KPNIC); aim to reduce antibiotic initiation and duration in low-risk infants.
audits.f: 13% of live births started on antibiotics for suspected EONI in 2018; 12.4% of live births >35 weeks in 2019; 1089 transitional care cefotaxime care days in 2019.
audits.c: Five PDSA cycles: CRP threshold raised to 20 mg/L to stop antibiotics at 36 hours in well culture-negative infants ('20 is the new 10'); GBS-positive mothers added to KPNIC; use of KPNIC risk after clinical exam rather than risk at birth; background EONI rate changed to 1/1000; KPNIC extended to 34 weeks. Supported by guideline updates, teaching, posters, emails and newsletters.
audits.r2: 6.8% of live births >34 weeks on antibiotics in 2024 and 6.6% in 2025 (to 30 June); transitional care cefotaxime days fell to 270 in 2024 (75% reduction).

audits.t: Ultrasound Image Capture during Central Venous Catheter Insertions: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.st: SMART aim: ultrasound image capture of correct guidewire position in 2 planes before vessel dilation from 0% to 90%; supported by ASA and Society of Hospital Medicine recommendations
audits.f: 0% (no standard process to document guidewire position).
audits.c: Image capture and EHR upload workflow (laminated guide, later condensed to 1 page), image capture step and QR survey added to the central line observation guide, reminders and booster education, simulation in fellow boot camp, troubleshooting guide and visual aid on ultrasound machines.
audits.r2: Successful image capture and upload 117/270 (44%) overall; monthly mean rose to 58%, peak 64%. DICOM order placement 194/270 (74%); mean 83%, peak 100%.

audits.t: Improving Lidocaine Topicalisation Practices in Paediatric Airway Management: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Topical lidocaine in paediatric airway procedures
audits.st: Advocated standards based on APAGBI guidance and published evidence: maximum topical lidocaine dose 4.0 mg/kg at concentration ≤4%; nil-by-mouth 60 minutes after topicalisation; mucosal atomisation device as standard.
audits.f: Median self-reported maximum dose 3.0 mg/kg (range 2.0–9.0); 2/22 (9.1%) used the 4.0 mg/kg standard; median NBM time 120 minutes (range 60–360), 8/22 (36.4%) adherent; Jelco device 18/22 (81.8%), MAD 14/22 (63.6%).
audits.c: 45-minute structured teaching session within mandatory departmental teaching presenting survey findings, complications and advocated guidelines.
audits.r2: Median maximum dose 4.0 mg/kg; 8/15 (53.3%) used 4.0 mg/kg (p=0.006); median NBM 60 minutes, 11/15 (73.3%) adherent (p=0.045); Jelco 12/15 (80.0%), MAD 10/15 (66.7%), unchanged.

audits.t: Reducing surgical site infections in paediatric cardiac surgery in a resource-constrained setting: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: International Quality Improvement Collaborative (IQIC) benchmark SSI rate of about 2.2%
audits.f: SSI rate 12 per 100 surgeries (initial 3-month rate 23%, 3/13); hand hygiene about 45%, environmental cleaning about 20%, wound documentation 0%.
audits.c: Measurement dashboards; single-use sterile consumables and skin preparation bundle; preoperative SSI risk screening tool; nurse-led wound clinic with 30-day photo follow-up by messaging; aseptic technique and hand hygiene training with daily audits; infection prevention champions, huddles and checklists.
audits.r2: SSI rate 5 per 100 surgeries (lowest 2 per 100, July to November 2024); overall 31 SSIs in 500 surgeries (6.2 per 100).

audits.t: Improving Adherence to Infection Prevention and Disinfection Protocols Within the Ophthalmology Department: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project (QIP).
audits.st: Hospital infection control standards in line with MOH and CBAHI frameworks; aim >90% compliance across all domains
audits.f: Staff self-report survey: aware of disinfection policy 87.5%; annual training 45.8%; staff wear masks 39.6%; disinfection logs maintained 75.0%; multidose drops used for one patient only 58.3%; high-touch surfaces cleaned after each patient 66.7%.
audits.c: Revised guidelines with visual guides for infection protocols and hand hygiene, emphasis on mask use and log keeping, quality team reminders, online training for all clinical staff and training at induction.
audits.r2: Aware of policy 93.2%; annual training 63.4%; masks 68.2% (p=0.01); logs maintained 95.4% (p=0.01); multidose drops single-patient use fell to 18.2% (p<0.01); high-touch cleaning 72.7%.

audits.t: Closing the gap in postoperative delirium detection: addressing low screening rates in the surgical recovery room.
audits.st: NICE delirium guidance: high-risk patients (age over 65, cognitive impairment, hip fracture) screened with a validated tool (4AT or CAM) before PACU discharge. Target at least 50% adherence within 1 month of launch.
audits.f: 3/130 (2.3%) at-risk patients screened for delirium in PACU; nurse confidence median 7/10 and guideline clarity median 4/10.
audits.c: PDSA 1: new trust-wide perioperative delirium guideline. PDSA 2: 4AT made easily accessible on electronic systems, PACU discharge checklist updated to require screening, simplified guidance signposted, daily list review at morning huddles to flag at-risk patients, staff education, and leadership engagement using coding/funding data.
audits.r2: 48/67 (71.64%) at-risk patients screened (p<0.0001); 81.50% in final week; nurse confidence and guideline clarity both median 10/10 (p<0.0001).

audits.t: Evaluation of the Quality of the Pre-ARCP (Pre-Annual Review of Competency Progression) Corporate Report for Postgraduate Doctors (Core Trainees) in Relation to Their Postgraduate Teaching Attendance and Audit Involvement
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 11/12 (92%) received report in time and agreed with RCPsych teaching and audit records; locality teaching attendance accurate for 58%
audits.c: Results discussed with Medical Education and suggestions implemented

audits.t: Assessing the Number of Patients Receiving 1:1 Sessions and Their Frequency per Week
audits.tp: Named nurse one-to-one sessions on mental health wards
audits.st: Recommended frequency of 1:1 sessions with named nurse is twice a week
audits.f: 4/20 patients had 1:1 sessions; 2 of the 4 had them at least twice a week, the others once a week
audits.c: Speaking to nursing staff about the importance of 1:1 sessions and reminders in morning meetings
audits.r2: 12/20 patients had 1:1 sessions; 5 of those had them at least twice a week

audits.t: PP79. DIAGNOSIS TO TREATMENT TIME FOR BRAIN TUMOURS: AUDIT
audits.tp: Brain tumour time to diagnosis and treatment
audits.st: NICE CSG10: 2 months from first referral to definitive treatment and 1 month from diagnosis to definitive treatment
audits.f: 126 patients (41%) had surgery; mean 50.82 days from radiological diagnosis and 59.70 days from first referral for imaging; referral-to-treatment within 60-day standard but diagnosis-to-treatment exceeded target by about 21 days

audits.t: MEMBRAIN PROJECT: PROVISIONAL RESULTS OF UK NATIONAL, PROSPECTIVE AUDIT ON THE MANAGEMENT EVALUATION OF METASTASES IN THE BRAIN
audits.tp: Brain metastases referral and MDT management
audits.st: NICE guidelines for brain metastasis referral and management
audits.f: Preliminary King's data: mean 7 referred cases per MDT; solitary metastases 44.6% of referrals; specialist intervention (surgery or stereotactic radiosurgery) recommended in 48.0%

audits.t: 1310. Improving Infectious Disease Electronic Medical Records Documentation: A Quality Improvement Study in an Academic Teaching Hospital
audits.st: Four-point note efficiency score; aim >50% improvement by May 2018
audits.f: Mean note efficiency score 2.0 ± 0.84
audits.c: Needs assessment survey and education (cycle 1), then new standardised EMR note template with removal of auto-populated irrelevant information (cycle 2)

audits.t: 193. quality Improvement Initiative for Non-purulent Cellulitis Management in Urgent care setting: provider-level Performance Feedback
audits.st: Institutional guidelines recommending beta-lactam antibiotics and no empiric MRSA cover for non-purulent cellulitis
audits.f: 40% of cases scored good; antibiotic duration >7 days 68%; combination therapy 12%.
audits.c: Review of practice guidelines with providers and individual performance feedback from the pre-intervention phase
audits.r2: 69% of cases scored good and no poor cases; duration >7 days 52%; combination therapy 4%.

audits.t: 71. Impact of Prospective Audit and Feedback on Fluoroquinolone Use: A Large Academic Medical Center Experience
audits.st: FDA recommendation to reserve fluoroquinolones for infections lacking alternatives
audits.f: Median fluoroquinolone days of therapy 7.
audits.c: Prospective audit and feedback by the antimicrobial stewardship programme
audits.r2: Median fluoroquinolone days of therapy 4 (significant reduction).

audits.t: 91 An audit of COVID-19 Awareness and Public Health Message Effectiveness in the Hospital Setting Over the Course of the Pandemic
audits.st: Public Health England COVID-19 information campaign content (symptoms, spread, risk factors, means to reduce transmission)
audits.f: Symptom recognition 84%; identification of means of transmission 76%; risk factor recognition 85% (253 responses across all cycles)
audits.c: PHE materials shown to respondents before cycle 2
audits.r2: Symptom recognition 88%; means of transmission 95%; risk factor recognition 93%

audits.t: An audit on the diagnosis of primary CNS lymphoma
audits.tp: Brain tumour time to diagnosis and treatment
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median imaging to biopsy 25 days; median first investigation to pathological confirmation 36 days (range 6-86)

audits.t: Are the rapid tranquilisation nice guidelines adhered to, in patients with agitated/aggressive behavior? a QIP
audits.st: NICE NG10 rapid tranquilisation guidance
audits.f: Adherence was noted to be low before the second audit (figure not given).

audits.t: 588 Utilizing a Quality Improvement Approach to Increase Compliance with Patient Positioning in the Burn Unit

audits.t: Identification and Management of Substance Misuse in Patients Referred for Psychodynamic Psychotherapy: A Service Evaluation Project
audits.tp: Substance misuse screening in mental health patients

audits.r2: Alcohol vs other substances differentiated in 100%; current vs historic misuse discernible in 71%

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative for Strengthening Prescription Writing Practices Among Medical Interns at Healthcare Facilities of Delhi
audits.st: Standardised prescription audit checklist

audits.t: Embedding National Benchmarking Within Integrated Intermediate Care Pathways: A Quality Improvement Protocol Using BEPOP to Enhance Exercise Provision for Frail Older Adults in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough

audits.t: Quality Improvement (QI) Project: Enhancing Surgical Safety Checklist Utilization at a Rural Primary Hospital
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist utilisation and completion

audits.t: Neighborhood Social Vulnerability and Access to Expedited Partner Therapy Prescriptions: A Secret Shopper Audit Survey.
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: How fast is fast enough? An audit and league table of response times of acute hospital NHS Trust switchboards in England.
audits.st: Switchboard answer within 20 seconds
audits.f: Only 36% of 219 switchboards met the 20 second target; average answer time 45 seconds (best mean 1 second, worst 381 seconds).

audits.t: Family tracing to identify patients with familial hypercholesterolaemia: the second audit of the Department of Health Familial Hypercholesterolaemia Cascade Testing Project.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: About 70% of index cases took part in family tracing; 76% of untested relatives in the catchment area came forward for testing.

audits.t: An audit of the level of knowledge and understanding of informed consent amongst consultant orthodontists in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.
audits.st: All questions on the legal requirements of informed consent answered correctly (standard required for lawful practice)
audits.f: Mean correct response rate 12 of 21 answers (57%), median 11 (52%), mode 10 (48%).

audits.t: Verifying patient identity and site of surgery: improving compliance with protocol by audit and feedback.

audits.t: Criteria-based audit on management of eclampsia patients at a tertiary hospital in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.

audits.t: Introduction of a qualitative perinatal audit at Muhimbili National Hospital, Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Suboptimal factors in 80% of cases, half likely causal and preventable; perinatal mortality 92 per 1000 births

audits.t: Perioperative use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs: results of a UK regional audit.
audits.st: Manufacturers' recommendations and product licences for NSAIDs
audits.f: All 189 respondents (51% of 371) used NSAIDs; ketorolac (41% of respondents), diclofenac (61%) and ketoprofen (7%) were not used according to the manufacturer's recommendations.

audits.t: A prospective multicenter audit of labor-room episiotomy and anal sphincter injury assessment in the Netherlands.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 420 (21.2%) had an episiotomy (mean angle 40 degrees from midline, most sufficiently wide); 58 (2.9%) had anal sphincter injury

audits.t: Audit of parenteral nutrition use in Guernsey.
audits.st: NICE and local Guernsey guidelines on initiation, monitoring and cessation of parenteral nutrition
audits.f: PN initiated appropriately; re-feeding risk assessed routinely except for two weekend admissions; five patients not given appropriate IV Pabrinex; only 13 had accurate daily fluid-balance charts; 11 of 17 planned cessations weaned appropriately.

audits.t: Audit of nutritional and dietary outcomes of bariatric surgery patients.
audits.st: UK national standards for bariatric dietetic care
audits.f: Preoperative dietary advice 5 (7%); postoperative advice 26; any dietetic follow-up 12 (18%); psychological support 1

audits.t: Audit of treatment of Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia.
audits.st: National guidance: minimum 14 days of antibiotics for uncomplicated S. aureus bacteraemia
audits.f: Compliance 44% (MSSA 45%, MRSA 42%)
audits.c: Extra text on laboratory reports advising minimum treatment length

audits.t: Awareness and understanding of nuclear medicine among junior doctors in a district general hospital setting: an audit and personal experiences.
audits.tp: Junior doctor knowledge of nuclear medicine
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Junior doctors knew a mean of 3.1 nuclear medicine investigations and 0.8 therapies.
audits.r2: Mean of 7.5 investigations and 3.4 therapies listed (statistically significant improvement).

audits.t: Peripheral intravenous catheters: the road to quality improvement and safer patient care.
audits.st: Peripheral venous catheter care bundle based on Health Protection Scotland drafts (insertion and maintenance measures, duration less than 72 h)
audits.f: Initial care bundle compliance 54%.
audits.c: Monthly PDSA cycles with daily review of PVC necessity, weekly audit and feedback displayed on the ward, monthly patient safety meetings, new PVC dressings and new PVC care plans
audits.r2: Compliance improved by 1.11% per week to 82% (95% CI 0.6-1.6%; P=0.0001).

audits.t: Cleanliness audit of clinical surfaces and equipment: who cleans what?
audits.st: ATP cleanliness benchmark of 100 relative light units (RLU) per 100 cm²
audits.f: 84% (37 of 44) items exceeded the 100 RLU benchmark; overall geometric mean 249 RLU/100 cm²; 24 of 27 (89%) items cleaned by clinical staff and 11 of 12 (92%) with no cleaning responsibility failed.

audits.t: Audit of a fetal central monitoring station in a clinical setting.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Antepartum tracings identified in 92%; mean signal quality 96.4%; mean signal loss 7.4%; intrapartum CTGs identified in 44%
audits.c: Measures to correct identified problems (not described in abstract)
audits.r2: Mean signal quality 97.1% (p = 0.009); mean signal loss 5.8% (p = 0.012); intrapartum CTGs identified in 69%

audits.t: Improvements in compliance with medical force protection measures by simplification of the anti-malarial chemoprophylaxis regime.
audits.st: Medical force protection measures including antimalarial chemoprophylaxis
audits.f: Chemoprophylaxis compliance 30% with weekly chloroquine and daily proguanil
audits.c: Regime simplified to weekly chloroquine alone, consistent briefings and emphasis on malaria threat

audits.t: Implementation and evaluation of a multisite drug usage evaluation program across Australian hospitals - a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline audit of inpatient records, patient interviews and GP surveys; audit results not reported in the abstract.
audits.c: Academic detailing, group education, audit and feedback, point-of-prescribing prompts and system changes, followed by a repeat audit.
audits.r2: Repeat audit results not reported in the abstract. In the evaluation survey, 18 of 23 respondents (78%) reported improved documentation of pain scores and 15 (65%) agreed participation increased multimodal analgesia prescribing.

audits.t: Water Temperature From Hot Water Outlets in a Major Public Hospital: How Hot is Our Water?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Several taps and showers supplied water hot enough to cause scalds, mostly in the oldest section
audits.c: Engineering and Building Services replaced faulty and re-set poorly set thermostatic mixing valves
audits.r2: Previously unsafe outlets re-tested and found safe

audits.t: 30-days mortality in patients with perforated peptic ulcer: A national audit.
audits.st: Danish National Indicator Project 30-day mortality standard of 10%
audits.f: Observed 30-day mortality was 28% against the 10% standard; 115 deaths were audited, and the audit indicated postoperative observation was insufficient.
audits.c: The mortality standard was raised to 20% and new indicators for postoperative monitoring were developed.

audits.t: A tale of two audits: closing the feedback loop on clearance rates of anogenital warts at three months.
audits.st: 90% clearance of anogenital warts at three months
audits.f: 95% clear by case-note review but only 81% by confirmed outcome.
audits.c: Clinic staff advised to emphasise the importance of regular treatment
audits.r2: By case-note review 127/134 (95%) clear; by confirmed outcome 74/89 (83%) clear (P = 0.004).

audits.t: The STAR score: a method for auditing clinical records.
audits.st: Surgical Tool for Auditing Records (STAR) score
audits.f: STAR score 83.344%
audits.c: Structured form for surgical notes and an education exercise

audits.t: Rational use of blood components - an audit.
audits.st: Predetermined criteria for appropriate blood component use
audits.f: 153 (83.1%) transfusion episodes appropriate and 31 (16.9%) inappropriate; inappropriate FFP 18/41 (58%), packed red cells 11/110 (35.5%), platelets 2/5 (6.45%), cryoprecipitate none

audits.t: The ebbs and flows of changing acute bed capacity delays.
audits.tp: Hospital bed capacity and patient flow
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: About 75% of beds used positively for care; 25% hidden capacity
audits.r2: Bed use for positive care not significantly changed; non-clinical discharge delays 10% of beds

audits.t: Observing and improving hand hygiene compliance: implementation and refinement of an electronic-assisted direct-observer hand hygiene audit program.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Perinatal death audits in a peri-urban hospital in Kampala, Uganda.
audits.st: not reported

audits.r2: Perinatal mortality rate 47.9 per 1000 total births; 120 of 350 perinatal deaths audited (34.2% macerated stillbirths, 31.7% fresh stillbirths, 34.2% early neonatal deaths)

audits.t: Proposal for a prospective multi-centre audit of chronic subdural haematoma management in the United Kingdom and Ireland.

audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Snapshot of transurethral resection of bladder tumours in the United Kingdom Audit (STUKA).
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median 11 days referral to first appointment and 27 days to TURBT; 119 (61%) received post-TURBT mitomycin C; no muscle in specimen in 40 (20.8%); incomplete resection in 26 (13.5%); bladder perforation 5 (2.6%)

audits.t: Healthier choices in an Australian health service: a pre-post audit of an intervention to improve the nutritional value of foods and drinks in vending machines and food outlets.

audits.t: An Audit of Management of Patients on Oral Anticoagulant Therapy With International Normalized Ratio (INR) Five or Above.

audits.t: Clinical audit to enhance safe practice of skilled birth attendants for the fetus with nuchal cord: evidence from a refugee and migrant cohort.
audits.st: Evidence-based management of nuchal cord avoiding ligation of the umbilical cord before birth
audits.f: Nuchal cord ligation before birth in 15.9% (178/1123).
audits.c: Audit feedback action phase by site doctors, then a registered midwife present six days a week for three months coaching skilled birth attendants.

audits.t: Thromboprophylaxis patterns and determinants in critically ill patients: a multicenter audit.
audits.st: Thromboprophylaxis guideline concordance (thromboprophylaxis given to patients without contraindications and withheld from those with contraindications)
audits.f: Guideline concordance occurred for 95.5% of patient-days; patients received UFH (54.0%) or LMWH (27.6%).

audits.t: Improving the performance of nutrition screening through a series of quality improvement initiatives.
audits.st: Correct completion of 3-Minute Nutrition Screening tool and referral of at-risk patients to dietetics

audits.c: Screening protocol, training, nurse-initiated online dietetic referral, closed-loop feedback and removal of the most error-prone tool component
audits.r2: Non-referrals 3%; mean screening to referral time 0.3 ± 0.4 days (from 4.3 ± 1.8)

audits.t: Unexplained abdominal pain as a driver for inappropriate therapeutics: an audit on the use of intravenous proton pump inhibitors.
audits.st: Hospital guidelines for intravenous PPI indication, dose and duration
audits.f: Intravenous PPI was inappropriately prescribed for indication, dose or duration in 56/106 (52.8%) patients.

audits.t: Echocardiographic assessment of mitral valve regurgitation, pattern and prevalence, expanding clinical awareness through an institutional survey with the perspective of a quality improvement project.

audits.f: 322 (33.50%) had MR; MR pattern not specified in 49.68%; eyeball and colour jet area used in 90.06% and 27.95%, vena contracta and flow convergence in 1.55% and 2.17%.

audits.t: "Concerns" about medical students' adverse behaviour and attitude: an audit of practice at Nottingham, with mapping to GMC guidance.

audits.t: A Study of Clinical Coding Accuracy in Surgery: Implications for the Use of Administrative Big Data for Outcomes Management.

audits.f: At least 1 coding change in 15,402 patients (51%); primary diagnosis changes 3911 (13%), procedure changes 3620 (12%); HRG changed in 5183 (17%), income variance £3,974,544 (+6.2%)

audits.t: Term perinatal mortality audit in the Netherlands 2010-2012: a population-based cohort study.

audits.t: Improving operation notes and postoperative care: an audit of current practice.

audits.r2: Improvement in nearly all criteria (figures not reported)

audits.t: Prospective Audit of Blood Donor Selection Process in a Tertiary Care Hospital of a Developing Country.

audits.f: 29 (14%) had no pain score with their last observations; recorded scores did not match directly reported scores in 41% of medical and 71% of surgical patients; 20 (15%) medical and 26 (38%) surgical patients were in moderate to severe pain.

audits.t: Remote video auditing with real-time feedback in an academic surgical suite improves safety and efficiency metrics: a cluster randomised study.

audits.f: Sign-in, time-out and sign-out pass rates 25%, 16% and 32%.

audits.t: Early Experience with a Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Quality Improvement Program.

audits.f: 114 complications in 233 liver operations; 86 complications in 99 pancreatic resections.

audits.r2: 37 patients (11.3%) had complications; 17 complications in 45 liver operations (OR 0.63, p=0.17); 20 complications in 30 pancreatic resections (OR 0.30, p=0.01).

audits.t: Improving the accuracy of operation coding in surgical discharge summaries.

audits.t: Improving the quality of discharge summaries: implementing updated Academy of Medical Royal Colleges standards at a district general hospital.

audits.t: Chest drain care bundle: Improving documentation and safety.
