audits.t: The management of chronic osteoarticular pain in the outpatient setting: results of an ASON audit.

audits.t: Out of Sight, out of Mind? An Audit Which Proposes a Follow-Up and Management Pathway for Inferior Vena Cava Filters.

audits.t: An audit cycle of consent form completion: A useful tool to improve junior doctor training.

audits.f: Benefits documented 91%; additional procedures 0%

audits.t: Reducing co-administration of proton pump inhibitors and antibiotics using a computerized order entry alert and prospective audit and feedback.

audits.t: Audit of a program to increase the use of vacuum extraction in Mulago Hospital, Uganda.

audits.tp: Sexually transmitted infection management in primary care
audits.st: Best practice guidelines for chlamydia, gonorrhoea and syphilis testing and sexual health counselling
audits.f: Wide variation; health centre factors accounted for 43% of variation; 1-2 CQI cycles associated with higher testing and counselling (OR 1.34; 95% CI 1.16-1.55).

audits.t: Case review of perinatal deaths at hospitals in Kigali, Rwanda: perinatal audit with application of a three-delays analysis.
audits.st: Perinatal audit using the three-delays model to identify contributing factors and avoidable deaths
audits.f: Contributing factors found in 79% of deaths; delay in care-seeking 39%, delay in arriving 10%, suboptimal facility care 37%; half of deaths potentially avoidable.

audits.t: Scope to improve: a multi-centre audit of 16 064 colonoscopies looking at caecal intubation rates, over a 2-year period.
audits.st: JAG quality standard: caecal intubation rate 90% and 100+ colonoscopies per operator per annum
audits.f: Overall caecal intubation rate 90.57% (95% CI 90.11% to 91.01%); operators doing 100+ procedures per annum 91.76%.

audits.t: Inadequate programming, insufficient communication and non-compliance with the basic principles of maternal death audits in health districts in Burkina Faso: a qualitative study.
audits.tp: Maternal death and severe morbidity review
audits.st: National standards and core principles for maternal death audits (programming, communication, confidentiality, no name no shame no blame)
audits.f: Maternal death audits were irregularly scheduled, mostly event-driven; preparation, communication and conduct were mostly inadequate compared with national standards; anonymity rarely preserved.

audits.t: Impact of policy support on uptake of evidence-based continuous quality improvement activities and the quality of care for Indigenous Australians: a comparative case study.
audits.tp: Audit and feedback in primary care
audits.st: Adherence to best practice guidelines (Audit and Best Practice in Chronic Disease programme)
audits.f: Progressive CQI uptake and steady improvement or maintenance of high-quality care where policy support was long-term.
audits.c: State/territory policy and infrastructure support for CQI.

audits.t: High agreement between the new Mongolian electronic immunization register and written immunization records: a health centre based audit.
audits.st: Written health provider immunisation records as reference (target not stated)
audits.f: Completeness of the electronic register 90.9% (95% CI 88.4-93.4) and accuracy 93.3% (95% CI 84.1-97.4).

audits.t: Does audit and feedback improve the adoption of recommended practices? Evidence from a longitudinal observational study of an emerging clinical network in Kenya.
audits.st: 34 indicators of adherence to national paediatric guideline recommendations
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Audit and feedback (passive and active), a standardised paediatric admission record (PAR) form and simple job aides within a clinical network.

audits.t: In-patient Tolvaptan use in SIADH: care audit, therapy observation and outcome analysis.
audits.st: Local trust guidelines for tolvaptan use in SIADH-associated hyponatraemia
audits.f: 94% achieved treatment targets after mean 3.48 days; mean sodium rose from 117.8 to 128.7 mmol/L; no rise >12 mmol/L/24 h, liver injury or CNS myelinolysis.

audits.t: Audit of the management of patients at high risk of carbapenemase-producing enterobacteriaceae (CPE): Are we ready?
audits.st: Hospital CPE policy adapted from the Public Health England 2013 toolkit (risk assessment on admission, isolation and three screens 48 h apart)
audits.f: Only 23 of 147 patients (15.6%) risk assessed on admission; 15 of 28 (54%) screened patients identified and isolated on admission; 10 of 19 (53%) had three screens 48 h apart.

audits.t: Improving the quality and speed of access to operation notes.
audits.st: National guideline standards for operation notes
audits.f: 4% of operation notes had all measured domains completed

audits.t: Rheumatic Heart Disease Prophylaxis in Older Patients: A Register-Based Audit of Adherence to Guidelines.
audits.st: Australian national guidelines on duration of secondary antibiotic prophylaxis after acute rheumatic fever
audits.f: Guideline concordance 39% by national guidelines, 68% when documented reasons for departure were included, and 82% if severe RHD was deemed to need lifelong prophylaxis.

audits.t: Mealtime Assistance ... From Chaos to Calm: A Collaborative Best Practice Implementation Project.
audits.st: Best practice for appropriate and timely mealtime assistance (JBI best practice implementation)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Staff engagement, redesigned model of care at mealtimes, clarified nutrition roles, protected mealtimes, two-tiered coloured tray system and education programme
audits.r2: Significant improvements in mealtime assistance (figures not reported)

audits.t: Using a common data platform to facilitate audit and feedback on the quality of hospital care provided to sick newborns in Kenya.
audits.st: Recommended items for documentation on admission and accurate gentamicin dosing
audits.f: Gentamicin dosing accuracy in babies under 2 kg 60% (2013).
audits.c: Revised standardised newborn admission record (NAR) form with 13 audit and feedback meetings.
audits.r2: Documentation scores improved overall; gentamicin dosing accuracy under 2 kg 83% (2016).

audits.t: Clinical impact of a prospective audit with intervention and feedback without carbapenem restriction in patients receiving carbapenem injection.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Choice of effective antimicrobials on day 2 from onset of infection 63.2% (non-intervention group).
audits.c: Prospective audit with intervention and feedback, without carbapenem pre-authorisation, by an antimicrobial stewardship programme.
audits.r2: Choice of effective antimicrobials on day 2 from onset of infection 90.2% (intervention group).

audits.t: Using knowledge translation for quality improvement: an interprofessional education intervention to improve thromboprophylaxis among medical inpatients.
audits.st: Use of LMWH for VTE prophylaxis in treatment-eligible medical inpatients (target not stated)
audits.f: LMWH used in 12.1% of treatment-eligible hospitalised medical patients.
audits.c: Several PDSA cycles of resident-of-resident and pharmacist-of-resident education with performance audit and feedback, sustained by a monthly pharmacist-led interprofessional session at resident orientation.

audits.t: Improving the nutritional intake of hospital patients: how far have we come? A re-audit.
audits.st: British Dietetic Association Nutrition and Hydration Digest energy and protein standards
audits.f: not reported beyond an increase of 19% (energy) and 36% (protein) by the re-audit
audits.r2: Digest standards met for energy by 35% and protein by 63% of patients

audits.t: Reducing Healthcare-associated Infections in Neonates by Standardizing and Improving Compliance to Aseptic Non-touch Techniques: A Quality Improvement Approach.
audits.st: Pictorial standard operating procedures for aseptic non-touch technique (ANTT) for commonly performed NICU procedures
audits.f: Baseline compliance: procedure tray/trolley use 16%, iv hub scrubbing 0%, local skin cleaning 33%, PPE use 55%, disposal 27%, non-touch technique 50%, key part contamination 45%.
audits.c: Pictorial SOPs developed, initial intensive teaching, and multiple PDSA cycles targeting areas revealed by audits.
audits.r2: Post-intervention: tray/trolley 49% (P=0.001), iv hub scrubbing 60% (P=0.001), skin cleaning 67% (P=0.004), PPE use 80% (P=0.02), disposal 51% (P=0.03), non-touch technique 70% (P=0.001), key part contamination 31% (P=0.03).

audits.t: Decreasing Central Line-associated Bloodstream Infections Through Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Hand hygiene and CLABSI care bundle protocols (audited as process indicators)
audits.f: Baseline CLABSI rate 31.7 per 1000 line-days; bloodstream infections 7.3 per 1000 patient-days; mortality 2.9%.
audits.c: QI team formed; measures to strengthen hand hygiene and central line bundle care, reinforced through multiple PDSA cycles with audits.
audits.r2: CLABSI 3.5 per 1000 line-days (89% reduction); bloodstream infections 2.3 per 1000 patient-days; mortality 1.7%.

audits.t: The quality of hand-written operative notes in a surgical unit at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital (QECH), Malawi: A prospective completed audit loop study.
audits.st: RCSEng operative note guidelines
audits.f: Documented: time of operation 0%, urgency 2%, estimated blood loss 14%, complications 38%, extra procedure 11%
audits.c: Surgeon education, detailed proformas with heading prompts and aide memoirs
audits.r2: Time 62%, urgency 84%, blood loss 62%, complications 70%, extra procedure 32%

audits.t: Creating a CNE Audit Tool Using the Plan-Do-Study-Act Model.
audits.st: American Nurses Credentialing Center's Commission on Accreditation 2015 Criteria for Continuing Nursing Education and local provider unit requirements
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Audit tool and process developed through three PDSA cycles.

audits.t: Objective assessment of compliance with a state-wide school food-service policy via menu audits.
audits.st: Healthy Food and Drink Policy traffic-light targets: ≥60% green items, ≤40% amber items, no red items
audits.f: 84% of menus met ≥60% green, 90% met ≤40% amber, 52% excluded all red items; 48% met all three targets. On average 70% of items green, 28% amber, 2% red.

audits.t: Audit of Early Mortality among Patients Admitted to the General Medical Ward at a District Hospital in Botswana.
audits.st: Modified root cause analysis of care management problems (no explicit standard)
audits.f: Septic shock in 20 (74%); care problems included delayed antibiotics (15, 56%), inappropriate fluid management (15, 56%) and deficient coordination of care (15, 56%).

audits.t: Preoperative Patient Preparation Audit: Completed Loop Cycle.
audits.st: Complete preoperative preparation (up-to-date bloods, group and save, cross-match, site marking, among others)
audits.f: Number of patients completely ready for surgery (figure not reported)
audits.c: Preoperative preparation proforma signed and checked by the ward doctor
audits.r2: Preoperative preparation improved by 50% compared with no proforma

audits.t: Sort your waste! An audit on the use of clinical waste bins and its implications.
audits.st: Hospital clinical waste guidelines
audits.f: 347 items in 80 bins: 59% non-clinical, 40% clinical
audits.c: Results presented at a medical department meeting and to waste management teams with suggestions
audits.r2: No improvement on test ward: 66% non-clinical, 31% clinical

audits.t: Clinical coding and data quality in oculoplastic procedures.
audits.tp: Hip fracture and registry data quality
audits.st: Accurate coding of oculoplastic procedures (no national standard)
audits.f: Correct 30.7%, incomplete 12.9%, incorrect 56.5%
audits.c: Tick-box coding proforma for surgeons and discussion with the coding team

audits.t: A quality improvement education initiative to increase adolescent human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine completion rates.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Pilot: mean HPV vaccine completion 45%; missed opportunities 45%. Phase 2: initiation 46%, completion 62%.
audits.c: QI education (QI methods, data tracking and analysis) and system changes to reduce missed opportunities; monthly chart audits with run charts over 6 months.
audits.r2: Pilot: completion 65%; missed opportunities 19%. Phase 2: initiation 61%, completion 94%.

audits.t: Improving the practice of inferior vena cava filter retrieval: a quality improvement intervention and audit outcomes.
audits.st: All non-permanent IVC filters should have attempted retrieval within manufacturer's recommendations, with success rate of ≥80%
audits.f: Retrieval attempted in 92%; 82% within manufacturer's recommendations; 86% successful.
audits.c: Quality improvement intervention (details not given in abstract)
audits.r2: Retrieval attempted in 95%; 92% within manufacturer's guidelines; success rate 97%.

audits.t: The National Pain Audit for specialist pain services in England and Wales 2010-2014.
audits.st: Faculty of Pain Medicine of the Royal College of Anaesthetists standards for specialist pain services
audits.f: 94% of clinics responded; multidisciplinary staffing 35%.
audits.c: Quality improvement measures introduced through roadshows led by the British Pain Society
audits.r2: 83% of clinics responded; multidisciplinary staffing 56% (significant improvement).

audits.t: Integrated disease surveillance and response implementation in Liberia, findings from a data quality audit, 2017.
audits.st: Integrated disease surveillance and response data quality and core performance indicators (target not stated)
audits.f: 23% (7/29) had a dedicated reporting phone, 17% (5/29) daily internet access, 56.6% (17/29) consistent electricity; 91% of staff mentored on data quality and 65% of facilities supervised on IDSR core indicators.

audits.t: Over-admission and over-treatment of patients with cellulitis: a 5-year audit against international guidelines.
audits.st: CREST and IDSA international guidelines for cellulitis admission and antibiotic therapy
audits.f: 35% (n = 182) of admissions inappropriate against CREST and IDSA guidelines; 96% (n = 501) received combination flucloxacillin and benzylpenicillin.

audits.t: Long-term audit of the use of fresh frozen plasma in a university hospital.
audits.st: Appropriate use of fresh frozen plasma with coagulation testing before and after infusion (target not stated)
audits.f: 68,480 FFP units used over 22 years; use fell by 30.9% to its lowest level in 2000; coagulation testing before and after infusion in almost all obstetrics and gynaecology patients, 90% of surgical patients and about 70% in other departments.

audits.t: Immunoglobulin for Kawasaki disease: a 3-year retrospective audit.
audits.st: Local trust guideline and revised American Heart Association (AHA) guidelines for IVIG in Kawasaki disease
audits.f: 7/10 received IVIG within 10 days of illness onset; no patient had more than one follow-up echocardiogram (at 2 and 6 weeks).

audits.t: Improving the quality of operation notes: Effect of using proforma, audit and education sessions.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons operation note guidelines
audits.f: 14 parameters >90%; poor: time of operation 0%, emergency/elective 0%, prosthesis 65.3%, closure 36.6%, anaesthetist name 0%, position 1.3%, blood loss 0%
audits.c: Results presented at clinic training, aide-memoire in theatres, then an operation note proforma
audits.r2: Third audit after proforma: at least 80% compliance in all parameters

audits.t: Understanding quality improvement collaboratives through an implementation science lens.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline colorectal cancer screening rates in 9 participating health centres (figures not given in the abstract).
audits.c: Quality improvement collaborative with funding, training, facilitation, and audit and feedback; teams used aim statements, process maps, root cause analysis and PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: Colorectal cancer screening rates increased by 8.0% between 2017 and 2018.

audits.t: The use of an invitational letter to increase the vaccine uptake of patients with coeliac disease.
audits.st: Green Book chapter 7 (Department of Health 2013) vaccinations for individuals with underlying medical conditions
audits.f: Total vaccine uptake 38.6%
audits.c: Single invitation letter to attend a vaccine clinic sent to patients due vaccinations

audits.t: Impact of Systematic Training and CPAP Checklist in the Prevention of NCPAP Related Nasal Injuries in Neonates- A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.st: Manufacturer's recommendations for fixing the NCPAP interface (evidence-based checklist)
audits.f: Compliance with fixing NCPAP as per recommendation 35%; CPAP injuries 91 per 1000 CPAP days.
audits.c: Evidence-based NCPAP checklist applied by a designated CPAP nurse, with videos, small seminars, handouts and hands-on training; checklist modified over three PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: Compliance 95%; CPAP injuries 8 per 1000 CPAP days.

audits.t: Foundation doctor knowledge of wounds and dressings is improved by a simple intervention: An audit cycle-based quality improvement study.
audits.st: Local wound dressing formulary
audits.f: Mean knowledge score 32% correct
audits.c: ID-badge sized quick reference guide for lanyards and introduction to the formulary in routine teaching

audits.t: Audit and feedback of therapist-assisted internet-delivered cognitive behaviour therapy within routine care: A quality improvement case study.
audits.st: Audit measure of 15 undesirable therapist email behaviours (no acceptable levels set)
audits.f: Undesirable therapist behaviours occurred in 12% or less of emails across audit periods (1840 emails from 8 therapists).
audits.c: Audit feedback given to therapists four times from October 2018 to September 2019.
audits.r2: Trend towards improvement for most behaviours across four audit cycles; three behaviours (failure to ask one question, poor instructions, not linking email to course content) did not improve.

audits.t: Feedback Frequency in Competence by Design: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Target of one Competence by Design assessment per resident per week
audits.f: Baseline 0.22 assessments per resident per week (about 1 assessment every 4 weeks).
audits.c: First, a rule set on which clinical instances to assess plus weekly reminders (10 weeks, unsuccessful); second, an audit-and-feedback leaderboard with weekly comparison e-mails to residents and the programme director.

audits.t: National audit of cognitive assessment in people with pwMND A national audit of cognitive assessment in people with motor neurone disease (pwMND) in Scotland.
audits.st: NICE MND guideline (2016): 14 recommendations on cognitive and behavioural assessment
audits.f: Health professionals increasingly recognise cognitive screening and use more structured approaches than in previous years (no figures in abstract).

audits.t: Pilot Audit of Trichiasis Surgery Outcomes Using a Mobile App in the Republic of Chad.
audits.st: Surgeon trichiasis recurrence rate below 25% (25% or more indicates need for retraining)
audits.f: Recurrence in 20 of 170 patients (11.8%); mean surgeon recurrence rate 8.3% (range 0%-17.9%); no surgeon reached 25%, so no retraining was needed.

audits.t: Assessing Implementation of Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response in Rwanda.
audits.tp: Maternal death and severe morbidity review
audits.st: Six-step audit cycle for maternal and perinatal death surveillance and response
audits.f: Maternal death audits were conducted regularly with action plans, but perinatal death audits were not formally done; implementation varied between facilities.

audits.t: Patterns of prevalence and contemporary clinical management strategies in complicated acute biliary calculous disease: an ESTES 'snapshot audit' of practice.
audits.st: International guidelines for acute complicated biliary calculous disease
audits.f: Index admission cholecystectomy in 50% of cases; 28% had ERCP; morbidity and mortality low.

audits.t: Improving the quality of care for female rape survivors at Scottish Livingstone Hospital, Molepolole, Botswana: A quality improvement cycle.
audits.st: Current international standards: 10 structural and 10 process standards
audits.f: 1 of 10 structural standards met; no process standards met
audits.c: Improvements to structures for patients and upskilling of the practice team
audits.r2: 8 structural standards fully met; no process standards met, but significant improvement in 6 of 10 criteria

audits.t: Audit of Post-Splenectomy Prophylaxis in a Single Tertiary Center in Slovenia: Where Are We and What Should Be Done?
audits.st: Recommended post-splenectomy prophylaxis (vaccinations, antibiotic prophylaxis, education)
audits.f: Pneumococcal vaccination 121/156 (77.5%); re-vaccination after five years 27/70 (38.6%); meningococcal 89/156 (57.0%); Hib 87/156 (55.7%); antibiotic prophylaxis over two years 30/146 (20.5%).

audits.t: REPLICCAR II Study: Data quality audit in the Paulista Cardiovascular Surgery Registry.
audits.st: Modified Aggregate Data Quality score for completeness and accuracy (target not stated)
audits.f: Direct audit: agreement for categorical data kappa 0.7 (95% CI 0.59-0.83); only 2 of 15 continuous variables had ICC below 0.9. Indirect audit of all 2229 patients: 77% of 23 selected variables had a good ADQ score.

audits.t: Shortening Postoperative Stay after Parathyroidectomy - A District General Hospital Experience.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median length of stay 3 days (range 2-9; mean 3.32); biochemical cure 40/42 (95.2%)
audits.c: Short-stay protocol with preoperative patient education and rationalised postoperative calcium management
audits.r2: Median length of stay 2 days (range 2-3; mean 2.16); biochemical cure 33/34 (97.1%)

audits.t: Limiting spread of COVID-19 in Ghana: Compliance audit of selected transportation stations in the Greater Accra region of Ghana.
audits.st: WHO recommendations on hand hygiene and social distancing, scored with an adapted WHO hand hygiene assessment scale
audits.f: Compliance inadequate in 13 stations, basic in 16, intermediate in 7 and advanced in 9; 80% had at least one handwashing bucket, but handwashing was not or rarely observed in 95%, 93% lacked hand sanitiser and social distancing was practised in 2%.

audits.t: Compliance of primary and secondary care public hospitals with standard practices for reprocessing and steam sterilization of reusable medical devices in Nepal: findings from nation-wide multicenter clustered audits.
audits.st: Standard practices for reprocessing and steam sterilisation of reusable medical devices
audits.f: Mean compliance with standard practices was 25.9% (95% CI 21.0-30.8%) across 189 reprocessing cycles.

audits.t: Surgical consent during the COVID-19 pandemic.
audits.st: Intercollegiate and EAES guidance to discuss and document COVID-19 exposure risk in surgical consent
audits.f: 6/17 (35.3%) documented discussion of COVID-19 risk

audits.t: Could health information systems enhance the quality of Aboriginal health promotion? A retrospective audit of Aboriginal health programs in the Northern Territory of Australia.
audits.st: Validated paper-based audit tool for Aboriginal health promotion quality
audits.f: 34/39 projects recorded planning-phase information (goals, needs assessment, community consultation); evaluation findings reported in approximately one third of projects; community participation strategies not recorded in almost half.

audits.t: Awareness About Sharps Disposal Leads to Significant Improvement in Healthcare Safety: an Audit of Compliance in the National Health Service During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
audits.st: Health and safety regulations for sharps containers
audits.f: 56% of containers overfilled; overall compliance 44%
audits.c: Meetings with staff and posters throughout the hospital

audits.t: Retrospective quality assurance audit of Lateral Cephalometric Radiographs at postgraduate teaching hospital.
audits.st: National Radiation Protection Board quality grading standards; Royal College of Surgeons of England criteria
audits.f: 31 Grade I, 16 Grade II and 3 Grade III; only one Royal College criterion (correct head positioning) met the 100% standard.
audits.c: Recommendations made for comprehensive radiation protection regulations (no re-audit reported).

audits.t: Repeated analyses of national clinical audit reports demonstrate improvements in feedback methods.
audits.st: Good practice criteria for content and delivery of audit feedback
audits.f: Strengths at baseline: repeated audit cycles 21 (91%), topic importance 22 (93%), multi-modal data 23 (100%), key findings summarised 23 (100%).
audits.c: HQIP published reporting guidance for national audits (reassessed January 2017 with 20 reports).
audits.r2: At least 13/14 (93%) presented easily identifiable key findings and recommendations, linked recommendations to standards and proposed action plans.

audits.t: Assessing the impact of a quality improvement program on the quality and timeliness of discharge documents: A before and after study.
audits.st: National quality of discharge documents (QDD) score; discharge documents given to patient at discharge
audits.f: 63% of discharge documents given to patients at discharge; mean QDD score 41 (95%CI [36-46]).
audits.c: Quality improvement programme: revision of the EMR, educational programme, audit with scoring and feedback with ranking of clinical units (October 2016 to November 2018).
audits.r2: 95% of discharge documents given to patients; mean QDD score 82/100 (95% CI [80-85]).

audits.t: An on-site dosimetry audit for high-energy electron beams.
audits.st: Belgian-Dutch code of practice for high-energy electron beams; audit acceptance level 2.4%
audits.f: All absorbed dose to water results satisfactory, differences mostly smaller than 0.5% and always smaller than 1%; except for one, R50,dos differences smaller than 0.2 cm and always smaller than 0.3 cm.

audits.t: Quality improvement strategies to improve inpatient management of small and sick newborns across All Babies Count supported hospitals in rural Rwanda.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Syringe pumps available in 57%, vital sign monitors 51%, CPAP 14%; NCU case fatality rate 12.4%.
audits.c: All Babies Count package: equipment and supplies, clinical training, mentorship, QI coaching and learning collaborative sessions.
audits.r2: Syringe pumps, vital sign monitors and CPAP 100%; NCU case fatality rate 7.8% (p = 0.001).

audits.t: Audit of qualitative fit testing for FFP3 respirators.
audits.st: Health and Safety Executive standards for fit testing records
audits.f: 6% of records had missing or incomplete data; 80.6% (470/583) passed the fit test and 19.4% (113/583) failed.

audits.t: The effects of trained observers (dofficers) and audits during a facility-wide COVID-19 outbreak: A mixed-methods quality improvement analysis.
audits.st: 21-point audit of infection control bundle (signage, equipment, PPE use, environmental cleaning, cohorting and social distancing)
audits.f: Mean error rate 9.81%.
audits.c: Trained observers (dofficers, furloughed staff) giving real-time corrective feedback on PPE use, and weekly quality improvement reports to units.

audits.t: Improving the quality of electronic discharge summaries from medical wards: A quality improvement project.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: E-discharge workshops with local GPs and crib sheets emailed to junior staff and posted on medical wards
audits.r2: Quality of e-discharges improved, especially documentation of test results and patient progress and outcome.

audits.t: A national audit of estimated glomerular filtration rate and proteinuria and the MACD CKD task force recommendations.
audits.st: MACB CKD Task Force recommendations
audits.f: 42/140 (30%) laboratories responded; eGFR reported with creatinine by 61.9%; MDRD used by 64.3%; term microalbumin still used by 83.3%.

audits.t: National audit of antidote stocking in UK emergency departments.
audits.st: 2017 joint Royal College of Emergency Medicine and National Poisons Information Service guidance on antidote availability (category A immediately, category B within 1 hour, category C supra-regionally)
audits.f: 178 of 233 hospitals replied (76.4%); 73 (41.7%) fully compliant for category A, 34 (19.1%) for category B and 18 (10.1%) for both A and B.

audits.t: The quality assessment of the University hospital bone bank in Central Serbia: the second audit after fourteen years.
audits.st: International standards for allograft rejection and infection rates
audits.f: Overall rejection rate 74/267 (27.71%); contamination at retrieval 4.49%; failed blood screening 2.62%; infection after transplantation 1.30%.

audits.t: Infection Prevention Performance among Hospital Staff during Vaginal Birth: Results from a Criterion-Based Audit at a Zonal Referral Hospital in Tanzania.
audits.st: Criterion-based audit criteria set with staff from national and international guidelines
audits.f: Hand washing after a procedure 46.7%; alcohol-based hand rub before procedure 1.7% and after procedure 0%; knowledge test mean 59.3%.
audits.c: Discussion of baseline findings with staff, short training session and preparation of alcohol-based hand rub.
audits.r2: Hand washing after procedure 80% (RR=1.71); alcohol-based hand rub before procedure 33.3% and after 30%; knowledge test 65.3% (not significant).

audits.t: Reducing healthcare-associated infections by improving compliance to aseptic non-touch technique in intravenous line maintenance: a quality improvement approach.
audits.st: Aseptic non-touch technique (ANTT) audit proforma; aim to reduce HCAI by 50% over 6 months
audits.f: Aseptic field 0%, closed ports 0%, key part contamination 80%, hub scrubbing 0%; HCAI 26 per 1000 patient days.
audits.c: Pictorial standard operating procedure based on ANTT implemented through PDSA cycles with monthly run charts.
audits.r2: Aseptic field 100%, closed ports 100%, key part contamination 0%, hub scrubbing 72%; HCAI 8 per 1000 patient days.

audits.t: Medical management of first trimester miscarriage: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Effectiveness of primary medical treatment for first trimester miscarriage 53.8%.
audits.c: Introduction of mifepristone pretreatment into medical management of missed miscarriage

audits.t: Audit of the Sydney Local Health District Public Health Unit notification and contact tracing system during the first wave of COVID-19.
audits.st: Completeness and accuracy of notifiable conditions data
audits.f: Variables measuring completeness improved over time.
audits.c: Real-time audit team correcting missing and inaccurate data as a continuous quality improvement activity.

audits.t: Locked the Car, Why Not the Computer: A Qualitative and Quantitative Study on Data Safety Compliance.
audits.st: Trust Information Technology Safe Usage Policy
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Interventions not specified; junior doctors interviewed about reasons for non-compliance

audits.t: Audit of data redaction practices in NICE technology appraisals from 1999 to 2019.
audits.tp: Data redaction in health technology appraisals
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 333 TAs (81.6%) had data redaction; 86 (25.8%) heavily redacted; all 10 HST evaluations redacted.

audits.t: UK national bladder outlet obstruction surgery snapshot audit.
audits.tp: Preoperative assessment before bladder outlet surgery
audits.st: Guidelines for preoperative assessment of men with lower urinary tract symptoms (frequency-volume chart and symptom questionnaire)
audits.f: In non-catheter-dependent men, no evidence of a frequency-volume chart in 73% and of a urinary symptom questionnaire in 50%.

audits.t: Institutional Audit of Adaptive Re-Planning With Pencil Beam Scanning Proton Beam Therapy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 43% underwent plan adaptation.
audits.c: Skin rind evaluation for head and neck patients, modified planning techniques, avoidance of certain beam angles and changes to class solutions.

audits.t: Beyond audit: Embracing QI methodology to drive improvements in lung-protective ventilation.
audits.st: Tidal volumes 6-8 mL/kg predicted body weight; target >85% of tidal volumes compliant by end of November 2019
audits.f: Only 60.1% of recorded tidal volumes were compliant with lung-protective ventilation.
audits.c: IHI quality improvement methodology with repeated PDSA cycles and real-time data collection and reporting (specific changes not detailed)
audits.r2: Sustained compliance with lung-protective ventilation for >85% of tidal volumes.

audits.t: The Value of On-Site Proton Audits.
audits.st: Task Group-recommended QA and measurement-based peer review

audits.t: Time for change in practice of in-patient oxygen therapy: a period-limited, multidimensional approach to improve oxygen prescription compliance: quality improvement project at Hamad General Hospital, Qatar.

audits.t: Audit on knowledge, attitudes and practices on developmental assessment among public health midwives in a sub-urban health area in Sri Lanka.

audits.f: Mean knowledge score 63.7% (SD 8.4); primary reflexes 49.8%; milestone cut-off ages 32.9%; none fully confident in comprehensive assessment

audits.t: NetZero deep brain stimulation: A carbon footprint minimisation audit and environmental impact analysis.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean total waste 19 kg per procedure before workflow changes.
audits.c: NetZero-DBS workflow with five high-impact changes to waste management, consumable use and product choice
audits.r2: Mean total waste 15.5 kg per procedure (not statistically significant); consumable use reduced by 21.36 kgCO2e (12%) per procedure.

audits.t: Perinatal Deaths in Suriname: A Nationwide Cohort Study on Causes of Death and Lessons Learned from Facility-Based Audits.
audits.st: WHO Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response cycle
audits.f: 83 stillbirths and 72 neonatal deaths; PMR 28.2 per 1000 total births; 63 audited cases had 150 modifiable factors, half related to quality of care.

audits.t: Taming the contaminants: a quality improvement initiative to minimize blood culture contamination and enhance patient care in a resource-limited setting.
audits.st: International benchmark blood culture contamination rate below 3%
audits.f: Mean BCC rate 12.9%.
audits.c: Regular training, didactic sessions, re-competencies, 'hardened' aseptic protocols, Master Trainer mentorship, monthly monitoring with feedback and BCC as a KPI (PDSA).
audits.r2: Mean BCC rate 6.09%, still above the 3% benchmark.

audits.t: Learning opportunities in eclampsia care: A ten-year audit from Norway, 2013-2022.
audits.st: Clinical guidelines for eclampsia care (case review)
audits.f: 22 women with eclampsia among 93 139 deliveries (2.4 per 10 000); none received magnesium sulfate before the seizure; cerebral imaging in 11 of 22; learning opportunities in 18 of 22, and different management could potentially have prevented eclampsia in eight.

audits.t: Reducing On-Shelf Wastage of Fresh Frozen Plasma and Cryoprecipitate in a Tertiary Care Hospital Blood Centre: A Clinical Audit Using the Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) Method.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Breakage of FFP and cryoprecipitate 2.66% (also given as 2.50%); wastage from other reasons 4.96%.
audits.c: Measures to reduce breakage through PDSA cycles, including staff training, SOP adherence and monitoring.
audits.r2: Breakage 1.03% (p<0.001); overall on-shelf wastage reduced from 3.9% to 0.22%.

audits.t: Multicentre international audit of IMACS malignancy screening guidelines in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies: insights from the myositis audit and research collaborative group.
audits.st: IMACS consensus guidelines for malignancy screening in idiopathic inflammatory myopathy, by risk category
audits.f: Full panel of IMACS-recommended tests done in 6.2% of high-risk, 2.7% of moderate-risk and 11.1% of standard-risk patients.

audits.t: Changes in the indications for and outcomes of gastrostomy tube placement: an analysis of serial, prospective multi-site audits in Northern England.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Prophylactic antibiotics used in 83%; 7-day mortality 2%; 30-day mortality 9%; mean age 71 years.
audits.r2: Prophylactic antibiotics used in 93%; 7-day mortality 1%; 30-day mortality 2.5%; mean age 63 years.

audits.t: Auditing CV risk assessment of inpatients with acute high-risk chest pain: room for improvement?
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk testing in chest pain admissions
audits.st: LDL-C and HbA1c checked during inpatient stay; target 100%
audits.f: LDL-C checked in 49%; HbA1c checked in 45%
audits.c: Planned intervention to improve admission testing (not detailed)
audits.r2: Improvement in testing, mainly driven by LDL-C testing (figures not reported)

audits.t: Reinstating and augmenting prospective audit and feedback for carbapenem stewardship: A quasi-experimental interrupted time-series study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Prospective audit and feedback resumed in December 2024, augmented with ward round-based feedback from January 2025.
audits.r2: Immediate level reduction of -17.7 carbapenem DOT per 1000 patient-days (95% CI -26.2 to -9.25).

audits.t: Making every test count: Insights from a test kit efficiency audit.
audits.st: Manufacturer benchmark test kit efficiencies for 96 chemistry analytes
audits.f: Under-performing analytes included CSF total protein, alkaline phosphatase, glucose, ferritin, direct bilirubin and vancomycin.
audits.c: Root cause analysis and targeted interventions (kit size, batching).
audits.r2: Test kit efficiency improved by 12.6% - 37.7% for each targeted analyte.

audits.t: Audit cycle improves the quality of assistance in the management of stillbirth: A 10 years' experience.
audits.st: Quality of assistance in stillbirth management (audit cycle with preventability assessment)
audits.f: Inadequate care 9.92%; stillbirth proportion 0.313%.
audits.c: Audit cycle implemented at local and central levels.

audits.t: Transforming central line associated blood stream infection prevention in neonates: Results from a multimodal quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Target of 50% reduction in CLABSI rates within 12 months, sustained for a further 18 months
audits.f: Baseline CLABSI rate 6.4 per 1000 central line days
audits.c: Multimodal bundle: strengthened hand hygiene, updated CLABSI prevention bundles, revised environmental cleaning protocols, regular audits of line insertion and maintenance, and structured nursing education, refined over multiple PDSA cycles
audits.r2: CLABSI rate 1.1 per 1000 central line days (83% reduction)

audits.t: Timely care for tiny lives: quality improvement for golden hour management bundle.
audits.st: Golden hour management bundle (GHMB) completed within the first 60 min of life
audits.f: Baseline audit: only 7.7% of preterms received the GHMB; median time to complete GHMB 107 min
audits.c: Process mining to identify rate-limiting steps, with reorganisation and reassignment of tasks
audits.r2: Median time to complete GHMB 55 min (p value truncated in abstract)

audits.t: Implementing day-case parathyroidectomy in a large multi-site UK trust: a prospective case series.
audits.st: GIRFT recommendation: 90% of parathyroidectomies for primary hyperparathyroidism as day cases
audits.f: 7% discharged within 24 h
audits.c: Standardised checklist-guided day-case pathway (eligibility criteria, morning list prioritisation, expedited postoperative biochemistry, protocolised discharge), then emphasis on judicious drain use
audits.r2: 5/16 suitable patients (31.3%) discharged same day; drain use 1 case (6.3%)

audits.t: Effect of a closed-loop audit and feedback system on compliance with multidrug-resistant organism prevention measures.
audits.st: Multidrug-resistant organism prevention and control measures
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Closed-loop system: standardised checklist audits, fluorescent marker monitoring and real-time mobile app feedback
audits.r2: Overall compliance increased by 24.97 percentage points (95% CI 22.28-27.66)

audits.t: Medicines management audit cycle, St. Brigid’s Hospital Ballinasloe
audits.st: Local, national and international guidelines on medicines management
audits.f: Original audit identified need for a fit-for-purpose medication chart, prescribing education/training and a prescribing formulary/Drugs & Therapeutics Committee
audits.c: Introduction of a new medication chart incorporating recommendations
audits.r2: Considerable improvement in patient demographics, pharmacist involvement, generic prescribing, block capitals, Medical Council Registration Number, PRN prescribing and discontinuation procedures

audits.t: Improving general practitioners’ referral details of antidepressant use for patients referred for depression to primary mental health care: re-audit
audits.tp: GP referral documentation of antidepressant use
audits.st: Local standard for documenting antidepressant treatment details in GP referral letters
audits.f: 100% documented current antidepressant treatment/dose; only 33% documented previous antidepressant use, 15% dose/duration, 3% reason for stopping
audits.c: Feedback and introduction of a pro forma
audits.r2: 25% and 24% rise in documenting previous antidepressant used and maximum dose reached respectively; 20% rise in documenting reason for stopping

audits.t: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026LB64 RECENTLY COMPLETED RE-AUDIT OF OUT-OF-HOURS MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY ACCESS FOR ANTERIOR CIRCULATION STROKE IN A UK TERTIARY CENTRE
audits.st: not reported (structured late-window reassessment protocol introduced locally for out-of-hours anterior circulation LVO stroke)
audits.f: Lower CT angiography/perfusion utilisation at baseline (not quantified); out-of-hours mechanical thrombectomy (MT) rate 22%.
audits.c: Structured protocol: mandatory CT angiography, defined CT perfusion triggers, registrar-level neuroradiology discussion, documented reassessment before the next available MT session.
audits.r2: CT angiography performed in 100% of cases, CT perfusion in 71%; documented neuroradiology discussion in all eligible cases; MT rate increased to 39%; approximately 65% of MT recipients achieved modified Rankin Scale 0-2 at discharge.

audits.t: P33 Improving compliance with early IV-to-oral switch of antibiotics using quality improvement methodology
audits.st: UKHSA National IV-to-oral switch (IVOS) criteria for adults
audits.f: Antibiotic review within 24h of prescription 10%; eligible patients switched when criteria met 33.3%; median time to switch 22h34min; median duration of IV therapy 96h.
audits.c: Email correspondence and IVOS decision-aid posters; education sessions in weekly teaching/board rounds; ACED-tool lanyard cards; twice-weekly pharmacist IVOS ward rounds.
audits.r2: Antibiotic review within 24h rose to 94%; eligible patients switched when criteria met rose to 90%; median time to switch fell to 6h22min; median duration of IV therapy fell to 48h.

audits.t: P08 Audit of compliance with MHRA alerts with regards to patient counselling when prescribing fluoroquinolones
audits.tp: Fluoroquinolone counselling compliance with MHRA alerts
audits.st: MHRA alerts requiring patient counselling on fluoroquinolone risks at initiation, during treatment and at discharge
audits.f: Counselling before initiation documented for 10/60 (17%) patients, mostly via MHRA leaflet; 87% of prescriptions were in line with Trust antimicrobial guidelines/microbiology input; over 80% received no documented counselling at any stage; over 75% had at least one risk factor, more than half aged over 60.
audits.c: Findings shared in educational sessions and clinical governance forums; a re-audit is planned but had not been completed.

audits.t: P39 ‘Watch’ Out! An audit of piperacillin/tazobactam prescribing in a district general hospital
audits.st: Trust antimicrobial guidelines for piperacillin/tazobactam indications and National Antimicrobial IV-to-oral switch review criteria at 48/72/96 hours
audits.f: 66% correctly initiated for a first-line indication (34% warranted another antibiotic); 86% of inappropriate prescriptions started on admission day without trial of first-line agents; documented review at 48h 68% (of 38 remaining), at 72h 74% (of 31), at 96h 70% (of 27); only 46% had blood cultures taken; 27% had microbiology input within 96h.
audits.c: Trust plans to implement an indication-based prescribing system (not yet implemented); a second-cycle audit is planned to evaluate impact.

audits.t: P43 Improving therapeutic attainment with continuous vancomycin infusions in critical care: a quality improvement project
audits.tp: Therapeutic attainment with continuous vancomycin infusion
audits.st: MFT guidance targeting plasma vancomycin concentrations of 15-25 mg/L
audits.f: 44% achieved a therapeutic plasma concentration on first measurement; 53% sub-therapeutic, 2.3% supra-therapeutic; correct loading dose in 87%, correct maintenance infusion rate in 88%.
audits.c: Guideline update with more dose banding and increased loading and maintenance doses.
audits.r2: 55% achieved therapeutic concentration on first measurement; sub-therapeutic fell to 17% but supra-therapeutic rose to 29.3%; correct loading dose in 95%, correct maintenance rate fell to 71%.

audits.t: An audit into the prescription of syntocinon and magnesium sulphate infusions
audits.tp: Syntocinon and magnesium sulphate infusion prescription compliance
audits.st: Trust Prescribing Guidelines (12 standards)
audits.f: Drug administered but not prescribed in 6/76 cases; legibility 53-70%; block capitals 13-27%; prescriber identifiability 13-27%; abbreviations frequent (70-83%) for magnesium sulphate
audits.c: Poster campaign, availability of prescribing policies on wards, redesign of Trust fluid chart, and stickers for prescription of the two infusions

audits.t: Third degree tears: the impact of audit upon clinical practice
audits.tp: Third degree perineal tear documentation and management
audits.st: Local guideline for management/documentation of third degree tears (recommended intraoperative/postnatal antibiotics, laxatives, postnatal consultation documentation)
audits.f: Inadequate documentation of tear classification and repair; poor compliance with intraoperative antibiotics, postnatal antibiotics, laxatives and postnatal consultation documentation
audits.c: Revision of local guideline, simplification of antibiotic regime, dissemination of results within department
audits.r2: Statistically significant (p<0.05) improvements in documentation of tear classification, suture materials and correct postoperative laxatives; reduction in lack of documentation of postnatal follow-up

audits.t: Operative vaginal deliveries at a district general hospital – an audit
audits.tp: Instrumental (operative vaginal) delivery safety and documentation
audits.st: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists Green-top Guideline on instrumental delivery
audits.f: 49/496 (10%) deliveries were instrumental; documentation of abdominal examination missing in 28 (62%); only half (25) had documentation of examination for third/fourth degree tears
audits.c: Recommendations to improve documentation, avoid sequential instruments, proper case selection and examination; proposal for improved standard proforma

audits.t: An audit of the management of threatened preterm labour
audits.tp: Management of threatened preterm labour and fibronectin testing
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Almost 20% of admissions presented with symptoms/signs of threatened preterm labour; management mainly steroids and tocolysis, with in-utero transfer for a small number
audits.c: Planned introduction of fetal fibronectin testing

audits.t: Re-audit of management of anaemia in pregnancy
audits.st: NICE Antenatal Care guideline: routine haemoglobin screening at 12 and 28 weeks gestation
audits.f: Pilot audit done in 2005 (not detailed)
audits.c: not reported (information card with tables for blood results/treatments suggested)
audits.r2: Prevalence of anaemia 10%; booking Hb done >12/40 in 74% (of whom 74% anaemic); only 48% had further Hb screen at 28/40 (77% anaemic); 23% remained anaemic by term; treatment successful in 55% overall

audits.t: PM.55 Developing and Defining Auditable Standards of Care For Obstetric Women Admitted to ITU: Completing the Audit Cycle
audits.tp: Auditable standards for obstetric ITU admissions
audits.st: CNST standards 2.9, 4.8 and 5.10, and 12 locally derived auditable standards for obstetric ITU admission care
audits.f: Highlighted poor documentation and difficulty identifying evidence against CNST standards.
audits.c: Twelve auditable standards defined (reason for transfer, daily multidisciplinary review, SBAR handover, entry level, length of stay, discharge criteria, outreach follow-up, clinical incident form); local guidelines revised; named person to ensure compliance.
audits.r2: Re-audit confirmed improved documentation, although extracting evidence from notes continued to be difficult.

audits.t: PL.77 Compliance in Obstetrics and Gynaecology Shifts Handover – Re-Audit
audits.tp: Shift handover compliance against NHSLA guidelines
audits.st: NHSLA guideline for effective multidisciplinary shift handover using the SBAR tool
audits.f: 100% of medical staff used SBAR tools; morning handover attendance 83% medical staff, 80% lead midwife, 53% consultants; poor handover documentation.
audits.c: Recommendations made to improve the quality of shift handover (specific changes not detailed in the abstract).
audits.r2: Morning handover attendance rose to 88% medical staff, 88% lead midwife, 63% consultants (up to 27% increase in evening handover attendance); 93% used SBAR tools correctly (from 87%); all midwives met documentation requirements when transferring women to postnatal ward.

audits.t: PL.82 An Audit of Compliance with Current Guidelines on the Management of Third and Fourth Degree Tears in the Rotunda Hospital
audits.tp: Management of third and fourth degree perineal tears
audits.st: Rotunda Hospital 'Guidelines for Management of Episiotomy and Repair of Perineal Trauma' (Sept 2010)
audits.f: 100% repaired under regional anaesthesia; only 66% received correct dose/duration of antibiotics; 95% received laxatives but only 51% appropriate non-opiate analgesia; 44.6% reviewed by senior staff; 81% received physiotherapy; 87% followed up in perineal clinic.
audits.c: Recommended: revise perineal repair form to include headings specific to 3rd/4th degree tears; sticker on drug Kardex to flag the tear and avoid opiate prescription; discharge information leaflet; senior staff review on day 1 postpartum.

audits.t: PL.85 Umbilical Vein Injection in the Management of Retained Placenta-Closing the Audit Loop
audits.tp: Oxytocin route for management of retained placenta
audits.st: NICE intrapartum guidelines (2007) recommending umbilical vein oxytocin injection over intravenous oxytocin infusion for retained placenta
audits.f: High rates of intravenous oxytocin infusion use (57%) and lower rates of intra-umbilical oxytocin injection use (28%).
audits.c: Introduction of local guidelines unified with NICE guidance in 2012.
audits.r2: Intravenous oxytocin infusion use fell to 15%; umbilical vein injection use also fell, to 18%.

audits.t: PL.96 An Audit on Major Postpartum Haemorrhage at Queens Hospital, Romford
audits.st: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 52 for postpartum haemorrhage management, and comparison with a previous local audit
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: 27 patients required blood transfusion of up to 10 units; 6 manual removals of placenta and 8 other surgical interventions including 1 hysterectomy; improvement seen in PPH proforma completion and patient debriefing, but deterioration in emergency call-out (2222) use and incident reporting compared with the previous audit.

audits.t: PP.66 An Audit of Reduced Fetal Movements in a District General Hospital in Lanarkshire
audits.st: RCOG Green-top Guideline 57 (Reduced Fetal Movements, February 2011)
audits.f: All women received CTG (100% normal); no documentation of IUFD risk factors or fundal height at presentation; only 4% were booked for ultrasound within 24 hours; 82% of women meeting referral criteria were not scanned; 35% had no follow-up arranged.
audits.c: Development of a local RFM guideline, as none previously existed.

audits.t: PC.65 A tale of pigtails – Audit on the outcome and efficacy of pigtail catheters
audits.tp: Efficacy of pigtail catheter size for neonatal pneumothorax drainage
audits.st: not reported (local recommendation to use 8.5F pigtail catheters based on audit findings)
audits.f: Chest drain ineffective in 5 babies; 5F size used in 3 babies on 7 occasions; 8.5F used in only 1 baby; recommendation made to use 8.5F catheters in all gestations.
audits.c: Standardisation on 8.5F pigtail catheters for all gestations.
audits.r2: 8.5F pigtail inserted in 7 babies without need for a subsequent drain; 4 babies remained asymptomatic without needing a drain; no re-accumulation since switching to 8.5F only; no adverse insertion events.

audits.t: PFM.29 Audit on management of twin pregnancies in a district general hospital
audits.tp: Management of twin pregnancies against NICE guidance
audits.st: NICE multiple pregnancy guideline (September 2011)
audits.f: Chorionicity confirmed before 14 weeks and consultant-led referral achieved in 100%; Down's syndrome screening uptake 55.5%; scan-frequency adherence MCMA 100%, MCDA 80%, DCDA 92%; elective delivery at recommended gestation 100% monochorionic, 71% dichorionic; TTTS incidence 3.7%; 2 pregnancy losses.
audits.c: Introduction of a regional guideline in response to NICE recommendations.

audits.t: PLD.05 Audit of Informed Consent and Recall of Risks for Caesarean Section
audits.tp: Informed consent and recall of risks for caesarean section
audits.st: Sunderland Royal Hospital guideline (7 risks) and RCOG advice (16 risks) for caesarean section consent; 100% compliance expected
audits.f: Written consent obtained for 2 of 3 category-1 'crash' caesareans (1 had no documented consent); of 37 less-urgent cases, 36 had written and 1 verbal consent; 60% recalled all 7 SRH risks with prompting but only 2.5% recalled all 16 RCOG risks; only 44% of obese women were aware obesity increased risk; 55% would want written antenatal CS information.
audits.c: Recommended staff training on individualised consent forms and provision of written antenatal caesarean information (not yet implemented).

audits.t: PMM.07 The Hyperemesis Gravidarum Protocol: A retrospective audit of management in a DGH
audits.st: Local hospital guidelines for hyperemesis gravidarum management, based on best-evidence expert advice (no national guideline exists)
audits.f: Correct admission investigations were performed in 15-65% of cases; ward-based monitoring occurred in 10-57%; advice provided to patients in only 2-9%; recommended medications were omitted in 12% or misprescribed in 8-43%.
audits.c: Root-cause analysis performed; guidelines extensively revised, patient information leaflets written, MDT education undertaken.

audits.t: PMM.11 Audit of identification of antenatal risk factors for pre-eclampsia
audits.tp: Identification and management of pre-eclampsia risk factors
audits.st: NICE clinical guideline CG107 (Hypertension in Pregnancy): aspirin 75mg daily or serial growth scan/umbilical Doppler every 4 weeks from 28-30 weeks for women with risk factors
audits.f: Only 33 of 117 (28%) cases with risk factors were managed appropriately; 14 patients with risk factors developed pre-eclampsia requiring induction/caesarean section, of whom 6 had not been appropriately risk-managed.
audits.c: Staff education on NICE guidance and review of booking interview structure recommended (not yet implemented).

audits.t: PMM.12 Audit of identification of antenatal patients with a raised BMI requiring high dose folate
audits.tp: High-dose folate prescribing for obese antenatal patients
audits.st: CMACE/RCOG guideline: 5mg folate daily periconceptionally and through the first trimester for women with BMI ≥30 kg/m2
audits.f: Only 14 of 161 (9%) patients with BMI ≥30 received the recommended 5mg folate; 3 of 821 fetuses had spina bifida, of whom 2 mothers had BMI ≥30 and neither had taken high-dose folate.
audits.c: Further education and dissemination of results to staff recommended (not yet implemented).

audits.t: PMM.26 Audit of Hypertension in Pregnancy
audits.st: NICE guideline CG107 (2010) and local Trust guidelines for hypertension in pregnancy; standard of 80%
audits.f: Protein on urine dipstick with PCR/MSU sent 59%; fetal biometry scan for pre-eclampsia <34 weeks 40%; next available antenatal appointment made 30%; delivery by 37 weeks for pre-eclampsia 100%; no formal diagnosis recorded in 17% of cases.
audits.c: Further teaching sessions on hypertension in pregnancy during junior doctor induction; a proforma/checklist proposed (not yet implemented).

audits.t: A complete audit cycle demonstrating that increased use of intra-partum fetal monitoring using fetal ecg st segment analysis (STAN) is associated with reduced rates of fetal blood sampling (FBS)
audits.tp: STAN fetal monitoring use and fetal blood sampling rates
audits.st: Local guideline recommendations to increase use of STAN (fetal ECG ST segment analysis) monitoring
audits.f: STAN used in 253/1510 (17%); fetal blood sampling (FBS) attempted in 40/253 (16%)
audits.c: Findings presented at local audit meetings; recommendations made to increase STAN use
audits.r2: STAN use increased to 268/638 (42%) (p<0.0001); FBS attempts fell from 16% to 12/268 (4%) (p<0.0001)

audits.t: An audit of medical documentation on standardised electronic neonatal database (SEND) in a large level-2 neonatal unit
audits.st: Academy of Medical Royal Colleges generic medical record-keeping standards
audits.f: Completion rates varied widely by field, e.g. routine examination on admission 37%, routine screening/immunisation 44-69%, NNAP data items 54-93%; most demographic fields 90-100%
audits.c: not reported (continued in-house training and supervision recommended)

audits.t: Care bundle for induction of labour of intrauterine fetal death >24/40: completed audit cycle of a UK teaching hospitals' practice before and after rcog green-top guideline implementation
audits.tp: Care bundle for induction of labour in intrauterine fetal death
audits.st: RCOG green-top guidance (2010) on induction of labour for intrauterine fetal death (IUFD) >24/40
audits.f: 10 different induction-drug combinations identified; only 10 (50%) had mifepristone/misoprostol combination, 90% of which received unsafe doses; 12/20 management plans unclear, 16/20 poorly followed
audits.c: Hospital guideline implemented based on published evidence and RCOG guidance, using a care bundle (8 essential requirements) with a sticker for the notes
audits.r2: Huge improvement in management, documentation and plan implementation; 90% received safe recommended misoprostol doses

audits.t: Re-audit of the use of fetal blood sampling prior to emergency caesarean section
audits.tp: Fetal blood sampling prior to emergency caesarean for abnormal CTG
audits.st: Local practice standard for use and interpretation of fetal blood sampling (FBS) before emergency caesarean for abnormal CTG
audits.f: 9/50 (18%) had a successful normal pH but all proceeded straight to caesarean regardless
audits.r2: 50% increase in FBS attempted; 85% increase in appropriate interpretation/management; 11/13 (85%) had successful normal pH and were reviewed appropriately; general improvement in documentation of FBS procedure

audits.t: Second stage caesarean section – the importance of regular audit
audits.tp: Second stage caesarean section seniority and complications
audits.st: Local and national guidelines for second stage caesarean sections
audits.f: Most senior clinician available not present in 13% of cases; intra-operative complication rate 34%; 7% required transfusion; 23% stayed more than 3 days
audits.c: Unit-wide education raising awareness of results; increased hours of consultant cover on labour ward
audits.r2: Most senior clinician present in all deliveries (80% consultant); complication rate improved to 30%; no transfusions required; length of stay >3 days reduced to 20%

audits.t: P5-S6.29 Intensive use of a clinical documentation audit tool to bring about sustained improvement in the standard of record-keeping in a busy genito-urinary medicine (GUM) clinic
audits.tp: Clinical documentation audit tool sustained improvement in GUM
audits.st: Locally set internal standard of 100% for each of 31 documentation criteria
audits.f: Overall scores for individual clinicians ranged from 72% to 96% (median 82%, mean 83%)
audits.c: Monthly audit tool with feedback: collective scores issued monthly, individual scores quarterly, over 12 months
audits.r2: At month 12, scores ranged 87-100% (median 98%, mean 97%); repeat audit after 12-month lapse showed scores 89-100% (median 98%, mean 97%)

audits.t: P117 Audit on uptake of HIV test in sexual health clinic, antenatal and TOP services in Dumfries between January and June 2011
audits.tp: HIV testing uptake in sexual health, antenatal and TOP services
audits.st: BASHH UK National Guideline for HIV testing 2008 (universal HIV testing in GUM/sexual health, antenatal and TOP services)
audits.f: HIV test performed in 400/844 (47%) sexual health clinic episodes; 507/511 (99.2%) antenatal; 6/42 (14.2%) TOP
audits.c: not reported (recommendations made: offer HIV test to all, document declines, update local TOP guideline; re-audit planned)

audits.t: P157 Re-audit reflections: management of sexual assault attendances to GUM
audits.tp: Sexual assault attendance management and documentation
audits.st: BASHH guidelines (2011) for management of sexual assault attendances
audits.f: Proforma use 62%; assailant details asked 97%; anal/oral penetration asked 68%; condom use documented 88%; emergency contraception offered 100%
audits.c: Specific proforma and health advisor led care introduced after 2008 audit
audits.r2: Proforma use improved to 82% (p=0.002); anal/oral penetration asked 92% (p=0.001); condom use documented 100% (p=0.001); documentation of newer BASHH standards remained poor: self-harm risk assessment 3.4%, physical injuries 17%, bleeding 0%

audits.t: P28 A Re-audit of partner notification in HIV positive individuals in Plymouth
audits.tp: Partner notification in HIV positive individuals
audits.st: Local standard for partner notification (PN) outcomes and documentation in newly diagnosed HIV patients
audits.f: Baseline audit of partner notification approach and outcomes conducted in 2010
audits.c: Changes in approach to partner notification in newly diagnosed HIV patients
audits.r2: 100% of patients had a contact tracing proforma in notes and 97% (30/31) completed; 40% of partners were untraceable; of 13 patients transferred in 2010, 3 had PN performed since joining the clinic

audits.t: P067 All better now?: completing the audit cycle for pepse in the edinburgh gum service
audits.tp: PEPSE (post-exposure prophylaxis for sexual exposure) pathway compliance
audits.st: 2011/2015 BHIVA guidelines for PEPSE
audits.f: Baseline HIV test 81%; prescriptions fitting recommended indications 55%; within 72 hours 83%; within 24 hours 36%; course completion 47%; STI screen 51% (all below BHIVA standards)
audits.c: New local PEPSE pathway: more detailed patient discussion, full 28-day course provided at first visit, STI screening at initial visit
audits.r2: Baseline HIV test 90%; recommended indications 71%; within 72 hours 100%; within 24 hours 44%; course completion 49% completed (19 ongoing, 32 unknown/incomplete); STI screen 80%

audits.t: P140 A need to reinforce the importance of pregnancy testing and correct antibiotic regimen: a re-audit of pid management against bashh guidelines
audits.st: BASHH guidelines (2011) for pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) management
audits.f: Pregnancy exclusion 70% at previous audit
audits.c: not reported (actions taken: individual feedback to clinicians, re-audit planned)
audits.r2: STI screening 47/49 (96%); HIV screen 41/49 (84%); pregnancy excluded in 22/49 (45%), down from 70%; BASHH recommended antibiotic regimen used in 28/49 (57%)

audits.t: P159 Audits of both management of chlamydia and also emergency contraception provision as a marker of quality in an integrated service
audits.tp: Chlamydia management and emergency contraception provision equity across sub-units
audits.st: Local standards for chlamydia management and emergency contraception provision
audits.f: Anti-chlamydial treatment offer 100%; partner notification 47% (STI units), 58% (C+RHC units); written information 45%/18%; retesting offer for under-25s 61%/68%; quick start contraception 96%; IUCD offer 73%/57%
audits.c: not reported (emphasis placed on documentation with staff, reaudit planned)

audits.t: P004 Prospective comparison of charcoal swabs versus near-patient direct culture plate inoculation for the culture of gonorrhoea in high-risk patients. a repeat audit
audits.tp: Gonorrhoea culture method comparison (direct plating vs charcoal swab)
audits.st: Requirement for gonorrhoea culture to monitor antibiotic resistance in known/suspected infection
audits.f: Culture positive rate 24% lower for charcoal swabs than direct plating
audits.c: Laboratory implemented an urgent transport system for charcoal swabs
audits.r2: No difference in culture positive rates between direct plating and charcoal swabs (both 34/47, 72%); only 2 discrepancies

audits.t: P033 Improving clinical standards in GU medicine: a retrospective audit of neisseria gonorrhoeae
audits.st: BASHH guidelines for gonorrhoea (GC) management across 5 domains
audits.f: Baseline comparator data for same 6-month period in 2007-2015
audits.c: Teaching sessions and a quality improvement project to ensure patient information leaflets offered
audits.r2: Test of cure recommended 87% (61% had one); Chlamydia screening/treatment 100%; partner notification 88%; written information 56%; first-line treatment or documented reason 97%; recommending TOC, partner notification and information leaflets decreased over the last year

audits.t: Improving the quality of operation notes with electronic proformas
audits.st: Good Surgical Practice guidelines (2014), 21 criteria for operation note content
audits.f: 6 of 21 criteria were recorded in ≥95% of operation notes.
audits.c: Education session and introduction of an electronic operating proforma.
audits.r2: 9 of 21 criteria recorded in ≥95% overall; in the proforma subgroup, 15 of 21 criteria were recorded in ≥95% of notes.

audits.t: An audit and trial aiming to reduce the rate of surgical site infections for women having a caesarean section
audits.tp: Surgical site infection rate following caesarean section
audits.st: Local target to reduce SSI rate following caesarean section
audits.f: Audit found women with wound covered for longer were less likely to develop wound infection
audits.c: Trial of two different wound dressings; new dressings introduced remaining in place for 5 days

audits.t: Improving practice and reducing significant postpartum haemorrhage through audit
audits.tp: Postpartum haemorrhage risk assessment and management
audits.st: Local standard for risk assessment and informed choice regarding third stage management to reduce PPH
audits.f: Concern over incidence of PPH and physiological third stage management prevalence prompted the audit
audits.c: Findings shared with midwifery team who generated solutions, implemented 2013/14 (agreed pathway and PPH boxes)
audits.r2: Incidence of PPH >1000mL decreased; no women inappropriately managed physiologically during third stage; improved quality and speed of treatment

audits.t: An audit on the use and utility of midstream specimen of urine cultures in general practice
audits.tp: Appropriate use of midstream urine (MSU) cultures
audits.st: NICE quality standard QS90 for lower urinary tract infection management
audits.f: 66% of MSU samples were clinically indicated; adherence to QS90 68% (doctors 71%, practice nurses 36%)
audits.c: Educational intervention based on QS90 with new management algorithms
audits.r2: Clinically indicated MSUs increased to 77%; adherence to QS90 increased to 84% (doctors 78%, practice nurses 55%)

audits.t: Identifying and rectifying prescriptions of long-acting antimuscarinic and beta-agonist inhalers without inhaled corticosteroids to asthma patients: an audit from a UK general practice surgery
audits.tp: LABA/LAMA prescribing without inhaled corticosteroid in asthma
audits.st: Asthma UK national review guidelines; target 100% co-prescription of ICS with LABA/LAMA in asthma
audits.f: 7% (n=4) lacked a relevant coded diagnosis; of remaining 50, 16% (n=8) had asthma (+/-COPD) diagnosis on LABA/LAMA without ICS
audits.c: Ensuring coded diagnoses, reviewing LABA/LAMA without ICS prescriptions, discussing results with prescribers, activating electronic alerts
audits.r2: 3% (n=2) lacked a coded diagnosis; patients with asthma (+/-COPD) on LABA/LAMA without ICS decreased to 11% (n=7)

audits.t: Measuring the quality of Hospital Food Services: Development and reliability of a Meal Quality Audit Tool
audits.tp: Hospital meal quality audit tool development
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Statistically significant interrater reliability for Temperature and Accuracy domains (P<0.001) but not for Appearance or Sensory

audits.t: Improving Physical Health Monitoring for Patients Diagnosed With Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder
audits.tp: Physical health monitoring for emotionally unstable personality disorder patients
audits.st: SMI physical health monitoring standards applied to EUPD (annual medical review: height, weight, BP, lipids, alcohol/substance use)
audits.f: 0% of patients had all requested information complete
audits.c: Proforma developed to clarify information sought from GPs; more proactive engagement of GPs and other physical care teams
audits.r2: Compliance improved from 0% to 57%, including 100% for blood pressure/pulse and 86% for documented weight

audits.t: Improving Cardiac Monitoring for Patients on Depot Antipsychotic Medication in a Mental Health Service for Homeless People
audits.tp: Annual ECG monitoring for patients on depot antipsychotics
audits.st: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines in Psychiatry: annual ECG monitoring for patients on depot antipsychotics
audits.f: Only 48.8% of patients had an ECG recorded on SystmOne within the last year
audits.c: PDSA cycles: updating SystmOne from existing GP/secondary care ECGs; emailing GPs to invite annual ECG; JHT directly inviting patients for targeted ECGs
audits.r2: Recorded ECGs increased to 72.1% after intervention 1, 74% after intervention 2, and 83.7% after intervention 3

audits.t: A315 FREQUENCY AND PREDICTORS OF FASTING ORDERS IN INPATIENTS WITH ULCERATIVE COLITIS: THE AUDIT OF DIET ORDERS - ULCERATIVE COLITIS (ADORE-UC) STUDY
audits.tp: Fasting (NPO) orders in inpatient ulcerative colitis
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines recommending a normal diet or enteral nutrition for UC flares unless not tolerated
audits.f: 252 NPO/clear-fluid orders in 142 admissions (75.9%); 112 orders (44%) were unjustified; patients with unjustified orders averaged 3 days NPO/CF, corresponding to 10 missed meals

audits.t: 806. Decreasing Central Line-associated Bloodstream Infections Through Quality Improvement Initiative on a High Acuity Transplant Unit
audits.st: Best-practice central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) prevention bundle (line care standardisation); no numeric target rate stated
audits.f: CLABSI rate 4.825 per 1,000 central line days (11 infections) as the initiative began, following a progressive rise in CLABSI rate observed from 2016.
audits.c: Re-education on CLABSI reduction; two-nurse validation of central line dressing changes; blood draws from central lines requiring nurse manager, physician lead and transplant quality physician approval; designated CLABSI-prevention phlebotomists; daily line review of necessity/removal shared with the physician lead and quality team; ongoing audits with feedback and clinician accountability
audits.r2: CLABSI rate fell to 0 per 1,000 central line days (0 infections) in the first two quarters of 2020.

audits.t: Compliance to completion of sodium valproate annual risk acknowledgement form among women of child-bearing age prescribed sodium valproate in the intellectual disability (ID) services of an NHS trust
audits.tp: Sodium valproate annual risk acknowledgement form compliance
audits.st: MHRA (2018) guidance requiring an Annual Risk Acknowledgement Form for women of child-bearing age on sodium valproate
audits.f: 18 of 28 patients had ARF filled (64% compliance); ARF compliance 93% in neurology-initiated prescriptions vs 36% in psychiatrist-initiated
audits.c: not reported (recommendation to increase doctors' awareness and IT flagging of out-of-date ARFs)

audits.t: Delirium – are we doing enough prevention and basic management in acute settings?
audits.st: SIGN and NICE guidelines on non-pharmacological prevention/management of delirium
audits.f: Nurses unsure about hearing/visual aids in 41%/29% of patients; no clear signage, digital clock, calendar; earplugs not offered on any of the four wards; 18/57 (32%) patients died within a month of review
audits.c: not reported (recommendations proposed: bedside board, clock/calendar, checklist, emphasis on aids and reorientation)

audits.t: Constipation and clozapine: a QI project in Leicestershire Partnership NHS Trust, (LPT)
audits.st: Local protocol requirement for monitoring/managing constipation during clozapine initiation (informed by international Porirua protocol)
audits.f: Bowel chart started in only 1 inpatient; laxatives started in 50% (15, only 3 outpatients); 12 inpatients and 1 outpatient had constipation
audits.c: New local protocol for laxative prescribing and bowel chart use written and implemented by the trust

audits.t: The quality of handover on an inpatient psychiatric unit - information is key!
audits.tp: Quality of nursing-to-doctor handover on inpatient psychiatric unit
audits.st: Locally developed SBAR-based handover criteria (minimum information for safe handover)
audits.f: Patient name given in 49%, ID number in 10%, diagnosis/history and NEWS score in 18%; current issue 90%, recommendation 95%
audits.c: Awareness raised with nursing colleagues about handover standards
audits.r2: Patient name given in 51%, ID number 18%, diagnosis/history 12%, NEWS score 17%, current issue 92%, recommendation 51%

audits.t: Physical health monitoring before commencing regular antipsychotics in a Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) - A Quality Improvement project
audits.tp: Physical health monitoring before starting antipsychotics in PICU
audits.st: Standard PICU practice guidelines: physical examination, vitals, baseline bloods and ECG within 24 hours before commencing antipsychotics
audits.f: 13% of blood investigations completed before treatment; 7% consented to ECG; 27% had full physical examination; 37% had vitals only within 24 hours; 20% refused any physical examination
audits.c: not reported (recommendations proposed to meet standards)

audits.t: Psychiatric liaison team memory pathway: does it achieve the standards set out in NICE clinical guideline 97?
audits.tp: Psychiatric liaison memory pathway adherence to NICE dementia guideline
audits.st: NICE Clinical Guideline 97 (CG97): assessment, management and support for people living with dementia and their carers
audits.f: 63% given a memory diagnosis; 34% had anticholinergic medication but only 14% documented as reviewed; primary care informed in 100%; post-diagnostic support 100%; no ethnic minority patients identified
audits.c: not reported (pathway newly implemented; focus areas for improvement identified)

audits.t: P072 Audit on the uptake of COVID-19 vaccination in biologic patients with autoimmune conditions
audits.tp: COVID-19 vaccine uptake and safety in biologic-treated patients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 329/352 received double dose, 8 single dose, 15 (4.3%) declined; 146 had mild side effects, 3 (2.1%) severe (Grade 3+); 15/146 (10%) reported arthritis flare

audits.t: Adherence to WHO Hand Hygiene Protocols in the Surgical Department, Police Hospital, Nile River- Sudan
audits.tp: Hand hygiene compliance with WHO Five Moments
audits.st: WHO 'Five Moments for Hand Hygiene'
audits.f: Compliance 48.9%; 'after body fluid exposure' 27.3%; 'before aseptic procedures' 76.1%
audits.r2: Compliance rose to 93.4%; 'after body fluid exposure' rose to 91.2%; 'before aseptic procedures' rose to 100%; 'after touching a patient' decreased from 100% to 66.7%

audits.t: Diagnostic delay and gaps in guideline-recommended baseline evaluation among adults with tuberous sclerosis complex in China: a single-centre retrospective medical record audit
audits.tp: Diagnostic delay and baseline evaluation gaps in tuberous sclerosis complex
audits.st: 2021 International TSC Consensus recommendations for baseline multisystem evaluation
audits.f: Median diagnostic delay 23.4 years (range 6.1-31.9) in the adult-diagnosed subgroup; genetic testing documented in only 2/6 patients, dental/oral assessment in none; median 2 undocumented core baseline items per patient

audits.t: Audit of Current Care Pathways for Tinnitus: INTEGRATE ACCEPT Audit
audits.st: No single named national guideline; audit assessed practice against expected components of tinnitus care pathways (e.g. use of severity questionnaires, follow-up)
audits.f: 73% (824/1136) had hearing loss on audiometry, 38% of these received hearing aids; only 4% (46) received CBT; 94% had no tinnitus questionnaire used to document symptom severity, and only 2 patients had follow-up questionnaires

audits.t: Identifying and addressing the factors that impact maternal and perinatal deaths using facility-based death audit review system and integrating community engagement: A Mixed-Methods Study
audits.tp: Facility-based maternal and perinatal death audit with community engagement
audits.st: WHO facility-based maternal and perinatal death surveillance and response guidelines; Four Delays Model
audits.f: Key delay factors identified: lack of education/awareness (Delay 1-2), inadequate transport (Delay 3), multiple referrals (Delay 3-4), and limited facility hours/delayed care (Delay 4)
audits.c: Community awareness sessions, ambulance services, improved referral systems, antenatal cards, DHIS records and inter-facility communication

audits.t: An audit of electron microscopy in the diagnosis of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis – are current pathological techniques missing important abnormalities in the glomerular basement membrane?
audits.tp: Electron microscopy use in FSGS diagnosis
audits.st: Expectation that histologically diagnosed FSGS samples undergo electron microscopy to detect underlying collagen IV disorders
audits.f: Only 30 of 43 patients with a histological diagnosis of FSGS underwent electron microscopy; 2 of these samples showed changes suggestive of an underlying collagen IV disorder

audits.t: Implementation of an institutional communication pathway using electronic flagging and organisational audit for non-emergent actionable radiologic findings
audits.tp: Electronic flagging and organisational audit of actionable imaging findings
audits.st: not reported
