audits.f: 520 examinations (1.83%) had flagged non-emergent actionable findings; organisational audit identified 10 unopened reports and 50 cases with unconfirmed follow-up out of 526 flagged findings.

audits.t: Treatment-administered drugs are reported as positive screens in a trauma registry: an audit of compliance with the National Trauma Data Standard exclusion rule
audits.st: National Trauma Data Standard (NTDS) Drug Screen exclusion rule for treatment-administered drugs
audits.f: 914/1421 (64.3%) tested positive; under the rule as written 569/914 (62.3%) should have excluded a treatment-administered analyte and 350/914 (38.3%) should have been recorded as 'None'; applying the rule reduced positivity from 64.3% to 39.7%; noncompliance rose from 25.5% (ages 16-45) to 51.4% (81+).

audits.t: Audit of Haemodialysis Vascular Access in a Sub-Saharan Tertiary Hospital
audits.st: Guidelines recommending arteriovenous fistula as preferred vascular access for haemodialysis
audits.f: Femoral catheters were most commonly used rather than AVF; catheter-related infection in 49.8%; 66.4% used catheters <1 month, 24.8% >6 months.

audits.t: Regional organisational audit of district departments of public health.
audits.tp: Organisational audit of public health departments
audits.st: King's Fund organisational audit programme 'vital' organisational factors
audits.f: 20/54 (37%) vital factors achieved in all 12 districts; 16 (30%) in all but one; overall vital factors not achieved in 9% of cases.

audits.t: [Audit and standardization of allergologic practices for urticaria].
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An audit tool for health visitors and SLTs working with the pre-school population.
audits.tp: Speech and language therapy and health visiting services for pre-school children
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Preliminary findings only; no quantified results reported.

audits.t: Occupational health and safety management systems in the Canadian pulp and paper industry: methods of auditing.
audits.tp: Occupational health and safety management system audit
audits.st: Canadian Pulp and Paper Association's eight Guiding Principles for Management of OH&S
audits.f: System ownership and goals/procedures more often in place; measures of performance, review of measures and corrective action less often present.

audits.t: Prospective vancomycin audit in Auckland healthcare hospitals.
audits.st: Standard definitions of appropriate prophylactic, empirical and directed vancomycin therapy
audits.f: Half of vancomycin use could potentially be modified; 63% of inappropriate use was for empirical therapy.

audits.t: Perinatal audit on avoidable mortality in a Dutch rural region: a retrospective study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 31.50% of deaths classified as probably or possibly avoidable (18.75% primary care, 44.86% secondary care, 25.00% tertiary care); consensus kappa 0.9.

audits.t: Audit of early bladder management complications after spinal cord injury in first-treating hospitals.
audits.tp: Early bladder management after spinal cord injury
audits.st: Recommended practice of early intermittent catheterisation for the paralysed bladder
audits.f: At transfer, 48.8% still had an indwelling urethral catheter and only 16.5% were on intermittent catheterisation; urine cultures positive in 100% of indwelling-catheter cases vs 28.6% of intermittent.

audits.t: An audit of percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy in a general hospital in Singapore.
audits.tp: Timeliness of percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy referral
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Interval between dysphagia diagnosis and PEG was >60 days in 38% of patients, 31-60 days in 16%.

audits.t: A retrospective audit of electroconvulsive therapy at King Khalid University Hospital, Saudi Arabia.
audits.st: Ethical and technical standards for ECT administration (seizure monitoring, staff training)
audits.f: Deficiencies in early years: no seizure monitoring, no staff training/education, atropine used as premedication for all patients.
audits.c: Introduction of regular staff education/training and routine seizure timing monitoring

audits.t: Charter for disabled people using hospitals: a completed access audit cycle.
audits.tp: Access for disabled people to hospital facilities
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians Charter for Disabled People using Hospitals
audits.f: Baseline access assessment identified problems against the Charter standards
audits.c: Implementation of changes to overcome identified access problems

audits.t: An audit on access to coronary artery surgery within a health district using New Zealand priority criteria as a benchmark.
audits.tp: Access to coronary artery bypass surgery using priority criteria
audits.st: New Zealand priority criteria for access to CABG
audits.f: Clinical threshold for access to CABG was much higher in Sunderland than New Zealand; no evidence of inequity by age, gender, smoking or deprivation after adjustment.

audits.t: Consultative Committee on Road Traffic Fatalities: trauma audit methodology.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: In the case example, 16 management deficiencies were identified, 11 assessed as contributing to death; death judged non-preventable.

audits.t: Measuring the quality of clinical audit projects.
audits.tp: Measuring the quality of clinical audit projects
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: [Perinatal mortality assessed: results of a regional audit].
audits.st: Evidence-based criteria for standard perinatal care (expert panel checklist)
audits.f: One or more substandard care factors identified in more than half of cases; in 19% possibly and in 6% probably contributed to death.

audits.t: An audit of audits: are we completing the cycle?
audits.tp: Completion rates of clinical audit cycles
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 102 (48%) audits were 'partial' and 29 (14%) were 'full'; recommendations emerged from 134 (63%); cycle completed by re-auditing in only 51 (24%) over the subsequent 3 years

audits.t: Immunization activities of private-practice physicians: a record audit.
audits.st: Public Health Service recommended immunisation schedule for a 2-year-old child
audits.f: 36% had completed all recommended immunisations; 44% of 'active' patients complete vs 8% of 'inactive' patients.

audits.t: Continuous quality assessment; development of a simple computer based model for audit.
audits.tp: Computer-based quality indicator audit for laparoscopic cholecystectomy
audits.st: Literature-derived quality indicators: conversion rate and length of stay
audits.f: Conversion rate to open cholecystectomy 9.96%; mean length of stay 3.39 days (7.17 days for converted cases).

audits.t: Substandard factors in perinatal care in The Netherlands: a regional audit of perinatal deaths.
audits.st: Explicit evidence-based perinatal audit criteria
audits.f: Substandard factor possibly/probably related to death in 25% (95% CI 20-30%); mainly maternal/social factors and antenatal care factors (10% each); no significant difference between midwives and obstetricians or home vs hospital births.

audits.t: The last 48 hours of life in long-term care: a focused chart audit.
audits.tp: End-of-life symptom management in long-term care
audits.st: Literature-based expected treatment for common terminal symptoms (pain, dyspnoea, delirium etc.)
audits.f: Dyspnoea untreated in 23% of affected patients; opioids used in only 27%; delirium untreated in 38%; 99% of patients with pain were treated.

audits.t: Re-auditing a regional lithotripsy service.
audits.tp: Regional lithotripsy service outcomes and patient selection
audits.st: Comparison against results of 1994 regional audit of shock wave lithotripsy
audits.f: Disappointing results from lithotripsy, attributable to poor patient selection and an inadequate fixed-site lithotripter
audits.c: Changes implemented after the 1994 regional audit (not further specified)
audits.r2: Overall improvement in patient selection, but stone-free and success rates remained poorer than reported elsewhere

audits.t: A district-based audit of the causes and circumstances of maternal deaths in South Kalimantan, Indonesia.
audits.tp: Maternal death audit and quality improvement
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Leading causes: haemorrhage (41%) and hypertensive disease (32%); delays in decision-making contributed to 77% and poor facility care to 60% of deaths.
audits.c: Regular accountability meetings between providers, policy-makers and community, and review processes

audits.t: Introducing qualitative perinatal audit in a tertiary hospital in Sudan.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Perinatal mortality rate 8.2%; internal audit produced specific suggestions for improving data collection, interdisciplinary collaboration, and obstetric/neonatal care.

audits.t: Trauma deaths in an Italian urban area: an audit of pre-hospital and in-hospital trauma care.
audits.st: Predefined panel review criteria for preventability of trauma death
audits.f: 57% judged not preventable, 32% possibly preventable, 11% definitely preventable (inter-panel kappa 0.88); main failures were lack of airway control/IV access pre-hospital and missed injuries in the emergency department.

audits.t: Audit of prenatal and postnatal diagnosis of isolated open spina bifida in three university hospitals in The Netherlands.
audits.tp: Prenatal detection of open spina bifida
audits.st: Dutch policy of offering detailed ultrasound only to high-risk patients
audits.f: Only 38 (43%) of prenatal cases were diagnosed before 24 weeks; of 112 newborns with spina bifida, 65 (58%) were an unexpected finding at birth.

audits.t: Differences in perinatal mortality and suboptimal care between 10 European regions: results of an international audit.
audits.tp: Suboptimal care in perinatal death (EuroNatal international audit)
audits.st: Explicit international audit panel criteria for perinatal care
audits.f: Suboptimal factors identified in 715 (46%) of consensus cases; lower proportion in Finland and Sweden than other regions; failure to detect severe IUGR (10%) and smoking with severe IUGR/placental abruption (12%) were most frequent.

audits.t: Audit of the nutritional content of patient meals in Ayrshire and Arran.
audits.tp: Nutritional adequacy of hospital patient meals
audits.st: Health of the Nation Nutrition Guidelines for Hospital Catering (1995)
audits.f: Approximately 45% of days across the three Trusts failed to provide the recommended minimum energy; about one third of vegetarian meals failed to provide the recommended protein; calcium, iron and zinc provision was sometimes inadequate.
audits.c: Menus to be altered and a menu coding system introduced to meet the guideline standards, with the three Trusts collaborating on core menus

audits.t: [Health surveillance audit of wood dust exposure].
audits.tp: Occupational health surveillance quality for wood dust exposure
audits.st: Italian medical surveillance law for wood-dust exposed workers (Law 66/2000, EU carcinogens directive)
audits.f: Audit of occupational health physicians led in many cases to revision of the Security Document, improved programmes/protocols, and enhanced training; in a few cases it enabled diagnosis of wood dust-related occupational disease.

audits.t: Perinatal audit of one hundred consecutive vacuum extractions in Maputo.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Extractions with the fetal head above the ischiatic spines were associated with an 81% risk of neonatal asphyxia and severe neonatal trauma.

audits.t: Prospective audit of an aminoglycoside consultative service in a general hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline audit of aminoglycoside use, dosing efficiency and toxicity before the consultative service.
audits.c: Introduction of an aminoglycoside (gentamicin/tobramycin) consultative service
audits.r2: Significant improvement in appropriate use and dosing efficiency with a marked decrease in clinical toxicity, sustained at 18 months.

audits.t: An audit of the clinical investigation of pleural effusion.
audits.st: Recommended practice of pleural aspiration with biopsy, and a minimum 30 ml cytology sample
audits.f: About two thirds of cytology samples were less than the recommended 30 ml; pleural biopsy rate was 30% overall, varying from 0% (surgery) to 68% (thoracic medicine); 29% of biopsy samples were of poor quality.

audits.t: An audit of hearing aid quality in Denmark.
audits.st: Expectation that hearing aids remain functional within their guarantee period
audits.f: 60.4% of attendances were due to defective hearing aids; 20.6% of defective aids had been used less than one year (within guarantee); some series had defect rates of 6.6-70.9% in the first year.

audits.t: Acute contrast reaction management by radiologists: a local audit study.
audits.tp: Radiologist knowledge of contrast reaction management
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 53% of questions answered correctly overall; only 43% knew the correct adrenaline dose; only 26% had completed a resuscitation course in the past 2 years.

audits.t: Peer review audit of trauma deaths in a developing country.
audits.st: Peer review classification of preventable/potentially preventable/non-preventable trauma death
audits.f: 6 deaths judged preventable, 7 potentially preventable, 4 non-preventable; key contributing factors were inadequate prehospital transfer and limited hospital resources.

audits.t: Suboptimal care and perinatal mortality in ten European regions: methodology and evaluation of an international audit.
audits.tp: Suboptimal care in perinatal death (EuroNatal audit methodology)
audits.st: Explicit international audit panel criteria for perinatal care
audits.f: 90% of eligible cases were audited; consensus reached in 95%; 75% of gradings were based on explicit criteria, with reasonable to good inter/intra-panel agreement.

audits.t: Digoxin therapeutic drug monitoring: an audit and review.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: No clear indication for testing in 53% of requests; only 29% of requests were performed appropriately with regard to indication, sampling and dose alteration.

audits.t: Audit of prioritisation for coronary revascularisation procedures: implications for rationing.
audits.tp: Waiting times for coronary revascularisation against urgency rating
audits.st: Urgency rating score defining a nominally optimal waiting time
audits.f: Only 9/56 (16%) had CABG within the maximum optimal time; 19/36 (53%) had PTCA within the optimal period; mean CABG waiting time at least 163 (SD 116) days.

audits.t: An audit of splenectomies in a teaching hospital in North India. Are postsplenectomy guidelines being complied with?
audits.st: Postsplenectomy guidelines for vaccination and infection prevention
audits.f: 36/56 received pneumococcal vaccination but 20 had no vaccination documented; only 3/50 discharge notes recorded vaccination details.

audits.t: An audit of obstetricians' management of women potentially infected with blood-borne viruses.
audits.tp: Antenatal blood-borne virus screening and management
audits.st: RANZCOG antenatal screening recommendations and evidence-based guidelines for blood-borne viruses
audits.f: 51% would always offer HIV screening and 60% HCV screening; 34% incorrectly advised increased HBV transmission risk with breastfeeding, and 47% for HCV.

audits.t: Fetal abnormality: an audit of its recognition and management. Northern Regional Survey Steering Group.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Proportion of confirmed postnatal abnormalities recognised antenatally varied fivefold between units, unrelated to unit size or ultrasound workload; over 10% of antenatal diagnoses were wrong for some conditions.

audits.t: An audit of head trauma care and mortality.
audits.tp: Peer review of head trauma deaths
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Peer review committee identified pre-hospital deficiencies (inappropriate transfer, delayed transfer) and hospital deficiencies (lack of ICU beds/ventilators, delayed CT scan).

audits.t: [The treatment of osteodystrophy in dialyzed uremic patients: results of the first Sardinian audit].
audits.tp: Management of renal osteodystrophy in dialysis patients
audits.st: National and international guidelines for optimal management of renal osteodystrophy (phosphate, PTH, calcium, aluminium targets)
audits.f: Good control of average phosphorus; a worrying proportion of patients had PTH levels compatible with adynamic bone disease; poor aluminium control; low parathyroidectomy incidence (1.8%).

audits.t: Home enteral feeding audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Delayed first deliveries (>=7 days) 47%; equipment missing from first delivery 41%; difficulty obtaining GP prescription 17%; changed equipment with minimal training 26%.

audits.t: An audit of the process of developing the Health Improvement Programme into Strategic and Financial Framework in two health authorities.
audits.tp: Health needs to commissioning consistency (HImP to SaFF)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Needs identified in Health Improvement Programmes (HImPs) were not fully reflected in the service provision described in the final Strategic and Financial Frameworks (SaFFs); HImP priorities disappeared and non-HImP priorities appeared in the SaFF.

audits.t: Blood usage in elective surgery--a 3-month audit at Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town.
audits.st: Maximum Surgical Blood Ordering Schedule (MSBOS)
audits.f: Just over half of blood bank requests were within the MSBOS; overall crossmatch-transfusion ratio 1.7 (range 1.4 in cardiac surgery to 4.7 in neurosurgery); 29% of postoperative transfusions considered excessive.

audits.t: An audit of training in public health medicine.
audits.st: Guidelines set by the Education Committee of the Faculty of Public Health Medicine
audits.f: Several weaknesses in training were identified by the Trainee Members Committee; no numerical results reported in the abstract.

audits.t: Audit of pre-employment health assessment in the National Health Service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 17/22 (77%) departments replied; only 5/17 (29%) based interview/examination decision on a self-administered questionnaire; interview-all departments had higher rejection/restriction rate (6/232, 2.6%) than selective departments (16/1140, 1.4%), RR 1.6, 95% CI 0.8-3.4, p=0.31; median proportion seen by nurses 56%, by doctors 12% where not automatically interviewed.

audits.t: National audit of incontinence surgery in the United Kingdom.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 54% response rate; large variations found in role of surgeon, operation numbers/type, use of urodynamics and physiotherapy pre-operatively, complications, and follow-up length/method.

audits.t: Audit of the detection and notification of meningococcal disease at a North London university district hospital.
audits.tp: Meningococcal disease notification and sample completeness
audits.st: All four readily obtainable samples (blood culture, EDTA blood, throat swab, acute serum) recommended in suspected meningococcal disease
audits.f: 18/36 notifications confirmed as bacterial (mostly meningococcal meningitis); all four sample types obtained in only 2 cases.
audits.c: A single form requesting all four samples in suspected meningococcal disease cases is recommended; out-of-hours notification to public health specialists could be rationalised.

audits.t: Prospective audit of deaths at a teaching hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 8/58 head-injury-related trauma unit deaths and 1/76 emergency unit deaths were certified brain dead and referred, though 5/7 relevant neurosurgical ICU deaths were referred.

audits.t: Audits of radiopharmaceutical formulations.
audits.st: FDA guidelines for radiopharmaceutical identity, strength, quality, purity, sterility
audits.f: Problems identified across audits included lack of sterility/apyrogenicity testing, non-pharmaceutical-grade chemicals, and inadequate quality control records; no numeric compliance rate is given.

audits.t: Adult tetanus in Accra, why the high mortality? An audit of clinical management of tetanus.
audits.st: Expected tetanus treatment actions (wound debridement, antibiotics, immunoglobulin)
audits.f: Case fatality rate varied from 25% (1999) to 72.7% (2001); case fatality rose when expected treatment actions (debridement, antibiotics/immunoglobulin) were not performed; most patients were not treated with immunoglobulin and antibiotics.

audits.t: Access inequalities addressed by audit.
audits.st: Disability Discrimination Act (1995) requirements for access to services
audits.f: Many access problems identified by a simple access audit.
audits.c: Access improvements implemented, costing approximately GBP 100,000, plus changes in staff attitudes and practices
audits.r2: Considerable improvements had been made; no quantified re-audit figures reported.

audits.t: Quality of interhospital transport of critically ill patients: a prospective audit.
audits.tp: Quality of interhospital critical care transport
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 34% of transfers had adverse events, in 50% of these pretransport recommendations were ignored; ICU mortality 27%; 37% had more abnormal vital variables on arrival than departure

audits.t: An audit of the use of magnesium sulphate in severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia.
audits.tp: Magnesium sulphate use in pre-eclampsia and eclampsia
audits.st: Hospital protocol for MgSO4 use in severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, including recommended monitoring of serum levels
audits.f: Patient selection appropriate in all cases; correct loading dose given in all cases; serum MgSO4 levels recorded in only 30/50 (60%); no seizures in treated group; 72% (36) delivered by caesarean section; mean birth weight 2.54 kg.

audits.t: Audit of local performance compared with standards recommended by the national guidelines for aetiologic investigation of permanent childhood hearing impairment.
audits.tp: Aetiological investigation of childhood hearing impairment
audits.st: National guidelines for aetiologic investigation of permanent childhood hearing impairment (Newborn Hearing Screening Programme)
audits.f: For bilateral severe-profound deafness: imaging accepted in 53.0%, declined 5.9%, not offered 41.2%; ECG accepted 47.1%, declined 52.9%; connexin testing accepted 70.6%, declined 29.4%; ophthalmic referral accepted 63.8%, declined 17.0%, not offered 19.1%; genetics referral accepted 46.8%, declined 44.7%, not offered 8.5%.

audits.t: Auditing the clinical learning environment in West Glamorgan: evaluating the process.
audits.tp: Evaluation of a clinical learning environment audit tool
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Ward/area managers identified a range of benefits from using the new audit tool, and accepted the need to maintain standards; no quantified compliance figures reported.

audits.t: An audit of fresh frozen plasma usage in a tertiary referral centre in a developing country.
audits.st: Clinical indication criteria for appropriate FFP transfusion
audits.f: Overall 40% of units transfused were appropriate; only 31% of transfusion episodes were for appropriate indications; inappropriate use highest in surgical services (68%) and orthopaedics (64%), lowest in paediatrics (40%).

audits.t: Quality of training in public health in the UK: results of the first national training audit.
audits.st: 75 standards for public health specialist training covering induction (30), health protection (13) and general training (32); benchmark of meeting >=80% of respondents for a standard
audits.f: 62% response rate; only 16/75 standards (21%) met by at least 80% of respondents, with problems in induction, health protection, secretarial facilities and exam support; across 10 key standards, 59% of trainees indicated their training met at least 8/10; deaneries with specialists scored lower (median 8 vs 9, p=0.003); results differed significantly between deaneries (p=0.02).

audits.t: Audit of intrapartum group B streptococcus prophylaxis.
audits.tp: Group B streptococcus intrapartum prophylaxis adequacy
audits.st: Established risk-factor-based protocol for intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis; adequacy defined as antibiotics given more than 4 hours before delivery (protocol), with RCOG guidance suggesting a 2-hour threshold
audits.f: 44/396 (11%) women eligible for prophylaxis; adequate prophylaxis (4h threshold) achieved in 21/44 (49%).

audits.t: Audit of specialist registrar training in tympanomastoid surgery for chronic otitis media.
audits.tp: ENT trainee surgical experience and outcomes in tympanomastoid surgery
audits.st: Minimum otology dataset-based proforma with SR operative contribution graded per England Royal College of Surgeons guidelines
audits.f: 409 form-ones and 156 form-twos analysed; SR contribution to procedures increased with training year without significant effect on graded outcome ('gold'/other), which was independent of SR training year; SR results comparable to consultant-performed procedures.

audits.t: Providing guidelines and education is not enough: an audit of gentamicin use at The Royal Melbourne Hospital.
audits.st: Existing hospital aminoglycoside dosing and therapeutic monitoring guidelines
audits.f: 66% of initial gentamicin dosing was not in accordance with hospital guidelines; of courses requiring therapeutic drug monitoring (77% received it), only 8.8% were monitored according to guidelines.

audits.t: Using peer audit in health visiting.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Smoking cessation and health inequality: an equity audit.
audits.st: National average 52-week quit rate of 15%
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Home enteral feeding audit 1 year post-initiation.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Sleep disturbance 75%; frequent tube dislodgement 46%; tube blockages 41%; inability of some home delivery companies to provide all paediatric special feeds required 43%; pump inaccuracy 23%.

audits.t: An audit of electroencephalography requests: use and misuse.
audits.st: Clinical guideline recommendations for EEG referral; target wait of 4 weeks
audits.f: 50 sets of notes from 90 eligible patients reviewed; 26% of requests considered inappropriate (92% of these for 'funny turns'); EEG contributed to diagnosis/management in only 22% of cases (all appropriately requested); 42% of all patients, and <10% of outpatients, had EEG within the 4-week guideline target.

audits.t: Implementation of neuroreflexotherapy for subacute and chronic neck and back pain within the Spanish public health system: audit results after one year.
audits.st: Referral protocol for neuroreflexotherapy (NRT) for non-specific back/neck pain
audits.f: Appropriate referral rate 95.5%; pain score (VAS) fell from median 8 to 1, referred pain 7 to 1, disability (Roland-Morris) 12 to 1; NRT refused by 2.7%, skin reaction in 3.3%

audits.t: Treating claudication in 5 words (stop smoking and keep walking) is no longer enough: an audit of risk factor management in patients prescribed exercise therapy in New Zealand.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Documentation of risk factors by referrers: antiplatelet 40/60, hypertension 48/60, hyperlipidaemia 39/60, smoking 40/60, diabetes 37/60, CAD 38/60; vascular surgeons attempted modification of risk factors in 12 (antiplatelet), 11 (lipid), 10 (smoking) of 58 patients seen

audits.t: [Audit of the quality of treatment of "near miss" patients in referral maternities in Southern Benin].
audits.st: WHO Guidelines for Monitoring Emergency Obstetric Care (EOC); timely care defined as within 30-60 minutes depending on intervention
audits.f: Immediate emergency care given within 30 minutes for 61% of patients; caesarean section started within 60 minutes for 42-45%; blood transfusion within 60 minutes in only 10% of anaemic near-miss cases; overall EOC quality good in only 16.4% of cases

audits.t: An audit of influenza vaccination rates.
audits.st: National influenza vaccination rate for patients aged 65 and over (national rate 79% in 2004)
audits.f: Influenza vaccination rate 77% among patients aged 65 and over
audits.c: Computer search to identify target population; telephone recruitment and booking by receptionist; removal of cost by bulk billing; nurse-led immunisation
audits.r2: Vaccination rate increased to 83%; refusal rate 10%

audits.t: Audit of nutritional advice given to bone marrow transplant patients in the United Kingdom and Eire.
audits.tp: Nutritional advice for bone marrow transplant patients
audits.st: Compared current advice with published literature recommendations for nutritional care of BMT patients
audits.f: 75% response rate; wide variation in dietary advice, catering practices, anthropometry and nutritional support given to BMT patients.

audits.t: Re-audit of clients from ethnic and local communities in Greater Manchester attending St. Mary's Sexual Assault Referral Centre.
audits.tp: Recording of ethnicity, residence and assault type at sexual assault referral centre
audits.st: Local recording standards for client ethnicity, area of residence and assault type
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Staff training following the initial audit
audits.r2: Recording of ethnicity improved considerably; recording of area of residence slipped just below standard; recording of assault type dropped markedly

audits.t: Cost savings and quality improvement--single-use suture instruments?
audits.tp: Quality and cost-effectiveness of single-use suture instrument kits
audits.st: Local standard for satisfactory quality of suturing instruments
audits.f: Audit of established practice showed numerous problems with traditional suture kits (breaking or unsuitable instruments)
audits.c: Trial and introduction of single-use suture kits
audits.r2: Repeat audit demonstrated no identifiable problem with the new suture kits

audits.t: Audit of perinatal deaths in a tertiary level hospital in Latvia (1995-1999) using the Nordic-Baltic perinatal death classification: evidence of suboptimal care.
audits.st: Nordic-Baltic Perinatal Death (PND) classification
audits.f: Perinatal mortality rate did not decline over the study period; classification used to assess preventability of deaths

audits.t: Developing audit standards required for outbreaks of communicable diseases-lessons from a mumps outbreak.
audits.st: Audit standards developed from the memorandum of understanding between the NHS and Health Protection Agency (no pre-existing comprehensive standards for outbreak audits were found)
audits.f: Audit identified improvement areas including training, strategic co-ordination, inter-organisational communication, and consistency/timeliness of communication.

audits.t: An audit of the management of patients with acute pancreatitis against national standards of practice.
audits.tp: Acute pancreatitis management against national standards
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology guideline standards: overall mortality <10%, SAP mortality <30%, diagnosis/severity stratification within 48h, aetiology determined in >80%, CT/HDU-ITU availability, definitive treatment of gallstone pancreatitis within 2 weeks
audits.f: 219/759 (28.9%) had severe acute pancreatitis (SAP); overall mortality 5.9%, SAP mortality 19.6%; diagnosed within 48h in 96.3%; aetiology classified in 87.5%; 95.9% of SAP patients had CT within 6-10 days; 48% of 93 severe gallstone pancreatitis patients had urgent ERCP; 89.6% of 359 gallstone pancreatitis patients had definitive management within 2 weeks.

audits.t: Audit of peripheral venous cannulae by members of an i.v. therapy forum.
audits.st: RCN 'Standards for Infusion Therapy' and Department of Health 'Winning Ways' report action area 2
audits.f: Poor documentation of cannula insertion; the person who performed the cannulation could not be identified for 236 (37.7%) of PVCs audited
audits.c: not reported (draft recommendations proposed, feedback sought)

audits.t: Yorkshire regional audit of hepatitis B vaccination.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B vaccination uptake in GUM clinics
audits.st: Targets set by the National Strategy for Sexual Health and HIV (NSSHHIV) for offer and uptake of hepatitis B vaccination in men who have sex with men
audits.f: 226/254 (93%) eligible cases offered vaccination, only 187/254 (77%) offered at first visit; first dose uptake 83% MSM, 56% IDU, 82% CSW; of 193 who started vaccination, third dose uptake 49% MSM, 29% IDU, 24% CSW; super-accelerated course most commonly prescribed but standard/accelerated regimens produced higher antibody titres (>10 IU/L).

audits.t: Justifying the clinical use of fresh frozen plasma - an audit.
audits.st: British Committee for Standards in Haematology (BCSH) guidelines for FFP use
audits.f: 66.12% of FFP units transfused appropriately; 33.88% transfused inappropriately per BCSH guidelines

audits.t: Suboptimal care in stillbirths - a retrospective audit study.
audits.st: Perinatal audit classification of optimal/sub-optimal care factors
audits.f: Sub-optimal care factors identified in 37% of stillbirths; non-western women had increased risk of stillbirth (OR 2.2, 95% CI 1.3-3.8) and of sub-optimal care (OR 2.4, 95% CI 1.5-3.9)

audits.t: An audit and trends of perinatal mortality at the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, Karachi.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Perinatal mortality rate 97.2/1000 total births; stillbirth rate 73.4/1000

audits.t: How intravenous immunoglobulin is used in clinical practice: audits of two Sydney teaching hospitals.
audits.st: Australian Health Ministers' Advisory Council (AHMAC) 2000 guidelines for approved indications for IVIg
audits.f: 165 recipients received 24,251 g of IVIg (mean 147 g/patient) for 36 diagnoses, 5.5% mortality; drug committees supplied 1580 g (6.5%) to 12 recipients (7.3%); immunology/haematology/neurology accounted for 92.9% of use, 51.8% for replacement indications; 42 patients (25.5%, 4718 g/19.5% of product) received IVIg for non-category 1 indications; 94.4% compliance with guideline prerequisites for category 1 indications where assessable.

audits.t: Clinical audit: optimal positioning of endotracheal tubes in neonates.
audits.st: Local standard: endotracheal tube in satisfactory position in >80% of cases
audits.f: 73% of endotracheal tubes had a satisfactory position
audits.c: Implementation of nasal-tragus length (NTL) as a consistent predictor method for insertional length
audits.r2: 94% of endotracheal tubes had a satisfactory position, meeting the standard

audits.t: Ensuring accurate oral mucositis assessment in the European Group for Blood and Marrow Transplantation Prospective Oral Mucositis Audit.
audits.st: World Health Organization (WHO) Oral Toxicity Scale used to standardise oral mucositis (OM) assessment across centres
audits.f: First quality control analysis of 82 worksheets showed nurse assessment accuracy of 74%; most common errors were assigning WHO grade 0 or 1.
audits.c: 22 trainers received comprehensive training and educated staff at the 25 transplant centres about OM assessment using the WHO Oral Toxicity Scale.
audits.r2: Subsequent quality control analyses of 1949 and 4111 worksheets showed nurse assessment accuracy of 90% and 90% respectively.

audits.t: Assessment of kindergarten immunization rates in Colorado: school self-reports vs. health department audits, 2004-2005.
audits.st: Colorado kindergarten entry vaccination requirements
audits.f: Audit found 76.3% (95% CI 73.2-79.4) of kindergarteners received all required vaccines, versus 89.4% estimated from school self-report

audits.t: The South West Thames Regional Health Authority approach to the method of audit in public health medicine.
audits.tp: Framework for audit in public health medicine
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Avoidability of maternal death in Mozambique: audit and retrospective risk assessment in 106 consecutive cases.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Maternal mortality rate 340 per 100,000 live births; causes: haemorrhage 31%, hypertensive disease 15%, puerperal sepsis 12%, septic abortion 9%; approximately 40% of deaths judged avoidable with existing resources

audits.t: Quality assurance audits of medical surveillance programs for hazardous waste workers.
audits.tp: Medical surveillance quality audit for hazardous waste workers
audits.st: OSHA Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response Regulation (29 CFR 1910.120)
audits.f: Required paperwork (fitness for duty, restrictions) mostly completed, but many components of occupational history not performed; spirometric examinations often performed incorrectly; documentation of baseline tests not uniform

audits.t: Setting standards in homeopathic practice--a pre-audit exploring motivation and expectation for patients attending the Bristol Homeopathic Hospital.
audits.tp: Patient motivation and expectations at a homeopathic hospital (pre-audit)
audits.st: not reported (standard being set as a result of this pre-audit)
audits.f: 70% had used complementary and alternative medicine; only 10% had specialist homeopathic care

audits.t: Ethnic differences in perinatal mortality. A perinatal audit on the role of substandard care.
audits.tp: Perinatal mortality substandard care audit (ethnic differences)
audits.st: Standardised perinatal audit procedure for classifying substandard care
audits.f: Substandard care prevalence differed significantly by ethnic group (p=0.034), highest among Surinamese mothers; perinatal mortality 4.01% Surinamese vs 1.07% native Dutch mothers

audits.t: Selective immunisation strategy to protect newborns at risk for transmission of hepatitis B: retrospective audit of vaccine uptake.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B selective immunisation vaccine uptake audit
audits.st: Proposed vaccination schedule for neonates at risk of perinatal HBV (immunoglobulin plus active vaccine at 0, 1 and 6 months)
audits.f: Immunisation started in 94% of infants (78% within 24 hours); only 54% of at-risk infants immunised fully correctly per schedule

audits.t: Severe allergy: an audit and service review.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Deficiencies found in allergy management relating to assessment, diagnosis, medication provision, education, support and ongoing follow-up for children carrying epipens.
audits.c: Development of a paediatric allergy clinic and a multi-professional collaborative approach to care in response to the audit findings.

audits.t: Risk of malnutrition in a sample of acute and long-stay NHS Fife in-patients: an audit.
audits.tp: Malnutrition risk screening in hospital inpatients
audits.st: Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST) and Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN) standards for food and fluids
audits.f: Minimum risk of malnutrition varied from 14 to 25% depending on the standard used; 42% of patients had a BMI >25; mean weight change from admission to audit was +0.4 kg (range -11 to +13 kg); most malnourished patients were referred to a dietitian or given nutritional support.

audits.t: Audit of health promotion practice within a UK hospital: results of a pilot study.
audits.st: UK public health policy requiring hospitals to screen for and address modifiable risk factors (smoking, alcohol, diet, exercise, obesity)
audits.f: 88% of inpatients asked about smoking, 74% about alcohol, but only 18% screened for obesity, 5% asked about diet and 3% about physical activity; health promotion delivered to a third of smokers and over half of those reporting alcohol misuse; only 3 inpatients screened for all risk factors.

audits.t: Avoidable risk factors in perinatal deaths: a perinatal audit in South Australia.
audits.tp: Perinatal death avoidable risk factor audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 44.4% of perinatal deaths had an avoidable maternal risk factor; 11.2% were associated with deficiencies in professional care; commonest deficiency was failure to act on/recognise high-risk pregnancy (8.1%)

audits.t: A 15-year audit of home parenteral nutrition provision at the John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford.
audits.tp: Home parenteral nutrition provision and complications
audits.st: Comparison with published outcome/complication rate data from other home parenteral nutrition (HPN) centres and designated intestinal failure units
audits.f: 121 patient-years (median duration 217.8 days); line sepsis 0.35 episodes/patient-year, line occlusion 0.25, subacute bacterial endocarditis 0.02, cholestasis 0.17, central venous thrombosis 0.03; all within the range of published data.

audits.t: Are patients with familial hypercholesterolaemia well managed in lipid clinics? An audit of eleven clinics from the Department of Health Familial Hypercholesterolaemia Cascade Testing project.
audits.tp: Familial hypercholesterolaemia management in lipid clinics
audits.st: UK 'Simon Broome' register diagnostic criteria for familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH), and appropriate advice/treatment and family tracing
audits.f: 79% met Simon Broome criteria for definite/possible FH; 89% on a statin; family pedigree recorded in notes ranged 1-71% (mean 35%) between sites; GP advised to test first-degree relatives in 4-52% (mean 27%); relatives contacted and tested in 6-50% (mean 32%).

audits.t: Provision of medical and community services to people with severe arthritis; an audit.
audits.tp: Community services provision for severe arthritis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Patients with RA were referred to hospital far more often than those with OA (only half of OA patients referred); provision of social services/community OT was greater for those seen in hospital; a substantial minority with severe OA had not been considered for joint replacement or had suboptimal provision of aids and adaptations.

audits.t: Quality audit programme for (99m)Tc and (131)I radioactivity measurements with radionuclide calibrators.
audits.st: Activity measurement accuracy within +/-10% window
audits.f: 94% of centres were within +/-10% for 131I activity measurement; for 99mTc, 1 of 10 centres deviated by more than +/-10%

audits.t: National comparative audit of the use of platelet transfusions in the UK.
audits.st: Audit standards developed from national guidelines for platelet transfusion (documented reason for transfusion, platelet count checked pre-transfusion, appropriate thresholds)
audits.f: 3726/4421 (84%) transfusions evaluable; 1601/3726 (43%) non-compliant with audit standards; reason documented in 93%; platelet count not measured pre-transfusion in 29%; threshold >10x10^9/L used for 60% of prophylactic haematology transfusions without risk factors; threshold >30x10^9/L used for 59% of prophylactic critical care transfusions; platelet transfusion given without bleeding in 11% of cardiac surgery patients.
audits.c: Recommended written local guidelines for platelet transfusion and clinician training about appropriate use; audit to be repeated in about three years.

audits.t: Design and evaluation of a regional perinatal audit.
audits.tp: Regional perinatal audit design and evaluation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Substandard care factors present in 25% of all perinatal death cases; 35% after 23 completed weeks; 52% of intrapartum deaths

audits.t: [Audit of the prehospital management of severe head injured patients in the "Pays-de-la-Loire" region].
audits.tp: Prehospital severe head injury management audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Field medical care 54+/-28 min; transport 32+/-29 min; total time to hospital 1h55+/-48min; direct admission to a centre with on-site neurosurgery 68%; mortality before 24th hour 23%

audits.t: UK audit of glomerular filtration rate measurement in 2001.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall root median square (RMedS) variability was 5.8 ml/min/1.73m2 for normalised data, decreasing to 0.6 ml/min/1.73m2 when centres were grouped by analysis method; variability was mainly due to different methods of analysis.

audits.t: Audit into blood-borne virus services in Her Majesty's Prison Service.
audits.tp: Blood-borne virus testing and treatment access in prison
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Almost a quarter of arrivals had contact with blood-borne virus (BBV) services; 75.4% reported IV drug use history; 20% of these declined testing; average time from imprisonment to testing was 86 days (halved since October 2006); 50% positive for hepatitis C antibody, 83.3% of these had active virus; average 38 days from testing to referral; all tested for HIV were negative.

audits.t: Basics in advanced life support: a role for download audit and metronomes.
audits.st: 2005 Resuscitation Guidelines emphasis on chest compressions, monitored via electronic ECG/CPR download analysis
audits.f: Deficiencies in the standard of basic life support were identified, though not unique to this service.
audits.c: Introduction of metronomes and provision of feedback to ambulance crews based on download audit.
audits.r2: Major improvements in basic life support performance following introduction of metronomes and crew feedback (no numeric data reported).

audits.t: Picture archiving and communication systems lead to sustained improvements in reporting times and productivity: results of a 5-year audit.
audits.tp: Radiology reporting turnaround time and productivity
audits.st: Internal baseline reporting time and productivity metrics compared before and after PACS installation
audits.f: Baseline reporting time: plain radiographs 6.8 days, specialist modalities (CT/MRI/ultrasound/nuclear medicine) 4.1 days; patient episodes 11,531/month; 32 whole-time-equivalent (WTE) reporting radiologists.
audits.c: Introduction of picture archiving and communication system (PACS) and digital dictation.
audits.r2: Plain radiograph reporting time decreased 26% (6.8 to 5 days, p=0.002); specialty modality reporting time decreased 24% (4.1 to 3.1 days); productivity improved 18%; patient episodes increased 30% to 15,057/month with WTE radiologists up 15% to 37.

audits.t: Two year audit of perinatal mortality at Kathmandu Medical College Teaching Hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Perinatal mortality rate 30.7/1000; extended perinatal mortality rate 47.9/1000
audits.c: Improvements in care of mothers and newborns; standard perinatal death audit forms used
audits.r2: Significant reduction in perinatal mortality rate compared with the earlier one-year study, despite increased births

audits.t: Physical interventions to manage patients with brain injury: an audit on its use and staff and patient injuries from the techniques.
audits.tp: Physical intervention use and injury rates in brain injury unit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Physical interventions (PI) used on 1427 occasions; 90.1% lasted less than 10 minutes; patient injury rate 0.98%; staff injury rate 6.5%, both considerably lower than rates reported for other clinical populations.

audits.t: Departmental audit of malaria control programme 2001-2005 north west frontier province (NWFP).
audits.st: Roll Back Malaria (RBM) initiative strategy targets
audits.f: Budget fell from Rs 5.043 million (2002) to Rs 3.3 million (2005); slides examined increased 62% from 2001 to 2005; annual parasite incidence peaked at 3.01-3.57/1000 in 2002-2003 then fell to 2.01/1000 in 2005 (double the 2001 rate of 1.09/1000)

audits.t: Improvement in the management of acutely poisoned patients using an electronic database, prospective audit and targeted educational intervention.
audits.tp: Acute poisoning patient assessment and management quality
audits.st: Predefined criteria for clinical assessment and management of acutely poisoned patients, derived from identified shortfalls
audits.f: 77.6% of poisoned-patient presentations had clinical management graded as 'good'.
audits.c: Bimonthly audit meetings; targeted educational lectures and case-based clinical scenarios; weekly case-based anonymised electronic feedback reports sent to ED staff caring for poisoned patients.
audits.r2: Proportion of presentations graded as 'good' management significantly increased to 89.4%.

audits.t: An audit of vaccination coverage among vaccination service workers in Puglia, Italy.
audits.st: Recommended vaccinations for healthcare workers (hepatitis B, influenza, varicella, MMR)
audits.f: 54.5% had received hepatitis B vaccine and 32.7% influenza vaccine (2007-08 season); 4.6% susceptible to varicella (2.6% vaccinated); 9.3% susceptible to measles/mumps/rubella (5.9% vaccinated)

audits.t: Maternal mortality: an autopsy audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Maternal mortality rate 1133/100,000 live births; acute fulminant viral hepatitis was the commonest indirect cause of death (41.5%); pregnancy-induced hypertension 13.4%; puerperal sepsis 11.2%

audits.t: Audit from preschool developmental surveillance of vision, hearing, and language referrals.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median waiting time for appointment: ophthalmology 46 days, audiology 175 days, speech therapy 83 days; poorest attendance rate in speech therapy (75%); approximately 60% of ophthalmology referrals were justified and 20% had a clear defect; 55% of audiology referrals had altered impedance or hearing impairment (only half of those under review improved spontaneously); 80% of speech therapy assessments found a language problem.

audits.t: An audit of competency assessments on court-referred rape survivors in South Africa.
audits.tp: Forensic competency assessment audit for rape survivors with intellectual disability
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 91.5% female, 21.7% under 16 years old; ~80% classified with moderate or severe mental retardation; over 90% were judged able to testify; almost two-thirds unable to make an informed decision to consent to sexual intercourse

audits.t: Interhospital transport audit criteria for helicopter emergency medical services.
audits.st: Nationally established criteria for medically appropriate helicopter interhospital transport
audits.f: 97% (1792/1839) of interhospital transfers judged justified for helicopter transport per national criteria

audits.t: UK National Audit of Sexual History-taking: case-notes audit.
audits.st: National guidelines for sexual history-taking in genitourinary medicine clinics
audits.f: A high proportion of case-notes were completely legible; considerable inter-regional variation in adherence to national guidelines, particularly for documentation of discussing condom use, HIV risk assessment, offer of a chaperone, assessment for hepatitis B vaccination and hepatitis C testing, and sexual contact issues (percentages not given in this abstract).

audits.t: Perinatal audit using the 3-delays model in western Tanzania.
audits.st: 3-delays model methodology
audits.f: Perinatal mortality rate 38/1000; first delay occurred in 19.0% of cases, second delay in 21.5%, third delay in 72.5%; leading causes birth asphyxia (19.0%) and prolonged/obstructed labour (18.5%)

audits.t: Decreasing trends in malnutrition prevalence rates explained by regular audits and feedback.
audits.st: Dutch National Prevalence Measurement of Care Problems (LPZ) malnutrition indicators
audits.f: Malnutrition prevalence rates in 2004 formed the baseline of a decreasing trend to 2007 in hospitals and home care; rates remained stable in nursing homes
audits.c: Annual multicentre audit and feedback from the national LPZ measurement; participation in national improvement programmes
audits.r2: More frequent LPZ audit participation was associated with lower malnutrition prevalence (P<0.001); participation in national improvement programmes also reduced prevalence (P=0.027)

audits.t: Audit of post-exposure treatment to prevent lyssavirus infection in Sydney South West Area Health Service, 2005-2007.
audits.st: NSW Health post-exposure prophylaxis protocol for lyssavirus
audits.f: 76% of potential exposures occurred overseas; all people who commenced post-exposure treatment completed the prescribed course, but often not within the stipulated timeframe

audits.t: Multi-modality blood conservation strategy in open-heart surgery: an audit.
audits.tp: Blood conservation strategy audit in cardiac surgery
audits.st: In-house blood conservation protocol for open-heart surgery
audits.f: 82.6% (256) did not receive any blood or blood products; 17.4% (54) received one or more units of allogenic transfusion; mean discharge haemoglobin 9.8 g% (8.9-12 g%)

audits.t: Audit of well-baby care in primary health care centers in Buraidah, Saudi Arabia.
audits.tp: Well-baby care documentation and utilisation audit
audits.st: Quality Assurance and Maternal and Child Health Care Manual, Saudi Ministry of Health
audits.f: Pregnancy/delivery history available in >90%; neonatal history in 74.3%; nutritional status in 96.3% (breastfeeding duration recorded in only 37.8%); growth charts completed in >90%; >90% of infants attended well-baby clinic visits but under one-third of toddlers did; all completed the first-year EPI schedule and >75% were age-appropriately immunised

audits.t: An audit of health education services within UK hospitals.
audits.st: Standards: 100% of hospitalised patients screened for smoking, alcohol use and obesity; 70% of smokers offered smoking-cessation health education; 50% of patients identified as misusing alcohol, obese, eating unhealthily or physically inactive offered appropriate health education
audits.f: 4/9 hospitals screened all patients for smoking; none met standards for screening alcohol or obesity; all hospitals met the standard for diet education, 4/9 for alcohol misuse education and 4/9 for physical activity education; none met standards for smoking or obesity education delivery.

audits.t: The German NET-registry: an audit on the diagnosis and therapy of neuroendocrine tumors.
audits.st: Proposed guidelines for neuroendocrine tumour (NET) diagnosis and management
audits.f: Imaging available for 79% of patients; specific laboratory tests for 67%; somatostatin receptor scintigraphy for 56%; pathology findings for 79%; high-quality pathology reports rare (2%)

audits.t: Facility-based audit of maternal mortality in Lebanon: a feasibility study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Maternal mortality rate 39/100,000 live births; 55 pregnancy-related deaths per 100,000 live births

audits.t: Prescription auditing of griseofulvin in a tertiary care teaching hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 64.20% of patients had complete cure following griseofulvin treatment; most common adverse drug reaction was headache (5.83%); quality of life score improved significantly

audits.t: The online outpatient booking system 'Choose and Book' improves attendance rates at an audiology clinic: a comparative audit.
audits.tp: Outpatient booking system effect on attendance (Choose and Book)
audits.st: Comparative internal benchmark of new patient attendance rate: Choose and Book online booking versus traditional booking system
audits.f: Traditional booking system patients had a lower attendance rate than the Choose and Book group (comparator).
audits.c: Introduction and use of the online 'Choose and Book' outpatient booking system for new patient appointments.
audits.r2: Choose and Book patients had a significantly better attendance rate than traditional appointment patients (95% CI -3.0 to 16.2%); Choose and Book patients were significantly older than traditional appointment patients.

audits.t: Audit of hospital transfers January to March 2006 from Sussex police custody.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 188 patients (1.57%) identified as requiring hospital assessment; 80 cases (0.65%) for potentially life-threatening conditions; health care team assessed 37.7% of detainees and were involved in 151/188 (80%) transfers; categories included head injury 13.8%, overdose/poisoning 10.6%, chest pain 9.0%, collapse 6.4%, unrousable intoxication 5.3%.

audits.t: Audit of a new appointments system in a hospital outpatient clinic.
audits.tp: Outpatient appointment system and waiting time
audits.st: Internal target of reducing patient waiting time via a needs-based appointment system replacing fixed 10-minute-interval appointments
audits.f: Mean waiting time 39.6 minutes.
audits.c: Replacement of a fixed 10-minute-interval appointment system with one in which the doctor arranged appointments according to individual patient requirements (December 1988 to June 1989).
audits.r2: Mean waiting time reduced to 9.5 minutes (about 30 minutes less); no change in number of patients attending (mean 15.8 vs 15.4) or clinic duration (mean 187 vs 160 minutes).

audits.t: An audit of TB prevention on Italian health care workers.
audits.tp: Tuberculosis prevention audit among healthcare workers
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: TB screening had been undergone by 80.5% of respondents (78.6% advised by occupational health physician); of those PPD-negative, 60.6% had received BCG vaccination

audits.t: Documentation of preventive screening interventions by general practitioners: a retrospective chart audit.
audits.st: Canadian Task Force on Preventive Health Care, American College of Physicians and Canadian Cancer Society screening recommendations
audits.f: Documentation of preventive interventions ranged from 40.3% (cholesterol) to 0.9% (pneumococcal vaccination) within 1 year, and 67.4% to 1.8% within 3 years

audits.t: The audit process: Part I. Pre-audit preparation.
audits.tp: Infection prevention and control audit preparation process
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Uptake of the Perinatal Society of Australia and New Zealand perinatal mortality audit guideline.
audits.tp: Perinatal mortality audit guideline uptake survey
audits.st: Perinatal Society of Australia and New Zealand (PSANZ) perinatal mortality clinical practice guideline (2004)
audits.f: Only 42% of clinicians were aware of the guideline (53% midwives vs 28% doctors); 19% had received training in its use; 33% reported never referring to it; 70% regularly attended perinatal mortality audit meetings but 45% never received feedback from these meetings

audits.t: Utilizing audit and feedback to improve hospitalists' performance in tobacco dependence counseling.
audits.tp: Tobacco dependence counselling audit and feedback
audits.st: not reported (internal counselling and NRT prescribing practice expectations)
audits.f: Documentation of tobacco dependence counselling in progress notes 36%; in discharge summaries 7.5%
audits.c: Peer-led audit and feedback with one-on-one academic detailing on counselling and NRT prescribing practices, plus education
audits.r2: Documentation of counselling in progress notes increased to 44% (p=.002); in discharge summaries increased to 46.8%

audits.t: Pre-hospital intubation by anaesthesiologists in patients with severe trauma: an audit of a Norwegian helicopter emergency medical service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 238/240 successful pre-hospital intubation attempts (99.2% success rate); 47 patients (16% of intubated) were intubated only on arrival in the emergency department

audits.t: Communication skills in HPV prevention: an audit among Italian healthcare workers.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 74.2% judged the HPV vaccine very important for the immunisation calendar; 88.9% did not believe vaccination implies consent to sexual activity; 62.2% believed boys should also be vaccinated

audits.t: Delays in discharge of vascular surgical patients: a prospective audit.
audits.st: Expected/planned discharge date and time set by the clinical team
audits.f: 47% discharged on the planned day and time; 21% on the planned day but later than predicted; 32% delayed by more than 1 day, accounting for 135 of 729 total bed days; 85% of delays due to external factors such as lack of rehabilitation/placement beds

audits.t: Audits of adolescent prenatal care rendered in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe.
audits.st: Expected prenatal care activities checklist (history taking, health education/counselling, physical examination, laboratory tests, client evaluation, birth planning)
audits.f: Recorded prenatal care was incomplete, especially regarding health promotion and social history aspects

audits.t: Measuring how well the NHS looks after its own staff: methodology of the first national clinical audits of occupational health services in the NHS.
audits.tp: Occupational health clinical audit for depression and back pain (methodology)
audits.st: Audit criteria for depression and back pain case management in occupational health, developed for the first national clinical audits of NHS occupational health services
audits.f: Sites submitted up to 40 cases per audit; median kappa scores above 0.7 for both pilot and full audits (good inter-rater reliability); 79% of dissemination conference participants said they had changed clinical practice, either during data collection (52%) or after receiving results (27%).

audits.t: IBD care in Europe: A comparative audit of the inpatient management of Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis using the national UK IBD audit tool.
audits.tp: IBD inpatient care audit (National UK IBD audit tool)
audits.st: National UK IBD Audit standards (2006 UK IBD Audit)
audits.f: Milan did not meet UK IBD standards for specialist nurse input, dietitian visits, heparin prophylaxis and abdominal radiography in UC; both sites paid little attention to stool cultures, smoking cessation and bone protection
audits.c: Application of the National UK IBD audit tool to compare organisation and process of care across sites
audits.r2: Oxford showed improvements since its own 2006 audit: IBD specialist nurse visits, dietitian visits, fewer active smokers, more stool samples, prophylactic heparin, bone protection and nutritional assessment

audits.t: Ten PM note of organophosphate poisoning: successful outcome of a medical audit with complete seven steps.
audits.tp: Organophosphate poisoning night monitoring note-keeping audit
audits.st: not reported (local standard: regular 10pm notes documenting clinical and drip status)
audits.f: 10pm notes documenting clinical/drip status and communication with nurses/relatives completed in 15.5% of cases
audits.c: Introduction of a formal '10pm note' requirement for residents managing organophosphate poisoning patients

audits.t: Auditing the management of vaccine-preventable disease outbreaks: the need for a tool.
audits.tp: Public health service quality in outbreak management
audits.st: Pilot audit questionnaire with structure, process and results indicators developed by the authors
audits.f: 18 of the indicators had satisfactory mean scores; 'updated guidelines' and 'timely reporting' scored poorly (2.84 and 2.44 respectively); statistically significant differences by outbreak size for availability of updated guidelines (p=0.03) and days needed for control (p=0.04)

audits.t: Prospective audit of perinatal mortality among inborn babies in a tertiary health center in Lagos, Nigeria.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Perinatal mortality rate 84.6/1000

audits.t: Compliance with best practice in oral health: implementing evidence in residential aged care.
audits.tp: Compliance with best practice oral health care in residential aged care
audits.st: Joanna Briggs Institute evidence-based best practice recommendations for oral hygiene care for adults with dementia in residential aged care
audits.f: Compliance achieved in only one of six evidence-based criteria
audits.c: Plan implemented to improve compliance with three of the remaining five criteria over 4 weeks
audits.r2: Improvement in compliance with evidence-based best practice

audits.t: Audit of outcomes from pre-school stammering intervention in a defined catchment population in the west of Ireland.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 97% (61 of 63 with documented fluency status) reported free of stammer at follow-up, exceeding natural recovery rates

audits.t: Perinatal mortality audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Perinatal mortality rate 26.9/1000; 11 stillbirths and 11 early neonatal deaths; 76.5% of perinatal deaths and 100% of early neonatal deaths were low birth weight babies

audits.t: [(No) Fear of audits? Control is good, trust is better. Audits as a core element of quality management].
audits.tp: Role of clinical audits in radiology quality management
audits.st: European Commission guidelines for clinical audits in medical radiology (Council Directive 97/43/EURATOM)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Appropriate seating for medical patients: an audit.
audits.st: Expert panel minimum criteria for appropriate patient seating (functional, occupational health and safety, ergonomic, infection control, usability)
audits.f: 85% (231/270) of chairs did not meet the minimum criteria; only 39 chairs met the criteria, leaving 66% (113) of patients unable to sit out of bed

audits.t: Peer review audit of occupational health reports--process and outcomes.
audits.tp: Occupational health report quality peer review
audits.st: Abbreviated Sheffield Assessment Instrument for Letters (SAIL), Questions 4-12
audits.f: 27% of occupational health reports required modifications: 18% related to typographical/spelling/grammar/administrative errors, and 9% to more complex issues such as unaddressed manager questions or unclear review arrangements/readability.

audits.t: Measles/mumps/rubella vaccine (MMR): an audit of Leeds health professionals' knowledge of contraindications and intention to vaccinate assessed by postal questionnaire.
audits.tp: Health professional knowledge of MMR vaccine contraindications
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Some health professionals would have given MMR vaccine when contraindicated (e.g. to a child on chemotherapy/radiotherapy); a greater proportion would have wrongly withheld MMR when there was no valid contraindication; some incorrectly applied pertussis vaccine contraindications to MMR.

audits.t: An audit of clinical service examining the uptake of genetic testing by at-risk family members.
audits.tp: Genetic testing uptake audit in at-risk family members
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Uptake of genetic testing by at-risk family members ranged from 11% to 18% across four genetic conditions (chromosomal translocations, fragile X, Huntington disease, spinal muscular atrophy)

audits.t: An audit to assess awareness and knowledge of nutrition in a UK spinal cord injuries centre.
audits.tp: Nutrition knowledge in spinal cord injury staff
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 46.5% (62/134) response rate; 83% of staff aware there is a nutrition screening tool; poor knowledge shown of calorie content of IV fluids, malnutrition indicators, and choice of nutritional support; all doctors but only 38% of nurses could calculate BMI; 49% thought at least 20% weight loss indicated malnutrition; median knowledge scores: dietitians 92.8%, doctors 53.5%, nurses 35.7%.

audits.t: Reduction in hospital time to thrombolytic therapy by audit of policy guidelines.
audits.st: Target time to thrombolytic treatment of 15 minutes from hospital admission
audits.f: Unacceptable in-hospital delays to thrombolysis were occurring before the audit (specific baseline time not stated)
audits.c: Paramedic pre-identification of candidates; rapid checklists for inclusion/exclusion criteria in the Accident and Emergency Department; review of reasons for delays greater than 30 minutes
audits.r2: Median time from admission to thrombolysis was 17 minutes overall; the 39 patients treated with APSAC had a median delay of only 13 minutes

audits.t: Quality improvement in travel medicine: a programme for yellow fever vaccination centres in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.
audits.tp: Yellow fever vaccination centre standards compliance
audits.st: National Travel Health Network and Centre (NaTHNaC) registration, training and clinical standards programme, per International Health Regulations 2005
audits.f: Baseline questionnaire prior to the programme highlighted a need for training and institution of standards to reinforce best practice in vaccination and knowledge about yellow fever.
audits.c: NaTHNaC introduced a programme of registration, training, clinical standards and audit for Yellow Fever Vaccination Centres in 2005.
audits.r2: Among respondents who attended NaTHNaC training, 95.8% said it improved their confidence about yellow fever vaccination; 68.5% of centres made changes to their practice; improved adherence to core standards was observed.

audits.t: Meal provision in a UK National Spinal Injury Centre: a qualitative audit of service users and stakeholders.
audits.tp: Meal provision and satisfaction in spinal cord injury centre
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 64% response rate (67 patients) for food intake, 50% response (166 evaluations) for satisfaction; 29/67 (48%) patients consumed 3 full meals a day, 17 (26%) received oral nutritional supplements, 22 (34%) vitamin/mineral supplements, 23 (35%) needed assistance to eat; satisfaction (patients vs stakeholders): taste good 25% vs 17%, appropriate temperature 55% vs 72% (p=0.002), received meal ordered 65% vs 37%.

audits.t: National audit of antidote stocking in acute hospitals in the UK.
audits.st: Joint National Poisons Information Service (NPIS)/College of Emergency Medicine (CEM) guidelines for antidote stocking (2008)
audits.f: Over 90% of hospitals stocked acetylcysteine, activated charcoal, dantrolene, desferrioxamine, naloxone, flumazenil and vitamin K within the recommended time; pralidoxime held in only 33% of hospitals; cyproheptadine and viper venom antiserum held in around 50%; 9/196 (5%) held no antidote for cyanide poisoning; 30/196 (15%) held no antidote for toxic alcohol/glycol poisoning.

audits.t: Concurrent audit of fresh frozen plasma: experience of a tertiary care hospital.
audits.st: not reported (FFP transfusion appropriateness criteria)
audits.f: 78.2% (686/877) of FFP requisition episodes were found to be inappropriate; the most inappropriate requests came from orthopaedics (88.9%) and paediatrics (80.17%)

audits.t: An audit of assessment tools in a medical school in eastern saudi arabia.
audits.tp: Assessment tools used in a medical school curriculum
audits.st: Basic educational principles of validity, reliability and currency for assessment tools
audits.f: Wide variation in use of assessment tools (MCQs, essays, OSCE) and adherence to good assessment practice across departments

audits.t: HPV vaccination of adult women: an audit of Australian general practitioners.
audits.tp: HPV vaccination uptake audit in adult women
audits.st: Australian National HPV Vaccination Program
audits.f: Nationally, only 1.9% of women aged 27-45 who consulted GPs commenced HPV vaccination from 2007-2010; auditing the last 50 consecutive patients per GP showed a higher commencement rate of 11.4%, of whom 63% had had a Pap test in the last two years

audits.t: A computer-assisted quality assurance audit in a multiprovider EMS system.
audits.tp: EMS run sheet quality assurance audit
audits.st: County EMS protocol performance criteria
audits.f: Average deficiencies per run per quarter across all paramedics was 0.47 at the start of the study
audits.c: Computer-assisted quality assurance audit of run sheets, with results returned to agency supervisors and feedback to paramedics
audits.r2: Average deficiencies per run per quarter decreased to 0.34 (P<.006); one agency's deficiencies fell from 1.98 to 1.06 per run (not statistically significant, P=.068)

audits.t: SURF - SUrvey of Risk Factor management: first report of an international audit.
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk factor control in coronary heart disease outpatients (SURF)
audits.st: Secondary prevention risk factor targets (e.g. LDL-cholesterol target) comparable to the EUROASPIRE audit series
audits.f: Physical inactivity 41-45%; overweight/obesity 59-78%; ongoing smoking 15%; lower attendance at cardiac rehabilitation in Asia; more Europeans than Asians reached the LDL-cholesterol target; data collection took 60-90 seconds per subject using a one-page data collection sheet.
audits.co: Not reported (multinational pilot: Ireland, Belgium, Croatia, Singapore, Taiwan, India, Korea)

audits.t: Surgical site infection prevention: a qualitative analysis of an individualized audit and feedback model.
audits.tp: Audit and feedback model for surgical site infection prevention (qualitative evaluation)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Individualised audit and feedback (AF) data on surgical site infection (SSI)-related process metrics for clinicians

audits.t: Audit of splenectomy at Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, Karachi.
audits.st: Recommendations for post-splenectomy patient care (vaccination, prophylactic antibiotics)
audits.f: Vaccination performed in 83.6% of patients; 12 patients had post-splenectomy complications with no cases of overwhelming post-splenectomy infection (OPSI); mean hospital stay 6.4 days

audits.t: Optimisation of hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance in patients with viral hepatitis: a quality improvement study.
audits.st: 6-monthly ultrasound surveillance for hepatocellular carcinoma in higher-risk viral hepatitis patients (standard of care)
audits.f: 46% had appropriate surveillance in the prior 6 months (one cycle); 0% had appropriate surveillance in the prior 2 years (four cycles)
audits.c: Improved doctor education, system redesign, and improved patient education to address barriers to HCC surveillance
audits.r2: 92% had appropriate surveillance in the prior 6 months (vs 46% at baseline); 64% had appropriate surveillance in the prior 2 years (vs 0% at baseline)

audits.t: Management of type III female genital mutilation in Birmingham, UK: a retrospective audit.
audits.st: Local guidelines for management of type III female genital mutilation (FGM)
audits.f: 91/253 (36%) booked into antenatal care after 16 weeks gestation; only 26/253 (10.3%) managed fully according to guidelines; presence of normal genitalia documented in only 52/134 (38.8%) medical notes following birth of a female infant; 214/253 (84.6%) had been deinfibulated in a previous pregnancy; of 39 infibulated at booking, only 9 (23.1%) deinfibulated antenatally, rest had intrapartum deinfibulation.

audits.t: Treatment of hepatitis B and C through national programme--an audit.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B and C national treatment programme adherence
audits.st: National programme inclusion/exclusion criteria and follow-up testing protocol for hepatitis B and C treatment
audits.f: Protocol adherence in 7572/7752 (97.6%) hepatitis C patients; of these 3440 (45.4%) completed 6 months therapy, PCR at 6 months available in 1686 (49%), not detected in 1133/1686 (67%); for hepatitis B, 85/454 (18.72%) fulfilled inclusion criteria and only 9 (10.58%) completed treatment

audits.t: The Western Australian Audit of Surgical Mortality: outcomes from the first 10 years.
audits.tp: Surgical mortality external peer review audit
audits.st: External, peer-reviewed audit of surgical deaths (Western Australian Audit of Surgical Mortality), assessing perioperative care including thromboembolic prophylaxis, consultant supervision and fluid management
audits.f: Annual number of surgical deaths peaked in 2006
audits.c: External, peer-reviewed mortality audit with feedback, driving changes in practice such as thromboembolic prophylaxis, consultant supervision and fluid management
audits.r2: Deaths fell 22% from the 2006 peak by 2011; overall reduction from 2002 to 2011 was 30% after correcting for population growth (P=0.002)

audits.t: The use of the Thoracic Morbidity and Mortality system for the internal analysis of performance: a case-matched temporal audit.
audits.tp: Thoracic surgery morbidity and mortality scoring audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 14 patients with major (TMM grade >2) complications in the matched early-period cohort (n=209 matched pairs)
audits.r2: 29 patients with major (TMM grade >2) complications in the matched recent-period cohort (n=209 matched pairs), P=0.02, indicating a decline in quality of care

audits.t: An audit of a therapeutic drug monitoring service for allopurinol therapy.
audits.tp: Allopurinol therapeutic drug monitoring request completeness
audits.st: Established therapeutic range for plasma oxypurinol (5-15 mg/L), sampled 6-9 hours post-dosing
audits.f: Time of allopurinol dosing recorded on 48% of requests; only 79/412 (19%) samples collected within the 6-9 hour therapeutic window; of these, 32 (8% of total) were within the therapeutic range, 5 (1%) below and 41 (10%) above; daily dose documented on only one-third of request forms; plasma urate and creatinine concomitantly requested in 66% and 58% of cases respectively (49% for all three).

audits.t: Improvement in rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease management and prevention using a health centre-based continuous quality improvement approach.
audits.tp: Rheumatic fever/rheumatic heart disease secondary prophylaxis
audits.st: National best-practice ARF/RHD management guidelines (target: ≥80% of scheduled 4-weekly benzathine penicillin injections)
audits.f: 70% (81/116) received ≥40% of scheduled benzathine penicillin (BPG); proportion receiving ≥80% of scheduled BPG did not change; 56% (31/55) had ARF episode documentation
audits.c: Continuous quality improvement (CQI) strategy using a system assessment tool, participatory action research to identify barriers, better record-keeping, triage systems and follow-up strategies
audits.r2: 82% (84/103) received ≥40% of scheduled BPG (p=0.04); 86% (134/156) reviewed by a doctor within 2 years (p=0.003); influenza vaccination up from 37% to 55% (p=0.001); ARF documentation up to 81% (50/62, p=0.004); RHD risk category documentation up to 76% (103/145)

audits.t: Haemorrhage after home birth: audit of decision making and referral.
audits.tp: Postpartum haemorrhage referral and substandard care audit
audits.st: Timely and adequate referral to hospital for postpartum haemorrhage, per Dutch community midwifery practice and the CAVE pre-hospital obstetric emergency training programme
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Haemorrhage after home birth: audit of decision making and referral. Part 2: Results and discussion.
audits.tp: Postpartum haemorrhage referral and substandard care audit
audits.st: Timely and adequate referral to hospital for postpartum haemorrhage, per Dutch community midwifery practice and the CAVE pre-hospital obstetric emergency training programme
audits.f: Major substandard care was identified in 2 of 7 cases (28.6%) by the multidisciplinary audit panel

audits.t: An audit of chronic hepatitis B contact tracing in metropolitan Western Australia.
audits.st: Contact tracing success defined as contacts tested and vaccinated if required, per national priority for hepatitis B testing and vaccination
audits.f: Overall contact tracing success rate 75%; 100% successful when traced by nurses, falling to 57% when nurse-led tracing excluded; 58% of GPs felt public health units should be responsible for contact tracing

audits.t: A cross-sectional cohort study of speech in five-year-olds with cleft palate ± lip to support development of national audit standards: benchmarking speech standards in the United Kingdom.
audits.tp: Cleft palate speech outcome national audit standards
audits.st: National speech outcome standards for 5-year-olds with cleft palate: at least 50% with speech within normal range; at least 70% with no structurally related speech problems or secondary surgery; at least 50% with no serious cleft-related articulation errors (Cleft Audit Protocol for Speech-Augmented)
