audits.f: 48% (530) had speech within normal range (standard 50%, not significantly different, P=.20); 66% (734) had no structurally related speech problems/secondary surgery (standard 70%, significantly below, P=.007); 60% (666) had no serious cleft-related articulation errors (standard 50%, significantly better)

audits.t: An audit of hepatitis C service provision in a representative sample of prisons in England.
audits.tp: Hepatitis C service provision in prisons
audits.st: National best-practice guidelines for hepatitis C testing and treatment in prisons
audits.f: Testing for hepatitis C offered in 20/21 prisons audited; only two-thirds had a written policy on testing and treatment; less than a third had a steering group to oversee the process; inconsistencies found across data sources on testing.

audits.t: Quantifying severe maternal morbidity in Scotland: a continuous audit since 2003.
audits.st: Consistently defined severe maternal morbidity events; adherence to clinical guidelines for antenatal risk identification and consultant obstetrician/anaesthetist involvement
audits.f: ICU admission required in 1 in 700 births; major obstetric haemorrhage (the most common cause of severe morbidity) experienced by 1 in 172 women and increased over the audit period while most other causes decreased; cases of eclampsia decreased; deficiencies found in antenatal risk identification and action planning; direct consultant obstetrician/anaesthetist involvement was below recommended levels.

audits.t: Glasgow coma scale: how to improve and enhance documentation.
audits.st: Standard for documentation of Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) for traumatically injured patients
audits.f: Audit confirmed insufficient documentation of GCS
audits.c: Educational plan developed and implemented to improve documentation
audits.r2: Improvement demonstrated, though additional action taken to further enhance electronic medical record documentation

audits.t: [Evaluating the implementation of involuntary hospitalization procedures: a profile of people, audits and recommendations].
audits.st: New consent/evaluation protocol for involuntary psychiatric hospitalisation, implemented after training of 335 health workers and 85 physicians
audits.f: New required form present in only 51% of files; where consent was given, it was documented in only 27% of cases
audits.c: Development and implementation of a new consent/evaluation protocol and forms for involuntary hospitalisation, following staff training

audits.t: UK audit of glomerular filtration rate measurement from plasma sampling in 2013.
audits.st: British Nuclear Medicine Society (BNMS) guidelines recommending the averaged Brochner-Mortenson correction and the Haycock body surface area formula
audits.f: In the 2001 audit, only 50% of centres applied the recommended Brochner-Mortenson correction.
audits.c: Publication and adoption of British Nuclear Medicine Society (BNMS) guidelines for GFR measurement between the 2001 and 2013 audits.
audits.r2: 97% of centres applied an early exponential clearance correction (vs 50% in 2001), 80% using the recommended averaged Brochner-Mortenson correction; approximately 75% used the recommended Haycock body surface area formula for adults (78% for children); the number of samples used did not significantly affect variability.

audits.t: How an extended perinatal audit may improve perinatal policy.
audits.tp: Perinatal death and intrapartum asphyxia audit
audits.st: Standards of intrapartum care including continuous fetal monitoring and timely intervention on significant ST events during the second stage of labour
audits.f: 3 perinatal deaths occurred, none preventable; of 19 cases of proven metabolic acidosis, 3 were possibly preventable and 4 preventable; fetal monitoring was absent in 3 (possibly) preventable cases and intervention was delayed in 2 preventable cases

audits.t: The Wellington Life Flight Helicopter Emergency Medical Service (HEMS): a retrospective audit against new Ministry of Health criteria.
audits.tp: Helicopter EMS activation audit against Ministry of Health criteria
audits.st: Draft Ministry of Health activation criteria for helicopter emergency medical services
audits.f: Majority of missions satisfied MOH activation criteria; main dispatch reasons were anticipated time savings (47%), geographical access (36%), provision of skills (7%) or combination (10%); median air arrival time 26 minutes vs 11 minutes 45 seconds by road, but transfer to hospital was quicker by air in 99% of cases (median 15 vs 49 minutes)
audits.c: Proposed changes to the Helicopter Dispatch Flowchart to address time-saving issues identified

audits.t: A 2D ion chamber array audit of wedged and asymmetric fields in an inhomogeneous lung phantom.
audits.st: ACDS Level II dosimetric audit tolerance: Pass (Optimal Level) maximum dose difference <=3.3%; Pass (Action Level) <=5.0%; Fail (Out of Tolerance) >5.0%
audits.f: 63% of audits passed, 33% failed, 1 not assessable; of 15 passes, 3 were at Pass (Action Level); high fail rate largely due to a systemic issue modelling asymmetric 60-degree wedges causing a 5%-8% delivered overdose
audits.c: Recommendations from audits led facilities to modify clinical practice and change treatment planning protocols

audits.t: A prospective audit of the adherence to a new magnesium sulphate guideline for the neuroprotection of infants born less than 30 weeks' gestation.
audits.tp: Antenatal magnesium sulphate neuroprotection guideline adherence
audits.st: Guideline for antenatal magnesium sulphate for neuroprotection of infants born less than 30 weeks' gestation, implemented 2012
audits.f: Magnesium sulphate safely administered to 58/71 (82%) eligible women, and 58/61 (95%) of women where it was clinically appropriate and practically achievable

audits.t: Adherence to guidelines: a national audit of the management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding. The REASON registry.
audits.tp: Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding guideline adherence audit
audits.st: Established best-practice guidelines for management of nonvariceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding (e.g. early endoscopy, endoscopic haemostasis for high-risk stigmata, IV proton pump inhibitor after haemostasis)
audits.f: Early endoscopy performed in 65.6%; assistant present in 83.5%; only 64.5% of patients with high-risk stigmata received endoscopic haemostasis (also given to 9.8% with low-risk stigmata); IV proton pump inhibitor given after haemostasis in 95.7%; rebleeding 10.5%, mortality 9.4%

audits.t: Assessment of vitamin D and its association with cardiovascular disease risk factors in an adult migrant population: an audit of patient records at a Community Health Centre in Kensington, Melbourne, Australia.
audits.tp: Vitamin D testing and cardiovascular risk in migrants
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Migrants from lower latitude regions were 1.48 times (95% CI 1.32-1.65) more likely to have vitamin D deficiency and 0.44 times (95% CI 0.31-0.62) less likely to have >15% 10-year coronary heart disease risk than Australian-born patients

audits.t: Radiation safety audit of a high volume Nuclear Medicine Department.
audits.tp: Radiation safety of nuclear medicine staff
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average annual whole-body radiation exposure: 1.74 mSv (physician), 2.93 mSv (technologist), 4.03 mSv (nursing staff); average 6478 PET/CT and 3856 nuclear medicine scans/year

audits.t: Preventable deaths following emergency medical dispatch--an audit study.
audits.tp: Preventable deaths after emergency medical dispatch
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: No same-day deaths found definitively preventable; 18 (11.8%) potentially preventable; dispatch protocol not used or used incorrectly in 13 of these 18 cases

audits.t: Implementing NICE obesity guidance for staff: an NHS trust audit.
audits.tp: Staff obesity management per NICE guidance (occupational health)
audits.st: NICE guideline CG43 on preventing and managing overweight and obesity, applied to the NHS as an employer
audits.f: Trust met NICE standards as an employer, but its occupational health service showed significant lack of compliance: only 53% of staff attending medical examinations had weight recorded; OH resources were inadequate; 75% of OH staff had received no training.
audits.c: Proposed action plan: consultant-led working party liaising with the trust's health and well-being committee, staff training, enhanced occupational health resources, an obesity protocol, a database and weight management clinics.

audits.t: Emergency referral transport for maternal complication: lessons from the community based maternal death audits in Unnao district, Uttar Pradesh, India.
audits.tp: Maternal death emergency referral transport audit
audits.st: Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) requirement for ambulance availability for emergency obstetric referral transport
audits.f: Only 10 ambulances available at 15 facilities against 19 required per IPHS; 47% of maternal deaths occurred in a facility, 30% en route, 23% at home; 16% of women could not arrange transportation to reach any facility; mean travel time home to facility-1 was 1 hour, facility-1 to facility-2 1.4 hours, facility-2 to facility-3 1.6 hours

audits.t: A systemic approach to quality improvement in public health services.
audits.tp: Hospital management quality improvement audit programme (Quality Contest)
audits.st: 80-item hospital management quality assessment tool combining self-evaluation and external audit scores (the Quality Contest)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Quality Contest: a quality improvement programme run every 18 months from 2007, combining self-evaluation, external audits with feedback, hospital ranking, awards and performance disclosure
audits.r2: Hospitals participating in all three contests significantly improved their performance levels in quality of management; a significant association was found between the number of times hospitals participated and the performance scores attained

audits.t: Implementing a nationwide quality improvement approach in health services.
audits.tp: Hospital management quality improvement audit programme (Quality Contest)
audits.st: 80-item hospital management quality assessment tool combining self-assessment and external audit scores (the Quality Contest)
audits.f: Earlier quality improvement pilots were not sustainable, attributed to lack of recognition of participating teams' efforts and lack of accountability pressure on managers
audits.c: Quality Contest: a nationwide quality improvement intervention introduced in 2005, combining self-assessment and external audit with structure ranking, performance disclosure and a reward system, held every 18 months
audits.r2: Improvement in performance was seen among participating structures, with constructive exchange of practices between structures and auditors

audits.t: Assessing psychosocial distress: a pain audit at IRCH-AIIMS.
audits.st: Holistic pain assessment covering physical, psychological, social and spiritual components
audits.f: Physical aspects of pain were recorded at almost 100%, but psychosocial components were recorded far less: anxiety in 1.2% and depression in 4.4% of forms, despite prior Indian literature showing 33-80% incidence of such distress
audits.c: Selected two validated psychosocial assessment tools (Distress Inventory for Cancer-2 and American Pain Society Patient Outcome Questionnaire), from 14 reviewed, for incorporation into existing pain assessment practice

audits.t: Immunization of babies born to HBsAg positive mothers: An audit on the delivery and completeness of follow up in Norfolk and Suffolk, United Kingdom.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B perinatal transmission prevention follow-up completeness
audits.st: National schedule of 4-dose hepatitis B vaccination (plus HBIG at birth where indicated) for babies born to HBsAg-positive mothers, with serological testing recommended
audits.f: Vaccination completion: 99.4% (162) for dose 1 at birth, 95.6% (152) for dose 2, 94.3% (148) for dose 3, 83.4% (106) for dose 4 at 12 months; only 29.9% (38) of babies were serologically tested at 12 months, all of whom were HBsAg negative.

audits.t: An audit of the adult hearing aid provision service in Scotland.
audits.tp: Hearing aid provision waiting times audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median wait of 8 weeks from referral letter to being seen by an otolaryngologist, plus a further median wait of 4 weeks for mould manufacture before the final hearing aid was provided

audits.t: Audit of allied health assistant roles: suggestions for improving quality in rural settings.
audits.tp: Allied health assistant role quality audit
audits.st: Audit indicators of training, supervision, performance, duties and scope of practice for allied health assistant roles
audits.f: Metropolitan and rural/regional audits showed consistency across qualifications, duty statements and formal supervision arrangements; rural positions could not provide comparable in-service training and supervision, and had a more restricted scope of practice

audits.t: Preliminary results of the global audit of treatment of refractory status epilepticus.
audits.tp: Refractory status epilepticus treatment practice (global registry)
audits.st: Current guidelines for status epilepticus first-line treatment
audits.f: First-line treatment was often delayed and not in line with current guidelines; midazolam was the most widely used first-choice anaesthetic (59%), followed by propofol and barbiturates; seizure control achieved in 74% of patients; 22% died during treatment and 4% had treatment actively withdrawn; neurological outcome good in 36%, poor in 39.3%, and 25% died in hospital.

audits.t: Elective Delivery at Term after a Previous Unexplained Intra-Uterine Fetal Death: Audit of Delivery Outcome at Tygerberg Hospital, South Africa.
audits.tp: Elective induction after previous unexplained stillbirth
audits.st: Protocol of routine induction of labour at full term (39-40 weeks) after previous unexplained intra-uterine death
audits.f: 42 of 145 patients developed complications needing earlier intervention (29%); 50% of remaining patients went into spontaneous labour before elective induction

audits.t: A 23 years audit of packed red blood cell consumption in a university hospital in a developing country.
audits.st: Crossmatch:transfusion ratio as an indicator of appropriate blood ordering practice
audits.f: Grand total packed red blood cell consumption was 345,642 units over 23 years, peaking in 1994 then dropping 30.4% by 6 years later before rising again; the crossmatch:transfusion ratio revealed gross over-ordering and wastage of blood bank resources in most divisions, most notably Obstetrics and Gynaecology
audits.c: Implementation of strict blood ordering guidelines, alongside heightened concern about transfusion-transmitted infection (e.g. HIV), contributed to reduced overuse of blood products

audits.t: Comparing Resident Self-Report to Chart Audits for Quality Improvement Projects: Accurate Reflection or Cherry-Picking?
audits.tp: Resident self-reported versus independent chart audit accuracy for guideline adherence
audits.st: 16 US Preventive Services Task Force primary care guidelines
audits.f: Self-reported guideline compliance was 82%, significantly higher than the 68% found on independent external audit of 70 randomly selected charts

audits.t: Audit of workplace walkability in an Irish healthcare setting.
audits.st: US Centre for Disease Control (CDC) Healthier Worksite Initiative Walkability Audit Tool
audits.f: 20 walking segments audited; campus scored medium risk to walkability overall on the CDC tool; staff survey (20% response, 151 respondents) found 66% sat at their desk for most of the day, with the majority sitting 5-7 hours a day.

audits.t: Auditing chronic disease care: Does it make a difference?
audits.tp: Chronic disease care quality (diabetes, hypertension, asthma, COPD, epilepsy)
audits.st: Integrated audit tool for five chronic diseases, developed locally and used annually since 2009
audits.f: Provincial average process/documentation scores; longstanding ('2012 old') districts had better facility audit and folder review scores than districts that started auditing recently ('2012 new'), including 8 clinical indicators (OR for recording processes 0.25, 95% CI 0.21-0.31 for new vs old)
audits.c: Annual internal clinical audits of facility processes, equipment and folder review, feeding back results for comparison between districts
audits.r2: Facilities audited increased from 29 (2009) to 129 (2012); overall provincial average appeared worse in 2012 than 2011, though longstanding districts outperformed newer ones

audits.t: Compliance with Evidence-Based Guidelines in Acute Pancreatitis: an Audit of Practices in University of Toronto Hospitals.
audits.st: Best Practice in General Surgery Management of Acute Pancreatitis Guideline
audits.f: 22.6% had only serum lipase tested for biochemical diagnosis; admission ultrasound performed in 70.2% (27.8% also had CT); 80.6% of non-ICU patients kept nil per os; only 34.6% of ICU patients received enteral nutrition (starting an average of 7.5 days post-admission); prophylactic antibiotics given to 25.5% of non-ICU and 48.1% of ICU patients; only 22.6% with gallstone pancreatitis had index admission cholecystectomy; ERCP with sphincterotomy was under-used (31% of biliary obstruction cases, 22% of prophylactic candidates)

audits.t: Improving the frequency of visual infusion phlebitis (VIP) scoring on an oncology ward.
audits.st: Local target: 100% use of the VIP scoring tool on the oncology ward
audits.f: Under 30% of cannulas were properly documented and assessed using VIP scoring
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles: junior doctor education (presentations/posters), then bedside intentional rounding charts giving ready access to the VIP tool
audits.r2: Compliance rose to around 80% by end of second PDSA cycle and reached 100% by end of third cycle

audits.t: Improving compliance with iron infusion therapy in the treatment of chronic anemia in haemodialysis patients with chronic kidney disease.
audits.tp: Compliance with iron infusion monitoring checklist in paediatric haemodialysis
audits.st: Departmental protocol on iron infusion for children with chronic anaemia on haemodialysis
audits.f: Blood investigations (haemoglobin, ferritin, CRP) lagged relative to pre/post infusion timing requirements
audits.c: Checklist devised for nursing staff specifying set times for measuring haemoglobin, ferritin and CRP, through multiple PDSA cycles
audits.r2: 100% adherence to investigations done prior to infusion; improved compliance and adherence, with prevention of over-treatment with iron infusion

audits.t: A prospective audit of preprocedural fasting practices on a transplant ward: when fasting becomes starving.
audits.st: Maximum six-hour preprocedural fasting guideline recommended by the majority of Anaesthesiology Societies prior to anaesthesia
audits.f: 22/34 patients (65%) were fasted, with 43 fasting episodes and a median fasting time of 13.5 hours; fasting exceeded the 6-hour guideline on 40 of 43 occasions; 97% of patients were malnourished

audits.t: Maternal death audit in Rwanda 2009-2013: a nationwide facility-based retrospective cohort study.
audits.st: Nationwide facility-based maternal death audit programme
audits.f: 71.6% of deaths occurred at district hospitals; postpartum haemorrhage was leading direct cause (22.7%); health system failures identified as main factor in 61.0% of cases

audits.t: Development and efficiency of dedicated upper limb trauma lists in a district general hospital.
audits.tp: Dedicated upper limb trauma lists efficiency
audits.st: Local target to reduce hospital stay/improve satisfaction for upper limb trauma patients via dedicated theatre lists
audits.f: Baseline data on patients treated on routine trauma lists
audits.c: New pathway of dedicated upper limb trauma lists, with safe discharge home and written instructions pending surgery
audits.r2: Reduced in-patient stay without affecting care/outcomes; improved patient satisfaction

audits.t: Introducing paediatric grommet "rapid turnover" lists. A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Paediatric grommet 'rapid turnover' list waiting times and cancellations
audits.st: NICE CG60 criteria for grommet insertion; NHS 18-week referral-to-treatment (RTT) target
audits.f: 78% of children breached the 18-week RTT target; average wait 90 days; 8% on-the-day cancellations; 38% had audiograms older than 90 days; only 5.8 grommet cases completed per list
audits.c: Introduction of 'rapid turnover' paediatric day case theatre lists with a pre-operative consent clinic and dual anaesthetic pods
audits.r2: No children remained in breach of the 18-week RTT target; 0% on-the-day cancellations (24% cancelled at consent clinic instead); £3255 increase in gross income per list

audits.t: [A process audit of stillbirths in a rural family medical practice].
audits.st: Expected standard of antenatal instruction on fetal movement monitoring and appropriate labour/hospital management
audits.f: Stillbirth rate 81/1000 vs national rate of 4.5/1000 (p<0.015); all 5 fetal deaths were judged probably preventable with more intensive patient instruction on fetal movement interpretation or different hospital management

audits.t: MATERNAL MORTALITY AUDIT IN A TERTIARY HEALTH INSTITUTION IN NIGERIA: LESSONS FROM DIRECT CAUSES AND ITS DRIVERS.
audits.st: Expected standard of antenatal care attendance and timely obstetric intervention (three-delay model)
audits.f: Maternal mortality ratio 1265/100,000 live births, decreasing steadily over the study period; major causes were haemorrhage (36%), sepsis (17%) and hypertensive disorders (16%); delays were identified in 34.3% of cases, most (70.1%) being Phase III (facility) delays

audits.t: Perinatal mortality audit at Tikure Anbessa Teaching Hospital, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: 1995 to 1996.
audits.st: Expected standard that all pregnant women attend antenatal care booking
audits.f: Perinatal mortality rate 71.6/1000 live births; 77.2% of women were booked for antenatal care versus 22.8% unbooked; risk of perinatal mortality more than doubled among mothers who failed to book; leading causes among unbooked/uninvestigated mothers were birth asphyxia (15.4%) and prematurity (12%)

audits.t: Perinatal mortality audit in a Zimbabwean district.
audits.st: Standard of antenatal care attendance and monitoring/management of complications (syphilis, hypertension, diabetes, amniotic fluid infection) to reduce avoidable perinatal death
audits.f: Perinatal mortality rate 30.6/1000 births; classified as 83 macerated stillbirths, 28 congenital malformation, 79 immaturity, 111 intrapartum asphyxia and 18 specific problems; an avoidable factor was detected in 242/319 (75.6%) cases: maternal in 120, maternity centre in 28, hospital in 94

audits.t: Venous thromboembolism capture on electronic systems in obstetrics patients at St Thomas' Hospital.
audits.tp: VTE risk assessment completion on electronic systems in obstetrics
audits.st: CQUIN payment framework target: 95% VTE risk assessment completion within 24 hours of admission
audits.f: Mean baseline VTE assessment completion rate on EPR 20.7%
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles: whiteboard magnet reminder system, then posters/stickers, then a loyalty card incentive scheme, alongside staff education at handovers
audits.r2: Completion rate rose to 67.5% after cycle 1, 65.7% after cycle 2, and averaged 65.6% in cycle 3 overall (79.5% in final week, 92.3% on the last day)

audits.t: An audit of the quality of online immunisation information available to Australian parents.
audits.st: WHO Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety (GACVS) criteria for assessing vaccine safety websites
audits.f: Overall mean quality score 57/100 (range 14-92); pro-vaccine sites averaged 61/100, anti-vaccine sites averaged 30/100; main weakness was lack of transparent authorship

audits.t: Military Emergency Medical Service System Assessment: Application of the National Park Service Needs Assessment and Program Audit to Objectively Evaluate the Military EMS System of Okinawa, Japan.
audits.st: National Park Service EMS Program Audit Worksheet scoring criteria
audits.f: NPS EMS Program Audit Worksheet score of 31, suggesting the programme is well planned and operating within standards; averaged 1,345±137 patient transports annually; an advanced life support provider would have been dispatched on 558 EMS runs (38%) based on chief complaint in 2014 had one been available
audits.c: Formal recommendations made by a joint committee of Military EMS physicians following the assessment

audits.t: Lessons from a national audit of acute pancreatitis: A summary of the NCEPOD report 'Treat the Cause'.
audits.st: NCEPOD organisational, clinical and peer review assessment of acute pancreatitis care (recommends standardised early warning scoring from emergency department, antibiotic stewardship, nutrition assessment)
audits.f: Room for improvement identified in over 50% of patients; 21% had one or more previous episodes with inadequate prevention of recurrence (gallstones/alcohol); 1/5 given antibiotics unnecessarily; nutrition management adequate in only 85%; early warning score omitted in 31% of emergency department admissions.

audits.t: The Usefulness of Nap Sleep Recording During Routine Electroencephalography: An Audit Study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 744/2547 (29.2%) EEGs abnormal; nap sleep obtained in 258 (34.7%); 39/258 (15.1%) abnormal during nap sleep; nap sleep abnormalities represented only 2.7% of all abnormal EEGs (20/744 solely on nap sleep).

audits.t: Small for gestational age and perinatal mortality at term: An audit in a Dutch national cohort study.
audits.tp: Small for gestational age perinatal mortality audit
audits.st: Standards of antenatal referral and monitoring for small for gestational age infants at term
audits.f: 162 small for gestational age infants died perinatally; risk factors included gestational age of 37 completed weeks (aOR 2.6), male gender (aOR 1.4), South Asian (aOR 3.6), African (aOR 3.5) and other non-Western ethnicity (aOR 1.9); at 37 weeks, audit results showed 26% of mothers smoked, 91% of deaths were male infants, and death occurred before birth in all but one case; 61% of deceased SGA infants at 37 weeks were referred from primary midwifery care to the obstetrician because of antepartum death before labour

audits.t: Quality Assessment of Family Planning Sterilization Services at Health Care Facilities: Case Record Audit.
audits.tp: Family planning sterilization service quality audit
audits.st: Government of India Standard Operating Procedures for Family Planning Sterilization services
audits.f: Informed consent had 100% compliance in all records; previous contraceptive history was documented in only 89.5% of Primary Health Centre records and 58.7% of Community Health Centre records; mental illness assessment was inadequate (only 70% at CHCs); postoperative counselling was also found to deviate from standards

audits.t: Audit sur la qualité de la vaccination en milieu scolaire dans la région de Monastir (Tunisie).
audits.st: National immunization programme criteria for vaccination sessions (cold chain, hand hygiene, waste disposal, health education)
audits.f: Cold chain was respected in most cases; accumulators available in 85.5%, sharps collector in 76.4%, alcohol-soaked cotton in 98.2%, emergency box in only 41.8% of cases; hand washing before immunisation performed in only 29.1% of cases; waste disposal per hygiene rules done by 40 agents; health education of students done in 67.3% of cases

audits.t: Developing better practices at the institutional level leads to better outcomes after pancreaticoduodenectomy in 3,378 patients: domestic audit of the Japanese Society of Pancreatic Surgery.
audits.st: Institutional standardization, defined as implementing 7 or more of 13 defined quality initiatives for pancreaticoduodenectomy care
audits.f: 16.5% of pancreaticoduodenectomies were performed in standardized institutions in 2006
audits.c: Institutional standardization: implementation of 7 or more of 13 defined quality initiatives for pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) care
audits.r2: The proportion of PDs performed in standardized institutions increased to 46.4% by 2014; the standardized institution group had an improved process of care and a lower frequency of severe complications than non-standardized institutions

audits.t: Specialist perioperative allergy clinic services in the UK 2016: Results from the Royal College of Anaesthetists Sixth National Audit Project.
audits.st: BSACI, Association of Anaesthetists of Great Britain and Ireland, and NICE CG183 recommendations for investigation of perioperative drug allergy
audits.f: >1200 patients evaluated annually across 44 centres; variation in workload, waiting times, access, staffing and diagnostic approach; chlorhexidine and latex not part of routine testing in many centres; paediatric centres had longest waiting times (most >13 weeks).

audits.t: Frequency and Variables Associated with Fasting Orders in Inpatients with Ulcerative Colitis: The Audit of Diet Orders-Ulcerative Colitis (ADORE-UC) Study.
audits.tp: Fasting order appropriateness audit in ulcerative colitis inpatients
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines recommending patients hospitalised with an ulcerative colitis flare be offered a normal diet unless not tolerated
audits.f: 252 nil-per-os or clear liquid diet orders occurred in 142/187 admissions (75.9%); 112 orders (44%) were unjustified; patients with unjustified orders spent a mean of 3 days on NPO/CLD, missing a mean of 10 meals; registered dietitian consultation obtained in only 17.1% of admissions; admission weight recorded in only 36.4%

audits.t: Cirrhotic patients with portal hypertension-related bleeding and an indication for early-TIPS: a large multicentre audit with real-life results.
audits.tp: Early-TIPS eligibility and use audit in variceal bleeding
audits.st: Baveno VI consensus criteria for early transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) in high-risk cirrhotic patients with variceal bleeding
audits.f: 35% of patients were eligible for early-TIPS, but only 6.8% actually underwent early-TIPS placement, mainly due to lack of availability; 1-year survival was significantly higher with early-TIPS (85.7% vs 58.9%, p=0.04)

audits.t: CTPA protocol optimisation audit: challenges of dose reduction with maintained image quality.
audits.st: Local and national CT pulmonary angiography diagnostic reference levels (DRLs) for dose-length product (local 300 mGy·cm, national 400 mGy·cm)
audits.f: Average dose-length product 559 mGy·cm, exceeding both local (300 mGy·cm) and national (400 mGy·cm) DRLs, despite acceptable image quality parameters.
audits.c: CTPA scanner protocol changed: SureExposure preset changed to 'Standard' noise level (SD 19) and minimum tube current lowered from 80 to 40 mA
audits.r2: Average dose-length product reduced to 359 mGy·cm, now compliant with national and local DRLs; image quality preserved as assessed by three consultant cardiothoracic radiologists.

audits.t: Incidence of hypoglycemia in newborns at risk and an audit of the 2011 American academy of pediatrics guideline for hypoglycemia.
audits.tp: Neonatal hypoglycaemia screening guideline compliance audit
audits.st: 2011 American Academy of Pediatrics guideline for hypoglycaemia screening in at-risk newborns
audits.f: Incidence of hypoglycaemia was 16.6% (infant of diabetic mother), 12.7% (large-for-gestational-age), 12.2% (small-for-gestational-age) and 34% (late preterm infants); lower gestational age was associated with higher incidence (P=0.02); compliance with the AAP guideline was found to be satisfactory

audits.t: Redesigning the Peer Audit Process to Enhance Clinical Dialogue.
audits.tp: Peer audit process redesign in rehabilitation therapy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: A wide variety of differing peer audit processes, tools and requirements were used across therapy disciplines and clinical sites
audits.c: Group redesign project using a project charter, developing a single peer audit tool and unified audit process across therapy disciplines and care settings
audits.r2: Survey responses indicated favourable change: the peer audit process was completed more consistently and was more likely to be perceived as resulting in meaningful discussion, encouraging critical thinking, and improving clinical skills

audits.t: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery as an auditing framework for identifying improvements to perioperative nutrition care of older surgical patients.
audits.tp: Perioperative nutrition care ERAS adherence audit in older patients
audits.st: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) guideline targets for perioperative nutrition, including fasting of 2-4 hours for fluid and 6-8 hours for food, preoperative carbohydrate loading, and early upgrade to full diet
audits.f: 17% and 4% of patients met fasting targets for fluid and food respectively; 55% were upgraded to full diet by the first postoperative day; no patients received preoperative carbohydrate loading; minimally invasive surgery (p=0.01) and no anastomosis formation (p=0.05) were associated with receiving ERAS-concordant nutrition care

audits.t: [Audit as a tool to improve the efficiency of the immunization services: the experience of a Local Health Authority in Rome].
audits.st: National Prevention Plan 2014-2018 and National Immunization Plan 2017-2019 target of at least 95% vaccine coverage; 4-step Ministry of Health audit methodology
audits.f: Vaccine coverage had fallen below 95% since 2014 for many paediatric vaccines, prompting the improvement programme
audits.c: Structured annual 30-hour audits at each of 5 vaccination centres, following 4 defined steps (verify current situation, analyse concerns, evaluate solutions, implement feasible improvement actions), run from February 2014 to December 2016
audits.r2: Significant improvement in vaccine coverage, along with an increase in the number of vaccine sessions and total vaccines administered

audits.t: Audit of pulse oximetry screening for critical congenital heart disease (CCHD) in newborns.
audits.tp: Critical congenital heart disease pulse oximetry screening compliance audit
audits.st: Ontario Provincial Council for Maternal Child Health 2014 recommendation for CCHD screening using pulse oximetry as part of the newborn examination
audits.f: Compliance was 88% overall (95% excluding deliveries by midwives who did not agree to comply); median age of screening 25 hours (range 6-80); specificity 99.4%; 4 patients screened positive and were seen by a paediatrician, none had CCHD

audits.t: Surveillance, Auditing, and Feedback Can Reduce Surgical Site Infection Dramatically: Toward Zero Surgical Site Infection.
audits.tp: Surgical site infection surveillance, auditing and feedback bundle
audits.st: Compliance with pre-operative, peri-operative and post-operative surgical site infection (SSI) care bundle components
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Implementation of a Surveillance of SSI, Auditing, and Feedback (SAF) programme with an SSI care bundle, in three phases (pre-SAF, early-SAF, late-SAF) from January 2014 to December 2016
audits.r2: Significant decrease in SSI rate in orthopaedic implant surgery (relative risk 0.19, 95% CI 0.12-0.31) and in mitral/aortic valve cardiac surgery (relative risk 0.08, 95% CI 0.03-0.22); SSI rate was inversely correlated with compliance for pre-operative (r=-0.738, p=0.037), peri-operative (r=-0.802, p=0.017) and post-operative (r=-0.762, p=0.028) bundle components

audits.t: [Vitamine K antagonists overdose: Physician adherence to the French guidelines].
audits.tp: Vitamin K antagonist overdose management guideline adherence audit
audits.st: 2008 Haute Autorité de Santé (HAS) guidelines for management of an excessively elevated INR in patients on vitamin K antagonists
audits.f: Overall physician adherence to guidelines was 58%; for patients with INR greater than 6, adherence was only 33%; use of vitamin K was the major source of errors; mortality rate was 20%

audits.t: Perinatal death: audit and classification.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 213 perinatal deaths occurred among 10,539 deliveries; of 110 deaths in normally formed babies weighing 800g or more, 54 were antepartum, 5 intrapartum and 51 neonatal; the majority of all perinatal deaths involved serious malformation or birth weight under 800g

audits.t: Variation in hospital mortality after pancreatoduodenectomy is related to failure to rescue rather than major complications: a nationwide audit.
audits.st: Mandatory nationwide Dutch Pancreatic Cancer Audit benchmarking hospital mortality, major complication rates and failure to rescue after pancreatoduodenectomy
audits.f: 391 patients (29%) developed a major complication; in-hospital mortality was 4.2%; failure to rescue occurred in 56/391 (14.3%); mortality was 0.9% in the lowest-mortality hospital quartile (4 hospitals, 327 patients) versus 8.1% in the highest-mortality quartile (5 hospitals, 310 patients); the major complication rate increased 40% (25.7% vs 35.2%) between quartiles, while the failure-to-rescue rate increased 560% (3.6% vs 22.9%)

audits.t: Implementation of Quality Systems in Nuclear Medicine: Why It Matters. An Outcome Analysis (Quality Management Audits in Nuclear Medicine Part III).
audits.tp: QUANUM nuclear medicine quality management conformance
audits.st: IAEA QUANUM (Quality Management Audits in Nuclear Medicine) checklists scoring conformance 0-4 against international regulations and standards
audits.f: Baseline established by IAEA external audit; external audit training given to local teams for subsequent internal audits.
audits.c: Implementation of a comprehensive quality management system (QUANUM) with training of local teams via the external audit and subsequent internal audits using the same checklists
audits.r2: 88% (22/25) of centres improved conformance status and 92% (23/25) improved conformance levels; on average 55 requirements moved from nonconformance to conformance; significant improvement (P<0.01) in nearly all checklists except Hormones and Tumor marker determinations.

audits.t: Influence of an independent quarterly audit on publicly reported vancomycin-resistant enterocococi bacteremia data in Ontario, Canada.
audits.tp: Public health data reporting accuracy audit (VRE bacteraemia)
audits.st: Accurate self-reporting of vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) bacteraemia cases to Ontario's Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care for public reporting
audits.f: 114/367 (31%) VRE bacteraemia reports were found to be incorrect
audits.c: Independent quarterly audits of publicly reported VRE bacteraemia data by Public Health Ontario, from September 2013 to June 2015
audits.r2: 12/147 (8.1%) VRE bacteraemia reports were found to be incorrect; quarterly audits were associated with a significant reduction in reporting errors (relative risk 0.17, 95% CI 0.05-0.63)

audits.t: Quality of Medicine Information in Product Information Leaflets: A Retrospective Audit.
audits.tp: Medicine product information leaflet quality audit
audits.st: National drug regulations for required product information leaflet content; British National Formulary and/or Australian Medicines Handbook for clinical fact compatibility
audits.f: 28% of product information leaflets were missing at least one essential required item (commonly pharmacokinetics, treatment duration, overdose and special dosage information); of 900 cross-matched clinical information items, 80 (8.9%) were partially compatible and 8 (0.9%) totally incompatible with reference sources; 48% of leaflets had at least one incompatibility

audits.t: Audit of a human papillomavirus vaccine programme for men who have sex with men delivered through an Integrated Sexual Reproductive Health service.
audits.st: Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (November 2015) recommendation for HPV vaccination of men who have sex with men up to age 45 attending genitourinary medicine/HIV services
audits.f: 539/693 (77%) eligible men who have sex with men commenced vaccination; full vaccination course completed in 40% of those who commenced, within the audit timeframe.

audits.t: Specialist perioperative allergy clinic services in the UK 2018: Results from the Royal College of Anaesthetists Sixth National Audit Project (NAP6) investigation of perioperative anaphylaxis.
audits.st: Published NAP6/BSACI guidance on investigation of perioperative anaphylaxis, compared with a prior NAP6 baseline clinic survey
audits.f: 192/266 (72%) had a trigger identified, of which 140/192 (75%) met criteria for IgE-mediated allergic anaphylaxis; adherence to guidance on waiting time for clinic assessment was similar to the baseline survey, but chlorhexidine and latex testing, and harmonised testing practices, remained lacking.

audits.t: Audit of Intrapartum Care Based on the National Guideline for Midwifery and Birth Services.
audits.tp: Intrapartum care national guideline compliance audit
audits.st: National Guideline for Midwifery and Birth Services
audits.f: Compatibility with the national guideline: history taking 88.3%, vital sign measurement 64.6%, Leopold's manoeuvre 38.5%, initial assessment 83.4%, labour care 22.5%, use of pain relief methods 63.5%, labour progress assessment 71.5%, process of delivery 89.5%, postpartum management 89.5%

audits.t: Audit and Feedback: A Quality Improvement Study to Increase Pneumococcal Vaccination Rates.
audits.tp: Pneumococcal vaccination audit and feedback quality improvement
audits.st: Recommended pneumococcal vaccination for at-risk adults
audits.f: Generalised feedback that did not provide actionable information did not improve the pneumococcal immunisation rate
audits.c: Timely, individualised audit and feedback on pneumococcal immunisation status, compared with generalised feedback
audits.r2: Timely, individualised audit and feedback significantly increased the pneumococcal vaccination rate compared with generalised feedback (chi-square [1, N=1993] = 124.7, P<.001)

audits.t: Clinical impact of developing better practices at the institutional level on surgical outcomes after distal pancreatectomy in 1515 patients: Domestic audit of the Japanese Society of Pancreatic Surgery.
audits.tp: Institutional standardisation of distal pancreatectomy care
audits.st: Institutional standardisation defined as implementing ≥6 of 11 departmental quality initiatives (Japanese Society of Pancreatic Surgery domestic audit)
audits.f: Standardised institutions had lower severe complications (22% vs 29%), lower clinically relevant pancreatic fistula (22% vs 31%, p<0.05); proportion of patients treated at standardised institutions rose from 16.5% (2006) to 46.4% (2014)

audits.t: Molecular Auditing: An Evaluation of Unsuspected Tissue Specimen Misidentification.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1 of 972 (0.1%) specimen pairs showed a discordant genotype, indicating that one of the two specimens had been misidentified

audits.t: Audit of the community-directed treatment with ivermectin (CDTI) for onchocerciasis and factors associated with adherence in three regions of Cameroon.
audits.tp: Ivermectin community-directed treatment (CDTI) coverage for onchocerciasis
audits.st: Community-directed treatment with ivermectin (CDTI) programme targets and coverage surveys
audits.f: 2014 weighted therapeutic coverage was 64.1% (95% CI 56.8-70.9%); survey coverage was 14.1-22.0% lower than reported coverage; 57.8% reported five-year adherence

audits.t: Emergency inserted peripheral intravenous catheters: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Emergency-inserted peripheral IV catheter timely removal audit
audits.st: Local Queensland guideline recommending removal or replacement of ambulance/emergency inserted peripheral intravenous catheters within 24 hours
audits.f: Routine clinical audits demonstrated a delay in removing ambulance/emergency inserted PIVCs beyond acceptable dwell times; these catheters were not being recognised by ward staff as requiring removal
audits.c: Key stakeholder engagement, roll-out of a sticker to identify ambulance/emergency inserted PIVCs, and education of ward staff
audits.r2: A significant reduction in the number of ambulance/emergency inserted PIVCs remaining in situ for longer than 24 hours

audits.t: Adoption and use of guidelines for whiplash: an audit of insurer and health professional practice in New South Wales, Australia.
audits.tp: Whiplash guideline adherence by insurers and clinicians
audits.st: 2014 NSW clinical practice guidelines for management of acute whiplash-associated disorders
audits.f: 90% given active treatments in line with guidelines; use of Quebec Task Force classification only 19.9%; specialised imaging avoided in only 45.8% of grade I/II WAD; passive treatments avoided in 94.0%; prognostic tool use only 12.8%

audits.t: An audit of healthcare provision in internally displaced population camps in Nigeria.
audits.st: Sphere minimum standards in humanitarian crises
audits.f: 5 of 15 assessed standards met to some extent (including water and shelter availability); sanitation and vaccination unmet in five camps; severe overcrowding in five camps; inadequate waste disposal in all camps.

audits.t: Perineal outcome following educational intervention: a retrospective audit of primiparous women.
audits.tp: Episiotomy rate and perineal outcome audit after educational intervention
audits.st: Agreed standards for episiotomy use to reduce postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction
audits.f: Overall 30% had an intact perineum, 51% a spontaneous tear, and 19% an episiotomy; where the accoucheur was an obstetrician or obstetric registrar, the baseline episiotomy rate was 56%
audits.c: A teaching session on pelvic floor anatomy, the impact of vaginal delivery on pelvic floor dysfunction, and relevant local/international research, delivered by the Head of Urogynaecology
audits.r2: No significant overall change in episiotomy rates (p=.17); however, the episiotomy rate rose from 56% to 70% (p<.01) when the accoucheur was an obstetrician or obstetric registrar, while the midwife-led rate changed minimally (11% to 18%, p=.27)

audits.t: Are pre-operative lymphoscintigrams needed for localization prior to sentinel node biopsy?: An audit to ensure safe practice and to provide another view.
audits.tp: Pre-operative lymphoscintigram use before sentinel node biopsy
audits.st: Local standard: reported node count and biopsied node count concordance to ensure safe sentinel node biopsy localisation without preoperative lymphoscintigraphy (no external guideline target stated)
audits.f: Reported node count vs biopsied node count showed only fair agreement (Cohen's kappa 0.34, 95% CI 0.195-0.482); reported node count was zero in two cases but sentinel node biopsy still succeeded; 90% of lymphoscintigrams performed on day of surgery.
audits.c: Lymphoscintigraphy discontinued before sentinel node biopsy to reduce delay to theatre and demand on Nuclear Medicine
audits.r2: Biopsied node count range 0-4 (mean 1.80); two cases of failed localisation; no significant difference in biopsied node count with vs without scans (p=0.16); sentinel node positivity 36% (with scan) vs 25.3% (without), not significant (p=0.11).

audits.t: Community management of lactational mastitis and/or breast abscess: a retrospective audit.
audits.tp: Community management of lactational mastitis and breast abscess
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Majority of admitted patients self-presented to the emergency department; low use of available community resources; poor patient knowledge of natural history and self-management.

audits.t: Physical accessibility audit of primary health centers for people with disabilities: An on-site assessment from Dakshina Kannada district in Southern India.
audits.tp: Physical accessibility of primary health centres for people with disabilities
audits.st: Accessible India Campaign (AIC) Physical Accessibility Audit Checklist (>116 items)
audits.f: 85% (57/67) had accessible pathway, 90% (60/67) had a wheelchair ramp, only 36% (25/67) had accessible doors; no PHC had height-adjustable examination table or disabled-friendly toilets, only 2 had accessible weighing scales

audits.t: Adequacy of bystander actions in unconscious patients: an audit study in the Ghent region (Belgium).
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Suboptimal actions recognised in 54/142 (38%) cases, most often delayed (n=35) or inaccurate (n=12) alerting; dispatcher advice ignored in 21/81 (25.9%) cases; CPR started in only 29/67 (43.3%) indicated cardiac arrest cases.

audits.t: The incidence of post-thyroidectomy hypocalcaemia: a retrospective single-centre audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall incidence of post-thyroidectomy hypocalcaemia within 24 hours was 21.4% (13.8% at 6 hours, 15.8% at 24 hours); 3.6% remained hypocalcaemic at 6 months requiring continual supplementation; benign thyroid disease and age <50 were associated with higher risk.

audits.t: 2015 UK software audit of hepatobiliary scintigraphy.
audits.st: Recommended acquisition of 60 minutes after fatty stimulus (used for normal range references) and fatty stimulus content of at least 10 g, with motion correction applied
audits.f: Only 48.1% of centres acquired for 60 minutes after stimulus as recommended; 13.5% administered fatty stimuli below the recommended 10 g; 25% of participants did not use motion correction, which could change gallbladder ejection fraction substantially (e.g. from 44% to 9% in one dataset).

audits.t: Collaborative, Innovative Quality Improvement Activity: Development of Queensland Ambulance Service Stickers: Drivers, Approaches, Implementation, and Outcomes.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: QAS-IVC identification stickers, mandatory IVC documentation at handover, and clinician patient education on IVC infection signs
audits.r2: Ward audits reflected the interventions were apparent and beneficial (fewer in-dwelling QAS-inserted catheters, increased staff/patient awareness), but authors explicitly state they lacked comparative data to objectively quantify success.

audits.t: Combating hospital malnutrition: Dietitian-led quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Hospital malnutrition and early oral nutrition supplement delivery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Early delivery of ONS within 6h (EDONS) was 10%; delayed delivery (>24h) was 40%; ONS prescription rate 2%.
audits.c: Sensitisation of clinical dietitians (Phase 2) followed by formation of a multidisciplinary team (MDT) coalition to improve timely ONS delivery (Phase 3)
audits.r2: EDONS rose to 44.6%, delayed delivery (>24h) fell to 8.4%, ONS prescription rose to 16% (p=0.000); length of stay fell from 6.82 to 5.60 days (p=0.010).

audits.t: Health profile of the PASSI surveillance system according to the second self-audit data.
audits.tp: Self-audit of PASSI public health surveillance programme conformity
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Data used more for communication (60%) and planning (80%) than scientific purposes; central support valued for quality monitoring and training.

audits.t: Auditing fungal disease in leukemia patients in a tertiary care center: opportunities and challenges for an antifungal stewardship program.
audits.tp: Antifungal prophylaxis and treatment in leukaemia (antifungal stewardship)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Proven/probable invasive fungal disease in 6% of cases (14% ALL, 6% AML); mould-active antifungal prophylaxis used in 84% overall (94% AML, 23% ALL).

audits.t: Appropriateness of intravenous immunoglobulin use in immune thrombocytopenia (ITP): A Canadian centre deep dive audit.
audits.tp: Appropriateness of IVIG use in immune thrombocytopenia
audits.st: Accepted guideline indications for IVIG use in ITP (active bleeding, pre-operative/antepartum care, corticosteroid contraindication, antithrombotic/myelosuppressive therapy requirement)
audits.f: Most IVIG use fell within accepted guideline indications: active bleeding 17%, pre-operative/antepartum 29%, corticosteroid contraindication 11%, antithrombotic/myelosuppressive requirement 7%; some use fell outside guidelines as a diagnostic challenge.

audits.t: Increasing antepartum Tdap vaccine administration: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: CDC recommendation for antepartum Tdap vaccination with every pregnancy
audits.f: 362/636 (56.9%) eligible women received Tdap during current pregnancy.
audits.c: 5-step intervention: provider/patient education, increased Tdap availability, staff reminders of standing order, encouraging obstetricians to offer Tdap, and transferring documentation from office to hospital
audits.r2: 457/708 (64.5%) eligible women received Tdap (absolute increase 7.6%, relative increase 13.4%, p<0.01).

audits.t: Venom allergy treatment practices in Poland in comparison to guidelines: next edition of the national audit.
audits.tp: Venom immunotherapy practice vs European guidelines
audits.st: European guidelines for venom immunotherapy (VIT)
audits.f: Ultrarush protocol used by 71% (22/33); 5 years of VIT declared by 71% (22); sting challenge to confirm efficacy performed by only 26% (8/33); 45% (14/33) stopped beta-blockers before treatment

audits.t: A regional audit system for stillbirth: a way to better understand the phenomenon.
audits.st: Regional Audit System for Stillbirth, using ReCoDe classification for cause of death
audits.f: Total stillbirth rate 3.09/1000 births; 16 stillbirths not registered by Regional Birth Register; regional group attributed different cause of death than local audits in 17% of cases; 10.9% judged possibly/probably preventable

audits.t: A Prospective Audit of Inappropriately Occupied Hospital Beds in Patients with Newly Acquired Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury
audits.tp: Inappropriate bed occupancy in spinal cord injury care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 44 patients spent 3915 inappropriate bed-days total (78 awaiting acute care admission, 3126 awaiting rehabilitation admission, 711 awaiting discharge from rehabilitation).

audits.t: Prehospital Management of Acute Addison Disease: Audit of Patients Attending a Referral Hospital in a Regional Area.
audits.tp: Prehospital stress-dose management of Addison disease
audits.st: Recommended patient-initiated stress dosing (oral/parenteral hydrocortisone) to avert adrenal crisis
audits.f: Only 17.9% (45/252) of presentations followed any form of stress dosing; among clinician-diagnosed adrenal crises, only 32.8% (20/61) had used stress dosing beforehand; IM hydrocortisone used pre-presentation in only 2.8% (7/252)

audits.t: Management of uncomplicated malaria in private health facilities in North-West Ethiopia: a clinical audit of current practices.
audits.tp: Malaria diagnosis and treatment guideline adherence
audits.st: National and international malaria diagnosis and treatment guidelines
audits.f: Only 19.4% (320/1650) received acceptable malaria diagnosis; 82.9% of P. vivax cases managed with ideal recommended treatment; malaria parasite positivity rate 20.30%

audits.t: Availability of Antidotes in Kuwait: A National Audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: None of the 14 hospitals had a complete stock of essential antidotes; mean immediate antidote availability was 79.6% (public) vs 52.1% (private); non-immediate availability 64.5% (public) vs 14.7% (private).

audits.t: Preventable Deaths in Multiple Trauma Patients: The Importance of Auditing and Continuous Quality Improvement.
audits.st: Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) guideline used to classify preventability
audits.f: 1 of 8 trauma deaths was considered preventable, the other 7 unpreventable; causes reviewed included delayed examination/treatment and insufficient guidance.
audits.c: Decision that bedside trauma series X-ray (chest/pelvis) and FAST scan must be performed in the resuscitation room by a person meeting trauma team activation criteria

audits.t: Voriconazole: an audit of hospital-based dosing and monitoring and evaluation of the predictive performance of a dose-prediction software package.
audits.tp: Voriconazole dosing and therapeutic drug monitoring guideline adherence
audits.st: Australian national guidelines for voriconazole dosing and therapeutic drug monitoring
audits.f: Adherence to dosing guidelines was poor unless the most commonly prescribed 200mg oral dose was used (56% of prescriptions); TDM obtained for 82% of courses; of trough concentrations, 57% therapeutic, 37% subtherapeutic, 6% supratherapeutic.

audits.t: Should physicians perform their own quality assurance audits?
audits.tp: Preventive care ordering audit (influenza vaccination and mammography)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline influenza vaccination ordering rate 40%; baseline screening mammography ordering rate 8%.
audits.c: Residents randomised to audit their own charts for vaccination, audit their own charts for mammography, or receive other groups' results passively
audits.r2: Passive receipt of audit results improved vaccination ordering to 59% and mammography to 16%; residents who performed their own audit improved mammography ordering to 26% but did not improve vaccination ordering.

audits.t: [Audit on management of seizures in six Swedish hospitals].
audits.tp: Emergency department management of first seizures
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Eyewitness statements sought in 72% of visits after a first seizure; documentation of alcohol/drug exposure and driving information was poor; only 56% of patients with known epilepsy had seen a neurologist in the preceding year.

audits.t: Diagnosis and management of acute cholecystitis: a single-centre audit of guideline adherence and patient outcomes.
audits.tp: Acute cholecystitis diagnosis and management guideline adherence (Tokyo Guidelines)
audits.st: Tokyo Guidelines (2013/2018) for diagnosis and management of acute cholecystitis, including antibiotic use and time to operation
audits.f: Severity was not documented preoperatively for any patient; antibiotic recommendation compliance was 18.0%; time-to-operation compliance was 86.0%, improving to 91.0% (vs 76.0%, p=0.025) when an acute care surgery team was involved.

audits.t: Effect of a prospective audit with intervention and feedback on Clostridioides difficile infection management.
audits.tp: Clostridioides difficile infection management guideline adherence
audits.st: International/local treatment guidelines for Clostridioides difficile infection management
audits.f: Conformity to local protocol was 23.9% during the PAIF intervention period.
audits.c: Educational programme with a prospective audit with intervention and feedback (PAIF) team of pharmacists, an infectious diseases specialist and a microbiologist reviewing all cases
audits.r2: Conformity to local protocol rose to 67.3% (p<0.001); Fidaxomicin prescriptions increased significantly (p=0.006); recovery at 10 days increased (p=0.001) and relapse decreased (p=0.016); CDI incidence improved to 1.3 per 10,000 patient-days.

audits.t: Nutritional Care of Patients Admitted to Hospital for Alcohol Withdrawal: A 5-Year Retrospective Audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Nutrition-related biochemistry available for most patients (sodium/urea/creatinine 93.5%, magnesium/phosphate 60.5%); no patients had serum thiamine levels assessed; parenteral thiamine given to 88.0%; only 21.2% seen by a dietitian, of whom 16 had a comprehensive nutritional assessment.

audits.t: Impact of Unannounced Standardized Patient Audit and Feedback on Care, Documentation, and Costs: an Experiment and Claims Analysis.
audits.tp: Unannounced standardised patient audit and feedback on care quality
audits.st: Guideline-based provider care behaviour checklists (diabetes, depression, back pain, smoking, preventive cancer screening)
audits.f: Expected clinical behaviours performed in 46% of baseline visits
audits.c: Feedback to providers on standardised patient-identified care and documentation gaps
audits.r2: Expected clinical behaviours increased from 46% to 56% (OR=1.53, 95% CI 1.29-1.83)

audits.t: Peer review audit of non-specialist occupational physician reports.
audits.st: Modified Sheffield Assessment Instrument for Letters (SAIL(OH))
audits.f: 159/200 (80%) reports from non-specialists; 87% or more of non-specialist reports rated 'satisfactory' or 'above expected' on each question; mean overall score (out of 10) was 6.8 for non-specialists vs 7.3 for specialists.

audits.t: Implementing Screening Guidelines for Preeclampsia Prevention in a Birth Center: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Preeclampsia risk screening in birth centre care
audits.st: Preeclampsia screening guidelines recommending low-dose aspirin (LDA) initiation for high-risk women
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Screening for preeclampsia risk factors in women at 12-28 weeks' gestation with initiation of low-dose aspirin for those at high risk
audits.r2: Screening significantly increased low-dose aspirin use; preeclampsia incidence showed a moderate (non-statistically-significant) reduction; LDA use showed a large (non-statistically-significant) reduction in preeclampsia diagnoses.

audits.t: Provider Prescription Drug Monitoring Program Utilization and Self-Auditing-A Pilot Study.
audits.tp: Opioid prescribing and prescription drug monitoring programme (PDMP) self-auditing
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 81% of participants had never conducted a self-audit prior to the intervention; mean monthly opioid prescriptions written 32.28 (range 3-142).
audits.c: Educational presentation on the PDMP followed by providers conducting a self-audit using the PDMP
audits.r2: 85.7% planned to increase self-auditing use; mean monthly opioid prescriptions 32.26 (range 3-149), essentially unchanged.

audits.t: Establishing local diagnostic reference levels for mini C-arm use in upper limb surgery - A step towards national audit.
audits.tp: Diagnostic reference levels for upper limb mini C-arm fluoroscopy
audits.st: No existing national diagnostic reference level for upper limb mini C-arm use; study proposes local levels as a step towards this (Public Health England requires multiple patients, rooms and hospitals for a national DRL)
audits.f: 1719 closed procedures: median dose area product 0.48 cGycm2, median screening time 7s; 1054 open procedures: median dose area product 1.88 cGycm2, median screening time 28s; proposed local DRLs (third quartile) of 0.82 cGycm2/11s (closed) and 3.07 cGycm2/40s (open).

audits.t: Audit of homograft valve bank.
audits.st: American Association of Tissue Banks recommendations and Transplantation of Human Organs Act 1994 for donor selection, procurement, sterilisation and preservation
audits.f: 546 (32%) homografts rejected; 967 (56.7%) used in procedures; 154 (16%) antibiotic preserved, 813 (84%) cryopreserved.

audits.t: Polypharmacy and drug interactions amongst cirrhotic patients discharged from a tertiary center: Results from a national quality improvement audit.
audits.tp: Polypharmacy and drug interactions in cirrhotic patients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 168/181 (92.8%) used at least one medicine, mean 7.8±3.1 drugs/patient; 102 (56.3%) had polypharmacy; 6 (3.3%) had class X, 30 (16.6%) class D, and 65 (35.9%) class C drug interactions.

audits.t: Perinatal death audit and classification of stillbirths in two provinces in Papua New Guinea: A retrospective analysis.
audits.st: Perinatal Problem Identification Program (PPIP) classification of avoidable factors in stillbirths
audits.f: Stillbirth rate 23 per 1000 births (59/2558); perinatal cause of death identified in 63% (37/59) - most commonly intrapartum asphyxia/traumatic breech birth (30%) and pre-eclampsia (19%); at least one avoidable factor identified in 95% (56/59) of stillbirths.

audits.t: Medical Nutrition Reimbursement in Singapore: Who Are the Patients Receiving MediFund Assistance? An Audit of Clinical Outcomes and Issues Pertaining to Reimbursement in a Public Hospital in Singapore.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median financial support 115 days (IQR 37-269); BMI increased after nutrition support (20.9±5.1 vs 20.4±5.3, p=0.012); malnourished patients decreased from 86.8% to 55.1%.

audits.t: Could a multidisciplinary regional audit identify avoidable factors and delays that contribute to stillbirths? A retrospective cohort study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 30% of stillbirths assessed as probably/possibly preventable; a delay by the healthcare system was identified in 15% of cases; possibly preventable stillbirth more common among non-Swedish-speaking women (p=0.03)
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team review of each stillbirth case

audits.t: Oral squamous cell carcinoma resection and neck dissection mortality: a 10-year national audit study.
audits.tp: Surgical mortality after oral squamous cell carcinoma resection
audits.st: Australian and New Zealand Audit of Surgical Mortality (ANZASM) structured independent peer case review of surgical deaths
audits.f: 25 deaths after oral squamous cell carcinoma resection identified; 44% cardiac-related, 40% respiratory-related; management issues identified in 14 cases (25 issues raised), 36% relating to the decision to operate.

audits.t: Translating Evidence-Based Guidelines into Practice-Are We Getting It Right? A Multi-Centre Prospective International Audit of Nutrition Care in Patients with Foregut Tumors (INFORM).
audits.tp: Nutrition care for foregut tumour patients vs evidence-based guidelines
audits.st: International evidence-based guidelines (EBGs) for nutrition care in head and neck/oesophageal cancer
audits.f: Adherence was good (≥80%) for baseline nutrition screening/assessment and nutrition prescription; moderate (60-80%) for validated tool use and pre-radiotherapy dietitian consultation; poor (<60%) for early post-operative nutrition support and ongoing dietetic consultation during/after radiotherapy

audits.t: Potentially preventable antepartum stillbirths in a high-resource setting: a prospective audit-based study.
audits.tp: Stillbirth care quality review (perinatal mortality audit)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Inadequate care identified in 56/524 (10.7%) fetal deaths; non-Italian women and pregnancies with fetal growth restriction had double the risk of inadequate care (aOR 2.0).

audits.t: An audit of health student immunisation at a University Department of Rural Health reveals the imperative for a coordinated approach.
audits.st: Australian Immunisation Handbook national recommendations for healthcare worker immunisation
audits.f: Around one-quarter (26%) of healthcare students provided evidence of immunisation in line with national standards.

audits.t: Systematic Suicide Audit: An Enhanced Method to Assess System Gaps and Mobilize Leaders for Prevention.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 31 recommendations generated across 13 of 14 cases, none of which had originally been made by the coroner; most common recommendations were professional training, mobile crisis teams and improved access to a family physician.

audits.t: Making every birth count: Outcomes of a perinatal mortality audit program.
audits.st: Perinatal Society of Australia and New Zealand (PSANZ) perinatal mortality audit guidelines
audits.f: Contributing factors identified in 46/65 (71%) deaths: 6 insignificant, 20 possibly related, 20 significantly related; 51.8% of stillbirths classified as unexplained.

audits.t: Extended Perinatal Mortality Audit in a Rural Hospital in India.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Stillbirth rate 11.8/1000 births, neonatal mortality rate 4.4/1000 livebirths, perinatal mortality rate 15.8/1000 births; leading antepartum stillbirth causes preeclampsia/eclampsia and abruptio placentae.

audits.t: An Audit of Lung Donor Pool: Optimal Current Donation Strategies and the Potential of Novel Time-Extended Donation After Circulatory Death Donation.
audits.tp: Lung donor pool identification and unrecognised donor opportunities
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 473 potential lung donors and 122 further time-extended DCD potential lung donors identified; only 2 traditional lung donors were missed under current practice.

audits.t: Calculation algorithms and penumbra: Underestimation of dose in organs at risk in dosimetry audits.
audits.tp: Radiotherapy dosimetry audit of organ-at-risk dose accuracy
audits.st: ACDS dosimetry audit comparing radiotherapy planning system calculated dose with measured dose (ion chamber, microdiamond, film, ion chamber array) in organs at risk
audits.f: Across 43 anthropomorphic spine plans and 1318 C-shaped target plans, Acuros XB-calculated plans underestimated dose to the spinal cord organ-at-risk by 5%-10% for SBRT spine cases and by 3%-10% for other C-shape-target audit cases compared with measurement; Monaco Monte Carlo plans were on average 7% colder than measurements.

audits.t: Audit of a Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy Course Within a Prison.
audits.tp: Mindfulness-based therapy for depression in prison
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Depression and anxiety levels reduced and mindfulness scores increased from start to end of the 8-week course.

audits.t: Implementing a Suicide Audit in Montreal: Taking Suicide Review Further to Make Concrete Recommendations for Suicide Prevention.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Five prevention recommendations generated, including mobile crisis teams, substance use disorder screening training, and universal access to a general practitioner.

audits.t: Perinatal mortality audit in a rural referral hospital in Tanzania to inform future interventions: A descriptive study.
audits.tp: Perinatal mortality audit and contributing factors
audits.st: WHO checklist for perinatal death review
audits.f: 62% had inadequate labour monitoring documentation; 12% had inadequate labour monitoring; Apgar <7 at 5 minutes, prematurity and meconium aspiration were top causes of neonatal death

audits.t: On-table hepatopancreatobiliary surgical consults for difficult cholecystectomies: A 7-year audit.
audits.tp: On-table hepatopancreatobiliary consults for difficult cholecystectomy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 18 (36%) patients had subtotal cholecystectomy; 15/48 (31%) required open conversion; 98% of consults were reactive rather than proactive.

audits.t: Unlocking the benefits of the Baveno VI guidance when screening for varices: an audit of clinical practice across London.
audits.st: Baveno VI consensus criteria for avoiding screening endoscopy in patients with compensated advanced chronic liver disease, based on platelet count and transient elastography
audits.f: 177/351 (50.43%) had a transient elastography test within the preceding 12 months; of these, 142/177 (80.23%) did not meet criteria for screening endoscopy, indicating avoidable procedures; transient elastography provision varied widely between sites.

audits.t: Auditing Management of Acute Pancreatitis Using Comprehensive Quality Indicators.
audits.st: 40 comprehensive quality indicators across acute pancreatitis management domains
audits.f: 28 of 40 quality indicators (70%) could be used to audit management retrospectively; medical service had lower adherence for indicators 12 (11% vs 22%, p=0.009), 14 (72% vs 88%, p=0.003) and 33 (83% vs 100%, p=0.006); surgical service had lower adherence for indicators 4, 5 and 6.

audits.t: The advanced life support base hospital audit for medical control in an emergency medical services system.
audits.tp: Advanced life support base hospital audit for medical control
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Semi-annual rigorous evaluation of ALS base hospital performance using objective written criteria.

audits.t: A medical audit of acute alcoholism and chronic alcoholism.
audits.tp: Medical audit of acute and chronic alcoholism management
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Description of medical audits performed for acute alcoholism (general medical service) and chronic alcoholism (rehabilitation unit).

audits.t: Improving the weekend spinal ward round at a major trauma centre.
audits.st: Local documentation standard for ward round entries
audits.f: 80% of encounters had inadequate documentation
audits.c: Weekend ward round proforma designed and introduced
audits.r2: Significant improvement in documentation in six of seven fields, maintained in four of seven fields at cycle 3 two years later

audits.t: Improving Access to Patient Education: an Audit of Extant Educational Materials.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Most materials found in Haematology (75), Genitourinary (74) and Gastrointestinal (57) clinics; most common topics were treatment (277), about cancer/disease (134) and symptom management (120); significant gaps for some diagnoses (e.g. 0 penile cancer materials vs 28 prostate cancer materials)

audits.t: Labeling of penicillin allergy in patients admitted to a tertiary hospital in Qatar: A retrospective audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 30/139 (21.5%) had clear documentation of the allergic reaction event; 20/139 (14.4%) received a penicillin-class antibiotic safely despite the allergy label

audits.t: coMpliAnce with evideNce-based cliniCal guidelines in the managemenT of acute biliaRy pancreAtitis): The MANCTRA-1 international audit.
audits.tp: Compliance with acute biliary pancreatitis guidelines (MANCTRA-1)
audits.st: Contemporary evidence-based guidelines for management of acute biliary pancreatitis (timing of index CT scan, prophylactic antibiotic use, early cholecystectomy)
audits.f: Overall poor compliance with evidence-based guidelines; discordant gaps found in optimal timing of index CT scan (6.1%), use of prophylactic antibiotics (44.2%), and implementation of early cholecystectomy strategies (29%), with wide variability by admitting speciality.

audits.t: Audit of cervical excision depth of large loop excision of the transformation zone procedures at Counties Manukau District Health Board.
audits.st: Public Health England 2020 Colposcopy Guidelines, target ≥95% correct excision depth
audits.f: 48% of LLETZ procedures had the correct excision depth relative to the ≥95% threshold, primarily due to excisions being too shallow (48% correct in type 2 and 86% in type 3 transformation zones).

audits.t: Improving health services for patients with extreme obesity requiring bariatric level care at Wellington Regional Hospital: a clinical audit.
audits.st: Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) national moving-and-handling and patient care best practice standards
audits.f: Prevalence of hospitalised patients requiring bariatric care 6.4%; 34.3% not identified by clinical teams as requiring bariatric support; 80% of beds and 83% of bathrooms failed the facility design standard; only 26.1% had a documented discharge plan.

audits.t: Review of maternal death audits in refugee camps in UNHCR East and Horn of Africa and Great Lakes Region, 2017-2019.
audits.tp: Quality of refugee maternal death audits
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Obstetric haemorrhage was leading direct cause (49%, including 77 postpartum haemorrhage cases); delays in care identified in 185 (97%) cases, most commonly delays in receiving care (81%)

audits.t: Audit of the Southern DHB B4 School hearing screening referral process: is there unmet need?
audits.tp: Childhood hearing screening referral pathway (B4 School Check)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Māori and Pasifika children were significantly less likely to pass the hearing screening tests; a mismatch was found between census and screening programme eligible-child estimates in Otago.

audits.t: UK audit of variation in nuclear medicine occupational exposure calculations in 2021.
audits.tp: Nuclear medicine occupational exposure dose estimation consistency
audits.st: UK Ionising Radiations Regulations 2017 (IRR17) requirement to evaluate the magnitude of doses in radiation risk assessments and accidental exposure scenarios
audits.f: Wide variation found in estimated exposures across most of the 15 foreseeable scenarios (except internal exposure); variation often exceeded the relevant threshold for classification and annual dose limits, mainly due to differences in methods, models and assumptions used.

audits.t: The cost of rejection: an internal audit of the clinical genetics service active triage pathway at CHI Crumlin, Ireland.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 128/1581 (8.3%) of referrals rejected, mostly (75%) for non-enclosure of family/patient genetic report; follow-up information requested on 78% of rejected referrals, received in 57%; estimated cost of rejection process was €11,878.4/year for the department.

audits.t: Donor Safety, Discrepancies Between Practice and Theory: Analysis of the Polish Supreme Audit Office's Report.
audits.st: Polish Supreme Audit Office inspection of legal/procedural compliance for genetic testing
audits.f: Shortcomings identified in formalities accompanying testing, patient documentation and personal data protection, including lack of proper consent

audits.t: A novel allocation strategy for the difficult-to-allocate donor: audit of deceased donor kidneys utilised for preemptive recipients within Western Australia.
audits.tp: Novel kidney allocation strategy for preemptive recipients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Transplantation using a novel same-state preemptive-recipient allocation pathway (used only when no well-matched dialysis-dependent recipient was available) was associated with good clinical and immunological outcomes.

audits.t: Sports foods are not all they shake up to be. An audit of formulated supplementary sports food products and packaging in Australian retail environments.
audits.st: Mandatory food packaging/labelling attribute requirements for Formulated Supplementary Sports Foods
audits.f: Only 275/558 products displayed correct mandatory packaging attributes; only 184 appeared to display correct energy value based on listed macronutrients; 19 different sweeteners identified

audits.t: Self-Assessment Tool and Clinical Audits: A Way to Manage Organ Donation and Transplantation in Hospital Settings.
audits.tp: Self-assessment tool for hospital organ donation and transplantation management
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: The self-assessment tool (SAT), scoring 5 components across 30 questions, classified hospital donation management as insufficient, basic, intermediate or advanced, and results were compared with external audit results.

audits.t: Perioperative anaphylaxis management and testing: a quaternary centre audit.
audits.tp: Perioperative anaphylaxis management and allergy testing referral quality
audits.st: Australian and New Zealand Anaesthetic Allergy Group (ANZAAG) guidelines
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Hepatitis B infection prevention: Audit of selected healthcare facilities in the Greater Accra Region, Ghana.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B infection prevention at healthcare facilities
audits.st: Recommended strategies, structures and programmes for hepatitis B virus (HBV) prevention
audits.f: Overall adherence mean score 37.02 (95% CI 33.98-40.05); statistically significant difference in adherence between facility categories (F=9.698)

audits.t: Harnessing the Benefits of the Nutrition Care Process Quality Evaluation and Standardization Tool: A National Auditing Initiative to Improve Quality of Documentation.
audits.st: NCP QUEST validated audit instrument for Nutrition Care Process documentation quality
