audits.f: Mean NCP QUEST score 13.71 for nonuser facilities and 13.88 for user facilities.
audits.c: Monthly national digital training on NCP QUEST provided to registered dietitian nutritionists
audits.r2: Mean score for nonuser facilities 14.00 (no significant improvement, p=0.69); user facilities improved significantly to 17.65 (p≤0.001); word count of assessment notes fell significantly across all facilities (p=0.04).

audits.t: Complication profile in a cochlear implantation- surgical audit in a large study population of low socio-economic status in a developing country.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall major complication rate 9.04% (including 6.0% device failure, 3.04% excluding device failure); minor complication rate 6%.

audits.t: [Inter-radiopharmacy audit, a tool for individual and collective progress].
audits.st: A 125-item internally designed evaluation tool applied to the whole radiopharmacy activity
audits.f: Internal audit vs cross-audit comparison: unit 1 had 12 items rated differently (4 of 10 non-conformities missed internally were rated critical by the cross-auditor); unit 2 had 15 items rated differently, 2 of which were critical.

audits.t: Quality audits of nuclear medicine practices in a middle-income African setting.
audits.tp: Nuclear medicine department quality management compliance
audits.st: IAEA Quality Management Audits in Nuclear Medicine (QUANUM) programme
audits.f: Site A conformed 67% (247/370), Site B 60% (205/342), Site C 75% (259/345), Site D 48% (166/349); 125 overall recommendations made

audits.t: [Study of factors associated with maternal mortality by the audit method in the Segou region].
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Direct obstetric causes accounted for 51.23% of deaths, led by haemorrhage (17.08%) and eclampsia (14.63%); 31.71% of deaths were judged preventable; main risk factors were delayed care, referral/evacuation delay, diagnostic errors, and non-availability of blood.

audits.t: Cochlear implant referral patterns in the UK suggest a postcode lottery with inequitable access for older adults; results of a pilot audit in five Audiology sites.
audits.st: UK cochlear implant audiometric candidacy criteria
audits.f: 64% (521/810) of potentially eligible adults were considered for cochlear implant referral, varying by site from 50% to 83%; 24% (123/521) declined referral; median age of those not considered was 80 vs 73 for those considered.

audits.t: Implementation of a Patient-Reported Outcome Measure: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) implementation in rehabilitation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Participatory implementation of the Patient-Specific Functional Scale (PSFS) using the Institute for Health Care Improvement Model for Improvement, with chart audits and clinician feedback
audits.r2: Increased collection of the PSFS and incorporation into patient-centred goal setting; opportunistic clinician feedback found the single PROM useful and acceptable.

audits.t: Characteristics and outcome of patients referred to a specialized outpatient clinic for the management of malnutrition: A retrospective audit.
audits.st: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN) guidelines for medical nutrition therapy
audits.f: 74% of patients had severe malnutrition; consistency between the decided medical nutrition therapy and ESPEN guidelines was moderate at 47.1%; 23.1% of patients died during follow-up (median 70 days).

audits.t: Audit and Inventory of Federal Law Enforcement Agency Tactical Medic Bags.
audits.st: Authorised medical protocols aligned with Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC) and Tactical Emergency Casualty Care (TECC) guidelines
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Tuberculose résistante au Burkina Faso : audit organisationnel et enquête de satisfaction.
audits.st: Agence nationale d'accréditation et d'évaluation en santé (ANAES) accreditation standards, adapted for resistant tuberculosis care
audits.f: Overall audit score was 63.2% for CHUYO and 59.8% for CLAT; problems related to intake/equipment/infrastructure, patient rights and information, and management/administration.

audits.t: Intraoperative use of processed electroencephalogram in a quaternary center: a quality improvement audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Educational programme for anaesthesiologists, residents and technicians on intraoperative EEG monitoring (May-June 2022)
audits.r2: 233/379 (61%) cases had processed EEG monitoring; use ranged from 100% (cardiothoracic surgery) to 0% (neuroradiology).

audits.t: Audit of a monitoring service for free phenytoin.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Free level determinations comprised 20% of all phenytoin assays; total phenytoin was below the normal optimum range in 61% of cases, but free levels were probably therapeutic or above in 70% of cases; dosage adjustments were followed more often when the doctor had requested the free level.

audits.t: Therapeutic drug monitoring--the need for audit?
audits.st: Established therapeutic ranges for digoxin, lithium, theophylline, phenytoin, carbamazepine and phenobarbitone
audits.f: 56% of digoxin levels were within the therapeutic range (25% potentially toxic); 50% of lithium levels were below 4mg/L; only 29% of theophylline and 32% of phenytoin concentrations were within their established ranges; adequate clinical information was supplied in only around 20% of theophylline/phenytoin requests.

audits.t: First-line treatment with ceftriaxone for <i>Neisseria gonorrhoeae</i> infection less likely to be prescribed to patients with a penicillin allergy label: a retrospective audit of medical records.
audits.tp: First-line antibiotic prescribing for gonorrhoea and penicillin allergy labels
audits.st: First-line ceftriaxone treatment guidelines for Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection
audits.f: Cases with a penicillin allergy label were more likely to receive antibiotics other than ceftriaxone (7/41, 17.1%) than cases without the label (8/687, 1.2%); a validated allergy assessment tool was applied in 68.3% (28/41) of labelled cases.

audits.t: Appropriateness of gentamicin therapeutic drug monitoring at a Middle Eastern tertiary hospital setting: a retrospective evaluation and quality audit.
audits.st: Evidence-based criteria for gentamicin therapeutic drug monitoring (indication, sampling times, post-analytical actions)
audits.f: Overall appropriateness achieved in 50% (29/58); inappropriate sampling time in 44.8% (26/58); inappropriate post-analytical actions in 22.4% (13/58)

audits.t: Lost in Transition: Insights from a Retrospective Chart Audit on Nutrition Care Practices for Older Australians with Malnutrition Transitioning from Hospital to Home.
audits.tp: Nutrition care transition from hospital to home
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 10% had nutrition care recommendations documented in the electronic discharge summary; post-discharge oral nutrition supplementation offered to 46%, accepted by 34%; only 23% attended dietetics follow-up within 6 months

audits.t: Why do patients refuse hospital meals? Reflections on the nutritionDay Audit at the University Hospital in Krakow.
audits.tp: Hospital meal refusal and nutritional status deterioration (nutritionDay Audit)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 61% of patients reported weight loss prior to the current hospital stay; 25 patients did not consume a whole portion of their main meal on the audit day; around 17% of complaints could be resolved within the ward.

audits.t: Adherence to New Zealand's Major Trauma Destination Policy: an audit of current practice.
audits.tp: Major trauma destination policy adherence (prehospital triage)
audits.st: New Zealand Major Trauma Destination Policy (MTDP)
audits.f: Overall adherence to the MTDP was 94%; adherence was 98.9% (86/87) for cases not requiring an advanced-level trauma centre versus 61.5% (8/13) for cases that did require one.

audits.t: [The network of the EASY-NET programme: a contribution to knowledge on the effectiveness of audit&feedback].
audits.tp: Effectiveness of audit and feedback interventions (EASY-NET network)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Measurable improvement from audit and feedback (A&F) interventions was observed across settings (chronic disease management, emergency care, rehabilitation, oncology, childbirth/caesarean section), more in processes than outcomes.

audits.t: An audit of the detection and management of small-for-gestational age babies.
audits.tp: Detection and management of small-for-gestational-age babies
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 34/129 (26%) SGA babies were identified antenatally; for every two correctly identified SGA babies there were three false positives; management appeared unrelated to test results.

audits.t: Implementation of maternal death audits and changes in maternal health care in Cambodia, 2010-2017.
audits.st: WHO maternal death audit/surveillance and response guidance
audits.f: 68.2% had antenatal care; 55.3% gave birth in a facility; 73% received a prophylactic uterotonic; quality of MDA recommendations was 2.8% adequate in 2011
audits.c: Strengthening of MDA implementation and reporting between 2010 and 2017, following the national MDA programme instituted in 2004
audits.r2: 90.0% had antenatal care (p=0.004); 81.6% gave birth in a facility (p=0.01); 95.7% received a prophylactic uterotonic; quality of MDA recommendations improved to 42% in 2018

audits.t: Implementation of the WHO Standardized Emergency Unit Form: Trauma at Bashair Teaching Hospital.
audits.tp: Trauma documentation using WHO Standardized Emergency Unit Form
audits.st: WHO Standardized Emergency Unit Form: Trauma
audits.f: Case coverage (documentation using the form) 31% in first week, improving to 67% after
audits.c: Implementation of the WHO Standardized Emergency Unit Form: Trauma, piloted in one unit with training then generalised to all surgical units
audits.r2: Second cycle coverage 84-91%; final cycle affected by doctor strikes fell to 53% then recovered to 78%; mean time to initial assessment reduced from 39±7.2 to 27±5.8 minutes (p=0.023)

audits.t: An audit of completeness of Road to Health Booklet at a community health centre in South Africa.
audits.tp: Completeness of Road to Health Booklet documentation
audits.st: Expected full (100%) completion of the Road to Health Booklet (RTHB) sections
audits.f: Overall completeness was 40.3%; no section was 100% completed; HIV status not recorded for 49.4%; developmental screening only 17.2% completed; oral health only 1.6% partially completed

audits.t: Audit of linkage to care and administration of immunoprophylaxis to infants born to mothers with chronic hepatitis B infection at Monash Health 2014-2022.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B immunoprophylaxis timing for infants of infected mothers
audits.st: WHO recommendation for hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) within 12 hours and birth-dose vaccine within 24 hours of birth
audits.f: 99.7% received both HBIG and birth dose vaccine; 97.4% received vaccine within 12h; 88.3% received HBIG within the recommended 12-hour window; maternal referral to specialist care 83.1%

audits.t: Getting the timing right: An implementation study and pre post audit to implement evidence-based parathyroid scan guidelines.
audits.tp: Parathyroid scintigraphy scan timing guideline compliance
audits.st: European Association of Nuclear Medicine (EANM) guidelines for timing of parathyroid scintigraphy scan phases
audits.f: Compliance with EANM guideline scan timing was 18% pre-intervention.
audits.c: A3-framework implementation strategy addressing capability (education), opportunity (updated policies/procedures) and motivation (feedback and celebration of success)
audits.r2: Compliance with EANM guideline scan timing improved to 98% post-intervention (OR 205.3, 95% CI 24.9-1691.7).

audits.t: Reducing Waste During Midurethral Slings: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Surgical waste reduction during midurethral sling surgery
audits.st: Local target to decrease surgical waste during MUS surgery
audits.f: Preaudit median weight of waste per case 5.6 kg; 10 of 21 nondisposable instruments and 7 of 26 disposable items had utilisation rate <20%
audits.c: Updated MUS surgical tray and created a custom surgical pack including only items with utilisation rate >20%
audits.r2: Median weight of waste per case decreased to 4.9 kg (P=0.04); average $348.93 saved per case

audits.t: Data quality assessment in the SWEDEHEART registry: Insights from serial audits on completeness and accuracy.
audits.tp: SWEDEHEART registry data quality audit (completeness and accuracy)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall data completeness and accuracy audited against electronic medical records at 4 time-points from 2011 to 2018.
audits.r2: Data completeness was 99.1% (ACS), 99.2% (PCI) and 94.5% (CR); accuracy versus medical records was over 95.0% for all subregistries at all four audits.

audits.t: Which hospital services are most overused? Results from a medical audit.
audits.tp: Appropriateness of hospital service ordering (utilisation review)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 21% of clinical services ordered by house staff were judged unwarranted; nuclear medicine services were most overordered, followed by laboratory tests; laboratory services accounted for 78% of all unwarranted orders.

audits.t: Aotearoa New Zealand cochlear implant programmes equity audit: addressing disparities and equity for Māori with severe and profound hearing loss.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: No significant difference between Māori and non-Māori in acceptance-for-surgery rates or time from acceptance to surgery; Māori children and adults had a higher rate of proceeding to surgery than non-Māori.

audits.t: A perioperative audit of smoking, smoking cessation advice and pharmacological management of nicotine dependence: Are guidelines enough?
audits.st: Australian and New Zealand College of Anaesthetists (ANZCA) guidelines on perioperative smoking management
audits.f: 46% of smokers did not report receiving advice to stop smoking; 83% did not think smoking might cause a problem with their surgery/anaesthetic; nicotine replacement therapy used by 11% pre-operatively and 7% post-operatively.

audits.t: A Culturally Informed Audit of Psychological Formulations Completed in Prison and Community Settings on the Offender Personality Disorder Pathway.
audits.st: London Pathways Partnership (LPP) formulation audit tool and London Pathways Unit culturally informed formulation (LPU-CIF) audit tool, both with a defined threshold of adequacy
audits.f: First custodial audit of 23 formulations scored on the LPP and LPU-CIF tools; both tools showed mean scores below the threshold of adequacy.
audits.c: Training on culturally informed formulation implemented between the two custodial audits
audits.r2: Second custodial audit of 24 formulations; LPU-CIF scores increased across all items compared with the first audit, but remained below the threshold of adequacy.

audits.t: Results of the international audit for faecal incontinence on behalf of the European Society of Coloproctology (ESCP) collaborating group.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Prevalence of faecal incontinence was 6.3% of clinic attendance; in the surgical audit (n=363), 61.1% had received previous treatment; sacral neuromodulation (28.9%) and sphincteroplasty (22.0%) were the most common of 395 procedures performed.

audits.t: A national audit of head injury discharge advice.
audits.st: NICE head injury guideline (NG232); target compliance score of 0.95 on a standardised proforma
audits.f: None of the 99 leaflets (0/99) complied with all aspects of NICE guidance; mean score 0.42 out of 1, below the 0.95 target; safety information on surgically-relevant deterioration met the 95% compliance target, but concussion management advice was generally poor; 50.5% (50/99) advised against returning to activities 'until feeling completely back to normal', contradicting current guidance.

audits.t: UK audit of the interoperability of ordered-subset expectation-maximisation reconstruction algorithms.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Excellent agreement found among platforms offering similar reconstruction methods; one platform could not perform a true 'pencil-beam' OSEM reconstruction and results varied with different manufacturer data.

audits.t: Differences in call profiles, interventions and physician staffing between ground and helicopter emergency medical services in Austria : A sub-analysis of the Austrian Emergency Day 2024 audit.
audits.tp: Ground vs helicopter EMS call profiles
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Primary calls proportion was lower for HEMS than GEMS (71.7% vs 83.7%); interfacility transfer proportion higher for HEMS (18.3% vs 4.7%)

audits.t: Emergency physician attended calls that could have been covered by advanced emergency medical technicians in Austria : Results of the Austrian Emergency Day 2025 audit.
audits.tp: Emergency physician calls potentially manageable by advanced EMTs
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 53.4% (95% CI 46.8-60.0%) of emergency calls and 48.0% (95% CI 28.4-67.6%) of interhospital transfers judged manageable by advanced emergency medical technicians (AEMTs); AEMTs correctly assessed severity in 88.4% of cases

audits.t: Improving Compliance With Safe Sleep Guidelines for Vulnerable Patients in a Community Safety Net Hospital Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
audits.tp: Safe sleep practice compliance in NICU
audits.st: National safe sleep guidelines (supine, flat empty crib, no loose swaddling) for infants >32 weeks
audits.f: Baseline weekly compliance 58% (0.58)
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles: resident/fellow education and EMR smart phrase (cycle 1), nurse education and non-recline cribs (cycle 2), bedside reminder signs (cycle 3)
audits.r2: Mean compliance increased to 91% (0.91), exceeding the target of 85%

audits.t: Early protocol computed tomography scan in asymptomatic high-risk patients diagnosed with pancreatic fistula after pancreatoduodenectomy: Results of a prospective audit.
audits.tp: Early CT scan protocol for high-risk pancreatic fistula
audits.st: Local protocol: early protocol CT scan in asymptomatic postoperative pancreatic fistula patients with clinically relevant score ≥5 after pancreatoduodenectomy
audits.f: 149/437 (34.1%) developed postoperative pancreatic fistula; managed without protocol CT scanning; patients with clinically relevant score ≥5 were more likely to progress to clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula.
audits.c: From September 2022, protocol CT scan introduced for asymptomatic high-risk (clinically relevant score ≥5) postoperative pancreatic fistula patients after pancreatoduodenectomy
audits.r2: Implementation of protocol CT scans was associated with earlier CT scans and more invasive interventions, but this did not translate into improved short-term outcomes.

audits.t: SENTRY - A Systems-Based Model for Quality and Safety Surveillance with Continuous Quality Improvement in Emergency Care.
audits.tp: ED systems-based quality and safety surveillance
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean/median time from ED arrival to prostacyclin reconciliation decreased by half after automated pharmacist consults; aspiration-related ED safety events fell from an average of three per year (2023-2024) to zero (2024-2025); same-day specialty pathways credited with averting more than 27 inpatient admissions over 7 months.
audits.c: Introduction of SENTRY: automated pharmacist consults, automated aspiration precautions/NPO standing orders, AI-based triage tool, same-day specialty pathways, nurse-driven safety rounds.

audits.t: Cleft Care India Study: A National Audit on Patients with Non-Syndromic Unilateral Cleft Lip and Palate Patients. Part 2: Oral Health Outcomes.
audits.tp: Oral health in cleft lip and palate patients (Cleft Care India)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 36% of 5-year-olds, 41% of 12-year-olds and 29% of 20-year-olds had never visited a dentist; mean dmft/DMFT was 5.6, 3.4 and 3.0 respectively; untreated active caries in 53%, 34% and 14% of the three age groups.

audits.t: Evaluating EEG Requisition Quality and Clinical Factors Influencing Outcomes: A Retrospective Audit.
audits.tp: EEG requisition quality and diagnostic yield
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: EEGs detected abnormalities in ~40% of cases; 56% of requisition forms were incomplete; requisition completeness varied by specialty, with neurologists least likely to complete forms; indications such as 'neuro-prognostication' had 100% yield, 'syncope/presyncope' 12.8%.

audits.t: Medication adherence in adults with chronic disease in an outpatient rural clinic: a best practice implementation project.
audits.tp: Medication adherence best practice implementation in chronic disease
audits.st: JBI Best Practice Evidence Summary recommendations (8 best practice items) for promoting medication adherence
audits.f: Pre-audit data revealed variable compliance with best practices
audits.c: Staff education on best practices, scheduling adjustments for more provider time, patient resources about prescribed medication
audits.r2: Post-audit showed improvements in five of eight criteria

audits.t: Establishing and Improving Role 2 Documentation Performance: A 2-Part Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Trauma documentation completeness in military Role 2 care
audits.st: Joint Trauma System (JTS) Clinical Practice Guidelines and key performance indicators for documentation completeness, accuracy and clinical relevance
audits.f: Self-reported provider confidence and ability improved significantly across all 4 competency domains after training (P not given); structured audit of documentation found training improved confidence but did not fully translate into consistent documentation practice.
audits.c: Targeted training for providers, nurses and corpsmen on JTS documentation requirements and structured handoff tools (MIST, I-PASS, SBAR).

audits.t: Systematic standardization improves compliance and performance across a large IVF network through audits and digitally enabled quality management.
audits.tp: Compliance with laboratory audit checkpoints across an IVF network
audits.st: 149 internal laboratory audit checkpoints across 5 categories (laboratory management, process, KPIs, equipment, documentation)
audits.f: Mean compliance rate 74.4% ± 7.6% pre-audit
audits.c: Development of a laboratory audit programme with trained specialist audit team, cloud-based dashboards, scorecards and monthly growth charts
audits.r2: Mean compliance rate increased to 80.1% ± 7.8% (P=0.002); blastocyst rate increased from 51.2% ± 7.6% to 56.5% ± 8.2%

audits.t: Impact of audit on preventive measures.
audits.tp: Preventive care recording in general practice
audits.st: not reported (locally agreed preventive-care recording measures, no named external guideline)
audits.f: Cervical cytology recorded 56%; rubella immunity 28%; polio immunity (adults) 15%; completed primary immunisation 68%; recorded blood pressure 53%; smoking information 22%.
audits.c: Postgraduate education course involving audit, undertaken between the two reviews.
audits.r2: Cervical cytology 64%; rubella immunity 40%; polio immunity (adults) 21%; completed primary immunisation 78%; recorded blood pressure 61%; smoking information 30%.

audits.t: An audit of requests for therapeutic drug monitoring of digoxin: problems and pitfalls.
audits.tp: Appropriateness of digoxin therapeutic drug monitoring requests
audits.st: not reported (locally defined formal criteria for appropriate request, recognition and action on digoxin levels)
audits.f: Reason for requesting the test could not be determined in 165/200 (82.5%); only 73/200 (36.5%) of results were adequately recognised; about 1 in 4 results followed by an inappropriate decision.

audits.t: An audit of therapeutic drug monitoring procedures--use of theophylline assay services.
audits.tp: Appropriateness of theophylline therapeutic drug monitoring
audits.st: not reported (locally defined categorisation of subtherapeutic/therapeutic/potentially toxic assay values)
audits.f: 60% of theophylline assay results were within the therapeutic range at the time of sampling; only 38% of samples were taken under steady-state conditions; significant delay in relaying results to clinicians.
audits.c: Procedural changes to sampling times, analytical techniques, recording and conveying of results, and cooperative policies between pharmacy and clinical biochemistry departments.

audits.t: A prospective audit of total parenteral nutrition at a major teaching hospital.
audits.tp: Total parenteral nutrition use and compliance with hospital guidelines
audits.st: Hospital guidelines for TPN initiation (compliance criteria not further specified)
audits.f: Deviations from approved hospital guidelines for TPN initiation were common; 18% of men and 13% of women were underweight by BMI; 36% were malnourished by serum albumin criteria; 29% of patients died; ICUs accounted for 57.7% of TPN use.

audits.t: An audit of fatal acute pancreatitis.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 15% of fatal cases were post-mortem diagnoses; 72% had respiratory and 67% renal complications; only 34% admitted to intensive care; biochemical severity criteria (pO2 and calcium) analysed in about 80% of cases; only 3 of 14 patients with gallstone pancreatitis had ERCP.

audits.t: Audit of sickness absence and fitness-for-work referrals.
audits.tp: Sickness absence and fitness-for-work referral documentation quality
audits.st: Expected completeness of referral and consultation documentation for sickness absence/fitness-for-work assessments (internal peer-review criteria, no external named standard)
audits.f: Referral record adequately specified or quantified long-term absence in 90% and 84% of relevant cases respectively, but only 12% of referral records described the job/task; physicians' response rate on likely date of return to work was 96% but lower for other items; response times did not correlate with completeness.

audits.t: EEG requests in paediatrics: an audit.
audits.st: Introduced guidelines and recommendations for EEG request criteria
audits.f: Inadequate clinical information provided in requests; 40% of requests considered unnecessary; approximately 50% of clinicians felt EEG could diagnose epilepsy.
audits.c: Introduction of guidelines and recommendations on EEG requesting
audits.r2: Inadequate clinical information persisted in the second survey; findings on request necessity and clinician beliefs were similar to before guidelines were introduced.

audits.t: Dietetic audit--a giant step for nutritional care. The approach at Brooke Army Medical Center.
audits.tp: Dietetic audit programme for diabetes nutritional care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Quality improvement in action: development of a tool.
audits.tp: Child anaemia care against public health nursing standards
audits.st: not reported (established standards of care for childhood anaemia management, locally defined)
audits.f: Audit identified conflicts in the established protocols of the county health department and an unexpectedly high prevalence of childhood anaemia.

audits.t: Towards improved perinatal care--perinatal audit.
audits.st: not reported (internal avoidability review of perinatal deaths)
audits.f: Perinatal mortality rate (PNMR) 14.6/1000.
audits.c: Improved antenatal care availability/acceptance, improved antenatal and intrapartum fetal surveillance, advances in neonatal care.
audits.r2: PNMR declined to 8.9/1000 (5.7/1000 excluding lethal congenital malformations); review found standard of care could have been improved in a third of cases (83/235).

audits.t: An audit of the handling of medical negligence complaints by a health board.
audits.st: Wilson Report recommendations on complaints handling
audits.f: Potential identified for reducing complaints proceeding to litigation through prompt handling; A&E and Obstetrics and Gynaecology carried greatest relative risk of claims and greatest difficulty returning case notes/reports quickly.

audits.t: Audit of pre-employment assessments by occupational health departments in the National Health Service.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Most common assessment method was self-administered questionnaire alone (49.4%); 98% of applicants assessed as 'fit for work'; 1.3% 'fit with restriction'; 0.7% 'unfit'; most common reasons for rejection were abnormal body mass index (40%), skin conditions (21.5%) and psychiatric conditions (10.8%).

audits.t: A continuing quality improvement (CQI) approach to improving the results of treatment in intussusception.
audits.tp: Continuing quality improvement in intussusception management
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit incorporating avoidability and appropriate intervention can significantly decrease perinatal mortality.
audits.st: not reported (ICA - Identification, Cause, Avoidable factor - Solution method of perinatal audit)
audits.f: Potentially avoidable factors identified in almost 50% of perinatal deaths (assessed in second year of study); major causes were intrapartum trauma, intrapartum asphyxia and infection.
audits.c: Appropriate intervention based on identified avoidable factors.
audits.r2: Appropriate intervention lowered the perinatal mortality rate by 23% (P value not given).

audits.t: An audit of occupational medicine consultation records.
audits.st: Standard for completeness of occupational health consultation and referral records (internally defined audit criteria)
audits.f: Audit not possible for 58/313 (19%) as records could not be found; shortcomings found in referral/consultation records; 'career' occupational physicians recorded specific diagnoses in 91% of consultations vs 67% for 'non-career' physicians (P<0.0001), and occupational implications in 86% vs 74% (P<0.0001).
audits.c: Prospective internal audit commenced within one health board, 9 months after the external audit
audits.r2: Multivariate analysis showed a highly significant improvement in recording of occupational implications associated with the internal re-audit, though the improvement was smaller than the independent difference from physicians' career status.

audits.t: Multicentre audit of death from acute pancreatitis.
audits.tp: Death from acute pancreatitis, assessment quality
audits.st: Use of Ranson's criteria for severity assessment and computed tomography in the investigation of acute pancreatitis
audits.f: 57 deaths (9%); diagnosis reached in 50 patients (88%) before death and 7 (12%) at autopsy; 21 patients (42%) had been inadequately evaluated by Ranson's criteria; only 22/50 (44%) with a premortem diagnosis had a CT scan; of 26 infection-related deaths, 15 had CT but only 9 underwent necrosectomy or surgical drainage.

audits.t: A computer-based approach to quality improvement for telephone triage in a community AIDS clinic.
audits.tp: Telephone triage documentation in an AIDS clinic
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Retrospective chart audit identified difficulties accessing relevant clinical data and a large amount of missing documentation for telephone triage encounters.
audits.c: Development of a computer-based telephone triage system with performance standards and guidelines (proposed).

audits.t: Who is ordering all those cyclosporin concentrations and how do they use them? An audit of cyclosporin therapeutic drug monitoring.
audits.tp: Appropriateness of cyclosporin therapeutic drug monitoring actions
audits.st: not reported (locally defined audit criteria: action predictable from stated therapeutic range, or justified by clinical considerations)
audits.f: 246/347 (71%) of results fulfilled audit criteria; 75% of concentrations were for the cardiopulmonary unit, of which 66% fulfilled criteria.

audits.t: Regional audit of pedestrian accident care.
audits.tp: Prehospital and ED trauma care in pedestrian accidents
audits.st: Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) treatment protocols for prehospital and emergency department trauma care
audits.f: Of 125 patients arriving at hospital alive, only 38% of unconscious patients had a cervical collar applied and only 67% were intubated; 34% of those transferred for neurosurgical care were not intubated; TRISS analysis showed 32% of deaths and 12% of survivors were unexpected.

audits.t: An audit of therapeutic drug monitoring of anticonvulsants.
audits.tp: Appropriateness of anticonvulsant therapeutic drug monitoring requests
audits.st: Expected appropriate clinical indication and consultant-level oversight for anticonvulsant therapeutic drug monitoring requests (implicit local standard, no named external guideline)
audits.f: Only 18.7% of requests originated from the adult neurology department; 90% ordered by junior medical staff (only 10% by consultants); approximately 50% were 'routine' with no satisfactory clinical reason given; tendency to manipulate doses on drug levels alone without clinical context.

audits.t: Management of asplenic patients in South Buckinghamshire: an audit of local practice.
audits.tp: Immunisation and antibiotic prophylaxis of asplenic patients
audits.st: not reported (local programme encouraging immunisation against pneumococcal, meningococcal and Hib infection in asplenic patients since 1992, plus issue of an 'alert' card)
audits.f: Vaccine uptake: pneumococcal 91%, meningococcal 80%, Hib 79%; 23% advised prophylactic antibiotics immediately post-splenectomy; 9% taking prophylaxis at time of analysis; alert cards distributed to 88% of eligible patients; 34 different antibiotic regimens recommended for adults.

audits.t: Audit of referral and explant diagnoses in lung transplantation: a pathologic study of lungs removed for parenchymal disease.
audits.tp: Diagnostic concordance between referral and explant pathology in lung transplantation
audits.st: Quality indicator: concordance between pre-transplant clinical/referral diagnosis and final pathological diagnosis on explanted lungs
audits.f: 29 significant discrepancies or additional features identified; discrepancy rate 19% (12/65) in single lung recipients and 16% (17/109) in heart-lung recipients; unsuspected diagnoses included tuberculosis (8, four active), sarcoidosis (9, six unsuspected) and veno-occlusive disease (3).

audits.t: Preventable prehospital trauma deaths in a Hellenic urban health region: an audit of prehospital trauma care.
audits.st: not reported (clinical assessor judgement of preventability using autopsy, toxicology and injury scoring)
audits.f: 4 (4.87%) deaths judged 'definitely preventable' and 35 (42.65%) 'possibly preventable'; 24 (29.26%) had a survival probability >0.5.

audits.t: An audit of the cochlear implant service in Manchester.
audits.tp: Cochlear implant service quality and satisfaction
audits.st: Local standard: patient satisfaction and information-provision expectations for the cochlear implant service (no external named target)
audits.f: 78% of patients felt the implant gave as much or more benefit than expected; areas for improvement identified: more written information, reduced waiting times for first appointment, more information on surgical risks, and more auditory training instruction for family/friends.
audits.c: Clinical practice and service provision for cochlear implantation modified as a result of the audit findings (not further specified)

audits.t: Audit of the distraction test of hearing at about 8 months of age: results of a survey of Scottish health boards.
audits.tp: Feasibility of auditing infant hearing distraction testing
audits.st: Hall Report 'Health for all Children' recommendation of distraction testing at 8 months
audits.f: All boards regarded the test as worthwhile; variation found in attention to quality standards (technique, recording, equipment, training); only one board could realistically audit the test at all stages using routinely collected data.

audits.t: An audit of BCG immunisation and tuberculin skin testing in Scotland. Scottish BCG Study Group.
audits.tp: BCG immunisation and tuberculin testing practice
audits.st: UK national policy of BCG vaccination for tuberculin-negative schoolchildren and high-risk groups (in place since 1954)
audits.f: Only 6/15 (40%) Health Boards immunised all tuberculin-negative children; all boards immunised TB contacts; 11/15 offered vaccination to healthcare workers and to immigrants from high-prevalence countries; only 7/15 offered it to high-risk ethnic group offspring, 5/15 to students and 4/15 to animal workers.

audits.t: An audit of flexor tendon injuries in zone II and its influence on management.
audits.tp: Flexor tendon zone II injury management outcomes
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Results of a controlled mobilization programme for zone II flexor tendon injuries were compared with results from other units (specific figures not given in the abstract).

audits.t: Implementation of Department of Health guidelines for hepatitis B vaccination: a regional audit of NHS occupational health policies and procedures.
audits.st: UK Health Departments' guidelines on protecting healthcare workers and patients from hepatitis B infection
audits.f: Compliance with national guidelines on vaccination was variable; marked variation in interpretation of serological data; failure to establish hepatitis B status of surgeons performing exposure-prone procedures in some cases.

audits.t: Therapeutic drug monitoring of gentamicin: a 6-year follow-up audit.
audits.st: not reported (locally defined therapeutic/toxic ranges for gentamicin peak and trough concentrations)
audits.f: 65% of peak concentrations were within the therapeutic range at first monitoring, 79% of troughs within the non-toxic range; after dosage adjustment 81% of peaks were therapeutic and 7% of troughs became toxic.

audits.t: Audit of a pre-employment risk identification form.
audits.st: Local standard: accuracy of pre-employment risk identification form assessments compared with actual occupational health risks identified after starting the job
audits.f: Agreement between managers' assessments and actual risks identified ranged 83-100%, compared with 59-100% for an independent occupational health nurse's assessment based on job title alone; managers' assessments had higher sensitivity and positive predictive value in nearly all categories.

audits.t: An audit of occupational health care for employees with low-back pain.
audits.tp: Compliance of occupational rehabilitation with low back pain guidelines
audits.st: not reported (locally derived criteria for good practice of occupational rehabilitation for low-back pain)
audits.f: Six performance rates calculated: two below 25%, two around 50%, and the highest (curative policy) at 90%.

audits.t: An audit on guidelines used for the initial management of patients with minor head injuries in Denmark.
audits.tp: Compliance with guidelines for minor head injury management
audits.st: Guidelines recommended by Danish neurosurgeons for management of minor head injuries
audits.f: More than 80% of hospitals recommended admission for unconsciousness, significant headache, dizziness, or nausea/vomiting; skull X-ray was always used in only 2 of 64 hospitals; compliance with guidance on history-taking symptoms was unsatisfactory.

audits.t: Audit of prenatal diagnosis for haemoglobin disorders in the United Kingdom: the first 20 years.
audits.tp: Prenatal diagnosis service utilisation for haemoglobin disorders
audits.st: Expected level of utilisation and early (first-trimester) referral for prenatal diagnosis of haemoglobin disorders, for equitable antenatal screening access
audits.f: National utilisation of prenatal diagnosis for haemoglobin disorders was around 20% overall - far lower than expected; steady at about 50% for thalassaemias but rose from 7% to 13% for sickle cell disorders over the past 10 years; wide regional variation (sickle cell 2-20%; thalassaemia 0% to over 60% for British Pakistanis, ~90% for Cypriots); less than 50% of first referrals were in the first trimester.

audits.t: Intrapartum death of nonmalformed fetuses in Denmark and Sweden in 1991. A perinatal audit.
audits.st: not reported (expert panel review of avoidability of intrapartum death using surveillance/intervention criteria)
audits.f: Insufficient care (surveillance/intervention) found in 66% of Danish cases vs 55% of Swedish cases; potentially avoidable fetal deaths 59% (Denmark) vs 52% (Sweden), difference not statistically significant.

audits.t: Environmental control systems--an audit of existing provision in three inner London districts.
audits.st: British Society of Rehabilitation Medicine special interest group recommendations on environmental control system provision and review
audits.f: 6/29 users had systems so outdated or poorly planned as to be nearly useless; 7/29 users were felt not to justify an environmental control system; many systems were over-specified, leading to wastage of equipment; many other unmet medical and non-medical needs were identified.

audits.t: An audit of the investigation and treatment of folic acid deficiency.
audits.tp: Investigation of folic acid deficiency aetiology
audits.st: Expected standard of thorough aetiological investigation of folate deficiency (dietary, alcohol, drug history, coeliac screening) - implicit local standard, no named external guideline
audits.f: In 52/84 (61.9%) no diagnosis was reached; a definitive diagnosis was established in only 32/84 (38.1%): 16 dietary deficiency, 9 drug-associated, 5 coeliac disease, 1 Crohn's disease, 1 combined variable immunodeficiency; in most cases no attempt was made to establish aetiology.

audits.t: An audit of therapeutic drug monitoring service provision by laboratories participating in an external quality assessment scheme.
audits.tp: Therapeutic drug monitoring service consistency across laboratories
audits.st: Expected consistency in therapeutic drug monitoring target ranges and reporting practice among laboratories (implicit standard, revealed as inconsistent)
audits.f: Target ranges for lithium, digoxin, carbamazepine and phenobarbitone were highly variable, while phenytoin, theophylline and valproic acid ranges were more consistent; units of reporting varied (45% mass, 34% molar, 22% mixed, excluding lithium); 93% provided paper reports, only 28% reported by computer; 73% offered a 24-hour emergency service.

audits.t: An audit of anti-D sensitisation in Yorkshire.
audits.st: Recommendations on administration of anti-D immunoglobulin following potential RhD-sensitising events (e.g. miscarriage, termination of pregnancy)
audits.f: Iatrogenic failure to adhere to recommendations for anti-D immunoglobulin administration occurred in a significant proportion of women who developed immune anti-D antibodies; anti-D failed to protect against immunisation despite protocol adherence in 20/98 events (20%), 13 of which involved miscarriage or termination; 81% of all identified immunising events were miscarriages or medical terminations.

audits.t: Nutritional screening: an audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit matrix for evaluating Finnish occupational health units.
audits.tp: Quality scoring of occupational health units against a national audit matrix
audits.st: Finnish 'good practice in occupational health services' principles, scored via a 12-area, 0-72 point audit matrix
audits.f: No unit scored below 18/72; 9 units scored 19-36, 17 scored 37-54, 4 scored over 54; highest mean scores for maintenance of work ability (4.1), curative care (4.0) and multidisciplinarity (3.9); lowest for planning of activities (3.1), customer orientation (3.2) and quality improvement (3.2).

audits.t: 756 ORTHOPAEDIC SURGEONS CAN PRESCRIBE LAXATIVES & ANALGESICS TOO - A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT SPANNING 7 YEARS
audits.tp: Analgesia and laxative prescribing in hip fracture admission
audits.st: Local standard for regular laxative and analgesia prescribing at hip-fracture admission (no explicit percentage target stated)
audits.f: Laxative prescribing 40%, paracetamol prescribing 100%, regular strong opioid prescribing 60%
audits.c: Repeated PDSA cycles: induction prompts and prompts in admission document (Phase 1); added flow diagram (Phase 2); induction prompts plus electronic prescribing protocol and removal of flow diagram (Phase 3); Phase 3 plus more effort explaining to locum doctors (Phase 4)
audits.r2: Laxative prescribing 74% (90% by 24h post-admission), paracetamol 82% (90% at 24h), regular strong opioid 80% (90% at 24h)

audits.t: 1043 FRAGILITY FRACTURE RISK ASSESSMENT IN THE OLDER PERSON’S RAPID ACCESS CLINIC (OPRAC): A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
audits.tp: Fragility fracture risk assessment in older person's clinic
audits.st: NICE recommendation for fragility fracture risk assessment in all women aged over 65 and men over 75
audits.f: Only 3% had a fracture risk assessment done; height and weight documented in 74%
audits.c: Departmental teaching, posters, and inclusion of fracture risk assessment in the induction handbook
audits.r2: Risk assessment increased to 33%; height and weight documentation increased to 98%

audits.t: 2329 A quality improvement project to improve bone health plan in trauma and orthopaedic discharge summaries
audits.tp: Bone health plan documentation in hip fracture discharge summaries
audits.st: National Osteoporosis Guideline Group (NOGG) recommendation of IV zoledronate as first-line treatment following hip fracture, with documentation on discharge summary
audits.f: 28.3% of discharge summaries had no bone health plan; Vitamin D level not mentioned in 57.1%; inpatient zoledronic acid administration mentioned in 32.1%
audits.c: A blank bone health paragraph was copied into every discharge summary from day 1 of admission, to make completion easier for the Trauma and Orthopaedic junior doctor
audits.r2: 25% of discharge summaries had no bone health plan; Vitamin D not mentioned rose to 59.4%; mention of inpatient zoledronic acid fell to 25%

audits.t: 2883 Quality improvement initiatives to improve one year follow up as per FLS-DB National Recommendations in a welsh health board
audits.st: FLS Database (FLS-DB) recommendation to identify 80% of expected fragility fractures, treat 50%, and monitor 80% at 16 and 52 weeks; national benchmark for one-year follow-up
audits.f: 18.4% (92/875) followed up at one year, versus a national benchmark of 22.3%
audits.c: Process mapping under a Plan-Do-Study-Act quality improvement methodology led to a dedicated annual review clinic code, led by a geriatrics specialty trainee
audits.r2: One-year follow-up performance of 21.4% (310 cases), comparable to the national benchmark of 22.2%

audits.t: 3727 Addressing inequities in dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) access: a multi-dimensional quality improvement approach
audits.tp: DXA scan access and turnaround for fragility fracture patients
audits.st: Fracture Liaison Service Database (FLS-DB) Key Performance Indicator 5: percentage of patients receiving DXA within 90 days of fracture (target not stated)
audits.f: 29.2% (255) scanned within 90 days; average DXA waiting list 1028 patients/month
audits.c: Multi-dimensional improvement project (Model for Improvement): process mapping, radiographer training, expanding scanning from 3 to 5 days/week, dedicated DXA reporting training and a non-reporting agreement for FLS patients
audits.r2: 25.7% (673) scanned within 90 days, a 163% increase from 2021; DXA waiting list dropped to an average of 849/month

audits.t: 3788 Multi-stakeholder approach: building on existing quality initiatives to improve 52-week follow-up based on FLS-DB guidance
audits.st: FLS Database (FLS-DB) recommendation: identify 80% of expected fragility fractures, commence treatment in 50%, and monitor 80% at 52 weeks; national benchmark for one-year follow-up 24.2%
audits.f: 52-week follow-up 25.9% (360 cases), just above the national benchmark of 24.2%
audits.c: Multi-stakeholder Quality Assurance group (clinicians, pharmacist, GP, patient representatives) meeting quarterly, plus a dedicated 52-week follow-up clinic led by a specialty geriatric trainee, within ongoing PDSA cycles since 2022
audits.r2: 52-week follow-up improved to 62.7% (1010 of cases), more than double the national benchmark; case identification reached 70% (2620 cases, vs 39.9% national benchmark) and treatment commencement 61.5% (1611 cases, vs 56.4% national benchmark)

audits.t: 3650 Optimising bowel management in patients with neck of femur fractures: a quality improvement project using admission pelvic X-rays
audits.tp: Bowel management in hip fracture patients
audits.st: Local protocol for proactive bowel management guided by pelvic X-ray (PXR) faecal loading grade
audits.f: Mean time to bowel opening 5 days (range 0-10); patients with higher constipation scores (2-3+) had delayed bowel opening (5.7 vs 4.4 days); only 8% received triple laxative therapy on day 0
audits.c: Implementation of a bowel management guideline advocating early, targeted laxative use based on PXR constipation grade
audits.r2: Mean time to bowel opening reduced to 3.8 days; patients with significant faecal loading (2-3+) opened bowels on average 2 days earlier when the protocol was followed

audits.t: 3829 Evaluating and improving post-operative pain management in hip fracture patients: a multidisciplinary quality improvement project
audits.tp: Postoperative pain management in hip fracture
audits.st: Local standard for postoperative pain management and PRN analgesia administration to support mobilisation (no national target stated)
audits.f: 30% of patients reported pain of 8/10 or more on day one; poor correlation between pain scores and PRN analgesia administered
audits.c: Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles including a trial of a one-off buprenorphine patch, staff education on prescribing behaviours, and nursing workflow optimisation
audits.r2: Buprenorphine patch introduction gave a 20% reduction in day-one pain and 23% reduction on day two; highest reported pain fell to 7/10 (vs 10/10 pre-intervention); no significant increase in postoperative delirium; PRN administration remained inconsistent despite improved pre-op analgesia bundle prescribing

audits.t: 60 Post Inpatient Fall Medical Assessment (PIFMA) Performa Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Local standard for assessment and documentation of inpatient falls, informed by a 2011 NPSA rapid response report
audits.f: Physical examination documented in 80%, neurological observations 49%, medication review 53%, lying-standing blood pressure 83% (after raising-awareness-and-teaching intervention)
audits.c: Development of the Post Inpatient Fall Medical Assessment (PIFMA) proforma to aid assessment and documentation, following an initial raising-awareness-and-teaching (RAT) PDSA cycle
audits.r2: Physical examination 97%, neurological observations 98%, medication review 83%, lying-standing blood pressure 90%

audits.t: 1018 Did COVID Compromise the Care of Closed Paediatric Hand Fractures?
audits.tp: Time to treatment for paediatric hand fractures
audits.st: National guidance compliance for operative management timelines for closed paediatric hand fractures
audits.f: 73% of patients referred within 48 h but waited a median of 5 days to be seen by a hand surgeon, causing significant treatment delays
audits.c: Establishment of a rapid-access musculoskeletal unit (March 2020) with direct assessment by Plastic Surgery and a dedicated theatre
audits.r2: All patients operated on within 72 h of decision to operate; mean time to surgery 1.5 days (range 0-3); mean referral-to-clinic time 1.33 days; 4 patients operated within 7 days of injury

audits.t: 498 Junior Doctor Checklist for the Management of Neck of Femur Fracture: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Junior doctor checklist for neck of femur fracture management
audits.st: Local standard for pre-operative optimisation of neck of femur fracture patients (fluids, anti-emetics, laxatives, anticoagulant reversal)
audits.f: Compliance for fluids 56%, anti-emetics 44%, laxatives 42%, anticoagulant reversal 50% (other parameters over 90%)
audits.c: Development and distribution of a junior doctor checklist outlining the management plan
audits.r2: Compliance for fluids 90%, anti-emetics 66%, laxatives 74%, anticoagulant reversal 80%

audits.t: 366 Vitamin D3 Assessment and Supplementation in Elderly Hip Fracture Patients: A Closed Loop Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Vitamin D assessment and supplementation in hip fracture patients
audits.st: Local standard for vitamin D3 assessment and supplementation in elderly hip fracture patients with orthogeriatric review within 72 hours
audits.f: Vitamin D3 measured during admission in 20%; vitamin D3 supplementation prescribed on discharge in 73.3%
audits.c: Postoperative hip blood profile pathway on ICE with information posters on ordering bloods, teaching sessions for doctors and nurses, and twice-weekly orthogeriatric review emphasising bone protection
audits.r2: Vitamin D3 measurement during admission improved to 93.3%; supplementation prescribed on discharge declined to 26.7%

audits.t: 423 Implementation of Standardised Consent Forms for Hip Fracture Surgery: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: British Orthopaedic Association-endorsed standardised consent forms
audits.f: On Consent 1 forms (n=37), nearly 60% lacked documentation of benefits and 78% missed more than 5 risks; procedure name was the only documentation on Consent 4 forms; VTE was documented on all forms; 98% completed by registrars or consultants
audits.c: Introduction of standardised consent forms endorsed by the British Orthopaedic Association (September 2023)
audits.r2: New standardised forms (Consent 1 and 4) used in 86% of cases, including by foundation year 2 doctors clerking on admission

audits.t: 543 Improving Outcomes in Patients with Fragility Femur Fractures: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Best Practice Tariff variable completion in hip fracture
audits.st: Best Practice Tariff (BPT) for fragility femur fractures: completion of AMTS, 4AT delirium screen, MUST and Falls Assessment
audits.f: AMTS completion 54.5%, 4AT 16.6%, MUST 82.7%, falls assessment consistently above 95%
audits.c: Daily fractured femur reports identifying admitted patients and tracking BPT completion (first PDSA cycle, April 2023), followed by junior doctor induction teaching and a fragility femur fracture handbook (second PDSA cycle, August 2023)
audits.r2: AMTS completion rose to 100%, 4AT to 97.8%, MUST to 100%, falls assessment remained above 95%

audits.t: SRS180 - Addressing delays in post-operative X-rays in hip replacement surgery: a quality improvement project
audits.tp: Timeliness of post-operative X-rays after hip replacement
audits.st: Local protocol for prompt acquisition of post-operative X-rays after hip replacement surgery
audits.f: 74% of X-rays requested on the day of surgery; only 50% performed within one day post-operatively
audits.c: Structured PDSA-methodology quality improvement approach with targeted interventions, protocols and educational tools implemented across three cycles
audits.r2: 73% of requests submitted within one hour of surgery; average request time decreased from 12.3 to 5.8 h; time from surgery to X-ray reduced from 44 to 35.6 h; X-rays performed within one day increased from 50% to 65%

audits.t: MO811: A Closed Loop Audit of CKD-MBD Parameters in Patients Receiving Home Haemodialysis in North West London Centre
audits.tp: CKD-MBD parameter monitoring in home haemodialysis
audits.st: UK Renal Association 2015 standards for CKD-MBD (target ranges for corrected calcium, PTH and phosphate)
audits.f: 14 (42%) had all bone parameters within target range; 27 (82%) calcium in range, 22 (66%) PTH in range, 17 (51%) phosphate in range
audits.c: Monthly multidisciplinary review of blood tests (nephrologists, specialist nurses, dieticians) focusing on CKD-MBD parameters to facilitate timely prescription changes, plus adherence and diet questionnaires
audits.r2: 10 (43%) had all bone parameters within target range; PTH in range improved from 66% to 83%; phosphate in range 54% (not significantly changed); calcium in range 78%

audits.t: Timely completion of spinal fusion: A multidisciplinary quality improvement initiative to improve operating room efficiency
audits.tp: Operating room efficiency for spinal fusion surgery
audits.st: Local target: timely completion of first-case spine fusion surgery within 30 minutes of scheduled time, target 80%
audits.f: Timely case completion 25%
audits.c: Multidisciplinary tests of change: effective scheduling, team communication, family engagement, data collection veracity, standardised pathways, and situational awareness, over three overlapping phases across 16 months
audits.r2: Timely case completion increased to 68% (95% CI 15.1-62.7, p=0.003), sustained in a further 14 cases; on-time surgical starts improved from 50% to 70%; timely completion improved for anaesthesia induction (60% to 85%), surgical procedure (26% to 48%) and emergence (44% to 80%), but not intraoperative patient preparation (30% to 25%)

audits.t: Quality Improvement Protocol to Reduce Excessive Postoperative Recovery Following Cleft Palate Repair.
audits.tp: Postoperative recovery after cleft palate repair
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline PACU length of stay prior to standardisation not given numerically
audits.c: Consistent multimodal analgesic protocol, selective use of above-elbow arm splints, intraoperative dexmedetomidine infusion, via iterative PDSA cycles
audits.r2: 16% reduction in mean PACU stay with standardised anaesthetic approach, 15% with splint rationalisation, 11% with dexmedetomidine; unplanned PICU intervention reduced from 7.3% to 1.2%, with significant reductions in perioperative adverse respiratory events in the dexmedetomidine phase (23% to 12%)

audits.t: An audit and reaudit of the management of shoulder dystocia: an incomplete audit cycle
audits.st: Trust and Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists guidelines, target 100% compliance including use of an emergency chart
audits.f: Call for help 58%, suprapubic pressure 47%, McRoberts 97%, episiotomy 42%, cord pH taken 65%, anterior shoulder documented 7%, incident form completed 26%, paediatrician attended 34%
audits.c: Recommendation from the first audit for 100% compliance with standards and use of the emergency chart for shoulder dystocia
audits.r2: Call for help 56%, suprapubic pressure 41%, McRoberts 93%, episiotomy 37%, cord pH taken 66%, anterior shoulder documented 16%, incident form completed 35%, paediatrician attended 45%, emergency chart used 10% (5/48)

audits.t: PMM.69 The role of continuous audit in monitoring care for women with diabetes in pregnancy; 4 years experience in a high-risk London unit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall antenatal care reached national standards with early booking and timely investigations; caesarean section rate 70% (half elective) in pre-existing diabetes; among 178 women with gestational diabetes, 44% booked after 12 weeks and 63% had a caesarean section; macrosomia >4kg 13% (GDM) vs 6% (pre-existing diabetes)

audits.t: PA.40 Ahead of times or behind? An audit evaluating the accuracy of timekeeping devices in an obstetric unit
audits.tp: Timekeeping device accuracy in obstetric unit
audits.st: Agreement of all clinical timepieces with a radio-controlled clock synchronised to the MSF radio signal

audits.t: Improving the management of musculoskeletal conditions: can an alternative approach to referral management underpinned by quality improvement and behavioural change theories offer a solution and a better patient experience? A mixed-methods study

audits.t: Compliance with national guidelines for antibiotic prophylaxis in hip fracture patients: a quality assessment study of 13 329 patients in the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register

audits.t: Increasing the use of patient decision aids in orthopaedic care: results of a quality improvement project
audits.tp: Patient decision aid use in orthopaedic care

audits.c: Three-phase approach: a quality improvement bonus to raise awareness (phase 1), adapting the electronic referral system to enable DA orders at referral (phase 2), and engaging clinic staff and specialists to design workflows promoting DA delivery (phase 3)
audits.r2: 56% (90/162) of spine patients and 69% (213/307) of hip/knee patients received a DA (significantly more than phase 1, p<0.0001); DAs ordered by clinic staff rose to 56% vs 34% in phase 1 (p<0.001); DAs sent before the visit rose to 74% vs 17% in phase 1 (p<0.001); patients reviewing the DA when delivered before the visit 63% vs 50% (p=0.005)

audits.t: Implementation of a maternity hospital rotational thromboelastometry (ROTEM<sup>®</sup>) guided transfusion strategy: a quality improvement study.

audits.f: mean annual fibrinogen concentrate use 175g (EUR93,170); 22% of PPH >=1500mL patients received fibrinogen, with only 23% meeting evidence-based transfusion criteria; 23% received empirical fibrinogen without testing
audits.c: Implementation of a ROTEM-guided transfusion strategy in September 2022, supported by an electronic smartphone-based decision tool with conditional logic, departmental education (lectures, hands-on training, simulation) and regular audits
audits.r2: mean annual fibrinogen use fell to 94g (EUR50,045, 46% reduction); Octaplas use fell 72% and platelet use fell 79%; compliance with evidence-based fibrinogen triggers rose to 84%; no empirical fibrinogen administration in the post-ROTEM group; total cost saving EUR51,738

audits.t: 137 Antibiotic Provision in Adult Acute Appendicectomy: A Quality Improvement Initiative at a London Tertiary Centre
audits.st: Recent evidence recommending postoperative antibiotics be reserved for infectious complications, with no routine need for long-term prescriptions in uncomplicated cases
audits.f: 96% received preoperative IV antibiotics; 48% had complicated appendicitis; all complicated cases received postoperative antibiotics (mean duration 9.6 days, 73% IV with oral stepdown); 30% of uncomplicated cases received postoperative antibiotics (mean 5.1 days); only 4% received no postoperative antibiotics; 6 patients had infection-related complications or readmissions

audits.t: 217 Quality Assessment of Post-Take Ward Round Documentation in General Surgery Patients at a Single Centre Hospital: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Good Medical and Surgical Practice standards for clinical record documentation
audits.f: 51% of cases could not identify the doctor who documented; a history of presenting complaint (HPC) was not documented in 45.2% of cases, and of those with an HPC, 74.5% lacked sufficient detail; documentation also lacked detail in past surgical/medical history, drugs, social history, radiology, observations, recent bloods, allergy status, and fluid monitoring
audits.c: Introduction of a documentation pro-forma targeting the identified poorer areas (planned)

audits.t: 542 Post-Operative Packing of Perianal Abscess Drainage: Has the Postoperative Packing of Perianal Abscess Cavities (PPAC2) Trial Changed Our Practice?
audits.tp: Post-operative packing of perianal abscess cavities
audits.st: PPAC2 trial evidence recommending avoiding cavity packing after perianal abscess drainage
audits.f: 89% received post-operative packing; recurrence/fistula/readmission within 3 months similar for packed (20%) and unpacked (22%), OR 1.0; 67% of consultants/registrars reported evidence prompted a change in clinical management
audits.c: New protocol delivered following results shared with consultants and registrars
audits.r2: Only 37% received post-operative packing; no patients readmitted for complications at time of report

audits.t: 732 Appendicectomy: Swift Surgery and Quick Recovery Through Quality Improvement
audits.tp: Length of stay for emergency appendicectomy
audits.st: Getting It Right First Time (GIRFT): discharge within 2 days for acute appendicitis
audits.f: Median length of stay was 4.40 days (range 0.97-17.1); only 6.67% met the GIRFT 2-day standard; 91.1% had preoperative imaging (73.3% CT, 14.4% ultrasound); median time from operation to discharge was 3.26 days
audits.c: Departmental presentation and posters communicating recommendations for improvement
audits.r2: not reported (data collection ongoing at time of reporting)

audits.t: 858 Last One Out, Turn Out the Lights
audits.tp: Green theatre checklist compliance for HVAC and lighting
audits.st: Intercollegiate green theatre checklist, expected minimum 66% of timepoints with lights off/HVAC in standby
audits.f: 15 of 20 theatres had HVAC on at all measured time points; best performing theatre had lights off at 56.3% (9) of timepoints; two theatres had lights on at every measured timepoint; 17/20 had lights on >50% of timepoints
audits.c: Educational intervention to theatre teams on the green theatre checklist (planned)

audits.t: 886 Benefits of Implementing 'Rub Don't Scrub' - Saving Water and Money
audits.tp: Alcohol-based hand rub use for clean cases
audits.st: Intercollegiate Green Theatre Checklist recommendation for ABHR use for clean cases after first case of the day
audits.f: 0 individuals used ABHR; average scrubbing time 98 seconds with 3.5 individuals per operation; estimated 441,000L water used annually trust-wide
audits.c: Posters in theatres and presentation to the entire general surgical team

audits.t: 446 The Compliance of Using the Handover Tab on HIVE (EPR) Between the Surgical Teams in the General Surgery Department
audits.st: NICE guidelines recommendation for structured handover, implemented via HIVE EPR handover tab
audits.f: EGS 94.44% (17/18), Colorectal 14.28% (3/21), HPB 0% (0/40); overall compliance 25.32% (20/79)
audits.c: Word-of-mouth communication, posters, circulating emails, incorporating topic into junior doctors' inductions

audits.t: 813 Improving Discharge Medication Compliance for Secondary Prevention in Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Discharge medication compliance for secondary prevention in peripheral arterial disease
audits.st: COMPASS trial recommendations: Atorvastatin 80mg, Rivaroxaban 2.5mg, and Aspirin 100mg on discharge
audits.f: Baseline compliance was: Atorvastatin 16.67%, Rivaroxaban 0%, and Aspirin 0%
audits.c: Week 2: poster detailing correct medication dosages; Week 3: email reminder to junior doctors; Week 4: consultant-led discussion reinforcing discharge medication protocol
audits.r2: Week 2: Atorvastatin 20%, Rivaroxaban 0%, Aspirin 20%; Week 3: Atorvastatin 75%, Rivaroxaban 25%, Aspirin 50%; Week 4: Atorvastatin 50%, Rivaroxaban 25%, Aspirin 50%

audits.t: MTP6.16 Investigating the length of time to surgical treatment from urgent referral and date of decision colorectal cancer with surgery between patients who require an IV iron infusion and those who don't require an infusion
audits.tp: Time to surgical treatment for colorectal cancer
audits.st: National cancer guidelines: maximum 31 days from decision to treat to surgery, 62 days from urgent referral to treatment
audits.f: Patients requiring iron infusions had longer delays than those not needing infusions (mean 56.1 vs 27.9 days from decision-to-treat; 144.1 vs 101.9 days from urgent referral); both groups breached national waiting time targets
audits.c: Targeted intervention including earlier iron testing and expedited referrals for infusions
audits.r2: Delays for infusion patients decreased significantly (mean 24.3 vs 31.4 days from decision-to-treat; 71.7 vs 82.1 days from urgent referral); pattern reversed so infusion patients had shorter delays than non-infusion patients; breaches reduced in both groups

audits.t: MTP8.09 Evaluating post-operative wound care advice given to patients after emergency general surgery – a quality improvement project
audits.st: NICE guideline 125 on wound care advice after surgery
audits.f: Dressing advice, showering advice, and infection signs were included in discharge summaries in 51.1%, 19.1%, and 40.4% of cases respectively
audits.c: Wound care advice template for discharge summaries, promoted with posters and reminder emails (PDSA cycle 1); a leaflet for patients was planned for PDSA cycle 2
audits.r2: Dressing advice 58.5%, showering advice 7.5%, infection signs 47.2%; infection consequences addressed increased significantly from 0% to 15.1% (p=0.05)

audits.t: TTP2.08 Enhancing Preoperative Care: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Improve Compliance with Fasting Guidelines in Elective Colorectal Surgery
audits.tp: Preoperative fasting guideline compliance in elective colorectal surgery
audits.st: National and international preoperative fasting guidelines (including 'sips till send')
audits.f: Median fasting time for food 15 hours (9,18), for fluids 4.5 hours (3,7); 28.2% informed about 'sips to send'; 79.4% understood importance of preoperative fasting.
audits.c: Posters and educational sessions for patients and healthcare staff (doctors, nurses, anaesthetists, healthcare assistants).
audits.r2: Median fasting time for food reduced to 7 hours (6,8.5), fluids to 4 hours (2,6); 72.4% informed about 'sips to send'; 96.5% understood importance.

audits.t: TTP3.05 Nourish to Flourish – Improving Post-Operative Nutrition as Part of Enhanced Recovery Programme at a District General Hospital
audits.st: 2018 ERAS Society recommendations for post-operative nutrition
audits.f: All patients commenced on oral fluids from day of surgery; 89% established on oral diet day 1; oral nutritional supplements (ONS) not offered routinely as part of ERAS programme; average weight loss 2.67kg
audits.c: Local nutritional guideline drafted and approved at trust level ('Nutrition in Enhanced Recovery after Colorectal Surgery Guideline'), leading to introduction of Fortisips
audits.r2: 80% established on oral diet day 1; ONS (Fortisip) uptake rate 75%; average weight loss 1.19kg (not statistically significant difference from cycle one, paired t-test)

audits.t: TTP4.15 Are Patients Admitted with Gallstone Pancreatitis Being Treated as per the Current UK Guidelines?
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) 2005 guidelines: definitive gallstone management during same admission unless treatment planned within two weeks
audits.f: 47% did not receive appropriate interventions per BSG guidelines; severity scores documented in only 20% of cases; antibiotics administered to 59%, with documented indications in 27%; 9% treated through HTC pathway for laparoscopic cholecystectomy; 29% placed on inpatient waiting list
audits.c: Recommendation for a proforma based on guidelines and annual re-audits (not yet implemented)

audits.t: WTP2.08 Ceiling of care and escalation pathway decision making in general surgical patients at a busy tertiary care centre in NHS
audits.tp: Ceiling of care and escalation pathway documentation
audits.st: South Tees Trust resuscitation guidelines: escalation plan completed within 24 hours of admission
audits.f: 6 patients had documented ceiling of care on day of admission or within 24 hours, giving adherence of 6.18%; 9 of 10 patients on ward-based level of care died; in 7 of these 9 cases, ITU escalation and ceiling of care decisions occurred overnight; median age for DNACPR/ward-based ceiling of care 74 years, median Charlson Comorbidity Index 9
audits.c: Email to be sent to all surgical team doctors regarding documentation of ceiling of care at admission or on post-take ward rounds (planned)

audits.t: WTP4.02 Use of Antibiotics in Diverticular disease – A double edged sword
audits.st: World Society of Emergency Surgery (WSES) guidelines for management of diverticular disease
audits.f: 88% had CT scan on admission within first 24 hours; 29% diagnosed with complicated diverticular disease; antibiotics administered in 88% of patients, indicating injudicious use particularly in uncomplicated disease; no patient benefitted from interventional radiology
audits.c: Recommendations about use of antibiotics; local guidelines established to improve service delivery
audits.r2: Waiting time for CT scan and use of antibiotics became more prudent, particularly in systemically well patients with uncomplicated disease

audits.t: WTP7.10 Optimising Intravenous Fluid Prescribing for Nil-by-Mouth Acute Surgical Patients
audits.tp: IV fluid prescribing for nil-by-mouth surgical patients
audits.st: NICE guidelines for IV fluid management
audits.f: IV fluid volume adherence 71.0%; IV potassium adherence 19.4%; IV glucose adherence 16.1%
audits.c: Results shared via an educational poster
audits.r2: IV fluid volume adherence increased to 75.9% then 87.0%; IV potassium adherence improved to 20.7% then 30.4%; IV glucose adherence rose to 40.0% but fell to 25.0%; reduction in hypoglycaemia, hypokalaemia and AKI observed

audits.t: 151 Improving Timeliness and Quality of Prescribed Medicines Supply for Bariatric Patients at a Large Teaching Trust
audits.tp: Timeliness of prescribed medicines supply for bariatric patients
audits.st: LTHT guidance/national recommendations for switching bariatric patients to liquid/crushed medication forms for 6 weeks post-operatively
audits.f: Baseline average discharge medication wait time was 6.5 hours
audits.c: Redesigned workflow: completing drug histories before admission, starting the electronic discharge advice note (eDAN) earlier, a discharge medication protocol integrated into prescribing software, and pharmacy technician training
audits.r2: Redesigned workflow eliminated discharge medication wait times, saving approximately 325 hours; quality indicators for eight medications showed 97-100% guideline adherence, with justified exceptions

audits.t: 337 Improving the Accuracy of Drain Lipase Testing Following Pancreatectomy: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Drain fluid lipase testing timing post-pancreatectomy
audits.st: 2016 International Study Group of Pancreatic Surgery (ISGPS) POPF definition; local target of 100% postoperative day 3 (POD3) drain fluid lipase (DFL) testing
audits.f: 61.7% of patients were tested for DFL in a timely manner (POD3)
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles: educational posters, and a pre-filled ward round and operation note template providing clear instructions
audits.r2: 100% compliance with timely POD3 DFL testing achieved by the end of the fourth cycle; postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF) was diagnosed more frequently in timely-tested patients (70.7% vs 27.8%), and clinically relevant POPF was higher in the delayed testing group (70% vs 43.9%)

audits.t: IBC Oxford Oral Abstract 7 - Optimizing perioperative care in bariatric surgery: a quality improvement study using an ERAS-based protocol
audits.tp: ERAS protocol and length of stay in bariatric surgery
audits.st: ASMBS guidance endorsing ERAS protocols in bariatric surgery
audits.f: 31.3% discharged on postoperative day 1; median length of stay 1.73 days.
audits.c: Comprehensive ERAS protocol: non-narcotic pain control, TAP blocks, early mobilisation, standardised anti-nausea strategy, early diet progression from postoperative day 0.
audits.r2: 71.8% discharged on postoperative day 1 (p<0.00001); median length of stay 1.31 days (p<0.001); complication rates similar (6.8% vs 5.4%, p=0.66); readmissions and ED visits similar between groups.

audits.t: SRS288 - Timing of re-resection following initial TURBT in high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer: a retrospective review
audits.tp: Re-resection timing after TURBT for bladder cancer
audits.st: EAU/AUA/NICE recommend re-resection within 2-6 weeks for high-risk NMIBC or incomplete initial TURBT
audits.f: Re-resection indicated in 28.7% of cases; only 8.6% underwent re-resection within the recommended 6-week timeframe; mean interval 62.7 ± 26.9 days; mean time TURBT to MDT 13.7 ± 10.5 days; MDT to re-resection 49.0 ± 25.0 days; tumour upgrading in 8.6% of re-resected cases
audits.c: Proposed modifying the TURBT operative note template to prompt surgeons to request re-resection at initial surgery when high-grade features identified (not yet implemented)

audits.t: 123 Optimising MRCP Referrals in Low-to-Moderate Risk Patients for Common Bile Duct Stones: A Two-Cycle QI Project
audits.tp: MRCP referral quality for common bile duct stones
audits.st: iRefer clinical decision support criteria and Sunflower Study criteria for low-to-moderate risk gallstone patients with suspected CBDS
audits.f: Explicit indication documentation 37%, biochemistry documentation 71%, prior imaging documentation 63%, MRCP yield 6.9%, median MRCP wait 12 days, median time to lap chole 15 days (range 1-54), complication rate 3%
audits.c: Implementation of iRefer clinical decision support for MRCP referrals
audits.r2: Explicit indication documentation 81% (+44%), biochemistry documentation 88% (+17%), prior imaging documentation 80% (+17%), MRCP yield 7%, median MRCP wait 8 days (33% reduction), median lap chole time 11 days (range 1-38, 27% reduction), surgery rate 90%

audits.t: 411 Implementation of a Patient-Initiated Follow-Up Pathway Following Paediatric Grommet Insertion: A Quality Improvement Study
audits.st: National guidelines recommend 6-week post-operative audiometry after grommet insertion, with discharge and safety-netting if hearing has normalised
audits.f: 16 patients had normal audiometry at 6 weeks; of these, 9 patients (21% of total cohort, over 50% of normal-audiometry group) were followed up with no documented indication
audits.c: Development of a Patient-Initiated Follow-Up (PIFU) proforma for low-risk children over five years old

audits.t: 144 Renal Colic Management Improvement Through Bitesize Teaching in Emergency Department
audits.tp: Renal colic management (CT KUB timing, analgesia, metabolic screening)
audits.st: BAUS guidelines: CT KUB within 14 hours for renal colic, appropriate analgesia (NSAID or IV paracetamol), metabolic screening bloods including calcium and urate
audits.f: CT KUB performed within 14 hours 75.96%; NSAID prescriptions 44%; patients with no analgesia 33%; serum calcium measured 61%; urate measured 5%
audits.c: Bite-sized teaching sessions for junior doctors and seniors (25 March and 1 September)
audits.r2: CT KUB within 14 hours improved to 88%; NSAID prescriptions rose to 62%; no analgesia fell to 26%; calcium measurement decreased slightly to 57%; urate measurement rose to 11%

audits.t: 469 Improving the Documentation of Wound Reviews for Diabetic Foot Wounds by Foundation Doctors on Vascular Surgery Ward Rounds Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Documentation of diabetic foot wound reviews
audits.st: Local structured wound assessment standard (target >=80% compliance)
audits.f: Documented wound reviews 84% (27/32); appropriate wound photographs 50% (16/32); senior clinician agreement 28% (9/32).
audits.c: 30-minute teaching session for foundation doctors/ACPs; visual reminder posters in the doctors' office.
audits.r2: Documented reviews 86% (18/21); appropriate photographs 76% (16/21); senior clinician agreement 81% (17/21).

audits.t: 809 Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) for Emergency Colorectal Patients - a Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: ERAS referral rates for emergency colorectal surgery
audits.st: Local standard for referral of patients aged 18 and over undergoing emergency colorectal surgery to the Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocol
audits.f: ERAS referral rate 9.1% through multiple referral routes
