audits.c: Education session with the ERAS team for clinical staff highlighting the ERAS service and referral criteria, plus display of referral criteria in clinical areas
audits.r2: ERAS referral rate increased to 23.3%; reduced length of hospital stay by 1.5-3 days compared with literature; median 2 days to mobilisation and 4 days to first diet post-operatively

audits.t: 1075 Local Prostate Cancer Guidelines: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: NICE, EAU and Northern Cancer Network prostate cancer guidance
audits.f: 60% reported limited or no understanding of prostate cancer guidelines; 53% not confident discussing care pathways; 33% uncertain requesting investigations; 53% did not know how to refer to oncology; 93% agreed a local guideline would help.
audits.c: Development and dissemination of a unified local prostate cancer guideline (email, digital folders, printed copies).

audits.t: 1268 Ensuring Accurate and Consistent Lesion Tattooing in Colonoscopy: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: JAG, St Mark's and Rex' criteria for colonoscopic tattooing
audits.f: 60.05% tattooed when indicated (39.45% not tattooed); 8.26% of 121 lesions where tattooing was not indicated were tattooed unnecessarily; endoscopist compliance ranged from 12 achieving 100% to 14 with <50% compliance.
audits.c: Planned: guideline posters, mandatory documentation prompts, improved reporting of lesion distance from the anal verge.

audits.t: 1349 Adapting Systems to Improve Imaging Adequacy in Patients With Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Preoperative imaging completeness for abdominal aortic aneurysm
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Complete imaging of the aorta (including thoracic aorta/arch) in 45%; repeat imaging needed in 18%; requests specifically included 'thoracic aorta' in 15%.
audits.c: Clinicians asked to include 'thoracic aorta' in CT requests; new 'CT Whole Aorta' order entry introduced on EPIC, protocoled to include the aortic arch.
audits.r2: Complete imaging improved to 80% (p<0.0005); repeat imaging decreased to 13% (p=0.23, not significant); requests specifying thoracic aorta 17%.

audits.t: SP 6.01 A Human-Factor Intervention Bundle to Improve Rescue Efforts for Post Operative Deteriorating Emergency Surgery Patients – A Pilot Study Using Quality Improvement Approach
audits.tp: Human factors bundle for rescue of deteriorating post-operative emergency surgery patients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median response time 259 minutes pre-intervention
audits.c: Bundle of four human factors interventions: patient involvement, team strengthening, standardised communication protocols, and emergency process algorithms for staff, over an 8-month implementation period
audits.r2: Median response time 155 minutes during intervention and 154 minutes post intervention across three sites combined (40% reduction, p=0.014)

audits.t: SP 6.08 A Quality Improvement Project to Improve Compliance with Follow-Up Chest X-Ray Guidance for Pneumonia on a General Surgery Ward
audits.tp: Follow-up chest X-ray for pneumonia guidance compliance
audits.st: National guidance recommending follow-up chest X-ray 6-8 weeks after inpatient pneumonia treatment in higher-risk patients
audits.f: Only 8% (2/24) had follow-up imaging documented or arranged; 10 of 24 met NICE criteria strictly, a further 12 could reasonably have been considered depending on clinical context.

audits.t: EP 031 Quality Improvement Project: The Use of Routine Blood Testing in General Surgery; Are we Testing too Much and is it of Clinical Significance?
audits.tp: Routine blood testing appropriateness in general surgery
audits.st: Expert opinion/departmental consultant surgeon guidance on blood testing frequency for gallstone pancreatitis, cholecystitis, diverticulitis, colorectal resection with anastomosis, post laparoscopic appendicectomy, and complex hernia repair
audits.f: Baseline frequency of blood tests assessed for 6 conditions; discrepancy noted between actual testing frequency and expert opinion recommendations
audits.c: A poster calling for reduction of blood tests, followed by a condition-specific guideline poster using feedback from consultant surgeons
audits.r2: Average cost of blood tests per patient decreased by 24% by end of Cycle 2; no statistically significant difference in mean blood test numbers between cycles (p=0.12)

audits.t: Genetic testing for breast cancer—adherence, outcomes and impact on surgical management: a quality review
audits.tp: Adherence to genetic testing criteria in breast cancer
audits.st: Swedish national breast cancer guidelines - germline genetic testing criteria
audits.f: Gene panel testing completed for 87% (114/138) meeting criteria; pathogenic variants detected in 11% (13/114), highest in triple-negative breast cancer (15%); surgical management modified for 15 patients (14 bilateral mastectomy).

audits.t: Implementing an electronic patient record autotext to improve toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) documentation and care: a single-centre response to the British Association of Dermatologists’ national TEN audit
audits.tp: Toxic epidermal necrolysis documentation and care
audits.st: British Association of Dermatologists national TEN audit standards
audits.f: not reported (baseline documentation deficiencies identified from the national BAD TEN audit, prompting this local response)
audits.c: Implementation of a semistructured electronic patient record autotext template to improve documentation and early management of TEN
audits.r2: Positive trend towards improved documentation of SCORTEN, medication history and early ophthalmology referral; inconsistencies remained in urogenital assessment and discharge planning

audits.t: DOP81 Quality improvement by semi-automated benchmarking of a core outcome quality indicator set in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A multicentric feasibility study
audits.tp: Automated benchmarking of IBD quality indicators
audits.st: International Consortium for Health Outcomes Measurement (ICHOM) IBD outcome indicator definitions
audits.f: Feasibility demonstrated for a platform automatically capturing 12 consensus quality indicators (patient-reported outcomes, automated extraction of anaemia/deep remission, and yearly clinician-confirmed items), benchmarked anonymously across centres.

audits.t: P129 IBD care in the UK: A comprehensive, novel service assessment with feedback from 10,222 patients and 166 NHS organisations to inform a vision for quality improvement
audits.tp: IBD service quality against UK IBD Standards
audits.st: UK IBD Standards 2019
audits.f: 89% (9100/10222) found it hard to cope with Crohn's or Colitis over the previous year; 72% (6954/9640) rated quality of care good or better; 26% (535/2089) waited more than a year for diagnosis; 41% (849/2087) visited A&E before diagnosis; 32% (656/2057) not offered information at diagnosis; 91% (8284/9099) had no personalised care plan; no adult IBD services reported meeting WTE staffing recommendation

audits.t: P132 An audit of quality of histopathology reporting of colorectal mucosal biopsies for the diagnosis and assessment of Inflammatory Bowel Disease
audits.tp: Histopathology reporting quality for IBD colorectal biopsies
audits.st: UK Royal College of Pathologists and European (ECCO/Magro et al) guidelines for reporting colorectal mucosal biopsies for IBD; satisfactory compliance set at 90%
audits.f: 14 of 24 criteria met the 90% compliance standard; non-compliant items included duration of disease stated 86%, endoscopy findings provided 79%, actual endoscopy report copy provided 4%, endoscopist probability of IBD stated 63%, adequate sampling 50%, distribution within sites recorded 68%, basal plasmacytosis comment 32%, UC/Crohn's preference stated 71%

audits.t: P482 Pre-screening IBD patients starting biologic therapies, a positive single centre quality improvement project
audits.tp: Pre-screening before biologic therapy in IBD
audits.st: BSG (Lamb et al 2019) consensus guidelines on pre-screening investigations before starting biologic therapy in IBD
audits.f: Compliance with screening for baseline bloods and infections 58.1%; vaccination history checked 0%; adequate cervical screening 3.2%; 0% met full BSG pre-screening guidelines
audits.c: Pre-screening checklist proforma led standard operating procedure (SOP) for IBD patients starting biologics
audits.r2: Compliance with screening for baseline bloods and infections improved to 100%; vaccination history checked improved to 88%; adequate cervical screening improved to 66.7%; 80% met full BSG pre-screening guidelines

audits.t: N29 Audit of Inflammatory Bowel Disease Telephone Advice Line
audits.st: IBD Standards UK: rapid access to specialist advice via telephone/email advice line with response by end of next working day
audits.f: 23/80 (29%) calls for Hi Tech prescription; flare-up calls 21.2%; results investigation queries 21.2%; administration/medication queries 7.5%; clinical queries 9%; 59% of calls returned within 36 hours; mean interval 34.7 hours; median interval 28 hours

audits.t: N30 Understanding Inflammatory Bowel Disease Emergency Department Admissions in a Tertiary Referral Inflammatory Bowel Disease Centre in England: A quality Improvement project
audits.tp: IBD emergency department admissions and advice line contact
audits.st: Quality standards recommend review within 5 days of a flare
audits.f: 29 (60.42%) admissions; 19 (39.58%) discharges (5 self-discharges); 4/41 (9.76%) had no IBD diagnosis; 32/48 (66.67%) attendances had no prior contact with the IBD advice line
audits.c: Adding advice line details to clinic letters, advertising in clinic, and setting up a rapid access flare clinic led by Advanced Nurse Practitioners

audits.t: P837 Improving Vaccination Rates in Patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Single Centre Audit and Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Societal recommendations for influenza (IFV) and pneumococcal (PCV) vaccination in IBD
audits.f: 6/30 (20%) at-risk patients received IFV, 11/30 (36.7%) received PCV
audits.c: Provider education on vaccination schedules, standardised electronic documentation template, laminated poster guidelines, personalised patient vaccination cards
audits.r2: 20/65 (30.7%) obtained IFV coverage post-intervention (p=0.01); 12/63 (19%) received PCV

audits.t: P926 Improved standards of colonoscopy for Inflammatory Bowel Disease through implementation of key performance measures - A quality improvement initiative
audits.st: ESGE key performance measures for IBD colonoscopy; ECCO and SCENIC consensus guidelines
audits.f: Suboptimal performance in use of disease activity scores and chromoendoscopy
audits.c: Multimodal education: didactic teaching, diagrammatic reminders in endoscopy suites over 12 months
audits.r2: Significant improvement in all performance measures

audits.t: P0871 Textbook Outcomes in Acute Severe Ulcerative Colitis: A Novel Approach to Assessing Patient Quality of Care in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
audits.tp: Textbook outcome in acute severe ulcerative colitis
audits.st: Guideline-based standards of care for ASUC (BSG and ECCO-ESGAR guidelines): IV steroids and VTE prophylaxis on admission, stool sample screening, abdominal imaging within 24h, flexible sigmoidoscopy within 48h
audits.f: 14.0% (n=24) achieved textbook outcome; stool sample screening 91.3%, IV steroids 79.1%, VTE prophylaxis 73.3%, timely flexible sigmoidoscopy only 36.0%

audits.t: P1040 Steroid use and dependency in South Indian Inflammatory Bowel Disease patients- A multi-center clinical audit
audits.tp: Steroid use and dependency in IBD
audits.st: ECCO Guidelines on Therapeutics in Ulcerative Colitis and steroid assessment tool for steroid dependency/excess
audits.f: Steroids given to 208 (52%) patients; 127 (32%) had steroid excess or dependence (84 UC, 43 CD); inappropriate steroid excess in 48% of those given steroids; annual incidence of inappropriate excess 15.25% of total cohort; 26 (12.5%) started steroids without biochemical/endoscopic evaluation; 128 (61%) received no concomitant bone protection

audits.t: P531 A retrospective audit of the inflammatory bowel disease specialist nurse-led telephone advice service
audits.tp: IBD specialist nurse-led telephone advice service
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 56% ulcerative colitis, 44% Crohn's disease callers; medication changed in 49% of consultations; phlebotomy/faecal calprotectin requested for 59%; 17% discussed with a consultant; 8% required an IBD nurse-led or consultant clinic; calls avoided GP attendance in 25%, A&E in 2%, IBD nurse clinic in 41%, consultant clinic in 6%

audits.t: P561 The management of Crohn’s disease (CD) patients post ileocaecal resection: a multicentre, regional audit in Northern England
audits.tp: Post-operative Crohn's disease recurrence assessment after ileocaecal resection
audits.st: ECCO guidelines: identify patients at risk of post-operative recurrence, use imidazole antibiotics post-surgery, assess for recurrence (ileocolonoscopy with Rutgeerts score) within 12 months
audits.f: 76% (29/38) had at least one high-risk factor for recurrence; only 13% (5/38) received imidazole antibiotics postoperatively; only 29% (11/38) had ileocolonoscopy within 12 months; 32% (12/38) had alternative assessment (mostly calprotectin); treatment escalation required in 25% (9/38); 40% (15/38) had no maintenance therapy before assessment
audits.c: A postoperative CD management bundle is being developed for future implementation

audits.t: P691 Corticosteroids usage in patients with inflammatory bowel disease: Results of a multi-national audit in Asia
audits.st: not reported (cases classified as non-IBD/appropriate/avoidable use)
audits.f: 339 patients (26.3%) received corticosteroids in the past year; 36 events (10.6%) classified as avoidable CS use

audits.t: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A609 ACUTE STROKE CARE IN UKRAINE 2021–2024: TRENDS, QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, AND SYSTEM PERFORMANCE DURING WARTIME
audits.st: WHO-supported national stroke care quality indicators and National Health Service of Ukraine stroke care package standards
audits.f: 85% of stroke cases treated in hospitals contracted for the stroke package; intravenous thrombolysis rate 4.6%; endovascular thrombectomy rate 0.3%; inpatient rehabilitation access 4.8%; in-hospital mortality 16-17%, 30-day mortality 24%.
audits.c: WHO technical support for stroke system strengthening and national stroke care network consolidation, 2021-2024
audits.r2: 96% of stroke cases treated in contracted hospitals; intravenous thrombolysis rose to 13.2%; endovascular thrombectomy to 2.4%; inpatient rehabilitation access to 13.4% (outpatient rehabilitation remained 1-2%); in-hospital mortality (16-17%) and 30-day mortality (24%) remained unchanged.

audits.t: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026YS116 HYPERGLYCAEMIA AUDIT
audits.tp: HbA1c testing in patients admitted with ischaemic stroke
audits.st: Local standard requiring HbA1c testing within 3 months preceding admission for patients admitted with ischaemic stroke
audits.f: 77% had HbA1c results during admission or within 3 months before admission; 11% of results were reported only after discharge; 4% had a HbA1c consistent with diabetes despite a negative past medical history; of the 34% with diabetes, only 21% were reviewed by diabetes specialist nurses

audits.t: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A132 AUDIT OF MECHANICAL VTE PROPHYLAXIS COMPLIANCE IN STROKE PATIENTS ON A NHS STROKE WARD: A SERVICE IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVE
audits.tp: Mechanical VTE prophylaxis compliance on a stroke ward
audits.st: National Clinical Guideline for Stroke (2023): consistent use of mechanical VTE prophylaxis until the patient no longer has significantly reduced mobility relative to their normal or anticipated mobility
audits.f: only 19 patients (45%) received mechanical VTE prophylaxis as prescribed; 23 (55%) were noncompliant at least once (33% missed one observation, 17% missed two, 5% missed three)
audits.c: Staff meeting presenting the results, ward posters highlighting the importance of VTE prophylaxis, and modifying the prescribing schedule from 'daily' to 'QDS' to encourage staff checks

audits.t: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1187 EVALUATION OF TENECTEPLASE USE IN ACUTE ISCHAEMIC STROKE: A QUALITY AUDIT FROM A HYPERACUTE STROKE UNIT
audits.tp: Tenecteplase use in acute ischaemic stroke thrombolysis
audits.st: Local agreed standards for safe Tenecteplase administration, including safety checklist completion, documentation, and international door-to-needle and imaging timeline standards
audits.f: safety checklist completion documented in 82% (14.0% incomplete/missing, 4% unavailable); Tenecteplase administration fully documented in 62% (34.0% incomplete/undocumented, 4% unavailable); post-Tenecteplase monitoring completed in 86%; door-to-needle time <=60 minutes achieved in 63.8%; all patients scanned within 60 minutes (94.0% within 20 minutes); haemorrhagic transformation in 6.1%

audits.t: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1399 APPROPRIATENESS OF DUAL ANTIPLATELET THERAPY PRESCRIBING IN A TIA CLINIC: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
audits.tp: Dual antiplatelet therapy prescribing appropriateness in a TIA clinic
audits.st: National and international stroke guidelines on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) indication and duration for high-risk TIA and minor ischaemic stroke
audits.f: median time to DAPT initiation 72 hours; inappropriate DAPT prescribing 6%; DAPT most often given for TIA/stroke despite antiplatelet therapy, high-risk TIA, and mild ischaemic stroke (NIHSS <=3)
audits.c: Introduction of a guideline-based DAPT decision-support flowchart in August 2025
audits.r2: median time to DAPT initiation increased to 96 hours; inappropriate DAPT prescribing increased from 6% to 25%

audits.t: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1731 INCREASING UK STROKE THROMBOLYSIS RATES: A NATIONAL QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVE
audits.tp: Stroke thrombolysis rates and door-to-needle times
audits.st: Local SSNAP-derived thrombolysis rate and door-to-needle time targets, improved via a measurement-for-improvement approach
audits.f: Cohort 1 average thrombolysis rate 9.7%; Cohort 2 average thrombolysis rate 11.2%
audits.c: Coaching and mentoring on use of local SSNAP data, a structured webinar series supporting diagnostic data use, Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycles, and monitoring progress over time
audits.r2: Cohort 1 thrombolysis rate rose to 14.1% (45% relative increase), sustained at 16.5% six months later in 3 sites; Cohort 2: 11 of 12 sites improved, average rising from 11.2% to 17.5% (62.6% relative increase); many sites also showed statistically significant reductions in door-to-needle times

audits.t: Balancing quality and quaternary care imperative using a high-risk case review committee in adults
audits.st: Local standard: pre-defined predicted risk of mortality cut-offs for referral to a high-risk case review committee (HRC)
audits.f: HRC discussed 205 patients with median predicted risk of mortality 10.6% (range 0.4-66%); 155 underwent operation (risk 10.3%), 12 had surgery deferred for optimization (risk 6%), 50 had surgery declined (risk 11.7%), and 12 had a deferred decision; overall 30-day survival was 86% for the cohort and 89% for operated patients.

audits.t: Development and evaluation of a national gentamicin and vancomycin quality improvement programme.
audits.tp: Gentamicin and vancomycin dosing guideline adherence
audits.st: Scottish Antimicrobial Prescribing Group (SAPG) 2009 national guidance standardising gentamicin/vancomycin dosing, monitoring and administration
audits.f: 44% of patients received the recommended gentamicin dose; correct vancomycin loading dose in 50% and correct maintenance dose in 55%
audits.c: Development and implementation across Scotland (2013-16) of revised guidelines, online/mobile dose calculators, educational material, and specialised prescribing and monitoring charts, developed with antimicrobial specialists and multidisciplinary teams
audits.r2: Recommended gentamicin dose given to 89% of patients (OR 10.99, 95% CI 6.37-18.95 vs 2011); correct vancomycin loading dose 85% (OR 5.69, CI 2.76-11.71) and correct maintenance dose 90% (OR 7.17, CI 3.01-17.07)

audits.t: A multifaceted strategy to optimize pharmacokinetics of antimicrobial therapy in patients with hospital-acquired infections—a monocentre quality improvement project
audits.tp: Antimicrobial therapeutic drug monitoring in hospital-acquired infection
audits.st: not reported (locally defined dose-adjustment protocol via TDM and continuous beta-lactam infusion)
audits.f: Compliance with TDM-dose adaptation 20.3%; 90-day mortality 27.6%
audits.c: Clinician training on TDM-guided dose adjustment and continuous infusion of beta-lactam antibiotics
audits.r2: Compliance with TDM-dose adaptation increased to 59.3% (p<0.0001); 90-day mortality 17.3% (adjusted RR 0.53, 95%CI 0.27-1.07, p=0.08)

audits.t: Effect of a bundle intervention on adherence to quality-of-care indicators and on clinical outcomes in patients with Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia hospitalized in non-referral community hospitals
audits.st: Five structured quality-of-care indicators for SAB management (evidence-based bundle)
audits.f: Pre-intervention adherence to bundle indicators (baseline)
audits.c: Structured recommendations for five quality-of-care indicators provided to investigators, then monthly thereafter
audits.r2: Non-significant improvements in bundle adherence, follow-up blood cultures and adequate treatment duration; echocardiography performance was significantly associated with improved adherence (adjusted OR 2.13, 95%CI 1.13-4.02)

audits.t: External quality assurance (EQA) network in South and South-East Asia: experience and results from an international EQA programme in One Health sector reference laboratories
audits.tp: External quality assurance for bacteriology laboratories
audits.st: WHO GLASS and FAO priority pathogen panels; recognized international EQA standards
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Significant improvement in laboratory performance over time; overall performance across six rounds ranged 75-100% (average 93.3%, median 93.6%); Campylobacter spp. and Enterococcus spp. panels were most often misidentified.

audits.t: An evidence-based bundle improves the quality of care and outcomes of patients with candidaemia
audits.st: Eight evidence-based quality-of-care indicators (early treatment, echinocandins in septic shock, source control, follow-up blood culture, ophthalmoscopy, echocardiography, de-escalation, length of treatment)
audits.f: Pre-intervention national surveillance data (baseline QCI adherence)
audits.c: Prospective implementation of a written evidence-based bundle of recommendations
audits.r2: Adherence to all QCIs improved; early mortality OR 0.46 (95%CI 0.23-0.89, p=0.022); overall mortality OR 0.61 (95%CI 0.4-0.94, p=0.023)

audits.t: P18 Audit on compliance with the preventive measures on Clostridioides difficile
audits.st: Local guidance on managing new-onset inpatient diarrhoea (medication review, isolation precautions, stool testing)
audits.f: 32% (10) had documented medication review; of 90% (28) on a PPI, only 21% (6) were held; of 90% (28) on regular laxatives, only 39% (11) were held; 19% (6) continued on antibiotics for other organisms after microbiology discussion; 55% (17) isolated after new-onset diarrhoea; 65% (20) had a stool culture sent for CDI testing; 25% (5) tested positive for C. difficile

audits.t: P37 A retrospective audit of molnupiravir prescribing in the virtual hospital via the CMDU pathway
audits.tp: Molnupiravir prescribing appropriateness via a virtual hospital COVID-19 pathway
audits.st: NHS England Interim Clinical Commissioning Policy on antivirals/neutralizing monoclonal antibodies for non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients, with 4 local standards each set at 100% (confirmed infection; ineligibility for nirmatrelvir/ritonavir due to renal/liver impairment or drug interactions; documented reason for sotrovimab ineligibility)
audits.f: 100% had confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection; only 29% were ineligible for nirmatrelvir/ritonavir due to stage 3-5 CKD; only 29% ineligible due to significant drug-drug interactions; only 22.6% had a documented reason for sotrovimab ineligibility; majority (71%) did not have severe renal/liver impairment excluding them from first-line treatment
audits.c: not reported (feedback given to virtual hospital team to document rationale for treatment choice; access to a dedicated antimicrobial pharmacist introduced)

audits.t: O03 Scale and spread of a quality improvement initiative promoting metronidazole IV to oral switch (IVOST) in the acute hospital setting: antimicrobial stewardship, patient safety, workforce and environmental sustainability benefits
audits.tp: IV to oral antibiotic switch (metronidazole) scale and spread
audits.st: Local antimicrobial stewardship IV-to-oral switch (IVOST) targets for metronidazole (bioavailability >90%), scaled from a prior single-site QI result of 45% reduction
audits.f: baseline oral and IV metronidazole usage data collected prior to the scale-and-spread intervention
audits.c: QI scale and spread approach: pharmacist/pharmacy technician prospective audit and feedback, presentations to medical/nursing/pharmacy teams, ward posters, staff champions, and HEPMA electronic IVOST prompts
audits.r2: 64% median reduction in IV metronidazole defined daily doses (23,724 fewer IV administrations annually); 26% median shift in IV proportion of total use; 38% median reduction in drug cost; annual carbon footprint saving of 35.1 tonnes CO2e; nursing time saved 7908 hours/year

audits.t: P31 An observational prospective audit on the use of vancomycin and ciprofloxacin in the treatment of severe community-acquired pneumonia in penicillin-allergic patients in NHS Lothian
audits.tp: Vancomycin and ciprofloxacin prescribing for severe community-acquired pneumonia in penicillin-allergic patients
audits.st: NHS Lothian local guidelines for treatment of severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in penicillin-allergic patients, and MHRA guidance on fluoroquinolone counselling
audits.f: vancomycin levels taken in 11/18 patients, 8 reaching therapeutic levels in a median of 2 days; 83% received ciprofloxacin orally; no patients had documented fluoroquinolone counselling despite 72% being aged >65 and 39% on oral steroids; only 33% were stepped down to oral doxycycline; mean antibiotic duration 7.3 days

audits.t: Clinical pharmacist-led antifungal drug utilization reviews in cancer care hospital: a prospective audit and feedback
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Antifungals were prescribed for suspected fungal infection in 41.7%; febrile neutropenia was present in 55.4%; most common isolate C. albicans (15.4%); most prescribed antifungals were voriconazole (38.8%) and amphotericin B (31.7%); pharmacist-led interventions included IV-to-oral switch (18%), change of drug therapy (17.4%) and dose reduction (16.9%), and all interventions were accepted by the antifungal stewardship team (100%).

audits.t: P11 A quality improvement baseline evaluation of IV gentamicin management in the acute hospital setting following introduction of an electronic prescribing system (HEPMA)
audits.tp: IV gentamicin prescribing, administration and monitoring management
audits.st: Local prescribing, administering and monitoring (PAM) chart standards for IV gentamicin, restricted to 4 days treatment with provision of patient information leaflets
audits.f: median 80% of initial gentamicin therapeutic drug monitoring samples taken at the correct time pre-HEPMA
audits.c: Introduction of electronic prescribing (HEPMA) in 2021, changing the IV gentamicin prescribing process at ward level
audits.r2: IV gentamicin appropriately prescribed on both PAM chart and HEPMA in 96%; initial dose (96%) and frequency (100%) calculations of high standard; 96% of durations within the 4-day window; but 21% of doses delayed >1 hour, only 32% of administered doses documented on HEPMA, initial TDM sampling at correct time fell to 63%, and only 5% of patients had documented provision of a patient information leaflet and counselling

audits.t: P24 Scale and spread of a metronidazole ‘Go Green’ IV to oral switch (IVOST) grassroots quality improvement initiative in Scotland’s largest acute health board
audits.tp: IV to oral antibiotic switch (metronidazole) scale and spread
audits.st: Local antimicrobial stewardship IV-to-oral switch (IVOST) targets for metronidazole, scaled from a prior single-site QI result of 45% reduction in IV administrations
audits.f: baseline oral and IV metronidazole usage data collected prior to the health-board-wide scale-and-spread intervention
audits.c: QI scale and spread grassroots initiative: ward posters, HEPMA IVOST prompts, a promotional blog, targeted prospective audit/feedback and antimicrobial ward round review, multidisciplinary staff champions and 'Gold Star' awards, and regular governance feedback
audits.r2: 33% median reduction in total metronidazole DDDs/1000 occupied bed days; 46% median reduction in IV metronidazole DDDs (63,000 fewer IV administrations annually); nursing time saved 21,000 hours/year; 37% (£60,000) annual drug cost reduction; annual carbon footprint saving of 93.3 tonnes CO2e

audits.t: P25 A quality improvement initiative to improve IV gentamicin management and promote a multidisciplinary approach to patient-centred care in the acute setting
audits.st: Local standard: NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde prescribing, administering and monitoring (PAM) chart targets for IV gentamicin, including therapeutic drug monitoring, counselling and patient information leaflet provision
audits.f: Counselling/patient information leaflet provision 4%; 48-hourly prescribing documentation 58%; doses given on time 75%; administration documentation on HEPMA 38%; initial gentamicin sample taken at the appropriate time 51%.
audits.c: QI tests of change: 'bite-size' multidisciplinary ward teaching, a pharmacy technician gentamicin counselling service, collation of patient feedback, 'Gold Star' awards, multidisciplinary staff champions, a 'Top Tips' poster, prospective audit/feedback, and removal of outdated PAM charts
audits.r2: Counselling/PIL provision increased to 21%; 48-hourly prescribing documentation increased to 85%; doses given on time increased to 88%; HEPMA administration documentation improved marginally to 41%; initial sample timing improved marginally to 55%; removal of outdated PAM charts was the only QI target fully met.

audits.t: P31 An audit investigating community acquired pneumonia (CAP) antibiotic duration at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT)
audits.st: National and local antimicrobial guidelines recommending 5 days of antibiotic treatment duration for community-acquired pneumonia (CAP)
audits.f: adherence to 5-day guidance was 58% (96/165); of the 42% (69) treated >5 days, reasons were extra doses prescribed on discharge (n=35), no reason documented (n=17), documented intent of 7-day course (n=7), symptoms not improved (n=7), infection markers not normalized (n=3); of 75 courses completed after discharge, only 53% (40/75) adhered to the 5-day guidance
audits.c: not reported (consideration being given to an order set/digital tool to standardize antimicrobial prescribing, not yet implemented)

audits.t: In a bind: a quality improvement project for reducing fluoroquinolones drug–drug interactions with multivalent cations
audits.st: Local standard: avoidance of fluoroquinolone co-administration with multivalent cations within 2 hours
audits.f: Among patients who received a multivalent cation on the same day as a fluoroquinolone (n=101 overall), co-administration within 2 hours of the fluoroquinolone occurred in 62% pre-intervention.
audits.c: Bundle of interventions: nursing education, updated medication administration record (MAR) comments, and new administration times
audits.r2: Co-administration within 2 hours fell to 22% post-intervention (p<0.001).

audits.t: P08 Improving antibiotic stewardship in paediatric appendicitis: a quality improvement project
audits.st: BSAC (British Society for Antimicrobial Chemotherapy) recommendations for antimicrobial management of paediatric appendicitis
audits.f: Overall guideline adherence 26%; 45% of uncomplicated cases were managed appropriately, but no complicated cases received guideline-based therapy; broad-spectrum piperacillin/tazobactam was frequently used inappropriately; only 25% of complicated cases had appropriately timed post-operative blood tests, 87.5% received prolonged antibiotic courses, and infection-related readmission occurred in 12.5% of cases.
audits.c: Structured departmental teaching session for medical and nursing staff, supported by visual reminder posters displayed in the paediatric surgical department
audits.r2: Overall adherence improved substantially; appropriate management rose to 60% in uncomplicated and 40% in complicated cases; piperacillin/tazobactam use fully aligned with guideline indications; 70% of complicated cases received the correct antibiotic duration, 50% had appropriately timed post-operative blood tests, and no infection-related readmissions occurred.

audits.t: P19 Antibiotic MOT: improving antimicrobial stewardship through nurse-led audit
audits.tp: Nurse-led antimicrobial stewardship audit and feedback
audits.st: Local antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) quality indicators covering IV antibiotic administration, blood culture collection, IV-to-oral switch (IVOS) assessment and documentation, assessed via a 19-question nurse-led audit tool (Tendable)
audits.f: 98% (44/45) of IV antibiotic doses administered without omission; blood cultures taken prior to first IV dose in 95% (19/20); only 67% (26/39) of medical/surgical patients appropriately receiving IV rather than oral antibiotics; IVOS documented electronically in only 3% (1/31) of nursing assessments; in surgical areas, only 57% (4/7) of patients with EWS >=5 had two sets of blood cultures taken
audits.c: not reported (planned next steps: targeted ward-based interventions, strengthening the ward nurse role in IVOS, and governance reporting via performance infographics)

audits.t: P29 A nudge to safe dosing and sound sleeping: using visual cues to improve safety and sleep quality of patients prescribed intermittent IV vancomycin in the acute hospital setting
audits.tp: Timing of intermittent IV vancomycin doses to protect sleep and safety
audits.st: Local quality improvement target of reducing intermittent IV vancomycin doses prescribed between midnight and 6am to less than 10% by January 2026
audits.f: median 18% of intermittent IV vancomycin doses prescribed between midnight and 6am
audits.c: Nudge-theory based visual cues (colour-coded blue prescribing boxes and moon symbols) added directly to the prescribing, administering and monitoring (PAM) chart to direct prescribing/administration away from the middle of the night
audits.r2: median proportion of doses prescribed between midnight and 6am fell to 7%, meeting the QI target of less than 10%

audits.t: P64 Improving antimicrobial stewardship in critical care through a structured 72 h review: a quality improvement study
audits.tp: Antimicrobial stewardship documentation via a structured 72-hour review
audits.st: NHS England 'Start Smart Then Focus' antimicrobial stewardship strategy, endorsed by the Faculty of Intensive Care Medicine, requiring early structured review of antimicrobial therapy
audits.f: intended duration documented in microbiology notes in 46.7% (June), 55.5% (August) and 45.4% (October) of cases; duration documented on the actual prescription in 17.6%, 18.2% and 23.5% respectively; documentation of indication was 41.2%, 9.1% and 0% respectively
audits.c: A structured 72-hour antimicrobial review ('72h pause') embedded into electronic microbiology round documentation, with mandatory prompts to document duration and select a review outcome (continue, amend, cease), supported by departmental teaching sessions and posters
audits.r2: duration documentation in microbiology notes improved to 84.6%; duration stated on the prescription improved to 55%; documentation of indication showed no improvement, remaining low at 10%

audits.t: P69 A cross-sectional audit of antibiotic utilization and AWaRe stewardship alignment in hospitalized patients
audits.st: WHO AWaRe (Access, Watch, Reserve) antibiotic classification framework
audits.f: Antibiotics prescribed in 44.4% (114/257); Watch group use 72.8%, Access 10.5%, Reserve 8.8%; mean duration 3.62 days (median 3, IQR 2-5); approximately 60% of prescriptions met stewardship alignment criteria; cultures obtained in 67.3%, with 28.1% positivity.

audits.t: P85 An audit of the appropriateness of systemic antifungal prescribing for non-haematology/oncology indications
audits.tp: Appropriateness of systemic antifungal prescribing outside haematology/oncology
audits.st: Local antimicrobial guidelines with audit standards of >=90% for: indication per infection specialist advice or treatment guidelines; dose appropriate for renal/hepatic function; dose appropriate for weight; and duration appropriate per guidelines or clinical documentation
audits.f: choice of antifungal in line with guidelines except for dermatophyte infections (4.8%); dosing appropriate for renal function in 95.2% and for weight in 97.6% (meeting the >=90% standards); duration guideline-compliant or per specialist advice in 83.3% (below the 90% standard); therapeutic drug monitoring undertaken for all patients where indicated, but sampling timing errors were common (post-dose rather than pre-dose trough); significant azole-statin and azole-citalopram interactions were identified

audits.t: SO016SPREAD OF ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY IMPROVEMENT PROGAMME ACROSS A LARGE  MULTI SITED NHS HOSPITAL
audits.tp: Acute kidney injury detection and management quality improvement
audits.st: UK-wide AKI audit (2009) benchmarks and local standards for timely AKI recognition and management
audits.f: AKI recognition within 24 hours 52% (Central Campus); poor AKI care and delays in detection identified by 2009 UK-wide and 2014 local audits
audits.c: Multifaceted QI Programme: electronic AKI alert, education, stakeholder engagement, AKI Priority Care Checklist (PCC), AKI Clinical Nurse Specialist change agents, staggered rollout across Central, West and South Campus hospitals including paediatric adaptation
audits.r2: Recognition within 24h improved from 52% to 100% (Central Campus); 34% reduction in AKI incidence (p<0.00001), 26% reduction in AKI length of stay, 42% reduction in AKI days, 10% less AKI-associated mortality; Children's Hospital 24% reduction in AKI incidence (p<0.0001) and 34% reduction in hospital-acquired AKI, recognition improved 42% to 100%; South Campus recognition improved 67% to 100%, 19% reduction in AKI incidence (p<0.0015); West Campus recognition 100%

audits.t: P0629ESTABLISHING MORTALITY ASSOCIATED WITH AKI IN A DGH AND THEN TRYING TO DO SOMETHING ABOUT IT- INTRODUCTION AND AUDIT OF THE AKI7 CARE BUNDLE
audits.tp: AKI care bundle (AKI7) introduction and audit
audits.st: NCEPOD 2009 report benchmark that only 50% of AKI patients received good care; locally introduced AKI7 care bundle standard
audits.f: 79% did not progress beyond AKI stage 1, 13% stage 2, 8% stage 3; 75% investigated with urinalysis, 94% fluid balance monitoring, 5% renal tract ultrasound, 58% referred to nephrologist; 1-year mortality 29% stage 1, 51% stage 2, 65% stage 3, all-stage combined 39.1%
audits.c: Electronic alert system and order set proforma: the AKI7 care bundle
audits.r2: Following AKI7 launch, renal tract ultrasound requests increased from 5% to 20%, urinalysis from 75% to 83%, and renal physician input requests from 65% to 75%

audits.t: P1156TWO YEAR FOLLOW UP QUALITY INDICATORS COMPLIANCE IN A LARGE INTERNATIONAL PERITONEAL DIALYSIS INSTITUTION
audits.st: Twelve locally-defined quality indicators derived from English/Spanish CKD and PD guidelines
audits.f: Baseline QI achievement year 2017
audits.r2: Significant increase in QI achievement in 2018 vs 2017; ≥75% of patients met target for total weekly Kt/Vurea, 24h fluid removal, mean arterial pressure and serum albumin

audits.t: Prolonged patient survival after implementation of a continuous quality improvement programme empowered by digital transformation in a large dialysis network
audits.tp: Continuous quality improvement in dialysis (KPI achievement and survival)
audits.st: Fresenius Medical Care medical patient review key performance indicators (KPIs)
audits.f: Baseline KPI target achievement before MPR-CQI implementation
audits.c: Medical patient review continuous quality improvement (MPR-CQI) policy
audits.r2: Increase in KPI target achievements; mediation analysis showed significant mortality reduction (OR 0.70, 95%CI 0.65-0.76, p<0.0001) via improved KPI achievement
audits.co: not reported (Europe, Middle East and Africa)

audits.t: MO926: Development and Implementation of an Electronic Patient-Reported Outcome System to Support Health-Related Quality of Life Management in a Large, European Dialysis Network
audits.tp: Electronic patient-reported outcome measures in dialysis quality of life management
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 152 centres (93%) joined; 22.5% reported moderate to very severe pruritus; 10%-20% reported complications during last dialysis session; recovery time >3h ranged 34.8% (France) to 46.4% (Ireland)

audits.t: Impact of a continuous quality improvement program on contrast-induced nephropathy in outpatients with chronic kidney disease: an interrupted time-series study
audits.st: Locally developed CIN-QI protocol (shorter saline hydration protocol) triggered by automatic eGFR alert
audits.f: Annual prophylactic hydration rate ranged 2.0%-23.2%; follow-up kidney function testing 18.6%-25.8%
audits.c: Automatic medical record alert instructing prophylactic hydration and nephrology consultation for eGFR <45
audits.r2: Prophylactic hydration rate rose to 59.2%-75.2% (p<0.001); follow-up testing rose to 34.1%-42.5% (p<0.001); CIN incidence declined by 10.0% at level (p=0.002) and 2.9%/year in trend (p<0.001)

audits.t: #3123 INCREASING THE USE OF REGIONAL CITRATE ANTICOAGULATION FOR CKRT IN A LARGE TERTIARY CENTER: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
audits.tp: Regional citrate anticoagulation uptake in CKRT
audits.st: KDIGO recommendation for regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) as first-line CKRT anticoagulation
audits.f: RCA-CKRT uptake baseline 10.5%±7.7% (median 9.8%) of all CKRT sessions
audits.c: PDSA cycles: standardised inclusion/exclusion criteria and poster, peer-review learning, ICU resident didactic teaching, nurse refresher course
audits.r2: RCA-CKRT uptake increased to 22.5%±14.6% (median 21.5%, p=0.022); 25.3%±15.8% excluding supply-disruption months

audits.t: #4727 FLOZINATION: A ROLLING QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROGRAMME
audits.tp: SGLT2 inhibitor prescribing for chronic kidney disease
audits.st: Evidence-based prescribing criteria for SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin/dapagliflozin) in CKD per licensing and CREDENCE/DAPA-CKD trial evidence
audits.f: 326 patients identified as suitable under initial canagliflozin licensing criteria; 562 with diabetes and 5262 without diabetes identified as potentially suitable under dapagliflozin licensing
audits.c: Electronic patient record alert for eligible patients, SGLT2i protocol advertised via poster in outpatient clinics, evaluation of clinician attitudes
audits.r2: 1146 patients prescribed SGLT2i; 94% of clinicians surveyed felt well equipped to prescribe SGLT2i; 54% of prescribed patients lived in areas of high socioeconomic deprivation; compared with general outpatient population, distribution of deprivation was similar but higher proportion female (46%)

audits.t: #5868 PREVALENCE AND MANAGEMENT OF CHRONIC COMPLICATIONS IN PATIENTS WITH DIABETES AND ADVANCED CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE: A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT
audits.tp: Management of anaemia, bone mineral disorder and metabolic acidosis in advanced CKD with diabetes
audits.st: KDIGO guidelines for monitoring and treating anaemia, mineral bone disorder and metabolic acidosis in CKD stage 3b or higher
audits.f: 47% had at least one diabetes-related complication; anaemia present in 93.4% (171/183), only 22% (38/133) of those with anaemia treated, of which 36.8% treated adequately; BMD present in 81.2% (82/101), 47.6% (39/82) treated, 42% optimally corrected; metabolic acidosis present in 82.8% (135/168), 40% (54/135) treated, 53% optimally corrected; 33.9% (65/192) had all 3 complications

audits.t: #1452 Halting the progression of chronic kidney disease; an audit of the use of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone blockers and SGLT-2 inhibitors
audits.tp: RAAS blocker and SGLT2 inhibitor prescribing in CKD outpatients
audits.st: EMPA-KIDNEY trial evidence and UK Kidney Association Clinical Practice Guidelines for RAAS blockade and SGLT2i use in CKD
audits.f: 57% (94/165) already on RAAS blockade; 12.1% (20/165) already on SGLT2i (75% of these also on RAASb); 7.9% (13/165) maximised on RAASb and 2.4% (4/165) started SGLT2i at the clinic visit; missed opportunity for therapeutic optimisation in 79.5% (66/83) of eligible patients
audits.c: not reported (single prospective audit, no re-audit)

audits.t: #2489 Implementing a clinical governance and performance benchmarking model in dialysis: the DaVita quality index experience in Brazil
audits.tp: Dialysis quality index clinical governance benchmarking
audits.st: DaVita Quality Index (KPIs: Kt/V≥1.3, haemoglobin control, phosphorus ≤5.5mg/dL, IDWG, CVC use), benchmarked against Brazilian Society of Nephrology, ISN and ERA registries
audits.f: Mean DQI score 39.67
audits.c: Implementation of the DaVita Quality Index structured clinical governance and benchmarking model
audits.r2: Mean DQI score rose to 57.29, a 44.41% improvement (p<0.001)

audits.t: #805 Effects of healthcare quality on renal outcomes in early-stage chronic kidney disease patients: a nationwide cohort study
audits.tp: Quality indicators in early-stage CKD care
audits.st: Three quality indicators: RAS inhibitor prescription, proteinuria testing, NSAID avoidance
audits.f: 14.3% achieved maximum QI score of 3; 53.3% received RAS inhibitors, 47.9% underwent proteinuria testing, 59.2% avoided NSAIDs

audits.t: #3723 Implementation of a holistic quality improvement framework is associated with lower mortality in hemodialysis patients across 6 countries
audits.tp: Holistic quality improvement framework and mortality in haemodialysis
audits.st: Locally set KPI targets within the 'InterStellar' quality framework (35 KPIs covering patient safety, nursing care and traditional medical indicators)
audits.f: All-cause annualised mortality 17.8% [7.2%-26%] at the beginning of the framework
audits.c: Implementation of the 'InterStellar' holistic quality improvement framework with quarterly KPI scoring across patient safety, nursing care and medical indicators
audits.r2: Total InterStellar scores increased by 17% [10%-24%]; patient safety indicators improved by 20.1% [2%-34%]; nursing care audit indicators by 15% [8%-26%]; traditional medical outcomes by 16% [9%-30%]; all-cause annualised mortality improved to 13.6% [5.1%-19%], statistically significant reduction in all but one country

audits.t: Audit of waist measurement methods during statutory diving medical assessments.
audits.tp: Waist circumference measurement technique in diving medicals
audits.st: World Health Organization (WHO) consensus guidance on waist circumference measurement
audits.f: Only 7/76 (9%) of respondents measured waist circumference fully in line with WHO guidance; consistency in clothing/breathing/posture but variability in measurement site

audits.t: Using clinical audit to improve the quality of mental health-care services for people with learning disabilities
audits.tp: Psychotropic prescribing in learning disability mental health services
audits.st: NICE and Royal College of Psychiatrists standards on psychotropic prescribing and behavioural interventions
audits.f: Prescribing within BNF maximum limits for all patients; undocumented off-label prescribing in a significant proportion; objective outcome measures used in only a small proportion of patients
audits.c: not reported (action plan recommended a prescribing database and standardised measures)

audits.t: Adult ADHD outcome audit based on NICE guidelines
audits.st: NICE guideline for adult ADHD (15 standards identified)
audits.f: Service achieved 80-95% in medication monitoring, transition service, and shared-care prescribing; underperformed on non-pharmacological interventions such as CBT

audits.t: Do demographic, and clinical characteristics influence meeting NICE quality standards for young people transitioning to adult intellectual disability services?
audits.tp: Transition to adult intellectual disability services
audits.st: NICE quality standard QS140 for transition to adult services
audits.f: Only 22% had sufficient recorded data to determine compliance with the standard; available data indicated poor compliance
audits.co: not reported (UK, implied by NICE standard)

audits.t: Quality Improvement in Cystectomy Care with Enhanced Recovery (QUICCER) study.
audits.tp: Enhanced recovery pathway audit for radical cystectomy
audits.st: Cystectomy Enhanced Recovery Pathway (CERP) quality composite score / adherence to CERP elements
audits.f: Non-CERP group median length of hospital stay was 8 days.
audits.c: Implementation of a cystectomy enhanced recovery pathway (CERP), July 2013.
audits.r2: CERP group median length of stay was 5 days, significantly shorter, with no increase in complications or readmissions; audited CERP quality measures were associated with reduced length of stay.

audits.t: Analysis of a 7-year national online audit of the management of open reconstructive urethral surgery in men.
audits.tp: Urethral reconstruction surgery management and outcomes
audits.st: Comparison of UK practice with contemporary literature and accepted guidelines/standards for urethral stricture management
audits.f: Data entered by 50 surgeons at 39 centres; field completeness 70.7% preoperative, 74.3% operative, 53.7% follow-up; low risk of Clavien-Dindo grade >=3 complications overall, with outcomes similar to contemporary series except for posterior urethral fistulae

audits.t: Surgical checklist adherence across urology expertise levels impacts transurethral resection of bladder tumour quality indicators
audits.tp: Surgical checklist adherence in bladder tumour resection
audits.st: Standardised peri-procedural nine-item TURBT checklist
audits.f: Median checklist completion rate was higher for residents and young consultants than experts (56% and 56% vs 44%, p=0.009); residents were more likely to have detrusor muscle present in the specimen than expert consultants (OR 1.75, 95% CI 1.03 to 2.99, p=0.04); persistent disease at second-look TURBT was associated with resident status at initial TURBT (OR 4.24, 95% CI 1.14 to 17.70, p=0.037).

audits.t: Impact of ureteroscopy on nephroureterectomy and standards of care compliance in upper tract urothelial carcinoma: the BAUS UK I-DUNC audit.
audits.tp: Diagnostic ureteroscopy and standards of care in upper tract urothelial carcinoma
audits.st: Compliance with post-operative intravesical Mitomycin C instillation and adjuvant chemotherapy for >=pT2 disease
audits.f: Diagnostic ureteroscopy performed in 61.3% of cases, delaying nephroureterectomy by a median of 53 days (130 vs 77 days); associated with increased metachronous bladder cancer recurrence and higher positive surgical margin rates in >=pT2 disease; compliance with MMC therapy and adjuvant chemotherapy was low

audits.t: An audit of growth hormone replacement for GH-deficient adults in Scotland.
audits.tp: Growth hormone replacement compliance with NICE criteria
audits.st: NICE guidelines (August 2003) for growth hormone therapy in GH-deficient adults
audits.f: Comparing pre- and post-NICE guidance: documented AGHDA-QoL score >11 before starting GH rose from 25% (pre-NICE) to 77% (post-NICE); overall only 18% (39/208) met the full NICE criteria for starting and continuing GH (11% pre-NICE, 35% post-NICE).

audits.t: Variations in the management of acute illness in children with congenital adrenal hyperplasia: An audit of three paediatric hospitals
audits.tp: Management of acute illness in children with congenital adrenal hyperplasia
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 66.7% (214) resulted in admission; 49.2% (158) received IV hydrocortisone; 9.0% diagnosed with adrenal crisis; 64.2% (206) had used oral stress dosing and 22.1% (71) IM hydrocortisone prior to presentation; management varied significantly between hospitals, IM hydrocortisone use ranging from 7.0% to 45.8%

audits.t: Initiation and Maintenance of Low‐Dose Transdermal Testosterone in Non‐Binary Individuals: A Retrospective Audit
audits.tp: Low-dose testosterone dosing in gender-affirming care
audits.st: Current gender affirmation guidelines for testosterone dosing (standard, full masculinising doses)
audits.f: Median dose at initiation was 12.5 mg for testosterone 1% gel, rising to 25 mg at last follow-up (p<0.01); for testosterone 5% cream, median dose was 50 mg at initiation and 50 mg (50-68.8) at last follow-up (p=0.02); median serum total testosterone was 11 nmol/L; 40 of 46 (87%) remained on low-dose testosterone at last follow-up and 6 (13%) increased to full dose; of those with 12 months or more follow-up (n=30), 26 (87%) remained on low dose; 3 (7%) developed polycythaemia (haematocrit greater than 0.5).

audits.t: Attendance at iron deficiency anaemia clinic: audit of outcomes 5 years on
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for anaemia investigation
audits.f: Diagnosis found initially in 266 (42%); 124 (19%) had a GI luminal neoplasm, 54 (8%) malignant
audits.r2: Of 373 initially undiagnosed patients, 6 (2%) later diagnosed with GI luminal malignancy, 18 (5%) with non-luminal/non-GI malignancy
audits.co: not reported (UK, implied by BSG guidelines)

audits.t: A dedicated high‐quality service for the management of patients with an inherited risk of colorectal cancer
audits.tp: Family history of bowel cancer service quality (colonoscopic surveillance guideline adherence)
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guidelines for colonoscopic surveillance in family history of colorectal cancer; revised Bethesda criteria for Lynch syndrome identification
audits.f: Colonoscopies not indicated by BSG guidelines 39.6%; surveillance colonoscopy performed 10.6 years too early on average; adenoma detection rate 17%; tumour mismatch repair (MMR) testing rate 3.4%
audits.c: Implementation of a specialist family history of bowel cancer service in secondary care
audits.r2: Colonoscopies not indicated by BSG guidelines reduced to 5.8% (P<0.001); surveillance colonoscopy performed 5.9 years too early (P=0.01); adenoma detection rate increased to 31.9% (P<0.01); tumour MMR testing increased to 91.8% (P<0.01)

audits.t: International evaluation of circumferential resection margins after rectal cancer resection: insights from the Swedish and Dutch audits
audits.tp: Circumferential resection margin quality in rectal cancer surgery
audits.st: Swedish ColoRectal Cancer Registry and Dutch ColoRectal Audit: circumferential resection margin (CRM) quality indicator
audits.f: Overall positive CRM (CRM+) rate was 7.8% in Sweden and 5.4% in the Netherlands; common independent risk factors for CRM+ in cT1-3 disease were cT3 stage, abdominoperineal excision, and multivisceral resection; no common risk factors were found for cT4 disease; hospital volume was independently associated with CRM+ in the cT1-3 Dutch population.

audits.t: An audit of process and outcome for emergency colectomy in England and Wales.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 37% (440/1204) underwent colectomy within 5 days of admission; 32% (383/1204) admitted >10 days prior to surgery; colorectal surgeons present in 72% (869/1204); consultants attended 94% (1137/1204); laparoscopy attempted in 32% (390/1204, range 0-100% between institutions); 30-day mortality 2.9% (35/1204)

audits.t: The learning curve of transanal total mesorectal excision for rectal cancer is associated with local recurrence: results from a multicentre external audit
audits.tp: Transanal total mesorectal excision learning curve and local recurrence
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Corrected 3-year local recurrence rate was 9.7% in the implementation cohort; crude local recurrence rate after implementation was 12.5%.
audits.r2: Corrected 3-year local recurrence rate fell to 3.5% in the prolonged experience cohort (3.4% overall once experience increased); overall 2- and 3-year local recurrence rates across all 624 patients were 4.6% and 6.6% respectively; procedural experience was an independent risk factor for local recurrence, alongside advanced stage and pelvic sepsis.

audits.t: Reducing surgical site infection rates in colorectal surgery - a quality improvement approach to implementing a comprehensive bundle.
audits.tp: Surgical site infection prevention bundle in colorectal surgery
audits.st: NICE and WHO guidance on core SSI-prevention interventions; locally agreed comprehensive perioperative SSI bundle with a target of 95% compliance for each component
audits.f: overall SSI rate 16.7% (38/228), predominantly superficial SSI (79.0% of infections)
audits.c: Multidisciplinary colorectal SSI bundle implemented via quality improvement methodology, amended four times (December 2012, March 2013, June 2013, October 2015) based on emerging evidence and compliance data, with education, visual reminders, root cause analysis of SSI cases and integration into the surgical safety checklist
audits.r2: overall SSI rate 8.8% (34/386); overall rate fell to 5.1% in the final study year (2018) from 16.4% in the first year (2012), with 87 consecutive cases without infection in 2018

audits.t: Microscopic colitis in Northern Ireland: an updated clinicopathological audit and assessment of compliance with European guidelines.
audits.tp: Microscopic colitis diagnosis and management audit
audits.st: 2020 European guidelines for microscopic colitis
audits.f: 89 (41%) collagenous colitis, 128 (59%) lymphocytic colitis; incidence 7.6-11.5 per 100,000 adults; separate right/left colon sampling in 85% (2019-2020) vs 30% (2008-2016)

audits.t: Incidence and risk factors for secondary failure after acute obstetric sphincter injury repair – an audit of 239 women
audits.tp: Secondary failure of obstetric sphincter injury repair
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 41.8% (100/239) had EAUS evidence of sphincter defects; only 20% with repair failure were symptomatic

audits.t: Patterns of <scp>DNA</scp> mismatch repair protein expression for primary and recurrent colorectal cancer at an advanced surgical unit: A retrospective audit
audits.tp: Mismatch repair testing in recurrent colorectal cancer
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: IHC testing completed in 88.7% of primary resections vs 39.3% of recurrent resections; MMR profile changed in 10.6% (9/85) of paired cases

audits.t: Experience of a single academic institution with the National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer and the resulting improvement in care
audits.st: National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer (NAPRC) standards
audits.f: Pre-rectal tumour board cohort often failed to meet attendance standards
audits.c: Establishment of an accredited rectal cancer multidisciplinary tumour board (accredited 2019)
audits.r2: All patients in the rectal tumour board cohort met all NAPRC criteria; compliance improved for 13 clinical service metrics, 10 significantly

audits.t: Acute pilonidal abscess: Prospective nationwide audit in the Netherlands
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Incision and drainage was performed in 205 of 208 patients (99%); wound healing rate after incision and drainage was 42.2% at the outpatient clinic, with a median time to closure of 43 days; complication rate 4.4%; 1-year questionnaires were completed by 158 of 205 patients (77.1%), of whom 15 (7.3%) had a recurrent abscess and 8.8% had symptomatic chronic disease.

audits.t:
Towards safer colorectal surgery worldwide: Outcomes and benchmarks from the
                    <scp>ESCP CORREA</scp>
                    2022 audit
audits.st: ESCP CORREA benchmarking of 30-day postoperative outcomes against previous audits
audits.f: 72.2% of resections were for malignancy, 74.4% elective; minimally invasive surgery was used in 55.2% (48.7% laparoscopic, 6.5% robotic); primary anastomosis in 90.3%; 30-day anastomotic leak rate 7.96% overall (7.3% in malignant and 10.2% in benign disease); leak rates by procedure were 6.9% (right colectomy), 7.7% (left colectomy), 9.7% (anterior rectal resection), 16.0% (pouch) and 11.8% (subtotal colectomy); risk factors for leak were male sex (9.3% vs 6.3%, OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.95, p=0.023) and emergency surgery (11.4% vs 7.1%, OR 1.58, 95% CI 1.10 to 2.27, p=0.013); 30-day mortality 2.38%.

audits.t: Ditch the drapes: Non‐sterile substitution in proctology, a population‐based cost and carbon life cycle analysis with early implementation audit
audits.tp: Sustainability and waste reduction in proctology procedures
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Suction unused in 54% and diathermy unused in 46% of audited procedures; source reduction projected to save AUD 40, 1.36 kg waste and 7.9 kg CO2e per procedure; no infective complications recorded in 100 procedures
audits.c: Non-sterile substitution: drape avoidance, clean non-sterile protective equipment, selective opening of suction/diathermy

audits.t: Quality of initial <scp>HIV</scp> care in Canada: extension of a composite programmatic assessment tool for <scp>HIV</scp> therapy
audits.tp: Quality of initial HIV care (Programmatic Compliance Score)
audits.st: HIV treatment guideline-based noncompliance indicators (CD4/viral load testing frequency, resistance testing, baseline CD4, regimen choice, viral suppression)
audits.f: Median PCS score 1.0 (Q1-Q3 1.0-2.0); 21% scored 0, 8% scored ≥4

audits.t: Monitoring of older HIV‐1‐positive adults by HIV clinics in the United Kingdom: a national quality improvement initiative
audits.tp: Monitoring of older HIV-positive adults against BHIVA guidelines
audits.st: British HIV Association (BHIVA) monitoring guidelines for adults aged 50 and over with HIV
audits.f: 97% had viral load measured within target interval; 94% had all medications recorded within 15 months; only 67% had 10-year CVD risk calculated within 3 years; 80% had smoking status documented within 2 years; 92% had blood pressure checked within 15 months; HIV services communicated with GPs for 90% of consenting individuals but consulted electronic primary care records for only 10%
audits.c: Individual feedback provided to clinical services to support quality improvement (as part of the national audit process)

audits.t: Quality improvement report: Investigating barriers in HIV testing oncology patients to optimize HIV testing practice.
audits.tp: HIV testing offer rate in oncology patients
audits.st: Swiss national HIV testing recommendations (updated November 2013)
audits.f: IBITOP I: 18% of patients with newly diagnosed non-AIDS-defining cancers were offered HIV testing; 91% of those offered accepted
audits.c: Interactive training sessions for oncology staff on HIV testing (2015)
audits.r2: Of 423 patients, 257 (60.8%) were offered HIV testing; patient acceptance of testing offered was 83.2%; no HIV test was positive

audits.t: Outcomes for People with Atrial Fibrillation in an Australian National Audit of Stroke Care
audits.tp: Outcomes for stroke patients with atrial fibrillation (national audit)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Stroke unit management (aOR 0.57) and swallow assessment within 24h (aOR 0.71) associated with increased survival; AF independently associated with in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.46)

audits.t: An audit of liquid‐based cervical cytology screening samples (ThinPrep and SurePath) reported as glandular neoplasia
audits.tp: Liquid-based cervical cytology glandular neoplasia diagnostic accuracy
audits.st: not reported (local and national audit of glandular neoplasia reporting)
audits.f: PPV of category 6A was 100% for both ThinPrep and SurePath; combined PPV for 6A+6B was 88.4%

audits.t: Review of invasive cervical cancers and uptake of disclosure of results: an audit of procedures and response
audits.tp: Invasive cervical cancer case review and results disclosure
audits.st: not reported (local case review process)
audits.f: 61 women in Group A (screening/management factor implicated); 36 (37%) classified in Group B (never screened or defaulted)

audits.t: An audit of the adequacy of acute wound care documentation of surgical inpatients.
audits.st: Australian Wound Management Association guidelines for wound care documentation
audits.f: Three-quarters of patients had no documentation of wound margins; over half had no documentation of dimensions, exudate or wound bed; only 75 (60%) dressing changes reviewed by both medical and nursing staff; wound dimensions/skin sensation recorded in <5% of dressing changes

audits.t: An audit of laryngoscopes and application of a new ISO standard.
audits.st: ISO 7376:2009 minimum illuminance level (500 lux); published minimum acceptable luminance of 100 cd/m2
audits.f: 190 reusable laryngoscopes screened; of 18 examined in detail against the ISO standard, only 2 met the minimum illuminance level of 500 lux after 10 minutes

audits.t: Two-year audit of computed tomographic colonography in a teaching hospital: are we meeting the standard?
audits.tp: Computed tomographic colonography (CTC) practice against published recommendations
audits.st: Published recommendations for CT colonography implementation
audits.f: Only 16% of ascending colon/caecal segments were clear of faecal or fluid contamination; rectum and sigmoid colon clear in 78% and 74% of cases; 91% of studies reported by appropriately trained radiologists; sensitivity 89%, specificity 94%, PPV 90% (all polyps), sensitivity 98.5% for lesions >5 mm; 25% had extracolonic abnormalities; no recorded complications.

audits.t: What interval between colorectal cancer resection and first surveillance colonoscopy? An audit of practice and yield
audits.tp: Surveillance colonoscopy interval after colorectal cancer resection
audits.st: not reported (guideline timings for first surveillance colonoscopy vary)
audits.f: Colonoscopic follow-up rate by 2 years was 32.8%
audits.r2: Colonoscopic follow-up rate by 2 years improved to 54.1%

audits.t: Quality of pathological reporting for renal cell cancer: implications for systemic therapy, prognostication and surveillance
audits.tp: Pathology reporting quality for renal cell cancer
audits.st: College of American Pathologists (CAP) reporting guidelines for renal cell carcinoma
audits.f: Only 59.9% of reports met CAP guidelines for tumour classification, margin, size, histology and grade; tumour classification omitted in 27.8%

audits.t: Oncologic multidisciplinary team meetings: evaluation of quality criteria
audits.st: Newly developed national guideline for optimal MDT meeting structure and function
audits.f: Good adherence to organisational criteria, but coordinator/administrative support often absent; core discipline attendance target of 100% never reached; specific documentation form used in only a quarter of meetings

audits.t: Guideline‐based development and practice test of quality indicators for physiotherapy care in patients with neck pain
audits.tp: Quality indicators for physiotherapy care in neck pain
audits.st: 40 newly developed guideline-based quality indicators (28 process, 12 outcome) for neck pain care
audits.f: Average 55.6% adherence to process indicators, with wide variation by step of clinical reasoning; outcomes for pain, headache and daily functioning improved significantly vs baseline

audits.t: Pain treatment facilities: do we need quantity or quality?
audits.st: International Association for the Study of Pain (IASP) Recommendations for Pain Treatment Services
audits.f: 88.9% (n=72) reported organised specialised pain care, provided by a pain management team in 86.1%; only a few hospitals could adhere to all IASP criteria

audits.t: Combining training in knowledge translation with quality improvement reduced 30‐day heart failure readmissions in a community hospital: a case study
audits.tp: Heart failure readmission reduction quality improvement
audits.st: Mandated heart failure quality measures
audits.f: 30-day heart failure readmission rate 23.1%
audits.c: Multidisciplinary evidence-based practice training combined with a three-phase protocol (patient education, medication reconciliation, transition to community care) and a full-time HF nurse coordinator
audits.r2: 30-day readmissions decreased to 16.4% (adjusted OR 0.64, 95%CI 0.42-0.97); comparison hospital changed from 22.3% to 20.2% (adjusted OR 0.87)

audits.t: Development of a proforma to improve quality of handover of surgical patients at the weekend.
audits.st: National guidelines used to design a standardised weekend handover proforma
audits.f: Baseline survey highlighted inadequate provision for weekend handover; after proforma introduction, 70% compliance with a median handover score of 83% (IQR 0-100)
audits.c: Standardised weekend handover proforma reinforced by three strategies: presentation at a clinical governance meeting, email reminder, and induction training combined with one-to-one interactive training
audits.r2: After governance meeting/refinement: 71% compliance, median score 65% (IQR 0-80, p=0.0516); after email: 69% compliance, median score 80% (IQR 0-90, p=0.1037); after induction training: 94% compliance, median score 90% (IQR 80-90, p=0.013), the only significant improvement

audits.t: Concordance between Optimal Care Pathways and colorectal cancer care: Identifying opportunities to improve quality and reduce disparities
audits.tp: Concordance with Optimal Care Pathway recommendations
audits.st: Australian Optimal Care Pathway (OCP) recommendations for colorectal cancer, 10 recommendations
audits.f: GP investigation use ranged from 66% (colonoscopy) to 13% (digital rectal exam); around a third exceeded recommended waiting times; 28% of specialists reported a pretreatment MDT meeting; colonoscopy within 4 weeks 51% rural vs 78% urban (OR 0.30, 95% CI 0.11-0.79)

audits.t: Nutritional screening of elderly patients: a health improvement approach to practice
audits.st: Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST) standard: local Trust stretch target of accurate documentation within 6 hours of admission
audits.f: MUST documented in <60% of patients within 6 hours of admission; only 70% accurate compared with dietitian assessment
audits.c: Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles testing a study day, one-to-one ward-based nutrition training, alternative anthropometric measurement methods, a training pack, and identification of assessment challenges
audits.r2: All wards achieved improved documentation of MUST within 6 hours of admission; one ward achieved 90% accuracy in scores

audits.t: Evaluation of the nutrition care process documentation in the patients' records using the Diet-NCP-Audit: experience in a medium-sized multi-site Swiss hospital.
audits.st: Nutrition Care Process (NCP) documentation standard, assessed with the Diet-NCP-Audit tool
audits.f: Documentation quality assessed as high in 62% of records; nutrition assessment inconsistent with nutrition diagnosis in half of records; only 4 of 73 NCP nutrition problems (5%) accounted for 58% of the 189 problems identified

audits.t: Malnutrition in emergency general surgery: a survey of National Emergency Laparotomy Audit Leads
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Nutritional screening performed preoperatively in 25.3% (42/166) and assessment in 15.7% (26/166); Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool used by 56.6%; albumin used to determine malnutrition risk by 73.5% contrary to guidance; postoperative nutrition pathways common (71.7%)

audits.t: Postsurgery wound assessment and management practices: a chart audit.
audits.st: Current evidence-based guidelines for prevention of surgical site infection
audits.f: Wound assessments were fully documented in 41.4% (63/152) of cases; 38.8% (59/152) had assessments documented on a change of patient condition; 9.9% (15/152) had charted postoperative wound complications

audits.t: Stop. Think. Delirium! A quality improvement initiative to explore utilising a validated cognitive assessment tool in the acute inpatient medical setting to detect delirium and prompt early intervention
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Delirium screening occurred in 49-61% of the target population monthly, with challenges in compliance and documentation
audits.r2: An increase in nursing knowledge was demonstrated after additional training, but success in identifying sufficient cases of delirium was not evident

audits.t: Evaluating fundamentals of care: The development of a unit‐level quality measurement and improvement programme
audits.tp: Fundamentals of care quality measurement programme
audits.st: Locally developed Patient and Whanau Centred Care Standards (PWCCS), nine fundamental elements of care
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Development and implementation of a unit-level quality measurement and improvement programme (PWCCS) with peer reviews every six months
audits.r2: Significant improvement overall in 6 of 27 units, in 7 of 9 standards and 3 of 4 measures; 89% (24) of units improved their overall result

audits.t: Have you SCAND MMe Please? A framework to prevent harm during acute hospitalisation of older persons: A retrospective audit.
audits.tp: Preventable harm prevention documentation audit in older inpatients (SCAND MMe framework)
audits.st: SCAND MMe mnemonic framework covering eight factors contributing to preventable harms in older inpatients
audits.f: Skin integrity, mobility and pain assessments documented in 93-98% of records; gaps in assessment of continence (4-31%), nutrition (9-49%) and cognition (10-24%); no record had all eight factors assessed; about 80% had interventions documented for one or more factors; about 20% had a new preventable harm documented during hospitalisation

audits.t: Diagnosis and treatment of infected wounds: A multi-centre audit of current clinical practice across the UK, Ireland and Scandinavia.
audits.tp: Wound infection diagnosis and antimicrobial use practice
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Infection rate of 8.9% reported; antimicrobials used in 35% of wounds considered not infected and not used in 41% of wounds identified as infected
audits.co: United Kingdom, Ireland, Norway, Denmark, Sweden, Finland

audits.t: Impact of a quality improvement intervention on the incidence of surgical site infection in patients undergoing colorectal surgery: Pre‐test–post‐test design
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline surgical site infection incidence measured retrospectively (T0); exact percentage not reported
audits.c: Complex multicomponent multidisciplinary quality improvement intervention/care bundle, including a patient information booklet
audits.r2: Notable decrease in surgical site infection incidence rates from baseline (T0) through T1 and T2; logistic regression found a significant reduction in the probability of SSI between T0 and T2

audits.t: Implementation of an external female urinary catheter strategy on prevention of skin breakdown in acute care: A quality improvement study
audits.tp: Skin breakdown prevention with external urinary catheters
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Both external female urinary catheter devices were associated with an overall low risk (5%) of new or worsening skin breakdown.
audits.c: Randomized allocation of two commercially available external female urinary catheter devices, with daily nursing skin assessments documented in the electronic health record before, during and after application

audits.t: DEVELOPING AN INTERVENTION TO PREVENT ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY: USING THE PLAN, DO, STUDY, ACT (PDSA) SERVICE IMPROVEMENT APPROACH
audits.tp: Patient awareness of medicines management for AKI prevention
audits.st: NICE guidelines for acute kidney injury prevention
audits.f: 92% had received no advice about AKI/medicines management; 77% wanted more advice; only 17% would feel comfortable stopping their own medication without medical consent
audits.c: not reported (PDSA cycle used to develop, not yet implement, an intervention)

audits.t: Diet quality in patients with end‐stage kidney disease undergoing dialysis
audits.tp: Diet quality (omega-3 intake) in haemodialysis patients
audits.st: Evidence Based Practice Guidelines (EBPG) for energy, protein, potassium and dietary fat intake in dialysis patients
audits.f: Majority did not meet EBPG for energy, protein and potassium; all participants exceeded recommended saturated fat intake; only 22% met the suggested dietary target for omega-3 (n-3 LCPUFA) intake; mean Total Diet Score 10.2 vs 9.3 in a healthy cohort (p<0.05)

audits.t: The quality, accuracy and appropriateness of UK optometric age‐related macular degeneration referrals
audits.tp: Optometric referral quality for neovascular age-related macular degeneration
audits.st: NICE guidelines recommending a 14-day window for suspected neovascular AMD to be seen

audits.r2: Proportion seen within the 14-day window dropped to 5% during the pandemic (p<0.001)

audits.t: A retrospective audit to examine the effectiveness of preoperative warming on hypothermia in spine deformity surgery patients.
audits.tp: Preoperative warming to prevent intraoperative hypothermia in spine deformity surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline prevalence and extent of intraoperative hypothermia recorded before preoperative warming was introduced.
audits.c: Introduction of preoperative warming for children undergoing spine deformity surgery.
audits.r2: Preoperative warming reduced the percentage of case duration spent hypothermic by a median of 111.1 minutes (statistically significant).

audits.t: Pulmonary aspiration under <scp>GA</scp>: a 13‐year audit in a tertiary pediatric unit
audits.tp: Pulmonary aspiration incidence under general anaesthesia
audits.st: Standardized critical incident audit form
audits.f: 22 cases of pulmonary aspiration reported, incidence 0.02% (1 in 4655); emergency surgeries had higher risk (OR 4.321, 95% CI 1.735-10.687, P=0.001)

audits.t: Analgesic management after thoracotomy for decortication in children: a retrospective audit of 83 children managed with a paravertebral infusion‐based regime
audits.st: not reported (no named guideline; poor analgesia locally defined as VAS/Smiley Face score of 7 or more)
audits.f: 77.1% (64/83) had good quality analgesia, 20.5% (17/83) moderate, and 2.4% (2/83) poor quality analgesia (VAS/SF score >=7) using a paravertebral infusion-based regime.

audits.t: A quality improvement initiative to optimize dosing of surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis
audits.st: National guidelines recommending cefazolin 30 mg/kg preoperative dosing (increased from 25 mg/kg); target >=90% compliance
audits.f: Mean compliance with cefazolin at 30 mg/kg was 40%
audits.c: New electronic medical record order sets, personal provider antibiotic dose badges, pharmacist preparation of antibiotics
audits.r2: Mean compliance 93%, meeting the target; electronic orders had higher compliance than verbal orders (94% vs 76%)
