audits.t: A quality improvement initiative to increase the safety of pediatric emergency airway management
audits.st: Locally designed emergency airway algorithm and process measures (preintubation checklist, apneic oxygenation, EtCO2 confirmation etc.)
audits.f: First pass success without hypoxia or hypotension 49%
audits.c: Emergency airway algorithm, standardized equipment, preintubation checklist, EtCO2 monitoring, postintubation debriefing, multidisciplinary team training
audits.r2: First pass success without hypoxia or hypotension 78% (absolute risk reduction 29.0%, 95% CI 12.3-45.6%, NNT 3.5); overall process measure uptake 85%

audits.t: A quality improvement project to reduce postoperative adverse respiratory events and increase safety in the postanesthesia care unit of a pediatric institution
audits.tp: Postoperative respiratory adverse events in PACU
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median percentage of respiratory adverse events in PACU 2.8%
audits.c: Key Driver Diagram interventions: safety culture, resource allocation, education/training, standardisation of care, improved handoff, PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Median percentage of respiratory adverse events decreased to 1.4%, over 30% reduction, with no significant change in mean recovery time

audits.t: A multifaceted quality improvement project improves intraoperative redosing of surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis during pediatric surgery
audits.tp: Surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis intraoperative redosing compliance
audits.st: National guidelines for weight-based intraoperative antibiotic redosing; target 70% compliance
audits.f: Mean monthly redosing compliance 4.3%
audits.c: Electronic countermeasures (dose timing display, 5-minute alert, weight-based dose recommendation), physical countermeasures (badge cards, posted guidelines, manual updates)
audits.r2: Mean monthly compliance 73% (P<0.001); dose-only compliance 76% to 89% (P<0.001); time-only compliance 4.9% to 82% (P<0.001); electronic vs verbal order dose compliance 90% vs 86% (P=0.015)

audits.t: A 4 year quality improvement initiative reducing post‐operative nausea and vomiting in children undergoing strabismus surgery at a quaternary paediatric hospital
audits.tp: Postoperative nausea and vomiting reduction in strabismus surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting 18%
audits.c: Evidence-based therapeutic PONV bundle via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Incidence reduced to 4.72%, comparable to general PACU population incidence over previous six months

audits.t: Intravenous cannula placement in children for induction of general anesthesia: Prospective audit and identification of success factors
audits.tp: Intravenous cannulation success in paediatric anaesthesia induction
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: IV cannulation successful in 90% of the 562 IV induction cases; anxiolytic premedication given in 6%

audits.t: Enhanced recovery after cleft palate repair: A quality improvement project
audits.tp: Enhanced recovery pathway for cleft palate repair
audits.st: Locally developed ERAS pathway with target >70% bundle adherence and 30% reduction in postoperative opioid use
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: ERAS pathway: patient/provider education, maxillary nerve blockade, enhanced intra/postoperative medication regimens
audits.r2: Pathway compliance 77.0%; postoperative opioid consumption reduced 49% (p<0.0001, mean difference -0.33 +/-0.11 mg/kg); intraoperative opioid reduced 36% (p=0.002); time to first oral intake reduced 45% (p=0.02)

audits.t: Pediatric influenza vaccination in the perioperative setting: A quality improvement project.
audits.st: SMART aim targets: 10% (season 1), 15% (season 2), 18% (season 3) influenza vaccination rate
audits.f: Vaccination rate goal of 10% exceeded (exact rate not reported)
audits.c: Perioperative vaccination policy updates, vaccine supply acquisition, EHR tools, staff education, patient-family communication, via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Vaccination rate goal of 18% exceeded (exact rate not reported); 695 vaccines administered in total across 3 seasons

audits.t: The implementation of a pectus bar insertion enhanced recovery after surgery pathway: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: ERAS pathway for pectus bar insertion
audits.st: SMART aim: >70% compliance with perioperative bundle elements within 1 year
audits.f: Mean length of stay 33 hours (95% CI 28.76-37.31); compliance not reported
audits.c: Multidisciplinary ERAS pathway for pectus bar insertion (Evidence Based Practice, Surgery, Anesthesiology, Perioperative Nursing) via multiple PDSA cycles
audits.r2: 90% compliance with perioperative bundle elements; mean length of stay decreased to 18 hours (95% CI 14.54-21.70); zero 24-hour readmissions

audits.t: Reducing postoperative hypothermia in infants: Quality improvement in China.
audits.st: SMART aim to reduce postoperative hypothermia rate (target not fully stated)
audits.f: Postoperative hypothermia rate >60%
audits.c: Perioperative-thermoregulation protocol, optimised transfer process, and staff education, via PDSA cycles with QI expert collaboration (Children's Hospital of Philadelphia)
audits.r2: Postoperative hypothermia rate decreased from 60% to 37% (special cause variation on SPC chart)

audits.t: Effectiveness of implementing a standardized perioperative pain management protocol in children undergoing tonsillectomy: A quality improvement project
audits.tp: Standardized perioperative pain management protocol for tonsillectomy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Postoperative opioid usage 93.8%; respiratory interventions in 24.7%
audits.c: Standardized perioperative pain management protocol used intraoperatively
audits.r2: Postoperative opioid usage reduced to 54.5%; IV fentanyl reduced (28.3% vs 49.4%, p=0.004); respiratory interventions reduced to 7.1%; 100% adherence to protocol

audits.t: Documentation of Core Temperature in Pediatric Patients Undergoing General Anesthesia: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Increase Compliance.
audits.tp: Core temperature documentation in paediatric anaesthesia
audits.st: ASA standard monitoring guidelines for core temperature documentation; SMART aim 10% to 60% by October 2023
audits.f: Baseline 10% documented core temperature
audits.c: Educational email, posted OR sign, Morbidity and Mortality Conference, integrated EHR pop-up reminder; 5 interventions tested via PDSA
audits.r2: Documentation increased to 60% by October 2023 and to 90% by January 2024

audits.t: Decreasing Opioid Usage in Pediatric Cholecystectomy Through Care Standardization: A Quality Improvement Project Using Enhanced Recovery After Surgery Protocols
audits.tp: Reducing opioid use in paediatric cholecystectomy via ERAS
audits.st: Locally set SMART aim: reduce opioid use (morphine milligram equivalents) by 25% over 32 months
audits.f: Mean pain scores 4.69 (95% CI 4.32-5.06); PONV incidence 18% (95% CI 11.7-26.7); pruritus 6% (95% CI 2.8-12.5); mean length of stay 1.37 days (95% CI 1.33-1.41)
audits.c: ERAS protocol with electronic best practice advisories, monthly education sessions, stakeholder engagement
audits.r2: Morphine milligram equivalents decreased by 27%; mean pain scores 4.10 (95% CI 3.84-4.36); PONV 15% (95% CI 9.3-23.3); pruritus 5% (95% CI 2.2-11.2); mean length of stay 1.34 days (95% CI 1.30-1.38)

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Improve Early Postoperative Pain Outcomes After Tonsillectomy in Children
audits.st: Local QI aim: reduce moderate-to-severe pain in PACU after paediatric tonsillectomy/adenotonsillectomy by 50% within 12 months
audits.f: 65.8% of patients had moderate-severe pain in PACU; 69% received rescue opioids in PACU.
audits.c: A six-item perioperative pain toolkit was introduced from April 2021, with patients categorised by toolkit adherence (standard of care, partial toolkit, 100% toolkit).
audits.r2: With 100% toolkit adherence, moderate-severe pain fell to 31% (53% overall reduction) and rescue opioid use fell to 45% (35% overall reduction).

audits.t: Implementing undergraduate quality improvement
audits.st: not reported (adherence to QI methodology: SMART aims, PDSA cycles, run charts)
audits.f: 90% of QIPs based in secondary care and 10% in primary care; 72% led to improvements in clinical care and 14% achieved their stated aim; 75% had a SMART aim; 96% used at least one PDSA cycle; 80% had appropriate run charts.

audits.t: Postgraduate Pedagogical Training and Interventions to Promote High‐Quality Discharge Summaries
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Multipronged pedagogical, assessment and training strategies: locally-adapted templates and teaching material, blended educational modalities, workplace-based assessments, continued clinical audits
audits.r2: Significant and sustained improvement in the quality of discharge summaries written by junior doctors

audits.t: The Use of Memes to Improve Feedback Form Completion Rates Among Medical Students: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Medical student feedback form completion rates
audits.st: Local aim to improve feedback form response rate (no fixed numeric target stated)
audits.f: Response rate 32.3% using standard email/WhatsApp reminders (no memes)
audits.c: Introduction of placement-individualised humorous memes added to the reminder system, sent at key intervals before, on, and after form distribution
audits.r2: Response rate increased to 85.5% with meme-based reminders (statistically significant by chi-square test)

audits.t: Quality indicators for the hospital transfusion chain: a national survey conducted in 100 dutch hospitals
audits.tp: Hospital transfusion chain quality indicator compliance
audits.st: 2011 Dutch Blood Transfusion Guideline, seven internal quality indicators
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: 23% of hospitals complied with recommended minimum of four annual transfusion committee meetings and 8 h/week for TSO; 90% complied with pretransfusion haemoglobin threshold in >80% of transfusions; 58% measured pretransfusion platelet count in >80% of transfusions; 87% complied with mandatory traceability in >95% of transfusions

audits.t: Audit of appropriate use of platelet transfusions: validation of adjudication criteria.
audits.st: Predetermined adjudication criteria for appropriate platelet transfusion
audits.f: 78% (95% CI 72-84%) of platelet transfusions adjudicated appropriate, ranging 62-94% by site; prophylactic transfusions 85% appropriate (n=80); therapeutic transfusions 73% appropriate (n=99); lowest appropriateness in operating rooms (60%) and general surgery service (55%)

audits.t: Use of O RhD-negative red blood cells: A nationwide, prospective audit.
audits.tp: Appropriate use of O RhD-negative red blood cells
audits.st: Appropriate-use criteria for issuing O RhD-negative red blood cells (reserved for O RhD-negative patients and emergencies)
audits.f: 47.9% (529/1105) of O RhD-negative units were issued to non-O RhD-negative patients; only 22.3% (118) were issued to females under 50; 32.5% (172) were issued for emergency transfusion among ABO-nonidentical transfusions

audits.t: A comprehensive approach to continuous quality improvement of massive transfusion by developing key performance indicators
audits.st: Local standard: institutional goal-directed massive transfusion (GDMT) protocol benchmarks for activation and turnaround time
audits.f: Appropriate GDMT activation was observed in only 43.47% of events; turnaround time was within benchmark in 85.8% of events (average 16±10 min); average blood component utilisation was 20.5 (IQR 11.3) in the appropriate group vs 5.5 (IQR 4.25) in the inappropriate group, with a wastage rate of 3.5%; duration of activation was 6.19±4.59 hours; adherence to thromboelastography was 66.3%; overall mortality was 45.65% and average hospital stay 6.1±5.9 days.

audits.t: Audit of management of women with one previous caesarean section at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh
audits.tp: VBAC and previous caesarean section management
audits.st: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists guideline 'birth after previous Caesarean birth'; national VBAC rate 33%
audits.f: VBAC rate 42% overall, 71% in women with one previous vaginal delivery; success rate among those attempting VBAC 73%; antenatal counselling documented in 86%, by consultant in 61%

audits.t: Audit of vaginal birth after one caesarean: the experience of a medium-sized district general hospital
audits.st: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists guideline (VBAC success rate assumption >70%)
audits.f: Overall VBAC success rate 54.7% (50% in women whose previous CS was their only delivery, 69% with prior vaginal deliveries), lower than the guideline's quoted 70%; complications included two suspected scar dehiscence (1.73%) and one scar rupture (0.86%)

audits.t: An audit of cord blood sampling at a large city hospital
audits.tp: Cord blood sampling for high-risk deliveries
audits.st: Sunderland Royal Hospital Trust Guidelines for indications for cord blood sampling
audits.f: 47 deliveries had an indication for cord sampling; only 38 (81%) of these had a sample taken; 95% of samples taken were paired; 52% correctly documented

audits.t: Maternal intrapartum pyrexia audit
audits.st: Departmental guideline for management of intrapartum fever >38C (blood cultures, infective screen, IV antibiotics for 48h)
audits.f: Blood cultures performed in 28 (77%); antibiotics given per protocol in 23 (63%); 17 (47%) delivered within 4 h of temperature spike; 14 (40%) babies admitted to neonatal unit

audits.t: Audit into reasons for maternal request for caesarean sections at the Norfolk & Norwich University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
audits.tp: Maternal request caesarean section counselling documentation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Documented discussion of future family/fertility only 12.4%; discussion of CS risks 38.9%; 51% of maternal request CS after one previous LSCS; 23% for breech with no ECV offered

audits.t: Audit of the ultrasound detection of congenital anomalies in Royal Gwent Hospital, Newport, UK
audits.tp: Antenatal ultrasound detection of congenital anomalies
audits.st: Detection rate standards from the Congenital Anomaly Registry and Information Service for Wales
audits.f: Detection rate 100% for neural tube defect (standard 90%), renal (85% standard, achieved 100%), missing limb (90% standard, achieved 100%), exomphalos/gastroschisis (90% standard, achieved 100%), cardiac 37% (standard 25%); overall 50% (83/163) detected antenatally, 47% missed

audits.t: Audit of the management of women exposed to B19 parvovirus in pregnancy
audits.tp: Management of parvovirus B19 exposure in pregnancy
audits.st: 23 locally created standards for management of parvovirus exposure in pregnancy
audits.f: 62% immune, 28% susceptible, 10% infected; 98% had no documentation of reassurance; 89% had no documentation of exposure date; 59% of susceptible women did not have 4-week follow-up sampling

audits.t: Audit of external cephalic version
audits.st: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists guideline No.20A on external cephalic version
audits.f: Success rate 44% (primigravidae 33%, multigravidae 54%), comparable to standard; no complications; guideline followed appropriately

audits.t: Audit of vitamin D deficiency in ethnic pregnant population at Liverpool Womens Hospital: Abstract PM.13
audits.tp: Vitamin D deficiency screening and supplementation in pregnant ethnic populations
audits.st: NICE guidance on vitamin D supplementation for women at greatest risk (South Asian, African, Caribbean, Middle Eastern origin)
audits.f: Majority of Asian, African and Arab women had severe vitamin D deficiency; Chinese women had moderate deficiency, a group not highlighted by NICE

audits.t: Audit on the use of empirical antibiotics in pregnant women with presumed UTI and their correlation to MSU results
audits.tp: Empirical antibiotic use for presumed UTI in pregnancy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 19% of patients had positive culture growth; combination of symptoms and nitrite dipstick had PPV 26%, specificity 82%, sensitivity 27%; 14% of episodes grew Cefradine-resistant bacteria; only 37% had repeat MSU sent

audits.t: Audit of preconception advice to women of childbearing age with conditions likely to affect the outcome and course of pregnancy
audits.tp: Preconception counselling documentation for women with pre-existing conditions
audits.st: Confidential Enquiry into Maternal and Child Health 'Saving Mothers' Lives 2003-2005' recommendation for preconception counselling
audits.f: Almost all women with pre-existing diabetes had received advice; ~75% with epilepsy and 60% with thyroid disorders had counselling; only ~15% with serious mental illness, BMI >30, or renal/cardiovascular problems had received advice
audits.c: Local action plan developed to improve multidisciplinary communication

audits.t: Audit of obstetric haemorrhage and the use and electronic traceability of blood transfusions in the maternity unit, Sunderland Royal Hospital
audits.tp: Obstetric haemorrhage blood transfusion traceability compliance
audits.st: Trust Blood Transfusion Policy including electronic traceability (PBAR system)
audits.f: 16/36 (44.4%) Trust Blood Transfusion Pathways completed; only 4/149 (2.68%) units checked with PBARS scanner

audits.t: Postpartum hypertension – an evidence based audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 23% (Ulster) and 31% (RJMH) of postpartum women required antihypertensive treatment; no uniformity in management; BP checked in 92%, proteinuria checked in only 45% at postnatal review

audits.t: Investigations after stillbirth: a criterion based clinical audit in the Grampian region of Scotland (1998–2008)
audits.st: Locally developed protocol for investigating causes of stillbirth
audits.f: Routine investigations complete in 97.9% of cases; full postmortem done in 64.02%, limited PM in 4.23%; in 40% (75) no cause could be attributed

audits.t: Antepartum stillbirth in twins: a regional multi-centre audit of antenatal care
audits.tp: Antenatal surveillance in twin pregnancy antepartum stillbirth
audits.st: Regional consensus standards of care for antenatal surveillance of twin pregnancy
audits.f: Autopsy performed in 18 (47%) pregnancies; major causes were antepartum hypoxia (n=25) and TTTS (n=14, 9 pregnancies); 66% delivered within 24h of diagnosis of death; antenatal surveillance in the majority was in line with regional standards

audits.t: An audit of screening for anaemia and the characterising of red cell indices and ferritin in pregnancy in one hospital
audits.st: National Collaborating Centre for Women's and Children's Health guideline: screen for anaemia at booking and 30 weeks
audits.f: Adherence to guideline for blood sampling 98% (both booking and 30-week FBC done in 40, 92%); 27 (54%) had MCV<82 or Hb<=11; 18 (67%) had documentation of prescribed iron

audits.t: An audit of the care and outcomes of pregnant epileptic patients
audits.st: National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidelines for epilepsy in pregnancy
audits.f: 5/50 (10%) GP referrals for preconceptual counselling; 14/50 (28%) received preconceptual folic acid; 19/50 (38%) experienced increased seizure frequency during pregnancy; birth weight <50th centile in 30/50 (60%)

audits.t: Audit of management of eclampsia and severe pre-eclampsia against RCOG standards
audits.tp: Management of eclampsia and severe pre-eclampsia
audits.st: RCOG Green Top Guideline No.10(A) (2006) for severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia
audits.f: Labetalol used in 65 cases (88%); 39 (55%) with severe pre-eclampsia and all with eclampsia received magnesium sulphate; consultant obstetricians reviewed 75 patients within 24h; senior anaesthetic input in 50%

audits.t: PM.28 Audit on Care and Outcome of Pregnancy in Women with Morbid Obesity
audits.tp: Management of pregnancy with morbid obesity
audits.st: RCOG/CMACE Joint Guideline on Management of Women with Obesity in Pregnancy (March 2010)
audits.f: Glucose tolerance test performed in 96.2%; only 55.2% had an anaesthetic review; 47.3% had postnatal thromboprophylaxis, of whom 81.4% had a sufficient dose for weight; major postpartum haemorrhage in 8.2%.

audits.t: PM.35 Changing from 24-Hour Urinary Protein Collections to Protein-Creatinine Ratios: An Audit of One Hospital’s Experience of Trying to Reduce Admission Rates For Pre-Eclampsia
audits.st: Local and NICE Hypertension in Pregnancy guidelines; ordering/processing of tests compared with a 95% standard
audits.f: Baseline admission rates and length of stay before the switch from 24-hour urinary protein collection to protein-creatinine ratio (PCR) testing.
audits.c: Change from 24-hour urinary protein collection to spot protein-creatinine ratio (PCR) testing, introduced December 2011.
audits.r2: Patients in the PCR group were significantly less likely to be admitted (p=0.017, odds ratio 0.2) and, if admitted, had significantly shorter length of stay (p=0.027).

audits.t: PM.45 Increased NT – a Retrospective Audit from a University Hospital
audits.st: RCOG Green-top Guideline No.8 (Amniocentesis and Chorionic Villus Sampling)
audits.f: 46/54 (85%) agreed to invasive testing; 100% compliance with the Green-top Guideline No.8 standards; one failed CVS attempt and one failed amniocentesis; no miscarriages.

audits.t: PM.56 Audit of Care of Critically Ill Pregnant Women
audits.tp: Care of critically ill pregnant women in ITU
audits.st: Joint RCOG guideline 'Providing equity of critical and maternity care for the critically ill pregnant or recently pregnant woman' (July 2011)
audits.f: 100% compliance with MEWS chart; VTE assessment on admission in 65%; debriefing of patient in 78% and of family in 61% of cases; Datix completed in only 10%; no maternal deaths.

audits.t: PM.59 Audit of the Management of Pregnant Women with Epilepsy (2011)
audits.tp: Management of pregnant women with epilepsy
audits.st: NICE and SIGN guidelines for management of pregnant women with epilepsy
audits.f: Only 23% had preconception counselling and 60% had pre-pregnancy folic acid; 83% had specialist referral; of those on enzyme-inducing antiepileptics, only 50% received vitamin K at 36 weeks; only 32% received postnatal infant-care advice.

audits.t: PM.85 Diagnosing PE in Maternity Patients. An Audit of Radiological Investigations and Clinical Interpretation
audits.tp: Radiological investigation of suspected pulmonary embolism in pregnancy
audits.st: American Thoracic Society guidelines (VQ scan preferred over CTPA when chest x-ray and leg Doppler negative); local audit standard of 100% for investigation pathway
audits.f: Chest x-ray performed in 92% (audit standard 100%) and lower limb Doppler in 68% (audit standard 100%); VQ scans in 59% and CTPA in 56%; sensitivity of VQ was 33% and specificity 60% in those who had both tests; 5 patients had PE confirmed on CTPA.

audits.t: PL.50 An Audit Exploring the Impact of NICE Caesarean Section Guidance on Elective Caesarean Section Rates at the Countess of Chester Hospital (COCH)
audits.tp: Impact of NICE guidance on elective caesarean section rates for maternal request
audits.st: NICE CG132 Caesarean section guideline (November 2011) on maternal request
audits.f: Overall elective CS rate increased by 2% (Jan-June 2011 to 2012) versus only 1% rise 2009-2011; maternal request rate rose from 0.5% (2010-2011) to 1.4% (Jan-Sept 2012); within the cohort maternal request rate was 7.5% versus 5.5% in 2010; 30% disparity between documented and actual indication for delivery.

audits.t: PL.57 Audit of Midwives’ Knowledge of Neuraxial Analgesia in Labour
audits.st: Obstetric Anaesthetists' Association publication 'Pain Relief in Labour'
audits.f: Only 6/27 midwives perceived epidurals as the most effective analgesia; knowledge of side-effect risks (e.g. failure 74% correct, increased assisted delivery risk 96.3% correct, epidural abscess only 33.3% correct) varied and differed from current evidence.

audits.t: PL.86 Audit of Placenta Accreta and its Antenatal Imaging
audits.st: RCOG Green-top Guidelines for antenatal imaging of suspected placenta accreta
audits.f: Of 9 high-risk women (placenta praevia with previous caesarean), only 5 had an MRI scan; predictive value of MRI for placenta accreta was 60% (3 true negative, 1 false negative, 1 false positive).

audits.t: PL.88 Syntocinon Infusion: A Prospective Audit at St John’s Hospital (Nov 2010 – April 2011)
audits.st: Pan-Lothian guideline and NICE guideline on syntocinon infusion use in labour
audits.f: 99.08% of patients continued to delivery without syntocinon being stopped; 66.9% had no reduction, while 33.1% had the infusion rate reduced at least once (commonest reason hyperstimulation, 42/51 cases); practice conformed to the Pan-Lothian guideline.

audits.t: PL.98 Indications and Outcomes in Caesarean Section – A Prospective Audit
audits.tp: Caesarean section indications and outcomes vs NICE guidance and CQUIN targets
audits.st: NICE CG132 Caesarean Section guideline (including 1.2.9.2 on maternal request), CQUIN targets for infection control and thromboprophylaxis, and RCOG projected VBAC outcomes
audits.f: Targets met for antibiotic prophylaxis, clipper use, VTE prophylaxis, diabetic control, and counselling against CS for maternal request (100% documented counselling, 100% explored reasons for request); targets not met for written/verbal debriefing post-CS and Stellisept prescribing; CS rate 21% across the trust; VBAC success rate 64.3%.

audits.t: PP.74 Audit on the Management of Multiple Pregnancies and Review of Outcomes
audits.tp: Antenatal care and outcomes in multiple pregnancy
audits.st: Trust guidelines on management of multiple pregnancy
audits.f: 85% had dating scan at 11-14 weeks; chorionicity determined in 100%; only 67% had documented Down's syndrome counselling, of whom 29% had screening done; caesarean section rate 57%; survival rate 97% for dichorionic and 95% for monochorionic twins.

audits.t: The impact of a regional care bundle on maternal breast milk use in preterm infants: outcomes of the East of England quality improvement programme
audits.tp: Maternal breast milk use in preterm infants
audits.st: Local QI programme target: increase maternal breast milk (MBM) use in preterm infants <=32+6 weeks gestation
audits.f: Exclusive MBM use at discharge was 26% and any MBM use was 50% before the care bundle.
audits.c: A regional 'care bundle' to promote maternal breast milk use was introduced in the East of England Perinatal Network.
audits.r2: Exclusive MBM use at discharge rose to 33% and any MBM use to 57%; exclusive MBM use improved significantly faster in the East of England (0.22%/month, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.34) than the rest of the UK Neonatal Collaborative (0.05%/month, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.09, p=0.007).

audits.t: PC.33 Quality Improvement in use of Vancomycin dosing regimens
audits.st: Desired vancomycin trough level range of 10-15 mg/L
audits.f: Only 28% of 155 measured trough vancomycin levels were within the desired range (10-15); 40% were sub-therapeutic and 32% supra-therapeutic; median 5 doses to reach a therapeutic level; only 8 of 51 UK NICUs surveyed used continuous infusion vancomycin.

audits.t: PC.64 Audit of the Management and follow up of infants who received Therapeutic Hypothermia for Neonatal Encephalopathy in NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde (GG&C) from January 2008 to December 2010
audits.tp: Management and follow-up of therapeutic hypothermia for neonatal encephalopathy
audits.st: Local standards and NICE IPG374 (Therapeutic hypothermia guidance, May 2010)
audits.f: Clinical care of infants receiving cooling was consistent with local and national standards, but documentation was substandard against local guidelines; only 19% of infants had documentation of optimal follow-up to 24 months.

audits.t: PC.95 Clinical audit on lumbar punctures performed in a tertiary neonatal unit
audits.tp: Lumbar puncture use for suspected neonatal infection
audits.st: NICE guidance on antibiotics for early-onset neonatal infections
audits.f: Raised CRP was the reason for lumbar puncture in 61 cases (median CRP 66); no positive bacterial cultures, though one was PCR-positive for herpes simplex virus type 1; 4 babies were diagnosed with meningitis.

audits.t: PC.115 Audit of Neonatal Enteral Nutrition in Northern Ireland
audits.st: NICE Quality Standards for Specialist Neonatal Care
audits.f: All units had breastfeeding policies, 80% had EN progression guidelines; 63% of babies received some maternal breast milk (EBM) but this fell from 48% at initiation to 28% at discharge; on discharge 55% were on formula.

audits.t: PC.126 An audit of the investigation and management of early-onset neonatal infection against a new national guideline
audits.tp: Early-onset neonatal infection management vs NICE guideline
audits.st: NICE CG149 (August 2012) guidance on identification and management of early-onset neonatal infection
audits.f: Compliance with the 8 NICE standards ranged widely from 0% to 100%; practice diverged particularly on timing of repeat investigations and antibiotic dosage/course length; compliance could not be accurately assessed for some standards.

audits.t: PFM.17 Audit of the management of the small for gestation age (SGA) fetus against RCOG (2002) and regional guidelines: Case recognition and implications for the next regional guideline
audits.st: Greater Glasgow and Clyde regional guideline, based on RCOG (2002) guidance
audits.f: 98% of cases had umbilical artery Doppler at identification; hospitals used a mix of customised and non-customised growth charts; 57% of babies had birth weight >10th centile at delivery, suggesting overestimation by customised and underestimation by non-customised charts.

audits.t: PFM.64 Audit of Small for Gestational Age - Diagnosis and Clinical Outcomes
audits.tp: Detection of small-for-gestational-age babies using customised growth charts
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Where GROW charts were used, 88% had serial symphysial height measurement and 63% of those scanned were correctly identified as SGA (16% of the total cohort); where GROW charts were not used, 62% had serial measurements and 80% of those scanned were correctly identified (9% of total cohort).

audits.t: PLD.02 Audit on the assessment and administration of thromboprophylaxis after caesarean section
audits.st: Local trust guidelines on thromboprophylaxis assessment and administration after caesarean section (informed by 1995 RCOG guidelines)
audits.f: Only 70% of patients were assessed for thromboprophylaxis at admission, while 90% were assessed after delivery; all patients received Dalteparin after caesarean section; mean time to commencing Dalteparin was 8 hours 43 minutes after delivery.

audits.t: PLD.04 Audit of Adherence to Antacid and Fasting Guidelines for Elective Caesarean Section at the Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle upon Tyne
audits.tp: Fasting and antacid prophylaxis before elective caesarean section
audits.st: RCN fasting guidelines (6 hours for solids, 2 hours for clear fluids, endorsed by RCoA and RCoM) and NICE caesarean section guideline on antacid prophylaxis
audits.f: 100% of mothers followed fasting and antacid prophylaxis guidelines; mean time without solids was 14 hours (range 9-24) and without clear fluids 12 hours (range 3-17); 94% received written Trust fasting instruction; 0% drank clear fluids around 2 hours before their anaesthetic; low urine output delayed recovery in 12 patients.

audits.t: PMM.41 A decade of improvement? Management of severe PET
audits.tp: Quality of local guidelines for severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia
audits.st: Criteria used in a 2004 national survey of severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia guidelines, updated against NICE guidance published in 2010
audits.f: 2004 survey found guideline standards were poor: 86.1% had clear inclusion criteria, 26.4% recommended consultant input, and 56.1% included blood pressure targets (of which all that had a target systolic threshold recommended >160 mmHg).
audits.c: Publication of NICE guidance on severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia management in 2010.
audits.r2: 99.1% of guidelines now had clear inclusion criteria (p<0.05), 91.7% recommended consultant input (p<0.05), 99.1% recommended magnesium sulphate and fluid restriction, and 96.3% included blood pressure targets (p<0.05); only 14.8% now recommended a systolic BP target >160mmHg, though 14.8% (nearly 1 in 7) of units were still not adherent to safe BP targets.

audits.t: PPO.32 Audit of management and outcomes of obstetric patients with pre-existing renal disease managed in a specialist obstetric clinic
audits.tp: Management of pregnancy with pre-existing renal disease
audits.st: Set standards for antenatal management of women with pre-existing renal disease (e.g. preconception advice, aspirin prophylaxis timing)
audits.f: 1 in 4 women received preconception advice; half started prophylactic aspirin before 16 weeks, with a higher rate (65%) by 2011; highest pregnancy complication rates were in women with severe renal impairment, including 1 in 4 risk of not completing pregnancy.

audits.t: PA.08 Neonatal Hypoglycaemia-A Quality Improvement Project to Improve Service Delivery Using a RHINO
audits.tp: Recognition and treatment of neonatal hypoglycaemia
audits.st: Local standard for prompt sugar monitoring, referral and treatment of at-risk neonates
audits.f: 11% of at-risk babies missed sugar monitoring, 32% had it done incorrectly, and 4 neonates had low sugars untreated for unacceptable durations; staff familiarity with 4 key management areas was very poor.
audits.c: The RHINO Project: a Plan-Do-Check-Act (Deming cycle) programme using point-of-care posters and nursery-nurse champions to cascade education on referral of hypoglycaemia detected in newborn observations to over 200 multidisciplinary staff.
audits.r2: 100% compliance with blood sugar monitoring and review of at-risk neonates; documentation improved from 89% to 100%, skin-to-skin care from 86% to 100%, and early feeding from 89% to 100%; 92% (12/13) of neonates admitted with hypoglycaemia in the first 6 months complied with guidance on early review and intervention.

audits.t: PA.13 Audit on the Management of Pregnancies in Women 40 years and over at Epsom and St Helier’s NHS Trust Hospital Jan–Dec 2012
audits.tp: Management of pregnancy in women aged 40 and over
audits.st: RCOG Scientific Impact Paper No.34, 'Induction of Labour at Term in Older Mothers' (February 2013)
audits.f: No women were referred antenatally as high risk due to age alone; IOL at term was discussed in only 2 cases; IOL rate was 18%, comparable to the trust rate (19%); 25% delivered by emergency caesarean (trust 17.8%) and 20% by planned caesarean (trust 9.3%).

audits.t: PA.46 Audit of Clinical Coding: An aspect of practice often neglected but with profound implications on clinical care!
audits.tp: Accuracy of clinical coding against documented notes
audits.st: Coding should accurately match what clinical staff document in the patient record
audits.f: 6 amendments were made to original coding, an amendment rate of 14.28%; primary diagnosis was correct in 100% of cases, but secondary diagnosis and procedure codes were affected.

audits.t: PA.51 Indications for the Use of High Vaginal Swabs in Obstetrics: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Appropriateness of high vaginal swab use
audits.st: Local expectation that high vaginal swabs be taken only with an appropriate clinical indication
audits.f: The majority of swabs were culture negative and only a minority of culture-positive swabs required treatment; 18% of swabs were taken without an appropriate clinical indication, most commonly abdominal pain with no signs/symptoms of infection.
audits.c: A formal guideline on indications for the use of high vaginal swabs was produced with the aim of reducing unnecessary investigations.

audits.t: The impact of a sepsis quality improvement project on neurodisability rates in very low birthweight infants
audits.tp: Sepsis reduction care bundle in very low birthweight infants
audits.st: not reported (locally introduced sepsis reduction care bundle target: reduce late-onset sepsis)
audits.f: Preintervention: coagulase-negative Staphylococcus (CONS) infection rate 26.7%; death before discharge 14.1%; moderate cognitive impairment 18.8%.
audits.c: A sepsis reduction care bundle was implemented between July 2006 and December 2007.
audits.r2: Postintervention: CONS infection rate fell to 14.1% (p<0.001); death before discharge fell to 10.9% (p=0.195, not significant); cognitive disability fell to 6.1% (p=0.042); adjusted OR for CONS infection was 0.46 (95% CI 0.29 to 0.72).

audits.t: CLABSI reduction using evidence based interventions and nurse empowerment: a quality improvement initiative from a tertiary care NICU in Pakistan
audits.tp: CLABSI reduction using bundle and nurse empowerment
audits.st: Evidence-based CLABSI prevention interventions (hand hygiene, aseptic insertion/care, fungal infection prevention)
audits.f: CLABSI rate 17.1/1000 device days
audits.c: CLABSI Prevention Package: hand hygiene, aseptic central line insertion/care techniques, fungal infection prevention, nurse empowerment
audits.r2: CLABSI rate decreased to 5.0/1000 device days (RR=0.36, CI 0.17-0.74); device utilisation ratio declined from 0.30 to 0.25

audits.t: Reduction of cardiac iron overload by optimising iron chelation therapy in transfusion dependent thalassaemia using cardiac T2* MRI: a quality improvement project from Pakistan
audits.tp: Cardiac iron overload reduction via optimised chelation using T2* MRI
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Key-driver based QI: protocol optimisation and treatment compliance via training, communication, feedback; standardised adverse event severity tool for chelators
audits.r2: Increase or stabilisation of T2*CMR in 82% postintervention, especially in severe overload subgroup (5.5 vs 5.3 ms, p<0.01); significantly fewer abnormal echocardiographic findings (3.5% vs 26%, p<0.05)

audits.t: P13 Optimising paediatric intravenous fluid management plans: a quality improvement project
audits.tp: Paediatric IV fluid management plan documentation
audits.st: NICE guidance NG29 (Intravenous fluid therapy in children and young people in hospital) and National Patient Safety Alert 22 on reducing hyponatraemia risk
audits.f: Daily fluid management plan completed in 41%; nursing fluid balance completed in 19%; blood glucose recorded in 64%; daily weight documented in 10%
audits.c: Sticker with monitoring checklist and fluid balance section attached to notes; posters for medical and nursing staff
audits.r2: Daily fluid management plan completed 56% (15% increase); nursing fluid balance completed 46%; blood glucose recorded 83%; daily weight documented 49%

audits.t: Impact of a standardised parenteral nutrition protocol: a quality improvement experience from a NICU of a developing country
audits.st: Nutrition society recommendations for standardised parenteral nutrition (SPN) solutions
audits.f: Hyperglycaemic episodes 37.5%; electrolyte abnormalities 56.3%; PN-associated liver disease 52.5%; sepsis 26%; median length of stay 14.0 days (IQR 12.0-21.0)
audits.c: Design and implementation of two evidence-based standardised PN (SPN) formulations for preterm neonates
audits.r2: Hyperglycaemic episodes 6.2% (p<0.001); electrolyte abnormalities 21% (p<0.001); PNALD 18.5% (p<0.001); sepsis 20% (p<0.05); median length of stay 8.0 days (IQR 5.0-13.0); greater weight gain velocity (beta=13.40, 95% CI 12.02-14.79)

audits.t: Video laryngoscopy-assisted less-invasive surfactant administration quality improvement initiative
audits.tp: Transition to video laryngoscopy-assisted less-invasive surfactant administration
audits.st: Locally set SMART aim: deliver surfactant by LISA for 65% of total doses by 31 December 2021
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Guideline development, education programmes, hands-on training, provider credentialing for video laryngoscopy-assisted LISA
audits.r2: 69% (79/115) received surfactant via LISA, exceeding the 65% goal within 1 month of go-live

audits.t: Prevalence and early surgical outcome of congenital diaphragmatic hernia in the Netherlands: a population-based cohort study from the European Pediatric Surgical Audit
audits.tp: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia care and outcomes registry
audits.st: European Pediatric Surgical Audit (prospective clinical audit for congenital anomalies)
audits.f: National prevalence rate 2.06/10,000 live births; patient population, treatment and 1-year outcomes comparable between the two hospitals except length of hospital stay

audits.t: Alcohol-impregnated port protectors to reduce central line-associated bloodstream infection in the neonatal intensive care unit: a quality improvement study
audits.tp: Alcohol-impregnated port protectors to reduce CLABSI
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Preimplementation CLABSI rate not separately stated in the abstract; overall preimplementation vs postimplementation CLABSI rate was 5.5 vs 6.6 per 1000 central line days (p=0.5).
audits.c: Alcohol-impregnated port protectors (AIPPs) were applied to intravascular access ports not used for fluid infusion, from March 2018 to February 2020, with daily audits for 3 months post-implementation and quarterly audits thereafter (3-month washout period March-May 2018).
audits.r2: No significant difference in overall CLABSI rate (5.5 vs 6.6 per 1000 central line days, p=0.5); rates of CLABSI with confirmed pathogens (rather than coagulase-negative Staphylococcus) were higher postimplementation (0.5 vs 2.7, p=0.012); adjusted OR for overall CLABSI risk was 1.05 (95% CI 0.57 to 1.91, p=0.886).

audits.t: Reduction of IVH in very preterm infants via a two-step quality improvement project: a retrospective study of 14 years’ experience
audits.tp: Reduction of intraventricular haemorrhage in very preterm infants
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: IVH rate 22.2%
audits.c: First quality improvement bundle (2010) and a second intervention bundle (2019) targeting identified risk factors
audits.r2: IVH rate reduced to 10.5% (p=0.0002), mainly in infants below 26 weeks gestation; low rate maintained over 14 years with second bundle

audits.t: Parental care pathway after late fetal loss and stillbirth: an audit of cases in sunderland royal hospital over a 2-year period
audits.st: RCOG Green-Top Guideline 'Late Intrauterine Fetal Death & Stillbirth', 19 locally derived standards
audits.f: 5 of 19 standards met in >90% of cases (cytogenetic investigation offer, chaplaincy visit, medical photography, support group information, lock of hair/prints); only 55% counselled about cytogenetic investigations by a consultant; only 13% offered lactation suppression; support group leaflets given to 33%

audits.t: Induction of labour of intrauterine fetal death >24/40: audit of a UK teaching hospital's practice over 1 year, prior to introduction of recent RCOG green-top guideline no. 55
audits.tp: Induction of labour for intrauterine fetal death
audits.st: not reported (audit conducted prior to introduction of RCOG green-top guideline no. 55)
audits.f: 50% had mifepristone/misoprostol with average induction-to-delivery interval 11.7h vs 18h for dinoprostone; diagnosis-to-delivery interval 36.5h (mife/miso) and 30h (prostin)

audits.t: Audit of performance of regional ECV services against RCOG standards: Abstract PLD.57 Table 1
audits.st: RCOG Green-top guideline No.20a on external cephalic version
audits.f: 158 (81%) women offered ECV; documented information on benefits varied 8-96% between units; 85 accepted, 35 (41%) had successful version; 44 (52%) received tocolytics

audits.t: Induction of labour audit – barnsley district general hospital
audits.tp: Induction of labour compliance with trust standards
audits.st: Local trust standards for induction of labour
audits.f: All women with previous CS induced on labour ward per standards; a third had no documented discussion of uterine rupture risk with prostin; 17% had more than two doses of 3mg prostin; only 14% had requisite 6h interval; 22% delivered by emergency caesarean

audits.t: Audit on trial of instrumental deliveries: Abstract PLD.70 Figure 1
audits.st: RCOG Guideline No.26 on Operative Vaginal Delivery (trial in theatre criteria)
audits.f: Incidence of operative vaginal delivery 14.8%; strict guideline adherence indicated 11 cases should have been managed as trial in theatre; 7 cases required caesarean section, all with fetal malposition

audits.t: Forceps delivery audit poster
audits.tp: Forceps delivery rate and guideline adherence
audits.st: RCOG and UCLH guidelines for instrumental vaginal delivery
audits.f: In 9.5% of forceps delivery cases the guideline was not followed (no recognised indication present)

audits.t: Audit on the management of ruptured membranes at term
audits.tp: Management of ruptured membranes at term
audits.st: NICE guideline on induction of labour after spontaneous rupture of membranes (SROM) at term, avoiding digital examination
audits.f: 23 women offered IOL after 24h of SROM; Syntocinon infusion time range 8-24h; 17 vaginal delivery, 4 assisted, 2 emergency caesarean; remaining 19 with SROM diagnosed via digital examination had higher intervention rates (9 LSCS, 4 instrumental) and higher complications

audits.t: Quality of care of the preterm infant project – a multidisciplinary approach to service improvement: Abstract PF.30 Table 1
audits.tp: Immediate intensive care of infants under 30 weeks gestation
audits.st: Locally agreed guidelines and standards for immediate resuscitation, stabilisation and respiratory support of infants <30 weeks gestation
audits.f: Infants intubated within 5 min of birth 44%; transfer respiratory parameters recorded 27%; admission temperature 36.5-37.5C 57%; umbilical lines inserted within 2h 18%; parents given information from nurses within 4h 33%; parents seen by senior doctor within 24h 55%
audits.c: New guidelines and standards launched July 2009 after training days; brief-rebrief-debrief cycle introduced
audits.r2: Infants intubated within 5 min 67%; transfer respiratory parameters recorded 78%; admission temperature in range 65%; umbilical lines within 2h 69%; parents given nurse information within 4h 60%; parents seen by senior doctor within 24h 86%

audits.t: Audit of energy and protein intake in infants < 32 weeks gestation, during the first 28 days of life: impact on growth
audits.st: Recommended energy and protein intake for preterm infants (published recommendations, target not stated)
audits.f: By 28 days, 43% met energy intake recommendations and 20% met protein recommendations; median energy deficit 349 kcal/kg (range 915-203), median protein deficit 20 g/kg (range 34-6.8)

audits.t: Does estimating the mid-spinal canal depth improve lumbar puncture success rates? a single centre tertiary neonatal care audit: Abstract PF.20 Table 1
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Without mid-spinal canal depth (MSCD) estimation, 13/25 LPs successful; with MSCD estimation, 5/19 successful; OR 0.25 (95% CI 0.06 to 1.05, p=0.06), a non-significant trend to lower success with MSCD estimation

audits.t: Audit on the management of infants with maternal Hepatitis C (HCV) infection at a neonatal abstinence (NAS) follow-up clinic
audits.tp: HCV screening of infants born to HCV positive mothers
audits.st: 2008 HCV protocol requiring screening of infants born to HCV positive mothers
audits.f: 12 mothers declined or were not offered HCV antenatal screening; of 71 tested, 20/71 (28%) were HCV antibody positive, of whom 8 were HCV RNA PCR positive; 18/20 (90%) of exposed infants were screened per protocol and all were HCV antibody negative at final testing

audits.t: Eighteen-year prospective audit of LASIK outcomes for myopia in 53 731 eyes.
audits.st: Refractive surgery outcome benchmarks: safety index, efficacy index, uncorrected visual acuity ≥20/40, and refractive predictability within ±0.5 D/±1.0 D of target
audits.f: Overall efficacy index 0.91 across the 18-year audit; more than 99% of eyes achieved uncorrected visual acuity of 20/40 or better
audits.r2: More than 70% of eyes achieved 20/20 uncorrected vision since 2010; safety index exceeded 1.05 from 2010; more than 94% within ±1.0 D and at least 70% within ±0.5 D of target refraction from 2010 onward; retreatment rate 2.55%; overall complication rate 0.98%

audits.t: EPIDEMIOLOGICAL INJURY SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM DURING MAJOR ATHLETICS CHAMPIONSHIPS: WHAT IS THE METHODOLOGICAL QUALITY?
audits.tp: Injury surveillance system quality in athletics championships
audits.st: Centre for Disease Control and Prevention guidelines for evaluating public health surveillance systems
audits.f: Mean 41.7+/-17.4% of registered countries participated, covering 79.5+/-10.2% of registered athletes; medical staff returned 89.2+/-8.4% of expected report forms; completeness of injury data averaged 95.8+/-6.5%

audits.t: Will our junior doctors be ready for the next major incident? A questionnaire audit on major incident awareness across three NHS Trusts in Wales.
audits.tp: Junior doctor major incident awareness and teaching
audits.st: Standard NHS Trust Major Incident Contingency Plan role expectations for junior doctors in Wales
audits.f: 91% did not know what would be expected of them during a major incident; only 3% would go to their ward first; 31% unaware who to contact
audits.c: Formal teaching by Emergency Planning Faculty
audits.r2: 97% knew who to call, where to go and what to do during a major incident after teaching

audits.t: Fall in peptic ulcer mortality associated with increased consultant input, prompt surgery and use of high dependency care identified through peer-review audit.
audits.tp: Consultant input, timely surgery and HDU/ITU use in peptic ulcer mortality
audits.st: Scottish Audit of Surgical Mortality (SASM) peer-review methodology
audits.f: Consultant presence at operation 40.0% in 1994; operations within 2h 10.3%; HDU/ITU use 52.7%
audits.c: Increased consultant input, prompt surgery, greater use of high dependency/intensive care, identified and driven through peer-review audit over time
audits.r2: Consultant presence rose to 73.4%; operations within 2h to 28.1%; HDU/ITU use to 84.4%; consultant involvement (p=0.005) and HDU/ITU care (p=0.026) significantly associated with reduced operative deaths

audits.t: Use of FMEA analysis to reduce risk of errors in prescribing and administering drugs in paediatric wards: a quality improvement report.
audits.tp: Medication error risk reduction in paediatric drug delivery (FMEA)
audits.st: Local risk-reduction target based on failure mode and effect analysis (FMEA) risk priority numbers (RPN) for the drug-delivery process
audits.f: 37 high-risk failure modes (with 71 associated causes/effects) were identified across the 5 units, with RPNs as high as 496; the most critical failure mode was drug dose calculation, especially for infusion drugs (RPN 60), found in all units
audits.c: Multidisciplinary FMEA-guided corrective actions: standardised and single-formulary prescribing, dose/dilution reference tables, double-checking and double-signing practices, pre-printed labels with barcodes, and other unit-specific process changes
audits.r2: After implementation, none of the revised process steps had an RPN above 32; RPNs for the higher risks fell by around 60% at almost all units, and 23 of the 37 high-risk failure modes moved into the low-risk area; clinical audits at 3 and 6 months confirmed the changes remained in place

audits.t: Prevention and management of chronic disease in Aboriginal and Islander Community Controlled Health Services in Queensland: a quality improvement study assessing change in selected clinical performance indicators over time in a cohort of services.
audits.tp: Chronic disease KPI improvement in Aboriginal health services
audits.st: Key performance indicators for chronic disease prevention and management (Close the Gap Collaborative)
audits.f: Baseline performance on key risk factor and healthcare activity indicators.
audits.c: Implementation and use of an electronic clinical information system integrated with electronic health records, supported by the QAIHC Close the Gap Collaborative quality improvement programme.
audits.r2: Aggregated performance was high on some indicators (tobacco use assessment, hypertension management) but low on others; greatest variation between services was for care planning and health-check activity.

audits.t: Quality of newborn care: adherence to guidelines for parenteral nutrition in preterm infants in four European countries
audits.tp: Parenteral nutrition guideline adherence in preterm infants
audits.st: International guidelines for parenteral nutrition in preterm infants: amino acids started day 0 at initial dose >=1.5 g/kg/day, target 3-4 g/kg/day; lipids started within 3 days at initial dose >=1.0 g/kg/day, target 3-4 g/kg/day
audits.f: 80% aware of PN guidelines; for amino acids, 63% aimed to start on day 0, 38% used initial dose >=1.5 g/kg/day, 91% used target dose of 3-4 g/kg/day; for lipids, 90% started within 3 days, 39% used initial dose >=1.0 g/kg/day, 76% used target dose 3-4 g/kg/day

audits.t: Clinical management issues vary by specialty in the Victorian Audit of Surgical Mortality: a retrospective observational study.
audits.tp: Clinical management issues in the Victorian Audit of Surgical Mortality
audits.st: Victorian Audit of Surgical Mortality educational peer-review process
audits.f: 15% of cases had significant issues of care; the most common clinical management issue was delay in delivery of treatment; issues varied significantly across surgical specialties (notably complications, communication, postoperative care).

audits.t: An audit of anticoagulant management to assess anticoagulant control using decision support software.
audits.tp: Anticoagulant control using computerised decision support
audits.st: Time in therapeutic range (TTR) target for warfarin management
audits.f: Overall TTR of 72.9%; TTR was significantly better for patients managed by pharmacists than doctors (75.1% vs 67.4%).

audits.t: What drives quality improvement in chronic kidney disease (CKD) in primary care: process evaluation of the Quality Improvement in Chronic Kidney Disease (QICKD) trial
audits.tp: Quality improvement drivers in CKD blood pressure control
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported (qualitative process evaluation; no quantitative blood pressure control results given in this abstract)
audits.c: Audit-based education (ABE, including specialist interaction) or sending clinical guidelines and prompts (G&P), compared with usual practice, to improve CKD systolic blood pressure control

audits.t: Incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia in Australasian intensive care units: use of a consensus-developed clinical surveillance checklist in a multisite prospective audit
audits.st: Consensus-developed five-item VAP clinical surveillance checklist, informed by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention guidelines
audits.f: 17% (n=29) met checklist VAP criteria and 17% (n=30) had an independent physician VAP diagnosis, but only 17% of cases were identified by both methods; VAP rate per 1000 ventilator days was 25.9 (checklist) vs 26.7 (clinician diagnosis)

audits.t: Prospective audit to evaluate the potential of the coronial system to increase solid organ donation.
audits.tp: Coronial referral impact on solid organ donation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Full permission for organ retrieval given in 87% of cases, partial in 9%; up to 77 organs potentially lost to unjustified restrictions

audits.t: Health professionals’ experiences of tuberculosis cohort audit in the North West of England: a qualitative study
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported (qualitative study of health professionals' experience of tuberculosis cohort audit; no compliance data reported)

audits.t: Reporting quality of randomised controlled trial abstracts among high-impact general medical journals: a review and analysis
audits.st: CONSORT for Abstracts 19-item checklist
audits.f: Overall adherence to the CONSORT for Abstracts checklist was 67% (95% CI 66-68%); The Lancet had the highest adherence (78%), NEJM the lowest (55%); adherence differed by more than 25% between journals on 8 checklist items

audits.t: Traumatic brain injury in England and Wales: prospective audit of epidemiology, complications and standardised mortality.
audits.tp: Traumatic brain injury epidemiology, complications and standardised mortality
audits.st: Ps14n multivariate logistic regression TBI outcome prediction model (risk-adjusted W score funnel plot)
audits.f: Median time to CT scan in severe TBI (GCS≤8) 0.5 hours; median time to craniotomy 2.6 hours; median time to ICP monitoring 3 hours; bronchopneumonia in 5% of severe TBI patients

audits.t: National audit of pressure ulcers and incontinence-associated dermatitis in hospitals across Wales: a cross-sectional study.
audits.tp: Pressure ulcer and incontinence-associated dermatitis prevalence
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 748 (8.9%) had pressure ulcers; 158 new pressure ulcers not previously known to ward staff; 152 pressure ulcers incorrectly categorised by ward teams; incontinence-associated dermatitis in 360 (4.3%); medical device-related pressure ulcers rare (n=33); 2537 (30.3%) had one or more skin wounds

audits.t: Are food and drink retailers within NHS venues adhering to NICE Quality standard 94 guidance on childhood obesity? A cross-sectional study of two large secondary care NHS hospitals in England
audits.tp: Healthy food and drink availability in NHS venues
audits.st: NICE Quality Standard 94 (childhood obesity), quality statements 1-3
audits.f: Only 7/18 (39%) vending machines served both a healthy food and a healthy drink option; neither hospital displayed nutritional information on menus (quality statement 2); compliance with prominent display of healthy options (quality statement 3) was inconsistent, with shops and cafes prioritising unhealthy items.

audits.t: Emergency Room Safer Transfer of Patients (ER-STOP): a quality improvement initiative at a community-based hospital to improve the safety of emergency room patient handovers.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: ED wait time 5.74+/-1.04 hours; ICU admission rate 4.61% (n=278); cardiac care unit admission rate 9.60% (n=579)
audits.c: Locally validated ER-STOP checklist (Modified Early Warning Score + urinary catheter in situ + nurse concern) with an intentional pause, added to the existing ED-to-ward transfer of accountability fax report.
audits.r2: Risk of unexpected critical care response team call within 24 hours of admission significantly decreased (OR 4.1, 95% CI 2.17 to 7.77); ED wait time 5.66+/-1.54 hours (unchanged, p=0.30); ICU admission rate 3.84% (n=233, unchanged p=0.06); cardiac care unit admission rate 9.51% (n=577, unchanged p=0.198)

audits.t: Reporting quality of randomised controlled trial abstracts on age-related macular degeneration health care: a cross-sectional quantification of the adherence to CONSORT abstract reporting recommendations
audits.st: CONSORT statement checklist for abstracts (16 items)
audits.f: Median number of CONSORT items fulfilled was 7 (95% CI 7-8) of 16; no abstract reported all 16 items; maximum 14, minimum 3 items fulfilled

audits.t: Does the architectural layout of a NICU affect alarm pressure? A comparative clinical audit of a single-family room and an open bay area NICU using a retrospective study design
audits.tp: NICU architectural layout and alarm pressure
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: The open bay area NICU generated 44% more alarms per infant per day than the single-family room NICU, although the single-family room NICU generated 2.5 times as many critical desaturation alarms per infant per day

audits.t: Improving the quality of administration of the Surgical Safety Checklist: a mixed methods study in New Zealand hospitals
audits.tp: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist administration quality audit tool
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist administration quality, assessed using the validated WHOBARS audit tool
audits.f: 87% of WHOBARS score variance was attributable to differences in Checklist administration between cases; self-ratings were significantly higher than observer ratings; error variance from all raters was less than 10%

audits.t: How is the audit of therapy intensity influencing rehabilitation in inpatient stroke units in the UK? An ethnographic study
audits.tp: Stroke therapy intensity audit target implementation
audits.st: UK audited performance target: 45 minutes of each therapy (occupational therapy, physiotherapy, speech and language therapy) for patients deemed appropriate
audits.f: not reported (ethnographic/qualitative study of how the audit target influences practice; no quantitative compliance figures reported in this abstract)

audits.t: What motivates general practitioners to change practice behaviour? A qualitative study of audit and feedback group sessions in Dutch general practice
audits.tp: GP motivation from audit and feedback sessions
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported (qualitative study of GPs' motivational response to audit and feedback; no compliance or outcome data reported)

audits.t: Implementation of the WHO manual for Robson classification: an example from Sri Lanka using a local database for developing quality improvement recommendations
audits.st: WHO manual for the Robson Ten Group Classification System for caesarean section rates
audits.f: Overall caesarean section (CS) rate 30.0% (11.9% prelabour); Robson Group 5 contributed most to the CS rate (29.6%), followed by Group 1 (14.0%), Group 2a (13.3%) and Group 10 (11.5%)
audits.c: 18 agreed recommendations including updating protocols, hands-on training, monitoring and supervision, criterion-based audits and risk management meetings

audits.t: Malnutrition, nutritional interventions and clinical outcomes of patients with acute small bowel obstruction: results from a national, multicentre, prospective audit
audits.tp: Nutritional care in small bowel obstruction
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 35.7% at moderate and 5.7% at severe risk of malnutrition (Nutritional Risk Index); dietitian review occurred in only 36.4% of moderate-risk and 55.9% of severe-risk patients; nutritional intervention given to 30.3% of low-risk, 40.7% of moderate-risk and 62.7% of severe-risk patients

audits.t: Quality of essential newborn care and neonatal resuscitation at health facilities in Afghanistan: a cross-sectional assessment
audits.tp: Essential newborn care and resuscitation quality
audits.st: Global guidelines for essential newborn care and neonatal resuscitation practices
audits.f: 87.9% (569/636) of babies dried immediately after birth; only 49.2% (313/636) placed in skin-to-skin contact; 89.7% (581/636) had umbilical cord cut with a sterile instrument; of 87 resuscitation attempts, only 62% (54/87) used a correct mask size and 3 babies died after unsuccessful bag-and-mask resuscitation

audits.t: Association between compliance with quality indicators and hospitalisation expenses in patients with heart failure: a retrospective study using quantile regression model in China
audits.st: 5 heart failure quality indicators (evaluation of left ventricular function, diuretics, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, beta-blockers, aldosterone receptor antagonists)
audits.f: Compliance rates were 90.3% for left ventricular function evaluation, 43.8% for diuretics, 62.0% for ACE inhibitors/ARBs, 67.4% for beta-blockers, and 58.9% for aldosterone receptor antagonists; median hospitalisation expense was Yuan 10.9 thousand (IQR 6.9-31.6 thousand); compliance with left ventricular function evaluation, diuretics, or ACE inhibitors/ARBs was associated with lower hospitalisation expenses, while beta-blocker compliance was associated with higher expenses; differences were significant above the 80th percentile of expenses (Yuan 39.7 thousand).

audits.t: Developing an Australian multi-module clinical quality registry for gynaecological cancers: a protocol paper
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Investigating the benefits and challenges of including bereaved women in research: a multifaceted perinatal audit in a socially disadvantaged French district
audits.tp: Perinatal mortality audit with family engagement
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: One-third (75) of women agreed to be interviewed, with acceptance ranging from 6% to 60% by maternity unit; 41% of interviews contained new information relevant to the expert panel's assessment; 35% of interviewed women were referred to a medical professional, psychologist or social worker.

audits.t: Quality of healthcare for children with severe acute malnutrition in a refugee setting: cross-sectional study in West Nile Region, Uganda
audits.tp: Quality of care for severe acute malnutrition in children
audits.st: International Sphere standards for severe acute malnutrition treatment (cure rate 75% or higher, default rate 15% or lower)
audits.f: Average cure rate was 50.4% versus the Sphere standard of 75% (p<0.001); default rate was 23.2% versus the standard of 15% (p<0.001); 201 of 305 (65.9%) National Nutrition Service Delivery Assessment scores were 'good' or 'excellent', but 66.7% of facilities had 'poor' quality improvement mechanisms and 43.3% had 'poor' human resources; refugee-hosting and non-refugee-hosting facilities had similar cure rates (47.1% vs 52.1%) but refugee-hosting facilities had higher transfer rates (21.5% vs 1.9%, p<0.001).

audits.t: Can the adherence to quality of care indicators for early rheumatoid arthritis in clinical practice reduce risk of hospitalisation? Retrospective cohort study based on the Record Linkage of Rheumatic Disease study of the Italian Society for Rheumatology
audits.tp: Quality indicator adherence in early rheumatoid arthritis
audits.st: 6 quality-of-care indicators for early rheumatoid arthritis (early DMARD use with/without glucocorticoids, early glucocorticoid interruption, early clinical assessment)
audits.f: Early DMARD prescription rate was 52% and timely clinical monitoring rate was 25% at the start of the study period.
audits.r2: Early DMARD prescription rose to 62% (p for trend<0.001) and timely clinical monitoring rose to 30% (p for trend=0.009); intermediate and high summary adherence score categories (vs low) were associated with lower 12-month hospitalisation risk (adjusted HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.77 to 0.93, p<0.001 and HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.69 to 0.84, p<0.001 respectively); during 1-year follow-up, 2609 hospitalisations occurred, 704 involving RA and 252 primarily for RA.

audits.t: Loss to follow up of pregnant women with HIV and infant HIV outcomes in the prevention of maternal to child transmission of HIV programme in two high-burden provinces in Papua New Guinea: a retrospective clinical audit
audits.tp: Prevention of mother-to-child HIV transmission programme performance
audits.st: WHO guidelines for lifelong antiretroviral therapy in pregnant women diagnosed with HIV
audits.f: 45.1% of women knew their HIV-positive status prior to the current pregnancy; 6.6% (50/763) of exposed infants had a positive HIV DNA test; younger age, new HIV diagnosis in the current pregnancy and serodiscordant relationship were associated with maternal loss to follow-up before birth (adjusted OR 2.92, 3.50 and 2.94 respectively)

audits.t: Does adherence to a quality indicator regarding early weaning from invasive ventilation improve economic outcome? A single-centre retrospective study
audits.tp: Adherence to ventilator weaning quality indicator
audits.st: Local standard: daily weaning protocol quality indicator with a threshold of 65% or greater compliance
audits.f: The low adherence group (under 65% compliance) had a median negative economic result of minus €3969 versus minus €1030 in the high adherence group (p<0.001); median ventilation duration was 476 hours (low adherence) versus 389 hours (high adherence) (p<0.001); ICU length of stay was 21 days versus 16 days (p<0.001); hospital length of stay was 36 days versus 26 days (p=0.001).

audits.t: Long-term quality of integrated community case management care for children in Bugoye Subcounty, Uganda: a retrospective observational study
audits.tp: Community health worker adherence to childhood illness protocol
audits.st: Ugandan national integrated community case management (iCCM) protocol for malaria, pneumonia and diarrhoea in children under 5
audits.f: Overall correct care (protocol adherence) was provided in 74% of clinical encounters; for the first cohort (trained from March 2013), quality of care rose modestly for about 3 years (OR 1.022 per month, 95% CI 1.005 to 1.038), then decreased modestly thereafter (OR 0.978 per month, 95% CI 0.970 to 0.986); for the second cohort (trained from July 2016), quality of care was essentially constant over time (OR 1.007 per month, 95% CI 0.989 to 1.025).

audits.t: What is the suitability of clinical vignettes in benchmarking the performance of online symptom checkers? An audit study
audits.tp: Online symptom checker diagnostic accuracy benchmarking
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Moderate agreement on triage recommendation between inputters (kappa=0.48) and substantial agreement on consultation outcomes (kappa=0.73); online symptom checker performance improved significantly from baseline when compared against the final consolidated diagnostic and triage solution (p<0.001).

audits.t: Estimating excess visual loss from neovascular age-related macular degeneration in the UK during the COVID-19 pandemic: a retrospective clinical audit and simulation model
audits.tp: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration referrals during COVID-19
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline nAMD referral volume pre-pandemic
audits.r2: nAMD referrals dropped by an average of 72% (range 65-87%) during the COVID-19 pandemic; simulated 3-month treatment delay increased eyes with vision <=6/60 from 15.5% to 23.3% and reduced eyes with vision >=6/12 from 35.1% to 26.4%

audits.t: Perceived usefulness of trauma audit filters in urban India: a mixed-methods multicentre Delphi study comparing filters from the WHO and low and middle-income countries.
audits.st: Trauma audit filters from WHO, Ghana, Cameroon and locally developed filters
audits.f: 26 predefined and 15 new filters evaluated; mean overall usefulness score 9.01/10; LMIC filters scored significantly higher than WHO and new filters.

audits.t: Assessing the quality of tuberculosis care using routine surveillance data: a process evaluation employing the Zero TB Indicator Framework in Mongolia
audits.st: Zero TB Indicator Framework, 14 indicators across 3 care cascades for TB case-finding, treatment and prevention
audits.f: The cumulative proportion of participants receiving guideline-adherent care ranged from 96% for community-based active case-finding to 79% for TB preventive therapy among household contacts to only 67% for passive case-finding in primary health centres and dispensaries (range 29%-80% across districts); odds of completing active TB treatment decreased with age (adjusted OR 0.76 per decade, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.83, p<0.001) and among men (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.36 to 0.88, p=0.013); contacts of older index patients had lower odds of completing preventive therapy (aOR 0.60 per decade, 95% CI 0.38 to 0.93, p=0.022).

audits.t: The role of teams in shaping quality of obstetrical care: a cross-sectional study in Dire Dawa, Ethiopia
audits.tp: Team effects on obstetric care process quality
audits.st: Recommended routine clinical actions for intrapartum and immediate postpartum care, across 5 phases of delivery
audits.f: For the average client, 50% of recommended routine clinical actions were completed overall, with immediate maternal postpartum care being the least well performed (17% of recommended actions); multiple providers were involved in 55% of deliveries; a one standard deviation increase in a coworker's performance was associated with a 2 percentage point increase in quality of care (p<0.01).

audits.t: Impact of practicing internal benchmarking on continuous improvement of cataract surgery outcomes: a retrospective observational study at Aravind Eye Hospitals, India
audits.st: Local standard: internal benchmarking of cataract surgery outcome parameters against the best-performing hospital (CATQA)
audits.f: Intraoperative complication rate was 1.2%; surgeries with uncorrected visual acuity of 6/12 or better were 80.8%; surgeries with postoperative refractive error within plus or minus 0.5D were 76.3%.
audits.c: Internal benchmarking of surgery outcome parameters (CATQA) practised since 2012, comparing hospitals against the best-performing hospital and driving improvements in facilities, protocols and processes
audits.r2: Intraoperative complication rate decreased to 0.6%; surgeries with uncorrected visual acuity of 6/12 or better rose to 89.8%; surgeries with postoperative refractive error within plus or minus 0.5D rose to 87.3%; variability in outcomes across hospitals declined.

audits.t: Use of a digital job-aid in improving antenatal clinical protocols and quality of care in rural primary-level health facilities in Burkina Faso: a quasi-experimental evaluation
audits.tp: Digital clinical decision support for antenatal care quality
audits.st: Recommended antenatal care protocols (quality-of-care scores based on actual versus expected care)
audits.f: Overall quality of health service provision score was 51% in comparison facilities; median antenatal care visit duration was 12 minutes (IQR 8).
audits.c: Digital clinical decision support (CDS) tool to improve health provider adherence to recommended antenatal protocols
audits.r2: Overall quality score was 52% in intervention facilities, comparable to the comparison arm despite a significantly higher proportion of lower-skilled providers (42.5% vs 17.8%); median visit duration was 24 minutes (IQR 18); the intervention arm had higher scores for women's knowledge of counselling received (16.4-point difference, 95% CI 10.37 to 22.49) and satisfaction (16.18-point difference, 95% CI 9.95 to 22.40).

audits.t: Assessing safe chemotherapy needs and practices in Ile-Ife, Nigeria: a multi-disciplinary quality improvement project
audits.st: American Cancer Society (ACS) ChemoSafe Facility Assessment, benchmarked against international standards for safe handling of hazardous drugs
audits.f: 75% of respondents reported a lack of training resources for safe chemotherapy handling; 61% reported dissatisfaction with assessment practices for preparing and administering chemotherapy.
audits.r2: Only 33 of 169 items (19.5%) received a 'Yes' response, indicating compliance with international standards for safe handling.

audits.t: Investigating the implementation of a Trial of Labour After Caesarean (TOLAC) delivery bundle with respect to decreasing caesarean delivery rates: a multisite quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Trial of labour after caesarean (TOLAC) uptake
audits.st: Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada guideline on TOLAC/VBAC eligibility and safety
audits.f: Caesarean delivery (CD) rate in TOLAC-eligible patients 77%; TOLAC rate 31%; VBAC rate 75%; induction of labour rate 5%
audits.c: A TOLAC delivery bundle introduced at each site in 4-month staggered stages: educational rounds for healthcare providers with individualised audit-and-feedback of CD rates, a physician-patient TOLAC discussion sheet for shared decision-making, and patient-centred educational handouts/posters/videos in 9 languages
audits.r2: CD rate fell to 71% (p<0.001); TOLAC rate rose to 37% (p<0.001); VBAC rate rose to 78% (p=0.277, not significant); induction of labour rate rose to 9% (p<0.001); no significant increase in uterine rupture or NICU admission rates (balance measures)

audits.t: Adherence to guidelines on quality neonatal resuscitation practices among healthcare professionals in Ghana: an observational study
audits.st: Quality neonatal resuscitation practice guidelines, assessed via a validated observational checklist
audits.f: 53% of healthcare professionals showed good adherence (80-100%); 36% moderate (50-79%); 11% poor (0-49%). Increased staffing and a bachelor's degree or higher were positively associated with performing positive pressure ventilation (aOR 19.3, p=0.005; aOR 9.9, p=0.043).

audits.t: Quality of maternal and newborn care, perinatal mental health and the emotional birth experience of women: findings of the IMAgiNE EURO study in Belgium
audits.tp: Quality of maternal and newborn care (WHO standards)
audits.st: WHO-based quality of maternal and newborn care standards (IMAgiNE EURO questionnaire)
audits.f: Median QMNC index 260/300; 33.5% reported ineffective communication, 34.0% lack of involvement in decision-making, 8.7% no emotional support, 8.2% reported abuse; 40.9% reported emotional difficulties related to childbirth.

audits.t: Quality improvement initiative using transcutaneous bilirubin nomogram to decrease serum bilirubin sampling in low-risk babies
audits.tp: Transcutaneous bilirubin screening to reduce serum sampling
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 882/1815 (49%) babies had at least one serum bilirubin sample taken
audits.c: Introduction of a protocol using a transcutaneous bilirubinometer (Dragger JM-105) with a TcBR nomogram in the postnatal ward
audits.r2: 236/1394 (17%) babies had at least one serum bilirubin sample taken; odds of performing serum bilirubin sampling were 79% lower post-implementation (OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.18-0.25)

audits.t: Comprehensive assessment of pediatric acute and inpatient care at a tertiary referral hospital in Malawi: opportunities for quality improvement.
audits.st: National malaria treatment protocol, WHO Emergency Triage Assessment and Treatment (ETAT) danger signs, WHO severe acute malnutrition (SAM) management guidance, and universal HIV testing guidance
audits.f: 92% of malaria patients had a rapid diagnostic test; 99% of pneumonia patients received antibiotics but only 80% had oxygen saturation documented; only 27% of SAM patients had a random blood sugar performed; laboratory test completion ranged 21-49%, radiology 32-42%, subspecialty consultations 13-70%; overall mortality 4%, with 60% of deaths in the first 48 hours

audits.t: Implementation of the WHO Standards to assess quality of paediatric care at the facility level using service users’ perspective as source of data: a multicentre quality improvement study in Italy
audits.tp: Quality of paediatric care (WHO Standards, service users)
audits.st: 75 WHO Standard-based Quality Measures for paediatric quality of care
audits.f: Physical resources domain had the most reported gaps: quality of meals 48.1% (range 35.3-61.7%), cooking areas 50.9% (range 34.6-70.0%), family/friend spaces 51.3% (range 31.8-77.4%). Experience of care: information on rights of the child 76.6% (range 59.9-90.4%) needing improvement; other measures 5-35%. COVID-19 reorganisational items <25% needing improvement.

audits.t: Implementation of the WHO Standards to assess the quality of paediatric care using health workers as source of data: findings of a multicentre study (CHOICE) in Italy
audits.tp: Quality of paediatric care (WHO Standards, health workers) (CHOICE)
audits.st: 75 WHO Standard-based Quality Measures for paediatric quality of care
