audits.f: High reported need for improvement with high variability across hospitals: clear paediatric emergency protocols 44.6% (range 10.6-92.6%), clear diarrhoea hospitalisation criteria 50.5% (range 30.3-71.7%), hand-washing stations 13.2% (range 3.4-37.0%), equipped working rooms 66.1% (range 32.1-97.0%), pain management training 43.5% (range 17.9-76.7%), audits 48.8% (range 29.7-76.7%).

audits.t: Midazolam as premedication for less invasive surfactant administration: a prospective single-centre audit
audits.tp: Premedication for less invasive surfactant administration (LISA)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Procedure deemed successful in 119/120 (99.2%) cases; side effects: surfactant reflux 18.5%, bradycardia 16.0%, apnoea 24.4%, oxygen desaturation 47.1%; only 9/119 (7.6%) required endotracheal intubation within 24 hours

audits.t: Implementing a checklist to strengthen IMCI-based assessment of childhood illnesses in an urban primary care setting in Delhi: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: IMCI-based checklist assessment in primary care
audits.st: WHO Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) guidelines for children aged 2 months to 5 years
audits.f: Complete IMCI assessment was performed for 0% of children; danger sign assessment 0%; cough assessment 86.8%; diarrhoea assessment 13.2%; fever assessment 64.2%; ear problem assessment 3.8%; malnutrition assessment 23.1%; anaemia (haemoglobin) assessment 25.0%; immunisation status documentation 1.9%. Of 45 children presenting with cough/breathing difficulty, only 3 (6.7%) were assessed for pneumonia or danger signs.
audits.c: Two 6-week PDSA cycles: age-specific IMCI-based child health assessment checklists (developed and validated with faculty input), a dedicated paediatric OPD room, improved anthropometry equipment and essential supplies; cycle 2 added formatting the checklist as the main OPD card, ensuring regular printing, 6-monthly refresher training for rotating resident doctors, and weekly case-based discussions
audits.r2: Complete assessment rose to 18.3% after PDSA1 and to 50% after PDSA2 (77.8% if haemoglobin testing excluded); danger sign assessment rose to 88.3% then 97.2%; cough screening rose to 90.0% then 100%; diarrhoea assessment rose to 76.7% then 94.5%; fever assessment rose to 88.3% then 91.7%; ear problem assessment rose to 63.3% then 88.9%; malnutrition assessment rose to 41.7% then 94.4%; haemoglobin testing rose to 48.3% then 69.4%; immunisation documentation rose to 61.7% then 83.3%.

audits.t: Quality improvement: prevention of cardiac arrest in children with heart disease on the paediatric intensive care unit.
audits.tp: Cardiac arrest prevention in paediatric intensive care
audits.st: Cardiac arrest prevention (CAP) bundle modelled on the North American Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium (PC4) collaborative programme; local target of reducing cardiac arrest incidence by over 33%
audits.f: cardiac arrest incidence 6.2% (28/449) overall; 5.2% in surgical admissions, 9% in medical admissions
audits.c: A comprehensive cardiac arrest prevention bundle: proactive high-risk patient identification, twice-daily safety huddles, bedside pre-prepared low-dose epinephrine, prospective adverse event data collection with risk-adjusted process monitoring (RSPRT charts), and formal multidisciplinary arrest review meetings
audits.r2: overall cardiac arrest incidence fell to 4.4% (29/664), a 30% relative reduction (target 33%, not quite met, p=0.212); in the surgical cohort, RSPRT monitoring showed a statistically significant 'halving' of risk-adjusted cardiac arrest rate (special cause variation) within fewer than 200 admissions

audits.t: Structures and processes of care in ambulatory oncology settings and nurse-reported exposure to chemotherapy
audits.tp: Ambulatory oncology chemotherapy safety practices and nurse exposure
audits.st: Seven ambulatory chemotherapy administration safety standards (not individually specified in the abstract)
audits.f: 16.9% of nurses reported chemotherapy exposure to skin or eyes in the past year; exposure risk was lower with adequate staffing and resources (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.17-0.73) and frequent two-nurse dose verification (OR 0.17, 95% CI 0.05-0.59)

audits.t: Reducing post-caesarean surgical wound infection rate: an improvement project in a Norwegian maternity clinic
audits.st: Norwegian national caesarean section surgical wound infection rate of below 8%
audits.f: Caesarean section surgical wound infection rate was 17.4%
audits.c: A bundle of measures based on Cochrane evidence as gold standard, implemented September 2008 with multidisciplinary staff involvement and monthly reporting to the Head of Maternity Clinic
audits.r2: Overall caesarean section surgical wound infection rate reduced to 3.1% (about 1% in 2010), shown as a marked shift on a statistical process control g-chart

audits.t: Building information for systematic improvement of the prevention of hospital-acquired pressure ulcers with statistical process control charts and regression
audits.tp: Hospital-acquired pressure ulcer surveillance using statistical process control
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 337 hospital-acquired pressure ulcer (HAPU) incidents; mean incidence rate 1.17%, remaining in statistical control; 40.5% of patients were risk-stratified using the Braden scale on admission; HAPU incidence was below the national mean

audits.t: Using quality improvement to accelerate highly active antiretroviral treatment coverage in South Africa
audits.st: Universal HAART coverage target for estimated regional need
audits.f: Baseline HIV testing 891/month (SD 94.2) and HAART initiations 179/month (SD 17.22); proportion of estimated regional HAART need met was 35.8%
audits.c: Quality improvement 'learning network' with collective and individual performance targets, real-time data feedback and simple system changes to improve HIV testing and HAART initiation, phased scale-up August 2006 to November 2009
audits.r2: HIV testing increased 301.8% to 3580/month (SD 327.7, p<0.0001); HAART initiations increased 185.5% to 511/month (SD 44.93, p<0.0001); proportion of estimated need for HAART met increased to 72.4%

audits.t: The Australian Primary Care Collaboratives Program: improving diabetes care
audits.tp: Primary care diabetes risk-factor control (Australian Primary Care Collaboratives)
audits.st: Target levels for HbA1c, total cholesterol and blood pressure
audits.f: 25% of patients were at target HbA1c level at baseline.
audits.c: A large-scale quality improvement collaborative delivered in seven waves (2004-2009): workshops, local program managers, PDSA cycles and comparative feedback against other services in the same wave.
audits.r2: Mean numbers of patients at target HbA1c improved by 50%, from 25% at baseline to 38% at month 18; lipid and blood pressure measures showed similar improvement.

audits.t: The Housestaff Incentive Program: improving the timeliness and quality of discharge summaries by engaging residents in quality improvement
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average time from discharge to completion of discharge summary was 3.5 days; 38% of summaries completed on day of discharge; 5% included all recommended elements; 38% reported unavailable at outpatient follow-up
audits.c: Housestaff Incentive Program: a discharge summary improvement bundle with an educational curriculum, an electronic discharge summary template, regular data feedback and a financial incentive, led by resident champions
audits.r2: Average time fell to 0.61 days (p<0.001); 83% completed on day of discharge (p<0.001); 88% included all recommended elements (p<0.001); unavailability at follow-up fell to 4% (p<0.001)

audits.t: A prospective, observational study of the effects of implementation strategy on compliance with a surgical safety checklist
audits.tp: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist compliance by implementation strategy
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist correct administration of Sign In, Time Out and Sign Out domains
audits.f: Domain compliance at Hospital 1 vs Hospital 2 was: Sign In 96% vs 31% (p<0.0005); Time Out 99% vs 48% (p<0.0005); Sign Out 22% vs 9% (p=0.008)

audits.t: Effective prevention of thromboembolic complications in emergency surgery patients using a quality improvement approach.
audits.tp: VTE prophylaxis delivery in emergency surgery admissions
audits.st: local/national thromboprophylaxis delivery guidelines
audits.f: Delivery of thromboprophylaxis according to guidelines was 35% before intervention.
audits.c: multifaceted industrial process-improvement intervention to correct deficiencies in thromboprophylaxis delivery
audits.r2: Delivery improved to 87% three months after intervention (χ²=87.412); associated with a 61% reduction in radiologically detected DVT/PE episodes two months after admission, compared with the year before intervention.

audits.t: Patterns in the recording of vital signs and early warning scores: compliance with a clinical escalation protocol
audits.tp: Compliance with vital signs and early warning score escalation protocol
audits.st: Hospital's clinical escalation protocol (VitalPAC Early Warning Score, ViEWS)
audits.f: 23.84% of datasets with ViEWS >=9 were measured at night versus 10.12-19.97% for other ViEWS values; 47.42% of patients with ViEWS 7-8 and 31.22% with ViEWS >=9 in the evening did not have vital signs recorded in the following 6 hours.

audits.t: Challenges to implementing expanded team models: lessons from a centralised nurse-led cholesterol-lowering programme
audits.tp: Nurse-led cholesterol-lowering programme for diabetes/CVD patients
audits.st: Target LDL cholesterol below 100 mg/dL in patients with diabetes and cardiovascular disease
audits.f: 50% of enrolled patients did not complete the programme; among those enrolled, median LDL decreased by 21 mg/dL and 52% (33/64) achieved the LDL target
audits.c: Centralised, expanded team-based quality improvement programme in which registered nurses followed a protocol to adjust cholesterol-lowering medications

audits.t: Improving outcomes for patients with type 2 diabetes using general practice networks: a quality improvement project in east London
audits.tp: Type 2 diabetes care using general practice networks
audits.st: not reported (local key measures: care plan completion, retinal screening attendance, biomedical targets)
audits.f: Completed diabetes care plans were at 10%; digital retinal screening attendance was 72%; 35.3% of patients achieved a combination of blood pressure <=140/80 mmHg and cholesterol <=4 mmol/L; mean HbA1c was 7.80%.
audits.c: Practices grouped into networks with a network manager, clerical staff and educational budget; a multidisciplinary 'care package' for type 2 diabetes with financial incentives, monthly electronic performance dashboards, and network MDT meetings.
audits.r2: Completed care plans rose to 88%; retinal screening attendance rose to 82.8%; achievement of combined BP/cholesterol target rose to 46.1%; mean HbA1c fell to 7.66% (60 mmol/mol).

audits.t: Oral antibiotics at discharge for children with acute osteomyelitis: a rapid cycle improvement project.
audits.tp: Oral antibiotics at discharge for acute osteomyelitis
audits.st: Local target: at least 70% of acute osteomyelitis cases discharged on oral antibiotics
audits.f: Virtually all patients were discharged on intravenous therapy prior to the project (baseline near 0% oral)
audits.c: Multifaceted intervention: shared decision-making tool, electronic health record order set, and education to faculty/trainees, plus an identify-and-mitigate real-time reinforcement strategy
audits.r2: Cases discharged on oral antibiotics increased from a median of 0 preintervention to a maximum of 9 cases following the identify-and-mitigate intervention; improvement sustained for 1 year

audits.t: P097 Adherence to Guidelines for Preventive Child Health Care in The Netherlands
audits.tp: Adherence to preventive child health care guidelines
audits.st: Nine national Preventive Child Health Care guidelines developed since 1998 at the request of the Dutch Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport
audits.f: Completeness of use of key guideline activities varied from 28% to 98% per activity; lack of time and lack of client cooperation were the most commonly cited obstacles

audits.t: P198 Adherence To Infertility Guidelines With Regard To Treatment Policy
audits.tp: Guideline adherence in unexplained infertility treatment
audits.st: Dutch national network guideline on infertility (supported by ESHRE and NICE international guidelines), recommending a prognostic model to prevent unnecessary treatment for unexplained infertility
audits.f: Prognostic model was used in 54% of couples; the right treatment decision was primarily made in 69% of couples; ultimately 41% of all couples received unnecessary treatment

audits.t: P200 Suicide Risk Assessment According to Best Practice Guidelines: The Development of a Chart Audit Performance Measure
audits.tp: Suicide risk assessment documentation chart audit tool development
audits.st: Registered Nurses' Association of Ontario best practice guideline: Assessment and Care of Adults at Risk for Suicidal Ideation and Behaviour (2009), five key recommendations
audits.f: not reported (this paper describes development of a 15-indicator, 3-point Likert chart audit tool to measure documentation congruence with the best practice guideline; no audit was conducted or results reported)

audits.t: Sustained improvement in nutritional outcomes at two paediatric cystic fibrosis centres after quality improvement collaboratives
audits.tp: Nutritional outcomes in paediatric cystic fibrosis
audits.st: Cystic Fibrosis Foundation practice guidelines for nutrition management
audits.f: One centre's mean BMI percentile was at the 40th percentile in 2001 and the other at the 37th percentile in 2003.
audits.c: Implementation of CFF nutrition practice guidelines through changed care-delivery processes, nutritional interventions, team engagement and use of run/statistical process control charts to display data, as part of national QI collaboratives.
audits.r2: One centre rose to the 60th percentile and the other to the 55th percentile by 2011, having reached the 49th and 45th percentiles respectively by 2003/2004 shortly after the intervention.

audits.t: Redesigning care to meet national recommendation of four or more yearly clinic visits in patients with cystic fibrosis
audits.st: Cystic Fibrosis Foundation recommendation of at least 4 clinic visits per year (every 3 months); project target of 90% or greater attendance
audits.f: 35% of patients attended clinic 4 or more times a year in 2004, rising to 56% in 2005 (CF Foundation Registry data)
audits.c: Redesigned scheduling system, timely rescheduling of missed appointments, and a process to monitor attendance
audits.r2: Percentage of patients attending clinic 4 or more times a year reached the goal of 90% in 2012

audits.t: The effect of a clinical pharmacist-led training programme on intravenous medication errors: a controlled before and after study
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Prevalence of clinically relevant erroneous doses was 64.0% on the ICU (intervention ward) and 57.9% on the PSU (control ward)
audits.c: Clinical pharmacist-led training programme including lectures, practical ward-based teaching sessions and protocols/guidelines, delivered by a pharmacist and a nurse
audits.r2: Erroneous dose prevalence decreased significantly on the intervention ward to 48.9% (p<0.001) but was unchanged on the control ward (64.1%, p=0.132); intervention ward doses were 2.60 times less likely to have clinically relevant errors (95% CI 1.27-5.31, p=0.013)

audits.t: The impact of transforming healthcare delivery on cystic fibrosis outcomes: a decade of quality improvement at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital
audits.tp: Cystic fibrosis clinical outcomes quality improvement
audits.st: Cystic Fibrosis Foundation National Patient Registry benchmarks (below-average outcomes identified against registry norms)
audits.f: Median forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) was 81.7% predicted; median body mass index was at the 35th centile
audits.c: Decade-long comprehensive quality improvement programme (2001-2010): sharing outcomes data, a QI steering committee with parent/hospital leadership, real-time data management, restructured chart conference and individualised inpatient schedules, an influenza vaccination campaign, redesigned infection control, best-practice airway-clearance guidelines, evidence-based clinical algorithms and added care-team members
audits.r2: Median FEV1 increased to 100.1% predicted; median body mass index increased to the 55th centile

audits.t: Improving transition from paediatric to adult cystic fibrosis care: programme implementation and evaluation
audits.tp: Cystic fibrosis transition from paediatric to adult care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Discussion of transition with families occurred in 35% of encounters at the paediatric centre
audits.c: Multi-phase transition curriculum, agreed care standards, standardised patient transfer protocols, and quarterly paediatric-adult team meetings sustained over 4 years
audits.r2: Discussion of transition with families increased to 73% (p<0.001), with a trend towards improved Transition Readiness Assessment Questionnaire self-advocacy scores and decreased in-hospital transfer

audits.t: Using quality improvement to optimise paediatric discharge efficiency
audits.st: Target: increase the percentage of patients discharged within 2 hours of meeting discharge criteria from 42% to 80%
audits.f: 42% of patients were discharged within 2 hours of meeting discharge criteria
audits.c: Multidisciplinary development of standardised discharge criteria for 11 common diagnoses embedded in electronic medical record order sets, EMR time-stamping, pharmacy process redesign, improved subspecialty consult timeliness and feedback to frontline staff
audits.r2: Percentage discharged within 2 hours improved to 80%; median length of stay decreased from 1.56 to 1.44 days (p=0.01) without increased readmissions (4.60% to 4.21%, p=0.24)

audits.t: GUIDELINE BUNDLES ADHERENCE AND MORTALITY IN SEVERE SEPSIS AND SEPTIC SHOCK: RESULTS OF A NATIONAL PATIENT SAFETY PROGRAM IN THE NETHERLANDS
audits.tp: Surviving Sepsis Campaign bundle adherence and mortality
audits.st: Surviving Sepsis Campaign bundles completed within 6 and 24 hours of ICU admission; target individual bundle adherence >80% and relative mortality reduction of at least 15% (absolute reduction 5.2%) by end of 2012
audits.f: In-hospital mortality among severe sepsis and septic shock ICU patients was 34.8%
audits.c: National programme to screen for severe sepsis and septic shock and implement Surviving Sepsis Campaign bundles within 6 and 24 hours of ICU admission
audits.r2: Bundle target adherence improved (adjusted OR per month 1.024, 95% CI 1.016-1.031) and in-hospital mortality decreased (adjusted OR per month 0.992, 95% CI 0.986-0.997), equivalent to 5.8% absolute and 16.7% relative mortality reduction over 3.5 years, in participating ICUs only

audits.t: ENHANCED FEEDBACK FROM PERIOPERATIVE QUALITY INDICATORS: STUDYING THE IMPACT OF A COMPLEX QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INTERVENTION
audits.tp: Perioperative quality indicator feedback to anaesthetists
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Preliminary audits demonstrated variations in patient temperature, pain and nausea measures; mapping showed delays in patient transfer from the Post Anaesthetic Care Unit were stretching resources
audits.c: Continuous monitoring and feedback initiative using process mapping and statistical process control, with monthly ward reports and personalised monthly performance reports to individual consultant anaesthetists
audits.r2: Interrupted time series analysis showed a significant increase in mean patient temperature on arrival in recovery associated with introduction of temperature feedback; large variation in transfer times between wards was attributable to bed management and staffing; pain and nausea scores remained relatively stable at the department level

audits.t: Application of a trigger tool in near real time to inform quality improvement activities: a prospective study in a general medicine ward
audits.tp: Adverse event identification using an augmented trigger tool
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 14 patients (10%, 95% CI 5-15%) experienced at least one preventable adverse event; 32 patients (23%, 95% CI 16-30%) experienced at least one potential adverse event; the most common contributing factors were policy/procedural problems (37%), communication/teamwork problems (34%) and medication process problems (23%)

audits.t: A quality improvement project to improve early sepsis care in the emergency department
audits.tp: Early sepsis care compliance in the emergency department
audits.st: Recommended sepsis management bundle: serum lactate measured in the emergency department, 2L intravenous fluid within 2 hours of triage, antibiotics within 3 hours of triage, and blood cultures drawn before antibiotic administration
audits.f: Overall bundle compliance was 28%; mortality rate for ED sepsis admissions was 13.3%
audits.c: Three-tiered intervention: a nurse-driven sepsis screening and management protocol, a computer-assisted 'Sepsis Alert' pop-up in the electronic medical record, and automated suggested sepsis-specific order sets
audits.r2: Overall bundle compliance increased 154% to 71% (p<0.001); mortality fell to 11.1% after implementation (p=0.230), and to 9.3% in the last two quarters (p=0.107)

audits.t: Reducing the incidence of oxyhaemoglobin desaturation during rapid sequence intubation in a paediatric emergency department
audits.tp: Rapid sequence intubation safety in paediatric emergency department
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Frequency of oxyhaemoglobin desaturation (SpO2<90%) during rapid sequence intubation was 33%
audits.c: Simultaneous testing of an RSI checklist, a pilot/copilot model for checklist execution, a video laryngoscope, and restricting laryngoscopy to specific providers, refined through plan-do-study-act cycles
audits.r2: Frequency of desaturation fell to 16% (50% lower than historical); when all six key processes were performed, only 6% of patients experienced desaturation; special cause variation seen on G-charts for 3 of 6 key processes plus attempt failure and desaturation

audits.t: Do pneumonia readmissions flagged as potentially preventable by the 3M PPR software have more process of care problems? A cross-sectional observational study
audits.tp: Pneumonia readmission quality flagging (Potentially Preventable Readmissions)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Total quality-of-care scores were slightly higher, though non-significantly, among PPR-yes cases (71.2+/-8.7) than PPR-no cases (65.8+/-11.5), p=0.14, out of a maximum score of 100

audits.t: A qualitative study of the variable effects of audit and feedback in the ICU
audits.tp: Clinician experience of audit and feedback in the ICU
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported (qualitative grounded theory study of clinicians' experience of audit and feedback; no compliance or outcome data reported)

audits.t: Implementing an institution-wide quality improvement policy to ensure appropriate use of continuous cardiac monitoring: a mixed-methods retrospective data analysis and direct observation study
audits.tp: Appropriate use of continuous cardiac monitoring
audits.st: American Heart Association guidelines limiting continuous cardiac monitoring to clinically indicated patients
audits.f: Cardiac monitoring rate 0.535 per patient day; monitored transport rate 0.216 per patient day; emergency department boarding rate 5.5%; false alarms 18.8%
audits.c: Institution-wide continuous cardiac monitoring policy based on AHA guidelines, developed by a cross-functional alarm management task force with leadership support
audits.r2: Cardiac monitoring rate decreased 53.2% to 0.251 per patient day (p<0.001); monitored transport rate decreased 15.5% to 0.182 (p<0.001); ED boarding rate decreased 36.6% to 3.5% (p<0.001); false alarms decreased to 9.6% (p<0.001)

audits.t: Implementation of HIV treatment as prevention strategy in 17 Canadian sites: immediate and sustained outcomes from a 35-month Quality Improvement Collaborative
audits.tp: HIV antiretroviral therapy uptake and viral suppression quality improvement
audits.st: Global targets for antiretroviral therapy (ART) coverage and viral suppression; chronic care model and HIV care and treatment guidelines
audits.f: 73% of HIV-diagnosed people in the intervention setting were on ART and 49% were achieving viral suppression in 2011
audits.c: 35-month Breakthrough Series Quality Improvement Collaborative implementing the chronic care model and HIV care/treatment guidelines, with monthly implementation scoring
audits.r2: Comprehensive chronic care model implementation with evidence of improvement was achieved by 29% of sites; sustained improvement was observed in patient engagement (88.8-90.4%), ART uptake among those in need (92.9-94.8%), and ART uptake/viral suppression (57.3-78.4%), all p<0.05

audits.t: A ‘paperless’ wall-mounted surgical safety checklist with migrated leadership can improve compliance and team engagement
audits.tp: Surgical safety checklist compliance with migrated leadership
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist domain and item administration compliance
audits.f: Sign In, Time Out and Sign Out administered in 96%, 99% and 22% of cases; relevant checklist items administered in 60%, 84% and 80% of cases respectively; two-subteam engagement at Sign In 40%; three-subteam engagement at Time Out 15% and Sign Out 9%
audits.c: Introduction of a wall-mounted paperless checklist with migrated process leadership (Sign In led by anaesthesia, Time Out by surgery, Sign Out by nursing)
audits.r2: Sign In, Time Out and Sign Out administered in 98%, 99% and 84% of cases (p=0.69, 1.00, <0.001); relevant items administered in 92%, 93% and 99% (p<0.001 for all); two-subteam engagement at Sign In 94%; three-subteam engagement at Time Out 92% and Sign Out 25% (p<0.001 for all)

audits.t: Theory-based and evidence-based design of audit and feedback programmes: examples from two clinical intervention studies.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Feedback Intervention Theory (FIT)-based design of audit and feedback interventions: a personalised one-on-one intervention to reduce inappropriate CAUTI diagnosis, and a web-based report-style feedback intervention for hypertension care.

audits.t: STANDARDIZATION AND IMPROVEMENT IN PEDIATRIC CELIAC CARE
audits.tp: Celiac disease follow-up serology testing adherence
audits.st: NASPGHAN celiac disease guidelines recommending repeat serology testing 6 months after diagnosis; project target of 90% having repeat testing within 9 months by December 2015
audits.f: 54.8% of patients had repeat serology testing within 9 months of diagnosis; baseline follow-up clinic visit within 9 months (Q4 2012-Q4 2013) was 82.2%
audits.c: Creation of a tracking registry, implementation of a local standard of care, practitioner educational sessions, reporting of practitioner adherence, and improved administrative staff utilisation to identify patients needing follow-up
audits.r2: Repeat serology testing within 9 months increased to 72.8% (p=0.000); follow-up clinic visit within 9 months increased to 96.6% (Q1 2014-Q2 2015, p=0.000)

audits.t: REDUCING THE INCIDENCE OF CLABSI IN LATIN AMERICAN ICUS: A MULTI-COUNTRY QUALITY IMPROVEMENT COLLABORATIVE. PRELIMINARY RESULTS FROM THE SECOND PHASE
audits.st: 'Goodbye Bacteremia' campaign target: reduce central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) rate by 50% or to less than 2 episodes per 1000 central line days within 12 months
audits.f: Baseline mean CLABSI rate 2.67 per 1000 central line days; insertion bundle compliance 65.55%; maintenance bundle compliance 82.56%
audits.c: Quality improvement collaborative promoting evidence-based bundles of care for central line insertion and maintenance, with virtual bi-weekly learning sessions and continuous feedback, June 2014 to June 2015
audits.r2: CLABSI rate reduced 24.34% to a mean of 2.02 per 1000 central line days (median rate zero throughout); insertion bundle compliance increased 49.49% to 97.99%; maintenance bundle compliance increased 14.86% to 94.83%

audits.t: REDUCING INTRAVENTRICULAR HEMORRHAGE IN A LEVEL III NEONATAL INTENSIVE CARE UNIT
audits.tp: Severe intraventricular haemorrhage reduction in preterm infants
audits.st: Project target: reduce severe intraventricular haemorrhage (IVH) incidence in infants born under 30 weeks from 8% to 4% between October 2014 and December 2015
audits.f: Average monthly rate of severe IVH was 8.3%
audits.c: Multidisciplinary bundle: midline head positioning during the first week of life, a minimal handling bundle with multidisciplinary admission huddle, a web-based IVH risk calculator, and standardised infusion rates for boluses/blood products
audits.r2: Average monthly rate of severe IVH decreased to 5.1%; midline head positioning and admission huddle compliance reached 100% for infants under 30 weeks

audits.t: IMPROVING COMMUNICATION DURING CARDIAC INTENSIVE CARE UNIT MULTIDISCIPLINARY ROUNDS THROUGH VISUAL DISPLAY OF PATIENT DAILY GOALS
audits.tp: Multidisciplinary rounds communication of patient daily goals
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline percent agreement on patient daily goals among care team members was 62%; parent selection of the best possible satisfaction score was 19% at baseline (mean satisfaction 4.6 out of 6)
audits.c: Implementation of a daily patient goal write-down/read-back process using a whiteboard and later a laminated sheet, developed and refined through multiple plan-do-study-act cycles
audits.r2: Percent agreement on patient goals improved to 85%; family satisfaction mean score improved from 4.6 to 5.7 out of 6; parent selection of the best possible score improved to 75%

audits.t: INCREASING TRICHOMONAS TESTING IN THE PEDIATRIC EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
audits.tp: Trichomonas testing in adolescents in the emergency department
audits.st: Project target: increase Trichomonas testing among high-risk adolescents from 40% (July 2014) to 100% by 31 March 2015, sustained through 2015
audits.f: Baseline Trichomonas testing rate was 25%
audits.c: Increased staff awareness and education, combined test availability, STI order sets, a Licensed Professional Initiated Protocol for nurse ordering, and feedback on individual missed cases, using plan-do-study-act cycles
audits.r2: Testing rate rose to 98% by March 2015, sustained through August 2015

audits.t: BUNDLES OVERCOME HURDLES IN THE GOLDEN HOUR FOR <28 WEEK NEONATES
audits.tp: Golden hour stabilisation for extremely preterm neonates
audits.st: Project target: improve golden hour stabilisation rate at 135 minutes of life from 17% to 80% by 31 January 2017 and sustain indefinitely; stabilisation defined as achieving neutral thermal environment, rapid treatment of presumed sepsis, and prevention of hypoglycaemia via timely IV glucose/protein
audits.f: Golden hour bundle compliance was 88% at baseline
audits.c: Multidisciplinary Golden Hour QI team (formed October 2014) using process mapping, Pareto chart, fishbone diagrams and plan-do-study-act cycles, with a discipline-specific bundled approach
audits.r2: Bundle compliance increased steadily from 88% to 95%; times to neutral thermal environment, IV fluid and antibiotic administration decreased, surpassing goals; no change in mortality rate (below 20%)

audits.t: MANAGING INPATIENT PEDIATRIC HEALTH CARE WITH A 24 HOUR CARE PROGRESSION BUNDLE
audits.tp: Paediatric inpatient discharge and length of stay improvement
audits.st: Project target: decrease time to discharge by 25% and average length of stay by 20% within 6 months
audits.f: Average discharge time was 2.45 hours; average length of stay was 80 hours
audits.c: 24-hour Care Progression Bundle developed and implemented via iterative plan-do-study-act cycles to improve nursing/physician handoff and support 24/7 clinical progression of care
audits.r2: Discharge time decreased 30% to 1.76 hours (p=0.001); average length of stay decreased significantly to 57.3 hours (p=0.003); discharge time of day was significantly earlier (p<0.001)

audits.t: REDUCING BPD IN A LEVEL IV NICU
audits.tp: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia reduction in extremely preterm infants
audits.st: Project target: decrease incidence of any bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) at day of life 28 from 78% to 62%, and severe BPD at 36 weeks corrected gestational age from 62% to 48%, in infants born before 30 weeks, by 31 December 2015 and sustained indefinitely
audits.f: Incidence of any and severe BPD was higher than comparison NICUs even after controlling for NICU type, gestational age and age at admission (baseline rates 78% any BPD, 62% severe BPD)
audits.c: Multidisciplinary QI team developed protocols addressing barotrauma, atelectrauma and oxygen toxicity, followed by a culture-change 'stand-down' campaign emphasising a 'wingman' approach, through multiple plan-do-study-act cycles
audits.r2: Both 'any' BPD and, a few months later, 'severe' BPD showed statistical improvement; time to first extubation attempt also declined

audits.t: QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PRACTICE FACILITATORS IN COMMUNITY PRACTICES: INCREASING FLUORIDE VARNISH APPLICATION
audits.tp: Fluoride varnish application in primary care
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics Periodicity Schedule (fluoride varnish at well-child visits); local aim to increase to 50% by 30/06/2017
audits.f: Fluoride varnish use 0.0% at baseline
audits.c: QI practice facilitators trained 5 practices using IHI Model for Improvement; interventions included product selection/training, consent, visual reminders, parent education, and learning-collaborative webinars
audits.r2: Fluoride varnish use rose to a median of 44.2% within 3 months, then to 54.8% by months 4-7 (centre line shifted to 51.2%)

audits.t: RELIABLE ADHERENCE TO BEST PRACTICES THAT MITIGATES SYSTEM-LEVEL ERRORS REDUCES COPD READMISSIONS: A SYSTEM REDESIGN USING IMPROVEMENT SCIENCE
audits.st: Locally developed 5-element COPD care bundle (appropriate inhaler regimen, bedside inhaler education, 30-day medication supply, follow-up within 15 days, standardised discharge instructions)
audits.f: 42 system-level failures identified among 52 readmissions in 31 patients; bundle compliance below 50%; 30-day all-cause readmission rate 22.7%
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team designed a 5-element COPD care bundle and used the Model for Improvement with SPC charting to redesign care delivery
audits.r2: Bundle compliance rose to approaching 90% reliability; 30-day all-cause readmission rate fell to 14.79% with a system shift on the SPC chart

audits.t: IMPROVING PATIENT SAFETY IN LATIN AMERICA: A MULTI-COUNTRY QUALITY IMPROVEMENT COLLABORATIVE PROJECT TO REDUCE THE INCIDENCE OF CLABSI IN ICUS
audits.tp: CLABSI prevention bundle compliance in ICU
audits.st: Central line insertion and maintenance care bundles; target to reduce CLABSI incidence by 50% or to under 2 episodes/1000 central line days within 12 months
audits.f: CLABSI incidence 2.58 episodes/1000 central line days; insertion bundle compliance 67.8%; maintenance bundle compliance 82.3%
audits.c: Quality-improvement collaborative promoting adoption of central line insertion/maintenance bundles plus virtual bi-weekly learning sessions, June 2014-June 2015
audits.r2: CLABSI incidence fell to 2.02 episodes/1000 central line days (26% reduction, IR 0.78, 95% CI 0.61 to 0.92, p<0.01); insertion bundle compliance 86.0%; maintenance bundle compliance 90.9%
audits.co: Latin America (5 countries, not individually specified)

audits.t: LEVERAGING THE ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORD TO REDUCE THE RATE OF HOSPITAL ACQUIRED CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE AT AN ACADEMIC SAFETY NET HOSPITAL
audits.tp: C. difficile testing appropriateness and isolation via EMR
audits.st: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services target Standardized Infection Ratio of 1 or less for Hospital Onset C. difficile
audits.f: Standardized Infection Ratio 1.573, above the US national benchmark of 1
audits.c: EMR changes: modified CDI order with test-frequency instructions, automated display of past results, Best Practice Alert for recent laxative use, combined CDI/Contact-Plus-Isolation order panel, and instructions to discontinue isolation on negative results
audits.r2: Test volume decreased 39%; inappropriate repeat testing reduced by 80% (7-day) and 66% (30-day positive); 4-quarter average SIR 0.78, better than the national goal

audits.t: Successfully reducing newborn asphyxia in the labour unit in a large academic medical centre: a quality improvement project using statistical process control.
audits.tp: Newborn asphyxia prevention care bundle compliance
audits.st: Evidence-based care bundles (delivery bundle, oxytocin bundle, vacuum extraction bundle) for prevention of newborn asphyxia
audits.f: Baseline compliance with care bundles and asphyxia rate before the QI project (numbers not reported)
audits.c: Quality improvement project using Model for Improvement and Deming's system of profound knowledge: implementation of three clinical care bundles, improved cardiotocography interpretation skills, QI methods training, and participation in a national learning network
audits.r2: Compliance with all three care bundles improved to 95% or more; percentage of newborns with asphyxia reduced by 48%

audits.t: Implementation of a colour-coded universal protocol safety initiative in Guatemala
audits.tp: Universal protocol/patient identification checklist error rate
audits.st: Locally implemented two-step colour-coded universal protocol (patient identification and documentation checklist)
audits.f: 30/51 patients (58.8%) had at least one documentation or universal-protocol error
audits.c: Colour-coded universal protocol: chart-verification checklist with a blue-hat visual cue after preoperative completion, plus OR checklist confirmation; iteratively modified over three phases
audits.r2: 2/43 patients (4.6%) had any errors; all errors were corrected prior to surgery with no adverse outcomes

audits.t: Standardisation of perioperative urinary catheter use to reduce postsurgical urinary tract infection: an interrupted time series study
audits.tp: Perioperative urinary catheter use to reduce UTI
audits.st: ACS NSQIP postsurgical UTI outcome measure; locally standardised urinary catheter insertion/removal criteria
audits.f: 22.5% of patients catheterised for surgery; 0% removed in the operating room; catheter-days per patient-days 17.4%; postsurgical UTI 2.5% (95% CI 2.0% to 3.1%)
audits.c: Standardised perioperative catheter approach: standard insertion criteria, sterile-technique insertion training, and nurse-initiated medical directive for removal in the OR and on the surgical unit
audits.r2: OR catheter removal rose to 12.2%-30.0%; catheter insertion sustained below baseline (8.4%-15.6%); catheter-days per patient-days fell to 8.3%; postsurgical UTI fell to 1.4% (95% CI 1.1% to 1.9%, p=0.002)

audits.t: Standardising hospitalist practice in sepsis and COPD care
audits.tp: Hospitalist standardisation via simulated-patient audit and feedback
audits.st: Sepsis 3-hour bundle; evidence-based practice measured via the Clinical Performance and Value (CPV) simulated-patient tool
audits.f: Baseline CPV scores not stated numerically; simulated-patient vignettes (COPD and sepsis) used with feedback and group discussion at each round
audits.c: Simulated-patient engagement rounds with individual feedback and group discussion, using the Clinical Performance and Value (CPV) tool
audits.r2: Evidence-based practice improved +13.7 points (p<0.001); variation reduced -1.4 points (p=0.018); correct sepsis diagnosis +19.1 points (p=0.004) and COPD +22.7 points (p=0.001); sepsis 3-hour bundle adherence +33.7 points (p=0.010); correct COPD admission level +26.0 points (p=0.042); $5 million system-wide savings

audits.t: Major reductions in unnecessary aspartate aminotransferase and blood urea nitrogen tests with a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Choosing Wisely; internal target AST/ALT and BUN/Cr ratio <5%
audits.f: AST/ALT ratio 0.37, BUN/Cr ratio 0.57; tests per 100 hospital days: 20 AST
audits.c: Guidelines for appropriate AST/BUN test indications, audit and feedback education, removal of AST and BUN from institutional order sets
audits.r2: AST/ALT ratio decreased to 0.14, BUN/Cr ratio to 0.14; tests per 100 hospital days fell to 7 AST; target of 0.05 not achieved

audits.t: Altering standard admission order sets to promote clinical laboratory stewardship: a cohort quality improvement study
audits.tp: Laboratory test overuse (TSH order set) reduction
audits.st: Local clinical indication criteria for TSH testing (order labelled 'inappropriate' if no clinical indication or repeated within 6 weeks)
audits.f: 60.6% (66/109) of orders were inappropriate
audits.c: Removal of the TSH checkbox from the CCU admission order set

audits.t: Improving rates of ferrous sulfate prescription for suspected iron deficiency anaemia in infants
audits.tp: Iron deficiency anaemia treatment (ferrous sulfate prescribing) in infants
audits.st: Local target: ferrous sulfate prescription rate of 75% or greater for suspected IDA in infants aged 8-13 months within 24 months
audits.f: Prescription rate 41%; screening rate 89%; haemoglobin recheck within 6 months in 41% of anaemic patients; 20% normalised haemoglobin by 6 months
audits.c: Clinical pathway with screening/treatment recommendations, multiple PDSA cycles including provider education, targeted reminders when ferrous sulfate not prescribed, and standardised procedures for abnormal labs
audits.r2: Prescription rate rose to 78%; screening rate remained 89%; haemoglobin recheck rose to 56% (p<0.001); 30% normalised haemoglobin by 6 months (p<0.05)

audits.t: Reducing door-to-needle times in stroke thrombolysis to 13 min through protocol revision and simulation training: a quality improvement project in a Norwegian stroke centre
audits.st: Local revised treatment protocol target (improving on a sustained under-30-minute baseline)
audits.f: Median door-to-needle time 27 minutes (baseline already under 30 minutes and sustained)
audits.c: Revised treatment protocol plus in situ simulation-based team training (14 sessions February-June 2017; 12 further sessions November 2017-March 2018)
audits.r2: Median door-to-needle time reduced to 13 minutes and remained consistent after 13 months; reduced proportion deceased or bedridden at 90 days

audits.t: Novel quality improvement method to reduce cost while improving the quality of patient care: retrospective observational study
audits.tp: Cost per patient quality improvement (continuous value management)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Initial average cost per patient admitted £807.70 (Oct 2016–May 2018 pilot, 18 months)
audits.c: Continuous value management (CVM): standard care model, weekly 'box score' performance tracking, visual management board, QI methods to reduce/repurpose resources
audits.r2: Cost per patient reduced 21.8% to £631.50 (p<0.0001); agency nursing spend down 30.8%; patients admitted per week up 28.9%

audits.t: Assessment of a quality improvement intervention to decrease opioid prescribing in a regional health system.
audits.st: Procedure-specific opioid prescribing guidelines
audits.f: Before intervention, prescription size was decreasing over time (slope -0.7 tablets of 5mg oxycodone/month, 95% CI -1.0 to -0.5)
audits.c: Three iterations of procedure-specific postoperative opioid prescribing guidelines released across a regional surgical collaborative
audits.r2: Statewide postoperative opioid prescribing reduced by 50% while providing satisfactory pain care

audits.t: Adherence to guideline-recommended HbA1c testing frequency and better outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes: a 5-year retrospective cohort study in Australian general practice
audits.tp: HbA1c testing frequency adherence and outcomes in type 2 diabetes
audits.st: Australian guidelines recommending 6-monthly HbA1c testing (3-monthly if inadequate control)
audits.f: Overall median HbA1c testing frequency was 1.6 tests per year, with an overall adherence rate of 50%; high adherence was associated with lower risk of chronic kidney disease (OR 0.42, 95% CI 0.18-0.99) than low adherence; no association found with ischaemic heart disease

audits.t: Virtual learning collaboratives to improve urine culturing and antibiotic prescribing in long-term care: controlled before-and-after study
audits.tp: Reducing unnecessary urine culturing and antibiotic prescribing in long-term care
audits.st: Quality improvement programme to reduce unnecessary urine culturing and antibiotic overprescribing for presumed UTIs
audits.f: Baseline rates of urine culturing and urinary antibiotic prescriptions per 1000 resident days.
audits.c: Virtual learning collaborative sessions (May-August 2018) providing orientation and implementation guidance for a QI programme, compared with propensity-matched controls.
audits.r2: Differential reductions of 19% in urine culturing and 13% in urinary antibiotic prescriptions per 1000 resident days vs matched controls (p<0.0001); no significant change in ED visits, hospital admissions or mortality.

audits.t: Sustainability of paediatric asthma care quality in community hospitals after ending a national quality improvement collaborative
audits.tp: Paediatric asthma care guideline adherence sustainability
audits.st: Paediatric asthma pathway guideline-adherence measures (early bronchodilator via MDI, secondhand-smoke screening, smoking-cessation referral)
audits.f: Guideline adherence improved 29% during the collaborative (vs 15% in hospitals that dropped out, p=0.02); early MDI administration 81%
audits.c: National Pathways for Improving Paediatric Asthma Care (PIPA) QI collaborative; access to pathways, education, mobile app and mentorship continued after the collaborative ended, but active coaching stopped
audits.r2: Early MDI administration fell from 81% to 68% (adjusted OR 0.26, 95% CI 0.15 to 0.42); smoking-cessation referral rate declined (adjusted OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.75 to 0.98); no significant change in length of stay or secondhand-smoke screening

audits.t: Examining the effect of quality improvement initiatives on decreasing racial disparities in maternal morbidity
audits.tp: Racial disparities in severe maternal morbidity from haemorrhage
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Statistically significant disparity in severe maternal morbidity from haemorrhage between Black and White women (p<0.001); rate in Black women 45.5%
audits.c: Stratification of monitoring data by race/ethnicity presented as run charts at monthly meetings, an obstetric haemorrhage patient-safety bundle, and health-equity-focused case reviews of adverse outcomes
audits.r2: Disparity no longer statistically significant (p=0.138); rate in Black women fell to 31.6% (p=0.011)

audits.t: Repurposing the Ordering of Routine Laboratory Tests in Hospitalised Medical Patients (RePORT): results of a cluster randomised stepped-wedge quality improvement study
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline routine laboratory test ordering rate used as the reference for the reported incidence rate ratio
audits.c: Educational tools and social comparison reports with peer-facilitated discussion sessions, implemented via a stepped-wedge design across 8 units
audits.r2: 14% reduction in routine test ordering (incidence rate ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.79 to 0.92); 14% reduction in testing costs; $C1.15 per patient-day savings; 20% increase in routine-test-free patient-days

audits.t: Variation in the use of primary care-led investigations prior to a cancer diagnosis: analysis of the National Cancer Diagnosis Audit
audits.tp: Variation in primary care investigations before cancer diagnosis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Odds ratio for 97.5th to 2.5th centile practice variation: 4.02 (any investigation), 4.33 (blood test), 3.12 (imaging); after accounting for patient case-mix, the spread increased to 5.61, 6.30 and 3.60 respectively

audits.t: Implementation of national guidelines on antenatal magnesium sulfate for neonatal neuroprotection: extended evaluation of the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of the National PReCePT Programme in England
audits.tp: Antenatal magnesium sulfate for neonatal neuroprotection uptake
audits.st: NICE guidelines (2015): antenatal magnesium sulfate for mothers in preterm labour under 30 weeks gestation
audits.f: MgSO4 administration rate was 65.8% in England
audits.c: National PReCePT quality improvement programme rolled out across England from 2018
audits.r2: MgSO4 administration rate rose to 85.5%; PReCePT was associated with a 5.8 percentage point improvement (95% CI 2.69-8.86, p<0.001), and 8.67 percentage points for births under 34 weeks (95% CI 6.38-10.96, p<0.001); net monetary benefit of GBP597,000 with 89% probability of cost-effectiveness

audits.t: Socioeconomic inequalities in adherence to clinical practice guidelines and breast cancer survival: a multicentre population-based study in Spain
audits.tp: Socioeconomic inequalities in adherence to breast cancer guidelines
audits.st: European and Spanish clinical practice guidelines for breast cancer diagnosis and treatment (16 indicators)
audits.f: No differences in type of treatment received, but women in lowest SES areas were less likely to undergo sentinel lymph node biopsy, reconstruction after mastectomy, surgery within 30 days of diagnosis, and adjuvant treatment within 6 weeks after surgery; higher risk of death in lower SES areas (HR=1.57, 95% CI 1.04-2.36), attenuated after accounting for guideline adherence.

audits.t: Association between Child Opportunity Index and paediatric sepsis recognition and treatment in a large quality improvement collaborative: a retrospective cohort study
audits.tp: Paediatric sepsis recognition and bundle compliance (equity)
audits.st: IPSO recommended sepsis care bundle (standardised recognition, fluid bolus under 1 hour, antibiotic under 3 hours)
audits.f: Patients in the Very High Child Opportunity Index (COI) quintile were most likely to be identified via standardised recognition protocols (67.7%) and to receive the recommended care bundle (46%)
audits.c: Improving Pediatric Sepsis Outcomes (IPSO) quality improvement collaborative, using standardisation and shared learning
audits.r2: Standardised sepsis recognition improved for all COI quintiles over time; the greatest improvement was among the Very Low COI quintile

audits.t: Implementing and evaluating a low-carbon, high-quality perioperative patient warming pathway
audits.tp: Perioperative patient warming pathway (environmental and quality)
audits.st: Best-practice environmental warming guidelines, adapted locally
audits.f: Flannel blanket use averaged 6 per patient; active warming 55% preoperatively and 0% postoperatively; hypothermia incidence 18%
audits.c: Optimised patient warming pathway: expanded pre-warming criteria, preserved forced-air-warming Flex Gown, staff education and training, behaviourally informed strategies, gamification and policy development, over nine PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Flannel blanket use fell to an average of 3 per patient (p<0.01); active warming rose to 80% preoperatively (p=0.04) and 55% postoperatively (p<0.01); hypothermia 15% (p=0.77, not significant)

audits.t: When documentation changes but behaviour persists: de-implementation in a neonatal intensive care unit
audits.tp: De-implementation of routine gastric residual checks in NICU
audits.st: Local de-implementation protocol eliminating routine gastric residual checks in infants under 1500g birth weight
audits.f: Routine gastric residual checks were standard practice prior to the initiative (baseline rate not quantified)
audits.c: Multifaceted de-implementation: education, electronic medical record workflow modification, and reinforcement of symptom-based feeding assessment
audits.r2: Documented gastric residual checks declined to zero, with no increase in necrotising enterocolitis or feeding intolerance and no improvement in time to full enteral feeds; 7/24 (29%) nurses reported continuing checks without documentation

audits.t: Inequality in quality? Regional and educational differences in treatment with fluoroquinolone in urinary tract infection of 236 376 Swedish patients
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing variation (fluoroquinolone use in UTI)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Fluoroquinolone prescription rate varied from 17.1% to 29.5% across 21 Swedish regions; middle-aged women with 15+ years of schooling more often prescribed fluoroquinolones (OR 1.28, 95% CI 1.23 to 1.34)

audits.t: Evaluation of a preoperative team briefing: a new communication routine results in improved clinical practice
audits.st: Accepted treatment guidelines for timing of preoperative antibiotic prophylaxis
audits.f: Antibiotic prophylaxis on time in 77.6% of cases
audits.r2: Antibiotic prophylaxis on time in 87.6% of cases (p<0.01)

audits.t: Elimination of central-venous-catheter-related bloodstream infections from the intensive care unit
audits.tp: Central venous catheter-related bloodstream infection reduction
audits.st: Evidence-based CVC insertion/maintenance care bundles; Scottish Patient Safety Programme
audits.f: Annual CRBSI rate 3.4 per 1000 patient days
audits.c: Infection surveillance plus care-process bundles for CVC insertion and maintenance, supported by educational interventions and statistical process control feedback
audits.r2: CRBSI rate fell to 0 per 1000 patient days, with zero episodes in the final 19 months

audits.t: Addressing the sociotechnical drivers of quality improvement: a case study of post-operative DVT prophylaxis computerised decision support.
audits.st: Institutional deep venous thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis recommendations
audits.f: Performance compliance with DVT prophylaxis was 77% pre-implementation; initial computerised decision support menu use rate was only 20%
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team developed and implemented electronic order menus with DVT prophylaxis recommendations, refining the intervention using the sociotechnical 'Fit between Individuals, Task and Technology' (FITT) framework to identify and address barriers (workflow styles, guideline validity concerns, cycle times, risk ambiguity)

audits.t: Quality of after-hours primary care in the Netherlands: adherence to national guidelines
audits.st: National guidelines for after-hours prescribing of pain medication and antibiotics, emergency case performance, and specialist referral
audits.f: Average guideline adherence 77%; referrals 92%, pain medication prescribing 90%, antibiotic prescribing 69%, emergency treatment 71%; antibiotics overprescribed in 42% and underprescribed in 21% of cases

audits.t: Effectiveness of collaborative improvement: evidence from 27 applications in 12 less-developed and middle-income countries
audits.tp: Improvement collaborative effectiveness across low- and middle-income countries
audits.st: Locally set compliance standards/indicators for maternal, newborn and child health, HIV/AIDS, family planning, malaria and tuberculosis
audits.f: Baseline performance was below 50% in two-thirds of charts
audits.c: USAID-funded improvement collaborative approach (1998-2008), adapted for resource-constrained settings
audits.r2: 87% of charts reached 80% or higher performance and 76% reached at least 90%; average increase 51.9 percentage points (SE 28.0); average time to reach 80% performance was 9.2 months and to 90% was 14.4 months; performance sustained for an average of 13 months (69% of observed months)
audits.co: 12 low- and middle-income countries (not individually specified)

audits.t: Student-observed surgical safety practices across an urban regional health authority: Table 1
audits.tp: Surgical safety practice adherence to WHO checklist (student observation)
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (2007)
audits.f: Student-observed adherence to WHO-mandated practices 75%-86%, although no formal checklist was used; 5 errors with potential for injury were observed

audits.t: The introduction of a surgical safety checklist in a tertiary referral obstetric centre
audits.tp: Surgical safety checklist compliance in obstetric theatres
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist
audits.f: Compliance with pre- and postoperative checks 61.2% and 67.6% respectively
audits.c: Introduction of a surgical safety checklist for elective cases in obstetric theatres
audits.r2: Compliance improved to 79.7% (preoperative) and 84.7% (postoperative); 69.6% of staff felt interprofessional communication had improved

audits.t: Rebound in ventilator-associated pneumonia rates during a prevention checklist washout period
audits.st: Ventilator-associated pneumonia prevention bundle (head-of-bed elevation, oral care, suctioning device management, ventilator tubing care, standard infection-control precautions)
audits.f: Bundle compliance rose from under 50% to over 75%; VAP rate fell from 4.2 to 0.7 per 1000 ventilator days (p<0.059)
audits.c: VAP prevention checklist, later incorporated into nursing and respiratory-care bedside flowsheets for sustainability
audits.r2: VAP rate rose to 4.8 per 1000 ventilator days during washout (p<0.042); rate dropped to 0.8 per 1000 ventilator days in the flowsheet phase (p<0.047)

audits.t: Comparison of postal and non-postal post-vasectomy semen sample submission strategies on compliance and failures: an 11-year analysis of the audit database of the Association of Surgeons in Primary Care of the UK
audits.st: Post-vasectomy semen analysis (PVSA) required to confirm clearance before stopping other contraception; one-test/two-test clearance guidance
audits.f: Compliance with postal strategy 79.5% vs non-postal 59.1% (difference 20.4%, 95% CI 19.7-21.2%); early failure detection 0.73% postal vs 0.94% non-postal

audits.t: Carriers of haemophilia a and B – a 5 year retrospective audit of management in pregnancy in the setting of a tertiary referral clinic
audits.st: Local delivery care plan guidance (regional anaesthesia, judicious fetal blood sampling/forceps use, cord bloods, oral vitamin K)
audits.f: 15 of 20 women had delivery care plans written at 36 weeks; postpartum haemorrhage advice included in 5 (28%) plans; of 16 delivered at the centre, 12 (75%) had normal vaginal deliveries, 1 mid-cavity forceps and 3 emergency LSCS; 3 of 15 (20%) male babies were affected, with no neonatal morbidity

audits.t: Obstetric cholestasis – an audit on its management and complications in Leeds
audits.st: Current guidelines for obstetric cholestasis management (not further specified)
audits.f: 95% monitored by fetal ultrasound and 47% by CTG antenatally; labour induced in 72%; 22% preterm deliveries; fetal distress in 30% of cases

audits.t: An audit of the care and outcome of pregnancies complicated by diabetes at the Leeds teaching hospitals NHS trust
audits.tp: Diabetic pregnancy antenatal care and outcomes
audits.st: NICE guideline 'Diabetes in Pregnancy'
audits.f: Pre-conception clinic attendance 37% (type 1) and 14% (type 2); recommended folic acid dose in 88% of attenders vs 40% of non-attenders; 77% of gestational and 44% of pre-existing diabetics delivered at 38 weeks or later; caesarean rate over 80% in type 2 diabetes; pre-eclampsia in 20%

audits.t: Impact of recent changes in protocol on the management of anaemia in pregnancy in NHS Tayside: a retrospective audit
audits.st: Local protocol: routine haemoglobin check at 28 weeks and more aggressive oral/intravenous iron treatment
audits.f: 35.6% had haemoglobin under 11g% at 28 weeks; 225 units of packed red cells used
audits.c: Introduction of a routine haemoglobin check at 28 weeks and more aggressive oral and intravenous iron preparation
audits.r2: 23% had haemoglobin under 11g% at 28 weeks; packed red cell use fell to 179 units despite increased deliveries and complications; only 2 of 10 significant postpartum haemorrhages required transfusion

audits.t: Implementing change through clinical audit cycle to improve care of obese pregnant women: a reality!
audits.tp: Maternal obesity in pregnancy care pathway
audits.st: Locally developed care pathway for management of maternal obesity in pregnancy
audits.f: Counselling on implications of obesity given to 5% of women; glucose tolerance test offer/uptake 88%
audits.c: New guidelines, an evidence-based care pathway, supportive information leaflets, and dedicated antenatal anaesthetic review clinics for BMI 40 or above
audits.r2: 100% compliance with height/weight/BMI documentation; counselling uptake rose to 14%; appropriate care pathway planning 100%; hospital birth appropriately planned in 92%; consultant antenatal review in 77%; glucose tolerance test offer/uptake rose to 93%; anaesthetic review referral/uptake 94%/81%; active 3rd-stage management 100%

audits.t: A retrospective audit on the management of trauma in pregnancy
audits.st: Trust-guideline-based proforma for abdominal trauma in pregnancy
audits.f: 85% (41/48) presented following a fall; 11/48 had significant complications; 83% (40/48) had no documentation of bruising inspection; Kleihauer-Betke test performed in only 33% (16/48); 75% (36/48) were discharged the same day without the minimum 4 hours of continuous CTG required

audits.t: Audit on postnatal venous thromboembolism risk assessment
audits.st: RCOG guideline and hospital guideline for VTE risk assessment
audits.f: 78% had a risk assessment done, of which 73% were assessed correctly; 3% had the wrong Clexane dose and 8% the wrong duration; assessment was missed in 1 of 4 morbidly obese patients and 3 of 28 emergency LSCS patients

audits.t: Audit of blood sugar management in diabetic pregnancies
audits.tp: Blood sugar management in diabetic pregnancy (steroid administration)
audits.st: Local guideline for management of women with type 1 and type 2 diabetes
audits.f: Sliding scale managed per protocol in 90% of cases; postnatal plan documentation and pre/post-meal blood sugar monitoring were lacking in about half of women

audits.t: Sickle cell disease and pregnancy – a 5 year audit of cases managed at a tertiary referral unit within the north west
audits.st: Trust guidelines (established ahead of RCOG recommendations); multidisciplinary team management recommended by RCOG
audits.f: Management was audited against trust guidelines established ahead of RCOG guidance; outcome data were reported but not further quantified in the abstract

audits.t: Audit of massive obstetric haemorrhage in southmead hospital using modified Scottish confidential audit of severe maternal morbidity (SCASMM) data collection tool: Nov 2010 – OCT 2011: Abstract PL.31 Table
audits.st: Departmental guideline; modified Scottish Confidential Audit of Severe Maternal Morbidity (SCASMM) data collection tool; compared with the 2009 Scottish national audit
audits.f: Rate comparable to the Scottish national audit (4.61 vs 5.18 per 1000 for over 2500mL); consultant presence 72% for over 2000mL cases (Nov 2010-Apr 2011 subperiod)
audits.c: Introduction of a proforma (November 2010), presentation at 6-monthly departmental meetings, and improved awareness and accountability
audits.r2: Consultant presence rose to 84% (over 2000mL) and 100% (over 2500mL); proforma use rose from 65% to 80%; blood used in major haemorrhage packs reduced from 6 to 4 units

audits.t: An audit exploring the effectiveness and sustainability of a protocol aimed at increased rates of vaginal birth after caesarean section (VBAC)
audits.tp: Vaginal birth after caesarean (VBAC) rate protocol
audits.st: Locally introduced protocol and ethos change encouraging VBAC
audits.f: 46% of eligible patients attempted VBAC
audits.c: New protocol and ethos change actively encouraging VBAC as a positive choice after a single previous caesarean
audits.r2: VBAC attempt rate rose to 59% (94/159) at 6 months and 60% (95/159) at 2.5 years

audits.t: The management of moderate pph: an audit from the royal infirmary Edinburgh
audits.st: Local postpartum haemorrhage management protocol
audits.f: Syntocinon/syntometrine used in 99.7% of cases, oxytocin infusion in 66%, ergometrine in 23%, carboprost in 23%; manual removal of placenta in 11%; only 50% of patients observed in HDU postnatally

audits.t: A prospective audit of decision to delivery interval among women having emergency caesarean section
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Grade I median decision-to-delivery interval 33 minutes (spinal) and 23 minutes (epidural top-up); Grade II median 50 minutes (spinal) and 45 minutes (epidural top-up); low cord pH in 11.1% (grade I) and 6.9% (grade II)

audits.t: Audit of the management of obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASIS) ASIS at Guy's and St Thomas' hospital
audits.st: Agreed local standards of OASIS management
audits.f: Standards for repair in theatre, regional/general anaesthesia, repair by accredited personnel, PDS suture to sphincter muscle, PR examination, antibiotics and laxative prescribing all scored over 90% compliance; follow-up with link consultant 73.2% and pelvic floor clinic follow-up 80.3%

audits.t: Obstetric anal sphincter injury audit at Borders general hospital (2004-2009)
audits.tp: Obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) incidence and management
audits.st: RCOG guideline for OASI management
audits.f: Incidence 2.6% as at 2009; management was overall compliant with RCOG guideline standards, but a significant number of repairs were performed under local anaesthesia in the room, not in keeping with RCOG guidance

audits.t: Aspiration prophylaxis in labour – room for improvement?
audits.tp: Aspiration prophylaxis in high-risk labouring women
audits.st: Local guideline: dietary restriction and ranitidine 150mg orally every 6 hours for high-risk labouring women
audits.f: 8/34 (23%) received ranitidine and 20/34 (58%) had dietary restriction, indicating poor guideline compliance; of two women who had general anaesthesia, only one had been prescribed acid prophylaxis

audits.t: Audit of diagnosis and management of placenta praevia: Abstract PL.84 Table
audits.st: RCOG Green-top Guideline 27
audits.f: Placental localisation documented at the 20-week scan in 93% (standard 100%); follow-up imaging at 32 weeks in 96% (standard 100%); MRI performed in 2/7 women with previous caesarean; a consultant obstetrician was present in 94% of elective and 50% of emergency deliveries (standard 100%); consent for haemorrhage, transfusion and hysterectomy was 96%, 85% and 73% respectively (standard 100%)

audits.t: Caesarean section audit spiral spanning 6 years of management in 3 major obstetric units of Glasgow
audits.st: NICE and local guidelines for caesarean section
audits.f: Decision-to-delivery time for the most urgent caesareans had a median of 33 minutes (range 20-60); syntocinon use for the third stage 91%; double-layer uterine closure 63%
audits.c: Iterative re-auditing across the 'audit spiral' (November 2006 and January 2011), including introduction of an operative proforma to improve surgical documentation
audits.r2: Decision-to-delivery time fell to a median of 26 minutes (range 20-36); syntocinon use for the third stage rose to 98%; double-layer uterine closure rose to 93%; all women received thromboprophylaxis; 95% of caesareans were under regional anaesthetic; umbilical cord pH performed in 75% of emergency caesareans

audits.t: Third and fourth degree perineal tear audit, NHS Lothian
audits.tp: Third and fourth degree perineal tear incidence and management
audits.st: not reported (compared with a 2008 local audit)
audits.f: Incidence was thought to be rising in the 2008 audit
audits.c: New discharge checklist introduced, and multi-disciplinary education on management, prevention and identification
audits.r2: Incidence 2.8% of deliveries, a statistically significant rise from 2008 (p<0.05); 76% primiparous, 62% following spontaneous vaginal delivery; 98% of repairs performed by an SpR or consultant, 100% in theatre; antibiotic documentation met standards in the main tertiary hospital but needed improvement in the district general hospital; physiotherapy review and incident-reporting documentation also needed improvement

audits.t: Management of idiopathic oligohydramnios- audit of practice
audits.st: Unit policy definition of oligohydramnios (amniotic fluid index below the 5th centile) and management approach
audits.f: 62% had induction of labour, mostly at 37-38 weeks; 1 case of intrapartum CTG abnormality with SCBU admission; no adverse perinatal outcome overall
audits.c: not reported (a new unit guideline was created following this baseline survey)

audits.t: Findings on interval colonoscopies: an auditable performance indicator for colonoscopy quality?
audits.tp: Colonoscopy quality - missed pathology on interval colonoscopy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 19/137 (14%) repeat colonoscopies had new findings including one cancer (234 days after normal colonoscopy); missed polyp rate 9% (13/137); total 5747 colonoscopies performed over study period

audits.t: Quality improvement initiative to reduce adverse effects associated with parenteral nutrition overfeeding
audits.st: Guideline-recommended predictive equations or adjusted body weight for estimating energy requirements
audits.f: Mean maximum total daily kilocalorie dose 30.2 kcal/kg/day
audits.c: Standardised parenteral nutrition products with lower dextrose-to-amino-acid ratios, reduced use of intravenous lipid emulsion, and use of adjusted body weight or guideline-recommended predictive equations for energy needs
audits.r2: Mean maximum kilocalorie dose fell to 23.4 kcal/kg/day (p<0.001); more patients received reduced lipid emulsion in the first week (p<0.001); significantly fewer central-line-associated bloodstream infections, hyperglycaemia and liver dysfunction cases were observed

audits.t: Quality of care in adult patients with inflammatory bowel disease transferring between healthcare providers: multicentre audit
audits.tp: Quality of transfer of care referrals for inflammatory bowel disease
audits.st: an established transfer of care checklist
audits.f: Over half of transfers were due to patient relocation; referral letters were often incomplete; in over 70% of cases the referral letter came from primary care even when a tertiary opinion was sought

audits.t: Lessons from an audit of exclusive enteral nutrition in adult inpatients and outpatients with active Crohn’s disease: a single-centre experience
audits.tp: Exclusive enteral nutrition use in Crohn's disease
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 28/49 completed exclusive enteral nutrition (EEN) and 24 achieved clinical remission/response; 21 withdrew prematurely (15 due to intolerance, 6 due to disease factors); malnutrition halved from 40% to 20%

audits.t: Multimethod study of Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangio Pancreatography (ERCP) service delivery: stakeholder perspectives on opportunities for quality improvement
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 100% organisational survey response rate; 74% individual practitioner survey response rate; many practitioners reported insufficient time allocated for audit/feedback and training; multidisciplinary team meeting arrangements varied

audits.t: UK and Ireland hepatopancreatobiliary (HPB) nursing: an audit of practice
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Discrepancies in current practice for diagnosis and treatment against recommended ESPGHAN-NASPGHAN guidelines: a multicentre audit on Helicobacter pylori infection in children
audits.tp: Helicobacter pylori diagnosis and treatment in children
audits.st: ESPGHAN-NASPGHAN guidelines for diagnosis and management of Helicobacter pylori infection in children
audits.f: 88% of primary treatment and 60% of re-treatment courses deviated from guidance (mainly treatment duration); follow-up stool antigen testing done in only 53% of initial diagnosis cases and 64% of eradication cases, often outside recommended timeframe

audits.t: Who is doing the tap? A multicentre audit and trainee survey exploring barriers to performing diagnostic paracentesis
audits.tp: Time to diagnostic paracentesis in suspected spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
audits.st: National guidance recommending diagnostic paracentesis within 6 hours of presentation for suspected spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
audits.f: Median time to paracentesis 10 hours 51 minutes; no centre met the 6-hour standard

audits.t: 16 Extended vte prophylaxis for all – ensuring correct prescirption after major gi oncological resection
audits.st: NICE CG92 extended post-operative VTE prophylaxis after major GI oncological resection, endorsed by AUGIS, ACPGBI and GBIHPBA
audits.f: Lack of adequate extended post-operative VTE prophylaxis (EVTEP) identified in patients after major GI cancer resection; not reported as a percentage
audits.c: Creation of a Trust-wide EVTEP policy, teaching for junior doctors at induction, and an electronic fail-safe on discharge letters preventing pharmacy sign-off unless EVTEP addressed

audits.t: 20 Improving the documentation of lumbar punctures in children
audits.st: 11 locally identified essential documentation parameters for lumbar puncture (local standard, informed by Australian proforma study)
audits.f: Overall documentation of lumbar puncture 60%; consent documented 33.3% of the time; paired glucose level documented 37.5% of the time
audits.c: Introduction of a novel lumbar puncture proforma with 11 key parameters, promoted with educational sessions and trust-wide e-mails
audits.r2: Overall documentation improved to 75%; consent documentation rose to 86%; paired glucose documentation rose to 100%; a re-audit one year later showed the proforma still used for 65% of lumbar punctures, with better documentation when used

audits.t: 106 Maintaining essential physical health checks in an acute psychiatric hospital
audits.tp: Physical health checks in acute psychiatric admission
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists (RCPsych) integrated physical health guidelines: ECG within 48 hours of admission
audits.f: Only 33% of patients had an ECG performed within 48 hours of admission
audits.c: Introduction of a three-times-weekly 'Physical Health Board Round' on three wards
audits.r2: ECGs performed within 48 hours in 45 cases and not in 68 cases (compliance 45/90=50%, excluding those who declined, n=23)

audits.t: 91 Nil by mouth means what? Putting evidence into practice, a prospective pre-operative fasting audit
audits.st: Local pre-operative fasting policy (6 hours solids, 2 hours liquids)
audits.f: Mean fasting time for solids 20 hours (standard 6 hours) and for liquids 8 hours (standard 2 hours); 23% encouraged to drink until 2 hours before surgery; 21% given pre-operative advice on chewing gum/smoking, of whom only one received correct advice
audits.c: Training for frontline healthcare professionals, an information poster for wards, correction of incorrect information on the trust patient advice leaflet, and a change in fluid fasting policy to 1 hour for elective assessment unit admissions

audits.t: 53 Audited quality improvement project on oxygen prescribing on an acute surgical ward
audits.st: British Thoracic Society guidelines on oxygen prescribing (target saturations must be stipulated)
audits.f: Target saturations documented 13.6%; route of administration 15.9%; timing of oxygen delivery 11.4%; signature and dating of prescription 15.9%
audits.c: Teaching sessions for junior and senior doctors and allied prescribers on oxygen prescribing importance and documentation
audits.r2: Target saturations documentation improved to 42.2%; route of administration to 28.9%; timing to 24.4%; signature and dating to 40%

audits.t: 102 Implementing positive change to the prescribing system on the renal ward in Ninewells Hospital
audits.st: World Health Organisation Patient Safety Challenge; local aim to reduce drug chart errors by 50%
audits.f: 86% of drug charts contained errors in week one; 100% and 50% in weeks two and three respectively
audits.c: Introduction of vancomycin and gentamicin stickers for the ward prescription chart to highlight antibiotics given on dialysis, with staff informed via departmental meeting
audits.r2: Week one showed no errors; weeks two and three showed 20% and 60% of charts with mistakes respectively; overall 66% decrease in drug chart errors

audits.t: 20 Improving oxygen prescribing practices at an acute tertiary care hospital
audits.st: British Thoracic Society 2015 National Oxygen Prescribing Audit standards: 95% valid drug chart prescription, 100% target saturation range specified, 100% saturations documented with sufficient frequency for NEWS score, 90% actual SpO2 within target range
audits.f: Significant proportions of patients at risk of hypercapnia; inadequacies in prescribing, monitoring and documentation of oxygen
audits.c: PDSA Cycle 1: introduction of NEWS2 scale and redesigned drug charts with tick-boxes for target saturations; PDSA Cycle 2: mandatory junior doctor teaching, 'Oxygen Safety' posters, handover reminders
audits.r2: All patients with valid oxygen prescriptions had a specified target range; all patients had actual saturations within target range; 99% had saturations documented with sufficient frequency for NEWS score; 14% of patients still used oxygen without valid prescriptions

audits.t: 7 Improving the documentation of risk assessments and discharge advice in anti-coagulated patients with head injuries and normal imaginghead injuries & anticoagulation
audits.tp: Head injury anticoagulation risk assessment documentation
audits.st: Local Trust guideline on documenting risk assessment and discharge advice for anticoagulated patients with head injury and normal CT
audits.f: 37% of encounters had documentation of both risk assessment and discharge advice; 51% documented neither
audits.c: Amendment to Trust head injury leaflet and CT Head Form Requests to include an anticoagulation section, structured teaching, e-mailing policy to A&E staff, Staff Bulletin/Intranet entries, induction of new joiners, weekly safety message
audits.r2: 44% of encounters had documentation of both; only 28% documented neither

audits.t: 77 Improving the initial inpatient blood investigation of COVID-19 patients at the Hillingdon hospitals NHS foundation trust: a quality improvement project
audits.st: Trust guidelines for initial blood investigation of COVID-19 inpatients
audits.f: FBC, U&E, CRP, LFT adherence 99.7%, 99.2%, 98.7%, 96.6% respectively; coagulation screen adherence 72.8%; D-dimer appropriately requested 19.9%; inappropriate troponin requisition 38.9%
audits.c: Results presented locally and a COVID-19 panel added to the electronic order-request system with prompts for appropriate investigations
audits.r2: FBC, U&E, CRP, LFT adherence increased to 100%; coagulation screen adherence increased to 90%; D-dimer requesting increased to 50%; inappropriate troponin requisition decreased to 26.3%

audits.t: 80 Education of antimicrobial stewardship: teaching methods and their effectiveness
audits.st: National guidance (WHO/NICE) on safe antimicrobial prescribing
audits.f: Poor compliance with national guidance on safe antimicrobial prescribing (no numbers reported)
audits.c: First: posters on correct antibiotic prescribing procedure in key clinical areas; second: four-week teaching programme developed with microbiology department
