audits.r2: Minor, non-significant improvement after posters; clear improvement in compliance after the teaching programme (no numbers reported)

audits.t: 83 Assess the rate of VTE assessments in the emergency decisions unit (EDU) completed in line with NICE guidance & trust policy
audits.st: NICE guideline 89 on reducing the risk of hospital-acquired VTE, and trust policy

audits.t: 215 Audit of staff attitudes to influenza immunisation and the factors which may encourage or prohibit uptake
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 63% of respondents were clinical staff; results informed quality improvements for the following campaign
audits.c: Increased information sessions and additional mobile 'out-of-hours' immunisation clinics
audits.r2: 75% of respondents were clinical staff; 64% of respondents were previously immunised; 35% of respondents were not previously immunised

audits.t: ESRA19-0157 Coagulopathy due to obstetric cholestasis in patients undergoing regional techniques
audits.tp: Coagulation testing in obstetric cholestasis before regional anaesthesia

audits.f: 27 (41%) of patients had coagulation tests done during the antenatal period; 10 patients had tests done within 24 hours of a regional technique

audits.t: P1-S6.09 An audit of management of prenatal syphilis serology in the STI Clinic, Calgary, AB, Canada
audits.st: Canadian national guidelines for prenatal syphilis screening and staging
audits.f: 9 biological false positives; 22 previously adequately treated; 13 late latent cases treated with 7.2 mega-units benzathine penicillin; 4 early latent cases treated with 2.4 mega-units; mean time to first contact 1.8-10.2 days; mean time to first penicillin dose 8.8 days (early latent) and 17.8 days (late latent); 1 case of congenital syphilis in a mother with no prenatal care

audits.t: P5-S3.01 Developing a multi-pronged quality improvement (QI) strategy to increaseChlamydia trachomatis(CT) retesting rates: building a framework for success

audits.t: Re-screeningChlamydia trachomatispositive subjects: a comparison of practices between an STI clinic, general practitioners and gynaecologists

audits.t: Screening tests forChlamydia trachomatisorNeisseria gonorrhoeaeusing the cobas 4800 PCR system do not require a second test to confirm: an audit of patients issued with equivocal results at a sexual health clinic in the Northwest of England, UK
audits.tp: Chlamydia/gonorrhoea PCR equivocal result confirmation testing

audits.t: P29 An audit of HIV partner notification practices in the North East

audits.r2: Capped theatre utilisation improved to 81% (still below the 85% GIRFT target)

audits.t: Thromboprophylaxis in Intensive Care: A Nationwide, Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Evidence-based guidance on appropriate pharmacological thromboprophylaxis prescribing for eligible ICU patients
audits.f: 15% of eligible patients not receiving pharmacoprophylaxis; 10% of ineligible patients had thromboprophylaxis prescribed
audits.c: Pharmacist-delivered daily checks for thromboprophylaxis prescription, prompting of medical staff, local checklists
audits.r2: Rate of eligible patients receiving thromboprophylaxis rose to 96% (p=0.02); mechanoprophylaxis use increased; no prophylaxis fell to 8% (p=0.005); prescription to ineligible patients 14% (p=0.65, not significant change)

audits.t: The Effect of Repeated Audit on the Quality of Transfer of Brain-Injured Patients into a Regional Neurosciences Centre
audits.tp: Quality of transfer of brain-injured patients to regional neurosciences centre
audits.st: Association of Anaesthetists of Great Britain and Ireland (AAGBI) guidelines on inter-hospital transfer
audits.f: Gradual improvement in quality and outcome of transfers across most domains of patient care over successive audit/intervention cycles
audits.c: Three successive interventions implemented between audit rounds
audits.r2: Significant improvement in transfer quality according to AAGBI guidelines across most domains after repeated audit cycles

audits.t: Prophylaxis for postoperative atrial fibrillation: A quality initiative study exploring adherence to NICE guidance in a UK tertiary cardiothoracic intensive care unit.
audits.tp: Postoperative atrial fibrillation prophylaxis adherence to NICE guidance
audits.st: NICE guidance recommending prophylaxis for postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF)
audits.f: 83 (62%) patients were on prophylactic rate control medications prior to surgery; 50 patients (36%) developed POAF, of whom 28 had been on prophylactic medication

audits.t: Improving patient diary use in intensive care: A quality improvement report.
audits.tp: Patient diary use in intensive care
audits.st: Internal QIP target of 100% diary provision for patients admitted over 72 hours to ICU
audits.f: Diary provision at 26.1% baseline
audits.c: Alerts added to the online patient note system, education sessions, and a new guidance document to facilitate diary entry completion (PDSA methodology)

audits.t: Implementing target range oxygen in critical care: A quality improvement pilot study.
audits.tp: Oxygen prescribing and target saturation range
audits.st: Locally agreed oxygen target range prescribing policy
audits.f: 85% of patients had an oxygen prescription with a target range and 85% had an appropriate prescribed target saturation range; 33 staff completed baseline attitude survey
audits.c: Promotion of a structured, agreed oxygen target range prescribing policy
audits.r2: Target range prescribing improved to 95% (chi-square=5.17, p=0.02) and appropriate target range prescribing to 91% (chi-square=1.4, p=0.24); improvement maintained at 96% at 12 months; 29 staff completed follow-up survey

audits.t: Clocks on the intensive care unit: A quality improvement initiative to improve patient orientation
audits.tp: Patient orientation and delirium prevention (ICU clocks)
audits.st: National guidelines recommending visible 24-hour clocks for ICU patients
audits.f: Proportion of patients orientated to time 45% initially
audits.c: Introduction of clocks at each ICU bedspace, then clock repositioning
audits.r2: Orientation improved to 70% post-implementation, then 94% following clock repositioning

audits.t: Lifting the lid: a clinical audit on commode cleaning
audits.st: Evidence-based practice for commode cleaning
audits.f: Commodes not always cleaned after every use; ATP bioluminescence showed 'clean' commodes not always cleaned to a high standard
audits.c: Implementation of audit recommendations: staff education, standardised cleaning procedures

audits.t: Community nurses’ wound audit – a proxy measure for surgical site infections?
audits.tp: Community nurse wound caseload audit as surgical site infection proxy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An audit of cleaning effectiveness using adenosine triphosphate (ATP) bioluminescence assay following outbreaks of infection
audits.tp: Cleaning effectiveness (ATP bioluminescence) after infection outbreaks
audits.st: Previously established benchmark of 100 RLU (relative light units) for ATP bioluminescence
audits.f: 23% of swabs failed to reach 100 RLU benchmark; nurse call bells the most common failure point (40%)
audits.c: Simplification of the cleaning procedure at the Trust

audits.t: Infection prevention and control self-audit: just a tick box exercise?
audits.tp: Infection prevention and control self-audit implementation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Implementation of an infection prevention and control self-audit (IPCSA) project to empower practice staff

audits.t: An audit of neonatal and infant hepatitis B immunisation and serological testing in two counties of England, 2007–12
audits.tp: Neonatal and infant hepatitis B immunisation and serological testing
audits.st: National hepatitis B virus (HBV) immunisation policy for neonates/infants born to HBV-positive mothers
audits.f: HBIG required at birth in 29.9% (County X) and 23.5% (County Y); first dose coverage 92.3-100%; fourth dose coverage 44.4-91.9%; serological testing coverage 8.6-81.0%

audits.t: The misuse and overuse of non-sterile gloves: application of an audit tool to define the problem.
audits.st: Hand hygiene/glove-use audit tool (local observational tool); no external target stated
audits.f: 22 episodes of care observed (35 procedures); 68.6% (24/35) had no contact with blood/body fluid; 54.3% (19/35) glove use was inappropriate; inter-rater reliability 100% for 8/12 components, Kappa 0.72-0.87 for hand hygiene before/after glove removal

audits.t: The effect of a quality improvement programme reducing blood culture contamination on the detection of bloodstream infection in an emergency department.
audits.st: Recommended standard for blood culture contamination rate (target not stated in abstract)
audits.f: 73/1829 (4.0%) blood cultures hospital-wide contaminated; 11.7% contamination in the emergency department vs 2.5% elsewhere
audits.c: Collaborative quality improvement strategy in the ED: education, modified blood culture packs, and regular feedback of blood culture results.
audits.r2: ED contamination reduced to 7.4% (p=0.01); true bloodstream infection detection rate 10.7% vs baseline 12.8% (p=0.35, no significant adverse effect)

audits.t: Factors associated with better alcohol hand rub in 2020. Results from the French national audit "Pulpe'friction".
audits.st: WHO/national 'Pulpe'friction' hand hygiene moments standard
audits.f: Average ABHR compliance: 75% before patient contact, 95% before an invasive technique, 86% after patient contact, 79% after contact with patient surroundings

audits.t: Reducing inappropriate non-sterile glove use in an acute NHS trust: A quality improvement evaluation of the Gloves Off campaign.
audits.tp: Non-sterile glove use and hand hygiene
audits.st: Appropriate non-sterile glove use, targeted by a trust-wide quality improvement campaign (no fixed numeric target stated)
audits.f: Glove use 57.24 per occupied bed day at baseline
audits.c: Multimodal 'Gloves Off' campaign (February 2023 to April 2026): education, policy refinement, visual prompts, and audit feedback, informed by the COM-B behaviour model
audits.r2: Glove use decreased to 49.52 per occupied bed day (difference 7.71, approximately 13.5% reduction), but statistical process control analysis showed common-cause variation with no sustained improvement; mean staff knowledge score 89% (76% scoring >=80%); confidence was high (95.1%) but only 65.9% felt comfortable challenging inappropriate practice

audits.t: BAUS Section of Endourology national Ureteroscopy audit: setting the standards for revalidation
audits.tp: Ureteroscopy practice and outcomes (BAUS national audit)
audits.st: not reported (audit establishing baseline standards for future revalidation)
audits.f: Overall stone free rate 78%; complication rate 4%; peri-operative practices varied in pre-operative imaging, stent usage and treatment modality

audits.t: The impact of relocation of chronic pain service from hospital setting to community centre on patient experience: a single-centre audit.
audits.tp: Patient-reported experience of chronic pain service relocation
audits.st: National NHS Scotland Patient-Reported Experience Measure (PREM) questionnaire for pain services
audits.f: Historical PREM data from Western General Hospital (WGH), a university teaching hospital
audits.c: Relocation of the chronic pain service from a hospital setting (WGH) to a community centre (Leith Community Treatment Centre)
audits.r2: Percentage of patients rating care as 'excellent' significantly greater at the community centre than WGH (p=0.0049); overall patient rating not significantly different, with ratings higher at the community centre; no correlation between deprivation (SIMD16) and PREM

audits.t: Prioritisation of catheterised patients for elective bladder outflow obstruction surgery in the current coronavirus disease 2019 era to reduce catheter-associated morbidity
audits.tp: Waiting times for TURP with catheter prioritisation
audits.st: Local goal of 30 days from waitlisting to operation for catheterised patients
audits.f: 36% of patients catheterised, median wait 119 days (IQR 59-163); catheterised patients had 93 A&E presentations, 13 admissions; median time from catheter insertion to first A&E attendance 20 days (IQR 2-101)
audits.c: Waiting-list form redesigned to include a catheter box, with a goal of 30 days from waitlisting to operation for catheterised patients
audits.r2: 33% catheterised, median waiting-list time fell to 32 days (IQR 22-46); all 11 A&E attendances were from catheterised patients with no admissions; median time from insertion to first A&E attendance 9 days (IQR 4-40); 88% of waiting-list forms had appropriately ticked the catheter box

audits.t: The ‘Emergency Stone Clinic’ – improving patient care: A collaborative, hospital-based quality improvement project
audits.tp: Time to definitive management for ureteric colic (Emergency Stone Clinic)
audits.st: British Association of Urological Surgeons (BAUS) 4-week target from diagnosis to definitive management or clinic review
audits.f: Time from CT diagnosis to clinic review 77 days; only 2.9% seen within 4 weeks of diagnosis; emergency stent insertion 69%
audits.c: Emergency Stone Clinic (ESC) model: weekly consultant-led specialist clinic for early management decisions, developed via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Time from CT diagnosis to clinic review reduced to 9 days; 90.5% seen within 4 weeks; primary intervention rate up to 72.1%; emergency stent insertion reduced to 27.9%; definitive procedure within 4 weeks improved from 26.2% to 51.2% (54.5% during pandemic); A&E re-presentation reduced from 3.0 to 1.6 episodes/month

audits.t: Prescription of blood pressure lowering treatment after intracerebral haemorrhage: Prospective, population-based cohort study
audits.tp: Blood pressure lowering after intracerebral haemorrhage
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 81/130 (62%) were prescribed blood pressure-lowering medication at hospital discharge
audits.c: Quality improvement intervention informed by review of reasons for avoiding BP-lowering medication in a Scottish Stroke Care Audit sample (January-November 2017)
audits.r2: 68/89 (76%) were prescribed blood pressure-lowering medication at discharge (p=0.028 versus the first cohort)

audits.t: Improving the quality of the daily ward round in a Plastic Surgery unit by adapting the SAFE Ward Round Tool of the Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh
audits.st: SAFE Ward Round Tool of the Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh
audits.f: 47% (n=42) completion rate of ward round documentation
audits.c: Introduction of an in-house sticker pro-forma (STAR – Surgical Tool for the Assessment of Rounds), further improved after discussion of results
audits.r2: Re-audit after sticker introduction found completion rose to 70% (n=42); third cycle examining sticker completion alone yielded 88% (n=61)

audits.t: A multicentre UK snapshot audit of symptom burden in patients with indolent systemic mastocytosis utilising the ISM-SAF ©
audits.tp: Symptom burden in indolent systemic mastocytosis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Previous single-centre audit found 36% of patients had TSS >=28 (moderate/severe disease)
audits.r2: Median TSS 31 (range 0-90); 54.5% had TSS >=28 and 34.7% had TSS >=42; 40.5% of patients (vs 36% previously) had TSS >=28 and required 2+ anti-mediator therapies

audits.t: A prospective re-audit of admissions and discharge delays occurring in patients admitted to a district general hospital's respiratory ward in the United Kingdom
audits.st: National Confidential Enquiry into Patient Outcome and Death recommendation that patients be transferred to a ward appropriate to their clinical condition after initial assessment
audits.f: 75 patients had delayed discharge; average delay 8 days (respiratory) and 15 days (non-respiratory)
audits.c: Reduction in respiratory beds from 62 to 46 as recommended by Sarker et al 2010
audits.r2: 14 patients had delayed discharge; average delay 10 days (respiratory) and 11 days (non-respiratory)

audits.t: Making a bronchiolitis pathway work: If at first you don't succeed ...
audits.st: Locally developed 2008 bronchiolitis care pathway aiming to reduce unnecessary investigations and treatments
audits.f: X-rays 37.6%, blood tests 36.1%, blood cultures 27.0%, antibiotics 22.3%, steroids 9.0%; first winter showed no impact from pathway introduction
audits.c: Formal and informal feedback, focused teaching for doctors unfamiliar with the pathway, and monthly data dissemination to staff
audits.r2: X-rays 16.7%, blood tests 15.6%, blood cultures 7.8%, antibiotics 8.6%, steroids 3.7%; median length of stay fell from 3.0 to 2.0 days

audits.t: Safer intercostal drain (ICD) insertions
audits.st: Local standards for safe intercostal drain (ICD) insertion
audits.f: Complication rate 39% (excluding pain)
audits.c: Drain insertion moved to specialised areas (respiratory unit treatment room), strict sterility, ultrasound guidance, insertion sticker checklist, nursing care plan
audits.r2: 87% of insertions performed in respiratory unit; ultrasound guidance documented in only 41.9%; ICD stickers used in 83.9%; nursing care plan used in 77.4%; complication rate (excluding pain) decreased to 12.9%; complications: blocked drain n=2, pneumothorax n=1, surgical emphysema n=1, no complications n=27

audits.t: Are we effectively monitoring and treating vitamin D deficient patients with tuberculosis?
audits.tp: Vitamin D monitoring in tuberculosis patients
audits.st: Local guidelines on vitamin D replacement in TB patients (released after the audit period)
audits.f: 97 patients deficient, 25 insufficient, 2 replete on initial measurement; 30 patients had levels re-checked (mean interval 184 days): initial tests among these showed 7 insufficient, 23 deficient; after supplementation 6 insufficient, 21 deficient, 3 replete; 12 patients had lower vitamin D levels than at diagnosis, 3 unchanged
audits.c: Release of local guidelines on vitamin D replacement (occurred after this cycle)

audits.t: Audit of computed tomography pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) requesting at Hammersmith hospital
audits.tp: CTPA requesting compliance with Wells score/D-dimer
audits.st: NICE diagnostic pathway for suspected pulmonary embolism using Well's score and D-dimer
audits.f: 8 patients diagnosed with PE; only 3 had a Well's score calculated; 49 had a D-dimer; positive PE yield 10.5%
audits.c: Posters detailing Well's score and NICE guidance placed throughout the hospital; results presented at regional meetings
audits.r2: Increased number of Well's scores calculated; no increase in number of PE diagnoses observed

audits.t: Does Wells score documentation really prevent excessive CTPA requests in a teaching hospital? A retrospective study in 800 patients
audits.tp: CTPA requesting compliance with Wells score/D-dimer
audits.st: Local electronic CTPA request protocol requiring clinical details, Wells score and D-dimer (Wells >4 = PE likely, D-dimer not required)
audits.f: Of 747 CTPAs: 1% (7) equivocal, 83% (619) negative, 16% (121) positive; of 108 positive scans with full data, 72% (78) had Wells score >4, 28% (30) had score <=4; excessive CTPA requests made when Wells score criteria not followed
audits.c: Planned training sessions on use of the Wells score (not yet delivered)

audits.t: A new “surgical emergency care bundle power plan” improves physician prescribing compliance for emergency surgical admissions
audits.st: Evidence-based prescribing practice standards for emergency surgical admissions (prescribing essential medications and requesting investigations within 6 hours of decision to admit)
audits.f: Baseline compliance low across domains: VTE prophylaxis 25%, analgesia 60%, antiemetics 28%, gastric protection 44%, antibiotics 68%, IV fluids 72%, laxatives 8%, nutritional supplementation 5%, next-day blood tests 5%
audits.c: Implementation of a structured electronic order set ('surgical emergency care bundle power plan') within Cerner Millennium electronic prescribing system, supported by education and training
audits.r2: Compliance improved: VTE prophylaxis 70%, analgesia 82%, antiemetics 61%, gastric protection 46%, antibiotics 82%, IV fluids 90%, laxatives 60%, nutritional supplementation 70%, next-day blood tests 60%

audits.t: Improving cardiometabolic screening on an inpatient psychiatric ward: a quality improvement project
audits.tp: Cardiometabolic screening on psychiatric inpatient wards
audits.st: Lester Tool: Positive Cardiometabolic Health Resource; target 75% full cardiometabolic screen and 75% intervention rate for abnormalities
audits.f: Baseline 25% full cardiometabolic screen compliance; 0% intervention on identified abnormalities
audits.c: PDSA methodology across 8 cycles: protocol for full screen on admission review, nursing staff engagement, fixing blood transport/delivery inconsistencies, British Heart Foundation leaflets, Lester Tool use, and redesigned discharge summary template for GP communication
audits.r2: 100% compliance with full cardiometabolic screen; 100% intervention rate on identified abnormalities

audits.t: A quality improvement project to improve attendance to the physical health clinic at Southwark team for early psychosis
audits.tp: Physical health clinic attendance in early psychosis
audits.st: National and trust guidance for physical health checks at baseline, 3 months, 6 months and annually
audits.f: Average 27.8% of available clinic slots booked; average 80% of booked slots attended (10 patients booked, 8 attended per 9 weeks)
audits.c: Educational session to the STEP team, a protocol for booking and running the clinic, a physical health questionnaire including Maudsley antipsychotic monitoring guidelines, and a template letter to communicate results to the GP
audits.r2: Slots booked increased to 100%; slots attended reduced to 50% (36 patients booked, 18 attended)

audits.t: Monitoring and investigation of tachycardia in patients receiving clozapine therapy; a quality improvement project
audits.tp: Action on abnormal physical observations in clozapine monitoring
audits.st: Local target to halve rate of retrospective action on abnormal physical observations (e.g. tachycardia) within 4 months
audits.f: Baseline retrospective action needed on 41.2% of patients with abnormal observations, with delays up to 51 days
audits.c: Increased staff awareness during attempted protocol implementation (protocol itself not implemented due to organisational barriers), followed by a poster for the clinical room
audits.r2: Retrospective action reduced to 26.7% after initial awareness raising, then 26.3% after poster (37.5% decrease from baseline overall, sub-target)

audits.t: Physical health assessment quality improvement project
audits.tp: Physical health assessment for severe mental illness
audits.st: NICE guidance / NHS England priority that at least 60% of people with severe mental illness receive NICE-recommended physical assessments and follow-up from 2018/19 onwards
audits.f: 25% of clients had their physical assessment done before the changes
audits.c: Whole-team consultation and buy-in via email and MDT meeting; six weekly 30-minute physical assessment slots added to the timetable, booked by care coordinators; a tracking column added to the team spreadsheet; frequent reminders sent to the team
audits.r2: 63% of clients had their physical assessment done after the changes (three of the 27 clients had only started at the day unit that week)

audits.t: Improving the quality of GP referrals to the Croydon Assessment & Liaison Team
audits.tp: GP referral quality to mental health assessment and liaison team
audits.st: Locally developed criteria for 'good quality' referral (no pre-existing gold standard)
audits.f: 33% of GP referrals deemed good quality at baseline.
audits.c: New GP referral form developed with stakeholder consultation, uploaded to GP DSX electronic referrals platform, GP practices emailed.
audits.r2: Good quality referrals improved to 58% overall; only 32.5% used the new form, but 69% of those on the new form met criteria; no significant change in discussion time (7.7 vs 7.6 minutes).

audits.t: Reducing levels of Violence in the Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) - a multidisciplinary quality improvement project
audits.tp: Reducing violence on a Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit
audits.st: Locally set target: reduce Level 1 violent incidents by 30% by April 2020
audits.f: Considerable variation in weekly Level 1 violent incidents, with a small number of patients contributing to most incidents.
audits.c: Patient interventions (Mutual Respect exercise, Community Meetings), staff interventions (Safety Crosses, Daily Safety Briefings, Broset Violence Checklist), environmental review, PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: Initial 30% reduction goal not met, though staff and patient engagement/confidence improved (e.g. staff safety reports).

audits.t: Quality improvement by introduction of 72-hour admission pathway in Forest House Adolescent Unit (FHAU) for young people in crisis
audits.tp: Crisis admission pathway for adolescents with EUPD
audits.st: NICE 2009 guidelines on borderline personality disorder: acute psychiatric admission only for crises with significant risk, with explicit agreement on length and purpose of admission
audits.f: Longer routine admissions with more serious incidents linked to suicide, prior to the 72-hour crisis pathway
audits.c: Introduction of a 72-hour crisis admission pathway offering assessment, diagnosis, psychoeducation and a safety plan, plus respite, instead of longer admissions
audits.r2: Marked reduction in serious incidents linked to suicide; length of hospital stay reduced to half compared with the previous year; only about 10-15% of patients required readmission in the same year; about 90% of parents gave positive feedback on the intervention

audits.t: Let's get moving! Improving physical activity amongst rehabilitation patients; a quality improvement project
audits.st: National guidance on physical activity levels (specific guideline not named)
audits.f: Baseline weekly activity levels and weights recorded; baseline questionnaire showed limited patient confidence/attitude towards physical activity
audits.c: Co-designed 8-week programme of weekly 30-minute mixed-ability exercise sessions led by the multidisciplinary team, developed and adapted using weekly patient and staff feedback
audits.r2: Minutes of physical activity per week increased for all participants but remained below national guidance; weight reduction did not occur; mean self-rated energy levels increased 153% and mood 98% (mean score increase of 3.8 in both) on pre/post session Likert scales

audits.t: Redesigning community care for safer staff and patient experiences: quality improvement project to improve safety and reduce incidents of violence and aggression in a community mental health team
audits.tp: Violence and aggression reduction in community mental health team
audits.st: Local target of 20% reduction in violent/aggressive incidents over 1 year
audits.f: Staff confidence and safety protocol awareness 40%
audits.c: Multidisciplinary risk meetings, safety huddle tool, staff safety training, co-produced Welcome and Discharge Packs with care pathways
audits.r2: 30% reduction in incidents by December 2020; staff confidence/awareness increased from 40% to 70% by October 2020; 100% of patients in focus groups found Welcome and Discharge Packs helpful

audits.t: Quality improvement project: to improve adherence to DVLA (driving and vehicle liscensing agency) guidance in the tyrone & fermanagh hospital acute inpatients ward
audits.st: DVLA/DVANI (Driver and Vehicle Agency Northern Ireland) guidance for medical practitioners on fitness to drive; local target of 80% adherence
audits.f: Mean baseline completeness of driving advice documentation around 25%
audits.c: Cycle 2: medical staff education and a new driving advice pathway and patient leaflet; Cycle 3: admin staff involvement to add the driving advice pathway into the admission pack; Cycle 4: repeat medical staff education on documenting electronically
audits.r2: Completeness of driving advice increased to over 90%, with clear improvement seen after cycle 3

audits.t: Trust-wide improvement and standardisation of the medical handover
audits.st: Locally agreed quality standards for medical handover; target 80% completion by July 2019
audits.f: 54% Trust-wide completion rate for agreed quality standards; 53% completion for new patient checks.
audits.c: New handover document introduced June 2019, replacing previous format.
audits.r2: Completion rate for quality standards improved to 77% (from 54%); new patient checks improved from 53% to 56%; 82% of doctors agreed/strongly agreed the new handover improved quality.

audits.t: Melatonin prescribing practices and the provision of sleep hygiene/parent-led sleep behavioural Interventions in S-CAMHS, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board (ABUHB)- Service evaluation as part of quality improvement project
audits.tp: Melatonin prescribing and sleep hygiene intervention in CAMHS
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of a sample of 57 (from 115 of 346 patients on pharmacological therapies who were on melatonin), 46 were actively on melatonin; 39/46 (85%) had been on it for more than a year, including 10 for 5 years or more; 35/46 (76%) reported improved sleep or some benefit

audits.t: Antipsychotic Monitoring Within the Home Treatment Team in the Southern Trust, a Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Antipsychotic blood and physical monitoring compliance
audits.st: RCPsych PLAN Home Treatment Accreditation Scheme (HTAS) standards alongside NICE guidelines on antipsychotic monitoring; SMART aim of 100% of patients started on antipsychotics receiving appropriate blood/physical monitoring, documented within 10 days of discharge
audits.f: Baseline completion rates: 14-59% for various baseline bloods, 68-72% for heart rate/blood pressure/weight, 36% for ECGs; documentation of these parameters correct only 9-68% of the time
audits.c: PDSA cycle 1: multidisciplinary team education via presentation on findings and how to fix common documentation mistakes, staff input sought, and guidance posters printed
audits.r2: After PDSA cycle 1: completion rates improved to 55-100% for baseline bloods, 91% for heart rate/blood pressure/weight, 64% for ECGs; documentation improved to 18-73%

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project: Monitoring of Intellectual Disability Patients on Anti-Psychotic Medications in Outpatients Clinic, Northern Health & Social Care Trust, Northern Ireland
audits.tp: Antipsychotic blood and physical monitoring compliance
audits.st: NICE guidelines on physical health monitoring for patients on antipsychotic medication; target of monitoring 90% of patients on antipsychotics
audits.f: Baseline monitoring was essentially zero, as patients were often deemed too difficult in primary care for monitoring
audits.c: Newly established Community Intellectual Disability Team implemented systematic monitoring; two PDSA cycles were run, the second involving acquisition of a new ECG machine and establishing baseline ECG testing, training and analysis
audits.r2: 91% of patients met the target of having antipsychotic bloods monitored (aim 90%); 97% met the target of having physical observations monitored (aim 90%)

audits.t: Outcomes of a Quality Improvement Project to Reduce Unnecessary Blood Tests in Beechcroft Regional Child & Adolescent Mental Health Unit, Belfast Trust
audits.tp: Unnecessary blood test reduction in inpatient mental health
audits.st: Local quality improvement target to reduce baseline blood testing of glucose, lipids and thyroid function tests (TFTs) by 10% by June 2021
audits.f: Baseline fortnightly median of 7 glucose tests and 10 lipid/TFT tests for the unit; an initial scoping exercise found one young person had 40 blood tests during a single admission
audits.c: Six PDSA cycles: separate bloods diary per ward, diary brought into weekly care-planning meetings, education posters in clinical rooms, MDT meeting with Clinical Biochemistry, junior doctor updating the bloods diary post care-planning, and diary use plus new monitoring guidelines added to daily nursing handover
audits.r2: Glucose tests reduced by 68%, to a new fortnightly median of 2.2 (from 7); lipid and TFT median of 10 remained unchanged

audits.t: An Evaluation of Admissions to an Old Age Psychiatry Ward: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Avoidability of psychiatric admissions in older adults
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 14/21 admissions scored 5 (completely unavoidable), 1 scored 4, 1 scored 3, 5 scored 2 on a 1-5 avoidability scale; most common reason was behavioural/psychological symptoms of dementia (n=10)

audits.t: Do We Know if You Drive? a Quality Improvement Project Improving Compliance With DVLA Guidelines
audits.tp: DVLA driving status documentation in self-harm/depression patients
audits.st: DVLA guidance requiring advice and documentation on driving status for depression/anxiety with significant memory/concentration problems, agitation, behavioural disturbance or suicidal thoughts
audits.f: Baseline data collected but documentation rates not separately given for baseline weeks
audits.c: Weekly interventions: email communication highlighting guidance (weeks 1, 3), daily handover discussion of driving status (week 2), DVLA guidance posters in office (week 4), teaching session by occupational therapist (week 12)
audits.r2: Relevant documentation only made in week 1 (10%) and week 4 (20%); no documentation in any other week

audits.t: Nile Ward PICU Violence Reduction Quality Improvement Project - One Year on
audits.tp: Inpatient violence reduction in psychiatric intensive care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 35% reduction in ward violence
audits.c: Improved risk assessment tool, staff photo board, patient feedback board, co-produced mutual expectations, gardening sessions, tailored physical fitness programmes, diversity events, consultant-led daily reviews, cooking sessions, mindfulness meditation, triangle of care
audits.r2: 51% reduction in ward violence; average patient weight gain declined from 4.4 kg to 2.8 kg (a 39% reduction)

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project to Improve GP Referrals to a Rural Psychiatric Team
audits.tp: GP referral quality to community mental health team
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 17.4% of referrals accepted, 13.0% received Single Point of Access (SPOA) assessment, 17.4% rejected, 39.1% re-referred elsewhere, 21.8% no response
audits.c: Structured referral template developed with driver diagrams, via Plan-Do-Study-Act methodology
audits.r2: 28.0% accepted, 36.0% received SPOA assessment (statistically significant improvement, p<0.05), significant reduction in rejection rate; information on presenting complaint rose from 82.1% to 100%, personal history from 39.3% to 92.3%, and aims from 50% to 88% (all p<0.05)

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Project on Improving Electronic Prescribing System in an Adult Mental Health unit
audits.tp: Efficiency of electronic prescribing and medication tasks
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 21.5 hours spent on medication tasks; 10 hours ordering medications (7 of which were ward stock); 12.6 hours re-prescribing; 42% of tasks completed on Mondays
audits.c: Altered ward stocklists, aligned ward timings, and a collective tasks system to reduce duplication
audits.r2: 16 hours spent on medication tasks, a 25.8% reduction in time spent ordering medications; 7.45 hours ordering medications (3.35 hours ward stock); 9.7 hours re-prescribing

audits.t: Sustainable Prescribing in Secure Services – a Quality Improvement Initiative
audits.tp: Sustainable antipsychotic depot and PRN prescribing
audits.st: Department of Health 2021 report on safer, sustainable prescribing in health and justice mental health services
audits.f: 17/26 (65%) depot patients prescribed at longest evidence-based interval; 9/15 (60%) PRN medications prescribed but not in use
audits.c: Medication rationale analysed and discussed with Responsible Clinician over 6 weeks; PRN medication moved to fortnightly review cycle
audits.r2: Unused PRN medications reduced from 9 to 2 patients; 2 depot patients had dose reduced and interval increased

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project: Referral Process for Adults With Suspected ADHD
audits.tp: GP referral quality for suspected adult ADHD
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 89% of referrals explained current difficulties; 52% described resultant impairments; 61% mentioned symptoms present in childhood; 91% contained past medical history/medication; 0% mentioned family history; 6% contained physical health data; 85% of referrals were accepted and 13% rejected, mainly for a missing ADHD self-report scale
audits.c: New referral form and flowchart created for GPs, based on Royal College of Psychiatrists/NICE/ADHD UK guidance

audits.t: Assessment of Cardiovascular Disease Risk in Adults With Severe Mental Illness Admitted to Acute Psychiatric Unit Using QRISK-3 Assessment Tool: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Cardiovascular disease risk assessment in severe mental illness inpatients
audits.st: NICE guidance on CVD risk assessment/management, using the QRISK3 tool (>=10% risk threshold)
audits.f: 30.2% (13/43) had high CVD risk (QRISK3 >=10%); of these, 76.7% were aged 55 or over, 69.2% were current smokers, 23% diabetic and 15.2% hypertensive; 72% of all patients were smokers; mean BMI 23.6, with 41.9% having a BMI of 25 or above

audits.t: Improvement of Ward Referral Quality to the Mental Health Liaison Service (MHLS), Antrim Area Hospital, Northern Ireland
audits.tp: Ward referral quality to Mental Health Liaison Service
audits.st: Locally defined referral content criteria; target 90% of referrals with adequate information
audits.f: Reason for referral 95.07%, reason for admission 92.56%, past psychiatric history 14.88%, prescribed medication 16.53%, investigations 9.92%, substance use history 16.53%; 349 referrals in the comparable prior-year period.
audits.c: Two PDSA cycles: F1 doctor lunchtime teaching (February 2022), poster campaign for nursing staff (December 2022-January 2023), targeted top-ten referring wards.
audits.r2: Reason for referral 96.43%, reason for admission 100%, past psychiatric history 27.91%, prescribed medication 42.86%, investigations 17.86%, substance abuse history 42.86%; referrals fell to 307 in the same period.

audits.t: Development of a Multi-Disciplinary Team Memory Clinic Checklist: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: NICE guideline NG97
audits.f: Version 1 checklist trialled; feedback scored on 5-point Likert scale across five properties.
audits.c: Checklist updated iteratively across PDSA cycles based on Microsoft Forms feedback.
audits.r2: Two PDSA cycles needed to reach Version 3, rated over 4/5 average for all domains; significant improvement in ease of use, time efficiency, environmental friendliness and space availability.

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Project: Improving the Presentation of Assessments Within a Liaison Psychiatry Department
audits.tp: Quality of clinical assessment presentations (SBAR) in liaison psychiatry
audits.st: Adapted SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) communication tool for liaison psychiatry
audits.f: Risk assessment, impression and management plan often missing from presentations; global score >=7 achieved in 41% of presentations.
audits.c: Targeted teaching session on adapted LP SBAR framework with breakout groups.
audits.r2: Improvement in inclusion of key information except management plans; global score >=7 increased from 41% to 57%.

audits.t: Improving Screening and Standardising Interventions for Patients With Above Normal Body Mass Index (BMI) Admitted to a Male Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU): A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: BMI screening and intervention in psychiatric intensive care
audits.st: Local target to increase BMI documentation and standardised interventions for abnormal BMI on PICU admission
audits.f: 47% of PICU patients had their BMI recorded on admission; 69% of those meeting overweight criteria were offered an intervention
audits.c: Two Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles: cycle 1 engaged nursing staff and provided training to fix an electronic form glitch preventing automatic BMI calculation; cycle 2 introduced a protocol for consistent interventions (dietician referral, PICU gym instructor referral, MDT discussion) for abnormal BMI
audits.r2: After cycle 1, 91% of patients had BMI recorded and 71% of those overweight were offered an intervention; after cycle 2, all consenting patients had BMI recorded and 100% of those meeting overweight criteria were offered all protocol interventions, though not all agreed to engage

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project: Increasing the Proportion of Inpatients Being Re-Offered and Receiving Baseline Physical Investigations
audits.tp: Baseline physical health investigations (bloods and ECG) on psychiatric admission
audits.st: Trust standard: comprehensive mental and physical health assessment including ECG and routine bloods within 4 hours of admission
audits.f: 85.14% did not receive admission bloods and 83.79% did not receive an admission ECG; before the tracking list, 55.77% had baseline bloods (admission or reoffer) and 78.85% had a baseline ECG
audits.c: A tracking list of patients not receiving admission investigations, reviewed weekly at ward rounds to prompt re-offering
audits.r2: 97.5% of patients without admission bloods were reoffered (up from 90%); 85.14% of all patients had baseline bloods after 4 weeks; 95% without an ECG were reoffered (up from 85.72%); 86.49% of all patients had a baseline ECG after 4 weeks

audits.t: Improving Clozapine Prescribing at a London District General Hospital: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Clozapine prescribing/dose compliance in a general hospital
audits.st: not reported (safe clozapine prescribing practice)
audits.f: 67.4% of admissions inappropriately missed at least one clozapine dose; 40.8% of patients referred to the liaison team.
audits.c: Hospital guideline, automatic email to liaison team on clozapine prescription, online prescribing system alert, clinician teaching (from July 2022).
audits.r2: Missed dose rate fell from 67.4% to 31.1%; referral rate to liaison team rose from 40.8% to 89.2%.

audits.t: Effective Induction Programme for Higher Specialist Trainees: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Induction programme for Higher Specialist Trainees
audits.st: GMC induction standards (GMC Report 2020)
audits.f: Response rate 50%; Domain A (access to systems) 27%; Domain B (physical orientation) 45%; Domain C (day-to-day knowledge) 9%; Domain D (understanding expectations) 9%.
audits.c: Co-produced dedicated HST induction programme and updated induction booklet, implemented August 2023.
audits.r2: Response rate 64%; Domain A improved to 88% (p<0.001); Domain B to 88% (p<0.018); Domain C to 19% (not significant, p<0.48); Domain D to 69% (p<0.002).

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project on the Use of Clinical Global Impression (CGI) Scores in a Female Adult Inpatient Mental Health Ward
audits.tp: Use of Clinical Global Impression (CGI) scores in inpatient psychiatry
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 80% had admission CGI-S recorded (mean 2.77); 71% had discharge CGI-S recorded (mean 1.79); 58% had both recorded; mean reduction in CGI-S of 1.09; admission CGI-S significantly correlated with length of stay (p=0.016).

audits.t: Improving Carers’ Engagement for Patients Admitted to Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU): A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Carers' engagement for patients admitted to PICU
audits.st: National Association of PICUs and Royal College of Psychiatrists PICU guidance on carer engagement
audits.f: Baseline: 29% had carers' details documented; 42% contacted within 24 hours; 50% had carer views in care plan; 42% invited to CPA meeting; 50% offered an appointment.
audits.c: PDSA cycle 1: nursing staff engagement with baseline data/recommendations. PDSA cycle 2: admission protocol for consistent carer engagement.
audits.r2: After cycle 1/cycle 2: carer details documented 40%/80%; contacted within 24 hours 66%/30%; views in care plan 0%/30%; invited to CPA meeting 66%/30%; offered appointment 66%/30%.

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project on Standardising GP Discharge Summaries in Liaison Psychiatry Services for Older People in Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust
audits.tp: Standardising GP discharge summaries (liaison psychiatry, older people)
audits.st: Locally developed scoring criteria for discharge summary subheadings; target 100% within six months
audits.f: Discharge summary scores ranged 6-20 (max 20); mean score 12.3.
audits.c: New discharge summary template with standardised subheadings, guidance document with scoring criteria, team meeting.
audits.r2: Mean score improved to 19.0, consistent across the seven weeks; GPs were satisfied with the new format.

audits.t: VTE Prophylaxis Quality Improvement of Service Users Data in Older Adult Mental Health Inpatient Wards in St Charles Hospital, CNWL NHS Trust
audits.tp: VTE prophylaxis data completion in older adult inpatient wards
audits.st: Local target: 100% VTE prophylaxis data submission
audits.f: 63% VTE prophylaxis data compliance.
audits.c: PDSA cycle 1: nursing handover section for outstanding VTE checks and weekly MDT reminder. PDSA cycle 2: VTE poster distributed and displayed.
audits.r2: Compliance rose to 84% after cycle 1 (October 2023) and 100% after cycle 2 (December 2023).

audits.t: Developing and Delivering a Regional Teaching Programme in Liaison Psychiatry: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Regional teaching programme in liaison psychiatry
audits.st: RCPsych Psychiatric Liaison Accreditation Network (PLAN) best practice teaching standards
audits.f: 50% of respondents were not receiving any liaison-specific teaching.
audits.c: Cross-site monthly teaching programme delivered via Microsoft Teams by liaison clinicians.
audits.r2: Attendance ranged 15-27 professionals (mean 22); mean satisfaction 4.7/5; percentage increase in confidence scores ranged 4.6-48% (mean 24%).

audits.t: Psychiatric Admission Documentation at Leverndale Hospital, Glasgow
audits.st: Local admission template standard including CRAFT risk assessment, legal status, observation level, time-out status
audits.f: Medicines reconciliation absent in 55%; allergies absent in 70%; CRAFT risk assessment completed by admitting doctor in 55% of cases
audits.c: Replacement of the paper clerk-in booklet with a digitalised admission proforma on EmisWeb
audits.r2: Admission proforma usage little changed (80% vs 75% previously); CRAFT risk assessment by admitting doctor fell to 40% (from 55%); allergy recording improved to 55% (from 30%); medication recording improved to 95% (from 45%); 100% of admission documentation now available on EmisWeb (vs 85% previously)

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project to Improve the Resident Doctors’ Out-of-Hours Clinical Handover System at Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust (NHFT)
audits.tp: Resident doctors' out-of-hours clinical handover system
audits.st: Trust-agreed SharePoint handover system standard
audits.f: 80% compliance rate for handovers (20% neither face-to-face nor verbal); only 20% (42/209) of jobs marked complete against a 100% standard; 90% aware of the system but only 60% did regular face-to-face handovers.
audits.c: Awareness sessions at induction, IT changes moving SharePoint to a secure server with template/dropdown improvements, automatic email reminders, PowerBI dashboard.
audits.r2: 100% compliance (all handovers completed and recorded); only 23.03% of jobs marked complete on the system.

audits.t: Improving the Assessment and Management of Cardiovascular Risk in Adult Psychiatric Inpatients Using the QRISK3 Score – A Combined Quality Improvement and Pilot Study
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk assessment using QRISK3 in psychiatric inpatients
audits.st: not reported (QRISK3 10-year risk threshold used to offer atorvastatin as primary prevention)
audits.f: At start, only 1 of 17 patients on the ward was on a statin and none had a documented QRISK3 score.
audits.c: Routine QRISK3 score calculation for new admissions, counselling and offer of atorvastatin if score >=10%.
audits.r2: 10 of 50 patients had QRISK3 >=10%; 2 already on a statin; of remaining 8, 4 agreed to start atorvastatin and 4 declined; average time to calculate score was 6 minutes 24 seconds.

audits.t: Quality improvement project improving awareness of family planning risks with valproate in male patients
audits.tp: Valproate family planning risk awareness in male patients
audits.st: MHRA 2023 guidance on valproate-associated risks in male patients around conception
audits.f: All 22 patients received a text message; only one responded; phone contact successful with 18, of whom 8 confirmed receiving the text and 10 had not
audits.c: Accurx text message auto-coding advice into EMIS, followed by personalised phone calls
audits.r2: 5 patients already aware of the MHRA alert; 13 informed during calls; 4 could not be contacted; no patients requested further information or took further action

audits.t: Improving Documentation of Sleep Assessments in Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) Clinics at Havering Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service
audits.tp: Sleep assessment documentation in ADHD clinics
audits.st: NICE guidance essential components of sleep assessment; local target of 100% documentation by August 2024
audits.f: Initial audit showed only 20% (n=4) of records containing all essential components of sleep assessment
audits.c: PDSA Cycle 1: sleep assessment questionnaire designed for carer/patient completion; Cycle 2: questionnaire modified with new questions; Cycle 3: sleep hygiene leaflet introduced
audits.r2: PDSA Cycle 1: 50% (n=6); Cycle 2: 70% (n=7); Cycle 3 (final): 100% (n=20) of documentations contained all essential components

audits.t: Enhancing Lifestyle Counselling Targeted at Weight Management for Patients on Antipsychotics in a Community Mental Health Team: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Lifestyle counselling for weight management on antipsychotics
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists' Positive Cardiometabolic Health Resource / NHS Eat Well and Live Well guides / UK CMO physical activity guidance; target 80% staff awareness/confidence within 4 months
audits.f: Baseline survey (S1): mean staff awareness/confidence 5.32 (SD 3.461); mean correct MCQ answers 36.0%.
audits.c: PDSA1: informational posters in consultation rooms and shared areas. PDSA2: educational session on lifestyle guidance.
audits.r2: S2 (after posters): mean 4.7 (SD 3.303), MCQ 26.0% (decrease). S3 (after teaching): mean 4.96 (SD 2.166), MCQ 38.9% (increase).

audits.t: Improving Lone Work Practice Within a Mental Health Trust: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Lone working practice and safety for resident doctors
audits.st: Trust lone working policy; target 20% increase in awareness/adherence by September 2024
audits.f: 71% conducted lone working; 29% felt informed about policies; 43% received alarms, 66% of these trained to use them.
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles: lone work checklist in orientation, induction presentation, video on lone working/alarms/policy, supervisor reminders.
audits.r2: 68% conducted lone working, 63% felt well informed and received alarms, 72% felt confident using alarms; overall improvement in adherence/awareness of 33.83% (exceeding 20% target).

audits.t: Protecting Lives: A Quality Improvement Project to Improve Adherence to Fitness to Drive Policy in Mental Health Setting
audits.tp: Adherence to fitness to drive (DVLA) policy in mental health inpatients
audits.st: Local fitness to drive policy; target 100% driving risk assessment and 100% DVLA guidance information
audits.f: Driving risk assessment completed for 95% at admission; ~12% driving at admission; risk assessment during stay only 11.7%; advice on fitness to drive given in 12.5% of cases; a quarter of driving patients received no discharge advice.
audits.c: Educational training video developed and shared trust-wide via email (September 2024) with a reminder two weeks later.
audits.r2: Admission risk assessment 94% (similar); driving patients rose to 20%; in-stay risk assessment improved to 19% (+7%); discharge advice improved to 21.2% (+8%); but percentage of driving patients receiving advice fell from 75% to 53%.

audits.t: Implementing a Clinician-Built High-Dose Antipsychotic Therapy (HDAT) Calculator and Tracker: A Quality Improvement Project to Optimise HDAT Monitoring and Safe Prescribing
audits.st: Local trust HDAT monitoring guidelines and POMH Ready Reckoner Version 11
audits.f: ECG and blood test compliance both 91%; 2 of 11 due for annual weight assessment; 3 of 11 lacked a recorded antipsychotic side-effect assessment and 4 of 8 overdue for annual review.
audits.c: Clinician-built HDAT Calculator and Tracker (Microsoft Excel) to flag upcoming/overdue assessments.
audits.r2: not reported (tool implemented; formal re-audit not reported)

audits.t: Improving Communication of Discharge Medications to General Practitioners from Inpatient Psychiatric Wards: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Communication of discharge medications to GPs
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance: discharge summaries sent within 7 days; target 100% over 9 months
audits.f: 30% of discharge summaries not sent to GP within 7 days.
audits.c: PDSA1: discharge notification form for vital information, completed within 24 hours. PDSA2: addressed ward clerk cover and educated new doctors on the template.
audits.r2: After PDSA1: 51% delayed beyond 7 days (about 50% administrative issues), 5% notification sent within 24 hours, 13% within 7 days. After PDSA2: 30% of discharge summaries delayed beyond 7 days (due to late doctor completion), but 100% had discharge notifications sent within 24 hours.

audits.t: SAFE MED Quality Improvement Project: Supporting Availability and Functionality of Essential Monitoring Equipment for Drug Use in CAMHS (Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services) Outpatient Services in Oxfordshire
audits.tp: Availability and functionality of essential monitoring equipment in CAMHS outpatient clinics
audits.st: NICE guidelines, Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines and hospital guidelines on monitoring equipment (54-item checklist)
audits.f: On average 44% of checklist items were present (56% missing); of present items 96% were working well, 4% dysfunctional (e.g. clock with no battery, unstable scale, faulty thermometer, limited sanitiser).

audits.t: Prioritising Sexual and Reproductive Health on a Female Inpatient Psychiatric Ward: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Sexual and reproductive health screening on a female inpatient ward
audits.st: not reported (locally used women's physical health and contraception forms)
audits.f: 53% had the women's physical health (WPH) form completed, 0% the contraception form; 59% of completed forms found abnormalities but 0% were referred for investigation/treatment.
audits.c: Information posters highlighting existing forms; six referral pathways developed for doctors' use.
audits.r2: Completion remained static (50% WPH, 0% contraception); detected abnormalities rose to 88%; appropriate referrals rose to 40% (of the remaining 60%, 7 declined, mostly a smear test).

audits.t: An Evaluation of Emergency Detention Certificates in NHS Lanarkshire: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Mental Health Act principles and minimum clinical/legal completion criteria (standardised 28-point scoring system)
audits.f: Scores ranged from 16 to 28, average 23; 51.3% of certificates were completed by psychiatry resident doctors/consultants (average score 24.2), 11.1% by GPs (average 20.2) and 37.6% by resident doctors on medical wards (average 22.1); 35% had Mental Health Officer consent

audits.t: Improving Timely VTE Risk Assessment in Adult Psychiatric Inpatients: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: VTE risk assessment timeliness in psychiatric inpatients
audits.st: Trust and NICE guidance requiring VTE risk assessment within 24 hours of admission
audits.f: Timely completion within 24 hours was 50% (10/20); overall completion 100%; documentation of delay reasons 20%; mean time to assessment 36 hours
audits.c: Ward poster reminders, handover/MDT education, VTE training in resident doctor inductions, routine MDT review, a VTE column on handover sheets, ward-specific completion protocols
audits.r2: Timely completion improved to 84.6% (11/13); overall completion remained 100%; documentation of delay reasons improved to 100%; mean time to assessment reduced to 11.6 hours

audits.t: Lessons From a Quality Improvement Project Aiming to Reduce Missed Outpatient Appointments in a Community Mental Health Regional Centre
audits.tp: Reducing missed outpatient appointments (DNA rates) in community mental health
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline Did Not Attend (DNA) rate approximately 25%
audits.c: Three Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles: staff email/MDT discussion and posters on accurate DNA documentation, then patient-facing posters and leaflets
audits.r2: No sustained decrease in DNA rates was observed; median DNA rate 22.7%; the run chart indicated common-cause variation

audits.t: Improving Nearest Relative Legal Literacy and Support Under the Mental Health Act: A Quality Improvement Project in an Autism-Informed Inpatient Service
audits.tp: Nearest Relative legal literacy under the Mental Health Act
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Approximately 60% understood their Nearest Relative role; approximately 45% were confident in their legal rights; approximately 50% recalled receiving written information; approximately 40% felt emotionally supported; approximately 35% felt involved in discharge planning
audits.c: Autism-informed Nearest Relative information leaflet, standardised admission explanation script, NR support check-in, staff guidance on trauma and autism-informed communication

audits.t: VTE Assessment for Psychiatric Inpatients–Quality Improvement Project on Acute Male Ward
audits.tp: VTE risk assessment compliance in psychiatric inpatients
audits.st: NICE guidance: VTE risk review by first consultant review
audits.f: 12% completion rate of VTE risk assessment (VTRAP tool) prior to change
audits.c: VTE assessment added to the ward round proforma and poster reminders for resident (clerking) doctors
audits.r2: Completion was over 66% at every subsequent data collection point, with all but one over 80%

audits.t: Menopause and Mental Health: Improving Knowledge and Clinical Practice in a Community Mental Health Team–A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Menopause and mental health knowledge in community mental health team
audits.st: NICE menopause treatment guidelines (contextual standard)
audits.f: 74% aware of menopause's impact on mental health; 16% self-rated sufficient knowledge; 68% considered menopause in assessments; 42% incorporated it into mental state examinations; 23% knew appropriate treatment; 8% aware of available resources
audits.c: Targeted educational training, Trust resource review, patient leaflets, screening/diagnostic tools, a narrated training module, reminder posters
audits.r2: 80% aware of impact; 40% self-rated sufficient knowledge; 60% considered menopause in assessments; 87% incorporated it into mental state examinations; 80% knew appropriate treatment; 40% aware of resources; 100% recognised relevance both pre- and post-training

audits.t: Improving Accuracy and Efficiency of NEWS Chart Monitoring in a Forensic Mental Health Unit
audits.st: TEWV NEWS Policy and NICE guidance on NEWS monitoring
audits.f: 72% of wards recorded NEWS electronically; 80% recorded on paper (duplication); 0% electronic recalibration available; 100% of paper charts allowed manual parameter adjustment; 28% of wards used paper charts for non-NEWS tasks; 0% misused electronic charts
audits.c: Dissemination of findings, guidance development on adjusting NEWS parameters for atypical baselines, exploration of electronic customisation, staff education planned for Cycle 2

audits.t: Strengthening Advance Care Planning and DNACPR Documentation in an Older Adult Psychiatric Inpatient Setting: A Quality Improvement Initiative
audits.tp: Advance care planning and DNACPR documentation in older adult psychiatry
audits.st: National DNACPR guidance and the Mental Capacity Act (2005); target 100% documentation within 2 months
audits.f: 0% of patients had documented DNACPR status or recorded resuscitation discussions.
audits.c: PDSA1: mandatory DNACPR status review at weekly MDT ward rounds. PDSA2: clinician-led discussions with patients/families on resuscitation preferences, guided by Mental Capacity Act principles.
audits.r2: After cycle 1: documented DNACPR status increased from 0% to 100%. After cycle 2: 50% had documented discussions and 30% had an active DNACPR order (baseline 0%); compliance remained 100% at four-week follow-up.

audits.t: Evaluating Cardiovascular Disease Risk in Male Forensic Inpatients Using QRISK-3: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Cardiovascular disease risk assessment using QRISK3 (forensic inpatients)
audits.st: NICE CVD risk assessment/management guidance using QRISK3 (threshold 10%)
audits.f: 16 patients had QRISK3 >=10%; 11 already on a statin; of remaining 5, 4 agreed to start atorvastatin, 1 declined; mean time to calculate score 12 minutes 36 seconds; 91% had BMI >=25 (mean BMI 32.33).

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project (QIP) Bryngolau–Implement and Optimise Non-Pharmacological Approaches for Managing BPSD (Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia) to Minimise the Need for Pharmacological Interventions
audits.tp: Non-pharmacological management of BPSD in dementia
audits.st: Local target: reduce pharmacological interventions for BPSD by 40-60% using national guideline-based non-pharmacological strategies
audits.f: Pharmacological interventions used in 44.3% of BPSD incidents; non-pharmacological interventions 55.7%.
audits.c: Staff education, sensory room utilisation, guideline promotion, structured assessment tools (e.g. ABC charts) over four 15-day PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: Pharmacological interventions decreased to 23.5% by cycle 4 (average reduction 42.5%, exceeding target); non-pharmacological interventions rose to 76.5%; BPSD incidents dropped 56% and falls reduced 76% by cycle 3-4.

audits.t: Reducing Repeat Prescriptions (FP10s) Issued by South Hub Community Mental Health Team: A Quality Improvement Pilot
audits.tp: Reducing repeat prescriptions (FP10s) from secondary mental health care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median 6 repeat FP10 prescriptions per week at baseline
audits.c: Electronic prescribing prompts, an improved repeat-prescription tracking spreadsheet, Enhanced Shared Care Agreement/repatriation letter templates, a duty doctor rota
audits.r2: Data showed intermittent peaks and troughs without a sustained shift in the primary outcome; the 20% reduction target was not met

audits.t: Redesigning Follow-Up Care in Community Mental Health Teams Through Patient-Initiated Models: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Patient-initiated follow-up (PIFU) pathway in community mental health teams
audits.st: NHS England PIFU guidance
audits.f: By June 2025, Nechells CMHT showed a 37.22% reduction in routine clinic waiting times compared with Aston CMHT, with improved capacity for review within 14 days
audits.c: Patient-Initiated Follow-Up (PIFU) pathway: dedicated electronic record category, weekly PIFU review slots, staff training, screening criteria and MDT discussion before transfer
audits.r2: 66.7% of patients reported clear understanding of the pathway and 72.7% were confident in accessing care; 31.5% had contacted the team since initiation (68.2% found access easy); 76.8% preferred PIFU and 92.6% wished to continue on the pathway

audits.t: Clozapine Prescribing in General Hospitals: A Second-Cycle Service Evaluation Following Quality Improvement Interventions
audits.tp: Clozapine prescribing safety during general hospital admission
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Clozapine was correctly documented in community records in 16% of admissions; referrals to Liaison Psychiatry were reviewed within 24 hours in 68% of cases
audits.c: Local education, a Trust-wide clozapine policy for general hospitals, and a clozapine admission checklist
audits.r2: Correct community documentation improved to 26% (17/66); 79% (52/66) were referred to Liaison Psychiatry with mean referral time reduced from 41.07 to 32 hours; 87% (54/62) of referrals were reviewed within 24 hours (up from 68%); documentation was highest for medication concordance and physical health concerns (both 88%) and lowest for smoking status (19%) and signs of clozapine toxicity (33%)

audits.t: Clinical Global Assessment Scale (CGAS) Recording at Admission and Discharge for Young People Admitted to a General Adolescent Inpatient unit
audits.tp: CGAS recording completeness in adolescent inpatients
audits.st: Local target of >=90% completion of CGAS recording at admission and discharge
audits.f: CGAS recorded on admission for 39/50 (78.0%), below the >=90% target; recorded on discharge for 29/50 (58.0%), well below target
audits.c: Information Officer to routinely check discharge summaries and contact authors when CGAS missing; Medical Secretary to only accept discharge summaries including a completed CGAS

audits.t: Inpatient Discharge Letters
audits.st: EPUT policy on Discharge and Transfer Clinical Guidelines (CG24)
audits.f: Previous cycle data collected on 81 discharges (numbers not fully detailed)
audits.c: not reported (this report presents the re-audit; specific intervention not described)
audits.r2: Brief discharge summary copy to patient 100%; detailed discharge summary scanned onto electronic records 98%; GP received brief summary within 24 hours 86%; brief summary scanned onto electronic records 86%; GP received detailed summary within 5 working days 81%; detailed summary given to patient 0%

audits.t: Aftercare under the 1983 Mental Health Act
audits.st: Section 117 of the Mental Health Act 1983 aftercare planning requirements
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Completed audit cycle showed how discharge planning can be improved

audits.t: Improving electroconvulsive therapy practice through audit
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists guidelines on ECT stimulus adjustment
audits.f: Inconsistencies in clinical practice of stimulus adjustment in response to brief seizures identified (numbers not reported)
audits.c: Education programme to bring practice into line with Royal College of Psychiatrists guidelines
audits.r2: Marked improvement in the quality of stimulus adjustment shown at repeat audit (numbers not reported)

audits.t: The impact of a hospital audit on psychiatrists' letters to general practitioners
audits.st: Local quality standard for written communication with GPs
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Improved standards, particularly letters becoming less potentially offensive and easier to read by non-psychiatrists

audits.t: A repeat audit of the Cognitive Analytic Therapy Clinic at Guy's Hospital
audits.tp: Cognitive Analytic Therapy clinic outcomes and attendance
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Earlier audits showed higher drop-out and lower follow-up attendance (numbers not reported)
audits.c: Changes in training and supervision of therapists instituted since earlier audits
audits.r2: Lower drop-out rate and higher follow-up attendance; significant and consistent mean score reductions on three questionnaires across three cohorts

audits.t: Injecting some audit into substance misuse services
audits.tp: Regional audit programme development in substance misuse services
audits.st: Regional menu of 12 audit priority topics developed by the project's Agency Audit Representative Group
audits.f: 12 agencies had completed an initial audit of 2-4 topics each from the regional menu of 12 priorities
audits.c: Reciprocal peer audit system between agencies, supported by a dedicated facilitator, auditor training programme, and an Agency Audit Representative Group
audits.r2: 9 out of the original 12 (75%) completed their first audit cycle with a re-audit of the same topics; increase in agencies meeting all standards in chosen topics

audits.t: Audit of out-patients on ‘higher dose’ antipsychotics
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists consensus statement on the use of high-dose antipsychotics
audits.f: Baseline survey showed poor attendance at hospital appointments as the main problem (numbers not reported)
audits.c: Medical staff became more assertive and visited non-attenders at home; a phlebotomist visited patients at home
audits.r2: Two completed audit cycles showed improvement in monitoring and management of outpatients on higher dose depot antipsychotics (numbers not reported)

audits.t: Use of high dose antipsychotic medication
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists guidelines on high-dose antipsychotic prescribing (expressed as % of BNF maximum recommended dose)
audits.f: 16 (7%) patients found to be on high doses of antipsychotics
