audits.st: Interdisciplinary standardised perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis (AP) protocol covering drug/dose selection, timing (30 min before incision), dose recording, intraoperative re-dosing after 3 hours, and discontinuation within 48 hours.
audits.f: First post-intervention evaluation found 26.8% of surgeries were non-compliant with the AP protocol (43.75% of these were cardiac surgeries).
audits.r2: Appropriate drug and dosage regimen used in 57.1% (20/35); appropriate dose not used in 2.9% (1/35), appropriate dosage regimen not used in 34.3% (12/35), appropriate drug not used in 5.7% (2/35); dose recorded in electronic clinical history in 97.1% (34/35) but not on the surgical sheet in most cases; dose timing incorrect in 28.6% (10/35); all patients discontinued AP within 48 hours.

audits.t: 859. Remote Video Auditing (RVA) To Assess Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Compliance In Rooms With Clostridioides difficile Patients
audits.tp: Personal protective equipment and hand hygiene compliance monitoring
audits.st: Isolation precautions (PPE use, hand hygiene, doffing sequence) for Clostridioides difficile patients, per NHSN criteria
audits.f: Lower PPE/hand hygiene compliance rates seen during study period than historical controls; Cdiff cases per patient day 0.003
audits.c: Remote video auditing (RVA) introduced as a novel educational and monitoring measure for infection control
audits.r2: Increased compliance with PPE (not statistically significant) at room entry; significantly increased compliance with PPE/hand hygiene and proper doffing at room exit; Cdiff cases per patient day decreased to 0.001

audits.t: 97. Assessment of Personal Protective Equipment Adherence in Red Box Using Remote Video Auditing
audits.tp: Personal protective equipment and hand hygiene compliance monitoring
audits.st: Isolation precaution PPE use protocol; local "Red Box" protocol for PPE-free communication zone
audits.f: Among HCPs who stayed within the Red Box, 69.9% did not practise hand hygiene, 91.6% did not use gloves and 95.2% did not use gowns (as expected by protocol); HCPs who went beyond the Red Box had significantly increased non-compliance with PPE and hand hygiene compared with control rooms without a Red Box

audits.t: Evaluation of Turner Syndrome International Consensus Guideline Compliance in Multiple Subspecialty Clinics Verses a Coordinated Multidisciplinary Clinic Format
audits.st: 2016 Cincinnati International Turner Syndrome consensus guideline (Gravholt et al., Eur J Endocrinol 2017) for age-appropriate screening
audits.f: Only 36.6% of all girls met all age-appropriate screening recommendations; multidisciplinary clinic (MDC) girls had higher compliance than non-MDC girls overall (75.6% of compliant girls were in MDC, p=0.014) and for individual tests: TSH 95% vs 76% (p=0.017), auditory evaluation 85% vs 50% (p<0.001), HbA1c/glucose 97% vs 76% (p=0.017), tissue transglutaminase 95% vs 83% (p=0.048)

audits.t: Audit on Steroid Replacement in Confirmed or Suspected COVID-19 Patients With Adrenal Insufficiency or Adrenal Suppression in a District General Hospital
audits.tp: Steroid replacement in adrenal insufficiency with COVID-19
audits.st: Society for Endocrinology April 2020 guidance: hydrocortisone 100mg IV then 200mg/24h continuous infusion (or 50mg every 6h IV/IM) for steroid-dependent patients with confirmed/suspected COVID-19
audits.f: None of the 12 patients were managed as per updated guidelines; 6 had less than adequate dose (prednisolone 30-40mg), 4 had oral steroid dose only doubled, 1 received same dose, 1 confirmed Addison's had higher hydrocortisone dose
audits.c: Teaching sessions to doctors, posters on updated guidelines in major hospital areas, and updated trust guidelines on the intranet

audits.t: Annual Trainee Doctors’ Prize Day, Thursday 2nd November 2018. : Postgraduate Medical Centre, Belfast City Hospital.
audits.st: NICE Guideline 53: discharge summaries should reach GPs within 7 days; local target of at least 60% within 12 months
audits.f: 0% of discharge letters completed within 7 days
audits.c: 5 PDSA cycles introducing a new discharge trolley on each inpatient ward, a new discharge checklist, and restructuring the discharge letter to be easier to read and complete
audits.r2: Improvement from 0% to over 80% of letters completed within 7 days; mean time for community teams to receive letters improved from 51 days to 4 days

audits.t: P076 Adherence to COVID-19 risk stratification during the peak of pandemic: a District General Hospital experience
audits.tp: Adherence to COVID-19 risk stratification advice
audits.st: British Society for Rheumatology (BSR) risk stratification guide, March 2020 (shield or isolate vulnerable patients)
audits.f: 93% (373) confirmed receiving guidance; 267 shielding and 83 isolating, but 21 patients did not follow guidance and 2 stopped drugs due to fear of COVID-19; only 3 of 7 symptomatic patients confirmed COVID-19 positive

audits.t: 301 Theatre Timing Audit (TTA): HPB and Transplant theatre timing during COVID
audits.tp: Theatre timing during the COVID-19 pandemic
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Capacity 100%; ward-to-theatre and induction-to-start timings measured
audits.r2: Capacity 28.6% (period-1) and 85.7% (period-2); end-of-procedure-to-transfer-out delayed in period-1 (39.4±10.9 min) vs pre-COVID (16.6±12.8) and period-2 (17.6±10.5 min)

audits.t: EP.WE.31A snapshot audit on the current practice of minimal access surgery in the UK during COVID-19 pandemic
audits.tp: Minimal access surgery practice during COVID-19
audits.st: Early COVID-19 guidelines placing an embargo on minimal access surgery to reduce aerosolisation risk
audits.f: Volume of minimal access procedures decreased across units from 94.9% to 39.0% during the pandemic

audits.t: 99. Presence of Chronic Diseases and Compliance with Québec Provincial Guidelines for Outpatient Antibiotic Prescription, Québec, Canada, 2010-2017
audits.st: Québec provincial guidelines for outpatient antibiotic prescription of respiratory and urinary infections (correct agent for children; correct agent and dosage for adults)
audits.f: Between 14,677 and 312,786 prescriptions per infection type; agent choice compliance above 87% in children (lower by up to 3 points with asthma); in adults agent choice compliant in at least 73% of prescriptions except pharyngitis (53-61%); accounting for dosage, compliance ranged from 19% (cystitis with diabetes) to 77% (pyelonephritis, no chronic disease); compliant prescriptions were 2.4% to 20.4% less frequent in patients with chronic diseases

audits.t: 1177. Vaccinate Lurie (VaLu) a QI Project to Improve Pediatric Pre-Transplant Immunization Rates
audits.tp: Pre-transplant immunisation rates in paediatric transplant recipients
audits.st: CDC recommended tetanus and pneumococcal vaccination schedule by age at transplant
audits.f: Approximately 53% of heart and liver transplant recipients were up to date with tetanus and pneumococcal vaccinations
audits.c: Interdisciplinary team PDSA cycles: (1) team members gained access to the statewide vaccine database (ICARE); (2) ICARE was linked to the electronic medical record (EPIC) for automatic immunisation record integration
audits.r2: Immunisation rates improved to over 80% for late 2019-mid 2020, reaching 100% in the third quarter of 2020; rates subsequently decreased in 2021 after the improvement team stopped meeting during the pandemic, despite institutional ICARE access remaining in place

audits.t: Are we adequately reviewing confusion inducing drugs in patients referred to the memory assessment service?
audits.tp: Confusion-inducing drug review before dementia diagnosis
audits.st: NICE guideline NG97, Royal College of Psychiatrists Memory Service National Accreditation Programme (MSNAP), and National Institute on Ageing and Alzheimer's Association (NIA-AA) criteria
audits.f: 36% of patients had not had any cognitive assessment before referral; only 10 patients (5%) had a documented confusion-inducing drug (CID) prescription review in the notes
audits.c: Planned: issue each dementia support worker and nurse with a CID prescription review card listing medications to consider and flag for review

audits.t: P003 Quality improvement project on rituximab use in rheumatoid arthritis - how do we improve quality and cost effectiveness?
audits.tp: Rituximab retreatment dosing in rheumatoid arthritis
audits.st: Evidence from SMART, SERENE, IMAGE and MIRROR trials supporting reduced-dose rituximab retreatment as equally effective to standard dose
audits.f: 96% of patients received the standard 1g x2 (2 weeks apart) retreatment regime; 43% retreated 6-monthly, 33% 6-9 monthly, 24% more than 9 months; average age 66, 58% female, 83% seropositive
audits.c: Departmental retreatment schedule optimised from standard 2g dose to a reduced 1g dose

audits.t: TU7.4 Service Evaluation Audit of Virtual Outpatient Clinics in the Post-COVID-19 era
audits.tp: Patient satisfaction with virtual outpatient clinics
audits.st: NHS Outpatient Department Survey (2011) questions used as a comparator; no explicit compliance target stated
audits.f: Overall satisfaction with telephone consultations was significantly higher than pre-COVID face-to-face survey results; 51% confident and 27% confident to some extent about being listed for surgery without further examination; 8% not confident about how surgery was explained; 10% not confident about the risks of surgery; more than a third not happy to be discharged from clinic after a telephone consultation

audits.t: Benzodiazepine prescribing in tunisia: A study about psychiatrists prescribing habits
audits.st: Guidelines on benzodiazepine (BZD) prescribing (not individually named)
audits.f: Purpose of BZD treatment explained to patient in 98.2% of cases, risks explained in 87.7%; precautions taken in elderly (96.5%), respiratory failure risk (94.7%), personality disorders (80.7%), pregnancy (77.9%); 14.4% combined two BZDs for refractory symptoms; 18.4% did not systematically reassess necessity before repeating a prescription

audits.t: Successful Implementation of a Change in Practice to Optimize Timing of Umbilical Cord Clamping in Preterm Neonates: A Quality Improvement Initiative
audits.tp: Umbilical cord clamping timing in preterm infants
audits.st: Institutional guideline recommending natural (delayed) umbilical cord clamping (NCC) for at least 60 seconds in preterm infants; objective was to achieve over 50% compliance.
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Structured multidisciplinary educational approach: evidence presented at grand round, multidisciplinary team (neonatologists, obstetricians, neonatal nurse practitioners, respiratory therapists, nurses) developed the NCC guideline, local champions identified at each hospital, staff education before staged implementation (Oct 2013 for GA 33-35 weeks, Jan 2014 for GA >=28 weeks, Apr 2014 for GA >=26 weeks).
audits.r2: Compliance rates and proportion of infants receiving NCC of at least 45 seconds are reported in a table not reproduced in the abstract; 18% of infants 26-32 weeks gestational age eligible for NCC received cord clamping at less than 45 seconds to facilitate resuscitation.

audits.t: Implementation of a Quality Improvement Role for Unlicensed Assistive Personnel and Effects on Infection Prevention
audits.st: Infection prevention care bundle process measures for central-line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI), catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) and C. difficile prevention
audits.f: Baseline number of central-line audits and infection rates prior to the quality liaison role
audits.c: A dedicated unlicensed assistive personnel (certified nursing assistant) quality liaison role introduced in early 2019 to perform daily rounding, direct care tasks, patient education, process measure audits, and real-time feedback to RNs
audits.r2: Central-line audits increased by more than 1,400 compared with the previous year; rate reductions of 40-55% achieved for CLABSI, CAUTI and healthcare-associated C. difficile infections

audits.t: High-Level Disinfection in Ambulatory Care: Overcoming the Barriers of a Decentralized System through Auditing and Education
audits.tp: High-level disinfection compliance in ambulatory care
audits.st: Standard work for high-level disinfection (HLD) of semicritical instruments (manufacturer instructions and competency requirements)
audits.f: Audits found variability across departments with gaps in precleaning, transportation of used instruments, dilution of enzymatic cleaner, and maintenance of quality control logs; also gaps in staff understanding of standard work and inventory management
audits.c: Centralised HLD database of supplies, methodology, standard work and competency evaluations; infection control team led direct observation audits; monthly-driven HLD calendar for annual competencies; joint education sessions between infection control and manufacturers for reprocessing staff

audits.t: Prospective audit and feedback of Clostridioides difficile PCR at the time of ordering increases appropriateness of testing
audits.st: Antibiotic stewardship program's clinical criteria for appropriate C. difficile PCR testing (no positive test in prior 7 days plus a 3-step clinical review)
audits.f: ASP was alerted to and collected data on C. difficile PCR orders without intervening
audits.c: Antibiotic stewardship program implemented real-time prospective audit and feedback (PAF) at the time of C. difficile PCR test ordering, with direct provider conversation or a note on appropriate criteria, and recommendation to cancel inappropriate tests
audits.r2: Significant reduction in monthly test rate compared with preintervention period, driven mainly by reducing tests considered clinically inappropriate

audits.t: Hand hygiene adherence at entrances and exits of healthcare facilities in two rural districts of Uganda
audits.st: WHO recommendation for hand hygiene stations (soap and water, or alcohol-based hand rub) at entrances and exits of healthcare facilities
audits.f: Only 4/37 (11%) facility entrances/exits met recommended HH material guidance; 12/37 (32%) had no HH station, 13/37 (35%) had stations with no water, 8/37 (22%) had water but no soap; of 180 people observed, 52 (29%) attempted hand hygiene and only 10 (6%) used appropriate technology (4 ABHR, 6 water and soap); 42/52 (81%) used only water without soap; no hand hygiene occurred when exiting (0 of 68); only 9/180 (5%) adhered to both suggested technique and duration

audits.t: A81 OPTIMIZING THE INDICATIONS FOR BILIARY STENT PLACEMENT IN PATIENTS WITH CBD STONES: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVE TO ENHANCE PATIENT CARE AND REDUCE HEALTHCARE RESOURCE UTILIZATION
audits.st: Published guidelines on indications for biliary stent insertion in patients with CBD stones
audits.f: Inappropriate stent usage identified in 16% of CBD stone patients overall; 223/598 (37%) of first ERCPs had a stent placed, of which 63/223 (28%) were not in accordance with published guidelines
audits.c: Pre-intervention audit findings shared with the ERCP group; education to align biliary stent insertion practice with published guidelines
audits.r2: 192/661 (29%) of first ERCPs had a stent placed (vs 37% pre-intervention, not significant); only 13/192 (7%) were not in accordance with guidelines, compared with 28% pre-intervention (kappa=0.53 for independent blinded review)

audits.t: Prescription audit and effects of co-morbidities on indoor covid-19 patients of a tertiary care teaching hospital
audits.tp: Prescription audit in indoor COVID-19 patients
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators.
audits.f: Of 300 prescriptions analysed (2972 drugs prescribed), average 9.90 drugs per prescription; 88% of drugs prescribed by generic name; 99.66% of encounters had antimicrobials; 44% of encounters had injections; 83.34% of drugs were from the National Essential Drug List; 55.67% of patients had a co-morbidity; average hospital stay approximately 8 days.

audits.t: Strengthening patient safety in a Cambodian hospital through structured weekly reporting: a low-cost quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Local structured weekly reporting standard operating procedures for patient safety
audits.f: 0 formally adopted Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs); 38% of ER staff Basic Life Support-trained; 2 expired blood product incidents per month
audits.c: One-page Departmental Wise Checklist introduced across ER/ICU, obstetrics and gynaecology, outpatients and paediatrics; weekly reviews, feedback loops, departmental champions, PDSA cycles
audits.r2: SOPs increased from 0 to 10; Basic Life Support-trained ER staff rose to 98%; expired blood product incidents fell to none; reporting compliance averaged 92%; neonatal hypothermia cases fell from 6 to 2/month; ER adverse events dropped from 4 to 1/month

audits.t: A retrospective audit of accuracy of thoracolumbosacral pedicle screw fixation.
audits.st: Gertzbein grading of pedicle screw breach on postoperative CT, benchmarked against published accuracy rates (95.5% CT-navigation, 93.1% free-hand, 91.5% fluoroscopy-guided, 90.5% robot-assisted, from a 1990-2018 systematic review).
audits.f: 98.75% of screws (94.03% of patients) were accurately placed; 3 screws had asymptomatic Gertzbein grade 1 breach (<2mm); 1 patient had grade 2 breach (2-4mm) with radicular pain; accuracy by level was 99.08% lumbar, 98.39% thoracic and 97.5% sacral.

audits.t: Audit of radiation doses during endovascular aneurysm repair
audits.tp: Radiation dose monitoring in endovascular aneurysm repair
audits.st: not reported (no named diagnostic reference level or dose standard stated; project monitored trends in radiation dose over time)
audits.f: Median radiation dose was lower than in 2021; median screening time was 29% longer than in 2021; dose was lower with two operators than one.
audits.r2: Median radiation dose was 46.45% higher than in 2014; median screening time was shorter than in 2014 but increased with more operators, with 4-operator procedures having the longest screening times; operator number had no significant effect on dose in 2021.

audits.t: Operating Theatre Utilisation at Colombo South Teaching Hospital: A Single-institution Audit of Elective Surgical Efficiency
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean scheduled-session utilisation 58.1% (SD 14.2%); extended capacity utilisation 38.7%; first-case delays negatively correlated with utilisation (r=-0.60)

audits.t: Safely developing respiratory care during emergency neonatal transport by a long-term quality improvement program
audits.st: A locally defined set of quality indicators for respiratory care during transport (no external named guideline; no explicit ventilation protocol)
audits.f: Use of ventilation modes supporting all breaths (Volume Guarantee/HFOV) was 38%
audits.c: Systematic computerised data collection and analysis of ventilator parameters, waveforms and loops during transport, discussed at regular case review meetings (n=21)
audits.r2: Use of ventilation modes supporting all breaths increased to 56%

audits.t: An Audit Reviewing the Efficacy of the PROPEL Implant in Patients with Chronic Rhinosinusitis (CRS) with Frontal Sinus Disease that Underwent Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery/Computer Assisted Sinus Surgery (FESS/CASS) Between September 2021 and October 2023 in N.
audits.tp: PROPEL implant outcomes in chronic rhinosinusitis with frontal sinus disease
audits.st: Minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for SNOT-22 score taken as 9(8)
audits.f: Average reduction in SNOT22 score was 38 (range 1-75), an average percentage reduction of 70%; no significant complications reported

audits.t: Do Africans really need to go overseas for Phaco training? Performance audit of a locally trained phaco surgeon in rural Kenya
audits.tp: Phacoemulsification cataract surgery outcomes after local training
audits.st: WHO recommendations for cataract surgery outcomes
audits.f: Majority of eyes (83.6%) had preoperative vision less than 6/18; surgical complications were not severe enough to affect final best-corrected visual acuity

audits.t: Ceasing oxytocin in the active phase of the first stage of induced labours: A prospective audit at a tertiary hospital
audits.tp: Oxytocin cessation policy in induced labour
audits.st: Local policy based on randomised trial evidence that ceasing oxytocin in active phase reduces uterine tachysystole/abnormal fetal heart rate
audits.f: Caesarean delivery 29%; oxytocin ceased for at least two hours or until birth in 13% of women
audits.c: Introduced a policy recommending cessation of oxytocin infusion in the active phase of the first stage of induced labour
audits.r2: Caesarean delivery 28% (p=0.77, not significant); oxytocin cessation compliance rose to 35%; instrumental birth for maternal indications increased from 6.8% to 13% (p=0.0005); median labour length increased by one hour (5.4 vs 6.4 hours, p=0.006); maternal satisfaction modestly lower (median 41 vs 38, p=0.03)

audits.t: General practitioners' management of patients with psychological stress: audit results from Denmark.
audits.tp: GP management of patients with psychological stress
audits.st: not reported (descriptive audit of management patterns, no explicit target standard)
audits.f: Sick leave given in 54%, counselling 47%, pharmaceutical treatment 37%, referral to psychologist 38%; cause considered work-related in 69%

audits.t: Laparoscopic Colectomy in a Rural Australian Centre: A 10-Year Retrospective Audit of Safety and Operative Outcomes
audits.tp: Laparoscopic colectomy safety and operative outcomes
audits.st: Australia and New Zealand Bowel Cancer Outcomes Registry national benchmarks
audits.f: Laparoscopic or hybrid approach completed in 78.5% of cases; surgical complications 12.1%, anastomotic leak 3.7%; 30-day mortality 0.9%; mean lymph node yield 18.1, clear margins in 93.5% of malignant cases

audits.t: Early CPAP reduced mortality in covid-19 patients. Audit results from Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
audits.tp: Early CPAP timing and mortality in COVID-19
audits.st: not reported (local practice comparison of early vs late CPAP)
audits.f: Early CPAP (within 48 hours of admission) associated with better outcome/lower mortality than late CPAP (more than 48 hours after admission)

audits.t: Assessment of adherence level for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia management by various physicians in ‎Iraq: a multi-clinic study.
audits.tp: Physician adherence to neonatal hyperbilirubinemia management guidelines
audits.st: WHO, AAP and NICE guidelines for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia management
audits.f: Correct test-case management: 91.7% pediatricians, 58.9% GPs, 38.1% emergency physicians; bilirubin testing before discharge: 91.7% PDs, 5.5% GPs, 0% EPs

audits.t: Low serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25[OH]D) levels in patients hospitalised with COVID-19 are associated with greater disease severity: results of a local audit of practice
audits.tp: Vitamin D deficiency treatment protocol adherence in COVID-19
audits.st: Local protocol for treatment of vitamin D deficiency in hospitalised COVID-19 patients
audits.f: 55.8% of eligible patients received colecalciferol replacement, not always loaded as rapidly as protocol suggested; no new hypercalcaemia occurred following treatment

audits.t: Using Audit and Feedback and the Benchmark to Enhance Infection Prevention and Control of Multidrug Resistant Organisms: a Quasi-experiment Study
audits.tp: Infection prevention and control audit and feedback for multidrug-resistant organisms
audits.st: 40-item institutional infection prevention and control (IPC) implementation checklist for multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs)
audits.f: Implementation compliance ranged from 50.24% (doctors' use of personal protective equipment, lowest) to 96.46% (nurses' isolation warning signs, highest) across 40 IPC indicators.
audits.c: Multimodal audit-and-feedback intervention: twice-weekly checklist-based audits with immediate verbal feedback and monthly/quarterly written feedback benchmarking hospitals against each other.
audits.r2: Incidence of nosocomial MDROs decreased by 19.39%, 20.55% and 24.03% in hospitals A, B and C respectively; hand hygiene, environmental cleaning, patient/relative education and timely specimen sending were significantly associated with reduced incidence (all p<0.05).

audits.t: Knowledge and Compliance with Covid-19 Infection Prevention and Control measures among Health Workers in Regional Referral Hospitals in Northern Uganda: A cross-sectional Online Survey
audits.tp: COVID-19 infection prevention and control knowledge and compliance
audits.st: Local/institutional COVID-19 IPC guidelines; sufficient knowledge defined as ≥80% correct responses, adequate compliance as ≥75% of maximum score
audits.f: 69% of health workers had good knowledge of COVID-19 IPC and 68% had good compliance; good compliance was significantly associated with IPC training (p=0.039), access to IPC at work stations (p=0.036) and institutional support (p=0.031); no significant relationship between knowledge and compliance (p=0.007)

audits.t: Interactive Participatory Audit and Feedback (IPAF): Theory-based development and multi-site implementation outcomes with specialty clinic staff
audits.tp: Interactive participatory audit and feedback for CVD risk-reduction protocol adoption
audits.st: CVD risk-reduction protocols/evidence-based practices (specific target not stated in abstract)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Interactive Participatory Audit and Feedback (IPAF): theory-based individual monthly facilitation sessions and monthly feedback emails for frontline specialty-clinic staff.

audits.t: Improving vitamin D testing and supplementation in children with newly diagnosed cancer: A quality improvement initiative at Rady Children's Hospital San Diego.
audits.tp: Vitamin D testing and supplementation in childhood cancer
audits.st: Vitamin D testing and supplementation target >=80% for children aged 2-18 years with newly diagnosed cancer
audits.f: 4/26 (15%) had baseline vitamin D testing; 2/26 (8%) received appropriate supplementation
audits.c: Institutional vitamin D guideline, clinical decision tree, EMR triggers and automated testing options developed via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: 32/33 (97%) had testing; 33/33 (100%) received appropriate supplementation and timely follow-up testing; change sustained over 24 months

audits.t: The left outflow tract in foetal echocardiography screening: an audit of practices and quality criteria.
audits.tp: Fetal echocardiography left ventricular outflow tract screening quality
audits.st: French National Conference on Obstetrical and Foetal Ultrasound recommendations (since 2016) including left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) examination, assessed via 7 quality criteria scored 0-1
audits.f: Average LVOT quality score 5.49/7 (95% CI 5.36-5.62); LVOT images present in ultrasound reports in >93% of cases.
audits.c: Introduction of formal LVOT quality criteria into fetal echocardiography screening recommendations (2016).
audits.r2: Average LVOT quality score 5.91/7 (95% CI 5.80-6.03) in 2017 and 5.70/7 (95% CI 5.58-5.82) in 2020; no significant change 2017 vs 2020 (p=0.054).

audits.t: Effectiveness of prospective audit-and-feedback intervention in promoting appropriate third-generation cephalosporin use at a tertiary public hospital in Malaysia
audits.tp: Antimicrobial stewardship audit and feedback for third-generation cephalosporin prescribing
audits.st: National Antimicrobial Guidelines (NAG) and antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) team recommendations for third-generation cephalosporin use and timely culture and sensitivity (C&S) testing
audits.f: Appropriate cephalosporin use in 77.1% (54/70) of cases; timely C&S testing performed in 38.6% (27/70) of cases.
audits.c: Prospective audit-and-feedback by a ward pharmacist with a 2-hour feedback session presenting findings to prescribers.
audits.r2: Appropriate cephalosporin use increased to 95.8% (67/70, p=0.001); timely C&S testing increased to 58.6% (41/70, p=0.018).

audits.t: Impact of long-term care facility size on preparedness and adherence to infection prevention and control guidance for the mitigation of COVID-19
audits.tp: Infection prevention and control preparedness in long-term care facilities

audits.f: 308/362 (85.1%) facilities adhered to 14 or more recommendations (excellent); only 3 facilities classed as poorly adherent; larger facilities had lower adherence to screening visitors for COVID-19 symptoms (p=0.037) and to isolating patients until 2 negative tests (p=0.032) than medium/small facilities

audits.f: 77% vomited, 61% had large vomits
audits.r2: 53% vomited, 29% had large vomits; time to establish feeding and postoperative stay were comparable between groups

audits.t: Soft tissue sarcoma--compliance with guidelines.
audits.tp: Soft tissue sarcoma diagnostic guideline adherence
audits.st: Diagnostic guidelines for soft tissue sarcoma (biopsy before resection)
audits.f: Adherence to diagnostic guidelines significantly better in specialised centre; district hospitals treating <15 patients over 7 years significantly more often had inadequate or no biopsy before resection

audits.t: Use of clinical pictures in the management of nausea and vomiting: a prospective audit.
audits.tp: Nausea and vomiting management guideline in palliative care
audits.st: Local guideline for management of nausea and vomiting using clinical pictures to guide diagnosis and treatment
audits.f: Commonest clinical pictures were gastric stasis/outlet obstruction (35%) and chemical/metabolic (30%); nausea abolished in 28 of 34 cases (82%), vomiting resolved completely in 26 of 31 cases (84%); symptoms totally controlled in a mean of 3.4 days

audits.t: Retrospective audit of standards and quality in colposcopy services in a district hospital.
audits.st: National Health Service Cervical Screening Programme (NHSCSP) standards for colposcopy
audits.f: Deficiencies found in communication of clinic appointments for women with high-grade cytology and in information given to GPs about results; services fell short of standards in recording of colposcopy findings and grading of lesions; remaining audited parameters reached NHSCSP standards

audits.t: 'Change to cup': an audit to determine parental awareness and practices in changing from bottle to cup.
audits.st: Recommendation to introduce cup from 6 months and discontinue bottle after 1 year
audits.f: 8% of infants aged 12-28 months used bottle only, 62% used both; only 18% of parents thought a cup could be introduced as early as 6 months

audits.t: Ice machines--an audit of their use in clinical practice.
audits.tp: Ice machine management in clinical settings
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Audit highlighted the need to implement local policies for the purchase, use and maintenance of ice machines to reduce risk of nosocomial infection

audits.t: Public health physicians who contribute to on-call communicable disease control duties: national comparative clinical audit by questionnaire survey.
audits.tp: On-call communicable disease control knowledge assessment
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall scores ranged from 15% to 89%, mean 63%; highest in Consultants in Communicable Disease Control (70.9%), lowest in those not normally involved in on-call (56.1%)

audits.t: An audit of the use of antirheumatic drugs in a north Indian referral hospital.
audits.st: Standard international practice for antirheumatic drug use
audits.f: Prescribing pattern (NSAIDs, DMARDs, steroids; diclofenac and chloroquine most used) found to follow standard practices followed internationally

audits.t: Mini-audits facilitate quality assurance in outpatient units.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean PACU stay 91+/-55.3 min, about twice as long as other units; higher rates of hypotension, hypothermia and excessive pain than other centres

audits.t: The comparative study for quality of trauma treatment before and after the revision of trauma audit filter, Khon Kaen hospital 1998.
audits.tp: Trauma audit filter and preventable death rate
audits.st: Trauma audit filter (32 items)
audits.f: Higher preventable death rate and more pitfalls in trauma treatment before revision
audits.c: Revision of the trauma audit filter using participatory action research
audits.r2: Preventable death rate fell to 2%; physician compliance with 23 of 32 audit filter items exceeded 80%

audits.t: Quality improvement report: Linking guideline to regular feedback to increase appropriate requests for clinical tests: blood gas analysis in intensive care.
audits.st: Guideline for appropriate arterial blood gas analysis requests
audits.f: Baseline rate of 8.2 tests per patient day
audits.c: New multidisciplinary guideline, educational sessions and monthly feedback on adherence
audits.r2: Tests per patient day decreased to 4.8 with increased proportion of tests complying with the guideline, without affecting safety indicators

audits.t: An audit of blood cross-match ordering practices at the Aga Khan University Hospital: first step towards a Maximum Surgical Blood Ordering Schedule.
audits.st: Cross-matched to transfused (C/T) ratio ideally 2-2.5
audits.f: 97.56% of patients had C/T ratio higher than 2.5; only 21.11% of a subset had Transfusion Index above 0.5

audits.t: An audit of root canal treatment performed by undergraduate students.
audits.st: Not reported (internal categorisation of radiographic quality and root filling position)
audits.f: Postoperative radiograph available in 97% of cases; try-in point radiograph unavailable in one-fifth of cases; only 27 teeth (13%) categorised as satisfactory for radiographic quality and root filling position; overall technical quality of root canal treatment was poor

audits.t: First episode of psychosis - an audit of service engagement and management at 1-2 year follow-up.
audits.tp: First episode psychosis follow-up service engagement
audits.st: Locally-developed audit standards from literature review and colleague consultation
audits.f: Engagement standard met in 91%, maintenance medication standard met in 91%; 42-63% received psychological, family or educational interventions; less than half had structured daytime activity

audits.t: Audit of acute pancreatitis management: a tale of two hospitals.
audits.tp: Acute pancreatitis management against national guidelines
audits.st: UK guidelines for acute pancreatitis management
audits.f: Severe pancreatitis in 15.8% teaching hospital vs 15.3% DGH; 4 deaths at each hospital; Glasgow prognostic criteria completed within 48h in 43% (teaching) and 48% (DGH); cholecystectomy within 4 weeks in 5/25 (teaching) and 4/18 (DGH)

audits.t: Quality improvement report: Effect of a formal education programme on safety of transfusions.
audits.tp: Blood transfusion identification and monitoring compliance
audits.st: National guidelines on identification and monitoring of patients receiving transfusions
audits.f: Baseline audit found appreciable and avoidable failures in correct identification and monitoring of patients receiving transfusions (specific percentages not reported)
audits.c: Education programme: clinical skills package based on best practice for transfusion, delivered by a transfusion nurse specialist with trained instructors and display of standard operating procedures in clinical areas
audits.r2: Improvement in compliance with national guidelines to over 95% in six of seven recommendations on best practice

audits.t: Acetylcholinesterase treatment--modelling potential demand and auditing practice.
audits.tp: Cholinesterase inhibitor prescribing for Alzheimer's disease
audits.st: Eligibility criteria and prescribing practice agreed between clinicians and funders
audits.f: Estimated demand 89 patient-years of therapy vs 24.5 patient-years actually received, shortfall due to low referral rates; prescribing by clinicians matched practice guidelines; high proportion of 3-monthly assessments (cognition, function, global state) performed

audits.t: Evaluation of the management of optic neuritis: audit on the neurological and ophthalmological practice in the north west of England.
audits.tp: Optic neuritis management practice (neurology vs ophthalmology)
audits.st: Optic Neuritis Treatment Trial (ONTT) recommendations
audits.f: 65% of neurologists vs 46% of ophthalmologists would investigate further; 55% of neurologists vs 9% of ophthalmologists chose IV methylprednisolone (p<0.005); 64% of ophthalmologists vs 32% of neurologists chose no steroids (p<0.025)

audits.t: An audit of the Scoliosis Service at Hospital Kuala Lumpur.
audits.tp: Scoliosis service presentation and follow-up compliance
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 68.1% idiopathic, 10.4% neuromuscular, 14.8% congenital scoliosis; 25.5% had surgery, 10.4% brace, 69.1% observed; congenital scoliosis patients had better follow-up compliance

audits.t: Monitoring service development through audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of anticoagulant therapy and acute hospital admissions.
audits.st: Therapeutic international normalized ratio (INR) range
audits.f: 74 patients had therapeutic INR (4, 5.4%, bled from unrelated causes); 29 patients were over-anticoagulated (17, 59%, admitted with bleeding, 1 had very high INR without bleeding); 22 of 1480 admissions (1.5%) were due to warfarin complications and 16 of 21 bleeding patients had INR>4.5; causes of over-anticoagulation: poor compliance 31%, other medications 17%, congestive heart failure 28%, unknown 24%

audits.t: One-stop neck lump clinic: phase 2 of audit. How are we doing?
audits.tp: One-stop neck lump clinic waiting time
audits.st: British Association of Otorhinolaryngologists, Head and Neck Surgeons (BAO-HNS) recommended waiting time
audits.f: Waiting time to be seen was longer than recommended by BAO-HNS
audits.c: Measures implemented to reduce waiting time, including modification of the means of referral
audits.r2: Phase 2 audit assessed whether modified referral reduced waiting time and whether clinical performance from phase 1 was maintained or improved; specific numeric results not given in the abstract

audits.t: The Camino intracranial pressure sensor: is it optimal technology? An internal audit with a review of current intracranial pressure monitoring technologies.
audits.st: Manufacturer's specifications for static and dynamic calibration
audits.f: Zero drift range -13 to 22 mmHg (median -1 mmHg); 50% of devices tested for zero drift had absolute drift of at least 3 mmHg; 5 sensors (10%) failed during monitoring and were replaced; static and dynamic calibration within manufacturer specifications, but sensitivity to environmental temperature remains a problem

audits.t: Audit of investigation of subclinical hypothyroidism in Scottish laboratories.
audits.st: Standards derived from guidelines in current published literature for interpretation of thyroid function tests
audits.f: Significant differences found between laboratories in tests and strategies used; advice given was generally accurate and helpful but showed marked variation in interpretative comments

audits.t: A prospective, physician self-reported adverse incident audit on a general medical unit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: One-third of incidents occurred within 48h of hospitalisation; half associated with harm or inconvenience

audits.t: Pathways for continence care: background and audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline audit demonstrated that little advice or treatment was actually reaching the patient

audits.t: Death certification: an audit of practice entering the 21st century.
audits.st: Royal College recommendations and minimally accepted death certification standard
audits.f: Only 55% of certificates completed to a minimally accepted standard, many failing to allow adequate ICD-10 coding; nearly 10% completed to a poor standard (illogical or inappropriate)

audits.t: Preventing unnecessary suffering: an audit of a leg ulcer clinic.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Implementation of evidence-based follow-up assessment for patients with a history of venous ulceration resulted in successful prevention of leg ulcer recurrence (numbers not reported)

audits.t: Prospective audit of gastroscopy under the 'three-day rule': a regional initiative in Italy to reduce waiting time for suspected malignancy.
audits.tp: Three-day rule for urgent gastroscopy referral
audits.st: Regional 'three-day rule': diagnostic procedure within three working days of GP referral for suspected malignancy
audits.f: Significantly more oesophageal/gastric cancers (6% vs 1%) and serious benign disease diagnosed in three-day rule group than routine referrals

audits.t: An audit of the use of self-administered adrenaline syringes in patients with angio-oedema.
audits.tp: Self-administered adrenaline syringe use for angio-oedema/anaphylaxis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 3/29 (10%) prescribed syringes without a severe angio-oedema/collapse indication; only 14/25 (56%) demonstrated could perform all steps correctly; only 6/26 (23%) told to call an ambulance after use
audits.c: Developed a more detailed patient information leaflet; patients shown syringe use again at follow-up

audits.t: Safe transition from open to laparoscopic fundoplication by an established consultant--the importance of repeated audit.
audits.tp: Safe transition from open to laparoscopic fundoplication
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline reflux control, dysphagia rates and length of stay (median 7 days) documented
audits.c: Consultant training in laparoscopic fundoplication technique
audits.r2: No significant difference in relief of reflux; shorter postoperative stay (median 2 vs 7 days)

audits.t: A multidisciplinary audit of patients' seating needs.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit to improve use of central venous catheters.
audits.st: Current good practice guidelines for central venous catheter management
audits.f: Audit measured practice against current good practice guidelines, focusing on infection rates, aseptic technique and training

audits.t: Retinopathy of prematurity in the UK II: audit of national guidelines for screening and treatment.
audits.tp: Retinopathy of prematurity screening guideline adherence
audits.st: National guidelines for screening of retinopathy of prematurity (1990) and for screening and treatment (1995)
audits.f: 77% of ophthalmologists complied with or exceeded recommendations for determining which babies required screening, 7% used criteria resulting in substantially fewer babies being screened; only 17% of units and 12% of ophthalmologists provided written information for parents; lack of clarity about responsibility for continuation of screening on transfer or discharge

audits.t: Audit of aminoglycosides usage.
audits.st: Aminoglycoside prescribing guidelines
audits.f: Appropriateness was 72% for indication, 86% for dose, 85% for duration, 43% for safety and 53% for cost effectiveness

audits.t: Why catheterize?: audit findings on the use of urinary catheters.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 37.5% (27) catheterised for urinary incontinence, 64.7% (33) catheterised by nurses; 15 patients had no plan of care for the catheter, only 8 had a plan for catheter removal

audits.t: An audit of oxygen therapy on the medical ward in 2 different hospitals in Central Saudi Arabia.
audits.tp: Oxygen therapy appropriateness on medical wards
audits.st: Target oxygen saturation 92%-94% with titration
audits.f: Oxygen saturation was excessive (>97%) in 54.6% of patients and adequate (92-97%) in 40.7%; oxygen prescription was sub-optimal in both hospitals

audits.t: Audit of suspected meningitis in a district in 1996-1997 and in 1999.
audits.st: Public Health Laboratory Service guidance on investigation and public health action for meningococcal disease
audits.f: Penicillin before admission 22.4%; CSF microscopy requests 31%; blood PCR 34.5%; throat swab 25.9%; notification within 24 hours 42.8%
audits.r2: Penicillin before admission 7.1% (p=0.12); CSF microscopy 17.6%; blood PCR 64.7% (p<0.001); throat swab 55.9% (p<0.005); notification within 24 hours 52.9%

audits.t: Incomplete excision of basal cell carcinomas: a retrospective audit.
audits.tp: Basal cell carcinoma management and histology reporting
audits.st: Incomplete excision of skin malignancy, a clinical indicator of the Royal Australasian College of Surgeons/Australian Council on Healthcare Standards
audits.f: Overall rate of incomplete excision was 6.3% (223 of 3558), compared favourably with reported literature rates of 5-25%

audits.t: National audit of citrate toxicity in plateletpheresis donors.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Incidence of severe citrate toxicity was 0.03% of procedures, comparable to the incidence of severe fainting following whole blood donation

audits.t: Practice audits: reliability of sphygmomanometers and blood pressure recording bias.
audits.tp: Sphygmomanometer accuracy and blood pressure recording digit bias
audits.st: British Standard BS 2743 (1990) for sphygmomanometer accuracy (error greater than 10 mmHg defined as inaccurate)
audits.f: 17% of sphygmomanometers were inaccurate (4% with error greater than 10 mmHg): 1% of mercury and 10% of aneroid devices had error greater than 10 mmHg; 12% (16) were so deteriorated that immediate withdrawal was recommended; blood pressure recording audit showed digit bias to the nearest 10 mmHg for both systolic and diastolic readings

audits.t: Severe acute alcoholic hepatitis: an audit of medical treatment.
audits.tp: Treatment outcomes for severe acute alcoholic hepatitis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall mortality 26% (11/43); only 5 treated with steroids (1 died, 20% mortality); liver biopsy performed in 19/43 (12/19 had cirrhosis)

audits.t: Audit of attendance rates for an infra-inguinal graft surveillance programme--how complete is your graft surveillance?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Partial surveillance attendance rate rose from 31% to 78%; complete surveillance attendance rate rose from 0% to 38% over the 5 years; attendance rates were much lower than expected

audits.t: An email audit of prehospital doctor activity in an area of the West Midlands.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Nearly half of calls were to road traffic accidents; midazolam and ketamine commonly administered

audits.t: Effectiveness and relevance of MR acceptance testing: results of an 8 year audit.
audits.st: Acceptance testing criteria for new clinical MRI equipment (schedule presented in the study)
audits.f: Signal-to-noise ratio and geometric linearity were the parameters most likely to fail; 69% of these received successful corrective action; non-uniformity, ghosting and poor fat suppression were next most common but less successfully corrected; 49% of all non-compliant parameters received verifiable corrective action; parameter failure rates did not improve with time; safety audit of 11 installations found inadequate suite layout and poor use of signs to be the most common failings (mean 5 safety issues per installation from a 100-point questionnaire)

audits.t: An audit of first aid qualifications and knowledge among team officials in two English youth football leagues: a preliminary study.
audits.tp: First aid qualification and knowledge among youth sports officials
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 52 of 86 respondents did not have a current first aid qualification; only 12% and 38% gave the correct response to the 'choking' and 'unconscious' injury scenarios respectively; health/injury records kept by 40% and 19% of teams respectively; written parental consent to emergency treatment obtained by 30%

audits.t: Attributes of clinical recommendations that influence change in practice following audit and feedback.
audits.tp: Attributes of guideline recommendations influencing compliance after audit and feedback
audits.st: 42 locally developed clinical practice recommendations covering selected gynaecological topics
audits.f: Baseline compliance with 42 recommendations collected using standardised case-note abstraction
audits.c: Feedback of performance summaries to consultant gynaecologists in each hospital
audits.r2: Recommendations compatible with clinician values and not requiring changes to fixed routines were associated with greater compliance at baseline and follow-up; recommendations incompatible with clinician values were associated with greater change in practice following audit and feedback

audits.t: The assessment and management of strabismus and amblyopia: a national audit.
audits.tp: Strabismus and amblyopia assessment services (national survey)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 66% used orthoptic assessment without refraction, 66% combined orthoptist/ophthalmologist assessment, 22% entirely orthoptist/optometric system; ophthalmologists involved in initial assessment in 67% of units; considerable variation in tests used for visual acuity; LogMAR-based tests not routinely used in 75% of units

audits.t: Failure to administer methylprednisolone for acute traumatic spinal cord injury-a prospective audit of 100 patients from a regional spinal injuries unit.
audits.tp: Methylprednisolone administration for acute spinal cord injury
audits.st: NASCIS II/III protocols for methylprednisolone in acute traumatic spinal cord injury
audits.f: Only 25% received methylprednisolone correctly per NASCIS protocol at the referring hospital; an additional 10 patients received it incorrectly

audits.t: An audit of urodynamic standardization in the West Midlands, UK.
audits.st: Locally agreed guidelines for urodynamic practice (zeroing transducer to atmospheric pressure, 50 mL/min filling rate, ICS definition of detrusor instability)
audits.f: Initial survey found interest in standardising urodynamic practice; simple guidelines were proposed
audits.r2: 8 of 17 still zeroed to the patient (only 1 unit changed to zeroing to atmospheric pressure); varied filling rates still used; only 8 participants used ICS criteria to diagnose detrusor instability; 3 of 17 did not feel standardisation was achievable; no significant changes had been made since guidelines were issued

audits.t: National audit of the management of peritonsillar abscess.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average 29 cases treated per department per year, 94% managed as inpatients; main initial treatment was needle aspiration with intravenous antibiotics; departments treating over 20 cases/year more likely to use needle aspiration; England/Wales departments used more incision and drainage than Scotland; median hospital stay 2 days

audits.t: Percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy: a prospective audit of the impact of guidelines in two district general hospitals in the United Kingdom.
audits.tp: PEG insertion guideline impact on patient selection
audits.st: Locally constructed guidelines for appropriate patient selection for percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) insertion
audits.f: Hospital A (guidelines introduced): number of PEG insertions fell by 20; mortality 16% at 1 month, 26% at 3 months, 39% at 6 months, 46% at 1 year
audits.c: Construction and introduction of guidelines for PEG insertion patient selection at Hospital A (Rotherham District General Hospital)
audits.r2: Hospital B (no guidelines, Doncaster Royal Infirmary): PEG insertion rate continued to rise (p=0.02); mortality 26% at 1 month, 44% at 3 months, 58% at 6 months, 68% at 1 year; trend toward lower mortality with guidelines did not reach statistical significance (log rank test, p=0.1)

audits.t: The Data Protection Act 1998: an audit of its effect on surgical trainees' practice.
audits.tp: Data Protection Act 1998 compliance among surgical trainees
audits.st: Data Protection Act 1998 (eight principles)
audits.f: Knowledge of the Act was patchy and adherence to its principles was minimal among surgical specialist registrars surveyed

audits.t: Quality improvement report: Effect of a multifaceted approach to detecting and managing depression in primary care.
audits.tp: Depression detection and management in primary care
audits.st: Practice-developed clinical management guideline for depression, within a chronic disease management approach
audits.f: Baseline detection and management of depression assessed before the intervention (specific figures not reported)
audits.c: Multifaceted intervention: case register for depression, education and training programme on detection and management, facilitation of meetings with secondary care staff, and support in developing a practice guideline
audits.r2: Practice A (six partners, affluent population): case detection rate improved by 23%, prescribing of sub-therapeutic antidepressant doses reduced by 36%, adherence to preferred treatment regimens achieved; Practice B (three partners, deprived urban population): improved sensitivity of case detection but reduced specificity, did not reach consensus on its own guideline and was unable to sustain the model

audits.t: European audit of current practice in diagnosis and treatment of childhood growth hormone deficiency.
audits.tp: Growth hormone deficiency diagnosis and treatment practice
audits.st: Growth Hormone Research Society guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of GH deficiency
audits.f: 80% included IGF-I in initial evaluation; 68% confirmed diagnosis with two provocative tests; only 63% knew their GH assay and 57% knew its calibration

audits.t: An audit of the current consent practices of consultant orthodontists in the UK.
audits.tp: Consent practice for orthodontic and joint orthognathic treatment
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Written information on orthodontic treatment provided by 56%, written consent obtained by 41%; written information on joint orthognathic treatment provided by 47.5%, joint written consent obtained by 20%; 35% provided neither written information nor sought written consent for either treatment

audits.t: An audit of Territorial Army Medical Grades on presentation for mobilisation and full time reserve service at RTMC Chilwell.
audits.tp: Territorial Army medical grading accuracy audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Downgrading rate 18% among Territorial Army personnel compared with 6-6.5% in Regular Army personnel; errors in entry medical assessments found in 44% of records

audits.t: "It's good to talk"--an audit of the communication of post-operative thromboembolic complications.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Operating surgeon unaware of 87% of pulmonary embolism cases and 20% of DVT cases occurring post-discharge

audits.t: Don't wait for a sensory level--listen to the symptoms: a prospective audit of the delays in diagnosis of malignant cord compression.
audits.tp: Delay in diagnosis of malignant spinal cord compression
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 82% unable to walk or only able with help at diagnosis; pain reported by 94%, present for a median of 90 days, severe in 84%; median interval from GP presentation to confirmed diagnosis 66 days; plain films and bone scans predicted the level of compression accurately in only 21% and 19% of cases respectively

audits.t: Audit of emergency theatre utilisation.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 38% of booked patients had surgery performed; mean theatre utilisation 26.9% (range 5-50%)

audits.t: A seven-year audit of a diarrhoea training unit (DTU) in Port Harcourt, Nigeria.
audits.tp: Diarrhoea training unit case management outcomes
audits.st: Predetermined case-management performance indicators for the DTU
audits.f: Case-fatality rate 6 per 1000 in 1993
audits.c: Ongoing case management training and ORS use in the DTU
audits.r2: Case-fatality rate fell to 0.6 per 1000; severe dehydration cases eight times fewer than in 1993

audits.t: An audit of forceps delivery in Trinidad.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall forceps rate 0.81%; chief indications were prolonged second stage and poor maternal effort

audits.t: An audit of patients investigated by laparoscopy and dye for infertility.
audits.tp: Infertility investigation guideline compliance (laparoscopy and dye)
audits.st: Recommended guidelines for investigation of infertility (preoperative assessment of ovulation and semen analysis)
audits.f: Preoperative assessment of ovulation not performed in 20 women, semen analysis not performed in 30; bilateral tubal patency demonstrated in 86 patients, bilateral blocked tubes in 3, unilateral occlusion in 11; no additional findings in 54%; within one year 20 women became pregnant, 18 delivered a baby, 2 had a miscarriage

audits.t: Monitoring compliance with the International Code of Marketing of Breastmilk Substitutes in west Africa: multisite cross sectional survey in Togo and Burkina Faso.
audits.tp: Compliance with breastmilk substitute marketing code
audits.st: International Code of Marketing of Breastmilk Substitutes
audits.f: 40 commercial breastmilk substitutes violated labelling standards; 90% of health providers had never heard of the code

audits.t: Melbourne vascular surgical association audit.
audits.st: Melbourne Vascular Surgical Association audit benchmark
audits.f: Excellent compliance from academic vascular units; risk-adjusted outcome comparisons across units showed consistent standard of care

audits.t: Incomplete excision of basal cell carcinoma: a prospective multicentre audit.
audits.tp: Basal cell carcinoma management and histology reporting
audits.st: Not reported (paper notes no national standard exists for incomplete excision rate)
audits.f: 34 lesions (4.5%) were incompletely excised; incidence 3.2% in the regional unit, 3.1% in the district general hospital, and 7.5% in the supraregional cancer hospital; commonest site for incomplete excision was the eyebrow, then postauricular area, nose and temple; grade of surgeon, minimal excision margin and histological subtype were independently associated with incomplete excision

audits.t: Audit of Finn Chamber patch test preparation.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Weight variance was not significant for 2 of 3 panels and for single Finn Chambers with allergen in petrolatum; variance was significant for single Finn Chambers with allergen in solution and for the third panel containing an allergen in solution

audits.t: The influence of new guidelines on cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) decisions. Five cycles of audit of a clerk proforma which included a resuscitation decision.
audits.st: National guidelines advising discussion with patients before issuing a 'do not attempt resuscitation' (DNAR) order
audits.f: CPR decisions documented in 27 (36%) discharges
audits.c: Introduction of a clerk proforma including a resuscitation decision section; the final (fifth) audit cycle followed the latest national guidelines
audits.r2: Documentation improved to 102/119 (86%); following introduction of the latest guidelines, the proportion of patients in whom a decision was made, and the percentage of those decisions that were DNAR, fell

audits.t: Urgent 2-week referrals for CNS/brain tumours: a retrospective audit.
audits.tp: 2-week wait referral system for CNS/brain tumours
audits.st: Department of Health 2-week referral guidelines for suspected cancer
audits.f: None had CNS/brain cancer
audits.r2: 30% of referrals did not follow Department of Health guidelines; only 9% actually had CNS tumours; at least 69 neurological cancers were identified independently of the system in the same period

audits.t: Paying for quality improvement: compliance with tobacco cessation guidelines.
audits.st: Tobacco treatment guideline (identification of smoking status and cessation counselling)
audits.f: Mean tobacco use identification 49%+/-7%
audits.c: Data feedback combined with a financial bonus incentive for outcomes recognition
audits.r2: Mean tobacco use identification increased to 73%+/-7%; number of medical groups achieving >80% identification and advice rose from 0 to 8

audits.t: Effectiveness of report cards based on chart audits of residents' adherence to practice guidelines on practice performance: a randomized controlled trial.
audits.st: Preventive health and disease management practice guidelines
audits.f: No significant differences in baseline performance between intervention and control residents
audits.c: Individualised 78-item report card feedback based on chart audits, randomised controlled trial
audits.r2: No significant differences in performance scores between residents receiving report cards and controls across immunisations, counselling, diabetes and hypertension management

audits.t: Audit in occupational medicine: an audit of fitness to drive among voluntary drivers in an NHS trust.
audits.tp: Fitness to drive assessment for voluntary NHS drivers
audits.st: DVLA Group 2 fitness to drive standards
audits.f: Mean age 66.4 years; average 1.9 medical problems per driver; 5 drivers found unfit for minibus driving, 1 unfit for car driving

audits.t: Occupational health management: an audit tool.
audits.tp: Occupational health management audit tool development
audits.st: UK Health & Safety Executive guidance on health and safety management
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of a behaviour modification program for weight management.
audits.tp: Behaviour modification programme for weight management
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An audit of the investigation and use of anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis in Tayside.
audits.st: National guidelines on investigation and management of RhD disease
audits.f: Anti-D used appropriately in all cases at delivery; 91% of those requiring anti-D received it within 24 hours; no fetomaternal haemorrhage assessment carried out in 11 of 45 (23.7%) eligible antenatal sensitising events
audits.c: An EDTA plasma gel-based antibody detection system was commissioned, allowing internal laboratory referral for fetomaternal haemorrhage assessment

audits.t: Audit of the diagnosis, assessment, and treatment of osteoporosis in patients with ankylosing spondylitis.
audits.tp: Osteoporosis assessment and management in ankylosing spondylitis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 98 respondents (31.6%) indicated that osteoporosis assessment formed part of their routine management of ankylosing spondylitis; DEXA was the technique of choice for 91.6%; dietary advice offered by 32.6%, exercise advice by 98.7%

audits.t: Prescription audit: experience in Garhwal (Uttaranchal), India.
audits.st: WHO prescribing indicators
audits.f: Average 3.65 drugs per prescription; 51% prescribed by generic name; diagnosis mentioned in only 22.25%; patient compliance 71.5%

audits.t: A national audit of chronic constipation in the community.
audits.tp: Chronic constipation and laxative prescribing in the community
audits.st: National bowel-care standards
audits.f: High level of faecal impaction and rectal intervention use; 42% on combination laxative therapy; evidence of complex, ineffective or inappropriate laxative prescribing

audits.t: Audit of scope and culture techniques applied to samples for the diagnosis of Mycobacterium bovis by hospital laboratories in England and Wales.
audits.st: Recommended use of a pyruvate-containing culture medium and a minimum incubation period of 8 weeks
audits.f: 20% of responding centres did not use a pyruvate-containing medium or did not incubate for the minimum recommended 8 weeks

audits.t: Use of audit tools to evaluate the efficacy of cleaning systems in hospitals.
audits.tp: Hospital cleaning efficacy audit tools (ACE vs SEC/PEA)
audits.st: Standards for Environmental Cleanliness (SEC) checklist; National Health Service patient environment audit (PEA); microbiologic benchmark values
audits.f: Visual assessment (used by SEC and PEA) indicated 90% of sites were satisfactory, whereas adenosine triphosphate bioluminescence showed 100% and microbiologic sampling showed 90% of sites did not meet benchmark values; no significant difference between SEC and PEA audits (P=0.311); the ACE audit tool showed a significant difference and gave a better assessment of cleaning efficacy than SEC or PEA

audits.t: The Scottish Programme for Clinical Effectiveness in Reproductive Health (SPCERH): lessons from a three-year programme.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Integrated programme of audit, guideline and educational activities disseminated via publications, presentations and interactive meetings

audits.t: National audit of the management of injured patients in 20 Scottish hospitals.
audits.st: National standards agreed and implemented by the Scottish Trauma Audit Group (STAG) in 1997, addressing recommendations of the Royal College of Surgeons working party (1988) and National Audit Office (1992)
audits.f: 73.5% of seriously injured patients presented outwith normal working hours; survival was 65.3% at the start of the six-year audit period among 23479 patients admitted for at least three days or who died
audits.c: Increased presence of consultants in accident and emergency medicine, anaesthetics and surgery over the audit period
audits.r2: Survival of seriously injured patients increased significantly to 75.6%, significantly better than the rest of the UK; no trimodal distribution of death was found

audits.t: An audit of the positive predictive value of high-grade dyskaryosis in cervical smears: 2001-2002.
audits.st: Positive predictive value of high-grade dyskaryosis for CIN2 or worse, published annually for laboratories in the UK National Health Service Cervical Screening Programme (NHSCSP)
audits.f: Positive predictive value of high-grade dyskaryosis for CIN2 or worse was as high as 91.6% for one consultant
audits.r2: PPV fell for four of the five consultants reporting cervical smears, the greatest fall being from 91.6% to 77.9%; mainly attributed to the type of biopsy taken at colposcopy

audits.t: An audit of a specialist registrar-run outpatient diagnostic hysteroscopy service in a district general hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Hysteroscopy performed satisfactorily in 91.1% of cases; pathology found in 39% (endometrial polyp 34.1%, submucous fibroid 7.3%); endometrial biopsy performed in 65.8% with no malignancies found

audits.t: An audit of post-splenectomy prophylaxis--are we following the guidelines?
audits.tp: Post-splenectomy vaccination and antibiotic prophylaxis compliance
audits.st: Published guidelines for immunisation and antibiotic prophylaxis post-splenectomy
audits.f: 72% vaccinated (30/76 pneumococcal+HIB+meningococcal, 15/76 Pneumovax+HIB, 10/76 Pneumovax only); 63% discharged on prophylactic antibiotics; 81% of survivors had adequate GP communication

audits.t: Troponin testing: an audit in three metropolitan hospitals.
audits.st: Protocol for troponin I assay use disseminated at introduction
audits.f: Single assay used in 55% of episodes, serial in 45%; serial troponin testing followed the protocol adequately but single assays were used extensively and probably inappropriately

audits.t: Prospective audit of adverse reactions occurring in 459 primary antibody-deficient patients receiving intravenous immunoglobulin.
audits.tp: Adverse reactions to intravenous immunoglobulin in primary antibody deficiency
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall reaction rate 0.8% (could have been 0.5% if predisposing factors considered); no severe reactions

audits.t: Introduction, audit and review of guidelines for delegated authorization of nuclear medicine investigations in compliance with the Ionising Radiation (Medical Exposure) Regulations 2000.
audits.tp: Delegated authorisation compliance for nuclear medicine referrals (IRMER)
audits.st: Ionising Radiation (Medical Exposure) Regulations 2000; local Delegated Authorization Guidelines (DAG)
audits.f: 437/632 (69%) referrals fitted the DAG; 12% (75) required clarification; 19% (120) were directly authorized by the practitioner
audits.c: DAG revised following review of non-matching referrals

audits.t: Stereotactic breast biopsy: an audit of 18 months at BreastScreen Auckland.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 10 (2%) failed, 70.7% benign, 10.3% ADH, 18.6% malignant; failure rate and complication rate (0.5%) comparable with published series

audits.t: Preventive medical care in remote Aboriginal communities in the Northern Territory: a follow-up study of the impact of clinical guidelines, computerised recall and reminder systems, and audit and feedback.
audits.st: Best practice guidelines for preventive medical services (developed and disseminated as part of the intervention)
audits.f: Baseline levels of preventive service delivery prior to the multifaceted intervention
audits.c: Development and dissemination of best practice guidelines, an electronic client register with recall and reminder systems, associated staff training, and regular audit and feedback of clinical records against the guidelines
audits.r2: Initial improvement in service delivery levels following the intervention for most services, but improvements were in general not fully sustained over the 3-year period; baseline and follow-up levels were in many cases higher than comparable North American/UK studies

audits.t: Early warning system scores and response times: an audit.
audits.st: Established response timescale for calls triggered by the modified early warning system (DMEWS) (specific target not stated)
audits.f: Response by members of the surgical teams to calls triggered by DMEWS was below the agreed standard response timescale

audits.t: Cold provocation testing and hand-arm vibration syndrome--an audit of the results of the Department of Trade and Industry scheme for the evaluation of miners.
audits.tp: Hand-arm vibration syndrome cold provocation test evaluation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: The cold provocation test with measurement of digital rewarming times was found to be of no value in assessing vibration-induced vascular damage to the hands

audits.t: An audit of medicolegal conferencing.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Prospective study of 50 consecutive medicolegal conferences found conferencing time-consuming and expensive, of limited value where little disagreement existed, and more effective when held in person than by telephone

audits.t: Pathways for continence care: an audit to assess how they are used.
audits.st: Guidelines for Continence Care (Department of Health, 2000) promoting use of care pathways
audits.f: Nearly half of respondents were currently using the continence care pathways and found them effective

audits.t: Audit of the care of women requesting induced abortion.
audits.st: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists Evidence-Based Guideline No. 7 (2000)
audits.f: Prospective audit of all induced abortions identified areas of practice not meeting RCOG guideline standards (details not reported)
audits.c: Department guidelines produced to address identified areas for improvement

audits.t: Auditing and improving notification and chemoprophylaxis in bacterial meningitis.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 28/79 (35%) cases notified; chemoprophylaxis given to 20/26 (77%) meningococcal cases, inappropriate drugs used in 4 cases, distributed too widely in 10 cases
audits.c: Clinician education in the hospital with poorest notification performance, and districtwide education on chemoprophylaxis
audits.r2: Significant improvement in notification in the targeted hospital, no change in control hospital; chemoprophylaxis improved districtwide, though rifampicin still distributed too widely

audits.t: Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance: audit and the impact of potential litigation. Retrospective review of 682 cases.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 28.6% of original Class III diagnoses were cytological overdiagnoses on retrospective review; 197 cases reclassified to Class II

audits.t: Offering the vaccine and accepting it: an audit of hepatitis B vaccination in West Midlands region.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B vaccination uptake in GUM clinics
audits.st: 1999 Medical Society for the Study of Venereal Disease National Guidelines
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An audit of the management of soft tissue sarcoma within a health region in the UK.
audits.tp: Soft tissue sarcoma referral and management pathway
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 49.5% first referred to general surgeons, 16% to orthopaedic surgeons; only 15% of patients fit for surgery were referred to a specialist sarcoma surgeon before definitive exploration; 64% of deep tumours had a preoperative biopsy and only 68% had a scan before biopsy or definitive surgery
audits.r2: Only a marginal improvement in management compared with the first audit

audits.t: Do peer chart audits improve residents' performance in providing preventive care?
audits.tp: Peer chart audit and preventive care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean total chart audit scores across five time blocks over 45 months; performance improved significantly then declined in last 10 months but remained higher than baseline.
audits.c: Peer chart audit programme in which residents scored each other on 12 clinical preventive services

audits.t: The use of record linkage for auditing the uptake and outcome of prenatal serum screening and prenatal diagnostic tests for Down syndrome.
audits.tp: Down syndrome prenatal screening programme audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall uptake of serum screening 58%, uptake of prenatal diagnosis 4% (54% after a positive screen); detection rate 49%, false-positive rate 4%, odds of being affected after a positive result 1:59
audits.r2: Detection rate rose to 78%, false-positive rate 7%, odds of being affected after a positive result 1:58; using maternal age alone (cut-off >=37) would have given 40% detection and 7-9% false-positive rates across both periods

audits.t: Two-stage hypospadias repair: audit in a district general hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Audit of van der Meulen single-stage hypospadias repairs found an unsatisfactory revision rate of 11% and sub-optimal cosmetic result
audits.c: Senior surgeon retrained and changed to the two-stage Bracka technique from 1995
audits.r2: Primary repairs (n=81): stage I graft loss 2.5%, stage II complication rate 9.8% (fistula 7.4%, stenosis 1.2%, baggy urethra 1.2%); revision group with prior unsatisfactory single-stage repairs (n=31): graft loss 10%, fistula 12.9%, stenosis 6.5%

audits.t: The usefulness of routine preoperative chest X-rays and ECGs: a prospective audit.
audits.tp: Routine preoperative CXR and ECG audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 11/324 CXRs and 13/375 ECGs affected anaesthetic technique or choice of therapeutic procedure.

audits.t: Subclinical hypothyroidism: an audit of management.
audits.st: Thyroxine recommended if serum TSH is 10 mU/L or more, or 5-9.9 mU/L (mild subclinical hypothyroidism) with risk factors such as thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb) positivity
audits.f: TPOAb and goitre status were both determined in only 39% of subjects with mild subclinical hypothyroidism overall; determined more often by endocrinologists than general physicians (TPOAb 63% vs 22%; goitre 47% vs 17%, P = 0.001); endocrinologists treated 96% of eligible subjects with mild SH versus 67% treated by non-endocrine colleagues (P = 0.024)

audits.t: An audit of the management of induced abortion in England and Wales.
audits.st: Agreed audit criteria assessed via single-round questionnaire, prior to publication of the RCOG evidence-based guideline
audits.f: Standards of care were generally appropriate but areas for improvement were identified: choice of method, infection screening and delays in referral; unnecessary investigations such as cross-matching remained evident; only half of units audited their own procedures and complications

audits.t: Audit of surgeon awareness of readmissions with venous thrombo-embolism.
audits.tp: Surgeon awareness of postoperative VTE readmissions
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 34 unplanned readmissions with DVT/PE after surgery, 70.6% were readmitted under a different specialty, 8.8% under the same specialty but different surgeon, and 20.6% under the same surgeon; of 27 patients admitted under a different consultant, only 44.4% had documented evidence the original surgeon was aware of the readmission

audits.t: National biometry audit.
audits.st: Royal College of Ophthalmologists (RCOphth) biometry guidelines, including use of the Hoffer Q formula in eyes with axial lengths outside 22.0-26.0 mm
audits.f: Only 4% of departments adhered to RCOphth guidelines on formula selection by axial length; 17% still used the obsolete SRK II formula for all eyes; 36% used two or more formulae; only 37% of biometrists had attended external training courses; 71% of units claimed to audit refractive results but only 16% (17 departments) knew their percentage of eyes with a given prediction error

audits.t: National audit of women with abnormal cervical smears in New Zealand.
audits.st: National Cervical Screening Programme recommended assessment/treatment/follow-up times
audits.f: Initial assessment, treatment or follow-up fell outside recommended times in 17-35% of women; 72% of high-grade smears underwent treatment (91% excision biopsy).

audits.t: Social work and spiritual counseling: results of one state audit.
audits.tp: Social work and spiritual counseling regulatory compliance
audits.st: Federal and state regulations requiring social work and spiritual counseling services in hospice care
audits.f: State regulatory reports identified compliance issues with care planning, assessment and bereavement services for social workers and spiritual counsellors.

audits.t: Major complications after percutaneous nephrostomy-lessons from a department audit.
audits.st: Society of Cardiovascular and Interventional Radiology and American College of Radiology recommended threshold complication rates for percutaneous nephrostomy (major haemorrhage and sepsis)
audits.f: 10/318 (3.1%) cases sustained a major complication; major sepsis rate 2.2% and haemorrhage rate 0.6%, both within recommended threshold limits; complications were proportionately more common out of hours (6/105, 5.7%) than in hours (4/312, 1.8%; p=0.087); sepsis contributed to death in 2 of 10 cases

audits.t: Audit of consultant physicians' reply letters for referrals to clinics in a tertiary teaching hospital.
audits.st: Desirable attributes for specialist reply letters (diagnosis, management, investigations, prognosis, contingency plans, follow-up)
audits.f: 69 (56%) of 120 letters with diagnostic issues stated a diagnostic formulation; contingency plans in 13 (16%); prognosis mentioned in only 18 (9%); follow-up detailed in 123 (60%).

audits.t: Audit on flexible sigmoidoscopy for rectal bleeding in a district general hospital: are we over-loading the resources?
audits.tp: Flexible sigmoidoscopy use for rectal bleeding
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 18.9% of patients undergoing flexible sigmoidoscopy for rectal bleeding were under 45 years old; incidence of colorectal cancer and adenomatous polyps in this younger age group was very low

audits.t: Clinical pathway compliance and quality improvement.
audits.st: Documented compliance with a myocardial infarction clinical pathway
audits.f: Baseline documented pathway compliance 23%.
audits.c: Chart audit methodology used as part of a quality improvement process

audits.t: Achieving early surgery for undescended testes: quality improvement through a multifaceted approach to guideline implementation.
