audits.st: Surgery for undescended testes recommended before age 2 years
audits.f: Only 19% of boys had surgery by age 2 years; median age at surgery 4 years; late referral was the key reason.
audits.c: New GP referral guidelines (refer after 8-month check), parent information leaflet, amended personal child health record, and computer recall reminder to GPs
audits.r2: Median age at surgery reduced to 2.0 years.

audits.t: A prospective audit of the use of a buttress suture to reduce seroma formation following axillary node dissection without drains.
audits.tp: Seroma reduction after axillary node dissection
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Seroma rate without a drain or buttress suture was 52% (14/27) in patients with at least seven nodes in the axillary sample
audits.c: Buttress suture inserted between the axillary skin and chest wall to obliterate the axillary space after dissection
audits.r2: Seroma rate fell to 24% (9/37) with the buttress suture (P = 0.007)

audits.t: Post-exposure prophylaxis for human immunodeficiency virus infection in the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh--an audit.
audits.st: Lothian University NHS Trust protocols for post-exposure prophylaxis against blood-borne virus infections
audits.f: PEP offered to 22 (29%), accepted by 13 (59%); discontinued in 5/13 (38%) after source patient tested HIV-negative; only 11 (14%) attended serological testing 3+ months later; none seroconverted

audits.t: An audit of fresh frozen plasma usage in an acute general hospital in Singapore.
audits.st: College of American Pathologists 1994 criteria for FFP use
audits.f: Only 98 (27%) episodes were deemed appropriate; inappropriate use mainly for inadequately prolonged coagulation profiles or absence of bleeding/surgery.

audits.t: Paracetamol pro re nata orders: an audit.
audits.st: Hospital guidelines on the prescribing of paracetamol, compared with evidence-based practice
audits.f: 74% of all reviewed charts (of 313) had an order for paracetamol; in the audit of 100 children prescribed paracetamol PRN, only one physician had provided written indications for its use, and frequent miscommunication occurred between physicians and nurses about the order's intended meaning, with nurses tending to administer at lower temperatures than doctors intended

audits.t: Identifying the potential organ donor: an audit of hospital deaths.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 112 potential donors identified; 66 requests made, 39 consents (59% consent rate), 37 organ donors (33% of potential donors); 46 unrealised potential donors.

audits.t: Sequential audits of unacceptable delays in radiation therapy in Australia and New Zealand.
audits.st: Standard good practice times for starting radiotherapy
audits.f: One in three patients experienced unacceptable delay; only one in four started within standard good practice times; delays up to 151 days in Australia; >40% of curative, 30% of palliative and 56% of emergency treatments started outside standard times.

audits.t: Using statewide audit and feedback to improve hospital care in West Virginia.
audits.tp: Statewide quality indicator audit and feedback
audits.st: Quality indicators for AMI, heart failure, pneumonia, stroke and atrial fibrillation (Medicare Quality Improvement Organization programme)
audits.f: Baseline quality indicator performance before statewide feedback (not reported in detail).
audits.c: Written and orally presented statewide audit and feedback reports of quality performance
audits.r2: 14 of 15 quality indicators showed significant improvement; e.g. aspirin at discharge for AMI and pneumococcal vaccine for pneumonia improved by more than 10 percentage points.

audits.t: The evolution of a radiation safety audit program for a research institution.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Stage and treatment variation with age in postmenopausal women with breast cancer: compliance with guidelines.
audits.tp: Breast cancer stage and treatment variation by age
audits.st: not reported (comparison of guideline compliance between age groups)
audits.f: Women >70 presented with more advanced disease (12% metastatic/locally advanced vs 3%, P<0.02); higher mastectomy rate (57.5% vs 20.6%); more had no nodal surgery (6.7% vs 0.5%) or <4 nodes excised (10.7% vs 3.4%)

audits.t: Closing the feedback loop: an audit of the use of imiquimod for the treatment of genital warts.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall clinically confirmed complete clearance rate with imiquimod was 33% (81 treatment episodes); 37% in immunocompetent patients and 45% in those who tolerated treatment and returned for follow-up; 17% of patients did not return for full response assessment
audits.c: Clinic treatment guidelines for genital warts extended based on audit findings: imiquimod now offered after six or more episodes of failed other treatments, offered earlier for recurrent anogenital warts, and recommended as first-line therapy for multiple keratinized warts

audits.t: International Guidelines audit tool tested in Cambodia.
audits.tp: International Guidelines audit tool for HIV/AIDS human rights
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Preliminary findings from applying the audit tool in Cambodia, including government willingness to permit the audit and disseminate results.

audits.t: What do consultant occupational physicians do in the National Health Service? An audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average 18 hours face-to-face clinical work over 5 sessions (range 0-36 hours, 0-9 sessions)

audits.t: Arm position and blood pressure: an audit.
audits.tp: Blood pressure measurement arm position technique
audits.st: National/international guidance recommending the horizontal arm position for blood pressure measurement (specific document not stated)
audits.f: Only 8% and 4% of clinicians chose the horizontal arm position for sitting and standing patients respectively; marked variation in preferred arm position occurred within and between physicians, GPs and nurses, though about two-thirds used the same position sitting and standing

audits.t: Criteria for audit of annual reports on the public health: do they exist?
audits.tp: Audit criteria for annual public health reports
audits.st: Faculty of Public Health Medicine 'Toolbox' key indicators (common data set)
audits.f: Little agreement among Directors of Public Health on suitable audit criteria; Faculty Toolbox criteria considered unsuitable due to district diversity

audits.t: POSSUM--a model for surgical outcome audit in quality care.
audits.st: P-POSSUM predicted mortality (risk-adjusted benchmark)
audits.f: Observed mortality rates were not significantly different from P-POSSUM predicted rates across four risk groups, showing quality of care comparable to western series.

audits.t: Audit of severe acute morbidity in hypertensive pregnancies in a developing country.
audits.tp: Severe acute maternal morbidity in hypertensive pregnancy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Population-based incidence of hypertension 12%; SAMM incidence 3/1000 deliveries; MMR 42/100,000 deliveries; substandard care similar in SAMM, mortality and uncomplicated cases.

audits.t: An audit of the effectiveness of postoperative radiographs--do they make a difference?
audits.tp: Postoperative radiograph use after facial fracture repair
audits.st: Official guidelines that postoperative radiographs after facial fracture repair should not be used routinely, only when clinically indicated
audits.f: Only 3 of 257 patients (1.2%) returned to theatre within a month, in each case based on postoperative clinical findings; no patient returned to theatre solely on the evidence of an immediate postoperative radiograph

audits.t: Low vision service delivery: an audit of newly developed outreach clinics in Northern Ireland.
audits.st: Recommendations that low vision services be multi-professional, easily accessible, freely available to all with visual impairment, monitored by professional and patient groups, and responsive to user feedback
audits.f: Of 48 randomly selected clinic attendees, 58% were female, 56% were over 80 years, and 78% had age-related macular degeneration as the primary diagnosis; of 46 low vision aids issued at first appointment, 67% were illuminated stand magnifiers and 63% had magnification of x5 or less; 96% of patients reported benefiting from the service

audits.t: Audit of rabies post-exposure prophylaxis in England and Wales in 1990 and 2000.
audits.st: Department of Health recommendations for rabies post-exposure prophylaxis
audits.f: Prophylaxis issued to 656 people; vaccine issued for some 'no risk' exposures
audits.r2: Prophylaxis issued to 295 people; vaccine still issued for 15 'no risk' exposures including immunoglobulin in 6; delay before contacting PHLS fell (p=0.003)

audits.t: Prevention of perinatal hepatitis B transmission in a health authority area: an audit.
audits.tp: Perinatal hepatitis B prevention programme audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Antenatal HBV screening uptake 99.9%; vaccination completion rate 93%; only 50% of eligible infants tested for hepatitis carriage; none of those tested acquired HBV infection

audits.t: Changes in early psychosis service provision: a file audit.
audits.st: Australian clinical guidelines for early psychosis (27 clinical indicators)
audits.f: Baseline case-record audit against 27 clinical indicators of optimal early psychosis care.
audits.c: Introduction of specialised early psychosis teams and staff training
audits.r2: Improvements found on 10 of 27 indicators (psychosocial interventions, prescribing, family interventions, continuity of care); no deterioration on any indicator.

audits.t: An audit of cervical smears reported to contain atypical glandular cells.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Audit of glandular atypia reporting in cervical smears supported a three-tier sub-classification system, with the three sub-classifications showing distinct positive predictive values and correlating with the cell type of abnormality confirmed on histology

audits.t: Dose audit and evaluation of work practices during barium procedures using digital radiography techniques.
audits.tp: Radiation dose audit for barium procedures
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Effective dose ranged 0.03-3.5 mSv (barium swallow), 0.18-2.62 mSv (barium meal) and 0.56-4.24 mSv (barium enema); copper filter reduced patient dose.
audits.c: Use of additional 0.2 mm copper filter and optimised exposure factors

audits.t: Clinical audit of the use of tension-free vaginal tape as a surgical treatment for urinary stress incontinence, set against NICE guidelines.
audits.tp: Tension-free vaginal tape for stress urinary incontinence
audits.st: NICE clinical guidance (February 2003) on the use of tension-free vaginal tape (TVT) for surgical treatment of stress urinary incontinence
audits.f: Conservative management was tried and failed in 92% of cases before surgery; 95% of TVT patients were fully cured or substantially improved; complication rates were low (bladder/urethral perforation 4%, haemorrhage 1%, long-term voiding dysfunction 2%, tape rejection 0%, defective healing 0%, de novo urine retention 12%); a quarter of patients did not receive or have documented full information for informed consent

audits.t: Auditing the new decentralised oral treatment regimens in Malawi.
audits.tp: Decentralised oral TB treatment regimen audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1513 TB beds occupied by 807 (53%) TB patients; over 50% chose guardian-based DOT; correct knowledge of treatment duration only 45%; rates of unknown treatment outcome were high with oral regimens.

audits.t: Audit on nuchal translucency thickness measurements in Flanders, Belgium: a plea for methodological standardization.
audits.st: Fetal Medicine Foundation (FMF) reference values for nuchal translucency measurement
audits.f: 263 other sonographers showed systematic underestimation of NT (5th/50th/95th percentile delta-NT -0.81, -0.14, +0.73 mm) versus FMF trainee, who was close to FMF reference values.

audits.t: The Scotland Leukaemia Registry audit of incidence, diagnosis and clinical management of new patients with chronic myeloid leukaemia in 1999 and 2000.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Incidence 0.64/100,000/yr; all 18 units combined bone marrow examination with cytogenetics/FISH but only 13 performed RT-PCR; of 4 units calculating the Hasford Score, only 2 used it to inform decisions; 52% of patients entered clinical trials (57% involving imatinib mesylate); of 23 tissue-typed patients, suitable donors were found for 18 (11 sibling, 7 unrelated), 28% of the total patient population; only 13/64 (20%) lacked a transplant donor or trial entry; 56% received hydroxyurea +/- interferon as first-line therapy

audits.t: An audit of a British sample of death certificates in which anorexia nervosa is listed as a cause of death.
audits.tp: Death certification quality for anorexia nervosa
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 128 of 230 deaths (just over half) that mentioned anorexia nervosa were rated as likely to be true anorexia nervosa-associated deaths

audits.t: An audit of the use of epidural injections for back pain and sciatica.
audits.tp: Epidural injections for back pain and sciatica
audits.st: National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) guidelines on epidural injection use
audits.f: More than 80% of injections were used for conditions for which they were not indicated and which NHMRC considers experimental; informed consent was never recorded as recommended.

audits.t: An audit of conservative surgery for endometriosis in a district general hospital 1995-1998.
audits.st: Benchmarked against outcomes reported in published series for conservative surgery for endometriosis (no single named guideline)
audits.f: 81% response rate to postal questionnaire; 81% of respondents reported symptom improvement following conservative surgery; among those who had laparoscopic uterine nerve ablation (LUNA, 87% response), 64% reported some symptom improvement

audits.t: What's the evidence that NICE guidance has been implemented? Results from a national evaluation using time series analysis, audit of patients' notes, and interviews.
audits.st: National Institute for Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidance across multiple topics
audits.f: Implementation of NICE guidance varied by trust and by topic; guidance was more likely to be adopted where there was strong professional support, a stable and convincing evidence base, no increased or unfunded costs, established systems for tracking implementation, and professionals were not isolated

audits.t: A preliminary audit investigating remedy reactions including adverse events in routine homeopathic practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 24% (28/116) experienced an aggravation; 11% (13/116) reported an adverse event; 27% (31/116) described new symptoms; 18% (21/116) reported return of old symptoms

audits.t: Influence of guidelines on CPR decisions: an audit of clerking proforma.
audits.st: Local guidelines for documenting CPR/DNAR decisions
audits.f: Consultant documentation of CPR decisions was present in 27/75 (36%) departmental discharges before the proforma was introduced
audits.c: Introduction of new guidelines and a clerking proforma for CPR/DNAR decisions
audits.r2: Documentation improved to 102/109 (94%), 135/148 (91%), 133/140 (95%), 96/119 (81%), 148/157 (94%) and 167/169 (98%) across audits 2-7; the proportion of decisions that were DNAR was 64%, 72%, 45%, 68% and 62% across audits 3-7, with a statistically significant fall in both documentation and DNAR proportion in audit 5, when guidelines required discussion with the patient before a DNAR order

audits.t: IgA antibodies to human tissue transglutaminase: audit of routine practice confirms high diagnostic accuracy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Prevalence of new coeliac disease diagnoses in the population tested was 2.8%; positive predictive value at a 3 units/mL cut-off was 0.77 for primary care samples and 0.92 for hospital samples, with a sensitivity of 92% (75 consecutive new diagnoses assessed); EMA was rarely negative at TGA levels of 4.9 units/mL or above

audits.t: Audit of community-based anticoagulant monitoring in patients with thromboembolic disease: is frequent testing necessary?
audits.st: International guidelines for oral anticoagulant control
audits.f: 58.3% of INR measurements were in the therapeutic range, in line with international guidelines; 68% of patients had weekly INR testing even on long-term treatment.

audits.t: Age-standardisation when target setting and auditing performance of Down syndrome screening programmes.
audits.tp: Down syndrome prenatal screening programme audit
audits.st: Age-standardised target detection and false-positive rates for Down syndrome screening (e.g. 59-64% detection and 4.2-5.4% false-positive at a 1-in-250 term cut-off; 65-68% detection and 6.1-7.3% false-positive at a 1-in-270 mid-trimester cut-off)
audits.f: Audited detection rates among the five centres ranged from 7% below target to 10% above target; audited false-positive rates were better than target by 0.3 to 1.5 percentage points

audits.t: An audit of 2273 ureteroscopies--a focus on intra-operative complications to justify proactive management of ureteric calculi.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Intra-operative complication rate was 1% (23/2273 procedures) among 1936 patients; immediate JJ stenting was performed in 16 cases of ureteric injury; 5 patients (0.22%) required open surgery for perforation, Dormia basket problems, or impacted balloon dilator

audits.t: Management of congenital talipes equino varus in Scotland: a nationwide audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: The register recorded initial management and all subsequent non-operative and operative interventions for 216 children with idiopathic congenital talipes equinovarus, showing variation in duration of conservative management and variation in surgical intervention following different conservative approaches across Scotland

audits.t: Audit of primary and secondary care as a source of patch test clinic referrals.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 45 of 217 referrals (21%) were received from GPs; there was no significant difference in the percentage of positive or relevant positive patch test results from GP referrals compared with other sources, including dermatology departmental referrals

audits.t: A costed profile audit of the surgical management of female stress incontinence.
audits.tp: Costed profile audit of stress incontinence surgery
audits.st: Constructed profile of care (standard) for TVT, colposuspension and other surgical treatments for female stress urinary incontinence, including a theoretical profile cost
audits.f: Tension-free vaginal tape was the cheapest treatment by both expected profile and observed real-patient cost; colposuspension was the most expensive, with real costs significantly greater than the expected profile; length of stay was the main determinant of overall cost

audits.t: Theory-based identification of barriers to quality improvement: induced abortion care.
audits.st: RCOG clinical guideline 'The Care of Women Requesting Induced Abortion': offer an assessment appointment within 5 days of referral, and supply contraceptives at discharge
audits.f: Median unit compliance was 46% for offering an assessment appointment within 5 days of referral and 59% for supplying contraceptives at discharge

audits.t: An audit of the investigation and initial management of adults presenting with possible bacterial meningitis.
audits.st: British Infection Society (BIS) guidelines (1999, 2003) for the early management and investigation of adult patients with possible bacterial meningitis
audits.f: Only 2 of 26 patients presenting with possible bacterial meningitis had confirmed disease; basic laboratory investigations were performed on all patients, but more specific investigations (PCR, serology, throat swab) were frequently omitted; antibiotic choice was generally appropriate but dosage varied considerably; both confirmed cases received appropriate doses

audits.t: Bed usage in a Dublin teaching hospital: a prospective audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 70% of patients (mean age 54) went home on the day of medical discharge; 30% (mean age 70.3) remained in hospital awaiting step-down facilities, accounting for 486 bed-days; this capacity could have allowed treatment of 54% more patients without increasing bed numbers

audits.t: Multicentre audit of the treatment of uncomplicated urinary tract infection in South Thames.
audits.tp: Uncomplicated UTI treatment audit in GU medicine
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: The majority of centres used trimethoprim as first-line treatment for uncomplicated UTIs; the incidence of trimethoprim resistance was 22.6%
audits.c: Regional group recommended cephalexin replace trimethoprim as the first-choice antibiotic for suspected UTIs in GU medicine clinics

audits.t: Adherence to management guidelines in acute respiratory infections and diarrhoea in children under 5 years old in primary health care in Botswana.
audits.tp: Adherence to ARI and diarrhoea management guidelines
audits.st: Defined acceptable standards for history taking and physical examination for acute respiratory infection and diarrhoea
audits.f: Acceptable history taking, examination and both combined were found in 63%, 18% and 16% for ARI and 58%, 34% and 26% for diarrhoea; antibiotics prescribed inappropriately in 74% of cases prescribed.

audits.t: Diagnosis and management of simple ovarian cysts: an audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Documentation at ultrasound was often inadequate; management of women with ovarian cysts was haphazard; no malignancies found.

audits.t: Electrophysiologic and objective monitoring of the cochlear implant during surgery: implementation, audit and outcomes.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 303 of 427 implantation cases (71%) had completely normal intraoperative monitoring results across all protocol components; in remaining cases, some findings were anomalous with no impact on management, while others led to actions such as using a back-up device or repositioning the electrode array

audits.t: Changing practice: use of audit to change oral care practice.
audits.tp: Oral care practice in palliative care
audits.st: Oral care protocol and standard developed using audit tools by Lee et al. (2001), aiming for oral care consistent with best practice
audits.f: Baseline survey of nursing and medical staff oral care knowledge, plus retrospective review of 50 patients' notes, established current oral care practice before introduction of the new standard and documentation
audits.c: Introduction of a new oral care protocol and standard with documentation, and training provided to all unit staff
audits.r2: Re-audit of oral care practice showed improvement in all aspects of oral care practice

audits.t: An audit of acute pain service in Central, Saudi Arabia.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean pain score 0.7 (epidural) vs 1.7 (PCA); average APS duration 44.2 hours; epidural provided superior analgesia but more minor side effects.

audits.t: Evidence-based health care: development and audit of a clinical standard for research and its impact on an NHS trust.
audits.st: Benchmark clinical standard for nursing research, developed to fit within the trust's dynamic quality improvement (DQI) programme
audits.f: A baseline survey of 192 nurses after introducing the research standard found increased awareness of formal and informal educational/research opportunities, and identified nurses' strengths and weaknesses across the research process, particularly in obtaining ethical approval for studies
audits.c: Development of a clinical standard for nursing research, with a rolling programme of research education and a support/consultancy network

audits.t: Use of a patient information system to audit the introduction of modified early warning scoring.
audits.tp: Modified early warning score outcomes audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 619 triggers were recorded in 365 patients; 59 required ICU/HDU care and 71 died; survival was significantly worse for initial scores greater than 4 (35/104 died) than for scores 3-4 (P<0.004); age and trigger score (but not ward specialty) predicted death (P<0.001 each)

audits.t: A chart audit of postoperative pain assessment and documentation: the first step to implement pain assessment as the fifth vital sign in a University Hospital in Thailand.
audits.st: Locally accepted score threshold of 21/28 (75%) for adequate pain assessment documentation
audits.f: Nurses documented pain assessment far more often than doctors (98.8% vs 29.4%); regular pain assessment every 2-4 hours in first 24 hours found in only 0.5% of charts; mean audit score 10.7/28, below the accepted standard.

audits.t: Engaging in the audit of acupuncture practice.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 145 invited practitioners, 31 (21%) responded and only 9 (6%) contributed data; 69 patients participated (68% female, 73% aged 30-59); 52% had had their presenting problem for over 5 years; 32 of 41 patients (78%) with completed final outcome data recorded moderate or major benefit, with no reports of deterioration

audits.t: National Biometry Audit II.
audits.st: Royal College of Ophthalmologists (RCOphth) biometry guidelines
audits.f: Nurses alone performed biometry in 51% of departments and junior doctors alone in 15%; 37% of biometrists had attended external training courses; audit of prediction error was performed by 71% of units; partial coherence laser interferometry was used in 35% of departments
audits.r2: Nurses alone performed biometry in 67% of departments (up) and junior doctors alone in 9% (down); 45% of biometrists had attended external training; RCOphth-recommended IOL formulae (SRK-T, Hoffer Q, Holladay) were used more commonly (30% and 15%); audit of prediction error was performed by 78% of units; partial coherence laser interferometry use increased from 35% to 61%; only one UK department routinely used immersion ultrasound biometry; A constants were customized in 47% of departments

audits.t: [Internal audit based on the recording critical incidents: the first results].
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Critical incidents (CIs) were recorded in 42.1% of anaesthesias; 304 CIs noted in total, 0.84 CIs per anaesthesia, from a list of 53 CI items in 8 groups.

audits.t: Supervision and responsibility: The Royal College of Anaesthetists National Audit.
audits.st: National guidance that every NHS patient should have a named consultant; locally desirable criteria for anaesthesia record charts
audits.f: Anaesthesia record charts in use did not meet locally desirable criteria; most trainees but fewer than half of staff-grade/associate specialists received an induction programme, often without written documentation; around half of respondents disagreed with national guidance that every NHS patient should have a named consultant; 2% of non-consultants reported that consultant assistance was not obtainable soon enough during the audit period

audits.t: An audit of the use of isolation facilities in a UK National Health Service trust.
audits.st: Local guideline for GPs and hospital doctors on appropriate admission to isolation beds, developed from an earlier audit
audits.f: One-third of patients admitted to dedicated isolation room were not thought to be an infection risk by experienced healthcare staff
audits.c: Guideline for GPs and hospital doctors on isolation bed admission, implemented at the time of moving to a large central teaching hospital site
audits.r2: Utilisation of isolation beds deteriorated following the move by all three criteria used, mainly due to increased admission of general medical 'boarders' and low-risk infection patients

audits.t: Audit for extraoral radiographic examinations in a digital department.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 22% (346) of images requested by the orthodontic department were not opened within 3 months; non-opened rates were oral surgery 3%, periodontology 17%, treatment planning 33%, prosthetic 5%, county 21%, oral physiology 23%; panoramic images were 58% of non-opened images.

audits.t: Prospective audit of a one-centre combined nuchal translucency and triple test programme for the detection of trisomy 21.
audits.tp: Down syndrome prenatal screening programme audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Using a 3mm nuchal translucency cut-off, 16 of 25 trisomy 21 cases (64%) were identified; of 2725 women with a combined nuchal translucency plus triple test assessment, 79 (2.6%) had a term risk of 1:250 or greater; 40 (1.3%) had amniocentesis, identifying 6 of 9 remaining cases (67%); overall detection rate was 88% for a 4.8% false-positive rate

audits.t: Homeopathy service in a National Health Service community menopause clinic: audit of clinical outcomes.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Patients reported significant benefit from the homeopathy service using the Measure Yourself Medical Outcome Profile; the greatest response was seen in those reporting headaches, vasomotor symptoms, emotional/psychological symptoms and tiredness/fatigue as their primary symptoms

audits.t: Patient-centred quality improvement audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Preliminary findings from a newly developed instrument measured health outcomes in terms of quality improvement from the users' perspective, and highlighted gaps between what the service offers and what users perceive is delivered

audits.t: [Prescription practices: an audit of prescription quality among Lorrain general practitioners].
audits.st: Compliance with existing mandatory prescription regulations (patient identification, regulation content, legibility, computerisation).
audits.f: The patient's age was the only mandatory inscription often missing; average, highest and lowest performance among practitioners were reported but exact figures were not given in the abstract.

audits.t: Mapping changes in surgical mortality over 9 years by peer review audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Consultant surgeon and anaesthetist involvement in decision-making and operating increased significantly over the 9-year period
audits.c: Continuous peer review audit, critical event analysis and individual feedback of deaths occurring in surgical care
audits.r2: Changes in clinician practice (e.g. DVT prophylaxis) and provision of facilities (HDU/ITU) may have contributed to a decreased rate of adverse events over the audit period

audits.t: Bed-rest post-femoral arterial sheath removal--what is safe practice? A clinical audit.
audits.st: Best practice bed-rest duration identified via literature review and clinical benchmarking
audits.f: Baseline (median) bed rest post-femoral arterial sheath removal was 6 hours
audits.c: Bed-rest duration reduced from 6 hours to 3 hours, based on literature review and clinical benchmarking
audits.r2: Femoral wound site complication rates were not significantly affected by the reduction to 3-hour bed rest, for either diagnostic or interventional procedures

audits.t: Audit of treatment and contact-tracing rates in immediate (presumptive) versus delayed (polymerase chain reaction) diagnosis of chlamydial infection.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Treatment rates were 100% among 189 men presumptively diagnosed/treated versus 97.6% among 83 men diagnosed only by PCR (P<0.05); contact tracing was confirmed in 88.6% of the presumptive group versus 90% of the PCR-only group

audits.t: Influence of self-registration on audit participants and their non-participating colleagues. A retrospective study of medical records concerning prescription patterns.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Participants (45) prescribed antibiotics at a rate 6 percentage points lower than non-participants (35) at the start (RR=0.92; 95% CI 0.87-0.97), and 7 points lower at the end (0.88; 0.81-0.95); proportion of RTIs treated with antibiotics fell in both groups (to RR 0.86 and 0.90 respectively).

audits.t: Audit of a pathway for childhood idiopathic constipation.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: [Audit of obstetrical practices and prevention of perinatal deaths].
audits.st: Local critical analysis of obstetrical practices (Perinatal Enquiry) reviewing all perinatal deaths; no external numeric target stated.
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Bimonthly meetings of obstetricians and paediatricians to critically discuss observed fetal and neonatal deaths, which became a permanent audit tool.
audits.r2: Associated with a major reduction in perinatal mortality rates, though exact figures were not given in the abstract.

audits.t: Could sequential individual peer reviewed mortality audit data be used in appraisal?
audits.st: General Medical Council concept of 'good clinical practice'; voluntary participation in the Scottish Audit of Surgical Mortality (SASM)
audits.f: Compliance with the voluntary audit was high (97%); adverse events were infrequent and usually due to problems with the process of care rather than individual surgeon error; the number of case note reviews requested increased significantly over the 3 years

audits.t: Impact of a latex policy on an acute NHS hospital: an audit.
audits.st: Hospital latex policy introduced in 1999
audits.f: The latex policy was available on only 26 of 40 wards (65%); compliance with the policy was limited to 20 wards (50%)

audits.t: Abstract reporting in randomized clinical trials of acute lung injury: an audit and assessment of a quality of reporting score.
audits.st: A 32-item (reduced to 20-item long form and 12-item short form) checklist of recommended abstract reporting criteria for RCTs, developed by a focus group.
audits.f: Abstracts described objectives and interventions well, but key deficiencies were noted in reporting of study methods, setting and results; mean quality-of-reporting scores were significantly higher for structured than unstructured abstracts on the 32-, 20- and 12-item lists (p=.008, .014 and another value not fully reported).

audits.t: Putting smart money to work for quality improvement.
audits.st: Internal composite quality measures for diabetes process and outcome care (self-reported physician data spot-checked against medical charts; control group used HEDIS data); no explicit numeric target stated.
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Physicians paid a performance bonus for diabetes care quality, supplied with a diabetic registry, and met in groups to discuss progress towards goals.
audits.r2: Significant improvement on 5 of 6 process measures and 2 of 3 outcome measures (HbA1c control and LDL control); 13 of 21 physicians improved their composite score enough to earn a financial reward; of the 8 who received no reward, 6 still improved their composite score.

audits.t: Medical audit of maternal deaths in the Lagos University Teaching Hospital, Nigeria.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Autopsies were performed on 371/445 deaths (autopsy rate 83.37%); of 230 cases suitable for evaluation, 206 (89.57%) showed concordance and 24 (10.43%) discordance between clinical and autopsy diagnosis.

audits.t: Quality improvement of surgical prophylaxis in Dutch hospitals: evaluation of a multi-site intervention by time series analysis.
audits.st: National clinical practice guidelines for surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (antibiotic choice, duration, timing).
audits.f: Before the intervention, antimicrobial use was 121 defined daily doses (DDD)/100 procedures.
audits.c: Performance feedback plus implementation of national clinical practice guidelines for surgical antibiotic prophylaxis, evaluated with segmented regression (time series) analysis.
audits.r2: After the intervention, antimicrobial use fell to 79 DDD/100 procedures and costs fell 25% per procedure; antibiotic choice was inappropriate in 37.5% of cases versus an expected 93.5% without the intervention; prolonged prophylaxis occurred in 31.4% versus an expected 46.8%; inappropriate timing in 39.4% versus an expected 51.8% (all improvements statistically significant).

audits.t: An audit into the efficacy of single use bacterial/viral filters for the prevention of equipment contamination during lung function assessment.
audits.tp: Bacterial/viral filter efficacy in lung function testing
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Bacterial growth was found in 33 of 155 proximal (patient-side) samples versus 2 of 155 distal (equipment-side) samples (P<0.01); growth was obtained from the filter itself in 125 of 155 cases (80.6%), including pathogenic organisms such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa (4 cases) and Staphylococcus aureus (5 cases)

audits.t: Collaborative colorectal cancer screening: a successful quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Goal of increasing referrals for colorectal cancer screening to at least 85% among patients aged 50-75 years.
audits.f: Baseline review of over 5000 medical charts established a colorectal cancer screening referral rate of 47%.
audits.c: Screening protocol using chart stickers to flag patients needing screening, numbered referral forms faxed to gastroenterologists for follow-up, and patient education material on colorectal cancer screening.
audits.r2: Referrals for sigmoidoscopy, colonoscopy and double-contrast barium enema increased from 47% to 86%; faecal occult blood testing was also arranged for additional patients.

audits.t: The Western Australian Audit of Surgical Mortality: advancing surgical accountability.
audits.st: Peer review of all deaths under the care of a Western Australian surgeon (WAASM); no explicit numeric target stated.
audits.f: Deficiencies of care were reported in 179/876 (20%) reviewed deaths; deficiency was assessed to have caused death in 45/876 (5%), with 15 deaths considered preventable; autopsy was undertaken in 83/768 (11%) deaths with complete data; risk of a care deficiency was 1.9 times higher in elective than emergency admissions.

audits.t: An audit of clinical practice in the management of head injured patients following the introduction of the Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN) recommendations.
audits.st: Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN) head injury management guidelines, published August 2000
audits.f: 93% of patients with a SIGN indication for admission were admitted; 92% of admitted patients with a SIGN indication for skull X-ray had one; 36% of patients with a SIGN indication for CT had a scan; 57% of patients discharged from A&E were in accordance with SIGN recommendations; 50% of admitted patients had neurological observations
audits.c: Introduction of SIGN head injury guidelines (August 2000), with positive reinforcement in A&E and at ward level
audits.r2: 92% of patients with a SIGN indication for admission were admitted; skull X-ray compliance dropped to 79%; CT scan compliance rose to 64%; 44% of patients discharged from A&E were in accordance with SIGN recommendations; neurological observations rose to 88%

audits.t: Prospective audit of 106 consecutive human bite injuries: the importance of history taking.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Follow-up questioning of patients with cutaneous wounds who did not initially report a human bite history led some patients to subsequently disclose a bite history; certain patient groups were significantly more likely to give a factitious history and/or delay presentation

audits.t: Clinical neurophysiology referral patterns to a tertiary hospital--a prospective audit.
audits.tp: Neurophysiology referral patterns and waiting times
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 254 patients had EMG, 359 had EEG, 18 had VEP, 3 had SSEP and 1 had MSLT; average waiting time was 32 days for EEG and 74 days for EMG; more than 35% of patients waiting for EEG or EMG had their test within 4 weeks of referral; appointments were assigned on the basis of clinical need

audits.t: An audit of 'early debond' cases in the national outcomes audit of patients treated with upper and lower fixed appliances by Consultant Orthodontists in the UK.
audits.st: 75% of cases should show a PAR score reduction greater than 70%, with 3% or less showing a PAR score reduction of less than 30% (worse/no different)
audits.f: The 'early debond' cohort constituted 11% of the 823 total patients and fell below the published standards for orthodontic treatment outcomes; mean PAR reduction was 67%; 50% had a PAR reduction greater than 70%, and 6.5% had a PAR reduction less than 30%

audits.t: The impact of compliance with 6-hour and 24-hour sepsis bundles on hospital mortality in patients with severe sepsis: a prospective observational study.
audits.tp: Compliance with sepsis care bundles and mortality
audits.st: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 6-hour and 24-hour sepsis care bundles
audits.f: 6-hour bundle compliance 52%; 24-hour bundle compliance 30% (21/69); non-compliant group mortality 49% vs 23% compliant for 6-hour bundle (RR 2.12, 95% CI 1.20-3.76, P=0.01); 24-hour non-compliant mortality 50% vs 29% (RR 1.76, 95% CI 0.84-3.64, P=0.16)

audits.t: The EQUAL-ESTRO audit on geometric reconstruction techniques in brachytherapy.
audits.st: Geometric reconstruction check using the 'Baltas' phantom against an acceptance level, developed by the ESTRO Braphyqs task group (ESQUIRE project).
audits.f: 86% of reconstructions were within the acceptance level after the first check; 14% required a second check.
audits.r2: Most re-checks were within the acceptance level, except for 2% of reconstructions.

audits.t: Thromboprophylaxis post vaginal delivery: are we forgetting it? Audit on thromboprophylaxis prescription post vaginal births.
audits.st: Hospital maternity unit written guidelines on thromboprophylaxis after vaginal births
audits.f: 9% of spontaneous vaginal births (n=148) and 62% of instrumental vaginal births (n=29) required specific thromboprophylaxis per guidelines; however, only 31% of indicated spontaneous vaginal births and 22% of indicated instrumental vaginal births actually received the required treatment

audits.t: NICE guideline for the management of head injury: an audit demonstrating its impact on a district general hospital, with a cost analysis for England and Wales.
audits.tp: Head injury CT imaging guideline compliance
audits.st: NICE guideline for the management of head injury (indications for CT head/skull radiograph)
audits.f: not reported; described only as lower CT rate than after NICE guideline implementation
audits.c: Implementation of the NICE guideline on management of head injury
audits.r2: Of 17,472 ED attendances, 472 had a head injury; CT was indicated in 36, a significant increase from 2003

audits.t: Audit of nasendoscope disinfection practice.
audits.st: Health regulation requirements for nasendoscope disinfection; no numeric target stated
audits.f: Overall cost of disposable sheaths averaged £4008 per month over six months
audits.c: Introduction of chlorine dioxide (ClO2) wipes as a means of disinfection instead of disposable sheaths
audits.r2: Chlorine dioxide wipes enabled a monthly saving of £3145 over sheath usage and met health regulation requirements

audits.t: Outpatient oral anticoagulant management--an audit of 82 patients.
audits.st: Standard accepted guidelines for oral anticoagulant therapeutic range monitoring.
audits.f: Of 1631 INR/prothrombin time ratios recorded, only 17.8% were in the therapeutic range and 73% were sub-therapeutic; 16 (19.5%) patients had treatment-related complications; thrombotic and haemorrhagic event rates were 3.4 and 2.7 per 100 patient treatment years respectively.

audits.t: Barrett's oesophagus: an audit of surveillance over a 17-year period.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 232 of 466 patients had at least one follow-up endoscopy; of 195 with intestinal metaplasia who entered surveillance, 97 remained under active surveillance and 98 discontinued; 4 of 195 developed adenocarcinoma (incidence 0.37%)

audits.t: Which measure of contact tracing performance? -- using audit as the evidence base.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Evaluation of an audit with feedback continuing medical education program for radiation oncologists.
audits.tp: Audit and feedback in radiation oncology practice
audits.st: A validated 19-item instrument (10 targeted and 3 non-targeted behaviour items, 6 performance items) developed locally; no external guideline named.
audits.f: Mean targeted behaviour score was 8.7 out of 10.
audits.c: Audit with feedback (AWF) continuing medical education: fortnightly random patient chart audit scored via checklist, presented at institutional meetings with individualised educational feedback from senior peers.
audits.r2: Mean targeted behaviour score improved to 9.2 out of 10 (P=.0001); no significant improvement in non-targeted behaviour/performance items.

audits.t: Carcinoma breast: a histopathological audit.
audits.st: Quality assurance programme comparing re-examined (audited) histopathology results with original reports (local standard).
audits.f: 39 cases (20.4%) showed differences from the original report in grade, lymphovascular invasion or necrosis; differences in nuclear and tumour grade were statistically significant, but differences in lymphovascular invasion and necrosis were not (p=0.90 each).

audits.t: Influence of peer review medical audit on pathophysiological interpretation of nerve conduction studies in polyneuropathies.
audits.tp: Peer review audit of nerve conduction study interpretation
audits.st: Consistency of pathophysiological interpretation among neurophysiologists (no external numeric target); assessed by kappa statistics.
audits.f: Kappa values: demyelination 0.22, neuropathic findings 0.46, unspecific findings 0.35, axonal loss 0.26, normal findings 0.90.
audits.c: Regular peer review medical audit: physicians interpreted each other's nerve conduction cases electronically and discussed them at regular workshop meetings.
audits.r2: Kappa values: demyelination 0.45, neuropathic findings 0.64, unspecific findings 0.54, axonal loss 0.31 (unchanged), normal findings 0.90 (unchanged).

audits.t: User satisfaction with a constipation service: a comparative audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: A review of outcomes following establishment of a new constipation service showed significant improvements in outcomes and in support provided to families, though exact figures were not given; a qualitative substudy of 16 children and families found they appreciated the education and support offered.
audits.c: Establishment of a new constipation service.

audits.t: Day-case septoplasty and unexpected re-admissions at a dedicated day-case unit: a 4-year audit.
audits.st: Day-surgery guidelines: unexpected admission rate should be 2-3%
audits.f: 38 of 432 patients (378 septoplasties, 54 submucous resections) were admitted, an overall unexpected admission rate of 8.8% within the first 24 hours, mainly due to haemorrhage

audits.t: New Zealand's Christchurch Hospital at night: an audit of medical activity from 2230 to 0800 hours.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Resident Medical Officers were not working as a team; some were overextended while others were inactive; house officer tasks were largely generic; there was no formal handover from day/afternoon shifts; a third of admissions were to General Medicine.

audits.t: [Management of suicidal adolescents: a clinical audit in 76 hospitals].
audits.st: ANAES (French National Agency for Accreditation and Evaluation in Health) 1998 clinical practice guidelines: 15 criteria covering hospital management (9), contact with the patient's environment outside hospital (2), and discharge preparation (4).
audits.f: Compliance with criteria was >80% for 5 criteria, 50-80% for 3 criteria, and <50% for 7 criteria.
audits.c: 26 hospitals proposed a structured improvement plan (working group, results-analysis grid, structured report) following the ANAES recommendations.
audits.r2: Improvements were noted for 12 of the 15 criteria, mainly those with the poorest first-round results, though this affected only a few hospitals (e.g. just 4 hospitals for the criterion with the worst first-round result); compliance worsened for 3 criteria.

audits.t: Auditing possible side-effects of atypical antipsychotics.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Care practices for monitoring side-effects of atypical antipsychotics were towards the worst-practice end of the continuum; exact figures were not given in the abstract.

audits.t: How well is peripheral neuropathy investigated? An audit from a regional neurophysiology department.
audits.st: Patients with confirmed peripheral neuropathy should receive a basic blood screen to search for the aetiology (implied local expectation; no explicit numeric target stated)
audits.f: Over 50% of patients referred from within the hospital did not have a basic blood screen to search for the aetiology; no significant difference in investigation practice by patient age or referral source
audits.c: A protocol was prepared and distributed together with NCS/EMG reports

audits.t: An examination of covert observation and solution audit as tools to measure the success of hand hygiene interventions.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Observed hand hygiene adherence was 51%.
audits.c: Not described in the abstract beyond the study of covert observation and solution audit as two measurement methods.
audits.r2: Observed hand hygiene adherence rose to 58%; hand hygiene solution use was 55% higher than baseline.

audits.t: Audit of doctors' knowledge of major incident policies.
audits.tp: Major incident policy awareness among doctors
audits.st: Doctors should know their hospital's major incident policy and where to report (implied local standard; no explicit numeric target stated)
audits.f: Pre-intervention, 4.4% of doctors knew where to report to in a major incident
audits.c: A one-sided information sheet on the major incident policy was distributed to doctors and posted in areas frequented by doctors
audits.r2: Following the intervention, 78% of doctors knew where to report to in a major incident

audits.t: Let's get physical: an audit of medical practice in first episode psychosis.
audits.tp: Physical health assessment in first-episode psychosis
audits.st: National guidelines recommending medical examination, diagnosis, side-effect monitoring and routine investigations for first-episode psychosis; no explicit numeric target stated.
audits.f: Only 4 of 52 (8%) patients undergoing neuroimaging had any abnormality; 3 of 33 (9%) EEGs were abnormal; documentation of involuntary movement assessment occurred in only 4% of the sample and weight assessment in 15%.

audits.t: Audit of care of patients with congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 21-Hydroxylase deficiency in a referral hospital in South India.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Karyotyping was done in half of patients; half had adequate follow-up and 17-OHP measurements; only 7 of 30 children had normal height for age; bone age was done in 16 patients.

audits.t: Audit of over 500 percutaneous dilational tracheostomies.
audits.st: Written unit protocol standardising indication, authorisation and consultant supervision, antibiotic prophylaxis and anaesthetic technique for tracheostomy; no explicit numeric target stated.
audits.f: Bleeding was the most common complication in the percutaneous group (4.3%), followed by desaturation (1.0%), bradycardia (1.0%) and hypotension (0.8%); one death 11 days after the procedure from secondary haemorrhage; 11 percutaneous procedures were converted to surgical tracheostomy.

audits.t: Setting standards for planning off duty and audit of practice.
audits.st: Recommended standards for off-duty (rostering) planning proposed in the article
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: [Audit of management of arterial hypertension in primary health care in Sousse].
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Patients selected for first-line follow-up were 79% of the studied population; minimal recommended assessment ('bilan') was achieved in only 8% of cases; adequate drug therapy was prescribed in 64%; 59% of patients were considered compliant; blood pressure control was achieved in 5.5%; overall management quality was rated satisfactory in 28.7% of patients, with a significant difference between urban (24.9%) and rural (40.5%) areas.

audits.t: An audit of bone densitometry practice with reference to ISCD, IOF and NOF guidelines.
audits.st: National Osteoporosis Foundation (NOF), International Osteoporosis Foundation (IOF) and International Society for Clinical Densitometry (ISCD) guidelines for bone densitometry testing.
audits.f: Using clinical judgement alone, positive predictive value (PPV) for osteoporosis was 42.4%; using NOF guidelines, 236 women would have been tested with PPV 46.2%; using IOF or ISCD guidelines, PPV was 47.1% (also 236 tested).

audits.t: Finnish Trauma Audit 2004: current state of trauma management in Finnish hospitals.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: About 20% of hospitals had a trauma team and 25% had a systematic trauma education programme; only one hospital had established multidisciplinary systematic trauma team training; an estimated 1000-1300 severe trauma patients were treated in Finland per year (19-25/100,000 inhabitants).

audits.t: Parent questionnaires: are they effective for auditing services?
audits.tp: Parent satisfaction survey on children's surgical ward
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 100 of 180 questionnaires distributed were returned; parents were dissatisfied with noise levels and wanted more televisions; a large proportion were satisfied with nursing care and felt involved in their child's care
audits.c: Introduction of a quiet time on the ward in response to survey findings

audits.t: Follow-up of basal cell carcinomas: an audit of current practice.
audits.st: Local standard: all patients reviewed for 2 years after surgical excision of a low-risk primary basal cell carcinoma
audits.f: 114 patients had 121 primary BCCs excised; location recorded in 100% and size in 35% of cases; 2-year follow-up completed by 53% of patients and 1-year follow-up by 78%; 2 BCCs recurred within 2 years; risk of a new BCC was 11.6% in year 1 and 6.3% in year 2
audits.c: Follow-up period reduced to 1 year; a proforma developed to encourage documentation of prognostic factors

audits.t: Troponin testing for chest pain in primary healthcare: a New Zealand audit.
audits.tp: Troponin testing appropriateness in primary care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 10 of 433 (2.3%) troponin tests were positive; an ECG was performed in less than 50% of cases; patients were referred acutely to hospital on less than 5% of occasions.

audits.t: Utilizing audit to evaluate improvements in continuous veno-venous haemofiltration practices in intensive therapy unit.
audits.tp: CVVH record keeping practice in ITU
audits.st: Local standard for continuous veno-venous haemofiltration (CVVH) record keeping; specifics not stated
audits.f: Baseline audit identified a number of areas for improvement in CVVH record-keeping practice
audits.c: Dissemination of audit findings to the multidisciplinary team; redesign of the prescription chart to a more user-friendly format; development of a competency-based CVVH workbook
audits.r2: Second audit demonstrated positive outcomes and improvements in record keeping across the multidisciplinary ITU team

audits.t: An audit of implanted penile prostheses in the UK.
audits.tp: Penile prosthesis implantation volume and revision rate
audits.st: Worldwide average revision rate for penile prosthesis implantation, used as a comparison benchmark; no explicit guideline target stated
audits.f: 413 penile prostheses implanted by 76 surgeons; about 80% of surgeons implanted only 1-2 prostheses per year (usually malleable type, mostly private sector); only 4 surgeons implanted more than 20 per year; overall UK revision rate was 24%, far higher than the worldwide average

audits.t: Development of a clinical chart audit programme.
audits.st: A locally developed chart review tool assessing accuracy and completeness of radiation oncology chart documentation; no external guideline named.
audits.f: 56% of charts reviewed were radical treatments and 44% palliative; alpha coefficients for intra-rater and inter-rater reliability were 0.99 and 0.88 respectively.
audits.c: Introduction of a structured chart review/audit tool with monthly scoring and feedback to individual radiation oncologists.
audits.r2: Overall mean chart scores significantly improved over the course of the study (P<0.001), and individual radiation oncologists' scores also improved.

audits.t: Audit of feeding practices in babies<1200 g or 30 weeks gestation during the first month of life.
audits.tp: Nutrition and growth in very low birth weight infants
audits.st: Published reference data for nutritional intake and growth of infants <1200 g or 30 weeks gestation; no single named guideline.
audits.f: After the first week of life, median energy intake was 147 (78-174) kcal/kg/day and protein intake 3.9 (2.1-4.8) g/kg/day; median daily weight gain was 17 (-3.2 to 35.4) g/kg, significantly associated with energy and protein intake.

audits.t: Medical autopsy: whose gain is it? An audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: In 45% of autopsies, clinical impression did not match the final cause of death; in 14.2% the final cause of death could have been certified on clinical judgement alone; premortem and postmortem diagnosis agreed in 54.5%; gross findings matched histopathological findings in 67.6%.

audits.t: Potential for organ donation in Victoria: an audit of hospital deaths.
audits.tp: Organ donation potential and consent rate
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Consent rate was 53-65% depending on the definition of potential donor used; of 60 unrealised potential donors, 3 were category A, 17 category B and 40 category C; consent rate was 21% when discussions were held by trainees/registrars versus 57% by specialists (P=0.004).

audits.t: Stereotactic brain biopsy: An audit of sampling reliability in a clinical case series.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall diagnostic success rate 89.3%; significant positive correlation between number of targets taken and probability of diagnosis; in a glioblastoma subset, 96.1% could have been confidently diagnosed from any two targets

audits.t: Rapid assessment breast clinics--evolution through audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 154 (10.7%) had breast cancer, 87.7% of whom were seen expediently and 92.9% diagnosed at one attendance; 143 (10%) with a benign diagnosis were found to have significant familial risk; 176 (12.3%) had none of the referral symptoms; 283 (19.8%) had no objective clinical or radiological abnormality

audits.t: A breast center review of compliance with National Comprehensive Cancer Network Breast Cancer guidelines.
audits.st: National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Breast Cancer guidelines.
audits.f: NCCN guideline compliance rates were: preoperative evaluation 87%, breast surgery 97%, lymph node surgery 97%, radiation treatment 77%, systemic adjuvant therapy 63%.

audits.t: Efficacy of an integrated continuing medical education (CME) and quality improvement (QI) program on radiation oncologist (RO) clinical practice.
audits.tp: Audit and feedback in radiation oncology practice
audits.st: Departmental protocol/study adherence and a validated behaviour/performance instrument (local standard).
audits.f: Mean behaviour score 12.7 of 14, performance score 7.6 of 8; protocol/study adherence 90.3%.
audits.c: Integrated CME/QI programme: chart audit with feedback (C-AWF), simulation review audit with feedback (SR-AWF), reminder checklists, and targeted CME tutorials.
audits.r2: Mean behaviour score improved to 13.6 of 14 (P=0.0005); performance score improved to 7.9 of 8 (P=0.018); protocol/study adherence improved to 96.6% (P=0.005).

audits.t: The national comparative audit of surgery for nasal polyposis and chronic rhinosinusitis.
audits.st: Pre-operative steroid course expected before primary surgery for bilateral grade I/II nasal polyposis (implied practice standard)
audits.f: SNOT-22 scores improved from mean 42.0 pre-operatively to 25.5 at 3 months (nasal polypectomy 41.0 to 23.1; chronic rhinosinusitis alone 44.2 to 31.2), with similar scores at 12 and 36 months; excessive bleeding in 5% intra-operatively and 1% post-operatively; intra-orbital complications in 0.2%; 18% of patients having primary surgery for bilateral grade I/II polyposis had not received a pre-operative steroid course; 11.4% had undergone revision surgery by 36 months

audits.t: Using audit to change practice for routine glucochecks.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Staff education to improve follow-up action after glucocheck results

audits.t: Paracetamol use in musculoskeletal pain: an audit of use and patient perceptions of paracetamol as an effective analgesic.
audits.tp: Paracetamol use and perceptions in musculoskeletal pain
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: The audit prompted development of a multidisciplinary strategy to achieve optimum pain management

audits.t: Audit of the change in the on-call practices in neuroradiology and factors affecting it.
audits.tp: On-call neuroradiology imaging request workload after gatekeeper change
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: CT scans requested from A&E increased by 73.4% after the change from neuroradiologist to neuroradiographer gatekeeping, with head injury scan requests up 122%
audits.c: not reported (change in on-call practice was the exposure studied, not an intervention tested by this audit)

audits.t: Quality improvement process in the adherence to gastric decontamination guidelines for poison exposures as recommended by a poison control center.
audits.st: A revised (February 2002) guideline narrowing the use of ipecac syrup, gastric lavage, cathartics and activated charcoal for poison exposures.
audits.f: Recommendation rates were: ipecac syrup 1.50%, single-dose activated charcoal 5.39%, gastric lavage 4.19%, cathartic 1.48%.
audits.c: Implementation of a revised, narrower gastric decontamination guideline with a performance improvement process.
audits.r2: Recommendation rates declined to: ipecac syrup 0.02% (OR 0.02; 95% CI 0.01-0.03), activated charcoal 1.38% (OR 0.25; 95% CI 0.22-0.28), gastric lavage 0.22% (OR 0.05; 95% CI 0.04-0.06), cathartic 0.13% (OR 0.08; 95% CI 0.06-0.12); declines in utilisation were also significant.

audits.t: Clinching the contacts: a tale of two audits before and after the introduction of a contacts' clinic.
audits.st: Specialty's evidence-based National Outcome Standards for partner notification (numeric target not stated in abstract)
audits.f: 0.46 contacts per case seen within four weeks of initial partner notification interview (95% CI 0.36-0.56)
audits.c: Introduction of weekly contacts' clinics from October 2004, providing early appointments for partners of chlamydia-positive patients
audits.r2: 0.66 contacts per case seen within four weeks (95% CI 0.57-0.75), a significant improvement (P=0.005)

audits.t: Auditing secondary prevention of ischaemic heart disease in rural areas of Spain: an opportunity for improvement.
audits.tp: Secondary prevention of ischaemic heart disease
audits.st: International guidelines for secondary prevention of ischaemic heart disease (LDL and blood pressure targets)
audits.f: 30.9% reached target LDL; 68.1% reached target blood pressure; 48.5% were taking beta-blockers; 29% had not seen a specialist within the previous year.

audits.t: Colposcopic management of high-grade referral smears: a retrospective audit supporting 'see and treat'?
audits.tp: Colposcopy biopsy rate compliance for high-grade referrals
audits.st: NHS Cervical Screening Programme colposcopy standards (KC65 returns): Standard 7c, biopsy rate ≥90% at first colposcopy visit for high-grade referrals (2002 standards); CIN on histology ≥85% overall and ≥90% at index-visit biopsies; revised 2004 standards require biopsy in ≥95% of high-grade referrals and excision biopsy in 95% under specified criteria
audits.f: Biopsies taken from 94.47% of women at index colposcopy visit (standard ≥90%, met), including excision biopsies from 66.16% (87.97% of high-grade colposcopic appearances); CIN on histology found in 91.79% of the study group (standard ≥85%, met) and 96.71% of index-visit biopsies (standard ≥90%, met); positive predictive value of high-grade cytology 75.54%, with CIN present in 90.95%

audits.t: An audit of the use and complications of glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors in percutaneous coronary intervention against national UK standards.
audits.tp: GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor use in percutaneous coronary intervention
audits.st: National UK standards for use of glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors in percutaneous coronary intervention (specific numeric target not detailed in abstract)
audits.f: 104 of 170 screened patients (61%) had coronary intervention, of which 8 (8%) failed; GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors used in 57 (55%) patients (eptifibatide 33%, abciximab 18%, tirofiban 3%); overall complication rate not increased by GP IIb/IIIa use, with no stroke, thrombocytopenia, gastrointestinal bleed or death recorded

audits.t: Hospitals' compliance with prophylaxis guidelines for venous thromboembolism.
audits.st: Sixth ACCP Consensus Conference on Antithrombotic Therapy guidelines for VTE prevention
audits.f: Overall compliance with ACCP guidelines was 13.3% (range 2.8% neurosurgery to 52.4% orthopaedic surgery); only 15.3% of at-risk medical patients received guideline-compliant prophylaxis.

audits.t: The use of histology in 638 coronial post-mortem examinations of adults: an audit.
audits.tp: Histology sampling in coronial post-mortem examinations
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Histology contributory in 53% of cases; provided the cause of death in 49/203 (24%) cases with no cause after macroscopic exam; changed interim cause of death in 4.8% of cases
audits.c: Sampling practice revised to focus on left/right ventricle, coronary arteries, lungs, kidneys, brain and any macroscopically abnormal tissue

audits.t: [Medical audits contribute to good and comparable health services].
audits.tp: Regional medical audit programme (stroke, breast cancer, mental health)
audits.st: ISO-based guidelines and national/best-practice standards for stroke, breast cancer and mental health treatment
audits.f: Overall satisfactory treatment but improvement needed: breast-conserving surgery rate could be increased, stroke unit treatment should be offered to all acute stroke patients, and suicide risk assessments should be improved.
audits.c: Improvement measures were started quickly following each audit and followed up by directors and local boards.

audits.t: Management of hypertensive patients in primary health care setting, auditing the practice.
audits.tp: Hypertension management and documentation in primary care
audits.st: not reported (internal designed recording form and control target)
audits.f: Age, gender, diabetes, level of care, glucose, lipids and drugs were sufficiently recorded; smoking history, BMI and family history of IHD were poorly recorded; only a quarter of patients had adequately controlled blood pressure.

audits.t: Auditing the impact of implementing the Modern Matron role in an acute teaching trust.
audits.st: Agreed corporate objectives for the Modern Matron (Senior Nurse) role, introduced nationally in 2000 and required in all trusts by April 2002
audits.f: Senior nurses were satisfied with their role; improvements identified in patient care, infection control and leadership themes, including reductions in drug errors, complaints and MRSA bacteraemias
audits.c: Establishment of the Modern Matron (Senior Nurse) role across the trust

audits.t: Audit of the management of genital herpes simplex infection.
audits.st: BASHH (British Association for Sexual Health and HIV) standards for management of genital herpes simplex infection (specific numeric targets not detailed in abstract)
audits.f: 135 patients with primary HSV and 97 with recurrent HSV attended; 60% presenting within 5 days of primary infection were treated with oral acyclovir; 53% of primary HSV patients were given written/verbal information; follow-up appointments attended by 78%; 77% of recurrent HSV patients had at least one viral isolate typed; 72% of those with more than six episodes annually were offered suppressive therapy

audits.t: Explicit and implicit evaluation of physician adherence to hypertension guidelines.
audits.st: Seventh Report of the Joint National Committee (JNC 7) hypertension guidelines, 22 criteria
audits.f: Mean overall guideline adherence was 53.5% and did not improve significantly over time; nonadherence was judged justifiable in only 6.6% of failed criteria.

audits.t: Influencing referral practice using feedback of adherence to NICE guidelines: a quality improvement report for dyspepsia.
audits.st: NICE guidelines for the management of dyspepsia (referral criteria for upper GI endoscopy)
audits.f: GP adherence to guideline referral criteria was 55%; hospital doctor adherence was 70%; hospital doctor referrals averaged 26.6 per week
audits.c: Referrals were assessed against NICE dyspepsia guidelines by two part-time GPs, with feedback sent to clinicians whose requests did not adhere to the referral criteria
audits.r2: GP adherence increased significantly to 75%; no significant change in hospital doctor adherence; hospital doctor referrals fell 31% to 18.4 per week (highly significant); estimated drop of 3.2 referrals per week from general practice was not significant (p=0.065), while an estimated drop of 10.0 referrals per week for hospital doctors was very significant

audits.t: An audit of "do not attempt resuscitation" decisions in two district general hospitals: do current guidelines need changing?
audits.tp: Do not attempt resuscitation decision documentation
audits.st: National guidelines providing an ethical and legal framework for the process and documentation of do not attempt resuscitation (DNAR) decisions
audits.f: 50 medical inpatients (28 from hospital 1, 22 from hospital 2), average age 78.9 years; DNAR decisions discussed with relatives in 84%, documented in nursing notes in 100%, made by senior team members in 90%, dated and clearly documented in 98%; abbreviations were commonly used in hospital 2 (45.5% vs 0% in hospital 1)

audits.t: The surgical care practitioner: a feasible alternative. Results of a prospective 4-year audit at St Mary's Hospital Trust, London.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 381 minor operative cases performed over 4 years (32, 74, 114, 161 cases per year); 11 minor complications (7 wound infections resolved with oral antibiotics, 2 seromas, 1 wound dehiscence re-sutured); 71% seen within 1 month of referral, 16% within 1-2 months, 3% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months; 59% seen within 20 minutes of appointment time; a 3-month patient perspective audit (59 questionnaires) found 100% totally satisfied, 98% happy to see the surgical care practitioner and 98% would recommend them

audits.t: An audit of patients' understanding of routine preoperative investigations.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Most patients had only a vague understanding of the preoperative investigations they would undergo; doctors were identified as the main source of information

audits.t: Admission and discharge practices: High Dependency Unit audit outcome.
audits.tp: High Dependency Unit admission and discharge practice
audits.st: Local inclusion/exclusion guidelines and admission documentation protocols
audits.f: Inclusion/exclusion criteria were adhered to, but documentation of patient condition and care plan was poorly completed and frequently absent during intra-hospital transfer.

audits.t: Development of a TLD mailed system for remote dosimetry audit for (192)Ir HDR and PDR sources.
audits.tp: Remote dosimetry audit for brachytherapy sources
audits.st: EQUAL-ESTRO external radiotherapy dose-check methodology
audits.f: Total uncertainty in measured absorbed dose to water was 3.27% (1 SD); results were classified into four levels of agreement with the stated dose, and one error was detected.

audits.t: An audit of footwear for patients with leg bandages.
audits.tp: Footwear adequacy for patients with leg bandages
audits.st: Adequate footwear should be available for patients wearing bandages or dressings on the feet and legs (implied local standard; no numeric target stated)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An audit of compliance with motor traffic regulations and use of green warning lights by consultants recalled to hospital to attend emergencies.
audits.tp: Consultant compliance with traffic regulations on emergency recall
audits.st: UK motor traffic regulations; the Association of Chief Police Officers advised that consultants should observe all traffic regulations at all times
audits.f: 220 questionnaires distributed, 166 replies received; 21% of respondents owned a green warning light (GWL); almost 50% would consider exceeding speed limits when recalled to an emergency; between 43% and 80% would cross red traffic lights depending on GWL usage/ownership; 12.7% (21) had been stopped for traffic violations, 2.4% (4) prosecuted and 4.8% (8) involved in accidents while attending emergencies

audits.t: Facilitating quality improvement in physician management of comorbid chronic disease in an urban minority practice.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence in comorbid chronic disease management
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines for common chronic conditions (COPD, asthma, heart failure, coronary artery disease, etc.)
audits.f: 59% had >=2 comorbid conditions, 32% had >=3; guideline adherence was highest for COPD (90%) and asthma (80%), lower for heart failure (75%) and coronary artery disease (58%), and lower still for other conditions.

audits.t: Initial management of infertility: an audit of pre-referral investigations and exploration of couples' views at the interface of primary and secondary care.
audits.st: Expected pre-referral investigations for infertility: mid-luteal serum progesterone, rubella status and semen analysis (implied referral-pathway standard; no numeric target stated)
audits.f: Mid-luteal progesterone performed in 105 of 250 cases (51%); rubella status checked in 42 (20%); semen analysis arranged in 70 (34%); 93% of patients were satisfied or very satisfied with the hospital consultation versus 84% with the GP consultation

audits.t: A UK audit of screening for the metabolic side effects of antipsychotics in community patients.
audits.st: Audit standard derived from published guidelines: patients prescribed antipsychotics should have blood pressure, BMI (or other obesity measure), blood glucose (or HbA1c) and plasma lipids measured at least once a year
audits.f: A recorded measurement within the previous year was found for blood pressure in 26%, obesity in 17%, blood glucose/HbA1c in 28% and plasma lipids in 22%, with all four measures documented in only 11%; 6% had a documented diagnosis of diabetes, 6% hypertension and 6% dyslipidaemia

audits.t: Audit of the care of the dying in a network of hospitals and institutions in Queensland.
audits.tp: Care of the dying against the Liverpool Care Pathway
audits.st: 18 goals of the Liverpool Care Pathway for the dying
audits.f: Several goals were poorly documented, especially communication, resuscitation orders and care after death; written information for families was rarely documented; hospice units achieved most goals more often than other settings.

audits.t: Comprehensive coronary artery disease care in a safety-net hospital: results of Get With The Guidelines quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Coronary artery disease guideline-based medication use
audits.st: American Heart Association Get With The Guidelines coronary artery disease programme (4 cardioprotective drug classes)
audits.f: 18% of eligible patients received all 4 recommended drug classes at discharge (95% CI 12%-25%) in 1998-1999.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary, nurse-manager-led quality-improvement programme using the AHA Get With The Guidelines patient management tool, started August 2000.
audits.r2: 72% of eligible patients received all 4 recommended drug classes at discharge (95% CI 65%-79%), up from 50% in 2000 and 62% in 2001.

audits.t: The forgotten ureteric JJ stent and its prevention: a prospective audit of the value of a ureteric stent logbook.
audits.tp: Ureteric stent follow-up and removal tracking
audits.st: Local standard: ureteric stents should be tracked and removed on schedule via a logbook follow-up system (no explicit numeric target stated)
audits.f: 47 of 210 patients (22.4%) were unaccounted for as having their stents removed within the stent logbooks; one patient was lost to follow-up and re-presented with stent encrustation 10 months later
audits.c: A new system was introduced including a patient education leaflet and removal date scheduling prior to hospital discharge, replacing the stent logbook

audits.t: [Maternal deaths audit in four Benin referral hospitals: quality of emergency care causes and contributing factors].
audits.tp: Maternal death audit and quality of emergency obstetric care
audits.st: not reported (quality of emergency obstetric care assessed against expected standard of care)
audits.f: Poor quality of care was noted in 59% of maternal deaths; direct obstetric causes accounted for 74%, mainly haemorrhage (32.2%) and infection (31.6%); maternal mortality ratio did not improve over 10 years.

audits.t: Perioperative fluid management: prospective audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: No correlation between routinely available fluid balance parameters and quantities of fluid/electrolytes prescribed; 57 of 106 patients (54%) developed at least one fluid-related complication; these patients received significantly more fluid and sodium, had higher non-fluid complication and death rates and longer hospital stay; mean daily fluid load predicted fluid-related complications on multivariate analysis

audits.t: Peer chart audits: a tool to meet Accreditation Council on Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) competency in practice-based learning and improvement.
audits.st: ACGME practice-based learning and improvement competency requirement for documentation of diabetic foot examination (neurological, vascular, skin)
audits.f: 13% of patients had documented neurological foot exams; 45% had documented vascular exams
audits.c: Repeated peer chart audits by resident physicians on their peers' patient records, with no formal feedback or education provided
audits.r2: Documentation increased to 33% for neurological exams (+20 points, p=0.001) and to 71% for vascular exams (+26 points); skin exam documentation also improved (exact figure truncated in the abstract)

audits.t: Community-acquired pneumonia: doctors do not follow national guidelines.
audits.tp: Community-acquired pneumonia severity assessment guideline adherence
audits.st: British Thoracic Society (BTS) guidelines for assessment and management of community-acquired pneumonia, including severity scoring
audits.f: 65 of 165 patients were wrongly coded as CAP and excluded, leaving 100 in the study; 48% did not receive a severity score
audits.c: An educational programme on CAP management was introduced
audits.r2: 43 of 130 were excluded, leaving 87 enrolled; 87% did not receive a severity score, a significant increase (worsening) from 48% in 2001/2
