audits.t: An audit of treatment outcome in acromegalic patients attending our center at Bergamo, Italy.
audits.st: not reported (hormonal targets for GH/IGF-I)
audits.f: At last evaluation 22% were cured, 37.1% controlled by ongoing drugs, 22.6% had discordant GH/IGF-I, and 18.2% still had active disease; safe GH and normal IGF-I achieved in 78% and 63.5% overall.

audits.t: General practitioners and pharmaceutical sales representatives: quality improvement research.
audits.tp: Practice policy on pharmaceutical sales representative access
audits.st: Locally developed practice policy on GP-pharmaceutical sales representative interaction
audits.f: Before intervention GPs spent an average of 40 min/doctor/month with pharmaceutical sales representatives; 239 items of promotional material and 4,660 sample tablets were present.
audits.c: Staff survey and feedback, followed by a staff-voted practice policy restricting reception booking of PSR visits, sample cupboard access and consulting-hours visits.
audits.r2: Promotional material reduced by 32% and sample tablets by 59% at 3 months, sustained at 9 months; generic prescribing increased significantly at 3 months (OR 2.28) and 9 months (OR 2.07).

audits.t: Audit of compliance with NICE guidelines on the use of tension-free vaginal tape slings for stress incontinence.
audits.tp: TVT sling insertion NICE guideline compliance
audits.st: NICE guidelines on the use of tension-free vaginal tape (TVT) slings for stress urinary incontinence, including trialling conservative measures first and documenting risk factors and consent
audits.f: 95 TVT sling insertions (79 by gynaecologists, 16 by urologists); conservative measures had been tried by 43 patients (45.3%); documentation of risk factors ranged from 70% (failure, intermittent catheterisation) to 1% (laparotomy, dyspareunia); compliance and consent documentation were significantly better when insertions were carried out by gynaecologists than by urologists; all insertions were performed by, or under direct supervision of, consultants

audits.t: An audit of blood pressure control in clinical practice in Thailand.
audits.tp: Blood pressure control in clinical practice
audits.st: JNC 7 blood pressure target (130/80 mmHg for diabetic patients) and general target <140/90 mmHg
audits.f: 44% of patients had BP <140/90 mmHg; only 12.3% of diabetic patients reached the JNC 7 target of 130/80 mmHg.

audits.t: Transfer delay audit.
audits.tp: A&E to medical ward transfer time
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average transfer time for all patients was 91.5 minutes; the longest average (105 minutes) occurred in the 17:00-24:00 interval; 26.5% of patients arrived later than 2 hours after referral

audits.t: National audit of cerebrospinal fluid testing.
audits.st: National guidelines for spectrophotometric scanning of CSF for haem pigments and bilirubin; national reference ranges for CSF glucose, protein and lactate are not yet standardised
audits.f: Most laboratories analysed CSF satisfactorily; there was variation in reference ranges used for glucose, protein and lactate; concerns were raised about sample rejection policies and the wavelengths used to measure bilirubin; some hospitals lacked spectrophotometric scanning for haem pigments and bilirubin, though those that performed it did so in line with national guidelines

audits.t: Fall incidence and fall prevention practices at acute care hospitals in Singapore: a retrospective audit.
audits.tp: Fall incidence and fall prevention practice
audits.st: Fall Prevention Clinical Practice Guidelines
audits.f: 825 fallers; fall rates ranged 0.68-1.44 per 1,000 patient days; injury proportion 27.4%-71.7%; a fall risk assessment tool was documented in 77% of nursing records.

audits.t: Fluoroquinolone prescriptions in a teaching hospital: a prospective audit.
audits.st: not reported (local criteria for necessary/appropriate fluoroquinolone use)
audits.f: 55% of fluoroquinolone prescriptions evaluated were unnecessary or inappropriate.

audits.t: A comparison of patients' perceptions and an audit of health promotion practice within a UK hospital.
audits.tp: Health promotion screening and delivery documentation vs patient perception
audits.st: Requirement for UK hospitals to monitor health promotion services (screening for smoking, alcohol, obesity, diet, physical activity)
audits.f: Agreement between audit and questionnaire for screening was at best fair; agreement for health promotion delivery was moderate for alcohol, poor for exercise, and no different from chance for smoking and diet; agreement on risk factor identification was very good for obesity, good for smoking, moderate for alcohol

audits.t: The role of surgical audit in improving patient management; nasal haemorrhage: an audit study.
audits.tp: Home management of nasal haemorrhage (epistaxis) with nasal packing
audits.st: New locally developed guidelines for management of nosebleeds, nasal packing protocol (with Netcel) and discharge policy
audits.f: Previously all patients requiring nasal packing were admitted; mean 28 patients admitted per month, mean inpatient stay 2.67 days
audits.c: New guidelines for nosebleed management, nasal packing protocol, discharge policy, staff training, and patient information leaflets
audits.r2: Total admissions significantly reduced by over 70% (chi2=25.05, df=6)

audits.t: Setting the records straight--a prospective audit of the quality of case notes in a surgical department.
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England guidelines for case note content
audits.f: 80% compliance was achieved for 16/35 standards and 100% for 8 operation-sheet standards; entries such as every-entry timing (16%), clinician name printed (8%), designation (2%) and family history (11%) fell well short of 80%.

audits.t: An audit of technical pitfalls of gastric barostat testing in dyspepsia.
audits.tp: Technical pitfalls of gastric barostat testing
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 98.1% of studies were well tolerated and 94.1% were technically adequate; interpretation was hampered in 4.4% due to low intra-balloon volumes and 1.5% due to suspected air leaks.

audits.t: The under use of thromboprophylaxis in older medical in-patients: a regional audit.
audits.tp: Thromboprophylaxis use in elderly medical inpatients
audits.st: Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN) guidelines on the use of thromboprophylaxis
audits.f: 601 patients studied (mean age 84.6 years); 117 (19.5%) had indications for thromboprophylaxis with no contraindications, of whom only 34 (29%) were receiving prophylaxis as per guidelines; more than one indication was present in 17% of those left untreated; medical ward patients were more likely to receive appropriate treatment than geriatric ward patients (43% vs 23%, p=0.03)

audits.t: An audit of the safe use of the mini c-arm image intensifier in the out-patient setting.
audits.tp: Mini C-arm image intensifier use in outpatient clinic
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: [Audit of the severe obstetrical morbidity (near miss) in Gabon].
audits.st: not reported (quality of emergency obstetric care management from arrival to discharge)
audits.f: Near-miss prevalence was 3.15%; almost 40% of women waited more than 45 minutes to be seen by qualified personnel; clinical examination was impossible in 22% due to lack of equipment; average time to surgery was 5 hours 15 minutes.

audits.t: Adherence to and efficacy and safety of an insulin protocol in the critically ill: a prospective observational study.
audits.tp: Insulin protocol adherence in critically ill patients
audits.st: Local insulin protocol with target blood glucose 81-110 mg/dL
audits.f: Adherence to the protocol was 71%; blood glucose was in the target range 42% of the time; 60% of patients had at least one hypoglycaemic event.

audits.t: CLINICAL ACTIVITIES AUDIT: A Useful Tool for Changing Clinicians' Practice.
audits.tp: Objective pain and disability outcome measure use
audits.st: Six locally-devised audit criteria on assessment of pain/disability, investigations, referrals and outcome measures, as part of the CPD programme
audits.f: Baseline use of objective pain and disability outcome measures among chiropractors and osteopaths
audits.c: Each participant received a learning guide on clinical tools for pain and disability measurement after completing round 1
audits.r2: Practitioners' use of objective pain, disability and outcome measures was significantly higher in round 2 than round 1

audits.t: A 5-year audit of rhinology procedures carried out in a district general hospital.
audits.st: Quoted literature complication rates for rhinology surgery, used as a comparison benchmark; no formal named standard
audits.f: 2507 rhinology procedures out of 10,768 total ENT procedures; 39 complications, an overall rhinology complication rate of 1.56%, comprising 12 postoperative nosebleeds (0.48%), 5 infections after septal surgery (0.56%), 7 septal perforations (0.75%) and various minor FESS complications (2.17%); no major complications or deaths

audits.t: An audit of INR control in the Australian indigenous setting.
audits.tp: Warfarin (INR) control against target therapeutic range
audits.st: Cited benchmark of 60% time in therapeutic INR range (TTR)
audits.f: Patients were in the target INR range 44.9% of the time, below the cited 60% benchmark for time in therapeutic range.

audits.t: Educational quality improvement report: outcomes from a revised morbidity and mortality format that emphasised patient safety.
audits.tp: Morbidity and mortality conference redesign for patient safety
audits.st: not reported (educational quality improvement objectives on patient safety culture)
audits.f: Average attendance was 41+/-8 participants before the redesign; baseline attitudinal survey completed before the intervention.
audits.c: Interdisciplinary redesign of the internal medicine M&M conference to a Patient Safety MMC, with root cause analysis and system-improvement discussion for each adverse event.
audits.r2: 121 system-improvement recommendations were made, 39 pursued, 23 implemented, 11 partially implemented, 5 abandoned; attendance rose to 50+/-10; 6 of 20 survey items showed substantial change, mostly in the desired direction.

audits.t: Audit of an acute pain service in a tertiary care hospital in a developing country.
audits.st: American Society of Anesthesiologists task force guidelines for acute pain services
audits.f: Analgesic techniques used were intravenous infusion (50%), patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (18%) and epidural infusion (30%); nausea/vomiting occurred in 10% of IV infusion and PCIA patients, motor block in 29% of epidural patients.

audits.t: HIPAA compliance in U.S. hospitals: a self-report of progress toward the security rule.
audits.st: Federal HIPAA Security Rule requirements
audits.f: Baseline self-reported HIPAA security compliance recorded in 2004.
audits.c: not reported (repeat survey one year later)
audits.r2: Overall trend of increased HIPAA security compliance from 2004 to 2005, with no significant difference by hospital size for most standards.

audits.t: An audit of nutritional care in a health board in Scotland.
audits.st: Locally developed nutritional standards and audit tool, produced by a multidisciplinary team
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Initiatives were introduced to address areas of identified challenge in nutritional care (specifics not detailed in the abstract)

audits.t: Chronic wound audit: evaluation of a tissue viability service.
audits.tp: Chronic wound prevalence and tissue viability service
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 56 of 372 patients had 82 chronic wounds; pressure ulcers (grades 1-4 including moisture lesions) accounted for 47.5%, surgical wounds for 20.7%; mean bed stay for medical and surgical patients combined was 28.5 days, with surgical patients alone having a median stay of 45.5 days
audits.c: Purchase of pressure relieving equipment, development of a pressure ulcer helpline, and focused education on pressure ulcer prevention across the wards

audits.t: Physician peer assessments for compliance with methadone maintenance treatment guidelines.
audits.tp: Physician compliance with methadone maintenance treatment guidelines
audits.st: Methadone maintenance treatment (MMT) guidelines of the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario
audits.f: Compliance was greater than 90% for most areas of care; compliance was below 90% for take-home medication procedures, urine toxicology screening, HBV/HCV/HIV/TB/STI screening and psychosocial assessment; mean global compliance was 94.3% (SD 7.4%, range 70-100%).

audits.t: [Use of Eschmann's gum elastic bougie in difficult orotracheal intubation, an audit over eight years of clinical practice].
audits.tp: Gum elastic bougie use in difficult intubation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Eschmann's gum elastic bougie was used 276 times with a 99% success rate.

audits.t: Audit on source strength determination for HDR and PDR (192)Ir brachytherapy in Sweden.
audits.tp: Source strength determination audit for brachytherapy
audits.st: not reported (national dosimetry standard comparison)
audits.f: Reference air kerma rate values from the external audit, hospitals and vendors agreed within guaranteed uncertainty limits.

audits.t: Are we abusing our alginate impressions? An audit.
audits.tp: Alginate impression technique compliance in undergraduate clinic
audits.st: Proper clinical handling procedures and operator technique for alginate impressions, based on scientific principles and best practice
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Development of a series of guidelines/steps for correct alginate impression technique, used as a teaching tool

audits.t: [Pain-free hospital audit: a pre-post assessment].
audits.st: not reported (statistical process control monitoring of local quality indicators)
audits.f: Before stabilisation, baseline pain prevalence, relief and satisfaction were monitored monthly using P-charts.
audits.c: Implementation of care through a nurse-managed acute pain unit, with monthly monitoring using statistical process control methods.
audits.r2: Hospital-wide acute pain prevalence stabilised at 30%; 85% of patients achieved adequate pain relief and 90% were satisfied with pain management (p<.001).

audits.t: A national census of central neuraxial block in the UK: results of the snapshot phase of the Third National Audit Project of the Royal College of Anaesthetists.
audits.tp: National census of central neuraxial block use (NAP3)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Data received from 304 of 309 hospitals (98.7% response rate), over 90% judged accurate; 27,533 procedures reported in the 2-week period, extrapolated to an estimated 700,000 major central neuraxial blocks annually (315,000 spinal, 287,000 epidural, 42,000 combined spinal-epidural, 56,000 caudal epidural)

audits.t: Colo-anal pouches: lessons from a prospective audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 38 of 42 patients (90.5%) had water-soluble contrast enemas at 6-8 weeks postoperatively; 2 (5.3%) confirmed a normal colo-colonic pouch, 24 (63.2%) normal reports made no mention of the pouch; 3 (7.9%) reported true leaks, 1 (2.6%) an anastomotic stricture, and 8 (21.1%) reported leaks that on review were confirmed to be normal pouch/anastomosis appearances with no leak

audits.t: A post-implementation audit of Douglas Inquiry recommendations for medical record structure.
audits.tp: Compliance with medical record structure reforms
audits.st: Reforms recommended by the Douglas Inquiry into medical record structure
audits.f: Main issues found were staff lack of understanding of operational instructions, incorrect filing procedure, and allocation of inappropriate dividers.

audits.t: Hypertension guideline recommendations in general practice: awareness, agreement, adoption, and adherence.
audits.tp: Hypertension guideline awareness and adherence in general practice
audits.st: Current hypertension guideline recommendations, including statin therapy and measuring blood pressure in both arms initially
audits.f: 99% of GPs were aware of statin therapy guidance but fewer than half (43%, 95% CI 38-48%) adhered to it in practice; 77% were aware blood pressure should initially be measured in both arms, but only 30% agreed (95% CI 26-34%) and 13% adhered (95% CI 10-16%); 19% (95% CI 15-23%) reported adherence to financially incentivised statin guidance without being aware of it or agreeing with it

audits.t: Improving the quality of written prescriptions in a general hospital: the influence of 10 years of serial audits and targeted interventions.
audits.st: Predetermined local standards for good-quality prescribing
audits.f: Deficiencies included prescriber identification missing (58%), illegible prescriptions (14%), missing route (14%), dose (11%), date (11%) and inadequate patient identification (8%); only 53% of charts had medication alert information and 15% had a verbal order.
audits.c: Serial annual audits with feedback, educational sessions for doctors and nurses, modifications to medication charts, hospital-wide prescribing standards and an alert notification system.
audits.r2: Legibility improved to 97%, patient identification to 100%, date documentation to 98%, dose to 99%, route to 97%, and medication alert use to 98%, with reduced prevalence of verbal orders.

audits.t: An audit of viral load in one clinical population to describe features of viraemic patients on antiretroviral therapy.
audits.tp: Viral load suppression in patients on antiretroviral therapy
audits.st: Expected treatment target of undetectable viral load in patients on antiretroviral therapy (exact threshold value not given in the supplied abstract text)
audits.f: 1910 patients were under care on 1 January 2005; 1229 of 1332 (92%) of those exposed to ART for more than 16 weeks had an undetectable viral load

audits.t: A retrospective audit of the management and complications of pelvic inflammatory disease.
audits.tp: Pelvic inflammatory disease management guideline compliance
audits.st: British Association for Sexual Health and HIV (BASHH) guidelines for management of pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)
audits.f: 30 of 249 patients diagnosed with PID failed treatment; chlamydia was found in 30% of these and gonorrhoea in 10%; appropriate antibiotic regimens were used in 96.6% of patients and 66.7% of contacts were traced and treated; of 18 who had laparoscopy, findings were confirmed PID in 5.6%, endometriosis in 27.8%, adhesions with no PID in 27.8%, and no abnormalities in 38%

audits.t: Adherence to NICU transfusion guidelines: data from a multihospital healthcare system.
audits.st: Intermountain Healthcare NICU transfusion guidelines
audits.f: Compliance with guidelines was 70% for erythrocyte transfusions, 69% for platelet transfusions, 65% for fresh frozen plasma and 94% for cryoprecipitate; compliance fell with increasing numbers of transfusions.

audits.t: Audit of endometrial biopsy at outpatient hysteroscopy.
audits.tp: Outpatient hysteroscopy and endometrial biopsy outcomes
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 435 outpatient hysteroscopies performed, 427 available for audit; 405 (94.8%) procedures were successful; 65 endometrial biopsies (18.8%) were reported insufficient, of which 41 (63%) were in postmenopausal women

audits.t: An audit of preoperative blood tests.
audits.tp: Preoperative blood test use in elective surgery
audits.st: NICE 2003 guidelines on routine preoperative tests for elective surgery
audits.f: Preoperative blood tests were performed in excess of NICE guidelines; coagulation screens were requested in excess of guidance in 17.8% of cases.

audits.t: Compliance, attitudes and barriers to post-operative colorectal cancer follow-up.
audits.st: Local stringent colorectal cancer follow-up guideline adopted in 2000
audits.f: Guideline targets were met for 70% of clinic visits, 49% of CEA determinations and 62% of abdominal imaging studies; postoperative colonoscopy did not occur in 6 of 93 patients.

audits.t: Cholesterol goal attainment in patients with coronary heart disease and elevated coronary risk: results of the Hong Kong hospital audit study.
audits.tp: Cholesterol goal attainment in coronary heart disease
audits.st: LDL-C treatment targets for coronary heart disease/CHD-risk equivalent patients
audits.f: 44% of patients not at LDL-C goal at baseline failed to achieve goal over a median follow-up of 1.9 years; each 1 mmol/L increase in baseline LDL-C reduced the likelihood of attaining goal by 64%.

audits.t: Effect of audit and feedback on the accuracy of diagnosis summary for gynecological conditions in Songklanagarind Hospital, Songkhla Province, Thailand.
audits.st: not reported (local diagnosis summary accuracy standard)
audits.f: Correction rate for principal diagnosis in malignant-condition records was 16.7% before intervention.
audits.c: Audit and feedback intervention on diagnosis summary accuracy.
audits.r2: Correction rate for principal diagnosis in malignant-condition records improved to 42.9% after audit and feedback.

audits.t: Audit of use of the partograph at the University College Hospital, Ibadan.
audits.st: Partograph should be used universally to monitor labour, with high-risk patients receiving closer (quarter-hourly) monitoring (implied local/WHO-based standard)
audits.f: High-risk patients were more likely to receive quarter-hourly monitoring than low-risk women (chi2=45.7); labour outcome was favourable for the majority of both low- and high-risk women and their infants

audits.t: The use of antiembolic stockings. part 2: a clinical audit.
audits.tp: Antiembolic stocking (GECS) selection and use practice
audits.st: Best practice principles for graduated elastic compression stocking (GECS) use, derived from a literature review, ahead of new Trust-wide guidelines
audits.f: There was no consistent policy within the surgical services directorate for the correct use of GECS, with conflicting practices regarding whether patients received stockings and which lengths and brands were used
audits.c: Development and implementation of standardised Trust-wide guidelines for GECS selection and use

audits.t: [Perinatal mortality in The Netherlands: an audit is now more necessary than ever].
audits.st: WHO definition of perinatal mortality; comparison with 14 other European countries
audits.f: A 2004 audit feasibility study found that in 9% of perinatal mortality cases, substandard care was very probably related to the death.
audits.c: A nationwide perinatal audit programme in the Netherlands, starting the year of publication (2008).

audits.t: A regional audit of kilovoltage X-rays--a single centre approach.
audits.st: IPEMB Code of Practice (and its Addendum) for determination of absorbed dose for X-rays below 300 kV
audits.f: Mean ratio of visiting to local measured dose was 0.994 (SD 0.006) for 9 low-energy beams and 0.991 (SD 0.011) for 4 medium-energy beams; mean ratio of in-air to in-phantom dose at medium energy was 0.981 (SD 0.024); applicator factors were within ±4% for low and medium energies

audits.t: Prenatal screening for infectious diseases: an analysis of disparities and adherence to policy in California.
audits.tp: Adherence to prenatal infectious disease screening policy
audits.st: California prenatal infectious disease screening guidelines/policy
audits.f: Testing rates were 94.54% for syphilis, 92.69% for rubella, 94.23% for hepatitis B, but only 73.82% for HIV and 69.05% for group B streptococcus (GBS).

audits.t: Audit of sweat testing: a first report from Italian Cystic Fibrosis Centres.
audits.tp: Sweat testing practice for cystic fibrosis diagnosis
audits.st: UK and NCCLS sweat test guidelines
audits.f: Good adherence for storing samples before analysis (90.9%) and performing diagnosis with at least two sweat tests (100%) and chloride analysis (75.7%); quality control procedures were inadequate in 54.6% and external quality assessment scheme participation in 100% (none referred to one); only 15.1% gave proper patient/parent information.

audits.t: Compliance with a risk-factor-based guideline for the prevention of neonatal group B streptococcal sepsis.
audits.tp: Group B streptococcus prophylaxis guideline compliance
audits.st: Risk-factor-based guideline (adopted August 1994) for selective intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis against neonatal group B streptococcal sepsis
audits.f: 105 (13%) of charts reviewed were candidates for intrapartum prophylaxis; overall compliance rate was 65%; compliance by risk factor was preterm delivery 51%, prolonged rupture of membranes 73%, fever/chorioamnionitis 87%, and previous affected child 100%

audits.t: Dosimetric audits of photon beams in radiation therapy centres in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
audits.tp: Dosimetric quality control audit of radiotherapy photon beams
audits.st: Tolerance level of +/-3% deviation between measured and prescribed absorbed dose (Brazilian regulatory licensing standard)
audits.f: Deviations of up to 22% and 18.7% were measured, well outside the +/-3% tolerance, though some centres showed small deviations.
audits.c: Improvement in dosimetry quality control by the radiotherapy centres following the audit programme.
audits.r2: Most deviations fell within the +/-3% tolerance range, showing clear improvement in dose accuracy.

audits.t: Audit of the peri-delivery use of unfractionated heparin in women on therapeutic low-molecular weight heparin.
audits.tp: Peri-delivery anticoagulation regimen for women on therapeutic LMWH
audits.st: Locally developed regimen: fixed thromboprophylactic-dose unfractionated heparin (15,000 units/24 h) commenced the evening before planned delivery, stopped 4 hours pre-delivery and restarted 2-6 hours post-delivery
audits.f: Compliance was good, with 32 of 38 consecutive deliveries managed according to the regimen; there were no cases of postpartum haemorrhage or thrombosis among these 32 deliveries; 21 patients were delivered by caesarean section (11 elective) and 8 received epidural/spinal anaesthesia without complication

audits.t: Analysis of adherence to national nosocomial pneumonia treatment guidelines.
audits.st: National nosocomial pneumonia (HAP/VAP/HCAP) treatment guidelines (early appropriate antimicrobials, de-escalation, minimum effective duration)
audits.f: Adult pneumonia order set used in only 9% of patients; appropriateness of antimicrobial prescribing per guideline was the baseline comparator
audits.c: Multifaceted educational intervention on the guidelines, in conjunction with a pre-existing adult pneumonia order set
audits.r2: Order set utilisation increased to 48% post-education, but appropriateness of antimicrobial prescribing (guideline adherence) did not improve following the educational intervention; use of the order set still commonly resulted in overall noncompliance with consensus guidelines

audits.t: Indications for the removal of impacted mandible third molars at Ibadan--any compliance with established guidelines?
audits.st: NIH criteria and NICE guidelines for extraction of impacted third molars
audits.f: Pericoronitis was the commonest indication (33.6% recurrent, 13.4% acute), followed by apical periodontitis (26.1%); prophylactic extractions occurred in 12.7% of cases; compliance was 87.3% with NIH criteria and 73.9% with NICE guidelines.

audits.t: The effect of nurse champions on compliance with Keystone Intensive Care Unit Sepsis-screening protocol.
audits.st: Michigan Health and Hospital Association Keystone ICU sepsis screening protocol
audits.f: Compliance with sepsis screening was 23% before introduction of nurse champions
audits.c: Introduction of nurse champions into the ICU to promote sepsis screening protocol compliance
audits.r2: Compliance with sepsis screening improved to 74% after introduction of nurse champions

audits.t: [Current status of nutritional care provision to burnt patients: processes audit of a burnt patients department from a tertiary hospital].
audits.tp: Nutritional care process completeness in burns
audits.st: Locally defined nutritional care assessment and intervention process completion criteria
audits.f: Nutritional assessment process completed in 49.4% of audited charts and intervention process in 22.6%

audits.t: The UK nephrostomy audit. Can a voluntary registry produce robust performance data?
audits.st: Predetermined national performance standards/targets for percutaneous nephrostomy set by the Royal College of Radiologists Audit Sub-Committee
audits.f: 85 of 285 hospitals (29.8%) contributed 3262 cases; overall technical success rate 98% and complication rate 6.3%; significant risk factors for complications included rigors, anaemia and impaired renal function; low frequency operators had lower success and higher complication rates than high frequency operators, though all groups exceeded target thresholds; sepsis was a risk factor in most serious complications and all deaths

audits.t: Audit of performance of needle core biopsy diagnoses of screen detected breast lesions.
audits.tp: Needle core biopsy diagnostic performance in breast screening
audits.st: UK suggested performance thresholds for needle core biopsy (NCB) diagnosis of screen-detected breast lesions
audits.f: Absolute sensitivity increased from 84.9% to 96.4% and complete sensitivity increased from 90.9% to 99.7% over the study period; there was a gradual reduction in surgical interventions after benign (B2) and negative (B1) NCB diagnoses; results showed variance from suggested UK performance thresholds for NCB

audits.t: [Effect of a long-term quality improvement program on the risk of infection related to peripheral venous catheters].
audits.st: Local peripheral venous catheter (PVC) insertion and maintenance protocol, with annual prevalence audits
audits.f: Observational audit of practices found 15-20% of PVCs remained in place more than 3 days from 1996 through 2002
audits.c: Continued 10-year multifaceted programme: practice audits, continuing education sessions based on local surveillance data, and surveillance of nosocomial bacteraemia
audits.r2: Proportion of PVCs in place more than 3 days fell to 6.7% in 2005 and 10.7% in 2006; PVC-related bacteraemia fell by more than 50% from 2002 (n=23) to 2006 (n=10)

audits.t: Audit of pre-placement assessments undertaken in an NHS Trust.
audits.tp: NHS pre-placement health assessment outcomes and cost-effectiveness
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 98.5% of employees were passed fit without comment, 1.5% were passed 'fit with comments', and no potential employee was found unfit for NHS work; ten diagnostic categories contributed to a fit-with-comments result; the estimated manpower cost of processing the assessments was approximately £13,502 per year

audits.t: Maternal mortality in Bahrain 1987-2004: an audit of causes of avoidable death.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: National maternal mortality rate 24.7 per 100,000 total births; 17 (28.3%) of 60 deaths judged avoidable, nearly half due to shortage of intensive care beds

audits.t: Mass casualty incidents: are NHS staff prepared? An audit of one NHS foundation trust.
audits.tp: Major incident policy awareness among clinical staff
audits.st: Clinical staff should be familiar with the trust's major incident policy, including immediate action, stand-down procedure, reporting point and action card system (implied local standard; a rolling major incident education programme was in place)
audits.f: 307 proformas distributed with a 34% reply rate; only 41% had read the policy in full, but 70% knew the correct immediate action to take, 76% knew the correct stand-down procedure, 56% knew the correct reporting point, and fewer than 25% knew an action card system was used; nurses' knowledge differed significantly from other staff groups

audits.t: The Canadian Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Audit Study (CanBas).
audits.st: Canadian BPH guidelines
audits.f: Diagnostic evaluation tended to follow examinations recommended by Canadian BPH guidelines; treatment choices tended to follow an evidence-based algorithm by prostate-volume/PSA group; of 5616 patients seen, 849 (19.6% of men) had a BPH diagnosis

audits.t: Hospital quality improvement in Ethiopia: a partnership-mentoring model.
audits.st: 75 key hospital management indicators defined for the programme
audits.f: Baseline presence of 75 key management indicators assessed
audits.c: Countrywide quality improvement initiative placing 24 management mentors in hospitals for 1 year plus a professional development course
audits.r2: Improvement seen in 45 of 75 (60%) key management indicators, totalling 105 indicator improvements across the 14 hospitals (mean 7.5, SD 5.9, per hospital)

audits.t: Septic arthritis: clinical audits would help optimise the management.
audits.st: British Society for Rheumatology (BSR) guidelines for septic arthritis
audits.f: Management fell short of BSR guideline compliance in several areas, including obtaining appropriate cultures before antibiotics and use of inflammatory markers to monitor response; 58% of trainee doctors surveyed were unaware of the guidelines.

audits.t: Patient Advice and Liaison Services: results of an audit survey in England.
audits.tp: Patient Advice and Liaison Service (PALS) national standards compliance
audits.st: Seven national standards for Patient Advice and Liaison Services (PALS)
audits.f: Response rate 65% (representing an estimated 76% of trusts). PALS rated themselves highly against all standards overall, though less highly against standard 2 (seamlessness across health and social care) and standard 6 (acting as a catalyst for culture change). Significant association found between higher funding/staffing and higher performance.

audits.t: An audit of operative notes: facts and ways to improve.
audits.st: Local standard for operative note content: patient identity details, preoperative diagnosis, operation title/details, CMB code, postoperative instructions and author
audits.f: 51.57% of operative notes were incomplete; missing CMB code 13.68%, patient details 6.8%, preoperative diagnosis 6.31%, operation title 6.31%, postoperative instructions 14.73%; only 92 notes were complete

audits.t: A multi-centre audit on the use of vaginal prostaglandin for the induction of labour.
audits.tp: Vaginal prostaglandin induction of labour dosing compliance
audits.st: NICE guideline: maximum total dose of 6 mg prostaglandin E2 tablet or 4 mg prostaglandin E2 gel (3 mg gel for other women) for induction of labour
audits.f: A higher-than-recommended total dose was administered in 11% of women (1 in 9). Women given tablets were 2.6 times more likely to receive a higher-than-recommended maximum dose (OR 2.6, 95% CI 1.8-3.7, p<0.001) and 8.7 times more likely to receive double the recommended dose (95% CI 2.9-24.4, p<0.001).

audits.t: Helicopter scene response: regional variation in compliance with air medical triage guidelines.
audits.st: State consensus guidelines for HEMS scene dispatch (physiologic, anatomic and special criteria)
audits.f: 73% of flights met triage criteria (MTC); physiologic criteria met in 19%, anatomic in 49%, special criteria in 67%; regional MTC likelihood ranged 50-94% (P=0.006)

audits.t: Mood stabilizer loading versus titration in acute mania: audit of clinical practice.
audits.tp: Mood stabiliser loading strategy adherence to recommended practice
audits.st: Recommended practice for serum level monitoring with mood stabiliser loading
audits.f: Loading strategy used in 46.2% of admissions; serum levels taken inconsistently, particularly for valproate, not in accord with recommended practice; average length of stay 30.2 days

audits.t: Quality improvement in long term care: the psychotropic assessment tool (PAT).
audits.tp: Psychotropic medication documentation in dementia care
audits.st: Local quality improvement standard for documenting behavioural symptoms, psychotropic drug use, side effects and risk-benefit discussion
audits.f: 26.5% of residents on antipsychotics, 6.0% on anxiolytics, 2.6% on hypnotics, 55% on antidepressants before PAT
audits.c: Introduction of a Psychotropic Assessment Tool (PAT) form and process, plus a surrogate decision-maker information letter, as part of a quality improvement (PDSA-based) initiative
audits.r2: Antipsychotic use changed to 25.2%, anxiolytics to 4.0%, hypnotics to 3.4%, antidepressants remained 55%; PAT discussion led to medication change recommendations in 25% of residents

audits.t: An audit of the sleep medicine service in Oman.
audits.st: not reported (general reference to international standards)
audits.f: Otolaryngology was the main referring specialty (43%); only 94 of 261 (36%) patients with apnoea-hypopnoea index >15 received CPAP titration and treatment

audits.t: Efficacy of topical PUVA soaks for palmoplantar dermatoses: an audit.
audits.tp: Topical PUVA effectiveness for palmoplantar dermatoses
audits.st: Local standard of 70% positive treatment response
audits.f: Positive response occurred in 51.3% of patients, falling short of the 70% standard set. Number of treatments (P=0.04) and maximum single UVA dose (P=0.03) were associated with positive outcome.

audits.t: Integrated audit as a means to implement unit protocols: a randomized and controlled study.
audits.tp: Pressure ulcer and venous catheter protocol implementation
audits.st: Unit protocols for prevention of pressure lesions and management of peripheral and central venous catheters, with checklist indicators
audits.f: Initial checklist evaluation of protocol indicator adoption in both study groups
audits.c: Clinical-organisational integrated audit with feedback and departmental facilitators (experimental group) versus standard observation (control group), across five time points
audits.r2: Increment in adoption of correct practices for almost all indicators; final investigation showed a significant difference between groups

audits.t: Undertreatment of tracheal carcinoma: multidisciplinary audit of epidemiologic data.
audits.st: Multidisciplinary expert panel (Radboud panel) review of eligibility for curative therapy, compared against a second independent reviewer
audits.f: Actual treatment: surgery 12 (24%), radiotherapy 29 (58%), endobronchial treatment 6 (12%), observation 3 (6%); panel and second reviewer identified 16 additional surgical candidates, a total of 28 (56%) of 50 potentially undertreated; interreviewer disagreement in 4 cases (8%)

audits.t: Audit on the success of partner notification for sexually transmitted infections in the West Midlands.
audits.tp: Partner notification success for sexually transmitted infections
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: For each index patient, 0.54 partners screened for chlamydia and 0.44 for gonorrhoea; 24% of syphilis contacts and 35% of HIV contacts screened; only 9% of 311 screened partners were casual contacts.

audits.t: Cardiovascular risk management at a Maori-led Primary Health Organisation--findings from a cross-sectional audit.
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk screening and management in primary care
audits.st: National CVD risk assessment and management guideline targets
audits.f: 17.5% (248) had calculated 5-year CVD risk >=15%; guideline-practice gaps found in prescribing of cardiovascular medicines and attainment of recommended targets; Maori more likely to be high risk than non-Maori (OR 2.07, 1.51-2.84)
audits.c: Several Tamaki Healthcare initiatives to address the findings were discussed

audits.t: Implementing a pain management program in a long-term care facility using a quality improvement approach.
audits.tp: Pain assessment and management in long-term care
audits.st: Local quality improvement standard for structured pain assessment using verbal/nonverbal pain scales (PDSA model)
audits.f: 50% (19/38) of patients had mild to moderate pain; some regimens exceeded 3g/day of acetaminophen; nursing staff adopted the pain tools successfully
audits.c: Introduction of standardised verbal and nonverbal pain scales, staff training sessions and interdisciplinary decision-making, using the PDSA model

audits.t: Audit of the clinical use of fresh-frozen plasma in Umbria: study design and results of the pilot phase.
audits.st: International guidelines for appropriate indications for fresh-frozen plasma (FFP) use
audits.f: Completeness of request data was good in 50.7% of cases; indication was appropriate in 31.5% of evaluated requests (56.1% of the total); dosage appropriate in 62.7% of evaluated requests (62% of total); significant correction only in INR post-transfusion (p=0.02)

audits.t: Trauma care audit using Srinagarind hospital's audit filter.
audits.st: Srinagarind Hospital's own 14-criteria trauma audit filter (local standard)
audits.f: Mortality rate 0.5% (95% CI 0.3-0.8); emergency medical service, and accident and emergency out- and in-patient service rated satisfactory; obstacles included lack of hospital beds, inappropriate locale, financial and admission processes, and lack of equipment

audits.t: Informed consent in surgery: an audit of practice in Ile-Ife, Nigeria.
audits.st: not reported (local expectation of a well-structured, standardised consent process)
audits.f: 93.75% of patients had knowledge of diagnosis, 85% understood the procedure, but only 26.25% knew an alternative and 15% knew a complication of anaesthesia; 56.25% (45/80) of consent forms were properly filled; no consultant was involved in completing consent forms

audits.t: Use of fresh-frozen plasma at Royal Darwin Hospital: a retrospective audit.
audits.st: National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) and Australian and New Zealand Society for Blood Transfusion (ANZSBT) guidelines
audits.f: 648 of 950 units (68%) used with an appropriate indication; 14% (137 units) given without clear indication; appropriateness could not be established for 17% (165 units) due to inadequate information
audits.c: Employment of a transfusion nurse to monitor FFP (and other blood product) use and provide education, proposed to improve transfusion efficiency and safety

audits.t: Use of a "secure room" and a security guard in the management of the violent, aggressive or suicidal patient in a rural hospital: a 3-year audit.
audits.tp: Secure room and security guard use for psychiatric crises
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Secure room/security guard system used at rate of 1.1 uses/1000 ED visits; 80% of patients treated locally, most released within 2 days; average annual security cost was $16,259.61

audits.t: Audit of prescription of anti-malarial prophylaxis to patients admitted to Royal Centre for Defence Medicine (RCDM) following evacuation from Afghanistan.
audits.st: not reported (expectation that anti-malarial chemoprophylaxis (AMC) taken in theatre should be continued at RCDM)
audits.f: 9 of 26 had been taking AMC prior to admission; only 4 of these were continued on AMC at RCDM

audits.t: Long-term suppressive therapy for herpes simplex - an audit.
audits.tp: Long-term suppressive therapy for herpes simplex guideline compliance
audits.st: British Association for Sexual Health and HIV (BASHH) guidelines
audits.f: 82% (57) had infection for at least 12 months before starting therapy and 78.2% (54) had at least six recurrences per year before treatment. Only 5.8% (4 patients) had a treatment interruption at 12 months or less (not in line with guidelines), and 15.9% (11 patients) had fewer than six outbreaks per year at the start of treatment (in line with guidelines).

audits.t: Standards of care for patients with invasive fungal infections within the United Kingdom: a national audit.
audits.tp: Invasive fungal infection standards of care compliance
audits.st: British Society for Medical Mycology standards of care for invasive fungal infections
audits.f: Speciation of Candida/Aspergillus from sterile sites performed in 42-98% of hospitals; microscopy of bronchoscopy specimens not undertaken in 13 of 62 (21%) laboratories; cryptococcal culture and antigen undertaken routinely in 40-75% and 31-83% of at-risk patients respectively, but in only 12% of abnormal CSFs without risk factors.

audits.t: An audit of the time to initial treatment in avulsion injuries.
audits.tp: Time to initial treatment in dental avulsion injury
audits.st: not reported (implicit expectation of prompt replantation/appropriate storage after avulsion)
audits.f: Only 51 (42.5%) teeth were stored in an appropriate medium before attendance and only 48 (40%) were seen within 1 hour

audits.t: An audit on the reporting of critical results in a tertiary institute.
audits.st: Accreditation requirement for accurate critical result notification with recipient read-back
audits.f: 51 errors detected (error rate 10.8%); most errors were in recording folder number (64.7%), fewest in patient name (5.9%); calls to clinicians had the highest error rate (20%)

audits.t: An audit of referrals to a secondary care sedation unit.
audits.tp: Referral appropriateness to secondary care sedation unit
audits.st: Local referral protocol/standard (baseline measured prior to publication of a referral protocol)
audits.f: 306 referrals reviewed (100 examined in detail); 76.1% (233) from general dental services; average 1.68 referrals per clinician (max 18); 143 (46.7% of 187 assessed) planned for treatment with pharmacological help, 22 (7.2%) without; standards set for referral were not met.

audits.t: Evaluation of appropriate usage of fresh frozen plasma: Results of a regional audit in Iran.
audits.st: British Council for Standardization in Haematology (BCSH) Guidelines 2004
audits.f: 53% of transfusion episodes were inappropriate; 30% of episodes were 'inappropriate' active bleeding with normal/unmeasured coagulation tests; coagulation variables measured at some point in only 66% of transfused patients

audits.t: Sharps management in hospital: an audit of equipment, practice and awareness.
audits.tp: Sharps management equipment, practice and awareness
audits.st: Local infection prevention and control sharps management policy
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Sentinel lymph node biopsy experience in Taranaki: a prospective audit in a provincial New Zealand hospital.
audits.st: Established international performance standards for sentinel lymph node biopsy
audits.f: Sentinel node identified in 97% of patients (93% including training set); metastatic nodal disease in 40/152 (26%); false negative rate 5% (2/40) and negative predictive value 92% in the training set

audits.t: Lessons from an audit of psychoeducation at an older adolescent inpatient unit.
audits.tp: Psychoeducation delivery in adolescent inpatient care
audits.st: Unit philosophy of providing timely, pertinent psychoeducation on illness/diagnosis, medication, diet, outpatient follow-up and alcohol/drug use
audits.f: Patients reported adequate information on medication and illness, and mostly received information on follow-up and substance use, but the majority reported a lack of information on diet; awareness of relapse prevention was lower than expected

audits.t: A quality improvement plan for hypertension control: the INCOTECA Project (INterventions for COntrol of hyperTEnsion in CAtalonia).
audits.st: Recommended clinical practice guidelines for management of hypertensive patients; blood pressure control target
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: A quality improvement plan for primary care professionals comprising educational sessions, feedback, audit, and implementation of recommended clinical practice guidelines for hypertension management

audits.t: A limited effect on performance indicators from resident-initiated chart audits and clinical guideline education.
audits.tp: Chart audit and guideline education effect on quality indicators
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines and quality-of-care indicators for selected medical conditions
audits.f: Baseline chart review of selected patients affected by or eligible for selected conditions/services
audits.c: Educational intervention: seminar on clinical practice guidelines and quality indicators, with resident-initiated chart audits
audits.r2: Some quality indicators significantly improved (documentation of oral examination in children/chronic illness, decreasing medications in anxiety disorders, HbA1c compliance in diabetes); others did not improve

audits.t: UK National Audit of Sexual History-taking: clinic policies audit.
audits.st: Expected clinic policy standards for confidentiality, communication and accessibility in sexual history-taking (specific numeric standard not stated)
audits.f: Almost all clinics provided a confidential, private environment; fewer than half displayed a confidentiality policy in waiting areas, though more had it available by other means; about two-thirds of literature covered the need for sexual history; 60% of clinics assessed clinician communication skills; most had policies for patients whose first language is not English, but only around half had policies for hearing or learning difficulties; policies were lacking for chaperone offer documentation and under-16 consent competency assessment in some clinics.

audits.t: [Durability of the effects of a quality improvement intervention in hypertensive patients on long-term follow-up (CICLO-RISK study)].
audits.st: Clinical guidelines on cardiovascular risk factor management
audits.f: Baseline blood pressure, LDL-cholesterol, HbA1c, smoking, BMI and cardiovascular risk measured in both groups
audits.c: Quality improvement intervention combining audit, feedback and training sessions on cardiovascular risk factor clinical guidelines
audits.r2: Durability effect (intervention minus control) for systolic BP fell from 8.9 to 4.3 mmHg and diastolic from 3.9 to 2.3 mmHg; coronary risk fell from 2 to 1.2 percentage points and cardiovascular mortality risk from 0.6 to 0.4 percentage points

audits.t: Audit and feedback: effects on professional obstetrical practice and healthcare outcomes in a university hospital.
audits.tp: Audit and feedback for evidence-based obstetric practice
audits.st: Six evidence-based obstetric interventions (from the Reproductive Health Library systematic reviews)
audits.f: Baseline prevalence rates of six evidence-based interventions assessed
audits.c: Seminars and workshops presenting baseline audit results and systematic review evidence, with detailed topic discussion (audit and feedback)
audits.r2: Significant reduction in episiotomies (RR 0.84, 0.73-0.97) and increase in continuous companion support (RR 1.42, 1.24-1.63); shift toward the internationally recommended oxytocin dosage of 10 IU for third-stage management

audits.t: Audit of Echocardiographic Services at the University College Hospital Ibadan.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Commonest indications were hypertension (47.1%), pre-chemotherapy assessment (8.2%) and heart failure (7.6%); 44.6% diagnosed with hypertensive heart disease, 36.5% normal study

audits.t: Audit of the effectiveness of command and control arrangements for medical evacuation of seriously ill or injured casualties in southern Afghanistan 2007.
audits.tp: Medical evacuation (MEDEVAC) command and control timeliness
audits.st: 90-minute standard from notification to helicopter landing for Category A/B casualties (in hospital within 2 hours of wounding)
audits.f: Prior rotations showed comparatively longer response times (specific figures not given).
audits.c: Medical operations staff were relocated into the Combined Joint Operations Centre (CJOC), collocating medical and operations staff.
audits.r2: Three-quarters of Category A and B missions met the 90-minute target; mean response time improved compared with the two previous rotations, though median response changed little; no casualties died who were recoverable.

audits.t: [Audit "Toys and incubators in neonatology"].
audits.st: Local hygiene procedures for items and toys placed in incubators
audits.f: 13 of 17 incubators contained items not required by nursing procedures; 24 of 33 toys (73%) scored maximum fluffiness, only 10 had manufacturer cleansing labels; all 6 cultured samples tested positive, including Pseudomonas oryzihabitans matching a case of neonatal septicaemia
audits.c: General feedback to department staff followed by a permanent ban on all items not strictly required by nursing activities from incubators

audits.t: An audit of the Royal College of Ophthalmologists strabismic amblyopia treatment protocol: a departmental review.
audits.st: Royal College of Ophthalmologists strabismic amblyopia treatment protocol
audits.f: 5 of 26 patients failed to comply with the protocol (1 listed for surgery, 4 commenced premature occlusion); 8 patients had equal vision at presentation and all ultimately required occlusion with minimal improvement in only 3.

audits.t: Use of pressure-redistributing support surfaces among elderly hip fracture patients across the continuum of care: adherence to pressure ulcer prevention guidelines.
audits.tp: Pressure ulcer prevention adherence in hip fracture patients
audits.st: Pressure ulcer prevention guidelines for use of pressure-redistributing support surfaces (PRSS)
audits.f: PRSS observed at 36.4% of visits; odds of PRSS use lower in rehabilitation (adjusted OR 0.4), nursing home (adjusted OR 0.2) and on acute readmission (adjusted OR 0.6) than initial acute setting; wide variation in PRSS use by admission hospital

audits.t: Improving maternal care with a continuous quality improvement strategy: a report from the Interventions to Minimize Preterm and Low Birth Weight Infants through Continuous Improvement Techniques (IMPLICIT) Network.
audits.tp: Continuous quality improvement in maternal care (IMPLICIT Network)
audits.st: Five standard maternal care interventions (prenatal depression screening, smoking screening, postpartum contraception planning, and others)
audits.f: Baseline documented delivery of the five standard maternal care interventions assessed
audits.c: Continuous quality improvement (CQI) processes implemented across the practice-based research network
audits.r2: Significant improvement in prenatal depression screening (by 15 weeks), smoking screening at 30 weeks, and postpartum contraception planning; smoking screening by 15 weeks and asymptomatic bacteriuria testing were already >90% at baseline and did not increase significantly; postpartum depression screening remained 50-60% and did not increase significantly

audits.t: Quality improvement in depression care in the Netherlands: the Depression Breakthrough Collaborative. A quality improvement report.
audits.st: Clinical depression guidelines, implemented via a stepped-care model with two treatment intensity levels
audits.f: 78% of non-severely depressed patients and 57% of severely depressed patients were treated according to the stepped-care model; within 3 months 28% of monitored patients had recovered (BDI ≤10), rising to a further 27% between 3 and 6 months
audits.c: Depression Breakthrough Collaborative: development and implementation of a stepped-care depression model/care pathway across 13 multidisciplinary teams (101 health professionals)
audits.r2: The proportion of non-severely depressed patients receiving first-step treatment per the model improved during the project, but this improvement was not seen for severely depressed patients

audits.t: An audit of standards of the 'see and treat' approach in women with a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion on Pap smears.
audits.tp: See-and-treat approach for high-grade cervical lesions
audits.st: National Health Service Cervical Screening Programme (NHSCSP) 2004 guidelines: >90% of women treated at first visit have CIN on histology; primary haemorrhage <5%; admission for treatment complication <2%
audits.f: CIN I or higher prevalence was 92.7% (meets >90% target); primary haemorrhage occurred in 13 (5.3%) women (marginally above the <5% target); 4 (1.6%) women admitted for LEEP-related complications (meets <2% target)

audits.t: Development and implementation of an audit tool for quality control of parenteral nutrition.
audits.st: Locally defined parenteral nutrition (PN) quality criteria and standards, developed from the literature
audits.f: 13 PN quality criteria and standards initially defined and audited
audits.c: Iterative refinement of the audit tool over successive audits: criteria with lower validity were removed, others optimised, and new criteria added to expand coverage
audits.r2: Audit tool expanded to 22 quality criteria across 4 areas (indication/duration, nutrition assessment/monitoring, metabolic/infectious complications, overall efficacy); 9 of the 22 criteria met predefined standards in the past year

audits.t: An urgent access neurovascular clinic: audit of timeliness.
audits.tp: Timeliness of urgent access neurovascular (TIA) clinic
audits.st: National Clinical Guidelines for Stroke / National Stroke Strategy recommendation for evaluation within one week of symptoms
audits.f: Median delay from event to completion of evaluation was 16 days; 45% were seen within two weeks of symptom onset and 15% within one week.

audits.t: An audit of oral glucose tolerance tests at a large teaching hospital: indications, outcomes and confounding factors.
audits.st: Australian guidelines for diagnosis of diabetes mellitus (OGTT recommended for fasting plasma glucose 5.5-6.9 mmol/L)
audits.f: Only 55% of OGTTs had a previous FPG or RPG value warranting the test per guidelines; 41% were performed in the presence of confounding factors such as acute illness or medications affecting glucose

audits.t: Surveillance in Barrett's esophagus: an audit of practice.
audits.st: Recommended surveillance intervals for Barrett's oesophagus (no formal surveillance programme in place)
audits.f: 305 of 472 patients had only one endoscopy/biopsy with no follow-up surveillance; of 165 with repeat surveillance, 44 missed surveillance by >=6 months and 23 missed it by >=2x the recommended interval; none of the 165 progressed to oesophageal adenocarcinoma

audits.t: Requirements, in terms of root canal treatment, of undergraduates in the European Union: an audit of teaching practice.
audits.tp: Undergraduate root canal treatment teaching requirements across EU dental schools
audits.st: European Society of Endodontology (ESE) 2001 Undergraduate Curriculum Guidelines for Endodontology
audits.f: 48 dental schools in 20 countries responded; 94% required students to perform root canal treatment in anterior and posterior teeth; 81% required a minimum number of RCTs (with wide variation); 79% required retreatment; 4% required endodontic surgery.

audits.t: ChronoMedIt--a computational quality audit framework for better management of patients with chronic conditions.
audits.st: Locally defined audit criteria model (lapse in indicated therapy, no measurement recording, time to target, measurement contraindicating therapy)
audits.f: 59% (of 607) and 34% (of 679) of hypertensive patients had at least one episode of a lapse of more than 30 days in antihypertensive therapy

audits.t: Audit of the red cell units supply of a busy hospital blood bank in Nigeria.
audits.tp: Blood bank red cell supply and utilisation
audits.st: not reported (implicit blood bank crossmatch:transfusion ratio metric)
audits.f: Crossmatch performed for 64% of requests; 4.15% of crossmatched units returned unused; crossmatch:transfusion ratio was 0.9:1; Obstetrics/Gynaecology recorded the highest blood usage

audits.t: Cardiovascular disease risk management for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples in primary health care settings: findings from the Kanyini Audit.
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk screening and management guideline adherence (Kanyini Audit)
audits.st: 2004 National Heart Foundation of Australia (NHFA) adjusted Framingham CVD risk guideline
audits.f: 53% not adequately screened for CVD risk per national recommendations; 9% had established CVD; 29% of those >=30 years classified high risk; 40% of those with CVD not prescribed a combination of BP medicines, statins and antiplatelets; 56% of high-risk individuals without CVD not prescribed BP medicines and statins

audits.t: An audit of parents'/guardians' wishes recorded after coronial autopsies in cases of sudden unexpected death in infancy: issues raised and future directions.
audits.tp: Consent documentation for tissue retention after coronial post-mortem
audits.st: Human Tissue Act 2006 requirement for parental/guardian consent to retain or use tissue after Coroner's purposes are fulfilled
audits.f: Parental/guardian agreement for use of blocks and slides for education, audit, quality control and research was 94% (SCH staff), 77% (Coroners' Officers) and 75% (Police Family Liaison Officers); permission for frozen tissue retention was 90%, 62% and 100% respectively.
audits.c: In 2007, Sheffield Children's Hospital introduced a new form, 'Record of parents'/guardians' wishes regarding samples taken at a Coroner's post mortem', to clarify consent for tissue retention/use.
audits.r2: Parental/guardian agreement for use of blocks and slides was 84% (SCH), 37% (Coroners' Officers) and 100% (Police Family Liaison Officers); permission for frozen tissue retention was 90%, 44% and 100% respectively; 44% from Coroners' Officers were still outstanding at the time of audit.

audits.t: A case-based teaching module combined with audit and feedback to improve the quality of consultations.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean consult quality score 2.7 (pre-intervention)
audits.c: Case-based teaching module on medical consultation plus audit and feedback where participants critically reviewed their own recent written consultations
audits.r2: Mean consult quality score rose from 2.7 to 3.3 (P=0.0006); house-staff knowledge score improved 10/14 to 12/14 (P=0.03), faculty 11/14 to 12/14 (P=0.08)

audits.t: Postoperative fluid and electrolyte balance: alarming audit results.
audits.st: Latest consensus guidelines on perioperative fluid and electrolyte management (not named further)
audits.f: Results described as alarming, demonstrating a global lack of application of knowledge and understanding of fluid/electrolyte management (no numeric values given in abstract)

audits.t: Using audits to reduce the incidence of uterine rupture in a Malawian district hospital.
audits.st: Local audit-derived recommendations for obstetric care (no named external guideline)
audits.f: Incidence 19.2 per 1000 deliveries
audits.c: Audit sessions every 2-3 weeks with hospital staff, an extended audit with two external expert obstetricians, and implementation of recommendations addressing delays in referral, diagnosis and treatment
audits.r2: Incidence fell 68% to 6.1 per 1000 deliveries (OR 0.32; 95% CI 0.16-0.63)

audits.t: Improving the coverage of the PMTCT programme through a participatory quality improvement intervention in South Africa.
audits.st: National prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) programme protocol and coverage indicators
audits.f: Coverage of CD4 testing 40%, uptake of maternal nevirapine 57%, uptake of infant nevirapine 15%, six-week PCR testing 24%; weaknesses identified in training and supervision
audits.c: Participatory quality improvement intervention: initial assessment by district supervisors, workshops to identify weaknesses and set targets, monthly facility support with PMTCT protocol orientation, local data review and bottleneck identification using a continuous quality improvement approach
audits.r2: Coverage of CD4 testing increased to 97%, maternal nevirapine uptake to 96%, infant nevirapine uptake to 68%, and six-week PCR testing to 68%

audits.t: GP management of erectile dysfunction: the impact of clinical audit and guidelines.
audits.st: Evidence-based practice guide developed for Australian GPs for erectile dysfunction assessment and management
audits.f: Baseline levels of discussion, psychological history-taking and needs assessment not given numerically
audits.c: Combined clinical audit and practice guide developed specifically for GPs
audits.r2: GP-initiated discussions about erectile dysfunction nearly doubled; 18% increase in psychological history taking; 19% increase in assessment of needs/preferences; decreased specialist referrals; increased provision of phosphodiesterase inhibitor samples

audits.t: [Regional audit on fluoroquinolones usage in the hospital and the community: are these antibiotics over-used?].
audits.st: National recommendations for fluoroquinolone use and a regional referential established to preserve fluoroquinolones
audits.f: 56.8% of prescriptions complied with national recommendations, but only 14.3% complied with the regional referential

audits.t: Surprisingly low compliance to local guidelines for risk factor based screening for gestational diabetes mellitus - A population-based study.
audits.st: Local clinical guidelines for risk-factor-based screening for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)
audits.f: 257 (31.3%) women fulfilled at least one risk criterion for GDM screening per local guidelines; only 79 (30.7%) of these were actually exposed to an oral glucose tolerance test; 7 of these were diagnosed with GDM

audits.t: [Preoperative delay in patients with peptic ulcer perforation: a clinical audit from the Danish National Indicator Project].
audits.tp: Time to theatre for perforated peptic ulcer
audits.st: Danish National Indicator Project criterion: surgery for perforated peptic ulcer within 6 hours of perforation
audits.f: Only half of patients operated within 6 hours; preoperative delay >=6h associated with late first physician attendance, no senior physician involvement, and no oxygen saturation monitoring on admission

audits.t: Oxycodone--an audit of its prescription in a local hospital.
audits.st: Recommended opioid prescribing guidelines
audits.f: Two-thirds of patients not reviewed for analgesia within 24 hours; one-third had no dose titration; majority had appropriate indication and dosing; most had outpatient follow-up within 4 weeks

audits.t: Improving compliance with diabetes clinical practice guidelines in military medical treatment facilities.
audits.st: Health Plan Employer Data and Information Set (HEDIS) benchmarks for type II diabetes management
audits.f: Clinics not compliant with established diabetes management guidelines (HbA1c, lipid, blood pressure, foot check compliance below benchmark)
audits.c: Multidisciplinary, evidence-based care delivery model implemented across the diabetes management team
audits.r2: Site 1: adequately controlled HbA1c rose 80% to 85%, LDL 49% to 58% at 6 months (LDL fell to 56% at 9 months, HbA1c to 82% at 9 months); Site 2: HbA1c control rose 77% to 79% at 6 months

audits.t: A structured framework for improving outbreak investigation audits.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Issues identified: unclear roles/responsibilities, poor inter-agency communication, lack of performance standards especially timeliness

audits.t: Compliance with recommendations for routine HIV screening during pregnancy in Halifax.
audits.st: Canadian Paediatric Society recommendation for routine HIV counselling and testing offer during every pregnancy
audits.f: 65/155 (41.9%) counselled about HIV; 47/65 (72.3%) of those counselled underwent testing

audits.t: Audit of management of periorbital cellulitis and abscess in a district general hospital and a tertiary referral centre, in line with published guidelines.
audits.tp: Periorbital cellulitis and abscess management against published guidelines
audits.st: 2004 published guidelines for management of periorbital cellulitis/abscess
audits.f: District general hospital (58 cases) vs tertiary referral centre (61 cases): 63% vs 95% correctly seen by an ophthalmologist and 39% vs 82% by a senior ENT surgeon; one patient at each site missed an indicated CT scan; 68% (DGH) vs 76% (tertiary) correctly treated with intravenous antibiotics; neither site achieved 100% compliance with twice-daily ophthalmological monitoring.

audits.t: Burn injuries caused by hot water bottles: audit and loop closure.
audits.tp: Hot water bottle burn injury reduction
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Cases classified into bottle failure and/or patient misuse categories following a multimedia campaign after a scalding death
audits.c: Multimedia public awareness campaign, and advocacy for government review of manufacturing standards/legislation
audits.r2: Admissions from hot water bottle burns markedly decreased following legislation and the multimedia campaign

audits.t: Audit of initial management of congenital hypothyroidism in the United Kingdom--comparison of UK practice with European and UK guidelines.
audits.st: European and UK guidelines for management of neonatal congenital hypothyroidism
audits.f: Response rate 86%; the majority were largely compliant with both guidelines; 43% reviewed newly referred infants on the day of notification; 26% treated severe CH with a regimen not detailed in the available abstract text.

audits.t: Introducing maternal morbidity audit in the Netherlands.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Substandard care identified in 53/67 (79%) of women

audits.t: Auditing the technology used to measure blood pressure.
audits.tp: Accuracy and calibration of blood pressure measurement equipment
audits.st: Calibration and validation standards for sphygmomanometers
audits.f: Of devices surveyed, half were oscillometric, 32% aneroid and 18% mercury; faults found in 30% of aneroid and 32% of mercury devices (mostly cuffs, hoses, connectors); 18% of aneroid devices had calibration errors (mostly 4 mmHg at pressures above 200 mmHg); nearly 90% of aneroid devices had only one cuff size available.

audits.t: An audit of the quality of care of traumatic brain injury at a busy regional hospital in South Africa.
audits.st: Agreed standardised markers of quality of care for traumatic brain injury (locally agreed, not named)
audits.f: Referral letters and A&E clerking notes revealed major deficits against agreed quality-of-care markers

audits.t: Using PACS audit data for process improvement.
audits.st: Internal process-improvement goal: reduce time from examination arrival to verification (target <1 hour)
audits.f: Delays in report verification identified as a cause of poor clinical access to radiology reports; many examinations took longer than 1 hour to be verified
audits.c: Mining of PACS audit log data with an in-house application to identify specific examinations/users and use as an educational process-improvement tool
audits.r2: Dramatic reduction in examinations taking longer than 1 hour to be verified

audits.t: National UK audit of the short synacthen test.
audits.tp: Short Synacthen Test (SST) protocols across UK laboratories
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Workloads were highly variable; most laboratories broadly agreed on indications, contraindications, timing and reference ranges, but there was variability in cortisol assay bias, which had not been translated into corresponding cut-off values.

audits.t: The evaluation of a Taiwanese training program in smoking cessation and the trainees' adherence to a practice guideline.
audits.st: Practice guideline for smoking cessation counselling (ask, advise, assess willingness, assist, arrange follow-up)
audits.f: Significant difference existed between pre- and post-test knowledge scores; specific baseline knowledge score not given
audits.c: Government-mandated certification training programme in smoking cessation, required for reimbursement eligibility
audits.r2: Adherence to the practice guideline: 86% asked smoking status, 88% advised smokers to quit, 76% assessed willingness to quit, 59% assisted smokers to quit, 60% arranged follow-up visits; confidence in providing services was lower at long-term than short-term evaluation

audits.t: [Adherence to antibiotherapy guidelines for acute community-acquired pneumonia in adults, in a teaching hospital].
audits.st: National guidelines for antibiotic treatment of community-acquired pneumonia
audits.f: First antibiotic choice conformed to guidelines in 52.3% of cases; treatment duration inappropriate in 52.7% (usually too long); antibiotic modification at 48-72h in 46.8%

audits.t: Platelet function testing: auditing local practice and broader implications.
audits.st: Current CLSI guidelines for platelet aggregation testing
audits.f: Platelet count adjustment using autologous platelet-poor plasma (as recommended by CLSI) found to cause considerable diminution of detectable platelet function; different blood collection tubes altered PFA-100 closure times

audits.t: An audit of patients attending a general medical follow-up clinic.
audits.tp: Multiple clinic attendance in follow-up outpatients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 113 (27%) attending another clinic for the same or related problem; 98/113 (87%) at a different hospital

audits.t: Adherence to the National Quality Forum (NQF) breast cancer measures within cancer clinical trials: a review from ACOSOG Z0010.
audits.tp: Breast cancer national quality measure adherence
audits.st: National Quality Forum (NQF) performance measures for breast cancer treatment (2007)
audits.f: Whole-breast radiation given to 95% teaching-affiliate, 92% academic, 91% community patients; underinsured/uninsured patients received radiation less often (85% vs 93% insured); excisional biopsy for diagnosis 28.6% teaching-affiliate vs 36.8-37.4% academic/community; adjuvant chemotherapy given in 79-85% and tamoxifen in 79-82% of eligible institutions

audits.t: An audit of the implementation of the international consensus group's guidelines on reporting of blood films.
audits.tp: Implementation of international guidelines for reporting of blood films
audits.st: International Consensus Group for Haematology Review guidelines on reporting of blood films
audits.f: Of 151 laboratory sites (74 organisations), 24 laboratories had implemented the guideline (21 with local modification, 3 without).

audits.t: Compliance with atypical antipsychotic triage guidelines by Texas poison centers.
audits.st: Simplified version of published atypical antipsychotic triage guidelines (December 2007)
audits.f: Overall compliance rate 64.1% (71.7% aripiprazole, 43.6% clozapine, 71.6% olanzapine, 60.8% quetiapine, 65.5% risperidone, 59.0% ziprasidone)

audits.t: Quality of care of Egyptian asthmatic children: clinicians adherence to asthma guidelines.
audits.st: Asthma diagnosis and management guidelines (not individually named)
audits.f: 76.2% of physicians agreed with asthma guidelines; poor knowledge found in 28.5%, poor practice in 43.6%, and poor attitude in 14.4% of physicians; disagreement mainly attributed to poor patient socioeconomic status (18.1%) and poor patient compliance (16%)

audits.t: Exploring the factors associated with hand hygiene compliance of nurses during routine clinical practice.
audits.st: Guidelines for proper hand hygiene practice
audits.f: Compliance 41.7% before procedure, 72.1% after procedure; overall compliance 34.3%

audits.t: Management of COPD in general practice in Denmark--participating in an educational program substantially improves adherence to guidelines.
audits.tp: COPD guideline adherence in general practice
audits.st: Guidelines for diagnosis, staging and treatment of COPD
audits.f: FEV1 registered in GP files for 45% of patients; medication use in patients with mild disease (FEV1 >80% predicted) was 76%
audits.c: Educational programme for participating GPs and their staff on COPD diagnosis, staging and treatment
audits.r2: FEV1 registration increased to 69%; medication use in patients with mild disease (FEV1 >80% predicted) declined from 76% to 45%

audits.t: Adherence to perinatal group B streptococcal prevention guidelines.
audits.tp: Group B streptococcus prevention guideline adherence
audits.st: 2002 revised CDC perinatal GBS prevention guidelines (universal screening at 35-37 weeks and intrapartum chemoprophylaxis)
audits.f: 84.7% screened, though 26.3% of tests performed before 35 weeks; 61.2% of women with an indication received optimal chemoprophylaxis (70.9% among those admitted >=4h before delivery)

audits.t: Intrahospital transfer of critically ill patients; a prospective audit within Flinders Medical Centre.
audits.tp: Intrahospital transfer of critically ill patients
audits.st: Minimum standards for intrahospital transport of critically ill patients (PS39, 2003)
audits.f: Adequate staffing in 75%; oxygen saturation and blood pressure monitoring present in 97%, heart rate 90.5%, ECG 84.5%, capnometry 75%; 44% of transfers had an incident

audits.t: Improved clinical outcomes combining house staff self-assessment with an audit-based quality improvement program.
audits.tp: Unplanned ICU transfer review and escalation of care
audits.st: Institutional criteria for medical emergency response team/critical care consult activation
audits.f: Calls meeting medical emergency response team criteria 53%; nurse notification of change in condition 65%; nursing documentation of change/follow-up 65%
audits.c: Audit-based quality improvement using physician and nursing self-assessment tools and a focused monthly Morbidity & Mortality conference; new policies on vital signs and house-staff escalation of care
audits.r2: Calls meeting criteria rose to 73%; nurse notification rose to 100%; nursing documentation rose to up to 90%; cardiac arrests fell from 3.1 to 0.6/1000 discharges (p=0.002); deaths fell from 34 to 24/1000 discharges (p=0.024)

audits.t: Using an audit of medical student behavior to inform curriculum change.
audits.st: Standard precautions and faculty guidelines for HIV exposure incidents
audits.f: Not all students followed standard precautions or faculty guidelines for exposure incidents (no percentage given)

audits.t: An audit to establish the proportion of cervical punch biopsies that meet criteria for adequacy.
audits.st: Guideline-derived criteria for cervical punch biopsy adequacy
audits.f: Most biopsies met criteria for adequacy, except presence of an intact squamo-columnar junction (SCJ), seen in only 14%; grade discrepancy between punch biopsy and LLETZ was most likely when the SCJ was traumatised, not represented, or the original biopsy was negative or ungradable.

audits.t: Use of magnesium sulfate in pre-eclampsia and eclampsia in teaching hospitals in Addis Ababa: a practice audit.
audits.st: Hospital protocol for magnesium sulfate use in severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia
audits.f: Appropriate patient selection in 93.7% (89/95); correct loading dose given in 90.4% (85/95); overall clinical monitoring inadequate against hospital protocol; 2 maternal deaths (not attributed to MgSO4 toxicity)

audits.t: Prospective audit of febrile neutropenia management at a tertiary university hospital in Singapore.
audits.st: New risk-stratified febrile neutropenia management protocol (introduced October 2008)
audits.f: Overall compliance to protocol 56.7%, mainly due to reluctance to use oral antibiotics first-line for low-risk episodes
audits.c: Launch of a new febrile neutropenia protocol incorporating risk stratification

audits.t: Does a gating policy for ANCA overlook patients with ANCA associated vasculitis? An audit of 263 patients.
audits.tp: Targeted ANCA testing (gating) policy for suspected vasculitis
audits.st: Local clinical gating policy for ANCA testing
audits.f: Prior to the gating policy, ANCA requests averaged 287 (SD 30) per month.
audits.c: Introduction of a targeted ANCA gating policy with clinical guidelines to ensure appropriate test usage.
