audits.r2: Following the policy, monthly ANCA requests fell to 143 (SD 18); outcomes of 263 patients audited, including those in whom ANCA testing was declined, showed the policy did not result in missed or delayed diagnosis of small-vessel vasculitis.

audits.t: Testing the effect of a targeted intervention on nurses' compliance with "best practice" mechanical venous thromboembolism prevention.
audits.st: Best-practice mechanical venous thromboembolism prophylaxis guidance
audits.f: 59.4% of eligible patients received mechanical VTE prophylaxis; 0% had VTE risk documented in medication chart
audits.c: Educational outreach visits (EOVs) to nurses on best-practice mechanical VTE prophylaxis
audits.r2: Mechanical VTE prophylaxis rose to 75% (p=0.201, not significant); VTE risk documentation rose to 28% (p=0.002)

audits.t: Continuous quality improvement using intelligent infusion pump data analysis.
audits.tp: Intelligent infusion pump safety software compliance
audits.st: Evidence-based drug safety parameters used to build infusion pump drug libraries
audits.f: Compliance with safety software use 33%
audits.c: Continuous quality improvement process refining infusion pump drug libraries, with 7 library updates between June 2007 and June 2008, education and auditing
audits.r2: Compliance with safety software use rose to over 98%

audits.t: Using a file audit to evaluate retention in care and patient outcomes in a programme to decentralise antiretroviral treatment to primary health care facilities in a high prevalence setting in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
audits.st: Standard operating procedures for six-monthly CD4 count and viral load monitoring
audits.f: File audit identified gaps in monitoring and tracking of down-referred patients; adverse events/treatment failure appeared managed per SOPs but documentation needs improvement

audits.t: An audit of management of patients with borderline increased plasma-free metanephrines.
audits.tp: Follow-up of borderline plasma-free metanephrine results
audits.st: Laboratory interpretative comment recommending repeat testing for borderline raised plasma-free metanephrine results
audits.f: Test not repeated in 55/76 (72%) of followed-up cases despite recommendation; only 3/10 patients with an adrenal mass and only 3/9 with undetermined diagnosis had the test repeated

audits.t: Two years after a quality improvement intervention for chronic kidney disease care in a primary care office.
audits.tp: Chronic kidney disease guideline compliance (long-term QI maintenance)
audits.st: Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative (KDOQI) guidelines
audits.f: CKD recognition 38.1%; anaemia recognition 35%; PTH/vitamin D/phosphate evaluation 4.8%; nephrology referral 14%
audits.c: Chronic kidney disease quality improvement project implementing KDOQI guideline elements, evaluated for long-term maintenance 2 years later
audits.r2: CKD recognition declined from an immediate post-QI 70% to 60.8% (P=1.98, as reported); anaemia recognition declined from 70% to 50% (P=.132); PTH/vitamin D/phosphate evaluation declined from 44% to 33% (P=.216); nephrology referral declined from 77% to 61% (P=.369)

audits.t: Improving venous thromboembolic disease prophylaxis in medical inpatients: a role for education and audit.
audits.tp: Venous thromboembolic disease (VTED) prophylaxis in medical inpatients
audits.st: Internationally published guidelines for VTED prophylaxis in at-risk medical patients
audits.f: Pre-intervention, VTED prophylaxis was prescribed in only 48% of at-risk cases; compliance was best under stroke services and worst under acute medical teams; specialist units had higher prophylaxis rates than general wards (75% vs 53%; p=0.0019).
audits.c: Educational intervention to enhance compliance with VTED prophylaxis guidelines.
audits.r2: Overall compliance improved to 63% (p=0.041); general medical teams improved from 48% to 75% (p=0.001), and general wards from 52% to 74% (p=0.003).

audits.t: Impact of a computerized note template/checklist on documented adherence to institutional criteria for determination of neurologic death in a pediatric intensive care unit.
audits.tp: Documentation of neurologic determination of death
audits.st: Institutional guidelines/criteria for neurologic determination of death (15 specific elements)
audits.f: Mean 11.1 (SD 2.2) of 15 documentation elements recorded with handwritten notes
audits.c: Introduction of a computerised note template/checklist with educational prompts based on institutional criteria
audits.r2: Mean documentation elements rose to 14.9 (SD 0.7) with the template/checklist

audits.t: British Rhinological Society audit of the role of antibiotics in complications of acute rhinosinusitis: a national prospective audit.
audits.tp: Role of antibiotics in complications of acute rhinosinusitis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 78 patients admitted with complications of acute rhinosinusitis (ARS); 59% had been started on antibiotics before admission (64% penicillin/amoxicillin); complication rates were similar in patients with and without prior antibiotic treatment.

audits.t: Quality and quantity: an audit of urodynamics practice in relation to newly published National Standards.
audits.tp: Urodynamics practice against National Minimum Standards
audits.st: National Minimum Standards for urodynamics ('Good Urodynamic Practice', UKCS/NICE)
audits.f: 19 of 20 departments responded; approximately 4000 studies performed annually in Wales; 3 departments did not meet the minimum 30 studies/year standard; 84% had a clinical lead; 54 staff performed urodynamics (65% had attended a course, median score 3/6 describing transducer zeroing); of 168 studies audited, 122 (72%) asked a clear urodynamics question but 22 (13%) of these were not answered; the report was written immediately in 85% of cases.

audits.t: Audit of EEG reporting temporal abnormalities.
audits.tp: EEG reporting accuracy for temporal abnormalities
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 45/143 (31.5%) recordings reported as normal on independent re-review by two epileptologists; intra/inter-rater agreement moderate to substantial

audits.t: Presence and correlates of racial disparities in adherence to colorectal cancer screening guidelines.
audits.tp: Colorectal cancer screening guideline adherence and racial disparities
audits.st: Guidelines for colorectal cancer screening (CRCS)
audits.f: Unadjusted CRCS guideline adherence 72% for Black patients versus 77% for White patients

audits.t: Quality of care for veterans with chronic diseases: performance on quality indicators, medication use and adherence, and health care utilization.
audits.tp: Chronic disease guideline adherence in veterans
audits.st: Nationally recognised treatment guidelines for asthma, COPD, coronary artery disease, diabetes, heart failure and hyperlipidaemia
audits.f: Guideline-sanctioned pharmacotherapy prescription filled ranged from 28% (heart failure) to 91% (asthma); medication persistence ranged 21% (hyperlipidaemia) to 63% (asthma); compliance ranged 49% (COPD) to 85% (CAD); 88% of diabetics had >=1 A1c test but only 47% had A1c <7%

audits.t: Capacity Audit Tool: identifying inpatient delays to maximise service improvement.
audits.tp: Inpatient bed capacity and discharge delay audit
audits.st: Locally developed Capacity Audit Tool assessing appropriate use of inpatient beds (adapted from the Wasted Capacity Audit Tool)
audits.f: 95% compliance with completing the audit; 76% of beds audited were being used appropriately for acute care; top delays were awaiting post-acute care, empty beds awaiting allocation, and awaiting discharge transport

audits.t: Short- and long-term effects of a quality improvement collaborative on diabetes management.
audits.st: Chronic diabetes care guidelines (professional performance/guideline adherence for type 2 diabetes management)
audits.f: Baseline patient outcomes and professional guideline adherence measures for type 2 diabetes management prior to the collaborative
audits.c: Multi-institutional quality improvement collaborative focused on integrated, patient-centred chronic diabetes care management
audits.r2: Mean systolic blood pressure decreased 4.0 mmHg (vs 1.6 mmHg in control); mean HDL increased 0.12 points (vs 0.03 in control); positive but non-significant improvements in HbA1c, cholesterol and blood lipids; significant improvement in percentage of patients receiving foot examination advice/instruction; smaller reductions than control in percentage receiving blood glucose monitoring instruction and annual dietician visits; structural aspects of self-management and decision support improved significantly

audits.t: [Application of a hospital audit to the use of nebulizers: the Case of the Hôtel-Dieu de France-Lebanon].
audits.st: International guidelines on appropriate use of nebulised therapy
audits.f: Inappropriate prescription rate 11.9% (42/358 without indication treated; 3/19 with indication untreated)
audits.c: Two educational presentations, posters in all departments, emails to doctors and residents, and reassessment of prescriptions one week later
audits.r2: Inappropriate prescription rate 14.6% (15.7% without indication treated; no patients with an indication left untreated) - no improvement

audits.t: [Audit of medical records].
audits.st: Items used by the French national agency for evaluation of health services (HAS)
audits.f: Physical condition good in 95-100%; handwriting legible in 94-100%; staff identity determinable in 73-92%; social/demographic data present in 26-99%; mode of admission noted in 52-88%; main diagnosis reported in 68-100%; disposition on discharge missing in 31%; circumstances of death not recorded in 77% of deaths

audits.t: Collaborative quality improvement to manage pain in acute care hospitals.
audits.st: Institutional collaborative pain management programme target of adequate pain relief for all inpatients
audits.f: 4.5% of patients reported no pain relief during their stay; pain intensity measured with a visual analog scale in 27.9% of non-surgical patients; full pain relief in 57.3%
audits.c: Collaborative quality improvement programme using staff education, opinion leaders, patient education, and audit and feedback to improve pain management
audits.r2: No pain relief fell to 2.3% (P=0.05); pain assessment with VAS rose to 42.3% in non-surgical patients (P=0.012) and to 53.7% in surgical patients (vs 37.6%); full pain relief rose to 70.4% (P=0.008); regular/intermittent pain treatment rose to 95.1% (P=0.046)

audits.t: Feasibility and satisfaction with a tailored web-based audit intervention for recalibrating radiologists' thresholds for conducting additional work-up.
audits.tp: Web-based audit-feedback intervention for mammography recall thresholds
audits.st: US target screening mammography recall rate of 9%
audits.f: 36.3% of radiologists reported malpractice risk influenced their recall rates; 36.4% reported it influenced breast biopsy recommendations; mean self-reported recall rate 13.0% for those spending 40% time in breast imaging
audits.c: Tailored web-based educational intervention with individualised audit data on radiologists' own performance measures, malpractice risk perception and breast cancer risk
audits.r2: Radiologists reporting malpractice risk influences recall rates fell to 17.8%; influence on biopsy recommendations fell to 17.3%; >92% correctly identified the 9% target recall rate; self-reported and actual recall rates were highly correlated (0.991)

audits.t: [Audit of severe acute maternal morbidity (SAMM) in the Netherlands].
audits.tp: Severe acute maternal morbidity substandard care review
audits.st: Existing national/local obstetric guidelines and usual care (no single named target)
audits.f: Substandard care identified in almost 80% of the severe acute maternal morbidity (SAMM) cases discussed

audits.t: Physicians' knowledge of and compliance with guidelines: an exploratory study in cardiovascular diseases.
audits.tp: Physicians' knowledge of and compliance with cardiovascular disease guidelines
audits.st: Guidelines for treatment of arterial hypertension, heart failure and chronic coronary heart disease in primary care
audits.f: 437 (40%) of surveyed physicians knew the guidelines adequately; patient data from 30 physicians (15 with adequate guideline knowledge, 15 without) were analysed; compliance with CHD guideline questions was higher than for hypertension (74% vs 11%); physicians with adequate knowledge performed no differently on 12 of 16 compliance indicators, and worse on the remaining 4.

audits.t: A comparison of hospital and nonhospital colonoscopy: wait times, fees and guideline adherence to follow-up interval.
audits.st: Guideline-recommended follow-up interval (10 years) for low-risk screening colonoscopy patients
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: A nine-year audit of open-access upper gastrointestinal endoscopic procedures: results and experience of a single centre.
audits.tp: Open-access upper GI endoscopy indication appropriateness
audits.st: American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ASGE) indication appropriateness guidelines
audits.f: 38.57% of examinations were normal; adherence to ASGE-appropriate indications led to statistically significant, clinically relevant findings; two major complications and no mortality

audits.t: A regional quality improvement effort to increase beta blocker administration before vascular surgery.
audits.tp: Perioperative beta blocker use before vascular surgery
audits.st: 90% target for perioperative beta-blocker administration before vascular surgery
audits.f: 68% of patients received perioperative beta blocker treatment
audits.c: Regional quality improvement effort with feedback on beta-blocker utilisation given at biannual meetings across participating centres
audits.r2: 88% of patients received perioperative beta blocker treatment (p<0.05 vs baseline), but this was not associated with reduced postoperative myocardial infarction or resting heart rate

audits.t: An audit of alcohol brand websites.
audits.tp: Alcohol brand website content against advertising regulatory codes
audits.st: UK regulatory codes governing broadcast advertising of alcohol
audits.f: 27 of 40 leading alcohol brands had a dedicated website; sites featured sports/music sections, games, downloads and competitions; review against regulatory codes found some website content may breach the codes covering traditional advertising.

audits.t: Impact of coding errors on departmental income: an audit of coding of microvascular free tissue transfer cases using OPCS-4 in UK.
audits.tp: OPCS-4 coding accuracy for microvascular free tissue transfer
audits.st: OPCS-4 (Office of Population, Censuses and Surveys Classification of Surgical Operations and Procedures, 4th revision) correct coding requirements
audits.f: Incorrect coding occurred in 11 of 21 cases, resulting in a financial loss of £77,449 because reconstruction was not recorded as F39.1 (which would place it in the maximum income group, CZ04).

audits.t: An audit of informed consent in surgical patients at a university hospital.
audits.st: Standard of informed consent practice before surgery (no specific numeric target stated)
audits.f: No consent taken in 8.5% of cases; only 38% of patients understood the information given; 66% informed about anaesthesia type; only 11% signed the consent form themselves

audits.t: Mortality meetings: ethical considerations and adherence to evidence-based practice from 6 years of experience in a mixed cardiac department.
audits.tp: Mortality and morbidity review in cardiac care
audits.st: Adherence to evidence-based (class I) interventions, assessed through mortality conference review
audits.f: Class I interventions performed in 82% (120/146); at least one transgression from routine medical practice identified in 45% (66/146), with a suggested causal link to death in 23% (33/146); serious errors identified in 3% (5/146), with a causal link to death in 2 cases

audits.t: British Thoracic Society national pleural procedures audit 2010.
audits.st: British Thoracic Society guidance on pleural procedure practice, training, consent and use of ultrasound guidance
audits.f: Promising increase in use of real-time ultrasound guidance; deficiencies identified in pre-procedure consent practice; a significant rate of avoidable minor complications such as drain fall-out and procedure-related pain

audits.t: An audit of venous duplex ultrasonography in patients with lower limb cellulitis.
audits.tp: Duplex ultrasound use in lower limb cellulitis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 240 of 1515 patients with cellulitis underwent lower limb duplex ultrasonography; 15 showed deep vein thrombosis, with only 3 judged concurrent with cellulitis

audits.t: Adherence to guideline-directed venous thromboembolism prophylaxis among medical and surgical inpatients at 33 academic medical centers in the United States.
audits.tp: VTE prophylaxis adherence in hospital inpatients
audits.st: 2004 American College of Chest Physicians guidelines for VTE prophylaxis
audits.f: 48% of patients received guideline-directed VTE prophylaxis overall (59% of medical patients, 41% of surgical patients); prophylaxis was particularly underused among surgical patients

audits.t: British Thoracic Society emergency oxygen audits.
audits.tp: Emergency oxygen use in UK hospitals
audits.st: British Thoracic Society (BTS) guideline for emergency oxygen use in adult patients (2008)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Publication of the BTS emergency oxygen guideline in 2008.

audits.t: Long-term adherence to a local guideline on postoperative body temperature measurement: mixed methods analysis.
audits.tp: Postoperative body temperature measurement guideline adherence
audits.st: Local evidence-based guideline on postoperative body temperature measurement (BTM)
audits.f: Overall adherence to the guideline was 50% (617/1226 measurements); an indication for BTM was present in 55% (679/1226); BTM were actually taken in 60% (736/1226), of which 55% (403/736) was in accordance with the guideline

audits.t: National pilot audit of intermediate care.
audits.tp: Clinical governance of intermediate care services
audits.st: National Service Framework for Older People
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Use of gel caps to aid endoscopic insertion of nasogastric feeding tubes: a comparative audit.
audits.tp: Nasogastric tube insertion technique in head and neck cancer patients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: No significant difference in primary outcome between flexible nasendoscope insertion with vs without gel cap after failure of traditional methods

audits.t: A national dosimetric audit of IMRT.
audits.tp: National dosimetric audit of IMRT (intensity-modulated radiotherapy) implementation
audits.st: Gamma criteria for dosimetric accuracy of IMRT (3%/3mm for simpler plans, 4%/4mm for complex plans) and agreement with treatment planning system dose within 5%
audits.f: 57 of 62 centres participated with 78 plans submitted; all 176 fields from less complex IMRT plans achieved over 95% pixels passing a 3%/3mm gamma criterion; 8 of 245 (3.3%) complex plan fields achieved less than 95% pixels passing a 4%/4mm criterion; 4 of 78 (5.1%) alanine measurements differed by more than 5% from predicted dose (three large deviations of -77.1%, -29.1% and 14.1%); excluding these, mean difference was 0.05% (SD 1.5%).

audits.t: [Perinatal audit in the North of the Netherlands: the first 2 years].
audits.st: Local/national protocols, guidelines and usual-care standards for perinatal care (no single numeric target)
audits.f: 163 substandard factors identified: not following protocol/guideline/standard in 31%, insufficient documentation in 28%, communication problems between providers in 13%; 442 improvement actions reported across external collaboration, internal collaboration, practice management and training

audits.t: Prescription audit of outpatient attendees of secondary level government hospitals in Maharashtra.
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators and WHO 2003 Essential Medicines List
audits.f: Average 3.1 drugs per prescription; 60% prescribed by generic name; 23% in combination; 25% contained at least one injection; 35% contained an antibiotic; 16% contained a vitamin/tonic; 46% of single-ingredient formulations were on the WHO EML.
audits.c: An essential medicines list (EML) was developed for each hospital category based on the audit findings; not re-audited.

audits.t: Improving adherence to venous thromoembolism prophylaxis using multiple interventions.
audits.st: VTE prophylaxis guidelines for medical inpatients
audits.f: Weekly compliance rate in initial stage was 63% (14 of 22).
audits.c: Multiple interventions: physician education, development of a protocol, and weekly monitoring of compliance with feedback in multidisciplinary rounds.
audits.r2: Compliance increased to 100% (39 of 39) (p=0.002); overall 513/560 (91%) of eligible patients received recommended prophylaxis.

audits.t: Introduction of an electronic monitoring system for monitoring compliance with Moments 1 and 4 of the WHO "My 5 Moments for Hand Hygiene" methodology.
audits.st: WHO 'My 5 Moments for Hand Hygiene'
audits.f: Overall compliance 35.1%; per-indication compliance Moment 1 21.3% (95% CI 19.0-23.6), Moment 4 39.6% (95% CI 37.3-41.9), simultaneous 1 and 4 49.2% (95% CI 46.6-51.8).

audits.t: Compliance with best practice: implementing the best available evidence in the use of physical restraint in residential aged care.
audits.tp: Reducing physical restraint use in residential aged care
audits.st: Evidence-based best practice criteria for use of physical restraint (Joanna Briggs Institute PACES)
audits.f: Initial observation showed restraint devices used in up to 40% of residents, compared with a national range of 12-47%.
audits.c: Audit and feedback process using the Joanna Briggs Institute Practical Application of Clinical Evidence System, plus the Getting Research into Practice module to develop implementation strategies.
audits.r2: Follow-up audit showed a reduction in the number of residents restrained, increased use of alternatives to restraint, and increased staff awareness of relevant policies and procedures.

audits.t: A quality improvement programme to increase compliance with an anti-infective prescribing policy.
audits.tp: Compliance with an anti-infective prescribing policy
audits.st: Local adult anti-infective prescribing policy, target >90% compliance
audits.f: Baseline compliance with the new anti-infective prescribing policy was 30%.
audits.c: Quality improvement programme using PDSA cycles across three phases: raising awareness, education, and weekly feedback of results via run charts distributed to medical teams.
audits.r2: Compliance increased from 30% to 71% over the 11-month study period.

audits.t: Setting and maintaining standards in menopause care: audit of current practice in a specialist clinic.
audits.tp: Standards of documentation in menopause consultations
audits.st: British Menopause Society (BMS) guidelines on what should be recorded at the initial menopause consultation
audits.f: Published criteria were met for only 5 of the 23 audit standards, though areas of good practice were also highlighted.

audits.t: Improving asthma care for African American children by increasing national asthma guideline adherence.
audits.st: National Asthma Education and Prevention Program (NAEPP) guidelines for inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) use in asthma
audits.f: Under-utilisation of NAEPP guidelines and under-use of ICS as controller therapy in African American children at baseline (not numerically quantified in abstract)
audits.c: Introduction of a guideline reminder tool (Multi-colored Simplified Asthma Guideline Reminder) to increase healthcare provider adherence to NAEPP guidelines
audits.r2: The reminder tool increased healthcare provider adherence to NAEPP guidelines, evidenced by increased use of ICS as controller therapy (not numerically quantified in abstract)

audits.t: Impact of medical audit on electrodiagnostic medicine in polyneuropathy.
audits.tp: Peer review audit of electrodiagnostic practice in polyneuropathy
audits.st: International peer-reviewed consensus criteria for electrodiagnostic examination in polyneuropathy (ESTEEM project)
audits.f: Increased homogeneity found among physicians over time, most pronounced for abnormal motor nerve segments, abnormal F-wave studies and EMG studies
audits.c: Ongoing international collaboration involving peer review medical audit (ESTEEM project)
audits.r2: Continued increased homogeneity and agreement on pathophysiological interpretation attributed to years of participation in peer review medical audit

audits.t: Hypertension audit in clinical practice based in Thailand (HABIT).
audits.st: Hypertension guideline blood pressure control targets
audits.f: Blood pressure normalisation rate was 44% in the 2003 audit
audits.r2: Blood pressure normalisation rate was 51% in the 2007 audit (mean BP 140.45/77.84 mmHg); 29% of patients were on 3 or more medications

audits.t: Hospital-acquired pressure ulcers in two Swedish County Councils: cross-sectional data as the foundation for future quality improvement.
audits.tp: Hospital-acquired pressure ulcer prevalence and prevention
audits.st: European Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel and Collaborative Alliance for Nursing Outcomes pressure ulcer prevalence/prevention standards
audits.f: Pressure ulcer prevalence was 14.9%; hospital-acquired pressure ulcer (HAPU) prevalence was 11.6%

audits.t: Postal dosimetry audit test for small photon beams.
audits.st: Prescribed dose of 1.5 Gy at 10 cm depth; deviation tolerance below 5%
audits.f: Deviations between prescribed and measured absorbed doses were below 5% for 69% of centres (1x1 cm beam) and 64% of centres (3x3 cm beam); overall system accuracy was 2.9% (1 SD)
audits.c: Causes of deviations above 5% were investigated and corrections made

audits.t: Audit of otitis externa referrals and management in a tertiary care setting.
audits.tp: Management of acute otitis externa referrals from primary care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 98% of 100 referrals had acute otitis externa; 60% were referred with a correct diagnosis and 30% with no diagnosis; nearly half were prescribed oral antibiotics (11% exclusively); 59% had topical antimicrobials; 24% received no treatment; 73% were referred within 2 weeks of presentation, most without advice.

audits.t: SEER coding standards result in underestimation of positive surgical margin incidence at radical prostatectomy: results of a systematic audit.
audits.tp: Cancer registry coding accuracy audit (surgical margins)
audits.st: SEER coding guidelines for pathological stage and surgical margin status
audits.f: 92 of 305 cases (30%) were coded incorrectly; the most common error was failure to properly account for surgical margin status (46/92, 50%); positive margin incidence was 13% by SEER coding versus 28% by a clinical definition

audits.t: An audit of acute bacterial meningitis in a large teaching hospital 2005-10.
audits.tp: Investigation and treatment of acute bacterial meningitis
audits.st: British Infection Association guidelines for investigation and treatment of acute bacterial meningitis
audits.f: Classical triad of fever, neck stiffness and altered mental state present in only 21% on admission; lumbar puncture (LP) contraindicated in 69% of cases; immediate LP performed in only 17% of those without contraindication; antibiotics given after a median of 79 minutes (IQR 24-213), with 65% given within 3 hours; 85% received antibiotics in accordance with local guidelines.

audits.t: Variation in arterial inflow temperature: a regional quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Arterial blood temperature control during cardiopulmonary bypass
audits.st: Arterial blood temperature limited to 37 degrees C during cardiopulmonary bypass (Class IIa, Level B evidence); secondary threshold of 37.5 degrees C
audits.f: 90% of procedures had elevated arterial line temperatures (>=37 degrees C); 53% exceeded the 37.5 degree C threshold
audits.c: Regional quality improvement initiative: conference calls among cardiovascular perfusionists reviewing evidence, with centre-specific practice changes at each site's discretion
audits.r2: 69% of procedures had elevated temperatures (>=37 degrees C, p<0.001; absolute difference 21%); 19% exceeded 37.5 degrees C (absolute difference 34%, p<0.001)

audits.t: Assessing compliance with national comprehensive cancer network guidelines for elderly patients with stage III colon cancer: the Fox Chase Cancer Center Partners' initiative.
audits.st: National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guidelines for stage III colon cancer workup, treatment and gerontological assessment in elderly patients
audits.f: High compliance with staging/workup: chest imaging 100%, stage documented 98%, CT abdomen/pelvis 93%, pathology 91%, CEA 91%; colonoscopy 75%; activities of daily living documented 83%; age/life expectancy discussed in only 49%; 93% (123/124) received adjuvant chemotherapy, 61% (76/124) received oxaliplatin; 75% had >=12 lymph nodes sampled, 56% had the radial margin identified; 93% received surveillance history/physical and CEA, 78% surveillance CT

audits.t: A national audit of estimated glomerular filtration rate and proteinuria reporting in the UK.
audits.tp: Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and proteinuria reporting
audits.st: NICE 2008 chronic kidney disease (CKD) guidance on eGFR reporting
audits.f: 131 of 164 laboratories (80%) responded; 46% reported eGFR on all adult requests while 36% limited use to GP requests, and 21% did not issue eGFR to any inpatient; 62% had an upper reporting limit of >=90 and 30% of >=60 mL/min/1.73m2; 60% cited an ethnicity correction factor on the report, 59% in a guideline, 28% in neither; 63% used albumin:creatinine ratio and 37% exclusively used protein:creatinine ratio for proteinuria.

audits.t: To what extent are national guidelines for the management of urinary incontinence in women adhered? Data from a national audit.
audits.st: National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidelines on management of urinary incontinence in women
audits.f: No diagnosis documented in 6.8% of younger and 28% of older women in hospitals (P<0.001), and 8.6%/21% in primary care; multichannel cystometry before conservative therapy performed in 26%/15% (hospital) and 8.2%/4.7% (primary care) of younger/older women; discussion of causes/treatment documented in 76%/44% (hospital) and 75%/53% (primary care) of younger/older women

audits.t: A longitudinal study examining adherence to guidelines in diabetes care according to different definitions of adequacy and timeliness.
audits.st: Clinical pathway steps for HbA1c, blood pressure, LDL-cholesterol and ACR monitoring/treatment
audits.f: 86% had annual HbA1c testing, 86% SBP, 67% LDL-C, 49% ACR; adequate management over the full 3-step pathway was 73%, 53%, 46% and 41% for HbA1c, SBP, LDL-C and ACR respectively.

audits.t: Platelet audit: Assessment and utilization of this precious resource from a tertiary care hospital.
audits.st: BCSH guidelines on appropriate platelet transfusion
audits.f: 88% of prophylactic platelet transfusions were appropriate per BCSH guidelines; 12% were inappropriate in cardiopulmonary bypass surgery with normal counts and no bleeding; 1585/5444 (29.11%) RDP units were not utilised.

audits.t: Results from an Australian and New Zealand audit of left ventricular ejection fraction from gated heart pool scan analysis.
audits.tp: LVEF gated heart pool scan analysis audit
audits.st: Institute of Physics and Engineering in Medicine (IPEM) reference left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) dataset
audits.f: The Australia/New Zealand overall mean LVEF was 47.2%, 4.9 EF units higher than the IPEM mean; the average difference among software packages was 5.1 EF units; correlation with IPEM values was R=0.98

audits.t: Prevalence of violence risk factors in people at ultra-high risk of developing psychosis: a service audit.
audits.tp: Violence risk factor prevalence in ultra-high-risk psychosis service
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 38% (n=13) had a history of violent behaviour; 79.4% (n=27) had significant suspiciousness; 47.1% (n=16) had problems with anger; 29% (n=10) had previous convictions for violence; two-thirds of those with identified violence risk were engaged with treatment.

audits.t: Patient's experiences and satisfaction with preanesthesia services: A prospective audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 95% of patients completed the questionnaire; 60% were unaware of the purpose of the visit; most received fitness only after 2-3 visits; most were not satisfied with hospital amenities.

audits.t: Using high-technology to enforce low-technology safety measures: the use of third-party remote video auditing and real-time feedback in healthcare.
audits.tp: Hand hygiene compliance audit with video feedback
audits.st: Hand hygiene compliance on entering/exiting patient care areas
audits.f: Hand hygiene compliance was less than 10% (3933/60542) during the prefeedback period
audits.c: Remote video auditing of hand hygiene with real-time feedback via electronic boards in hallways and summary reports to supervisors
audits.r2: Hand hygiene compliance rose to 81.6% (59627/73080) after feedback began, and was maintained at 87.9% (262826/298860) through 75 weeks

audits.t: Simulated pediatric resuscitation use for personal protective equipment adherence measurement and training during the 2009 influenza (H1N1) pandemic.
audits.tp: PPE and resuscitation guideline adherence in simulation
audits.st: AHA basic/advanced life support algorithms and personal protective equipment (PPE) guidance
audits.f: PPE adherence: 61% eye shields, 81% respirators, 87% gown/gloves; all simulations showed deviation from paediatric basic life support protocols.
audits.c: Use of a 'gatekeeper' to control access and facilitate donning of PPE; rapid isolation carts; structured debriefing.
audits.r2: Gatekeeper presence associated with 100% adherence to gown/respirator precautions; median time to bag-valve-mask ventilation improved from 4.3 to 2.7 minutes; confidence in PPE use improved from 64% to 85% after debriefing.

audits.t: Identifying quality improvement opportunities in a universal newborn hearing screening program.
audits.tp: Universal newborn hearing screening quality indicators
audits.st: Universal newborn hearing screening (UNHS) quality assurance/quality indicator benchmarks (no single numeric target stated)
audits.f: Screening rates were >99% at all hospitals; rates of referral and diagnostic testing varied significantly between hospitals; documentation was insufficient to fully assess hearing-aid eligibility and early-intervention enrolment
audits.c: Feedback of hospital-specific quality indicators to nurses, audiologists and otolaryngologists; system changes to screening and referral processes (e.g. additional family contact information, increased referrals to Early Intervention Child Find services)

audits.t: Adherence to local guidelines for venous thromboprophylaxis: a cross-sectional study of medical inpatients in Argentina.
audits.tp: VTE prophylaxis appropriateness in medical inpatients
audits.st: Institutional local guidelines and American College of Chest Physicians recommendations for VTE prophylaxis
audits.f: 188 (60.6%) prescriptions were appropriate per institutional guidelines (14.2% excessive, 15.8% insufficient, 9.4% absent); 256 (82.6%) were appropriate per ACCP recommendations.

audits.t: An audit of basic practical skills acquisition of final year medical students in a Nigerian medical school.
audits.tp: Medical student practical skills competency audit
audits.st: Expected basic practical skill competencies for incoming house officers (implicit; no external named guideline)
audits.f: No student had performed an arterial puncture; 90.5% had not inserted a naso-gastric tube; only 16.7% had inserted more than 10 intravenous cannulae; 45.2% had never inserted a urinary catheter or used bag/mask skills; 70.2% had experience with intravenous antibiotic administration; 48.7% had 6 or more successful venous blood sampling attempts

audits.t: Monitoring universal protocol compliance through real-time clandestine observation by medical students results in performance improvement.
audits.tp: Universal protocol (surgical safety checklist) compliance audit
audits.st: Tufts Medical Center presurgical checklist / Universal Protocol compliance requirements
audits.f: Surgical site unmarked in 8.2% of cases; a Time Out occurred in 89.7%; the entire surgical team was attentive during the time out in 82%; the presurgical checklist was incomplete before incision in 13 cases; the operating room whiteboard was fully completed in 49%; team introductions occurred in 13 cases
audits.c: Modifications to the operating room whiteboard and presurgical checklist, plus specific feedback to surgical departments
audits.r2: Compliance increased in all Universal Protocol dimensions one year later

audits.t: Acute intestinal failure in surgical patients: an audit of incidence, management and outcomes in an irish hospital, and compliance with ASGBI guidelines.
audits.tp: Acute intestinal failure management compliance with ASGBI guidelines
audits.st: ASGBI (Association of Surgeons of Great Britain and Ireland) guidelines for management of acute intestinal failure
audits.f: 11.4% of surgical emergency admissions had AIF; 55.6% required nutritional support; 48.2% had surgical ± radiological intervention; 11.1% radiological intervention alone; 80% referred to nutrition teams early (mean 3.77 days, range 1-21); 72% had complete nutritional assessment clearly documented.

audits.t: A practical review of 'containment' during the influenza A (H1N1): an audit of the flu response centre in Yorkshire and the Humber.
audits.tp: Speed of antiviral delivery during influenza containment phase
audits.st: 48 hours from onset of illness to treatment/prophylaxis (reference standard)
audits.f: Median earliest time to treatment was 2 days (95% CI 2-3); median earliest time to prophylaxis for contacts was 4 days (95% CI 4-5); delays likely reduced containment effectiveness.

audits.t: Quality assurance analysis of participating centres' protocol compliance to a UK multicentre hypofractionated breast (FAST) trial.
audits.tp: Radiotherapy planning protocol compliance (FAST breast trial QA)
audits.st: FAST trial protocol: dose maximum (Dmax) ≤107% of prescribed dose, and ≤5% of breast planning target volume (PTV) receiving >105% of prescribed dose
audits.f: 93% of plans used forward-planned MLC segments; 94% (635/672) had Dmax ≤107%; 11% (74/672) delivered >105% dose to >5% of breast volume; overall 95% of plans complied with the protocol.

audits.t: Where do hands go? An audit of sequential hand-touch events on a hospital ward.
audits.tp: Hand hygiene compliance and hand-touch transmission pathways
audits.st: hand hygiene on entry to and exit from patient rooms (implicit infection control practice; no numeric target stated)
audits.f: Hand-hygiene compliance among clinical staff before/after entry was 25% (38/154); higher in summer (47%) than winter (7%).

audits.t: The Australian radiation protection and nuclear safety agency megavoltage photon thermoluminescence dosimetry postal audit service 2007-2010.
audits.tp: Radiotherapy megavoltage photon dosimetry postal audit
audits.st: ARPANSA reference dose standard for megavoltage photon beam output verification
audits.f: Average ratio of clinically stated dose to ARPANSA measured dose was 0.9993; average ratio of clinically stated to measured beam quality was 1.0087

audits.t: Zoledronic acid in metastatic bone disease: an audit based discussion.
audits.tp: Zoledronic acid dosing in metastatic bone disease
audits.st: best practice guidelines for Zoledronic acid dosing relative to creatinine clearance
audits.f: Dose appropriate to creatinine clearance in 64% (25/39), inappropriate in 13% (5/39), unclear from notes in 23% (9/39); commonest diagnosis was prostate cancer (49%).

audits.t: Practice trends in use of morphine for control of intraoperative pain: An audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Morphine induction dose varied widely (0.05-0.3 mg/kg); inadequate analgesia (VAS >=4) in 15% of patients; doses >0.1 mg/kg associated with significantly better postoperative analgesia.

audits.t: Audit on preoperative midazolam and level of sedation.
audits.st: Expected preoperative sedation level (Ramsay sedation score) and appropriate drug-to-door time (no explicit numeric target stated)
audits.f: Majority of patients received 7.5 mg oral midazolam; median Ramsay sedation score was 2; median drug-to-door time was 52.35 minutes; 11 patients were drowsy in recovery one hour after surgery

audits.t: Adherence to HIV treatment guidelines for comorbid disease assessment and initiation of antiretroviral therapy.
audits.st: US Department of Health and Human Services HIV treatment guidelines with Australian Commentary
audits.f: 'When to start' adherence was 87.6%, less likely with initiation in a clinical trial; 'what to start' guidelines were largely adhered to; pre-antiretroviral therapy comorbid disease assessment required greater attention (not numerically quantified in abstract)

audits.t: Real-life experience of managing vulval erosive lichen planus: a case-based review and U.K. multicentre case note audit.
audits.st: agreed audit standard set with the British Society for the Study of Vulval Disease (documentation of severity/impact, use of diagnostic biopsies, treatment and response assessment)
audits.f: Documentation of symptoms/findings 99% (170/172); schematic diagram present in 87%; disease impact measures poorly documented (DLQI 3%, VAS 1%); biopsies performed in 78% (135/172), 71% consistent with ELPV; first-line very potent topical steroid used in 75% (129/172) with improvement in 66% (85/129).

audits.t: An audit of pain control pathways following video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery.
audits.st: UK Audit Commission standard for postoperative pain relief
audits.f: 34% of patients experienced severe pain (VAS ≥7), almost seven times the Audit Commission standard; least severe pain with pathway B (percutaneous paravertebral catheter, 16.7%), followed by A (25.0%), D (33.3%), C (35.7%), E (52.4%).

audits.t: An audit of length of bone marrow trephine biopsies at a tertiary care hospital.
audits.tp: Bone marrow trephine biopsy adequacy audit
audits.st: Adequate trephine biopsy length criterion of >=1.5 cm
audits.f: Only 22.3% of biopsies (88/394) met the recommended >=1.5cm length; diagnostic positivity was 98.9% in the >=1.5cm group versus 81.4% in the <0.5cm group; 26 biopsies (6.6%) overall were unfit for evaluation, most in the shortest length group

audits.t: Clinicians' adherence versus non adherence to practice guidelines in the management of patients with sarcoma: a cost-effectiveness assessment in two European regions.
audits.tp: Adherence to sarcoma clinical practice guidelines and cost-effectiveness
audits.st: Sarcoma clinical practice guidelines (CONTICANET)
audits.f: Compliance with CPGs was observed in 118 patients (54%); compliant care cost 23,571 euros on average versus 27,313 euros for non-compliant care and was associated with better relapse-free survival.

audits.t: An observational study of compliance with the Scandinavian guidelines for management of minimal, mild and moderate head injury.
audits.st: Scandinavian guidelines for management of minimal, mild and moderate head injury
audits.f: Low compliance, with over-triage involving CT scanning and hospital admissions (exact percentage not given in this abstract).
audits.c: Feedback of the 2003 findings to hospital physicians plus a feed-back loop training programme for guideline implementation.
audits.r2: 738 (63%) patients were managed in accordance with the guideline and 442 (37%) were not; compliance was 56% for minimal and 59% for mild injuries, and 93% for moderate injuries.

audits.t: The diagnostic accuracy of cervical biopsies in determining cervical lesions: an audit.
audits.tp: Diagnostic accuracy of cervical punch biopsy vs cone excision
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Consistent diagnosis rate 68.7% (general pathologists reporting); overdiagnosis 16.7%, underdiagnosis 14.7%; sensitivity 87.5%, specificity 39.8%.
audits.c: introduction of specialist gynaecological histopathology reporting
audits.r2: Consistent diagnosis rate improved to 75.8% (specialist pathologists reporting); overdiagnosis 14.8%, underdiagnosis 9.4% (statistically significant decrease); sensitivity 89.7%, specificity 39.4%.

audits.t: Effects of increasing compliance with minimal sedation on duration of mechanical ventilation: a quality improvement intervention.
audits.tp: Minimal sedation compliance and duration of ventilation
audits.st: Institutional process standard for minimising sedation
audits.f: Baseline compliance with minimising sedation was 80.4% (95% CI 66.9-90.2).
audits.c: Quality improvement initiative to increase compliance with a minimal-sedation process (mechanism not detailed in abstract).
audits.r2: Compliance increased to 96.2% (95% CI 95.2-97.0); the improvement in compliance was associated with a reduction in duration of mechanical ventilation.

audits.t: Ensuring vitamin D supplementation in nursing home patients--a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Vitamin D supplementation in nursing home residents
audits.st: RCT evidence for adequate vitamin D dosing to reduce falls/fractures; local target 80% prescription rate
audits.f: Only 34.6% of patients were prescribed adequate doses of vitamin D.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary PDSA-based QI programme: patients not on adequate dose started on 800 IU daily; those falling on adequate dose for 3 months checked for deficiency and given high-dose replacement if deficient.
audits.r2: Prescription rate for adequate vitamin D increased to 86%, surpassing the 80% goal, over several PDSA cycles across 5 months.

audits.t: Who should swing the stethoscope? An audit of baseline physical examination and blood monitoring on new patients accepted by an early intervention in psychosis team.
audits.tp: Baseline physical health screening in early intervention psychosis services
audits.st: physical examination and blood monitoring should be performed at first-episode psychosis (established recommendation)
audits.f: Physical examination and blood tests were completed in the majority of service users; an unacceptably high number were not undergoing sufficient metabolic syndrome screening or baseline monitoring before starting antipsychotic medication.

audits.t: Spasticity management with botulinum toxin: development and evaluation of a tool for audit.
audits.tp: Spasticity management with botulinum toxin – audit tool development
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Service Organisation tools completed by 100% (8/8) of services and process-of-care tools by 88% (7/8); inter-rater reliability assessed on 34 records; 11 process-of-care items showed good agreement, 6 needed further development.

audits.t: Is there a gap between recommended and 'real world' practice in the management of depression in young people? A medical file audit of practice.
audits.tp: Depression management guideline adherence in young people
audits.st: Guideline recommendations for management of depression in young people
audits.f: 74.5% were prescribed an antidepressant before an adequate trial of psychotherapy; less than 50% were monitored for symptom improvement (35%) and treatment-emergent suicide-related behaviours (30%); 92% of first-line prescriptions in antidepressant-naive under-18s were fluoxetine as recommended.

audits.t: Clinician adherence to guideline for phototherapy use in newborns.
audits.st: 2004 American Academy of Pediatrics guideline for phototherapy use in newborns
audits.f: When phototherapy was given it was indicated in 37% of cases, not indicated in 8%, subthreshold in 56%; when not given it was appropriate in 99% and inappropriate/missed in 1%; adherence varied significantly between the two hospitals.
audits.c: Addition of a phototherapy nomogram to newborn charts.
audits.r2: Addition of the phototherapy nomogram did not change adherence to the guideline.

audits.t: The implementation of unit-based perinatal mortality audit in perinatal cooperation units in the northern region of the Netherlands.
audits.tp: Implementation of unit-based perinatal mortality audit
audits.st: Normal practice/guidelines for perinatal care
audits.f: 163 substandard factors identified; guidelines not followed in 31% of cases, care not according to normal practice in 23%, documentation not in order in 28%, communication insufficient in 13%.
audits.c: Implementation strategy comprising an information plan, an organisation plan and a training plan for unit-based perinatal mortality audit.
audits.r2: 442 actions to improve care were reported (practice organisation 26%, medical performance 27%, internal cooperation 17%, external cooperation 15%, training and education 10%).

audits.t: The effectiveness of a multidisciplinary QI activity for accidental fall prevention: staff compliance is critical.
audits.st: Institutional multifactorial fall-prevention protocol
audits.f: Fall rate 2.13 per 1000 patient days in 2004; compliance with fall risk assessment tool at admission was 91.5% (3998/4368) in first 6 months of 2007; intervention-plan compliance 85.9% in 2007.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary QI activity: fall risk assessment tool, intervention protocol, environmental safety interventions, staff education, and compliance monitoring with feedback.
audits.r2: Fall rate fell to 1.53 per 1000 patient days in 2010 (p=0.039); risk assessment tool compliance rose to 97.6% (10564/10828); intervention-plan compliance rose to 95.3%.

audits.t: British Thoracic Society national bronchiectasis audit 2010 and 2011.
audits.tp: Bronchiectasis management compliance with BTS guideline
audits.st: British Thoracic Society (BTS) bronchiectasis guideline recommendations (July 2010)
audits.f: Majority of guideline recommendations were not currently being adhered to, highlighting the need for national quality standards.
audits.r2: Second audit (2011), also based on BTS guideline recommendations, confirmed the majority of recommendations were still not adhered to across both years.

audits.t: Practice audits to reduce caesareans in a tertiary referral hospital in south-western China.
audits.st: Local target to reduce the caesarean delivery rate (no external guideline stated)
audits.f: Caesarean delivery rate ranged from 53.5% to 56.1% (mean 54.8%).
audits.c: Three-stage intervention introduced in 2005: staff education, patient education, and audit of surgeon practices.
audits.r2: Caesarean delivery rate fell to a range of 36.1% to 43.9% (mean 40.3%; OR 0.56, 95% CI 0.52-0.59), with no increase in NICU admissions.

audits.t: Reasons behind non-adherence of healthcare practitioners to pediatric asthma guidelines in an emergency department in Saudi Arabia.
audits.st: Pediatrics Asthma Management Protocol (PAMP), 8 evidence-practice-gap recommendations
audits.f: Non-adherence was found for 5 of the 8 PAMP recommendations (severity grading documentation, limiting ipratropium in severe asthma, inhaler-and-spacer salbutamol administration, parental education documentation, systemic corticosteroid prescription).

audits.t: Compliance with NICE guidance on the use of anti-TNFalpha agents in ankylosing spondylitis: an east and west Midlands regional audit.
audits.tp: Anti-TNFalpha use in ankylosing spondylitis compliance with NICE guidance
audits.st: NICE guidelines for anti-TNFalpha use in ankylosing spondylitis (pre-treatment and 12-weekly assessments)
audits.f: 41% of 238 prospectively recruited patients were receiving anti-TNFalpha; of 275 patients on anti-TNFalpha, pre-treatment assessments 12 weeks apart were documented in 55%; regular 12-weekly assessments after starting treatment occurred in 46%; compliance varied among centres.

audits.t: Patterns of adherence to NICE glaucoma guidance in two different service delivery models.
audits.tp: Adherence to NICE glaucoma guidance in different service delivery models
audits.st: NICE glaucoma guidelines (2009), 8 main indicators
audits.f: Choice of initial treatment: 96% vs 100% (settings 1, 2); monitoring intervals 92% vs 86%; optic disc image at initial visit 74% vs 10%; appropriate initial assessment 96% vs 58%; review interval compliance 92% vs 66%; medication concordance checked 88% vs 24% (setting 1 vs setting 2).

audits.t: Audit of hospital doctor training in sick note certification.
audits.tp: Hospital doctor training in sick note certification
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 64% of junior doctors reported no sick note certification training; only 40% felt confident writing sick note certificates; 54% could not identify commonly completed hospital certificates.
audits.c: e-learning module on sick note certification, locally advertised
audits.r2: After the e-learning module, doctors were better able to identify appropriate certificates: Fit note 78%, Med 10 78%, DS1500 67%; the module also increased confidence in writing certificates, assessing fitness for work and recommending work modifications.

audits.t: Clinical usefulness of adherence to gastro-esophageal reflux disease guideline by Spanish gastroenterologists.
audits.st: Spanish Association of Gastroenterology clinical practice guideline for GERD
audits.f: Endoscopy indicated in 41% (123); consistent with guideline in 98% when alarm symptoms present, but indicated in 33% of over-50s without alarm symptoms (not recommended); PPI dose adherence 80% (lower dose in 5%, higher in 15%); duration adherence 69% (shorter in 1%, longer in 30%).

audits.t: Hypertension care in Al asyah primary health care center, Al qassim, saudi arabia: an audit of structure, process, and outcome.
audits.tp: Hypertension care structure, process and outcome audit
audits.st: WHO, National Quality Assurance protocol, and JNC-VI hypertension management criteria
audits.f: Prevalence of hypertension among adults was 7.4%; blood pressure was well controlled in 79.6% of patients; 45.3% had at least one complication (most commonly ischaemic heart disease, LVH, stroke, MI).

audits.t: Audit of domperidone use as a galactogogue at an Australian tertiary teaching hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Domperidone dispensing increased steadily over the decade; 20% of women received more than one dispensing; median 12 days from delivery to first dispensing; multiparous women more likely to receive it within 3 days than primiparous women (8% vs 4%).

audits.t: [Audits of good practice: implantable medical devices are also concerned].
audits.st: French National Authority for Health and French National Health Insurance official references on pertinent use of costly implantable medical devices
audits.f: Hip arthroplasty procedures followed guidelines in 95.4% (retrospective) and 96.9% (prospective) of cases; cardiac stimulator audit showed 100% agreement with guidelines; traceability audit found 97% of files complete.

audits.t: "The 3/3 strategy": a successful multifaceted hospital wide hand hygiene intervention based on WHO and continuous quality improvement methodology.
audits.st: WHO multimodal hand hygiene strategy
audits.f: Baseline hand hygiene performance prior to intervention (exact percentage not stated; a 25% mean increase was achieved during the intervention relative to baseline).
audits.c: Multifaceted intervention: increased alcohol hand rub placement, increased audit frequency ('3/3 strategy'), a standardised corrective-action register, and Statistical Process Control (Continuous Quality Improvement, phase 2, 2011).
audits.r2: Sustained 82% compliance during the intervention; compliance rose from 79.5% (95% CI 78.2-80.7) in phase 1 to 84.6% (95% CI 83.8-85.4) in phase 2; healthcare-acquired MRSA rate decreased significantly.

audits.t: Otitis media with effusion: An audit on the indications and outcome.
audits.tp: Grommet insertion criteria and outcomes for otitis media with effusion
audits.st: 1995 Ipswich Hospital NHS Trust criteria for grommet insertion in children with otitis media with effusion
audits.f: 240 of 245 children (98%) who had grommet insertion met the preset criteria; 75% noticed hearing improvement, 41.6%/33%/20.4% improvement in speech/education/behaviour, 47% fewer acute otitis media episodes, 78.5% of parents pleased at 6-month review.

audits.t: How good is compliance with surgical antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines in a tertiary care private hospital in India? A prospective study.
audits.st: Hospital surgical antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines
audits.f: Appropriate antibiotic choice in 68%, timing in 89%, dose in 75%, duration in 63%; full compliance to all criteria in 52%; surgical site infection rate 3.3%.

audits.t: From intermittent antibiotic point prevalence surveys to quality improvement: experience in Scottish hospitals.
audits.tp: Antibiotic point prevalence survey to quality improvement in Scottish hospitals
audits.st: European Surveillance of Antimicrobial Consumption (ESAC) point prevalence survey protocol; ECDC protocol for follow-up survey
audits.f: Reason for treatment recorded in 75.9% (Scotland) vs 75.7% (Europe); compliance with antibiotic policy 81.0% vs 82.5% Europe
audits.c: Development of two quality prescribing indicators (compliance with antibiotic policy in acute admission units, duration of surgical prophylaxis), monthly data collection by clinicians from December 2009, indicators reviewed/modified March 2011
audits.r2: Follow-up PPS conducted using ECDC protocols as part of a national point prevalence survey of healthcare-associated infection and antimicrobial use

audits.t: Use of clinical practice guidelines on long-term prophylaxis in severe hemophilia in France: a retrospective audit.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence for long-term prophylaxis in severe haemophilia
audits.st: 2002 French national clinical practice guidelines on long-term prophylaxis in severe haemophilia
audits.f: Mean age at start of prophylaxis was 4.0 years (haemophilia A) and 6.1 years (haemophilia B).
audits.c: Introduction of the 2002 national guidelines on long-term prophylaxis.
audits.r2: Mean age at start of prophylaxis fell to 1.8 years (A) and 1.4 years (B); around 80% of children over age 3 were now receiving prophylaxis, a 2- to 3-fold increase.

audits.t: [Management of glycemia: an audit in 66 ICUs].
audits.tp: Glucose control protocol implementation in ICU
audits.st: International recommendations for tight glucose control in ICU
audits.f: A formalised glucose control protocol was present for 88% of patients; 3645 glycaemia measurements performed (median 6 per patient); hypoglycaemia in 15% and hyperglycaemia in 58% of patients; severe hypoglycaemia in 0.36% (2 episodes).

audits.t: Compliance with clinical practice guidelines for breast cancer treatment: a population-based study of quality-of-care indicators in Italy.
audits.tp: Breast cancer guideline compliance before/after regional guidelines
audits.st: Piedmont guidelines (PGL) for breast cancer diagnosis and treatment
audits.f: 77.1% received breast conserving surgery (BCS); of those, 87.7% received radiotherapy; 65.5% at medium/high metastasis risk received chemotherapy; 19.6% of ER-negative patients incorrectly received hormonal therapy.
audits.c: Introduction of regional (Piedmont) clinical practice guidelines for breast cancer diagnosis and treatment.
audits.r2: 77.5% received BCS; 87.9% of those received radiotherapy; 63.6% at medium/high risk received chemotherapy; incorrect hormonal therapy prescription fell to 10.8% (p<0.05).

audits.t: Clinical audit concerning the quality of management in patients with classic form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
audits.st: French National Authority for Health (HAS) 2011 national programme of care and diagnosis (PNDS) for congenital adrenal hyperplasia, aligned with 2002 and 2010 international recommendations
audits.f: Weight documented in 89% of records; BMI documented in only 26%; blood pressure measurement insufficient; delta4-androstenedione correctly monitored in 67%.
audits.c: Introduction of the national HAS guidelines (PNDS) in April 2011.
audits.r2: Blood pressure measurement remained insufficient at 74%; delta4-androstenedione monitoring improved from 67% to 100%; sodium/potassium monitoring remained stable at 68% (a deficit); fertility evaluation improved considerably but bone metabolism markers were still often lacking.

audits.t: Effect of audit and feedback on improving handovers: a nonrandomized comparative study.
audits.st: Completeness and accuracy criteria for resident shift-to-shift handovers
audits.f: Errors present in 16.1% of handovers in the standard card-based control system with no feedback.
audits.c: Introduction of an electronic handover system with standardised, real-time feedback to residents on handover quality.
audits.r2: Errors present in only 5.2% of handovers in the experimental electronic system with feedback, compared with 16.1% in controls.

audits.t: An audit of malaria mortality using the "malaria death investigation form" at United Bulawayo Hospitals, Zimbabwe: 1996-2000.
audits.tp: Malaria mortality review using a death investigation form
audits.st: National Malaria Control Programme guidelines on malaria investigation and treatment
audits.f: 53 of 470 confirmed malaria cases (11.2%) died; 74% had more than one complication; guidelines on investigation and treatment were not strictly adhered to; the death investigation form (MDIF) was used in only one case.

audits.t: A retrospective audit to evaluate the effect of the change in midazolam concentration from 10 mg/5 ml to 5 mg/5 ml ampoules on midazolam doses given to sedation patients following the rapid response report (RRR).
audits.tp: Midazolam dosing following ampoule concentration change (National Patient Safety Agency RRR)
audits.st: National Patient Safety Agency Rapid Response Report (RRR) on midazolam ampoule concentration change (10 mg/5 ml to 5 mg/5 ml)
audits.f: Midazolam doses documented before and after the concentration change for five clinicians, over a 6-month retrospective audit of 300 patients.
audits.c: change in midazolam ampoule concentration (10 mg/5 ml → 5 mg/5 ml) following the NPSA RRR
audits.r2: Mean midazolam dose decreased for three of the five clinicians after the concentration change; the number of patients given greater than 5 mg midazolam decreased for all five clinicians.

audits.t: Patient and physician related factors of adherence to evidence based guidelines in diabetes mellitus type 2, cardiovascular disease and prevention: a cross sectional study.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence in chronic disease management
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines for diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, heart failure and atrial fibrillation (9 quality indicators)
audits.f: Non-adherence to guideline recommendations was present in 16.8% (n=205, 95% CI 14.7-18.8) of all quality indicators; in 61.5% of these cases the physician had wrongly judged the treatment as not recommended.

audits.t: Reducing blood culture contamination in the emergency department: an interrupted time series quality improvement study.
audits.st: Target blood culture contamination rate below 3%
audits.f: 321 of 7389 (4.3%) blood cultures were contaminated using the traditional clean collection technique.
audits.c: Changed blood culture collection technique from clean to sterile procedure, using sterile gloves and a kit with 2% chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, sterile fenestrated drape, sterile needle and a procedural checklist.
audits.r2: 111 of 6590 (1.7%) blood cultures were contaminated, an immediate and sustained reduction (p<0.001) confirmed by segmented regression analysis.

audits.t: Quality improvement methods increase appropriate antibiotic prescribing for childhood pneumonia.
audits.tp: Appropriate antibiotic prescribing for community-acquired pneumonia
audits.st: August 2011 Pediatric Infectious Disease Society/Infectious Disease Society of America guideline for management of community-acquired pneumonia in children
audits.f: Appropriate first-line antibiotic prescribing was at a median baseline of 0% in the emergency department and 30% on hospital medicine resident teams.
audits.c: QI methods using multiple PDSA cycles targeting four key drivers, implemented separately in the emergency department and on hospital medicine resident teams, with weekly record review and run charts.
audits.r2: Appropriate first-line antibiotic prescribing increased to 100% in both the emergency department and hospital medicine resident teams.

audits.t: Quality improvement through implementation of discharge order reconciliation.
audits.tp: Discharge medication reconciliation for skilled-nursing facility transfers
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 30-day medication-related readmission rate of 9.5% (169 of 1780) among patients discharged to skilled-nursing facilities via standard procedures.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary closed-loop discharge order reconciliation workflow (residents, clinical nurse coordinators, clinical pharmacists), piloted after a failure modes and effects analysis, then rolled out hospital-wide.
audits.r2: 30-day medication-related readmission rate of 5.4% (4 of 74) in the pilot intervention group; maintained at about 6.7% after hospital-wide rollout.

audits.t: Do high symptom scores trigger clinical actions? An audit after implementing electronic symptom screening.
audits.tp: Clinical response to electronic symptom screening scores
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Pain and shortness of breath documented in 51.8% and 29.7% of charts respectively; a related clinical action occurred in only 16.9% and 3.9% of charts; documentation increased with symptom severity (e.g. pain documented in 36.9% at none vs 71.4% at severe).

audits.t: Emergency Physicians' Adherence to Center for Disease Control and Prevention Guidance During the 2009 Influenza A H1N1 Pandemic.
audits.st: CDC and American College of Emergency Physicians guidance for 2009 H1N1 influenza management
audits.f: 30 (88%) of 34 admitted pandemic-phase patients received influenza testing; 22 (65%) were prescribed antivirals; 19 (56%) received antibiotic treatment despite guidance.

audits.t: A multi-centre audit on genital lichen sclerosus in the North West of England.
audits.tp: Genital lichen sclerosus management compliance with updated guidelines
audits.st: updated guidelines for genital lichen sclerosus management (biopsy indications, follow-up, patient information, topical steroid regimen)
audits.f: 62/194 diagnosed clinically without biopsy; 98% offered follow-up after initial consultation, 19 discharged to primary care; 37% had documented evidence a patient information leaflet had been given; 112 treated with clobetasol propionate 0.05% per the guideline.

audits.t: Differences in compliance with Surviving Sepsis Campaign recommendations according to hospital entrance time: day versus night.
audits.tp: Surviving Sepsis Campaign bundle compliance by time of day
audits.st: Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) 6-hour bundle
audits.f: Compliance (night vs day): serum lactate measurement 57% vs 49%, blood cultures drawn 59% vs 37%; time to lactate measurement 4.5 vs 7 hours (p=0.018); compliance was generally higher at night.

audits.t: Treatment planning systems dosimetry auditing project in Portugal.
audits.tp: National radiotherapy treatment planning system dosimetry audit
audits.st: IAEA/national dosimetry reference values for treatment planning systems in 3D conformal radiotherapy
audits.f: All 24 Portuguese radiotherapy centres participated; 50 photon beams from 25 linear accelerators and 32 calculation algorithms were audited; very good consistency was observed for the same algorithm type across centres, with national status generally acceptable and no major causes for concern.

audits.t: An e-health decision support system for improving compliance of health workers to the maternity care protocols in South Africa.
audits.tp: Health worker compliance with maternity care protocols
audits.st: South African national maternity care guidelines/protocols
audits.f: Compliance with maternity care guidelines using the existing checklist system was 85.1%.
audits.c: Development and implementation of the Bacis (Basic Antenatal Care Information System) e-health clinical decision support system, over a two-year study.
audits.r2: Overall compliance improved to 89.3% (not statistically significant); statistically significant improvement seen in 3 of 9 categories: compliance at booking, patients under 18, and patients booking after 20 weeks.

audits.t: Development, implementation, and compliance of treatment pathways in radiation medicine.
audits.tp: Treatment pathway compliance in radiation oncology
audits.st: 87 disease-specific treatment pathways based on Institute of Medicine guidance
audits.f: Overall compliance with breast and prostate cancer treatment pathways was 97% and 99% respectively.
audits.c: Development and incorporation of evidence/consensus-based treatment pathways into the electronic medical record.
audits.r2: Non-compliance was mainly due to treatment discontinuation for toxicity, patient-elected discontinuation, or physician choice of higher dose for positive/close margins.

audits.t: Three decades of quality improvement in electroconvulsive therapy: exploring the role of accreditation.
audits.tp: ECT clinic compliance with standards under accreditation (ECTAS)
audits.st: 10 ECT audit standards under the Electroconvulsive Therapy Accreditation Service (ECTAS), introduced 2003
audits.f: Baseline compliance analysed retrospectively from three earlier audits.
audits.c: introduction of the ECT Accreditation Service (ECTAS) in 2003
audits.r2: Continuing improvements since the introduction of ECTAS in compliance with all 10 ECT audit standards, measured annually and by accreditation cycle; improvements were not linked to changes in clinical outcomes.

audits.t: Utilization of frozen plasma in Ontario: a provincewide audit reveals a high rate of inappropriate transfusions.
audits.st: Predefined criteria for appropriate frozen plasma transfusion indications
audits.f: 164 of 573 (28.6%) frozen plasma transfusion requests were judged inappropriate, most often given for an INR below 1.5 or in the absence of bleeding or emergency surgery.

audits.t: Bloodstream infection rates in outpatient hemodialysis facilities participating in a collaborative prevention effort: a quality improvement report.
audits.tp: Bloodstream infection prevention in outpatient haemodialysis facilities
audits.st: CDC evidence-based bloodstream infection prevention practices for hemodialysis catheter care
audits.f: Pooled mean bloodstream infection (BSI) rate was 1.09 and access-related BSI rate was 0.73 per 100 patient-months.
audits.c: CDC-guided intervention package: chlorhexidine for catheter exit-site care, staff training and competency assessment, hand hygiene and vascular access care audits, and feedback of infection/adherence rates to staff.
audits.r2: BSI rate fell to 0.89 (32% modelled decrease, p=0.01) and access-related BSI rate to 0.42 per 100 patient-months (54% modelled decrease); reductions were maintained.

audits.t: [Pain audit as a tool to optimize pain treatment in hospital departments].
audits.tp: Pain management assessment via patient-reported audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Patients with probable neuropathic pain reported the highest pain severity and burden; most did not receive secondary analgesics and their GPs were infrequently involved.

audits.t: The implications of the patterns of error associated with acute trauma care in rural hospitals in South Africa for quality improvement programs and trauma education.
audits.tp: Error analysis in rural trauma referrals
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 116 of 1512 referrals (13%) were judged problematic, sustaining 142 errors (1.2 per patient); 68% of errors were due to planning failure and 32% to execution failure, analysed using the JCAHO error taxonomy.

audits.t: An audit to determine if vitamin b12 supplementation is necessary after sleeve gastrectomy.
audits.tp: Vitamin B12 supplementation need after sleeve gastrectomy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 8/41 (20%) had vitamin B12 deficiency; 17/21 (81%) vitamin D deficient; 9/21 (43%) low selenium; none developed macrocytic anaemia

audits.t: A critique of current practice of transvaginal pudendal nerve blocks: a prospective audit of understanding and clinical practice.
audits.st: standard technique for pudendal nerve block administration (anatomical landmark and lag time)
audits.f: The majority of the 57 obstetricians audited were unable to correctly describe the point of infiltration and were unaware of the lag time required for adequate analgesia.

audits.t: An audit of the contribution to post-mortem examination diagnosis of individual analyte results obtained from biochemical analysis of the vitreous.
audits.tp: Diagnostic contribution of vitreous humour biochemistry in post-mortem examination
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of abnormal analyte values, urea contributed to 18 of 32 high results (mostly renal failure), creatinine to 12 of 22, osmolality to 12 of 36, glucose to 6 of 11, ketones to 8 of 21; potassium, calcium and ammonia values made no diagnostic contribution.

audits.t: Development and implementation of the internal audit mechanisms to be used in the health care facilities.
audits.tp: Internal audit mechanisms for quality of care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Analysis of 452 outpatient cards of hypertension patients defined level of awareness and compliance; stages of internal audit mechanism implementation were developed

audits.t: National BTS bronchiectasis audit 2012: is the quality standard being adhered to in adult secondary care?
audits.tp: Bronchiectasis management compliance with BTS quality standard
audits.st: British Thoracic Society (BTS) bronchiectasis quality standard
audits.f: The audit highlighted variable adoption of the BTS quality standard across 98 institutions.

audits.t: Perioperative anesthetic documentation: Adherence to current Australian guidelines.
audits.st: Australian and New Zealand College of Anaesthetists policy statement on documentation
audits.f: Significant deficiencies in adequacy of pre- and intraoperative documentation; documentation poorer in emergency vs elective cases (median scores 15 vs 21, p=0.03) and for airway assessment under regional vs general anaesthesia (42% vs 85%, p=0.05).

audits.t: Providing An audit of how patients get on to antiretroviral therapy in Malawi, and the weight gain they experience in the first six months.
audits.tp: Antiretroviral therapy referral and weight gain
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 74.5% (550/738) of eligible patients attended individual counselling and started ART; 16% dropped out between booking and group counselling and 9.5% between group counselling and ART start; mean weight gain 6.0 kg in men and 5.0 kg in women at 6 months

audits.t: Evaluating compliance with institutional preoperative testing guidelines for minimal-risk patients undergoing elective surgery.
audits.st: Institutional preoperative investigation guidelines for ASA I (minimal risk) patients
audits.f: Compliant testing was found in only 12.1% (95% CI 10.5-13.9); BUN and creatinine were the most frequently overprescribed tests; overinvestigation cost an estimated US $200,000 during the study period.

audits.t: Sudden unexplained death in childhood. An audit of the quality of autopsy reporting.
audits.tp: Autopsy reporting quality for sudden unexplained death in childhood
audits.st: Minimum Autopsy Standards (MAS) referenced in the text (details garbled due to a truncated source file)
audits.f: The supplied source text is truncated/garbled mid-sentence; recoverable figures include a comparison of '25/43 (58%) of SUDC cases' and specialist-centre autopsies meeting MAS in 19/21 (90%) SIDS cases and 18/19 (95%) SUDC cases. Exact sample composition and full percentages could not be reliably recovered from the supplied text.

audits.t: An audit to assess the consequences of the use of a pluripotential risk syndrome: the case to move on from "psychosis risk syndrome (PRS) ".
audits.tp: Assessment of pluripotential/psychosis risk syndrome using CAARMS
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 10 adult patients with four broad psychiatric diagnoses (depression, schizoaffective disorder, borderline personality disorder, psychotic illness) were assessed retrospectively using the CAARMS tool; findings were used to support proposing a broader 'Pluripotent risk syndrome' concept encompassing depressive as well as psychotic symptoms across diagnoses.

audits.t: Audit of the prevalence of anxiety in bipolar disorder--a comorbidity that requires attention and action.
audits.tp: Prevalence of anxiety comorbidity in bipolar disorder
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Prevalence of co-morbid bipolar disorder and anxiety symptoms was found to be especially high; the supplied abstract gives no numerical values.

audits.t: Resettlement of individuals with learning disabilities into community care: a risk audit.
audits.tp: Risk audit of community resettlement for people with learning disabilities
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: One or more risks were identified for 32 of 36 service users; overall 62 incidences (7%) of a possible 864 risk-items identified across 24 risk categories, though several areas needing attention were highlighted.

audits.t: Suspected viral maculopapular eruptions: an audit of practice.
audits.tp: Investigation of suspected viral maculopapular eruptions
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Measles suspected in 21/25 with a specific-virus presentation and confirmed in 20 (95%); causal agent confirmed in 6/34 (17.6%) of nonspecific cases; median 7 virology tests per patient, median cost EUR144

audits.t: Design and implementation of a film dosimetry audit tool for comparison of planned and delivered dose distributions in high dose rate (HDR) brachytherapy.
audits.tp: HDR brachytherapy dosimetry audit tool and pilot results
audits.st: gamma analysis criteria of 3% local dose normalisation and 3 mm distance-to-agreement (DTA)
audits.f: Mean gamma passing rate 98.6% using 3%/3 mm criteria across two pilot audits (Ir-192 and Co-60 sources); mean DTA between prescribed and measured film dose at point A was 1.2 mm.

audits.t: The Swiss Neonatal Quality Cycle, a monitor for clinical performance and tool for quality improvement.
audits.tp: Neonatal quality benchmarking and closed-loop quality cycle
audits.st: Swiss Neonatal Network Quality Cycle, benchmarking multiple quality indicators (mortality, morbidity, process measures) against QUALIFY criteria and standardised mortality/morbidity ratios
audits.f: 2025 very low birth-weight live-births (96.1% of all Swiss VLBW live-births) were analysed across 24 variables; overall mortality (13.6%) was similar to, but several morbidities were lower than, the Vermont Oxford Network and EuroNeoNet comparators; significant inter-unit variation was found in caesarean section rate, prenatal steroid use, mortality, early/late onset sepsis, growth, and measured umbilical artery pH
