audits.c: Biannual quality-cycle meetings ('guideline-perform-falsify-reform') using benchmarking p-charts and quality-indicator standardised ratio charts to identify and discuss improvement areas
audits.r2: The quality cycle led to revision of the Swiss Neonatal Society's guidelines on care at the limit of viability (lowering the recommended gestational age for intensive care from 25 to 24 weeks, 2011), replacement of hand disinfectant in one participating unit, and revision of oxygen saturation target levels across all Swiss level III units

audits.t: Compliance to advanced trauma life support protocols in adult trauma patients in the acute setting.
audits.tp: ATLS protocol compliance in trauma resuscitation
audits.st: Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) protocols
audits.f: Overall compliance was 81.8% for primary survey and 75% for secondary survey; presence of a trauma team leader (TTL) was associated with higher compliance (primary survey 90.9% vs 81.8%, p=0.003; secondary survey 100% vs 75%, p=0.004).

audits.t: Multicenter audit of emergency endovascular repair of infrarenal aortic aneurysms.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 7-day, 30-day and 12-month mortality rates were 15%, 17.5% and 35% respectively; results described as comparable to international standards

audits.t: Indications for invasive prenatal diagnostic procedures at a dedicated fetal medicine centre: an 8 year audit 2003-2010.
audits.tp: Invasive prenatal diagnostic procedure indications and fetal loss rate
audits.st: Auditable fetal loss rate standards set by the Royal College of Obstetricians & Gynaecologists (RCOG), London
audits.f: Fetal loss rate was 0.2% for amniocentesis and 1.2% for chorionic villus sampling, comparable to RCOG auditable standards

audits.t: Subsequent axillary surgery after sentinel lymph node biopsy: results from the BreastSurgANZ Quality Audit 2006-2010.
audits.tp: Axillary surgery after sentinel lymph node biopsy
audits.st: Australian and New Zealand guidelines recommending completion axillary lymph node dissection (cALND) for SLN-positive and no cALND for SLN-negative early breast cancer patients
audits.f: 79.8% of SLN-positive patients underwent cALND (guideline adherence) and 89.7% (10.3% cALND) of SLN-negative patients did not undergo cALND (guideline adherence)

audits.t: An audit of management practices in patients with suspected temporary monocular blindness.
audits.tp: Management of suspected temporary monocular blindness (TMB) referral practice
audits.st: 14-day target for performing carotid endarterectomy after TIA/TMB
audits.f: TIA clinic awareness and referral practice measured at baseline.
audits.c: daily TIA clinic offering single-visit imaging and implementation of best medical therapy (introduced 3 years before this audit)
audits.r2: TIA clinic awareness increased to 90%, but 80% remained unaware of the 14-day CEA target; 81% were aware ophthalmologists could refer TMB patients to the clinic, but virtually none used the service; 86% were happy to prescribe aspirin, virtually none would prescribe statins.

audits.t: The Uyo Trauma Registry-developed for sustainable audit of trauma care and cause in Nigeria.
audits.st: Locally set goal of satisfactory data capture of >=80% for the Uyo Trauma Registry (adapted from the Cape Town Trauma Registry)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Development and adaptation of the Cape Town Trauma Registry into the locally relevant Uyo Trauma Registry with 19 patient-variable items

audits.t: Measuring briefing and checklist compliance in surgery: a tool for quality improvement.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Introduction by name and role occurred in 15% of cases; discussion of critical procedure goals ranged from 0% to 100% between services; verbal contributions ranged from 11% (trainees) to 65% (surgeons)

audits.t: Application and interpretation of an interferon-gamma release assay: Results of an audit in a Canadian centre.
audits.tp: Interferon-gamma release assay use for latent TB
audits.st: Local algorithm derived from Canadian national guidelines for latent tuberculosis infection investigation and interpretation
audits.f: LTBI investigation was appropriate in 87.5% and QFT testing appropriate in 66.5% of patients; 28% (49/175) of QFT tests interpreted incorrectly

audits.t: Endotracheal tube cuff pressures - the worrying reality: a comparative audit of intra-operative versus emergency intubations.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Cuff pressures were significantly higher in the trauma centre than the theatre complex; risk of high cuff pressure roughly two- to threefold higher in emergency patients

audits.t: Changes in health promotion practice in hospitals across England: the National Health Promotion in Hospital Audit 2009 and 2011.
audits.tp: Health promotion practice assessment and delivery in hospitals (National HP in Hospital Audit)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 2009 baseline smoking assessment rate was 82%.
audits.r2: Assessment rates for smoking increased to 86% between 2009 and 2011; there remained little evidence overall of increased health promotion practice despite increased policy focus.

audits.t: Adherence to hypothermia guidelines: a French multicenter study of fullterm neonates.
audits.st: French Society of Neonatology guidelines for hypothermia treatment of hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy
audits.f: 65% were classified as optimal hypothermia treatment (OHT), 22% late (LHT), and 13% non-indicated (NIHT); guideline non-conformity for 35% overall (22% due to delay, 13% due to lack of adherence to clinical indications).

audits.t: Guidelines to identify abnormalities after childhood urinary tract infections: a prospective audit.
audits.tp: Comparison of childhood UTI imaging guidelines for detecting abnormalities
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians (1991) and NICE CG54 (2007) guidelines for imaging after childhood UTI
audits.f: RCP guidelines detected 32 abnormal cases; CG54 would have imaged only 150 children and detected 8 abnormal cases (sensitivity 44% for scarring, 10% for VUR, 40% for other abnormalities), missing 5 of 9 children with scarring
audits.c: not reported (comparison of two guideline versions, not a practice change over time)

audits.t: Is necropsy obsolete - an audit of the clinical autopsy over six decades: a study from Indian sub continent.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Discrepancy between antemortem and postmortem diagnosis in 2010 was 9.30%

audits.t: Adherence of surgeons to antimicrobial prophylaxis guidelines in a tertiary general hospital in a rapidly developing country.
audits.st: Hospital surgical antibiotic prophylaxis protocol
audits.f: Overall antibiotic use was 89%, but practice did not match recommended protocol in 53.5% of cases; prolonged antibiotic use (59.3%) was the commonest reason for non-adherence, followed by use of an alternative antibiotic (31.5%) and no prophylaxis (9.2%).

audits.t: Adherence to national recommendations for safe methotrexate dispensing in community pharmacies.
audits.tp: Safe methotrexate dispensing in community pharmacies
audits.st: 2009 Royal Dutch Pharmacists Society/Dutch Health Care Inspectorate safe methotrexate dispensing recommendations
audits.f: Notification of day of intake on the medication label was recorded in 9.9% of records per pharmacy
audits.c: Discussion and addressing of recommendations within pharmacy teams (implied by increased adherence; specific intervention not detailed)
audits.r2: Notification of day of intake on the medication label increased to 77.1% of records per pharmacy (p<0.001)

audits.t: A ten-year audit of fresh gas flows in a New Zealand hospital: the influence of the introduction of automated agent delivery and comparisons with other hospitals.
audits.tp: Fresh gas flow rates in volatile anaesthesia
audits.st: Locally derived achievable target flow rates (mean around 1.3 l/min, median 0.5-1.0 l/min), informed by comparison with other New Zealand hospitals
audits.f: Mean fresh gas flow was 2.05 l/minute in 2001, decreasing to 1.43 l/minute in 2006 and 1.27 l/minute in 2009
audits.c: Introduction of Aisys automated end-tidal agent delivery anaesthetic machines
audits.r2: Mean fresh gas flow initially increased to 1.5 l/minute after Aisys introduction, then fell to 1.09 l/minute over the following 12 months; proportion of time in automated delivery mode increased from 35% to 63%

audits.t: Reduction of central line-associated bloodstream infection rates in a neonatal intensive care unit after implementation of a multidisciplinary evidence-based quality improvement collaborative: A four-year surveillance.
audits.st: Comparison with CLABSI rates reported by other Canadian NICUs (unit's baseline rate was nearly twofold higher)
audits.f: Median CLABSI rate of 7.9 per 1000 catheter days at the start of the study period
audits.c: Multidisciplinary evidence-based QI collaborative: staff education, standardised skin preparation, new antiseptic agents, central catheter insertion/maintenance checklists, maximal sterile barrier precautions, and revised catheter maintenance protocols
audits.r2: Median CLABSI rate fell to 2.2 per 1000 catheter days (overall decrease significant, p=0.034), via intermediate periods of 3.3 and 2.6 per 1000 catheter days

audits.t: Bedside pleural procedures by pulmonologists and non-pulmonologists: a 3-year safety audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 16 (3.0%) procedure-related complications overall; no significant difference in complication rates between pulmonologists and non-pulmonologists
audits.c: Standardised training, pleural safety checklists and ultrasound guidance

audits.t: A controlled quality improvement trial to reduce the use of physical restraints in older hospitalized adults.
audits.tp: Physical restraint use in hospitalised older adults
audits.st: Locally set goal to reduce use of physical restraints (e.g. bed rails) in older hospitalised patients
audits.f: 13% to 27% of individuals were being restrained on the medical units before the intervention
audits.c: Multicomponent strategy: development of nursing opinion leaders, education/training of physicians and nurses, and implementation of least-restraint rounds
audits.r2: Restraint use decreased to 7% to 14% after the intervention; reduction in early-morning restraint use was statistically significant (p=.01)

audits.t: The effectiveness of bone banking in Central Serbia: audit of the first seven years.
audits.tp: Bone banking allograft discard and infection rate
audits.st: International standards for bone bank allograft discard rate and infection rate
audits.f: Overall discard rate was 26.1% (77/295); contamination rate 12.54% (37/295); postoperative allograft-related infection rate 2.22%, in accordance with international standards

audits.t: The "physician-led chart audit: " engaging providers in fortifying a culture of safety.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Close to 2000 physician-led audits were performed, engaging physician leaders and medical staff in the safety culture
audits.c: Development and deployment of physician-led audit (PLA) tools with training of leaders to teach their use to others

audits.t: An initiative to improve adherence to evidence-based guidelines in the treatment of URIs, sinusitis, and pharyngitis.
audits.tp: Antibiotic guideline adherence for URI, sinusitis and pharyngitis
audits.st: Evidence-based treatment guidelines for URI, acute sinusitis and pharyngitis
audits.f: Baseline guideline adherence: URI 79.28%, sinusitis 41.7%, pharyngitis 24.0%, overall 57.2%.
audits.c: First PDSA cycle of a QI programme: small-scale patient and provider education interventions on viral vs bacterial infections and antibiotic necessity.
audits.r2: Adherence improved to URI 88.58% (p=0.004), sinusitis 57.58% (p=0.086), pharyngitis 25.0% (p=0.918); overall adherence rose from 57.2% to 78.6%.

audits.t: Azithromycin add-on therapy in high-risk postendoscopic sinus surgery patients failing corticosteroid irrigations: A clinical practice audit.
audits.tp: Azithromycin add-on therapy after endoscopic sinus surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 63.2% (36/57) had a favourable outcome with budesonide irrigation alone at 4 months; of 21 non-responders, 12 received azithromycin and 66.7% (8/12) subsequently responded favourably
audits.c: Addition of azithromycin for patients failing standard corticosteroid irrigation

audits.t: Adherence to guidelines in the use of biological agents to treat psoriasis in Brazil.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence for biologic agents in psoriasis
audits.st: Consensus international guidelines for biologic agents in severe psoriasis (prior therapy failure and laboratory monitoring)
audits.f: Management failed to meet standards for prior topical/systemic therapy in 169 (83.2%) patients; of 91 patients on biologics, 23 (25.2%) did not undergo appropriate laboratory monitoring.

audits.t: Making pain visible: an audit and review of documentation to improve the use of pain assessment by implementing pain as the fifth vital sign.
audits.tp: Pain assessment documentation as the fifth vital sign
audits.st: pain assessment alongside routine observations as the fifth vital sign (internal quality target)
audits.f: Baseline pain assessment activity measured on surgical and medical wards; found the pain assessment tool was not visible to nurses.
audits.c: redesigned patient observation chart with pain assessment alongside the early warning score (Version 2), piloted then introduced hospital-wide
audits.r2: Pain was assessed more regularly than at baseline; on average pain was assessed alongside routine observations 70% of the time (>90% on medical wards); where a high pain score was recorded, analgesia was delivered in 88% of cases.

audits.t: Auditing of operating room times: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Operating room efficiency and turnover times
audits.st: Comparison with published operating room time benchmarks for otolaryngology procedures
audits.f: Overall OR efficiency was 20.58%; procedure time (T2) compared favourably with published benchmarks for T&A and PET, but turnover time (T4) was considerably longer than benchmark (average 31.09 minutes)

audits.t: Assessing Compliance With Established Pneumonia Core Measures at a Comprehensive Cancer Center.
audits.tp: Pneumonia core measure compliance in cancer patients
audits.st: National Pneumonia Core Measures (PCMs) national benchmarks
audits.f: Blood cultures obtained in 73% of pneumonia patients before intervention; sputum culture rate at baseline 24.6%
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team intervention: intensive PCM education, microbiologic analysis of pathogens, and development/implementation of an institutional pneumonia algorithm and order set
audits.r2: Blood cultures increased to 91% (p<.001); sputum cultures increased to 51% (p=.004) post order-set implementation; order-set utilisation increased from 40% to 77%; benchmark achieved for only one of five PCMs analysed (PN 3a)

audits.t: The Australian and New Zealand Audit of Surgical Mortality-birth, deaths, and carriage.
audits.st: Peer-review assessment of surgical deaths against expected standards of patient management and hospital processes
audits.f: 86% of audited deaths occurred in patients requiring emergency admission; significant criticism of patient care reported in 13% of cases, with 16% of clinical issues perceived as preventable
audits.c: Confidential peer review with feedback to treating surgeons and system/process recommendations
audits.r2: Western Australia, which began the audit process first, showed a 30% reduction in surgical deaths

audits.t: Has there been any progress in improving the quality of hospitalised death? Replication of a US chart audit study.
audits.tp: Quality of hospitalised death and palliative care consultation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 63 of 159 inpatients received a palliative care consultation (PCC); PCC recipients had fewer invasive interventions and more advance directives/DNR orders
audits.r2: 2008 decedents had higher rates of invasive interventions than the historical sample, but fewer invasive interventions were seen in the 2008 PCC subsample

audits.t: Guideline bundles adherence and mortality in severe sepsis and septic shock.
audits.tp: Surviving Sepsis Campaign bundle adherence and mortality
audits.st: Surviving Sepsis Campaign bundle target of >80% individual bundle adherence and a relative mortality reduction of at least 15% (absolute reduction 5.2%) by end of 2012
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: National programme to screen for severe sepsis/septic shock and implement Surviving Sepsis Campaign bundles within 6 and 24 hours of ICU admission
audits.r2: Bundle adherence improved (adjusted OR per month=1.024) and in-hospital mortality decreased (adjusted OR per month=0.992), equivalent to a 5.8% adjusted absolute mortality reduction over 3.5 years in participating ICUs

audits.t: Audit tool for external beam radiation therapy departments.
audits.tp: External beam radiation therapy department self-audit checklist
audits.st: Recommendations from professional radiation oncology organisations and generally accepted standards of practice (informing ACR-ASTRO accreditation)
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: The 65-item audit tool identified a total of 48 process improvements across the 3 sites audited

audits.t: Patient-as-observer approach: an alternative method for hand hygiene auditing in an ambulatory care setting.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall hand hygiene compliance was 96.8% by patient-as-observer survey; 75.1% of distributed survey cards were returned
audits.c: Patients asked to observe and record hand hygiene compliance of their health care providers

audits.t: Doctors' compliance with national guidelines and clinical pathway on the treatment of tuberculosis inpatients in Hubei, China.
audits.tp: Doctors' compliance with TB treatment guidelines
audits.st: Revised National Tuberculosis Control Program (NTP) guidelines and clinical pathway for new smear-positive pulmonary TB inpatients
audits.f: Adequate drug regimens prescribed in 26.95% (90/334); adequate drug dosages in 0% (0/90); adequate length of hospital stay in 28.44% (95/334)

audits.t: UK audit of analysis of quantitative parameters from renography data generated using a physical phantom.
audits.tp: Accuracy of quantitative renography parameters (UK national audit)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall average root-mean-square deviation from the true phantom value: 7.7% for time-to-peak (whole kidney), 4.5% for relative function; 61 centres responded, 21 provided a complete set of parameter measurements; results were comparable to a previous renogram audit by the same group.

audits.t: An audit of cavity and crown preparations and two direct restorations carried out by foundation dentists in the Oxford and Wessex Deaneries.
audits.tp: Foundation dentist restorative skills assessment (cavity and crown preparation)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 67 foundation dentists completed simulated clinical exercises (amalgam cavities/restorations, Class IV composite restorations, full crown preparations); results indicated a high level of concern and need for further evaluation of restorative practice for some foundation dentists.

audits.t: Febrile neutropenia: median door-to-needle time - results of an initial audit.
audits.st: New gold-standard 'door-to-needle' time of 1 hour for intravenous antibiotics in febrile neutropenia
audits.f: Median door-to-needle time was 45 minutes (range 10 minutes to 6 hours), within the accepted 1-hour target; long delays over 4 hours occurred in 4 (all adult) patients

audits.t: Suboptimal care and maternal mortality among foreign-born women in Sweden: maternal death audit with application of the 'migration three delays' model.
audits.tp: Maternal death audit using the migration three delays model
audits.st: 'Migration three delays' framework and modified UK Confidential Enquiry methodology
audits.f: Major and minor suboptimal factors were present in a majority of maternal deaths, significantly more often among foreign-born women (p=0.01); inadequate care was more common among foreign-born women (p=0.04).

audits.t: An audit of blood bank services.
audits.st: WHO/Directorate General of Health Services (Dhaka) blood bank checklist tool kit, July 2008
audits.f: No system for assessing staff training needs; no duty doctor's room, expert room or medical technologist room; no checklist for observing blood/plasma haemolysis and deterioration; no facility for confidential donor interview; requisition forms often lacked transfusion indications; PPE not properly worn outside serology laboratory.

audits.t: Australian and New Zealand Audit of Surgical Mortality: concordance between reported and audited clinical events and delays in management in surgical mortality patients.
audits.tp: Concordance in surgical mortality audit reporting (ANZASM)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Surgeons attributed delay to surgery/diagnosis as significant in 6.6% of cases versus 20% by assessors (p=0.01); preoperative management could be improved in 19% of cases per surgeons versus 45% and 36% per assessors

audits.t: Exploring post-fall audit report data in an acute care setting.
audits.tp: Post-fall audit reporting and fall rate
audits.st: National Database of Nursing Quality Indicators (NDNQI) fall and fall-injury rate benchmarks
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Implementation of systematic post-fall audit reporting to bedside nurses
audits.r2: Quarterly NDNQI 2011 and 2012 reports showed implementation of post-fall audit reports was associated with a lower overall fall rate and lower fall-injury rate

audits.t: An audit analysis of a guideline for the investigation and initial therapy of diarrhea negative (atypical) hemolytic uremic syndrome.
audits.tp: Outcomes audit following diarrhoea-negative (atypical) HUS guideline
audits.st: European Paediatric Study Group for HUS 2009 clinical practice guideline (early, high-volume plasmapheresis) for diarrhoea-negative/atypical HUS
audits.f: 83% (59/71) received plasma therapy within the first 33 days (10 received plasma infusion only); central venous catheter complications occurred in 31% (16/51) with a catheter in situ; median time to haematological remission was 11.5 days; 11% (8/71) had not entered remission by day 33; 17% (12) remained dialysis-dependent at day 33.

audits.t: Clinician adherence to recommendations for screening of adolescents for sexual activity and sexually transmitted infection/human immunodeficiency virus.
audits.tp: Adolescent sexual history documentation and STI/HIV screening
audits.st: Guidelines for documentation of sexual history and screening for STI/HIV during routine adolescent well visits
audits.f: Sexual history documented in 21.2% (212/1000) of visits; 2.6% (26/1000) tested for gonorrhoea/chlamydia and 1.6% (16/1000) tested for HIV

audits.t: National audit of continence care: adherence to National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidance in older versus younger adults with faecal incontinence.
audits.tp: Faecal incontinence assessment/management vs NICE guidance (National Audit of Continence Care)
audits.st: NICE guidelines on management of faecal incontinence (National Audit of Continence Care, 2009)
audits.f: Bowel history was not documented in 41% of older vs 24% of younger patients in hospitals, and 27% vs 19% in primary care (also submitted: 1729 primary care and 693 care home cases); care was significantly poorer for older people overall.

audits.t: Adherence to the cervical cancer screening program in women living with HIV in Denmark: comparison with the general population.
audits.tp: Cervical screening adherence in women with HIV
audits.st: International HIV guidelines for cervical cancer screening (twice in first year post-diagnosis, then annually)
audits.f: Only 2.6% of women with HIV obtained the recommended two cervical cytologies in the first year after diagnosis; 29-46% followed the HIV cervical screening guidelines across the study period.

audits.t: Audit of adult post-implant annual reviews and evaluation of patient-led review.
audits.tp: Cochlear implant post-implant annual review effectiveness
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 91% showed no change or improvement in aided thresholds; 89% no change or improvement in speech discrimination; 93% no change in impedances; 52% required a map check
audits.c: Introduction of a patient-led review system in place of routine historical annual review appointments

audits.t: Impact of a computerized decision support system on compliance with guidelines on antibiotics prescribed for urinary tract infections in emergency departments: a multicentre prospective before-and-after controlled interventional study.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing compliance for urinary tract infections
audits.st: National guidelines on empirical antibiotic choice and duration for community-acquired urinary tract infections
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Introduction of a computerised decision support system (CDSS) for antibiotic prescribing
audits.r2: CDSS intervention improved compliance in only one of three EDs (absolute increase +20%, p=0.007); choice of antibiotic was improved in multivariate analysis only when the CDSS was used (OR=1.94)

audits.t: Adherence to Immunoprophylaxis Regimens for Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection in Insured and Medicaid Populations.
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) immunoprophylaxis recommendations for respiratory syncytial virus
audits.f: Immunoprophylaxis administration for eligible infants increased from 15% in 1998 to 54% in 2007; adherence highest among infants with chronic lung disease (67% KPNC, 55% TennCare)

audits.t: Documentation of guideline adherence in antenatal records across maternal weight categories: a chart review.
audits.tp: Documentation of antenatal guideline adherence by maternal weight
audits.st: Standard antenatal care documentation and obesity guideline for obese women
audits.f: Completed field rates ranged from 100% (maternal age) to 52.7% (pre-pregnancy BMI); documentation of chlamydia/gonorrhoea testing 54.0%, anatomy scan 85.0%; discussion of preterm labour documented in only 20.6%/12.7%/13.4% of normal/overweight/obese charts.

audits.t: Quality of cardiovascular disease care in Ontario's primary care practices: a cross sectional study examining differences in guideline adherence by patient sex.
audits.tp: Sex differences in cardiovascular guideline adherence
audits.st: Process-of-care guidelines for cardiovascular disease (IDOCC initiative)
audits.f: Women were less likely to have lipid profiles taken (OR 1.17), be prescribed lipid-lowering medication (OR 1.54) or ASA post-stroke (OR 1.56); men with diabetes were less likely to be prescribed glycaemic control medication (OR 0.84).

audits.t: Monitoring compliance with transfusion guidelines in hospital departments by electronic data capture.
audits.tp: Red blood cell transfusion guideline compliance
audits.st: Danish national transfusion guideline recommending transfusion at haemoglobin 6-8 g/dL in non-bleeding patients
audits.f: Transfusion was initiated at the recommended 7.3 g/dL or lower in only 6.5% of cases; median pre-transfusion haemoglobin was 8.9 g/dL; 27% were transfused at 9.3 g/dL or higher
audits.c: Establishment of a Patient Blood Management database using electronic data capture for ongoing feedback

audits.t: Evaluating and operationalizing an environmental auditing program: a pilot study.
audits.st: Locally set target of >=80% of surfaces adequately cleaned (per manufacturers' guidelines) for a room to 'pass'
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Using fluorescent marking, 24% (9/37) of rooms passed; using ATP bioluminescence, 57% (21/37) of rooms passed

audits.t: Accuracy of burn size estimation in patients transferred to adult Burn Units in Sydney, Australia: an audit of 698 patients.
audits.tp: Accuracy of burn size (TBSA) estimation at referral
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Equivalent TBSA estimation between referring hospital and Burns Unit occurred in only 30% of patients; overestimation occurred more than 3:1 relative to underestimation

audits.t: Validation of Australian data in the Australasian Vascular Audit.
audits.tp: Data completeness and accuracy of the Australasian Vascular Audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Capture rate was 63% overall in Australia (only 50% in the private sector, decreasing further in 2013); data field error rate was 2.6%

audits.t: The adherence to initial processes of care in elderly patients with acute venous thromboembolism.
audits.tp: Adherence to initial VTE care processes in elderly patients
audits.st: 2008 American College of Chest Physicians (ACCP) guidelines for initial VTE care
audits.f: 86% (645/750) received parenteral anticoagulation for at least 5 days; 54% (405/750) started oral anticoagulation on day 1; 37% (274/750) had an INR >=2 for 24 hours before parenteral anticoagulation stopped; 35% of cancer patients received recommended LMWH monotherapy; 72% with DVT were prescribed compression stockings.

audits.t: An audit of operating room time utilization in a teaching hospital: is there a place for improvement?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean times: anaesthesia induction 19 min, surgery preparation 13 min, surgery 115 min, recovery 12 min, transfer to PACU/ICU 12 min; time increased with surgical complexity (P<0.001).

audits.t: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis guideline compliance: a pilot study of augmented medication charts.
audits.st: Local hospital VTE prophylaxis guidelines
audits.f: 58.6% (41/70) of patients' prescriptions were compliant with local guidelines; VTE prophylaxis was needed but not prescribed in 28.6% (20/70); 7.1% (5/70) had inappropriately low-dose LMWH and 2.9% (2/70) inappropriately high-dose LMWH
audits.c: Introduction of a medication chart with a dedicated VTE prophylaxis section, piloted over 4 weeks
audits.r2: Compliance with guidelines rose to 71% (27/38), though this increase did not reach statistical significance (p=0.09)

audits.t: A root-cause analysis of maternal deaths in Botswana: towards developing a culture of patient safety and quality improvement.
audits.st: Recommended obstetric practice, protocols and guidelines; Millennium Development Goal 5 maternal mortality target
audits.f: Failure to recognise seriousness of condition in 71% of cases, lack of knowledge in 67%, failure to follow recommended practice in 53%, lack of or failure to implement policies/protocols/guidelines in 44%; 61% of direct deaths were considered avoidable.

audits.t: Victorian Audit of Surgical Mortality is associated with improved clinical outcomes.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: A 20% reduction in surgical mortality over the past 5 years was identified from VAED data, with progressive increase in surgeon/hospital participation and a significant reduction in errors in management as perceived by assessors.

audits.t: Multicentre validation of IMRT pre-treatment verification: comparison of in-house and external audit.
audits.st: Dosimetric goals for IMRT plans (prostate and head and neck mock cases) and gamma index pass rate tolerance criteria
audits.f: All centres met dosimetric goals for the prostate case with homogeneous plan quality, but not for the head and neck case; in-house pre-treatment verification results disagreed with the external audit for two centres.

audits.t: Compliance with the national palestinian infection prevention and control protocol at governmental paediatric hospitals in gaza governorates.
audits.tp: Infection prevention and control protocol compliance
audits.st: National Palestinian Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) Protocol (2004)
audits.f: Compliance was low: hand washing 45.9%, wearing gloves 40.7%, using antiseptics/disinfectants 49.16%; only 2.3% of respondents had a copy of the Protocol and 65.8% did not know of its existence; response rate 92%.

audits.t: Auditing documentation on delivery room management using video and physiological recordings.
audits.st: Accurate and complete documentation of neonatal resuscitation/delivery room management, verified against video and physiological recordings
audits.f: Delivery room management was documented in 93% of records; clinical condition at birth in 76%; 1-minute Apgar in 98%; respiratory support correctly documented in 83%, heart rate in 37%, oxygen saturation in 13%; intubation correctly documented in 57% of 7 intubated infants.

audits.t: Improving enteral delivery through the adoption of the “Feed Early Enteral Diet adequately for Maximum Effect (FEED ME)” protocol in a surgical trauma ICU: a quality improvement review.
audits.st: Adequate enteral nutrition delivery (calories and protein) to target goal in mechanically ventilated ICU patients
audits.f: Rate-based feeding delivered 63% ± 20% of target EN volume/calories.
audits.c: Adoption of the FEED ME (Feed Early Enteral Diet adequately for Maximum Effect) volume-based feeding protocol.
audits.r2: FEED ME volume-based feeding delivered 89% ± 9% of target EN volume/calories (P<0.05 vs rate-based).

audits.t: Clinical audit of leg ulceration prevalence in a community area: a case study of good practice.
audits.st: Benchmarking of venous leg ulceration care against national or international standards
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Adherence to guidelines of antibiotic prophylactic use in surgery: a prospective cohort study in North West Bank, Palestine.
audits.st: American Society for Hospital Pharmacist guidelines for antimicrobial prophylaxis
audits.f: Overall compliance for all studied parameters was very low (2%); 59.8% received the first dose at an appropriate time, 18.5% had appropriate antibiotic selection, and 31.8% received antibiotics for an appropriate duration.

audits.t: An evaluation of compliance and performance following the introduction of the Inter-Facility Transport Triage Guideline.
audits.st: Inter-Facility Transport Triage Guideline (IFTTG), assessed on 8 performance indicators
audits.f: Appropriateness of pre-transport triage was 34.6% and appropriateness of transport team configuration was 73.1%.
audits.c: Introduction of the Inter-Facility Transport Triage Guideline (IFTTG).
audits.r2: Appropriateness of pre-transport triage rose to 54.8% and transport team configuration rose to 92.9%.

audits.t: High sensitivity Troponin T: an audit of implementation of its protocol in a district general hospital.
audits.tp: High sensitivity Troponin T testing protocol adherence
audits.st: Trust protocol for paired high sensitivity Troponin T (hsTropT) testing at 0 and 3 hours for suspected AMI
audits.f: 36.36% (24/66) had only a single sample rather than the protocol-recommended paired samples; among 42 (63.63%) with paired samples, mean interval was 4.41 ± 5.7 hours, with 22.73% too long and 3.03% too short.

audits.t: Suction posterior capsulorhexis: an audit of 15 years' experience.
audits.st: Cataract National Dataset (CND) multicentre audit benchmark
audits.f: At 2 weeks, 75.4% achieved best-corrected vision ≥6/6 and 87.3% ≥6/12 (improving to 95.8% and 100% on best-case analysis), significantly better than the CND benchmark, with low perioperative and postoperative complications.

audits.t: An audit and suggested guidelines for in-patient blood pressure measurement.
audits.st: current office blood pressure measurement guidelines (used as the comparator standard for in-patient practice)
audits.f: In-patient BP was measured only once in 96% of patients; 7% lying flat, 32% semi-reclined, 24% back unsupported, 15% legs crossed, 9% arms unsupported, 65% arm below heart level, 36% incorrect cuff size, 43% bladder not centred over brachial artery, 14% arrhythmia undocumented; staff/patients were conversing during 41% of measurements; overall 97% of patients had a technique that failed to adhere to office BP measurement principles.

audits.t: Lessons from audit and feedback of hospitalized patients with bacteriuria.
audits.st: Avoidance of antimicrobial treatment for asymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Audit and feedback of newly reported positive urine cultures to prescribers to empower them to leave asymptomatic bacteriuria untreated.
audits.r2: Feedback was successfully provided before antibiotics could be initiated in most cases, but only reduced treatment duration, without affecting antibiotic initiation.

audits.t: Histopathological audit of 373 nononcological hysterectomies in a teaching hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Leiomyoma was the most common finding (43.7%), followed by adenomyosis (19.3%); about 50% of hysterectomies were justified by matching preoperative diagnosis with histopathology (Cohen's kappa 0.36, fair agreement).

audits.t: Use of fecal occult blood testing in hospitalized patients: results of an audit.
audits.tp: Fecal occult blood testing appropriateness in hospitalised patients
audits.st: Appropriate use and follow-up of fecal occult blood testing (FOBT) in hospitalised patients
audits.f: 34% (650/1904) of hospitalisations with FOBT were positive; 66% of positive FOBT did not undergo further gastrointestinal investigation; of those with positive FOBT and overt GI bleeding/melena who underwent endoscopy, 60% had endoscopy before the FOBT result was reported and 38% underwent endoscopy ≥3 days after stool collection.

audits.t: Evaluating Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health promotion activities using audit and feedback.
audits.tp: Audit and feedback for health promotion quality improvement
audits.st: Standardised audit tool for best-practice health promotion activity design
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: The accuracy of quantitative parameters in (99m) Tc-MAG3 dynamic renography: a national audit based on virtual image data.
audits.st: Accuracy of differential renal function (DRF) and Tmax quantification against known digital phantom truth values
audits.f: Reported DRF estimates showed significantly lower precision for the phantom with impaired renal uptake than for the phantom with normal uptake, with significant bias caused by differing anterior-posterior kidney positions.

audits.t: An audit of the complications of intercostal chest drain insertion in a high volume trauma service in South Africa.
audits.st: Safe technique for intercostal chest drain (ICD) insertion (e.g. insertion within the 'triangle of safety')
audits.f: 203 ICDs (19%) were associated with complications (18% kinked, 18% inserted subcutaneously, 13% too shallow, 7% inadequate fixation, 41% outside the triangle of safety); junior doctors had a significantly higher complication rate (24%) than senior doctors (5%).

audits.t: Cross-sectional audit on the relevance of Elevated National Early Warning Score in medical patients at a Model 2 hospital in Ireland.
audits.tp: Clinical relevance of elevated National Early Warning Score (NEWS) triggers
audits.st: National Early Warning Score (NEWS) trigger threshold of ≥7 warranting escalation of care
audits.f: A NEWS score ≥7 did not result in a change in clinical management in 64.6% of cases; 94.1% of those with no management change were subsequently discharged home; oxygen supplementation and oxygen saturation were the primary determinants of elevated NEWS (89.9% and 31.6% of cases); 19.7% were on home oxygen therapy; retrospective application of the CREWS score would have reduced reviews by 70.3%.

audits.t: Application of a radiophotoluminescent glass dosimeter to nonreference condition dosimetry in the postal dose audit system.
audits.st: Agreement between measured and stated radiotherapy dose within estimated uncertainty for nonreference field sizes and wedge angles
audits.f: The mean difference between measured and stated doses was within 0.5% for all field sizes (5x5 to 25x25 cm) and wedge angles (15-60 degrees); standard deviations were within the estimated uncertainty except for the 25x25 cm field size data (n=16), which were unreliable due to poor statistics.

audits.t: Parenteral nutrition with standard solutions: not the best solution for everyone? A retrospective audit of 300 patients.
audits.tp: Standard parenteral nutrition solution adverse events
audits.st: Adequacy of protein provision and safety of a single premade total nutrient admixture for all parenterally nourished patients
audits.f: No patient had critically high triglycerides; 16% had a metabolic adverse event (raised bilirubin, urea, creatinine or liver enzymes); line sepsis occurred on 30 occasions (0.67 infections per 1000 catheter days); the standard formulation did not meet protein requirements of surgical or critically ill patients.

audits.t: The second national audit of intermediate care.
audits.st: National Audit of Intermediate Care governance/quality standards
audits.f: Weak local strategic planning, considerable under-provision, delays in accessing services, lack of mental health involvement; high positive patient experience but less satisfactory involvement in care decisions

audits.t: An audit of the knowledge and attitudes of doctors towards Surgical Informed Consent (SIC).
audits.tp: Surgical informed consent knowledge and attitudes
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Junior doctors (199) performed poorer than senior doctors (32) on knowledge and attitudes towards surgical informed consent across a 19-item questionnaire.

audits.t: Bipolar disorder: The importance of clinical assessment in identifying prognostic factors - An Audit. Part 1: An analysis of potential prognostic factors.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Prognostic factor data were frequently not recorded; among available data, 74.6% had a family history of bipolar disorder/depression/suicide/psychosis, 81.8% reported suicidal thoughts, and assignation of a care coordinator was not done on a clinical basis.

audits.t: Bipolar disorder: The importance of clinical assessment in identifying prognostic factors - An Audit. Part 2: Mixed state features and rapid cycling.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 71.7% of the sample reported mixed state features and 72.7% of these had more than 4 mood changes per year; assignation of a care coordinator did not appear associated with these prognostic factors.

audits.t: [How are excisional therapies for CIN performed in France? A national audit].
audits.tp: Colposcopic guidance for excisional treatment of CIN
audits.st: Recommended use of colposcopy to guide excisional therapy for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN)
audits.f: LLETZ was the most common excisional technique (84.9%); 69.3% did not use colposcopy at the time of excision, 16.9% excised under naked eye immediately after colposcopy, and 13.8% under direct colposcopic vision.

audits.t: Quantifying and improving the efficiency of Gamma Knife treatment plans for brain metastases: results of a 1-year audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Audited plans achieved higher median plan efficiency index (PEI) than earlier plans (1.08 vs 1.02); greater improvement (1.23 vs 1.03) after excluding smallest lesions
audits.c: Modified planning strategy informed by prior efficiency study

audits.t: Variations in the management of the axilla in screen-detected ductal carcinoma in situ: evidence from the UK NHS breast screening programme audit of screen detected DCIS.
audits.tp: Axillary surgery management in screen-detected DCIS
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 26.3% of women with final diagnosis of DCIS only underwent axillary surgery (72.4% at mastectomy, 23.8% at breast conservation, 3.8% axillary surgery alone); 10.8% had >8 nodes removed at mastectomy

audits.t: An audit of the use of platelet transfusions at Universitas Academic Hospital, Bloemfontein, South Africa.
audits.st: Local platelet transfusion guidelines
audits.f: 34% of platelet transfusions were not aligned with guidelines; 29.9% were given to patients with platelet counts ≥150x10^9/L; surgical disciplines transfused inappropriately more often than medical disciplines (53.7% vs 17.1%, p<0.0001); the indication was not clearly stated in 48.4% of orders.

audits.t: Impact of a quality improvement program on primary healthcare in Canada: a mixed-method evaluation.
audits.tp: Diabetes and cancer screening quality improvement in primary care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Between-group differences not statistically significant: A1c (p=0.10), foot exams (p=0.45), CRC screening (p=0.77), advanced access (p=0.22)
audits.c: Quality Improvement and Innovation Partnership Learning Collaborative (QIIP-LC) targeting diabetes management, CRC screening, access to care and team functioning

audits.t: Implementation of surgical quality improvement: auditing tool for surgical site infection prevention practices.
audits.tp: Surgical site infection prevention process measure compliance
audits.st: 10 evidence-based process measures for surgical site infection prevention
audits.f: 90% of the 10 process measures had lower compliance rates among the 59 patients with surgical site infection compared with the 49 without infection.
audits.c: System-level changes targeting identified defects: education of anaesthesia personnel on correct cefotetan redosing, flags to identify patients for preoperative warming, and clinic-based distribution of bowel preparation laxatives and antibiotics.
audits.r2: Quarterly compliance improved for 80% of the process measures among infected patients by the end of the study period.

audits.t: A population-based cohort study on adherence to practice guidelines for adjuvant chemotherapy in colorectal cancer.
audits.tp: Adherence to adjuvant chemotherapy guidelines in colorectal cancer
audits.st: National clinical guidelines for adjuvant chemotherapy in colorectal cancer
audits.f: Adherence to guidelines in colon cancer stage III was acceptable in younger, healthier patients and higher with an MDT conference; adjuvant chemotherapy started more than 8 weeks after surgery in 30% of colon and 38% of rectal cancer patients.

audits.t: Effect of 2013 National Healthcare Safety Network definition changes on central line bloodstream infection rates: audit results from the New York State Department of Health.
audits.tp: Central line-associated bloodstream infection surveillance definitions
audits.st: National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) CLABSI surveillance definitions
audits.f: CLABSI rate determined by applying the 2012 NHSN definitions to the audited records.
audits.c: Adoption of the 2013 National Healthcare Safety Network CLABSI definition changes.
audits.r2: A 16% decrease in CLABSI rates was found using the 2013 definitions compared with the 2012 definitions.

audits.t: Impact of the Provider and Healthcare team Adherence to Treatment Guidelines (PHAT-G) intervention on adherence to national obesity clinical practice guidelines in a primary care centre.
audits.st: National Institutes of Health guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of obesity (BMI ≥30)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: PHAT-G (Provider and Healthcare team Adherence to Treatment Guidelines) intervention: education sessions, additional provider patient-education resources, a provider reminder system, and provider feedback.
audits.r2: Providers did not significantly increase documentation of diagnosis and planned management for patients with BMI ≥30; medical assistants significantly increased recording of height, weight and BMI by 13%.

audits.t: A multicentre 'end to end' dosimetry audit for cervix HDR brachytherapy treatment.
audits.st: IPEM RT-SIG end-to-end dosimetry audit standard for HDR cervix brachytherapy
audits.f: Mean difference between planned and measured dose at Point A was -0.6% for plastic and -3.0% for metal applicators (standard uncertainty 3.0%); gamma passing rates exceeded 97%; two errors found (dose normalisation error, applicator library misalignment)

audits.t: Routine group and save unnecessary for gastric band surgery: a retrospective case review audit of 1018 bariatric patients.
audits.tp: Preoperative blood testing in bariatric surgery
audits.st: Trust guidance requiring routine preoperative group and save (G&S) and full blood count (FBC) for all bariatric patients
audits.f: No gastric band patient required transfusion; 9/411 (2.2%) gastric bypass patients needed transfusion; costs of FBC/G&S tests exceeded £15,700

audits.t: A retrospective audit of skin biopsies done in a tertiary care center in India.
audits.tp: Skin biopsy request and report quality and clinicopathological correlation
audits.st: Quality and completeness of histopathology request forms/reports and clinicopathological correlation for skin, mucosal and nail biopsies
audits.f: Pathological diagnosis was concordant with clinical diagnosis in 59.8% of biopsies, partially concordant in 7.6%, and discordant in 30.9%; concordant cases had shorter reporting duration and more frequently a definitive pathologist's diagnosis.

audits.t: An annual audit of the ear foreign bodies in hospital universiti sains malaysia.
audits.tp: Ear foreign body presentation and management
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 95% (69/72) of foreign bodies were removed in the clinic setting, 4.2% required general anaesthesia, and post-removal complications occurred in 1.4%.

audits.t: Operator's ability at assessing a high-speed (air turbine) handpiece before use: an audit.
audits.st: Ability of clinicians to identify unsafe high-speed handpieces
audits.f: Ability to detect three unsafe handpieces was 10% in first round
audits.c: Educational sessions and distribution of an instructional video
audits.r2: Detection ability increased to 44% overall; highest score 77% in those who received intervention, lowest 14% in those who did not

audits.t: Hospital, infants and feeding: The importance of audit.
audits.st: Comprehensive documentation of infant feeding history at presentation/admission
audits.f: Documentation was present for feeding mode in 57%, feeding type in 49%, feeding frequency in 26%, and feeding changes since birth in 19% of charts.

audits.t: Suboptimal compliance with surgical safety checklists in Colorado: A prospective observational study reveals differences between surgical specialties.
audits.st: Surgical Safety Checklist (SSC)
audits.f: Significant variation across hospitals in team introductions, cessation of activity, procedure affirmation, hypothermia risk assessment, beta blocker and VTE prophylaxis checks; uniformly poor compliance for case duration, blood loss, anaesthesiologist concerns and imaging display; only 71% of observers reported active physician participation.

audits.t: Quality of intrapartum care by skilled birth attendants in a refugee clinic on the Thai-Myanmar border: a survey using WHO Safe Motherhood Needs Assessment.
audits.tp: Quality of intrapartum care by skilled birth attendants
audits.st: WHO Safe Motherhood Needs Assessment tool
audits.f: Essential antenatal care elements >90%; episiotomy rate in nulliparous women 49% (34/70); newborn monitoring in first hours 30% (6/20)

audits.t: Reducing the rates of prescribing high-dose antipsychotics and polypharmacy on psychiatric inpatient and intensive care units: results of a 6-year quality improvement programme.
audits.st: Prescribing Observatory for Mental Health national standards on antipsychotic high-dose/polypharmacy prescribing
audits.f: Over half of patients prescribed high-dose antipsychotic or combination antipsychotics (58%), among the highest rates in the UK
audits.r2: Significant reduction in high-dose antipsychotic and polypharmacy prescribing (58% versus 10%)

audits.t: Are potential organ donors missed on general wards? A 6-month audit of hospital deaths.
audits.tp: Missed potential organ donors on general wards
audits.st: DonateLife Audit process for identifying potential organ donors
audits.f: Of 427 deaths, only 12 (2.8%) were referred to the DonateLife team, 10 (2.3%) were submitted for panel review, and only 3 were considered to have potential to develop brain death within 24 hours.

audits.t: Comparative dosimetry study of three UK centres implementing total skin electron treatment through external audit.
audits.tp: Total skin electron beam therapy dosimetry accuracy
audits.st: EORTC recommendations for total skin electron beam therapy dosimetry
audits.f: Output/energy measurements within 2% and 1 mm agreement of expected R50,D; clinical TLD simulation showed -1.6% and -6.7% agreement with expected mean trunk dose; film results complied with EORTC recommendations

audits.t: An audit of indications, complications, and justification of hysterectomies at a teaching hospital in India.
audits.tp: Audit of hysterectomy indications and complications
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Most common surgical approach was abdominal (74.7%); most common indication was symptomatic fibroid uterus (39.9%); overall complication rate 8.5%; around 84% had the same pathology as suspected preoperatively.

audits.t: Development and implementation of a dedicated postoperative evaluation service to improve compliance of postoperative visits.
audits.st: Departmental standard for completion of postoperative anaesthesia evaluations
audits.f: Compliance with postoperative evaluations was 47% in period 1.
audits.c: Development and implementation of a dedicated postoperative evaluation service (after an interim period delegating the task to subspecialty groups with rotating residents).
audits.r2: Compliance improved to 83% in period 3 (66% in the interim period 2); the number of adverse events reported per month rose from 95 to 215 and 201 in periods 2 and 3.

audits.t: A multifaceted hospitalist quality improvement intervention: Decreased frequency of common labs.
audits.st: Choosing Wisely campaign guidance against routine daily complete blood counts and basic metabolic panels
audits.f: A mean of 2.06 (SD 1.40) common labs were ordered per patient-day at baseline.
audits.c: Multifaceted QI intervention: academic detailing, audit and feedback, and transparent reporting of hospitalist-level daily common lab ordering frequency.
audits.r2: Common labs ordered per patient-day decreased by 0.22 (10.7%) compared with baseline (95% CI 0.34 to 0.11).

audits.t: [Audit of sterilization practices in two Tunisian hospitals: current situation and perspectives].
audits.st: Assessment grid of 123 criteria across 4 categories for medical device sterilization practice
audits.f: Non-compliance ranged from 53% to 62% depending on department; traceability was the most critical deficiency; staff and environment safety scores were 26/54 and 28/62 respectively at the two sites.
audits.c: A corrective action plan was implemented for the short, medium and long term.

audits.t: [Evaluation of practices of excisional therapies for CIN: An audit of surgery rooms from Marseilles' area].
audits.tp: Colposcopic guidance for excisional treatment of CIN
audits.st: Recommended use of colposcopy to guide excisional therapy for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN)
audits.f: A colposcope was available in only 36.5% of surgery rooms and used systematically for guidance in only 21% of those; 69.2% of surgery rooms performed excision without any colposcopic guidance.

audits.t: The implementation of an organised cervical screening programme in Poland: an analysis of the adherence to European guidelines.
audits.tp: Cervical screening programme adherence to European guidelines
audits.st: European guidelines (EuG) for quality assurance in cervical cancer screening
audits.f: The programme adhered only partially to EuG in policy and organisation; organised programme coverage fluctuated from 21% to 27% (rising to 35% combined with opportunistic screening in 2012); 30-50% of women referred for colposcopy/biopsy were managed within the programme.

audits.t: An audit of the initial resuscitation of severely ill patients presenting with septic incomplete miscarriages at a tertiary hospital in South Africa.
audits.tp: Resuscitation protocol adherence in septic incomplete miscarriage
audits.st: Strict protocol-based approach for septic incomplete miscarriage resuscitation
audits.f: 86.8% (SAMM) and 77.8% (maternal death group) had 2 intravenous lines for resuscitation; only 31.6% (SAMM) and 11.1% (death group) had a complete clinical examination including speculum exam; no antibiotics were given to 21.1% (SAMM) and 33.3% (death group).

audits.t: Adherence to and uptake of clinical practice guidelines: lessons learned from a clinical practice guideline on chemotherapy concomitant with radiotherapy in head-and-neck cancer.
audits.tp: Adherence to concurrent chemoradiotherapy guideline in head and neck cancer
audits.st: Ontario clinical practice guideline on concurrent chemotherapy with radiotherapy (CCRT) for oropharyngeal cancer
audits.f: CCRT was used in 55% of all oropharyngeal cancer patients overall, ranging from 39% to 82% between individual centres; only 4 of 9 centres were following the guideline for most patients 2-4 years later.

audits.t: National dosimetric audit network finds discrepancies in AAA lung inhomogeneity corrections.
audits.tp: Radiotherapy dose calculation algorithm accuracy audit
audits.st: Agreement between treatment planning system calculated dose and measured audit dose (ACDS Level II and III dosimetric audits)
audits.f: A systematic underdose averaging 2.9% ± 1.2% was found for the AAA algorithm in regions distal from lung-tissue interfaces with lateral beams in anthropomorphic phantoms (Level III audits); this was not seen for other algorithms (-0.4% ± 1.7%) or in slab phantom (Level II) geometries.

audits.t: Adherence to NICE guidelines on diabetes prevention in the UK: Effect on patient knowledge and perceived risk.
audits.tp: Patient awareness of diabetes risk status
audits.st: NICE guidelines for diabetes prevention (risk identification and communication)
audits.f: 44.1% at high risk, 42.4% moderate risk, 13.6% increased risk by Diabetes UK Risk Score; only 42% of patients had been informed of high-risk status by a health professional

audits.t: Intrauterine insemination: a UK survey on the adherence to NICE clinical guidelines by fertility clinics.
audits.tp: Fertility clinic adherence to NICE guideline on intrauterine insemination
audits.st: NICE guideline recommendation that IUI should not be offered routinely
audits.f: 96% (44/46) of clinics continued to offer IUI; 78% (36/46) had formally discussed NICE recommendations; 37% (17/46) had made some practice changes
audits.c: not reported (survey of guideline awareness/response, not a tested intervention)

audits.t: Assessing the appropriateness of information on childhood fever in thermometer package leaflets: a systematic audit of thermometers available in the UK.
audits.st: NICE 2013 guidance on management of feverish illness in children
audits.f: Only 17 (13.8%) defined fever using correct threshold (>=38.0C); only 12 (9.8%) included fever management advice, of which 4 suggested actions not advised by NICE; none referenced NICE guidance explicitly

audits.t: A multicentre audit of temperature patterns after traumatic brain injury.
audits.tp: Temperature patterns after traumatic brain injury
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean proportion of time per day with temperature >37°C ranged from 56% (Day 1) to 89% (Day 14); time >38°C ranged from 11% (Day 1) to 25% (Day 11).

audits.t: Comparison of the Victorian Audit of Surgical Mortality with coronial cause of death.
audits.tp: Validation of surgical mortality audit cause-of-death accuracy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: In 82% of 195 cases with a coronial cause of death, the cause reported to VASM by the treating surgeon matched the coroner's determination.

audits.t: Auditing Analgesic Use in Post-operative Setting in a Teaching Hospital.
audits.st: WHO/National List of Essential Medicines and recommended daily dosing for analgesics
audits.f: 81.94% of patients were prescribed drugs from the national essential/WHO drug list; all drugs except piroxicam were within the lower limit of the recommended daily dose; average 4.23 drugs per encounter, most commonly tramadol monotherapy or tramadol plus paracetamol, most often given intravenously.

audits.t: Prosthetic joint infection: A pluridisciplinary multi-center audit bridging quality of care and outcome.
audits.tp: Prosthetic joint infection quality of care
audits.st: 15 quality-of-care criteria for hip/knee prosthetic joint infection (diagnostic, therapeutic and pluridisciplinary), scored out of 20
audits.f: Median quality-of-care score was 15/20, with significant variation among hospitals (ranging from 9 to 17.5 points); care was heterogeneous and quality criteria correlated with outcome.

audits.t: The effect of using different competence frameworks to audit the content of a masters program in public health.
audits.tp: Public health masters curriculum audit against competence frameworks
audits.st: UK Faculty of Public Health Specialist Training Programme; American Association of Public Health; UK FPH Part A exam curriculum; European Core Competencies for MPH Education (824 competences total)
audits.f: Programme covered 88-96% of competences depending on framework used; coverage fell when restricted to the 3 mandatory modules

audits.t: Audit of carbapenem prescriptions comparing 2 assessment periods.
audits.st: Hospital local recommendations for carbapenem prescription appropriateness from initiation to reassessment
audits.f: At treatment reassessment, 15 (21%) of prescriptions were appropriate and continued; overall compliance with local guidelines from initiation to reassessment was 68%.
audits.c: Increased mobile infectious diseases specialist (IDS) interventions in medical and surgical departments.
audits.r2: At treatment reassessment, 12 (38%) of prescriptions were appropriate and continued; overall compliance with local guidelines was 75% (not a statistically significant change from 2009).

audits.t: Use of remote video auditing to validate Ebola level II personal protective equipment competency.
audits.tp: Remote video auditing of PPE donning/doffing competency
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Implementation of remote video auditing (RVA) to train and remediate nursing staff on Ebola level II personal protective equipment donning/doffing.

audits.t: Improving antibiotic adherence in treatment of acute upper respiratory infections: a quality improvement process.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection
audits.st: National antibiotic treatment guidelines for acute respiratory infections (ARI)
audits.f: compliance with sinusitis guidelines 57.58% at baseline
audits.c: Package of teaching sessions, antibiotic guideline posters, clinical decision support tools in EMR, adherence report cards, and monthly group feedback meetings

audits.t: An audit on the appropriate use of faecal calprotectin testing within the Taranaki DHB: a case for a more discerning approach.
audits.st: Appropriate indications for use of faecal calprotectin (FC) testing to exclude inflammatory bowel disease
audits.f: 37% (49/131) of tests did not add benefit; 22% (29/131) avoided further invasive investigation with a negative result; 91% of patients with known IBD avoided invasive investigation with a negative result; very high FC (>500 mg/g) correlated strongly with an IBD diagnosis (88%).

audits.t: A multifaceted feedback strategy alone does not improve the adherence to organizational guideline-based standards: a cluster randomized trial in intensive care.
audits.tp: Feedback strategy to improve adherence to ICU organisational standards
audits.st: Guideline-based standards for bed occupancy rate (≤80%) and nurse-to-patient ratio (≥0.5)
audits.f: Bed occupancy and nurse-to-patient ratio at baseline (specific rates not given in abstract)
audits.c: Multifaceted feedback strategy: extensive monthly feedback reports, outreach visits, and a quality improvement team (intervention ICUs) vs limited quarterly feedback (control)
audits.r2: Bed occupancy rate did not improve (adjusted OR 0.88 vs baseline, 0.67 vs control); nurse-to-patient ratio did not improve (OR 0.72 vs baseline, 0.65 vs control)

audits.t: Impact of Compliance with a Care Bundle on Acute Kidney Injury Outcomes: A Prospective Observational Study.
audits.tp: Care bundle compliance and acute kidney injury outcomes
audits.st: AKI care bundle (CB) with electronic recognition and interruptive alert, completed within 24 hours
audits.f: not reported separately for pre-implementation period
audits.c: AKI care bundle linked to electronic recognition with an interruptive alert
audits.r2: CB completed within 24 hours in 12.2% (306) of episodes; in-hospital case-fatality 18% (early CB) vs 23.1% (p=0.046); progression to higher AKI stage 3.9% vs 8.1% (p=0.01)

audits.t: Aligning complex processes and electronic health record templates: a quality improvement intervention on inpatient interdisciplinary rounds.
audits.st: Local standard for interdisciplinary rounds (IDR) documentation completion
audits.f: IDR note completion rate 27%
audits.c: Redesigned electronic note template with accompanying resident educational materials

audits.t: Utility of Baseline Home Visit Audit in Home Hemodialysis.
audits.tp: Home visit safety audit in home haemodialysis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 18 of 35 potential safety risks were documented at least once in the cohort of 84 patients; 33 of the 56 surveyed subjects presented more than one safety risk; the audit did not influence adverse events or technique survival.

audits.t: Improving the Quality of Voluntary Medical Male Circumcision through Use of the Continuous Quality Improvement Approach: A Pilot in 30 PEPFAR-Supported Sites in Uganda.
audits.tp: Voluntary medical male circumcision service quality
audits.st: National minimum quality standards for VMMC service delivery (target >80% "good" score)
audits.f: less than 20% of sites scored "good" (>80%) for supplies/equipment, patient counselling and surgical procedure
audits.c: Continuous quality improvement approach: sites identified barriers and carried out improvement plans using a 53-indicator quality assessment tool
audits.r2: sites scoring "good" rose to 67%, 93% and 90% for supplies/equipment, patient counselling and surgical procedure respectively

audits.t: A Development of Automatic Audit System for Written Informed Consent using Machine Learning.
audits.tp: Automated audit of informed consent records
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: A Novel Approach to Practice-Based Learning and Improvement Using a Web-Based Audit and Feedback Module.
audits.st: Complete diabetic foot examination performance
audits.f: Complete foot examination was performed in 52% of reviewed patients in phase 1.
audits.c: Web-based audit and feedback QI tool giving residents personal performance data relative to peers, prompting development of individual improvement plans.
audits.r2: Complete foot examination rate increased significantly to 73% in phase 2.

audits.t: Impact of Using Audit Data to Improve the Evidence-Based Use of Single-Fraction Radiation Therapy for Bone Metastases in British Columbia.
audits.tp: Single-fraction radiotherapy use for bone metastases
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines and meta-analyses recommending single-fraction radiation therapy (SFRT) for bone metastases
audits.f: SFRT use rates were 50.5%, 50.9%, 48.3%, 48.5% and 48.0% in 2007-2011 respectively; a 2012 audit identified interphysician and intercentre variation in SFRT use of 26%-73%.
audits.c: Dissemination to all radiation oncologists of anonymous physician-level and identifiable centre-level SFRT audit data together with published guidelines, meta-analyses and practice-leader recommendations.

audits.t: Management of Barrett's high-grade dysplasia: initial results from a population-based national audit.
audits.tp: Management of Barrett's oesophagus high-grade dysplasia
audits.st: Guidelines for management of high-grade dysplasia in Barrett's oesophagus
audits.f: 62.4% managed endoscopically, 5.6% had oesophagectomy; diagnosis confirmed by second pathologist in 79.4%; 86.0% had treatment planned at MDT meeting; a third of patients received no active treatment

audits.t: An audit of request forms submitted in a multidisciplinary diagnostic center in Lagos.
audits.st: Local standard for complete completion of diagnostic request forms
audits.f: Only 1.3% of request forms were fully completed; patient age 68.0%, request date 88.2%, clinical notes/diagnosis 65.9%, full address 5.6% complete

audits.t: A prospective survey of blood products transferred with patients during inter-hospital transfers in the East of England.
audits.tp: Blood product traceability during inter-hospital transfers
audits.st: National guidance on transfer of blood products with patients
audits.f: 6% of red cell units transfused en route, 3% transfused at destination, 35% wasted, 18% fate could not be established

audits.t: Compliance with standard precautions: Results of a French national audit.
audits.st: Standard precautions (SPs) for reducing cross-transmission of microorganisms, scored as percentage of objectives achieved (POA)
audits.f: Institutional-level POA was 88% (promotion 91%, procedures 99%, evaluation 63%); ward-level POA was 94%; health care workers reported 94.5% 'always' compliance changing gloves between patients but only 34.5% and 24.4% 'always' compliance for glove use in intramuscular injection and eye protection with blood exposure risk, respectively.

audits.t: High Flow Nasal Cannulas for Oxygenation: An Audit of Its Use in a Tertiary Care Hospital.
audits.tp: High flow nasal cannula oxygen therapy use
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: PaO2 increased from 68.2±16.3 to 83.1±32.2 mmHg (N=32, P=0.02) and O2 saturation increased from 93.1±4.5% to 95.1±3.0% (N=106, P=0.00015) after switching to HFNC; 65 patients avoided intubation/NIV, 16 required NIV, 16 required intubation and 9 required both; overall mortality 15%.

audits.t: Quality Improvement in Surgery Combining Lean Improvement Methods with Teamwork Training: A Controlled Before-After Study.
audits.tp: Lean process improvement and teamwork training for surgical safety
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (Time Out and Sign Out)
audits.f: WHO Time Out full compliance 14% in active group at baseline; Sign Out attempt rate 0%
audits.c: Combined teamwork training and lean process improvement delivered over 3 months by an experienced specialist team
audits.r2: WHO Time Out compliance increased from 14% to 71% (p=0.032); Sign Out attempt rate increased from 0% to 50%

audits.t: Non-adherence to standard treatment guidelines in a rural paediatric hospital in Sierra Leone.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence for paediatric malaria and LRTI treatment
audits.st: Standard treatment guidelines for malaria and lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI)
audits.f: Cumulative non-adherence to guidelines was 86% for LRTI cases (of 690 children) and 12% for malaria cases (of 865 children); non-adherence was significantly associated with unfavourable hospital outcomes for both conditions.

audits.t: Quis custodiet ipsos custodes? An audit of records of involuntary detention.
audits.st: New South Wales Mental Health Act requirements for involuntary detention certificates
audits.f: Considerable variability existed between professional groups in detail, appropriateness and compliance; over 10% of Schedule 1 certificates failed to meet MHA requirements, potentially invalidating detention.

audits.t: AUDIT OF THE AUDITS.
audits.st: Royal College criteria for evaluating quality of clinical audits (full/partial/potential/planning categories)
audits.f: 6 full audits, 11 partial audits, 2 potential audits and 0 planning audits out of 19 audits completed by trainees.

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Improve Emergency Department Care for Pediatric Patients with Sickle Cell Disease.
audits.tp: Sickle cell disease pain management in the emergency department
audits.st: Departmental protocol targets: first analgesic dose within 30 minutes of triage, and pain reassessment within 30 minutes of first dose
audits.f: Baseline mean time from triage to first analgesic dose was 89.9 ± 50.5 minutes.
audits.c: Implementation of a standardized sickle cell disease pain management protocol/order set in the emergency department, with provider education.
audits.r2: After order set implementation, mean time to first analgesic decreased to 35.2 ± 22.8 minutes (P<0.05), with improvements also seen in pain assessment and reassessment timing.

audits.t: Audit of memory clinic practice against CCG guidelines: West Suffolk Hospital.
audits.tp: Memory clinic assessment and diagnosis timeliness
audits.st: Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) standards for assessment, diagnosis, communication and post-diagnostic advice timelines
audits.f: Patients seen on average 37 days after referral; letters sent out on average 23 days after assessment (did not meet standard); post-diagnostic advice delivered to most who received a diagnosis

audits.t: GPs' adherence to guidelines for structured assessments of stroke survivors in the community and care homes.
audits.tp: GP structured assessment of stroke survivors
audits.st: National guidance for structured needs assessment of stroke survivors
audits.f: 31% of GPs did not offer structured assessment of stroke survivors' needs; 89% added review outputs to notes, 57% used them to change management; only a quarter had a follow-up protocol

audits.t: Adherence to NICE guidance on glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: an evaluation using the Clinical Practice Research Datalink.
audits.tp: Adherence to NICE guidance on GLP-1 receptor agonist prescribing
audits.st: NICE guidelines for initiating and continuing GLP-1 receptor agonists in type 2 diabetes
audits.f: Only 25% of patients initiated GLP-1 receptor agonists as part of a NICE-recommended regimen; 50% of triple-therapy initiators met both HbA1c and BMI criteria; 18% continuing dual therapy and 6.4% continuing triple therapy achieved NICE target reductions at 6 months

audits.t: An Audit of VDRL Testing from an STI Clinic in India: Analysing the Present Scenario with Focus on Estimating and Optimizing the Turnaround Time.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean absolute turnaround time for VDRL testing was 7.46±2.81 days; follow-up rate for report collection was 71%.

audits.t: Development of a brachytherapy audit checklist tool.
audits.st: Brachytherapy practice guidelines and NRC/agreement state inspection requirements
audits.f: Audit scores from four beta-test sites ranged from 17 to 71 (out of 690), identifying 7-16 noncompliance items per site; audits took 1.5-5 hours.

audits.t: A national benchmark for the initial assessment of men with LUTS: data from the 2010 Royal College of Physicians National Audit of Continence Care.
audits.tp: Adherence to NICE guidelines for male urinary incontinence assessment
audits.st: NICE guidelines on management of urinary incontinence in men
audits.f: Majority of men with LUTS did not receive management according to NICE guidance; older men less likely to receive guideline-concordant care than younger men

audits.t: The use of vascular access audit and infections in home hemodialysis.
audits.tp: Vascular access technique audit in home haemodialysis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Patients with five or more vascular access errors had a higher infection rate (0.47 vs 0.16 infections per patient-year, P<0.001); overall infection rate was similar between appropriate and erroneous technique groups (0.27 vs 0.28 per year, P=0.166).

audits.t: Balancing on the edge: implications of a UK national audit of the use of BSR-BHPR guidelines for the diagnosis and management of polymyalgia rheumatica.
audits.tp: Adherence to BSR-BHPR guidelines for polymyalgia rheumatica
audits.st: BSR-BHPR guidelines (2010) for diagnosis and management of polymyalgia rheumatica
audits.f: Core inclusion criteria followed >90%; initial glucocorticoid dosage per guidance 74%; steroid taper 41%; treatment of relapse 76%; bone protection 84%; patient follow-up 43%

audits.t: Radiology Quality Measure Compliance Reporting: an Automated Approach.
audits.tp: Automated compliance reporting for radiology quality measures
audits.st: CMS Quality Measure #195: stenosis measurement in ultrasound carotid imaging reports
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Implementation of an automated report scanner using the Mirth Connect interface engine to monitor compliance.

audits.t: The role of complexity metrics in a multi-institutional dosimetry audit of VMAT.
audits.tp: VMAT dosimetry accuracy and plan complexity
audits.st: Multi-institutional dosimetry audit tolerance for VMAT delivery (gamma index pass rates)
audits.f: MCS and MU significantly correlated with gamma pass rates for Varian linear accelerators; vendor-independent treatment planning systems (Type 2) produced more complex, poorer quality plans with higher MU/MCS

audits.t: Primary antifungal prophylaxis in adult patients with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia: a multicentre audit.
audits.tp: Antifungal prophylaxis prescribing audit in leukaemia
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 83 (85%) of patients received primary antifungal prophylaxis (PAP); proven/probable invasive fungal disease was significantly lower with PAP (2.6% vs 21.4%, P=0.024).

audits.t: A quality improvement project to reduce the intraoperative use of single-dose fentanyl vials across multiple patients in a pediatric institution.
audits.st: CDC guidelines against use of a single-dose vial across multiple patients
audits.f: Prior to the project, average percentage of failures (single fentanyl vial accessed for multiple patients) was just over 50%.
audits.c: PDSA-based quality improvement: provider education, provision of more fentanyl vials, alternate wasting processes, and pharmacy-prepared single-use fentanyl syringes.
audits.r2: Mean percentage of failures dropped to 5%, below the goal of 25%.

audits.t: Compliance With Guideline Statements for Urethral Catheterization in an Iranian Teaching Hospital.
audits.st: Guidelines for prevention of catheter-associated urinary tract infection
audits.f: Hand-washing rate was lowest before bag drainage (49.52%); documentation for bag change was 79%; closed drainage system was not available; multiple-use lubricant gel used in 66.35% of cases.

audits.t: Clostridium difficile infection incidence: impact of audit and feedback programme to improve room cleaning.
audits.st: Fluorescent marking audit and feedback programme (AFP) for discharge room cleaning thoroughness
audits.f: Pre-intervention room cleaning thoroughness baseline was 49%.
audits.c: Hospital-wide audit and feedback programme using fluorescent marking of high-touch surfaces, with weekly audit results presented to cleaning staff (implemented 2012).
audits.r2: Room cleaning thoroughness improved to 90% (1002 audits performed); hospital-acquired C. difficile infection incidence fell from 54 to 42 cases per 100,000 patient-days, with the rate of decline accelerating by 1.35 cases/100,000 patient-days per quarter post-intervention.

audits.t: Surgical mortality audit data validity.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall concordance between surgical case forms and medical records was 98.2% (median 100%, IQR 87-100%); discordances were mainly omissions.

audits.t: A tertiary hospital audit of opioids and sedatives administered in the last 24 h of life.
audits.tp: End-of-life opioid and sedative dosing audit
audits.st: New Zealand benchmarking study doses of opioids and sedatives in the last 24 hours of life
