audits.f: Mean midazolam dose was 6.0 mg vs 20.7 mg in the New Zealand benchmark study (lower); mean morphine dose was 56.5 mg vs 47.8 mg (similar); 83% of patients with a malignant diagnosis were supported with a modified Liverpool Care Pathway vs 51% of non-malignant patients.

audits.t: Medical emergency announcements on cruise ships: an audit of outcome.
audits.tp: Medical emergency response appropriateness on cruise ships
audits.st: Appropriate activation and response to medical emergency announcements
audits.f: Audit suggested system flaws in appropriateness of public address emergency announcements
audits.c: New elementary first aid training programme for crew emphasising patient assessment and correct response determination
audits.r2: Overall rate of public emergency announcements fell by 43%; proportion needing stretcher transfer rose from 5% to 33%, proportion needing >=4h medical intervention rose from 5% to 44%

audits.t: Improving acute kidney injury management in lower limb arthroplasty: an educational approach.
audits.tp: Acute kidney injury management in elective arthroplasty
audits.st: Recognition, documentation and management standards for acute kidney injury (AKI)
audits.f: 20 patients (19.2%) developed AKI; only 30% of AKI cases had recognition, documentation and management appropriately completed
audits.c: Renal protection protocol, checklist poster and educational sessions on AKI prevention, recognition and management
audits.r2: 12 patients (11.2%) developed AKI (p=0.13, not significant); 75% of AKI cases had appropriate documentation and treatment versus 30% before (statistically significant improvement)

audits.t: Quality improvement education to improve performance on ulcerative colitis quality measures and care processes aligned with National Quality Strategy priorities.
audits.st: National Quality Strategy priorities and CMS Physician Quality Reporting System (PQRS) measures for ulcerative colitis
audits.f: Baseline chart audit against nine quality measures (guideline-directed vaccination, disease assessment, counselling, documentation)
audits.c: Quality improvement education program including private audit and feedback sessions, QI tools and educational monographs
audits.r2: post-education improvements ranged from 0% to 48% across nine measures, mean improvement 15.9%

audits.t: Promoting the management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeds among junior doctors: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Junior doctor management of acute upper GI bleed
audits.st: Local guideline/algorithm for management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleed (UGIB)
audits.f: verbalisation of concern for hypotension 60%, two points of IV access requested in 53% of cases
audits.c: Simulation-based teaching with immediate debriefing and an algorithm summarising guidelines, introduced as an aide-memoire
audits.r2: verbalisation of concern for hypotension increased to 100%, two points of IV access in 100% of cases, 76 second reduction in time to call for senior support

audits.t: Improving physician's adherence to completing vaccination schedules for patients with type 2 diabetes attending non-communicable diseases clinics in West Bay Health Center, Qatar.
audits.tp: Vaccination schedule completion in diabetes patients
audits.st: American Diabetes Association (ADA) vaccination recommendations (target: 25% improvement by January 2015)
audits.f: 20% of type 2 diabetes patients had complete vaccination
audits.c: Vaccination form attached to NCD progress note, physician reminders about ADA guidelines, vaccination schedule summary, reminder posters, education/orientation sessions

audits.t: A quality improvement project to improve the effectiveness and patient-centredness of management of people with mild-to-moderate kidney disease in primary care.
audits.tp: Care bundle for chronic kidney disease management in primary care
audits.st: NICE (2008) guidance-based Care Bundle for CKD (blood pressure targets and other high-impact interventions)
audits.f: NICE (2008) blood pressure target achievement at baseline: 74.8% in CKD stage 3-5 without diabetes, 48% in CKD stage 3-5 with diabetes
audits.c: Care Bundle for CKD: three evidence-based interventions from NICE (2008) guidance plus a novel patient-led self-management element, with practice training and ongoing QI support
audits.r2: Blood pressure target achievement at project end: 76.7% (no diabetes) and 49.2% (diabetes); Care Bundle reliability 100% in those who received it; 671/998 (75%) agreed to self-management component

audits.t: Intravenous fluid prescribing: Improving prescribing practices and documentation in line with NICE CG174 guidance.
audits.st: NICE CG174 (December 2013): Intravenous fluid therapy in adults in hospital
audits.f: Necessary documentation components infrequently documented: prescriptions often had no indication for IV fluid, no 24-hour plan/review, no patient weight, no fluid balance charts
audits.c: Lanyard cards emphasising necessary IV fluid prescription components plus a copy of the NICE fluid prescribing algorithm, distributed to junior doctors on acute admissions units
audits.r2: Significant increase in documentation of defined prescription components, including indication for IV fluid and patient weight, on both medical and surgical units; increased percentage of maintenance IV fluid prescriptions conforming to NICE guidelines

audits.t: The endoscopy safety checklist: A longitudinal study of factors affecting compliance in a tertiary referral centre within the United Kingdom.
audits.st: Local endoscopy safety checklist (devised by expert panel)
audits.f: Baseline highly variable safety check procedure; completed checklist rate 53%, blank checklists 10%
audits.c: Devised a safety checklist via expert panel, then used electronic and physical reminders and incentives to increase compliance
audits.r2: Completed checklist rate increased from 53% to 66% (p=0.021); blank checklists decreased from 10% to 2% (p=0.03)

audits.t: Recognition of the deteriorating patient.
audits.tp: Recognition and escalation of the deteriorating patient (NEWS)
audits.st: National Early Warning Score (NEWS) guidelines, escalation for NEWS ≥5
audits.f: High NEWS escalated for review in 57% of cases; only half reviewed by a doctor; only a third reviewed within an hour; all NEWS guideline criteria met in only 20% of cases
audits.c: Education first, then monthly cycles over 6 months with increased medical staff availability, grand round presentations, and increased outreach provision
audits.r2: Increase to 87% of cases reviewed by a doctor of appropriate seniority

audits.t: Quality improvement in resident education: a pilot project to mitigate metabolic side effects from atypical antipsychotic medications in youth.
audits.st: Atypical antipsychotic metabolic monitoring guidelines
audits.f: baseline metabolic monitoring rate 9% (<1 year on medication), 58.9% (≥1 year); standardized data collection instrument use 0%
audits.c: Resident education on monitoring guidelines and side effects, provision of calibrated scales, introduction of monitoring templates
audits.r2: monitoring rate 29% for newly initiated patients post-intervention; standardized data collection instrument use increased to 70%

audits.t: Improving the documentation of nasogastric tube insertion and adherence to local enteral nutrition guidelines.
audits.tp: Nasogastric tube insertion documentation and guideline adherence
audits.st: National Patient Safety Agency 2005 guidelines (and 2011 update) for NG tube insertion and placement confirmation
audits.f: 3-point guideline quality score: 8/13 (62%) followed guidelines appropriately; 7-point documentation score: no case notes had full documentation
audits.c: Teaching intervention for junior doctors and nurses, followed by an NG tube bundle (pro forma, information poster, nurse sticker) trialled on the stroke unit
audits.r2: No significant improvement after teaching alone (49 insertions); after bundle, 10/12 (83%) followed guidelines appropriately, but only 2/12 (16%) had full documentation

audits.t: Improving venous thromboembolism risk assessment compliance using the electronic tool in admitted medical patients.
audits.st: Local VTE risk assessment key performance indicator using electronic VTE risk assessment tool
audits.f: VTE risk assessment compliance in general medicine 4%; overall SKMC compliance 21%
audits.c: Introduction of electronic VTE risk assessment form (computerized decision support tool) via multidisciplinary task force
audits.r2: compliance in general medicine improved to 98%; overall SKMC compliance improved to above 90%

audits.t: Risk assessment and prophylaxis of venous thromboembolism in surgical inpatients: improving adherence to national guidelines.
audits.tp: VTE risk assessment and prophylaxis in surgical inpatients
audits.st: National guidelines for VTE risk assessment (target 95% of surgical inpatients assessed at admission) and prescribing/wearing anti-embolism stockings with 24-hour reassessment
audits.f: Performance below the national target of 95% VTE risk assessment; gaps in prescribing anti-embolism stockings, ensuring correct wear, and 24-hour reassessment
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team approach with email reminders, posters, and senior input during ward rounds
audits.r2: Sustained improvement achieved, meeting the national guideline of 95% VTE risk assessment; improved performance across all parameters

audits.t: Audit and review for evidence-based red cell wastage reduction measures.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Red blood cell (RBC) wastage was 6.4% overall (5.3% non-AB/B RhD-positive); Group O RhD-negative wastage was 10.4%.
audits.c: Service improvement measures to reduce unnecessary RBC wastage based on a laboratory dashboard query, while maintaining adequate supply.
audits.r2: RBC wastage reduced to 4.4% overall (2.5% non-AB/B RhD-positive), a 32.8% reduction (P<0.0001); Group O RhD-negative wastage reduced to 4.4%; saved approximately 225 RBC units per annum.

audits.t: Medicines reconciliation in comparison with NICE guidelines across secondary care mental health organisations.
audits.tp: Medicines reconciliation compliance with NICE guidance in mental health organisations
audits.st: NICE guidance on medicines reconciliation
audits.f: 88.1% had a formal medicines reconciliation policy; ~80% of reconciliation carried out within 24h of admission; 71.4% conducted daily reconciliation on acute admission wards; only 38% reconciled medication for patients admitted from primary care to other teams

audits.t: International variation in adherence to referral guidelines for suspected cancer: a secondary analysis of survey data.
audits.tp: International variation in adherence to cancer referral guidelines
audits.st: National cancer referral guidelines for lung, colorectal and ovarian cancer symptoms
audits.f: Guideline adherence to clinical vignettes ranged from 20-82%; UK adherence for lung vignette was lower than other jurisdictions (47% vs 58%)

audits.t: Audit of annual medical appraisal and revalidation activity across the UK Defence Medical Services 2013-2014.
audits.st: GMC mandatory annual medical appraisal and revalidation requirements
audits.f: 82% of DMS doctors completed an annual appraisal; positive revalidation recommendations given for 90% without further evidence; ultimately 100% of doctors due revalidation received a positive recommendation

audits.t: Helsinki Trauma Outcome Study 2005: Audit on Outcome in Trauma Management in Adult Patients in Southern Part of Finland.
audits.st: Trauma Audit and Research Network (TARN, UK) benchmark prediction model
audits.f: Standardized W statistic +3.0 (95% CI +2.3 to +3.8) for Helsinki versus +0.2 (95% CI -0.1 to 0.4) for English hospitals; mean ISS higher in Helsinki (14 vs 11)

audits.t: Are Men at High Risk for Osteoporosis Underscreened? A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Guideline-recommended osteoporosis screening for high-risk men
audits.f: Baseline osteoporosis screening rate in high-risk men was 11%.
audits.c: Education and awareness-building for health professional trainees and nurses about osteoporosis screening in high-risk men, following a barriers survey.
audits.r2: After phased surveys and awareness building, the screening rate increased to 20%.

audits.t: [Management of outpatient medications in care units: An audit of clinical practices].
audits.st: Institutional procedure for outpatient medication management in care units
audits.f: The institutional procedure was unknown to 100% of interviewed surgeons and 69% of interviewed physicians; medical units followed recommendations more closely than surgical units; 86% of 21 patients interviewed were satisfied with information received.

audits.t: Evaluation of the application of the European guidelines for the diagnosis and clinical care of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) patients in six French ALS centres.
audits.st: 2005 European Federation of Neurological Sciences (EFNS) recommendations for multidisciplinary management of ALS
audits.f: Mean diagnostic delay was 13.6 months; communication quality criteria were satisfactory in more than 90%; clinic visits were scheduled every 2-3 months in 90%; poorer compliance found for visit schedule and delayed riluzole initiation.

audits.t: Guideline-Directed Medication Use in Patients With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction in India: American College of Cardiology's PINNACLE India Quality Improvement Program.
audits.tp: Guideline-directed medical therapy documentation in heart failure
audits.st: Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT): ACE inhibitor/ARB and beta-blocker use in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
audits.f: Documented use of ACEIs/ARBs, beta-blockers, and both were 33.5%, 34.9% and 29.6% respectively; documentation of GDMT gradually increased over the study period.

audits.t: Development and Feasibility of a Specialty-Specific National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (NSQIP): The Head and Neck-Reconstructive Surgery NSQIP.
audits.tp: Head and neck surgery outcomes registry (NSQIP)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 18.6% had an unplanned return to the operating room, 7.4% were readmitted within 30 days, 1.0% died within 30 days, and 51.3% had no postoperative occurrence.

audits.t: Hand hygiene compliance in Penang, Malaysia: Human audits versus product usage.
audits.st: Mandatory hand hygiene auditing programme for Malaysian public hospitals
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Compliance with National Institute of Health and Care Excellence risk-based screening for Gestational Diabetes Mellitus in nulliparous women.
audits.st: NICE risk-based screening criteria for Gestational Diabetes Mellitus
audits.f: 27% (650) had one or more NICE-defined GDM risk factors; of these, only 60.8% (395) were appropriately screened; 38.9% (253) had risk factors but were not screened; GTT completed in recommended window only 56.6% of the time

audits.t: Appropriate Use Criteria in Echocardiography: An Observational Institutional Study with the Perspective of a Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Appropriate use criteria for transthoracic echocardiography
audits.st: 2011 Appropriate Use Criteria (AUC) for echocardiography
audits.f: 74.66% appropriate, 16.96% inappropriate, 3.99% uncertain, 4.39% nonfitting
audits.c: Creation of a quality improvement project (QIP) based on findings

audits.t: The use of micronised progesterone for menopausal hormone therapy, a clinical practice audit.
audits.tp: Micronised progesterone use in menopausal hormone therapy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 93 postmenopausal women, treatment was ongoing for 68, 18 discontinued and 7 were lost to follow-up; the most common side effect was unscheduled bleeding; no evidence of endometrial hyperplasia.

audits.t: Getting our house in order: an audit of the registration and publication of clinical trials supported by the National Institute for Health Research Oxford Biomedical Research Centre and the Musculoskeletal Biomedical Research Unit.
audits.tp: Registration and publication of clinical trials at research institutions
audits.st: not reported (expectation that clinical trials are publicly registered and published)
audits.f: 4 (1.4%) had no findable registration; of trials with pre-2015 completion, 56% were published, and half of those (36/147, 25%) within 12 months

audits.t: Evaluation of a practice guideline for the management of respiratory distress syndrome in preterm infants: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Respiratory distress syndrome management in preterm infants
audits.st: New practice guideline for management of respiratory distress syndrome (introduced February 2012)
audits.f: Preguideline cohort had higher proportion treated with ongoing mechanical ventilation (49%)
audits.c: New practice guideline for management of respiratory distress syndrome in preterm infants
audits.r2: Proportion of infants treated with ongoing mechanical ventilation reduced from 49% to 26%

audits.t: Adherence to Asthma Guidelines in Children, Tweens, and Adults in Primary Care Settings: A Practice-Based Network Assessment.
audits.tp: Asthma guideline adherence in primary care
audits.st: 2007 US asthma guidelines
audits.f: Guideline adherence was highest for short-acting beta-agonist prescription (88.0%) and maintenance medication (70.4%), and lowest for an asthma action plan (3.1%); documentation of control was 15.0%.

audits.t: Optometric use of a teleophthalmology service in rural Western Australia: comparison of two prospective audits.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: An initial prospective audit identified barriers to optometrists' use of the telehealth service.
audits.c: Multifaceted intervention: logistical support, remuneration to optometrists, a more user-friendly referral pathway, and awareness raising.
audits.r2: Use of the telehealth service increased 3.5-fold after the intervention; a greater percentage of referrals were for non-urgent conditions (69% vs 32% previously).

audits.t: A prospective time-series quality improvement trial of a standardized analgesia protocol to reduce postoperative pain among neurosurgery patients.
audits.st: Hospital Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (HCAHPS) pain management domain
audits.f: Baseline mean pain scale score on the first postoperative day was 4.31 (5.45 for spinal surgery patients).
audits.c: Multimodal, interdepartmental standardized analgesia protocol with process improvements from preadmission to discharge, implemented over a 10-month prospective interrupted time-series trial.
audits.r2: Mean pain score fell to 2.94 overall (32% reduction, p<0.001) and to 3.10 for spinal surgery patients (43% reduction, p=0.036); improved documentation of pain and increased use of NSAIDs (p<0.009) and gabapentin (p<0.027); persistent reduction in HCAHPS pain scores (72.1% vs 82.0%).

audits.t: A Practice Quality Improvement Project: Reducing Dose of Routine Chest CT Imaging in a Busy Clinical Practice.
audits.st: American Board of Radiology Maintenance of Certification practice quality improvement process
audits.f: Baseline effective radiation dose established using standard filtered back projection algorithm.
audits.c: Stepwise implementation of iDose4 iterative reconstruction technique, then reduced kVp.
audits.r2: Effective radiation dose was reduced by 23.62% (Q2) and 43.63% (Q4) compared with baseline, with no perceived difference in diagnostic image quality.

audits.t: An Audit of Requests for Fresh Frozen Plasma in a Tertiary Care Center in South India.
audits.st: 2013 National Health and Medical Research Council/Australasian Society for Blood Transfusion FFP guidelines
audits.f: appropriate usage 59.3%, most appropriate in massive transfusions

audits.t: Identifying improvements for delivery room resuscitation management: results from a multicenter safety audit.
audits.tp: Delivery room resuscitation management safety audit
audits.st: Local unit policies/guidelines on delivery room care compared across the collaborative
audits.f: 83% had attendance policies, 81% personnel policies, 79% training policies; only 8% had briefing policies, 6% debriefing policies, 10% family communication policies; 88% of audited deliveries had attendance conforming to policy, 66% had briefing, 19% had debriefing, 92% had family communication within 30 minutes
audits.c: not reported (audit provided feedback for local QI planning; recommends teamwork tools)

audits.t: Case file audit of Lidcombe program outcomes in a student-led stuttering clinic.
audits.st: Published literature benchmark outcomes for the Lidcombe Program
audits.f: Clients who completed Stage 1 had final percentage syllables stuttered and severity ratings comparable to the literature, but with a longer median Stage 1 duration; 57% of clients withdrew before completing Stage 1.

audits.t: The use of log file analysis within VMAT audits.
audits.tp: VMAT delivery accuracy log file analysis
audits.st: VMAT audit MLC positioning accuracy tolerance
audits.f: Varian TrueBeam accelerators had better MLC positioning accuracy (lower RMS values) than Varian Clinacs (2300IX/2100CD)

audits.t: Making Quality Improvement Happen in the Real World: Building Capability and Improving Multiple Projects at the Same Time.
audits.tp: Building QI capability across multiple concurrent ICU projects
audits.st: not reported (local process reliability targets for four projects: septic shock bundle, early sedation vacation, ventilated patient mobilisation, medicines reconciliation)
audits.f: Initial process reliability low, between 10% and 38%, across the four projects
audits.c: Weekly multi-professional QI meeting built into an existing regular meeting, combining teaching and project review, extended from 30 to 45 minutes after 6 weeks
audits.r2: All four projects achieved their stated process reliability aim

audits.t: Doctor Who? A Quality Improvement Project to Assess and Improve Patients' Knowledge of Their Inpatient Physicians.
audits.st: Clinical Learning Environment Review expectation for effective patient-physician communication
audits.f: Before intervention, white board utilisation was 54.5% and business card use was 33.7%.
audits.c: Educational audit and feedback intervention (September 2013 to May 2014) on use of business cards and white boards for provider identification.
audits.r2: White board utilisation improved to 72.2% (P<.01) and business card use slightly improved to 44.4% (P=.07); overall physician recognition did not improve, and only 20.3% could name their physician without using these tools.

audits.t: Adherence to diabetes care processes at general practices in the National Capital Region-Delhi, India.
audits.st: Standard diabetes care processes (weight, BP, HbA1c, lipids, ECG, eye exam, foot exam)
audits.f: dilated eye exam 7.4%, foot exam 15.1%, ECG 29.1%, HbA1c/BP/lipids measured in 51.7%/88.4%/28.1% of patients

audits.t: Decreasing Diagnostic Hysteroscopy Performed in the Operating Room: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Institutional target of a 75% reduction in diagnostic hysteroscopies performed in the main operating room
audits.f: 111 diagnostic hysteroscopies were performed at baseline in the main operating room.
audits.c: Staff education and case review, accessible sonohysterography, and an operative hysteroscopy education programme.
audits.r2: 33 diagnostic hysteroscopies were performed during the intervention period (70% reduction from baseline), and 20 during the maintenance period (82% reduction); savings of $126,984 and 12.5 surgical days; complications remained constant.

audits.t: Introducing routine HIV screening for patients on an internal medicine residency inpatient service: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: CDC recommendation for universal HIV screening ages 13-64
audits.f: offers of HIV screening 7.9% (44/559 preintervention cohort), screening tests ordered 7.7% (43/559)
audits.c: Resident survey, email reminders, education, and friendly competition among residents
audits.r2: offers of HIV screening increased to 55.5% (300/541), screening tests ordered increased to 44.4% (240/541)

audits.t: Perioperative management of patients treated with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor blockers: a quality improvement audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 83 (26%) of 323 participants had their ACE inhibitor or ARB withheld on the day of surgery; no significant difference was found between continued and withheld groups in postoperative acute kidney injury (13% vs 18%, P=0.25) or atrial fibrillation (15% vs 18%, P=0.71).

audits.t: Adherence to Recommended Risk Management among Unaffected Women with a BRCA Mutation.
audits.tp: Adherence to cancer risk management guidelines in BRCA carriers
audits.st: Guidelines for cancer risk management in unaffected BRCA mutation carriers
audits.f: Adherence to recommended risk management was reported by 69% (breast cancer), 82% (ovarian cancer) and 66% (both cancers) of participants.

audits.t: Feasibility of a hemodialysis safety checklist for nurses and patients: a quality improvement study.
audits.st: Locally developed Hemo Pause hemodialysis safety checklist
audits.f: baseline (pre-checklist) hemodialysis treatments without checklist use
audits.c: Introduction and training on the Hemo Pause safety checklist to be completed jointly by nurses and patients each session
audits.r2: checklist completed for 556/757 (73%) treatments; 93% of nurses found it easy to use, 73% of patients felt safer

audits.t: Mandibular fractures - towards a national standard for "time to theatre" - national audit by the BAOMS Trauma Specialist Interest Group.
audits.tp: Time to theatre for mandibular fracture fixation
audits.st: Proposed national standard for treating mandibular fractures by end of next working day
audits.f: 80% of patients operated on by end of next working day; time to theatre ranged from 1h15min to 11 days 20h51min (median 22h7min); units with dedicated OMFS trauma list more likely to meet standard (p=0.011)

audits.t: Compliance with an empirical antimicrobial protocol improves the outcome of complicated intra-abdominal infections: a prospective observational study.
audits.tp: Antimicrobial protocol compliance in intra-abdominal infections
audits.st: Institutional empirical antibiotic therapy protocol for complicated intra-abdominal infections, based on guidelines
audits.f: Empirical antibiotic therapy complied with the protocol in 52.3% of patients; non-compliance was associated with higher mortality (14.9% vs 5.6%, P=0.011).

audits.t: Improved Guideline Adherence With Integrated Sickle Cell Disease and Asthma Care.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence for sickle cell disease and asthma co-management
audits.st: National Asthma Education and Prevention Program guidelines
audits.f: asthma action plan utilisation 56% (n=16), spirometry use in children ≥5 years 65% (n=41)
audits.c: Integrated SCD and asthma clinic with dual respiratory therapist/case manager, SCD nurse practitioner, onsite pulmonary function lab, and pediatric hematologist
audits.r2: asthma action plan utilisation increased to 100% (p=0.003); spirometry use increased to 95%

audits.t: Client Factors Affect Provider Adherence to Clinical Guidelines during First Antenatal Care.
audits.tp: Provider adherence to first antenatal care guidelines
audits.st: Safe Motherhood Protocol (SMP) thirteen-point first antenatal visit checklist
audits.f: complete adherence to guidelines in 48.1% of pregnant women

audits.t: Quality Improvement Initiative to Decrease Variability of Emergency Physician Opioid Analgesic Prescribing.
audits.st: Local target to reduce variability of ED opioid analgesic prescribing (no external guideline named)
audits.f: Stage 1 mean opioid prescribing rate variability 20%
audits.c: Physicians informed prescribing data would be collected and shared (Stage 2), then individual prescribing data shared unblinded (Stage 3)
audits.r2: Stage 2 mean 13% (46% reduction); further reduction in Stage 3

audits.t: AUDIT OF BLOOD REQUISITION.
audits.st: Standard blood requisition documentation requirements
audits.f: Urgency of requirement and blood group were omitted in 56% of forms; 104 forms lacked indications for transfusion; history of previous transfusion and pregnancy/HDN were omitted in 25.1% and 37.38% of cases; 14.61% of total collection was discarded.

audits.t: Evaluation of Compliance for Treatment of Sudden Hearing Loss: A CHEER Network Study.
audits.st: American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery Foundation Clinical Practice Guideline: Sudden Hearing Loss
audits.f: Compliance for otolaryngologists was >95% for key action statements (KAS) 1, 3 and 6, and 90-95% for KAS 5 and 10; there is opportunity for nonotolaryngologists to improve compliance with statements 3 and 5-7.

audits.t: Assessment and improvement of HIV screening rates in a Midwest primary care practice using an electronic clinical decision support system: a quality improvement study.
audits.tp: HIV screening rates in primary care
audits.st: CDC recommended universal HIV screening guidelines (ages 13-65)
audits.f: 1.80% of eligible patients screened for HIV
audits.c: Provider survey and education on CDC guidelines, plus an HIV screening alert added to existing electronic clinical decision support tool
audits.r2: 3.34% of eligible patients screened for HIV (difference -1.54% [-2.1%, -0.99%])

audits.t: Implementation of WHO Near-Miss Approach for Maternal Health at a Tertiary Care Hospital: An Audit.
audits.st: WHO Near-Miss Approach for maternal health
audits.f: There were 3 maternal deaths; prevalence of severe acute maternal morbidity (SAMM) was 2.025%.

audits.t: The effect of a postoperative quality improvement program on outcomes in colorectal surgery in a community hospital.
audits.st: National Dutch clinical audit benchmark for oncological colorectal surgery outcomes
audits.f: Severe complication rate (Clavien-Dindo >=3b) 25.0%; mortality 8.7%; anastomotic leak 9.8%; median length of stay 9 days (IQR 5-19); failure-to-rescue rate 34.9%
audits.c: Quality improvement programme: avoidance of postoperative NSAIDs, pursuit of peri-operative normovolaemia, avoidance of resectional surgery in frail patients over 80 with ASA 3/4, and a standardised postoperative surveillance protocol (CRP on day 2 and 4, with CT if abnormal)
audits.r2: Severe complication rate fell to 13.7% (p=.001); mortality fell to 2.6% (p=.003); anastomotic leak fell to 4.2% (p=.013); median length of stay fell to 7 days (IQR 4-12); failure-to-rescue rate fell to 15.0% (p=.039); QIP implementation was an independent predictor of fewer major complications (OR 0.53)

audits.t: Health Worker Compliance with a 'Test And Treat' Malaria Case Management Protocol in Papua New Guinea.
audits.tp: Health worker compliance with malaria test and treat protocol
audits.st: Papua New Guinea Department of Health 'test and treat' malaria case management protocol (2011)
audits.f: Across both surveys: 77.6% tested for malaria by RDT/microscopy; 65.6% of confirmed cases prescribed correct antimalarials; 15.3% of RDT-negative febrile patients incorrectly prescribed antimalarials; overall strict protocol compliance 62.8%
audits.c: not reported (repeated cross-sectional surveys; attitudinal support assessed over time)
audits.r2: Attitudinal support for the protocol improved across time (specific compliance figures not separated by year in abstract)

audits.t: Closing the delivery gaps in pediatric HIV care in Togo, West Africa: using the care delivery value chain framework to direct quality improvement.
audits.tp: Pediatric HIV care delivery quality improvement
audits.st: Care Delivery Value Chain (CDVC) framework targets for pediatric HIV/AIDS service activities
audits.f: infants receiving routine PCR testing at 2 months 39%; HIV-exposed children receiving confirmatory testing at 18 months 67%; initial CD4 testing within 3 months 67%
audits.c: 13 distinct QI activities mapped using the CDVC framework over 12 months
audits.r2: PCR testing at 2 months increased to 95%; confirmatory testing at 18 months increased to 100%; CD4 testing within 3 months increased to 100%; 11 of 13 activities met or exceeded targets

audits.t: Prospective audit showing improved patient-assessed skin toxicity with use of betamethasone cream for those at high risk of radiation dermatitis.
audits.st: Risk-based skincare policy for patients at high risk of radiation dermatitis
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Introduction of risk-based skincare policy with prophylactic betamethasone cream for high-risk patients
audits.r2: Significant reduction in redness, itch, discomfort, sleep disturbance and use of analgesia with addition of steroid cream

audits.t: Clinical Pathway and Monthly Feedback Improve Adherence to Antibiotic Guideline Recommendations for Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
audits.tp: Antibiotic guideline adherence for community-acquired pneumonia
audits.st: Local community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) antibiotic guideline recommendations
audits.f: concordance rate 28.1% at baseline
audits.c: Clinical pathway for CAP management introduced in ED with monthly feedback to ED physicians on concordance rates (after an initial educational intervention showed no benefit)
audits.r2: concordance rate increased to 61.5% (vs 28.1% baseline); educational intervention alone achieved 31.2% (not significant)

audits.t: Evaluating appropriate red blood cell transfusions: a quality audit at 10 Ontario hospitals to determine the optimal measure for assessing appropriateness.
audits.tp: Red blood cell transfusion appropriateness audit
audits.st: Appropriateness criteria for red blood cell transfusion (expert adjudication)
audits.f: 78% of audited RBC units were adjudicated as appropriate (kappa=0.9603), with significant variability between institutions.

audits.t: Promoting the role of patients in improving hand hygiene compliance amongst health care workers.
audits.tp: Hand hygiene compliance amongst healthcare workers
audits.st: WHO hand hygiene compliance guidelines
audits.f: baseline hand hygiene compliance (specific % not reported)
audits.c: PDSA cycles empowering patients to promote staff hand hygiene compliance
audits.r2: compliance increased by 15% during the 10 days of testing

audits.t: Assessment of trauma quality improvement activities at public hospitals in Thailand.
audits.tp: Trauma quality improvement programme implementation audit
audits.st: WHO recommended trauma quality improvement programme (TQIP) core elements: morbidity and mortality conferences, preventable death panels, trauma registries, and audit filters
audits.f: 90% of respondents had a trauma registry, 88% used audit filters, 88% conducted regular morbidity and mortality conferences, 56% had preventable death panels, and 48% reported all four elements.

audits.t: Pre-NELA vs NELA - has anything changed, or is it just an audit exercise?
audits.st: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) standards for emergency service provision
audits.f: 75.0% had decision to operate made by consultant; 9.1% admitted directly to critical care; 10.0% unexpected escalation to higher level of care; 52.3% uneventful recovery; 30-day mortality 2.3%
audits.c: Introduction of the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) standards
audits.r2: 100% had decision to operate made by consultant (P<0.001); 27.3% admitted directly to critical care; 0% unexpected escalation (P=0.036); 76.4% uneventful recovery (P=0.018); 30-day mortality 7.3% (P=0.378, not significant)

audits.t: Practice patterns of radiation therapy technology in Australia: results of a national audit.
audits.tp: National census of radiation therapy technology practice patterns
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: IMRT used for 37% of patients; increasing use of image fusion and image-guided radiotherapy

audits.t: Team Training in the Perioperative Arena: A Methodology for Implementation and Auditing Behavior.
audits.tp: Perioperative team training and safety checklist audit
audits.st: Surgical safety checklist time-out and debrief conversation standard (merged with TeamSTEPPS)
audits.f: 1610 audits of time out and debrief conversations were performed by live auditors.
audits.c: TeamSTEPPS team training programme merged with a surgical safety checklist.

audits.t: An audit of urine culture results at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital (QECH) in 1994-95 and 1999-2001.
audits.st: Malawi first-line (cotrimoxazole) and second-line (nitrofurantoin) drug policy for urinary tract infection
audits.f: E. coli was isolated in 50% of cultures; isolates were sensitive to cotrimoxazole in only 13% and nitrofurantoin in 48% of cultures, and to gentamicin (40%) and augmentin (20%); levels of drug resistance did not differ between the two periods.

audits.t: Overcoming the tyranny of distance: An audit of process and outcomes from a pilot telehealth spinal assessment clinic.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 25 consultations were held for 22 patients; 88% of disorders were lumbar; 64% of initial consultations were discharged to the general practitioner; total cost was AUD$11,187, a 23% reduction versus the outreach clinic; no adverse outcomes were reported.

audits.t: Assessment of national dosimetry quality audits results for    teletherapy machines from 1989 to 2015.
audits.st: ICRU optimal (±2.5%), IAEA (±3.0%) and ICRU minimal (±5.0%) dose accuracy limits
audits.f: 20.44%, 16.02% and 4.42% of audits were outside acceptable limits of ±2.5%, ±3.0% and ±5.0% respectively

audits.t: Audit of fibroepithelial tumors of the breast in a Nigerian tertiary institution.
audits.st: WHO classification criteria for phyllodes tumours
audits.f: Of 19 lesions initially reported as phyllodes tumour, only 16 (84%) met WHO criteria on review; 3 (16%) were reclassified as fibroadenoma; reclassified phyllodes tumours were 75% benign, 18.7% borderline and 6.3% malignant.

audits.t: Hand Hygiene Compliance in the Setting of Trauma Resuscitation.
audits.tp: Hand hygiene compliance during trauma resuscitation
audits.st: World Health Organization 2009 Five Moments for Hand Hygiene guidelines
audits.f: Overall hand hygiene compliance was 7% (71/1034 opportunities); 0% before clean procedures, 15% after patient contact; glove use was more common than hand hygiene (69% before, 47% after patient contact); combined glove/hand hygiene compliance was 57%.

audits.t: Academic hospital staff compliance with a fecal immunochemical test-based colorectal cancer screening program.
audits.st: Institutional faecal immunochemical test (FIT)-based colorectal cancer screening programme for staff aged over 50
audits.f: Of 211 eligible employees, 59 (27.9%) consented to participate and 41 (19.4%) completed the first FIT round.
audits.r2: 24 (11.4%) completed the second FIT round; physicians had markedly lower participation than other staff (13.5% vs 70.2%).

audits.t: Compliance of Perioperative Antibiotic Dosing and Surgical Site Infection Rate in Office-Based Elective Surgery.
audits.tp: Perioperative antibiotic dosing compliance and surgical site infection
audits.st: Best practice target for perioperative antibiotic administration timing window
audits.f: timely prophylactic antibiotics administered in 96% of cases, surgical site infection rate 0.36% (vs reported hospital rate 3.7%)

audits.t: The compliance of thromboprophylaxis affects the risk of venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing hip fracture surgery.
audits.tp: Thromboprophylaxis compliance after hip fracture surgery
audits.st: Thromboprophylaxis regimen compliance standard (non-compliant/poor/good compliance categories)
audits.f: 761 (64.7%) non-compliant, 224 (19.0%) poor compliant, 192 (16.3%) good compliant; overall VTE rate 7.9%

audits.t: Improving quality of care in general practices by self-audit, benchmarking and quality circles.
audits.tp: Quality of chronic disease care via self-audit and benchmarking
audits.st: Locally developed quality indicators (35-item score) based on pre-existing quality management systems for 8 chronic diseases
audits.f: mean quality score 62.0 at baseline
audits.c: Self-audit, benchmarking, and quality circles ('Improvement of Quality by Benchmarking')

audits.t: Improved compliance with the World Health Organization Surgical Safety Checklist is associated with reduced surgical specimen labelling errors.
audits.tp: Surgical safety checklist compliance and specimen labelling errors
audits.st: World Health Organization Surgical Safety Checklist (Sign Out domain)
audits.f: There were 19 labelling/completion errors in 4760 specimens (rate 3.99 per 1000) before the new checklist administration approach.
audits.c: New approach to administering the Sign Out domain of the surgical safety checklist using wall-mounted charts and migrated leadership among operating room sub-teams.
audits.r2: There were 8 errors in 5065 specimens (rate 1.58 per 1000) after the change (P=0.0225).

audits.t: Improving the diagnostic stage of the suspected colorectal cancer pathway: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Suspected colorectal cancer diagnostic pathway lead-time
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline data highlighted lead-time and patient experience problems in the diagnostic stage of the suspected colorectal cancer pathway
audits.c: New pathway designed via stakeholder workshop (lean thinking, experience-based design) increasing proportion going straight-to-test
audits.r2: Median time from referral to endoscopy reduced from 26 to 14 days (P<0.001); proportion going straight-to-test increased from 6% to 43%

audits.t: Compliance and Effectiveness of WHO Surgical Safety Check list: A JPMC Audit.
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (SSC) compliance standard
audits.f: SSC properly marked in 172 (20.4%) cases; SSI 59 (7.50%) cases
audits.c: SSC included as part of routine ward history sheets over 4 years, with ongoing use
audits.r2: SSC properly marked in 838 (89.9%) cases; SSI reduced to 20 (2.12%) cases

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Project to Reduce the 'No Show' rate in a Paediatric Neurology Clinic.
audits.st: Local target to reduce the no-show rate from 49% to 25% by 31 December 2013 (international benchmark for primary care clinics is 5%-10%)
audits.f: No-show rate was 49% (26/53); median waiting time to the third available appointment was 11 weeks
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles: offering an immediate re-book option to patients, refilling cancelled morning slots from the urgent waiting list, and discharging patients from the clinic after two non-attendances
audits.r2: No-show rate fell to 18% after the third PDSA cycle and was sustained below the 25% target for 2 years; median waiting time to the third available appointment reduced to 8 weeks (a 30% improvement)

audits.t: The construction and implementation of a clinical decision-making algorithm reduces the cost of adult fracture clinic visits by up to £104,800 per year: a quality improvement study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline rate of inappropriate referrals to new patient fracture clinic recorded before intervention
audits.c: Clinical decision-making algorithm disseminated electronically and orally to emergency department staff
audits.r2: Inappropriate referrals reduced by almost 20% (P=0.0445); potential annual cost saving of up to £104,800

audits.t: Reducing blood stream infection in patients on hemodialysis: Incorporating patient engagement into a quality improvement activity.
audits.st: National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) bloodstream infection benchmarks and hand hygiene/cannulation/catheter audit standards
audits.f: Facilities selected were the 20% of the network with the highest bloodstream infection (BSI) rates, capturing 31% of the patient population.
audits.c: Joint quality improvement/patient engagement activity involving patients in the infection control process.
audits.r2: Statistically significant improvement was reached in reduction of BSIs, in patient engagement in infection control, and in correct completion of hand hygiene audits (P<0.001); significant improvement in cannulation audits (P<0.01); improvement in catheter audits was not significant.

audits.t: Adherence to recommended UK sampling protocols for detecting mast cell mediator release in perioperative anaphylaxis.
audits.tp: Tryptase sampling protocol adherence for perioperative anaphylaxis
audits.st: UK guidelines on serial tryptase sampling for perioperative anaphylaxis
audits.f: 98% of cases provided two or more acute tryptase samples, but only 60% supplied sufficient clinical information; 308 patients never dropped within the reference range across three samples.

audits.t: Automated hand hygiene auditing with and without an intervention.
audits.st: World Health Organization hand hygiene guidelines
audits.f: Covert automated hand hygiene compliance was 30% (medical ward) and 49% (surgical ward); Hand Hygiene Australia human audit rates were 85% and 87% respectively.
audits.c: Overt automated auditing with daily feedback and a peer-reminder intervention (clinicians shared rates, set goals, nudged each other) for 6 months, continued without refreshment for a further 6 months.
audits.r2: Compliance on the medical ward was unchanged from covert baseline; surgical ward improved by 11 percentage points to 60%, then declined by 9 percentage points once the intervention was not refreshed.

audits.t: A single center observational study on emergency department clinician non-adherence to clinical practice guidelines for treatment of uncomplicated urinary tract infections.
audits.tp: Antibiotic guideline adherence for uncomplicated UTI
audits.st: 2010 International Clinical Practice Guidelines (ICPG) for uncomplicated UTI
audits.f: 63.1% received non-adherent treatment; fluoroquinolone use in 97.6% of non-adherent cystitis cases; inappropriate antibiotic choice in 39.1% of pyelonephritis cases

audits.t: Plastic in patient study: Prospective audit of adherence to peripheral intravenous cannula monitoring and documentation guidelines, with the aim of reducing future rates of intravenous cannula-related complications.
audits.tp: Peripheral IV cannula documentation and monitoring
audits.st: Peripheral intravenous cannula (PIVC) documentation and monitoring guidelines
audits.f: Documentation of PIVC 36.4%; early identification of non-indicated PIVCs 88.8%; early phlebitis rate 3.7%.
audits.c: Three interventions: a journey-board 'PIP strip' flagging inpatients with PIVCs, a 'PIP row' prompt in the medical admission proforma to review PIVC indication, and a 'PIP poster' visual cue on PIVC trolleys.
audits.r2: Documentation improved to 50% (P=.025); early identification of non-indicated PIVCs improved to 97.1% (P=.018); phlebitis rate trended down to 0% (P=.08).

audits.t: Compliance with the Surgical Safety Checklist Results of an Audit in a Teaching Hospital in Italy.
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist
audits.f: All Checklist records were correctly filled out on paper, but questionnaire responses showed the checklist was not actively supported by all surgical team members; 100% of nurses and 73.7% of surgeons completed the questionnaire.

audits.t: Multicentre dose audit for clinical trials of radiation therapy in Asia.
audits.tp: Multicentre radiotherapy dose audit for clinical trials
audits.st: Forum for Nuclear Cooperation in Asia (FNCA) dose uniformity tolerance of ±5%
audits.f: average relative deviation between measured and intended dose 0.4% (SD 1.5%); one beam exceeded ±5% tolerance
audits.c: External audit programme using radiophotoluminescent glass dosimeters (RGDs) run by NIRS Japan; cause of the single out-of-tolerance beam was investigated and resolved
audits.r2: excellent uniformity overall after investigation and correction of the single deviant beam

audits.t: Provider adherence to first antenatal care guidelines and risk of pregnancy complications in public sector facilities: a Ghanaian cohort study.
audits.tp: Provider adherence to first antenatal care guidelines
audits.st: First antenatal care thirteen-point checklist guidelines
audits.f: complete provider adherence to guidelines in 48.5% of women

audits.t: Impact of a care pathway for COPD on adherence to guidelines and hospital readmission: a cluster randomized trial.
audits.tp: COPD care pathway adherence to guidelines
audits.st: In-hospital COPD exacerbation management guidelines (process indicators, 24 main indicators)
audits.f: control group readmission and guideline adherence rates
audits.c: Implementation of a care pathway (CP) for COPD exacerbation management via cluster randomized trial
audits.r2: 30-day readmission rate significantly lower in intervention group (9.7%) vs control (15.3%, OR=0.427, p=0.040); adherence significantly higher for 2 of 24 indicators (8.3%)

audits.t: A quality improvement initiative on the management of osteoporosis in older people with Parkinsonism.
audits.st: Evidence-based osteoporosis guidance; target 100% of new referrals and 80% of follow-up patients treated accordingly
audits.f: Fragility fracture prevalence 22.6% (68/300); only 40% (27/68) on appropriate osteoporosis treatment
audits.c: PDSA-based QI methodology with introduction of a monthly multidisciplinary team (MDT) meeting
audits.r2: 100% of new patients and 91% of follow-up patients received evidence-based osteoporosis treatment

audits.t: No Ifs, No Butts: Compliance with Smoking Cessation in Secondary Care Guidance (NICE PH48) by Providers of Cancer Therapies (Radiotherapy and Chemotherapy) in the UK.
audits.tp: Compliance with NICE smoking cessation guidance in cancer care providers
audits.st: NICE PH48: smoking cessation in secondary care
audits.f: 79.1% of trusts smoke-free in theory but only 18.6% smoke-free in practice; gaps in NRT provision, staff training, and e-cigarette policy clarity

audits.t: Adherence to guidelines for creatinine and potassium monitoring and discontinuation following renin-angiotensin system blockade: a UK general practice-based cohort study.
audits.tp: Creatinine and potassium monitoring after ACEI/ARB initiation
audits.st: Guidelines for renal function monitoring following ACEI/ARB initiation (recommended monitoring within 2 weeks) and discontinuation after creatinine increase ≥30% or potassium >6 mmol/L
audits.f: 10% had neither baseline nor follow-up monitoring within 12 months before/2 months after initiation; 47% had both; 34% had baseline monitoring within 1 month before initiation; of 191 (0.4%) with potassium >6mmol/L, 80% continued treatment

audits.t: Reducing the incidence of Obstetric Sphincter Injuries using a hands-on technique: an interventional quality improvement project.
audits.st: Local target to halve incidence of obstetric anal sphincter injuries (from ~8% to ≤4%)
audits.f: incidence of sphincter injuries around 8% among first-time vaginal deliveries; median number of deliveries between injury cases 9.5
audits.c: Hands-on technique with four elements in a care bundle plus staff certification process on the delivery ward
audits.r2: incidence reduced to 3.4% (from 7.0%); median deliveries between injury cases increased to 20; adherence to 3 of 4 bundle elements rose significantly

audits.t: National audit of the quality of pain relief provided in emergency departments in Aotearoa, New Zealand: The PRiZED 1 Study.
audits.st: Timely and adequate provision of analgesia for painful ED presentations (quality-of-care indicator; no explicit numerical national target stated)
audits.f: 132 (15%) had no pain recorded; 205 (24%) received no pain relief; median time to analgesia 62 (IQR 30-134) minutes; adequate analgesia achieved in 141/277 (51%, 95% CI 45-57%).

audits.t: Multicentre observational study of adherence to Sepsis Six guidelines in emergency general surgery.
audits.tp: Sepsis Six adherence in emergency general surgery
audits.st: Sepsis Six standards (devised for severe sepsis)
audits.f: Timely delivery of all Sepsis Six elements achieved in only 4 patients with severe sepsis; individual guideline elements were delivered in 17.6-94.5% of cases; oxygen and blood cultures most often missed; median time to surgical source control 19.8 (IQR 10.0-35.4) hours.

audits.t: Impact of a hand hygiene audit on hand hygiene compliance in a tertiary care public sector teaching hospital in South India.
audits.st: World Health Organization hand hygiene guidelines (5 Moments)
audits.f: Overall hand hygiene complete adherence rate (HHCAR) 45.5%; monthly HHCAR started at 37.5%.
audits.c: Continuous hand hygiene auditing with monthly feedback over 1 year (audit itself used as the improvement tool).
audits.r2: Monthly HHCAR rose to 51.7% by the end of the study (statistically significant increase, P=.001); HHCAR highest among nurses (58.9%) vs other staff (46.7%) and doctors (46.6%).

audits.t: Preventing Pressure Injuries in Neonates Undergoing Therapeutic Hypothermia for Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy: An Interprofessional Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Hospital-acquired pressure injury prevention in neonates
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Interprofessional team revised protocols for therapeutic hypothermia/EEG monitoring, using PDSA cycles to optimise product selection, hardwire assessment practice and refine documentation.
audits.r2: A sustained zero hospital-acquired pressure injury rate was achieved in the therapeutic hypothermia population.

audits.t: Acute lower GI bleeding in the UK: patient characteristics, interventions and outcomes in the first nationwide audit.
audits.tp: Acute lower GI bleeding presentation and management
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 26.3% received red cell transfusion; only 2.1% received endoscopic haemostasis; 48% underwent no inpatient investigations; in-hospital mortality 3.4% (85/2528), highest in established inpatients (17.8%)

audits.t: Remote Video Auditing in the Surgical Setting.
audits.tp: Remote video auditing in the operating room
audits.st: Universal Protocol for preventing wrong site/procedure/person surgery
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Remote video auditing using low-resolution cameras, large-screen displays and cell phone alerts, with real-time results-sharing.

audits.t: Tobacco Cessation Interventions in Tertiary Hospitals in Nigeria: An Audit of Patient Records.
audits.st: WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control, Article 14 (5A's brief intervention model)
audits.f: 33.1% of records documented physician inquiry about tobacco use; among identified users, 12.9% were offered cessation advice, 2.6% had readiness to quit recorded, 1.5% were offered assistance, 0.8% had follow-up documented.

audits.t: Reducing Non-Attendance Rates for Assessment at an Eating Disorders Service: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Non-attendance at eating disorder service assessment appointments
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Historical non-attendance rate at first appointments was 20.4%
audits.c: Introduction of a 'partial booking' system for initial appointments (January 2013)
audits.r2: Non-attendance rate reduced from 20.4% to 15.1%, a medium-sized effect

audits.t: Clinical applicability and cost of a 46-gene panel for genomic analysis of solid tumours: Retrospective validation and prospective audit in the UK National Health Service.
audits.tp: Clinical applicability and cost of 46-gene NGS panel for solid tumours
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Panel sequencing successful in 97% (342/351); at least one mutation identified in 87% (296/342); locally actionable mutation in 35% (122/351); 40 patients received targeted treatment, 55% (22/40) solely due to the panel

audits.t: Impact of modified quality control checklist on protocol adherence and outcomes in a post-surgical Intensive Care Unit.
audits.tp: Protocol adherence via modified quality control checklist in surgical ICU
audits.st: WHO surgery checklist and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA) infection prevention guidelines
audits.f: documentation of quality indicators 32% in retrospective sample
audits.c: Introduction of a comprehensive compliance checklist combining WHO surgery checklist and SHEA guidelines, with supervised documentation
audits.r2: documentation of quality indicators improved to 98%

audits.t: An external dosimetry audit programme to credential static and rotational IMRT delivery for clinical trials quality assurance.
audits.tp: IMRT/VMAT dosimetry credentialing for clinical trials
audits.st: RTTQA external dosimetry audit tolerances for IMRT/VMAT credentialing
audits.f: Average ratio of measured output between auditor and host was 1.002±0.006; average point dose agreement -0.3±1.8%; gamma pass rates at 2%/2mm, 3%/2mm and 3%/3mm were 92%, 96% and 98% respectively

audits.t: Adopting and sustaining a Virtual Fracture Clinic model in the District Hospital setting - a quality improvement approach.
audits.st: Local target: at least 50% of new orthopaedic outpatient referrals reviewed in a Virtual Fracture Clinic (VFC), based on the Glasgow Royal Infirmary VFC model
audits.f: 0% of new patients seen in VFC; 412/958 (43.0%) of interactions were first attendances
audits.c: Introduction of a Virtual Fracture Clinic model via three PDSA cycles: pilot testing, full roll-out with A&E pathway change and diary management, then embedding with mandated investigation requests and clearer plaster-team escalation pathway
audits.r2: 56.1% of new referrals seen in VFC soon after full introduction, plateauing at an average of 56.4% in the final 6 months (final data collection point 60.1%), against a target of 50%

audits.t: Virtual EPID standard phantom audit (VESPA) for remote IMRT and VMAT credentialing.
audits.tp: Remote virtual phantom dosimetry credentialing for IMRT/VMAT
audits.st: Published IMRT QA dosimetric tolerance criteria applied via virtual phantom gamma analysis
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of aspects of practice in relation to patients with suspected community-onset blood stream infection.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median time from registration to first antimicrobial administration was 226 minutes and was guideline compliant in 121/151 (80.7%) of treated patients; 8.5% blood cultures positive, 5.0% clinically significant

audits.t: A medical curriculum in transition: audit and student perspective of undergraduate teaching of ethics and professionalism.
audits.tp: Delivery of GMC professionalism competencies in undergraduate curriculum
audits.st: General Medical Council (GMC) professionalism competency requirements
audits.f: C21 curriculum delivers explicit or implicit teaching for all major GMC professionalism competencies, though some missed opportunities remain identified

audits.t: A retrospective audit of the first screening round of the Maltese breast screening programme.
audits.st: European Guidelines recommendations for breast screening performance parameters
audits.f: Met European Guidelines for technical repeat rate (0.26%), early recall rate (0.45%), cancer detection rate (13.77 per 1000) and PPV (7.58%); local recall rate (18.53%) and further assessment rate (18.27%) were higher than recommended

audits.t: A multi-faceted strategy to reduce ventilation-associated mortality in brain-injured patients. The BI-VILI project: a nationwide quality improvement project.
audits.st: Protocol targets: low tidal volume (<=7 ml/kg), moderate PEEP (6-8 cm H2O), early extubation protocol
audits.f: 8 patients (2%) fully compliant with the recommended bundle.
audits.c: Recommendations for low tidal volume, moderate PEEP and an early extubation protocol were disseminated nationally after the baseline period.
audits.r2: Full compliance rose to 52 patients (15%); no significant difference in ventilator-free days at day 90 overall (71 vs 67 days, P=0.746), but compliant patients had more ventilator-free days than non-compliant patients.

audits.t: User compliance with documenting on a track and trigger-based observation and response chart: a two-phase multi-site audit study.
audits.tp: Compliance with observation and response chart documentation
audits.st: Local calling criteria and chart completion guidelines for track-and-trigger observation charts
audits.f: Compliance was mixed (4-14%); numbers rather than dots written in graphing section in 60% of cases; emergency call initiated in 33% of cases during retrospective audit
audits.c: Introduction and routine adoption of a newly designed track-and-trigger observation and response chart
audits.r2: Compliance improved slightly with new chart; emergency call initiated in 41% of cases with new chart; recognition of abnormal vital signs improved slightly, particularly for higher surveillance levels

audits.t: Quality Improvement Initiatives Lead to Reduction in Nulliparous Term Singleton Vertex Cesarean Delivery Rate.
audits.tp: Nulliparous term singleton vertex (NTSV) caesarean rate
audits.st: NTSV caesarean delivery rate benchmark (recognised as a meaningful quality benchmark; no single numeric national target stated)
audits.f: NTSV caesarean delivery rate was higher than state and national averages, around 35%.
audits.c: Multi-strategy approach: provider education, provider feedback, and implementation of new policies targeting evidence-based and inferred drivers of NTSV caesarean rate.
audits.r2: NTSV caesarean delivery rate declined from 35% to 21% over the eight years (total caesarean rate also declined).

audits.t: Reducing Pediatric Sternal Wound Infections: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: not reported (institutional sternal wound infection prevention bundle)
audits.f: Sternal wound infection in 32 patients (3.8%) preintervention.
audits.c: Implementation of a sternal wound infection prevention bundle across the preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative periods.
audits.r2: Sternal wound infection fell to 19 patients (2.1%) postintervention (p=0.04); in delayed sternal closure cases, infection fell from 10.6% to 3.9% (p=0.02).

audits.t: New Guidelines for the Management of Chest Pain: Lessons From a Recent Audit in Tauranga, New Zealand.
audits.st: New NICE guidance on chest pain management
audits.f: 99.2% received ECG on admission; only 59.3% had documented repeat ECG (day admissions 51.5% vs overnight 69.2%, P=0.04); gaps also in aspirin therapy and appropriate oxygen use
audits.c: not reported (chest pain management pathway planned)

audits.t: Implementation of a Quality Improvement Initiative: Improved Congenital Muscular Torticollis Outcomes in a Large Hospital Setting.
audits.st: American Physical Therapy Association (APTA) congenital muscular torticollis guideline (2013): resolution of CMT within 6 months of evaluation
audits.f: 42% of patients achieved full resolution of CMT within a 6-month episode of care.
audits.c: Quality improvement initiative using PDSA cycles: a CMT registry, statistical process control charts, timely access to care, audit and clinician feedback, and improved documentation, aligned with the Chronic Care Model.
audits.r2: Percentage achieving full CMT resolution within 6 months rose to 61%.

audits.t: Improving Guideline Compliance in Australia With a National Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Outcomes Registry.
audits.tp: Guideline-concordant therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention
audits.st: Secondary prevention guideline therapies after PCI (statins, dual antiplatelet therapy)
audits.f: Statin therapy at discharge 92.1% in the first year.
audits.c: Real-time benchmarking and local reporting of practice/outcome data via the national Genesis Cardiovascular Outcomes Registry (GCOR-PCI).
audits.r2: Statin therapy at discharge improved to 94.4%.

audits.t: Optimizing Radiation Doses for Computed Tomography Across Institutions: Dose Auditing and Best Practices.
audits.st: Previously published CT radiation dose benchmarks
audits.f: Mean effective dose 13.2 mSv (chest) and 20.0 mSv (abdomen) at baseline.
audits.c: Audit reports of dose distribution were shared with the 5 centres and radiology professionals attended a 1.5-day in-person meeting to review reports and share best practices.
audits.r2: Mean effective dose fell to 10.7 mSv for chest (18.9% reduction) and 15.0 mSv for abdomen (25.0% reduction); scans exceeding benchmarks fell by 48% (chest) and 54% (abdomen); head CT dose variation decreased but with mixed centre-level changes.

audits.t: Using a quality improvement model to enhance providers' performance in maternal and newborn health care: a post-only intervention and comparison design.
audits.tp: Maternal and newborn health provider performance
audits.st: Standards Based Management and Recognition (SBM-R) approach to maternal and newborn health quality standards
audits.f: comparison facility mean performance scores: ANC 61.0%, labour/delivery 65.6%, PNC 50.6%
audits.c: Implementation of SBM-R quality improvement approach at intervention facilities
audits.r2: intervention facility scores: ANC 63.4% (not significant), labour/delivery 77.5% (p=0.002), PNC 72.8% (p=0.001)

audits.t: The impact of facility audits, evaluation reports and incentives on motivation and supply management among family planning service providers: an interventional study in two districts in Maputo Province, Mozambique.
audits.tp: Facility audits and family planning supply management
audits.st: Local standard for contraceptive supply/stock management (avoiding stock-outs)
audits.f: supply management/stock-out levels prior to monthly audits
audits.c: 10 monthly facility audits of stock cards/counts; 2 intervention groups also received monthly evaluation reports, one with added material incentives
audits.r2: intervention groups had fewer stock-outs than control; effect was only significant for the group receiving both incentives and evaluation reports; control group (audit only) also improved

audits.t: Hypokalaemia: Addressing human factors and improving education around prescription and administration of Intravenous(IV) Potassium infusion in Trauma and Orthopaedics.
audits.tp: Hypokalaemia management on trauma and orthopaedic wards
audits.st: Local departmental guideline for management of mild, moderate and severe hypokalaemia (no external national standard cited)
audits.f: 33% (10/30) aware 40mmol IV potassium available; 67% (20/30) confident prescribing/administering; 27% (8/30) aware cardiac monitoring not required; 93% felt need for further learning
audits.c: Awareness and education sessions, departmental hypokalaemia guideline/poster, improved ward stock of 40mmol potassium IV fluids, and a hypokalaemia management pathway/flowchart for mild, moderate and severe hypokalaemia
audits.r2: 70% (21/30) aware 40mmol IV potassium available; 87% (26/30) confident prescribing/administering; 70% (21/30) aware cardiac monitoring not required

audits.t: Return of experience on the initial audit of Cofrac and projects for the release of results of emergency biological tests.
audits.tp: Laboratory accreditation audit and emergency result release
audits.st: ISO 15189 international standard and Cofrac accreditation requirements
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Improving CKD Diagnosis and Blood Pressure Control in Primary Care: A Tailored Multifaceted Quality Improvement Programme.
audits.tp: CKD diagnosis and blood pressure control in primary care
audits.st: Local blood pressure targets and modelled CKD prevalence estimates (NIHR CLAHRC Greater Manchester programme)
audits.f: BP target achievement at baseline: 34% (P1), 60% (P2), 68% (P3), 63% (P4)
audits.c: Multifaceted quality improvement programme tailored to each practice's support needs following contextual analysis, over four phased 12-month QI projects.
audits.r2: BP target achievement at close: 74% (P1), 83% (P2), 71% (P3), 76% (P4); total CKD cases increased by 2,347 (27%) to 10,968 in an adult population of 231,568; 88-91% of nonproteinuric CKD patients achieved target BP

audits.t: Compliance with evidence-based multidisciplinary guidelines on perihilar cholangiocarcinoma.
audits.tp: Guideline compliance for perihilar cholangiocarcinoma management
audits.st: Evidence-based multidisciplinary guideline on perihilar cholangiocarcinoma management (implemented 2013)
audits.f: Biliary drainage attempted at regional centres in 83/158 (52.5%), with technical/therapeutic success of 79.5%/50% and a 45.8% complication rate; CT protocol not guideline-compliant in 52.8% of referrals; 54.2% of drained patients needed additional drainage after referral.

audits.t: Choosing Wisely: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Decrease Unnecessary Preoperative Testing.
audits.st: Choosing Wisely recommendations against routine low-value preoperative testing
audits.f: unnecessary testing rate approximately 36%
audits.c: Associate Provider (NP/PA)-run preoperative clinic with standardized protocols, scheduling changes, and EHR tools using PDSA cycles
audits.r2: unnecessary testing rate 4% in Associate Provider clinic vs 23% in usual care cohort (p<.001)

audits.t: A Multifaceted Quality Improvement Programme to Improve Acute Kidney Injury Care and Outcomes in a Large Teaching Hospital.
audits.tp: Acute kidney injury care bundle compliance
audits.st: Local Priority Care Checklist for nine key aspects of AKI care (detection within 24 hours, fluid assessment, drug review etc.)

audits.t: The enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) Greenie Board: a Navy-inspired quality improvement tool.

audits.t: Understanding Patient Referral Wait Times for Specialty Care in Ontario: A Retrospective Chart Audit.

audits.t: A Statewide Quality Improvement Collaborative to Increase Breastfeeding Rates in Tennessee.
