audits.t: Improving the use of intravenous antihypertensive medications in the hospital setting: a quality improvement initiative for patient safety.
audits.tp: Unindicated IV antihypertensive use for asymptomatic hypertension
audits.st: Internal QI target: reduce unindicated IV antihypertensive (IVAH) use by at least 25% within 1 year
audits.f: not reported (baseline rate not given numerically in abstract)
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles of education on IVAH indications targeting different staff groups
audits.r2: Unindicated IVAH use fell by 66% overall, reducing patient exposure by approximately 248 cases; 52% increase in a patient safety measure

audits.t: The Whittington Frailty Pathway: improving access to comprehensive geriatric assessment: an interdisciplinary quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Frailty identification and ambulatory pathway in the emergency department
audits.st: National guidelines mandating identification and tailored management of patients living with frailty who attend the acute hospital setting
audits.f: Overall admission rate of 50% for patients over 75 years (comparator)
audits.c: Integration of Clinical Frailty Scale scoring into the electronic record, a continuing education and awareness programme, dedicated project staff, and creation of an ambulatory frailty pathway with same-day comprehensive geriatric assessment.
audits.r2: 73% of patients over 75 presenting to the ED by ambulance received a Clinical Frailty Scale score; admission rate of 14% for the frailty pathway cohort versus 50% overall for over-75s; 1% decrease in overall ED admission; 7-day ED reattendance rate 15.1%; 30-day readmission rate 18.9%; consultant review estimated 87% of patients avoided a longer admission

audits.t: Adherence to Current Lipid Guidelines by Physicians in Kuwait.
audits.st: American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association 2013 blood cholesterol guideline
audits.f: Over 90% of physicians claimed to use lipid guidelines; 72.4% identified time limitation as a key barrier

audits.t: Quality improvement initiative for reduction of false alarms from multiparameter monitors in neonatal intensive care unit.
audits.tp: False alarm reduction in NICU monitoring
audits.st: Local QI aim to reduce false alarm activation from multiparameter monitors by 50% from baseline within 12 weeks (SQUIRE 2 reporting guideline)
audits.f: Median 23 (range 18-35) false alarms/hour/monitor; baseline staff knowledge score 40% (28-67%)
audits.c: Staff education on MPM use (group and 1:1 teaching, certification), individualised alarm limits for SpO2 and heart rate, WhatsApp reminders, expanded team, and a unit policy for alarm checks at shift change, delivered over five PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Median false alarms fell to 9 (6-12)/hour/bed after five PDSA cycles; knowledge score improved to 84% (60-90%); sustained at median 3/hour/bed over the following 10 months

audits.t: Factors affecting guideline adherence in the initial treatment of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer: Retrospective study in a French peripheral hospital.
audits.tp: Non-muscle invasive bladder cancer treatment guideline adherence
audits.st: European Association of Urology guidelines for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer
audits.f: Nonadherence in 61% of cases overall; intermediate-risk patients receiving mitomycin C 14%; high-risk patients receiving intravesical BCG 39%

audits.t: Effectiveness of a quality improvement collaborative in reducing time to surgery for patients requiring emergency cholecystectomy.
audits.st: NICE guidance: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 7 days of diagnosis of acute cholecystitis (8 days from presentation used as the project target)
audits.f: 8-day surgery rate 9.4% in the Chole-QuIC cohort versus 14.2% in the control group of other English/Welsh hospitals
audits.c: A surgeon-led quality improvement collaborative (Institute of Healthcare Improvement Breakthrough Series model): collaborative learning meetings, webinars, site visits, local audit data analysis support, and locally developed solutions (e.g. ring-fenced theatre capacity, dedicated pathway coordination)
audits.r2: 8-day surgery rate rose to 14.6% in the Chole-QuIC cohort versus 15.3% in the control group; relative change 1.56 (95% CI 1.38-1.75) vs 1.08 in controls; 8/12 sites showed significant improvement

audits.t: Decreasing radiographs in neonates through targeted quality improvement interventions.
audits.tp: Radiograph use reduction for PICC and ETT monitoring
audits.st: Internal QI target: decrease radiograph use by 20% (Nov 2017-Nov 2018)
audits.f: Radiographs per PICC day 0.86; radiographs per ETT day 1.45
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles: radiograph protocol standardising positioning/views/frequency; standardising ETT depth per NRP guidelines; institution-specific ETT depth guideline
audits.r2: Radiographs per PICC day decreased to 0.46 (p=0.004); radiographs per ETT day decreased to 1.07 (p=0.002)

audits.t: Hypertension as a reason for cancellation of elective surgical cases on day of surgery: A five year audit report from The Aga Khan University Hospital Karachi.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 2903 (6.8%) of scheduled cases cancelled; hypertension the primary reason in 11 (0.37%) cases

audits.t: Vancomycin: Audit of American guideline-based intermittent dose administration with focus on overweight patients.
audits.st: American guideline-based vancomycin intermittent dosing recommendations
audits.f: 38.3% of patients commenced on guideline-adherent vancomycin doses; 28.3% of overweight patients received an adherent first dose vs 51.1% of non-overweight patients (difference 23%, 95% CI 4-41%, p=0.024); overweight patients more frequently underdosed (p=0.039), with longer hospital stay, higher mortality and more treatment failures

audits.t: Transparency about internal audit results to reduce the supervisory burden: A qualitative study on the preconditions of sharing audit results.
audits.tp: Sharing internal audit results with external supervisors
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Interviewees favoured sharing internal audit results with external supervisors to reduce administrative burden

audits.t: A standardized approach to bereavement risk-screening: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: Project target of 80% outreach to at-risk individuals
audits.f: Social workers screened 100% (52/52) of identified bereaved family members; 28/52 (54%) identified 'at-risk'
audits.c: Standardized Bereavement Risk-Screening Tool (BRST) piloted via PDSA approach, with referral and follow-up process
audits.r2: 89% of at-risk individuals received a telephone outreach attempt, surpassing the 80% project target

audits.t: Addition of Efficiency Measures to Current Accuracy Measures in the Vascular Laboratory Can Be Used for Future Accreditation and Payment Models.
audits.tp: Vascular laboratory efficiency measures for accreditation
audits.st: MACRA/Intersocietal Accreditation Commission improvement activity requirements
audits.f: Time to interpretation (TI) mean 3.3 hr; TI 5.0 hr on weekdays at baseline
audits.c: Process improvement strategy reviewing time to interpretation, study time, wait time, technologist productivity, critical results reporting
audits.r2: TI improved from 5.0 to 2.1 hr on weekdays (longer on weekends, 4.9 hr); wait time and critical results reporting remained steady

audits.t: A multidisciplinary quality improvement effort to reduce bronchopulmonary dysplasia incidence.
audits.st: Internal best-practice guidelines for oxygen management and noninvasive ventilation to reduce BPD
audits.f: Severe BPD rate 57% at baseline
audits.c: PDSA-tested protocols leading to a large-scale '0.21 by 28' oxygen-management campaign in 2014, reinvigorated at end of 2017
audits.r2: Severe BPD decreased from 57% to 29% after 2014 campaign; after 2017 reinvigoration, 'any BPD' rate fell to 41% and severe BPD to 21%

audits.t: Enhancing Pain Assessment in Pediatric Sickle Cell Disease by Applying Quality Improvement Science.
audits.tp: Standardized pain-related functional ability assessment in sickle cell disease
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Standardized assessment of pain-related functional ability not integrated into standard clinical care at baseline
audits.c: PDSA cycles integrating standardized self-report functional ability assessment into inpatient psychology visits, with project target of 85%
audits.r2: Routine standardized assessment increased to an average of 93% over 12 months

audits.t: Avoiding NICU Transfers for Newborns With Neonatal Opioid Withdrawal Syndrome (NOWS): A Quality Improvement Initiative to Manage NOWS on the Mother-baby Unit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Transfer to NICU for NOWS management was 71.4% before the QI project
audits.c: Multidisciplinary task force emphasising nonpharmacologic and dyad-centred care, standardised pharmacologic management, then transition to a functional assessment tool and as-needed morphine administration on the postpartum floor
audits.r2: NICU transfer rate dropped to 5.6% (P not reported)

audits.t: Improving preoperative haemoglobin using a quality improvement approach to treat iron deficiency anaemia.
audits.tp: Preoperative anaemia optimisation before elective surgery
audits.st: NICE recommendation to optimise preoperative haemoglobin before elective surgery
audits.f: Severe preoperative anaemia (Hb<100 g/L) in 10%; overall preoperative anaemia (Hb<130 g/L) in 57.9%; blood transfusion rate 16%
audits.c: Early diagnosis of iron deficiency at preoperative assessment clinic attendance, a new clinical guideline for treating preoperative anaemia, and a one-stop clinic for same-day intravenous iron treatment, delivered through three quality improvement cycles.
audits.r2: Severe preoperative anaemia fell to 1.6%; overall preoperative anaemia fell to 43.9%; blood transfusion rate fell to 6.5% (63% reduction in units transfused); no patient with preoperative anaemia required postoperative transfusion in 2018

audits.t: An audit of nitrofurantoin use in three Australian hospitals.
audits.st: International/Australian guidelines recommending nitrofurantoin as first-line treatment for uncomplicated UTIs
audits.f: 151 prescriptions; 68% (103/151) for UTI treatment vs 32% (48/151) for UTI prophylaxis; treatment duration consistent with guidelines but dosage/frequency often incorrect for formulation and not adjusted for renal function

audits.t: A Pilot Quality Improvement Project to Reduce Preoperative Fasting Duration in Pediatric Inpatients.
audits.st: ASA preoperative fasting guidelines (clear liquids up to 2 hours before anaesthesia); project aim to reduce fasting duration by 25% within 1 year
audits.f: Average fasting duration 12.5 hours with NPO-at-midnight order
audits.c: Creation of a standardised preanaesthesia clear liquid diet order integrated into the EMR to replace the NPO-at-midnight order, plus provider and nursing education
audits.r2: Average fasting duration reduced to 5.7 hours (p<0.001); average adoption rate 17.6% of eligible inpatients; no significant change in aspiration rate (11/13,341 vs 14/14,810 cases, p=0.842)

audits.t: Prospective audit of complications after ultrasonography-guided percutaneous nephrostomy for upper urinary tract obstruction using modified Clavien classification system.
audits.st: Modified Clavien classification system; thresholds set by the American College of Radiology and Society of Interventional Radiology
audits.f: Grade I complications 16.84%, Grade II 10.0%, Grade IIIa 9.2%, Grade IIIb 1.1%, Grade IVa 2.2%, no Grade IVb/V; PCN successful in 356 renal units

audits.t: Checklist for Head Injury Management Evaluation Study (CHIMES): a quality improvement initiative to reduce imaging utilisation for head injuries in the emergency department.
audits.tp: CT scan utilisation for minor head injury
audits.st: Choosing Wisely Canada campaign and the Canadian CT Head Rule (CCTHR); aim to reduce CT scan rate by 10% over 6 months
audits.f: 49.2% of patients underwent a CT scan of the head; audit of 200 charts found 79% of CT scans were not indicated by the CCTHR; mean weekly baseline CT rate 48.1%
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles: education on CWC/CCTHR recommendations, introduction of the CHIMES flow-chart checklist at triage/registration, a CWC-themed patient handout, and bi-monthly feedback of CT rates to providers
audits.r2: 13.9% relative reduction in CT rate at 3 months and a sustained 8.0% reduction at 16 months (48.1% vs 44.3%, p<0.05); ED length of stay fell by 1.5 minutes (p=0.74); 72-hour return visits unchanged (4.4% vs 4.6%, p=0.68); 33.3% of audited charts had the checklist added, of which 84.0% were completed

audits.t: Surgical preference regarding different materials for custom-made allograft cranioplasty in patients with calvarial defects: Results from an internal audit covering the last 20 years.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Reoperation rate 6.5% vs 28%, osseointegration 69% vs 24%, satisfaction 66% vs 44% for PHA (Group A) vs PMMA (Group B) cranioplasty

audits.t: Quality improvement model (IHI) as a strategy to implement a sepsis protocol in a public hospital in Brazil.
audits.st: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 3-hour care bundle (blood cultures, lactate, antibiotics, fluids); local target case fatality rate ≤25%
audits.f: Case fatality rate highly variable, 15%-35%; general 3-hour bundle compliance about 30%-40%; time to antibiotics and fluids 60-120 minutes
audits.c: IHI Model for Improvement using PDSA cycles across ICU, wards, obstetric and emergency units: a 'suspected sepsis stamp', priority lab stamp, nurse sepsis training, a sepsis standard order set, revised colour-coded vital sign forms, sepsis champions, a patient education video and a communication plan
audits.r2: Case fatality rate stabilised at about 15.9%, below the 25% target; overall 3-hour bundle compliance about 38.94%; average time to antibiotics 39 min 19s, to fluid administration 1h20min, to blood cultures 46 min

audits.t: Measuring vital signs in children with fever at the emergency department: an observational study on adherence to the NICE recommendations in Europe.
audits.tp: Vital signs measurement adherence in febrile children (NICE)
audits.st: NICE guideline for fever in under-fives: routine measurement of temperature, heart rate, capillary refill and respiratory rate
audits.f: Temperature measured 97%, capillary refill 86%, heart rate 73%, saturation 56%, respiratory rate 51%; complete 4-sign NICE measurement in 48% of under-fives

audits.t: Improving Access to Psychological Therapies for older adults: auditing management of newly diagnosed mild and moderate depression in six general practices within the Birmingham and Solihull CCG.
audits.tp: Depression management adherence to NICE guidelines
audits.st: NICE guidelines for management of depression in adults: psychological therapies first-line, alongside or before pharmacological treatment
audits.f: Psychological therapies discussed at 63.2% of diagnostic appointments overall; 70.8% for ages 18-29 falling to 56.3% for ages >=65; pharmacological management discussed at 89.9% of appointments across all ages
audits.c: Feedback of audit results and professional reminders to GPs, implemented through the 2019-2020 QOF year

audits.t: Guideline adherence in the management of head injury in Australian children: A population-based sample survey.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence in paediatric head injury care
audits.st: 38 indicators derived from national and international head injury guidelines, developed via a modified RAND-UCLA method (CareTrack Kids study)
audits.f: Overall adherence to guideline-based recommended practice 78.3% (95% CI 75.1-81.2) for head injury; avoidance of nasotracheal airways 100%, nasogastric tubes 99.7%; documentation of past history (e.g. seizures) adhered to in only 29.9% (95% CI 24.5-35.7); CT scan decision indicators had insufficient data to report

audits.t: An innovative quality improvement approach for rapid improvement of infection prevention and control at health facilities in Sierra Leone.
audits.tp: Infection prevention and control compliance improvement
audits.st: National Infection and Prevention Control (IPC) Policy and Guidelines (2015); 37-item compliance checklist
audits.f: Aggregate compliance for 37 indicators 67%; PPE compliance 85%; waste disposal 63%; environmental cleanliness 51%
audits.c: Rapid Improvement Model QI initiative over 6-month compressed timeframe: collaborative targets, QI training, weekly coaching, monthly learning sessions, 'harvest package' of best tools
audits.r2: Aggregate compliance increased to 96%; PPE improved to 89%; waste disposal to 99%; environmental cleanliness to 99%

audits.t: Quality improvement programme reduces errors in oral medication preparation and administration through feeding tubes.
audits.tp: Medication preparation and administration errors via feeding tubes
audits.st: Good practice guidance for oral medication preparation/administration through feeding tubes
audits.f: Crushing enteric-coated tablets/mixing drugs 54.9%; triturating modified-action/dragee forms 32.8%; crushing to fine homogeneous powder 7.4%; feeding tube obstruction 41.8%
audits.c: Good practice guidance developed/implemented, formal nurse training, printed do-not-crush medication list and prescriber alternatives table, PDSA-based multidisciplinary feedback
audits.r2: Crushing enteric-coated tablets/mixing drugs decreased to 26.2% (p<0.001); triturating modified-action forms decreased to 19.7% (p<0.001); but crushing to fine powder worsened to 95% (p<0.001) and feeding tube obstruction worsened to 52.5% (p=0.095)

audits.t: Are radiation oncologists following guidelines? An audit of practice in patients with uncomplicated bone metastases.
audits.tp: Single-fraction radiotherapy use for bone metastases
audits.st: Best-practice guideline recommending single-fraction radiotherapy (SFRT) over multi-fraction (MFRT) for uncomplicated symptomatic bone metastases
audits.f: 85.4% of courses delivered as single fraction of 8 Gy; younger age (<70) and breast histology associated with more MFRT use (p=0.04; p=0.0046)

audits.t: Completeness and accuracy of data in spine registries: an independent audit-based study.
audits.tp: Spine registry data completeness and accuracy
audits.st: German Spine Society (DWG) registry documentation requirements
audits.f: Of 17 centres, 4 had no data entries; among 13 audited centres, 28.50% (95% CI 22.46-34.55) of entries finalized only after audit announcement, 82.55% (95% CI 79.12-85.98) of surgeries documented, 14.95% (95% CI 10.93-19.00) of entries inaccurate (range 6.21-27.44% between centres)

audits.t: Prescription Pattern of Drugs Used for Neuropathic Pain and Adherence to NeuPSIG Guidelines in Cancer.
audits.tp: Adherence to NeuPSIG neuropathic pain prescribing guidelines
audits.st: Neuropathic Pain Special Interest Group (NeuPSIG) Guidelines for cancer-related neuropathic pain
audits.f: Only 12 prescriptions completely adhered to NeuPSIG guidelines; 275 partial adherence; 13 poor adherence; pregabalin prescribed in 78.7%, amitriptyline in 67%

audits.t: The impact of real-time clinical alerts on the compliance of anesthesia documentation: A retrospective observational study.
audits.st: Immediate Preoperative Assessment (IPOA) documentation requirement (CMS and Joint Commission standards)
audits.f: Compliance rate of IPOA completion was 76% pre-implementation
audits.c: Real-time clinical alert system (CAS) implemented in August 2018 to flag missing IPOA documentation
audits.r2: Compliance rate of IPOA completion increased to 88% post-implementation (P not reported)

audits.t: A quality improvement approach to reducing hospital readmissions in patients with cancer and heart failure.
audits.st: Local DMAIC quality improvement target: reduce 30-day readmission rate for patients with cancer and heart failure by 10% over 6 months (institutional Heart Success Program had already reduced the rate from 40% to 27%)
audits.f: 38/120 (31.7%) patients with cancer and heart failure were readmitted within 30 days
audits.c: DMAIC quality improvement: revised patient/family education workflow, improved documentation of heart failure diagnosis, staff teaching/job aids, comprehensive discharge planning and post-discharge symptom monitoring
audits.r2: 30-day heart-failure-related readmission fell to 11/133 (8.3%), a reduction of 23.43 percentage points from baseline, exceeding the 10% target

audits.t: Pain assessment and management: An audit of practice at a tertiary hospital.
audits.st: No formal South African guideline existed; audited against general good-practice expectation for regular pain assessment/reassessment
audits.f: Nearly half of patients had no documented pain assessment; Verbal Rating Scale predominant tool; assessments mostly by ward doctor; interventions not evidence-based

audits.t: Does an Orthopedic Ward Round Pro Forma Improve Inpatient Documentation?
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons Ireland and England, and Medical Council guidelines from both countries
audits.f: 0% of notes fulfilled the full criteria selected for pro forma documentation before its introduction
audits.c: Introduction of a ward round pro forma to standardise medical record keeping on patient ward rounds
audits.r2: Initial average 86% of required information captured after introduction; reaudit 2 months later showed a 9% decrease to 75%

audits.t: Improving provider awareness to statin prescribing guidelines: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Statin prescribing guideline adherence in peripheral artery disease
audits.st: Guideline recommending statin therapy for all patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD)
audits.f: Baseline chart review showed only 54.16% of PAD patients were on a statin medication
audits.c: Nurse-practitioner-led PDSA quality improvement project: PDSA cycle 1 implemented a paper evidence-based algorithm tool for 6 weeks; PDSA cycle 2 implemented an electronic pop-up reminder in the EHR for a further 6 weeks
audits.r2: After PDSA cycle 1, average 70.8% of patients were on a statin; after PDSA cycle 2, average 73.3% were on a statin (ANOVA p=0.003 overall; both interventions significantly better than baseline, no significant difference between the two interventions)

audits.t: Addition of CORES to the I-PASS Handoff: A Resident-led Quality Improvement Study.
audits.st: I-PASS handoff bundle; internal target of 90% of handoffs including all 6 I-PASS elements within 6 months
audits.f: Illness severity 13%, diagnosis 62%, patient summary 52%, contingency planning 87%, action list 42%, receiver synthesis 25%; overall compliance 47%
audits.c: PDSA 1: implementation of CORES electronic tool; PDSA 2: resident re-education on I-PASS elements
audits.r2: Illness severity remained 13%; other elements rose to 84%, 82%, 93%, 91%, 37%; overall compliance increased to 67%

audits.t: A 30-day prospective audit of all inpatient complications following acute care surgery: How well do we really perform?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median length of stay 3.3 days; 42% had substantial comorbidities, 15% morbid obesity; 66% of procedures laparoscopic; high postoperative morbidity rate reported

audits.t: ACT-FAST: a quality improvement project to increase the percentage of acute stroke patients receiving intravenous thrombolysis within 60 minutes of arrival at the emergency department.
audits.st: Target of acute ischaemic stroke patients receiving rtPA within 60 minutes of ED arrival
audits.f: 52.3% of eligible stroke patients received rtPA within 60 minutes of arrival; door-to-needle time 59 minutes
audits.c: Standardised acute stroke activation guidelines, screening question at ED registration, prehospital notification of stroke activation, public education, scripting for thrombolysis consent, easy access to equipment
audits.r2: Percentage thrombolysed within 60 minutes increased to 60.6% (p = 0.27); door-to-needle time decreased to 54.5 minutes (p = 0.15); length of stay significantly reduced by 1.5 days

audits.t: Newborn screening timeliness quality improvement initiative: Impact of national recommendations and data repository.
audits.st: ACHDNC goals: time-critical results reported by day 5 of life, non-time-critical by day 7
audits.f: Specimens collected before 48 hours: 95% (IQR 88-97%); time-critical results in 5 days: 49% (IQR 26-74%); non-time-critical results in 7 days: 64% (IQR 58-78%)
audits.c: Multi-year NewSTEPS 360 quality improvement initiative with national recommendations and shared data repository
audits.r2: Specimens collected before 48 hours improved to 97% (IQR 92-98%); time-critical results improved to 64% (IQR 42-71%); non-time-critical improved to 81% (IQR 68-91%); ~41% of specimens transported within 1 day

audits.t: Novel team-based approach to quality improvement effectively engages staff and reduces adverse events in healthcare settings.
audits.tp: Team-based quality improvement to reduce patient safety incidents
audits.st: Five national safety standards
audits.f: Baseline incident rates in comparator (rest of hospital) units used as reference
audits.c: Weekly 35-minute team-based 'map-enabled experiential review' conversations about routine practices relating to five national safety standards, using interactive graphical logic maps, over 10 months.
audits.r2: 34% statistically significant decrease in recorded incident rates relating to patient identification in participating units relative to the rest of the hospital; increased staff awareness and engagement in quality improvement

audits.t: Overcoming non-compliance with clinical trial registration and results reporting: One Institution's approach.
audits.tp: Clinical trial registration and results reporting compliance
audits.st: FDAAA 801 and NIH Final Rule requirements for ClinicalTrials.gov registration/results reporting
audits.f: not reported (baseline compliance issues identified but not numerically stated)
audits.c: Hiring a dedicated ClinicalTrials.gov coordinator, workflow flagging trials at IRB approval, one-on-one consultations, 'Lunch and Learns', new training tools

audits.t: Introduction of Group Electronic Monitoring of Hand Hygiene on Inpatient Units: A Multicenter Cluster Randomized Quality Improvement Study.
audits.st: Hand hygiene adherence standard (monitored via electronic monitoring)
audits.f: Baseline monthly hand hygiene adherence measured prior to intervention (rate not stated numerically)
audits.c: Introduction of group electronic monitoring of hand hygiene with daily reporting to guide unit-led improvement strategies
audits.r2: Significant overall improvement in hand hygiene adherence, incidence rate ratio 1.73 (95% CI 1.47-1.99)

audits.t: Ketamine Sedation and Hypoxia: A Quality Improvement Project to Reduce Respiratory Events Receiving Intervention.
audits.st: Target to reduce respiratory events receiving intervention (REs) during i.v. ketamine sedation from >10% to a lower target
audits.f: REs occurred at 11.4%, higher than nationally reported rates
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team identifying key drivers and interventions, tested via 2 Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycles, monitored with Shewhart P charts
audits.r2: REs decreased from 11.4% to 4.9%, maintained below 6% for 12 months

audits.t: Are genital examinations necessary for STI screening for female sex workers? An audit of decriminalized and regulated sex workers in Melbourne, Australia.
audits.tp: Necessity of genital examination for asymptomatic STI screening
audits.st: Victorian legislation requiring exclusion of sex workers with visible anogenital herpes or warts; routine practice of genital examination
audits.f: 7 asymptomatic FSW (0.21%, 95% CI 0.08-0.42%) diagnosed with visible anogenital herpes and/or warts on examination

audits.t: Potentially Inappropriate Medications in a Psychogeriatric Inpatient Ward: An Audit Based on Beers Criteria.
audits.tp: Potentially inappropriate medications in psychogeriatric inpatients (Beers Criteria)
audits.st: 2015 American Geriatrics Society (AGS) Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medications
audits.f: Mean medications at admission 7.7, at discharge 8.9; of 49 patients with 63 high-risk medications, 16 patients had high-risk medication stopped, 23 had one started, 10 had no change; benzodiazepines changed in 56/120 (47%)

audits.t: Risk-adjusted hospital clinical management issue rates using data from the Victorian Audit of Surgical Mortality.
audits.tp: Preventable surgical mortality clinical management issues
audits.st: Victorian Audit of Surgical Mortality (VASM) process, assessing definitely/probably preventable clinical management issues contributing to death
audits.f: 5 of 60 hospitals (8.3%) deviated significantly from the state-wide preventable clinical management issue rate of 0.00012

audits.t: Oncology Fellow-Led Quality Improvement Project to Improve Rates of Palliative Care Utilization in Patients With Advanced Cancer.
audits.tp: Palliative care referral for advanced cancer
audits.st: ASCO guidelines recommending palliative care referral for patients with advanced or metastatic cancer; local target of 30%
audits.f: Palliative care utilisation was 11.5% (5 of 43 patients)
audits.c: PDSA cycles including focus groups with stakeholders, standardising referral via single order set, identifying a single scheduler with bidirectional communication, disseminating process changes
audits.r2: Palliative care utilisation increased to 48.4% (48 of 99 patients)

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Increase the Opportunity of Play Activities and Reduce the Screen Time Among Children Admitted in Hospital Setting of a Tertiary Care Centre, North India.
audits.tp: Play activity and screen time in hospitalised children
audits.st: Local target to increase play activity time and reduce screen time by 25% over 10 weeks
audits.f: Baseline assessment showed low play activity and high screen time; root cause analysis found problems with procedure and policy
audits.c: Day-to-day play implementation procedure protocol developed and implemented via 3 PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Day-to-day play implementation score and time spent on play activities increased by 50% and 20% respectively; screen time reduced by 73%

audits.t: Medicines reconciliation in primary care: a study evaluating the quality of medication-related information provided on discharge from secondary care.
audits.st: National minimum standards for medication-related information on hospital discharge summaries
audits.f: Compliance was good overall but poor for indication (11.7%), formulation (60.3%) and instructions for ongoing use (72.5%); reason for change documented for 49% (1550/3164) of newly started medicines, 39% (186/477) of dose changes, and 57% (420/738) of stopped medicines; changes not acted on within 7 days for 12.5% of patients

audits.t: Intermediate Dose Prophylaxis in Adults with Haemophilia: A Clinical Audit from a Resource Limited Setting.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean bleed rate 5.13 episodic vs 0.63 prophylactic (p=0.01); work days lost 30.63 vs 0; hospital visits 20.63 vs 0
audits.c: Short-term intermediate dose prophylaxis with recombinant factor VIII (23 IU/kg twice weekly for 2 months) replacing episodic treatment
audits.r2: Clinical audit at 4 months confirmed intermediate dose prophylaxis reduced bleed frequency; median trough level 2.50% (range 1-5%)

audits.t: Apneic Oxygenation for Emergency Intubations in the Pediatric Emergency Department-A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Apneic oxygenation during rapid sequence intubation
audits.st: Evidence-based practice of apneic oxygenation during rapid sequence intubation (RSI) as a routine standard of care to prevent desaturation
audits.f: Apneic oxygenation was not performed in any of the 22 RSIs
audits.c: Care bundle developed via simulation-based PDSA cycles: pre-intubation checklist, additional oxygen source and reminders in resuscitation bays, incorporation into airway doctor/nurse roles ('copiloting'), education/simulation training, and enhanced documentation
audits.r2: Apneic oxygenation performed in 17/25 (68%) RSIs; no significant difference between emergency physicians and paediatric anaesthetists (both median 100%, p=0.28); no desaturation documented with apneic oxygenation use

audits.t: Improving Disposition Decision-Making for Pediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.tp: PICU admission disposition for diabetic ketoacidosis
audits.st: Institutional criteria for PICU admission of children with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)
audits.f: Potentially avoidable PICU stays 4.1% of DKA admissions; total PICU admissions for DKA 19.1%
audits.c: EHR dot-phrase prepopulated with institutional PICU admission criteria and reference note for providers; EHR-based data report to monitor disposition and dot-phrase use
audits.r2: Dot-phrase use averaged 33.4%; potentially avoidable PICU stays decreased to 0.5%; total PICU admissions for DKA decreased to 8.4%; ward-to-PICU transfers declined from 0.8% to 0%

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Intervention Bundle to Reduce 30-Day Pediatric Readmissions.
audits.st: Internal QI target to reduce 30-day pediatric readmission rate
audits.f: Pre-implementation readmission rate 10.3%
audits.c: Bundle: pre-discharge planning with transition coordinator, SDH screening/intervention, post-discharge medication reconciliation, PCP communication, transition clinic access, 24-hour telephone line, implemented sequentially October 2013 to February 2017
audits.r2: Readmission rate declined to 7.4% and remained stable; 48% of 1394 families screened for SDH received assistance with >=1 concern; length of stay increased from 4.10 to 4.30 days

audits.t: Decreasing Usage of Lights and Sirens in an Urban Environment: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Lights and sirens use in interfacility transport
audits.st: Industry standards for lights and sirens use in EMS transport (internal policy revised against these)
audits.f: Lights and sirens use 76% en route and 73% on return, exceeding industry standards
audits.c: Revised internal policy (2012); use-justification process (2012); accountability measures requiring justification (2014); ongoing evaluation, education, data gathering
audits.r2: Return-trip use decreased to 53% by 2013, then to 14% en route and 13% on return by 2015; sustained at or below 20% for following 3 years

audits.t: Improving the Compliance of Intraoperative Antibiotic Redosing: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Infectious Disease Society of America recommendations for intraoperative antibiotic redosing timing; national SSI benchmark 1.87%
audits.f: Intraoperative antibiotic redosing compliance 11%; organisational SSI rate 3.19%, above national benchmark of 1.87%
audits.c: New organisational redosing guidelines, antibiotic-specific EMR reminder alert, education for anaesthesiologists/surgeons/circulating nurses, monthly data evaluation
audits.r2: Redosing compliance reached and sustained an average of 99%; SSI rate decreased from 3.19% (2014) to 2.3% (2018)

audits.t: Awareness and compliance to anti-smoking law in South Bengaluru, India.
audits.tp: Compliance with anti-smoking law (COTPA) in public places
audits.st: Indian Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA) 2003, Section 4
audits.f: Complete compliance 1.9%, partial compliance 28.1%; smoking observed in 3.9%, visible ashtrays 6%, cigarette butts 13%; only 19% of places requiring designated smoking areas complied

audits.t: Assessing the Effect of Unit Champion-Initiated Audits on Fall Rates: Improving Awareness.
audits.st: National benchmark for inpatient fall rates
audits.f: Fall rates were consistently above the national benchmark; pre-implementation fall rate 3.75
audits.c: Fall Champion Audits (FCAs) conducted by unit fall champions assessing fall risk, interventions, and barriers, alongside a division-wide fall program
audits.r2: Postimplementation fall rate decreased significantly to 1.62

audits.t: Quality improvement strategy to enhance compliance with the World Health Organization Surgical Safety Checklist in a large hospital: Quality improvement study.
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist, target 100% use of performed surgeries
audits.f: Time out compliance began at 26%
audits.c: PDSA-based QI strategy: checklist adapted to local context, surgeon engagement discussions, nursing team training and empowerment
audits.r2: Mean overall checklist compliance reached 89%; time out compliance increased, varying from 60% to 90%

audits.t: Rapid implementation of virtual clinics due to COVID-19: report and early evaluation of a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Local target: reduce face-to-face consultations to 20% of outpatient attendances (80% delivered virtually) during the COVID-19 pandemic
audits.f: On average 7% of consultations were delivered virtually via telephone before the initiative
audits.c: Rapid implementation of virtual (telephone/video) clinics by a multidisciplinary COVID-19 Action Team using the Institute for Healthcare Improvement Plan-Do-Study-Act approach, including process redesign and delivery support.
audits.r2: 87% of consultations delivered virtually against an 80% target; patient satisfaction 90/100, clinician satisfaction 78/100

audits.t: Compliance to prescribing guidelines among public health care facilities in Namibia; findings and implications.
audits.tp: Prescribing compliance with national standard treatment guidelines
audits.st: Namibian National Standard Treatment Guidelines
audits.f: 73% of prescriptions complied with the guidelines; 69% had an antibiotic; 64% of 3759 medicines prescribed generically (mean 3.0+/-1.1 per prescription); 94.6% of prescribers were aware of and had access to the guidelines

audits.t: Effect on thromboprophylaxis among hospitalized patients using a system-wide multifaceted quality improvement intervention: Rationale and design for a multicenter cluster randomized clinical trial in China.
audits.tp: Multifaceted QI intervention for VTE thromboprophylaxis (trial protocol)
audits.st: Guideline-recommended in-hospital VTE thromboprophylaxis (dynamic VTE/bleeding risk assessment)
audits.f: not reported (protocol/design paper, results not yet available)
audits.c: System-wide multifaceted QI: electronic alert/CDS, risk-based prophylaxis, periodical audit and interactive feedback, strengthened training/education

audits.t: Improved treatment of community-acquired pneumonia through tailored interventions: Results from a controlled, multicentre quality improvement project.
audits.st: CAP care bundle: chest X-ray, CURB-65 severity score, lower respiratory tract sample and antibiotics all completed within 8 hours of admission
audits.f: Full care bundle completed within 8 hours in 7.1%-11% of cases at baseline; CURB-65 documented in 31.2% (26.9% within 8h); lower respiratory tract samples collected in 60.6% (39.6% within 8h); chest X-ray within 8h 88.7%; antibiotics within 8h 75.1%
audits.c: Tailored technical (hands-on tracheal suction/sputum induction training) and non-technical interventions (repeated education, personal feedback, standard educational material, authorising nurses to order X-rays/samples, combined microbiology sampling, CURB-65 EHR tool, CAP order sets) at three intervention sites via PDSA cycles, March-October 2018
audits.r2: Care bundle completion rose from 11% at baseline to 41% at follow-up at intervention sites (control site remained below 3%); CURB-65 documentation rose from 34% to 68%; lower respiratory tract sample collection rose from 43% to 63%

audits.t: Expansion of a multi-pronged safe sleep quality improvement initiative to three children's hospital campuses.
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics ABCs of safe sleep (infant Alone, on Back, in a Clear Crib); local goal of ≥25% ABC compliance post-intervention
audits.f: ABC compliance 4.4% (95% CI 2.0-8.2%); safe sleep position/location 78.4%; safe sleep environment only 5.9%
audits.c: Multi-pronged QI initiative: nursing education, nurse safe-sleep champions, crib cards with an ABC checklist, regular crib audits, and weekly tracking boards reporting unit compliance
audits.r2: ABC compliance improved to 32.5% (95% CI 27.2-38.2%, p<0.01), exceeding the 25% goal at all three campuses; safe sleep environment improved to 39.8% (p<0.01); sleep position/location unchanged (76.6%, p=0.64)

audits.t: Epidemiology and clinical features of emergency department patients with suspected COVID-19: Results from the first month of the COVID-19 Emergency Department Quality Improvement Project (COVED-2).
audits.tp: COVID-19 emergency department screening and monitoring
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 702 of 3453 ED patients (20%, 95% CI 19-22) tested for SARS-CoV-2, with significant increase during study period (IRR 1.019, 95% CI 1.017-1.021)

audits.t: Factors associated with utilisation of health care interpreting services and the impact on length of stay and cost: A retrospective cohort analysis of audit data.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Interpreting services used at least once for 54.4% (43) of admissions; females more likely to receive interpreter (65.1% vs 47.1%, P=.04)

audits.t: Nurse-Led Vital Signs Monitoring Can Safely Identify Low-Risk Hematology-Oncology Patients For De-Escalation.
audits.tp: Vital signs monitoring de-escalation in hematology-oncology
audits.st: Local protocol target for safe de-escalation of vital signs monitoring frequency in low-risk patients
audits.f: Routine practice was vital signs monitoring every 4 hours; root causes for frequent VSM identified (perception of VSM, lack of concise guidelines, lack of nurse empowerment)
audits.c: Consensus criteria to define suitable low-risk patients and a nurse-led VSM de-escalation protocol
audits.r2: 50% reduction in mean number of nurse encounters per month among the 1,065 patients undergoing nurse-led VSM de-escalation, without adverse outcomes

audits.t: Inpatient prescribing of dual antiplatelet therapy according to the guidelines: a prospective intervention study.
audits.st: Cardiology, neurology and vascular surgery guidelines on recommended duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), 3 weeks to 30 months depending on indication
audits.f: 21/411 (5.1%) had DAPT treatment deviating from guidelines; 11/411 (2.7%) deviations were unintended and erroneous; DAPT before admission was a major risk factor for erroneous deviation (OR 18.7, 95% CI 4.79-72.7), with 8/58 (13.8%) erroneous among those on DAPT before admission versus 3/353 (0.8%) started during admission
audits.c: Pharmacist review of all inpatients on DAPT, contacting the prescriber by phone with advice to adjust therapy to the guideline whenever an unintended deviation was found; this was a real-time correction within the same audit period rather than a separate re-audit cycle

audits.t: Evaluating standards of care in psoriatic arthritis of the QUANTUM project (qualitative initiative to improve outcomes): results of an accreditation project in Spain.
audits.tp: Compliance with psoriatic arthritis care standards (QUANTUM accreditation)
audits.st: QUANTUM project quality standards for psoriatic arthritis care (shortening diagnosis time, disease management, multidisciplinary collaboration, patient monitoring)
audits.f: Overall 64.1% of quality standards met; disease management 72%, multidisciplinary collaboration 63.9%; quality of life assessment 9.8%, locomotor system assessment 12.2%, physical exam data record 14.6%, periodic cardiovascular risk assessment 17.1%; accessibility to treatments 100%, diagnostic equipment availability 97.6%

audits.t: Suboptimal care for chronic pancreatitis patients revealed by moderate to low adherence to the United European Gastroenterology evidence-based guidelines (HaPanEU): A Netherlands nationwide analysis.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence in chronic pancreatitis management (HaPanEU)
audits.st: United European Gastroenterology evidence-based guidelines for chronic pancreatitis (HaPanEU 2016), 39 quality indicators
audits.f: Mean 26 relevant quality indicators per patient applicable, average adherence rate 53%; 45% of patients had guideline adherence <50%

audits.t: Translating research into clinical practice: quality improvement to halve non-adherence to methotrexate.
audits.st: Local target: halve self-reported non-adherence to methotrexate
audits.f: Self-reported non-adherence to methotrexate 24.7%; consistency of key staff messages 64% (September 2016); biochemical non-adherence 56% (September 2016); remission rate at 6 months post-MTX initiation 13% (2014/15)
audits.c: Motivational interviewing training for staff, consistent information messaging about methotrexate, and development of a summary bookmark, monitored over 2.5 years.
audits.r2: Self-reported non-adherence reduced to an average of 7.4%; consistency of messages improved to 94% (January 2018); biochemical non-adherence reduced to 17% (June 2019); remission rate at 6 months improved to 37% (2017/18); estimated cost savings of GBP 30,000 per year

audits.t: Adherence to prescription-writing guidelines for outpatients in Southern Gauteng district hospitals.
audits.st: Legal/professional regulations for prescription writing (essential elements, generic names, abbreviations/decimals, legibility)
audits.f: Essential elements: patient identifiers 44%, prescriber identifiers 77%, regimen 99%, date 99%; legibility 90%; generic names 39%; recommended abbreviations/decimals 35%; global accuracy score 80-100% achieved by only 38%

audits.t: Oral Care with Mother's Own Milk in Sick and Preterm Neonates: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Oral care with mother's own milk in preterm/sick neonates
audits.st: Local target to increase oral care with mother's own milk (OC-MOM) from 5.9% baseline to 80%
audits.f: Baseline proportion of neonates receiving OC-MOM was 5.9%; MAT score '0' baseline was 24.4%
audits.c: OC-MOM protocol designed and implemented via 4 Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycles using POCQI model, with customised Mouth Assessment Tool (MAT)
audits.r2: Proportion receiving OC-MOM increased to 83.3%; proportion with MAT score '0' improved to 94.4%

audits.t: An audit of the measurement and reporting of male testosterone levels in UK clinical biochemistry laboratories.
audits.tp: Testosterone measurement and reporting practice in clinical biochemistry laboratories
audits.st: Published guidance documents for diagnosis and management of hypogonadism, including standardised pre/post-analytical testosterone testing protocols
audits.f: 74/96 labs communicated optimal sampling time; 81/96 used immunoassays; wide variability in reference range limits (50% from manufacturers, 18.8% historical); 64/96 used action limits but 63/96 did not report a borderline range as guidance suggests; interpretative comments provided by 67/96 labs but none referenced management guidelines; UK NEQAS data showed considerable variation in assay performance

audits.t: Urinary tract stone deaths: data from the Australian and New Zealand Audits of Surgical Mortality.
audits.tp: Urinary tract stone surgery mortality clinical management issues
audits.st: Australian and New Zealand Audit of Surgical Mortality (ANZASM) peer review process
audits.f: 100 (9.7%) of 1034 urological deaths related to stones; 39% (37/95) of stone deaths associated with clinical management issues (CMIs), vs 26% for general urology/all surgery

audits.t: Implementation of a Clinical Decision Laboratory Ordering Algorithm for Preeclampsia: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Institutional protocol for preeclampsia laboratory investigations (updated to evidence-based algorithm)
audits.f: 2923 tests ordered monthly at a cost of CAD$18,306; most providers ordered broad panels and were unaware of associated costs
audits.c: Multidisciplinary-developed laboratory ordering algorithm for preeclampsia investigations, posted on wards, with pocket aides and educational seminars, implemented via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: 39.9% reduction in costs related to blood tests (savings of CAD$7304/month); performance of essential investigations (e.g. creatinine) unchanged as control measure

audits.t: Auditing the Routine Microbiological Examination of Pus Swabs From Uncomplicated Perianal Abscesses: Clinical Necessity or Old Habit?
audits.tp: Microbiological pus swab practice for perianal abscess
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Pus swabs sent in 66.7% of cases; only a third of microbiology reports were reviewed by the surgical team; all patients were discharged before results were released with no subsequent change in management; no consistent association found between microbiology results and re-admission with perianal abscess or fistula-in-ano

audits.t: Implementing a Process to Systematically Identify and Address Poor Medication Adherence in Pediatric Liver Transplant Recipients.
audits.tp: Medication adherence screening in paediatric liver transplant recipients
audits.st: Internal QI process to systematically screen for and address poor medication adherence
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Multiple PDSA cycles developing a system to screen for adherence risk, identify barriers, and partner with patients/families to address them
audits.r2: System implemented with high reliability (>90% of patients received the bundle of interventions); most common barriers were 'forgetting' (patients/caregivers), activity interference, and difficulty swallowing pills

audits.t: Designing a Process for Cardiology Patient Transfers: A Quality Improvement, Descriptive Study on Interprovider Communication and Resident Education.
audits.st: Internal QI target: increase resident-reported comfort at handoff (no fixed percentage target stated)
audits.f: 15% of residents reported feeling 'always'/'very often' prepared; 23% had concerns about floor appropriateness
audits.c: Failure Mode Effect Analysis and key driver diagram leading to a transfer checklist and algorithm, inter-team huddle, and education on the transfer process
audits.r2: Residents reporting preparedness increased to 83%; concerns about floor appropriateness decreased to 4%

audits.t: Improving Concussion Management by Including Driving Recommendations for Adolescents with Concussions: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Internal QI target: 75% of adolescents with concussion receive driving recommendations
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: EHR 'smart phrase' reminding providers to give driving recommendations during concussion visits (August 2017-August 2018)
audits.r2: Achieved 75% target by second month, sustained through the year except one month (December); 43% of evaluated concussion patients met inclusion criteria, 48% of those were driving before injury

audits.t: Auditing RadExam: Employing Psychometrics to Improve Exam Quality.
audits.st: Psychometric validity standards for exam questions (question p value, Discrimination Index)
audits.f: Audit 1 identified 617 questions with poor Discrimination Index performance
audits.c: RadExam subspecialty editors evaluated and modified/removed/replaced poorly performing questions identified by audit
audits.r2: Significant decrease in number of flagged questions and improved overall exam performance in Audit 2

audits.t: Multicentre study found that adherence to national antibiotic recommendations for neonatal early-onset sepsis was low.
audits.tp: Adherence to neonatal early-onset sepsis antibiotic guidelines
audits.st: Dutch neonatal early-onset sepsis (EOS) guidelines (adapted from UK guidance)
audits.f: Antibiotics recommended for 438/1024 (42.8%) at-risk neonates, but only 186/438 (42.5%) received them; withholding recommended for 586/1024 (57.2%), adhered to in 570/586 (97.3%); antibiotics continued >3 days in 56/178 (31.5%) despite negative blood culture

audits.t: National approaches to trichiasis surgical follow-up, outcome assessment and surgeon audit in trachoma-endemic countries in Africa.
audits.tp: National policy for trichiasis surgical follow-up and surgeon audit
audits.st: WHO recommendation for regular follow-up, outcome assessment and audit of trichiasis surgeons
audits.f: Only 4/27 countries had a national policy for surgical follow-up/outcome assessment; only 2/27 had a national policy for surgeon audit; only 9/27 had a cut-off for poorly performing surgeons

audits.t: Multidisciplinary, patient-centred approach to improving compliance with venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis in a district general hospital.
audits.tp: VTE prophylaxis compliance in medical inpatients
audits.st: NICE guidance on prevention of VTE in hospitalised patients; local target of over 85% compliance with VTE prophylaxis prescription within 3 months
audits.f: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours of admission 51% compliance; dose adjustment for patient weight 69% compliance; dose adjustment for renal function 80% compliance
audits.c: Multidisciplinary quality improvement team introduced a 'VTE sticker' to prompt risk assessment, educational material for medical staff and allied health professionals, and patient information leaflets, over three quality improvement cycles.
audits.r2: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours improved to 94% compliance; dose adjustment for weight improved to 100%; dose adjustment for renal function improved to 100%; results were replicated in a different clinical environment

audits.t: A quality improvement programme to reduce hospital-acquired pressure injuries.
audits.st: Internal QI target: reduce HAPIs by 60% within 2 years, using IHI evidence-based practices (SSKIN bundle)
audits.f: HAPI incidence 6.1/1000 patient-days; prevalence 9.7/100 patients surveyed
audits.c: SSKIN bundle (Surface, Skin inspection, Keep moving, Incontinence, Nutrition), turning clocks, PI 'calendars', attention to endotracheal tube ties, tested via PDSA with IHI collaboration
audits.r2: HAPI incidence dropped to 1.1/1000 patient-days (83.5% reduction); prevalence fell to 2.0/100 patients surveyed (73.4% decline)

audits.t: A Descriptive Study on Sepsis: Causes, Outcomes, and Adherence to Guidelines on Patients with Sepsis at a Tertiary Care Hospital in Sri Lanka.
audits.tp: Adherence to Surviving Sepsis Campaign hour-1 bundle
audits.st: Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) hour-1 bundle, International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2018
audits.f: Bundle compliance: IV fluids 10.9%, blood cultures before antibiotics 58.1%, first-dose antibiotic within 1 hour 3.9%, arterial blood gas 15.5%; mortality rate 9.6%

audits.t: Evaluation of a Patient-Collected Audio Audit and Feedback Quality Improvement Program on Clinician Attention to Patient Life Context and Health Care Costs in the Veterans Affairs Health Care System.
audits.tp: Clinician attention to patient contextual factors (audio audit and feedback)
audits.st: Content Coding for Contextualization of Care (4C) method standard for addressing patient contextual 'red flags'
audits.f: At baseline, clinicians addressed 413/618 contextual factors in care plans (67%)
audits.c: Audio audit and feedback QI programme: clinicians received feedback (standard or enhanced intensity) on attention to patient contextual factors, stepped wedge design
audits.r2: Contextual factors addressed increased to 1707/2367 (72%), OR 1.3 (95% CI 1.1-1.6, p=0.01); associated with greater likelihood of improved outcomes (adjusted OR 2.5, 95% CI 1.5-4.1) and cost savings

audits.t: Increasing Assessment, Diagnosis, and Intervention of Overweight and Obesity Among College Students: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Overweight and obesity screening in college students
audits.st: Evidence-based practice recommendations for screening/diagnosis/intervention of overweight and obesity
audits.f: Baseline manual EHR audit of 241 records; assessment, diagnosis and intervention rates before education not numerically stated
audits.c: Two educational seminars to increase provider awareness of evidence-based practice recommendations and available resources
audits.r2: Assessment, diagnosis and intervention of overweight/obesity all significantly increased (p=.00) following provider education

audits.t: Reducing opioid utilization after appendectomy: A lesson in implementation of a multidisciplinary quality improvement project.
audits.st: Internal QI targets: three measures (ice packs, pain scores, standardised order set) to minimise opioid use post-appendectomy
audits.f: not reported (baseline opioid utilisation, no specific percentage given)
audits.c: Three measures: ice packs to incision in PACU, standard pain scores within 30 minutes of ward admission, standardised postoperative order set minimising opioids with limited discharge prescriptions
audits.r2: Compliance: ice packs 66.9%, pain scores 88%, postoperative order set 94.7%; statistically significant decreases in IV/enteral opioids administered, discharge opioid doses, and patients discharged with an opioid prescription

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Project to Standardize Surfactant Delivery in the Era of Noninvasive Ventilation.
audits.tp: Standardising surfactant delivery timing in noninvasive ventilation
audits.st: Internal standard criteria for timely intubation and surfactant administration (within 1 hour of intubation) for premature infants
audits.f: Mean time to intubation for infants 28-32 weeks gestation was 321 minutes; surfactant given within 1 hour of intubation in 78% of cases
audits.c: Literature review and education for physicians, free-text orders for notification, trainee program, coordination with radiology
audits.r2: Mean time to intubation for 28-32 week infants decreased to 81 minutes (no change for infants <28 weeks); surfactant given within 1 hour of intubation improved to 100%

audits.t: Vaccinating in the Emergency Department, a Novel Approach to Improve Influenza Vaccination Rates via a Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Influenza vaccination in the emergency department
audits.st: AAP/CDC recommendation for universal annual influenza vaccination from 6 months of age; local project goal to increase ED-administered vaccines from 75 to 1000 in one season
audits.f: Only 75 influenza vaccinations given in the ED; 0% of patients screened for vaccine status
audits.c: Mandatory EHR vaccine screening, a nurse-driven vaccine administration protocol with clinical decision support/best practice advisories, provider/nurse/family education, a revised pharmacy workflow to reduce wastage, and weekly staff feedback, tested via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Screening improved from 0% to 90%; 1,323 vaccines administered (1,167 via the protocol, 8.5% of eligible patients), exceeding the goal of 1,000; no significant increase in ED length of stay (139 min); about $22,500 net revenue to the hospital

audits.t: The Road to Transfusion-free Craniosynostosis Repair in Children Less Than 24 Months Old: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Perioperative blood transfusion in craniosynostosis repair
audits.st: Local goal of transfusion-free craniosynostosis repair, informed by multimodal blood management literature (Pediatric Craniofacial Collaborative Group benchmark of 95% transfusion rate)
audits.f: Total allogeneic transfusion rate 100% in 2013
audits.c: Sequential PDCA cycles 2014-2016: a perioperative temperature-management protocol, a postoperative transfusion protocol (transfuse only if haemoglobin <7 g/dL), intraoperative tranexamic acid (12.5 mg/kg bolus), preincisional 0.25% lidocaine with epinephrine injection, a dedicated core anaesthesia team, and intraoperative cell salvage
audits.r2: Total allogeneic transfusion rate fell to 22.7% by 2018, a statistically significant 77.3 percentage point reduction from the 2013 baseline (p<0.05)

audits.t: Appropriateness of trimethoprim as empiric treatment for cystitis in 15-55 year-old women: an audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 340 eligible samples, 181 (53.2%) had a urinary pathogen identified; trimethoprim susceptibility 73.6% (E. coli), nitrofurantoin 100%, cefalexin 96.6%; overall trimethoprim resistance 13.5%

audits.t: Quality improvement project for improving inpatient glycaemic control in non-critically ill patients admitted on medical floor with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
audits.tp: Inpatient glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes
audits.st: American Diabetes Association 2019 guidelines for inpatient hyperglycaemia management; target 50% protocol compliance and glycaemic control improvement from 45% to 70%
audits.f: Adequate glycaemic control (7.8-10 mmol/L) achieved in 45% of patients; lack of uniformity in insulin regimen initiation
audits.c: Standardised inpatient hyperglycaemia management protocol, teaching sessions for trainees and nurses, consultant supervision, regular reminders/feedback, and patient education
audits.r2: Target glycaemic control of 70% achieved in 4 of 10 PDSA cycles, without increase in hypoglycaemic episodes

audits.t: High Frequency of Non-Compliance with Quality Indicators of Enteral and Parenteral Nutritional Therapy in Hospitalized Patients.
audits.tp: Enteral and parenteral nutrition quality indicators
audits.st: 12 literature-recommended quality indicators of nutritional therapy (QINT)
audits.f: Only 25% (3 of 12) QINT achieved goals: involuntary withdrawal of enteral feeding tube 0.01%, feeding tube occlusion/withdrawal per occlusion 0%, measurement of energy/protein requirements 92%; high frequency of non-compliance (75% of QINT)

audits.t: An intelligent system for improving adherence to guidelines on acute stroke.
audits.tp: Acute stroke guideline adherence intelligent decision system
audits.st: Guidelines for assessment and treatment of acute stroke patients
audits.f: Documentation completeness 78.66%; mean adherence to guideline 65%; error rate 1.69% by traditional methods
audits.c: Development and implementation of an intelligent decision-support system using decision-tree rules for acute stroke assessment and treatment
audits.r2: Documentation completeness increased to 100%; mean adherence to guideline increased to 99.5%; system accuracy 98.30%

audits.t: Neonatal transitional support with intact umbilical cord in assisted vaginal deliveries: a quality-improvement cohort study.
audits.tp: Early cord clamping reduction in assisted vaginal delivery
audits.st: Guidelines recommend deferred cord clamping; local target to reduce early cord clamping (ECC) using new delivery-room protocol
audits.f: Overall prevalence of ECC 13%
audits.c: New delivery-room protocol using mobile resuscitation equipment (LifeStart) allowing resuscitation at the mother's bedside

audits.t: Random colonic biopsies in macroscopically normal colonoscopies: is there any benefit? A two-centre audit of current practice.
audits.tp: Random colonic biopsy yield in normal colonoscopy
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines (April 2018) recommending random colonic biopsies to rule out microscopic colitis
audits.f: Only 1.5% of random colonic biopsies positive for microscopic colitis; 3.1% of diarrhoea patients had microscopic colitis; cost per positive diagnosis $10,862.42

audits.t: Review of Junior Resident Plain Film Reporting and Audit in Singapore.
audits.tp: Junior resident plain film reporting quality
audits.st: ACGME-I accreditation teaching and quality assurance framework requiring 50% random audit of junior resident plain film reports
audits.f: Major discrepancy rate ranged from 0.04% to 1.13% (mean 0.34%) nationwide; one resident required remediation

audits.t: Impact of Multidisciplinary Audit of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS)® Programs at a Single Institution.
audits.st: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocol compliance, via ERAS Interactive Audit System (EIAS)
audits.f: EIAS pre-ERAS control cohort (n=311) compared for 30-day outcomes
audits.c: Implementation and multidisciplinary auditing of ERAS programs across HPB, colorectal and urology subspecialties
audits.r2: Significant reduction in postoperative length of stay of 1.5 days in the ERAS cohort (n=1374) compared with pre-ERAS controls; improved ERAS compliance associated with improved outcomes

audits.t: SINAS: Effective Impact in the Quality Improvement of Ambulatory Surgery at an Ambulatory Centre.
audits.st: Portuguese National Health Assessment System (SINAS) seven quality indicators for ambulatory surgery
audits.f: Baseline validation and record of SINAS indicators before implementation, from 46 procedures in 2008
audits.c: Introduction of National Health Assessment System (SINAS) evaluation at the ambulatory centre
audits.r2: Improvement seen in all indicators after SINAS implementation, except criterion 4, among 100 consecutive procedures selected by the 2015 audit

audits.t: Improving the quality of trauma meetings by implementation of a modern trauma management platform.
audits.tp: Trauma referral documentation and trauma meeting quality
audits.st: 21 key data points for trauma referrals derived from Royal College of Surgeons and Royal College of Physicians handover guidelines; local SMART aim of significant improvement in 50% of key data points within 6 months
audits.f: 12 of 21 key data points documented in <80% of referrals (e.g. bed allocation 0%, allergies 6.7%, drug history 5.3%)
audits.c: Implementation of a new cloud-based trauma management platform (eTrauma) with structured/coded data entry fields, on-site training and support, followed by standardising trauma list printing order and encouraging documentation of management plans (PDSA cycles 2 and 3)
audits.r2: significant improvement in 12/21 (57%) key data points (e.g. allergies 33%, drug history 51%, mechanism of injury 100%); questionnaire showed improved response in 7/8 (87.5%) qualitative feedback questions

audits.t: Fasting and surgery timing (FaST) audit.
audits.st: International guidance advocating avoidance of prolonged preoperative fasting (over 12 hours)
