audits.t: Assessment of adherence to pneumonia guidelines and its determinants in an ambulatory care clinic in Ghana: findings and implications for the future.
audits.tp: Community-acquired pneumonia antibiotic prescribing guideline adherence
audits.st: Ghana Standard Treatment Guidelines for empirical antibiotic treatment of community-acquired pneumonia
audits.f: Overall adherence to the Ghana Standard Treatment Guidelines was 32.50% (627/1929); 62.50% female; 41.84% children (0-12 years); 97.15% had valid national health insurance; adherence was associated with duration of antibiotic prescribing, number of additional antibiotics prescribed and clinical characteristics

audits.t: Assessment of a quality improvement programme to improve telephone dispatchers' accuracy in identifying out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
audits.tp: Dispatcher recognition of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
audits.st: Resuscitation Academy/American Heart Association performance goals: OHCA recognition sensitivity >95%, median time to recognition <120s, median time to first compression <180s
audits.f: Sensitivity for OHCA recognition 82.3% (95% CI 76.4-87.2%); median time to recognise OHCA 68s (IQR 43-114.5); median time to first compression 148s
audits.c: Quality improvement programme: mandatory NO-NO-GO algorithm pop-up tool on the dispatcher's screen, quarterly telephone-CPR education and CPR training, quarterly voice-log audits with individual feedback, and focus-group review of recorded OHCA calls
audits.r2: Sensitivity for OHCA recognition improved to 92.7% (95% CI 88.2-95.8%, p=0.0014), still below the 95% target; median time to recognition 56s (not statistically significant, p=0.097); median time to first compression 148s (unchanged, p=0.918)

audits.t: COVID-19 personal protective equipment protocol compliance audit.
audits.st: COVID-19 personal protective equipment (PPE) protocol
audits.f: Average compliance 58.61% with donning and 68.84% with doffing

audits.t: Improving Services for HIV-Exposed Infants in Zambia and Cameroon Using a Quality Improvement Collaborative Approach.
audits.tp: Early infant HIV diagnosis and ART initiation
audits.st: National standards for early infant diagnosis (EID) coverage and antiretroviral therapy (ART) initiation timing for HIV-exposed infants
audits.f: EID coverage: Cameroon 57% (113/197) baseline; Zambia 77% (4773/6197) baseline
audits.c: Quality improvement collaborative (QIC) with monthly supportive supervision, root cause analysis, PDSA rapid tests of change, and quarterly learning sessions
audits.r2: EID coverage improved to 80% (165/207) in Cameroon and 89% (2144/2420) in Zambia; ART initiation improved from 44% to 80% in Zambia

audits.t: Development and Implementation of a Real-time Bundle-adherence Dashboard for Central Line-associated Bloodstream Infections.
audits.st: Central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) prevention bundle adherence
audits.f: All-element adherence across the hospital 25% in September 2018
audits.c: Development and deployment of a real-time electronic bundle-adherence dashboard in the electronic health record, populated from twice-daily bundle checks
audits.r2: All-element adherence increased to 44% by December 2019; average adherence to each bundle element increased between 2018 and 2019

audits.t: Improving hand hygiene in a low-resource setting: A nurse-led quality improvement project.
audits.st: Local target to increase hand hygiene practice and facility availability from baseline (37% practice, 22% facilities)
audits.f: Hand hygiene practice compliance 37%; hand hygiene facility availability 22%; 50% of burns unit patients had acquired pseudomonas infections
audits.c: Checklists to observe hand hygiene compliance and facilities, appointment of a hand hygiene committee to monitor and sustain activities, procurement and distribution of handrub, and placement of hand-washing buckets and soap at strategic points.
audits.r2: Hand hygiene facility availability increased to 95.6%; hand hygiene practice compliance increased to over 80%

audits.t: A Basic Intervention to Improve Compliance With Thromboprophylaxis in Patients With Neck of Femur Fracture.
audits.st: NICE guidance on VTE prophylaxis
audits.f: 63 (76.8%) correctly prescribed enoxaparin; 14 (17.1%) prescribed other anticoagulants; 5 (6.1%) received no thromboprophylaxis for no apparent reason
audits.c: Posters placed in key prescribing areas of all orthopaedic wards between the two audit cycles.
audits.r2: 56 (87.5%) correctly prescribed enoxaparin, with the remaining patients covered by alternative therapies

audits.t: Reporting ethical approval in health and social science articles: an audit of adherence to GDPR and national legislation.
audits.st: Swedish Ethics Review Act and EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requiring independent ethical review
audits.f: Ethical review information lacking in 12/200 (6%) somatic health science articles, 21/200 (11%) non-somatic health science articles, and 54/200 (27%) social science articles

audits.t: Organisational and advance care planning program characteristics associated with advance care directive completion: a prospective multicentre cross-sectional audit among health and residential aged care services caring for older Australians.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median advance care directive prevalence across organisations 19.4% (range 0-100%); higher in residential aged care facilities (unadjusted 28.7%) than hospitals (6.4%) or GP practices (2.5%); regional/rural facilities higher than metropolitan; government-funded/not-for-profit organisations and those with an advance care planning programme running for 3 or more years had higher prevalence

audits.t: BAOMS QOMS: findings from the pilot phase and lessons learned in the feasibility evaluation of a national quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: OMFS quality outcomes measures programme feasibility (QOMS)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 128 REDCap accounts issued; 45 (35%) completed registration and 22 (17%) were active users participating in pilot data entry across six audits (oral/dentoalveolar, oncology, orthognathic, reconstruction, trauma, skin)

audits.t: Enhanced lateral flow testing strategies in care homes are associated with poor adherence and were insufficient to prevent COVID-19 outbreaks: results from a mixed methods implementation study.
audits.tp: Care home COVID-19 lateral flow testing protocol adherence
audits.st: Local SARS-CoV-2 lateral flow device testing protocol for staff and visitors
audits.f: Protocol adherence was poor: only 8.6% of staff achieved more than 75% adherence, and 25.3% achieved 50% or more; six of the 11 care homes had outbreaks during the study, with no significant difference in outbreak proportion or size compared with non-pilot homes

audits.t: Continuous quality improvement (CQI) Institutionalization to reach 95:95:95 HIV targets: a multicountry experience from the Global South.
audits.st: UNAIDS 95:95:95 HIV cascade targets
audits.f: Baseline: Rwanda partner testing acceptance 21.7%; Botswana linkage to treatment 63%; Kenya viral load testing uptake 65%, viral load suppression 53%
audits.c: Continuous quality improvement (CQI) model implemented via quality improvement collaboratives, including root cause analysis, change packages, monitoring systems, and PDSA cycles, with MOH and ICAP support
audits.r2: Rwanda partner testing acceptance rose to 48.2% (HIV testing yield 2.1% to 6.3%); Botswana linkage to treatment rose to 94%; Kenya viral load testing uptake rose to 96%, suppression to 88%
audits.co: Kenya, Tanzania, Botswana, Zambia, Nigeria, Rwanda

audits.t: Patient information - is it ever enough? A prospective audit of information provision for orthognathic treatment at the Queen Victoria Hospital (QVH), East Grinstead.
audits.tp: Patient information provision for orthognathic treatment
audits.st: Queen Victoria Hospital (QVH) orthognathic information patient protocol
audits.f: 75/77 (97%) patients reported receiving sufficient information to make an informed decision; 69 had read the information leaflet before attending the MDT, but only 37 had accessed the British Orthodontic Society online resource

audits.t: Improving accuracy of American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status using audit and feedback and artificial intelligence: a time-series analysis.
audits.tp: Accuracy of ASA Physical Status classification
audits.st: Accurate ASA Physical Status classification incorporating BMI (ASA >=3 if BMI >=40 kg/m2)
audits.f: Slope of inaccurate ASA PS classification unchanging pre-intervention (coefficient 0.002, 95% CI -0.034 to 0.038, p=0.911)
audits.c: Audit and feedback on ASA PS/BMI documentation, followed by a rule-based AI alert algorithm
audits.r2: Immediate level change in accuracy after first intervention (coefficient -0.821, 95% CI -1.236 to -0.0406); further sustained improvement after AI algorithm

audits.t: Patterns of Antimicrobials Prescribed to Patients Admitted to a Tertiary Care Hospital: A Prescription Quality Audit.
audits.st: Anatomic Therapeutic Chemical Classification (ATC)/Defined Daily Dose (DDD) metrics for antibiotic prescribing quality
audits.f: Average 2±1 antibiotics prescribed per patient; only 23% had confirmed bacterial infection; generic names used in 55% and parenteral formulations in 72% of antibiotics prescribed; metronidazole most prescribed (34.2%)

audits.t: More than half of front-line healthcare workers unknowingly used an N95/P2 mask without adequate airborne protection: An audit in a tertiary institution.
audits.st: Fit-testing following standard guidelines for adequate N95/P2 respiratory protection
audits.f: First fit-pass rate using routinely available masks was only 47%
audits.c: Fit-testing with different types and sizes of N95/P2 masks
audits.r2: Fit-pass rates increased by testing different types and sizes of masks (overall rate not stated); confidence in mask fit increased significantly after fit-testing (median Likert 4.0 vs 3.0, p<0.001)

audits.t: Do We Need a Specific Guideline for Assessment and Improvement of Acromegaly Patients Adherence?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Pilot study found almost 90% of hospitalised Bulgarian acromegaly patients reported strict compliance with prescribed treatment regimen

audits.t: Institution of an antibiotic stewardship programme for rationalising antibiotic usage: a quality improvement project in the NICU of a public teaching hospital in rural central India.
audits.st: Local QI target to reduce antibiotic exposure from 75% to 40% within 6 months via an antibiotic stewardship programme
audits.f: Point prevalence of antibiotic usage 75%; median antibiotic duration 3 days per baby; culture-positive sepsis 18%; all-cause mortality 25 per 1000 live births
audits.c: Six PDSA cycles: department antibiotic policy with preauthorisation, universal aseptic precaution reinforcement led by a dedicated infection control nurse, a hard stop of antibiotics at 72 hours, streamlining/de-escalation per culture sensitivity, delegating 72-hour stop reminders to nursing staff, and staff confidence-building/team-building sessions
audits.r2: Antibiotic exposure fell to 40-41%; median antibiotic days per baby fell from 3 to 0 (IQR 0-6); culture-positive sepsis fell to 11.56%; all-cause mortality fell to 16 per 1000 live births; sustained at around 20% exposure at 2-year follow-up

audits.t: Antibiotic stewardship in a tertiary care NICU of northern India: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Local QI target to reduce antibiotic usage rate (AUR) by at least 20% from baseline, using WHO Point of Care Quality Improvement methodology
audits.f: Total AUR 574 per 1000 patient-days; AUR in culture-negative babies 451; vancomycin AUR 62; only 22% of newborns never exposed to antibiotics; antibiotics stopped within 48 hours in culture/screen-negative patients in only 16% of cases
audits.c: Five PDSA cycles over 10 months: a unit sepsis/antibiotic protocol adapted from NICE and paediatric sepsis guidelines, mandatory checkpoints for early antibiotic stoppage at 48 hours/7 days, restricted antibiotic initiation requiring consultant review, an antibiogram-based antibiotic policy revision, and a specific vancomycin-restriction protocol
audits.r2: Total AUR fell to 390 per 1000 patient-days (32% reduction, p=0.001); AUR in culture-negative babies fell to 361 (20% reduction, p=0.015); vancomycin AUR fell to 44 (29% reduction, p=0.03); proportion never exposed to antibiotics rose to 37% (p=0.045); early stoppage at 48 hours rose to 54% (p<0.001); protocol compliance for starting/upgrading antibiotics 75%/82%

audits.t: Improving Compliance with a Rounding Checklist through Low- and High-technology Interventions: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Local safety/improvement rounding checklist completion target (internal QI target of >75%)
audits.f: Average biweekly checklist compliance 31% before interventions; checklist completion time 46 seconds
audits.c: Low-technology intervention (human factors-based redesign of hard-copy checklist) followed by a high-technology clinical decision support tool within the electronic health record
audits.r2: Average biweekly checklist compliance improved to 80% after interventions; completion time decreased to 11 seconds

audits.t: National audit of a hereditary and acquired angioedema cohort in New Zealand.
audits.st: Expected monitoring standard for androgen prophylaxis (regular liver ultrasound screening)
audits.f: Icatibant used in 73% of HAE patients; androgens used as prophylaxis in half of patients, of whom 33% not having regular liver ultrasound screening; tranexamic acid used in one-fifth

audits.t: Specialist pneumonia intervention nurse service improves pneumonia care and outcome.
audits.tp: Community-acquired pneumonia guideline adherence and specialist nursing
audits.st: British Thoracic Society (BTS) pneumonia guidelines (CURB-65 scoring, radiological diagnosis, antibiotics within 4 hours, dual antibiotics for severe CAP)
audits.f: in-hospital mortality 20.0%, 30-day mortality 22.4% (crude); guideline adherence not separately quantified at baseline
audits.c: Introduction of a specialist pneumonia intervention nursing (SPIN) service: two dedicated nurses systematically screening admissions, applying CURB-65 scoring, and driving adherence to BTS guideline elements, supported by a Trust-wide educational campaign
audits.r2: in-hospital mortality fell to 14.2% (OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.60-0.73, p<0.0001); 30-day mortality fell to 18.3% (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.70-0.85, p<0.0001); 82% of SPIN-reviewed patients received antibiotics within 4 hours (vs 68.5% national audit) and 86.3% dual antibiotics for severe CAP (vs 48.0% national audit)

audits.t: Quality of service and continuous quality improvement in voluntary medical male circumcision programme across four provinces in South Africa: Longitudinal and cross-sectional programme data.
audits.tp: Voluntary medical male circumcision quality of service
audits.st: National Department of Health (NDoH) continuous quality improvement (CQI) assessment tool standards for VMMC services
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: CQI support: coaching, provision of standard operating procedures and guidelines, mentoring and on-site in-service training
audits.r2: Significant increase in quality of service scores after CQI support, including 12% increase for infection prevention (95% CI 7-17)

audits.t: A retrospective single-site data-linkage study comparing manual to electronic data abstraction for routine post-operative nausea and vomiting audit.
audits.tp: Postoperative nausea and vomiting audit methodology
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Manual audit captured 142 patients (PONV rate 10% in recovery, 20% next day); electronic audit captured 294 patients (PONV rate 5% in recovery, 15% at 24h); electronic audit missed 5.8% of manually-identified PONV patients

audits.t: Assessing the Hawthorne effect on hand hygiene compliance in an intensive care unit.
audits.st: World Health Organization 'My Five Moments for Hand Hygiene' guidelines
audits.f: Hand hygiene compliance 31.95% (340/1064) covert vs 68.10% (790/1160) overt before campaign
audits.c: Educational campaign on hand hygiene plus electronic panel display of overt compliance rates for feedback
audits.r2: Hand hygiene compliance 56.11% (615/1096) covert vs 80.98% (1086/1341) overt after campaign; infection rate reduced from 18.87% to 14.60% (22.62% relative reduction)

audits.t: Compliance of antibiotics used for surgical site infection prophylaxis among patients undergoing surgery in a Congolese teaching hospital.
audits.st: International surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (SAP) guidelines
audits.f: Compliance rate of SAP was 18.1%; inappropriate initial dose compliance 23.8%, incorrect duration compliance 30.9%; emergency surgery increased non-compliance risk 3-fold (OR=3.5, 95% CI 1.0-11.8, p=0.033)

audits.t: Compliance of Mumbai-based clinical trial sites with the Quality Council of India guidelines and evaluation of the challenges faced by the investigators.
audits.st: Quality Council of India (QCI) accreditation standards for clinical trial sites
audits.f: Over 80% of sites complied with QCI-recommended standards; most frequent issues: lack of archival space (25%), no system to evaluate training adequacy (31.81%), lack of understanding of informed consent form language (39.02%)

audits.t: [Audit & Feedback: an example of use to improve adherence to therapies.]
audits.tp: Audit and feedback strategy for therapy adherence
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Perioperative temperature management: a survey of 6 Asia-Pacific countries.
audits.st: International perioperative temperature management guidelines
audits.f: 24.2% prewarm, 44.0% perform intraoperative active warming, 42.1% postoperative active warming in majority of patients; 46.0% measure temperature preoperatively, 67.5% intraoperatively, 82.6% postoperatively
audits.co: Singapore, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand, India, South Korea

audits.t: Using the WHO safe childbirth checklist to improve essential care delivery as part of the district-wide maternal and newborn health quality improvement initiative, a time series study.
audits.tp: WHO Safe Childbirth Checklist bundle adherence
audits.st: WHO Safe Childbirth Checklist (WHO-SCC) 'On Admission', 'Before Pushing' and 'Soon After Birth' clinical bundles
audits.f: not reported (baseline pre-improvement adherence not separately quantified in abstract)
audits.c: District-wide system improvement collaborative integrating WHO-SCC into maternal and newborn health quality improvement programme
audits.r2: Improved adherence over time across four MNH collaboratives; in Tankua Abergele collaborative (Tigray), mean adherence to 'On Admission' bundle was 86% with beta=1.39 (95% CI 0.47-2.32)

audits.t: Relationship Between Research Culture and Research Activity of Medical Doctors: A Survey and Audit.
audits.tp: Research culture and research activity audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median Research Capacity and Culture scores: 5/10 organisational, 5.5 team, 6 individual level; one research project commenced per 12.5 doctors employed, one publication per 7.5 doctors

audits.t: Posttraumatic stress disorder collaborative care: A quality improvement study in veterans affairs primary care.
audits.tp: PTSD collaborative care in VA primary care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 53.4% (94/176) reported clinically significant improvement in depression (PHQ-9 >=5-point decrease); 42.2% (35/83) reported clinically significant PTSD Checklist improvement (>=10-point decrease)
audits.c: Depression collaborative care protocol modified to include PTSD assessment and support for medication adherence, self-management and engagement in evidence-based PTSD care

audits.t: Audit-Based Quality Validation of the Japan Cardiovascular Surgery Database.
audits.st: On-site institutional audit comparing registry entries to source data
audits.f: Case registration accuracy 98.74%; data input accuracy >90% for almost all fields; ~99% accuracy for diabetes, aortic stenosis and mortality fields

audits.t: A clinical perspective study on the compliance of surgical safety checklist in all surgical procedures done in operation theatres, in a teaching hospital, Ethiopia, 2021: A clinical perspective study.
audits.st: World Health Organization Surgical Safety Checklist
audits.f: Patient identity, procedure and informed consent, anaesthesia machine checking, and medication preparation had 100% compliance; some other checklist items were not fully compliant (not quantified individually in abstract)

audits.t: Self-Reported versus observed audit: Measuring CHG bathing compliance.
audits.st: Direct observation audit of CHG bathing process compliance
audits.f: Difference between mean observed and mean self-reported CHG bathing compliance was not significant (p=.06)

audits.t: Home spirometry utilisation in telemedicine clinic for cystic fibrosis care during COVID-19 pandemic: a quality improvement process.
audits.tp: Home spirometry uptake in telemedicine cystic fibrosis care
audits.st: Cystic Fibrosis Foundation chronic care guidelines recommending spirometry monitoring at quarterly multidisciplinary visits
audits.f: 37% (49/131) of patients owned a home spirometer; 50% (9/18) of telemedicine patients performed spirometry at home
audits.c: Standardised Model for Improvement QI process: home spirometers distributed to eligible patients and spirometry monitored at each telemedicine visit for clinical decisions
audits.r2: 97% (127/131) of patients owned a home spirometer by September 2020; 96% (24/25) provided spirometry results during telemedicine encounters by October 2020

audits.t: Assessment of Adherence to the Core Elements of Hospital Antibiotic Stewardship Programs: A Survey of the Tertiary Care Hospitals in Punjab, Pakistan.
audits.st: CDC Core Elements of Hospital Antibiotic Stewardship Programs (CEHASP), 7 elements assessed via 19-item checklist
audits.f: No hospital showed 'perfect' adherence; 48.6% of private and 54.5% of public hospitals were 'poor' in adherence; most neglected elements were reporting and tracking antibiotic use and outcomes

audits.t: Statins in Patients with Uncomplicated Hypertension: A Prescription Audit.
audits.st: Guideline recommendation for statin prescription in all high-risk hypertensive patients regardless of cholesterol level (US guideline-based intensity classification)
audits.f: Statins prescribed overall in 41.2% (95% CI 39.4-42.9%); by risk group: low 28.4%, moderate 46.6%, high 55.1% (p trend <0.001); more in men than women (47.7% vs 33.7%, p<0.001)

audits.t: Current UK clinical practice in diagnosing dementia in younger adults: compliance with quality indicators in electronic health records from mental health trusts.
audits.st: International Delphi consensus proforma defining a minimum standard (11 statements) and gold standard (31 statements) for diagnostic assessment of young-onset dementia
audits.f: Compliance rates varied by site and statement; the additional 20 gold-standard statements had consistently higher compliance than the minimum standard set at every site; commonly missed items identified in examination and enquiry compared with expert consensus

audits.t: Evaluation of an Educational Outreach and Audit and Feedback Program to Reduce Continuous Pulse Oximetry Use in Hospitalized Infants With Stable Bronchiolitis: A Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
audits.tp: Continuous pulse oximetry deimplementation in bronchiolitis
audits.st: National guidelines recommending against continuous pulse oximetry in hospitalised children with bronchiolitis not receiving supplemental oxygen
audits.f: Guideline-discordant continuous pulse oximetry use 53% (95% CI 49%-57%) at baseline
audits.c: Educational outreach on existing guidelines plus audit and feedback (weekly aggregate data feedback to teams and real-time 1:1 feedback to clinicians on guideline-discordant use)
audits.r2: Guideline-discordant continuous pulse oximetry use decreased to 23% (95% CI 20%-25%)

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative Addressing Provider Prescription of Weight Management Follow-up in Primary Care.
audits.tp: Weight management follow-up prescription in primary care
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics recommendation to prescribe weight management follow-up between well-child checks for children with obesity/overweight
audits.f: Mean prescription rate for weight management follow-up 32% at baseline
audits.c: Four PDSA ramps: provider education, electronic health record note changes, discharge order modifications, and provider feedback
audits.r2: Mean prescription rate increased to 58%, with special cause variation demonstrating improvement; of those prescribed follow-up, 40% attended vs 13% before the initiative

audits.t: An audit of 70 maternal deaths.
audits.st: Confidential-enquiry audit categorisation of suboptimal obstetric/critical care
audits.f: Suboptimal care identified in 30/70 (43%) cases; leading causes: cardiovascular disease (14), hypertensive disorder (10), suicide (10), thromboembolism (7); 34% of deaths judged potentially avoidable

audits.t: Chest X-rays of newborns in a medical facility: variation between the entrance skin dose measurements using the indirect and direct methods for clinical dose audit.
audits.tp: Neonatal chest X-ray entrance skin dose
audits.st: Diagnostic reference levels for neonatal chest X-ray entrance skin dose (ACR-AAPM-SPR, European Commission and UK reference levels)
audits.f: Mean entrance skin dose 0.67 (SD 0.09) mGy; 75th percentile 0.75 mGy, higher than ACR-AAPM-SPR/EC/UK reference levels; variation between indirect and direct dose-measurement methods 39.6% (33.7-45.1%)

audits.t: Implementation of an Early Palliative Care Referral Program in Lung Cancer: A Quality Improvement Project at the Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai, India.
audits.tp: Early palliative care referral rates in lung cancer
audits.st: Recommendation for early palliative care (EPC) referral for all patients with metastatic lung cancer
audits.f: Average EPC referral rate 50% at baseline
audits.c: QI bundle: process flow mapping, key driver identification, root cause analysis (identifying lack of documentation), and teaching/encouraging staff to incorporate EPC referral into initial visits
audits.r2: Referral rate increased to 75%, mean difference 12.64 (SD 10.13, 95% CI 22.01-3.29), P=0.016

audits.t: Improving turnaround times for HLA-B*27 and HLA-B*57:01 gene testing: a Barts Health NHS Trust quality improvement project.
audits.st: Local 5-day turnaround time target for HLA-B*27 and HLA-B*57:01 testing
audits.f: Mean turnaround time 3.8 days; 78% of tests within the 5-day target
audits.c: Three Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles testing IT-based removal of manual administrative steps and alerts for progressing samples (two changes retained); separating out the targeted tests was tried but not retained.
audits.r2: Mean turnaround time reduced to 3.3 days; proportion within the 5-day target increased to 100%; sustained at 3.4 days and 97% over the following 3 months

audits.t: Level of adherence to vitamin D supplementation guidelines in an antenatal centre in Birmingham, UK, and its effect on biochemical and obstetrical outcomes: a single-centre cross-sectional study.
audits.tp: Vitamin D supplementation guideline adherence in pregnancy
audits.st: NICE standards for vitamin D supplementation in pregnancy (target 100% compliance)
audits.f: 41.8% (61) received written and/or verbal supplementation advice versus the NICE standard of 100%; 72.6% (106) had one or more risk factors for vitamin D deficiency, of whom 38.7% (41) were asked about supplementation (NICE standard 100%); among those asked, 85.4% (41) received the correct dosage (NICE standard 100%); the non-supplementation group had offspring 1.40 cm longer at birth (95% CI 0.01 to 2.80, p=0.04)

audits.t: Biopsy for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma: results of a multicentre UK audit.
audits.tp: Biopsy practice for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma
audits.st: NICE mandate for histological confirmation before sorafenib use (2017)
audits.f: 76% had chronic liver disease, 66% cirrhotic; new biopsy in 270 patients confirmed HCC in 93.4%; non-invasive radiological criteria sensitivity 65.4%, positive predictive value 91.4% in cirrhotic patients; post-biopsy bleeding in 2 (0.7%)

audits.t: An audit of safety reporting in randomized controlled trials over a five-year period in a high impact factor journal.
audits.tp: Safety reporting quality in randomised controlled trials
audits.st: CONSORT guidelines for reporting of safety outcomes in RCTs
audits.f: 275/623 (44.1%) articles reported statistics for safety outcomes; significant difference between investigator-initiated and industry-sponsored studies (cOR=4.0, 95% CI 2.8-5.5)

audits.t: Multidisciplinary, early mobility approach to enhance functional independence in patients admitted to a cardiothoracic intensive care unit: a quality improvement programme.
audits.st: Evidence-based early mobility practice; local aim of 95% early activity/mobilisation within 3 hours of extubation by 30 June 2018
audits.f: Patients were confined to bed exercises until chest tube removal; maximum functional mobility was sitting in a chair; ICU Mobility Scale score 5 and Functional Independence Measure 56 on transfer out of CTICU; patients typically ambulated only on the second postoperative day after ward transfer
audits.c: Multidisciplinary early mobility programme (Institute for Healthcare Improvement model) with 9 PDSA cycles: an evidence-based 5-level activity/mobility protocol, universal physiotherapy referral on admission, a patient/family education booklet, pain assessment before mobilisation, a colour-coded risk categorisation system, technology (cordless telemonitoring, reclining chairs), a written protocol, visual flags, and communication of mobility levels at rounds/handover
audits.r2: Compliance with early mobilisation rose from 55% to 95% (sustained); mean time to out-of-bed mobilisation fell from 22.77 to 11.74 hours; mean Functional Independence Measure rose from 54.23 to 58.62; mean ICU Mobility Scale rose from 3.96 to 7.23 (all p<0.005); functional independence at discharge achieved by postoperative day 5 versus day 6 pre-intervention

audits.t: Clinical audit of current Helicobacter pylori treatment outcomes in Singapore.
audits.tp: Helicobacter pylori eradication treatment outcomes audit
audits.st: Recommended H. pylori eradication regimens (14-day PAC, PBMT first-line; 14-day PBMT, PAL second-line) and treatment duration
audits.f: 14-day treatment duration appropriately prescribed in 65.2% of first-line and 82.7% of second-line patients; 14-day PAC success 92.0%, PBMT 87.5%, PBAC 100%; 14-day treatment superior to 7-day (90.8% vs 71.4%, P=0.028)

audits.t: Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology advertising guidelines: How likely are member clinics to maintain compliance after resolving their violations?
audits.st: Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology (SART) advertising guidelines (6 categories)
audits.f: 44/161 (27%) clinics had at least one violation not corrected within the two-week grace period; improper presentation of supplemental data was most common violation, 32/44 (73%)
audits.c: Disciplinary and educational correction process by SART advertising committee
audits.r2: 10/43 (23%) clinics had violations on rereview; supplemental data issues remained most common, 7/10 (70%)

audits.t: An Audit of UK Hospital Doctors' Knowledge and Experience of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Few respondents had formal teaching on myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME); most lacked confidence in diagnosing or managing it; 82% believed ME was at least in part psychological; little accurate knowledge of ME definitions, diagnosis or clinical manifestations

audits.t: Exploration of a quality improvement process to standardised preoperative tests for a surgical procedure to reduce waste.
audits.st: Recommendation against routine preoperative testing in the absence of specific clinical indications
audits.f: High volumes of routine preoperative tests performed without clinical indication before intervention
audits.c: Series of six PDSA cycles: root cause analysis, process mapping, development of a standardised tool (GRID), education and feedback, pilot testing and implementation
audits.r2: Unnecessary coagulation tests reduced by 81% (91% to 17%), electrolyte/renal panel tests reduced by 81% (41% to 7%), ECGs reduced by 68% (35% to 11%); no surgery delayed or cancelled due to missing tests

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Intervention to Inform Scale-Up of Integrated HIV-TB Services: Lessons Learned From KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
audits.st: National HIV-TB process indicator targets (HTS, TB screening, IPT, ART, VL testing)
audits.f: IPT initiation 15.9%, HTS 84.8%, TB screening 76.2%, VL testing 61.4%, ART initiation 95.8%
audits.c: Learning collaborative of nurse supervisors; patient-flow redesign, daily data quality checks, prior identification of patients eligible for IPT and VL testing

audits.st: Internal QI target to reduce severe intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) or death in the first week of life via evidence-based bundle

audits.c: Bundle of evidence-based potentially better practices implemented via specific electronic order sets (carbon dioxide/pH targeting, delayed cord clamping, expanded indomethacin prophylaxis)
audits.r2: Rate of severe ICH or death in the first week decreased to 15.0%; severe ICH rate decreased to 10.0%

audits.t: The importance of the autopsy in ascertaining the cause of death and as an audit tool at the university college hospital, Ibadan.
audits.st: Goldman criteria classification of clinicopathological diagnostic discordance
audits.f: Concordance between postmortem and clinical diagnosis in 298/533 (55.9%) cases

audits.t: Establishing communication with relatives of admitted obstetrical patients with COVID-19 infection during COVID-19 pandemic: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Communication with relatives of COVID-19 obstetric inpatients
audits.st: Locally set target for counselling relatives of admitted COVID-19 obstetric patients (66.5% per day)
audits.f: Baseline counselling rate 14% per day
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles with various interventions following root-cause fishbone analysis (Point of Care Improvement methodology)
audits.r2: Counselling rate improved to the target of 66.5% per day

audits.t: 'Where is the ECG machine?': a quality improvement project using WhatsApp to improve the efficiency in locating shared medical devices in an inpatient unit.
audits.tp: Locating shared medical equipment via staff communication technology
audits.st: Local target: overall effectiveness metric (OEM, event count/engagement count) to remain ≥1, indicating improved efficiency in locating the unit's single ECG machine
audits.f: average weekly 'where is the ECG machine' event count 2.3
audits.c: WhatsApp-based protocol asking doctors to post a photo and location caption of the ECG machine after use (PDSA 1), reinforced with a printed memorandum attached to the machine (PDSA 2), then revised photo-posting confidentiality guidelines (PDSA 3)
audits.r2: OEM peaked at 3.5 during PDSA 1 (improvement) but fell to 0.5 in PDSA 2 and ended at 0.4 by PDSA 3, i.e. engagement was not sustained; 60% of surveyed doctors reported the protocol saved them time

audits.t: Higher Adherence to ERAS Society® Recommendations is Associated with Shorter Hospital Stay Without an Increase in Postoperative Complications or Readmissions in Bariatric Surgery: the Association Between Use of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery Protocols and Postoperative Complications after Bariatric Surgery (POWER 3) Multicenter Observational Study.
audits.tp: ERAS Society pathway adherence in bariatric surgery
audits.st: ERAS Society recommendations for bariatric surgery (24 individual pathway components)
audits.f: 8% (114/1419) developed postoperative complications overall; highest adherence quartile >72.2% vs lowest <55%; higher adherence associated with shorter hospital stay (2 vs 3 days, p=.015) without increased complications, readmissions or mortality

audits.t: Evidence-Based Practice for Non-Specific Low Back Pain: Canadian Physiotherapists' Adherence, Beliefs, and Perspectives.
audits.tp: Physiotherapist adherence to low back pain guidelines
audits.st: Evidence-based clinical practice guidelines (EBCPGs) for non-specific low back pain
audits.f: 406/525 (77%) survey respondents demonstrated higher adherence (score 3 or 4) to EBCPGs; only 29.5% chose interventions addressing psychosocial issues

audits.t: Practices of Procedural Pain Management in Neonates through Continuous Quality Improvement Measures.
audits.tp: Procedural pain management practices in neonates
audits.st: Evidence-based neonatal pain control practices for procedures (IV cannulation, venous sampling, heel prick, nasogastric tube insertion)
audits.f: Minimal pain control measures used for identified procedures (3-4%) before the project
audits.c: Multiple PDSA cycles (7 interventions over 5 months, April-September 2019) encouraging evidence-based pain control measures (skin-to-skin contact, breastfeeding, expressed breast milk, oral sucrose)
audits.r2: Target of 80% compliance with pain control interventions achieved after seven interventions over five months, with retention on reassessment at 2 and 4 months after stopping intervention

audits.t: Multi-Institutional Quality Improvement Project to Minimize Opioid Prescribing in Children after Appendectomy Using NSQIP-Pediatric.
audits.st: Minimising opioid prescribing at discharge after paediatric appendectomy (multi-institutional QI target)
audits.f: Baseline opioid prescribing at discharge 18.2%
audits.c: Multi-institutional QI project using NSQIP-Pediatric platform to standardise/minimise opioid prescribing (5 hospitals already had a no-opioid protocol, 5 had unstandardized prescribing)
audits.r2: Opioid prescribing decreased to 4.0%; no increase in emergency room visits or decrease in patient satisfaction

audits.t: Bifascicular block in unexplained syncope is underrecognized and under-evaluated: A single-center audit of ESC guidelines adherence.
audits.tp: Bifascicular block guideline-directed evaluation in unexplained syncope
audits.st: European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines recommending electrophysiology study (EPS), implantable loop recorder and/or permanent pacemaker for bifascicular block with unexplained syncope
audits.f: Only 3 of 29 (10.3%) patients received guideline-directed evaluation per ESC recommendations; cardiology consulted in 58.6% of cases; 2 patients underwent EPS (1 refused), no patients received empiric PPM

audits.t: Audit of Clinical Care for Women with Preeclampsia or Eclampsia and Perinatal Outcome in Ethiopia: Second National EmONC Survey.
audits.tp: Clinical care for preeclampsia/eclampsia (national EmONC audit)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 90% hospitalised in public facilities; perinatal mortality 16.3% (95% CI 13.4-19.6%) among 553 records with recorded outcomes; substantial missing data

audits.t: Impact of a system to assist in clinical decision-making in primary healthcare in Catalonia: prescription Self Audit.
audits.st: Self Audit clinical decision-support alerts for medication-related problems (therapeutic duplications, safety alerts, polymedication in over-65s)
audits.f: Overall resolution of safety-based MRPs was 9% (21,547) in 2016; resolution of the 3 highest-relevance MRP types linked to the safety indicator was 41% (17,358) in 2016.
audits.c: Incentive-based safety indicator linked to the 3 most clinically relevant medication-related problems
audits.r2: Overall resolution fell to 1% (2392) in 2018; resolution of the safety-indicator-linked MRPs was 21% (8135) in 2018 (20% in 2017, 7655).

audits.t: Rapid implementation of an outpatient arthroplasty care pathway: a COVID-19-driven quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Local QI target: perform 25% or more of primary total joint arthroplasty (TJA) as outpatient procedures by 30 June 2021, driven by COVID-19 inpatient resource constraints
audits.f: No outpatient TJA pathway existed; all TJA were performed as inpatient procedures before the pandemic
audits.c: Outpatient TJA care pathway bundle developed via PDSA cycles: explicit patient selection criteria, tailored short-acting spinal anaesthesia with nerve blocks, enhanced patient education, a PACU physiotherapy assessment before discharge, and virtual postoperative follow-up at 24/48 hours
audits.r2: 55/65 (84.6%) outpatient candidates were successfully discharged home the same day; outpatient TJA accounted for 33.3% of all primary TJA performed, exceeding the 25% target; 30-day emergency department visits 6.15% (outpatient) vs 8.93% (inpatient); no 30-day readmissions among outpatients

audits.t: Implementing an Antimicrobial Stewardship Programme to Improve Adherence to a Perioperative Prophylaxis Guideline.
audits.st: Local perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis guideline
audits.f: Non-adherence to surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis protocol was common before the programme (not reported as a single percentage).
audits.c: Establishment of a surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis guideline, educational sessions, and monthly revision of prescriptions
audits.r2: Reduced antibiotic consumption, decreased cost of prophylaxis, and a decrease in surgical site infection rate after the antimicrobial stewardship programme (exact figures not reported).

audits.t: Impact of staffing levels and resources of intensive care units on compliance to standard mechanical ventilator guidelines: A city-wide study in times of COVID-19 pandemic.
audits.st: Standardised mechanical ventilator care bundle guidelines
audits.f: Median ventilator care bundle compliance score 26/30 (IQR 21-28) overall; 24 (IQR 19-26) in medical ICUs and 28 (IQR 23-30) in surgical ICUs; least compliant component was head elevation

audits.t: QI Project Promoting NP Compliance with an AOM Bundle in Pediatric Hospital-owned Retail Clinic.
audits.st: AOM quality bundle (5 predetermined criteria) for antibiotic prescribing in acute otitis media
audits.f: Baseline AOM bundle compliance mean 42%; antibiotic choice or duration errors in 48% of reviewed charts.
audits.c: NP education, electronic medical record improvements, and parent engagement via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Goal of 95% compliant bundles was achieved and maintained; 98% of antibiotic prescriptions were accurate at project conclusion.

audits.t: Engagement and Bundle Compliance during COVID-19: A Virtual Strategy.
audits.st: Bundle compliance standards for unplanned extubation, CLABSI, and staff safety overexertion injuries (HAC bundles)
audits.f: Baseline monthly bundle compliance for each HAC (not reported as a specific percentage).
audits.c: Virtual leadership meetings, improved audit process, and fidelity to bundle elements via multiple virtual modalities
audits.r2: Goal of maintaining bundle compliance without more than a 20% decrease was exceeded, with a significant positive change in the rate of audits after COVID-19 (exact figures not reported).

audits.t: Improving Fecal Immunochemical Test Return Rates: A Colorectal Cancer Screening Quality Improvement Project in a Multisite Federally Qualified Health Center.
audits.tp: Fecal immunochemical test return rate for colorectal cancer screening
audits.st: Colorectal cancer screening improvement target (PDSA quality improvement project)
audits.f: Usual care (live telephone reminders): 79% FIT return rate, 9% positive; automated reminder group: 76% FIT return rate, 10% positive; system-wide baseline CRC screening rate 30.5%
audits.c: Automated electronic medical record patient reminder system for FIT completion, compared with usual-care live telephone reminders (PDSA methodology)
audits.r2: System-wide CRC screening rate increased to 47.3%; no significant difference in contacts per patient (2.0 vs 1.8, p=.248); automated group required fewer live calls (17 vs 56)

audits.t: Value of BI-RADS 3 Audits.
audits.st: Benchmark of 2% probability of malignancy for BI-RADS 3 category; audit metrics include follow-up rate, upgrade rate, PPV3, cancer yield
audits.f: Among 135,765 screening exams, 13,453 recalled, 1,037 BI-RADS 3 cases; follow-up rate 86.7%; upgrade rate 7.4% (77/1,037); PPV3 33.8% (26/77); cancer yield 2.51% (26/1,037), not significantly different (p=0.243) from 2% expected

audits.t: Improving the quality and content of discharge summaries on acute medicine wards: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: 10 core criteria for discharge summary content based on Royal College of Physicians and Professional Record Standards Body guidance; target of 95% compliance by June 2021 (ward 22) and 90% on the second ward
audits.f: average 55% compliance with the 10 core criteria (ward 22); second ward (ward 2) baseline 61%
audits.c: PDSA cycles: pharmacist input on ward rounds, individualised feedback to clinicians completing <80% of criteria, a discharge summary template with core criteria as subheadings, and ward posters with weekly compliance updates; second ward also used patient feedback questionnaires
audits.r2: ward 22 reached 97% compliance (sustained at 80-85% over following months); ward 2 reached 92% compliance after its first PDSA (sustained around 86-93%)

audits.t: Rotating opportunistic prevalence audit: A new pragmatic audit method is effective at identifying misuse of ciprofloxacin in a large academic hospital.
audits.st: Appropriateness criteria for ciprofloxacin prescribing
audits.f: Rotating opportunistic prevalence audit (ROPA) captured 82% of all ciprofloxacin prescriptions; 69% were assessed as inappropriate.

audits.t: A quality improvement initiative to improve the appropriateness of candidemia management by the implementation of a comprehensive candidemia care bundle at a tertiary care hospital in South India: Results of a quasi-experimental study.
audits.st: Comprehensive candidemia care bundle (antifungal stewardship)
audits.f: Appropriateness of antifungal prescriptions 30%; inpatient mortality 40%
audits.c: Clinical pharmacist-driven comprehensive candidemia care bundle
audits.r2: Appropriateness of antifungal prescriptions 65% (P=.0005); inpatient mortality 36% (P=.26); no significant difference in length of stay

audits.t: Scale-up of ABC care bundle for intracerebral haemorrhage across two hyperacute stroke units in one region in England: a mixed methods evaluation of a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: ABC care bundle scale-up for intracerebral haemorrhage
audits.st: ABC care bundle for intracerebral haemorrhage (developed at Salford Royal Hospital)
audits.f: HASU1 anticoagulant reversal door-to-needle time 132 min; BP lowering door-to-target time 345 min
audits.c: Scale-up of ABC care bundle to new hyperacute stroke units with facilitation support
audits.r2: HASU1: door-to-needle time reduced to 76 min; BP door-to-target time reduced to 84 min; no significant improvements at HASU2; no significant change in 30-day mortality at either site

audits.t: Access to essential surgical care in district hospitals of Sarawak Malaysia: outcomes of an audit and the need for urgent attention.
audits.tp: Access to essential surgical care in district hospitals
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 259 referrals for five essential surgical procedures from district hospitals; referred patients were older (43.2 vs 39.7 years, p=0.008) with different racial composition than the local cohort

audits.t: Impact of Guideline Adherence on Outcomes in Patients Hospitalized with Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) in Hungary: A Retrospective Observational Study.
audits.st: National and international community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) guidelines for empirical antibiotic choice and dose
audits.f: Adherence to national CAP guideline was 30.61% (45/147) for agent choice and 88.89% (40/45) for dose; 30-day mortality 15.56% in adherent vs 16.67% in non-adherent (p>0.05).

audits.t: Adherence to European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Quality Performance Measures for Upper and Lower Gastrointestinal Endoscopy: A Nationwide Survey From the Italian Society of Digestive Endoscopy.
audits.tp: Adherence to ESGE endoscopy quality performance measures
audits.st: European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) quality performance measures for upper and lower GI endoscopy
audits.f: 18.2% recorded EGD duration; 51% provided photo documentation in >=90% of cases; 52.8% monitored complications after therapeutic EGD; 93.9% used Boston Bowel Preparation Scale; cecal intubation rate >=90% reported by 93.9%.

audits.t: Adherence to guidelines at the patient- and hospital-levels is associated with improved overall survival in patients with gastric cancer.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence in gastric cancer treatment
audits.st: NCCN Guidelines for gastric cancer (stage-specific, annual guidelines 2004-2015)
audits.f: 32% of patients received NCCN Guideline-adherent treatment; guideline-adherent treatment associated with longer overall survival (51 months vs 22 months)

audits.t: The Consent Process for Elective Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: Does Information on Handwritten Forms Meet Prescribed Standards?
audits.st: British Orthopaedic Association (BOA) endorsed consent form standards (orthoconsent.com) for hip and knee arthroplasty, classifying risks as common (2-5%), less common (1-2%) and rare (<1%)
audits.f: 0% of forms fully compliant with BOA standards; common risks mentioned in 25.7% (hip) and 42.8% (knee) of forms; no form (0%) mentioned all rare risks for either procedure; 17.1% of forms had legibility issues

audits.t: Effectiveness of quality clinical active audit in improving healthcare of a multispecialty hospital in a developing country.
audits.st: National Accreditation Board of Hospitals (NABH) accreditation criteria for medical record documentation
audits.f: Active audit found documentation lacking in several criteria, e.g. desired outcomes recorded in only 25.2% of files

audits.t: Improving delirium screening in older adults at the Royal United Hospital, Bath.
audits.tp: Delirium screening compliance in older adults
audits.st: National (NICE) and hospital guidelines for delirium screening on admission
audits.f: 25% of notes met national standards; 63% met hospital criteria
audits.c: Teaching, changed admission proforma, and rewritten hospital guidelines for delirium
audits.r2: 41% met national standards and 87% met hospital criteria at 18 months (at 6 months: 52% national, 82% hospital)

audits.t: Impact of long-term care facilities' size on adherence to COVID-19' infection prevention guidance.
audits.tp: Adherence to WHO COVID-19 infection prevention guidance in care facilities
audits.st: World Health Organization Infection Prevention and Control guidance for COVID-19
audits.f: 308/362 (85.1%) facilities adhered to 14 or more of 20 recommendations (classified excellent); adherence was lower in larger facilities for symptom screening (p=0.037) and isolation of positive visitors (p=0.032).

audits.t: Long term outcomes of chronic pain patients attending a publicly funded community-based interdisciplinary pain program in the Greater Toronto area: results of a practice-based audit.
audits.tp: Interdisciplinary chronic pain programme outcomes audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 158 patients completed the programme; global impression of change (much/very much improved) was 77% at exit, 58% at 6 months, 76% at 12 months post-discharge.

audits.t: Impact of respiratory therapists-driven assess-and-treat protocol on unplanned adult neurovascular ICU readmissions: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Respiratory therapist protocol to reduce ICU readmissions
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Retrospective review found respiratory-related causes were the leading cause of unexpected ICU readmissions in adult neurovascular patients at baseline.
audits.c: Respiratory therapist-driven assess-and-treat protocol with standardised algorithm
audits.r2: No effect on rate of unexpected ICU readmissions; intervention group showed significant improvement in respiratory severity scores (p<0.01); ICU stay comparable (4.5 vs 4 days, p=0.42).

audits.t: Rational use of antibiotics for major elective gynaecological and obstetrical surgical procedures: quality improvement journey from a tertiary care public facility.
audits.tp: Surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis for gynaecological/obstetric surgery
audits.st: Single-dose surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis (SSAP) guideline for elective major gynaecological and obstetrical surgery, target >60%
audits.f: Baseline SSAP use was 2.1%.
audits.c: Root cause analysis, departmental antimicrobial policy, awareness sessions/lectures/workshops, antimicrobial stewardship team
audits.r2: SSAP increased from 2.1% to 67.7% within 6 months, sustained at 80-90% for more than 2 years without increase in SSI rate.

audits.t: An initiative to reduce medication errors in neonatal care unit of a tertiary care hospital, Kolkata, West Bengal: a quality improvement report.
audits.st: POCQI (WHO) model for medication error reduction, target <10%
audits.f: Baseline total error was 71.1/100 prescriptions (median medication error percentage 63%).
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles including training of doctors and nurses, signature/countersignature, computer-generated and software-generated prescriptions
audits.r2: Median medication error percentages across 4 PDSA cycles were 48%, 42%, 30%, 14%; total error reduced to 10.4/100 prescriptions.

audits.t: Quality improvement in Kangaroo Mother Care: learning from a teaching hospital.
audits.st: Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) coverage target, revised to 80% for 6-hour KMC
audits.f: Baseline 6-hour KMC coverage was 30%; baseline 1-hour KMC coverage was 20%.
audits.c: PDSA cycles customising KMC tools (book format, bag, mother's gown), training and minimising interruptions
audits.r2: 6-hour KMC coverage increased from 30% to 80% within 12 weeks, sustained at 76.5%±2.49% for over 2 years (January 2018-February 2020); 1-hour KMC coverage reached 100% within 15 days.

audits.t: Adherence to Prescribing Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy at Hospital Discharge in Subjects With Acute Coronary Syndrome, and the Relationship With Mortality.
audits.tp: Guideline-directed medical therapy adherence after ACS
audits.st: International guideline recommendations for guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) after acute coronary syndrome
audits.f: Adherence to GDMT achieved in 70.87% of subjects; highest for statins (95.22%), lowest for ACEIs/ARBs (81.09%); adherence associated with fewer deaths (OR=0.38, CI 0.16-0.93).

audits.t: A standardized implementation of multicenter quality improvement program of very low birth weight newborns could significantly reduce admission hypothermia and improve outcomes.
audits.tp: Admission hypothermia prevention in VLBW infants
audits.st: Hypothermia prevention bundle for very low birth weight (VLBW) infants
audits.f: Pre-QI incidence of admission hypothermia was 95.9%.
audits.c: Hypothermia prevention bundle implemented 1 January 2019 via sequential PDSA approach
audits.r2: Post-QI incidence of admission hypothermia decreased to 71.3%; mortality risk ratio 0.26 (95% CI 0.13-0.50); late-onset sepsis risk ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.50-0.87).

audits.t: Coaching quality improvement in primary care to improve hypertension control.
audits.tp: QI coaching for hypertension control in primary care
audits.st: Hypertension guidelines for accurate blood pressure measurement, effective treatment and timely follow-up
audits.f: Baseline uncontrolled hypertension rate greater than 50% in Ohio Medicaid practices
audits.c: PDSA cycles facilitated by QI coaching and APRN collaboration over 18 months in two practice sites, implementing accurate blood pressure measurement, effective treatment and timely follow-up
audits.r2: Percentage of patients with controlled hypertension, repeat blood pressure measurement, and timely follow-up improved (exact figures not reported)

audits.t: Sustaining immediate newborn care processes (delayed cord clamping and early breastfeeding initiation) in the delivery room: a quality improvement study.
audits.tp: Delayed cord clamping and early breastfeeding initiation
audits.st: Delayed cord clamping (DCC) and early breastfeeding initiation (EBFI) evidence-based newborn care practices
audits.f: Baseline DCC was 25% (median); baseline EBFI was 50% (median).
audits.c: Sensitisation, adding DCC to pre-birth checklist, and daily dashboard recording of outcomes via 3 PDSA cycles
audits.r2: DCC improved from 25% to 96% over 2 years; EBFI improved from 50% to 97%.

audits.t: The PONTE (PDTA FOR INTEGRATED FOLLOW-UP TERRITORY HOSPITAL OF THE PATIENT WITH CARDIAC HEART FAILURE) (BRIDGE) Heart Failure project: increased adherence to guideline-recommended therapies through web-based shared clinical database.
audits.st: Guideline-recommended drug therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
audits.f: At 1-year follow-up, 91% assuming beta-blockers, 86% mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, 98% ACEI/ARB/ARNI; ARNI prescription 13% overall.
audits.c: Web-based shared clinical database (PONTE project) linking hospital and district cardiologists
audits.r2: ARNI prescription increased from 13% (before 2020) to 60% (2021), p<0.001; 30% of patients had ARNI prescribed before discharge.

audits.t: Quality Improvement Initiative to Improve Initiation and Acceptability of Noninvasive Ventilation in Critically Ill Children.
audits.tp: Quality improvement for noninvasive ventilation acceptability in critically ill children
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: NIV failure in 5/12 (42%) patients
audits.c: Process changes including adherence to a checklist, monitoring, and a one-day orientation programme (phase 2), with increased use of sedation
audits.r2: NIV failure decreased to 2/25 (8%) patients (p=0.025 vs phase 1)

audits.t: Compliance with the surgical safety checklist in Switzerland: an observational multicenter study based on self-reported data.
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (Sign In, Team Time Out, Sign Out)
audits.f: Overall mean compliance rate was 91% (applied/partially applied vs not applied); Sign In 93%, Team Time Out 94%, Sign Out 86%; all three sections applied in 79% of interventions.
audits.c: Peer observation and feedback as part of a quality improvement project

audits.t: Teledermatology to reduce face-to-face appointments in general practice during the COVID-19 pandemic: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Teledermatology quality improvement in general practice
audits.st: Local QI targets: >80% remote consultations concluded remotely, <50% face-to-face dermatology consultations
audits.f: Baseline percentages not separately reported; overall 170 telephone consultations with 308 supporting images
audits.c: '4 Key Instructions' and patient information leaflet to improve image quality; triage pathway guidance tool for reception staff
audits.r2: Primary outcome (>80% concluded remotely) achieved; face-to-face consultations could not be reduced much below 50% without high-quality images

audits.t: Audit of flexible laryngoscopy use and decontamination using a chlorine dioxide wipe system during COVID-19: Assessing the risk of disease transmission.
audits.st: ENT UK decontamination guidelines for flexible nasoendoscopes
audits.f: 93%-100% compliance with decontamination guidelines; no evidence of nosocomial SARS-CoV-2 transmission among 544 patients or 22 staff

audits.t: Evaluation of risk stratification and adherence to venous thromboembolism prophylaxis among hospitalized obstetric women: Retrospective case file review at East Jeddah Hospital during 2018-2019.
audits.tp: VTE risk stratification and prophylaxis adherence in obstetrics
audits.st: Local hospital venous thromboembolism (VTE) thromboprophylaxis protocol
audits.f: Thromboprophylaxis was ordered for 21.3% of antenatal and 23.7% of postnatal patients; risk documentation adherence was 95% antenatal vs 83.6% postnatal (p=0.000).

audits.t: Adherence to national malaria clinical management and testing guidelines in selected private clinics of Gambela Town, Gambela Region, Ethiopia: a mixed method study.
audits.tp: Malaria clinical management and testing guideline adherence
audits.st: National malaria clinical management and testing guidelines
audits.f: Only 65% of 430 suspected malaria cases were tested; 85% of workers claimed adherence to guidelines but only 40% had been trained on guideline content.

audits.t: Improvement of Hand Hygiene Compliance Using the Plan-Do-Study-Act Method: Quality Improvement Project From a Tertiary Care Institute in Bihar, India.
audits.st: WHO/CDC hand hygiene recommendations
audits.f: Pre-intervention hand hygiene compliance was 40.6%.
audits.c: Root cause analysis (fishbone), 3 PDSA cycles targeting awareness, dispenser location and forgetfulness
audits.r2: Post-intervention hand hygiene compliance increased to 69.8% (p<0.0001), sustained; improvement significant in all HCW categories except doctors.

audits.t: Improving viral load testing using a quality improvement approach in Blantyre, Malawi.
audits.st: WHO-recommended viral load testing coverage, target 80%
audits.f: Baseline viral load testing coverage was 27%.
audits.c: Re-orienting ART providers on VL test order in EMR and a dedicated ART provider for VL-tested patients, via 5 PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Viral load testing coverage increased from 27% to 71% by end of study.

audits.t: Lack of Adherence to Guideline-Based Imaging Before Subsequent Radiation in Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Impact on Patient Outcomes.
audits.tp: Guideline-based imaging before radiotherapy in NSCLC
audits.st: National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) recommendation for 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging before subsequent radiation therapy in NSCLC
audits.f: 43.6% of patients were imaged with CT alone instead of the guideline-recommended PET/CT before subsequent radiotherapy; PET/CT was associated with improved cancer-specific survival (hazard ratio 1.43, 95% CI 1.32-1.55)

audits.t: The National Audit of Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC) in the United Kingdom: Defining the Audit Dataset and Data Collection System.
audits.tp: National audit of primary biliary cholangitis care
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) primary biliary cholangitis management guidelines
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Development of a checklist for auditing completion of patient report forms: A Delphi study.
audits.tp: Patient report form completion checklist development
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Implementing use of sucrose analgesia (non-pharmacological management of neonatal pain) in a standalone private facility level 3 neonatal care unit using point of care quality improvement methodology.
audits.tp: Sucrose analgesia for neonatal procedural pain
audits.st: Local QI aim: increase compliance with sucrose analgesia for 4 painful procedures (IV cannulation, tracheal suctioning, tape removal, phlebotomy) from 0% to >80% within 8 weeks, informed by Cochrane evidence for sucrose analgesia
audits.f: 0% of eligible neonates received sucrose analgesia before painful procedures
audits.c: Point-of-care QI methodology with 8 PDSA cycles: staff/doctor training, testing of administration methods (settling on prefilled syringes/vials fixed to warmers), bedside sucrose-availability tracking on handover sheets, pharmacy stock assurance, a bedside documentation checklist, a standard operating procedure for new staff, consultant audit rounds, and daily team huddles
audits.r2: Compliance rose to 96.27% by the end of the 8-week study (97.5% IV cannulation, 94% tracheal suction, 100% phlebotomy, 93.6% tape removal); sustained above 80% over the following 4 years

audits.t: Reducing Early Antibiotic Use: A Quality Improvement Initiative in a Level III Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
audits.st: European guidelines for prudent antimicrobial use, with process indicators (early antibiotics, antibiotics >3 days, no antibiotics) benchmarked against the Pediatrix Group 100,000 Babies Campaign
audits.f: Early antibiotics given to 91% of VLBW infants; antibiotics continued beyond 3 days despite negative culture in 53%; only 6% of infants received no antibiotics during their NICU stay
audits.c: Departmental protocol updates (2015: early suspension of antibiotics at 72 hours if blood culture negative; 2018: no antibiotics for VLBW infants at low risk of early-onset sepsis) plus a surveillance system from 2017 (daily audit, discharge report check, coding, annual feedback)
audits.r2: Early antibiotics fell to 49% (46% relative reduction, p<0.001); antibiotics beyond 3 days fell to 5% (90% relative reduction, p<0.001); no-antibiotics rate rose to 30% (fivefold increase, p<0.001)

audits.t: Quality improvement in juvenile idiopathic arthritis: a mixed-methods implementation pilot of the CAPTURE-JIA dataset.
audits.tp: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis data collection for quality improvement
audits.st: National JIA audit questions
audits.f: 14/62 data items had >40% missing data; feasible but time-consuming
audits.r2: Data appeared complete; system reported easy to use

audits.t: Improving pain management in a neonatal intensive care unit with single-family room-A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Neonatal pain assessment and management guideline adherence
audits.st: COMFORTneo-based pain assessment and management guidelines
audits.f: Baseline: only 10% of sick term and preterm infants were assessed for pain and stress daily; parental involvement in procedures was 50.3% before.
audits.c: Translation of COMFORTneo, guideline/flowchart development, staff certification, and supervision on parental involvement
audits.r2: 88.8% of COMFORTneo assessments performed according to guidelines; parental involvement increased to 82.3%; inter-rater kappa 0.81-0.95 (median 0.90).

audits.t: Improving Blood Product Transfusion Premedication Plan Documentation: A Single-institution Quality Improvement Effort.
audits.st: Institutional premedication plan documentation target of 80%
audits.f: Baseline premedication plan documentation was 19%; 34% of patients received premedication.
audits.c: Computerized provider order entry alert, clinical care pathway development, and clinician education
audits.r2: Premedication plan documentation increased from 19% to 87%; premedication administration decreased from 34% to 25%; no change in transfusion reaction rate (1.8 per 100 transfusions).

audits.t: High-stage Device-related Pressure Injury Reduction in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Device-related pressure injury reduction in the NICU
audits.st: Solutions for Patient Safety (SPS) Network benchmark for high-stage hospital-acquired pressure injuries; local aim to reduce device-related high-stage HAPI rate by 30% within 12 months
audits.f: Baseline high-stage HAPI rate 0.98 per 1000 patient days (above SPS network average of 0.107); device-related high-stage HAPI rate 0.94 per 1000 patient days, accounting for 84% of all high-stage pressure injuries
audits.c: Interprofessional QI bundles developed via PDSA cycles: an EEG monitoring bundle (specialised electrode kit, transparent contact dressing, pressure-relieving mattress overlay, application checklist, earlier electrode removal) and a respiratory device bundle (foam dressing, device fit assessment, scheduled CPAP mask/prong rotation, two-provider pressure point checks), plus Braden QD risk scoring and monthly active skin surveillance
audits.r2: Device-related high-stage HAPI rate fell 60% to 0.37 per 1000 patient days, exceeding the 30% target; EEG-related and CPAP-related high-stage HAPI rates both fell to 0 and were sustained for 10 months

audits.t: Improving Blood Pressure Screening in Neonatal Follow-up Clinic: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Blood pressure screening in neonatal follow-up
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics blood pressure screening recommendation for children with history of prematurity/NICU care
audits.f: Baseline: only 15.3% of patients had documented blood pressure.
audits.c: Standardised blood pressure measurement protocol, staff training/education, streamlined documentation via 2 PDSA cycles

audits.t: Improving Adherence to AAP Acute Otitis Media Guidelines in an Academic Pediatrics Practice through a Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: AAP Acute Otitis Media guidelines (2013), target 90%
audits.f: Baseline 78% of AOM patients met AAP guidelines; 20% of eligible patients received a safety-net antibiotic prescription (SNAP).
audits.c: Ear pain note template with guideline-based recommendations, staff education sessions, workstation reminders
audits.r2: Adherence to AAP AOM guidelines increased from 78% to 92%; SNAP use among eligible patients increased from 21% to 78% (n=421); note template use increased from 0% to 44%.

audits.t: Application of lean management after audit of Medical Records Department in a COVID19 dedicated center during the COVID pandemic.
audits.tp: Medical records department audit and lean management
audits.st: Medical records department norms (space, staffing standards)
audits.f: MRD had 13 current processes, 26 wastes identified, and 10 values; deficiencies found in physical examination, history, radiology and laboratory report documentation.
audits.c: Lean management application with process mapping and staff recommendations

audits.t: Audit of waiting time-to-treatment of atypical endometrial hyperplasia.
audits.st: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists and NZ Ministry of Health Faster Cancer Treatment standards (62-day referral-to-treatment; 31-day decision-to-treat)
audits.f: Only 18% met the 62-day referral-to-treatment target and 56% met the 31-day decision-to-treat target; surgical standards of care were met for 55 women managed surgically.

audits.t: Adherence to pre-operative fasting guidelines and associated factors among pediatric surgical patients in selected public referral hospitals, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: Cross sectional study.
audits.tp: Pre-operative fasting guideline adherence in paediatric surgery
audits.st: International pre-operative fasting guidelines for paediatric anaesthesia
audits.f: 89.96% (n=251) of pediatric patients did not follow fasting guidelines; mean fasting time for clear liquids was 10±4.03 hours (guideline typically recommends ~2 hours).

audits.t: Quality of surgical management of placenta accreta spectrum in a tertiary center in Sri Lanka: baseline study for quality improvement project: problems and solutions.
audits.tp: Placenta accreta spectrum multidisciplinary care quality
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Care bundle for PAS evaluated in all cases; 82% had elective surgery; 85% received blood transfusions; mean total hospital stay 19.5 days (SD 11.4).
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team meeting to formulate a comprehensive care plan

audits.t: Hand Hygiene Auditing: Is It a Roadway to Improve Adherence to Hand Hygiene Among Hospital Personnel?
audits.st: WHO 5 Moments hand hygiene compliance standard
audits.f: Overall hand hygiene complete adherence rate was 29.9% (11,981/39,998); partial adherence rate 45.3%; non-adherence rate 24.7%.

audits.t: System-Level Quality Improvement Initiatives for Tobacco Use in a Safety-Net Health System During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
audits.st: Guideline-recommended tobacco cessation care (screening and counselling)
audits.f: Tobacco screening was 29% and in-person visits 20% at pandemic onset.
audits.c: Direct patient telephone outreach and increased staff capacity for cessation care delivery
audits.r2: Tobacco screening increased from 29% to 74%; best practice cessation care increased by 23% overall (24% for African American/Black patients, 23% for others).

audits.t: Management of Acute Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Survey to Assess Adherence to Guidelines Across the United Kingdom and Ireland.
audits.tp: Lower GI bleeding management guideline adherence
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) 2019 lower GI bleeding (LGIB) management guidance
audits.f: 64.1% (n=41) said BSG CG 2019 was practically applicable; ~75% did not use or were unaware of Shock Index/Oakland score; 37% were unaware of the interventional radiology referral pathway.

audits.t: The Design of an Audit Test for 60Co Brachytherapy Treatment Planning System.
audits.tp: Brachytherapy treatment planning system dosimetry audit
audits.st: Dosimetry audit tolerance level for 60Co HDR brachytherapy treatment planning system (pass <5%)
audits.f: 80% of measured dose points were within the 5% pass level; 20% were out of tolerance (between 5% and 6.99%).

audits.t: Passive order auditing associated with reductions in red blood cell utilization: National blood shortage experience.
audits.tp: Passive alert auditing for red blood cell transfusion
audits.st: Hemoglobin transfusion threshold lowered from 7.0 g/dL to 6.5 g/dL for stable, nonbleeding inpatients during blood shortage
audits.f: 5182 full-unit RBC transfusions; 50.3% single-unit transfusions
audits.c: Passive alert system modified to activate at a lower hemoglobin threshold (6.5 g/dL instead of 7.0 g/dL)
audits.r2: Full unit RBC transfusions decreased 15% to 4421; 49.8% single-unit; average pre-transfusion hemoglobin decreased from 7.18 to 7.05 g/dL (p=0.0002)

audits.t: Implementing the HEART score in an NHS emergency department: can identity leadership combined with quality improvement promote racial equality?
audits.tp: HEART score implementation for chest pain pathway
audits.st: Implementation of the HEART score (HS) as a standardised risk-stratification protocol for chest pain patients
audits.f: Staff survey identified reasons for lack of implementation of a clinical protocol for chest pain patients
audits.c: Implementation of the HEART score via Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycles over nine months, combined with identity leadership approach
audits.r2: 60% reduction in waiting time for chronic chest pain patients in the emergency department

audits.t: Quality improvement initiative to address bed shortage in the maternity ward at the National Referral Hospital.
audits.tp: Postoperative discharge process for low-risk caesarean section
audits.st: Second-day postoperative discharge target of 25% for low-risk caesarean section mothers (modified ERAS)
audits.f: Pre-intervention second-day postoperative discharge was 0%.
audits.c: Modified enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) implemented via PDSA cycle after fishbone analysis
audits.r2: Second-day postoperative discharge increased to median 65.5% (IQR 45-80); daily waiting obstetric patients decreased from median 6.0 to 1.0 (p=0.0001).

audits.t: A quality improvement project reduces time spent at an inflammatory bowel disease infusion center with accelerated infliximab infusion protocol.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Standard protocol mean infliximab infusion time was 2.4h (142±14 min).
audits.c: Accelerated infliximab infusion protocol and change of collection location for infliximab
audits.r2: Mean infliximab infusion time reduced by 47% to 1.2h (75±10 min), p<0.05.

audits.t: Analysis of Radiology Report Recommendation Characteristics and Rate of Recommended Action Performance.
audits.st: Institutional practice of documenting actionable follow-up recommendations in a dedicated radiology report field, with the target that all recommended actions be carried out (loop closure)
audits.f: Overall loop closure rate 87.4%; 31 open-loop cases (5.2%) judged to pose substantial clinical risk; loop closure was lower for repeat-imaging recommendations (81.8%), those with contingency language (81.9% vs 89.7% unconditional), and time frames over 1 year (76.1% vs 87.4%)

audits.t: Audit of Data Sharing by Pharmaceutical Companies for Anticancer Medicines Approved by the US Food and Drug Administration.
audits.st: Industry data-sharing policy eligibility for individual participant data (IPD) sharing
audits.f: 136/304 (45%) trials were eligible for IPD sharing; 168 (55%) were not, most commonly because long-term follow-up data collection was ongoing (89/168, 53%).

audits.t: Developing a trigger tool to monitor adverse events during haemodialysis in children: a pilot project.
audits.tp: Adverse event monitoring during paediatric haemodialysis (trigger tool)
audits.st: Locally developed 'Evelina London paediatric Haemodialysis Trigger Tool' (pHTT, 54 triggers across 6 domains), adapted from a published adult haemodialysis trigger tool
audits.f: 139 triggers identified; harm rate per session 1.03 (94/91); top triggers included failure to have nursing safety huddle (16.5%), high ultrafiltration rate (10.8%), need for tissue plasminogen activator (9.4%)
audits.c: Interventions informed by first cycle results: regular multidisciplinary dialysis education days, re-evaluation of estimated target weights, adherence to safety huddles, and liaison with laboratory/IT/biomedical teams to reduce result delays and machine failures
audits.r2: 102 triggers identified; harm rate per session significantly reduced to 0.32 (29/91), p<0.001; trigger rate per session fell from 1.53 to 1.12 (p=0.001)

audits.t: Efficiency in the Endoscopy Unit: Can We 'Turn Around' Room Turnover? An Observational Quality Improvement Study.
audits.st: Institutional targets: non-procedure time (NPT) of 15 minutes or less and turnover time (TT) of 5 minutes or less between cases
audits.f: Median NPT 19 minutes (IQR 16-22), with 75% of cases exceeding the 15-minute target; median TT 6 minutes (IQR 4-9), with 60% of cases exceeding the 5-minute target; variation attributable to individual endoscopists was 14.7% for NPT and 3.9% for TT, with 80.4%/93.2% of variation unexplained by measured factors
audits.c: not reported (this was an observational/diagnostic phase; a planned next phase involving focus groups and direct observation had not yet tested or re-measured any intervention)

audits.t: Compliance to Infection Prevention and Control Practices Among Healthcare Workers During COVID-19 Pandemic in Malaysia.
audits.tp: COVID-19 infection prevention and control compliance among healthcare workers
audits.st: WHO Interim Guidance on infection prevention and control for COVID-19
audits.f: 63.7% of healthcare workers were compliant with IPC; non-compliance associated with working in emergency department (AOR 3.16), laboratory (AOR 15.13), and inadequate PPE training (AOR 2.02).

audits.t: Development of a Standardized Clinical Assessment and Management Plan for Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
audits.tp: Standardized management plan for paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome
audits.st: Pediatric Acute Lung Injury Consensus Conference (PALICC) definitions and institutional ventilator management guidelines (tidal volume)
audits.f: False best practice alert rate 66.7% (68/102)
audits.c: Standardized Clinical Assessment and Management Plan (SCAMP) methodology with a best practice alert (BPA) in the EHR and iterative PDSA cycles
audits.r2: False BPA alert rate decreased to 29.2% (19/65); statistical process control chart showed a shift in adherence with the tidal volume guideline

audits.t: Lessons learned from the perinatal audit of uterine rupture in the Netherlands: A mixed-method study.
audits.st: National and local clinical guidelines and professional standards for labour management
