audits.f: Audit revealed 178 improvable factors and 200 recommendations; 6% (n=11) of improvable factors were very likely related to the outcome, 18% (n=32) likely.

audits.t: Integrating hypertension and HIV care in Namibia: A quality improvement collaborative approach.
audits.tp: Hypertension screening and treatment integration in HIV care
audits.st: National hypertension treatment guidelines (screening/treatment target for people with HIV)
audits.f: Hypertension screening occurred in 86% of encounters; among 1759 people newly diagnosed with hypertension, 992 (56%) were initiated on treatment (61% at facilities with an on-site physician vs 51% without).
audits.c: Quality improvement collaborative with monthly performance measurement, coaching and learning sessions, 14 identified interventions

audits.t: National audit on maternal mortality in Guinea-Bissau, West-Africa: A retrospective observational study of 2020.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Hospitals under EU/PIMI-II showed lower maternal mortality ratio than previous national figures (previously 900/100,000 live births per UNICEF 2014)
audits.c: EU Integrated Programme to reduce Maternal and Infant Mortality (EU/PIMI)

audits.t: International Guideline Adherence in Girls with Turner Syndrome: Multiple Subspecialty Clinics Versus Coordinated Multidisciplinary Clinic.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence in Turner syndrome screening
audits.st: 2016 Cincinnati International Turner syndrome consensus guideline (9 age-appropriate screening recommendations)
audits.f: 42% of girls met all 9 screening recommendations; multidisciplinary clinic (MDC)-managed girls had higher adherence for 7 of 9 screenings (e.g. TSH 95% vs 78%, p=0.034)
audits.c: Single-day coordinated multidisciplinary clinic (MDC) format versus multiple subspecialty clinics

audits.t: 2-Dimensional IMRT dose audit: An Indonesian multicenter study.
audits.st: AAPM TG-119 structure sets; gamma index tolerance criteria of 3%/3mm and 3%/2mm
audits.f: 100% gamma index passing rate mostly in 3%/3mm evaluations; passing rates dropped in the 3%/2mm analysis; most centres satisfied the tolerance limit of the action level

audits.t: Improving the Quality of Electronic Medical Record Documentation: Development of a Compliance and Quality Program.
audits.tp: Electronic medical record documentation quality and compliance programme
audits.st: Expected practices for EMR documentation quality and completeness (>80% classified as good)
audits.f: 5 of 9 nursing/midwifery and 4 of 10 medical documentation components were classified as good (>80%)
audits.c: Iterative quality improvement programme using Model for Improvement PDSA cycles, an audit tool, and targeted intervention activities

audits.t: Quality Improvement: Implementing Nurse Standard Work in Emergency Department Fast-Track Area to Reduce Patient Length of Stay.
audits.tp: Emergency department fast-track length of stay
audits.st: Local Lean/A3 target: average length of stay (ALOS) of 162 minutes in the fast-track area (average demand plus 1 SD); national left-without-being-seen (LWBS) standard of under 2%
audits.f: ALOS 205 minutes; LWBS 4.7% in October 2018; registered nurse and nurse technician walking time for supplies 272 and 422 seconds respectively
audits.c: Nurse Standard Work (NSW) developed via A3/Lean problem-solving: standardised takt-time-based task sequences for nurse and nurse technician roles, 5S-organised supply storerooms with par levels, reassignment of patient-pulling and radiology-prep tasks to the nurse technician, earlier registration/discharge process changes, and elimination of provider order batching, sustained via daily manager audits
audits.r2: ALOS fell to 150.4 minutes in the 7 months after implementation (below the 162-minute target); walking time for supplies fell to 30 and 25 seconds for RN and nurse technician respectively; LWBS fell to 0.7% by March 2020

audits.t: Audit and feedback as a tool to increase compliance with carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (CPE) screening and decrease CPE transmission in the hospital.
audits.st: In-hospital CPE (carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae) screening guidelines
audits.f: Baseline compliance with CPE screening not separately reported (before real-time audit and feedback strategy from 1 January 2017).
audits.c: Real-time audit and feedback towards compliance with in-hospital CPE screening guidelines
audits.r2: Compliance with CPE screening increased from 74% in 2017 to 92% in 2018 and 95% in 2019 (statistically significant).

audits.t: Costs and Clinical Consequences of Compliance with COPD GOLD Recommendations or National Guidelines Compared with Current Clinical Practice in Belgium, Germany, Sweden, and the United States.
audits.st: GOLD 2022 recommendations and national COPD guidelines
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Timely intervention, monitoring and education MATTERS in MS (TIME MATTERS in MS): Development of a globally applicable quality improvement tool.
audits.tp: MS quality improvement benchmarking tool piloting
audits.st: Consensus MS care standards (from MS specialist neurologists, 19 countries)
audits.f: Over 50% of responders rated the tool 'very easy'/'easy' to use and 'very relevant'; 85% (11/13) planned to introduce service changes
audits.c: Piloting a refined Excel-based quality improvement benchmarking tool

audits.t: An Audit of Delays in the Management of Non-Metastatic Osteosarcoma at a Tertiary Care Center in South India.
audits.st: Hypothesised/expected time targets for MRI, neoadjuvant chemotherapy, surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy in osteosarcoma management
audits.f: Mean time to MRI 11.3±6.7 days (>7 days in 68%); mean time to NACT 15.3±12.7 days (>7 days in 74%); mean time to surgery 31.1±15.3 days (>21 days in 83%); mean time to ACT 29.7±10.1 days (>21 days in 82%).

audits.t: Increasing statin prescription rates to prevent cardiovascular disease among high-risk populations: a quality improvement intervention centred on a novel interactive tool.
audits.tp: Statin prescription rate for cardiovascular prevention
audits.st: Cholesterol/statin prescribing guidelines for primary and secondary ASCVD prevention
audits.f: Pre-intervention statin prescription rate was 82.3%; only one-third had follow-up cholesterol levels ordered (33.3%); one in five patients not prescribed appropriate statin therapy.
audits.c: Online interactive tool, physician education, guideline summary display, EHR documentation reminder
audits.r2: Statin prescription rate improved to 90.5% (p=0.006); 10-year ASCVD risk score documentation increased to 72.3% (p=0.039); follow-up cholesterol ordering increased to 64.1% (p<0.001).

audits.t: Team Science Principles Enhance Cancer Care Delivery Quality Improvement: Interdisciplinary Implementation of Breast Cancer Screening Shared Decision Making.
audits.tp: Shared decision-making implementation for breast cancer screening
audits.st: National guidelines recommending shared decision making in screening mammography for women aged 40-49
audits.f: Breast Cancer Risk Estimator shared decision-making tool was deemed valuable by 87% of patients surveyed
audits.c: Two iterative PDSA cycles developing and implementing a shared decision-making tool using team science principles
audits.r2: Tool utilisation increased from 2,000 sessions (2017) to 4,097 sessions (2019), while early-stage breast cancer diagnoses were maintained

audits.t: Improving Compliance with the CMS SEP-1 Sepsis Bundle at a Community-Based Teaching Hospital Emergency Department.
audits.st: CMS SEP-1 sepsis bundle compliance target
audits.f: Pre-intervention SEP-1 compliance was 57% (SD 0.27), met in 50% of months.
audits.c: Sepsis Macro and Sepsis Order Set in the EMR plus educational initiative for emergency medicine physicians
audits.r2: Post-intervention SEP-1 compliance improved to 62% (SD 0.11), met in 82% of months, though not statistically significant (p=0.562).

audits.t: Counseling Tobacco Smoke Exposure Reduction Measures in Pediatrics: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Tobacco smoke exposure screening and counselling
audits.st: AAP recommendation for tobacco smoke exposure (TSE) assessment and counselling at clinic visits
audits.f: Baseline TSE screening was 46%; physician counselling on TSE reduction was offered to only 44% of smoking caregivers.
audits.c: Refined patient intake passport and educational handout in electronic record, via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: TSE screening increased from 46% to 85%; TSE reduction counselling increased from 44% to 80%.

audits.t: Institutionalising maternal and newborn quality-of-care standards in Bangladesh, Ghana and Tanzania: a quasi-experimental study.
audits.tp: Maternal and newborn quality-of-care standards institutionalisation
audits.st: UNICEF/WHO Every Mother Every Newborn Quality Improvement (EMEN-QI) standards, target 75%
audits.f: Institutionalisation score 61%
audits.c: Provider-led implementation of EMEN-QI standards package
audits.r2: Institutionalisation score 80% (exceeding 75% target); newborn case-fatality fell 25% in Bangladesh (p=0.017) and 85% in Tanzania

audits.t: Radiation Monitoring Using Personal Dosimeter Devices in Terms of Long-Term Compliance and Creating a Culture of Safety.
audits.st: ICRP/NCRP occupational radiation exposure limits (20 mSv/year ICRP, 50 mSv/year NCRP) and local dosimeter-wearing policy
audits.f: Average 6-month cumulative doses 3.90, 2.55 and 2.02 mSv across the three systems (all below limits when annualised); 94.4% of physicians admitted not consistently using their dosimeter
audits.c: Policy change removing penalties for exceeding recommended radiation dose, replaced with monthly educational sessions on radiation risks and protective measures
audits.r2: Average 6-month cumulative doses rose to 13.9, 10.9 and 8.56 mSv (255-328% increases), with two of three systems exceeding the annual 20 mSv limit when annualised; physicians reporting consistent dosimeter use rose to 83.9%, 90.2% and 93.8%; radiation knowledge test scores rose from 49% to 84%

audits.t: 'Mali Matters': reflections on a leadership and quality improvement project to improve blood transfusion safety at Maluti Adventist Hospital, Mapoteng, Lesotho.
audits.st: Locally developed pre-transfusion bedside safety checklist target
audits.f: Baseline process mapping identified existing transfusion process gaps (no numeric baseline given)
audits.c: Introduction of a pre-transfusion bedside safety checklist and staff training via PDSA methodology, supported by NHS 'Improving Global Health' leadership programme
audits.r2: Bedside safety checklist completion reached 65.5% by 3 months; knowledge scores improved post-transfusion training; 77% of staff strongly agreed and 21% agreed the training was useful

audits.t: Compliance to donning and doffing of personal protective equipment among dental healthcare practitioners during the coronavirus pandemic: a quality improvement plan, do, study and act (PDSA) Initiative.
audits.st: CDC-approved donning and doffing protocols for personal protective equipment
audits.f: Baseline compliance with CDC-approved donning and doffing assessed before educational session (baseline percentages not individually reported).
audits.c: Educational session explaining stepwise donning and doffing guidelines, via PDSA cycle
audits.r2: 44.55% improvement in hand hygiene before wearing PPE after the educational session; 7.4% improvement for removing jewellery, gown and cap; no improvement in mask tie security, hand washing after respirator, or goggle/face shield placement.

audits.t: Full-text publications of presentations at neuroanesthesia meetings of India: A 5-year audit and analysis.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 17.5% (40/229) of conference abstracts were subsequently published as full-text papers.

audits.t: "Death audit is a fight" - provider perspectives on the ethics of the Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response (MPDSR) system in Ethiopia.
audits.tp: Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response audit ethics
audits.st: Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response (MPDSR) system
audits.f: Qualitative study; providers described fear of punishment/blame during death auditing and perceived the process did not reduce perinatal deaths (no numerical compliance data).

audits.t: Guideline adherence in febrile children below 3 months visiting European Emergency Departments: an observational multicenter study.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence in febrile children under 3 months
audits.st: NICE guideline for fever (or local guidelines) in febrile children
audits.f: Adherence: blood cultures 43% (374/868), lumbar punctures 29% (144/491), antibiotic prescriptions 55% (270/492), admission 67% (573/859); full adherence 15%, partial adherence 56%

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Unneeded Screening Chest Radiographs in a Pediatric Cardiovascular ICU.
audits.tp: Reducing unneeded screening chest radiographs in paediatric ICU
audits.st: Target to reduce unneeded daily screening chest radiographs in mechanically ventilated patients by 20% in 6 months
audits.f: Baseline 67% of subjects received a daily screening chest radiograph
audits.c: Criteria for daily screening chest radiograph need added to the daily rounding sheet for discussion; increased documentation of endotracheal tube positioning
audits.r2: Daily screening chest radiograph rate decreased to 44%, with no change in unplanned extubations; estimated $250,000 annual savings

audits.t: Impact of conducting hand hygiene audit in COVID-19 care locations of India-A large scale national multicentric study - HHAC study.
audits.tp: Hand hygiene compliance in COVID-19 care
audits.st: WHO hand hygiene audit tool (5 moments)
audits.f: Hand hygiene complete adherence rate (HHCAR) 27.3%; total adherence rate (HHTAR) 59.7%; HHTAR higher in west zone (72.2%), private institutes (65.6%), nurses (61.6%).

audits.t: Development, implementation and evaluation of high-quality virtual preoperative anaesthetic assessment during COVID-19 and beyond: a quality improvement report.
audits.tp: Virtual preoperative anaesthetic assessment during COVID-19
audits.st: Local SMART aim: over 95% of obstetric and gynaecology patients suitable for virtual assessment identified, referred and assessed via the virtual pathway between July 2020 and March 2021
audits.f: no virtual pathway existed; in-person preoperative assessment was standard prior to COVID-19
audits.c: PDSA cycles introducing a virtual (phone/video) preoperative anaesthetic assessment pathway with decision-making tools for patient suitability, a virtual consultation guide including video airway examination protocol, staff training and telehealth platform optimisation
audits.r2: mean rate of virtual assessment 50% (SD ±10); 99.9% of suitable patients correctly identified, referred and assessed (target >95% achieved); DNA rate 0.6% virtual vs 3% in-person; only 5 same-day cancellations and 1 delay among 2805 patients

audits.t: Association between VTE and antibiotic prophylaxis guideline compliance and patient-reported outcomes after total hip and knee arthroplasty: an observational study.
audits.tp: VTE and antibiotic prophylaxis guideline compliance in arthroplasty
audits.st: VTE and antibiotic prophylaxis clinical guidelines for THA/TKA
audits.f: Compliance with VTE guidelines 35%, antibiotic guidelines 13.2%; VTE non-compliance associated with lower 365-day Oxford score (β=-0.76, p=0.009) and lower EQ-5D Index at 90 and 365 days

audits.t: Effectiveness of a quality improvement strategy with implementation of a specific visual tool to promote ICU early mobilization.
audits.st: Institutional early mobilisation (EM) protocol, the 'E' component of the ABCDE bundle, requiring out-of-bed mobilisation of eligible patients without contraindications
audits.f: Non-compliance with the EM protocol 26.97%; patients walking 29.21%; ICU readmission rate 11.24%
audits.c: Multifaceted QI strategy: a visual 'mobility clock' tool showing goal versus achieved mobility level, a mobilisation-awareness week with a patient testimonial, staff education, an inter-unit 'mobilisation challenge', and improved multidisciplinary round communication
audits.r2: Non-compliance fell to 10.11% (p<0.004); patients walking rose to 49.44% (p=0.006); ICU readmission rate fell to 2.25% (p=0.017); no significant change in hospital/ICU length of stay or mortality

audits.t: When a segmentectomy is not a segmentectomy: Quality assurance audit and evaluation of required elements for an anatomic segmentectomy.
audits.tp: Quality assurance audit of anatomic segmentectomy criteria
audits.st: Operative criteria for anatomic segmentectomy: dissection and division of at least one major vascular structure (segmental artery or vein) and the segmental bronchus
audits.f: 219 (80.8%) met criteria for anatomic segmentectomy; 52 (19.2%) were nonanatomic; nonanatomic segmentectomies had smaller margins (1.0 vs 1.5 cm, p=0.02) and fewer lymph nodes (2.0 vs 6.0)

audits.t: An audit of questions asked by participants during the informed consent process for a phase 2/3 COVID-19 vaccine regulatory study at a tertiary referral centre.
audits.tp: Informed consent question content audit in a vaccine trial
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 127/129 participants asked at least one question (295 total); 67% asked about study procedure, 44.9% about vaccine/placebo safety, 2.4% about post-trial access.

audits.t: Real World Management of Anaphylaxis Versus the National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) Guidelines.
audits.st: NICE guidelines for anaphylaxis management
audits.f: All 49 received adrenaline IM appropriately; all 16 children admitted, seen by allergist and given auto-injector when indicated; only 5/33 adults admitted and seen by allergist, none received an adrenaline auto-injector on discharge, only 3/28 discharged adults referred to allergist

audits.t: An audit of frozen sections for suspected gastrointestinal malignancies in a tertiary referral hospital in India.
audits.st: Accuracy of frozen section diagnosis compared with the paraffin section reference standard
audits.f: Correct diagnosis in 1649 (96.77%); 20 (1.17%) deferred; 35 (2.05%) discrepant; sensitivity 91.71%, specificity 99.69%, PPV 98.84%, NPV 97.68%, accuracy 97.92%

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Decrease Time to Analgesia in Patients With Sickle Cell and Vaso-Occlusive Crisis: A Population With Disparities in Treatment.
audits.tp: Time to analgesia in vaso-occlusive crisis
audits.st: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) recommendation of analgesia within 60 minutes of registration for sickle cell VOC, target 75%
audits.f: Pre-intervention, the 60-minute analgesia target was met 17% of the time; average time to initial analgesia was 61 minutes.
audits.c: Rapid evaluation process with notification, multidisciplinary rapid evaluation, and electronic order set, via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Target met 72% of the time during the intervention period; average time to initial analgesia decreased to 42 minutes.

audits.t: Evaluation of an EPID in vivo monitoring system using local and external independent audit measurements.
audits.tp: EPID in vivo dose monitoring independent audit
audits.st: Independent Brazilian governmental radiotherapy dosimetry audit measurements
audits.f: Largest difference between PerFRACTION and reference measurement was 1.2%; against audit TLD measurements, 12 points had variation <2%, 2 points 2-3%, and 2 points >3% (max 3.7%).

audits.t: Palivizumab Prophylaxis for infants 29 to 32 weeks gestation at birth: A 10-year audit from Vancouver Island using BC Guidelines.
audits.tp: Palivizumab prophylaxis audit for preterm infants
audits.st: BC Guidelines for palivizumab (RSV) prophylaxis in infants 29 to 32 weeks gestation
audits.f: 336 (79%) did not receive prophylaxis, of whom 10 (3.0%, 95% CI 1.4-5.4%) had an RSV hospitalisation; 3 of 87 (3.5%, 95% CI 0.7-10%) who received prophylaxis were hospitalised

audits.t: Evaluation of a National Quality Improvement Collaborative for Improving Cancer Screening.
audits.st: Return-to-Screening collaborative target: restore prepandemic monthly screening test volume plus minimum 10% increase
audits.f: During preintervention period (April-May 2021), mean monthly test volume declined (slope -13.1 tests/month, 95% CI -23.1 to -3.2).
audits.c: Nationwide QI collaborative: Return-to-Screening plan-do-study-act protocol with evidence-based screening interventions
audits.r2: 676/859 projects (79%) reached target monthly test volume; intervention associated with immediate slope increase of 101.0 tests/month and sustained increase of 36.3 tests/month.

audits.t: Quality improvement project on the development of a management algorithm for iatrogenic perforations and the long-term impact on physician knowledge.
audits.st: ASGE/ESGE recommendations for acute iatrogenic endoscopic perforation (AIEP) management
audits.f: Pretest knowledge accuracy was 75%.
audits.c: Development and dissemination of an institutional AIEP management algorithm and one-page educational material
audits.r2: Immediate post-test accuracy increased to 95%; knowledge retention assessed again at 6 months with clinical scenario application.

audits.t: Testers' compliance to the quality standards of HIV rapid testing services in Primary Health Care Facilities in Makete District, Tanzania.
audits.tp: HIV rapid testing quality standards compliance
audits.st: Quality standards for HIV rapid testing services
audits.f: 22/23 (95.6%) testing points had lower compliance with quality standards; 1 (4.4%) had moderate compliance; none had high compliance.

audits.t: Implementing the Practice of Birth Companion in Labor During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Quality Improvement Endeavor in India.
audits.tp: Birth companion implementation for respectful maternity care
audits.st: WHO recommendation for respectful maternity care/birth companionship, target 90%
audits.f: Baseline birth companion practice was 0% during the COVID-19 pandemic.
audits.c: PDSA cycles addressing policy absence, guideline awareness, and RTPCR turnaround for relatives
audits.r2: Birth companionship achieved more than 90% during labour.

audits.t: Audit of Clinical Care Received by COVID-19 Patients Treated at a Tertiary Care Hospital of Nepal in 2021.
audits.st: National COVID-19 admission and treatment guidelines
audits.f: 97% of patients were eligible for admission per national guidelines; ~95% of severe patients received corticosteroids, anticoagulants and oxygen; remdesivir use was 22%; D-dimer/CRP missing in ~25% of patients.

audits.t: Implementing an audit and feedback cycle to improve adherence to the Choosing Wisely Canada recommendations: clustered randomized trail.
audits.tp: Choosing Wisely Canada audit and feedback for prescribing
audits.st: Choosing Wisely Canada recommendations (antibiotic prescribing for viral infections; antipsychotic prescribing for dementia)
audits.f: Baseline prescribing rates measured prior to intervention (specific baseline rate not reported as a single figure).
audits.c: Audit and feedback: recommendations summary alone, or recommendations summary plus personalised feedback
audits.r2: 91.6% of intervention group 1 and 95.9% of intervention group 2 reduced prescribing rate by >=1 vs 77.6% of controls (p=0.0073); reduction maintained at 91.4% in 2018/19.

audits.t: Impact of advanced practice nurses in hospital units on compliance with clinical practice guidelines: a quasi-experimental study.
audits.tp: Advanced practice nurse impact on guideline compliance (pressure ulcers and vascular access)
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines for pressure ulcer prevention/treatment and vascular access device management (18 recommendations, 41 indicators)
audits.f: Average compliance with recommendations was significantly higher in intervention units: pressure ulcer guidance 7.9±1.9 vs 6.0±1.7 (OR 1.86, 95% CI 1.67-2.05); vascular access 5.4±1.4 vs 4.4±1.6.
audits.c: Incorporation of advanced practice nurses into intervention units

audits.t: Outpatient Management of Epistaxis During COVID-19 to Reduce Inpatient Stay: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Outpatient management of epistaxis (Pack and Home pathway)
audits.st: COVID-19-era local 'Pack and Home' discharge criteria for epistaxis patients with nasal packs in situ, to reduce inpatient COVID-19 transmission
audits.f: All 72 patients (100%) were admitted for inpatient care; average total length of inpatient stay 45.7 hours
audits.c: Introduction of the 'Pack and Home' criteria pathway (March 2020) allowing selected epistaxis patients to be discharged home with nasal packs in situ and reviewed in outpatient clinic within 3 days, disseminated via posters, emails and intranet guidance
audits.r2: 21/59 (36%) were discharged home with nasal packs in situ, 38 (64%) admitted; average length of inpatient stay fell to 29.6 hours (p<0.05); 3 of 21 discharged patients (14%) represented within 48 hours, of whom 1 had rebled; all discharged patients were seen in clinic within 3 days

audits.t: Use of 'Printed Investigation Sheet' as Checklist in Admitted Antenatal Patients: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Checklist for antenatal patient clinical evaluation
audits.st: Complete clinical evaluation of antenatal women with anaemia, hypertension and/or diabetes by the third day of admission (target 80%)
audits.f: Baseline median percentage of patients with complete clinical evaluation was 29.2%
audits.c: Printed investigation sheet used as a checklist, developed via PDSA cycles after a root-cause analysis with a fishbone tool
audits.r2: Complete clinical evaluation improved to a median of 75%

audits.t: Adherence to coprescribing of laxatives with opioids and associated characteristics in general practices in the Netherlands.
audits.st: Guideline recommendation to coprescribe a laxative with an opioid
audits.f: Median proportion of first opioid prescriptions coprescribed with a laxative was 54% (practice range 18-88%).

audits.t: Preventing Teen Pregnancies on Teratogenic Drugs by Quality Improvement and Behavioral Economics.
audits.tp: Pregnancy prevention QI for adolescents on teratogenic medications
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Annual consents for postmenarcheal patients on teratogenic medications were 0% in 2017
audits.c: QI with behavioural economics: distinctly coloured consent forms, real-time reminders, peer comparison, and audit and feedback; phase 1 annual consenting, phase 2 sexual history screening and pregnancy prevention planning
audits.r2: Annual consents improved to 95% by 2021; sexual history screening/pregnancy prevention planning improved from 2% (2019) to over 78% (2021); days between pregnancies increased from 52 to over 900

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Project to Improve Periprosthetic Fracture Management at District General Hospitals.
audits.st: NICE guidelines on timely management/mobilisation of periprosthetic fractures
audits.f: 51 (76%) managed operatively, 16 (24%) conservatively; mean time to operation 89.2 hours; mean length of stay 23.6 days; mortality 10.4% (30-day), 20.9% (1-year), 25.4% (2-year)

audits.t: Starting a Swedish national quality registry for orthognathic surgery: a tool for auditing fundamentals of care.
audits.tp: National quality registry for orthognathic surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 91% coverage rate; reoperations in 32 patients (3.6%); patient satisfaction rate 95%.

audits.t: Improvement in Care and Maintenance of Port-A-Cath Following the Introduction of Care" Bundle.
audits.st: Institutional care bundle 'set standards' for port-a-cath care and maintenance (standard not externally named)
audits.f: Baseline: verbal consent 83%, drug/instrument arrangement 90%, needle non-touch technique 60%, saline flush 83.3% (25/30), heparin administration 71.1%, extravasation vigilance 80%, two-nurse involvement 23%, drug-expiry cross-check 26.6%, infections 3.
audits.c: Care bundle including education, training and live audio-visual sessions for nursing staff
audits.r2: Verbal consent 100%, drug/instrument arrangement 100%, extravasation vigilance 100%, two-nurse involvement 63%, drug-expiry cross-check 89.3%, infections reduced to 0 (vs 3).

audits.t: Vitamin D and Calcium Supplementation in Nursing Homes-A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.tp: Vitamin D and calcium supplementation in nursing home residents
audits.st: Recommendation for adequate vitamin D (≥20 µg) and calcium (≥800 mg) supplementation doses for nursing home residents (specific guideline not named)
audits.f: 32% (n=35) of residents had adequate doses of vitamin D and calcium.
audits.c: Information sheet on rationale for supplementation for nurses, and inclusion of supplementation discussion in admission meetings for new residents (2 PDSA cycles)
audits.r2: 65% (n=71) of residents had adequate doses of vitamin D and calcium (p<0.001).

audits.t: Respiratory support strategies in the prevention of bronchopulmonary dysplasia: A single center quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia reduction in preterm infants
audits.st: Local SMART aim to reduce moderate/severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD, NICHD/NHLBI 2001 definition) from 43% to 28% by January 2019, informed by published evidence on non-invasive ventilation, early surfactant and caffeine
audits.f: Moderate/severe BPD 38%; mechanical ventilation required in 52%; 51% received early non-invasive ventilation in the delivery room; 32% received caffeine within 24 hours; 25% received surfactant within 2 hours
audits.c: Sequential PDSA cycles: a 'Delivery Room Bundle' (early non-invasive ventilation, caffeine within 24h, early selective surfactant) from January 2017; a guideline to continue non-invasive ventilation until 32 0/7 weeks corrected gestational age from January 2018; and a revised early selective surfactant guideline from August 2020
audits.r2: Moderate/severe BPD fell to 15% (from 38% baseline, p<0.0001), an overall 56% reduction to a unit rate of 19% by 2022; severe BPD fell from 22% to 9%; ventilator days per infant fell to 2.6 (from 6.7); compliance reached 93% for delivery-room non-invasive ventilation, 94% for caffeine within 24h, 97% for continued CPAP to 32 weeks, and 85% for the revised surfactant guideline

audits.t: Implementation of systematic safety checklists in a neurocritical care unit: a quality improvement study.
audits.st: Local systematic safety checklist covering medication reconciliation, VTE prophylaxis, glycaemic control, daily awakening/breathing trial, diet, catheter/line duration monitoring and antibiotic de-escalation (institutional protocol, no external guideline named)
audits.f: Baseline compliance before checklist implementation not quantified in the abstract.
audits.c: Implementation of systematic safety checklist during daily patient rounds via iterative PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Checklist compliance reached 97.11%; compared with propensity/Euclidean-matched historical controls, reduced NCCU length of stay (β=-0.15, 95% CI -0.24 to -0.06), reduced new infections (OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.40-0.87) and reduced UTIs (OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.09-0.55).

audits.t: Quality improvement tools to manage emergency callbacks from patients with diabetes in a prehospital setting.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Iterative four-stage QI problem-solving model; education/training of paramedics and patients
audits.r2: Callback rate reduced but improvement was short-lived and callbacks increased again

audits.t: Quality Improvement of a Hip Injection Service.
audits.st: NHS Constitution 18-week referral-to-treatment (RTT) standard
audits.f: 36 (26%) experienced delays beyond 18 weeks RTT; mean wait 14 (SD 6) weeks; mean appointment time 12 min 36 sec pre-intervention
audits.c: Standardised proformas for documentation and discharge summaries
audits.r2: Mean appointment time reduced to 8 min 36 sec post-intervention, increasing list capacity

audits.t: UK National audit of the measurement of ammonia.
audits.st: MetBio.net updated best practice guidelines on hyperammonaemia sample handling and reporting
audits.f: 83% of laboratories were aware of updated MetBio.net guidelines; 64% still reject samples 'too old', 72% reject haemolysed samples, and 24% reject samples not sent on ice; 96% offer rapid ammonia analysis on a 24/7 basis

audits.t: A National Quality Improvement Program on Ultrasound Department in China: A Controlled Cohort Study of 1297 Public Hospitals.
audits.st: China National Ultrasound Quality Control Center (China-NUQCC) 8 quality control indicators (structural, process, outcome), including positive rate and diagnostic accuracy
audits.f: Positive rate of ultrasound examinations 66.21%; diagnostic accuracy 85.37%; doctor-to-patient ratio 1.05:10,000
audits.c: National QI programme: formation of a quality control team in each ultrasound department, structured training on standardised exam protocols and reports, and annual audit with feedback from provincial/national quality control centres
audits.r2: Positive rate rose to 73.91% (p<0.001); diagnostic accuracy rose to 89.74% (p<0.001); improvement was greater in secondary hospitals and in low-GDP provinces (diagnostic accuracy rose by almost 20% in low-GDP provinces); doctor-to-patient ratio fell to 0.96:10,000 (p=0.026)

audits.t: Diagnostic performance of biomarker S100B and guideline adherence in routine care of mild head trauma.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence for S100B testing in mild head trauma
audits.st: Scandinavian Neurotrauma Committee (SNC) guideline for use of serum S100B biomarker in mild low-risk traumatic brain injury
audits.f: ED practice adherent to the SNC guideline in 55% of patients; non-adherence in 64% of low-risk (SNC4) patients, including over- and under-testing of S100B and CT scans.

audits.t: Croatian national audit on videolaryngoscopes and alternative intubation devices in the era of COVID-19 pandemic.
audits.st: Guideline recommending anaesthesiologists be trained in and have immediate access to videolaryngoscopy (VL), especially for COVID-19 airway management (specific guideline not named)
audits.f: VL available in 86% of hospitals (83% response rate); only 16% reported regular use in everyday practice; VL available in 64% of COVID-19 wards but only 21% reported routine use there.

audits.t: Improving the management of left ventricular thrombus in a tertiary cardiology centre: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Left ventricular thrombus management quality improvement
audits.st: Guideline recommendation of repeat imaging within 3-6 months; local target to increase DOAC use from 25% to 70%
audits.f: 74% prescribed VKA; repeat imaging in 89% (55% same modality); mean time to repeat imaging 233±251 days
audits.c: Trust-wide guidelines on LV thrombus management recommending DOAC use and follow-up imaging
audits.r2: DOAC use increased to 70%; 70% had follow-up imaging at mean 140±61 days (36% same modality)

audits.t: A national audit of performance standards for blood cultures in Aotearoa New Zealand: opportunities for improvement.
audits.tp: National blood culture performance standards audit
audits.st: Published blood culture practice recommendations: positivity rate 8-15%, contamination rate below 3%, bottle fill volume at least 8mL
audits.f: 9 DHBs (60%) had a positivity rate within the 8-15% target; 8 DHBs (53%) had a contamination rate below the 3% target, 7 (47%) exceeded it; most DHBs had fill volumes below the 8mL target

audits.t: Improving the Timeliness of Discharge Summary Communication: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Trust target of discharge summaries sent within 2 working days of discharge
audits.f: 22.6% (12,965/57,367) of discharge summaries sent outside the 2-day target
audits.c: Three-pronged approach: educational material for deceased patient discharges, automated list for medical ward discharges, and technical optimisation of sending process
audits.r2: Deceased-patient intervention increased on-target summaries from 50% to 80% over 6 weeks (not sustained); medical ward intervention did not lead to improvement; automation intervention not completed

audits.t: Protocol-Driven Initiation and Weaning of High-Flow Nasal Cannula for Patients With Bronchiolitis: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Protocol for high-flow nasal cannula in bronchiolitis
audits.st: Target to reduce hospital and ICU length of stay by 10% between bronchiolitis seasons
audits.f: Baseline average length of stay 4.0 days, ICU length of stay 2.8 days, HFNC treatment 44.0 hours per patient
audits.c: High-flow nasal cannula initiation and weaning protocol with guidelines, modified respiratory assessment classification, education, and QI rounds
audits.r2: Average length of stay decreased to 2.8 days, ICU length of stay to 1.9 days, HFNC treatment hours to 36.3 hours; no difference in readmissions or adverse events

audits.t: An investigation into chiropractic intern adherence to radiographic guidelines in clinical decisions with a descriptive comparison to clinical practitioners.
audits.tp: Chiropractic intern adherence to radiographic guidelines
audits.st: Radiographic clinical practice guidelines for diagnostic imaging referral
audits.f: 43.75% of interns were aware of clinical practice guidelines, 38.75% were unsure, and 17.5% were not aware; interns showed lower compliance with the guidelines when evaluating clinical vignettes

audits.t: Endorsing: closing the loop on diagnostic tests in electronic health care records.
audits.tp: Timely endorsement of diagnostic test results
audits.st: Oxford University Hospital Trust policy: 85% of diagnostic tests endorsed within 7 days
audits.f: Performance consistently below the 85% target
audits.c: Team-based approach with clinical worklists, guidance document and endorsement newsletter, over four PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Endorsement improved to above 85% by end of second PDSA cycle, maintained through the project and for a further 6 months

audits.t: Improving Prescribing for Otitis Media in a Pediatric Emergency Unit: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing for acute otitis media
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) recommendations for shorter antibiotic duration and wait-and-see prescriptions (WSPs) for mild-to-moderate acute otitis media
audits.f: 39% of patients prescribed antibiotics received an appropriate duration; only 3% were prescribed wait-and-see prescriptions.
audits.c: Clinician education, a guideline card, visual reminders and updated emails, over 2 PDSA cycles across a 16-month project
audits.r2: Average of 67% of patients received an appropriate antibiotic duration, sustained for over 6 months; no substantial increase in wait-and-see prescriptions.

audits.t: Preparing for the Next Pandemic: An After-Action Review of Infection Prevention and Control Audit Strategies Within Airport and Hotel Quarantine Program.
audits.tp: Infection prevention and control audit strategy for quarantine programs
audits.st: Infection prevention and control (IPAC) standards adapted from healthcare settings for a quarantine programme
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Training and resources coupled with an IPAC quality assurance audit framework, provided by the Clinical Excellence Commission

audits.t: Factors Associated With Achieving Target A1C in Children and Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes: Findings From the T1D Exchange Quality Improvement Collaborative.
audits.tp: Type 1 diabetes glycaemic target achievement (T1D Exchange QI Collaborative)
audits.st: Target HbA1c (A1C) <7% for children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Improving Adolescent Depression in Primary Care: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Adolescent depression identification and treatment in primary care
audits.st: Guidelines for Adolescent Depression in Primary Care (GLAD-PC)
audits.f: 60% of patients identified as having depression received an intervention (baseline).
audits.c: Implementation of the GLAD-PC guideline-based protocol
audits.r2: 90% of patients identified as having depression received an intervention after GLAD-PC implementation.

audits.t: Adherence to Good Pharmacy Practices by Community Pharmacies in Lebanon and Opportunities for Quality Improvement: It is Time to Act.
audits.st: Order of Pharmacists in Lebanon (OPL) Good Pharmacy Practice (GPP) guidelines, recommended adherence threshold 75%
audits.f: Mean adherence to GPP standards was below the 75% threshold; only 65.09% adhered to all tested indicators (27% Attitude, 56.91% Services/Facilities, 68.61% Dispensing, 66.31% Storage).

audits.t: Are virtual consultations suitable for patients with vulval disease? A multicentre audit of outcomes in the COVID-19 pandemic.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 18.7% new, 81.3% follow-up; 28.5% provided supplementary imaging; photo quality higher when taken by a third party

audits.t: Driving communication forward: improving communication for palliative care patients around driving and opioids - a quality improvement report.
audits.st: Evidence-based recommendation that driving should be discussed and avoided until stable opioid dose reached
audits.f: 11.5% had documented driving status; 11.5% had documented discussion of driving and opioids
audits.c: MDT awareness-raising, prompt added to clerking proforma, reminder poster in ward office
audits.r2: Documented driving status improved to 65.2%; documented discussion improved to 60.9%

audits.t: Cross-sectional audit assessing the quality of dried bloodspot specimens received by UK metabolic biochemistry laboratories for the biochemical monitoring of individuals with Phenylketonuria.
audits.tp: Dried bloodspot specimen quality for phenylketonuria monitoring
audits.st: Proposed evidence-based national guidelines for dried blood spot (DBS) specimen acceptance/rejection
audits.f: Median specimen rejection rate was 4.0% (IQR 1.5-7.2%) using existing local laboratory guidelines
audits.r2: Median rejection rate increased to 21.9% (IQR 10.0-33.0%) using proposed national guidelines; 211/299 (70.6%) of rejections were for specimens too small or multi-spotted

audits.t: Improving patient satisfaction for patients with acute neurological symptoms by increased flow from the front door of hospital and more specific documentation in medical record notes: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: ED throughput and documentation for acute neurological patients
audits.st: Local aims: faster admission to the neurological subunit and documentation of tentative diagnosis, treatment plan and expected discharge time in medical records (institutional target, not an external guideline)
audits.f: Documentation compliance for the three topics: 62%, 45% and 28%; time to subunit 89 minutes (telephone contact) and 130 minutes (unknown to neurologist); baseline 45% of patients mentioned waiting time negatively.
audits.c: Education, one-to-one talks, feedback, checklists and raising project awareness (PDSA method)
audits.r2: Documentation compliance rose to 100%, 82% and 72%; time to subunit reduced to 34 minutes (telephone contact) and 107 minutes (unknown to neurologist); patient satisfaction increased 27%, and negative waiting-time comments fell from 45% to 10%.

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Project to Decrease Suboptimal Patient Transfers between Two Neonatal Units.
audits.tp: NICU to special care nursery transfer quality
audits.st: Local aim: reduce suboptimal transfers (discharge within 3 days of transfer, or return to NICU within 5 days) by 50% over 9 months (local target, not an external guideline)
audits.f: Parent notification before transfer 81%; staff satisfaction with transfer process 15%.
audits.c: Transfer checklist and algorithm, developed by a multidisciplinary team
audits.r2: Parent notification before transfer increased to 93%; staff satisfaction increased to 43%; suboptimal transfers decreased.

audits.t: Reducing the use of nil per os past midnight for inpatient diagnostic and therapeutic procedures: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Reducing unnecessary nil per os (NPO) past midnight
audits.st: Target to reduce NPO past midnight use before inpatient diagnostic/therapeutic procedures by 50% within 6 months
audits.f: NPO past midnight was used widely before amended protocols
audits.c: Diagnostic imaging protocols amended to reflect evidence-based fasting requirements; pre-procedure clear liquid diet implemented
audits.r2: NPO requirements removed from 70% of existing orders; immediate 50% reduction in NPO past midnight usage, further reduced to 33% of pre-procedural diet orders after stakeholder engagement

audits.t: Effective peer review audit and identification of the surgeon outlier.
audits.tp: Peer review audit of surgeon outcomes
audits.st: College's Morbidity Audit and Logbook Tool (MALT) for peer review of surgical activity and outcomes
audits.f: 9 complications grade 3 or greater, 6 deaths, 25 unplanned returns to theatre (8% failure to rescue rate), 7 unplanned ICU admissions, 8 unplanned readmissions; one surgeon outlier identified (>3 standard deviations over group mean) for unplanned returns to theatre
audits.c: De-identified peer comparison reports and review of the outlier's cases at a morbidity and mortality meeting using the MALT Self Audit Report
audits.r2: Practice changes were implemented for the outlier surgeon with future progress monitored (results not reported)

audits.t: Automated feedback modestly improves perioperative treatment adherence of postoperative nausea and vomiting.
audits.tp: Automated feedback for PONV medication compliance
audits.st: Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) prophylaxis medication recommendations based on patient risk scores
audits.f: Baseline PONV medication compliance and PACU PONV rates measured before intervention
audits.c: Clinical decision support with post-hoc reporting by email about PONV occurrences, followed by directive CDS with preoperative daily case emails recommending PONV prophylaxis
audits.r2: 5.5% (95% CI 4.2%-6.4%) improvement in PONV medication compliance; no improvement in PACU rates of PONV

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Decrease Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A "Zero Harm" Approach.
audits.st: Target to reduce CLABSI rate by 25% by 2023
audits.f: Baseline CLABSI rate 4.62 per 1000 line days; central line insertion checklist use 22.8%, capped lumens use 72%
audits.c: Interprofessional quality aim committee with root cause analysis; 4 Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles improving governance, education, standardising insertion/maintenance, equipment, data/reporting, and safety culture
audits.r2: CLABSI rate decreased to 2.34 per 1000 line days (51% reduction); checklist use increased to 56.9%, capped lumens to 94.3%; mean 30-day readmissions decreased from 1.49 to 0.1798

audits.t: An audit comparing management of patients with HFrEF at a DGH before and during the COVID-19 pandemic.
audits.tp: HFrEF management standard of care before and during COVID-19
audits.st: Standard of care for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: echocardiography and prescription of ACE inhibitors/ARBs and beta blockers
audits.f: Pre-pandemic period rates of echocardiography and ACE inhibitor/ARB/beta-blocker prescription in survivors not referred to palliative care
audits.c: not reported (comparison across the COVID-19 pandemic period, not a planned intervention)
audits.r2: Non-significant decrease in ACE inhibitor/ARB prescription rates (81.6% vs 71.4%, p=0.137), not seen for beta blockers; increased interval between admission and echocardiography in newly diagnosed patients; increased length of stay

audits.t: Decreasing the Rate of Surgical Site Infection in Patients Operated by Cesarean Section in a Tertiary Care Hospital in India: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Surgical site infection reduction after caesarean section
audits.st: Local target (via the Government of India Laqshya labour-room initiative): reduce surgical site infection (SSI) rate from 30% to under 5% over 6 months
audits.f: SSI rate approximately 30%.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary QI team implementing an antibiotic policy, surgical safety checklist and admission-discharge policy (POCQI model)
audits.r2: SSI rate reduced to and sustained at around 5%.

audits.t: Implementation of a Revised Montpellier Bundle on the Outcome of Intubation in Critically Ill Patients: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Revised Montpellier intubation care bundle (institutional evidence-based protocol: fluid loading, pre-oxygenation, positive-pressure ventilation, succinylcholine, stylet use, lung recruitment)
audits.f: Major complications occurred in 45.9% of intubations (whole-bundle did not yet exist).
audits.c: 2-month interphase developing the revised bundle and training staff, followed by the 3-month intervention period
audits.r2: ≥3 bundle components complied with in >92% of intubations; whole-bundle compliance 14.3%; major complications reduced to 23.8% (vs 45.9%, p=0.01); profound hypotension reduced (21.77% vs 29.51%, p=0.04).

audits.t: Leadership Driven Persistent Reduction in Cesarean Trends: An Interventional Study for Quality Improvement.
audits.tp: Leadership-driven reduction in caesarean section rate
audits.st: Quality improvement guidelines for reducing caesarean rates, assessed with the Robson classification
audits.f: Baseline annual caesarean rate 36.35%
audits.c: Multipronged interventions iteratively introduced from 2017, refined using multiple PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Caesarean rate reduced to 22.87% over four years

audits.t: Quality Indicators Compliance and Survival Outcomes in Breast Cancer according to Age in a Certified Center.
audits.tp: Breast cancer quality indicator compliance by age
audits.st: European Society of Breast Cancer Specialists quality indicators (EUSOMA-QIs): minimum standard and desirable target across 19 mandatory and 7 recommended indicators
audits.f: QI compliance 73.1% in patients ≤45 and 46-69 years vs 54% in patients ≥70 years.

audits.t: Quality Improvement in Pediatric Surgical Ward Rounds after Implementation of Checklist.
audits.st: Local standard for complete daily ward-round documentation (patient identification, diagnosis, operative status, vitals, examination, treatment, catheters/drains, bowel/urinary status)
audits.f: Documentation rates: patient identification 50%, diagnosis 47%, operative status 33%, fresh complaints 76%, vitals 63%, examination findings 43%, charting treatment 73%, catheters/drains/IV access 10%, bowel/urinary status 30%
audits.c: Introduction of a mandatory daily ward-round checklist (September 2018) covering identification, diagnosis, operative status, complaints, vitals, examination, treatment, lines/drains, and bowel/urinary status
audits.r2: Documentation rates rose to 100% for most items except catheters/drains/IV access (86%) and changes in management after rounds (93%); all differences were statistically significant (p<0.005)

audits.t: Reducing Avoidable Emergency Visits and Hospitalizations With Patient Risk-Based Prescriptive Analytics: A Quality Improvement Project at an Oncology Care Model Practice.
audits.tp: Reducing avoidable emergency visits with risk-based analytics
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Monthly ED visits 13.7 per 100 OCM patients; quarterly admissions 19.5 per 100 patients
audits.c: AI-based patient risk prediction tool (Jvion) with nurse-implemented patient-specific recommendations, PDSA methodology
audits.r2: Monthly ED visits reduced to 11.5 per 100 patients (18% reduction, sustained); quarterly admissions reduced to 17.1 per 100 patients (13% reduction, sustained)

audits.t: Statewide Perinatal Quality Improvement, Teamwork, and Communication Activities in Oklahoma and Texas.
audits.st: Alliance for Innovation on Maternal Health (AIM) patient safety bundles and teamwork/communication tools
audits.f: Standardized clinical processes for obstetric haemorrhage in 94% (Oklahoma) and 97% (Texas); multidisciplinary QI committees in 61% (Oklahoma) and 83% (Texas); recent teamwork/communication training in only 6% (Oklahoma) and 22% (Texas)

audits.t: Audit of 100 consecutive basal cell carcinoma specimens at a secondary care centre in the UK.
audits.st: Royal College of Pathologists dataset standards and British Association of Dermatologists 2018 guidelines for basal cell carcinoma excision
audits.f: All 100 (100%) pathology reports contained the mandatory information set by the Royal College of Pathologists; 7 (7%) were incompletely excised, within the acceptable range defined by BAD 2018 guidelines

audits.t: Quality improvement project to reduce unplanned extubations in a paediatric intensive care unit.
audits.tp: Unplanned extubation reduction in the PICU
audits.st: Local QI target to reduce unplanned extubation (UE) rate by 66% (from 2.02 to 0.7 per 100 ventilated days)
audits.f: UE rate 2.02 per 100 ventilated/day; mean 59 days between UE events
audits.c: Six-driver bundle tested via PDSA cycles: a new endotracheal tube fixation technique, standardised endotracheal tube positioning assessment, new physical restraint devices, sedation monitoring with the COMFORT-B scale, family education, and a UE-prevention checklist
audits.r2: UE rate fell to 0.00 from January 2019, sustained for up to 784 days without any event; mean days between events rose to 288 in the postintervention period (a 488% increase from baseline); estimated cost saving of R$955,096.65 (US$179,540.41) over 2 years

audits.t: Changing prescribing practice for rapid tranquillization-a quality improvement project based on the Plan-Do-Study-Act method.
audits.st: Local protocol to substitute intramuscular diazepam with intramuscular lorazepam for benzodiazepine rapid tranquillisation, with a standard vital-signs monitoring regimen (institutional decision, not an external guideline)
audits.f: Diazepam was the predominant benzodiazepine used for rapid tranquillisation before the QI intervention.
audits.c: Seven iterative PDSA cycles introducing lorazepam substitution and a standard vital-signs monitoring regimen
audits.r2: Lorazepam comprised 96% of benzodiazepine administrations for rapid tranquillisation, sustained post-intervention; mean dose stable (14.40 to 14.61 mg diazepam equivalents); vital-signs monitoring compliance exceeded 80% by the end of the observation period.

audits.t: Use of quality improvement methods to enhance implementation of a mental health care bundle in a pediatric emergency department.
audits.tp: Paediatric mental health care bundle in the emergency department
audits.st: Local bundle: Ask Suicide-Screening Questions (ASQ) risk assessment at triage, HEADS-ED brief assessment tool, and urgent appointment access within 96 hours for low-risk children (institutional QI targets, aiming for ≥80% use)
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: ASQ and HEADS-ED were used consistently in ≥80% of eligible patients; 89.3% of 159 referred families received an urgent appointment within 96 hours.

audits.t: The Ohio Maternal Safety Quality Improvement Project: initial results of a statewide perinatal hypertension quality improvement initiative implemented during the COVID-19 pandemic.
audits.tp: Severe hypertension in pregnancy treatment time
audits.st: Alliance for Innovation on Maternal Health (AIM) Severe Hypertension in Pregnancy bundle: appropriate acute antihypertensive therapy within 60 minutes of onset
audits.f: Baseline proportion receiving timely, appropriate treatment 56.5%.
audits.c: Multimodal statewide QI support adapting the AIM severe hypertension bundle across level 1-4 maternity hospitals, with statistical process control monitoring
audits.r2: Primary process measure increased 19.3 percentage points to 67.4%; improvements achieved across all hospital levels of maternal care, with no differences by race or ethnicity.

audits.t: In Situ Simulation as a Quality Improvement Tool to Identify and Mitigate Latent Safety Threats for Emergency Department SARS-CoV-2 Airway Management: A Multi-Institutional Initiative.
audits.tp: Latent safety threat identification via in situ simulation
audits.st: Local standardised in situ simulation protocol for acute SARS-CoV-2 airway management (institutional protocol, no external guideline)
audits.f: Overall latent safety threats (LSTs) per simulation began at 7.00.
audits.c: Standardised in situ simulation protocol with systems-based debriefs across equipment, infection control and communication categories, via 2 PDSA cycles

audits.t: Adherence to the therapeutic guidelines recommendations among the people with type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity, frailty, or recent diagnosis, attended in primary health care centers in Spain: A cross-sectional study.
audits.tp: Adherence to type 2 diabetes clinical practice guideline recommendations
audits.st: Clinical Practice Guideline (CPG) recommendations for management of type 2 diabetes mellitus with obesity, frailty, or recent diagnosis (specific guideline body not named)
audits.f: Adequate CPG adherence was highest among recently diagnosed T2DM patients (91.6%) and lowest among frail T2DM patients (74.7%); inadequate adherence was mainly among obese/frail patients treated by physicians with low CPG knowledge (3.4%/3.5%).

audits.t: Adherence of health workers to guidelines for screening and management of cryptococcal meningitis in Uganda.
audits.tp: Cryptococcal meningitis screening and management guideline adherence
audits.st: Ugandan Ministry of Health (MoH) guidelines for screening, diagnosis and management of HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis (CM)
audits.f: Mean adherence score 64.7% (classified 'red'/poor); 66.7% of facilities had not performed a baseline CD4 test within 2 weeks of ART initiation; none had potassium chloride tablets in stock; 60% scored 'light green' on knowledge of liposomal amphotericin B reconstitution.

audits.t: Uptake and Adherence to National Guidelines on Postpartum Haemorrhage in Italy: The MOVIE before-after Observational Study.
audits.st: Italian national guidelines on postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) management (17 key recommendations)
audits.f: Baseline adherence to the 17 key recommendations (not all quantified numerically in the abstract).
audits.c: MOVIE project training materials and tools targeting adherence to the national guideline recommendations
audits.r2: Post-test showed improved adherence in 16 of 17 key recommendations; clinical governance and communication with family members remained the weakest areas; 3 recommended procedures still showed a gap between adopted practice and guideline.

audits.t: Recognizing Nonaccidental Trauma in a Pediatric Tertiary Hospital: A Quality Improvement Imperative.
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics-recommended nonaccidental trauma (NAT) workup bundle for infants under 7 months with concerning injuries
audits.f: Appropriate NAT bundle completion 31%
audits.c: Hospital-wide NAT clinical guideline and EHR order bundle (age-based), a visual injury-indication chart, multidisciplinary education sessions, a 'Be a S.T.A.R.' communication campaign, caregiver communication scripts/handouts, and a 'One and Down in a Gown' infant examination protocol
audits.r2: Appropriate bundle completion rose to 100% and was sustained (no suspicious/incomplete cases from March 2020 to June 2021, up from a baseline of 11 patients between such cases); infant gowning compliance rose from 38% to 95%

audits.t: BLANKETS: a toasty tool to improve social history documentation for our older patients.
audits.st: Existing standards for social history content (derived into the BLANKETS acronym)
audits.f: Baseline documentation lower (part of two-cycle comparison)
audits.c: Introduction of the BLANKETS mnemonic tool for social history documentation
audits.r2: 194/403 (48.1%) vs 199/545 (36.5%) criteria met overall; on average 6.3/13 vs 4.7/13 criteria documented per patient

audits.t: Pre-COVID and COVID experience of objective structured clinical examination as a learning tool for post-graduate residents in Obstetrics & Gynecology-a quality improvement study.
audits.st: Local target: improve PG residents' OSCE-related knowledge and clinical skills via Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles (institutional target, not an external guideline)
audits.f: Baseline knowledge/clinical skills score around 30%.
audits.c: Fishbone analysis and 8 iterative PDSA cycles, with residents trained to conduct the OSCE

audits.t: Adherence to guidelines on the use of amoxicillin for treatment of ambulatory pneumonia in children younger than 5 years, Colombia, 2017-2019.
audits.tp: Amoxicillin prescribing adherence for paediatric pneumonia
audits.st: National clinical guidelines for treatment of ambulatory pneumonia in children under 5 years (amoxicillin prescribing recommendations)
audits.f: Overall guideline adherence 5.8%; adherence 86.0% for viral pneumonia vs 2.0% for bacterial pneumonia; only 9.4% of bacterial pneumonia cases were prescribed any antibiotic.

audits.t: Hospital-acquired E. coli bacteraemia at a large UK NHS Trust. A return towards baseline following implementation of a 5-year quality improvement programme.
audits.st: UK Department of Health target to reduce hospital-acquired E. coli bacteraemia by 50% over a 5-year period
audits.f: 134 episodes of hospital-acquired E. coli bacteraemia in the baseline year
audits.c: PDSA cycles modifying antibiotic prophylaxis for high-risk procedures and introducing 'good practice' interventions around medical devices
audits.r2: 159 episodes in 2021-22, an 18% reduction from the 2019-20 peak of 194 episodes but short of the 50% overall target; 30-day mortality 16.2%

audits.t: Implementing Pediatric Surviving Sepsis Campaign Guidelines: Improving Compliance With Lactate Measurement in the PICU.
audits.tp: Sepsis lactate measurement compliance in PICU
audits.st: 2020 Pediatric Surviving Sepsis Campaign (pSSC) guideline: lactate measurement within 60 minutes of severe sepsis/shock onset
audits.f: Baseline compliance 38%; baseline time to first lactate measurement 175 minutes (preshift mean 179 minutes).
audits.c: Multidisciplinary sepsis improvement team, education for frontline providers, peer-to-peer nursing education with feedback, and iterative PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Compliance improved to 47% (24% relative improvement); time to first lactate reduced to 94 minutes (46% improvement; postshift mean 81 minutes, a 55% improvement by SPC I-chart).

audits.t: Long-Term Impact of a Smartphone App on Prescriber Adherence to Antibiotic Guidelines for Adult Patients With Community-Acquired Pneumonia: Interrupted Time-Series Study.
audits.tp: Antibiotic guideline adherence via smartphone app for CAP
audits.st: Local antibiotic guidelines for community-acquired pneumonia (via SCRIPT app)
audits.f: Adherence 23% (46/200)
audits.c: Introduction of SCRIPT smartphone app providing local antibiotic guidelines
audits.r2: Adherence 31% (62/200) at 24 months (rose to 34% at 12 months then fell); sustained increase in patients with pulmonary consolidation on x-ray (14% to 31%, p=.04)

audits.t: Adherence to the Antibiotic Prophylaxis Guidelines for Appendectomy in Bahrain: An Observational Study.
audits.st: Local hospital guideline: prophylactic antibiotics (cefazolin 1g with metronidazole 500mg) given 30-60 minutes before appendectomy
audits.f: 98% (273/278) of patients were not given antibiotics within the prescribed 30-60 minute window; none of the 278 patients received the correct antibiotic choice per guideline; 1.8% (5/278) received no prophylactic antibiotics at all.

audits.t: Optimal management of post-discharge postpartum hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Management of post-discharge postpartum hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
audits.st: Expert recommendations for management of postpartum hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
audits.f: Optimal management observed in 65.0%; diagnosis and laboratory work-up were excellent, but adequate blood pressure surveillance and discharge recommendations were achieved in only 69.7%

audits.t: HIV rapid test performance among health facilities enrolled in HIV rapid test quality improvement initiative (RTQII) in Ethiopia.
audits.st: National HIV Testing Algorithm and Rapid Test Quality Improvement Initiative (RTQII) proficiency-testing standard (acceptable performance = 100% PT score with correct algorithm adherence)
audits.f: Overall acceptable performance 62%; 12% scored 80%; 11% scored 20-60%; 15% were unacceptable due to algorithm non-adherence; sites in External Quality Assessment schemes performed better than those not enrolled (70% vs 56%, p=0.057).

audits.t: Safe to Sleep in Tennessee: A Statewide Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Safe sleep practice compliance statewide QI
audits.st: 2016 American Academy of Pediatrics Task Force on Sudden Infant Death Syndrome safe sleep recommendations
audits.f: Baseline percent of infants audited compliant with safe sleep recommendations (not stated numerically)
audits.c: Safe sleep policies, staff/family education, monthly safe sleep audits, virtual huddles and semiannual learning sessions
audits.r2: Percent of infants audited compliant with safe sleep recommendations improved by 22%; main noncompliance reasons: additional objects in crib 49% (329/671), unsafe bedding 27% (181/671), head of bed elevation 24% (164/671)

audits.t: Implementation of a primary care asthma management quality improvement programme across 68 general practice sites.
audits.tp: Primary care asthma management quality improvement
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians Three Questions (RCP3Q) asthma control measure
audits.f: Good asthma control (RCP3Q=0) in 36.0% of patients
audits.c: Primary care asthma management QI programme (British Lung Foundation/Optimum Patient Care) delivered and cascaded to practice staff
audits.r2: Good asthma control increased to 39.2% (p<0.001); odds ratio of good control 1.15 (95% CI 1.09-1.22)

audits.t: The influence of enhanced recovery after surgery protocol adherence in patients undergoing elective neuro-oncological craniotomies.
audits.tp: ERAS protocol adherence for elective craniotomy
audits.st: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocol for elective craniotomy (institutional protocol; adherence dichotomised at ≥9 vs 7 items, not a fixed external compliance threshold)
audits.f: Median adherence 8 items (range 4-16); 55 patients classified high-adherence and 45 low-adherence.

audits.t: An Audit of Dietitians' Documentation - Comparing the Level of Agreement Between the Audit Instruments Diet-NCP-Audit and NCP-QUEST.
audits.tp: Audit instruments for dietitians' documentation quality
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: NCP-QUEST showed good inter-rater reliability for the quality category (ICC=0.85) and excellent reliability for total score (ICC=0.97)

audits.t: Quality Improvement Initiative to Improve Endoscopic Reassessment of Eosinophilic Esophagitis.
audits.tp: EREFS documentation completion in eosinophilic oesophagitis endoscopy
audits.st: EoE Endoscopic Reference Score (EREFS) documentation, local QI target ≥90% completion
audits.f: Baseline EREFS completion rate 72.7% (90% CI 67.4-77.4).
audits.c: Provider education and inclusion of EREFS in documentation templates, across 3 PDSA interventions
audits.r2: EREFS completion improved to 94.9% (90% CI 90.6-97.6), exceeding the 90% target.

audits.t: Lessons From a Quality Improvement Project to Standardize the Process of Gastric Biopsy Culture for Helicobacter pylori.
audits.tp: Gastric biopsy culture rate for Helicobacter pylori
audits.st: Pediatric societal clinical practice guidelines recommending gastric biopsy culture for initial H. pylori diagnosis (specific society not named)
audits.f: Gastric biopsy culture obtained in 39% (28/71) of patients; culture positivity 21% (3/14).
audits.c: Educational efforts among gastroenterologists, endoscopy suite personnel and laboratory personnel
audits.r2: Gastric biopsy culture obtained in 67% (36/54) of patients (P=0.004); culture positivity increased to 45% (5/11, P=0.39).

audits.t: Delirium screening in a stroke unit by nurses using 4AT: Results from a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Delirium screening compliance in stroke unit
audits.st: Local protocol: 4AT delirium screening within 24 hours of admission and at discharge (institutional QI target, not an external guideline)
audits.f: 4AT performed per protocol in 79.0% (49/62) at admission and 62.9% (39/62) at discharge; lack of time was the most common reason for non-completion (40%); 8% (5 patients) were diagnosed with delirium.

audits.t: Impact of a targeted temperature management quality improvement project on survival and neurologic outcomes in cardiac arrest patients.
audits.tp: Targeted temperature management after cardiac arrest
audits.st: International guidelines recommending targeted temperature management (TTM) for postresuscitation care after cardiac arrest with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC)
audits.f: TTM execution rate 18.1%; duration from ROSC to TTM 540 minutes; survival to discharge 27.1%; favourable neurologic outcome 17.4%
audits.c: TTM Quality Improvement Project: TTM protocols and standard operating procedures, documented shared decision-making with families, staff training programme, and lean medical management (starting TTM in the ED, an expedited CT pathway) to shorten ROSC-to-TTM time
audits.r2: TTM execution rate rose to 34.6% (p=0.003); ROSC-to-TTM duration fell to 356 minutes (p=0.042); survival to discharge rose to 39.4% (p=0.04); favourable neurologic outcome rose to 25.0% (p<0.001)

audits.t: Adherence to antipsychotic laboratory monitoring guidelines in children and youth: a population-based study.
audits.tp: Antipsychotic metabolic monitoring guideline adherence in children and youth
audits.st: Canadian Alliance for Monitoring Effectiveness and Safety of Antipsychotics in Children (CAMESA) guidelines for metabolic monitoring
audits.f: 23.5% (6505/27718) received at least one guideline-recommended baseline test; 3-month follow-up monitoring 13.0% (1179/9080); 6-month follow-up monitoring 11.4% (597/5261).

audits.t: Pleural procedures: an audit of practice and complications in a regional Australian teaching hospital.
audits.st: British Thoracic Society 2011 national pleural procedure audit benchmark
audits.f: Complication rate (excluding pain) was 16.9% for chest drains and 4.1% for thoracocentesis, giving an overall event rate of 10.8%; no major bleeding, organ puncture, infection or death

audits.t: Developing and delivering a hybrid Cardiac Rehabilitation Phase II exercise program during the COVID-19 pandemic: a quality improvement program.
audits.tp: Hybrid cardiac rehabilitation exercise programme during COVID-19
audits.st: Local SMART aim: enrol 70% of eligible patients into a hybrid cardiac rehabilitation phase II exercise programme (HCRP2-EP) by 30 September 2020, and achieve >=10% improvement in peak exercise capacity
audits.f: cardiac rehabilitation phase II services fully stopped due to COVID-19, with no hybrid delivery model in place
audits.c: Nine PDSA cycles: remote physical activity counselling, an educational home-exercise video, a telehealth platform for group/individual sessions, remote ECG telemetry, revised delivery structure and transfer criteria, staff training, infection control measures for hospital sessions, and technical issue tracking
audits.r2: monthly median enrolment 90% (above 70% target); 75.8% of those completing HCRP2-EP with final testing showed >=10% improvement in peak exercise capacity (mean 17%±6%); median Patient Satisfaction Score 96% (institutional target 90%)

audits.t: Implementing a Diabetic Algorithm for Ophthalmology Surgery Patients: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Perioperative diabetic management algorithm for ophthalmology surgery
audits.st: Local diabetic management algorithm based on best-practice guidelines (target: zero safety incidents; specific external guideline not named)
audits.f: 13 patient safety concerns/incident reports were reviewed under the existing diabetic protocol, including 2 serious hypoglycaemia cases.
audits.c: New diabetic algorithm developed by a multidisciplinary team, limiting use of the preoperative insulin protocol and reducing required nursing staff, trialled over 24 months
audits.r2: Zero safety incidents reported; 97.5% reduction in use of the preoperative insulin protocol; setup was 23 minutes faster and required one fewer nursing staff member; supply cost reduced by CAD $30.63 per patient.

audits.t: Reducing Central-Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections (CLABSI): An Improvement Project in a Specialized Tertiary Hospital.
audits.st: Local target: eliminate CLABSI events (institutional performance-improvement target)
audits.f: 144 CLABSI events; CLABSI rate 1.5 per 1000 device days.
audits.c: Bundle of standardised insertion/maintenance/removal policies, simulation-based physician training, an awareness campaign, root cause analysis, and automation/EHR documentation of bundle compliance, via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: CLABSI rate reduced to 1.03 per 1000 device days; events fell 24% by 2018 and a further 15% by end of 2019 (35% overall reduction from the 2017 baseline); 10 units reported zero CLABSI events in 2018 and 2019.

audits.t: Direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) monitoring within primary care: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: Nationwide Quality Assurance and Improvement Framework anticoagulant domains
audits.f: Monitoring levels had dropped significantly from near 100%; clinicians unfamiliar with DOAC monitoring requirements
audits.c: QI methodology with PDSA cycles to create sustainable DOAC monitoring processes, incl. a DOAC clinic
audits.r2: 49% seen in DOAC clinic, 78% had DOAC counselling, 97% had appropriate blood tests, 72% had a recent weight recorded; 74% (445/600) had an annual review adhering to gold standards after 3 years

audits.t: A Simple Admission Order-set Improves Adherence to Canadian Guidelines for Hospitalized Patients With Severe Ulcerative Colitis.
audits.tp: Admission order-set adherence for severe ulcerative colitis
audits.st: Toronto Consensus Statements for management of hospitalised severe ulcerative colitis (11 quality indicators)
audits.f: Baseline adherence to quality indicators, e.g. C difficile testing 75.5%.
audits.c: Standardised admission order-set based on the Toronto Consensus Statements
audits.r2: Adherence improved in 6 of 11 quality indicators; C difficile testing increased to 91.9% (P<0.05), with significant increases in several other indicators.

audits.t: Audit to assess the quality of 916 prosthetic prescriptions of removable partial dentures.
audits.tp: Quality audit of removable partial denture prosthetic prescriptions
audits.st: Acceptable clinical quality standard for completeness of removable partial denture prosthetic prescription information
audits.f: 74.2% of prescriptions were assessed as noncompliant, failing to meet the acceptable clinical quality standard; return date filled in only 6.4% (59/916); 86.8% (795/916) had inadequate design diagram information

audits.t: Critical pathways for continuous quality improvement: a multicentric analysis on the management of patients with lung cancer in Italian best performing hospitals.
audits.tp: Critical pathway adoption for lung cancer management
audits.st: National quality threshold for lung cancer treatment (Ministerial Decree n. 70/2015); SQUIRE guidelines used for methodology
audits.f: 68% of eligible hospitals had defined an internal Lung Cancer Critical Pathway (LCCP).

audits.t: A Quality improvement initiative to reduce central line-associated bloodstream infections in a neonatal intensive care unit in a low-and-middle-income country.
audits.tp: Central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) reduction in the NICU
audits.st: CDC-recommended central line insertion and maintenance bundle elements; local QI target to reduce CLABSI rate by 50% within 1 year
audits.f: CLABSI rate 4.82 per 1000 central line days (6 infections)
audits.c: Central line insertion and maintenance bundles (hand hygiene, maximal barrier precautions, skin preparation, optimal site selection, daily assessment of line necessity, insertion/maintenance checklists), with staff training, anonymous compliance auditing, and later permanent incorporation into standard NICU charting
audits.r2: CLABSI rate fell 76% to 1.09 per 1000 catheter days (2 infections) after 1 year; fell further to 0.66 per 1000 catheter days in year 2 and to 0 in year 3, with zero CLABSI sustained for 23 consecutive months (up to 713 CLABSI-free days)

audits.t: Implementation of a Consensus-Driven Quality Improvement Protocol to Decrease Length of Stay after Elective Carotid Endarterectomy.
audits.tp: Length of stay after elective carotid endarterectomy
audits.st: National guidelines: postoperative length of stay after elective CEA should not exceed 1 day on average
audits.f: LOS >1 day metric failure rate 58.3%
audits.c: Standardised antihypertensive medication management protocol (pre-op through POD1, with patient outreach) plus preoperative alpha-1 blockade for male patients, via 2 PDSA cycles
audits.r2: LOS >1 day failure rate improved to 32.8% (P=0.01); raw LOS similar (median 1 day, IQR 1-2, vs median 2 days, IQR 1-2, P=0.07); 30-day readmission 9.4% vs 6.3% (P=0.73)

audits.t: Prescribing in a pandemic: Electronic prescribing aids to improve non-specialist adherence to COVID-19 guidelines.
audits.tp: Electronic prescribing aids for COVID-19 guideline adherence
audits.st: COVID-19 management/prescribing guidelines (5 drugs)
audits.f: Dexamethasone prescribed or contraindication documented 85%; remdesivir 60%; 'as required' insulin for steroid patients 26%; oxygen 43%
audits.c: Introduction of an e-prescribing protocol for five COVID-19 drugs
audits.r2: Dexamethasone/contraindication documentation improved to 97%; remdesivir to 79%; insulin to 48%; oxygen to 79%

audits.t: Adherence to Guidelines for Acute Rehabilitation in the Norwegian Trauma Plan.
audits.tp: Adherence to acute rehabilitation guidelines after trauma
audits.st: Norwegian Trauma Plan: 3 operational recommendations for acute rehabilitation (PM&R assessment within 72h in ICU; early rehabilitation in ICU; direct transfer to specialised rehabilitation unit)
audits.f: Adherence to PM&R assessment within 72h documented in 18% of patients; early rehabilitation in ICU documented in 72% of those with severe trauma and ≥2 days ICU stay; direct transfer to specialised rehabilitation documented in 22% overall (26% severe trauma, 54% spinal cord injury, 39% traumatic brain injury).

audits.t: Antifungal stewardship in practice: Insights from a prospective audit and feedback program.
audits.st: Institutional antimicrobial (antifungal) stewardship prospective audit and feedback (PAF) programme, benchmarked against antibiotic PAF metrics
audits.f: PAF recommendation rate was lower for antifungals than antibiotics (21% vs 29%); highest antifungal recommendation rates were for liposomal amphotericin B, sepsis/respiratory-tract infections, and the cardiovascular ICU; recommendation acceptance rates were similarly high for antifungals and antibiotics.

audits.t: Blood culture quality assurance: findings from a RCPAQAP Key Incident Monitoring and Management Systems (KIMMS) audit of blood culture performance.
audits.st: Recommended positivity rate 8-15%, contamination rate <=3%, fill volume 8-10 mL per bottle
