audits.f: 62% (28/45) reported positivity rate outside 8-15% range; 15% (7/45) reported contamination >3%; 33% (15/45) reported average fill volume below 8-10 mL, 24% (11/45) reported <=5 mL; 29% (13/45) reported >=50% of blood cultures received as single set

audits.t: Get Smart, Canada: Exploring Smart Pump Implementation, Management, and Compliance with Standards through a Nationwide Survey.
audits.tp: Smart pump drug library management compliance
audits.st: Accreditation Canada standards and US Institute for Safe Medication Practices (ISMP) guidelines for smart pump drug libraries
audits.f: Only 30% (14/47) updated drug libraries at least quarterly; 47% (20/43) performed quality reviews at least every 6 months; 30% (11/37) did not perform regular compliance monitoring

audits.t: Introduction of a dedicated colic clinic reduces referral to treatment times in patients managed expectantly with acute ureteric colic: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Referral-to-treatment times for expectantly managed ureteric colic
audits.st: British Association of Urological Surgeons (BAUS) guideline: clinic review within 4 weeks of presentation
audits.f: Mean time from ED referral to urology clinic review 7.5 weeks; 25% reviewed within 4 weeks; mean time to intervention 15 weeks
audits.c: Introduction of a dedicated virtual colic clinic and updated ED referral guidance
audits.r2: Mean time to clinic review fell to 3.5 weeks; 82% reviewed within 4 weeks; mean time to intervention fell to 5 weeks

audits.t: Using Quality Improvement to Design Early Childhood Services Navigation in Primary Care.
audits.tp: Early childhood education referral and enrolment in primary care
audits.st: Local SMART aim: increase facilitated early childhood education (ECE) referrals from 0 to 15 per month and achieve 50% enrolment by 31 December 2020 (local target, not an external guideline)
audits.f: 0 facilitated referrals per month at baseline; enrolment rate 30% in 2018.
audits.c: An ECE Navigator role; interactive map of subsidised preschool options; streamlined enrolment forms; case management; population-based needs assessment
audits.r2: Facilitated referrals increased to 29 per month, remaining above the 15 target; enrolment increased to 74% in 2018 then decreased to 27% in 2020 as childcare availability declined during the pandemic.

audits.t: Adherence to evidence-based guidelines for the management of pneumonia in a tertiary teaching hospital in Riyadh.
audits.st: Infectious Disease Society of America (IDSA) guidelines for pneumonia management
audits.f: 50% (74/148) of patients were managed adherent to the IDSA guidelines; the adherent group had a higher cure rate (95% vs 84%), lower mortality (5% vs 14%) and shorter length of stay (6.5 vs 8 days), though not all differences were statistically significant.

audits.t: An independent audit of electroconvulsive therapy patient information leaflets in Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.
audits.st: 40-item accuracy measure for informed consent in ECT patient information leaflets (replicating an England audit)
audits.f: Accurate statements (out of 29 possible) ranged from 7 to 20, mean 16.9; inaccurate statements (out of 11) ranged 6-9, mean 7.0; all 23 leaflets wrongly stated that ECT saves lives

audits.t: Reducing post-operative caregiver after-hours phone calls to pediatric urology providers: A quality improvement study.
audits.tp: After-hours caregiver phone calls to surgical providers
audits.st: Internal quality improvement targets to reduce non-urgent after-hours calls and standardise telephone documentation
audits.f: 66% of after-hours calls were for post-operative patients; 59% of all calls were non-urgent
audits.c: PDSA cycle 1: standardised note template for telephone encounter documentation; PDSA cycle 2: updated post-operative discharge instructions detailing when to call after-hours
audits.r2: Proportion of post-operative calls decreased to 38% (from 67% in PDSA cycle 1); overall call volume and proportion of non-urgent calls unchanged

audits.t: Comparing Cesarean Birth Utilization Between US Hospitals: A Demonstration of the Robson Ten-Group Classification System for Use in Quality Improvement and Benchmarking.
audits.tp: Robson Ten-Group Classification System for benchmarking caesarean birth
audits.st: WHO-endorsed Robson Ten-Group Classification System (TGCS)
audits.f: Variation in cesarean birth, labour induction and TOLAC utilisation demonstrated across the 12 sites (specific rates not reported)

audits.t: Improving Hepatitis B Screening Prior to Rituximab: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B screening before rituximab therapy
audits.st: Recommendation for hepatitis B virus (HBV) screening prior to rituximab initiation in patients with rheumatic or kidney disease (evidence-based practice recommendation, not further named)
audits.f: Complete HBV screening in 6% of patients pre-intervention.
audits.c: Multimodal interventions: EHR dot phrase, display of screening recommendations/results in rituximab order sets, educational meetings, and email/paper reminders
audits.r2: Complete HBV screening increased to 44% (p<0.05); anti-HBsAb collection increased from 14% to 54% (p=0.006); other laboratory components were also significantly higher post-intervention (p<0.001); improvement was sustained over 18 months. 45 patients were identified as HBV-non-immune.

audits.t: Quality Improvement Initiative in a Community Hospital to Reduce Central Line Device Utilization Rate.
audits.tp: Central line device utilisation rate reduction
audits.st: Local target: reduce device utilisation rate (DUR) from 64% to 40% within 6 months (institutional target); baseline CLABSI rate 11.36 per 1000 device days
audits.f: Baseline CLABSI rate 11.36 (highest in 5 years); DUR 64% (up from a pre-pandemic rate of 45%).
audits.c: DMAIC methodology: reviewing current guidelines, enhanced care-team rounding, staff education, and a vascular access indication algorithm
audits.r2: DUR reduced to below 40% (target met); no CLABSI events reported since the project began.

audits.t: Preventing quality improvement drift: evaluation of efforts to sustain the cost savings from implementing best practice guidelines to reduce unnecessary electrocardiograms (ECGs) during the preadmisison testing evaluation.
audits.st: Best-practice guidelines for preoperative ECG testing
audits.f: Baseline ECG performance rate 54.0%
audits.c: New guidelines for ordering preoperative ECGs, with PDSA cycles over 3 years, reinforced training and individual feedback
audits.r2: ECG performance rate 21.9% (statistically significant decrease from baseline)

audits.t: Evaluation of Nationwide Trends in Nodal Sampling Guideline Adherence for Gastric Cancer: 2005-2017.
audits.tp: Nodal sampling guideline adherence for gastric cancer
audits.st: Surgical nodal sampling guideline for gastric cancer resection (>=15 lymph nodes)
audits.f: Adherence 27.8% at low-volume nonacademic programmes and 46.0% at high-volume academic programmes
audits.r2: Adherence improved to 50.1% at low-volume nonacademic programmes and 69.8% at high-volume academic programmes; overall 49.1% (27201/55421) met adherence criteria

audits.t: Continuous quality improvement: reducing informed consent form signing errors.
audits.st: Institutional requirement for correctly completed informed consent forms (ICFs) per ethical guidelines and regulations (specific guideline not named)
audits.f: Pre-intervention correct-signature proportion was lower than the post-intervention figure (baseline percentage not given precisely).
audits.c: Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle targeting specific ICF signing errors (multiple signatures, missing signatures, incorrect version, correction tape, non-research-member signature, etc.)
audits.r2: Correct ICF signature proportion was 83.3% (200/363) following the PDCA intervention, significantly higher than before the intervention.

audits.t: Evaluation of adherence with lung-protective ventilator strategies in moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome in a tertiary care setup in India: A prospective observational study.
audits.st: ARDS Network low-tidal-volume lung-protective ventilation strategy (tidal volume, plateau pressure, driving pressure, prone positioning, PEEP)
audits.f: Adherence to low-tidal-volume ventilation 78.12%; high PEEP 34.38%; prone ventilation 18.75%; mortality 71.8%; survival was higher in the low-tidal-volume-adherent group (+36%, p=0.06) and the high-PEEP-adherent group (73% survival, p=0.0004).

audits.t: Reducing Postoperative Length of Stay for Idiopathic Scoliosis Patients using Quality Improvement Methodology.
audits.tp: Length of stay after posterior spinal fusion for idiopathic scoliosis
audits.st: Local target (benchmarked against Pediatric Health Information System peer institutions): increase percentage of patients with length of stay ≤4 days from 39.13% to 90% after posterior spinal fusion
audits.f: 39.13% of patients were discharged within 4 days after posterior spinal fusion; average postprocedure length of stay 4.93 days; 13% off patient-controlled analgesia by postoperative day 2.
audits.c: New pain management protocol, a daily checklist, education on postoperative pain expectations, and updated order sets
audits.r2: 93.48% discharged within 4 days (P≤0.001); average length of stay reduced to 2.59 days (P≤0.001); 97.75% off patient-controlled analgesia by day 2 (P≤0.001); no adverse effect on readmissions or emergency department visits.

audits.t: Improved Compliance of Pediatrics High Blood Pressure Guidelines in Well-Child Clinic Visits.
audits.tp: Paediatric high blood pressure guideline compliance in well-child visits
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) high blood pressure clinical practice guideline steps, target 75% compliance over 12 months in children aged 9-18 years
audits.f: Compliance with 7 outcome measures was lower at baseline; repeat manual blood pressure measurement by provider was 38% at baseline.
audits.c: Provider education on the AAP guideline, integration of guideline steps into the electronic medical record, and individualised feedback/alerts across PDSA cycles
audits.r2: 6 of 7 outcome measures reached 86-100% after the 2nd PDSA cycle; repeat manual blood pressure by provider improved from 38% to 89% by the 4th PDSA cycle.

audits.t: A cross-sectional audit of informed consent of online survey: Characteristics and adherence to prevalent guidelines.
audits.tp: Informed consent quality in online research surveys
audits.st: Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) guidelines for informed consent
audits.f: 10 of 44 surveys had no informed consent; among the 34 with consent, median 6 sentences/84 words, median Flesch reading-ease score 45.7 (college level); majority stated the purpose (91.18%), voluntary participation (85.29%) and that it was research (64.71%), but other required components were largely absent.

audits.t: An audit of the dissemination strategies and plan included in international food-based dietary guidelines.
audits.st: Canadian Institute for Health Research dissemination-plan guidance; Model for Dissemination Research framework
audits.f: Guidelines from 53 countries reviewed; dissemination plans available in English for 12 countries (22.6%), none met all recommended criteria

audits.t: Factors affecting adherence to a high-risk surveillance protocol among patients with Li-Fraumeni syndrome.
audits.tp: Adherence to Li-Fraumeni syndrome surveillance protocol
audits.st: High-risk surveillance protocol for Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS) patients (protocol not specifically named)
audits.f: 29% (6/21) of patients were up to date with surveillance recommendations at time of review; mean duration of adherence 17 months; female sex and personal cancer history were associated with longer adherence (p=0.02 each).

audits.t: Diabetic control and compliance using glycated haemoglobin (HbA1C) testing guidelines in public healthcare facilities of Gauteng province, South Africa.
audits.tp: HbA1c testing guideline compliance and diabetic control
audits.st: HbA1C testing/monitoring guidelines for type 2 diabetes (target HbA1c ≤7% for normal control; guideline not further named)
audits.f: 51.5% of patients were poorly controlled (29.6% very poor control); most poorly controlled patients had only one HbA1c test during the study period.

audits.t: Decreasing Antibiotic Use in a Community Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Local QI target to reduce antibiotic use rate (AUR) from 22% to 17%, based on CDC core elements of antibiotic stewardship and AAP early-onset sepsis guidance
audits.f: AUR 22%
audits.c: Multidisciplinary antibiotic stewardship programme: standardised early-onset sepsis guidelines by gestational age, a sepsis risk calculator, daily antibiotic stewardship rounds, and staged antibiotic stop orders (48-hour stop, then 36-hour soft stop, then 36-hour hard stop)
audits.r2: AUR fell to 13.18%, a sustained 40% reduction from baseline, surpassing the 17% target; 3-day antibiotic treatment in infants 35 weeks or older fell from 26% (2020) to 18% (2021); sepsis calculator compliance rose from 51.1% to over 90%

audits.t: Reducing Retained Foreign Objects in the Operating Room: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Retained foreign objects in theatre (surgical count)
audits.st: Internal target to increase days between retained foreign object (RFO) events; final surgical count protocol
audits.f: Average 29 days between RFO events; 7 RFO events in 2021
audits.c: Multidisciplinary 6-step quality improvement initiative (quiet time, minimising interruptions, closed-loop communication) implemented via 7 PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Improved to 451 days between RFO events (exceeding upper control limit of 235 days); 0 RFO events in 2022; adherence to final count protocol 96.4% by end of cycle 7

audits.t: Reducing neuropathies between the 2020 and 2021 Covid-19 surges in a large UK intensive care unit: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Peripheral nerve injury reduction in prone-positioned ICU patients
audits.st: Updated prone positioning guidelines aiming to reduce risk of peripheral nerve injury (PNI)
audits.f: 21 patients (22.6%) had at least one high-grade PNI
audits.c: Implementation of updated prone positioning guidelines supplemented by face-to-face teaching for ICU professionals
audits.r2: 12 patients (3.9%) sustained an intermediate or high-grade PNI, an 82% reduction in PNI cases; high-grade injuries reduced from 14/21 (66%) to 4/12 (33%)

audits.t: Achieving durable compliance with venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in bariatric surgery: 3-year data from a major academic medical center.
audits.st: Standardised institutional VTE prophylaxis protocol; goal compliance >=90%
audits.f: Preoperative heparin administration 47% (107/228)
audits.c: Standardised MBS VTE prophylaxis protocol (preop SC heparin, postop LMWH) distributed to stakeholders; barriers addressed with PDSA cycles

audits.t: Leveraging quality improvement to promote health equity: standardization of prenatal aspirin recommendations.
audits.st: United States Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) recommendations for aspirin to prevent preeclampsia in at-risk patients
audits.f: 47% of patients met criteria for aspirin; only 28% received a documented recommendation.
audits.c: Nurse-administered checklist based on USPSTF criteria to identify high-risk patients, plus physician-placed orders, via a PDSA cycle
audits.r2: 99% of patients were screened at intake (goal 90% met); 48% met criteria for an aspirin recommendation, of whom 79% received the recommendation (goal 80%, approximately met).

audits.t: HIV viral load testing and monitoring in Côte d'Ivoire: A survival analysis of viral load testing and suppression, and evaluation of adherence to national recommendations.
audits.tp: HIV viral load testing guideline adherence
audits.st: Côte d'Ivoire national and WHO guidance for HIV viral load (VL) monitoring: first VL test within 12 months of ART initiation, with regular subsequent testing
audits.f: 72.4% of patients were virally suppressed within 1 year of ART initiation; median time to first VL test 7.8 months (within the recommended 12 months); approximately 30% received a second VL test during the 4-year period, with a median time between first and second VL tests of 24.9 months (exceeding the recommended interval).

audits.t: Multisite Quality Improvement Program Within the Project ECHO Diabetes Remote Network.
audits.tp: Multisite diabetes quality improvement via ECHO telementoring
audits.st: Clinic-chosen structural, process and outcome quality measures (e.g. HbA1c control)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Weekly tele-education sessions and quarterly QI mentorship via Project ECHO Diabetes
audits.r2: 25/31 (80.6%) initiatives made improvements and 6/31 (19.4%) were in progress; for one measure, 40.0% of clinics achieved a higher percentage of cumulative HbA1c measurement in Q3 vs the previous year's Q4

audits.t: Evaluating the Usage of Musculoskeletal Spinal Drop-In Services in East Lancashire: A Retrospective Audit of Performance Standards.
audits.st: National guidelines (Keele STarT Back prognostication) for MSK spinal drop-in service use
audits.f: Utilisation compared against STarT Back scores and national guidelines; some improvement required in patient management identified

audits.t: Outpatient management of urinary tract infections by medical officers in Nairobi, Kenya: lack of benefit from audit and feedback on adherence to treatment guidelines.
audits.tp: Urinary tract infection management guideline adherence
audits.st: Locally adapted urinary tract infection (UTI) treatment guidelines (adapted for the study from evidence-based UTI management)
audits.f: Baseline scores were lower across history-taking, examination, diagnosis, workup and treatment domains; nitrofurantoin use 4%, cephalosporin use 49%.
audits.c: Multimodal continuing medical education (CME) session using locally adapted UTI guidelines; feedback group received additional audit-based feedback after audit 2
audits.r2: Scores improved significantly after CME compared with baseline and were sustained at audit 3, but feedback added no further benefit beyond CME; nitrofurantoin use rose to 8%, cephalosporin use to 67%, and quinolone use decreased.

audits.t: Decreased fetal movements - An audit of predictors and an evaluation of management based on a locally developed flow chart.
audits.st: Evidence-based hospital guideline/flow chart for management of decreased fetal movements (DFM)
audits.f: Women with DFM more likely to be 20-34 years (82.8% vs 79.0%, p<0.01), have BMI>=30 (42.9% vs 34.4%, p<0.001), mental health conditions (31.1% vs 24.2%, p<0.01); composite neonatal outcome similar (22.9% vs 24.8%, P=0.18); induction more likely (40.7% vs 29.9%, p<0.01)
audits.c: Implementation of a locally developed flow chart for DFM management based on an evidence-based guideline
audits.r2: No difference in perinatal outcomes before and after implementation of the hospital guidelines on DFM management (exact figures not reported)

audits.t: Let Us Know Transfusion Triggers for Prophylactic Use of Platelet Concentrate-Analysis of Compliance with Recent Transfusion Guidelines in a Large Academic Medical Center.
audits.st: Recent platelet concentrate (PC) transfusion guidelines (guideline not specifically named)
audits.f: Inappropriate transfusions accounted for 53.3% of cases (80.2% of these given prophylactically); annual inappropriate-transfusion rate ranged from 50.7% to 60.8%; compliance varied by department.

audits.t: Identification of enteral nutrition errors in a single-center quality-improvement audit.
audits.tp: Enteral nutrition administration and documentation errors
audits.st: Correct EN order execution/documentation (hang time <=48h)
audits.f: 275 errors of execution from 1045 data points (135 labelling, 140 administration errors); 15.9% error rate; hang time >48h in 85%; only 14% compliance with 48-h hang time documentation

audits.t: Quality Review Committee Audit Improves Thoracic Enhanced Recovery After Surgery Protocol Compliance.
audits.st: Thoracic Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocol
audits.f: Overall compliance 53%
audits.c: Quality review committee meeting to identify and resolve barriers to ERAS protocol compliance

audits.t: Immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence utilization audit by subspecialty in an academic setting: A step toward stewardship.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average 21% of specimens had IHC/IF ordered (range 1% genitourinary to 59% renal pathology); average 4.9 stained slides per specimen where ordered (range 1.9-12.2); renal pathology significantly different from all other subspecialties

audits.t: Quality improvement initiative: implementing routine vertebral fracture assessments into an Australian Fracture Liaison Service.
audits.tp: Vertebral fracture assessment in a Fracture Liaison Service
audits.st: National/international osteoporosis guidelines recommending vertebral fracture assessment (VFA) alongside bone density testing; local target to increase VFA uptake from 0% to 50%
audits.f: 0% of patients received a VFA; treatment initiation occurred in 159 patients with osteopenia/osteoporosis and 28 patients with normal bone mineral density
audits.c: Routine VFA offered to all eligible patients as part of standardised osteoporosis assessment, implemented via a multidisciplinary quality improvement group using Proctor's implementation framework
audits.r2: VFA uptake rose from 0% to 90% of eligible patients (exceeding the 50% target); 41% of VFAs showed abnormalities, including 4% with normal bone density but abnormal VFA; there was no statistically significant increase in treatment initiation rates (chi-squared p=0.065)

audits.t: Group B Streptococcus Screening and Treatment Adherence in Pregnancy: A Retrospective Cohort Study and Opportunities for Improvement.
audits.tp: Group B Streptococcus screening and treatment adherence
audits.st: 2010 Group B Streptococcus screening and treatment guidelines
audits.f: Adherence occurred in 89% (1,610/1,810) of patients

audits.t: Improving the clinical monitoring of extrapyramidal symptoms: a local quality improvement project.
audits.st: Clinical guidelines recommending structured screening tool use for extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS)
audits.f: 14.8% of inpatient records contained evidence of EPS documentation; no evidence at all in the rehabilitation or assertive outreach settings
audits.c: Adoption of the Extrapyramidal Symptom Scale (EPSS) as a structured monitoring tool, with an educational session on its use
audits.r2: Guideline-concordant EPS monitoring found in 75% of inpatient records, 79.6% in rehabilitation, and 18% in assertive outreach

audits.t: Pain Assessment and Management Practices via Education & Reinforcement (PAMPER): A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Premature Infant Pain Profile score-based pain assessment for infants <=1800g
audits.f: Mean documented pain score for first 7 days 12.8 (SD 0.3)
audits.c: PAMPER group (resident doctors and nursing staff) education and reinforcement, fishbone analysis, multiple PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Mean pain score reduced to 7 (SD 2.5); 100% of procedures assessed for pain; practice sustained in >70% of infants over the next 2 years

audits.t: Implementing a safer and more reliable system to monitor test results at a teaching university-affiliated facility in a family medicine group: a quality improvement process report.
audits.st: not reported (internal quality target for reliable test-result tracking)
audits.f: Mean error rate 6.1% (range 2.7-12.1%, SD 2.1%) before changes
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles: recognising family medicine residents as prescribers, connecting prescribers to the regional techno-centre, and a computer protocol eliminating duplicate results
audits.r2: Mean error rate decreased to 1.9% (range 0-4.8%, SD 1.2%); 100% of 30 patients surveyed were satisfied; 75% of prescribers (15.8% of residents) responded and perceived the system as safer and more reliable

audits.t: A Trainee-Led Quality Improvement Project Using Change Management Theory to Improve Bedside Rounding.
audits.st: Internal target to increase bedside rounds to 50% within 6 months, sustained for 12 months
audits.f: Bedside rounds 18% on the initial team; 7% across all general paediatrics teams before spread
audits.c: Trainee-led quality improvement framework combined with change management theory; 12 PDSA cycles including a communication bundle
audits.r2: Bedside rounds increased to 89% on the initial team, sustained for 12 months; increased to 54% after spread to all teams (from 7%)

audits.t: Care and three-year outcomes of children with Benign Epilepsy with Centro-Temporal Spikes in England.
audits.tp: BECTS (childhood epilepsy) guideline adherence and outcomes
audits.st: NICE guidelines for specialist referral, EEG conduct and annual review in paediatric epilepsy
audits.f: 24/95 (25%) were seen by a specialist within two weeks of presentation; 59/100 (59%) received an EEG within two weeks of request; 59/114 (52%) were reviewed annually

audits.t: Improvement project to reduce surgical site infections: a retrospective cohort study.
audits.st: not reported (internal SSI reduction bundle and safe surgery checklist adherence)
audits.f: not reported (exact SSI rate not stated in abstract; 268 procedures analysed for SSI and checklist adherence)
audits.c: Package of measures to reduce surgical site infections and a safe surgery checklist, implemented across 2018-2020
audits.r2: Significant reduction in SSI rate with greater checklist adherence; exact percentages not reported; reduction was not maintained, influenced by the COVID-19 pandemic

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Increase Documentation of Preferences for Life-Sustaining Treatment in Hospitalized Adults.
audits.tp: Documentation of preferences for life-sustaining treatment (POLST)
audits.st: Portable Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST) completion for patients with inpatient DNR order
audits.f: 29.5% of hospitalised internal medicine patients with an inpatient DNR order and no DNR POLST at admission discharged with a DNR POLST
audits.c: Educational training on electronic POLST navigation, EHR discharge navigator notification, and quarterly individualised performance reports, via 3 PDSA cycles over 34 months
audits.r2: Proportion of DNR POLST forms completed by discharge increased from 0.36 to 0.60

audits.t: Quality improvement initiative improves the empiric antibiotic prescribing practices in a tertiary care children's hospital in India.
audits.st: National antibiotic guidelines (locally adapted antibiotic policy)
audits.f: Adherence of empirical antibiotic prescriptions was 59% before intervention
audits.c: New antibiotic policy based on national guidelines and local sensitivity patterns, disseminated via seminars, posters and cellphone-friendly documents, with compliance tracked twice weekly

audits.t: Optimizing Contraceptive Prescription in Smoking Women: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.st: WHO recommendation against combined hormonal contraceptives in female smokers aged 35 or older; local target of reducing use to ≤5%
audits.f: 16.4% prevalence of combined hormonal contraceptive use among smokers aged 35-54
audits.c: Educating medical staff, patient awareness campaigns, and evaluation of contraceptive methods (PDSA approach, SQUIRE 2.0 reporting)
audits.r2: 8.5% prevalence of combined hormonal contraceptive use; target of ≤5% not fully achieved; progestogen-only method use rose from 25.7% to 34.0%

audits.t: Development of the Nova Scotia Potential Donor Audit (PDA) Tool and 2020 Historic Performance Database: Lessons Learned From the First 1000 Medical Record Reviews.
audits.st: Nova Scotia definition of a potential donor and mandatory referral criteria
audits.f: 518/1028 (50.4%) met clinical triggers for referral; only 72 (13.9%) were referred (86.1% missed referral rate); 163 met the potential donor definition, of whom 53 (32.5%) were referred (110 missed potential donors); referral consent rate 71.7% (38/53)

audits.t: Observations from Australia's National Surgical Mortality Audit.
audits.tp: National surgical mortality audit and peer review
audits.st: Independent external peer review of every surgical mortality (standardised mortality ratio benchmarking)
audits.f: Standardised mortality ratio (SMR) established as the index for each state/territory and 9 surgical specialties
audits.c: National peer review of every surgical death with educational feedback (individual case reviews, state and national symposia/reports, deidentified case distribution)
audits.r2: Consistent progressive fall in SMR, usually >20%, in each state/territory and specialty compared with the index year, significant nationally (p=0.044)

audits.t: Reducing the rate of central line-associated bloodstream infections; a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Central line-associated bloodstream infection prevention bundle
audits.st: Central line care bundle compliance
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: PDSA quality improvement cycle with active surveillance and central line care bundles
audits.r2: 94% compliance with central line care bundles; 20 CLABSI events; an 18% reduction in CLABSI rate that did not reach statistical significance (p=0.252)

audits.t: Preoperative Snack Prescription: A Single-Centre Experience in Optimising Preoperative Fasting Time and Enhancing Guideline Adherence.
audits.st: Preoperative fasting guideline adherence (minimising unnecessarily prolonged fasting)
audits.f: Mean time from last meal to anaesthesia 17.8 hours (range 14.6-22.5) and to surgery 18.5 hours (range 16.0-23.3)
audits.c: Preoperative snack prescription (e.g. biscuits, chips, cakes) introduced for the post-intervention group and incorporated into local preoperative care policy
audits.r2: Mean time from snack to anaesthesia 10.9 hours (range 6.5-16.0) and to surgery 12.0 hours (range 7.5-16.5); fasting-to-anaesthesia time reduced from 18.3 to 10.9 hours

audits.t: Introducing Birth Companion in Labour: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Global recommendation for birth companionship in labour; target 0% to 100% over 6 months
audits.f: 0% birth companionship (not previously allowed)
audits.c: 5 successive PDSA cycles: introducing the concept, information dissemination, infrastructural changes in labour room, documentation column in birth register, antenatal counselling sessions and staff/trainee sensitisation
audits.r2: Birth companionship achieved in 98% of cases

audits.t: Enhancing early functional independence following cardiac surgery: a quality improvement programme.
audits.tp: Early mobility and functional independence after cardiac surgery
audits.st: Local QI target: Functional Independence Measure (FIM) score of 80% or more by postoperative day 3 in over 80% of uncomplicated cardiac surgery patients, and a 6-minute walk distance over 250m by postoperative day 4
audits.f: Only 5.3% achieved FIM 80% or more by postoperative day 3 (mean FIM 73.71±4.81%); mean 6-minute walk distance on day 4 was 188.23±48.65m (only 54% completed the test); only 21.4% reported confidence in independent activities of daily living by day 5
audits.c: Multidisciplinary QI programme ('4Is': Inform, Involve, Integrate, Inspect) via PDSA cycles: a standardised evidence-based mobility/activity protocol by postoperative day, staff education, standardised documentation, patient/family preoperative education, visual cues (floor markings, colour-coded flags, whiteboards), mandatory pain assessment before mobilisation, and a colour-coded risk categorisation system
audits.r2: FIM 80% or more by day 3 rose to 91.4% (sustained), mean FIM 81.20±3.77% (p<0.001); mean 6-minute walk distance rose to 267.90±36.10m (91% completed the test, p<0.001); confidence in independent activities of daily living rose to 89.4% (p<0.001); no adverse events reported

audits.t: Quality improvement of Dutch ICUs from 2009 to 2021: A registry based observational study.
audits.tp: Trends in ICU quality indicators (national registry)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: ICU length of stay, duration of mechanical ventilation, readmissions, in-hospital mortality, hypoglycaemia and pressure ulcers decreased significantly 2009-2019 (exact values not reported); COVID-19 years 2020-2021 disturbed the improving trend

audits.t: Results of the IAEA supported national end-to-end audit of the IMRT technique in Poland.
audits.st: IAEA end-to-end audit methodology and acceptance criteria for IMRT head & neck treatments (5% PTV, 7% OAR tolerance; 3%/3mm gamma 90% acceptance)
audits.f: Ionization chamber results all within tolerance (max 4.5% PTV, max 5.3% OAR); film global gamma results 91.5-99.7%

audits.t: Reducing first appointment delays for electron radiotherapy patients by improving the treatment planning pathway: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Radiotherapy new-start appointment delay quality improvement
audits.st: Local target: New Start radiotherapy appointments to begin within 30 minutes of allotted time; Final Checks completed 30 minutes prior
audits.f: 33% of electron-treatment New Start appointments started within 30 min (average delay 52.4 min); 48% of Final Checks completed by 30-min-prior target
audits.c: Redesigned treatment planning pathway, including a proxy 'day 0' appointment, automated planning calculations and standardised care path
audits.r2: 69.2% of New Start appointments started within 30 min (average delay reduced to 27.2 min); 92.3% of Final Checks completed by target; safety incidents due to plan-not-ready reduced from 10 to 0

audits.t: Systematic audit of Australian specialty colleges' policies on bullying, discrimination, and harassment.
audits.tp: Specialty college policies on bullying, discrimination and harassment
audits.st: National standard BDH (bullying, discrimination, harassment) policy checklist
audits.f: 14 of 16 Colleges had their own written BDH policies, with wide variation in content and processes against the checklist (no overall pass rate reported)

audits.t: Vision Screening in Older Adults Admitted with a Fragility Hip Fracture: A Healthcare Quality Improvement Report.
audits.tp: Vision screening in older adults with hip fracture
audits.st: NICE guidance (CG161) recommending multifactorial falls risk assessment including vision assessment; orthoptic-led inpatient vision screening service developed from Squirrell et al.'s model
audits.f: 51% (784/1532) of screened patients had an ocular abnormality requiring referral; only 38% (144/383) of GP-referred patients were successfully referred to ophthalmology, and only 58% (107/186) of those given appointments attended
audits.c: not reported (service was already established; project evaluated its 5-year effectiveness and identified areas for improvement such as removing the red reflex test and proposing an internal referral pathway)

audits.t: Adherence to National Asthma Guidelines in the Acute Care Setting: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
audits.tp: Peak flow use in acute asthma guideline adherence
audits.st: BTS/SIGN 158 asthma guidelines (use of peak expiratory flow rate)
audits.f: PEFR recorded for 29.3% (n=27); severity documented in 17.4% (n=16)

audits.t: Increasing the use of anxiolysis and analgesia for paediatric procedures in a community emergency department network: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: SMART aim to increase intranasal midazolam use from 2% to 25% for children <8 years
audits.f: Intranasal midazolam use 2%
audits.c: Guideline development, staff training and cognitive aids via PDSA cycles, key driver diagram, benchmarked to regional paediatric EDs
audits.r2: Monthly average intranasal midazolam use increased to 42% (exceeding the 25% target)

audits.t: Initiation of Palliative Care Referral from the Intensive Care Unit for Advanced Stage Metastatic Cancer Patients: A Quality Improvement Process from a Tertiary Referral Cancer Institute from South India.
audits.tp: Palliative care referral from the ICU
audits.st: Local SMART goal to initiate palliative care referral for 50% or more of progressive/palliative-intent cancer patients in the ICU
audits.f: 0% of eligible palliative-intent patients received a palliative care referral from ICU; 22/46 deaths were on best supportive care without palliative care intervention
audits.c: A3/PDCA quality improvement: development and staff education on a 10-item palliative care trigger tool for daily use in the ICU, sharing palliative care outpatient records with ICU via the hospital information system, a palliative care discharge protocol and list of local palliative care centres for the discharge desk, and ongoing resident/nurse education
audits.r2: Palliative care referral rate rose from 0% to over 50% by November 2019 and over 70% by March 2020

audits.t: Pediatric Ventilator-Associated Events Before and After a Multicenter Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: CDC pediatric ventilator-associated event (PedVAE) surveillance definition; local SMART aim to reduce PedVAE rate by 20% by December 2020
audits.f: Aggregate PedVAE rate 1.9 events per 1000 ventilator days
audits.c: Quality improvement bundle in the Pioneer cohort: multidisciplinary apparent cause analysis for every PedVAE, daily discussion of extubation readiness, and daily discussion of fluid balance goals, supported by national learning sessions and webinars
audits.r2: Aggregate PedVAE rate fell to 1.4 events per 1000 ventilator days (26% reduction, p<0.001) in the Pioneer cohort, with no significant change in the 33 non-Pioneer hospitals; the 3 hospitals reliably discussing extubation readiness saw rates fall from 2.6 to 1.2 per 1000 ventilator days (54% reduction, p<0.001)

audits.t: Healthcare workers' compliance with the catheter associated urinary tract infection prevention guidelines: an observational study in Yemen.
audits.tp: Catheter-associated urinary tract infection prevention compliance
audits.st: Catheter-associated urinary tract infection prevention guidelines (evidence-based insertion practice)
audits.f: Overall mean compliance score 7.31 of 10; 71% of healthcare workers had high/acceptable compliance, 29% had an unsafe level; compliance was low for aseptic technique, single-use lubricant, hand hygiene before insertion, and securing the catheter

audits.t: Intravenous albumin utilization audit at a large community hospital.
audits.st: A priori appropriateness criteria for albumin indication

audits.f: HRG code changes required in 58.5% of cases after clinician review
audits.c: Targeted education sessions for junior clinicians and clinical coding staff
audits.r2: HRG changes required in 20.5% of cases (p<0.0001)

audits.t: Using quality improvement approaches to increase emergency department provider engagement in research participant enrollment during COVID-19 and opioid overdose public health emergencies.
audits.tp: Provider engagement in research enrolment (QI methodology)
audits.st: Internal target to increase provider engagement by 50% from baseline within 9 months
audits.f: 63% decline in provider referrals from baseline
audits.c: Coffee Carts (5-minute educational presentations for providers on shift) and Suboxone Champions peer educator programme, via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Mean weekly provider referrals increased by 14.5% (PDSA cycle 1) and 49% (PDSA cycle 2) relative to baseline

audits.t: Enhanced recovery program in ambulatory pediatric urology: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Enhanced recovery protocol in ambulatory paediatric urology
audits.st: Institutional Enhanced Recovery Protocol (ERP) elements (nerve blocks, opioid reduction)
audits.f: Postoperative opioid prescribing 30% of patients; average 7.6 opioid doses prescribed
audits.c: Reliance on peripheral nerve blocks, reduction of intraoperative/postoperative opioids, implemented over 3 phases with iterative PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Intraoperative opioid use eliminated in >99% of cases; postoperative opioid prescribing reduced to 15% of patients; average opioid doses reduced to 6.1

audits.t: Transforming into a Learning Health System: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Learning health system quality improvement programme (multi-domain)
audits.st: not reported (internal quality indicators across efficiency, effectiveness, efficacy, equity and environmental safety, tracked with statistical process control)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Opioid-sparing analgesia protocol, pediatric enhanced recovery programme, surgical block time optimisation, monitoring of racial disparities in readmission, and reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from inhaled anaesthetics
audits.r2: 37% increase in monthly urology surgical volume; reduced postanesthesia care unit opioid administration for tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy; successful enhanced recovery programme implementation; more than 85% reduction in facility greenhouse gas emissions from inhaled anaesthetics; continued work on surgical readmission equity

audits.t: From targets to solutions: Implementing a trauma quality improvement bundle in Cameroon.
audits.tp: Trauma primary survey and vital sign documentation
audits.st: WHO Trauma Care Checklist and Cameroon Trauma Registry (CTR) primary survey standards for timely and complete vital sign collection and primary survey interventions
audits.f: 0% of patients had a complete set of vitals recorded; only 0.8% had respiratory rate and 7% had temperature recorded; 74% had vitals within 15 minutes; only 7% had repeated vital sign measurement; breathing interventions in 1%, cervical collar placement in 0%
audits.c: Trauma quality improvement (TQI) bundle: a hospital-specific trauma protocol, a bedside trauma checklist based on the WHO Trauma Care Checklist, staff training, provision of essential emergency trauma supplies in the resuscitation area, and monthly quality improvement meetings
audits.r2: Complete set of vitals recorded rose to 69% (p<0.001); respiratory rate collection rose to 76% and temperature to 91% (both p<0.001); vitals within 15 minutes rose to 90%; repeated vitals rose to 52%; breathing interventions rose to 8% and cervical collar placement to 7% (both p<0.001)

audits.t: Quality improvement project to improve adherence to lung protective ventilation guidelines.
audits.st: Lung protective ventilation (LPV) guidelines: tidal volume <=10 mL/kg predicted body weight, >75% of ventilation hours compliant
audits.f: Time spent >10 mL/kg PBW 7.65% of mechanical ventilation hours
audits.c: Sequential implementation of LPV reports, bedside whiteboards and targeted multispecialty education
audits.r2: Time spent >10 mL/kg PBW reduced to 4.04%; time spent below target from baseline to completion improved from 13.2% to 6.75%

audits.t: Venous Thromboembolism Risk and Adherence to Pharmacological Thromboprophylaxis in Hospitalized Patients in Uruguay: First Nationwide Study.
audits.st: Major thromboprophylaxis guidelines (Padua score for medical patients, Caprini score for surgical patients, RCOG guidelines for pregnant/postpartum patients)
audits.f: 71.9% of patients were at risk of VTE; of those, 58.6% received pharmacological thromboprophylaxis; reasons for non-receipt: prescribing omission 16.1%, contraindication 15.9%, already anticoagulated 9.4%; overall 68% of patients were "protected" against VTE; guideline recommendations followed in 70.1% of at-risk patients

audits.t: High Rates of Missed HIV Testing Among Oral PrEP Users in the United States From 2018-2021: A National Assessment on Compliance With HIV Testing Recommendations of the CDC PrEP Guidelines.
audits.tp: HIV testing compliance among PrEP users
audits.st: CDC PrEP guidelines recommending HIV testing every 3 months in oral PrEP users
audits.f: 34.3% of PrEP prescription refills lacked HIV Ag/Ab testing within the prior 3 months (25.8% lacked any HIV test); at 6 months this fell to 23.8%/14.6%, and at 12 months to 16.6%/7.8%

audits.t: Accessibility audit of a health care institute in India: Are people with disabilities being provided their rights?
audits.st: Central Public Works Department (CPWD) validated accessibility checklist
audits.f: 45 pointers fully compliant, 30 partially compliant, 51 not applicable

audits.t: Resident-led improvement project to screen for primary hyperaldosteronism in patients with resistant hypertension in an outpatient clinic.
audits.tp: Primary hyperaldosteronism screening in resistant hypertension
audits.st: Clinical practice guideline recommending screening for primary hyperaldosteronism (PH) in all patients with resistant hypertension; local target to increase screening from 24% to at least 80%
audits.f: Of 58 patients with resistant hypertension, 44 had not previously been screened for PH; baseline screening rate 24% (14/58 already screened or on an MRA)
audits.c: Three sequential PDSA cycles: preclinic PH screening labs ordered with hypertension follow-up clinic visits; resident phone calls to unscreened patients to confirm medication adherence and counsel on screening; and resident phone calls to screen-positive patients to discuss mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) initiation and endocrinology referral
audits.r2: Screening rate rose from 24% to 48% after cycle 1, then to 84% (37/44) after cycle 2; 9/37 (24%) screened positive for PH; 5 of 9 screen-positive patients were started on an MRA, with blood pressure improving in 3 of 5 and none developing hyperkalaemia

audits.t: Screening for Nephropathy in Pediatric Type 2 Diabetes: Quality Improvement to Increase Nephropathy Screening.
audits.tp: Diabetic nephropathy screening in paediatric type 2 diabetes
audits.st: American Diabetes Association (ADA) guideline recommending urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) nephropathy screening at diagnosis and yearly thereafter; local target to increase screening from 56% to 75%
audits.f: Baseline UACR screening rate (visits with screening completed within 12 months) 56%; baseline order rate 75% for the 5 months before interventions
audits.c: Multi-disciplinary QI initiative with iterative PDSA cycles: previsit planning workflow with a care coordination assistant identifying and facilitating screening, nursing/provider and patient/family education on nephropathy screening, and addition of UACR to the existing new-onset type 2 diabetes triage protocol
audits.r2: Screening rate rose to and was sustained at 75% (target met) from September 2022 for 12 months; order rate improved to a median of 97%; no significant difference in screening rate by race/ethnicity (NHB 63%, NHW 64%, Hispanic/Latino 72%, p=0.269)

audits.t: Adherence to Personal Protective Equipment practices during the COVID-19 pandemic: A pilot study.
audits.st: not reported (personal protective equipment adherence standard during COVID-19)
audits.f: Overall unit PPE adherence for all moments ranged from 50-61%; masking had the highest adherence (100%); hand hygiene prior to donning PPE had the lowest adherence (13%)

audits.t: Rapid implementation of blood pressure self-monitoring in pregnancy at a UK NHS Trust during the COVID-19 pandemic: a quality improvement evaluation.
audits.tp: Blood pressure self-monitoring implementation in pregnancy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 81.2% registered for telemonitoring; 3.5% took part in urine self-testing; engagement high with no safety issues

audits.t: "We restrict certain things": a cross-sectional study of health provider adherence to WHO's recommendation for intrapartum oral intake of fluid and food in Greater Accra, Ghana.
audits.st: WHO (2018) recommendation for oral fluid and food intake for low-risk women during labour
audits.f: 54% of women reported being counselled on fluid intake and 43% on food intake; 41% and 34% reported being asked their preference for drinking and eating respectively; 73% drank fluids and 19% ate food during labour

audits.t: Assessing the Adherence to Safety Protocol Among Personnel Working in the Dental Radiology Department: A Qualitative Cross-Sectional Study.
audits.tp: Radiation safety protocol adherence in dental radiology
audits.st: not reported (radiation safety protocol for dental radiology personnel)
audits.f: 71.4% (15/25) reported consistently wearing personal protective devices; 86.5% (18/25) agreed the radiology operatory was well-equipped for radiation safety

audits.t: Implementation of shared decision-making about rooming-in: A before and after an audit of breastfeeding in Taiwan.
audits.st: Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative 24-hour rooming-in policy, with prenatal shared decision-making introduced in Taiwan's certification in 2018
audits.f: Rooming-in rate during hospitalisation was 42.2%
audits.c: Introduction of prenatal shared decision-making (SDM) about rooming-in, integrating women's preferences into care decisions
audits.r2: Rooming-in rate fell to 25.6% (statistically significant decrease)

audits.t: Preclinical obesity curriculum: audit, implementation, and evaluation.
audits.st: Obesity Medicine Education Collaborative (OMEC) competencies for healthcare professionals
audits.f: Of 27 OMEC competencies, 55% were unmet and 41% partially met in the existing curriculum
audits.c: Introduction of a comprehensive first-year obesity curriculum for the class of 2025
audits.r2: Significant improvement in obesity attitudes (reduced belief that obesity is due to poor personal choices) and knowledge (improved in 14 of 15 areas); post-intervention cohort scored significantly better than a historical cohort that did not receive the curriculum

audits.t: Developing a Sustainable Quality Improvement Program in an Academic Center: The Experience of an Adolescent Unit.
audits.tp: Departmental quality improvement programme maturity (Adolescent Medicine)
audits.st: Internal quality improvement target: maintain 5 active formally structured QI projects and have 50% of active projects achieve a sustained centreline shift
audits.f: not reported (programme build-up period before the secondary aim target was consistently met)
audits.c: Formal QI methodology: mandatory QI education for fellows/residents, interdisciplinary QI teams, monthly leadership review of key driver diagrams and run/control charts, and regular reporting to staff and the Hospital Quality and Safety Committee
audits.r2: Consistently maintained 5 active projects; the 50% sustained-centreline-shift target was achieved in Q2 2018 and maintained in 16 of 20 subsequent quarters

audits.t: Quality Improvement in Neonatal Care: Successful Adoption of the Eat, Sleep, Console Protocol in a Rural Hospital Setting.
audits.tp: Eat, Sleep, Console protocol for neonatal opioid withdrawal
audits.st: Internal quality improvement targets: reduce NICU admissions, length of stay under 7 days, and medication use reduced by more than 80% within a year
audits.f: 60.7% of opioid-exposed infants received pharmacological treatment; average length of stay 14.5 days
audits.c: Multimodal Eat, Sleep, Console (ESC) approach: staff education, electronic medical record updates, and nonpharmacological care strategies for in-utero opioid-exposed infants
audits.r2: Pharmacological treatment decreased to 7.9%; average length of stay reduced to 5.25 days; improvements sustained for 24 months with no readmissions within 30 days; hospital charges reduced by over $5 million

audits.t: Using a Cohort-Based Quality Improvement Coaching Model to Optimize Chronic Disease Management for Federally Qualified Health Center Patients.
audits.tp: Chronic disease management quality improvement coaching (FQHCs)
audits.st: Clinic-selected clinical quality measures for hypertension, cholesterol, diabetes and chronic kidney disease; target 10% improvement
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Cohort-based QI coaching model with practice transformation coaches, quarterly peer check-ins, and at least 1 PDSA cycle per year per measure
audits.r2: All 5 FQHCs reached their 10% improvement goals for their chosen clinical quality measures

audits.t: Quality improvement initiative 'S-A-F-H' to reduce healthcare-associated neonatal sepsis in a tertiary neonatal care unit.
audits.tp: Hand hygiene and aseptic technique compliance in the NICU
audits.st: WHO Multimodal Hand Hygiene Improvement Strategy (five moments of hand hygiene) and aseptic non-touch technique (ANTT) principles; local target to reduce healthcare-associated infection (HAI) incidence by 50%
audits.f: HAI incidence 16.1% of admissions; HAI rate 21.8 per 1000 patient days; baseline compliance with ANTT 62%, hand hygiene five moments 79%, hand washing 84%
audits.c: The 'S-A-F-H' (scrub the hub/aseptic non-touch technique/five moments of hand hygiene/hand hygiene) protocol implemented through 9 PDSA cycles: protocol formulation and staff presentations, observation checklists (paper then Google form), group reinforcement at shift handover, weekly focused group discussions, central line care bundle checklists, an ultrasound machine cleaning protocol, a barrier nursing protocol, and structured training for newly posted residents/staff
audits.r2: HAI incidence fell from 16.1% to 8.4% in the intervention phase and to 6% in the sustenance phase (62.8% reduction sustained over a year); HAI rate per 1000 patient days fell from 21.8 to 8.1 (62.9% reduction); compliance with ANTT, hand hygiene and hand washing all improved to above 90% and were sustained

audits.t: Compliance of healthcare workers in a psychiatric inpatient ward to infection control practices during the COVID-19 pandemic: a participant observation study supplemented with a self-reported survey.
audits.tp: Infection control practice compliance in psychiatric inpatient wards
audits.st: Infection control practice guidelines (hand hygiene and personal protective equipment use) during COVID-19
audits.f: Overall compliance rate 42.6%; mask-wearing 91.2%, clinical waste handling 87.5%, sharps handling 67.7%, linen handling 72.7%, hand hygiene 3.3%, glove use 40.9%, personal protective equipment use 20%, surface disinfection 0.4%

audits.t: Enhancing nutritional formula expiry monitoring: A quality improvement project in a tertiary-level hospital in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
audits.st: Joint Commission International Standard MMU.3.1 (storage of medications/nutritional products requiring special consideration)
audits.f: Average 28 expired nutritional formula safety incidents
audits.c: Hospital-wide audit of risks/practices, new hospital policy, flow charts, forms and audit tools, and educational presentations

audits.t: Reducing Adverse Events Associated with Pediatric Cardiac Catheterization: A Quality Improvement Project Focusing on Decreasing Catheterization-Associated Blood Transfusions.
audits.tp: Blood transfusion after paediatric cardiac catheterization
audits.st: Standardised institutional transfusion criteria
audits.f: Red blood cell transfusion (RBCT) frequency within 72h of catheterization 10%
audits.c: Intraprocedural interventions (reduce hemodilution/blood loss/anticoagulation), standardisation of institutional transfusion criteria, and a 'hard stop' requiring QI team consultation before elective postcatheterization RBCT, via PDSA methodology
audits.r2: RBCT frequency decreased to 1.9%, with increased cases between transfusions and no increase in length of stay

audits.t: Adherence to therapeutic gastroscopy guidelines for acute esophageal food bolus impaction: Impact on adverse outcomes and length of stay.
audits.tp: Time-to-gastroscopy guideline adherence for food bolus impaction
audits.st: European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE): gastroscopy within 6h (complete obstruction) or 24h (incomplete obstruction)
audits.f: Of 134 (54.0%) with complete obstruction, 51 (38.1%) received EGD within 6h; of 114 (46%) with incomplete obstruction, 93 (81.6%) received EGD within 24h

audits.t: Patient-Reported Outcome Measures Within a National Multispecialty Surgical Quality Improvement Program.
audits.tp: Patient-reported outcome measure collection in national surgical QI programme
audits.st: Target to accrue >30 hospitals and achieve PROM collection rates >=30% within 3 years
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: IHI Model for Improvement with 15 PDSA cycles targeting HIT platform functionality and patient engagement (email/SMS reminders, personalised communications)
audits.r2: 58 of 65 hospitals (89.2%) achieved collection rates >=30%; 9 (13.8%) achieved >=50%; median maximum hospital collection rate 40.7% (IQR 34.6-46.7%); target exceeded in Q3 2022

audits.t: Reducing Waiting Times and Admission Periods through Pre-Admission Testing: A Quality Improvement Study on In-Hospital Renal Biopsy.
audits.tp: Pre-admission testing to reduce renal biopsy waiting times
audits.st: not reported (internal efficiency target to reduce waiting time and admission period for renal biopsy)
audits.f: Mean waiting time for admission was 13.72±40.30 days (period 1) and 10.00±47.80 days (period 2, post-SARS-CoV-2 outbreak), without statistical significance between periods
audits.c: Implementation of pre-admission testing (PAT) for renal biopsy
audits.r2: Waiting time for admission reduced to approximately 0.76 days, then 2.09±2.65 days; hospitalisation expenses per patient decreased significantly from about USD 69.62±97.09 to USD 41.66±52.82; percentage of missed biopsies significantly low; no significant difference in severe bleeding incidence (p=0.617)

audits.t: Improved Cardiac Rehabilitation Referral Rate Utilizing a Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Team.
audits.st: 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI Coronary Revascularization Guidelines Class IA recommendation for cardiac rehabilitation participation; CDC/CMS Million Hearts Campaign target to increase CR participation from 20% to 70%
audits.f: Cardiac rehabilitation referral rate 51.2%; African American patients significantly less likely to be referred than Caucasian patients (41.0% vs 51.2%, p=0.01)
audits.c: Multidisciplinary QI team via PDSA methodology: standardised/updated EMR orderset with automated CR referral order and evidence-based medicine reminder, provider education, computerised provider order entry reminder, new bedside nursing workflow verifying CR order before discharge, and monthly QI committee monitoring
audits.r2: CR referral rate rose to 87.1% (p=0.0001), a 35.9% absolute increase; improvement significant across gender, race and insurance subgroups; racial disparity in referral no longer significant post-intervention (83.7% White vs 78.4% African American, p=0.166)

audits.t: Proactive advance care planning conversations in general practice: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: Royal College of General Practitioners and Marie Curie Daffodil Standards (2020)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Proactive offer of a personalised advance care planning conversation using a 'What Matters To You' framework
audits.r2: 81% accepted the offer; future care guidance documented using the ReSPECT plan in most cases; clinician and patient satisfaction high

audits.t: Assessment of clinician adherence to Fingolimod instructions and its effect on patient safety.
audits.tp: Clinician adherence to fingolimod monitoring instructions
audits.st: Manufacturer's instructions and monitoring recommendations for fingolimod (bradycardia observation, ophthalmic examination, liver enzymes, infections)
audits.f: 72 patients (51.4%) had poor physician adherence (0-1 instructions followed); 65 (46.4%) had moderate adherence (2-3 recommendations); only 3 (2.1%) had all recommendations followed; complications included bradycardia in 18 patients, macular oedema/infections in 4, and elevated liver enzymes in 6

audits.t: A Prospective Quality Improvement Program to Reduce Prolonged Postoperative Antibiotic Prophylaxis in Ethiopia.
audits.st: International guidelines for surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (adapted locally); target to reduce patients receiving ≥24 h of prophylaxis after clean/clean-contaminated surgery
audits.f: 50.9% of patients received ≥24 h of postoperative antibiotic prophylaxis
audits.c: Hospital-specific guideline development adapting international guidelines to local disease burden, medication availability and cost; multidisciplinary "timeout" discussion of antibiotic indication, choice and duration during clinical rounds
audits.r2: 40.9% received ≥24 h of antibiotic prophylaxis (p=0.027), associated with 0.5 day reduction in postoperative length of stay (p=0.047)

audits.t: Evaluation of the adherence to surgical antibiotic prophylaxis recommendations and associated factors in a University Hospital: A cross-sectional study.
audits.st: Hospital surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (SAP) protocol (indication, antibiotic choice, dosage, duration)
audits.f: Only 20.7% of surgeries adhered to SAP protocols; lower adherence for antibiotic choice and duration, especially in neurological surgeries

audits.t: An audit for the inpatient management of patients with severe hypertension without acute end-organ damage at the Northern Sydney Local Health District.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Antibiotic Stewardship in Chorioamnionitis Exposed Neonates, A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: 2018 AAP guidelines for management of infants at risk for early-onset sepsis (multivariate risk assessment/EOS calculator)
audits.f: 100% of chorioamnionitis-exposed infants received antibiotics, average duration 68 hours
audits.c: Implementation of the EOS calculator to guide antibiotic use in chorioamnionitis-exposed infants, via multiple PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Antibiotic exposure decreased from 100% to 75%, average duration decreased from 68 to 40 hours

audits.t: [A quality improvement project on reducing antibiotic use duration in very low birth weight preterm infants in the neonatal intensive care unit].
audits.tp: Antibiotic use duration in very low birth weight preterm infants
audits.st: Internal quality improvement target: reduce antibiotic use duration percentage by 10% within 12 months
audits.f: Baseline antibiotic use duration percentage was 49%
audits.c: Established sepsis evaluation/management standards; staff education on rational antibiotic use; supervision of standard enforcement on ward rounds; discontinuing antibiotics 36 hours after initiation if no infection evidence and negative cultures; reducing duration of central venous catheterisation and parenteral nutrition
audits.r2: Antibiotic use duration percentage reduced from 49% to 32% (statistically significant)

audits.t: Intervention Bundle for Optimization of Procedural Sedation for Newborns Undergoing Magnetic Resonance Imaging: A Single-Center Quality Improvement Project in Qatar.
audits.st: Local QI project standard developed from an initial internal audit finding an adverse event rate of about 17% with buccal midazolam sedation for neonatal MRI; no external clinical guideline existed for this indication
audits.f: 13% (30/238, after excluding infusion-sedated babies) had adverse events during MRI procedural sedation; optimal documentation in only 25%; 72% required buccal midazolam
audits.c: Consensus MRI procedural sedation intervention bundle (DMAIC framework): weight/risk-tailored buccal midazolam dosing recommendations (100 microg/kg for preterm babies on respiratory support, 200 microg/kg for term babies off support), a transportation checklist, defined MRI-suite monitoring requirements, and a standardised documentation template
audits.r2: Adverse events fell to 7% (8/108); documentation improved by 37 percentage points to 62% optimal; 58% required buccal midazolam, mostly at the lower single dose; image quality was similar between epochs (92% vs 87% optimal)

audits.t: A study on awareness and perception about perinatal death auditing among health care workers in two districts of Karnataka State, India.
audits.tp: Perinatal death auditing awareness among clinicians
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 22 eligible doctors, 16 consented; knowledge of contributors to perinatal death was inadequate and doctors were apprehensive about legal consequences of death auditing.

audits.t: Keys to successful clinical audit and feedback: essential steps to making impactful improvements in patient care.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Project to Decrease Fractures Secondary to Metabolic Bone Disease of Prematurity.
audits.tp: Metabolic bone disease of prematurity screening and fracture prevention
audits.st: Recommended intakes of calcium, calcium:phosphorus ratio and vitamin D; local screening guideline for osteopenia of prematurity
audits.f: Baseline fracture rate 13%, with poor compliance with recommended mineral intakes.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team implemented a screening guideline through four Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles addressing staff education, vitamin D screening and incorporation of calcitriol.
audits.r2: Fracture incidence decreased from 13% to 5.3%; infants born after the guideline were 4.8 times less likely to develop fractures; compliance with mineral intakes improved.

audits.t: Increasing healthcare proxy documentation in an intensive care unit: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: New York State Health Care Proxy Law and hospital guideline requiring solicitation and documentation of a healthcare proxy; local QI target to increase completed HCP documentation by 15% over 3 months
audits.f: Weekly median percentage of sampled charts with completed HCP forms (baseline rate) 40%
audits.c: Multi-faceted intervention targeting education, workflow, access and technology: resident education at noon conference, faculty champions and daily rounds coaching, new expectation to discuss HCP at initial ICU consultation, physical HCP forms placed in ICU/ED work areas, an EHR note template auto-populating HCP status, smartphone app upload prompts, and an EHR tool flagging missing HCP forms
audits.r2: Weekly median percentage of completed HCP forms rose to 67%, sustained at 12 weeks post-intervention; the increase was not statistically significant (chi-squared 8.524, 15 df, p=0.9011)

audits.t: Assessment of thermal index compliance in clinical ultrasound examinations.
audits.st: British Medical Ultrasound Society (BMUS) thermal index guidelines (limits for thermal index for soft tissue [TIS] and bone at focus [TIB])
audits.f: All examinations complied with TIS limits; TIB breaches occurred in obstetrics (44/4643 image intervals, 1.01%, across 47/627 examinations, 7.02%) and non-obstetrics (2/19228 intervals, 0.02%, across 2/1023 examinations, 0.44%)

audits.t: Changing the Culture to Improve CCF: An Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Chest compression fraction during cardiac arrest resuscitation
audits.st: Internal target: monthly median chest compression fraction (CCF) ≥90% (baseline 81.5%)
audits.f: Baseline monthly median CCF 81.5%
audits.c: Standardised clinician feedback forms, increased follow-up for ongoing resuscitations, designated CPR team leader during resuscitations, pre-charged defibrillator prior to rhythm checks, via repeated PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Average CCF increased to 89.0%, with special cause variation on control chart analysis

audits.t: Colonoscopy quality measures and adherence to follow-up guidelines among endoscopists participating in a U.S. endoscopy registry.
audits.tp: Colonoscopy quality and follow-up interval adherence
audits.st: Colonoscopy quality targets (bowel preparation, cecal intubation rate, adenoma detection rate) and guideline-recommended follow-up intervals
audits.f: ≥90% of endoscopists met targets for bowel preparation, cecal intubation and adenoma detection; but 12.0% given ≤5yr follow-up instead of 10yr for no findings, 13.5% given ≤3yr instead of 5-10yr for 1-2 small tubular adenomas, 30.7% given ≤3yr instead of 5yr for small sessile serrated polyps, 18.2% of advanced serrated lesions given ≥5yr instead of 3yr

audits.t: Development and implementation of evidence-based, nurse-leading early warning model and healthcare quality improvement project for transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy: a mixed-methods, before-and-after study.
audits.tp: Nurse early-warning model for transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Nurse awareness/knowledge of early TA-TMA parameters was 26.7% before improvement action.
audits.c: Staff training and assessment, suspected TA-TMA identification pathway and patient education, based on an evidence-based nurse-led early warning model.
audits.r2: Nurse awareness/knowledge rate significantly improved to 100% after the improvement action.

audits.t: The Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland quality improvement project and integrated chronic kidney disease system: implementation within a primary care network.
audits.tp: Chronic kidney disease medicines optimisation in primary care
audits.st: NICE guideline NG203 for chronic kidney disease and NICE Technology Appraisal TA775 for dapagliflozin in CKD
audits.f: 42.9% of nephrology outpatient referrals were discharged following their first secondary care appointment (indicating patients being referred without adequate community optimisation)
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team meetings between primary care clinicians, a consultant nephrologist and nephrology pharmacist; development of SystmOne decision-support tools for CKD case-finding and management; primary-care-led medicines optimisation clinics (ACEi/ARB and SGLT2 inhibitor optimisation)
audits.r2: percentage of outpatients discharged at first attendance fell to 10% (reduction of 32.9 percentage points); 329 (62.5%) optimised per NICE guidelines, 298 achieved target blood pressure, 339 optimised to maximum tolerated RAAS inhibitor therapy, and all 329 optimised patients tolerated addition of an SGLT2 inhibitor

audits.t: Father Engagement in Home Visiting: Findings From a Continuous Quality Improvement Learning Collaborative.
audits.tp: Father engagement in home visiting programmes
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Rapid-cycle PDSA projects (3 per agency) using SMART aims to increase father engagement
audits.r2: Mean father engagement scores increased 39% from first to second assessment; over 60% of PDSAs met or exceeded their SMART aim goal

audits.t: Interdisciplinary quality improvement in oculoplastic surgery: transforming biopsy follow-up through PDSA cycles.
audits.st: Quebec Ministry of Health target: 80% of pathology reports for malignant lesions issued within ≤7 days
audits.f: Absolute compliance rate 37.9% for malignant lesions; pathology turnaround ≤7 days achieved in 37.9% of malignant lesions, versus target of 80%
audits.c: Three simultaneous PDSA cycles: enhanced clinician-pathologist communication channels, a priority system for urgent cases, and an automatic reminder system for pathologists
audits.r2: Absolute compliance rate increased to 93.3%; pathology turnaround compliance rate also reached 93.3%

audits.t: Disparities in Guideline Adherence for Febrile Infants in a National Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence disparities for febrile infants
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics clinical practice guideline for febrile infants aged 8-60 days
audits.f: No differences in primary guideline-adherence measures by race/ethnicity at baseline
audits.c: A national QI collaborative intervention designed to standardise care per AAP guideline for febrile infants
audits.r2: Disparities emerged: e.g. non-Hispanic Black infants had -12.5% (95% CI -23.1 to -1.9) documented shared decision-making for CSF testing; Hispanic/Latino infants had -2.3% appropriate inflammatory markers and -3.6% appropriate ED follow-up compared with overall

audits.t: A UK multicentre audit of the management of patients with primary hypercholesterolaemia or mixed dyslipidaemia with bempedoic acid against published lipid-lowering treatment targets.
audits.st: Joint British Societies (JBS2) lipid-lowering treatment targets
audits.f: 54% (99/184) of patients achieved the JBS2 audit standard for total cholesterol

audits.t: Applying Quality Improvement Methodology to Standardize Pediatric Urinary Tract Infection Diagnosis and Management throughout a Healthcare System.
audits.tp: Paediatric urinary tract infection antibiotic prescribing
audits.st: Local antibiotic stewardship recommendation of cephalexin as first-line empiric treatment for uncomplicated paediatric UTI, target 75%
audits.f: Baseline first-line cephalexin prescribing 34%, with wide variation in antibiotic choice, duration and dosing across 13,000 children.
audits.c: Standardized UTI pathway, electronic health record enhancements and provider education, implemented via Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles with bimonthly monitoring.
audits.r2: First-line cephalexin prescribing for UTI improved from 34% to 66% (target 75% not reached); no change in 14-day return visits.

audits.t: Managing unwarranted variation in hospital care - findings from a regional audit in Norway.
audits.tp: Managing unwarranted clinical variation, leadership compliance
audits.st: Regional leadership strategy for reducing unwarranted variation in outcomes and utilisation
audits.f: Audit found the aim of reducing unwanted variation was not clearly communicated by senior management; a third of leaders lacked scrutiny/awareness of strategic expectations.

audits.t: Nutrition practices in Australia and New Zealand in response to evolving evidence: Results of three point-prevalence audits.
audits.st: Practice compared over time against evolving evidence from the TARGET trial via single-day point-prevalence audits (no fixed numeric target)
audits.f: 42% of patients received enteral nutrition (EN); 33% received calorie-dense EN formula (>=1.5 kcal/ml)
audits.c: Publication of TARGET trial results (a 4000-patient trial showing augmented enteral calorie dose did not improve outcomes)
audits.r2: 33% of patients received EN (down from 42% in 2010, p=0.012); 23% received calorie-dense EN formula (down from 33% in 2010, p=0.038); calorie dose and density were similar to the 2018 audit (22.9 +/- 8.6 vs 23.4 +/- 12.8 kcal/kg/day, p=0.816)

audits.t: Compliance and determinants of infection prevention and control practices among sanitary workers in public hospitals, Eastern Ethiopia: A cross-sectional study.
audits.tp: Infection prevention and control compliance among hospital sanitary workers
audits.st: National and international infection prevention and control (IPC) guidelines
audits.f: Compliance with IPC practice among sanitary workers was 36.21% (95% CI 32.72-39.82%).

audits.t: UK Trainee Experience with WALANT - An Audit of 102 Cases.
audits.st: British Society for Surgery of the Hand (BSSH) guidance on WALANT use
audits.f: Average WALANT volume used was 6.6 ml versus 12.9 ml in published UK data for similar procedures; for single digit flexor tendon repair, 10 ml versus 16.3 ml; all trainees used premixed 1:200,000 adrenaline rather than the 1:100,000 in Lalonde's original formula

audits.t: Best Practices for Optimizing Patients Undergoing Surgical Procedures to Prevent Postoperative Venous Thromboembolism: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Caprini risk score-based VTE chemoprophylaxis recommendations, referenced via American College of Surgeons NSQIP guidance for VTE prophylaxis in surgical patients
audits.f: 13/17 (76%) of patients who suffered a postoperative VTE had received appropriate perioperative chemical DVT prophylaxis based on retrospectively calculated Caprini risk score; 4/17 (24%) received insufficient prophylaxis; average Caprini score 9.9 (highest risk category); original Caprini scores were not found documented in any EMR despite hospital protocol requiring calculation

audits.t: A quality improvement project: Rapid Access Hysteroscopy Clinics with nurse pre-procedural telephone support in the outpatient setting.
audits.tp: Rapid access hysteroscopy pathway with nurse telephone support
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Lead time from first specialist appointment to outpatient hysteroscopy was 25 days (SD 21 days); wait time referral to provisional diagnosis 26 days
audits.c: Implementation of a Rapid Access Clinic (RAC) for hysteroscopy with nurse pre-procedural telephone support, tested via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: FSA-to-OP hysteroscopy lead time eliminated; wait time referral to provisional diagnosis increased to 31 days but standard variation reduced from 30 to 15 days; clinician productivity increased 25% per session; 27/207 women diagnosed with endometrial cancer via RAC

audits.t: Continuous quality improvement in a community-wide TB screening and prevention programme in Papua New Guinea.
audits.tp: Community TB screening and preventive treatment cascade
audits.st: Local TB/TPT screening and treatment care cascade targets
audits.f: 13.7% screened positive; of those without active TB, 82.0% had TST, 78.7% of eligible initiated TB preventive treatment.
audits.c: Continuous quality improvement using PDSA framework; adjustments to CAD4TB threshold and TPT eligibility criteria across three PDSA review cycles.
audits.r2: PDSA cycles increased detection of TB disease/infection and accelerated pace of screening; challenges included meeting screening targets and consumable stock-outs.

audits.t: Using Quality Improvement to Expand and Align State Public Health Long-Term Follow-up Data Collection Across Newborn Screening Conditions.
audits.tp: State public health long-term follow-up data collection for newborn screening
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 77% of attempted long-term follow-up measures were successfully collected; 7% of cases closed to further follow-up (often move out of state).
audits.c: QI Steering Team collaboration developed common measures, refined data sources (EHRs, paper/PDF records, electronic data form) and piloted collection.

audits.t: Adherence to sepsis protocol in a high-risk maternity reference center.
audits.tp: Sepsis protocol adherence in obstetric triage
audits.st: Institutional sepsis protocol for obstetric triage
audits.f: Lactate collected 97.1%, blood cultures 98.1%, antibiotic therapy 94.3%, hydration 51.4% of the sepsis protocol steps completed.

audits.t: REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH IN TRANS AND GENDER DIVERSE PATIENTS: Mind the gap: a nationwide audit of LGBTQ+ inclusion in fertility care providers in the United Kingdom.
audits.st: A checklist of measures for LGBTQ+ inclusion (cultural competence, clinical considerations, online presence), co-created with the LGBTQ+ community
audits.f: Audit identified widespread lack of LGBTQ+ inclusion, particularly for transgender and gender-diverse patients, with deficiencies in clinical knowledge and cultural competence

audits.t: A Quality Improvement-based Approach to Implementing a Remote Monitoring-Based Bundle in Transitional Care Patients for Heart Failure.
audits.tp: Remote monitoring bundle for heart failure transitional care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Remote patient monitoring, clinical telepharmacy, remote therapeutic monitoring and community paramedicine bundle, delivered via 5 PDSA cycles with an equity lens; mid-program adjustment to a hub-based model to reduce technology barriers
audits.r2: Complete bundle recipients (42.2%) had 2.6% readmission vs 14.3% for partial bundle and 20.0% for RPM alone

audits.t: Lean Six Sigma quality improvement approach to implement clinical practice guidelines for prescribing opiates for chronic pain in a primary care setting.
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines for chronic opioid management; target increase from <20% to 50% within 1 year
