audits.f: Baseline rate of chronic pain evaluations and urine toxicology testing was less than 20%.
audits.c: Lean Six Sigma DMAIC approach: stakeholder mapping, root cause analysis, process flow mapping, driver diagram; patient/provider education, health IT, care coordination and new clinic protocols.
audits.r2: Completion rates of chronic pain evaluation clinic visits rose from 19.0% to 51.9%.

audits.t: Management of bone health in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies: A two-center audit in the United Kingdom and Hong Kong.
audits.tp: Bone health management in inflammatory myopathies
audits.st: Regional guidelines/standards for osteoporosis investigation and bone protection in at-risk patients
audits.f: DXA scan performed in 50% (UK) vs 35% (HK), several outdated; of those with BMD measured, osteopenia 35% (UK)/36% (HK), osteoporosis 5% (UK)/36% (HK); 25% (UK) and 64% (HK) exceeded treatment thresholds; treatment given: anti-osteoporotic agents 55% (UK)/15% (HK), vitamin D/calcium 95% (UK)/52% (HK), no treatment 5% (UK)/15% (HK)

audits.t: Implementation of standardized feeding pathways for infants with gastroschisis to improve patient outcomes: A quality improvement project in a level IV surgical NICU.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: No defined feeding pathway/guideline; used as historical comparison group.
audits.c: Created three feeding pathways based on gastroschisis complexity after literature review.
audits.r2: Mean parenteral nutrition duration was 18.9 days shorter (95% CI -31.8 to -7.0) in the pathway group; length of stay 13.1 days shorter (not statistically significant); no significant difference in days to full feeds.

audits.t: Improving role allocation for cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in the emergency department: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: American Heart Association six-person high-performance CPR team model with defined, preassigned roles; local target to increase role-delegation awareness from 19% to 80% within 2 months
audits.f: Only 19% (8/43) of staff were aware of their individual CPR role on the day of a resuscitation; only 13% followed preassigned team roles
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles: staff sensitisation on team dynamics; a simplified standardised format for assigning team roles on the whiteboard; assigning responsibility for role allocation to the shift nursing team leader; and sharing progress charts to sustain motivation
audits.r2: Process indicator (percentage of shifts with roles preassigned) rose to 70% after cycle 1, 81% after cycle 2, 91% after cycle 3 and 95% by week 8; outcome indicator (CPRs where preassigned roles were followed) reached 100% by the end of cycle 3

audits.t: Implementation of a novel daily performance improvement checklist (PIC) improves alcohol screening and intervention compliance in trauma.
audits.tp: Alcohol screening and brief intervention (SBIRT) compliance in trauma
audits.st: American College of Surgeons mandate for SBIRT in trauma centre accreditation
audits.f: Alcohol screening rate 52%.
audits.c: Implementation of a daily Performance Improvement Checklist (PIC) integrating alcohol screening into morning report, from January 2023.
audits.r2: Screening improved to 88%; pre-PIC unscreened patients were more often uninsured.

audits.t: Midwives' compliance with post-exposure prophylaxis guidelines in Tshwane District, South Africa.
audits.tp: Midwives' compliance with post-exposure prophylaxis guidelines
audits.st: Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) guidelines for HIV occupational exposure
audits.f: Midwives had good knowledge of PEP, but underreporting of accidental blood/body fluid exposures and underutilisation of PEP services was found.

audits.t: Computed tomography referral guidelines adherence in Europe: insights from a seven-country audit.
audits.st: European Society of Radiology (ESR) iGuide appropriateness criteria
audits.f: Average CT appropriateness rate 75%, ranging from 58% in Greece to 86% in Denmark; higher rates in public hospitals, inpatients, and specialist referrals.
audits.co: Multiple European countries (Belgium, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Greece, Hungary, Slovenia)

audits.t: Assessment of preparedness for emergency cesarean section by utilizing a checklist before and after an educational intervention: A quality improvement study.
audits.st: Institutional 22-item emergency caesarean section preparedness checklist
audits.f: Baseline mean completion of checklist actions was 78.80%.
audits.c: Educational intervention sessions for obstetrics/anaesthesiology residents and nursing officers on checklist steps often missed.

audits.t: Dialysis Modality Education Timing and Home Dialysis Uptake: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.st: Local referral protocol for modality education (eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73m2 or specified Kidney Failure Risk Equation score)
audits.f: Proportion of eligible patients receiving modality education was 27.1% before the new referral protocol.
audits.c: New referral protocol from September 15, 2022 with updated referral form/process directing nephrologists to refer eligible patients to modality education.
audits.r2: Proportion receiving modality education increased to 56.7%; home dialysis selection rate remained constant at 50.9%; centre home dialysis prevalence 19.6% versus provincial average 24.4%.

audits.t: Adherence to Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Acute Infectious Gastroenteritis in Children as a Measure of Quality of Care Delivered by a Primary Care Facility in Rural Philippines: A Descriptive Retrospective Study.
audits.tp: Acute infectious gastroenteritis guideline adherence in children
audits.st: 2019 Department of Health Clinical Practice Guidelines on Management of Acute Infectious Diarrhea (rehydration, zinc, laboratory use, antibiotics); adherence <70% defined as low
audits.f: Low-osmolarity ORS prescribed in 52%, zinc in 74%; stool analysis in 25%, CBC in 20%; antibiotics (metronidazole 44%, cotrimoxazole 33%); adherence to deferring antibiotics for non-specific AGE was 24%, to deferring stool analysis 73%, to deferring CBC 70%, to correct antibiotic use for indicated cases 95%.

audits.t: Advance Care Planning: A Retrospective Audit in a National Referral Center for Interstitial Lung Diseases.
audits.tp: Advance care planning documentation in interstitial lung disease
audits.st: Guideline-derived 14 key elements of Advance Care Planning (ACP)
audits.f: An ACP element was recorded in 57/60 (95%) of charts; no chart contained all fourteen key elements; most frequent were knowledge of illness, goals of treatment, and fears/concerns.

audits.t: Developing a large-scale quality improvement program for thyroid cancer surgery.
audits.st: Current national guidelines for thyroid cancer surgical care; 10 selected quality indicators
audits.f: Preoperative cytology not performed in 34.3% of cases; 50.0% of patients with >4cm papillary cancer underwent lobectomy; positive margins in 16.2%; 19.2% lacked documented follow-up and 18.6% lacked surveillance plans.

audits.t: Prevent Acute Chest Syndrome checklist (PACScheck): A quality improvement initiative to reduce acute chest syndrome.
audits.tp: Acute chest syndrome prevention checklist in sickle cell disease
audits.st: Internal QI target: decrease development of acute chest syndrome (ACS) by 5% in hospitalised paediatric sickle cell disease population
audits.f: Baseline ACS rate and checklist documentation prior to PACScheck implementation (not reported as a single percentage)
audits.c: Implementation of the Prevent Acute Chest Syndrome checklist (PACScheck) driving appropriate opioid, incentive spirometry, IV fluids, oxygen desaturation evaluation and bronchodilator use, by a multidisciplinary team
audits.r2: g-chart showed fewer encounters developed ACS during PACScheck; p-chart showed increased incentive spirometry documentation; run chart showed median 100% PACScheck documentation at least once per hospitalisation in final 6 months

audits.t: Introducing a Framework for Surgical Discharge Summaries to Improve Accuracy and Succinctness in a Busy District General Hospital.
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians and Royal College of Surgeons guidance on discharge summary content, operationalised as a local 5-component framework (Reason for Admission, Intervention, Surgical Details, Discharge Plan, Follow-up Instructions)
audits.f: 70% (42/60) of TTOs were missing at least one essential element, most often follow-up details; 55% missed two or more, 35% missed three or more; format varied widely by individual writing style
audits.c: A standardised TTO framework agreed with surgical consultants, introduced via teaching sessions and ward posters (PDSA cycle 1), then integrated as an auto-text e-template into the electronic patient record (CERNER) system (PDSA cycle 2)
audits.r2: After cycle 1: complete TTOs increased 30% and TTOs missing 2+ elements fell 48%, though follow-up information remained the dominant missed element (90.9% of missed points); after cycle 2: TTOs missing one or more points fell a further 21%, but follow-up omissions and excessive/duplicated information persisted

audits.t: Multidisciplinary protocol to reduce surgical readmissions in Australia: American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program.
audits.st: ACS-NSQIP 30-day unplanned readmission rate (historical institutional benchmark 7.9%)
audits.f: Historical pre-protocol readmission rate 7.9%
audits.c: Multidisciplinary protocol: surgical readmissions nurse-patient liaison, access to a surgical walk-in clinic, and early post-discharge phone contact
audits.r2: 30-day readmission rate 5.6% (49/874), a 30% reduction compared with the historical 7.9% rate (p=0.03); median length of stay after readmission 4 days

audits.t: Using Quality Improvement to Optimize Blood Product Utilization in a Pediatric Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory.
audits.tp: Blood product ordering optimisation in cardiac catheterisation
audits.st: Internal target: increase adherence to packed red blood cell (PRBC) ordering guidelines to greater than 97%
audits.f: Adherence to PRBC ordering guidelines was 86%
audits.c: Revised PRBC ordering guidelines, updated procedure reports to include PRBC administration, via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Adherence to new protocol guidelines increased from 86% to 100%

audits.t: Improving routine mental health screening for depression and anxiety in a paediatric lupus clinic: a quality improvement initiative for enhanced mental healthcare.
audits.tp: Mental health screening in a chronic disease clinic
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics recommendation for annual routine mental health screening in youth aged 10+ and Canadian Paediatric Society Mental Health Task Force endorsement of age-appropriate screening; local target to increase PHQ-9/GAD-7 screening from 15% to 80% by November 2023
audits.f: Mean baseline PHQ-4 screening completion rate 15% (28/189); of completed screens, 14% were positive
audits.c: A standardised MH screening clinical workflow and referral algorithm developed with stakeholders, two virtual MH educational workshops for healthcare providers, a designated 'MH champion' role, preclinic reminders of eligible patients, and a patient/caregiver MH resource handout, tracked with SPC p-charts across multiple PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Screening rate rose from 15% baseline, met the 80% target by October 2022 (peaking at 100% in December 2022), but was not sustained after MH champion staff turnover, settling to a mean of 56% by the end of the project; 45% of patients screened positive for mild or greater depression/anxiety symptoms; 10% of screens led to MH service referral, seen within 2-12 weeks

audits.t: Impact of a Medication Reconciliation Improvement Package on Adherence to Medication Reconciliation Among Internal Medicine Physicians: A Quality Improvement Project in a Lower-Middle Income Country.
audits.st: Internal target: improve adherence to medication reconciliation at admission (pre-intervention <50%)
audits.f: Adherence to medication reconciliation was 44.4% (1983/4471) pre-intervention
audits.c: Medication reconciliation improvement package: physician meetings, dedicated WhatsApp reminder groups, and appreciation messages for timely adherence, following root-cause analysis by a QI team
audits.r2: Adherence increased to 67.2% (2314/3443) in the intervention phase

audits.t: Practices of Informed Written Consent for Elective Urological Procedures at a Tertiary Care Hospital in Sudan.
audits.st: General Medical Council (UK) Guidance on Professional Standards and Ethics for Doctors: Decision Making and Consent (2020) and Royal College of Surgeons of England Consent: Supported Decision-Making (2016)
audits.f: Diagnosis and procedure documented in 100%; potential benefits in 85.7%; potential risks in only 42.9%; likely result of not having the procedure in 23.8%; alternative treatment in 28.6%; senior doctor (consultant) involvement in only 33.3%; consultant-obtained consents were 100% complete versus 66.7% for registrars and 35.7% for medical officers

audits.t: Impact of an antibiotic stewardship program on adherence to antibiotic prescription in children admitted with urinary tract infection.
audits.tp: Antibiotic stewardship for paediatric urinary tract infection
audits.st: Local guidelines for empiric and targeted UTI antibiotic therapy
audits.f: Adherence to local guidelines for empiric therapy was highest immediately after each of two interventions (2018 and 2021) and decreased thereafter.
audits.c: Pediatric antimicrobial stewardship programme interventions in 2018 and 2021.
audits.r2: Adherence to local guidelines was highest immediately post-intervention then slightly decreased; use of cephalosporins remained high; increased resistant E. coli strains observed.

audits.t: Adolescent Chlamydia Screening in Pediatric Primary Care: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Adolescent chlamydia screening in primary care
audits.st: Internal target: increase chlamydia screening in adolescents 15-19 years from 7.8% to 15%
audits.f: Chlamydia trachomatis screening rate was 7.8%
audits.c: Universal opt-out chlamydia screening with universal urine collection at well visits, plus patient and staff education and STI treatment protocols
audits.r2: Screening rate increased to 34.1% (exceeding the 15% target)

audits.t: Quality Improvement Initiatives for Pleural Infection Managed with Intrapleural Therapy.
audits.tp: Pleural infection management care-process quality improvement
audits.st: Internal pleural infection management care-process standards (drainage practices, intrapleural therapy adequacy) identified as deficient by prior audits
audits.f: Surgical management rate 14%; drains smaller than 12F used in 51% of cases; various care-process gaps identified by prior audits
audits.c: Pleural drainage policy and order set, intrapleural therapy protocol and preprinted order, nurse-administered intrapleural therapy, local pleural infection guideline development, and an online learning module for physicians
audits.r2: Surgical management decreased from 14% to 0% (P=0.01); drains smaller than 12F decreased from 51% to 7% (P<0.05, quoted as significant); additional drain insertion 62% to 48% (P=0.12, not significant); 70% of intrapleural therapy doses given by nurses

audits.t: Analysis of Adherence to AAO-HNSF Clinical Practice Guidelines for Sudden Hearing Loss.
audits.st: 2019 AAO-HNSF guidelines for diagnosis and management of sudden hearing loss/sudden sensorineural hearing loss
audits.f: 59.1% underwent recommended audiogram testing (35.8% within 2 weeks); of 3107 SSNHL cases, only 25.5% obtained MRI/ABR within 1 month; steroids prescribed to 54.5%.

audits.t: Improving the non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTEACS) pathway using quality improvement methodology.
audits.tp: Time to angiography for non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome
audits.st: NICE guideline NG185 quality standard: coronary angiography within 72 hours of first hospital admission for intermediate/higher-risk NSTEACS patients
audits.f: compliance with the 72-hour standard was 18%; average pathway time was 172 hours
audits.c: Four sequential PDSA cycles: earlier cardiology senior decision-maker involvement, earlier completion of electronic angiography referrals, ring-fencing cardiac trolley beds for 'treat & repatriate' patients, and expanding the angiography laboratory to 6-day working
audits.r2: average pathway time reduced from 172 to 94.72 hours, a 45% improvement, with reduced variability, though the 72-hour target compliance was still not fully achieved

audits.t: Adherence to Synoptic Cancer Pathology Reporting Among Pathologists in the National Department of Veterans Affairs Health Care System.
audits.st: College of American Pathologists anatomic site-specific cancer protocols for synoptic reporting
audits.f: 778/1618 (48%) reports were synoptic; 77% of resections vs 19% of biopsies; colorectal resections 97%, colon biopsies 0.5%

audits.t: Tecniche di scavo: audit sugli esiti in medicina generale.
audits.tp: Netaudit peer-led general practice audit network
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Indwelling urinary catheter use and adherence to clinical practice guidelines: A point prevalence study in adult hospital inpatients.
audits.tp: Indwelling urinary catheter use and guideline adherence
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines for indwelling urinary catheter (IDC) management
audits.f: 77/502 (15.3%) had an IDC; 57% (44/77) had no documented removal plan; 43% (32/74) lacked a securement device; 61.4% (27/44) of patients did not know reason for catheter

audits.t: Quality Improvement Report: The Sliding Sign Initiative-Facilitating Earlier Detection of Deep Endometriosis in an Academic US Department.
audits.tp: Sliding sign ultrasound protocol for endometriosis detection
audits.st: Internal target: improve sliding sign (SS) maneuver performance and reporting consistency to 80%
audits.f: SS maneuver performed correctly in 52.1% of eligible patients; SS reported in 69% of cases and reported and interpreted correctly in 59%
audits.c: Protocol development and educational sessions (cycle 1); reminder posters (cycle 2, revised cycle 3) and revised eligibility criteria; in-person discussions, reference guide distribution, and a dictation software macro (cycles 4-5)
audits.r2: SS maneuver performance increased to 83.9% by cycle 5; correct reporting and interpretation reached 79.5% by cycle 3 and plateaued; 37 patients newly diagnosed with endometriosis

audits.t: Determinants of non-adherence to antibiotic treatment guidelines in hospitalized adults with suspected community-acquired pneumonia: a prospective study.
audits.tp: Antibiotic treatment guideline adherence in community-acquired pneumonia
audits.st: Antibiotic treatment guidelines for community-acquired pneumonia (choice and duration)
audits.f: 91.6% received empirical antibiotics within 48h, 79.7% adhering to guidelines for choice; of 341 analysed for duration, only 20.2% received guideline-consistent duration.

audits.t: Enhancing Outcomes and Efficiency in Large Epidermal Cyst Management: Quality Improvement Approach in Primary Care.
audits.tp: Epidermal cyst management in primary care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average operative time 45 minutes; postoperative complication rate 18%; follow-up adherence and satisfaction not separately quantified at baseline
audits.c: Standardising surgical protocols, implementing a new scheduling system, and developing patient education materials, via PDSA cycles over three phases
audits.r2: Average operative time reduced to 30 minutes; follow-up adherence rose to 92%; postoperative complication rate declined to 9%

audits.t: Documenting Trends in Malaria Data Reporting Accuracy Using Routine Data Quality Audits in Zambia, 2015-2022.
audits.tp: Malaria data reporting accuracy quality audits
audits.st: Routine data quality audit threshold of >=85% for high reporting accuracy
audits.f: Facilities with high accuracy (>=85%) at visit 1: 23% (HMIS) and 42% (MRRS).
audits.c: Routine data quality audit (DQA) visits repeated over successive visits.
audits.r2: Facilities with high accuracy increased to 56% (HMIS) and 85% (MRRS) by visit 8; low-accuracy facilities (<70%) were uncommon (<15%).

audits.t: Effects of Prospective Audit and Feedback in Patients with Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase-Producing Escherichia coli Bacteremia.
audits.tp: Prospective audit and feedback for antimicrobial stewardship in bacteraemia
audits.st: Infectious Diseases Society of America antimicrobial stewardship guideline recommendation for prospective audit and feedback (PAF)
audits.f: Antibiotic de-escalation to narrow-spectrum cefmetazole occurred in 32.4% of pre-PAF patients; treatment failure rate 38.7%.
audits.c: Implementation of prospective audit and feedback (PAF) for all patients with positive blood cultures from July 2022.
audits.r2: De-escalation rate increased to 80.7% (p=0.0003); treatment failure decreased to 12.9% (p=0.04).

audits.t: Evaluating compliance with quality indicators of HIV and AIDS clinical care and analyzing those associated with mortality in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
audits.tp: Compliance with HIV/AIDS clinical care quality indicators
audits.st: 66 core quality indicators for HIV/AIDS clinical care (locally developed 2023)
audits.f: Overall compliance with quality indicators was 78.79%; indicators associated with mortality included late HIV diagnosis, resistance assessment in virologic failure, and cardiac risk evaluation.

audits.t: Patients with functional gastrointestinal disorders spend less time in tertiary care when managed by a single clinician: results of a multicentre audit in South Australia.
audits.tp: Functional gastrointestinal disorder management against guidelines
audits.st: Guidelines recommending early, positive diagnosis of functional gastrointestinal disorders to reduce over-investigation
audits.f: Median time to FGID diagnosis 70 days (IQR 0-175), over a median of 4 outpatient encounters (IQR 3-6), overall time in service 182 days (IQR 105-344); single-clinician care associated with earlier diagnosis (HR 1.6, 95% CI 1.25-2.04)

audits.t: Report on an audit of two decades' activities of a clinical ethics committee: the Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust Clinical Ethics Advisory Group (CEAG).
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 223 matters discussed: 86 Trust policy issues, 117 clinical cases (84 adult, 33 child), 12 procedural issues, 8 UK Clinical Ethics Network cases; 47% (105/223) rated 'excellent' and 70% (156.5/223) 'good or better'; 41% (92/223) deemed suitable as sentinel cases

audits.t: Guideline on the Use of Intravenous Ketamine for Procedural Sedation in the Children's Emergency Department: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Ketamine procedural sedation guideline in children's emergency department
audits.st: Royal College of Emergency Medicine (RCEM) guidance on ketamine sedation for children
audits.f: only 1/16 (6%) reductions used ketamine sedation, 9/16 (56%) required general anaesthesia; 61% of staff reported awareness of ketamine sedation steps, 56% felt competent in airway management, 61% confident using ketamine, 83% wanted a structured guideline
audits.c: Development and implementation of a standardised intravenous ketamine sedation policy/brochure, with staff training and workshops, reviewed by a multidisciplinary stakeholder group
audits.r2: support for guideline rose from 61% to 94%; airway management competence rose from 56% to 94% (+38 percentage points); confidence in administering sedation and guideline-related metrics all improved (e.g. 89% believed guideline reflected evidence-based practice)

audits.t: Reducing wait times for access to inpatient rehabilitation for patients with acquired brain injury: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Provincial targets/benchmarks for wait times; project aim was to reduce mean referral-to-admission wait from 27 to 19 days (30% reduction) and mean decision wait from 9.5 to 5 days
audits.f: Mean wait time from referral to admission 27 days; mean wait time for decision 9.5 days, both exceeding provincial targets/benchmarks
audits.c: Standardised intake protocol and a referral checklist, developed via process mapping, value analysis, five-why analysis and iterative PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Mean decision wait time reduced to 4 days (58% reduction); mean admission wait time reduced to 12 days (54% reduction)

audits.t: Taking risk to heart: An evaluation of cardiometabolic risk and screening guideline adherence in outpatients with spinal cord injury.
audits.tp: Cardiometabolic risk screening in spinal cord injury
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines for cardiometabolic disease (CMD) risk identification and management (frequency of screening for obesity, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, diabetes)
audits.f: 43.8% had established CMD (≥3 risk factors), 94.5% had at least one risk factor (obesity 82.2%, dyslipidaemia 71.7%, hypertension 46.5%, diabetes mellitus 34.8%); hypertension screening completed at 14.3% of appointments and obesity screening at 10.4%; dyslipidaemia and diabetes screening frequency could not be determined

audits.t: Assessment of adherence to American Diabetes Association guidelines and evaluation of social determinants of health and interventions in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in a nurse practitioner-owned clinic.
audits.tp: Type 2 diabetes management adherence to ADA standards and SDOH screening
audits.st: 2023 American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Care
audits.f: Average A1C improved for most patients except those with positive social determinants of health (SDOH) screens, who had higher overall A1Cs
audits.c: Multiple PDSA cycles generating new recommendations to promote adherence to diabetes metrics; current cycle implemented evidence-based interventions and social worker collaboration to address SDOH
audits.r2: Improvement in addressing social needs in patients with type 2 diabetes following social worker collaboration with NPs; overall mean A1C improved

audits.t: Optimizing neuromuscular block monitoring and reversal: A large-scale quality improvement initiative in a diverse healthcare setting.
audits.tp: Neuromuscular block monitoring and reversal optimisation
audits.st: Evidence-based best practices for dosing, monitoring (Train-of-Four) and reversal of neuromuscular block
audits.f: Baseline Train-of-Four (TOF) monitoring rate was 42%
audits.c: Interdisciplinary quality improvement using the IHI framework: interventions to increase TOF monitoring and promote evidence-based, cost-effective use of reversal agents (sugammadex), including financial incentives for department-wide target monitoring rates
audits.r2: TOF monitoring increased from 42% to 83%; postoperative respiratory complication rates decreased 41% (RR 0.59, 95% CI 0.32-0.96)

audits.t: Standardisation of Blood Pressure Measurement Among Patients Attending an Urban Primary Health Centre: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: World Health Organisation blood pressure measurement guideline checklist
audits.f: Baseline adherence to standardised BP measurement was 0.4% (n=1).
audits.c: Crowd management, infrastructure/equipment improvements, standard operating procedures and staff training, over two PDSA cycles within six weeks.
audits.r2: Adherence to standardised BP measurement increased to 86.2% (n=119).

audits.t: Real-World Retrospective Audit on the Use of the TechnoClone TECHNOSCREEN ADAMTS-13 Assay in the Diagnostic Process for Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura at LabPlus, New Zealand.
audits.tp: ADAMTS-13 lateral flow assay diagnostic protocol audit
audits.st: Internal laboratory protocol for confirmatory ADAMTS-13 testing (TECHNOSCREEN then TECHNOZYM ELISA)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Introduction of the TECHNOSCREEN ADAMTS-13 lateral flow assay (ADSC) into the diagnostic protocol
audits.r2: ADSC had 100% negative predictive value on diagnostic samples; protocol increased median turnaround time by 18 hours (p=0.01); if ADSC of 0.1 IU/mL taken as negative, median TAT decreased by 17 hours (p=0.0003) in adjacent hospital samples

audits.t: Stroke nurse-led intravenous thrombolytic therapy strategy for ischemic stroke based on timeline process: A quality improvement program from China.
audits.st: Door-to-needle time targets for intravenous thrombolysis in ischaemic stroke
audits.f: Door-to-needle time (DNT) was 46 (38, 58) minutes.
audits.c: Timeline process management system, nurse-led stroke process management team, homogeneous training, standardised IVT process and an incentive policy, from June 2021-August 2023.
audits.r2: DNT reduced to 30 (24,44) minutes (B1) and 31 (24,41) minutes (B2), both significantly lower than group A.

audits.t: When Auditing Is Not Enough: Analysis of a Central Line Bundle Audit Program.
audits.tp: Central line bundle audit and CLABSI rates
audits.st: Central line maintenance bundle audit process to reduce central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI)
audits.f: No correlation between CLABSI rates and audit bundle performance at hospital level (adult P=.619, r-sq 2.13%; peds/NICU P=.825, r-sq 0.43%) or unit level (n=7; P=.8-.896)
audits.c: Central line maintenance bundle audit program (already in place during the study period; study analyses its impact rather than introducing a new change)
audits.r2: No correlation found between audit volume and CLABSI rates at hospital or unit level; a single non-participating unit had a lower CLABSI rate than comparable participating units (P=.008)

audits.t: Audit for antifungal treatment usage in adults with invasive fungal infection: A prospective observational study.
audits.tp: Antifungal treatment usage audit for invasive fungal infection
audits.st: Predefined antifungal appropriateness scoring against prescribing standards
audits.f: Optimal antifungal use observed in 66.0% of cases; non-optimal reasons: alternate drug selection 18%, inappropriate dosage 12%, lack of adjustment after microbiology results 14%, incorrect therapy duration 16%; 39.7% of days of therapy were non-optimal

audits.t: Impact of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery Protocol Compliance on Outcome After Pancreatic Surgery: Results From a Certified ERAS Center.
audits.tp: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery protocol compliance in pancreatic surgery
audits.st: ERAS guideline recommendations (27 items) for pancreatic surgery
audits.f: Only 90 patients (15.2%) achieved high overall ERAS compliance (>=70%); high compliance was associated with fewer complications, reduced 30-day mortality and shorter hospital stay.

audits.t: Development of a transition program for emerging adults with type 1 diabetes: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Transition program for young adults with type 1 diabetes
audits.st: Got Transition's Six Core Elements of Health Care Transition adapted with American Diabetes Association transition guidelines
audits.f: Baseline transition activity score was 12/32 on the Current Assessment of Healthcare Transition Activities tool.
audits.c: Institute for Healthcare Improvement Model for Improvement used to design a structured transition programme for ages 16-18, integrated into the electronic health record.
audits.r2: Transition activity increased to 28/32 on the Current Assessment of Healthcare Transition Activities tool.

audits.t: Compliance to international guidelines and rational use of antibiotics in urinary tract infections in a country without national guidance: a cross-sectional study.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing conformity for urinary tract infection without national guidance
audits.st: International guidelines for UTI antibiotic prescribing (molecule, dose, duration)
audits.f: Global conformity to international guidelines was 31.4%; conformity on drug choice 83.2%, daily dose 74.7%, duration 41.6%.

audits.t: Increasing Premedication for Neonatal Intubation: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Local aim to increase premedication use for nonemergent neonatal intubation from 22% to 80%
audits.f: Baseline premedication use for neonatal intubation was 22%.
audits.c: Key driver diagram-guided PDSA cycles; premedication bundle and unit-specific protocol.
audits.r2: Premedication use increased to 52% (target of 80% not reached); first-attempt intubation success 77.6% (premedicated) vs 66.7% (not premedicated), not statistically significant.

audits.t: Reducing inappropriate antibiotic prescribing for acute uncomplicated bronchitis: a systemwide quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Inappropriate antibiotic prescribing for acute bronchitis
audits.st: Antimicrobial stewardship appropriateness criteria for acute uncomplicated bronchitis
audits.f: Baseline proportion of inappropriate antibiotic prescriptions was 44.9%.
audits.c: Bundle of antimicrobial stewardship interventions implemented systemwide.

audits.t: A clinical decision support tool for improving venous thromboembolism risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis prescribing compliance within an electronic medication management system: a retrospective observational study.
audits.tp: VTE risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis prescribing compliance
audits.st: Local venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention protocol
audits.f: Pre-implementation rates of timely VTE risk assessment documentation and guideline-compliant prophylaxis prescribing were lower (baseline, pre-CDS).
audits.c: Implementation of an integrated electronic alert system with a computerised physician order entry (CPOE)-based order set for VTE risk assessment within the electronic medication management system.
audits.r2: Rates of VTE risk assessment documentation within 24h increased by 29.9 percentage points post-implementation; guideline-compliant VTE prophylaxis prescribing also improved.

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Surgical Site Infections in Pediatric Patients Undergoing Cardiothoracic Surgery.
audits.tp: Surgical site infection reduction in paediatric cardiothoracic surgery
audits.st: Centers for Disease Control National Healthcare Safety Network SSI definitions; target <1 SSI per 100 cases
audits.f: Baseline/preintervention SSI rate was higher than the intervention period.
audits.c: QI bundle developed over two eras (2015: enhanced hygiene bundle, scripted discharge calls; 2019: SSI risk factors, SSI-QI rounding team, wound care education and standardisation).
audits.r2: SSI rate decreased to 2.82 per 100 cases during intervention and 0.55 per 100 cases postintervention (95% CI 0.24-1.26), below the <1/100 goal; bath compliance improved from 80% to 96.1%.

audits.t: Adolescents with first-episode psychosis and clinical high risk in the Province of Ferrara: an audit on the implementation of a specialised early intervention program.
audits.tp: Early intervention programme implementation for first-episode psychosis
audits.st: Standardised assessment protocol for the first-episode psychosis/clinical high-risk (FEP-CHR) early intervention programme
audits.f: 29 patients admitted (19 FEP, 10 CHR); lower-than-expected incidence rate; sub-optimal adherence to standardised assessment; one in three had psychiatric hospitalisation during treatment; 5 patients achieved full recovery
audits.c: not reported (audit prompted subsequent quality improvement initiatives including professional training, but these were not yet measured)

audits.t: Optimizing the Use of Computed Tomography for Appendicitis Diagnosis in the Pediatric Emergency Department Through the Quality Improvement Methodology.
audits.tp: CT scan use in paediatric appendicitis diagnosis
audits.st: Local aim to decrease CT use by 50% while maintaining diagnostic accuracy for suspected appendicitis
audits.f: 14 CTs performed in June (baseline); 36.5% of patients underwent CT after right lower quadrant ultrasound.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary coordination requiring surgical consult before ordering CT, with monthly PDSA cycles, June-December 2023.
audits.r2: CT use decreased to 4 in September (71% decrease, p=0.029); CT after ultrasound fell to 11.8%; surgical consult rate before CT rose from 50% to 100% by December.

audits.t: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Decrease Behavioral Health Unit Readmission Rates.
audits.st: Internal target: decrease 7-day and 30-day readmission rates to BHU by 20% by May 2023
audits.f: Baseline mean readmission rates: 5.54 per 100 hospitalisations at 7 days and 11.52 per 100 hospitalisations at 30 days
audits.c: Standardised workflows and checklists trialled via PDSA cycles, October 2021 to November 2022
audits.r2: 7-day readmission rate decreased from 5.54 to 2.83 per 100 hospitalisations (49% reduction); 30-day rate decreased from 11.52 to 7.38 (36% reduction); readmission checklist used for 81/83 patients (97.5%)

audits.t: Higher compliance with the enhanced recovery after surgery protocol improves postoperative recovery and 6-month mortality in upper gastrointestinal surgery.
audits.tp: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery protocol compliance in upper GI surgery
audits.st: ERAS protocol for upper gastrointestinal surgery
audits.f: Patients grouped by compliance: conventional care (58), moderate-compliance (33), high-compliance (67); high-compliance group had reduced GI recovery time (61h vs 96h vs 72h), shorter LOS (6 vs 10 vs 12.5 days) and lower 6-month mortality (0% vs 15.2% vs 13.8%).

audits.t: Increasing Contraception Documentation in an Academic Rheumatology Clinic: A Quality Improvement Approach.
audits.st: Local aim to increase contraception screening/documentation to >50% by 24 weeks
audits.f: Baseline contraception documentation rate was 11%.
audits.c: Six interventional cycles over 24 weeks: introductory educational session with documentation instruction/scripts, email reminders from nursing leadership, and interim educational sessions.
audits.r2: Contraception documentation increased to 54% at 24 weeks (median 30%) and was sustained at 50% at one year.

audits.t: Quality of referrals and adherence to guidelines for adult patients with minimal to moderate head injuries in a selection of Norwegian hospitals.
audits.tp: Head injury referral quality and guideline adherence
audits.st: Scandinavian guidelines for mild, minimal and moderate head injuries, and general referral guidelines
audits.f: 65% of referrals were assessed as justified according to the guideline by at least one rater; 17% were justified outside the guideline; in 52% at least one rater required more information.

audits.t: Introducing and establishing birth companionship in labour ward of a tertiary care centre in North India: a quality improvement journey through and beyond COVID-19 pandemic.
audits.tp: Birth companionship implementation in labour ward
audits.st: Local aim to increase birth companionship from 0% to 70% in 8 weeks (respectful maternity care)
audits.f: Baseline rate of mothers accompanied by a birth companion was 0%.
audits.c: Fishbone analysis, antenatal sensitisation and counselling, WhatsApp groups and monthly labour room induction classes, tested via PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: Target of 70% was achieved after multiple PDSA cycles, with practice sustained after COVID-19 disruption.

audits.t: Reduction in bacterial culture positivity rates at a human milk bank facility of a tertiary care hospital: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Reducing bacterial culture positivity in human milk bank
audits.st: Local aim to reduce milk-culture positivity rate by 50% or more over 3 months
audits.f: Milk-culture positivity rose from 105/4376 (2.37%) in 2018 to 125/3823 (3.27%) in 2019.
audits.c: Fishbone analysis and PDSA cycles from 2020: improved hand hygiene, sanitisation of donors, steam sterilisers for breast-pump accessories, and recruitment of staff nurses.
audits.r2: Culture positivity declined to 23/2103 (1.09%) in 2020, 12/2345 (0.51%) in 2021, 9/2985 (0.30%) in 2022, and 1/1322 (0.08%) in June 2023, a >99% reduction sustained over time.

audits.t: COVID Effects on Adherence to Joint Committee on Infant Hearing Newborn Screening Recommendations.
audits.tp: Newborn hearing screening follow-up and loss to follow-up
audits.st: Joint Committee on Infant Hearing newborn hearing screening (NBHS) recommendations
audits.f: Loss to follow-up rate 90.7% pre-COVID vs 83% during COVID among infants failing initial screening; 342/388 (88.1%) of those failing follow-up screening had no record of a Diagnostic ABR assessment

audits.t: Enhancing Data Quality in a Statewide Birth Defects Registry: Insights from an Ongoing Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Data quality improvement in a statewide birth defects registry
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Survey completion rate 45% in year 1
audits.c: Open-text anonymous staff survey (abbreviated from 9 to 3 questions in years 2-3) to identify operational/data quality issues, followed by internal strategic planning, training initiatives and data system enhancements
audits.r2: Completion rates 74% (year 2) and 49% (year 3); thematic analysis identified 7 themes including data timeliness and workflow optimisation

audits.t: The good, the bad, and the ugly: Compliance of e-pharmacies serving India and Kenya with regulatory requirements and best practices.
audits.st: Global 'best practice' standards for e-pharmacies; national regulations (Kenya, 12 requirements) and 'proposed requirements' from local guidelines/draft bills (India, 14 requirements)
audits.f: India: 61 websites and 37 apps identified, prescription upload facility on 90% of websites, complete drug information on 16%, met 7.5 of 14 (54%) proposed requirements, none displayed registration numbers, 34% listed narcotic/controlled drugs; Kenya: 26 websites and 3 apps identified, prescription upload facility on 58%, complete drug information on 42%, met 8.9 of 12 (74%) regulatory requirements, 31% displayed registration numbers, 62% listed narcotic/controlled drugs

audits.t: Multicenter Retrospective Registry Study on BCG Use in Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer in Latin America: BLATAM (Bladder Cancer in Latin America) Group.
audits.tp: BCG induction and maintenance therapy timing for bladder cancer
audits.st: Lamm BCG maintenance schedule (instillations at 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 and 36 months ±15 days); SWOG 8507/EORTC 30962 recommendation to begin BCG induction within about 15 days (60-day window used locally) post-TURBT; 2020 EAU risk stratification for NMIBC
audits.f: Mean time to first BCG dose 2.4 months, with 26.7% exceeding the 60-day induction window; 84% completed induction; only 45.9% followed the Lamm maintenance schedule (33.9% used a different regimen, 20.2% had no maintenance); median delay to first maintenance cycle over 36 days beyond the target window, and 65 days for the second cycle; 1-year and 5-year relapse-free survival in high-risk patients 87.3% and 53.3%
audits.co: Argentina, Mexico, Chile, Peru, Brazil (Latin America)

audits.t: Outcomes of robotic-assisted radical nephrectomy during service implementation: Lessons from an audit.
audits.st: not reported (before/after comparison of outcomes following service implementation, no external standard)
audits.f: Pre-robotic era: 55 radical nephrectomies performed by open or laparoscopic approach
audits.c: Implementation of a robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) platform for radical nephrectomy
audits.r2: Robotic era: 45 robotic-assisted (RARN), 48 laparoscopic (LRN) and 7 open (ORN) radical nephrectomies; following full RAS implementation all radical nephrectomies transitioned to RARN; significant reductions in blood loss and length of stay versus the pre-robotic period, though operative times were longer; RARN vs LRN direct comparison showed no major difference in perioperative outcomes except significantly longer RARN operative time

audits.t: Rationalising blood tests in a resource-limited emergency unit: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Rationalising blood test ordering in the emergency department
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines for appropriate blood test ordering
audits.f: Baseline showed frequent full-panel blood test requests with financial strain from indiscriminate ordering.
audits.c: Educational intervention with informative visual aids to guide appropriate blood test ordering, using PDSA methodology.
audits.r2: Total daily blood tests ordered decreased by 48.7%, with fewer full-panel requests and more individual test ordering.

audits.t: Strengthening Reliability and Sustainability: Integrating Training Within Industry (TWI) in a Quality Improvement Collaborative.
audits.tp: Care bundle reliability for healthcare-associated infection prevention
audits.st: Care bundles for CLABSI, VAP and CAUTI prevention
audits.f: Baseline data preceded implementation of Training Within Industry job instruction (JI) methodology.
audits.c: Structured job instruction (JI) training for hub leaders integrated into a nationwide breakthrough series collaborative, with visual management tools.
audits.r2: Mean compliance with prevention bundles exceeded 90%, with overall reductions of 44% (CLABSI), 52% (VAP) and 54% (CAUTI).

audits.t: Aligning with Obesity Guidelines: A Quality Improvement Initiative in Pediatric Primary Care.
audits.tp: Obesity screening and documentation in primary care
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics Expert Committee Recommendations (2007, updated 2023) for BMI-based obesity diagnosis and comorbidity screening from age 2; USPSTF 2017 screening recommendations; local target of a 20% increase in appropriate coding and universal laboratory screening
audits.f: Appropriate combined E+Z obesity diagnosis coding averaged 15% (clinic 1) and 40% (clinic 2); nutrition/physical activity counseling codes used in near 0% (clinic 1) and about 10% (clinic 2) of charts; baseline lipid panel, A1c and ALT screening in ages 9-18 were 56%, 67% and 31% respectively
audits.c: 6 PDSA cycles: initial staff training and clinical toolkit introduction, monthly education sessions, an SBAR memo on E/Z coding, large-group staff training with a coding expert, individual provider coaching/feedback, and EMR changes (diagnosis label update, pop-up prompts, and later nutrition/activity counseling templates)
audits.r2: E/Z obesity coding rose above 80% and was sustained; nutrition/activity counseling coding rose to up to 96% after EMR templates were added; ALT screening met the 20% increase target, but lipid panel and A1c screening did not; extraneous laboratory test collection decreased significantly, though inconsistencies persisted, especially in the 2-8 year age group

audits.t: Dosimetry audit service in Italy: Results of the partnership between Italian Association of Medical Physics (AIFM) and Italian National Institute of Ionizing Radiation Metrology (ENEA-INMRI).
audits.tp: Dosimetry audit service for radiotherapy centres
audits.st: International dosimetry protocols; satisfactory audit result defined as |En score| ≤ 1.0
audits.f: En scores normally distributed, 95% between -0.54 and 0.7; 99.5% within [-1.0,1.0]; 81.1% within optimal range [-0.5,0.5]; one unsatisfactory result traced to a measurement setup error

audits.t: Reducing prematurity-related neonatal mortality: a quality improvement project in Gandhi Memorial Hospital, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
audits.st: Local QI target to reduce prematurity-related neonatal mortality from a median of 20.7% to 14.5%, informed by evidence-based CPAP therapy and infection prevention practice
audits.f: Median prematurity-related neonatal mortality 20.7 per 100 live births; Pareto analysis showed 57.7% of neonatal deaths were prematurity-related
audits.c: Three change ideas via PDSA cycles: transporting premature neonates from the labour ward to NICU using CPAP, increasing use of a CPAP device with integrated oxygen concentrator/blender/compressor in the NICU (blenders increased from 1 to 4), and implementing a 4-component infection prevention checklist
audits.r2: Prematurity-related neonatal mortality fell from a median of 20.7% to 15.4% (a 25.6% relative reduction), shown by 7 consecutive data points below the baseline median; CPAP transport use rose from 40% to 100%; checklist adherence rose from 0% to 100%; staff satisfaction rose from 81% to 83%

audits.t: A quality improvement project on implementing a standardized pain assessment and opioid stewardship guidance at a level IV NICU.
audits.tp: Opioid stewardship and pain assessment standardisation in NICU
audits.st: Internal QI target: reduce opioid usage by 5% within 1 year via standardised pain assessment and opioid stewardship guidance
audits.f: Mean cumulative opioid use (morphine equivalent) was 2.7 mg/kg
audits.c: Multidisciplinary standardised guidance for regular pain assessment and appropriate initiation/weaning of opioids, developed using PDSA methodology, survey and Pareto analysis to identify key drivers
audits.r2: Mean cumulative opioid use decreased to below 0.85 mg/kg, a reduction of >50% (target of 5% far exceeded); no worsening in pain or opioid withdrawal scores at 3 and 5 days after weaning

audits.t: Improving Commitment to Family-Centered Care in the NICU: A Multicenter Collaborative Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Family-centred care committees in the NICU
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline 18% of NICUs had Family-Centered Care committees and 18% had Family Partnership Councils.
audits.c: Collaborative mentoring model with small groups, key driver diagram, Pareto charts, and bi-monthly educational webinars.
audits.r2: Percentage with FCC committees increased to 59% and Family Partnership Councils to 45%; average webinar views increased from 28 to 182.

audits.t: Adherence to minimal retesting interval for HbA1c, vitamin D and thyrotropin in the University Hospital of Nepal.
audits.tp: Adherence to minimum retesting intervals for laboratory tests
audits.st: Minimum retesting interval guidelines for HbA1c, vitamin D and thyrotropin (TSH)
audits.f: Minimum retesting interval breaches: TSH 4.71% (n=1317), HbA1c 13.54% (n=1159), vitamin D 4.28% (n=232); associated cost $12,817.

audits.t: Optimising timely and safe oxygen delivery systems for enhanced patient care: a quality improvement project at Wallaga University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, 2024.
audits.tp: Timely and safe oxygen delivery system
audits.st: Local aim to increase timely and safe oxygen delivery from 30% to 75%
audits.f: Baseline timely and safe oxygen delivery rate was 30%.
audits.c: PDSA cycle with fishbone/driver diagrams: staff orientation on safe handling, clear job descriptions, improved handover, regular maintenance/inventory checks, more cylinders, use of hospital vehicles for transport, and supplier communication system.
audits.r2: Timely and safe oxygen delivery increased to 75%; inventory improved to 76%, equipment checks 65%, onsite training 75%, delivery within 1 day for 70% of orders.

audits.t: Adherence to Perioperative Antimicrobial Prophylaxis in Children in the Settings of Neurosurgery, Otorhinolaryngology, and Orthopedics.
audits.tp: Perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis adherence in paediatric surgery
audits.st: Perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis (PAP) guidelines for paediatric surgical subspecialties
audits.f: PAP was received by 82.7% of children (100% in neurosurgery/orthopaedics, 48% in ORL); indications for PAP present in only 50.8% overall; guideline-appropriate PAP given in 0% (neurosurgery), 2% (orthopaedics) and 2.1% (ORL).

audits.t: Quality Improvement Project to Improve Adherence to Best Practices to Decrease Incidence of Necrotizing Enterocolitis in Preterm Infants.
audits.st: Adherence to a 9-item evidence-based NEC prevention bundle (delayed cord clamping, breast milk education/consent, feeding protocol, avoiding routine gastric residuals, timely antibiotic discontinuation, antacid restriction, NGT replacement schedule, central line removal)
audits.f: Baseline clinically proven NEC incidence 7% at start of intervention
audits.c: Implementation of a 9-item evidence-based NEC prevention bundle with staff dissemination, run as two PDSA cycles over 2 years

audits.t: Follow-Up Adherence After Treatment With Curative Intent for Stage II and III Colorectal Cancer Patients.
audits.st: Dutch CRC follow-up guideline (CEA tests, imaging, colonoscopy schedule) until 2021
audits.f: 18.3% had fewer CEA tests, 41.4% fewer imaging, and 56.1% fewer colonoscopies than recommended by the guideline

audits.t: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery Compliance and Outcomes for Head and Neck Reconstructive Surgery.
audits.st: ERAS guideline compliance across 17 care elements
audits.f: 76.3% moderate compliance, 19.5% low compliance, 4.3% high compliance; preoperative compliance 86%, intraoperative 73%, postoperative 38%; highest compliance for preincision antibiotics (99.6%), lowest for postoperative early mobilisation (10.2%)
audits.c: not reported (retrospective cohort, no intervention tested)

audits.t: Drug prescription patterns and compliance with WHO and beers criteria in older patients.
audits.tp: Prescribing compliance with WHO and Beers criteria in older adults
audits.st: WHO prescribing indicators (mean drugs per prescription, injectable and antibiotic use, generic naming, use of Essential Drug List) and Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medications
audits.f: 36.2% of prescriptions involved polypharmacy (≥5 drugs); average 4.1±2.1 drugs per prescription; 47.3% contained at least one potentially inappropriate medication (NSAIDs most common, 17.9%); injectable drugs in 20.8% and antibiotics in 18.9% of prescriptions; 7.6% did not use generic names

audits.t: Sustained success in endoscopic performance demonstrated by the Irish National Endoscopy Quality Improvement Programme.
audits.tp: Colonoscopy key quality indicator performance (national registry)
audits.st: National Guidelines for the Implementation of the QI Programme in GI Endoscopy (NEQI 2020 key quality indicator targets): caecal intubation rate, comfort score, polyp detection rate, sedation use
audits.f: polyp detection rate 34% (maximum-activity), 31.2% (intermediate-activity), 25.6% (low-activity); comfort scores and caecal intubation rates were lower across all groups than in 2022
audits.c: Ongoing national quality assurance and improvement system (NQAIS-Endoscopy) providing quarterly individual and annual centre-level feedback against key quality indicator targets, as part of the established NEQI programme (not a discrete new intervention within this study)
audits.r2: polyp detection rate improved to 36.3% (maximum-activity), 34.2% (intermediate-activity), 30.1% (low-activity); caecal intubation rate and comfort scores also improved across all activity groups; minimum KQI targets exceeded nationally

audits.t: Efficient quality improvement through the monitoring of Key Performance Indicators in the Quality management Review of a Blood Establishment (BE).
audits.tp: KPI monitoring in blood establishment quality management review
audits.st: Quality Management Review Key Performance Indicators for Blood Establishments
audits.f: Pre-intervention KPI values for expired red blood cell units (WAPI%), units collected per blood drive, and blood unit deficit (not given as single numbers)
audits.c: Interventions to enhance blood sufficiency and blood stock management, monitored via KPIs within the Quality Management Review over 2018-2023
audits.r2: WAPI% index for expired red blood cell units reduced; acceptance limits for units collected per blood drive met; blood units collected increased; deficit in red blood units reduced; KPIs significantly improved with minor exceptions

audits.t: The NorCal brachytherapy waste audit: A simple, validated, toolkit for clinician led waste reduction.
audits.st: Internal QI toolkit standard for waste categorisation and reduction (NorCal Brachytherapy Waste Audit Toolkit)
audits.f: Baseline levels of biohazardous, nonbiohazardous and anesthesia waste and improper biohazardous waste sorting rates prior to intervention
audits.c: Standardised waste audit template weighing/cataloguing waste after each procedure, identification of key drivers, and high-impact interventions selected for waste reduction
audits.r2: Biohazardous waste reduced by more than 50%; improper biohazardous waste sorting eliminated by over 90%; cost savings of $4.22/kg; landfill waste reduced by over 20%

audits.t: Expanding Access to Continuous Glucose Monitoring Through Empowering Primary Care: A Joint Endocrinology-Primary Care Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Continuous glucose monitoring access in primary care for type 2 diabetes
audits.st: Guideline recommendation to offer continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) to all patients with diabetes using insulin
audits.f: 28% of eligible patients using CGM; 8% of patients using CGM started in primary care; weekly CGM orders 0.3 per week
audits.c: Directory for durable medical equipment (DME) suppliers, nursing education with device company representatives, a new electronic ordering system for DME, and a nursing outreach programme for eligible patients, via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Eligible patients using CGM increased from 28% to 42%; patients with CGM started in primary care increased from 8% to 14%; weekly orders increased from 0.3 to 2.3 per week

audits.t: Reducing caesarean section rates in Robson groups 1 and 3: a quality improvement initiative in a private Brazilian hospital.
audits.st: WHO Robson Ten-Group Classification framework for monitoring caesarean section (CS) rates; local SMART aim of a 20% relative decrease in CS rates in Robson groups 1 and 3 managed by internal healthcare providers within 18 months
audits.f: Robson-1 CS rate 65.7%; Robson-3 CS rate 25.4%; overall CS rate (internal HCPs) 82.7%
audits.c: A 5-component intrapartum QI bundle for internal on-duty healthcare providers: a collaborative midwifery-obstetrician model of care for Robson-1 and 3 women, a new labour ward medical coordinator, daily supportive supervision, updated evidence-based intrapartum guidelines, and refresher simulation training
audits.r2: Robson-1 CS rate fell to 44.6% (32% relative decrease, RRR 0.68, p<0.0001); Robson-3 CS rate fell to 14.5% (43% relative decrease, RRR 0.57, p=0.007); overall CS rate fell to 73.8% (11% relative decrease, p<0.0001); no significant change in adverse maternal/perinatal outcomes or maternal satisfaction

audits.t: Maternal Mortality Determinants in Rural Kenya: An Audit of Three Hospitals.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Leading causes of maternal death: haemorrhage 34.70%, eclampsia 20.80%, sepsis 15.80%; unmonitored partograph use, HIV positivity, postpartum period, referral from periphery and low socioeconomic status associated with higher risk

audits.t: Educational audit of radiography clinical training sites in a limited resource setting: Zambian clinical educators perspectives.
audits.st: National Quality Clinical Learning Environment Audit Tool (NQCLEAT), covering 5 clinical education standards
audits.f: 3 of 5 standards showed high adherence (orientation of students, feedback/assessment, achievement of clinical learning outcomes); 2 standards not fully implemented in most sites (demonstrating HEI commitment and supporting student supervision)

audits.t: The clinical outcomes of a hybrid-virtual infant hip clinic for the nonoperative treatment of developmental dysplasia of the hip : a quality improvement study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 53% (77/144) of follow-up visits occurred virtually; 94% (48/51) completed brace treatment; 8% (4/51) had brace-related complications; 10% (5/51) made unplanned visits
audits.c: Replacement of specific in-person follow-up visits with virtual appointments and creation of a dedicated hip clinic email

audits.t: Improving screening rates for sexually transmitted and blood-borne infections among patients initiating care in a low-barrier addiction medicine clinic: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: STBBI screening uptake in addiction medicine
audits.st: Annual screening for HIV, hepatitis B and C, syphilis, gonorrhoea and chlamydia per clinic guidelines; aim to improve screening by 50%
audits.f: At baseline only 65% of patients were offered screening and only 6% completed screening blood work
audits.c: Creation of clinic screening guidelines and hiring of an on-site phlebotomist
audits.r2: Screening rates increased to an average of 33%, with greatest improvement after phlebotomist addition

audits.t: 'Tired all the time': What general practitioners request and find in patients with tiredness/fatigue - an audit against NICE clinical knowledge summary of tiredness/fatigue in adults.
audits.st: NICE Clinical Knowledge Summary (CKS) recommended first-line investigations for tiredness/fatigue in adults
audits.f: First-line investigations requested: FBC 89%, U&Es 83%, LFTs 80%, TSH 80%, bone profile 70%, CRP 66%, plasma viscosity 46%, ferritin 9.4%, TTG 3.2%, CK 1.4%; abnormal result rates ranged from 37% (plasma viscosity) to 3% (TTG)

audits.t: Compliance with infection control practices among healthcare workers in radiology departments: a participant observation study and adenosine triphosphate assay evaluation of environmental cleanliness.
audits.tp: Infection control practice compliance in radiology
audits.st: Infection control practice (ICP) guidelines including hand hygiene, PPE and glove use
audits.f: Overall ICP compliance 41.4%; hand hygiene 10.4%; PPE use 29.4%; glove use 68.2%
audits.c: not reported (observational study, no intervention tested)

audits.t: Integrating Palliative Care Consultation Into Inpatient Liver Transplant Evaluations: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.tp: Palliative care consultation integration into liver transplant evaluation
audits.st: Internal QI target: increase palliative care consultation during inpatient liver transplant evaluation
audits.f: Cycle 1 identified need for increased PC education of ICU nurses and interdisciplinary collaboration
audits.c: Two PDSA cycles led by PC nurse practitioner and social worker: cycle 1 focused on ICU nurse education and interdisciplinary collaboration; cycle 2 modified protocol to prioritise high-risk patients
audits.r2: Palliative care consultation increased by 262.5% from 2018 to 2019, with consults completed on 19% of all patients admitted for inpatient liver transplant evaluation over the study

audits.t: Promoting Effective Pain Assessment: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Pain assessment documentation and nurse adherence to guidelines
audits.st: Updated evidence-based practice guidelines/national standards for pain management
audits.f: Pain assessment documentation rate was 18%
audits.c: Pre- and post-tests, two identical educational training sessions, interviews and chart audits for 49 nurses over three months
audits.r2: Pain assessment documentation rate increased from 18% to 29%; nurses' knowledge of pain assessment significantly increased (t=8.03, p<0.001)

audits.t: Increasing take-home naloxone kit distribution to patients with substance use disorder before hospital discharge: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Take-home naloxone kit distribution before discharge
audits.st: WHO recommendation for take-home naloxone (THN) kits; target increase from 51% to over 80% within 10 months
audits.f: Baseline 51% of eligible patients received a THN kit before discharge
audits.c: Adjusted THN kit inventory, nurse education sessions, just-in-time whiteboard training, streamlined documentation, standardised ordering process
audits.r2: 4 months of sustained THN kit provision above 80%

audits.t: A Hospital-Based Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Postdural Puncture Headache in Cesarean Deliveries.
audits.st: not reported (internal QI target on PDPH incidence)
audits.f: PDPH incidence 16% (21/140); OR time 105 minutes; ephedrine 17 mg, phenylephrine 30 mcg
audits.c: PDSA cycles: preoperative catheterisation, synchronised scrubbing, improved surgeon-anaesthetist coordination, atraumatic needle technique, standardised vasopressor use
audits.r2: PDPH incidence dropped to 1.5% (2/127); OR time decreased to 85 minutes; ephedrine reduced to 6 mg, phenylephrine to 5 mcg

audits.t: Adherence to Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) With Bellwether Surgical Procedures in Ethiopia: A Retrospective Study.
audits.st: Five ERAS guideline recommendations (early mobilisation, feeding initiation, PONV prophylaxis, early catheter removal, IV fluid discontinuation)
audits.f: Overall adherence 65.2% (1810/2275 recommendations) across caesarean section, obstructed labour/fistula and laparotomy cases
audits.c: not reported (retrospective registry review, no intervention)

audits.t: [Compliance with the surgical safety checklist in a hospital in Santander. A cross-sectional studyCumprimento do checklist de segurança para cirurgia em hospital do Santander. Um estudo transversal].
audits.st: WHO surgical safety checklist
audits.f: Overall compliance 13.3% (n=6); pre-anaesthesia phase highest at 55.6% (n=25); surgical instrumentation staff highest compliance (100%, n=8), nursing staff lowest (25%, n=3), p=0.005
audits.c: not reported (cross-sectional observational study, no intervention)

audits.t: Reducing laboratory delays in blood culture pathogen identification: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Time to blood culture pathogen identification
audits.st: Guidance requiring full bacterial identification from bottle flagging positive within 48 hours with older technology and within 24 hours with modern platforms
audits.f: Mean 60 hours to pathogen identification using older API biochemical technology; 0% availability of ID within 24 hours
audits.c: Introduction of a MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry platform to replace the API process, rolled out via two PDSA cycles (indirect analysis from agar plate colonies, then direct from blood)
audits.r2: Mean time to pathogen identification reduced to 10.2 hours; availability of ID within 24 hours improved from 0% to 95%

audits.t: Transfer to Home of Low-Birth-Weight Infants in Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC)-A Point of Care Quality Improvement (POCQI) Approach.
audits.tp: Transfer home of low-birth-weight infants in Kangaroo Mother Care
audits.st: Kangaroo mother care (KMC) as standard of care for low-birth-weight infants at discharge
audits.f: Mean hours of KMC prior to study was 4 hours; baseline rate of transfer home in KMC not given as a single number
audits.c: Fishbone analysis of barriers followed by 4 PDSA cycles: policy of transport KMC, ambulation in KMC during hospital stay, root cause analysis of missed babies, and poster reinforcement
audits.r2: 89% of 59 LBW infants discharged in transport KMC; acceptability 98%; efficacy (euthermia at destination) 88%, mean temperature 36.9°C; mean hours of KMC increased from 4h to 8h; practice sustained at 74% following the study

audits.t: Prospective Audit and Feedback of Targeted Antimicrobials Use at a Tertiary Care Hospital in the United Arab Emirates.
audits.st: IDSA core antimicrobial stewardship interventions (prospective audit and feedback, formulary restriction)
audits.f: Control group data collected without intervention
audits.c: Pharmacist-led prospective audit and feedback system with formulary restriction, implemented February 2024
audits.r2: 186 interventions recommended, 76% accepted; length of stay, length of therapy and days of therapy lower than control group

audits.t: Incidence, Compliance, and Risk Factor Associated with Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infection (CLABSI) in Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Patients: A Multicenter Study in an Upper Middle-Income Country.
audits.tp: Central venous catheter care bundle compliance (CLABSI)
audits.st: Central venous catheter (CVC) care bundle
audits.f: Overall compliance with CVC care bundle components averaged 65%; CLABSI incidence rate 4.16 per 1000 central line days (18 cases/4330 CL days)
audits.c: not reported (prospective observational study, no intervention)

audits.t: Sustained Reduction in Severe Intraventricular Hemorrhage in Micropremature Infants: A Quality Improvement Intervention.
audits.st: not reported (site-specific brain-protective bundle)
audits.f: Baseline severe IVH rate 21%
audits.c: Multidisciplinary brain-protective bundle (e.g. midline head positioning, minimal handling), implemented March-December 2015
audits.r2: Severe IVH rate reduced to 6.45%, sustained at 4.5%, with no change to balancing measures

audits.t: Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis Compliance in Orthopedic Patients With Cardiac Risk Factors.
audits.st: VTE prophylaxis protocols (pharmacological and mechanical)
audits.f: Overall compliance 84% (n=49) elective surgery vs 63% (n=20) emergency surgery; VTE incidence 6.7% (n=6); bleeding complications 8.9% (n=8)
audits.c: not reported (observational compliance monitoring study, no intervention)

audits.t: Adherence to the current guidelines on antibiotic prescription among dental practitioners: A national survey.
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing guideline adherence in dentistry
audits.st: Current antibiotic prescription guidelines
audits.f: 68.55% (218) had good practices, 31.44% (100) showed poor practices; mean knowledge score 19.62±4.28

audits.t: Same-day discharge pathway for elective total hip and knee arthroplasty patients: a quality improvement project at a Canadian community hospital.
audits.st: not reported (internal target for same-day discharge rate)
audits.f: Baseline same-day discharge (SDD) rate 8%, target 15% within 12 months
audits.c: Screening tool, automated arthroplasty same-day track, surgical/anaesthesia standardisation, patient education resources, via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: SDD rate increased to 20% with an 82% success rate; readmission rate decreased to 4-7% from baseline 7-8%; no increase in ED visits or readmissions within 30 days

audits.t: Using quality improvement methodology to reduce Did Not Attends in healthcare within a UK prison.
audits.st: Local target to reduce and sustain the Did Not Attend (DNA) rate below 10% across five core healthcare clinics
audits.f: Pre-intervention DNA rate 21% per week; clinical time wasted 284 minutes per week; cost wastage £303 per week
audits.c: Quality improvement project using the Model for Improvement and PDSA cycles, including standard processes, partnership working with the prison and better patient engagement
audits.r2: DNA rate reduced to 3% per week (86% decrease); clinical time wasted reduced to 66 minutes per week (76% decrease); cost wastage reduced to £99 per week (67% decrease)

audits.t: Enhancing Safety in Mechanical Ventilation: A Quality Improvement Initiative Targeting Unplanned Extubations in a Tunisian PICU.
audits.st: not reported (internal QI target)
audits.f: Baseline UE rate 3.62 per 100 ventilation days
audits.c: Standardised ETT fixation procedures, sedation management protocol, staff training, guided by key driver diagram and Pareto analysis
audits.r2: UE rate decreased to 2.06 per 100 ventilation days, a 42.7% reduction (p=0.015)

audits.t: Effect of ICU Quality Control and Secondary Analysis: A 12-Year Multicenter Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: ICU quality control indicators and mortality
audits.st: Beijing Intensive Care Medical Quality Control and Improvement Center national/local ICU quality control indicators, including Surviving Sepsis Campaign 3-hour and 6-hour bundle compliance, Chinese infection prevention standard WS/T 509-2016, and national guidelines for pain/sedation, nutrition and early mobilisation
audits.f: Proportion of ICU admissions among total inpatients 4.1%; proportion with APACHE II score ≥15 was 52.0%; higher baseline ICU mortality and standardized mortality ratio; VAP historically reported at 12-18 per 1000 ventilator days regionally
audits.c: A 12-year multicentre PDCA-based QI initiative: establishment of QI teams, infection prevention protocols, pain and sedation management, nutritional support programmes, early mobilisation strategies, and regular staff training and feedback
audits.r2: ICU admission proportion rose to 7.3% and APACHE II ≥15 proportion to 67.5% (both p<0.001, reflecting increased case complexity); 3-hour and 6-hour sepsis bundle compliance and pre-antibiotic microbiology testing significantly improved; CRBSI and CAUTI rates, ICU mortality and standardized mortality ratio significantly decreased; VAP fell to a mean of 6.29 per 1000 ventilator days (below historical benchmarks)

audits.t: Impact of an evidence-based sepsis pathway on paediatric hospital clinical practice: A quality improvement study.
audits.tp: Paediatric sepsis pathway time to antibiotics
audits.st: Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care (ACSQHC) Sepsis Clinical Care Standard (2022) and Surviving Sepsis Campaign paediatric recommendations for early antibiotic administration
audits.f: Median time from recognition to antibiotics 60 minutes; 70.0% of septic shock episodes received antibiotics within 60 minutes; 86.2% of sepsis-without-shock episodes received antibiotics within 180 minutes
audits.c: A site-specific sepsis pathway and competency-based education program (screening/recognition tool, escalation pathway, and audit tool), developed by the CAHS Sepsis Working Group and aligned with the ACSQHC standard, with >80% of doctors/nurses trained before launch
audits.r2: Median time to antibiotics fell to 45 minutes (p<0.001); proportion receiving antibiotics for septic shock within 60 minutes rose to 92.5% (p<0.03); proportion for sepsis without shock within 180 minutes rose to 94.8% (p=0.005); no significant change in length of stay, PCCU admission, or mortality

audits.t: Effect of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery compliance on postoperative venous thromboembolism.
audits.st: ERAS guideline compliance (low/moderate/high)
audits.f: 118 (1.5%) patients experienced postoperative VTE; low/moderate compliance more common among VTE patients (11.0%/44.1%) vs no-VTE patients (5.6%/34.5%), p=0.001

audits.t: Improving respiratory rate monitoring in general wards following implementation of a rapid response system: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Respiratory rate monitoring after rapid response system implementation
audits.st: not reported (internal QI target)
audits.f: Baseline RR measurement proportion approximately 3% of total vital sign measurements
audits.c: Three phases: public announcement/education, early warning system implementation, inter-department handoff template modification
audits.r2: Phase 1 IRR 1.148; Phase 2 IRR 2.113 with increasing slope; Phase 3 IRR 1.163 with increasing slope

audits.t: A pilot cluster-randomized controlled trial of an audit, feedback, and coaching intervention on compliance with elementary physical education laws and student physical activity during lesson time.
audits.st: Elementary school physical education law/mandated minutes
audits.f: No statistically significant differences in scheduled/estimated PE minutes between groups
audits.c: PE audit, feedback and coaching (PEAFC) cluster-randomised pilot intervention
audits.r2: No statistically significant difference in law compliance change between intervention and control groups; both groups increased MVPA lesson time (~9-10%) but not significantly different

audits.t: Improving ototoxicity monitoring in patients receiving aminoglycosides using a novel digital approach: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Ototoxicity monitoring adherence in aminoglycoside therapy
audits.st: Recommendation for baseline audiometric testing before/during aminoglycoside therapy to monitor for ototoxicity
audits.f: Baseline adherence to the ototoxicity monitoring programme 36%
audits.c: Ototoxicity monitoring programme using tablet-based audiometry (Shoebox app on iPads) performed by non-audiologists, with PDSA cycles improving patient identification via referral and reporting systems
audits.r2: Adherence improved to 88% after PDSA cycle 1 (p=0.03), with an overall adherence rate of 69% at 12 months

audits.t: Reducing door-to-triage time with improving triage coverage in a rural primary healthcare centre in India: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: not reported (internal QI targets: 50% reduction in door-to-triage time; 90% triage coverage)
audits.f: Baseline door-to-triage time 10 minutes
audits.c: Standardisation of triage protocol, reorganisation of resources, dedicated triage space/staff, staff training; 4 PDCA cycles
audits.r2: Door-to-triage time reduced to 3 minutes; triage coverage improved from baseline to 100%

audits.t: A quality improvement project targeting postoperative hospital revisit rates after pediatric appendicitis.
audits.tp: Postoperative hospital revisits after paediatric appendectomy
audits.st: National Surgical Quality Improvement Program-Pediatric (NSQIP-P) benchmark revisit rate; local target of 30% relative reduction in unnecessary revisits over 1 year
audits.f: hospital revisit rate 16.7%; institution's NSQIP-P historical revisit rate as high as 20%, with patients 40-50% more likely to revisit than the average NSQIP-P hospital
audits.c: Bundle of interventions: enhanced bedside nursing/family education at discharge, a revised discharge instruction pamphlet, and a post-discharge follow-up phone call from the surgery nurse practitioner within 72 hours
audits.r2: revisit rate fell to 13.4% (relative reduction 20%, against a 30% target, not fully achieved); revisit rate for complicated appendicitis fell from 30.0% to 12.6%; 74% of contacted families received the discharge pamphlet and 98.7% found the follow-up call useful

audits.t: Small bowel obstruction outcomes according to compliance with the World Society of Emergency Surgery Bologna guidelines.
audits.tp: Compliance with WSES Bologna guidelines for small bowel obstruction
audits.st: World Society of Emergency Surgery (WSES) Bologna guidelines for adhesive small bowel obstruction management, compliance assessed as complete or partial
audits.f: Successful non-operative management (NOM) in 561 (57.1%), NOM followed by surgery (NOM-T) in 224 (22.8%), direct-to-surgery in 197 (20.1%); mean length of stay 5.3, 12.9 and 7.7 days respectively; guideline-compliant care associated with shorter length of stay and more 'optimal outcomes' (length of stay ≤5 days, no complications, no 30-day readmission)

audits.t: Trauma referral audit impact assessment on the outcomes of injured patients via an interrupted time-series analysis: an 11-year before-and-after study of trauma cases at the Maharaj Nakorn Chiang Mai hospital, Thailand.
audits.st: Trauma referral audit (TRA) programme
audits.f: Overall mortality 5.5% pre-full-TRA period; median ISS 9 in 2010
audits.c: Full implementation of the trauma referral audit (TRA) programme at end of 2010
audits.r2: Overall mortality 6.2% post-full-TRA; monthly mortality increased 1.57 percentage points (post) and annual trend +0.11%; among severely injured only, mortality level/trend unchanged

audits.t: Quality improvement initiative to improve safe injection practices by nurses in labour room of a tertiary care centre, India.
audits.tp: Safe injection practices compliance in labour room
audits.st: WHO and CDC safe injection practice guidelines; target 20% to 80% within 6 weeks
audits.f: Baseline SIP compliance 20%
audits.c: 15-point practice observation checklist aligned with WHO/CDC guidelines; 12 PDSA cycles, Point of Care QI methodology
audits.r2: Median compliance rose to 87% in first half of sustenance phase, falling to 67% later

audits.t: Ending PJ paralysis for hospitalised patients: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: not reported (internal target: 50% of patients dressed/up for meals/mobilising)
