audits.f: 14.3% dressed in own clothing daily, 6.4% sitting for all 3 meals, weekly mean 0.9 (SD 0.7) mobilising to activities
audits.c: PJ paralysis education for staff/patients/families, new dress code care standard, physician patient care order

audits.t: Improving Surgical Outcomes in Resource-Limited Settings: A Quality Improvement Approach to Unplanned Returns to Theater.
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist adherence, as part of a multi-modal quality improvement programme to reduce unplanned return to theatre (RTT)
audits.f: Overall RTT rate 7.9%; general surgery 6.3%; obstetrics and gynaecology 10.5%
audits.c: Staff training on secure surgical knot techniques, enhanced adherence to the WHO surgical safety checklist, and mandatory consultant supervision during high-risk operations
audits.r2: Overall RTT rate reduced to 3.7% (p=0.004); general surgery 3.0% (p=0.048); obstetrics and gynaecology 4.8% (p=0.037)

audits.t: Need for User-Friendly Audit Tools: Investigating Dietitians' Use and Requirements of Clinical Documentation Audit Tools.
audits.tp: Dietitians' use of clinical documentation audit tools
audits.st: Nutrition Care Process (NCP) documentation standards
audits.f: 53% of respondents indicated clinical documentation audits were conducted in their workplaces

audits.t: Implementing a Successful Quality Improvement Curriculum With a Required Resident-Led Project in a Pediatric Residency Program.
audits.st: ACGME requirement for resident training in quality improvement
audits.f: 7% of residents completed a QI project pre-implementation
audits.c: Structured QI curriculum with didactics, faculty mentorship, instructional worksheets, culminating in a resident-led PDSA-based QI project
audits.r2: 100% of residents completed a project post-implementation; 97 residents completed 72 QI projects, 90% presented at regional symposia, 19% at national/regional conferences

audits.t: Improving Safety, Efficiency, Cost, and Satisfaction Across a Musculoskeletal Pathway Using the Digital Assessment Routing Tool for Triage: Quality Improvement Study.
audits.st: Predefined local outcome targets for safety, efficiency, cost and satisfaction for the MSK triage pathway
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Introduction of a Digital Assessment Routing Tool (DART) as the first point of contact for self-referring MSK patients, using a Plan-Do-Study-Act design and Integrated Knowledge Translation model
audits.r2: 93% of patients self-assessed using DART; 96% agreement between clinician judgement and DART; no safety incidents; 9.8% (401) urgent cases immediately stratified; 203 fewer cases requiring clinical escalation; administrative time reduced by 51% with cost saving of £80.16 per 100 referrals; new self-management route reduced costs by 73% (£1272.90 per 100 referrals); patient satisfaction mean 90%

audits.t: Keep the PEEP: A quality improvement project assessing safety and feasibility of prolonged non-invasive positive end expiratory pressure.
audits.tp: Positive end expiratory pressure guideline standardisation in preterm infants
audits.st: Internal "Keep the PEEP" guideline for early initiation, continuation to 32-week PMA, and discontinuation of PEEP in infants <32 weeks gestation
audits.f: Pneumothorax incidence 14 cases; bronchopulmonary dysplasia incidence 82 cases; median post-menstrual age at first oral feed 34.1 weeks; median length of stay 55 days
audits.c: Implementation of the "Keep the PEEP" guideline with team member education and team engagement through auditing
audits.r2: Median compliance with PEEP use through 32-week PMA was 100%; pneumothorax 13 cases (p=0.86), BPD 68 cases (p=0.65), median PMA at first oral feed 34.1 weeks (p=0.56), median length of stay 43 days (p=0.2) – no statistically significant differences from baseline

audits.t: Early compliance with lung cancer lymph node standard 5.8: An analysis of 2022 and 2023 Commission on Cancer site reviews.
audits.tp: Lung cancer lymph node sampling standard compliance
audits.st: Commission on Cancer Standard 5.8: ≥3 mediastinal lymph node stations and ≥1 hilar station sampled and documented in a synoptic pathology report for curative-intent lung cancer resection
audits.f: In 2022, compliance required 5/7 pathology reports meeting the standard; overall compliance and noncompliance rates for 2022 and 2023 combined: 272/504 (54%) compliant, 232/504 (46%) noncompliant, median 29% of pathology reports meeting the standard among noncompliant sites
audits.c: not reported (federally funded collaborative supporting implementation of Standard 5.8, but no specific intervention tested here)
audits.r2: Median percentage of adherent pathology reports increased from 2022 to 2023, but overall compliance rate dipped in 2023 as the pass threshold rose

audits.t: Quality improvement project to reduce beta-D-glucan turnaround times in an NHS pathology network.
audits.st: South West London Pathology (SWLP) user handbook standard of 5 working days turnaround for beta-D-glucan (BDG) testing; project aim was at least 90% of results authorised within 5 working days
audits.f: Mean turnaround time 11.6 days (more than twice the 5-working-day standard); only 0.88% of results authorised within 5 working days
audits.c: Implementation of an in-house BDG testing assay after electronic reporting from the reference laboratory proved unviable due to IT and staffing limitations
audits.r2: 92.8% of results authorised within 5 working days; mean turnaround time reduced to 2.5 days, at lower unit cost

audits.t: Adherence to Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy Target in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction: a cross-sectional study.
audits.tp: Guideline-directed medical therapy adherence in HFrEF
audits.st: Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) target doses for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
audits.f: 93.1% prescribed ACEi/ARB/ARNi, 95.8% beta-blockers, 69.2% spironolactone; only 21.2% at GDMT target doses of ACEi/ARB/ARNi and 52.3% for beta-blockers; 98.5% of spironolactone prescriptions reached target doses
audits.c: not reported (cross-sectional observational study, no intervention)

audits.t: Striking the right balance between accountability and quality improvement: a discharge summary timeliness tale.
audits.st: Ontario Health/College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO) regulatory mandate: discharge summary authentication within 48 hours; local target to increase compliance from 62% to 75% within 1 year
audits.f: 62% of discharge summaries authenticated within 48 hours; average time from discharge to authentication 53 hours
audits.c: Model for improvement with iterative PDSA cycles: consultant-level performance feedback with peer comparison, revised metrics (average/median time), workflow changes (same-day transcription release, earlier notification emails, correcting authentication workflow), and trainee template/education interventions
audits.r2: average time to authentication fell from 53 to 38 hours (sustained); percentage authenticated within 48 hours reached 75% (target achieved) but was not sustained thereafter

audits.t: Ensuring Timely Pulmonary Follow-up after an Inpatient Asthma Hospitalization: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: not reported (internal target: 90% scheduled, 80% attendance within 45 days)
audits.f: Baseline 58.7% of patients had scheduled follow-up appointments; 45.3% attendance rate
audits.c: Standardised asthma care guidelines, timely pulmonology consultation in PICU, notification of pulmonary team for prior patients
audits.r2: Scheduled appointments increased to 97.3%, attendance improved to 85.2%; sustained at 93% scheduled/82.7% attended 3 years later

audits.t: Evaluating Surgical Safety and Quality Assurance by Conducting an Audit of WHO Checklist Implementation in a Tertiary Care Hospital.
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (Sign In, Time Out, Sign Out)
audits.f: Sign Out phase compliance 89% (178), Sign In 82% (164); lowest compliance in Time Out phase; full 100% compliance for consent, anaesthesia protocol, sterilisation, team introductions
audits.c: not reported (audit only, no intervention tested)

audits.t: Decreasing prevalence of anaemia in pregnant women at delivery: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Anaemia in pregnancy screening and management
audits.st: National anaemia in pregnancy screening/management guidelines
audits.f: Baseline anaemia prevalence 35.57% among booked pregnant women at delivery
audits.c: Systematic point-of-care haemoglobin screening at 30-34 weeks, dedicated anaemia management room, standardised operating procedures, weekly team meetings; 4 PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Screening coverage reached 95-100%, median anaemia prevalence at delivery reduced to 20.04%, sustained 3-month median of 15%

audits.t: Utilizing Quality Improvement Methodology to Decrease Surgical Delays.
audits.tp: Surgical case delay reduction via preoperative paperwork standardisation
audits.st: Internal QI target: reduce overall case delays and first-start case delays
audits.f: Up to 21.5% of cases were delayed per month; preoperative paperwork issues were the most common cause of delays
audits.c: Standardisation of preoperative paperwork completion process and provider-preoperative team communication
audits.r2: 39.2% relative reduction in overall delays; 25.0% relative reduction in first-start delays; cases delayed by paperwork reduced by 60.1%; first-start cases delayed by paperwork reduced by 49.6%; rate of paperwork issues in all cases decreased by 43.3%

audits.t: Bridging Gaps in Congenital Syphilis Care: A Quality Improvement Initiative for Comprehensive Management at a Large Public Hospital in Los Angeles, California, USA.
audits.st: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention guidelines for comprehensive evaluation, treatment and follow-up of infants born to mothers with syphilis; internal target 90% compliance
audits.f: Among 15 syphilis-exposed infants, appropriate management was 85% at baseline and follow-up scheduling was 54% at baseline; gaps found in risk stratification, treatment decisions and outpatient follow-up
audits.c: "Congenital Syphilis Pathway": recommended Pediatric Infectious Disease consultation for eligible infants, targeted provider education at three implementation points, and systematic scheduling of outpatient follow-up
audits.r2: Pediatric Infectious Disease consultation rates reached 100% by June 2024; appropriate management improved from 85% to 100% in Q2 2024; follow-up scheduling increased from 54% to 91% in Q2 2024

audits.t: Improving Job Completion in Acute Medical Units Through Role-Specific Documentation: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Documentation quality and job completion in acute medical units
audits.st: Internal QI target: improve job completion rates and reduce missed jobs per patient per day
audits.f: Standard Documentation: 1,291 jobs documented, 294 missed jobs, 77.99% jobs completed, 2.94 completed jobs per patient per day
audits.c: Role-Specific Documentation: separate headings for "Doctors", "Nurses" and "MDT" instead of a single "Plan" heading
audits.r2: Role-Specific Documentation: 1,007 jobs documented, 147 missed jobs (vs 294, p=.0002), 85.74% jobs completed (vs 77.99%, p=.0003), 3.47 completed jobs per patient per day (vs 2.94, p=.0052)

audits.t: Reducing Computed Tomography Use for Appendicitis Evaluation in a Pediatric Emergency Department: A Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: not reported (internal target: reduce CT utilisation from 31.3% to 15%)
audits.f: Baseline CT rate 31.3%
audits.c: Clinical practice guideline, EMR order set for clinical decision support, radiologist ultrasound report template
audits.r2: CT rate reduced to 12.1%, sustained for 10 months, without increasing negative pathology appendectomies or 72-hour ED returns

audits.t: Implementation of a Targeted Technologic Screening Tool to Increase Pneumococcal Vaccine Uptake in Health-System Retail Pharmacies: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Pneumococcal vaccine uptake in retail pharmacies
audits.st: Updated pneumococcal vaccination guidelines (PCV20)
audits.f: Baseline PCV20 vaccination rate (prior year comparison period)
audits.c: Targeted technologic screening tool and pop-up alert in pharmacy software identifying PCV20-eligible patients
audits.r2: 130 patients (9%) received PCV20 through the alert; overall 140% increase in PCV20 vaccination rate vs same period prior year

audits.t: Quality improvement project to improve cardiovascular risk screening in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk screening in rheumatoid arthritis
audits.st: National/international CV risk screening guidelines for RA; target 46% to 65% within 18 months
audits.f: Baseline CV risk screening 46.4%
audits.c: Patient education, standard CVRM text reminder in EPR, educational meeting for rheumatologists/nurses, feedback sessions with current data
audits.r2: CV risk screening increased to 55.4% at 18 months; primary 65% goal not reached

audits.t: Optimizing Morbidity and Mortality Conference for Education and Quality Improvement.

audits.f: Age-appropriate discharge instruction rate 36%
audits.c: Educational curriculum, e-reminders, workspace materials, pre-written EMR smart phrases for age-specific discharge instructions (0-5y, ≥6y), tested through 5 PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Age-appropriate discharge instruction rate improved to 56%; smart phrases used in 58% of relevant cases (n=628); no change in CT orders, ED revisits, or neurology referrals

audits.t: A sustained reduction in the rate of severe intraventricular hemorrhage in very low birth weight infants: a novel quality improvement project in a large perinatal-neonatal centre in Asia.
audits.tp: Severe intraventricular haemorrhage prevention in very low birth weight infants
audits.st: Evidence-based neuroprotective care bundle drawn from published best practices, combined with a novel Root Cause-Process Compliance-System (RC-PC-S) analysis; local SMART aim to reduce severe IVH (SIVH) by 20% within 2 years and 50% within 6 years
audits.f: SIVH rate 5.9% (23/390), already in the best-performing quartile of the Vermont Oxford Network but targeted for further reduction
audits.c: An 8-component evidence-based SIVH prevention bundle implemented sequentially over 6 years: neutral head positioning, developmental care, timed antenatal steroids, RC-PC-S case-by-case root cause analysis from 2015, antenatal magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection, a hypothermia management protocol, a selective PDA management protocol, and a prophylactic indomethacin protocol (later modified)
audits.r2: SIVH rate fell to 1.9% (a 57% reduction from the intervention period's 4.4%, adjusted OR 0.266, p=0.006) in the post-intervention period, and was 2.7% in the sustainment period; neonatal mortality declined from 11.5% to 8.6% (p=0.067); compliance with process measures exceeded 80% for 7 of 8 interventions

audits.t: Less Invasive Surfactant Administration: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: LISA compliance 47% (16 infants LISA pre-project vs 16 INSURE pre-project)
audits.c: Interprofessional LISA checklist, instructional video, improved equipment storage, standardised charting, re-education, via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: LISA compliance increased to a consistent 100% for eligible infants (43 infants LISA vs 4 INSURE post-project); reduction in grade III/IV IVH, second surfactant dose need, and chronic lung disease

audits.t: Decreasing differences in first-line therapy for respiratory infections in urgent cares, results of a multi-institutional quality improvement collaborative.
audits.tp: Equity in first-line respiratory infection therapy
audits.st: National guidelines defining first-line therapy (FLT) for acute respiratory infections
audits.f: Baseline difference in first-line therapy (ΔFLT): Spanish vs English-speaking 3.1%, Hispanic vs non-Hispanic 1.6%, commercial vs government-insured 1.6%; baseline ΔFLT Black vs White patients 3.6%
audits.c: Local multidisciplinary QI teams used cause-and-effect analyses, driver diagrams and PDSA cycles (education alone vs education plus other modalities e.g. clinical decision support)
audits.r2: No change in ΔFLT by language, ethnicity, or insurance; ΔFLT between Black and White patients widened from 3.6% to 5.8%; overall FLT rates fluctuated

audits.t: Reducing door-to-ECG time in the emergency department: a quality improvement report.
audits.tp: Door-to-ECG time for chest pain patients
audits.st: American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association guideline recommending ECG acquisition within 10 minutes of ED arrival for patients with chest pain
audits.f: Median door-to-ECG time 12.9 minutes (12 months prior) and 16.7 minutes (6 months prior, peaking at 20.7 minutes); only 35.5% of patients received an ECG within 10 minutes
audits.c: Process standardisation and role redistribution via a multidisciplinary team: a dedicated ECG station in triage, reassignment of triage ECGs to nurses (floor ECGs to technicians), a standardised ECG protocol with documentation stamps, and staff education/awareness flyers
audits.r2: Median door-to-ECG time fell to 11.4 minutes (10.8% reduction vs 12 months prior, 32% vs 6 months prior; ARIMA-estimated reduction of 4.68 minutes, 95% CI -7.74 to -1.62); proportion within 10 minutes rose to 43.4% (from 35.5%, p<0.0001); median ECG interpretation time fell 74% from 101 to 26.5 minutes

audits.t: Adherence to national recommendations for the control of multidrug-resistant microorganisms in Swiss acute care hospitals - an updated national survey.
audits.tp: Adherence to national multidrug-resistant organism screening recommendations
audits.st: Swissnoso 2021 national recommendations for prevention and control of multidrug-resistant organisms
audits.f: Overall adherence with national recommendations for on-admission screening across five MDRO targets was 69% (weighted score, IQR 55-86%); only 20% of institutions reported universal screening during hospitalisation

audits.t: Improving viral load testing coverage among orphan and vulnerable children in Jinka Town, South Ethiopia: a quality improvement project implemented by the USAID FFHPCT activity team.
audits.tp: HIV viral load testing coverage in orphans and vulnerable children
audits.st: PEPFAR/UNAIDS 95-95-95 global HIV targets and USAID minimum service quality standards for viral load (VL) monitoring; local target to raise OVC VL testing coverage from 89% to 95%
audits.f: OVC viral load testing coverage 89%
audits.c: Five interventions tested across 3 PDSA cycles: on-the-job capacity building and targeted supportive supervision for social service/case workers, an SMS appointment-reminder system for caregivers, community caregiver awareness sessions, weekly VL result tracking and feedback, and enhanced community-facility referral linkages
audits.r2: VL testing coverage rose to 96% by the end of September 2024 (a 7 percentage-point increase), shown by 6 consecutive run-chart data points above the median (a statistically significant shift)

audits.t: A prospective audit of thoracic reirradiation practice and peer-review in a high-volume academic center.
audits.tp: Thoracic reirradiation practice and peer review
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 85 reirradiation cases (18.2% of 466 cases) identified at 26 QA meetings; peer review prompted plan revision in 11.8% of cases

audits.t: Streamlining Apheresis: A Dual-Intervention Quality Improvement Initiative to Increase the Efficiency in Stem Cell Collection.
audits.tp: Efficiency of stem cell apheresis collection
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Third-day apheresis collection usage in high-risk myeloma patients 25%; mean collection days 2.21
audits.c: Lowered CD34+ cell count target thresholds (tandem collections 6×10^6 to 5×10^6 cells/kg; single collections 3×10^6 to 2.5×10^6) and increased total blood volume processed from 3× to 4× for eligible patients, tested over two PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Third-day collection usage decreased to 5.9%; mean collection days fell to 1.8 (p=0.0015); 39.4% of patients avoided at least one collection day; total cost savings CAD $72,734.97; no significant difference in neutrophil or platelet engraftment times

audits.t: Paediatric care in hospitals in Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan: impact of a quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: WHO Quality Assessment/Quality Improvement Tool for Maternal and Newborn Care (paediatric adaptation) and the WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children, within the WHO European Framework for improving RMNCH quality of care
audits.f: Mean score for assessment of suspected pneumonia 2.1 (Kyrgyzstan) and 1.6 (Tajikistan) out of 3; unnecessary painful/invasive procedures in 66% (Kyrgyzstan) and 70% (Tajikistan) of reviewed cases; incorrect ARI treatment in 63% and 70% of cases respectively
audits.c: A 2-year multifaceted QI approach: review and harmonisation of national clinical guidelines, capacity-building workshops based on the WHO Pocket Book, training in QI methods, supportive supervision, semi-annual collaborative improvement meetings, and hospital-specific QI plans developed by each facility
audits.r2: Suspected pneumonia assessment score improved to 2.7 (Kyrgyzstan, p=0.018) and 2.1 (Tajikistan, p=0.020); unnecessary painful procedures fell to 36% (Kyrgyzstan) and 48% (Tajikistan); incorrect ARI treatment fell to 43% and 41% respectively; triage/emergency care, diarrhoea management, and respectful care also improved significantly in most hospitals

audits.t: Increased Reporting of Infants Born With Congenital Syphilis to a Local Department of Public Health: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Congenital syphilis reporting to public health
audits.st: CDC case definition and reporting requirements for congenital syphilis
audits.f: 107/154 (69.4%) RPR-negative infants meeting CDC case definition and treated with penicillin were not reported to the local public health department
audits.c: Multidisciplinary communication, standardised electronic medical record data entry, and regular reminders (September 2023-February 2025)
audits.r2: 44 infants reported to the department of public health, of whom 15 (34.1%) were RPR-negative and successfully reported

audits.t: The Impact of Standardized Respiratory Care Practices on Delivery Room Intubation Frequency and NICU Ventilator Days in VLBW Infants: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Standardised respiratory care to reduce delivery room intubation and ventilator days
audits.st: Vermont Oxford Network benchmarking data
audits.f: Chronic lung disease incidence increased from 15% (2017) to 30.9% (2018); baseline centre line for delivery room intubation 44%; baseline ventilation days 19 per 100 patient days
audits.c: Standardised respiratory care practices and a delivery room resuscitation bundle implemented via sequential PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Special cause variation lowered the delivery room intubation centre line from 44% to 18%, and total ventilation days from 19 to 12 per 100 patient days

audits.t: Long-Term Impact of EGUIDE Training on Facility-Wide Guideline Adherence Rate in Schizophrenia and Major Depressive Disorder: A Multicenter Study.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence in schizophrenia and major depressive disorder treatment (EGUIDE)
audits.st: Quality indicators for schizophrenia (QI-S, n=11) and major depressive disorder (QI-D, n=7) treatment guidelines
audits.f: Baseline guideline adherence rates, e.g. TRS diagnosis assessment 42.2%, mECT use 6.1%, nonprescription of anticholinergics 70.7% (schizophrenia); severity diagnosis assessment 51.2%, mECT use 12.8% (MDD)
audits.c: EGUIDE educational outreach training programme for psychiatrists
audits.r2: 7 of 11 QI-S and 3 of 7 QI-D indicators significantly improved year-on-year, e.g. TRS diagnosis assessment rose to 62.5%, mECT use to 11.8%, anticholinergic nonprescription to 81.7% (schizophrenia); severity diagnosis assessment to 77.0%, mECT use to 26.6% (MDD)

audits.t: Quality improvement project to enhance adherence to RCEM standards for patients with paracetamol overdose.
audits.tp: RCEM standards compliance for paracetamol overdose management
audits.st: Royal College of Emergency Medicine (RCEM) standards for N-acetylcysteine (NAC) administration in paracetamol overdose
audits.f: Compliance with RCEM standard 1: 36%; median inpatient stay 35 hours
audits.c: Educational sessions, quick reference materials and enhanced prescribing tools, including introduction of the Scottish and Newcastle Acetylcysteine Protocol (SNAP), via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Compliance with RCEM standard 1 improved to 43%; no change in compliance with standards 2 and 3; median inpatient stay decreased to 30.5 hours; no significant difference in adverse events

audits.t: Reducing Inappropriate Abdominal X-ray Requests in a Surgical Admissions Unit: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: Royal College of Radiologists iRefer national guidelines on abdominal X-ray (AXR) indications
audits.f: 69% of requests deemed inappropriate; 60% of requests were for suspected bowel obstruction
audits.c: Three sequential interventions: (1) locally agreed AXR indication guidelines, (2) guideline poster reminders in the assessment unit, (3) redesign of the electronic (EPIC) AXR order form to reflect local guidelines
audits.r2: inappropriate request rate fell to 11% (against a target of 10%, not quite achieved); bowel obstruction requests fell to 5.56%; concurrent CT scan requests remained unchanged (no significant increase, p=0.11)

audits.t: Assessing Adherence to Good Pharmacy Practices in a Provincial Hospital in Nepal: A Quality Improvement Perspective.
audits.st: Codes for Sales and Distribution of Drugs (CSDD) 2024 guideline, 16 components/121 indicators, Department of Drug Administration
audits.f: 74/121 indicators (61.2%) were compliant; 6 domains fully compliant (100%), 7 partially compliant (>=50%-99.9%), 10 poorly compliant (<50%)

audits.t: Digital Health Technology Compliance With Clinical Safety Standards In the National Health Service in England: National Cross-Sectional Study.
audits.tp: Digital health technology compliance with clinical safety standards
audits.st: NHS Data Coordination Board (DCB) 0129 and 0160 mandatory clinical risk management standards for digital health technologies
audits.f: 14,747 DHT deployments reported; mean 82.8 DHTs per organisation; median 25.6% (IQR 7.8-55.7%) of deployed DHTs fully assured overall, 24.5% (IQR 8.1-50%) for NHS provider trusts; 17.3% of DHTs fully assured against both standards, 13.3% partially assured, 70.1% with no documented assurance; 13 (6.4%) organisations fully assured all DHTs and 16 (7.8%) had none assured

audits.t: Compliance with global action plan on antibiotic prescription and utilization: a multi-facility cross-sectional study in southern Nigeria.
audits.st: WHO global action plan / AWaRe classification of antibiotics
audits.f: Access group antibiotics accounted for 48.7% (1086/2230) of prescriptions and Watch group 51.3% (1144/2230); no Reserve group antibiotics prescribed

audits.t: Improving the Acceptance Rate of Long Acting Reversible Contraception as a Method of Post-abortion Contraception: A Prospective Quality Improvement Study.
audits.tp: Long-acting reversible contraception as post-abortion contraception
audits.st: not reported (internal target: improve LARC acceptance by ≥50% of baseline)
audits.f: Baseline LARC acceptance as post-abortion contraception averaged 14.5%
audits.c: Improved communication and effective counselling by doctors, nursing staff and counsellors, delivered across three PDSA cycles (4 months each)
audits.r2: LARC acceptance improved to 40% after cycle 1, 52.6% after cycle 2, 75% after cycle 3; sustained average 62.9% (range 57.8-69.2%) during follow-up

audits.t: Vaping Education in Australian High Schools: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: At baseline, 70.9% (61/86) had vaped for over a year
audits.c: School nurse-led vaping cessation programme using PDSA framework and Social Cognitive Theory
audits.r2: 34.1% intended behaviour change immediately post-programme; 61% reported behaviour change at 4-week follow-up

audits.t: Adherence to guidelines for preventing catheter-associated urinary tract infections in hospitalized patients in a tertiary teaching hospital.
audits.st: CDC guidelines for preventing catheter-associated urinary tract infections
audits.f: 477/1262 (37.8%) patients were catheterised, with 57.3% overall adherence to CDC guidelines; emergency department adherence only 27.8%

audits.t: Optimising drowning prevention counselling through a physician Maintenance of Certification (MOC) quality improvement (QI) initiative.
audits.tp: Drowning prevention counselling in outpatient paediatric visits
audits.st: Local target: increase drowning prevention counselling and educational material provision to caregivers of children 0-10 years
audits.f: Mean counselling rate 26.8% preintervention; less than 25% of caregivers reported receipt of brochure/checklist and only 6% received a water watcher tag at baseline
audits.c: Refined educational programme with brochures and wearable water watcher tags across three PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Mean counselling rate rose to 64.9% by end of PDSA 3; 98% of caregivers received brochure/checklist and over 90% received water watcher tags; physicians counselling within 2 minutes rose from 69.3% (2022) to 82.1% (2023)

audits.t: Increasing MRI capacity at a clinical diagnostic centre and a trauma hospital using artificial intelligence-based image reconstruction (AI-IR): a quality improvement project using the Model for Improvement framework.
audits.tp: MRI scanning capacity using AI-based image reconstruction
audits.st: NHS England target of increasing MRI capacity by two scanned patients per day per scanner within a year of installing AI-enabled image reconstruction (AI-IR)
audits.f: average 8 scans/day at the CDC before AI-IR; scanning protocols not yet optimised with AI-IR
audits.c: Model for Improvement/PDSA cycles implementing AI-enabled image reconstruction (Siemens Deep Resolve) for musculoskeletal MRI protocols, with multidisciplinary radiologist/radiographer/physicist validation at each site
audits.r2: CDC achieved an average of 4 more scans/day after 5 months (exceeding NHS England's target of 2/day within a year), rising to 6 more per day by project end; trauma centre saved a mean 7:26 min/scan and increased the proportion of complex patients scanned from 7% to 15%, though overall throughput did not increase

audits.t: Getting Pabrinex Right: A Multi-cycle Quality Improvement Study Reducing Waste in Thiamine Prescribing at a Scottish District General Hospital.
audits.tp: Thiamine (Pabrinex) prescribing in alcohol use disorder
audits.st: Local guidelines on thiamine dosing for patients admitted with alcohol use disorder / Wernicke's encephalopathy risk
audits.f: 60% of patients received excess doses of IV Pabrinex, median 13 excess doses per patient (excess cost approximately £35 per patient); 30% received the correct initial dose
audits.r2: Median excess doses per patient fell to 7 then 4.5 after first and second interventions (p=0.0087); correct initial dose rose non-significantly from 30% to 51.3% (p=0.12)

audits.t: A multidisciplinary quality improvement initiative to improve neonatal end-of-life care in a level IV NICU.
audits.st: Local target: increase end-of-life symptom management by 50% and staff attitude/awareness scores by 20% by August 2024
audits.f: Baseline mortalities examined for analgesia administration and staff attitude/awareness before intervention
audits.c: Multidisciplinary QI team, implementation of end-of-life guidelines, EHR modifications, and staff education
audits.r2: Fentanyl equivalent administration in the 24h preceding death increased by 309% between epochs; significant increases in staff comfort, confidence, preparedness and awareness

audits.t: Adherence and Willingness to Participate in Cancer Screening Programs Among Women Living in Prison: A Cross-Sectional Study in Southern Italy.
audits.tp: Cancer screening adherence in women living in prison
audits.st: National cancer screening programmes (mammography, PAP-test, faecal occult blood test)
audits.f: 56.8% underwent mammography, 57.6% PAP-test, 27.6% FOBT among those eligible

audits.t: Health Literacy and Cardiac Medication Education: A Quality Improvement Study Using Teach-Back.
audits.tp: Teach-back method for discharge medication education
audits.st: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality-recommended teach-back method; American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association guideline recommending teach-back for post-ACS discharge medication education; local target of 85% comprehension by January 2024
audits.f: 54% of patients understood the purpose of their newly prescribed cardiac medication; only 26% were aware of potential adverse effects
audits.c: The teach-back method: tailored plain-language education for patients with knowledge gaps, delivered by medical students, residents and nursing staff, followed by patients explaining the medication's purpose and risks in their own words, via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: 92% of patients accurately explained both indication and side effects immediately post-intervention; 74% retained the information at 2-4 week follow-up

audits.t: Evaluating Compliance and Impact of the Sepsis Six Bundle in the Emergency Department: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
audits.tp: Sepsis recognition and treatment on wards
audits.st: Sepsis Six resuscitation bundle
audits.f: Compliance and impact of the Sepsis Six bundle evaluated in 660 sepsis patients; mortality rate 32%

audits.t: Adherence to low volume massive hemorrhage protocol: Experience from an urban level 1 trauma center.
audits.st: Institutional low-volume massive hemorrhage protocol (MHP)
audits.f: Adherence scores of >=50% achieved in 77% of MHP activations; timely issue of first transfusion pack achieved in all cases; hemorrhagic deaths within 24h in 13 patients, not affected by adherence scores

audits.t: Improving Sleep Quality on the First Postoperative Night in the Intensive Care Unit: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: First postoperative night sleep quality in ICU
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Patient-reported sleep quality baseline prior to interventions
audits.c: Staff engagement, earplugs/eye masks, standardised door closure, pain management review, noise monitoring, simplified surveillance protocols, melatonin, over six PDSA cycles across 7 months
audits.r2: Patient-reported sleep quality increased from 5.0 to 5.4/10 after culture shift promotion; nurse-perceived sleep quality showed favourable special cause variation after streamlined surveillance protocols; no increase in workload or adverse events

audits.t: Out-of-Home Care in Central Australia-A Retrospective Audit of Health Needs and Timeliness of Assessment Compared to the National Clinical Assessment Framework.
audits.tp: Health assessment timeliness for children in out-of-home care
audits.st: National Clinical Assessment Framework recommended timeframes for health assessment of children entering out-of-home care
audits.f: Less than half of children received a comprehensive health assessment within the recommended 3 months of entry into out-of-home care; 174/304 (57%) seen through paediatric clinics; 95% Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander; developmental concerns in 70% of children over 1 year, behavioural concerns in 63% of school-aged children, mental health concerns in 43%, FASD diagnosed/suspected in 43-66%, ADHD suspected/diagnosed in >50% of primary school-aged children

audits.t: Reference dosimetry data and machine performance comparison for tomotherapy delivery systems audited by IROC.
audits.st: IROC (Imaging and Radiation Oncology Core) on-site dosimetry audit standards
audits.f: Independent ion chamber measurements compared to institutional TPS calculations for percent depth dose and off-axis factors

audits.t: Increasing the rate of nursing process implementation: a quality improvement project at Wollega University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, 2025.
audits.st: Local target to increase nursing process implementation rate
audits.f: Rate of nursing process implementation was 27% at baseline
audits.c: Training of nurses/leaders, redistribution of nurses to higher-workload wards, clear job descriptions, protocols and work aids, nursing process formats, regular supportive supervision, via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Rate increased to 87.5%; assessment 93%, diagnosis 89.5%, planning 86.5%, implementation 85.5%, evaluation 83%; highest (96%) in orthopaedic ward, lowest (79%) in gynaecological ward

audits.t: Compliance and yield of follow-up colonoscopy after a positive FIT in real-life practice: a university hospital experience.
audits.st: US Multisociety Task Force 80% adherence benchmark for follow-up colonoscopy after positive FIT
audits.f: Only 618/1424 (43.3%) patients with positive FIT underwent follow-up colonoscopy, of whom 277 (44.8%) had adenomas and 28 (4.5%) were diagnosed with colorectal cancer

audits.t: Improving Time to Kidney Transplant Listing: A Single Center Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.st: Local target: reduce time to transplant listing by 25% within 12 months
audits.f: Median time from evaluation to listing was 437 days; only 9 patients listed predialysis; Indigenous patients (>25% of population) accounted for only 11% of those listed
audits.c: Improved documentation guidelines, expedited access for delayed investigations, dedicated transplant nurse for Indigenous patients, informatics-enabled coordination tool
audits.r2: Median time to listing improved by 17% to 362 days; higher proportion of Indigenous patients (23%) listed; modest reductions in cardiology-related delays

audits.t: Enhancing Safety in Clinical Practice: Cross-Sectional, Within-Subjects, Simulated-Use Compliance Study Using BD PosiFlush SafeScrub.
audits.st: Aseptic non-touch technique (ANTT) disinfection protocol for needleless access devices
audits.f: Compliance with standard disinfection practice was 17% (21% for Flush 1 specifically)
audits.c: Use of BD PosiFlush SafeScrub device with built-in scrub reminder, compared with standard alcohol swab/prefilled syringe practice
audits.r2: Compliance with BD PosiFlush SafeScrub was 34% overall (46% for Flush 1), roughly double standard practice

audits.t: Adherence to severe malaria treatment guidelines in Northern Uganda: a mixed-methods study.
audits.st: National/WHO severe malaria treatment guidelines
audits.f: Adherence to severe malaria treatment guidelines was 33.07%; non-adherence for IV-then-oral drug sequencing 38.3% and treating only confirmed malaria 25%

audits.t: Implementation of an Infection Prevention Care Bundle for Peripheral Intravenous Catheters (PIVCs): A Quality Improvement Study to Enhance PIVC Quality and Reduce Complications.
audits.st: Validated Peripheral Intravenous Catheter-Mini Questionnaire (PIVC-miniQ), 16 observation points
audits.f: Prevalence of phlebitis was 15.1% at baseline
audits.c: Implementation of a comprehensive PIVC infection prevention care bundle
audits.r2: Prevalence of phlebitis decreased to 9.4% post-intervention (p=0.018); improvements also seen in dressing/connection practices and documentation

audits.t: Bedside handover training and its effects on nurses' knowledge and compliance.
audits.st: ISBAR structured bedside handover practice standard
audits.f: Before training: head nurse knowledge 12.4±3.7, ISBAR score 25.7±6.5; staff nurse knowledge 10.6±4.2, ISBAR score 21.1±7.0
audits.r2: Head nurse knowledge rose to 89.5±4.4 post-training (90.6±3.2 at follow-up); ISBAR to 77.8±5.8; staff nurse knowledge to 89.6±5.7 (85.5±6.4 at follow-up); ISBAR to 82.6±6.6; audit compliance scores also improved significantly and were sustained (p<0.001)

audits.t: What Gets Measured Gets Counted: Food, Nutrition, and Hydration Non-Compliance in Ontario Long-Term Care Homes and the Role of Proactive Compliance Inspections, 2024.
audits.tp: Food, nutrition and hydration inspection non-compliance in long-term care
audits.st: Ontario Food, Nutrition, and Hydration (FNH) inspection standards
audits.f: FNH non-compliance identified in 12.2% (76) of all long-term care homes, and in 43.7% of those inspected using the FNH protocol (p<0.001, Φ=0.55)

audits.t: Assessment of compliance with good review practices by medicine assessors within the Zambia medicines regulatory authority.
audits.tp: Compliance with Good Review Practices in medicines regulation
audits.st: Good Review Practices (GRevPs) as assessed by the Centre for Innovation in Regulatory Science (CIRS) questionnaire
audits.f: 5 of 12 assessors (42%) reported GRevPs had been fully implemented and adopted; target timelines were not well followed at department or agency level; all participants reported a consistent method exists for documenting practices needing improvement

audits.t: Improving Risk Documentation in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A Single-Centre Before-and-After Study of a Pre-printed Consent Form.
audits.st: GMC guidance and Montgomery v Lanarkshire Health Board legal standard for informed consent, operationalised as a predefined set of procedure-specific risks for laparoscopic cholecystectomy
audits.f: 0% (0/46) of forms achieved full compliance with the predefined risk set; death documented in only 2.2%, chest infection in 6.5%, adhesional obstruction in 15.2%
audits.c: Introduction of a pre-printed, procedure-specific consent form for laparoscopic cholecystectomy listing all predefined risks in a checklist format, developed with consultant surgeons and clinical governance staff
audits.r2: 100% (23/23) of forms achieved full compliance with all predefined risks documented

audits.t: Implementation of a peripheral intravenous catheter bundle to reduce phlebitis and hospital-onset <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i> bacteremia: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Peripheral IV catheter care bundle to reduce phlebitis and bacteraemia
audits.st: epic3 national evidence-based guidelines and the 2016 Infusion Therapy Standards of Practice for peripheral intravenous catheter (PIVC) insertion and maintenance
audits.f: All-cause PIVC-related phlebitis rate 5.3-7% (pilot wards); 9 PIVC-related S. aureus bacteraemias identified in 2017; pre-implementation hospital-onset S. aureus bacteraemia (HO-SAB) rate 0.61 per 10,000 patient-days
audits.c: A structured PIVC insertion/maintenance care bundle (aseptic insertion, daily inspection with timely removal, standardised maintenance care) piloted in 2 wards using the Model for Improvement, then spread hospital-wide across 4 phases using Kotter's 8-step change model, with staff education, daily reminders, audit-feedback dashboards, and hospital-wide awareness campaigns
audits.r2: Pilot ward phlebitis rates fell to 1-2% (from 7%); hospital-wide point prevalence survey phlebitis fell from a mean of 0.87% to 0.21% post-implementation; PIVC-related HO-SAB fell to 0.26 per 10,000 patient-days (incidence rate ratio 0.42, 95% CI 0.25-0.72, p=0.002)

audits.t: Adherence to the acceleration of total postoperative recovery protocol and perioperative complications in cancer patients.
audits.st: ACERTO (Acceleration of Total Postoperative Recovery) project recommendations
audits.f: Complication frequency 68.5%; adherence to fluid resuscitation <=30 mL/kg was 56.6% intraoperatively and 90.4% postoperatively; nausea/vomiting prophylaxis prescribed in 93% intraoperatively and 100% postoperatively

audits.t: Bridging Communication Gaps to Enhance Patient Safety: A Quality Improvement (QI) Project on the Role of Abbreviations, Their Risks, and Pathways to Change.
audits.st: SQUIRE 2.0 guidelines for QI initiatives (local written expansion test of 82 ENT abbreviations)
audits.f: Mean accuracy 24.3%, with no participant exceeding 77%
audits.c: Educational seminars and a printed reference guide displayed in shared spaces
audits.r2: Mean accuracy improved by a relative 40% to 35% (range 24%-52%), statistically significant (p<0.05)

audits.t: Enteral feeding protocol: a quality improvement project on feeding interruptions and clinical outcomes in a tertiary intensive care unit.
audits.tp: Enteral nutrition feeding protocol in ICU
audits.st: ICU nutrition guideline recommending enteral nutrition (EN) initiation within 24-48 hours of admission and 70% of full feeding by day 3
audits.f: Feeding interruption (FI) occurred in 98.2% of patients; energy intake adequacy 67.3%; protein intake adequacy 67.3%; median time from admission to EN 12 hours
audits.c: An intermittent enteral feeding protocol (with a gastric residual volume management algorithm) introduced via a 4-week staff education programme (videos, tutorials, posters, test) for doctors and nurses in the general and COVID-19 ICUs
audits.r2: FI prevalence remained high (97.2%) with no significant change in FI duration (28 vs 30 hours, p=0.60); however, energy adequacy rose to 79.9% and protein adequacy to 80% (both p<0.001), and EN was initiated earlier; ICU mortality was not significantly affected by protocol implementation (OR 0.508, 95% CI 0.250-1.032, p=0.06)

audits.t: Community-acquired pneumonia in Indonesian children: insights into diagnosis, treatment compliance, and healthcare provider challenges.
audits.tp: Community-acquired pneumonia guideline adherence in children
audits.st: WHO and Indonesian Ministry of Health CAP diagnosis/treatment guidelines
audits.f: 37.6% of patients misclassified as CAP per WHO guideline (53.3% per MoH RI guideline); antibiotics prescribed in 89.3%/87.6% of these cases; among correctly classified cases, only 11.6% dosed within recommended amoxicillin range and 28.3% received appropriate duration

audits.t: A regional quality-improvement collaborative to reduce early neonatal hypothermia in critically ill newborns.
audits.tp: Early postnatal hypothermia in transported neonates
audits.st: Local SMART target: reduce admission hypothermia (axillary temperature under 36.5C) from a baseline of 82.1% to below 60% within 12 months across the referral network, aligned with WHO thermal care criteria
audits.f: Early postnatal hypothermia (EPH) incidence was 82.1%; severe (grade 3 or higher) intraventricular haemorrhage (IVH) occurred in 2.6%; mortality within 7 days 0.6%; hypoglycaemia 4.8%; shock 4.3%.
audits.c: Regional quality improvement collaborative: a standardised evidence-based thermal management protocol ('double RHBT' bundle covering room/radiant warmer, pre-warming/head, body/body weight, temperature/cluster care), staff training (action phase May 2023-April 2024) and monthly monitoring with feedback (sustain phase May-December 2024), developed via Delphi consultation and a key driver diagram
audits.r2: EPH incidence fell to 59.0% (adjusted p<0.001); severe IVH fell to 0.2% (adjusted p=0.002); no significant differences in mortality (0.7%), pulmonary haemorrhage, shock (3.7%), hypoglycaemia (4.1%), DIC, or invasive mechanical ventilation use.

audits.t: Assessment of knowledge and facility compliance with the WHO SAM Guidelines among health professionals in the Volta Region of Ghana.
audits.tp: WHO Severe Acute Malnutrition guideline compliance
audits.st: WHO treatment guidelines for Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM)
audits.f: 84% of staff had adequate knowledge of the WHO SAM protocol, but only 37.1% graded their facility as compliant with the feeding aspect; 41.4% had received training

audits.t: Reducing umbilical catheter migration rate by introducing regular POCUS assessment: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: UVC migration occurred in 57% of preterm infants (<30 weeks' gestation); two instances of extravasation injury; POCUS used at insertion in 29%, correct placement at insertion in 40%
audits.c: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) training programme for medical staff and updated local guidelines recommending POCUS assessment of UVC tip position at insertion and routine follow-up on days 3-5
audits.r2: POCUS use at insertion increased to 82%; correct UVC placement at insertion improved to 75%; UVC migration still observed in 30% of cases at days 3-5 follow-up; no extravasation injuries occurred post-intervention

audits.t: Enhancing identification and diagnosis of nightmare disorder in active duty patients at a sleep disorders center: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Nightmare disorder identification and diagnosis rate
audits.st: Local target: increase confirmed Nightmare Disorder diagnosis rate from 0.60% to at least 5% within 12 months
audits.f: Baseline diagnosis rate of Nightmare Disorder was 0.60% despite 59.28% of referred service members reporting nightmares and 19.76% screening positive
audits.c: Standardised documentation of Nightmare Disorder Index results, targeted provider education, and chart flagging for probable NDO, over tiered PDSA cycles across 7 months
audits.r2: Diagnosis rate increased to 9.12% after three PDSA cycles; recognition rate among those with probable NDO rose from 3.03% to 55.32%

audits.t: Effect of eHealth intervention (ADHERE) on adherence to partograph and WHO safe childbirth checklist in intrapartum care: implementation research in Ethiopia.
audits.tp: Partograph and WHO safe childbirth checklist adherence
audits.st: Partograph and WHO safe childbirth checklist (SCC) quality improvement tools
audits.f: Baseline partograph scores 4.11 (control) and 4.23 (intervention); baseline SCC adherence at admission 25.8% (control) and 49.6% (intervention)
audits.c: ADHERE eHealth system with clinical decision support
audits.r2: ADHERE increased partograph adherence score by 4.27 units (DiD, 95% CI 1.80-5.09) and SCC adherence by 9.3-22.3 percentage points at admission/before-birth/after-birth, but not at discharge

audits.t: Results of a remote audit program of reference and non-reference dosimetry of photon beams using alanine detectors.
audits.st: Treatment planning system beam commissioning and calibration standards
audits.f: Difference between measured and predicted doses was within +/-5% for all beams except one; uncertainty in alanine readout was 1%

audits.t: Guideline Adherence of Perioperative Antibiotics and Surgical Site Infections in Noncardiac Surgery.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence for perioperative antibiotics and surgical site infection
audits.st: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) perioperative antibiotic guidelines
audits.f: Failure to adhere to any IDSA metric occurred in 26.1% of cases (13.3% antibiotic choice, 9.0% weight-adjusted dosing, 3.0% timing, 4.8% redosing); SSIs occurred in 4.4% of cases

audits.t: Standardising Anaesthetic Induction in Code Red Trauma Patients: A Quality Improvement Initiative at a Major London Trauma Centre.
audits.tp: Anaesthetic induction cognitive aid for haemodynamically unstable trauma patients
audits.st: Difficult Airway Society (DAS) 2015 guidelines on modified rapid sequence induction, and European trauma anaesthesia literature recommending ketamine/etomidate in haemorrhagic shock
audits.f: 79% received ketamine and fentanyl, 21% received propofol and fentanyl (variable practice); median MAP fell 37% within 15 minutes of induction, and one patient required intraoperative cardiac massage
audits.c: Development and iterative refinement (2 PDSA cycles) of a one-page 'Code Red Quick Reference Guide' cognitive aid for induction drug selection and airway management, disseminated via teaching and posters in trauma theatres
audits.r2: not reported; only informal trainee/consultant feedback on confidence and perceived consistency was collected

audits.t: Impact of Floseal and NasoPore in Managing Epistaxis in the Emergency Department: A Quality Improvement Analysis.
audits.tp: Epistaxis management with bioresorbable nasal packing
audits.st: Revised Royal College of Surgeons (RCS) ENT UK guidelines for epistaxis management
audits.f: Rapid Rhino patients had a pain score of 7/10 (VAS), average ED length of stay 8 hours, and cost approximately £2000/patient (including ambulance transfer and admission)
audits.c: Introduction of Floseal and NasoPore bioresorbable haemostatic packing per updated RCS ENT UK guidelines, via two PDSA cycles, allowing patients to be discharged home rather than transferred for ENT admission
audits.r2: pain score fell to 2/10 (Floseal alone) or 5/10 (Floseal+NasoPore); ED length of stay fell to a maximum of 2-3 hours; cost fell to approximately £500/patient, a >65% cost reduction

audits.t: Adherence to breast and cervical cancer screening guidelines according to obesity status: a French cross-sectional multicenter survey.
audits.tp: Breast and cervical cancer screening adherence by obesity status
audits.st: National guidelines: biennial clinical breast exams/mammograms (age 50-74), triennial cervical samples (age 25-65)
audits.f: Women with class I/II obesity were less likely to be up to date for clinical breast exams (OR 2.35 and 2.68), mammography (OR 4.43 and 4.08), and cervical samples (OR 2.23 and 2.85) compared with normal weight peers

audits.t: National Quality Improvement Initiative to Increase Smoking Cessation Assistance in Commission on Cancer Programs and National Accreditation Program for Breast Centers.
audits.tp: Smoking cessation assistance in cancer care
audits.st: Beyond ASK national quality improvement initiative aiming to increase provision of evidence-based smoking cessation assistance to currently smoking cancer patients
audits.f: Baseline mean smoking cessation assist rate 48.0% (95% CI 43.7-52.2)
audits.c: National Plan-Do-Study-Act QI project (Beyond ASK): educational webinars, an online practice change package, training opportunities, and electronic health record guidance
audits.r2: Final mean assist rate 67.5% (95% CI 63.6-71.3); overall 63.7% (33,638/52,794) of currently smoking patients received cessation assistance; full adoption reported by 65.4% of programs; delivery increased over time for in-office brief counselling (33.9%-65.8%), behavioural counselling (7.1%-18.5%), in-house referral (14.5%-27.3%), community referral (12.1%-29.5%) and web-based referral (12.2%-33.9%), all p<=.02

audits.t: Real-world treatment trajectories preceding GLP-1 receptor agonist initiation in type 2 diabetes: A descriptive UK population-based cohort study on adherence to national clinical guidelines.
audits.tp: Guideline-adherent sequencing of glucose-lowering therapy before GLP-1 receptor agonist initiation
audits.st: UK national clinical guidelines (NICE NG28) on sequencing of glucose-lowering therapy, including post-2018 guidance recommending SGLT-2 inhibitors for those at high cardiovascular risk or with established cardiovascular disease
audits.f: 63.5% initiated GLP-1RA as fourth-line (35.4%) or later-line (28.1%) therapy; 0.8% first-line, 10.5% second-line, 25.2% third-line; post-2018, 50.8% of GLP-1RA initiators used SGLT-2 inhibitors concomitantly (47.8% with established cardiovascular disease vs 51.5% without); patients with BMI ≥35 kg/m2 initiated GLP-1RA earlier (46.3% vs 29.1% as first-, second- or third-line)

audits.t: Evaluating a Tailored Quality Improvement Intervention to Improve Vaccination Coverage in Sydney Residential Aged Care Facilities.
audits.tp: Vaccination coverage in residential aged care facilities
audits.st: Australian national vaccination recommendations and funded programmes for COVID-19, influenza, pneumococcal and shingles vaccination in aged care residents
audits.f: Baseline influenza coverage 68.5%; other baseline vaccination coverage rates not given numerically, reported via subsequent absolute change
audits.c: Tailored quality improvement package supporting consent processes, vaccination planning and tracking (including a consent template and vaccination tracker)
audits.r2: Shingles coverage increased by 23.4 percentage points, pneumococcal by 14.2 percentage points, influenza by 10.9 percentage points; COVID-19 coverage declined by 7.4% (using a 6-month reporting interval)

audits.t: Increasing Genetic Testing Uptake Through Workflow Optimization: A Quality Improvement Study in Pediatric Hearing Loss.
audits.tp: Genetic testing referral for paediatric hearing loss
audits.st: American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) and Joint Committee on Infant Hearing (JCIH) recommendation that all children with hearing loss be referred for genetic evaluation
audits.f: Any documented genetics referral occurred in 35.2% of patients; referral order placed in 18.2%; documentation in clinical note in 34.1%; note routed to genetics team in 5.7%; genetics appointment completed in 11.4%; genetic mutation identified in 4.6%. In Phase 1 all referral orders and documentation were made exclusively by ENT providers.
audits.c: Standardised referral protocol: three predefined referral pathways (documentation in clinical note, routing note to genetics team, electronic referral order) applied at diagnosis, supported by provider email communication, discussion at a monthly department meeting, laminated ID badge cards and posted clinic workstation instructions, and an EMR smart phrase for documentation
audits.r2: Any documented genetics referral rose to 68.4% (chi-square=22.03, p<0.001; OR 3.98, 95% CI 2.21 to 7.18); referral order placement rose to 46.5%; documentation in clinical note to 64.0%; note routing to 34.2%; genetics appointment completion rose to 38.6% (p<0.001); genetic mutation identified in 28.2% (p<0.001). Referral initiation became more distributed, with audiologists placing 23.7% of orders and documenting 43.0% of referrals.

audits.t: Evaluation of Adherence to Clinical Guidelines for Antimicrobial Prescribing in Pregnant Patients: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Observational Study in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
audits.tp: Antimicrobial prescribing guideline adherence in pregnancy
audits.st: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) and Health Service Executive (HSE) antimicrobial prescribing guidelines
audits.f: 77.4% of prescriptions were guideline-compliant; 22.6% inappropriate, due to incorrect drug selection (9.4%), dosing errors (7.2%), and inappropriate duration (6.0%)

audits.t: Evaluating a Large-Scale Multi-Center Outreach Program for Appointment Booking and Patient Engagement: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.tp: Centralised outbound call programme for appointment booking
audits.st: Local target to improve appointment booking and patient engagement
audits.f: 66238 new appointments booked (12.1% of calls; adjusted booking rate 14.6%); 90774 calls (16.6%) confirmed existing follow-up; about 28.6% of all calls resulted in verified engagement with care
audits.c: Centralised call-centre outbound call programme (administrative recovery, continuity of care, preventive/safety outreach campaigns)

audits.t: Effect of a Quality Improvement Project on Point-of-Care Ultrasound Utilization During Inpatient Cardiac Arrest.
audits.tp: Point-of-care ultrasound use during inpatient cardiac arrest
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Prevalence of point-of-care ultrasound during cardiac arrest (PDCA) 13% pre-intervention
audits.c: Created and implemented a protocol for POCUS use during cardiac arrest (PDCA), via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: PDCA prevalence 21%, 10%, 47% and 23% by quarter; combined into 6-month periods, 16% and 35% respectively; code leaders felt PDCA had clinical utility 57% of the time

audits.t: The Role of Standardizing the White's Fast Track Handoff From Operating Room to Postanesthesia Care Unit: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Operating room to PACU handoff standardisation
audits.st: Institutional handoff protocol using the revised White's Fast Track Score (WFTS)
audits.f: Compliance with WFTS handoff elements: mean 48% (SD 8%)
audits.c: Revised WFTS handoff tool reinforced with a memory aid, keyword prompts, and staff training (PDSA cycle 3)
audits.r2: Compliance with WFTS handoff elements improved significantly to mean 85% (SD 20%), U=55.00, Z=-4.83, P<.001; documentation of anaesthesia details, level of consciousness, haemodynamic and respiratory stability notably increased

audits.t: Impact of establishing a comprehensive tobacco cessation service at a primary healthcare setting in the quit attempts: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (WHO FCTC) best-practice cessation standards
audits.f: No operational tobacco cessation service existed at the centre
audits.c: Establishment of a best-practice tobacco cessation service with very brief advice, behavioural and pharmacological support, via PDSA approach
audits.r2: 80.0% of attendees were ready to quit and 88.9% of those made a quit attempt

audits.t: Compliance of Aerosol Therapy with Evidence-based Guideline and Cost Incurred in Adult Critically-ill Patients: A Prospective Observational Study.
audits.tp: Aerosol therapy guideline compliance and cost
audits.st: Indian Guidelines on Nebulization Therapy
audits.f: Compliance of aerosol drug therapy with evidence-based guidelines varied significantly by ICU stay duration (p=0.0062) and ICU category (p=0.0005); higher compliance in critical care and neurology ICUs

audits.t: Evaluation of guideline adherence to hypertension-mediated organ damage screening in Korean patients with hypertension: results from the Korean Registry of Target Organ Damage in Hypertension (KorHR).
audits.st: Guideline-recommended hypertension-mediated organ damage (HMOD) screening (UACR, ECG, GFR basic; echocardiography, carotid ultrasound, fundoscopy, ABI, baPWV extended)
audits.f: Overall adherence for basic screening was 68.4%; GFR 90.3%, ECG 95.2%, UACR 72.5%; adherence lower in on-treatment group (57.1%) than newly treated group (79.9%)

audits.t: Assessment of current good manufacturing practice (cGMP) compliance in pharmaceutical manufacturers in Ethiopia: Cross-sectional descriptive study.
audits.st: WHO Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) requirements
audits.f: Overall cGMP compliance rates of 62.8%, 85.84%, 84.95%, 86.72%, 84.95% and 84.1% for companies 1-6; only Company 1 had critical deviations

audits.t: Improved pain management after tonsil surgery in adults: a quality improvement programme.
audits.st: Locally set target to reduce pain-related recontact rate to below 15%
audits.f: Average recontact rate due to postoperative pain of 33.6% (range 29.0-38.1%) among participating units (27% nationally, range 12-39%)
audits.c: Standardised pain management programme: patient information brochure and prescription of multimodal analgesics (paracetamol plus COX-2 inhibitor etoricoxib) with supplementary tramadol, introduced June 2022-July 2024
audits.r2: Recontact rate due to pain decreased from 33.6% to 15.5%

audits.t: Advancing Radiographic Quality in Resource-Limited Countries: An Audit of Quality Assurance Practices in Ghana.
audits.tp: Radiography quality assurance and radiation protection compliance
audits.st: Internationally harmonised QA/radiation protection guidelines; IAEA Technical Cooperation Regional Project RAF6/053 protocols for exposure indicator metrics
audits.f: Only 1 facility had an established QA programme with periodic QC measurements; radiation protection satisfactory for aprons, barriers and waiting areas, but no facility had infant immobilisation devices; half-value layer below recommended limits in 11 facilities

audits.t: Prescriber adherence to treatment guidelines for monoclonal antibodies against Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide in migraine prophylaxis - a register-based cohort study.
audits.tp: Prescriber adherence to CGRP monoclonal antibody migraine guidelines
audits.st: National guidelines for CGRP mAb treatment covering patient eligibility, prescriber qualifications, treatment evaluation and monitoring/reporting
audits.f: 90% had a prior migraine diagnosis at first dispensation; 66% had tried at least two prior prophylactic drugs; 97% of prescriptions issued by neurology/headache specialists; 12-month persistence 58% in sequence 1, 53% in sequence 2, 46% in sequence 3

audits.t: Standardised neonatal nutrition care bundle and growth velocity in infants <32 weeks: a single-centre pre-quality/post-quality improvement study.
audits.tp: Neonatal nutrition care bundle and growth velocity
audits.st: Local standard: nutrition care bundle targets aligned with ESPGHAN feeding/energy guidance and Fenton growth references; postnatal growth failure defined as discharge weight Z-score below -1.5
audits.f: Average growth velocity was 12.52±2.49 g/kg/day; time to full feeds was 21.26±15.41 days; week 1 caloric intake was 87±24 kcal/kg/day; discharge weight Z-score was -1.41±1.13; postnatal growth failure occurred in 45.8% (76/166); feeding intolerance in 22.6%; necrotising enterocolitis in 4.2%.
audits.c: Standardised multicomponent nutrition care bundle: earlier initiation and advancement of enteral feeds, standardised daily feed advancement targets, protocolised human milk fortification, multidisciplinary daily review, staff education before implementation, and ongoing audit of time to full feeds, early caloric delivery, growth velocity and discharge weight Z-score
audits.r2: Average growth velocity increased to 15.50±2.30 g/kg/day (mean difference +2.98, 95% CI 2.45 to 3.52, p<0.001); time to full feeds decreased to 15.45±7.21 days (-5.81 days, p<0.001); week 1 caloric intake increased to 98±23 kcal/kg/day (+11.38, p<0.001); discharge weight Z-score improved to -1.12±1.00 (p=0.012); discharge weight was higher by 152g (p=0.033); postnatal growth failure decreased to 33.3% (56/168, p=0.020); feeding intolerance was 25.3% and necrotising enterocolitis 5.7% (neither significantly different from baseline).

audits.t: Countdown to lobectomy: interventions to improve waiting times for lung cancer resection.
audits.st: National targets (from 2022): definitive treatment within 62 days of referral and within 31 days of the decision to treat
audits.f: Mean time from referral to lobectomy 150.47 days; overall only 5.8% and 16.3% of patients met the 62-day and 31-day targets respectively
audits.c: Joint thoracic surgery-oncology clinic and a patient pooling initiative (cycles 1-2), followed by broader service reorganisation (cycles 2-3)
audits.r2: Mean time from referral to lobectomy decreased by 27% to 109.67 days (P=.005); no further improvement after service reorganisation; no change in time from decision-to-treat to surgery

audits.t: Exploring Patterns of D-Dimer Assay Ordering at an Australian Rural Referral Hospital: A Retrospective Audit.
audits.tp: D-dimer assay ordering patterns for pulmonary embolism
audits.st: Guideline-recommended investigation sequence for D-dimer and CTPA testing in suspected pulmonary embolism
audits.f: 79.2% of investigation sequences followed the guideline-recommended order; diagnostic yield of CTPA among D-dimer-tested patients was 4.9%; discordant pathways most commonly involved a positive D-dimer without subsequent CTPA, or CTPA performed despite a negative D-dimer

audits.t: Clinical Audit of Biomedical Waste Management, Awareness, and Challenges among Health Care Workers in Segregation of Biomedical Waste in a Tertiary Care Hospital, Puducherry-A Mixed-Method Study.
audits.st: Kayakalp checklist for biomedical waste management
audits.f: Biomedical waste management compliance was 86%; about 72% of health care workers exhibited good awareness

audits.t: SGLT2 inhibitors: between the zeal of the clinical studies and the challenges of the day-to-day practice.
audits.tp: SGLT2 inhibitor prescribing in heart failure
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines recommending SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin) therapy in eligible patients with HFrEF
audits.f: 31% of 225 HFrEF patients (aged 74 +/- 15 years) received dapagliflozin or had plans for initiation; prescription rates were influenced by age and specialty, with male patients more likely to be initiated (p=0.005)
audits.c: Targeted teaching, empowering pharmacists, and use of digital tools to improve prescribing compliance
audits.r2: Substantial improvement in dapagliflozin prescription rates was reported following the interventions, though the exact re-audit percentage was not given in the supplied text

audits.t: The infusion after the bolus: a quality improvement programme to support emergency department airway governance in Ireland.
audits.tp: Emergency department airway governance and intubation safety
audits.st: Local SMART targets aligned with international airway registry benchmarks: first-pass success (FPS) >90%, complication rate <15%, and 100% data capture on the Emergency Medicine Airway Registry Ireland (EMARI)
audits.f: no consistent documentation of intubations; FPS, complication rates and operator experience were not measurable due to absent data capture
audits.c: Sequential interventions across 4 PDSA cycles: appointment of an EM airway lead, EMARI QR-code data capture, standardised preintubation checklist and airway equipment ('airway drop'), video laryngoscopy with recording, daily RSI drills, competency-based sign-off, senior airway supervision, and structured multidisciplinary teaching ('Airways, Biscuits, Caffeine')
audits.r2: overall FPS 91.7% and complication rate 12.3%, both within predefined safety targets across all 4 PDSA cycles; by the final cycle (PDSA 4), FPS reached 96.2% and complications 7.7%; EMARI data capture reached 99.2-100% and video capture rose to 72%

audits.t: Assessment of compliance with quality laboratory standards in medical laboratories within the Kumasi Metropolis, Ghana.
audits.st: WHO Stepwise Laboratory Quality Improvement Process Towards Accreditation (SLIPTA) checklist; minimum compliance level 55%
audits.f: Overall median compliance score 61 (IQR 53-66), minimum 49, maximum 104; all facilities had a zero-star rating and failed to meet the 55% minimum compliance level

audits.t: The endocrine impact of immunotherapy: audit and future service implications.
audits.tp: Thyroid immune-related adverse event management with immunotherapy
audits.st: European Society of Endocrinology (ESE) guidelines for managing thyroid immune-related adverse events
audits.f: 10.4% developed thyroiditis, 9.4% hypothyroidism without prior thyroiditis, 47.9% other TFT abnormalities; 9/11 (82%) started on levothyroxine were appropriately managed per ESE guidelines

audits.t: Optimising door-to-needle-time in children with febrile neutropenia in the paediatric emergency unit-a quality improvement study.
audits.st: International Paediatric Fever and Neutropenia Guideline Panel: first dose of antibiotic within 60 minutes of arrival (door-to-needle time, DTNT) for children with febrile neutropenia
audits.f: Median DTNT was 80 minutes (IQR 65-105); only 22% of children received antibiotics within 60 minutes; chemoport was accessed to administer antibiotics in only 19% of children; 10% required PICU admission.
audits.c: PDSA-based quality improvement: development and implementation of a validated clinical care pathway (triage, assessment, investigations, antibiotic dosing, disposition), a dedicated isolation cubicle for febrile neutropenia patients, mannequin-assisted and bedside training for doctors/nurses in chemoport access and maintenance, redefined nursing handover responsibilities, a dedicated chemoport access equipment trolley, stocking restricted antibiotics in the PER pharmacy, and repeated training to address staff attrition
audits.r2: Median DTNT fell to 40 minutes (IQR 30-50), a 50% reduction (p<0.001); the proportion of children receiving antibiotics within 60 minutes rose to 86% after PDSA 1 and 100% after PDSA 2; chemoport was accessed to administer antibiotics in all children post-intervention; no PICU admissions occurred post-intervention (versus 10% at baseline, p=0.002); no CLABSIs were reported from chemoport handling in the PER.

audits.t: Adherence to Pediatric Asthma Guidelines in Children with Asthma Exacerbation at the Emergency Department.
audits.tp: Adherence to paediatric asthma exacerbation guidelines in the emergency department
audits.st: Pediatric asthma exacerbation guidelines implemented March 2021
audits.f: Pre-guideline group outcomes for scheduled follow-up and admission
audits.c: Implementation of pediatric asthma exacerbation guidelines in the emergency department
audits.r2: Overall adherence to guidelines approximately 42.1%; post-implementation patients more likely to have scheduled next-business-day follow-up (aOR 4.82) and less likely to be admitted (aOR 0.30)

audits.t: Addressing barriers to CGM prescriptions in primary care: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Continuous glucose monitor prescribing in primary care
audits.st: American Diabetes Association standard of care: CGM use for patients with diabetes on insulin
audits.f: CGM prescriptions low relative to endocrinology practices
audits.c: Three interventions over 10 months: educational pamphlet on insurance/ordering/documentation, EHR ordering and documentation tools, and a didactic session on CGM data interpretation
audits.r2: CGM prescriptions increased by 6.6%; referrals to endocrinology for type 2 diabetes decreased by 25.3%

audits.t: Bridging the Gap: Implementation and Uptake of AUDIT-C Alcohol Screening for Inpatient Surgery.
audits.tp: AUDIT-C alcohol screening implementation in surgical inpatients
audits.st: Hospital-wide quality improvement initiative for AUDIT-C alcohol screening completion in surgical inpatients
audits.f: 9540 (31.1%) had a completed AUDIT-C score; completion varied by surgical service (15.2%-52.4%) and was higher in emergent (51.7%) and urgent (48.4%) than elective (29.1%) cases; 6.5% of those screened were moderate/high-risk

audits.t: Use .FAST to Sip Til Send: A Quality Improvement Initiative Using Digital Solutions to Facilitate Best Practice Preoperative Fasting Protocols in Emergency General Surgery.
audits.tp: Preoperative fasting protocol compliance in emergency general surgery
audits.st: Australian national anaesthetic guidelines: solid food until 6h, unlimited clear fluids until 2h, and (since 2024) sips of clear fluids up to 200mL/h until sent to theatre
audits.f: Uptake of best practice fasting guidelines 1%
audits.c: Staff education campaign and an EMR smart phrase (".FAST") to prompt the sip-til-send protocol
audits.r2: Uptake of best practice fasting guidelines increased to 47%; decreased total fasting time and preoperative IV fluid use; no patients had surgery cancelled due to inadequate fasting

audits.t: Nurses' Compliance with Delirium Assessment Protocol in a Tertiary Hospital: A Retrospective Study.
audits.tp: Nurses' compliance with delirium assessment protocol
audits.st: Hospital's Nursing Operational Guidelines: Modified 4AT delirium assessment within 24 hours of admission
audits.f: 73.5% (n=3545) received a 4AT assessment; only 32.9% (n=1168) of those assessed were screened within the recommended 24 hours

audits.t: Reducing unnecessary coagulation screening in ambulatory patients in the emergency departments of a multi-site trust: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Unnecessary coagulation screening in ambulatory ED patients
audits.st: NHS England guidelines on coagulation screening in the emergency department
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: PDSA cycles including posters, relocating coagulation sample bottles, involving other specialties, and a survey to identify educational needs, highlighted at regular nursing and medical meetings
audits.r2: Gradual and sustained decrease in coagulation screens (26.97%) and coagulation:FBC ratio (28.51%) at 28 weeks, with no increase in the proxy measure for repeat coagulation or D-dimer sampling; projected annual cost savings of £81,700-£86,400 and about 250 kg CO2 per year

audits.t: Reducing unnecessary preoperative testing in Day Surgery: a Choosing Wisely-based quality improvement study.
audits.tp: Reducing unnecessary preoperative testing in day surgery
audits.st: Choosing Wisely guidelines on preoperative testing for low-risk surgery
audits.f: Pre-intervention routine preoperative laboratory testing, ECG and chest radiography rates (baseline higher than post-intervention)
audits.c: Redesigned preoperative pathway separating minor day surgery cases (ASA I-III) from intermediate/major surgery, eliminating routine testing unless clinically indicated after anaesthesiologist evaluation
audits.r2: Laboratory testing dropped to 2.6%, ECG to 6.7%, chest radiography to 0.3%; no surgeries cancelled for insufficient work-up; no unplanned postoperative admissions; wait times reduced from weeks to less than 7 days

audits.t: A Structured Protocol to Optimize Proton Pump Inhibitor Use: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Proton pump inhibitor deprescribing in older adults
audits.st: not reported (guideline recommendations for limited-duration PPI use)
audits.f: Baseline inappropriate PPI use without appropriate indication 35.3%
audits.c: Nurse-led PPI medication review using a structured deprescribing algorithm, EHR text templates, patient education resources, and interprofessional huddles (Iowa Model)

audits.t: Optimizing Large-Volume Paracentesis in a Gastroenterology Ward: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Large-volume paracentesis equipment preparation and documentation
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) eight-point checklist for large-volume paracentesis
audits.f: 56% of doctors needed 6-10 minutes to gather equipment and 78% had incomplete knowledge of required items; for documentation, 50% needed guidance from colleagues and 25% spent over 10 minutes per note
audits.c: Cycle 1: a standardised equipment checklist poster displayed in the doctors' office. Cycle 2: a smart-text documentation proforma in the electronic patient record aligned with the BSG eight-point checklist
audits.r2: all respondents had seen the poster and 83% felt it reduced preparation time; all respondents found the smart-text proforma useful, with 83% anticipating documentation in 1-6 minutes and all reporting increased confidence to document independently

audits.t: Prescriber adherence to asthma treatment guidelines and its impact on symptom control in Ethiopia: a mixed-methods study.
audits.tp: Prescriber adherence to asthma treatment guidelines
audits.st: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) guidelines
audits.f: Patients managed by non-adherent prescribers had 72% lower odds of achieving symptom control (AOR 0.28)

audits.t: Quality improvement project: Implementing a mortality screening tool post hospital discharge to guide goals of care conversations and improve hospice admissions.
audits.tp: Mortality screening tool to guide goals of care and hospice referral
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Hospice admission rate 18.5%; average hospice length of stay 30.5 days
audits.c: Prognosis/mortality screening tool implemented at post-hospital-discharge follow-up visits, with written then video provider education and a hospice reference pamphlet, across three PDSA cycles

audits.t: Application of the PDCA cycle management in quality improvement of endotracheal intubation in emergency department among standardised training residents.

audits.t: A multi-centre quality improvement project to assess the impact of a standardised NIV care bundle on mortality outcomes in patients with acute type 2 respiratory failure.

audits.r2: mean mortality fell to 21% (a 7% absolute reduction from 28%, equating to 143 fewer deaths in 2023 vs 2022), against a target of 10% (not achieved); among appropriately selected NIV patients, mortality was 9.76% in the final month, within control limits of the 10% target
