audits.t: A quality improvement initiative to reduce central line-associated bloodstream infection rates in the polytrauma intensive care unit of a tertiary care trauma hospital in India.
audits.tp: CLABSI reduction in the polytrauma ICU
audits.st: Local standard: aim to reduce CLABSI rate by 30% (from 14 to 10 per 1000 central line days) by June 2024, using the CDC/NHSN-based CLABSI surveillance definitions adapted for India
audits.f: CLABSI rate was 14.1 per 1000 central line days (14 per 1000 in the latter half of 2023); CLIP tool completion, full-body drape use and aseptic insertion practice were infrequently documented at baseline (quantitative baseline data unavailable due to poor documentation); crude mortality among CLABSI patients was 31.3% (5 of 16).
audits.c: 9 PDSA cycles: staff education/training on infection prevention and central line care, increased frequency of ICU rounds by infection control nurses and the QI team, mandatory use of the electronic Central Line Insertion Practice (CLIP) tool with monthly audits, maximal barrier precaution monitoring via checklist, mandatory chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, hand hygiene refresher training with WHO 'Five Moments' monitoring and public recognition of top compliers, a central line maintenance bundle with daily necessity review and early removal, a maintenance bundle checklist, and 'scrub the hub' training and monitoring
audits.r2: CLABSI rate fell to 8.04 per 1000 central line days, a 43% reduction (p=0.04), with 49 consecutive CLABSI-free days; CLIP tool completion rose to 88.3%; full-body drape use documented in 78.4% of cases; aseptic conditions maintained in 75%; central line maintenance bundle compliance rose to 75%; 'scrub the hub' compliance rose to 65%; chlorhexidine skin antisepsis compliance reached 100%; crude mortality among CLABSI patients fell to 27.3% (3 of 11).

audits.t: Using a Quality Improvement Initiative to Decrease Oxygen Toxicity among Mechanically Ventilated Children.

audits.f: Average monthly hyperoxia rate (SpO2 98-100% with FiO2 greater than 0.21) was 54.8%; average duration of mechanical ventilation was 8.16 days (SD 18.8); mortality was 11.7%.
audits.c: Two PDSA cycles: (1) staff education on hyperoxia harms plus standardised default SpO2 goal (90-97%) and FiO2 weaning permission in the electronic ventilator order set; (2) a best practice advisory (BPA) in the electronic health record alerting bedside nurses/respiratory therapists when SpO2 was 98-100% with FiO2 above 0.21, prompting FiO2 weaning (capped at one alert per 4 hours, excluding pulmonary hypertension patients)
audits.r2: Average monthly hyperoxia rate fell to 41.0% after PDSA 1 and to 28% after BPA launch, sustained for over a year; average duration of mechanical ventilation was 4.8 days (SD 6.1, p=0.11 vs baseline); mortality was 9.4% (p=0.2 vs baseline, not significant).

audits.t: Reduced wait times for hepatology referrals in a prospective quality improvement initiative.

audits.t: Antibiotic Stewardship Quality Improvement Project for Neonatal Sepsis in a Tertiary NICU in Lima, Peru.
audits.st: Local standard: institutional clinical practice guideline (CPG) for neonatal sepsis, as part of the Andean Health Organization (ORAS) regional antibiotic stewardship initiative, with a target of reducing antibiotic use rate (AUR) by 20% for early-onset (EOS) and late-onset sepsis (LOS)
audits.f: AUR for EOS was approximately 104 days per 1000 patient-days and for LOS approximately 158 days per 1000 patient-days at project start; institutional infection-related mortality was 4.4 deaths per 1000 live births (not broken down by sepsis type); CPG adherence in a 2021 evaluation was 84.4% for EOS and 66.8% for LOS.
audits.c: 5 PDSA cycles: (1) identifying antibiotic overuse and adding an infectious disease specialist; (2) faster blood culture reporting, evolving from photographed results to an automated electronic platform updating every 8 hours; (3) improving blood culture collection technique (chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, minimum 1 mL blood volume, staff training); (4) updating the neonatal sepsis clinical practice guideline (minimum blood volumes, 48-hour antibiotic discontinuation for negative cultures without compatible symptoms, extension to 5 days if symptoms persist, delayed collection of acute-phase reactants); (5) regular dissemination of AUR control charts to staff
audits.r2: AUR fell by 17.3% for EOS (from 104 to 86 days per 1000 patient-days, with the steepest decline from January to April 2024) and by 25.9% for LOS (central line falling from 158 to 117 days per 1000 patient-days, steepest decline September-October 2023, reaching a minimum AUR of 36 for EOS by May 2024); rule-out sepsis predominated in EOS (67.2%) while confirmed sepsis predominated in LOS (40.6%); no treatment failures or early recurrent sepsis were observed after antibiotic discontinuation, and no readmissions occurred within 30 days.

Weight-stability control chart improved to a mean of 93.6% (approaching upper control limit 98.9%) with no rule violations; process capability was high (Cp=2.809, Cpk=2.541), also well-centred and capable for the >3% weight loss (Cp=2.536, Cpk=0.899) and >3% weight gain balancing measures (Cp=2.786, Cpk=0.806).

audits.r2: No significant improvements observed in process indicators, medication-related adverse events, or clinical incidents; implementation fidelity varied (100% prophylactic antibiotic timing, 80% app use, 40% pain scale use)

audits.t: Utilizing Quality Improvement Methodology to Implement a Perioperative Intravenous Acetaminophen Protocol in Neonatal Gastrointestinal Surgery.
audits.st: ERAS guidelines recommending multimodal analgesia to limit opioid exposure (no numeric target stated)
audits.f: Overall protocol compliance 43.9% (46.0% preoperative, 90.2% postoperative); compliance was greater when the order set was used (67.7% preoperative vs 77.4% postoperative order set use)
audits.c: Multidisciplinary PDSA cycles: standardized perioperative IV acetaminophen dosing protocol with training (cycle 1), followed by an online order set for administration (cycle 2)

audits.t: Impact of quality improvement initiative on incidence of hypothermia in neonates in the delivery room.
audits.tp: Neonatal hypothermia prevention in delivery room
audits.st: Local QI target: reduce hypothermia (temperature <36.5°C) rate to <50% of baseline (<25.8%) within 12 weeks
audits.f: Baseline hypothermia incidence 51.67%
audits.c: Multidisciplinary PDSA cycles: protocol establishment and OSCE-based staff training (cycle 1); immediate skin-to-skin contact and equipment readiness (cycle 2); pre-operative maternal counselling and post-operative staff sensitisation (cycle 3)
audits.r2: Hypothermia incidence decreased from 51.67% to 13.16% (P<.001); per-cycle rates were 31.7%, 37.03% and 22.58%; STS ≥60 min increased 25% to 85% (P<.001); early breastfeeding increased 30% to 78% (P<.001); sustained at 13.16% through a 3-week sustainability phase

audits.t: Reducing medical equipment downtime using Lean Six Sigma: a quality improvement project at Suhul Hospital, Shire.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline total equipment downtime 89,735 minutes; 842 defects.
audits.c: Lean Six Sigma: 5S, process mapping, corrective maintenance standardisation, structured preventive maintenance plan.
audits.r2: Downtime reduced to 292 minutes (-99.67%); defects reduced to 43 (-94.89%); Sigma level improved from 2.74 to 3.62.

audits.t: Go Decaf!: implementing 'decaf by default' as a quality improvement intervention to reduce toileting-related falls and improve care environments in acute hospital settings.
audits.tp: Toileting-related falls reduction via caffeine reduction
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Toileting-related falls accounted for 19%-21% of all inpatient falls at pilot sites; organisation-wide baseline 33.2% of inpatient falls were toileting-related
audits.c: 'Decaf by default' approach (decaffeinated hot drinks offered as default, caffeinated available on request), supported by staff education, shared decision-making materials and a patient-facing activity, tested over two PDSA cycles then organisation-wide rollout
audits.r2: Toileting-related falls as a proportion of inpatient falls reduced to 11%-15% at pilot sites (approximately 11% reduction in Cycle 1 and 20% in Cycle 2, with seven wards achieving reductions greater than 50%); organisation-wide, the proportion fell from 33.2% to 25.9%

audits.t: Hypertension Control Rates Before and After Implementation of a Multicomponent Quality Improvement Program in Medicare Beneficiaries Primarily of Hispanic Origin in a Large Health System in South Florida, 2011-2018.
audits.st: Guideline-based hypertension management (target not stated numerically)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Multicomponent programme: team-based care, standardised BP measurement, guideline-based management, EHR support, pharmacy/transportation services, culturally tailored engagement.
audits.r2: Adjusted odds of hypertension control 5.7x higher (95% CI 5.4-6.0) after implementation; crude AVG-BP control rate approximately 90%.

audits.t: Therapeutic Drug Monitoring of Vancomycin Based on Ratio of Area under the Curve to Minimum Inhibitory Concentration: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.tp: Vancomycin AUC/MIC-based therapeutic drug monitoring implementation
audits.st: Target AUC/MIC ratio of 400-600 for vancomycin therapeutic drug monitoring
audits.f: 22% (n=6) of pharmacists felt knowledgeable and 19% (n=5) comfortable with AUC/MIC-based TDM before implementation
audits.c: Implementation of AUC/MIC-based TDM for vancomycin (April 2021) with educational sessions, a dosing calculator, guidelines and written communications developed over 8 months
audits.r2: 88% (n=21/24) knowledgeable and comfortable at 1 month, 81% (n=26/32) at 2 years; satisfaction 88% (21/24) at 1 month and 94% (29/31) at 2 years

audits.t: Nurse-Led Evidence-Based Quality Improvement Programme to Reduce Urinary Leakage in Intensive Care Unit Patients with Urinary catheters: A Pre-Post Quasi-Experimental Study.
audits.st: Local evidence-based standard: 21 audit standards forming the Urinary Leakage Bundle (catheter selection, securement, obstruction prevention, staff training), developed from 15 best-evidence recommendations via the i-PARIHS framework
audits.f: Urinary leakage rate was 25.41% (31/122); preliminary audit found 10 of 21 audit standards had implementation rates below 60% (e.g. appropriate catheter size selection 32.50%, smallest appropriate size 32.50%, effective bowel management 20.00%); nurses' knowledge, attitudes and practices questionnaire score was 3.36±0.31 overall (knowledge 3.34±0.38, attitudes 4.04±0.28, practices 2.44±0.34).
audits.c: Nurse-led evidence-based Urinary Leakage Bundle implemented via i-PARIHS: a catheter material/size selection guide, standardised diagrams for secondary catheter securement, structured departmental education, simulation workshops on catheter selection and securement, one-to-one bedside coaching, and departmental policy/consumables changes (silicone catheter stock, dedicated securement dressings) to support the 4 bundle domains
audits.r2: Urinary leakage rate fell to 13.27% (15/113) (chi-square p=0.019); nurses' knowledge, attitudes and practices questionnaire score rose to 4.40±0.31 overall (knowledge 4.28±0.35, attitudes 4.78±0.43, practices 4.36±0.65, all p<0.001); adherence improved in key bundle elements including catheter selection, securement, and management of catheter bypassing.

audits.t: Examining variations in adherence to guideline-recommended post-acute kidney injury care in primary care in England: a population-based cohort study.
audits.tp: Post-acute kidney injury care in primary care
audits.st: 14 guideline-recommended post-AKI care indicators covering AKI coding, post-discharge primary care contact, kidney health and blood pressure monitoring, and guideline-indicated prescribing
audits.f: AKI coded in primary care within 30 days of discharge in 19.5% of episodes; documented general practice contact in 72.6%; at 90±30 days, serum creatinine measured in 34.2%, blood pressure in 34.6%, albumin-creatinine ratio in 4.2%; renin-angiotensin system inhibitor prescribing was low in patients likely to benefit

audits.t: Implementing a RPM-enabled transitional care pathway for adults with poorly controlled diabetes: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Remote patient monitoring transitional care for diabetes
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Enrolment grew from 10.5% to 39.7% across PDSA cycles.
audits.c: Remote patient monitoring integrated into nurse-led transitional care pathway via iterative PDSA cycles.

audits.t: Compliance with the national personal protective equipment guideline for COVID-19 among hospitals in Indonesia: a cross-sectional study.
audits.st: Indonesian Ministry of Health national PPE guideline for COVID-19 (April 2020, 15 situations)
audits.f: Overall compliance low (median 1 of 15 situations compliant); overuse predominated (median 7 of 15 situations).

audits.t: [Reduction of expenditure on intravenous albumin with the implementation of rational use protocols with audit and feedback in a private hospital].
audits.st: Local rational use protocol for intravenous albumin (no external guideline named)
audits.f: 28 patients received IV albumin; consumption 0.09 vial-ampoules/bed-day; 14.7 containers per patient; cost USD4 per bed-day
audits.c: Implementation of a rational use protocol with audit and feedback, monthly consumption measurement and case monitoring (April 2023)
audits.r2: Patients receiving IV albumin decreased from 28 to 8 (-67.3%, p=0.005); consumption/bed-day 0.09 to 0.01 (IRR 0.139); containers per patient 14.7 to 6.6 (IRR 0.451); cost/bed-day USD4 to 0.57 (-86.1%); projected annual savings USD57,091

audits.t: [A quality improvement study to increase the breastfeeding rate in very preterm infants in the neonatal intensive care unit].
audits.tp: Breastfeeding rate in very preterm infants NICU
audits.st: Local QI target: increase breastfeeding rate by 10 percentage points from baseline of 75%
audits.f: Breastfeeding rate 75%
audits.c: PDSA-based multidimensional quality improvement strategies guided by a key driver diagram, monitored with a run chart
audits.r2: Breastfeeding rate increased to 89%, a 14 percentage point increase from baseline (P=0.039)

audits.t: Using the KTA framework to improve evidence-based umbilical cord care for newborns in the NICU: a pre-post implementation study.
audits.tp: Evidence-based umbilical cord care in NICU
audits.st: Evidence-based recommendations for neonatal umbilical cord care generated via the KTA framework (no numeric target stated)
audits.f: Nurses' knowledge score 62.31±8.70; professional identity score 75.16±5.90
audits.c: Implementation of an evidence-based standardized umbilical cord care operational procedure guided by the Knowledge-to-Action framework, November 2024 to April 2025
audits.r2: Nurses' knowledge score increased to 90.78±3.70; professional identity score increased to 84.11±6.70

audits.t: Clinical outcomes and opportunities for improvement across modified trauma quality improvement cohorts: a registry-based cohort study.
audits.st: American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Improvement Program (TQIP) risk-adjusted mortality benchmarking, combined with structured multidisciplinary peer review identifying opportunities for improvement (OFIs)
audits.f: Overall 30-day mortality was 8.8% (727/8298), ranging from 15.9% in blunt multisystem trauma without TBI to 52.8% in isolated severe TBI, versus 4.1% in the non-TQIP reference cohort; unfavourable Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS less than 4) at discharge ranged from 35% (penetrating truncal injury) to 91.1% (isolated severe TBI) versus 25.8% in the reference cohort; opportunities for improvement were identified overall in 5.9% (493/8298), highest in blunt multisystem trauma without TBI (16.9%) and with TBI (10.6%).

audits.t: Impact of Structured Data Validation on Case Completeness and Key Quality Indicators in the SWISS Implant Registry (SIRIS Spine): A SINGLE-CENTER Audit.
audits.tp: Spine implant registry data completeness audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Dural tear rate 9%; first reoperation/revision rate 10% (pre-validation).
audits.c: Semi-automated, chart-adjudicated structured data validation workflow.
audits.r2: 32% of records modified (76% added, 24% deleted); dural tear rate 10%; first reoperation/revision rate 17% after validation (both changes p<0.001).

audits.t: Quality Improvement Through Morbidity and Mortality Meetings in Interventional Radiology: A Retrospective Review.
audits.tp: Morbidity and mortality meeting recommendation implementation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 139 cases discussed yielded 70 recommendations, of which 45 (64.3%) were successfully implemented; department process-related recommendations were most frequent (45.7%) and most likely implemented (87.5%)

audits.t: Beginning Restorative Activities Very Early: A Quality Improvement Project to Advance ABCDEF Bundle Practice in a Pediatric Oncology Intensive Care Unit.
audits.tp: ABCDEF bundle implementation in paediatric oncology ICU
audits.st: Local SMART targets aligned with SCCM ABCDEF ICU liberation bundle guidance: positive delirium (CAPD) screen rate 30% or less, PT/OT consultation within 72 hours 80% or more, and early mobilisation within 72 hours 80% or more
audits.f: Overall positive delirium screen rate (CAPD 9 or higher) was 15.5%, meeting the target of 30% or less; PT/OT consultation within 72 hours occurred in 80.7% of patients, meeting the 80% target; but only 49.7% of consultations were fully completed within 72 hours (mobilisation target not met); 90.4% of patients with tracked mobility ambulated at some point during their ICU stay; no mobility-related safety incidents (unplanned extubation, central line dislodgement, or injury) occurred.
audits.c: Comprehensive ABCDEF bundle rollout (BRAVE2), building on the earlier BRAVE1 early-mobility project: standardised age-appropriate pain assessment, daily extubation readiness trials, preference for lighter non-benzodiazepine sedation (dexmedetomidine, ketamine), twice-daily Cornell Assessment of Pediatric Delirium screening, a nurse-driven continuous mobility programme with standardised BRAVE mobility levels, and structured family engagement (education packets, twice-daily family-centred rounds), monitored via statistical process control (p-charts)

audits.t: Audit of temporal artery biopsy reporting in South Australia.
audits.st: Society for Cardiovascular Pathology 2023 consensus guideline for temporal artery biopsy reporting (four main areas plus 7 microscopic sub-points required to be classed 'complete')
audits.f: No TAB reports were complete against the guideline (0% complete)
audits.r2: No TAB reports were complete against the guideline; reporting of a final diagnosis and final diagnosis comment decreased significantly over time (p=0.001 and p=0.004)

audits.t: Evaluation of acne vulgaris patient care in outpatient clinics: guideline adherence and patient education.
audits.tp: Acne guideline adherence and patient education
audits.st: American Dermatology Association (ADA) 2016/2024, NICE 2021, Turkiye Dermatology Association (TDA) 2018 acne guidelines
audits.f: Adherence was highest to ADA guidelines followed by TDA; deviations noted, particularly oral antibiotic monotherapy; gaps in structured patient counselling.

audits.t: Improving Lipid Screening Adherence in Inflammatory Arthritis Using a Two-Cycle Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) Quality Improvement Intervention.
audits.tp: Lipid screening adherence in inflammatory arthritis
audits.st: Cardiovascular risk lipid screening guidelines for seropositive RA/PsA/AS
audits.f: Baseline: 62.4% (98/157) had a completed lipid panel in prior 12 months; after PDSA1 (education, reminders, Epic dot phrase) screening fell to 57.1% (28/49).
audits.c: PDSA1: provider education, physical/email reminders, Epic dot phrase. PDSA2: pre-visit chart review and pre-emptive pending lipid order placement.

audits.t: Participatory accessibility audits as a tool for disability-inclusive health systems: Findings from two Indian states.
audits.tp: Participatory disability accessibility audits of hospitals
audits.st: Reference accessibility guidelines used to develop a participatory audit checklist
audits.f: Physical accessibility efforts (e.g. ramps) often inappropriate; large gaps in accessibility for people with sensory impairments.
audits.c: Audit findings shared with state/district officials; action plans co-created with government.

audits.t: Achieving Faster Bleeding Disorder Treatment in the Emergency Department: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.tp: Time to clotting factor treatment for bleeding disorders in ED
audits.st: Local SMART aim: reduce median time to clotting factor concentrate (CFC) from 129 to 99 minutes within 6 months
audits.f: Baseline median time to CFC 129 minutes.
audits.c: Educational initiatives, personalised management cards, improved haematology-ED communication, evidence-based algorithm/guideline.
audits.r2: Median time to CFC reduced to 82 minutes at 6 months (exceeding SMART aim); 61 minutes since project initiation (53% reduction); 41 minutes in most recent 6 months (68% reduction from baseline).

audits.t: Incidence of Urinary Retention Following OnabotulinumtoxinA: A Multi-Centre Audit Challenging the Necessity of Universal CISC Training.
audits.tp: Urinary retention risk after BoNT-A for overactive bladder
audits.st: NICE NG123 guidance requiring clean intermittent self-catheterisation (CISC) counselling prior to OnabotulinumtoxinA injections for overactive bladder
audits.f: Urinary retention rate was 4.0% (10/250, 95% CI 2.2%-7.2%), notably lower than published clinical trial benchmarks (6.5%-40%); retention was more frequent after first-time than repeat injections (6.4% vs 3.2%), though not statistically significant (p=0.27)
audits.c: not reported (a selective, risk-stratified 'just-in-time' CISC teaching model was proposed but not yet implemented)

audits.t: Discordance between early mobility protocol expectations and nurse-led mobilizations of critically ill children: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Fidelity of paediatric ICU early mobility protocol
audits.st: PICU Up! early mobility protocol, which assigns patients a mobility level (1-3) based on physiologic criteria and recommends corresponding activities
audits.f: Agreement between protocol-expected and nurse-reported mobility level was moderate (53.5%, kappa=0.32); agreement for highest level of mobility (HLM) achieved was poor (40.6%, kappa=0.20); the PICU Up! level was undocumented in the EHR for 13.9% of patients and reported as unknown by nurses for 27.7%; median mobilisations per shift were 1 by EHR documentation versus 6 by nurse report versus 6 expected; discordance between nurse-reported and expected mobility level occurred in 46.5% of patients and discordance in HLM in 59.4%; severe baseline disability (Pediatric Cerebral Performance Category) was associated with higher odds of discordant mobility level (OR 8.33, 95% CI 2.50 to 27.76, p=0.001) and discordant HLM (OR 3.71, 95% CI 1.15 to 12.01, p=0.029), while mechanical ventilation, vascular access lines, and sedation over 30 minutes were associated with lower odds of HLM discordance.

audits.t: Real-time AI assistance improves adherence to standardized biliopancreatic EUS examination: a real-world comparative study.
audits.st: Standardised eight-station biliopancreatic EUS examination protocol
audits.f: Documentation completeness 81.29%.
audits.c: Real-time AI assistance system during EUS examination.
audits.r2: Documentation completeness 89.93% (adjusted absolute difference +8.65%, 95% CI 6.58-10.71); higher detection rate of pancreatic masses <2cm.

audits.t: Implementation of Glycemic Management Guideline: A Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Initiative for Patients with Diabetes Receiving Bolus Enteral Feeding.
audits.tp: Glycaemic management guideline implementation in enteral feeding
audits.st: Multidisciplinary glycaemic management guideline aligning CBG monitoring and insulin timing with enteral feeding
audits.f: CBG readings per 100 patient-days decreased 22%; pre-feed CBG monitoring 59% to 68%; pre-feed insulin administration 54% to 71%.
audits.c: Standardised guideline, structured education, visual workflow aids, train-the-trainer model.
audits.r2: CBG monitoring per 100 patient-days decreased 29.4%; hyperglycaemia 37.1% to 32.3%; normoglycaemia 61.9% to 66.1%; pre-feed CBG monitoring 72% to 79%; pre-feed insulin 53% to 73%.

audits.t: Brief report of a pilot test of an audit tool for assurance of Declarations of Interest policy in NICE COVID-19 guidance production.
audits.tp: Declarations of interest policy compliance (guideline committees)

audits.t: Quality improvement project for minimising red blood cell unit wastage at a secondary referral hospital in Malawi.
audits.st: Local target: reduce blood unit wastage to zero; First Expire First Out (FEFO) adherence
audits.f: Mean expiry rate 4.16% (37/890), highest in March at 5.4%.
audits.c: Adjusted blood ordering mechanism, strict FEFO adherence, improved coordination and staff coverage (5 PDSA cycles).
audits.r2: Wastage declined to 1% (6/520, p=0.007); zero expiries from September 2024 to March 2025; ward-returned units declined from 1.1% (8/713) to 0.7% (4/570), p=0.45.

audits.t: Factors associated with compliance among urban street food vendors with the food safety and standards authority of India (FSSAI) checklist: evidence from multinomial logistic and gamma regression models.
audits.tp: Street food vendor compliance with FSSAI checklist
audits.st: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) checklist for street food vendors (4 domains)
audits.f: Significant hygiene and sanitation non-compliance; male sex associated with higher odds of personal hygiene compliance (OR 1.31); no pre-placement exam associated with lower Maintenance & Sanitation compliance (OR 0.61).

audits.t: Audit of Blood Component Utilization and Request Appropriateness in a Tertiary Care Hospital: A Cross-Sectional Study.
audits.st: National Blood Transfusion Council (NBTC) India, BCSH and AABB blood component request appropriateness criteria
audits.f: 70.9% (6202) met appropriateness criteria (95% CI 69.9-71.8); FFP lowest appropriateness (35.2% not meeting), PRBC 28.7%, PC 21.6%; PRBC crossmatch-to-transfusion ratio 2.1:1.

audits.t: Prescribers' adherence to clinical practice guidelines for the management of hypertension at public hospitals in Northwest Ethiopia: An explanatory sequential mixed-methods study.
audits.st: JNC 7 hypertension clinical practice guideline adherence scale
audits.f: 41.1% of prescribers had low adherence to hypertension CPGs; 90.5% were aware of the guidelines.

audits.t: Quality Improvement Initiative: Implementation of a Unified Pediatric Asthma Pathway Reduces Critical Care Requirements.
audits.st: Local unified paediatric asthma clinical pathway (based on standardised asthma care pathways)
audits.f: 31% of patients required PICU-level care.
audits.c: Unified clinical pathway across ED/PICU/ward, EMR order set, standardised discharge checklist, clinician education.
audits.r2: 13% required PICU-level care (vs 31% baseline); time on continuous albuterol reduced from 7.4 to 3.2 hours; overall hospital/PICU length of stay unchanged; balancing measures (transfers, readmissions, ED revisits) unchanged.

audits.t: Effect of improved uterotonic availability on postpartum hemorrhage and maternal morbidity after vaginal delivery, review of a single-center quality-improvement initiative.
audits.st: Local hemorrhage risk stratification/management bundle; second-line uterotonic availability policy
audits.f: PPH 6.33%, SMM-H 22.9%; low-risk PPH 5.7%, low-risk SMM-H 18.6%; misoprostol most common first second-line agent (60%).
audits.c: Improved availability of second-line injectable uterotonics in the delivery room regardless of PPH risk.
audits.r2: PPH 6.61% (p=0.61, not significant), SMM-H 25.6% (p=0.40, not significant); low-risk PPH 6.1%, low-risk SMM-H 18.8%; methylergonovine most common first agent (45%), a statistically significant change from baseline.

audits.t: Closing the audit loop: a patient satisfaction survey.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Postal survey 22% dissatisfied vs interview survey 12% dissatisfied
audits.c: Changes made to address areas of criticism identified by the first survey
audits.r2: Significant reduction in dissatisfied responses in the areas addressed

audits.t: An audit of environmental health calls to a department of public health medicine.

audits.r2: Calls increased to 3.29 per week; signing increased to 83%, dating to 72%

audits.t: Improving diabetes preventive care in a family practice residency program: a case study in continuous quality improvement.
audits.st: Diabetes management indicators: dietary counselling, exercise counselling, foot care counselling, ophthalmology referral, HbA1c and renal function measurement (numeric compliance target not stated)
audits.f: Baseline compliance with diabetes management recommendations was 40%
audits.c: Continuous quality improvement (CQI) programme using diabetes management indicators as measures of quality of care

audits.tp: Ultrasound referral timing for developmental hip dysplasia

audits.t: Improving the quality of orthopaedic elective and trauma operative notes: A completed audit loop study
audits.st: British Orthopaedic Association (BOA) guidelines (elective notes) and Royal College of Surgeons of England (RCSE) guidelines (trauma notes)
audits.f: Baseline compliance with BOA/RCSE documentation standards (not fully specified numerically)
audits.c: Surgeon education and circulation of a guideline-based electronic operative note
audits.r2: Significant improvement (p-value reported but truncated) in quality of elective and trauma operative notes

audits.t: Improving weekend handover in trauma and orthopaedics: A four cycle audit
audits.tp: Weekend handover quality in trauma and orthopaedics

audits.t: Health economics: The cost of treatment of persistent fracture non-unions using bone morphogenetic protein-7 (BMP-7)
audits.tp: DEXA scan referral for fragility fracture patients
audits.st: Secondary prevention of fragility fractures (DEXA scan referral)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Improving the clinical assessment of patients with fractured neck of femur: Audit and loop closure of clerking practice after introduction of a clerking proforma

audits.st: Gold standard for completion of Adults with Incapacity (Scotland) Act 2000 certificates

audits.t: Simple changes save lives: a multi-centre clinical audit of the management of trauma patients on arrival at the emergency room in the Gaza Strip, occupied Palestinian territory
audits.tp: WHO trauma checklist adherence in emergency room
audits.st: WHO trauma checklist for basic trauma care standards
audits.f: IV fluids used in 32%, 34%, 60% of indicated cases (hospitals A, B, C); oximeters used in 72%, 74%, 76% of indicated cases; treatment plan not documented in 126 of 150 patients (84%); urinary catheters used without indication in 8% and 16% of cases in hospitals A and B

audits.t: 1282 EVALUATION OF THE IDENTIFICATION BONE HEALTH OF PATIENTS ON GERIATRIC WARDS

audits.t: CLINICAL AUDIT ON BONE MINERAL DENSITY (BMD) CONDUCTED IN SERDANG HOSPITAL IN THE YEAR 2023
audits.tp: Bone mineral density testing and treatment adequacy
audits.st: not reported (osteoporosis treatment eligibility criteria: fragility fracture, T score ≤-2.5, or osteopenia with qualifying FRAX score)

audits.t: Audit of a Standard Operating Procedure to Prevent Wrong-Level Lumbar Spinal Surgery with Intra-Operative X-Ray
audits.st: Established local standard operating procedure (SOP) for use of X-rays to identify lumbar spinal level
audits.f: One patient did not receive pre-operative X-ray; number of exposures recorded in only 71% of patients; 28 cases (13.9%) had intra-operative X-ray level checked due to doubt, of which 22 were found to be on an incorrect level
audits.c: Findings presented at local clinical effectiveness meeting to check local practice and suggest improvements
audits.r2: All patients received pre-operative X-rays with number of exposures recorded for all; 20 cases (9.7%) had intra-operative X-ray level checked due to doubt, of which only 7 were found to be on an incorrect level

audits.t: Comparative analysis of landmark-guided intra-articular knee injections in outpatient clinics versus ultrasound-guided injections: a quality improvement study
audits.st: not reported (local waiting time/cost benchmarking)
audits.f: US-guided injections averaged 16.2 weeks waiting time and cost ~£700 each; landmark-guided injections averaged 15 weeks and cost ~£600 each
audits.c: Revised costing model and increased clinic-based (landmark-guided) procedures to reduce ultrasound demand
audits.r2: US waiting times reduced to 9 weeks; annual savings of ~£96,000 achieved; no reported adverse events

audits.t: The Impact of Online Problem-Based Mentoring Programme on Postgraduate Orthopaedics Exam Performance-A Re-Audit of a Previous Study
audits.tp: FRCS exam pass rates and structured teaching
audits.st: not reported (comparison of exam pass rates, not a clinical care standard)

audits.r2: Career-grade surgeons' passing rate more than doubled after establishing teaching activities

audits.t: PRESCRIPTION AUDIT AT A TERTIARY CARE HOSPITAL – A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY
audits.st: National Health Mission Prescription Audit Guidelines 2021

audits.st: Preoperative antibiotic administration within 60 minutes before surgical incision (SSI prevention)

audits.t: Procedural sedation in a tertiary referral trauma centre: A retrospective audit
audits.st: Complication definitions and benchmark rate from a comparable previous major Australasian study (7.2%, 95% CI 6.2-8.2)
audits.f: Complication rate 4.0% in the initial six months of the review period
audits.c: Multiple education sessions on prevention of sedation complications
audits.r2: Complication rate dropped to 1.3% after education sessions, then rebounded to 3.1% in the last six months; overall complication rate over 2.5 years was 3.1% (95% CI 2.3-4.0), significantly lower than the comparator study's 7.2% (P<0.0001)

audits.t: An observational audit of pain scores post-orthopaedic surgery at a level two state hospital in Cape Town
audits.tp: Postoperative pain control after orthopaedic surgery
audits.st: Local standard: VAS pain score ≥4 regarded as unacceptable

audits.c: Pain rounds, staff education and training, increased postoperative epidural time, patient-controlled analgesia pumps, indwelling femoral catheters following total knee replacement
audits.r2: Mean pain scores <4 at every time point measured, significantly lower than audit 1 at most times (p<0.05); patient satisfaction with pain control improved to 54.9%

audits.t: An audit of elective outpatient magnetic resonance imaging in a tertiary South African public-sector hospital
audits.st: 2012 American College of Radiology (ACR) guidelines for appropriate use of MRI

audits.t: Audit of post-operative notes in a Nigerian tertiary hospital: A comparison against the Royal College of Surgeons of England’s Good Surgical Practice Guidelines
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England (RCSE) Good Surgical Practice guidelines (2014)
audits.f: Good compliance (90-100%) with documentation of date, diagnosis, operating surgeon and assistants' names, operative procedure, post-operative instructions, and signature
audits.c: Guideline printed and pasted on operation theatre walls as memory aid; weekly reminder sent via WhatsApp group to resident doctors
audits.r2: No significant improvement in poorly documented items (P>0.05); significant improvement (P<0.001) in filling identification of prostheses used and their serial number

audits.t: Improving Documentation of Vital Signs during Triage in Surgical and Orthopedic Patients: A Clinical Audit from a Rural District Hospital
audits.st: not reported (local standard for complete triage vital sign documentation)
audits.f: Documentation rates: pulse 72%, blood pressure 75.2%, temperature not given at baseline (post-intervention 92%), respiratory rate 40% (least frequent), SpO2 not given at baseline; complete documentation of all 5 vital signs 32%
audits.c: Structured triage checklist, reminder posters, brief staff education
audits.r2: Documentation improved: pulse 96%, blood pressure 97.2%, temperature 92%, respiratory rate 84.8%, SpO2 90% (P<0.001 for all); complete documentation of all 5 vital signs increased to 79.2%

audits.t: Improving the Quality of Total Hip Arthroplasty Operative Notes: A Clinical Audit Study
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England Good Surgical Practice Guidelines (2014 edition), plus 21 additional hip arthroplasty-specific points
audits.f: Good compliance with date documentation (85%), diagnosis (97%), operating surgeon name (95%), assistants' names (89%), procedure description (70%), postoperative instructions (100%), signature (96%), responsible consultant named (93%) and prosthesis serial number (98%); poor compliance with description of other procedures e.g. catheterisation/calf stimulators/foot pumps (67%) and details of suture used (69%)

audits.r2: Memory aid improved compliance for some criteria (some rates rising from 0% to 100%), but some items remained poorly filled in; exact repeat-audit figures not given in the abstract

audits.t: Prescription Audit, Drug Utilization Pattern and Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring in Outpatients of Orthopedics Department of Tertiary Care Teaching Hospital: A Pilot Study
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators and Essential Medicine List of the Government of National Capital Territory, Delhi

audits.t: Audit of the Operation Note of the Orthopaedic Surgery Department of Federal Medical Center Birnin Kudu
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England (RCSE) guidelines for operation notes
audits.f: Mean compliance 47.44%, with significant deficiencies in several key documentation parameters
audits.c: Education and redesign of operation note templates
audits.r2: Mean compliance rose to 94.44%, with notable improvements across all parameters and some criteria rising from 0% to 100%

audits.t: A Single Surgeon’s Experience of Infection Rates in K-Wires in Hand Surgery: Buried vs. Exposed.
audits.tp: K-wire pin track infection rates in hand surgery

audits.t: Audit of orthopedic trauma theatre usage: Observation from Secondary Regional Referral Hospital, Oman
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit about pain management and patient satisfaction in HGH ED
audits.tp: Pain management audit in the emergency department
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Administration of pain-relieving medication was associated with significant pain reduction on disposition; pain was still inadequately treated and pain scoring was not adequately recorded in patient files; trauma-related cases were 22.3% of pain presentations

audits.t: Improving Adherence to WHO Surgical Hand Preparation Guidelines in Elective Operating Theatres of a Teaching Hospital in Gujrat, Pakistan: A Completed Audit Cycle

audits.t: Retrospective audit of prescription of drugs among inpatients of orthopedic wards at Medical College Teaching Hospital, Mandya

audits.f: 12,543 formulations prescribed; 9 (0.07%) unnecessary; 684 (5.45%) irrational fixed dose combinations; highest irrational FDC rate in ENT (8.58%) then pulmonary medicine (8.16%); cough and cold formulations were the most common irrational FDCs (47.51%)

audits.t: Prescription audit in post-operative patients of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital, Bengaluru
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators
audits.f: Female preponderance (54.4%); 77.3% of drugs prescribed under brand name; average 6.25 drugs per prescription; NSAIDs the most common drug group; Cephalosporins the most common antibiotic (77.5%); no irrational antibiotic use found

audits.t: Clinical Audit on Well Baby Services at Primary Health Care Corporation, Qatar

audits.t: Audit of Spinal Deformity Surgery Cases to Improve Future Surgical Outcome – A Retrospective Institution-Based Study
audits.st: Institutional benchmarks predefined through departmental consensus based on contemporary spine literature and institutional performance data
audits.f: Mean hospital stay 7.67±4.50 days (range 1-23); mean blood loss 911.67±383.34 mL; mean operative time 379.03±134.77 minutes; 3 patients (4.2%) had early complications (2 transient neurological deficits, 1 pseudomeningocele); 52 scoliosis, 10 kyphosis, 10 kyphoscoliosis surgeries

audits.t: Documentation for Orthopaedic Surgery: An Audit to Ensure Compliance with the Most Recent Guidelines
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons (RCS) guidelines for surgical documentation

audits.t: Audit of Computed Tomography (Brain) Referrals from the Accident and Emergency Department in a Tertiary Care Hospital

audits.t: Reducing Surgical Site Infections in Fractured Neck of Femur Patients: A Closed Loop Audit and Literature Review

audits.st: not reported

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Intensive Care Unit- Comparative Audit

audits.t: Acute pancreatitis at the Aga Khan University Hospital, Nairobi: a two year audit
audits.st: Published evidence-based international guidelines for management of acute pancreatitis (diagnostic modalities, severity stratification, critical care management, treatment timing)
audits.f: 26 (74%) male; median age 46 years; aetiology alcohol 51%, gallstones 11%, other 9%, idiopathic 29%; median length of stay 11 days; formal severity stratification (Ranson's score) done in only 3 (8%); 8 (23%) had severe disease; 27 mild-disease patients also had abdominal CT (unnecessary); only 54% had an initial ultrasound to exclude gallstones; 10 mild-disease patients received unnecessary prophylactic antibiotics for a median of 7 days; carbapenem-based antibiotics given to 4 severe cases; early nasojejunal feeding in 6 severe cases; overall mortality 2.9%, mortality in severe subgroup 12.5%

audits.t: OPTIMAL MEDICAL THERAPY IN CHRONIC HEART FAILURE – AN AUDIT
audits.tp: Optimal medical therapy use in chronic heart failure
audits.st: ACCF/AHA and ESC guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of heart failure
audits.f: Only 4.3% of patients on beta blockers; 64.3% not on any beta blocker; 55.7% not on ACE inhibitors

audits.t: Errors in Prescription Writing: An Audit of General Practitioners
audits.st: Standard components of a correctly written prescription (superscription, inscription, subscription, transcription, signature, refill information)
audits.f: 473 total errors identified across 100 prescriptions: 303 in superscription, 6 in inscription, 67 in subscription, 34 in transcription, 1 in prescriber's signature, and 62 in refill information

audits.t: Audit of unbooked post- Anaesthesia admissions to intensive care unit in Enugu, Nigeria
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 150 post-operative ICU admissions (from 3000 operations), 9 (6%) were unbooked; of these, 6 (67%) were considered predictable and 4 (44%) had preventable features

audits.t: Audit of Nursing Handover in Emam Reza & Madani Hospitals in Tabriz by FOCUS PDCA Method
audits.st: Self-made researcher checklist of nursing handover standards
audits.f: Before intervention, average compliance with handover standards was 29.3% and delivery took 12 minutes
audits.c: Intervention in ENT ward (training on handover) after FOCUS PDCA method
audits.r2: Compliance and duration increased from 22% and 12 minutes to 63% and 19 minutes in ENT ward after intervention

audits.t: Audit nursing reports in intubated neonates admitted in neonatal intensive care unit of Ayatollah Rouhani Hospital, Babol, Iran
audits.tp: Nursing documentation quality in intubated neonates
audits.st: Researcher-developed checklist based on national and international nursing documentation standards
audits.f: Quality of nursing records was good in 93%, moderate in 1%, poor in 6%

audits.t: Clinical Audit Of Blood Requisition And Transfusion Practices In Obgyn Surgeries In A Secondary Care Setting
audits.tp: Blood cross-match transfusion ratio in Ob/Gyn surgery
audits.st: JCIA quality criteria: Cross-match Transfusion ratio of 2:1
audits.f: Over-ordering of cross-matched blood resulted in a high cross-match transfusion (CT) ratio
audits.c: Use of group-and-screen instead of routine cross-matching; listing major indications for cross-matching; preoperative and antenatal anaemia correction; ensuring O-negative blood availability; staff and doctor education
audits.r2: Number of units cross-matched fell, moving toward group-and-save, with significant improvement in CT ratio

audits.t: An Insight into the Antibiotic Prescription Practices of Post-Graduate Dentists, Discerned through a Clinical Dental Audit
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing practice by postgraduate dentists
audits.st: Evidence-based antibiotic prescribing guidelines
audits.f: Amoxicillin 53.5% and metronidazole 46.3% most commonly prescribed; tetracycline prescribed in 17.5%

audits.t: Facility-Based Treatment of Under Five Diarrhoea in Cross River State: A Clinical Audit
audits.st: World Health Organization (WHO) recommended cost-effective, evidence-based interventions for diarrhoea case management
audits.f: Prescription for diarrhoea was appropriate in 10.8% (40), inappropriate in 62.4% (231), wrong in 22.2% (82), and none in 4.6% (17)

audits.t: Audit of records of consultations of nursing in gynecology
audits.st: Checklist of expected identification, socio-demographic and gynaecological record data
audits.f: 52% of identification data records incomplete, 35% complete, 13% partially incomplete; family history and personal antecedents least valued items

audits.t: The use of the practice walk test in pulmonary rehabilitation program: National COPD Audit Pulmonary Rehabilitation Workstream
audits.tp: Practice walk test use in pulmonary rehabilitation
audits.st: National COPD Pulmonary Rehabilitation audit standard/expectation of practice walk test use
audits.f: Only 1666 (22.6%) patients had a baseline practice walk test; practice-test group enrolled 2.2 times more and completed 17% more often, and walked further (ISWD 17.9 m, 6MWD 34.8 m) than the no-practice-test group

audits.t: Use of oxytocin during Caesarean section at Princess Marina Hospital, Botswana: An audit of clinical practice
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 20 IU infusion was commonest dose (31.7%); 10 IU intravenous bolus used in 12.9%; further doses used in 57 patients (41%); use of oxytocin did not follow recommended practice

audits.t: Clinical audit of medical care quality by computer informational analytical system in patients with hypertension followed in Saratov polyclinic
audits.tp: Compliance with hypertension diagnosis, treatment and follow-up recommendations
audits.st: Clinical recommendations on diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of hypertensive patients (2007-2008 guidelines)
audits.f: No correspondence found between recommendation statements and actual diagnostic/treatment/follow-up practice; target BP not achieved in 85% of patients

audits.t: An Audit of Nursing Care and Placement of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter in Infants
audits.tp: Nursing care and PICC placement in infants
audits.st: Researcher-made checklist based on standard nursing care for PICC insertion
audits.f: Compliance before insertion 97.43%, hand washing 100%, during procedure 87.14%, after insertion 94.84%; glasses not used in 85.4% and ultrasound guidance not used in 90% of insertions

audits.t: Improvement of Hypothermia Control and Management Methods in Term ‎Newborns after Training on Neonatal Hypothermia with the Help of Clinical ‎Audit
audits.st: Standards of care for prevention of neonatal hypothermia
audits.f: Mean nursing care scores before training: delivery rooms 8.4±1.4/13, operating rooms 5.9±1.8/11, NICUs 8.0±1.5/14; overall 4.6±1.1/10; mild hypothermia prevalence 38.1% (operating) and 21.5% (delivery) before training
audits.c: In-service training for nurses (speech, educational posters, leaflets, slides) on neonatal hypothermia care
audits.r2: Mean scores after training: delivery rooms 11.1±0.7, operating rooms 7.3±0.8, NICUs 9.8±2.0 (p=0.0001); overall 7.0±1.4/10; hypothermia prevalence reduced

audits.t: Clinical Profile and Discharge Criteria Compliance of Hospitalized Dengue Patients in Pakistan: An Audit-Based Cohort Study
audits.st: Standardised seven discharge criteria for dengue patients
audits.f: Discharge criteria fully met in 81.5% of patients; most commonly unmet criterion was rising platelet trend (11.5%), followed by absence of fever without antipyretics (3.8%)

audits.t: Audit Klinik Penggunaan Terapi Anti Platelet dan Luaran Klinik untuk Stroke Iskemik di RS Bethesda Yogyakarta
audits.tp: Antiplatelet therapy use in ischaemic stroke
audits.st: Current clinical practice guidelines for antiplatelet therapy in ischaemic stroke
audits.f: Mortality rate 6.03%; standard for antiplatelet therapy in all ischaemic stroke patients not achieved; only 10 cases had no justification for non-prescription

audits.t: Correlation of Ordered Cervical Spine X-rays in Emergency Department with NEXUS and Canadian C-Spine Rules; a Clinical Audit
audits.tp: Cervical spine X-ray ordering against clinical decision rules
audits.st: NEXUS and Canadian C-Spine clinical decision rules for ordering cervical spine imaging
audits.f: Accuracy of X-ray orders based on standard decision rules was 100/156 (64.1%) before training
audits.c: Educational training for physicians on NEXUS and Canadian C-Spine rules
audits.r2: Accuracy of X-ray orders increased to 143/156 (91.7%) after training (p<0.001)

audits.t: Understanding barriers to diabetes eye screening in a large rural general practice: an audit of patients not reached by screening services
audits.tp: Barriers to diabetes eye screening uptake
audits.st: Diabetes eye screening service attendance expectation (local screening programme)
audits.f: 154 of 571 (27%) missed at least one screening appointment; Māori patients had 20% higher missed appointments than European patients

audits.t: La atención hospitalaria al paciente con ictus en Cataluña: Resultados del «Primer Audit Clínic de l'Ictus. Catalunya, 2005/2006» In-hospital stroke care in Catalonia [Spain]: Results of the «First Clinical Audit of Stroke. Catalonia, 2005/2006»
audits.st: Stroke clinical practice guideline (GPC) recommendations, Catalonia
audits.f: Compliance: quality of medical records 78.5% (77.5-79.4); basic care standards 92.4%; neurological assessment 38.3%; rehabilitation assessment 44.9%; complication prevention/management 68.4%; initial preventive measures 78.9%

audits.t: EXERCISE ON PRESCRIPTION AUDIT : A TOOL FOR PHARMACOLOGY PRACTICAL LESSON
audits.tp: Prescription audit as pharmacology teaching tool
audits.st: WHO Guide to Good Prescribing and Essential Medicines list; standard prescription-writing format
audits.f: Completeness 100% for most indicators except judicious investigations (99.89%), medication information (89.32%), relevant advice (97.12%); generic prescription 54.05%
audits.c: Self-directed learning exercise where undergraduate students performed the prescription audit
audits.r2: Students improved markedly (p<0.001) in auditing real prescriptions after the exercise

audits.t: Audits of emergency trolleys’ contents in selected hospitals in Botswana
audits.st: Standardised checklist of expected emergency trolley equipment and drugs for CPR
audits.f: No ward/unit had all expected equipment or drugs; some units failed to check trolley contents daily

audits.t: Cataract Surgery Redesign: Meeting Increasing Demand, Training, Audit and Patient-Centered Care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Redesign of cataract surgery service delivery to meet increasing demand, including changes to list mix and outsourcing arrangements.

audits.t: Audit of Gastric Cancer Pathology Reports in Yazd
audits.st: Nationwide guideline, version 1.0 (Netherlands) minimum data set for gastric cancer pathology reports (histologic type, grade, T stage, N stage, margin distance, tumour size and location, perineural/lymphatic/vascular invasion)
audits.f: None of the reports were adequate. Tumour subtype not reported in 80.4%, grade in 16.1%, T stage in 8.9%, N stage in 26.8%, margin in 57.1%, tumour size in 10.7%, location in 41.1%.

audits.t: Should general surgeons treat gastric carcinoma? An audit of practice and results, 1980–1985
audits.tp: Gastric carcinoma treatment outcomes and variation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 150 operated; 87 gastrectomies (31 potentially curative); 92 stage IV, 34 stage IIIB, 42 earlier stage; anastomotic leakage in 16 (18%) after gastrectomy, 14 deaths (16%); 5-year survival 5% overall, 11% after gastrectomy, 32% after curative resection; rates varied considerably between surgeons.

audits.t: An audit of the use of antipsychotics in a geriatric psychiatry continuing care unit in Scotland
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 37.5% of the population were receiving regular antipsychotic medication; antidepressants rarely used, only one case of missed depression.
audits.c: Changes following the audit are described (specific change not stated) and recommendations for improved monitoring of medication use made.

audits.t: Antipsychotic drugs in continuing care: A 2‐year follow‐up audit
audits.st: Comparison with own unit's prescribing practice from 1990
audits.f: 37.5% of population on regular antipsychotics (RA); 46% on no psychotropic medication (NM).
audits.c: Increased use of high-potency antipsychotic preparations, given in low dosage, mainly to patients who had responded inadequately to low-potency preparations.
audits.r2: 31.5% of population on RA; 53% on NM; severity of behaviour problems in the RA group had fallen considerably compared with 1990.

audits.t: Audit of Ticarcillan/Clavulanate Usage in a Large Teaching Hospital
audits.st: Ticarcillin/clavulanate prescribing guidelines
audits.f: 65% compliant with guidelines; treatment considered appropriate in 76% of patients; non-compliant/inappropriate use most common in community-acquired pneumonia.

audits.t: Audit of Nausea and Vomiting Management in Palliative Care Hospital Patients
audits.st: Best practice guidelines for antiemetic prescribing
audits.f: 19 patients presented with uncontrolled nausea/vomiting; antiemetic prescribed for 43 (61%) patients; 5-HT3 antagonists prescribed per best practice in only one-quarter of cases; regular antiemetics gave better symptom control than prn dosing.

audits.t: Audit of the Use of a Smart Infusion Pump's Drug Libraries
audits.tp: Smart infusion pump drug library compliance
audits.st: Compliance with use of the smart infusion pump's drug libraries
audits.f: 86% (95% CI 83-89) of infusions administered via a drug library; 11% (95% CI 9.1-14) of these were programmed incorrectly.

audits.t: Don't rush to crush: audit of modification to oral medicines for patients with swallowing difficulties
audits.tp: Oral medicine modification for swallowing difficulties
audits.st: Don't Rush to Crush (DRTC) Handbook guidelines for modifying oral medicines
audits.f: 45% (37/82) of medications prepared safely; 33% (27/82) prepared according to optimal method; 52% (43/82) of modified medications were strained prior to administration.
audits.c: Nursing education strategies focused on medication modification for patients with fine-bore nasogastric tubes, developed with senior nursing staff.
audits.r2: 91% (68/75) of medications prepared safely; 60% (45/75) prepared according to optimal method; straining of medications eliminated.

audits.t: Audit of inpatient and outpatient paliperidone palmitate injection prescribing practices
audits.st: Major Australian medication references' recommendations on paliperidone palmitate dosing interval
audits.f: 25/29 patients received recommended initiation regimen; 16% of first monthly doses were the recommended 75 mg strength; 60% of maintenance doses given ≤28 days after previous dose; 78% of patients studied ≥1 year received at least 13 doses in 1 year rather than 12.

audits.t: Applying the National Inpatient Medication Chart audit to electronic medication management systems: what does it tell us?
audits.st: Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care (ACSQHC) National Inpatient Medication Chart (NIMC) audit tools (2012 version)
audits.f: eMMS charts exhibited higher compliance with audit criteria than NIMCs, except for documentation of indication for medication; both hospitals exceeded national averages on many parameters except documentation of weight and indication.

audits.t: An audit of medicines information quality in electronically generated discharge summaries – evidence to meet the Australian National Safety and Quality Health Service Standards
audits.st: NSW indicator 5.3, 'Percentage of discharge summaries that include medication therapy changes and explanations for changes' (National quality use of medicines indicators for Australian Hospitals, ACSQHC 2014), adapted
audits.f: 75% had electronic discharge summary (EDS) completed, 46% within recommended 48h; primary care provider nominated in 53% of sample; accuracy of post-discharge medicines information was 46%, mostly omissions; none of the EDSs documented reasons for medicine changes; 71% of short-term therapy patients had a documented community completion plan.
audits.c: An educational program has commenced to improve data entry of the patient's primary care provider on admission, and plans to improve compliance with the EDS policy.

audits.t: Assessment of the appropriateness of meningitis management and drug utilisation: a prospective audit for implementing an antimicrobial stewardship program
audits.st: Infectious Diseases Society of America guidelines for meningitis management; World Health Organization drug use evaluation guidelines (90-100% appropriateness threshold)
audits.f: Non-compliance with standard practice guidelines due to wrong regimen selection in more than 60% of patients; fewer than 10% received correct dexamethasone regimen; fewer than 20% had follow-up lumbar puncture; non-compliance resulted in extra charges for more than 70% of patients.

audits.t: Enoxaparin for thromboprophylaxis in overweight and obese patients: a prescribing audit at a tertiary hospital
audits.tp: VTE prophylaxis dosing in obese patients
audits.st: Reference dose for non-obese patients of enoxaparin 40 mg daily; appropriate dose-adjustment for obese patients (BMI ≥30 kg/m2)
audits.f: 92 (27%) obese and 108 (32%) overweight; of 141 normal BMI patients, 127 (90%) received appropriate doses; only 2 obese patients received adjusted enoxaparin doses (60 mg daily for 6 days, and 40 mg twice daily before titration).

audits.t: Audit of medication allergy referrals to an allergy outpatient service at a tertiary hospital
audits.st: Australasian Society for Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA) medication allergy referral template
audits.f: Overall poor level of adherence to all criteria (44.7%); GP referrals generally more detailed than internal referrals.

audits.t: A Quality Assurance Audit for an Aseptic Dispensing Facility
audits.st: UK quality assurance guidelines for aseptic preparation services, adapted against New South Wales and Australian standards
audits.f: An internal audit was performed and highlighted some areas for improvement.
audits.r2: External audits are planned (not yet reported).

audits.t: Audit of Celecoxib and Rofecoxib Use: St Vincent's Public Hospital, Darlinghurst
audits.st: St Vincent's Hospital (SVH) Formulary Guidelines and 'good clinical practice' as defined from the literature
audits.f: 79% (37/47) of patients continuing COX-2 inhibitor therapy were in accordance with current SVH guidelines; 46% were treated in accordance with 'good clinical practice' when precautions for hypertension, renal impairment and gastrointestinal safety were also considered.

audits.t: Oregon audit finds its MH system is failing children, staff
audits.st: Oregon Secretary of State Audits Division performance and workforce standards
audits.f: Audit found chronic workforce shortage, lack of performance measurements, high staff turnover, and inadequate training for staff managing high-risk children.

audits.t: Diabetic foot infections: an audit of antibiotic prescribing in a diabetic foot clinic
audits.st: Appropriateness of antibiotic prescribing against infected wound status per University of Texas Wound Classification System (UTWCS)
audits.f: 55 wounds (65%) were infected; antibiotics prescribed for 51 of 55 infected wounds (93%); 4 infected wounds not given antibiotics; 4 patients (7%) with infected ulcers required IV antibiotic admission; 3 of 52 swabbed wounds (6%) grew MRSA; 30 uninfected wounds (35%) received no antibiotics.
audits.c: As a result of the audit, a simple antibiotic protocol was devised to improve management of infected diabetic wounds.

audits.t: Reassessment of a hospital diabetes clinic after audit
audits.st: Minimum standards set: annual recording of HbA1c, blood pressure and fundoscopy; appropriate use of specialists (dietitians, health visitors, nephrologists)
audits.f: A previous audit had identified deficiencies in the care provided by the clinic.
audits.c: Simple changes in the organisation of the clinic were made, as extra doctors/resources were not available, with minimum standards set for annual monitoring and specialist referral.
audits.r2: Activity in the clinic improved in most of the categories observed on repeat audit; the proportion of patients who had undergone recent fundoscopy remained unsatisfactory.

audits.t: Diabetes audit from 1987 to 1993 carried out in a general practice clinic
audits.tp: Diabetes glycaemic control in general practice
audits.st: 'Acceptable' HbA1c control as defined by the practice (target level not stated)
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Some improvement in levels of control by 1993, with 75% of diabetic patients achieving 'acceptable' control; proportion diagnosed with diabetes within the practice increased from 1.1% to 1.6%.

audits.t: An audit of diabetes care in three district general hospitals in Cardiff
audits.st: A modification of guidelines recommended by the British Diabetic Association
audits.f: 8.4% of inpatients had diabetes; mean duration of stay 16 days; no foot examination record in 56%, no peripheral pulse record in 54%; no fundoscopy record in 66%; visual acuity not measured in 85%; glycated haemoglobin measured in <40%; blood lipids not measured in ~75%; half had not seen a dietitian; only 44% had a specific follow-up plan recorded.

audits.t: Audit of referrals for dietary advice from the diabetes clinic at Bedford Hospital
audits.st: Local standard: 100% of newly diagnosed diabetes patients to receive dietitian advice within a year of diagnosis, and annually thereafter
audits.f: 66% (121 patients) had seen a dietitian within one year of diagnosis; 19% (35 patients) had a dietetic update in the last 18 months; a proportion had never seen a state registered dietitian.

audits.t: An audit of amputations in a rural health district. Consultant Physician responsible for a district‐wide diabetes service
audits.st: Local guidelines for management of diabetic patients at risk of amputation
audits.f: Considerable potential for improvements in clinical practice in both primary and secondary care, which might reduce amputation rates.

audits.t: An audit of a comprehensive screening programme for diabetes in pregnancy
audits.st: WHO criteria for diagnosis of gestational diabetes via 75g OGTT; comprehensive screening protocol for antenatal care
audits.f: 67 women (1.7%) found to have gestational diabetes; 43 identified via screening protocol, 24 via OGTTs on clinical grounds; 52 (78%) referred to combined diabetes-antenatal clinic; only 8 (12%) received insulin; 35 (52%) returned for postnatal OGTT, of which 4 were abnormal.

audits.t: ‘Mild’ diabetic retinopathy—A fatal disease. Audit of eye screening and five year outcome of 203 people with diabetes: Part 1. Eye screening
audits.st: Screening interval standard: examination within 12 months of preceding visit
audits.f: 56 (28%) had retinopathy (10 hypertensive, 46 diabetic changes); 26 referrals from DR group led to laser therapy in 17; only 41% had every examination within 12 months, rising to 74% within 15 months and 87% within 18 months; failure to attend affected 51 (25%) patients.
audits.r2: In a randomly selected separate subgroup, annual screening frequency over 5 years had risen to 82%.

audits.t: A countywide primary care annual audit fails to demonstrate an improvement in diabetes care between 1996 and 2001
audits.tp: Diabetes annual review and complication screening
audits.st: Annual diabetes review including foot and eye screening, blood pressure, creatinine and HbA1c measurement

audits.t: Audit of time taken to heal diabetic foot ulcers
audits.st: Local standard: 80% of diabetic foot ulcers to be healed within six months of referral to the podiatry team
audits.f: 85% of diabetic foot ulcers healed within six months, exceeding the 80% standard; average healing time eight weeks.

audits.t: Audit of young people with type 1 diabetes transferring from paediatric to adult diabetic services
audits.tp: Paediatric to adult diabetes transition attendance
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Six patients supposed to transfer were not seen over the two-year follow-up; only six attended all scheduled appointments; attendance rated good in 36%, moderate in 33%, poor in 30%.

audits.t: Audit of staff knowledge of the correct management of hypoglycaemia in a busy teaching hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean questionnaire score 65.6% in area A (with diabetes education/specialist nurse input) vs 45% in area B (without); 33% of area A nursing staff had attended a diabetes education session in the last year, with mean score 86.7% for attendees vs 62.8% for non-attendees.

audits.t: Audit of GP practice records of patients prescribed clozapine
audits.st: GP practice registration on the severe mental illness register and documented record of clozapine treatment
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An audit of younger patient referrals to a memory clinic
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Confusion‐inducing drugs in a memory assessment service: an audit
audits.tp: Confusion-inducing drug review in dementia assessment
audits.st: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidance on the assessment and diagnosis of dementia
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Screening for depression in patients with cognitive impairment: a local audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of ophthalmological examination in psychiatry
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: A survey found psychiatrists felt ophthalmological examination was important for patient care; initial audit of practice preceded training.
audits.c: Training for psychiatrists on the importance of ophthalmological examination.
audits.r2: Further audit showed training improved the percentage of patients given ophthalmological examinations.

audits.t: Summary of the National Diabetes Audit 2015–16 report
audits.tp: National Diabetes Audit care processes and targets
audits.st: National Diabetes Audit care processes and treatment targets
audits.f: Some progress in NHS diabetes care but large variation across England and Wales.

audits.t: Findings of the National Diabetes Inpatient Audit 2016
audits.st: National Diabetes Inpatient Audit standards for quality of diabetes care in hospital
audits.f: Many areas identified with room for improvement in inpatient diabetes care, but inpatients remained mainly positive about their overall care.

audits.t: An audit of antibiotic resistance in urinary tract infection
audits.tp: Antibiotic resistance in urinary tract infection
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: High rate of local resistance to first-line trimethoprim use in urinary tract infection, based on MSU sample audit.

audits.t: Causes of death in stillbirth and quality of care—an example of a local audit
audits.tp: Stillbirth cause of death classification and substandard care review
audits.st: The Stockholm classification of stillbirth; local multidisciplinary audit group review for substandard care factors
audits.f: Cause of death determined in 91% (95% CI 81.02-95.63); leading cause IUGR/placental insufficiency (45%, 95% CI 33.73-57.43), infection (13%), placental abruption (9%); substandard care factors identified in 49% (95% CI 37.06-61.4), probably associated with cause of death in only 10%.

audits.t: An audit of inter‐hospital transfers of children with abdominal pain and their associated medical imaging findings
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean age 6 years 1 month, 66.3% boys, mean transfer distance 55.4km; suspected diagnoses: acute appendicitis 63.9%, intussusception 20.3%, hypertrophic pyloric stenosis 14.5%; false positive rates: pyloric stenosis 52.0%, appendicitis 50.9%, ileo-colic intussusception 74.3%.

audits.t: The sonographer's use of spectral Doppler in the common femoral vein for the assessment of iliac vein obstructions: A retrospective audit
audits.tp: Spectral Doppler technique for iliac vein obstruction
audits.st: Correct technique for taking and interpreting spectral waveforms at the common femoral vein
audits.f: Only 277 (74%) patients had spectral traces taken at the CFV; 29 (10%) had persistent monophasic waveforms not changing significantly with Valsalva; 8 (2%) had confirmed iliofemoral vein obstruction.

audits.t: Major trauma audit: Metrics for improving care
audits.st: Trauma Audit & Research Network (TARN) national trauma audit data quality, evidence-based measures and system indicators (Major Trauma Dashboard)
audits.f: 13,260 (35.4%) had ISS >15, 17,414 (46.6%) had ISS 9-15; median age 56.2 years; blunt trauma 96.9%, penetrating 3.1%; stepwise improvements in data quality; reduction in time to CT for head trauma; increases in consultant-led trauma teams; improved speed of secondary transfer referral.
audits.c: Implementation of regional Major Trauma Networks with financial incentives and mandatory audit submission (system went live April 2012).
audits.r2: 5-year trend for odds of survival (adjusted for age, gender, ISS, GCS) showed an increase, but not yet statistically significant.

audits.t: Posterior capsule rupture as a performance indicator in resident cataract surgery: An eight-year audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall posterior capsule rupture (PCR) rate 3.5%; higher in junior vs senior trainees (6.5% vs 2.7%; RR=0.42, P<0.001); senior residents adjusted RR=0.38 (95% CI 0.27-0.53); complex cases adjusted RR=4.15 (95% CI 2.98-5.73); 91.7% achieved BCVA ≥20/40; 91.4% within ±1D of refractive target.

audits.t: DIAGNOSTIC STEWARDSHIP: CLINICAL AUDIT OF BLOOD CULTURE REQUESTS MANAGED BY CLINICAL PHARMACY
audits.st: Institutional clinical decision flowchart for blood culture collection justification, developed by a multidisciplinary technical group
audits.f: 56.3% noncompliance (routine or admission requests without justification); historical monthly consumption averaged 938 blood culture collections.
audits.c: Multidisciplinary technical group created a clinical decision flowchart, provided pharmacist-led training, and performed prospective real-time audit and feedback on blood culture requests, withholding unjustified requests.
audits.r2: 410 collections performed (-56.8% vs baseline); of 309 audited requests, 188 (45.9%) cancelled and 121 (29.5%) approved; no cases of sepsis, shock or death related to denied requests at 48h follow-up, and no decrease in bloodstream infection diagnoses.

audits.t: Implementation of Day-1 Antibiotic Audit: Experience from a Philanthropic Hospital
audits.st: Institutional empirical antibiotic protocol reviewed within the first 24 hours of prescription
audits.f: 28% of audited antibiotic prescriptions required interventions (discontinuation, de-escalation/escalation, or route modification); the remainder complied with the institutional empirical antibiotic protocol; total cost savings of BRL 214,086.65 in the first semester.
audits.c: Implementation of a 'Day-1 antibiotic audit', with a daily pharmacist report of antibiotics in their first day of administration reviewed by infectious disease physicians.

audits.t: AUDIT ANALYSIS OF ANTIMICROBIAL PREPARATION AND ADMINISTRATION IN A TERTIARY HOSPITAL
audits.st: Institutional protocol for good practices in antimicrobial preparation and administration
audits.f: 17.65% of locations not clean/organised; 26.39% lacked a labelled alcohol bottle; 37.48% had an IV saline bottle with attached needle used as diluent; 55.29% of diluted antimicrobials stored in refrigerator (multi-dose), 53.27% of these in the refrigerator door; only 50.41% connected to a reservoir set; 91.42% administered at prescribed time; in 13%, 20mL was not infused after burette completion; 42.18% checked before scheduled time.

audits.t: AUDIT OF ADHERENCE TO PREVENTION MEASURES FOR NON–VENTILATOR-ASSOCIATED PNEUMONIA IN A TERTIARY HOSPITAL
audits.st: Institutional prevention measures for non-ventilator-associated pneumonia (head-of-bed elevation 30-45°, oral hygiene three times daily, respiratory physiotherapy, early ambulation, postoperative analgesia, protected nebulizer/bag-valve-mask)
audits.f: Head-of-bed elevation 30-45° present in 81.6%; oral hygiene three times daily not performed in 56.2%; respiratory physiotherapy not performed in 31.3% (40.9% not applicable); early ambulation in only 38.5%; postoperative analgesia not provided in 69.8%; nebulizer mask/bag-valve-mask protected in 47.4%.

audits.t: Closing the clinical gap: an audit of clinical compliance for early-onset neonatal sepsis management
audits.st: NICE quality standard QS75 for neonatal sepsis management
audits.f: Incidence of confirmed/suspected EONS 9.2% of 605 births; intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis (IAP) compliance 81.81% (18/22); 89.29% (50/56) received antibiotics within 1 hour; 36-h decision documented in 82.14% (46/56); verbal information given to 92.86% (52/56) of parents; written information given to 0%.

audits.t: Evaluating compliance with proper application of compression stockings in surgical patients: a clinical audit
audits.st: NICE guidelines and local Trust protocols on correct application, monitoring and patient education for anti-embolism compression stockings
audits.f: 60% of patients had incorrectly applied stockings; 88% did not have limb measured before issue; 69% reported not receiving information on reason for stockings; 100% received no written information; 25% of 25 surveyed nurses lacked confidence in correct sizing/fitting; 74% of patients wanted information leaflets/reminders; 80% of staff wanted refresher training.

audits.t: Introducing an abdominal paracentesis procedure box in the acute gastroenterology ward environment: a quality improvement and audit project
audits.st: Local Safety Standards for Invasive Procedures (LocSSIP) documentation
audits.f: 70% of procedures performed in the afternoon, contributing to discharge delays in two cases; pre-insertion LocSSIP completed in 73% of cases, post-insertion LocSSIP in only 27%; average time to gather equipment was 14 min 57 s.
audits.c: Introduction of a standardised abdominal paracentesis procedure box with equipment and a checklist on both acute gastroenterology wards, plus paracentesis training incorporated into resident induction and monthly simulated teaching sessions.
audits.r2: Average time to collect equipment reduced to 2 min 9 s; 100% of respondents reported increased confidence in locating equipment; procedures performed earlier in the day.

audits.t: Audit sur le bon usage du citalopram
audits.st: ANSM (French Health Products Safety Agency) recommendations on citalopram torsadogenic risk
audits.f: 54.9% of pharmaceutical interventions applied by the practitioner (citalopram substituted by paroxetine in three-quarters of these); 35.3% not followed; 9.8% not applicable. Of patients with interventions followed, 53.5% had discharge letters explaining reassessment to GPs, 17.9% had discharge letters without mention of reassessment, 28.6% had no discharge letter. 9 of 15 patients with complete discharge letters were re-hospitalised within the year without contraindication in admission treatment; 3 of 5 without reassessment mention were re-hospitalised with persistent contraindication.

audits.t: Audit of general practitioner referrals for erectile dysfunction within north central london
audits.st: North Central London Erectile Dysfunction Referral Pathway (EDRP): detailed patient history, specific blood tests, psychological support offer and medical treatment attempts before referral
audits.f: History completeness varied widely (e.g. Peyronie's disease documented n=72, sexual history n=47, medications n=40, BMI n=29); blood tests incomplete (testosterone n=26, TFTs n=26, HbA1c/fasting glucose n=37, lipid profile n=37); treatments trialled: sildenafil n=36, tadalafil n=17, both n=10, neither/unclear n=11.

audits.t: Audit on continuity of care and follow-up duration in interstitial lung diseases outpatient clinics
audits.tp: Continuity of care in outpatient follow-up
audits.st: Recommendations for continuity of care (same physician follow-up) and recommended follow-up interval standards
audits.f: 57% of patients were seen by the same physician in follow-up; average follow-up duration 3-6 months, up to 9 months in non-urgent cases, aligning with clinical guidelines; 70% followed up without delay.

audits.t: Clinical audit /QIP report: rhythm checks for patients admitted to the Hyper Acute Stroke Unit (HASU)
audits.tp: Cardiac rhythm monitoring in acute stroke
audits.st: Rhythm-monitoring protocol for HASU patients using continuous telemetry, aligned with national AF detection guidelines
audits.f: 100% of patients underwent 72-h telemetry monitoring; 32.7% had AF (18.1% pre-existing, 14.5% newly diagnosed, of which 75% detected after >24 hours); only 25% had complete documentation of rhythm monitoring outcomes, 7.2% had no ECG documentation.

audits.t: Quality of initial medical certificates in a Tunisian traumatology unit: A five-year retrospective audit
audits.st: Haute Autorité de Santé (HAS) recommendations, assessed via a 12-item checklist for initial medical certificates (CMI)
audits.f: Certificate issuance date and ITT duration documentation both 100% compliant; handwriting difficult to decipher in 22.9% (95% CI 14.7-33.2%); non-standard abbreviations in 31.0% (95% CI 21.7-41.8%); adequate anatomical injury description in 72.4% (95% CI 62.0-81.3%); ITT duration disproportionate to injuries in 11.5%; overall compliance 73.6% (95% CI 63.1-82.5%); 73.9% of non-compliant certificates had at least two concurrent deficiencies.

audits.t: Audit Of The Prevalence Of Malnutrition Using The Modified Subjective Global Assessment Tool In Maintenance Peritoneal Dialysis Patients In The Top End Renal Service Of The Nortehrn Territory Australia
audits.tp: Malnutrition prevalence in peritoneal dialysis patients
audits.st: Modified Subjective Global Assessment (SGA) tool for malnutrition classification
audits.f: 76% of MPD patients had some degree of malnutrition (SGA category B or C)
