audits.c: Implementation of free oral nutrition supplements to MPD patients and development of service-wide culturally appropriate education resources.
audits.r2: Malnutrition (SGA B or C) detected in 10% of PD patients

audits.t: Clinical audit of a Paediatric Emergency Warning Score (PEWS) in the paediatric oncology unit of a newly established tertiary cancer institute
audits.st: Paediatric Emergency Warning Score (PEWS) implementation and scoring accuracy, with target of 100% compliance in scoring
audits.f: Before PEWS: 14/234 admissions required PICU transfer; 10 (4.2%) planned, 4 (1.7%) unplanned
audits.c: Introduction of a numbers-based Paediatric Emergency Warning Score (PEWS) for all paediatric oncology inpatients, with audit of nursing scoring accuracy.
audits.r2: After PEWS: 28/727 admitted for intensive care; only 1 (0.14%) unplanned admission; unplanned admissions decreased from 1.7% to 0.14% (p<0.01); 100% compliance in PEWS scoring achieved

audits.t: Completed Audit of Physical Health Status of Patients with Severe Mental Illness in a Medium Secure Forensic Psychiatric Rehab Ward
audits.st: National guidelines for physical health monitoring of patients on anti-psychotic medication
audits.f: Lack of recording of physical health status identified before introduction of monitoring sheet
audits.c: Introduction of a physical health monitoring sheet in patient notes.
audits.r2: 100% physical health monitoring achieved; improvements in weight, cardiovascular risk, and total/HDL cholesterol ratio noted; 4 cases of significant QT prolongation and 3 cases of prolactin elevation detected due to monitoring

audits.t: Consent to Treatment, Second Opinion Appointed Doctors and Code Compliance - an Audit?
audits.tp: Consent to treatment documentation (Mental Health Act)
audits.st: Mental Health Act 1983 Code of Practice, section 58 documentation requirements (forms 38 and 39)
audits.f: Form 38: 100% completion of names, dosage, route, ECT numbers, but only 60% completion of treatment plan explanation/clozapine documentation; Form 39: 100% completed correctly with SOAD recommendation in 85% of cases, but no SOAD documentation in case notes and only phone contact with RMO; only 28% of cases had RMO documentation of SOAD visit and outcome

audits.t: P01-353 - Use of Antipsychotic Medication in Older People with Dementia. An Inpatient Dementia Ward Audit
audits.st: NICE guidelines on antipsychotic prescribing for behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia
audits.f: Prescription of antipsychotics was appropriate and all patients had target symptoms recorded; however documentation of risk-benefit analysis and discussion with patient/family about risks and side effects was lacking

audits.t: P02-46 - Audit on Ward Review Meeting
audits.tp: Ward review meeting quality and person-centred planning
audits.st: Proposed local standards for ward review meetings benchmarking the recovery model and person-centred planning
audits.f: Findings showed satisfaction with the ward meeting process, but participants identified issues that could be improved

audits.t: P02-79 - Community Forensic Mental Health Service, Hertfordshire- Referrals and Response Audit
audits.tp: Community forensic mental health service referral appropriateness
audits.st: Guidelines set by NICE, DoH, FR&D, Sainsbury Centre and principles from the Reed Report
audits.f: Results indicated number of referrals and quality of response from the team; service gaps identified

audits.t: P02-115 - Audit of Discussion About Contraception and the Risks of Pregnancy with Female Service Users
audits.tp: Contraception and pregnancy risk discussion documentation
audits.st: NICE guideline CG45 (Antenatal and Postnatal Mental Health) on discussing contraception and risks of pregnancy with women of child-bearing potential on psychotropic medication
audits.f: 12 (24%) patients aware of contraception; 17 (34%) knew about risks of relapse during pregnancy; 15 (30%) recognised risks of stopping/changing medication; 13 (26%) informed of risks to foetus
audits.c: Audit report and standards disseminated to clinicians via formal PowerPoint presentation and emails; information incorporated into the Doctors' Handbook for Junior Doctors.

audits.t: P03-375 - Audit on use of Hypnotics for Insomnia in Comparison with National Institute of Clincal Excellence Guidelines
audits.st: NICE guidelines on hypnotic prescribing for insomnia
audits.f: Overall compliance with guidelines was 42%; only 25% advised non-pharmacological measures first; duration ranged one week to over 10 years, with 33% under one year and 10% over 10 years; no evidence cost was considered; only one patient had hypnotic switched, no evidence of adverse reaction

audits.t: An audit of medical and nursing records of 100 emergency short-term (< 7 dys) psychiatric admissions to acute adult wards in Dumfries
audits.tp: Admission and discharge documentation quality on psychiatric wards
audits.st: Locally defined protocol/standards for recorded admission and discharge processes
audits.f: 51% of admissions occurred on weekends, 58% out of hours; 35% had a further admission within 4 weeks; alcohol/drug misuse contributed to 69% of admissions; 66% of medical records and 80% of nursing records had incomplete admission assessments; similar failings found in discharge records

audits.t: Clinical audit on nice guidance on anticholinesterases in a memory clinic
audits.st: NICE guidance on prescribing anticholinesterases in dementia
audits.f: Baseline MMSE score above the recommended score of 12 in all 16 (100%) patients; follow-up MMSE done in 12 (75%) at 4-6 months, none below 12; NICE guidance followed in most (75%) patients

audits.t: Audit of the resettlement process: Mallow ward, Muckamore Abbey Hospital
audits.st: Bamford Review of Mental Health and Learning Disability of Northern Ireland resettlement guidelines/Government Action Plan
audits.f: 11 (79%) children resettled in the community; standards achieved 100% in several domains (risk assessments, information sharing, patient/carer involvement); 5 (45%) discharged within 4 weeks of trial resettlement

audits.t: Physical health monitoring of patients on antipsychotic medication in community - findings of an audit
audits.tp: Physical health monitoring in antipsychotic prescribing (community)
audits.st: NICE guidelines (Schizophrenia) and Maudsley guidelines: urea & electrolytes, fasting blood glucose and fasting lipid profile at least once a year for patients on antipsychotic medication
audits.f: 58% had urea & electrolytes recorded, 58% had fasting blood glucose recorded, 46% had fasting lipid profile recorded

audits.t: Antpsychotics and CVD risk managment in rehabilitation inpatients - findings of an audit
audits.tp: Cardiovascular risk monitoring in antipsychotic prescribing (rehabilitation inpatients)
audits.st: NICE guidelines (Schizophrenia, Lipid Modification) and Maudsley guidelines: blood pressure, BMI, CVD risk assessment, fasting blood glucose and fasting lipid profile at least annually; lipid modification therapy if 10-year CVD risk ≥20%
audits.f: 26 (84%) had blood pressure recorded, 29 (94%) had BMI, 11 (35%) had fasting blood glucose or HbA1c; CVD risk assessment using a calculator was not done in any patients; 19 (61%) had lipid profile done, of whom 16 (84%) had abnormal lipid profile; 9 (26%) on lipid modifying drugs, 6 (19%) on appropriate dose

audits.t: Audit on inpatient risk assessment of mentally ill patients
audits.st: Local trust standard for risk assessment recording (self, aggression, violence, neglect, exploitation and abuse)
audits.f: 4 patients (8%) had no risk assessment forms filled in; of 46 forms completed, time/date not recorded in 8 (17%); completion date recorded in 9 forms (20%); review done in 11 cases (24%); 45% lacked name and signature of assessor; suicide risk, neglect and aggression documented in 90% of forms but only 20% had a further action plan
audits.c: Findings presented to the clinical governance team and highlighted as a priority for improvement, implemented in the trust.

audits.t: 361 – Audit of Attendance of Clozapine Clinic Two Years after First Audit
audits.st: not reported (target of full clinic attendance)
audits.f: Mainly young men from South Asian background were not attending clinic
audits.c: Education of patients about illness and importance of maintenance treatment; education of family to improve involvement and compliance; recommendation to synchronise clinic appointments with blood test appointments.
audits.r2: 8 DNAs (did not attend): 2 black British and 6 white English; improvement in non-attendance in South Asian client group; non-attendance in other groups mainly due to blood test/clinic appointment non-concordance

audits.t: 612 – Audit of Referrals to the Tertiary Affective Disorders Service in Newcastle
audits.tp: Referral appropriateness to a tertiary affective disorders service
audits.st: Specialised Services National Definitions Set (SSNDS) definition 22 (Mental Health), section 6 referral criteria
audits.f: 25% definitely met criteria (15 with bipolar disorder), 18% partially met criteria (11 unipolar), 57% did not meet criteria; of those not meeting criteria, 8 were healthcare professionals seen out of area, 2 were GP referrals for diagnosis clarification, 6 had non-affective disorder diagnosis, 17 met general but not specific criteria, 5 met neither

audits.t: 951 – Audit Of The Introduction Of Agomelatine In a District General Hospital
audits.st: Local guidelines for agomelatine initiation, developed by consensus given lack of national prescribing guidance
audits.f: Agomelatine initiated in 93% for major depressive disorder as third-line treatment; 89% completed baseline liver function tests, 63% had these reviewed at all 3 recommended time-points; 14% did not require dose increment to 50mg; 33% discontinued; 44% experienced mild side effects; 56% did not require additional anxiolytic, 14% successfully discharged

audits.t: 1112 – Every Contact Counts: Audit Investigating Extent Psychiatry Trainees Maximise Opportunity For Physical Health Assessment When Admitting Patients To Psychiatric Hospital
audits.tp: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists' Physical Health in Mental Health Scoping Group 2009 guidelines
audits.f: Physical examination: 102/125 (82%) received, 60/125 (48%) on admission, average delay 12 days; blood tests: 89/125 (71%) received, 50/125 (40%) thyroid function, 67/125 (54%) liver function, 28/125 (22%) glucose, 1/125 (0.8%) HbA1c, 38/125 (30%) lipid profile; 48/125 (38%) urine drug screening, 55/125 (44%) ECG; documentation: 102/125 (82%) PMH, 82/125 (66%) allergies, 90/125 (72%) smoking status; scanned into records: 23/55 (42%) ECG, 72/125 (58%) physical observation chart
audits.c: Teaching led by consultant physicians organised on identified topics including metabolic syndrome, based on trainee survey; recommendation to create comprehensive equipment lists for ward administrators.

audits.t: 1136 – Bridging The Gap: An Audit Of The Transitions Of Young People In Mental Health Services
audits.tp: CAMHS to adult mental health services transition policy adherence
audits.st: Trust's Transitions Policy for young people moving from CAMHS to AMHS
audits.f: Variable response rate; majority of young people and professionals were satisfied with planning and transfer of care with high policy adherence rates

audits.t: 1212 – Audit On The Management Of Patients With Alcohol Withdrawal Within Inpatient Setting In Relation To The Local Guidelines (based On Nice Recommendations)
audits.st: Local guidelines based on NICE recommendations: 3-day course of IM Pabrinex and 7-day reducing regime of benzodiazepine (commonly chlordiazepoxide) with additional PRN benzodiazepine
audits.f: All patients prescribed chlordiazepoxide; 17 prescribed both regular and PRN, 1 regular only, 3 PRN only; treatment period ranged 2-11 days; 5 received recommended 7-day reducing regimen; only 1 patient managed fully in accordance with local guidelines

audits.t: 2025 – Audit Of Monitoring For Metabolic Syndrome In Medium Secure Forensic Wards In Roseberry Park Hospital, Middlesbrough, Uk
audits.st: Maudsley Guideline for monitoring metabolic effects of atypical antipsychotics (clozapine): blood lipids and weight at baseline, 3 months and yearly; blood glucose and blood pressure at baseline, 4-6 months and yearly
audits.f: No patient on clozapine achieved 100% monitoring; baseline monitoring for cholesterol, weight, blood glucose and blood pressure were 88%, 50%, 75% and 88% respectively; at midterm 50%, 100%, 38% and 25% respectively

audits.t: 2305 – Audit On Effects Of Mood Stabilisers On Women's Health - Informed Decision Making
audits.tp: Informed decision making documentation for mood stabilisers in women
audits.st: NICE recommendations that healthcare professionals give relevant information at every stage of assessment/treatment, discuss contraception and pregnancy risks, and assess capacity to consent
audits.f: Verbal communication documented in only 35%, written information in only 11%; contraception advice documented in only 24%; capacity to consent assessment documented in only 31%

audits.t: Audit and Feedback to Ordering Providers to Reduce Inappropriate C. difficile Testing and Hospital Onset C. difficile Rate
audits.st: Appropriate indication for CDI testing defined as ≥3 liquid stools in 24 hours or symptoms of fulminant disease
audits.f: HO-CDI rate 3.92 per 10,000 BDOC pre-intervention; rate of all inappropriate tests 16.25 per 10,000 BDOC; average tests per month 37.8
audits.c: Diagnostic stewardship intervention comprising education on appropriate CDI testing indications plus real-time prospective audit and feedback to ordering providers/supervising physicians for tests not meeting appropriate indication.
audits.r2: HO-CDI rate decreased to 0.99 per 10,000 BDOC (p=0.03); rate of all inappropriate tests decreased to 7.96 per 10,000 BDOC (p=0.04); average tests per month decreased to 28.1; hospital onset inappropriate test rate trended toward decrease (4.77 vs 9.29 per 10,000 BDOC, p=0.07)

audits.t: The effectiveness of aseptic non-touch technique audit cycle implementation on reducing the surgical site infection at EMC Group Hospital
audits.tp: Aseptic technique compliance and surgical site infection
audits.st: Aseptic non-touch technique (ANTT) compliance standard
audits.f: Baseline data collected via pre-questionnaires, structured interviews and audit observations prior to implementing ANTT
audits.c: Implementation of the aseptic non-touch technique (ANTT) strategy through five stages: planning, launching, educating, assessing and monitoring, with electronic audit observation.
audits.r2: Mean compliance rate after ANTT implementation was 93% (glove use 92%, contaminated gloves 0%, aseptic area 84%, contaminated aseptic area 0%, disinfected procedure trays 75%, protected keypart 84%, contaminated keyparts by hands/equipment 2.6%, hand hygiene after gloves 98%); SSI rate dropped from 0.3% to 0.1% in 12 months (p<0.001)

audits.t: Assessing guideline concordance of antimicrobials used in Australian long-term care using a national point prevalence audit
audits.tp: Antimicrobial prescribing guideline concordance in long-term care
audits.st: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic 16th edition and Dermatology 4th and 5th editions
audits.f: Incorrect antimicrobial choices common (e.g. cefalexin and roxithromycin for pneumonia, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid and doxycycline for cellulitis); dosing errors ranged 3.4% (trimethoprim for cystitis) to 78.0% (amoxicillin for pneumonia); cefalexin frequently incorrectly dosed (70.3% cystitis, 72.8% wound infections, 68.2% cellulitis); over 40% of top five antimicrobial prescriptions per indication exceeded recommended duration, up to 96.8% (ketoconazole for tinea)

audits.t: P035: Development of a province-wide audit program for return visits to the emergency department
audits.tp: Emergency department return visit audit program
audits.st: Ontario Ministry of Health/Health Quality Ontario ED Return Visit Quality Program (RVQP) mandating audit of a minimum of 25-50 return visits per year, for return visits within 72 hours (or 7 days with specific diagnoses) resulting in hospital admission
audits.f: Hospitals conducted thousands of audits and identified quality and safety gaps to address; analysis of clinical observations planned for February 2017

audits.t: MP31: Safely reducing emergency physician admission rate through audit and feedback
audits.tp: Emergency physician admission rate audit and feedback
audits.st: Locally created audit tool comparing individual physicians' admission and bounce-back rates to peers, with established targets
audits.f: Significant variability in admission rates between physicians; no correlation between actual and self-reported admission rates
audits.c: Audit tool comparing individual physicians' admission and bounce-back rates to peers, shared every 2 months; physicians divided into low/medium/high admitter groups with targets; department heads met with high admitters.
audits.r2: Seven of nine sites experienced significant decrease in admission rate of top admitters; three sites showed significant increase in rate of low admitters, two in medium admitters; pooled results showed decrease in admissions of 773 patients annualised, with estimated 25.3 beds saved annually at the three biggest hospitals' top five admitters

audits.t: Multidisciplinary Central-Line Bundle Audit Rounding: A Strategy to Reduce CLABSIs
audits.tp: Central line bundle compliance to reduce CLABSI
audits.st: Central venous catheter (CVC) maintenance bundle elements: occlusive/intact dressing, healthy insertion site, labelled dressing with insertion date, correct dressing/tubing change timing, tubing labelling, capped unused ports (IDOL acronym)
audits.f: Overall compliance averaged 85%; 71% of sites without excess drainage, 57% of dressings occlusive or intact
audits.c: Multidisciplinary rounds monitoring nursing staff adherence to CVC bundle elements, with just-in-time staff coaching, leadership follow-up, and education using the 'IDOL' acronym.
audits.r2: Compliance increased to an average of 91%; 83% of sites without excess drainage, 89% of dressings occlusive or intact; 50% decrease in CLABSIs compared to previous 12-month period

audits.t: Audit of the incidence of persistent perforation of the tympanic membrane following grommet removal or extrusion.
audits.tp: Persistent tympanic membrane perforation after grommet removal
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Persistent perforation incidence was 0%; collar button grommets were retained longer than Shepard grommets; 51.9% of ears required two or more tube insertions

audits.t: Audit of regional screening guidelines for vestibular schwannoma.
audits.tp: Adherence to vestibular schwannoma screening guidelines
audits.st: Previously agreed regional MRI screening guidelines for vestibular schwannoma
audits.f: Posterior fossa tumour identified in 12 patients; scan requests were judged inappropriate in 28 cases.

audits.t: A ten year audit of the management of cancers of the larynx and pharynx.
audits.tp: Head and neck cancer referral patterns
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Changes in alcohol history taking by psychiatric junior doctors: an audit
audits.tp: Alcohol and drug history documentation by junior doctors
audits.st: Not an externally named guideline; standard implied by improvement literature on drinking history documentation
audits.f: 58% of histories had no mention of alcohol usage
audits.c: Publication of articles highlighting deficiencies in drinking histories taken by junior doctors (external literature, not a specific local intervention)
audits.r2: 25% of histories had no mention of alcohol usage, a statistically significant improvement (p<0.01); 27% of patients had illicit drug usage history recorded, also a significant improvement (p<0.02) versus four years earlier

audits.t: An audit of the care of 266 patients with schizophrenia in 16 general practices
audits.tp: Schizophrenia care recording in general practice
audits.st: not reported (local audit criteria for care recording)
audits.f: not reported (baseline levels of recording not given numerically)
audits.c: Audit of care by 16 general practices (specific change not detailed).
audits.r2: Improved levels of recording of six aspects of patient care: family care, Mental State Examination, quality of life, preventive physical care, co-ordinated care and details of medication

audits.t: Medical audit in an elderly depressed cohort
audits.tp: Drug therapy for elderly patients with depression
audits.st: not reported (implicit standard of appropriate antidepressant/prophylactic prescribing)
audits.f: 17 of 41 patients (41%) with Manic Depressive Psychosis were not taking antidepressant medication on admission; of 11 patients who received ECT, 7 (64%) did so under Section 3 of the Mental Health Act; 4 of 41 (10%) with Manic Depressive Psychosis not on prophylactic antidepressants or lithium on discharge; 17 patients (28%) taking benzodiazepine hypnotics on admission, 14 discharged on same type/dosage

audits.t: A Paramedic Peer-Review Quality Assurance Audit
audits.tp: Paramedic documentation and radio communication quality (peer review)
audits.st: Locally developed standards for run sheet documentation of care and paramedic radio presentation
audits.f: Deficiency rate 0.27 per run; 63% of days audited
audits.c: Introduction of a paramedic peer-review quality assurance audit programme with checklists for run sheet documentation and radio presentation.
audits.r2: Deficiency rate decreased to 0.21 per run, a statistically significant improvement (95% CI 0.02-0.08); 80% of days audited; for 12 paramedics who newly became auditors, deficiencies/run decreased from 0.13 to 0.08

audits.t: Mind the gap: a national audit of radiotherapy prescription conformance and traceability
audits.st: Board of Faculty of Clinical Oncologists/Royal College of Radiologists 1996 guidelines on management of unscheduled interruption or prolongation of radical radiotherapy
audits.f: Majority of UK radiotherapy centres had a protocol for managing radiotherapy prescription compliance, documenting causes of non-compliance; a statistically significant number of departments failed to monitor or evaluate causes of radiotherapy prolongation

audits.t: Towards conformal radiotherapy: an audit of technique accuracy
audits.st: Local verification procedure and treatment set-up accuracy requirements for conformal radiotherapy
audits.f: Head and neck: 26.6% had one or more errors >5mm, 3.3% had consistent errors >5mm throughout; chest and abdomen: large number of errors exceeding 10mm before modification
audits.c: Modification of the chest/abdomen treatment set-up technique after 20 patients due to high error rates.
audits.r2: Significant (p<0.01) reduction in number of errors in the modified technique group, and significantly (p<0.01) reduced range of errors in the y direction

audits.t: An audit of a radiotherapy review clinic for breast cancer patients: a multi-disciplinary approach
audits.tp: Radiotherapy review clinic patient satisfaction and side-effect reporting
audits.st: not reported (audit of satisfaction and reporting conformity)
audits.f: Patients satisfied with clinic visits: 84% and 85% confidence/trust in radiographer and nurse respectively, compared to 73% with the doctor; disparity found in recording of side effects between non-medical and medical staff groups

audits.t: CT-based post-implant dosimetry for I-125 prostate brachytherapy: a multi-centre audit in the UK and Ireland
audits.tp: Post-implant dosimetry variation in prostate brachytherapy (multi-centre)
audits.st: not reported (multi-centre audit of consistency, no external target stated)
audits.f: Significant variation in prostate outlines: for mean volume 43cm3, range was 39-57cm3, leading to D90 variation 119-154 Gy (mean 140 Gy) and V100 80-93% (mean 88%); uncertainty value around ±20 Gy on D90

audits.t: Audit of Adverse Clinical Incidents in the Anaesthetic Recovery Room
audits.tp: Adverse clinical incidents in anaesthetic recovery room
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: BARNA National Audit on Staffing in the Post Anaesthetic Care Unit – Results
audits.st: not reported (national general audit on PACU staffing, no explicit external target stated)
audits.f: Results clearly indicated many problems exist in ensuring safe and appropriate staffing in the PACU at all times

audits.t: An audit of clinical practice in an ACT team against NICE guidelines in schizophrenia
audits.tp: Assertive Community Treatment (ACT) team compliance with schizophrenia guidance
audits.st: NICE guidelines in the treatment of schizophrenia
audits.f: Baseline case note audit conducted 2 years earlier (specific figures not given)
audits.r2: Rates of compliance with NICE guidelines varied from 0% (provision of advance directive) to 85% (written information given, no antipsychotic polypharmacy); compliance greater than in the earlier audit

audits.t: An audit of the metabolic syndrome in two rehabilitation inpatient units
audits.tp: Metabolic syndrome screening in psychiatric rehabilitation inpatients
audits.st: Metabolic syndrome monitoring criteria (waist circumference, BP, fasting triglycerides, HDL cholesterol and glucose)
audits.f: 58% of patients met criteria for metabolic syndrome, but due to lack of appropriate physical monitoring only 19% had previously been diagnosed

audits.t: Audit of the Rapid Tranquilization Policy in the 2gether NHS Foundation Trust
audits.st: 2gether NHS Foundation Trust Rapid Tranquilisation (RT) policy incorporating NICE guidance across eight domains
audits.f: Adherence to majority of standards in most incidents; significant non-compliance in two areas: appropriate physical observations after RT incident and administration of RT in a private area
audits.c: Dissemination of audit results to clinical leads and trainers; effective training of staff emphasising need to meet standards and importance of contemporaneous documentation.
audits.r2: not reported (re-audit planned but results not yet available in this abstract)

audits.t: An audit of the use of advance statements surrounding management of disturbed behaviour on a PICU
audits.tp: Use of advance statements for disturbed behaviour management (PICU)
audits.st: Guidance advocating patient engagement in outlining preferences for management of disturbed behaviour (advance statements)
audits.f: Advance statements completed by 8 of 15 patients admitted (53%); patients' wishes followed for two thirds of patients following incidents needing interventions
audits.c: Changes to practice to promote and support completion of advance statements (specific change not detailed).
audits.r2: Only minimal improvement in patients completing advance statements, but completed sooner after admission; despite more incidents needing interventions, patients' wishes were followed in two thirds of those who completed an advance statement

audits.t: A simple clinical audit of antipsychotic medication prescribing on Hollywell Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU)
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists' 2006 consensus statement on use of high dose antipsychotic medication
audits.f: 9 (31%) received a single antipsychotic; 10 (33%) prescribed high dosages; 4 (13%) high dose combination prescriptions
audits.r2: Proportion receiving single antipsychotic increased to 22 (55%); high dosage prescriptions declined to 3 (8%); high dose combination prescriptions declined to 1 (3%)

audits.t: An audit of diabetes mellitus management within a specialist secure psychiatric hospital
audits.tp: Diabetes management in secure psychiatric hospital
audits.st: NICE guidelines on diabetes care and management
audits.f: 18 (28%) had an individual care plan addressing diabetic management and risk; majority had regular blood glucose and HbA1c monitoring

audits.t: An audit of service-user involvement and quality of HCR-20 version 2 risk assessments on rehabilitation and low secure wards
audits.tp: HCR-20 risk assessment quality and service-user involvement
audits.st: HCR-20 version 2 structured professional judgement instrument standard for risk assessment
audits.f: Historical section of HCR-20 more consistently completed than clinical and risk sections; quality of risk assessments was mixed
audits.c: In-house HCR-20 training programme; development of local standards for completion of HCR-20 assessments following the audit.

audits.t: Scottish Audit of Surgical Mortality, 1997
audits.st: Scottish Audit of Surgical Mortality (SASM) form completion compliance standard, examining all hospital deaths under surgical care and within 30 days of operation
audits.f: Compliance for completion of vascular death forms remained over 92% during 1994-1997
audits.r2: Compliance was 97% in 1997, compared with 92% overall compliance for other surgical specialties; vascular deaths numbered 507 in 1997, down from 554, 573 and 524 in 1994-1996; consultant surgeon made the decision to operate in 98% of vascular deaths and was principal surgeon in 70%

audits.t: Posters. P1 A 2‐year audit of thyroid fine needle aspiration cytology
audits.tp: Thyroid fine needle aspiration cytology diagnostic accuracy
audits.st: not reported (audit of diagnostic performance/accuracy)
audits.f: Six of 57 tumours had significant discrepancies between FNA and histology, including a malignant lymphoma diagnosed as Hashimoto's thyroiditis, a metastasis suggested as medullary carcinoma, and an insular carcinoma diagnosed as medullary carcinoma

audits.t: Posters. P4 Retrospective audit of smear and biopsy correlation
audits.tp: Cervical smear and biopsy correlation (positive predictive value)
audits.st: NHS Cervical Screening Programme (NHSCSP) expected average positive predictive value
audits.f: Concordance in 581/717 (81%) for high grade and 566/704 (80%) for low grade; positive predictive value above 80% for both groups, above the NHSCSP expected average

audits.t: Posters. P20 Fine needle aspiration of salivary glands in Beaumont Hospital: a 14‐year audit
audits.tp: Salivary gland FNA cytology diagnostic accuracy
audits.st: not reported (audit of diagnostic accuracy over 14 years)
audits.f: Good correlation between FNA and histology in 145 of 183 cases with follow-up; 89 aspirates inadequate, 89 inflammatory/normal/cyst, 113 diagnosed as benign, 33 malignant, 16 suspicious; diagnostic problem areas included lymphomas (7 called benign), Warthin's tumour (7 not diagnosed/misdiagnosed), mucoepidermoid carcinoma, and 7 pleomorphic adenomas not diagnosed on FNA

audits.t: Regular audit of colposcopic biopsies from women with a mildly dyskaryotic or borderline cervical smear results in fewer cases of CINIII.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Mandatory review of cases where the cervical smear result was discrepant with subsequent colposcopic or histological findings.
audits.r2: 3% with borderline smear and 6% with mild dyskaryosis had CIN III; 25% (borderline) and 33% (mild) required treatment; 18% with moderate dyskaryosis had CIN III (46% treated); 61% with severe dyskaryosis had CIN III/invasive cancer (90% treated).

audits.t: The influence of the cervix on smear quality. I: Atrophy. An audit of cervical smears taken post‐colposcopic management of intraepithelial neoplasia
audits.st: not reported (audit of smear quality/adequacy)
audits.f: 28% of poor-quality smears associated with clinical/cytological atrophy; in 91% of these, scantiness was the main adverse factor; relative risk of scanty smear 4.8 times greater with clinical atrophy versus no atrophy

audits.t: Safe entry during laparoscopy: a prospective audit in a district general hospital
audits.st: Middlesbrough consensus guideline on safe entry during laparoscopy
audits.f: All laparoscopies on the professional unit complied with the Middlesbrough guidelines; a large number of other procedures did not. Veress needle at umbilicus in 458 (97.4%), Palmer's point in 9 (1.9%), open method in 1; gas pressure of 25 mmHg used in 299 (63.6%); complications in 23 (4.5%), including bowel injury in 2 (0.42%), uterine perforation in 2 (0.42%), and 1 (0.21%) converted to laparotomy

audits.t: Audit of clinical management of von Willebrand disease during 1997 at a single institution and review of treatment patterns between 1980 and 1997
audits.tp: von Willebrand disease treatment guideline adherence
audits.st: UK Haemophilia Centre Directors Organization 1997 guidelines for diagnosis and management of von Willebrand disease (DDAVP for type 1 and 2N; considered in other type 2; ineffective in type 3; clotting factor concentrates if unresponsive or contraindicated)
audits.f: 10 patients received DDAVP and 30 received clotting factor concentrates (CFC, total 1.2 million IU); several patients with type 1 and 2 vWD received CFC without a preliminary DDAVP test dose

audits.t: The wider implications of an audit of care plan documentation
audits.st: Locally developed ideal assessment of care for four areas of district nursing work: leg ulceration, bath care, pressure area care and catheter care
audits.f: Evaluation of patient care was often inadequately recorded, reflecting poor documentation of the initial nursing assessment

audits.t: Are we achieving the dietary recommendations for diabetic patients? An audit of dietary advice to diabetic patients
audits.st: British Diabetic Association Recommendations (1992) and Dietary Reference Values (1991) for fat, carbohydrate, non-milk extrinsic sugars, cholesterol, non-starch polysaccharides and protein intake
audits.f: 70% achieved dietary recommendations for fat intake, 30% for carbohydrate; majority achieved recommendations for non-milk extrinsic sugars and cholesterol; less successful for non-starch polysaccharides and protein

audits.t: A team approach to the audit of nutritional care in community hospitals
audits.tp: Nutritional care quality in community hospitals
audits.st: Locally developed audit tool covering nutritional adequacy, documentation of nutritional assessments, nurses' nutritional knowledge, patients' perceptions of the meal service and good nutritional practice
audits.f: Overall results were better than initially anticipated; where issues were identified, discussions were taking place to write an action plan and implement recommendations

audits.t: Implementing a nutritional assessment tool in the community: a report describing the process, audit and problems encountered
audits.st: Use of a nutritional assessment tool (NAT) by community nurses
audits.f: Audit results, although inconclusive, suggest little change in nursing practice despite nurses acknowledging the usefulness of the NAT
audits.c: Training in and adaptation of the nutritional assessment tool for community use

audits.t: Audit for the Heartbeat Award in staff catering facilities in an NHS Trust
audits.st: Heartbeat Award Scheme (HBA) minimum criteria for healthy menu choices, food hygiene and eating environment
audits.f: It was usually clear whether food served achieved HBA criteria, but quantified criteria were needed for reliable assessment of main dishes, sandwiches and desserts; a summary of HBA achievement, observations and recommendations was produced

audits.t: Audit in clinical practice: evaluating use of a nutrition screening tool developed for trauma nurses
audits.st: Compliance with the Nutrition Checklist screening tool: recording a nutrition score within 24 hours of admission, re-scoring where applicable, and dietetic referral for scores ≥3
audits.f: 67% (32/48) had a nutrition score recorded; 75% (24/32) scored within 24h of admission; 38% (11/29) due for reassessment were rescored; 88% (23/26) of automatic referrals (score ≥3) were referred, and the dietitian documented 100% (23/23) of referrals

audits.t: An audit of laxative use and fibre/fluid intakes in a care of the elderly rehabilitation ward
audits.st: Recommended level of dietary fibre and fluid intake
audits.f: Ispaghula husk (Fybogel, Regulan) was the most commonly used laxative; the regular menu appeared to provide adequate fluid and fibre but the soft menu was less satisfactory; all three patients assessed had fibre intakes well below the recommended level

audits.t: Nutrition audit at a community hospital
audits.st: Department of Health (DoH) guidelines on hospital catering and Reference Nutrient Intakes
audits.f: Menus met DoH guidelines for vitamin C, fibre, iron and folate; dietary intake analysis (n=8) showed low intakes of iron, fibre, vitamin D and folate; mealtimes were relaxed and satisfactory

audits.t: Report of a nutritional screening audit
audits.tp: Nutritional screening tool use in nursing care plans
audits.st: National Professional Standards for Dietitians requirement for nutritional screening
audits.f: Use of the screening tool was variable and fewer than half of those identified as needing nutritional care were referred to the dietitian

audits.t: An audit of nutritional supplement distribution and consumption on a care of the elderly ward
audits.st: Prescribed volume of oral sip feed supplement should be offered to and consumed by patients
audits.f: Not all patients received the supplements prescribed; 39% of patients who received a supplement consumed none or hardly any of it; 43% consumed nearly all of the supplement provided

audits.t: Audit of supplement use on care of the elderly and rehabilitation wards
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Number of patients using supplements was lower than expected; more supplements were used than had been prescribed, a discrepancy of 22-113%; wastage was 24% for Entera and 45% for Enlive

audits.t: Clinical use of FFP: results of a retrospective process and outcome audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 66% of initial FFP requests appeared appropriate, rising to 73% after case-note review; 94% of FFP was traceable to identified patients; 88% of notes gave a reason for treatment; coagulation improvement documented in 78% of cases; 80% also received other blood products carrying virus risk.

audits.t: Australian and New Zealand 1997 thrombolysis audit
audits.tp: Thrombolysis time to treatment for myocardial infarction
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 29% received thrombolysis and 5% angioplasty; average emergency department door-to-needle time 49.4 min (median 38.6) vs 63.9 min (median 66.8) in coronary care units; primary angioplasty started on average 61.5 min (median 69.2) after arrival

audits.t: Audit of paediatric day‐case surgery in a district general hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Attendance rate 98.8%; 5 patients (2.2%) kept overnight for observation; 6 (2.6%) re-admitted after operation; 50 (22%) telephone hotline enquiries; overall minor complication rate 4.8%, no major morbidity

audits.t: Pre‐operative parent information and attitudes towards general anaesthetic induction technique in paediatric patients: An audit
audits.tp: Pre-operative parent information for paediatric anaesthesia induction
audits.st: Locally set standard that all parents should be told about the preferred induction technique (intravenous or gas), an alternative if it fails, related complications, and be able to discuss worries afterwards
audits.f: Only 40% were told about both gas and intravenous induction; 58% were told why the technique was chosen; 10% found the induction experience worse than expected; 16% felt the information given was too little; 12% could not discuss worries afterwards; 90% found the induction better than or as expected
audits.c: Planned preoperative educational programme with audio-visual aids, video-tapes, induction room visits and information leaflets

audits.t: An Audit of Preoperative Behaviour and Premedication Practise at Great Ormond Street Hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 75% had satisfactory behaviour scores in the anaesthetic room, dropping to 47% at induction; 12% of children received a sedative premedication (16 Midazolam, 3 Temazepam, 1 Triclofos); only 5% received an atropine premedication

audits.t: Parents with learning disabilities: service audit and development
audits.tp: Service audit for parents with learning disabilities
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Referrals rose from 2 in 1995 to 13 in 1997; only 3 of 32 children of referred parents were not subject to some intervention under the 1989 Children Act; 23 distinct professional teams were involved with the referred families
audits.c: Developed a four-tier service model: workshops/consultation for professionals, a parenting assessment service, legal work, and a parents' group

audits.t: Nuchal translucency audit: a novel image‐scoring method
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 11.4% of images classed excellent, 57.1% reasonable, 25.7% intermediate, 5.7% unacceptable; inter-reviewer agreement showed identical classification in 65.7-74.3% of cases

audits.t: Implementation of nuchal translucency image-scoring method during ongoing audit.
audits.st: Basic image quality standards for nuchal translucency scans set via an image-scoring method
audits.f: Mean final quality score 4.62 +/- 0.21
audits.c: Ongoing audit with blind image scoring feedback to three examiners
audits.r2: Mean final quality score improved to 6.91 +/- 0.16 (intermediate period score 6.19 +/- 0.19)

audits.t: An audit of invasive prenatal diagnosis for Bart's hydrops
audits.tp: Invasive prenatal diagnosis for alpha thalassaemia
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 18 cases of Bart's hydrops were diagnosed; iatrogenic fetal loss rate was 0%; only 27.3% of couples were identified as carriers in the first pregnancy at or before 12 weeks

audits.t: Investigating models of continence care and service provision in regional Australia: a retrospective clinical audit
audits.st: 2006 NICE guideline for the management of urinary incontinence in women; local 'Right care, right time, right place' service model
audits.f: 'Right care' was adhered to in only 25% of cases overall (22% community clinic, 3% surgical outpatient department); primary episode of care lasted 8-11 months and total length of care 15-17 months at the two services

audits.t: The Impact of a Clinical Audit on GP Detection of Depression
audits.st: Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) as reference standard for detection of depression by GPs
audits.f: Psychological problems identified by HADS in 65.9% of patients; mean age 35 years, 73.6% female
audits.c: Clinical audit with feedback plus a linked educational workshop and comprehensive treatment guidelines for GPs
audits.r2: Psychological problems identified by HADS decreased to 59.7%; non-significant increase in true negative detection and decrease in false negative detection rate; no change in true or false positive rates

audits.t: Physical Health and Activity of Inpatients under Forensic Mental Health Care: A Cross-Sectional Survey and Audit of Patients in a High Secure Setting in Queensland, Australia
audits.tp: Physical health and activity in forensic mental health inpatients
audits.st: World Health Organization recommended levels of physical activity
audits.f: Overweight in 50.0%, obesity in 46.6%, metabolic syndrome in 39.3%; mean waist circumference 110.8cm (females), 109.0cm (males); 46.4% did not meet WHO recommended physical activity levels

audits.t: Is quality control useful? An audit of the saving measures regarding prescriptions at National District Hospital in Bloemfontein
audits.st: Locally revised treatment protocols for chronic conditions using cheaper alternative drugs, following a prior baseline study
audits.f: A prior study identified the 20 most expensive or inappropriately prescribed drugs at the hospital
audits.c: New/updated treatment protocols for chronic conditions grouping the identified drugs and using cheaper alternatives
audits.r2: A saving of R215,395 in medicine dispensing over 8 weeks was demonstrated, with a calculated saving of R1.4 million achievable over one year; prescribers were made aware of correct dosages

audits.t: Audit of antenatal care in a rural district of KZN, South Africa
audits.st: National antenatal care standards for the booking visit and visits at 28 and 36 weeks gestation, as part of a quality improvement initiative
audits.f: Only 9% booked in the first trimester, most (two-thirds) booked in the second trimester; haemoglobin recording was 95% at first visit but fell to 46% and 30% at 28 and 36 weeks; syphilis screening was 18% at first visit and 2% at 36 weeks, with only 16% of positives adequately treated; 55% received three doses of tetanus toxoid before delivery

audits.t: Rising Caesarean Section Rates: An Audit of Caesarean Sections in a Specialist Private Practice
audits.st: WHO-suggested ideal caesarean section rate of 10-15% in low-risk obstetric populations
audits.f: 209/364 deliveries (60.4%) were by caesarean section, well above the WHO ideal rate; most were due to a previous caesarean section, with maternal request and HIV status also contributing

audits.t: An audit of PMTCT services at a regional hospital in South Africa
audits.st: Prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) programme protocol (HIV testing, CD4 counts, nevirapine administration)
audits.f: 96% (479) were offered HIV testing and 473 accepted; 48% (227/473) tested HIV positive; only 6.1% (15/246) of negatives were re-tested; CD4 counts done for 70% (159/227) of positive women, and 84.3% (134/159) received their results; only 57.7% (131/227) were given nevirapine at ≥28 weeks; 81.5% took nevirapine before delivery; 91.6% (208) of babies were given nevirapine within 72 hours

audits.t: An audit of surgical termination of pregnancy at a level 1 health facility in South Africa
audits.st: Expected provision of HIV/syphilis screening and contraceptive services alongside termination of pregnancy (TOP)
audits.f: None of the 645 women had any serological screening test performed or received information about STI/HIV testing before discharge; only 16.9% (109) accepted the condoms offered

audits.t: Drug therapy, lifestyle modification and blood pressure control in a primary care facility, south of Johannesburg, South Africa: An audit of hypertension management
audits.st: Target blood pressure control and appropriate choice of antihypertensive drug therapy
audits.f: 57% (171) achieved blood pressure control to target; appropriate antihypertensive drug choice documented in 81.3% (244); lifestyle modification documented in 56.3%; women more likely to have BP controlled than men (P=0.0028)

audits.t: Audit of antenatal care at a community health centre in Tshwane North subdistrict, Gauteng province
audits.st: Guidelines for maternity care in South Africa and the basic antenatal care (BANC) checklist
audits.f: Overall nurse compliance with antenatal care protocols was 85.1%; the response (decision-making and interpretation) component was only 57.6%; response to PMTCT protocols was only 50%

audits.t: Ensuring Compliance with Surgical Antimicrobial Prophylaxis Policy in High-Volume Resource-Limited Settings: Integrated Measures from Inception to Audit
audits.st: Locally developed preoperative antibiotic prophylaxis (PAP) guidelines
audits.f: 196/532 (36.8%) of cases were non-compliant, using additional antibiotics; most commonly for extensive adhesiolysis (29.7%) in gynaecological surgery and prolonged rupture of membranes (14.2%) in caesarean sections; surgical-site infection was more common in obstetric patients receiving additional antibiotics
audits.c: Internal audit exploring reasons for noncompliance and providing self-feedback, based on locally developed consensus PAP guidelines

audits.t: A27-11 An Audit of Oxygen Therapy in Paediatric Wards of Tertiary Hospitals in Nigeria
audits.tp: Oxygen therapy prescribing and monitoring documentation
audits.st: WHO designation of oxygen as an essential medicine; a six-point oxygen prescription/monitoring completeness score
audits.f: Pre-therapy SpO2 documentation absent in 37.6%; delivery device unspecified in 54.1%; target SpO2 undocumented in 86.1%; no monitoring records in 43.7%; mean completeness score 3.38 (±0.85), with 57.1% of prescribers scoring ≤3 and only 8.0% scoring ≥5

audits.t: 223. UNDERSTANDING POTENTIALLY PREVENTABLE MORTALITY FOLLOWING ESOPHAGO-GASTRIC CANCER SURGERY: ANALYSIS OF A NATIONAL AUDIT OF SURGICAL MORTALITY
audits.tp: Preventable mortality after esophagogastric cancer surgery
audits.st: ANZASM peer-review process assessing potentially preventable death after surgery
audits.f: 49 (46.7%) of mortalities were potentially preventable; preventable cases had higher rates of sepsis (59.2% vs 33.9%, P=0.011), multiorgan dysfunction (40.8% vs 25.0%, P=0.042) and reoperation (63.3% vs 41.1%, P=0.031); more clinical management issues per patient (median 2 vs 0, P<0.001)

audits.t: Hospital variation in downstream secondary preventive medication uptake: implications for quality and outcomes
audits.tp: Secondary prevention medication adherence after myocardial infarction
audits.st: Guideline-recommended secondary preventive medication after myocardial infarction
audits.f: Secondary preventive medication uptake ranged from 30.7% to 87.3% between low- and high-performing hospitals; discharge from high-adherence hospitals was associated with lower mortality/re-infarction (hazard ratio 0.82, 95%CI 0.69-0.98)

audits.t: Adherence to guideline-directed medical therapy and its association with re-hospitalization and mortality following coronary artery bypass graft surgery
audits.tp: Guideline-directed medical therapy adherence after CABG
audits.st: Guideline-directed medical therapy (antiplatelet therapy, beta-blockers, statins) in CABG discharge recommendations
audits.f: Guideline-directed medical therapy adherence was evident in discharge recommendations of 638 patients (56.4%); full adherence was associated with a 26% lower 1-year risk of re-hospitalisation/mortality (OR 0.74, 95%CI 0.57-0.97) and 24% lower intermediate (8-year) mortality (HR 0.76, 95%CI 0.59-0.98)

audits.t: Receiving care according to national heart failure guidelines is associated with lower total costs: an observational study in Region Halland, Sweden
audits.tp: Heart failure guideline adherence and cost
audits.st: International evidence-based guideline-defined appropriate pharmacotherapy (AP) for heart failure
audits.f: Total heart failure care cost €58.6 million (€9790/patient); receiving appropriate pharmacotherapy was associated with €1130 lower cost per patient (P<0.001, 95%CI 574-1687)

audits.t: Care gaps following newly detected dipstick proteinuria in treated hypertension: a Japanese nationwide database study
audits.tp: Follow-up of dipstick proteinuria in hypertension
audits.st: Clinical guideline recommendation for follow-up quantitative urine testing after dipstick-positive proteinuria and RASi initiation if confirmed, in hypertensive patients
audits.f: 365-day cumulative incidence of quantitative testing was 7.5% (95%CI 7.2-7.7); RASi initiation was 13.2% (95%CI 12.6-13.8) among 14599 baseline non-users; testing rose with dipstick grade (12.9%/16.1% for 2+/3+) but remained infrequent; RASi initiation showed no improvement over time (adjusted HR per year 1.01, 95%CI 0.99-1.03)

audits.t: Does the quality index of adherence to the evidence-based guidelines predict mortality in patients with myocardial infarction?
audits.tp: SWEDEHEART quality index for MI guideline adherence
audits.st: SWEDEHEART quality index of 11 indicators of evidence-based myocardial infarction treatment (reperfusion, timing, P2Y12 inhibitors, ACEi/ARB, follow-up, smoking cessation, exercise programme, LDL and blood pressure targets)
audits.f: Baseline quality index calculated as the reference year for comparison
audits.r2: Most hospitals (72.1%) improved their quality index by an average of 3.4% per year; no difference in mortality between quintiles of improvement at 30 days (OR 0.99, 95%CI 0.97-1.02) or long-term (OR 1.01, 95%CI 0.99-1.02)

audits.t: Measurement and achievability of quality indicators in an out-of- hospital cardiac arrest real population
audits.st: ACVC/EUSEM/ERC/ESICM consensus quality indicators for post-resuscitation care after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (90% compliance cut-off)
audits.f: Indicators were measurable in 93.1% of cases; overall achievability was 83.9%; achievability exceeded 90% for echocardiography (91.2%), mechanical ventilation (99.5%), blood gas at 2h (99.4%), mechanical circulatory support (92.3%), vasopressors (95.8%) and functional assessment before discharge (93.4%); it fell short of 90% for time to angiography (80%), temperature control (89.4%), organ donation (80%), CT within 72h (58%), EEG within 72h (68.1%), follow-up (88.3%) and 6-month outcomes (88.55%)

audits.t: Enhancing the precision of lipid management quality assessment in ASCVD using large language models
audits.st: LDL-C management guidelines for ASCVD (target LDL-C <70 mg/dL)
audits.f: Structured EHR data showed 7,122 (78.3%) had recent lipid panels, of whom 3,456 (48.5%) had LDL-C <70 mg/dL; among 3,854 patients with LDL-C >=70 mg/dL, 2,895 (75.1%) were on a statin and 1,755 (45.5%) on a high-intensity statin
audits.c: Applied a large language model (GPT-4o) to extract external lipid values and reasons for statin non-use from free-text clinic notes, in addition to structured EHR data
audits.r2: Incorporating LLM-extracted external results raised the lipid testing rate to 82.2% (from 78.3%) though the proportion with LDL-C <70 mg/dL was unchanged (48.5%); excluding 582 patients with LLM-identified statin intolerance improved statin use to 81.9% (from 75.1%) and high-intensity statin use to 53.6% (from 45.5%)

audits.t: P2448Evolution of clinical quality activities within a national echocardiography database: seven-year trends from the GenesisCare Outcomes Registry
audits.tp: Echocardiography data completeness and quality auditing
audits.st: Completeness of key echocardiographic data elements (AV peak velocity, EF, E/E', LA area, rhythm, RVSP), per ACC quality recommendations
audits.f: Data completeness was 72.0±26.8% in 2011
audits.c: Direct online entry of echocardiographic studies into an electronic database, plus selection and auditing of key data elements and quality improvement pathways
audits.r2: Data completeness improved to 88.2±13.5% by 2018 (p=0.02); inter-practice variability in EF and E/E' also fell (p<0.002)

audits.t: P384 APPROPRIATENESS OF PRESCRIBING DIRECT ORAL ANTICOAGULANTS IN THE REAL WORLD: THE ANMCO NATIONAL AUDIT INITIATIVES APPRO–FA EVO PROJECT
audits.tp: DOAC prescribing appropriateness in atrial fibrillation
audits.st: DOAC dosing indications per the summary of product characteristics (APPRO-FA EVO national audit)
audits.f: Among AF patients discharged on oral anticoagulant therapy (96.3%), 89.6% were on a DOAC; reduced dosage met reduction criteria in 90.2% of apixaban, 90.9% of rivaroxaban and 86.7% of edoxaban cases; dabigatran had higher use of reduced dose than full dose (10.2% vs 8.6%)

audits.t: Audit methodology for the quality assessment of medical records in the emergency department
audits.st: Internally developed structured checklist (4 sections, 14 items) for completeness/quality of ED medical records
audits.f: Medical records were scored 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent) on 14 items across 4 sections, giving a total score of 14 to 70 per record; specific results by score were not given
audits.c: Developed a structured audit checklist and internal audit process, with plans for corrective actions

audits.t: Improvement in adherence to antibiotic duration of therapy recommendations for uncomplicated cystitis: a quasi-experimental study
audits.tp: Antibiotic duration of therapy for uncomplicated cystitis
audits.st: National guideline-recommended antibiotic duration of therapy for uncomplicated cystitis
audits.f: Adherence to recommended duration of therapy was 29.4% before the intervention; average days of therapy (DOT) was 6.6
audits.c: Revising or adding pre-filled, modifiable default prescribing instructions for targeted antibiotics in the electronic health record
audits.r2: Adherence to recommended duration of therapy increased to 76.3% (P<0.01); average DOT decreased 23% to 5.1 (P<0.01)

audits.t: Audit of Management of Acute Infective Conjunctivitis in Primary Care
audits.st: Evidence-based management of uncomplicated acute infective conjunctivitis (delayed prescribing per Everitt et al, 2006, BMJ)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An Audit of Bone Densitometry Measurement in Patients with Coeliac Disease
audits.tp: Bone densitometry measurement in coeliac disease
audits.st: Clinical recommendations for measuring bone mineral density in subgroups of patients with coeliac disease
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: 584 Maintaining Success in Patient Safety and Quality Metrics Through Teamwork and Contextual Modification
audits.tp: Patient safety and quality metric benchmarking in a burn unit
audits.st: National benchmarks for CLABSI, CAUTI, VTE, C.Diff, falls and hospital-acquired pressure injury (HAPI)
audits.f: Baseline comparison year for CLABSI, CAUTI, VTE, C.Diff, falls and HAPI rates
audits.c: Daily leadership dashboard of harm events, teamwork initiatives (multidisciplinary review, proactive high-risk patient actions), and unit-specific contextual modifications (e.g. chlorhexidine bathing, HAPI/burn differentiation, environment modification for falls)
audits.r2: BICU was below national benchmarks for all six quality indicators; last patient harm event was 328 days prior versus an average of 32 days for the other 11 units; progressed in CAUTI, falls and HAPI while sustaining 2018 excellence in the other three areas

audits.t: 817 A Proactive Feeding Regimen on Meeting Caloric Goals with Continuous Enteral Nutrition Support: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Enteral nutrition caloric goal achievement in burn patients
audits.st: Meeting at least 85% of calculated calorie estimations with continuous enteral nutrition
audits.f: 52% of pre-protocol admissions met at least 85% of calorie estimations (continuous EN rates calculated on a 24-hour basis)
audits.c: Changed the dietitian's calculation of continuous enteral nutrition rates from a 24-hour to a 23-hour per day basis
audits.r2: 75% of post-protocol admissions met at least 85% of calorie estimations

audits.t: 104 A Quality Improvement Project to Reduce Orthoses Complications
audits.tp: Hand orthosis complication rates in burn therapy
audits.st: Locally defined orthosis complication criteria (erythema and orthotic-induced partial-thickness injury to the index finger)
audits.f: Erythema occurred in 23.4% (n=18) of orthoses and partial-thickness injury in 11.7% (n=9)
audits.c: Formal protocol mandating custom resting hand orthoses be fabricated by a single certified hand therapist (CHT) or co-fabricated by two non-CHT therapists
audits.r2: Erythema occurred in 2.0% (n=1) of cases and partial-thickness injury in 3.9% (n=2), decreases of 94.4% and 77.7% respectively; number of modifications fell from 22 to 13 (40.9% reduction)

audits.t: 623 Procedural Pain Management in Burn Patients – A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Procedural pain control during burn hydrotherapy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Pain scores significantly increased post-procedure compared with pre-procedure (5.39 vs 6.32, p=0.035); only 13 (46.4%) subjects received versed during hydrotherapy; no significant difference in satisfaction scores across encounters

audits.t: Early Palliative Care Consultation in the Burn Unit: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Increase Utilization
audits.tp: Early palliative care consultation triggers in burn patients
audits.st: Recommended triggers for early (<72 hours of admission) palliative care consultation
audits.f: Among patients surviving >24 hours, 67% (14/21) had palliative care consultation (PCC) before the protocol
audits.c: Protocol establishing recommended triggers for early palliative care consultation, instituted in 2019
audits.r2: Frequency of PCC increased to 100% vs 36% of these patients having PCC before death (P=.004); even so, less than half of patients meeting criteria at admission received early PCC

audits.t: Burn-Specific Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis: A 2-Year Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: 2022 prophylaxis guideline for adults with burns >=20% TBSA: enoxaparin 40 mg twice daily, renally and weight adjusted
audits.f: 5 patients developed venous thromboembolic complications (2 pulmonary emboli, 3 DVTs) on enoxaparin 40 mg daily; major bleeding affecting dermal substitute application in 1 case (2%)
audits.c: New burn-specific VTE prophylaxis guideline (enoxaparin 40 mg twice daily, renally/weight adjusted), with later addition of IV tranexamic acid and increased transfusion rates
audits.r2: 3 incidental thromboembolisms (1 pulmonary embolus, 2 DVTs); major bleeding affecting dermal substitute application increased to 7 cases (15%, not statistically significant), eliminated after 12 months following mitigation; overall 88% of patients received VTE prophylaxis in line with the guideline

audits.t: 2878. A Regional Antimicrobial Stewardship Collaboration to Address Fluoroquinolones
audits.st: National ASP regulatory standards for fluoroquinolone use (specific numeric target not stated)
audits.f: Outpatient fluoroquinolone fills approx. 13.6K at start of period; acute/LTC beds fluoroquinolone use 22.3 DOT/1,000 patient-days.
audits.c: FQ-targeted prospective audit/feedback, peer-peer reports, modified EMR order entry, shared educational materials, and regional messaging/events across six ASPs (started 2016).
audits.r2: Outpatient fills fell to 4.3K; DOT/1,000 unique outpatient visits fell by nearly 70% (p=.01); acute/LTC bed fluoroquinolone use fell to 10.8 DOT/1,000 patient-days.

audits.t: 141. Impact of Diagnostic Stewardship of Respiratory Cultures in the Pediatric ICU
audits.tp: Respiratory culture stewardship in paediatric ICU
audits.st: Locally developed multidisciplinary guideline criteria for respiratory culture collection (systemic signs of illness plus respiratory symptoms)
audits.f: 23/47 (48.9%) lower respiratory cultures were guideline-discordant.
audits.c: Introduction of multidisciplinary evidence-based guideline for respiratory culture collection (started 1 Dec 2021) with periodic feedback and reminders to providers.
audits.r2: 40/192 (20.8%) guideline-discordant, a 57% reduction in discordant cultures.

audits.t: P-826. Impact of Antimicrobial Stewardship Prospective Audit on the Treatment of Staphylococcus aureus Bloodstream Infections
audits.tp: Antimicrobial stewardship for Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia
audits.st: Institutional guideline-driven approach targeting narrowest effective (optimal) therapy for Gram-positive coccal bloodstream infection
audits.f: Optimal therapy within 24 hours achieved in 70.9%; step-down to oral therapy in 66.7%.
audits.c: Implementation of a guideline-driven stewardship pharmacist intervention with prospective review for Gram-positive coccal bacteraemia.
audits.r2: Optimal therapy within 24 hours 75%; step-down to oral therapy in only 23.5%.

audits.t: P-1132. Patient Pre-Selection Improves Efficiency and Acceptability of Antimicrobial Audit-and-Feedback Rounds in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 92% of NICU patients on systemic antimicrobials reviewed at audit-and-feedback rounds (AFR); AFR lasted 27 minutes on average; antimicrobial use appropriate in 88%; 75% (n=55) of recommendations accepted.
audits.c: Pharmacists pre-selected patients for AFR discussion from September 2021, excluding those considered by default appropriate (ID-followed, empiric early-onset sepsis regimens, reviewed prophylaxis).
audits.r2: AFR duration decreased to 13 minutes on average; adherence to recommendations increased to 92% (n=36).

audits.t: P-1648. Impact of Provider Education Versus Prospective Audit and Feedback on Outpatient Antibiotic Durations for Endodontic Infections at an Urban Veteran’s Affairs Medical Center
audits.st: American Dental Association guideline recommended duration 3-7 days for endodontic infections
audits.f: Mean duration of antibiotic therapy 7.8 days; 22.5% (64/284) of courses were 10 days or longer.
audits.c: Phase 1: provider education on indications/duration for dentists; Phase 2: pharmacist-directed prospective audit and feedback (PAF) via real-time EMR alerts.
audits.r2: Mean duration decreased to 6.5 days; courses of 10 days or longer fell to 2.2% (4/182), an 84% decrease vs the education-only phase (p<0.001).

audits.t: P-1728. Let's Settle the "Score": Implementation of a Prioritization Tool into an Antimicrobial Stewardship Prospective Audit and Feedback Program
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Intervention rate 46.2%.
audits.c: Implementation of a prioritisation scoring tool embedded in the EMR antimicrobial surveillance system, used alongside standard 48-hour prospective audit and feedback.
audits.r2: Intervention rate improved to 52.3% (p<0.001), a +2.2% difference per month; score subgroup (n=312) intervention rate 52.6% vs 40.9% for standard 48-hour review (p<0.0001).

audits.t: P-1788. Impact of standardized audit and feedback script and guide to reduce empiric fluoroquinolone use at two community hospitals
audits.st: Institutional target to reduce empiric fluoroquinolone use where local susceptibility is below guideline recommendations (no numeric target stated)
audits.f: 71 documented pharmacist interventions (average 6/month); acceptance rate 80%; monthly average DOT/1,000 patient-days 41.
audits.c: Standardised script and guide used by pharmacists during daily prospective audit and feedback of fluoroquinolones (implemented May 2023).
audits.r2: 240 documented interventions (average 20/month, +16/month increase); acceptance rate 86%; monthly average DOT/1,000 patient-days fell to 31 (a decrease of 10, p<0.05).

audits.t: P-1816. Stepwise Implementation of an Antimicrobial Stewardship Prospective Audit and Feedback Intervention at a Large Academic Center in Canada
audits.st: Institutional guideline concordance (agent, regimen, duration) for restricted antibiotics (carbapenems, daptomycin, linezolid, tigecycline)
audits.f: 3604/5185 (70%) prescriptions optimally prescribed; of empiric prescriptions, 636/3789 (17%) not guideline-concordant by indication; recommendation acceptance rate 91%.
audits.c: Stepwise implementation of prospective audit and feedback (PAF) targeting restricted antibiotics, rolled out in 16 discrete phases by inpatient programme readiness.

audits.t: P-237. The CLABSI (Central Line Audit by Staff Investigators) Intervention: Reducing Central Line Use in a Medical ICU using Physician-Led Prospective Audit and Feedback of Catheter Necessity
audits.tp: Central line necessity audit and feedback
audits.st: Locally defined criteria for central line necessity (irritant medication, renal replacement therapy, haemodynamic monitoring, TPN, no peripheral access); no external guideline named
audits.f: Central line device utilisation ratio (DUR, excl. HD lines) 0.48 line-days/patient-day; DUR incl. HD lines 0.61; CLABSI Standardized Infection Ratio (SIR) 2.84.
audits.c: Weekly physician-led electronic medical record audit and feedback of central line necessity, with text-message recommendation for removal sent to ICU team before rounds.
audits.r2: DUR (excl. HD) fell to 0.38 (20% decrease, p<0.0001); DUR (incl. HD) fell to 0.56 (8% decrease, p<0.0001); CLABSI SIR 2.83 (p=1.00, no change).

audits.t: P-844. Piloting Post Prescriptive Audit and Feedback for Outpatient Antimicrobial Prescriptions in a Tertiary Care Centre from Resource Limited Setting Effectively Reduced Quinolone Prescriptions for Respiratory Infections: Results from a Quasi experimental Study
audits.st: WHO AWaRe classification (aim to reduce Watch-group use, especially levofloxacin, and prioritise Access antibiotics)
audits.f: 46.4% of outpatient prescriptions were Watch antibiotics; high levofloxacin use (n=3,142).
audits.c: WHO AWaRe sensitisation (educational materials, tent cards, video), IT-based mandatory indication fields and AWaRe colour-coded EHR alerts, and a peer-comparison feedback tool with monthly audit of levofloxacin prescribing.
audits.r2: Around 95% reduction in levofloxacin prescribing post-intervention.

audits.t: P-883. A Prospective Audit of Discharge Antibiotic Prescribing: Patterns, Indications, and Stewardship Insights from a Tertiary Care Center
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 782/1607 (48.7%) discharge summaries included antibiotic prescriptions; 79% oral, 16% IV; empirical therapy most frequent (55%, mean 5.2 days), then prophylactic (30%, mean 3.8 days) and definitive (22%, mean 6.1 days); AWaRe categories: Access 45.7%, Watch 53.4%, Reserve 2.5%.

audits.t: P-935. A Mobile-Based Platform for Real-Time Antimicrobial Surveillance, Prescribing Audit, and Stewardship Intervention Tracking in a Resource-Limited Indian Tertiary Care Hospital
audits.st: not reported (institutional guideline adherence measured, guideline not named)
audits.f: Inappropriate prescribing 30.7%; de-escalation within 72h 26.1%; guideline adherence 59.8%; IV-to-oral switch compliance 21.7%; recommendation acceptance 48.5%; median response time 14.2 hours.
audits.c: Mobile-based antimicrobial stewardship platform enabling daily audit, IV-to-oral switch tracking, escalation alerts, and prescriber feedback via digital workflow.
audits.r2: Inappropriate prescribing fell to 18.2% (p<0.001); de-escalation to 55.8% (adjusted OR 3.55); guideline adherence 83.9%; IV-to-oral switch 50.1%; acceptance 82.3%; median response time 4.4 hours (log-rank p<0.001).

audits.t: P-965. Effectiveness of Augmented Prospective Audit and Feedback in Reducing Carbapenem Use Following Discontinuation of Preauthorization
audits.tp: Carbapenem stewardship prospective audit and feedback
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 25.0% (6/24) of noncompliant patients discontinued or modified carbapenem within 7 days.
audits.c: Augmented prospective audit and feedback (compliance monitoring, ward rounds, follow-up feedback), introduced after ASP suspension caused by a nationwide medical strike.
audits.r2: Discontinuation rate rose to 58.5% (31/53, p=0.008); carbapenem DOT decreased by a monthly 7.174 DOT (95% CI -13.014 to -1.334, p=0.017), a relative reduction of 30.9%.

audits.t: P-971. Adaptation of an Antimicrobial Scoring System to Optimize Prospective Audit and Feedback in a Large Academic Pediatric Hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 530 interventions from 8,503 patient reviews (6% intervention rate); ICU interventions 215, non-ICU 315.
audits.c: Implementation of an Epic-integrated antimicrobial stewardship scoring system (April 2023) to prioritise patients for prospective audit and feedback, following earlier 'handshake stewardship' in ICUs (July 2022).
audits.r2: 1,102 interventions from 6,916 patient reviews (16% intervention rate); ICU interventions rose to 526 (145% increase), non-ICU to 576 (83% increase).

audits.t: P-1356. Cross Sectional Audit and Prospective Study of AWaRe Antibiotics in Three Tertiary Care Hospitals
audits.st: WHO AWaRe classification (Access, Watch, Reserve; no numeric compliance target stated)
audits.f: 43% (163/376) prescribed an AWaRe-classified antibiotic; of those, Access 18% (30), Watch 84% (137), Reserve 12% (20).

audits.t: P-2019. Improving Biomedical Waste Segregation Through the Implementation of a QR Code–Enabled Mobile Audit and Alert System: A Quality Improvement Study in a Tertiary Care Hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline biomedical waste segregation compliance 68.4%.
audits.c: QR code-enabled mobile audit and alert system installed at waste disposal points in 12 high-risk areas, with automated real-time alerts to Infection Control Nurse and Unit Supervisor for noncompliance.
audits.r2: Compliance improved to 91.2% (p<0.001); category mismatch violations reduced by 72%; median response time to noncompliance alerts decreased from 8 hours to 1.5 hours.

audits.t: 1155. CAUTI Path to Zero: A Triple-Pronged Approach to Minding Our Pees and Cues
audits.st: NHSN Standardized Infection Ratio target of 0.78 or below (50th percentile); aim to reduce CAUTIs by 25%
audits.f: CAUTI SIR 0.990 (Clements University Hospital, CUH), 1.224 (Zale-Lipshy, ZL); 38 CAUTIs in 2017; average catheter dwell time 51 hours (CUH, excl. urology), 40 hours (ZL).
audits.c: Streamlined insertion indications, prompt catheter removal, alternative care pathways (in-and-out protocols, bladder scanners, female external catheters), and daily nursing-led necessity audits.
audits.r2: CAUTI SIR fell to 0.818 (CUH) and 0.496 (ZL); CAUTIs fell 34% from 38 to 25, exceeding the 25% reduction goal.

audits.t: 2083. A Targeted Remote Audit and Feedback Intervention Utilizing a Local Non-ID Trained Pharmacist
audits.tp: Ertapenem stewardship remote audit and feedback
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 51 unique patients received ertapenem in the month prior to intervention; 30 prescribers ordered ertapenem that month.
audits.c: Remote tele-stewardship collaboration: central ID physician/pharmacist reviewed charts with a local non-ID-trained critical care pharmacist, who made all interventions.
audits.r2: Median ertapenem usage (DOT/1,000 patient-days) dropped 55%; median purchasing cost decreased 73%; 35 patients/month and 17 prescribers/month on average post-intervention; overall intervention acceptance rate 88%.

audits.t: 1057. The Impact of Temporary Suspensions of an Antimicrobial Stewardship Audit and Feedback Program on Antimicrobial Utilization of General Internal Medicine Inpatients
audits.tp: Antimicrobial stewardship audit and feedback suspension impact
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Comparing nonactive-AAF vs active-AAF: significant changes in mean normalised DDD/1,000 patient-days for total antimicrobials (-19%), antipseudomonals (-21%), fluoroquinolones (-41%), and first-generation beta-lactams (-30%), all p<0.05 favouring active AAF.
audits.c: Temporary suspensions of an existing antimicrobial stewardship audit-and-feedback (AAF) programme due to human resource limitations.

audits.t: 1071. Implementation and Impact of an Antimicrobial Tier Structure Along with Prospective Audit and Feedback at a Large Health System: Collaborations for Care Transformation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average Tier 3/4 antimicrobial DOT/1,000 days present 89; cost $9.83 per adjusted patient-day.
audits.c: Implementation of a hospital-wide antimicrobial tier structure policy, with prospective audit and feedback performed jointly by pharmacists and transformation medical directors.
audits.r2: Average Tier 3/4 DOT/1,000 days present fell to 70 (21.3% decrease, p=0.001); cost fell to $7.27 (26% decrease, p<0.001); hospital-acquired C. difficile infections decreased 14% (p=0.41, nonsignificant).

audits.t: Improving early referrals for inflammatory arthritis through primary care engagement: a quality improvement initiative
audits.st: Standardised referral criteria co-developed with primary care physicians (locally developed, not a named national standard)
audits.f: Median referral time 51 days.
audits.c: Direct/rapid-access referral pathway plus electronic consultations (e-consults), concise referral guidelines and targeted training materials introduced in response to a PCP survey.
audits.r2: Median referral time decreased to 15 days, although only 21% of referrals met eligibility criteria.

audits.t: P65 Exploring ethnic disparities in early arthritis care
audits.tp: Ethnic disparities in early inflammatory arthritis care (NEIAA)
audits.st: National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit (NEIAA) against the seven NICE quality indicators for rheumatoid arthritis
audits.f: 124/471 (26%) had early inflammatory arthritis (34 non-white, 80 white); standards 1,2,3,6 had equiproportionate attainment; standards 4 (education) and 5 (agreed treatment target) showed fewer non-white patients meeting the target; standard 5 most disparate: 83% white vs 47% non-white had an agreed target (OR 5.6, 95% CI 2.2-14.1).

audits.t: E022 Reducing the number of rejected inpatient referrals to the rheumatology department at a district general hospital: a quality improvement project
audits.st: British Society for Rheumatology (BSR) referral criteria; target to reduce rejected referrals from 29.4% to 15% over 6 months
audits.f: 10/34 (29.4%) inpatient referrals rejected.
audits.c: Presentations at medical staff meetings on BSR referral criteria and display of posters summarising referral criteria across medical wards.

audits.t: P036 A single-service audit of non-invasive ventilation in myotonic dystrophy
audits.tp: Non-invasive ventilation service in myotonic dystrophy
audits.st: Consensus-Based Care Recommendations for Pulmonologists Treating Adults with Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1
audits.f: PAP prescription in 62 patients (43 BiPAP, 16 CPAP) was 85% compliant with consensus-based initiation recommendations; treatment uptake and adherence in approximately 50% of the cohort.

audits.t: Remifentanil Patient-controlled Analgesia in Labour: 6-Year Audit of Outcome Data of the RemiPCA SAFE Network (2010-2015)
audits.tp: Remifentanil PCA outcomes monitoring in labour
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Cardiac Arrest in Obstetric Patients Receiving Anesthetic Care: Results From the 7th National Audit Project of the Royal College of Anaesthetists
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Adherence to Rh Immune Globulin Prophylaxis Guidelines: An Audit of a Modern Obstetric Cohort [34Q]
audits.st: Guidelines for postpartum Rh immune globulin (RhIG) prophylaxis and fetomaternal haemorrhage (FMH) screening
audits.f: Of Rh-negative women eligible for RhIG, 97.7% received it and 98.9% were screened for FMH; of those ineligible, 4.6% inappropriately received RhIG and 91.9% were incorrectly screened for FMH; FMH evidence found in 26.6% of Rh-negative women, with 1.7% requiring additional RhIG

audits.t: Simple steps towards improving safety in obstetric airway management
audits.tp: Videolaryngoscope use in obstetric general anaesthesia
audits.st: Obstetric Anaesthetists' Association and Difficult Airway Society guideline that a videolaryngoscope should be immediately available for all obstetric general anaesthetics
audits.f: Videolaryngoscope use was 60%; low flow nasal oxygen use was 48%
audits.c: Introduction of an intubation checklist (December 2020) and multidisciplinary staff training (August 2021)
audits.r2: Videolaryngoscope use increased to 94% (88% in 2021); low flow nasal oxygen use increased to 90%; ramped positioning 97% (from 95% in 2021); checklist use 92% (from 63% in 2021); 94% first pass intubation success overall, only 0.9% needing three attempts

audits.t: Audit on physicians’ adherence with the WHO analgesic ladder to treat postoperative pain
audits.st: WHO analgesic ladder
audits.f: Pain severity: mild 18 (15%), moderate 51 (42.5%), severe 51 (42.5%); pain assessment done for only 3 (2.5%); 33 (27.5%) treated per the WHO analgesic ladder; 45 (37.5%) received no analgesia despite pain; no severe-pain patients received strong opioids.

audits.t: Audit on the assessment of the practice of storage, labeling, and usage of anesthetic medications in the operation theaters at a comprehensive specialized hospital, 2024: observational study
audits.tp: Anaesthetic medication storage and labelling practice
