audits.st: not reported (locally designed standards for storage, labelling and usage of anaesthetic medications, no named external guideline)
audits.f: No criterion was 100% accomplished; induction agent labelling had the highest accomplishment at 48 (77.4%); practices entirely unimplemented included swabbing vial tops, secure IV potassium storage, flushing the IV cannula, and reporting medication incidents in departmental meetings.

audits.t: Clinical audit on phlebotomy practices at comprehensive and specialized hospital, Ethiopia; cross-sectional study
audits.st: CLSI H3-A6 guidelines (25-item structured checklist)
audits.f: No healthcare worker fully adhered to all CLSI standards; 85% checked patient identity but only 46.7% correctly verified patients; hand hygiene entirely absent prior to procedures; 36.7% failed to disinfect the puncture site properly, 78.3% touched the site after disinfection; 58.3% uncapped needles improperly, 68.7% handled syringes one-handed, 20% failed to dispose of sharps correctly.

audits.t: Implementation of a Shielding Guideline for Pediatric Patients Receiving Intraoperative Ionizing Radiation
audits.tp: Intraoperative radiation shielding for paediatric patients
audits.st: not reported (locally implemented shielding guideline)
audits.f: not reported (baseline shield placement proportions not given numerically; staff sample n=9).
audits.c: Implementation of an intraoperative shielding guideline with staff education for pediatric intraoperative staff.
audits.r2: Statistically significant improvement in shield placements for thyroid, gonads, and breast tissue (p<.05); staff confidence in gonad shield placement improved (p=.013); self-reported frequency of gonad shield use improved (p=.032); knowledge scores improved nonsignificantly (p=.076); staff sample n=6.

audits.t: Implementation of an ICU Bundle: An Interprofessional Quality Improvement Project to Enhance Delirium Management and Monitor Delirium Prevalence in a Single PICU*
audits.st: Universal delirium screening with the Cornell Assessment of Pediatric Delirium (revised) tool
audits.f: 140 patients (17%) had delirium (Cornell score >=9 for >=48 hours); 74% of delirium-positive patients were mechanically ventilated
audits.c: Multidisciplinary ICU bundle using PDSA cycles: delirium protocol (Dec 2013), sedation protocol (Oct 2014), and early mobilisation protocol (Jun 2015), with staff education and case conferences
audits.r2: Mean delirium rate was 19.3% ten months after the delirium protocol; after the sedation and early mobilisation protocols it fell to 11.84%

audits.t: Practice Change From Intermittent Medication Boluses to Bolusing From a Continuous Infusion in Pediatric Critical Care: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Medication bolus timing practice in PICU
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Nursing satisfaction was 19.3% pre-implementation
audits.c: Practice change from administering bolus doses from an automated dispensing machine to bolusing directly from the continuous infusion
audits.r2: Time from decision to bolus infusing decreased by 169 seconds (p<0.01); nursing satisfaction increased to 100%; annualised cost avoidance was $124,160; barcode scanning compliance decreased slightly (1.4% for patients, 1% for medications)

audits.t: Comparison of Pediatric Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Quality in Classic Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Events Using Video Review*
audits.tp: CPR quality in classic versus extracorporeal resuscitation
audits.st: Resuscitation quality endpoints: end-tidal CO2 >=15 mmHg, diastolic blood pressure >=30 mmHg, chest compression fraction >80%, compression rate 100-120/min
audits.f: Classic CPR (11 events, 87.5 min) had ETCO2 >=15 mmHg in 56% of epochs vs 6.2% for extracorporeal CPR (p=0.01); classic CPR had compression rate 112/min vs 134/min for extracorporeal CPR (p<0.001); diastolic BP >=30 mmHg compliance was 38% (classic) vs 30% (extracorporeal)

audits.t: Protocol-Driven Management of Convulsive Status Epilepticus at a Tertiary Children’s Hospital: A Quality Improvement Initiative
audits.tp: Time to second-line anti-seizure medication in status epilepticus
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median time to administration of second-line anti-seizure medication was 52 minutes; total seizure time was 65 minutes
audits.c: Standardised treatment protocol uploaded to the hospital intranet, addition of anti-seizure medications to the Pyxis system, and a standardised order set in the electronic medical record, via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Median time to second-line medication decreased to 21 minutes (p=0.001), a 60% reduction; total seizure time decreased to 31 minutes (p=0.09, not statistically significant)

audits.t: Targeted Temperature Management After Pediatric Cardiac Arrest: A Quality Improvement Program With Multidisciplinary Implementation in the PICU
audits.tp: Targeted temperature management bundle after paediatric cardiac arrest
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median (IQR) percentage of febrile (>38C) time per patient was 7% (0-13%); 21/29 patients had fever at any time
audits.c: Targeted temperature management bundle: standard temperature goals, cooling blanket training, scheduled antipyretics, shivering management algorithm, and standardised EHR orders
audits.r2: Median febrile time decreased to 0% (IQR 0-3%, p<0.001); 16/46 patients had fever at any time (mean reduction 37%, 95% CI 13.8-54.8%, p=0.002); no significant association with hypothermia (<35C)

audits.t: Reduced Severity of Arterial Catheter-Associated Proximal Ischemic Injuries Through a Quality Improvement Initiative
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 11 severe arterial catheter-associated proximal ischaemic injuries (ACAPII) occurred prior to the QI project
audits.c: Phase I: defining ACAPII and daily rounding by a dedicated vascular access team (2021); Phase II: standardised recommendations including topical nitroglycerin ointment for mild injuries (2022)
audits.r2: During phase I, ACAPII increased to 35 (318% vs prior year); cumulative severe ACAPII incidence fell from a peak of 5.65 per 1000 line-days (April 2021) to 2.11 per 1000 line-days (December 2022); arterial line-days per catheter increased during phase II with topical nitroglycerin use (p<0.01)

audits.t: Stop the Clot: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce the Rate of Venous Thromboembolism in the PICU
audits.tp: Hospital-acquired venous thromboembolism reduction in PICU
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline hospital-acquired VTE (HA-VTE) rate was 2.07 per 1000 patient days; pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis was provided in 36% of at-risk patients
audits.c: Screening tool to identify patients at risk of VTE and provide thromboprophylaxis recommendations, addressing provider knowledge gaps and central line duration/location
audits.r2: HA-VTE rate decreased to 1.14 per 1000 patient days; pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis increased to 42%; central venous catheter days decreased from 43% to 31% of PICU patient days; two clinically relevant non-major bleeding events occurred

audits.t: Increasing Nurse-Led Mobilization of Critically Ill Children Through In Situ Simulation: A Quality Improvement Initiative
audits.tp: Nurse-led early mobilisation of critically ill children
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median number of nurse-led mobilisations per patient per 12-hour shift was 5; nurse self-efficacy in mobilising critically ill children was 67%
audits.c: In situ early-mobility simulation session for PICU nurses
audits.r2: Median mobilisations per patient per shift increased to 6 (p=0.02); simulation participation associated with an increase of 1.9 mobilisations per patient per shift after adjustment (p=0.004); nursing knowledge of mobility levels improved (p=0.004); self-efficacy rose to 93% (p<0.001)

audits.t: Reducing Acute Kidney Injury in Critically Ill Pediatric Patients: Quality Improvement Project Targeting Nephrotoxic Medication Exposures
audits.tp: Nephrotoxic medication exposure and acute kidney injury reduction
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Nephrotoxic medication (NTM) exposure rate was 30.6 per 1000 patient-days; NTM-associated AKI (NAKI) rate was 5.6 per 1000 patient-days
audits.c: Three-phase strategy: pharmacist-led monthly education for residents (phase 1), informational handout at orientations (phase 2), and daily pharmacist notifications to attending physicians for NTM exposures with monitoring recommendations (phase 3)
audits.r2: NTM exposure rate declined to 26.9 per 1000 patient-days (12.4% reduction); NAKI rate decreased to 2.5 per 1000 patient-days (55% reduction)

audits.t: Evolution to an Electronic Incentivized Kamishibai card System
audits.tp: Electronic Kamishibai card compliance tracking system
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean 127 K-cards completed per month for 11 hospital-acquired conditions across 10 inpatient units.
audits.c: Conversion from a standard paper Kamishibai card (K-card) system to an incentivised electronic K-card system built in REDCap, integrated with the infection prevention team's Quickbase tool.
audits.r2: Mean K-cards completed per month rose to 180 (a 41% increase) for the same scope of conditions and units.

audits.t: Delivering high quality documentation on operative consent forms: a UK major trauma center Quality Improvement Project
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons guidelines on full, accurate and legible completion of consent forms
audits.f: Average completion of the 3 outcome measures 59%; legibility 62%; omission of abbreviations 33%; patient signature 81%.
audits.c: Four weekly interventions targeting identified problem areas, accompanied by four further data collection cycles, using QI methodology.
audits.r2: Average completion rose to 93% and was sustained at 91% at 4-month re-audit; legibility rose to 100%; omission of abbreviations to 79%; patient signature to 100%.

audits.t: What about the Health of Ancillary Staff? A Management Audit
audits.st: Health at Work in the NHS initiative
audits.f: A recent audit found that very little health promotion activity had happened for ancillary staff despite national/regional priority

audits.t: Improving prescribing practice through pharmacy audit
audits.tp: Prescribing appropriateness in care of older people
audits.st: Appropriate prescribing of drugs of proven benefit and restriction of hazardous drugs in older people
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Pharmacy-led classic audit cycle applied to prescribing practice

audits.t: Medical Audit in the Quality Process: A Practical Implementation
audits.st: not reported

audits.c: Information technology (Hospital Information Support System) and training for medical audit

audits.t: Towards Integrative Audit: A Partnership for Quality
audits.st: Patient's Charter rights and standards

audits.t: Reviewing the value of clinical audit: is now the time for a change?
audits.tp: Value and methodology of clinical audit

audits.t: Developing Inter‐professional Training for Conflict Resolution ‐ A Scoping Audit and Training Pilot
audits.tp: Conflict resolution training provision in mental health trusts
audits.st: NHS Security Management Service (2004) national conflict-resolution training syllabus
audits.f: Wide variation found between trusts in conflict-resolution training organisation and monitoring; training co-ordinator role associated with improved governance of conflict-resolution training
audits.c: Inter-professional training pilot informed by the scoping audit findings

audits.t: Audit of the referrals to the psychology section of a mentally disordered offenders team
audits.tp: Referral patterns to psychology in a mentally disordered offenders team
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Clients referred for outpatient groups (not previously known to the team) had significantly higher non-attendance and drop-out rates than clients referred for other reasons; outpatients generally had higher non-attendance/drop-out than inpatients

audits.t: Audit of the NICE Guidelines for Schizophrenia in an NHS forensic psychiatric service
audits.tp: Adherence to NICE schizophrenia guidelines in forensic psychiatry
audits.st: NICE Guidelines for Schizophrenia (13 standards)
audits.f: The service met 3 of the 13 NICE standards for schizophrenia
audits.c: Recommendations implemented to improve practice on standards not met, including creative practice development

audits.t: The feasibility of a national audit of stroke
audits.tp: National organisational and process audit of stroke care
audits.st: 38 organisational standards and 71 process standards for stroke care
audits.f: Baseline round of the national organisational and process standards audit
audits.c: Individualised feedback reports comparing each trust's results to national data, and regional multidisciplinary workshops between audit rounds
audits.r2: 29 of 38 organisational standards improved (range 1-20%, median 5%); 64 of 71 process standards improved (range 1-20%, median 8%); inter-rater reliability kappa scores 0.49-0.87

audits.t: An audit of the care of patients with epilepsy in 15 general practices: lessons for Primary Care Groups
audits.tp: Epilepsy care audit in general practice
audits.st: Standards for care of patients with epilepsy, including annual review and care for women of child-bearing age
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Re-audit and review by questionnaire of epilepsy care standards
audits.r2: There were improvements in care, but less than half of the original participants completed the re-audit, which the authors attributed to the audit being over-complicated; review by questionnaire seemed acceptable to many patients

audits.t: Audit of 24‐hour pH monitoring in a large teaching hospital – are current guidelines being followed?
audits.tp: Appropriateness of referral for 24-hour pH monitoring
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for referral for 24-hour pH monitoring
audits.f: In the majority of cases guidelines were followed; referrals from non-gastrointestinal specialties accounted for 50% of cases where guidelines were not followed, and 40% of all referrals from non-gastrointestinal specialties failed to follow guidelines

audits.t: The “ASQUAM” programme: improving the standards of maternity care, using democratic prioritisation, guidelines and audit
audits.tp: Cyclical audit programme to improve maternity care standards (ASQUAM)
audits.st: 45 locally agreed standards for maternity care, chosen 1994-1997
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Local guidelines, cyclical audit of cases, monthly feedback meetings, patient-specific reminders, and educational training sessions

audits.t: Being kind to babies: an audit of paediatric radiology for first urinary infections
audits.tp: Radiological investigation of first urinary tract infection
audits.st: Radiological protocol for investigation of first urinary tract infections
audits.f: 12 of 71 children with first UTI were investigated inadequately; these were younger (average age 16 months) and their paediatricians had modified the protocol to avoid invasive investigations

audits.t: Incomplete excision of basal cell carcinomas: an audit.
audits.tp: Basal cell carcinoma management and histology reporting
audits.st: National audit figures for incomplete excision rates of basal cell carcinoma
audits.f: Incomplete excision rate was 13.73% (7 of 51 BCCs), comparing favourably with national audit figures

audits.t: Learning from Rowan ward ‐ developing an audit tool to improve the systems and processes for quality of care and safety of service users
audits.tp: Developing a ward-level audit tool for quality and safety
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Development of an audit tool to assess and improve systems and processes of care and safety

audits.t: Audit of fidelity of clinicians to the Mental Capacity Act in the process of capacity assessment and arriving at best interests decisions
audits.tp: Fidelity to the Mental Capacity Act in capacity assessment
audits.st: Mental Capacity Act (MCA) principles for capacity assessment and best-interests decisions
audits.f: There were no designated folders for MCA-related issues; entries about the assessment process were minimal, with only patchy documentation of the legal criteria used; clinicians only partially followed MCA procedure for determining best interests

audits.t: The inappropriate placement of older people in nursing homes in England and Wales: a national audit
audits.tp: Appropriateness of nursing home placement for older people
audits.st: Needs-driven criteria for publicly funded admission to nursing homes
audits.f: No evidence of extensive inappropriate placement was found; extrapolation suggested 6,750 admissions could have coped in a more independent environment; inappropriately admitted residents were more likely to live alone, be female, elderly, and not have seen a geriatrician

audits.t: An audit of the management of emergency surgical admissions in Wales: are we keeping pace with the trend?
audits.st: Confidential Enquiry for Peri-operative Deaths (CEPOD) recommendation that an emergency theatre is available 24 hours a day.
audits.f: Telephone survey of hospitals in Wales; a consultant-led emergency service was provided by only 29 per cent of hospitals.
audits.r2: Repeat telephone survey; provision of a CEPOD theatre had markedly improved throughout Wales, though most hospitals' working patterns had been unable to change to reflect increased emergency work.

audits.t: “Event tree” approach for facilitating audit of ambulance cardiac services
audits.tp: Ambulance cardiac care audit (AMI and cardiac arrest)
audits.st: Local audit targets for recording heart rhythms, administering aspirin and intravenous cannulation in suspected AMI, and defibrillation/anti-arrhythmic management in cardiac arrest.
audits.f: Audit targets not achieved for recording heart rhythms in non-arrest cases, administering aspirin and IV cannulation; only one-third of non-arrest patients received all three procedures; survival rates to hospital were similar for defibrillated VF arrests regardless of anti-arrhythmic drugs.
audits.c: An "event tree" technique linked electronically to the audit database was used to structure and report the audit.

audits.t: An audit of an ADHD Assessment Clinic in light of NICE guidelines
audits.tp: ADHD assessment clinic audit against NICE guidance
audits.st: NICE guidelines (2000) on use of methylphenidate for ADHD, including shared care recommendations.
audits.f: 63 children seen in the first year; success in achieving multi-disciplinary assessments, supervised medication initiation and shared care with GPs, but problems with waiting times, follow-up of psychometric screening abnormalities, physical screening before medication, and communication with schools.
audits.c: Changes were being implemented to address the identified problem areas (waiting times, screening follow-up, communication with schools).

audits.t: Quality and cost improvement in neonatal prescribing through clinical audit
audits.st: Desirable gentamicin level range: trough <=2 mg/L, peak 5-10 mg/L.
audits.f: Loop 1 (retrospective): 48 per cent of trough and 51 per cent of peak levels outside the desirable range; mean (±SD) trough 2.16 (±1.04) mg/L, peak 5.05 (±1.87) mg/L.
audits.c: Changes made to gentamicin dosing/monitoring regime following loop 1 (quality and cost improvement measures for prescribing and therapeutic drug monitoring).
audits.r2: Loop 2 (prospective): trough 15 per cent and peak 29 per cent outside range, mean trough 1.30 (±0.63) mg/L, peak 6.64 (±2.48) mg/L; improved further in loop 3 (trough 11 per cent, peak 26 per cent outside range, mean trough 1.23 (±0.62) mg/L, peak 6.2 (±1.81) mg/L). Doses required reduced by one-third to 50 per cent, and gentamicin discontinued before TDM was necessary in 27 per cent of cases.

audits.t: An audit investigating documentation of hospital urethral catheterisation and the improvements using proforma stickers
audits.st: Locally devised standards for documentation of urethral catheterisation set by the urology department.
audits.f: Only 3 per cent full documentation of catheterisation standards in the initial audit.
audits.c: Proforma catheterisation stickers were produced and distributed throughout the hospital wards.
audits.r2: 55 per cent usage rate of stickers; of notes with stickers, 84 per cent had full documentation compared with only 2 per cent without stickers.

audits.t: Paediatric surgery fluid management audit (January‐June 2004), John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford
audits.st: Target intravenous fluid regimen for paediatric surgery patients post-operatively.
audits.f: Patients undergoing major abdominal surgery received larger amounts of fluid than the target regimen; urine outputs normal to high; post-operative sodium levels normal in all patients.
audits.c: Interdepartmental seminars, a national survey of practice, and revision of fluid management protocols resulted from the audit.

audits.t: Audit of the quality of documentation in an eye casualty department
audits.st: Locally agreed standards for quality of documentation based on criteria integral to the patient pathway.
audits.f: 145 records audited over four cycles in nine months; department performed consistently well in most indicators, with some poorly performing indicators identified.
audits.c: Changes in practice including education and document redesign.
audits.r2: All but one of the poorly performing indicators improved with the changes in practice; improvements sustained with repeated re-audit.

audits.t: Effect of audit on critically ill pregnant women
audits.tp: Critically ill pregnant women outcomes with audit and feedback
audits.st: Local management protocols for critically ill pregnant women, supported by regular audit and feedback.
audits.f: Prevalence of critically ill pregnant women 8.40/1,000 births; maternal mortality ratio 133.2/100,000 births; mortality index 15.9 per cent; average dysfunctional organ systems per patient 1.41 (original protocol).
audits.c: Introduction of new management protocols supported by regular audit and feedback.
audits.r2: Prevalence increased to 10.22/1,000 births (p<0.014); MMR reduced to 104.9/100,000 births (OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.51-1.2); mortality index reduced to 10.3 per cent; average dysfunctional organ systems per patient 1.19; significant reductions in renal, metabolic and cerebral dysfunction.

audits.t: What were the lessons learned from implementing clinical audit in Latin America?
audits.tp: Clinical audit implementation for TB diagnosis in low-income settings
audits.st: Locally selected audit criteria for tuberculosis diagnosis, compared with agreed standards.
audits.f: 22 health centres completed a minimum of two audit cycles for TB diagnosis; local audit committees selected criteria, collected data and compared performance against agreed standards.
audits.c: Development of clinical audit process and local audit committees; recommended addressing clinical guidelines and routine data needs.

audits.t: Consistently inconsistent – an audit of laparoscopic cholecystectomy consent practice
audits.st: Local standard for quality and consistency of documented informed consent for laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
audits.f: 100 consent forms before introduction of patient information leaflet: consultant staff obtained only 27 per cent of consent; 64 per cent of consent taken on morning of surgery; only 2 per cent had documented evidence of receiving the information leaflet.
audits.c: Introduction of a detailed pre-operative patient information leaflet.
audits.r2: 100 consent forms after introduction of the leaflet: consent remained inconsistent and the leaflet did not improve documentation of risk required for informed consent.

audits.t: Audit of alcohol detoxification at Leeds Addiction Unit
audits.st: not reported (locally defined audit standard for detoxification practice)
audits.f: At 3 months post-detoxification, 23% had dropped out of treatment; 31% remained completely abstinent; 10% were drinking within safe limits.
audits.r2: Drop-out fell to 15%; abstinence rose to 36%; drinking within safe limits rose to 22%.

audits.t: From knife to paper: an audit of surgical communication
audits.st: 26-item checklist for operation note content.
audits.f: 404 operations identified, 45 excluded, 359 analysed; time of procedure (1 per cent), ASA grade (1 per cent) and blood loss (5 per cent) poorly reported; clinical indication documented in 52 per cent and post-operative instructions in 66 per cent; registrar notes scored higher than consultant notes on content (15.8 vs 13.5, p<0.001) and legibility (OR 19.0, 95% CI 11.6-31.2, p<0.001).

audits.t: Improving trainee psychiatrist's handover: standard setting and audit
audits.st: Trust-wide Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for handover.
audits.f: Handing over "active problems" perceived to occur frequently in 93.75 per cent; trainee satisfaction with handover 57 per cent.
audits.c: Development of a Trust-wide Standard Operating Procedure for handover.
audits.r2: 2009: 100 per cent for active problems, 98 per cent for "problems which may arise", satisfaction 75 per cent; 2010: deteriorated to 93 per cent for active problems and 69 per cent for problems which may arise, satisfaction improved to 87 per cent (X2=3.7, df=2, p=0.16).

audits.t: Audit of prescribing safety in a department of medicine for the elderly
audits.st: Agreed local criteria for safe prescribing practice.
audits.f: Initial audit of prescribing habits using agreed criteria; deficiencies identified, leading to recommendations for change.
audits.c: Recommendations made for change after the initial audit, emphasising safe prescribing within a multi-disciplinary setting.
audits.r2: Considerable improvements in legibility of prescriptions and recording of presence or absence of drug allergies.

audits.t: Audit of antenatal corticosteroid treatment in the South West
audits.tp: Antenatal corticosteroid treatment for preterm birth
audits.st: Local/national standard for administering antenatal corticosteroids for preterm birth.
audits.f: Of 550 preterm births examined, corticosteroids given in 301 (64%), ranging from 49-76% across hospitals; extremely premature babies less likely to receive steroids (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.28-1.03); complications occurred in 36% of babies whose mothers did not receive steroids; documentation of reasons for non-administration was poor.

audits.t: Accuracy of medication records for patients with learning difficulties: an interface audit between the Phoenix NHS Trust and Avon Primary Care Audit Group
audits.tp: Medication record accuracy for patients with learning difficulties
audits.st: Local interface audit standard for consistency of medication records between trust and primary care.
audits.f: Interface audit found no major discrepancies, but 27 cases (30%) of minor inconsistencies in medication records were uncovered.
audits.c: Recommendation that the home's drug chart accompanies patients for all medical contacts and is used to update all other medication records.

audits.t: Focusing on risk: a simple audit study can have a major impact on clinical practice
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: A two-part observational audit identified weak areas in the systems associated with the use of infusion devices.
audits.c: Actions implemented to rectify identified weaknesses and reduce risk to patients and staff.

audits.t: Breast cancer: development of a patient‐focused audit tool
audits.tp: Patient-focused breast cancer care audit tool
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 123 women with breast cancer audited using GP notes combined with patient questionnaires and interviews; combined approach found broadly similar information from both techniques and good coverage of interface issues.

audits.t: Audit as a method of reducing benzodiazepine prescribing in general practice
audits.st: Local audit standard to reduce benzodiazepine prescribing, assessed via Prescribing Analyses and Cost (PACT) data.
audits.f: 15 practices (87,902 patients) took part in an audit of benzodiazepine prescribing out of 291,993 patients registered with 55 practices in the district.
audits.c: Audit of benzodiazepine prescribing with feedback to participating GPs.
audits.r2: Significant reduction in defined daily doses dispensed for temazepam, nitrazepam and lorazepam during the audit; significantly greater reduction in items prescribed by participating doctors than non-participating colleagues.

audits.t: Electroconvulsive therapy audit
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists guidelines for ECT practice.
audits.f: Retrospective case note review plus concurrent observation of ECT practice; ECT practice generally of good standard.
audits.c: An education and training programme designed to correct practice deficiencies, implemented between the two phases.
audits.r2: Significant reduction in sub-optimal ventilation and significant reduction in unsatisfactory seizures after the training programme.

audits.t: An audit of anticoagulant guidelines: the relative influence of education, presentation and complexity of guidelines on compliance
audits.st: Locally introduced anticoagulant guidelines, audited on three occasions.
audits.f: First audit; guidelines introduced due to high incidence of bleeding complications.
audits.c: Changes made to educational input, presentation of the guidelines, and the guidelines themselves (e.g. using low molecular weight heparin for DVT) between audits.
audits.r2: Even with an intensive continuing education programme, the proforma work sheets were used in only 41 per cent of patients; compliance was good when used, better than when not used. Changing presentation/format did not materially influence compliance, but simplifying guidelines led to considerable improvement.

audits.t: Pain relief in the recovery room: an audit of current practice and a proposed solution
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 334 patients grouped as comfortable/pain/severe pain; 14% awoke from anaesthesia in pain and 10% discharged to the ward in pain; 37% of patients using PCA discharged in pain, 63% of these had not received a loading dose; 48% receiving sole intramuscular opioid discharged in pain; 90% receiving nurse-administered prn IV bolus opioids discharged comfortable.
audits.c: An algorithm developed for administration of loading doses of intravenous opioids in the recovery unit, used by recovery nursing staff prior to PCA or other analgesic methods.
audits.r2: An early re-audit established that the algorithm became widely adopted by anaesthetists, was safe and produced comparable discharge pain scores.

audits.t: Audit of a dedicated osteoporosis clinic
audits.st: Locally set standards for waiting time, communication, and standard of advice/treatment.
audits.f: 154 patients referred (150 female); 118 required bone density measurement and 34% had osteoporosis. GPs satisfied with waiting time and standard of advice/treatment (>90%), but the standard set for communication was not achieved.
audits.c: Improvements subsequently made to address deficiencies identified (including inadequate premises).

audits.t: Guidelines for coronary heart disease in general practice. Practice‐based audit: results from a dissemination and implementation programme
audits.tp: Coronary heart disease guideline implementation in general practice
audits.st: Locally developed coronary heart disease guidelines linked to research evidence (East London Clinical Guidelines Project).
audits.f: Baseline audit result reported (details not stated in abstract).
audits.c: Practice-based educational sessions combined with audit to help practices implement the guidelines.
audits.r2: One-year audit results following facilitation and implementation of the guidelines (details not stated in abstract).

audits.t: Setting the records straight: a study of hospital medical records undertaken by the Audit Commission
audits.tp: Hospital medical records study by the Audit Commission
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Enabling clinical governance: a primary care audit of prescribing for heart failure in central Auckland, New Zealand
audits.tp: Heart failure prescribing in general practice
audits.st: Audit criteria for necessary prescribing for systolic heart failure, developed by modified Delphi approach based on the RAND Health Services utilisation study method.
audits.f: Audit criteria applied to medical notes of 70 patients with heart failure in 30 practices; use of the criteria was feasible and appeared valid; a high frequency of ACE inhibitor prescribing for heart failure was noted as an uncommon but plausible finding.

audits.t: 999 telephone triage: a comparison of UK ambulance nurse and paramedic case mix, outcomes and audit compliance
audits.tp: 999 telephone triage nurse vs paramedic audit compliance
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 21,076 cases and 728 audits reviewed; little difference in case mix or clinical outcomes between nurses and paramedics; paramedics had more highly compliant call audits and fewer non-compliant ones, but the difference was small in percentage terms.

audits.t: Use of prone position restraint within a mental health trust
audits.tp: Prone position restraint use in mental health care
audits.st: Current guidelines for management of challenging behaviour, with emphasis on physical restraint.
audits.f: Clinical audit found non-physical techniques used prior to physical restraint in the substantial majority of episodes; limited use of staff debriefs after physical restraint; a potential diagnostic link to likelihood of prone position restraint use.
audits.c: A quality improvement project undertaken in response to the audit findings.
audits.r2: Significant and sustained improvements in adherence to most standards following the quality improvement project.

audits.t: An audit of the quality and effectiveness of review meetings between core and higher psychiatry trainees and their educational supervisors
audits.tp: Educational supervision review meeting quality (psychiatry trainees)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 25 feedback forms received; trainees gave mostly positive feedback on process, content, supervisor and administration of review meetings, with suggestions for improvement (e.g. shorter, more clinically focused forms).

audits.t: Recognising and responding to abuse in the community: an audit of community nurses’ knowledge and confidence in Irelands mid-west region
audits.tp: Safeguarding adults knowledge and confidence audit
audits.st: not reported (national safeguarding policy, procedures and guidelines referenced generically)
audits.f: No respondents identified familiarity with all forms of abuse; confidence in reporting abuse varied significantly.

audits.t: Quality of asthma care at a university-based primary care clinic in Malaysia: An audit of process, structure and outcomes
audits.st: Locally set standard targets: 80 per cent for process and structure indicators, 100 per cent for outcome indicators (18 quality indicators).
audits.f: Retrospective audit of 433 adult asthma patients; all indicators failed to reach standard targets; documentation of asthma-specific information and availability of resources were deficient; prescription rates of inhaled reliever and preventer were substandard but reasonably high compared to targets.

audits.t: Impact of occupational therapy in an integrated adult social care service: Audit of Therapy Outcome Measure Findings
audits.tp: Occupational therapy outcome measurement in adult social care
audits.st: Local audit using the "Therapy Outcome Measure" (TOMs) standardised tool across four domains (impairment, activity, participation, wellbeing/carer wellbeing).
audits.f: 93% of clients showed improvement in at least one TOMs domain; 79% of activity scores, 20% of participation scores and 50% of wellbeing scores improved; 79% of carer wellbeing scores improved following occupational therapy.

audits.t: Workforce development in dementia care through education and training: an audit of two counties
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Organisational audit of current dementia training found considerable investment in dementia awareness training, but learning was not targeted, assessed or structured to ensure ongoing professional development.

audits.t: An audit of an Intensive Interaction service
audits.st: Recommended number of trained staff per team for Intensive Interaction provision.
audits.f: 96 per cent of Trust employees thought training was right for them; 81 per cent of house teams/services had at least three staff and a manager who had received Intensive Interaction training; three areas of concern identified: discussion in supervision, responsibility for it happening, and sharing knowledge with those connected to the service user.

audits.t: Assessment of cervical spine CT by an image quality audit using qualitative and quantitative methods
audits.tp: Cervical spine CT image quality audit
audits.st: RANZCR CT Image Quality Self-Audit worksheet.
audits.f: 20 studies (10 per protocol) assessed by 5 radiologists using blinded visual grading analysis; no statistically significant difference in image quality between protocols (VGAS 0.65 vs 0.73); Protocol 2 gave a statistically significant 35% dose reduction (p=0.020) with higher but not significantly different noise.

audits.t: Recovery of the glaucoma service after the COVID‐19 pandemic; Barnsley glaucoma audit
audits.tp: Glaucoma referral compliance with NICE guidelines
audits.st: NICE guidelines for glaucoma management (visual acuity, Goldmann applanation tonometry, pachymetry, perimetry, gonioscopy, OCT, family history)
audits.f: not reported (prior audit result not numerically stated beyond being lower than the current audit).
audits.c: Minimised virtual clinics during recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic to allow fuller in-person assessment.
audits.r2: Visual acuity, Goldmann applanation tonometry, and OCT optic disc all performed in 100%; 97% underwent standard automated perimetry and pachymetry; 87% had family history recorded and underwent gonioscopy; treatable maculopathy discovered in 40%; compliance with pachymetry, gonioscopy and family history recording was significantly higher than the 2020 audit.

audits.t: Clinical care and other categories posters: Clinical audit/Service evaluation
audits.tp: Diabetes control in children with comorbidities
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 119/226 (52.65%) with chronic comorbidities had mean HbA1c 73.65 mmol/mol vs 66.14 for the 107 (47.34%) without comorbidities (p<0.0001); CSII users had lower HbA1c (65.31) than MDI users (75.18, p=0.05); CGM users had HbA1c 65.86 vs FGM users 73.88 (p<0.0001).

audits.t: COMPLIANCE WITH LOCAL VTE PROPHYLAXIS GUIDELINES IN AN ACUTE MEDICAL UNIT – A CLINICAL AUDIT
audits.tp: VTE prophylaxis compliance in acute medical unit
audits.st: Local comprehensive VTE prophylaxis guidelines; hypothesised compliance rate exceeding 80%
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: RETROSPECTIVE CLINICAL AUDIT OF SPIROGRAM QUALITY
audits.st: American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society (ATS/ERS) acceptability and repeatability criteria
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Premedication: an audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Many patients received premedication at times inappropriate for it to be effective; regular medication was sometimes suddenly stopped preoperatively; prolonged fasting occurred in elective and emergency patients; benzodiazepines and opioids were prescribed most often; antacids, H2-blockers and prokinetics were used very little despite aspiration risk.

audits.t: Audit of pre‐operative starvation
audits.st: Hospital's official pre-operative starvation policy; literature-based recommendation of only 3 hours of fluid withdrawal necessary.
audits.f: Both adults and children starved significantly longer than the hospital's official policy required; mean starvation time for children almost 10 hours, longer than the 8 hours at which hypoglycaemia becomes a risk.

audits.t: An audit of the safety of an acute pain service
audits.st: Standard respiratory monitoring protocol (continuous pulse oximetry, hourly respiratory rate, sedation scoring, intermittent arterial blood gas sampling).
audits.f: 2509 consecutive patients audited; protocol detected 6 episodes of bradypnoea, 13 of hypercapnia, 23 of oxygen desaturation in 39 patients (1.8%); 2 patients required naloxone, none had long-term sequelae; hypotension in 4 patients (1.2%); postoperative nausea/vomiting in 723 (28.8%) and vomiting in 380 (15.1%).

audits.t: ASTHMA IN DARLEY DALE: GP AUDIT
audits.st: Locally set audit criteria for recording asthma-relevant data (diagnosis entry, smoking history, peak flow readings).
audits.f: First audit cycle before starting an asthma clinic in the practice.
audits.c: An asthma clinic was set up in the practice.
audits.r2: Significant improvements in recording of asthma diagnosis in the computerised summary record, smoking history and numbers of peak expiratory flow readings; ratio of average:best peak flow rate improved from 81% to 89% (not statistically significant); no objective clinical improvement (steroid/salbutamol use) demonstrated.

audits.t: An audit of dynamic function tests: errors in the timing of blood specimens
audits.tp: Dynamic endocrine function test blood sampling timing accuracy
audits.st: Prescribed protocol timing for blood sampling after a stimulus in dynamic endocrine tests.
audits.f: 152 investigation procedures comprising 791 planned specimens; 627 timing intervals analysable, of which 366 did not differ from the planned interval; 22% of specimens taken more than 10 minutes early/late, 6% more than 30 minutes early/late.
audits.c: A new request form for dynamic tests was designed to record both planned and actual sampling times.

audits.t: An audit of oestradiol levels and implant frequency in women undergoing subcutaneous implant therapy
audits.st: Local clinical policy: not to repeat oestradiol implants if serum E2 level >400pmol/l, aiming to restore premenopausal levels.
audits.f: 275 women received a total of 759.50mg E2 implants; median length of therapy 34.2 months, median 4 implants per patient; mean recorded serum E2 level 425±187pmol/l in women with more than four implants; no significant progressive rise in serum E2 with time/implant number.

audits.t: Fine Needle Aspiration of Palpable Breast Lumps: A 1‐Year Audit Using the Cytospin Method
audits.tp: Fine needle aspiration cytology of breast lumps (diagnostic performance)
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 407 FNAs from 393 women; detected 112 of 121 cancers (92.6%); overall inadequate rate 11.0%; absolute sensitivity 89.7%, complete sensitivity 96.6%, specificity 94.4%; no false positives.

audits.t: O‐1 10 YEAR AUDIT OF GLANDULAR CYTOLOGY REPORTS WITH SPECIAL REGARD TO THE EFFECT OF CONVERSION TO LBC
audits.tp: Glandular cytology reporting accuracy over time
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1996 glandular cytology reporting: 39 cases reported as glandular neoplasia; PPV for any significant pathology 51%; PPV for correctly identified lesion 21%.
audits.c: Conversion to Liquid Based Cytology (LBC), plus changes to laboratory staffing structure and improved training.
audits.r2: 29 cases reported; PPV for any significant pathology 93%; PPV for correctly identified lesion 83%; an upward trend in accurate detection of glandular lesions, particularly CGIN, over the 10-year period.

audits.t: O‐7 AUDIT OF THYROID FINE NEEDLE ASPIRATION CYTOLOGY: A PROBABILISTIC APPROACH
audits.tp: Thyroid fine needle aspiration cytology diagnostic categories
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 392 thyroid FNA specimens classified in 5 categories; 85 follow-up thyroidectomies correlated with histology: neoplasia/cancer rates were inadequate 28.5%/0%, benign 10.8%/5.4%, equivocal 58.1%/35.4%, suspicious 80%/80%, malignant 100%/100%.

audits.t: O‐9 AUDIT ON BK VIRUS DETECTION IN RENAL TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS
audits.tp: BK virus screening in renal transplant recipients
audits.st: Local surveillance protocol for screening renal transplant patients by urinary cytology and electron microscopy at weekly intervals.
audits.f: 55 new renal transplant recipients; up to 8 samples sent for urinary cytology from 47 patients and up to 7 for electron microscopy from 42 patients; 11 urinary cytology-positive, 1 electron microscopy-positive; samples sent inconsistently rather than for structured screening.
audits.c: A screening protocol was agreed following the audit.

audits.t: P‐12 A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT OF FINE NEEDLE ASPIRATION CYTOLOGY OF PANCREAS
audits.tp: Pancreatic fine needle aspiration cytology diagnostic accuracy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 73 patients underwent pancreatic FNAC; overall inadequate rate 12%, inconclusive 4%, benign 42%, suspicious 10%, malignant 32%; EUS-guided inadequate rate 5% (small group); 3 false negative cases; no false positives.

audits.t: P‐19 THE LABORATORY AND CLINICAL ADVANTAGES OF PROMPT CERVICAL SMEAR HISTOLOGY MISMATCH AUDIT
audits.st: ABC guidelines requiring correlation of cervical biopsy and smear results for calculating positive predictive values; NHSCSP recommendation for longer follow-up of high-grade CIN.
audits.f: 578 women with abnormal cytology referred to colposcopy had biopsies; 491 (83%) correlated within one grade; 51 (9%) smear undercalls, of which 29 (5%) upgraded on review; 36 (6%) smear overcalls, of which 7 were true overcalls; correlation increased to 91% after smear and histology review.
audits.c: Prompt mismatch review process including independent review of both smear and biopsy, with supplementary reports issued when histology was upgraded.

audits.t: P‐2 COMPLETING THE AUDIT CYCLE OF NON‐GYNAECOLOGIC CYTOLOGY TURNAROUND TIMES
audits.st: Guidelines set after a 2002 audit: turnaround times of 3 days for urgent, 5 days for routine and 10 days for specimens requiring ancillary tests, with electronic authorisation by the reporting pathologist before hard copy report issue.
audits.f: Average turnaround time for reporting non-gynaecologic cytology was 7 days, with wide variation between pathologists due to delayed electronic authorisation.
audits.c: Guidelines requiring electronic authorisation before hard copy report issue, and turnaround time targets, introduced following the 2002 audit.
audits.r2: 718 non-gynaecologic cases reported by two cytopathologists; mean turnaround time 3.7 calendar days; 25.2% reported within 1 day, 48.6% within 2 days; 84% within 5 days; 95% within 10 days.

audits.t: Audit of laparoscopic surgery for tubal pregnancy in a district general hospital
audits.st: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG) guidelines: 100% of appropriate cases to be managed with laparoscopic surgery.
audits.f: 38 cases of tubal pregnancy reviewed (of 52 identified, 5 excluded as not tubal pregnancy, 9 untraceable); 18% underwent appropriate laparotomy, 82% deemed suitable for operative laparoscopy, but only 39% of tubal pregnancies deemed suitable were actually managed by laparoscopic surgery.

audits.t: An audit of the technical quality of primary orthograde root canal treatment performed by undergraduate dental students
audits.tp: Root canal treatment technical quality by undergraduate students
audits.st: Technical quality criteria: root filling within 0-2mm of radiographic apex, no voids, uniform taper.
audits.f: 253 canals in 144 teeth assessed; overall 163 canals (64.4%) and 87 teeth (60.4%) classed as satisfactory; endodontic clinic teeth 71.4% satisfactory vs restorative clinic teeth 58.5% satisfactory.

audits.t: An audit of intra‐oral digital radiographs for endodontics
audits.st: Faculty of General Dental Practitioners (FGDP) guidelines: not less than 70% of images scoring excellent on a three-point quality scale.
audits.f: Phase 1: 50 exposures with Schick CDR system compared with 50 using Digora Optime; Schick images inferior quality; both systems failed the 70% excellent FGDP standard (Schick 55%, Digora 69%).
audits.c: Training provided to the operator between phases 2 and 3 to improve positioning and image quality with the Schick CDR system.
audits.r2: Phase 3 (after training): quality improved to 80% of radiographs scoring excellent, exceeding the 70% FGDP standard; recommended purchase of size 1 or 0 Schick sensors to further improve positioning.

audits.t: An audit of the technical quality of orthograde endodontic treatment performed by undergraduate dental students on an endodontic clinic
audits.st: Root filling within 0-2 mm of radiographic apex, absence of voids, uniform taper (local criteria)
audits.f: 394/504 canals (78.1%) and 155/216 teeth (72.4%) satisfactory; anterior 45/51 (88.2%), premolar 32/38 (82.4%), molar 317/415 (76.6%)

audits.t: R5 An audit of local compliance with general anaesthetic guidelines outlined for paediatric dentistry
audits.st: National guidelines on diagnosis, treatment planning and consent for dental general anaesthetic
audits.f: GA use was justified in line with guidelines in most cases but consent and treatment planning could be improved (numbers not reported)

audits.t: A programme to audit the use of urinary catheters
audits.st: Literature-derived criteria for appropriate urinary catheter use (local tool)
audits.f: All catheters were appropriate size, balloon and lumen; significant bacteriuria in 5/18 (28%) catheters in situ for 3 days; all 3 catheters in situ >10 days had significant bacteriuria

audits.t: Quality audit – a review of the literature concerning delivery of continence care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Acquisition and use of clinical data for audit and research
audits.tp: Clinical data quality for audit and research
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of dietary input into a hospital lipid clinic
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average 17% fall in blood cholesterol and 3.2 kg weight reduction in first 3 months after intensive dietary advice; cost of diet and drugs approx £60/year vs £35 for diet alone (£5.20 dietetic cost)

audits.t: Audit of nasogastric feeding practice at two acute hospitals: is early enteral feeding associated with reduced mortality and hospital stay?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Patients starved 0-5 days before NG feeding had lower mortality than those starved >5 days; duration of starvation positively correlated with NG feeding duration and hospital stay

audits.t: An audit designed to assess the need for planned pretreatment PEG placement in patients with stage III & stage IV oral cancer
audits.tp: Pretreatment PEG placement need in oral cancer
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Nonsurvivors: 65% tube fed <30 days, mean length of tube feeding 97 days overall; survivors: 70% tube fed <30 days, mean 72 days; dietary consistency of nonsurvivors worse than survivors throughout treatment

audits.t: A nutritional screening audit of new adult out‐patients with HIV
audits.st: NICE (2006) Clinical Guideline 32: nutrition screening should be done on all out-patients at first appointment
audits.f: Height and weight recorded in 49 (BMI calculated in only 28); amount/duration of weight loss recorded for only 8/7 patients; referral to dietitian indicated for 23 but only 10 had a planned appointment; HIV/malnutrition symptoms recorded by physician for 22% of patients

audits.t: An audit to evaluate the effect of staff training on the use of Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool
audits.st: NICE (2006): patients admitted to hospital should be routinely screened for malnutrition using MUST
audits.f: 54% (212/392) of patients' records had a correctly completed MUST form
audits.c: Regular training on nutritional screening for ward staff delivered by dietitians, later incorporated into trust mandatory training
audits.r2: 67% (288/432) of patients' records had a completed MUST form, a significant increase (P<0.001) compared with 2005

audits.t: Audit of the use of packed red blood cells in association with seven common surgical procedures.
audits.tp: Appropriate use of packed red blood cells in surgery
audits.st: Locally derived audit 'triggers' for packed red blood cell use in seven common surgical procedures
audits.f: Established patterns of PRBC use across seven surgical procedures, used to derive surgical blood order schedules, autologous donation targets and audit triggers
audits.r2: Results of an audit applying the derived triggers are reported

audits.t: Audit of Nurses‐ Adherence to Pre‐transfusion Checking
audits.st: Best practice recommendations for pre-transfusion bedside checking
audits.f: Checking blood unit for normal appearance: Haem/Onc 43%, PICU 11%; checking patient wristband: Haem/Onc 19%, PICU 68%
audits.c: Multifaceted educational intervention: posters, in-services, web-based clinical practice guidelines, audit feedback, and pre-transfusion checking reminders on compatibility report
audits.r2: Checking blood unit for normal appearance: Haem/Onc 81%, PICU 58%; checking patient wristband: Haem/Onc 81%, PICU 79%

audits.t: SI39 West of Scotland Blood Centre Audit of Hospital Compliance with Traceability Arrangements for Cross‐Matched Blood
audits.st: UK Blood Safety and Quality Regulations 2005, Regulation 8 (vein-to-vein traceability)
audits.f: Total returns 64% (199/311); 31% of returned transfer receipts incompletely documented; time of receipt not recorded on 65%, condition of blood not documented on 21%

audits.t: P12 An Audit of Fresh Frozen Plasma Transfusion Use in the Royal Hospitals Trust (RGHT)
audits.st: British Committee for Standards in Haematology (BCSH) guidelines for FFP use - 100% standard for appropriateness and documentation
audits.f: 93 (68%) appropriate, 44 (32%) inappropriate; indication documented in 73 (53%), clinical effectiveness documented in 52 (38%)

audits.t: AUDIT OF FROZEN SECTIONS ON BRAIN AND SPINAL CORD LESIONS IN TUEN MUN HOSPITAL 1992–1999
audits.st: Concordance between intraoperative frozen section and permanent section diagnosis (local performance review)
audits.f: Differing diagnoses on frozen vs permanent section in 50 cases (15.2%); specimens inadequate for diagnosis in 6 cases (1.8%); diagnosis deferred to permanent section in 5 cases (1.5%); multiple differential diagnoses given in 15 cases (4.6%)

audits.t: CRITERIA AUDIT OF PERCUTANEOUS NEPHROLITHOTOMIES
audits.st: Local criteria for percutaneous nephrolithotomy management (quality assurance criteria audit)
audits.f: Audit demonstrated the surgeons' learning curve, current standards achieved and changes in patient admission rate (specific figures not reported)

audits.t: GS04 CAN EVIDENCE BASED PROFORMA’S AND DEPARTMENTAL AUDIT IMPROVE THE MANAGEMENT OF ACUTE PANCREATITIS?
audits.st: Published international guidelines for management of acute pancreatitis
audits.f: CT scans performed in 76/168 (45%); definitive treatment for mild biliary pancreatitis in 36/65 (55%); mortality 9/168 (5%)
audits.c: Evidence-based proforma prospectively completed for all patients, plus interim analysis presented to department highlighting guideline deviations
audits.r2: CT scans reduced to 30/113 (27%, p=0.002); definitive treatment for mild biliary pancreatitis increased to 35/43 (81%, p=0.006); mortality reduced to 1/113 (1%, p=0.047)

audits.t: ML02 INFORMED CONSENT FOR VASCULAR INTERVENTION IS IMPROVED BY DEPARTMENTAL AUDIT
audits.st: Local departmental standard for documentation of consent process for vascular procedures
audits.f: Consent form signed by a consultant in 2 (4%) cases
audits.c: Departmental audit and feedback of consent documentation practice
audits.r2: Consent form signed by consultant in 16 (32%) cases (p<0.013); risks documented in 31 (62%) surgical notes and 34 (69.4%) radiological notes

audits.t: SO16P MULTIDISCIPLINARY CANCER CARE IN AUSTRALIA: AN AUDIT OF CURRENT UPTAKE
audits.st: National Breast Cancer Centre Principles of Multidisciplinary Care
audits.f: National telephone survey audit of multidisciplinary care activity across five tumour streams (breast, gynaecological, lung, colorectal, prostate); results described as identifying gaps in uptake but specific figures not given

audits.t: ML03P CLINICAL HANDOVER: A NATIONAL AUDIT OF PRACTICE IN NEW ZEALAND HOSPITALS
audits.st: Local structured handover questionnaire criteria (national snapshot audit)
audits.f: Handovers completed without interruption for non-urgent tasks: 9%
audits.r2: Handovers completed without interruption for non-urgent tasks: 86%; most questions showed overall improvement

audits.t: Some standards and outcomes for a combined ENT/Speech Therapy Voice Clinic — a preliminary audit survey
audits.tp: Combined ENT/speech therapy voice clinic standards
audits.st: Locally set clinical and non-clinical standards for the voice clinic service
audits.f: Clinical standards were met; non-clinical standards (outside the immediate control of the voice clinic team) were not met (specific figures not given)

audits.t: Audit of service provision for adults and children with fluency disorders
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Impact of NPSA guidelines on intravenous fluid prescription in children – A retrospective audit on fluid prescription in children undergoing appendicectomy
audits.tp: IV fluid prescribing guideline compliance in children
audits.st: National Patient Safety Agency (NPSA, 2007) guidelines for paediatric IV fluid prescribing
audits.f: Significant discrepancies from NPSA guidelines shown in a previous audit (audit 1), e.g. 29% received hypotonic maintenance fluid intraoperatively, 84% postoperatively
audits.c: Dissemination and implementation of NPSA (2007) guidelines for IV fluid prescribing
audits.r2: Plasma electrolytes measured in 98% on admission; intraoperative hypotonic maintenance fluid fell to 10% (from 29%); postoperative hypotonic fluid fell to 56% (from 84%); daily electrolyte monitoring remained low at 14%

audits.t: The Diabetes Annual Review as an Educational Tool: Assessment and Learning Integrated with Care, Screening, and Audit
audits.tp: Diabetes annual review process and target attainment
audits.st: Locally set target range for HbA1c and structured diabetes annual review process
audits.f: 34% of patients had HbA1c outside target range in year 1
audits.c: Team changed in-house working practices and documentation and developed in-service training following the review
audits.r2: 46% had HbA1c outside target range in year 2; only 18% outside target in both years; knowledge scores improved by 44% between reviews

audits.t: Audit and family systems consultation: evaluation of practice at a child and family centre
audits.tp: Child and family centre referral and outcome audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Referral rate about one new case per day; almost half from GPs; most clients seen within two months; between half and three-quarters of cases had positive outcomes as rated by staff and parents

audits.t: A multi‐centre audit of the use of medication for the management of behavioural problems in adults with intellectual disabilities
audits.tp: Prescribing for behavioural problems in intellectual disability
audits.st: Audit criteria derived from a national guideline development project on medication for behavioural problems in intellectual disabilities
audits.f: High compliance for assessment of behaviour and communication of treatment plan; assessment of capacity and acquisition of consent/assent rarely documented

audits.t: Psychotic disorders in learning disabilities‐ outcome of an audit across community teams
audits.tp: Antipsychotic prescribing in learning disability with psychosis
audits.st: National Institute for Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidelines on treatment and management of schizophrenia
audits.f: All patients received medication within recommended British National Formulary doses; 25% of patients found treatment resistant; good regular monitoring of improvement and side effects found in most cases

audits.t: Audit of a children's epilepsy clinic
audits.tp: Children's epilepsy clinic patient satisfaction and needs
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: High degree of satisfaction reported by parents and children, but specific questions revealed a large number of unmet needs (numbers not given)

audits.t: West Midlands perinatal mortality survey, 1987. An audit of 300 perinatal autopsies
audits.st: Locally derived minimum score for perinatal autopsy report completeness (8 coded aspects)
audits.f: 44% of autopsies failed to attain the arbitrary minimum score of 300 (mean score 299); excluding regional centre autopsies, 50% failed (mean 268)

audits.t: Induced abortion: an audit of reported current pracl among consultant gynaecologists in Scotland*
audits.st: Agreed criteria for good quality abortion care based on literature review
audits.f: Regional inequalities in availability of early medical abortion and second trimester procedures; variation in screening for genital tract infection, cervical predilatation use, contraceptive provision and follow up; several aspects compared poorly with agreed criteria

audits.t: A Scottish audit of hysteroscopic surgery for menorrhagia: complications and follow up
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Complications occurred in 12% of cases including one death from toxic shock syndrome; uterine perforation and significant fluid overload each occurred in 1% of cases; 84% satisfied or very satisfied at 12 months

audits.t: Introducing external cephalic version at 36 weeks or more in a district general hospital: a review and an audit.
audits.tp: Breech presentation and external cephalic version
audits.st: Local target of reducing vaginal breech delivery and caesarean section rates by introducing external cephalic version (ECV) at >=36 weeks; no external numeric guideline target stated
audits.f: Breech presentation rate (ECV-suitable) 2.7% of all deliveries; vaginal breech delivery rate 0.98%; caesarean section rate 63% for ECV-suitable breeches
audits.c: Introduction of an external cephalic version service at >=36 weeks gestation
audits.r2: ECV successful in 39% of women; breech presentation rate fell to 2.4%; vaginal breech delivery rate fell to 0.51%; caesarean section rate 47% among women who had attempted ECV

audits.t: An audit of standards and quality in a teaching hospital colposcopy clinic
audits.st: National Health Service Cervical Screening Programme (NHSCSP) minimum standards for colposcopy services
audits.f: Delays in patient assessment and communication of results; overtreatment particularly at first visit; excessive treatments performed under general anaesthesia; many women failed to have follow-up smear performed
audits.c: Changes made to the structure and functioning of the colposcopy clinic

audits.t: Caesarean Section: An Audit of Time‐Based Efficiency in Providing a Clinical Service
audits.tp: Emergency caesarean section decision to delivery time
audits.st: Local target for decision-to-delivery time for emergency caesarean section (target not stated)
audits.f: Median decision-to-delivery time was 40 minutes (Audit 1)
audits.c: Discussion of Audit 1 findings at an interdepartmental obstetric, midwifery and anaesthetic meeting; recommendation for continuous audit and directive senior leadership
audits.r2: Median decision-to-delivery time improved to 31 minutes (Audit 2), p=0.068 (marginally significant, Wilcoxon Rank Sum Test)

audits.t: Investigation of microbial keratitis: an audit from 1988-1992.
audits.tp: Microbial keratitis investigation and isolation rate
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Pathogen isolation rate 37% in the first year of the audit.
audits.c: New investigation protocol developed; new method of inoculating enrichment broths introduced in late 1991; improved communication with the microbiology laboratory.
audits.r2: Pathogen isolation rate increased to 79% (p<0.05) by the final year.

audits.t: Audit of once-daily dosing gentamicin therapy in neutropenic fever.
audits.st: Local once-daily gentamicin dosing protocol with target trough/peak serum levels for febrile neutropenia
audits.f: 122/160 (76%) trough samples <1mg/l target range achieved; samples >2mg/l occurred mainly when taken at the wrong time and reverted to target with dose adjustment; nephrotoxicity 7%, no sepsis-related deaths

audits.t: Audit on extracorporeal shockwave lithotripsy of renal and ureteric stones in Tuen Mun Hospital using Dornier Lithotripter S
audits.tp: ESWL outcomes for renal and ureteric stones
audits.st: Local target clinical success/stone-free rate for ESWL (numeric target not stated)
audits.f: Clinical success 31% (stone-free 19%); overall complication rate 6.2%
audits.c: Upgrade to the power unit of the shockwave emitter (Dornier Lithotripter S) in September 2004
audits.r2: Clinical success improved to 61% (stone-free 38%), p<0.0001; complication rate reduced to 3.3%; obstructive complications fell from 4.8% to 0.5% (p=0.012)

audits.t: Percutaneous nephrolithotomy outcomes: Re‐audit in 2005
audits.st: Local target stone-free rate for PCNL (numeric target not stated)
audits.f: Staghorn stones single-session stone-free rate 30-40%; renal pelvis stones 50-60%
audits.c: Introduction of multiple tract access, flexible nephroscopic exploration, and new-generation ultrasonic lithotripter
audits.r2: Staghorn stones single-session stone-free rate improved to 70-80%; renal pelvis stones 100%; overall complication rate remained low at 13.9%; retreatment rate reduced by 15%

audits.t: An audit of all prostate‐specific antigen tests requested by non‐urologists in a 1‐year period in a district general hospital
audits.tp: Appropriateness of PSA testing by non-urologists
audits.st: Expected clinical indication, patient knowledge/consent and clear result interpretation for PSA testing (no named external guideline)
audits.f: Many PSA tests were requested without clinical indication, without patient knowledge or consent, and without clear interpretation of results; some positive patients did not receive appropriate follow-up

audits.t: Report on Psychotherapy Audit in the NHS: How Long Do Patients Stay in Therapy?
audits.tp: Psychotherapy treatment length vs prescribed length
audits.st: 'Prescribed' length of individual and group psychotherapy treatment
audits.f: A discrepancy was found between the 'prescribed' length of therapy and the length of time patients actually spent in therapy
audits.c: Change of practice prompted by the audit findings

audits.t: NEONATAL PALLIATIVE CARE: A SINGLE SITE CLINICAL AUDIT
audits.tp: Feeding tolerance assessment in preterm infants
audits.st: not reported (new collaboratively created algorithm)
audits.f: Days to full feeds 11; days requiring total parenteral nutrition 9; central venous line (CVL) days 7.
audits.c: New algorithm to assess feeding tolerance without checking gastric aspirates, supported by 12 educational meetings (67% of nursing staff attended, January-February 2018).
audits.r2: Days to full feeds decreased to 9; days requiring total parenteral nutrition decreased to 7; CVL days decreased to 3.

audits.tp: Post-extubation feeding protocol in paediatric intensive care
audits.st: Post-Extubation Early Feeding (PEEF) protocol: recommence enteral nutrition at 50% pre-fasting rate within 1 h of extubation, upgrade to pre-extubation rate within 2 h
audits.f: Median time to recommence enteral nutrition 4.2 h (3.2-5.5); median time to reach pre-fasting feeding rate 7.3 h (4.1-13)
audits.r2: Median time to recommence enteral nutrition reduced to 3.2 h (1.9-4.7), p=2.4x10^-13; median time to pre-fasting feeding rate reduced to 5 h (2.6-10.6), p=0.0005

audits.t: Assessing the efficacy of a single‐unit red blood cell transfusion policy at a multisite transfusion service using a computerized retrospective audit
audits.tp: Single-unit red blood cell transfusion policy compliance
audits.st: Institutional policy mandating clinical/laboratory reassessment of stable, non-bleeding patients after each red cell unit before issuing further units
audits.f: Single-unit transfusions: 17% (haematology), 57% (medicine), 63% (surgery)
audits.c: Implementation of a single-unit red blood cell transfusion policy in 2013
audits.r2: Single-unit transfusions increased to 89% (haematology), 94% (medicine), 87% (surgery); transfusion intensity decreased significantly in haematology and surgery (p<0.001) and medicine (p=0.008)

audits.t: Correcting preoperative iron deficiency as part of patient blood management in the ‘real world’: results of an audit on an Australian cohort
audits.tp: Preoperative iron deficiency correction in patient blood management
audits.st: Australian Patient Blood Management guidelines (perioperative module): preoperative iron therapy for surgical patients with, or at risk of, iron deficiency anaemia
audits.f: Intervention group: 17/93 (18.3%) required postoperative red cell transfusion vs 71/332 (21.4%) of controls; adjusted odds ratio 0.512 (95% CI 0.268-0.977, p=0.04)
audits.c: Preoperative haemoglobin optimisation programme with oral or intravenous iron supplementation

audits.t: Utility of a combined approach using audit, education and information technology tools to improve transfusion practices
audits.tp: Completeness of blood transfusion requisition forms
audits.st: Complete blood requisition form information (local requirement)
audits.f: 5,563/6,537 (85.1%) blood requisitions were incomplete
audits.c: Implementation of a clinical module of blood bank management software with autofill, plus staff education/training
audits.r2: 320/6,290 (5.08%) requisitions incomplete; 97.21% reduction in missing parameters (p<0.0001)

audits.t: A case study in healthcare quality management: a practical methodology for auditing total patient X-ray dose during a diagnostic procedure
audits.st: Ionising Radiation (Medical Exposure) Regulations 2000 (IRMER) requirement for local Diagnostic Reference Levels; HSC1999/065 Clinical Governance
audits.f: not reported (methodology paper describing a practical bootstrapping approach to set a local DRL with statistical confidence; no compliance percentage stated).

audits.t: Acupuncture Audit in Rheumatology
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Resulted in better standardisation of acupuncture usage within the clinics and more enthusiastic acceptance by new department members
audits.c: Introduction of a checklist of contraindications to acupuncture, better provision of information leaflets and explanation of side effects, more detailed assessment of outcome with better GP communication

audits.t: SAT0213 Tight treatment of patients with rheumatoid arthritis in the early stages of disease leads to high levels of remission and reduced use of biologics
audits.st: UK Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership (HQIP) 2015-2016 national clinical audit for rheumatoid and early inflammatory arthritis (national averages: 46% combination DMARDs, 31% DAS remission)
audits.f: 80% of patients started on combination DMARDs (Methotrexate and Hydroxychloroquine) at first appointment, vs national average 46%; 46% entered DAS remission, vs national average 31%; only 4.2% (9 patients) required biologics within the first year.

audits.t: AB1099 An audit on the screening guidelines for uveitis in children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis within the royal hospital for children, glasgow
audits.tp: Uveitis screening adherence in juvenile idiopathic arthritis
audits.st: British Society of Paediatric and Adolescent Rheumatology (BSPAR) guidelines for uveitis screening in juvenile idiopathic arthritis
audits.f: 97/115 patients entered the screening programme; 72/97 had their initial screen within the 6-week guideline; 463/641 (72.2%) appointments met the 3-4 monthly guideline after the initial 6 months; of 10 patients stopping immunosuppressants while still in the screening service, none were screened according to the recommended 2-monthly guideline.

audits.t: AB0457 AUDIT ON HYDROXYCHLOROQUINE RELATED RETINOPATHY SCREENING IN RHEUMATOLOGY PATIENTS IN SVUH
audits.st: American Academy of Ophthalmology 2016 Revision recommendations on screening for hydroxychloroquine retinopathy
audits.f: 69.6% (39/56) underwent baseline retinal screening; 30.4% (17/56) received no baseline screening after starting hydroxychloroquine; annual follow-up screening done in 33.9% (19/56), not done in 37% (21/56); only 1/56 (1.8%) had a history of hydroxychloroquine toxicity.

audits.t: SAT0447 MANAGEMENT OF GOUT: AN AUDIT IN PRIMARY CARE GENERAL PRACTICE IN LEICESTERSHIRE, UNITED KINGDOM
audits.st: British Society for Rheumatology (BSR) gout guideline (Hui et al 2017), treat-to-target approach
audits.f: 21.5% of patients were provided written information about gout; 60.5% treated with NSAIDs/COXIBs for acute attacks; 71% of colchicine prescriptions had no dose recorded; 37.5% (323) prescribed urate-lowering therapy (ULT), 73.8% started on allopurinol 100mg daily; dose titration recorded in only 21%; 62.6% (539) had no serum urate level check after starting ULT.

audits.t: An audit of the accuracy of neonatal inpatient prescription charts
audits.st: 100% compliance with correct demographic data, correct ward, legibility/unambiguous prescribing, signed and dated prescriptions, and correct cancellation of discontinued medicines
audits.f: No standard received 100% compliance; 12% (n=3) SMH and 3% (n=1) QCCH charts missing hospital number; correct ward not stated on 12% (n=7); 4% illegible; 11% (n=8) had no clear cancellation of all medicines

audits.t: An audit into the prescribing practices of warfarin in a paediatric setting
audits.st: Warfarin National Patient Safety Alert (NPSA) and Trust policies/national guidelines
audits.f: 62% of patients had warfarin appropriately prescribed; 30.7% had corresponding INR monitoring sheets; overall 28.6% adherence to expected audit standards, mainly due to missing INR levels

audits.t: To National Patient Safety Agency or not to National Patient Safety Agency: an audit on the current trends in paediatric intravenous fluid prescribing for surgical patients
audits.tp: Intravenous fluid prescribing for surgical patients
audits.st: Birmingham Children's Hospital in-house intravenous prescribing guidelines and national guidance
audits.f: 19/25 (75%) did not comply with local/national guidance; 44% prescribed an incorrect rate; 92% prescribed incorrect fluid type postoperatively per local guidance; 35% not monitored for sodium/potassium

audits.t: An audit of total parenteral nutrition prescribing for children
audits.st: Trust Medicines Policy requiring unambiguous, complete PN prescriptions
audits.f: 78% of prescriptions were unclear; 84-92% missing nutritional components; 83% did not specify route; over half missing weight or total fluid; 7% unsigned

audits.t: An audit of intravenous meropenem in inpatients at Alder Hey Children's NHS Foundation Trust
audits.st: Trust guidelines and national recommendations for meropenem use
audits.f: 70 courses (68%) compliant with audit standards; 24 courses prescribed with no microbiological support at all; 8 courses non-compliant despite bacteria being sensitive to cephalosporins

audits.t: Audit of BMT antibiotic febrile neutropenia guidelines
audits.tp: BMT febrile neutropenia antibiotic guideline compliance
audits.st: BMT antibiotic febrile neutropenia guidelines (updated 2009): first-line piperacillin/tazobactam plus gentamicin, gentamicin/vancomycin trough monitoring
audits.f: 88% compliance with first-line antibiotic standard; gentamicin trough taken before second dose in 94%; vancomycin trough taken at 24h in 83%, but 32% of vancomycin levels were subtherapeutic

audits.t: An audit of pharmacy interventions on paediatric outpatient and A and E prescriptions
audits.tp: Pharmacy interventions on paediatric outpatient prescriptions
audits.st: Trust policy for prescribing medicines
audits.f: 53% (166/314) of items required a pharmacist intervention; 40% of prescriptions had no documented allergy status; A&E prescriptions: 82% required intervention, 77% had no allergy documented
audits.c: Planned amendment of the A&E outpatient prescription to include allocated space for weight and allergy status

audits.t: G305 How much variation in paediatric epilepsy admission rates in england can be explained by variation in unit-level performance in the national clinical audit (epilepsy12)
audits.tp: Paediatric epilepsy admission rates and audit performance (Epilepsy12)
audits.st: Epilepsy12 national clinical audit quality indicators
audits.f: Increased paediatric neurologist involvement associated with a small relative increase in admission rates over time (beta=0.13, 95% CI 0.03-0.22, p=0.007); no significant cross-sectional relationship (beta=-0.04); no other Epilepsy12 performance indicator was associated with unit-level admission rates.

audits.t: P191 Audit on role of chest X-ray in childhood community acquired pneumonia (CAP)
audits.tp: Chest X-ray use in childhood community-acquired pneumonia
audits.st: British Thoracic Society (BTS) guideline (2011 update) for community-acquired pneumonia
audits.f: 27/31 (87.09%) had a chest X-ray during admission, with no clear documentation of the reason for most.

audits.t: P204 Precision entails perfection: do we need blood forms?
audits.st: Hospital standard for blood form accuracy
audits.f: 32.76% of blood forms filled incorrectly.
audits.c: Verbal reminders at Monday handover/grand rounds (weeks 3-4), followed by an ID-card-size written reminder distributed to non-consultant hospital doctors (weeks 5-6).
audits.r2: 31.97% incorrect after the verbal reminder (weeks 3-4); no improvement was found after the ID card reminder (weeks 5-6), though staff found the card useful.

audits.t: P206 Audit of compliance to guidelines of down syndrome(DS) management in nicu of university maternity hospital limerick(UMHL)
audits.tp: Down syndrome management guideline compliance in NICU
audits.st: Standard Medical management guidelines for Down Syndrome (National Children's Hospital, Tallaght, Dublin, updated 30 September 2009)
audits.f: 100% compliance for cardiac assessment, karyotype request, full blood count, cardiology referral, early intervention team referral, information leaflets to parents, and follow-up; 17% (1/6) failed compliance for admission examination, DS centile chart, Guthrie card, typed discharge letter, ophthalmology assessment, hearing assessment, and physiotherapy referral; medical social worker referral not sent in 67% (4/6); Down syndrome registry consent not obtained in 100% (6/6).

audits.t: P245 Enhancing CPD, quality improvement and best practice
audits.tp: CPD and audit engagement among physicians
audits.st: RCPI requirement of 50 CPD credits/year plus completion of a clinical audit
audits.f: 2,738 participants enrolled in 2012.
audits.c: Incentivising early completion of a Personal Development Plan (PDP) with 2 internal CPD credits, from 2017.
audits.r2: 4,446 participants enrolled in 2018; 88% of RCPI Fellows achieved >50 CPD credits with audit submission in 2017; PDP completion rose from 1,381 (40.3%) in 2016 to 1,824 in 2018; PDP completion associated with achieving >=50 credits and completing an audit (both p<=0.001).

audits.t: P564 A quality improvement project on oral food challenge
audits.st: Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital food challenge protocol
