audits.f: No informed written consent taken for any of the challenges; no parent information leaflets given; last skin prick test result documented in only 3/25 (12%); last antihistamine use documented before only 1/25 (4%) of challenges; none of the high-risk challenges had an IV line placed beforehand; 80% of children were not examined after the challenge; 44% waited more than 2 months after a negative skin prick test versus the recommended 2-4 weeks.
audits.c: Formation of a single-page pro-forma covering all relevant information required before a food challenge.

audits.t: P582 Audit on role of blood tests in children admitted with community acquired pneumonia
audits.tp: Blood tests use in childhood community-acquired pneumonia
audits.st: British Thoracic Society (BTS) guideline for community-acquired pneumonia
audits.f: 26/31 (83.87%) had CRP testing done, and all 26 also had white cell count done, despite this not being recommended routinely in mild-to-moderate community-acquired pneumonia.

audits.t: P584 A ‘triage’ audit
audits.st: Manchester Triage System
audits.f: not reported (results to be presented; not included in the supplied abstract text).

audits.t: G34(P) Changing practice – a quality improvement project
audits.tp: Weight documentation on paediatric discharge letters
audits.st: Local standard: 100% of discharge letters to include the child's weight
audits.f: 9.8% of discharge letters included the child's weight.
audits.c: Email and verbal reminders, posters put up in wards and on computers, new doctors informed at induction, and individual emails to non-conforming staff, applied across repeated PDSA cycles.
audits.r2: 55.8% achieved in September 2018, having peaked at 72.7% in July 2018; intermediate results were 41.4% (January 2018), 17.0% (March 2018), and 70.8% (May 2018).

audits.t: G368(P) An audit of unplanned extubations in a paediatric intensive care unit
audits.tp: Unplanned extubation in paediatric intensive care
audits.st: PICANET national average unplanned extubation rate 0.4/100 ventilator days; accepted literature benchmark <1/100 ventilator days
audits.f: Unplanned extubation (UE) rate 0.7/100 ventilator days in 2017 (an outlier vs the national average of 0.4); oral extubations accounted for 63% of UE; only 39% were receiving oral sedation; only 15% were flagged to staff as having loose tapes; only 12% had an incident form completed; 44% of UE required reintubation.
audits.c: New re-taping standard operating procedure introduced in May 2017; further plans included COMFORT scoring, staff training in re-taping practices, and nurse-led extubations.

audits.t: G396(P) Clinical audit on the antenatal detection rate of congenital heart disease
audits.tp: Antenatal detection of congenital heart disease
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 3/20 patients with congenital heart disease were antenatally diagnosed via referral to fetal medicine; 17/20 were diagnosed postnatally; departmental antenatal screen-positive rate 15%.

audits.t: G418(P) The factors driving overdiagnosis of chest sepsis in children
audits.tp: Overdiagnosis and overtreatment of childhood lower respiratory tract infection
audits.st: NICE guidelines (sepsis risk stratification) and British Thoracic Society (BTS) guidelines for lower respiratory tract infection
audits.f: 64% of patients with low oxygen saturations had co-existing wheeze; 66% were treated with IV antibiotics; only 9.8% were treated with oral amoxicillin per BTS guidance; 88% had a chest X-ray (half reported normal, of which 71% still received IV antibiotics); 78% had blood tests including CRP, which is not routinely recommended.
audits.c: not reported (mixed quantitative-qualitative study, including questionnaires, interviews and focus groups, planned to identify drivers of overdiagnosis before implementing a change of practice)

audits.t: G70(P) Reducing unnecessary blood taking in the NICU – a quality improvement project
audits.tp: Blood sampling reduction in neonatal intensive care
audits.st: not reported (internal guideline informed by point-of-care gas machine validation)
audits.f: Only 18% of tests resulted in or directly monitored a change in clinical management; median laboratory tests per patient 12 (range 0-42); median total tests 18 (0-92).
audits.c: Introduction of a guideline for blood sampling and use of the point-of-care gas machine for commonly requested tests.
audits.r2: 36% of tests led to a change in management (doubled); median laboratory tests fell to 4 (0-20, p<0.0001); median total tests fell to 10 (0-42, p<0.005); calculated laboratory test cost reduced by GBP 3.50 per patient.

audits.t: 24 Monitoring bone health in children and young people with coeliac disease – a clinical audit
audits.tp: DEXA bone density monitoring in paediatric coeliac disease
audits.st: Local GOSH coeliac protocol (DEXA scan after diagnosis); national guidance non-specific for the paediatric population
audits.f: 87% had a DEXA scan (81% of which were normal); scans performed a median of 3.5 years after diagnosis; BMAD z-scores completed in 78% (mean -0.27); serum vitamin D >25 nmol/L in 100% of patients, but 45-60 nmol/L in those with abnormal DEXA.

audits.t: G135(P) National impact of RCPCH best practice guide on timing of detection of cleft palate – time to adopt successful local quality improvement initiatives
audits.tp: MRSA screening compliance in high-risk paediatric/neonatal patients
audits.st: Locally-defined high-risk criteria for MRSA screening; Trust infection prevention and control standard of >90% (target 100%)
audits.f: Overall screening rate 78.6% (114/145) across all areas; Neonatal Unit highest at 97.6% (41/42), followed by Children's Assessment Unit 80% (16/20) and Bluebell ward 68.7% (57/83); June had the lowest monthly rate (50.0%), August the highest (95.0%).
audits.c: Mandatory routine MRSA screening implemented for patients meeting locally-defined high-risk criteria.

audits.t: 28 Paediatric medication error prevention (PMEP) a tripartite alliance working together
audits.st: EQUIP criteria (General Medical Council)
audits.f: 90% of admissions in the initial audit period had minor to significant medication errors recorded, using a zero-tolerance approach.
audits.c: Tripartite alliance of nursing, pharmacy and medical teams, with education placed at the heart of the change process; aimed to reduce prescription and administration errors by at least 10%.
audits.r2: Medication errors substantially reduced over the last five years (exact final figure not stated).

audits.t: A total audit of preventive procedures in 45 practices caring for 430,000 patients.
audits.tp: Recording of preventive procedures in general practice records
audits.st: New GP contract target of 90% coverage for recorded primary immunisations and cervical cytology
audits.f: Only one practice achieved the 90% coverage target for recorded primary immunisations; fewer than two thirds recorded 80% coverage for cervical cytology in the past 5 years

audits.t: What did audit achieve? Lessons from preliminary evaluation of a year's medical audit.
audits.tp: Criterion-based audit of medical inpatient records and clinical management
audits.st: Detailed questionnaire-based standards for medical records and clinical management, agreed by the audit group
audits.f: Baseline median scores for record-keeping questions prior to the audit programme
audits.c: Monthly audit meetings with case note review, feedback via questionnaire scores presented quarterly
audits.r2: Significant overall increase in median scores for record-keeping questions after the start of the audit (p<0.01), though interobserver variation was high

audits.t: Multicentre criterion based audit of the management of induced abortion in Scotland.
audits.st: 16 previously agreed criteria for the management of induced abortion (criteria not individually listed in the abstract).
audits.f: First round: baseline audit of 967 abortion episodes against 16 agreed criteria; 42 of 150 elements of care across the 10 hospitals were 'close to optimal'.
audits.c: Dissemination of first-round audit results and recommendations for change via a written report and postgraduate meetings at participating hospitals.
audits.r2: Second round of 1037 cases: 54 of 150 elements 'close to optimal' (not significant overall); four significant overall improvements (increased early medical abortion availability, decreased very-early surgical abortion, increased mifepristone priming before second-trimester abortion, increased follow-up provision); 31 individual elements improved significantly but 11 significantly deteriorated.

audits.t: Use of Quick Response (QR) coded bracelets and cards for the improvement of cortisol deficiency/Addison’s disease management: an audit of quality of care of the management of steroid deficiency in acute illness
audits.tp: Adrenal crisis management and QR-coded information access
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 37% of healthcare professionals had never seen and 59% had never managed an adrenal crisis; median confidence (1 low-7 high): doctors 5, nurses 2, paramedics 4.5, dentists 1.5; 94% found a proposed QR-coded system useful, 84% would use it; median usability score 6.5/7.

audits.t: 67 Transition to adult care audit cycle: impact of a central transition team
audits.tp: Transition to adult care compliance with NICE standards
audits.st: NICE quality standards for Transition (2016)
audits.f: not reported (supplied abstract text is truncated before the results are given).
audits.c: Central transition team measures: transition section in electronic notes, electronic 'live' transition plan, learning from complaints and incidents, transition champions, addressing organisation-wide barriers, clear pathways for complex transitional needs, and feedback collection.
audits.r2: not reported (supplied abstract text is truncated before the results are given).

audits.t: Audit of the use of a screening tool to improve recognition of delirium in a palliative care unit
audits.tp: Delirium screening in palliative care unit
audits.st: British Geriatric Society recommendation to screen older patients for delirium using a tool such as the abbreviated mental test (AMT)
audits.f: Previous audit showed no delirium screening tool was in use in the SPCU
audits.c: Junior doctors asked to perform AMT on every new admission; education and AMT question labels provided for notes
audits.r2: 70% of patients had an AMT performed on admission; 43% of those screened scored below 8, indicating high delirium risk

audits.t: Sharing clinical audit
audits.tp: Sharing clinical audit results within a hospice
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Four feedback sessions held with an average of 4 audits presented at each; number of audits undertaken increased
audits.c: Structured quarterly audit feedback meetings and dissemination leaflets

audits.t: The gold standards framework: an audit of local practice from a hospice perspective
audits.tp: Gold Standards Framework implementation in general practice
audits.st: Gold Standards Framework (GSF) standards for primary palliative care
audits.f: 53/58 practices held palliative care meetings and 45 maintained a palliative care register; a third of practices held GSF meetings less frequently than every 6 weeks

audits.t: An audit of the advice given to GPs by hospice community nurse specialists regarding step 3 opioids
audits.tp: Accuracy of opioid advice given by hospice nurse specialists
audits.st: Expected accurate, evidence-based and documented advice on step 3 opioids (based on Gold Standards Framework nurse specialist role)
audits.f: 100% appropriate interval/route for opioids prescribed; 89% recorded indication for advice in patient records; only 50% communicated written advice to the GP
audits.c: Development of a pro forma letter to standardise advice to GPs

audits.t: An audit around preferred place of death: one UK hospice experience
audits.tp: Documentation of preferred place of death
audits.st: End of Life Care Strategy recommendation that patients choose and have documented a preferred place of care/death
audits.f: Preferred place of death recorded in only 18.7% of cases; of these, 89.3% died in their chosen location; only 10.6% had documented conversations about preferences

audits.t: 124 Revisiting polypharmacy in the hospice in-patient setting
audits.st: Local standards (based on Lindsey et al deprescribing guideline): 80% of medications with limited benefit stopped; 80% of patients discharged on 7 medications or fewer
audits.f: 40% of patients were discharged on 10 or more medications; 83% were prescribed at least one potentially inappropriate medication (PIM).
audits.c: Deprescribing tool implemented as part of a polypharmacy quality improvement project, based on Lindsey et al's guideline for deprescribing unnecessary medications in palliative care.
audits.r2: 71% on at least one PIM pre-admission (vs 83% previously); 43% discharged on 7 or fewer medications (up from 38%); 50% reduction in total PIMs prescribed from admission to discharge; 65% had at least one drug rationalised on admission; 66% discharged on at least one PIM (vs nearly 80% previously).

audits.t: P-153 A hospice-wide project to develop and support multi-professional participation in clinical audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Six projects completed, covering communication, information sharing and timings around discharge; participants agreed priority areas, learned to find evidence/standards, and to design, collect, analyse and present audit data.
audits.c: A programme of six workshops covering audit stages, led by a project lead, providing training and support for staff-led quality improvement projects over three months.

audits.t: 5PSQ-106 Focusing audits on patient safety
audits.tp: Regulatory audit tool for pharmacy patient safety
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Seven case studies of patient-safety-related deficiencies identified: four dispensing problems, two inventory deficiencies, and one equity-of-treatment issue; 46 corrective and preventive actions were taken.
audits.c: Development and implementation of a new regulatory audit tool (documentation and observation phases) with interactive educational discussions with pharmacists, based on retrospective analysis of 512 audit reports and 12 interviews.

audits.t: 4CPS-031 Audit of antibiotic prophylaxis practice in visceral surgery in an African country
audits.st: SFAR (Societe Francaise d'Anesthesie et Reanimation) international recommendation on antibiotic prophylaxis
audits.f: 70.4% (50/71) of administrations conformed to indication criteria; 0% of the 48 patients with indicated prophylaxis received the recommended molecule (ceftriaxone most used, 31%); dose, timing and duration compliance were 35%, 14% and 21% respectively.

audits.t: Unscheduled re-attendances to a paediatric Emergency Department: an audit
audits.tp: Unscheduled re-attendances to paediatric emergency department
audits.st: Department policy that re-attending patients be assessed by/discussed with a senior doctor
audits.f: 67% initially assessed by a junior doctor; on re-attendance 74% again assessed by a junior doctor, contrary to department policy; only 70% discharged with documented safety-net advice

audits.t: Helicobacter pylori (HP) serology: an audit of action on positive serology results: Table 1
audits.tp: Action taken on positive Helicobacter pylori serology
audits.st: 'Test and treat' policy: positive H. pylori serology results should lead to eradication
audits.f: 33/196 (17%) positive results were not eradicated; in 13/30 (43%) eradication was not explicitly advised by the endoscopist; 14/33 (42%) had the result documented in notes but 12/14 were not acted on; complications occurred in 3/33 (9%), all rebleeds
audits.c: Local arrangement for microbiology to send copies of all hospital-initiated Hp-positive results to a specialist nurse as a single point of contact for review and action

audits.t: What is an adequate liver biopsy? a tertiary centre audit
audits.st: Royal College of Pathologists (RCPath) and AASLD guidelines for adequate liver biopsy length/complete portal tract count
audits.f: 47% of samples fulfilled RCPath length and CPT criteria; only 2% fulfilled AASLD criteria; 85% (128/150) measured >=10mm; no CPT comment recorded in 35% (53/150).
audits.c: Change to using a 16 gauge needle, aiming for samples at least 15mm long (planned, not yet re-audited).

audits.t: An audit of tumour markers requests (CEA, AFP, CA19-9) in a district general hospital
audits.st: National Academy of Clinical Biochemistry (NACB) guidelines for appropriate tumour marker (CEA, AFP, CA19-9) requesting
audits.f: Of 982 tumour markers requested, only 382 (39%) were appropriate; 70% of requests were for CEA of which 51% were inappropriate; CA19-9 was inappropriately requested in 85% of cases and AFP in 60%; all requests from cancer MDMs met guidelines.
audits.c: Production of locally agreed guidelines for tumour marker requesting (planned).

audits.t: PMO-186 Complication rates of colonoscopic removal of large colorectal polyps in a district general hospital: a retrospective audit
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology guideline targets for post-polypectomy bleeding requiring transfusion and perforation rate for large polyps (exact wording of thresholds was garbled in the abstract text)
audits.f: No perforation or major bleeding requiring transfusion in either pedunculated (n=49) or sessile (n=15) large polyp groups; minor bleeding in 8.1% of pedunculated and 6.66% of sessile polyp removals; en bloc removal in 87.7% of pedunculated and 20% of sessile polyps.

audits.t: PMO-187 A multi-centre audit of 16 064 colonoscopies looking at caecal intubation rates, over a 2-year period. Non-GI operators and those doing <100 p.a. need to improve or stop performing colonoscopy
audits.st: Joint Advisory Group on Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (JAG) standard: >=100 procedures per annum, target caecal intubation rate (CIR) 90%
audits.f: Overall CIR 90.57% (95% CI 90.11-91.01%); operators doing >=100 procedures/year had CIR 91.76% (95% CI 91.24-92.25%); operators doing <100 procedures/year and non-GI practitioners had CIR below 90%.

audits.t: PMO-221 Appropriateness of follow-up indications after colonic polyp removal: audit of current practice in a district general hospital
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guidelines for surveillance interval after colonic polyp removal, based on number and size of adenomas
audits.f: Follow-up indication compliant with BSG guidelines in 66.3% (136/205); scheduled too early in 16.1% (33), too late in 2% (4); 15.6% (32) deferred to outpatient clinic decision.

audits.t: PMO-251 A retrospective audit of colorectal cancer surveillance in inflammatory bowel disease in secondary care
audits.tp: Colorectal cancer surveillance in inflammatory bowel disease
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) 2010 guidelines for colonoscopic surveillance for colorectal cancer in colitis
audits.f: Of 24 patients eligible for repeat colonoscopy, only 3 (13%) underwent this at the recommended interval; 11 (46%) had inconsistent surveillance; 9 (38%) had no surveillance.

audits.t: PMO-261 Is Crohn's disease in the UK being under treated? Data from the 3rd round UK IBD audit: Abstract PMO-261 Table 1
audits.tp: Inflammatory bowel disease treatment escalation guideline adherence
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guidelines recommending escalation to immunosuppressives, and anti-TNF as 2nd line, for severe relapsing IBD
audits.f: 52.1% of established CD patients discharged on immunosuppressives (IS) and/or anti-TNF (aTNF) vs 39.8% of established UC (p<0.0001); 19.4% of new CD vs 15.0% of new UC discharged on IS/aTNF (p=0.18); 26.4% of new CD discharged on no treatment vs 10.7% of new UC (p<0.0001).

audits.t: PMO-046 Audit of a new pathway for enteral feeding head and neck radiotherapy patients: Abstract PMO-046 Table 1
audits.tp: Enteral feeding pathway for head and neck cancer radiotherapy patients
audits.st: Local enteral feeding pathway for head and neck radiotherapy patients, developed from a previous audit and informed by NICE guidance on head and neck cancer care
audits.f: not reported (previous, unpublished local audit that informed pathway development)
audits.c: New enteral feeding pathway giving guidance on timing of elective nasogastric feeding and selection of patients for elective day-case NG placement, launched May 2011.
audits.r2: Average length of stay reduced further to 3 days using the pathway; admissions >24 hours occurred in 2 of 11 patients; no significant complications identified.

audits.t: PMO-059 Parenteral nutrition: audit of usage in a district general hospital without a nutrition support team
audits.st: NICE guidelines for appropriate parenteral nutrition (PN) indications
audits.f: 24 episodes (26%), totalling 182 days of PN, were judged inappropriate, mainly due to inadequate consideration of enteral tube access; catheter-related sepsis complicated 16 episodes (17.4%), equating to 16.5 events/1000 catheter days.

audits.t: PTU-231 Bowel preparation for inpatient colonoscopy: an audit of quality and outcomes
audits.tp: Inpatient colonoscopy bowel preparation and caecal intubation quality
audits.st: Local standard bowel preparation protocol and implied national caecal intubation rate standard (>90%)
audits.f: Only 50% (25/50) of inpatient bowel preparation rated excellent/good vs 86% overall for the same period; inpatient caecal intubation rate only 74% (37/50) vs the >90% standard; overall inpatient colonoscopy success rate only 66% (33/50).

audits.t: PTU-244 Audit of 30-day mortality post endoscopy—a tertiary centre experience
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) 2006 guidelines on endoscopy-related mortality
audits.f: Overall 30-day mortality 1.3% (1:78); procedure-related mortality 0.03% for OGD and 0.56% for ERCP; individual mortality rates 1.7% (OGD), 0.61% (flexible sigmoidoscopy), 0.14% (colonoscopy), 7.8% (ERCP); 4 deaths causally related to the endoscopic procedure.

audits.t: PTU-258 A UK national comparative audit of appropriateness of red cell transfusion in medical patients
audits.tp: Red cell transfusion appropriateness in medical patients
audits.st: National guidelines for red cell transfusion triggers and pretransfusion assessment
audits.f: 4.1% of transfusions had pretransfusion Hb >10 g/dl (median 7.8); 5.8% had posttransfusion Hb >12 g/dl; serum ferritin measured in only 38% of cases, of whom 9.3% had ferritin <15 microg/l.

audits.t: PTU-098 The UK inflammatory bowel disease audit: key findings from the inpatient experience questionnaire
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall care rated fair by 7% and poor by 2.9% of adults; only 60% of adults reported a visit from a specialist nurse; scores for consistency/coordination of care were relatively low compared with the National Inpatient Survey 2009.

audits.t: PWE-222 Audit of upper GI cancer diagnosis by endoscopy: are diagnoses being missed?
audits.st: Local rolling annual audit programme threshold: delays of more than 1 month considered potentially significant
audits.f: 6/148 (4.1%) patients had significant potentially avoidable delays to diagnosis; most delays were due to booking/appointment systems rather than endoscopic misses; review of previous biopsies found no missed malignant diagnoses.

audits.t: PWE-244 Does thromboprophylaxis in ulcerative colitis work?: data from the UK IBD audit
audits.st: Recommendation that all patients admitted with acute flares of ulcerative colitis receive prophylactic subcutaneous heparin
audits.f: 87.5% (2668/3049) of patients were given prophylactic heparin; VTE occurred in 2.2% (66/3049) overall, with no significant difference between heparinised (2.2%) and non-heparinised (1.8%) patients (p<0.8).

audits.t: PWE-283 Surveillance for hepatocellular carcinoma: a clinical audit
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guideline (6-monthly USS + AFP) and AASLD guideline (6-monthly USS alone) for HCC surveillance in cirrhosis
audits.f: 95 (52%) received 6-monthly USS per AASLD recommendation; only 48 (26%) received 6-monthly USS and AFP per BSG recommendation; 114 had 6-12 monthly USS.

audits.t: PWE-090 West midlands multi-centre trainee-LED audit in the assessment, management and prophylaxis of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
audits.tp: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis assessment and management
audits.st: EASL, BSG and NICE standards for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP)
audits.f: Ascitic aspirates performed in 83% (range 60-92% by site); within 24 hours in 64%; cultures sent in 55%; 16.8% of aspirates met SBP criteria, with antibiotics started in 92%; secondary prophylaxis given in 44%; of those meeting criteria for primary prophylaxis (67%), only 13% commenced it; overall mortality 51%; SBP associated with lower median survival (79 vs 190 days, p=0.045).

audits.t: OTH-005 Prospective multi-site audit of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding delivered across multiple regions by trainee-led networks
audits.st: NICE QS38 and JAG Global Rating Scale (GRS) national quality standards
audits.f: Median time to OGD 22.5 hours (IQR 12.7-43.9); 54% performed within 24 hours (range by site 22-88%); Glasgow Blatchford score recorded pre-OGD in 47%; rebleed plan documented in 36%; rebleeding within 8 days in 7.9% (36 patients); mortality 6.3% (29) within 30 days; median length of stay 5 days.

audits.t: PTH-139 Gastrin now: establishing a trainee led research network
audits.tp: Trainee-led research network for gastroenterology audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 27 trainees and 25 consultants from 13 of 16 potential sites (81%) recruited; complete audit data obtained from 10 sites (77%).

audits.t: PTH-012 Implementation of UK acute upper GI bleeding bundle results in significant improvements in quality standards
audits.tp: Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding bundle implementation
audits.st: UK Acute Upper GI Bleeding (AUGIB) care bundle (BSG Endoscopy Quality Improvement Project), following the 2015 NCEPOD report
audits.f: Glasgow Blatchford Score recorded in 38.4% (163/459); target haemoglobin stated in 35.3%; transfusion threshold appropriate in 13.3%; rebleeding plan documented in 33.2%.
audits.c: Implementation of the UK AUGIB care bundle, with a period of bundle promotion between data collection cycles.
audits.r2: Glasgow Blatchford Score recorded in 57.3% (225/434, p<0.001); target haemoglobin stated in 44.8%; transfusion threshold appropriate in 19.6% (p=0.012); rebleeding plan documented in 50.7% (p<0.001); the bundle was used in 41.2% of patients.

audits.t: PWE-082 The art of combining clinical intuition and nuclear medicine in diagnosing bile acid malabsorption
audits.tp: SeHCAT scanning for bile acid malabsorption
audits.st: NICE DG7 (2012); 2018 BSG guidelines for investigation of chronic diarrhoea
audits.f: 49.8% of patients had an abnormal SeHCAT test; testing volume increased from 26/year to 124/year over 5 years; of 2,476 post-cholecystectomy patients, 64 developed diarrhoea, of whom 41 (64%) tested positive.

audits.t: PTU-75 A Clinical Audit of Severity Assessment of Acute Pancreatitis using scoring systems
audits.tp: Severity assessment scoring in acute pancreatitis
audits.st: not reported (scoring systems referenced, e.g. APACHE II; no named numeric target)
audits.f: At one centre 33% of patients were scored using APACHE II; at two other centres this rose to 77.8% and 33.3%; for all scored patients there was 0% ITU admission or mortality.

audits.t: 147 Thromboembolic risk stratification, anti-thrombotic and anticoagulation use for patients with atrial fibrillation, a clinical audit
audits.st: NICE guidance and ACC/ESC (CHADS2) guidance for thromboembolic risk stratification and antithrombotic/anticoagulation therapy in atrial fibrillation
audits.f: 91.4% reported using risk stratification tools; NICE risk assessment used by 26.6%, CHADS2 by 79.3%; warfarin was under-recommended for CHADS2 score of 2 (60% only); AF subtype inappropriately influenced antithrombotic choice for 34.3% of responders.

audits.t: 013 Audit of tertiary heart failure outpatient service to assess compliance with updated nice guidelines
audits.st: NICE August 2010 updated clinical guideline for chronic heart failure
audits.f: 89% correctly prescribed a beta-blocker, 91% an ACE-inhibitor/ARB, and 64% an aldosterone antagonist; rehabilitation referral rates were low: 15% offered a programme initially, later only 6% referred and 1% enrolled.

audits.t: 066 Anti-thrombotic therapy and atrial fibrillation in Scotland: results of a national audit: Abstract 066 Table 1
audits.tp: Atrial fibrillation anticoagulation in primary care
audits.st: CHADS2-based stroke risk stratification and anticoagulation guidance
audits.f: 79% of AF patients were prescribed antithrombotic therapy; formal stroke risk assessment was recorded in <1% of patients; in the high-risk group (CHADS2>=2) not on warfarin, only 10% had documented exclusion criteria; only 44% of patients with prior stroke/TIA were on warfarin.

audits.t: EP697 Establishing the audit and research in gynaecological oncology (ARGO) collaborative in the united kingdom and ireland
audits.tp: Gynaecological oncology audit and research collaborative
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 52 members recruited from all 14 deaneries of the UK, Northern Ireland and Republic of Ireland; a core committee of 6 trainees was elected; 7 multi-centre project proposals were received, 4 short-listed, and a project on frailty and outcomes after gynaecological oncology surgery was selected.

audits.t: 344 Clinical audit on quality of cancer care within the oncological network of Piedmont and Valle d’Aosta: ovarian cancer treatment
audits.st: International guidelines for ovarian cancer diagnostic-therapeutic pathway adherence (specific body not named)
audits.f: 2.3% of patients followed the correct diagnostic-therapeutic pathway in 2015 (compared with the earlier COROP 2009 study).
audits.c: Network-based prospective monitoring of ovarian cancer care with outcomes shared with clinical operators every six months.
audits.r2: 68.2% followed the correct diagnostic-therapeutic pathway in 2017, with further improvement in the following year; centralisation of treatment, earlier diagnosis, and improved overall survival observed versus the COROP 2009 comparison.

audits.t: 2022-LBA-1628-ESGO Clinical audit on ‘ESGO quality indicators’ of ovarian cancer care within a Northern Italy oncological network: a means to encourage change and to improve the quality of care?
audits.tp: Ovarian cancer care ESGO quality indicators
audits.st: ESGO (European Society of Gynaecological Oncology) quality indicators for ovarian cancer care
audits.f: 30 hospitals were treating ovarian cancer patients within the network in 2016.
audits.c: Audit and feedback of ESGO quality indicators used to encourage practice change across the oncological network.
audits.r2: Number of treating hospitals fell to 17 in 2020 (centralisation); improvement observed over the years in both diagnosis and treatment quality indicators; adherence to surgical guidelines had a strong favourable effect on overall survival (HR=0.54, 95% CI 0.39-0.74) after adjusting for age and stage; chemotherapy supply remained an area needing improvement.

audits.t: Audit of necropsies in a British district general hospital.
audits.tp: Necropsy value and diagnostic accuracy audit
audits.st: A modification of the audit format proposed by Schned et al (Vermont, USA) for evaluating necropsy value and clinical correlation
audits.f: Pathologist disagreed with clinical cause of death in 13% of cases; major unsuspected diagnoses found in 30%; 79% of necropsies provided additional information; necropsies rated 'very valuable' in 44%, 'valuable' in 54%, 'of no value' in only 2%.

audits.t: Blood component treatment: a retrospective audit in five major London hospitals.
audits.st: Accepted clinical indications for platelet or fresh frozen plasma (FFP) transfusion
audits.f: Reason for using the component was not stated in 61.5% of cases; documentation was inadequate in 66%; an accepted clinical indication was evident in only 36% of cases overall.

audits.t: Audit of bone marrow trephines.
audits.st: Minimum adequate trephine length criteria derived from the published literature and local analysis (1.2cm in section / 1.6cm before processing)
audits.f: Average trephine length in section was 1.15cm; 58% of trephines were inadequate by the 1.2cm minimum length criterion; the Jamshidi needle tended to produce longer trephines than the Islam needle.

audits.t: Histological audit of acute appendicitis.
audits.tp: Histological reporting consistency for acute appendicitis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Full agreement between reports in 73 cases and some discrepancy in 27 cases; a five-category reporting scheme was proposed to improve clarity.

audits.t: Prospective audit of mucosal biopsy specimens of the gastrointestinal tract.
audits.st: Local clinical/pathological justification criteria for taking a mucosal biopsy
audits.f: A clear justification for biopsy was identified in over 90% (171/190) of patients; histology was normal in 41% (78/190); management changed on receipt of results in 36% (68/190).

audits.t: Audit of an emergency biochemistry service.
audits.st: Local explicit criteria devised to categorise emergency test requests as appropriate or inappropriate
audits.f: 384 (75%) of requests were appropriate and 125 (25%) inappropriate; inappropriate requests were mainly preoperative samples (43.2%), missed routine samples (33.6%), and accelerated/priority analyses (16%).

audits.t: SP3-1 An audit of diabetes care at primary healthcare centers in Dubai/UAE 2010
audits.st: CDC and ICSI international standards for diabetes management (HbA1c, lipid, BMI, blood pressure, foot/eye examination, lifestyle advice)
audits.f: HbA1c checked >=2 times/year in 80.4% (meets standard); 67.82% had abnormal HbA1c; foot examination documented in only 22%; vision assessment in 40%; diet/exercise advice documented in 35%, against an international reference of 60% for documentation.

audits.t: THE TOS2 STUDY: AN INTERNATIONAL MULTI-CENTRE AUDIT ASSESSING THE STANDARD OF NEUROLOGICAL EXAMINATION
audits.st: Local audit standard for use of tendon hammer, ophthalmoscope and stethoscope prior to neurology referral
audits.f: 264 (64.86%) recalled tendon hammer examination, 119 (29.24%) ophthalmoscopy, 321 (78.87%) stethoscope examination.
audits.c: Results were disseminated to local medical teams (educational feedback/intervention).
audits.r2: Tendon hammer use improved to 298 (76.21%, p<0.001); ophthalmoscope use improved to 149 (38.11%, p=0.009); stethoscope use improved to 330 (84.4%, p=0.045).
audits.co: UK, Jordan, Sweden, United Arab Emirates

audits.t: 5 YEARS EXPERIENCE OF PRIMARY CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM LYMPHOMA (PCNSL): A RETROSPECTIVE PILOT AUDIT
audits.st: Criteria derived from 2011 British Neuro-Oncology guidelines for PCNSL diagnosis
audits.f: 20% of patients had steroids with a documented clinical reason pre-biopsy; 5% had HIV status checked; 88% had CT staging; 5 patients had negative CSF pre-biopsy.

audits.t: AUDIT OF CSF CYTOLOGY AT THE WEST MIDLANDS NEUROSCIENCE CENTRE
audits.tp: CSF cytology sample volume for neoplastic meningitis diagnosis
audits.st: European Guidelines on CSF analysis recommending a minimum of 10.5ml of CSF for cytology
audits.f: Median volume of CSF sent for cytology was 2ml (IQR 1-5ml); only a small number of samples met the >=10.5ml standard, with a further 8% (22 samples) close at 10-10.5ml.

audits.t: ONE YEAR RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT OF CNS MALIGNANCY 2 WW REFERRALS
audits.tp: Two week wait referral guideline compliance for suspected CNS malignancy
audits.st: NICE two-week-wait (2WW) referral guidelines for suspected CNS malignancy
audits.f: Only 48.5% of referrals fulfilled NICE 2WW guidelines; only 28% of referrals received diagnostic imaging and an outpatient appointment within 2 weeks; 3 tumours were diagnosed, all identified by guideline-compliant referrals.

audits.t: INDOMETHACIN TEST USAGE AT UNITED KINGDOM TERTIARY CENTRES OVER 20 YEARS-AN AUDIT
audits.tp: Indomethacin test protocol compliance for headache diagnosis
audits.st: A locally defined minimum data set requirement for conducting the placebo-controlled indomethacin test (P-Indotest)
audits.f: P-Indotest was positive in 78% of cases with paroxysmal hemicrania or hemicrania continua; the test procedure was reviewed for compliance against the minimum data set standard and re-scored by a blinded observer; no serious adverse events were noted.

audits.t: A CLINICAL AUDIT OF ACUTE MANAGEMENT OF STROKE-LIKE EPISODES FROM A NATIONAL MITOCHONDRIAL DISEASE CENTRE
audits.tp: Acute management of stroke-like episodes in mitochondrial disease
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Time to hospital admission and investigation was highly variable; recognition and treatment of seizure activity were often delayed.

audits.t: OCCIPITAL NERVE BLOCK: AUDIT OF A DEVELOPING SERVICE
audits.tp: Occipital nerve block service audit for headache
audits.st: Local standards determined through literature review, as no national guidelines exist for occipital nerve block (ONB)
audits.f: Mean 23 days headache freedom, 42% reduction in headache severity, 38% reduction in headache days per week; mean duration of effect 44 days; mild complications included injection site pain in 65%.

audits.t: WED 033 Minimum prevalence of non-compliance recorded in an audit of antenatal care in a district general hospital joint obstetric epilepsy
audits.tp: Antenatal epilepsy care and AED concordance
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 25/143 were not on any antiepileptic drug (AED) at booking; AED levels were undetectable in 10/57 (17.5%) tested; non-concordance at booking was documented in 1 in 6; 11/87 (12.6%) previously seizure-free patients lost seizure control.

audits.t: 072 Clinical audit of stroke admissions associated with atrial fibrillation and anticoagulation rates
audits.st: Guideline recommendation for anticoagulation in patients with AF-related stroke/TIA risk
audits.f: Anticoagulation rate reported as 41% at the time of the 2009 audit, with new AF diagnosed post-stroke in 22% of cases.
audits.r2: 61.9% of patients were receiving anticoagulants prior to stroke/TIA; anticoagulation rates on discharge improved to 81.6% (40/49); 60% of patients on warfarin had sub-therapeutic INR (<2.0) on admission; new AF diagnosed post-stroke in 17.1%.

audits.t: 108 Audit of the management of idiopathic intracranial hypertension in the context of new consensus guidelines
audits.st: 2018 consensus guidelines for management of idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH)
audits.f: 100% had lumbar puncture, brain imaging, and opening pressure recorded; brain imaging within 24 hours achieved in 84%, but only 53% within 48 hours; documentation of teratogenicity risk, side effects and BMI was poor.

audits.t: 111 An audit of headache referrals from primary care, and subsequent management in the outpatient clinic
audits.tp: Headache referral appropriateness from primary care
audits.st: LTHT referral criteria and Neuro Network Vanguard (NNV) headache pathway
audits.f: Referrals were appropriate in 44% (LTHT criteria) and 49% (NNV criteria); migraine was the suspected diagnosis in 50% of referrals and the final diagnosis in 72% of the 89 reviewed.

audits.t: 127 Audit of poor response to botulinum toxin in cervical dystonia
audits.tp: Botulinum toxin non-response management in cervical dystonia
audits.st: 2016 British Neurotoxin Network (BNN) recommendations for managing secondary non-responsiveness to botulinum toxin
audits.f: 37 (54%) had suboptimal response and 31 (46%) no response to BoNT-A; of the suboptimal group, 57% responded to dose/technique adjustment; in the no-response group, BoNT-A resistance was confirmed in 36% of those tested (8/22).

audits.t: 075 Meningitis management audit at a single centre: further support for culture-independent techniques in diagnosing meningitis
audits.st: British Infection Association (BIA) recommendations for meningitis diagnosis and management
audits.f: Median time to lumbar puncture (LP) was 19 hours (IQR 11.0-31.0), none performed within 1 hour; antibiotics given before LP in 72% of cases; serum PCR sent in only 11% of community-acquired cases (23% positive); CSF PCR sent in 28% (22% positive).

audits.t: 002 Management of idiopathic intracranial hypertension: an audit of the 2018 ABN guidelines
audits.st: 2018 Association of British Neurologists (ABN) guidelines for management of idiopathic intracranial hypertension
audits.f: CSF opening pressure recorded in 100%; only 42% had MRI brain and 24% MR-venogram within 24 hours; only 27% completed all neuroimaging within 48 hours; BMI recorded in only 3%; weight management discussed in 27%; drug side effect discussion documented in 15% and teratogenicity in 3%.

audits.t: 003 Diagnostic workup in suspected viral encephalitis-a single centre audit
audits.tp: Viral encephalitis diagnostic workup guideline compliance
audits.st: 2012 British Infection Society and Association of British Neurologists joint guidelines for management of encephalitis
audits.f: Time to lumbar puncture 30.47+/-6.98 hours; opening pressure documented in 46.6% (14/30); paired serum glucose sent in 20% (6/30); time to acyclovir administration 10.43+/-4.01 hours; viral PCR performed in 90% (27/30), 10% HSV-1 positive; repeat LP after 24 hours in only 10% (3/30).

audits.t: 032 Clinical audit research and evaluation for motor neurone disease (CARE-MND): alignment with clinical care standards
audits.tp: Motor neurone disease care data completeness (CARE-MND KPIs)
audits.st: HIS/QIS Neurological Standards (2009) and NICE Motor Neurone Disease guidelines (2016), operationalised as 14 key performance indicators
audits.f: 73% average completion in data capture across the 14 KPI areas of clinical care, based on 53 data fields.

audits.t: 11.51 Introducing atraumatic needles to the neurology ambulatory day case unit – a quality improvement project
audits.tp: Atraumatic needle use for lumbar puncture
audits.st: Local target to increase atraumatic needle use in lumbar puncture
audits.f: Atraumatic needle used in 26% of LPs
audits.c: Atraumatic needle training video for junior doctors, simulation mannequin practice, and ensuring atraumatic needles added to standard stock
audits.r2: Atraumatic needle use increased to 50% of LPs; junior doctor confidence rose from 2/10 to 8/10 (p=0.02)

audits.t: TP3-9 Assessment of seizures in over 75-year olds: a clinical audit
audits.tp: First seizure assessment in older adults (guideline compliance)
audits.st: NICE guidance (CG137) for assessment and specialist review of first seizures
audits.f: Only 38% of patients were seen by a specialist within the recommended 2 weeks; 65% of patients indicated for EEG had one, and 34% waited longer than 4 weeks; MRI within 4 weeks achieved in 95%; blood glucose measured in only 47% and 12-lead ECG performed in only 51%.

audits.t: 087 Audit of thymectomy for thymoma associated and non-thymoma associated myasthenia gravis at Southampton General Hospital
audits.st: 2016 randomised controlled trial evidence supporting thymectomy for non-thymoma associated myasthenia gravis, adopted into local practice
audits.f: Thymectomies increased 8-fold for non-thymoma and 3-fold for thymoma-associated MG; time from diagnosis to surgery for non-thymoma cases fell from 8.8 to 2.3 years; 15/24 cases performed by VATS (12% more than previously); 50% of patients were on reduced immunosuppression by 6 months without deterioration; a small increase in surgical morbidity was seen.
audits.c: Adoption of the 2016 RCT evidence supporting thymectomy for non-thymoma myasthenia gravis into local practice, and development of an MDT to streamline care.

audits.t: 096 Maintenance IVIg safe prescribing – audit of proforma and traffic light risk assessment system in NHNN
audits.st: Local traffic-light risk assessment protocol for IVIg safety monitoring (VTE/ATE screening, blood testing) for inflammatory neuropathies
audits.f: 26.1% (18/69) had bloods taken prior to administration; 87% were screened for VTE symptoms and 43.5% for ATE symptoms; only 2.9% and 0% were asked about VTE/ATE risk factors respectively; 91.3% were asked about infectious symptoms.
audits.c: Introduction of a proforma and traffic-light risk assessment system for IVIg safety monitoring.
audits.r2: Screening for VTE, ATE, and infectious symptoms/risk improved to 100%; appropriate pre-IVIg bloods were taken in only 6% (4) of cases.

audits.t: 126 Headache recognition and management in acute traumatic brain injury patients – a service audit
audits.tp: Headache recognition and management after traumatic brain injury
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 60% of patients received regular analgesia in hospital, but clear documentation of headache was found in only 5%; only 7.7% of patients discharged on regular analgesia received written headache management advice; TBI specialty review occurred in 22% of TBI patients.

audits.t: 135 A national audit of service provision for patients with atypical parkinsonian syndrome
audits.st: 2011 PSP Association care pathway for atypical parkinsonian syndrome (APS), recommending prompt specialist assessment and MDT approach
audits.f: 8 trusts had specialist APS clinics, 36 movement disorder clinics, 21 general clinics; a therapist/nurse was present in 88%, 53% and 10% of clinics respectively; a named point of contact was provided in 86%, 100% and 62% respectively.

audits.t: UK Multiple Sclerosis service audit of 70 centres: access to neuroradiology
audits.tp: Multiple sclerosis service access to neuroradiology
audits.st: GIRFT recommendation for disease-specific MS service data, including access to specialist neuroradiology reporting
audits.f: 76% felt at least half of MRI scans were reported in a timely manner; 46% felt lack of MRI access impacted the care they could offer; 68% of centres had scans reported by a neuroradiologist, but 63% outsourced reporting and 69% were concerned about reporting quality.

audits.t: 018 The national audit of seizure management in hospitals: round 3 (NASH 3)
audits.tp: National audit of seizure management in hospitals (NASH)
audits.st: National standards for acute seizure management, including eyewitness history, CT imaging, and specialist referral (NASH audit criteria)
audits.f: CT brain was requested in the ED in 45% of first-seizure attendances, and in 17% of patients with known epilepsy.
audits.r2: CT brain requested in 66% of first-seizure attendances (up from 45%); eyewitness contact attempted in 70.4%; onward referral for specialist review requested in 64%; for epilepsy patients, CT requested in 30% (up from 17%) and specialist review requested for 35-44%.

audits.t: 086 A UK multicentre audit on the use of MRI in multiple sclerosis
audits.tp: MRI use variation in multiple sclerosis care
audits.st: Recommended frequency for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) surveillance scanning in MS patients on disease-modifying treatment
audits.f: Routine monitoring accounted for 45% of MRI scans; inter-scan interval varied by centre from 12 to 32 months; only half of patients requiring PML surveillance were scanned at the recommended frequency.

audits.t: 107 The UK multiple sclerosis service and DMT prescribing audit of 70 centres: overview
audits.tp: Multiple sclerosis service and disease-modifying treatment (DMT) prescribing variation
audits.st: GIRFT recommendation for disease-specific MS service data collection
audits.f: Combined DMT spend exceeded GBP261 million in the financial year; findings across companion abstracts included high caseloads, inconsistent team structures, low staffing levels, and limited data collection.

audits.t: 108 UK multiple sclerosis service and DMT audit of 70 centres: variation in DMT prescribing
audits.tp: Multiple sclerosis service and disease-modifying treatment (DMT) prescribing variation
audits.st: GIRFT recommendation for disease-specific MS service data on DMT prescribing
audits.f: Proportion of people with MS on DMTs varied 5.5-fold across services (14.6% to 79.4%, mean 39%); proportion prescribed monoclonal antibodies varied 5-fold (9% to 50%); total annual spend exceeded GBP261 million (extrapolated GBP373 million for all 70); mean spend per patient GBP12096, varying 3.6-fold (GBP7116 to GBP25833).

audits.t: 109 UK multiple sclerosis service audit of 70 centres: observed staffing, proposed staffing, coping
audits.st: MS Trust recommendations for sustainable caseloads per MS neurologist and coordinator
audits.f: MS coordinators were present in 44% of services and neuropharmacists in 40%; the ratio of prescribing neurologists to MS nurses varied from 4:1 to 1:4; implied shortfalls of 1.8 MS neurologists, 2.4 MS nurses and 2.6 MS coordinators per centre; no centre felt they were 'coping very well' and 42% were 'struggling to cope'.

audits.t: 110 UK multiple sclerosis service audit of 70 centres: MS-MDTs
audits.st: NHS England requirement for an MS-MDT meeting for services prescribing disease-modifying treatments
audits.f: 68% (46/70) of centres had an MS-MDT, 63% of which met weekly; neuroradiologists attended only 49% of meetings, MS coordinators 79%, and neuropharmacists 50%; a mean of 9 patients (range 1-40) were discussed per meeting.

audits.t: 111 UK Multiple Sclerosis service audit of 70 centres: caseloads, patient lists and databases
audits.tp: Multiple sclerosis service caseloads and databases
audits.st: GIRFT recommendation for disease-specific data collection and digital maturity in MS services
audits.f: Median caseload per service was 1300 (range 96-5500); median DMT caseload 545 (range 79-2300); only 20% of participants graded their caseload estimates as 'very accurate'; 98% used an MS patient database, but many questioned its validity and most relied on Excel-based lists.

audits.t: 060 LFT monitoring for patients prescribed Cannabidiol -an audit of current practice at QEH -Birmingham
audits.tp: Liver function test monitoring for cannabidiol therapy
audits.st: NICE recommendation for liver function test (LFT) monitoring in patients prescribed cannabidiol (CBD) at baseline, 1, 3 and 6 months, then periodically
audits.f: Only 53% (16/30) of patients had LFTs undertaken at least once, of which 75% (12/16) were done by their GP; 3 patients had abnormal LFTs that normalised within 6 months.

audits.t: 150 The 70 UK centre multiple sclerosis service and DMT prescribing audit: practical project solutions
audits.tp: Multiple sclerosis service and DMT prescribing improvement
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Following a prior 70-centre UK audit, practical projects were developed with stakeholders (documentation, care mapping, outcome measures, prescribing database use, HES data quality), funded through a new not-for-profit community interest company.

audits.t: 169 An audit into the management of functional neurological disorder in Salford
audits.st: NICE (2021) Quality Standards for functional neurological disorder
audits.f: 91% had a motor deficit, 53% a sensory deficit; 44% had no documented management plan at discharge and follow-up plans were unclear in 80%.
audits.c: A multidisciplinary FND service was being developed (not yet established at time of audit).

audits.t: 174 Croydon neurology audit of the site of death of patients with motor neurone disease
audits.tp: Site of death documentation in motor neurone disease
audits.st: GIRFT Neurology (Sept 2021) recommendation to audit site of death in MND; NICE guidance on documenting resuscitation status
audits.f: 12 of 20 patients died; 42% died at home vs 27% nationally, 17% in hospital vs 39% nationally, ~15% in hospice; resuscitation status documented in 8 of 17 non-elective admissions.

audits.t: Multi-centre audit of myotonic dystrophy care in UK: is it the time for national recommendations?
audits.st: 2018 consensus-based care recommendations for myotonic dystrophy type 1
audits.f: Neurology reviewed 64% at least annually; cardiology review annual in only 30%; respiratory review six-monthly in 12%; swallowing assessed in 44% of those requiring it; cognitive assessment in 12%.

audits.t: Medical audit: a Well Woman Clinic in the Royal Naval training practice, Gibraltar.
audits.tp: Well Woman Clinic effectiveness and cervical screening uptake
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Attendances at a Well Woman Clinic were compared with attendances for the same reasons at other times; the Age/Sex Register was overhauled and uptake of cervical screening assessed.

audits.t: 56 Hospital at night; setting up from scratch and building sustainability and success in a paediatric teaching hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Multidisciplinary Hospital At Night (HAN) team set up with dedicated HAN room, escalation policy/SOP, ward teaching and 48 PDSA cycles over 18 months
audits.r2: Interruptions to handover stopped (saving 10 min per handover) and 95% of handovers occurred within the allotted time

audits.t: 61 Improving IV fluid prescription in newcastle, UK – a trainee doctor led quality improvement project
audits.st: NICE guidelines/NICE clinical audit tool for IV fluid prescription in adults
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: New IV fluid prescription sheet with decision-aids matching NICE guidance
audits.r2: Mixed response on the NICE Clinical Audit tool, with improvements in some areas and reductions in others; statistically significant reduction in hypokalaemia rates in the first 7 days after admission

audits.t: 71 Developing the hospital at night service at queen elizabeth hospital – an example of effective junior doctor leadership
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: PDSA cycles: regular H@N meetings, structured checklist, relocation, '10 min warning' bleep, trust-wide policy, bleep filtering
audits.r2: Reduction in average handover duration maintained; handover checklist consistently used; later changes adversely affected meeting flow and attendance

audits.t: 159 Improving baseline measurement of blood glucose and cholesterol levels in acute stroke patients: a quality improvement project
audits.tp: Baseline bloods (glucose and cholesterol) on stroke admission
audits.st: Local target: at least 80% of suspected stroke admissions have blood glucose and cholesterol measured on admission
audits.f: 30% had glucose and 34% had cholesterol requested on admission at baseline
audits.c: PDSA cycles: educational email to doctors, adapted Stroke Admission Clerking Proforma with bloods reminder, and an all-inclusive 'Stroke bloods panel' on the electronic ordering system
audits.r2: 82% had glucose and 85% had cholesterol requested on admission after all interventions, meeting the 80% aim

audits.t: 22 An audit of adult VTE risk assessment compliance with NICE guidelines
audits.st: NICE guideline NG89 / NICE Quality Standard 3 (QS3) VTE risk assessment
audits.f: Compliance with initial VTE assessment 91.7% and reassessment 78.2%; 8/60 had no accessible risk assessment form; mean time to initial assessment 38.6 hours; 21/37 at-risk patients not prescribed TEDS; only 20/42 weighed before pharmacological prophylaxis; 0% documented giving written VTE prevention information to high-risk patients
audits.c: not reported (single baseline audit; action plan proposed but not yet implemented)

audits.t: 354. Regional anaesthetic documentation during caesarean section: a clinical audit
audits.tp: Regional anaesthesia documentation in caesarean section
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: ESRA19-0457 Documentation of airway assessment during evaulation of labouring women for epidural placement: a quality improvement project
audits.tp: Airway assessment documentation for labour epidurals
audits.st: Joint Obstetric Anaesthetists' Association and Difficult Airway Society guidelines (documentation of airway assessment, e.g. Mallampati, mouth opening, jaw/neck movement, thyromental/sternomental distances)
audits.f: Airway assessment documented in 18% of cases; of those, 52% were of poor quality
audits.c: Epidural proforma edited to include mandatory airway assessment
audits.r2: Airway assessment documentation increased to 57%; 'good quality' assessments rose to 72%

audits.t: P113 Audit of care of patients with lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) in a sexual health clinic between 1st January 2019 and 30th September 2021
audits.st: British Association for Sexual Health and HIV (BASHH) guidelines: 97% of patients tested for blood-borne viruses; 97% of partners given an action plan
audits.f: 93% of LGV patients received treatment per BASHH guidelines; 93% had HIV testing, 86% syphilis testing and 64% HCV testing at presentation; 64% repeat HIV/syphilis testing outside the window period, 43% for hepatitis C; 93% underwent partner notification
audits.c: not reported (single audit; pandemic-related disruption discussed as a likely cause of shortfalls)

audits.t: 28 Delivering individualised end of life care on oncology, haematology, surgical oncology, renal and renal transplant wards: auditing the implementation of a symptom observation chart and guide to individualised care planning
audits.tp: Individualised end of life care planning and symptom observation
audits.st: The Five Priorities for Care (end of life)
audits.f: PRN medication given within 30 minutes on 61% of occasions; escalation standards (doctor/palliative nurse informed) adhered to on 36% of occasions; standard of completing 1 nursing care plan per 12 hours structured around the Five Priorities not consistently met
audits.c: Development and rollout of a 'Guide to individualised care planning in the last days of life' and an adapted Symptom Observation Chart, piloted then cascaded across wards

audits.t: 196 A clinical audit of use of octreotide in the management of inoperable malignant bowel obstruction at a large cancer centre
audits.tp: Octreotide use in malignant bowel obstruction
audits.st: Local and Palliative Care Formulary guidance: hyoscine butylbromide first line; octreotide started at 300-600 mcg/24h, not exceeding 1500 mcg/24h, with documented indication

audits.t: 58 Anticipatory prescribing and use of syringe drivers – cross boundary audit of practice
audits.tp: Anticipatory prescribing and syringe driver use
audits.st: National guidance on safe, individualised anticipatory prescribing at end of life
audits.f: 93% had an individualised approach to prescribing agitation medication; all had dose and route; 31% had a maximum dose documented; 93% had appropriate dose adjustment for renal impairment

audits.t: P95 Developing a public benchmarking table aligned with national audit quality improvement priorities in pulmonary rehabilitation
audits.st: National COPD Audit Programme quality indicators for PR services
audits.f: 79% of eligible patients captured in the clinical audit; 96% of services participated in the organisational audit; a public benchmarking table of 6 key indicators was created and colour-coded against the national median

audits.t: P193 Non-invasive ventilation: making changes and demonstrating improvement using quality improvement methodology
audits.st: BTS audit/NCEPOD standards and emerging BTS quality standards for NIV
audits.f: Documentation of NIV parameter plan followed approximately 50%
audits.c: NIV bundle, algorithm, standardised training and competency framework developed via PDSA cycles and Action-Effect Diagram; monitored with SPC charts
audits.r2: 111 of 185 possible NIV care-bundles completed since implementation (July 2017); 535 staff trained; documentation of NIV parameter plan increased from approximately 50% to 76%, with evidence of special cause variation from July 2017

audits.t: P25 Pulmonary rehabilitation quality improvement via a regional network
audits.st: National Asthma and COPD Audit Programme (NACAP) PR snapshot audit and BTS PR Guidelines/Standards of Care
audits.f: Region's referral-to-assessment conversion rate 76% (5362/7002) vs national 67% (42752/68073), p=0.26; completion rate 69% (393/564) vs national 62% (4396/7480), p=0.202; 84% vs 32% nationally completed a practice walk test; 91% vs 81% nationally received a written exercise programme at discharge

audits.t: S36 Improving asthma care in the emergency department (ED): a 2-year prospective quality improvement (QI) project
audits.tp: Peak expiratory flow assessment in acute asthma
audits.st: Royal College of Emergency Medicine Asthma Audit target; local aim of 80% of acute asthma patients having PEF within 30 minutes of ED arrival
audits.f: National comparator: 26% of patients had PEF assessed (RCEM Audit 16/17); local baseline lower before intervention (exact % not reported)
audits.c: 7 QI PDSA cycles focused on staff engagement, education and use of the existing asthma pathway, including a shortened asthma proforma and daily staff huddles
audits.r2: Primary QI objective (80% PEF within 30 minutes) achieved within 6 months via bespoke education and weekly reminders, though improvement was not sustained due to winter pressures, staff turnover, a new electronic record and a move to a new ED

audits.t: P163 An audit into the completeness of latent tuberculosis screening in the gastrointestinal department, prior to patients starting anti-tnf-Α therapy
audits.tp: Latent tuberculosis screening before anti-TNF-alpha therapy
audits.st: British Thoracic Society (BTS) guidelines for LTBI screening before anti-TNF-alpha therapy
audits.f: 49% (231/471) had insufficient LTBI screening; 33.3% (157) lacked adequate TB history; 20% (94) lacked a chest radiograph within 3 months; 18.3% (85) had no IGRA performed; 3.2% (15) diagnosed with LTBI; 1 case of TB reactivation after immunosuppression

audits.t: An Audit of Management of Ectopic Pregnancy in a Major Tertiary Healthcare Service
audits.tp: Ectopic pregnancy management adherence to local protocol
audits.st: Local hospital protocols for ectopic pregnancy management
audits.f: 72% received surgical management, 28% medical; 94% of methotrexate use within guidelines, 91% successfully managed without surgery; 97% of surgical cases had documented indications within protocol.

audits.t: Audit and Accreditation of ART Facilities in Japan; JISART’s Commitment Focusing on Quality Management Systems (QMS) and Patient Satisfaction
audits.tp: Accreditation and quality management of ART facilities
audits.st: JISART Code of Practice and quality/safety management guidelines for assisted reproductive technology
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Congenital Hypothyroidism: An Audit and Study of Different Cord Blood Screening TSH Values in a Tertiary Medical Centre in Malaysia
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 99.7% of newborns screened; recall rate 0.63% (n=163) at 25 mIU/L cut-off, rising to 1.3% (n=340) at 20 mIU/L with no additional cases detected; incidence of congenital hypothyroidism 1:1515 at 20 or 25 mIU/L cut-off vs 1:2380 at 30 mIU/L, which would have missed 35% of cases

audits.t: Abstract P1-02-09: Positive predictive value (PPV) of the diagnosis of atypia in breast core biopsies: An audit of MSKCC breast pathology service
audits.tp: Positive predictive value of breast atypia diagnosis on core biopsy
audits.st: Departmental positive predictive value monitoring for breast atypia diagnoses (previously reported PPV benchmark 20-40%)
audits.f: Departmental PPV for malignancy after atypia diagnosis was 24% overall; range 22.8-25% for 5 of 6 pathologists, one at 36.8%; PPV for ADH alone 29.9%, for CCCWA 10%.

audits.t: Abstract P2-11-03: Multidisciplinary breast cancer care registry and quality control system in the Netherlands: The NABON breast cancer audit
audits.tp: National multidisciplinary breast cancer care quality indicators
audits.st: NABON 30 multidisciplinary quality indicators for breast cancer care
audits.f: 94% discussed in MDT before first treatment, 98% after surgery; BI-RADS used in 98% of reports; positive margin rates 7.6% (neo-adjuvant), 5.0% (primary BCS invasive), 20% (DCIS).

audits.t: Abstract P3-07-18: The NABON breast cancer audit; quality improvement in three years' time
audits.tp: National multidisciplinary breast cancer care quality indicators
audits.st: NABON Breast Cancer Audit (NBCA) quality indicators, including guideline adherence for MDT meetings and time to surgery
audits.f: Preoperative MDT 81%, postoperative MDT 90%, time to operation ≤5 weeks 80%, tumour positive margins invasive 6.1%, DCIS 25%, preoperative systemic treatment 10%, immediate reconstruction 15% (invasive)/39% (DCIS).
audits.c: Weekly feedback of quality indicator data to participating hospitals over three years.
audits.r2: Preoperative MDT 96%, postoperative MDT 98%, time to operation ≤5 weeks 85%, tumour positive margins invasive 5.0%, DCIS 20%, preoperative systemic treatment 12%, immediate reconstruction 19% (invasive)/44% (DCIS).

audits.t: Abstract P3-18-17: Impact of change in margin negative guidelines for breast cancer on recurrence rates: Single institution audit
audits.tp: Breast conserving surgery margin positivity before and after guideline change
audits.st: 2014 consensus margin guidelines (no ink on tumour for invasive carcinoma, 2mm for DCIS)
audits.f: Margin positivity rate 8.5% (9.8% upfront BCS, 6.3% post-NACT).
audits.c: Adoption of revised 2014 consensus negative-margin definition.
audits.r2: Margin positivity rate 4.8% (5.3% upfront BCS, 4% post-NACT); 5-year local recurrence-free survival 94.6% (2013) vs 94.7% (2016), disease-free survival 84.9% vs 81.9% (both p=NS).

audits.t: Abstract PO1-22-09: Current margin assessment practice for breast-conserving surgery in China: a single institution audit
audits.tp: Breast conserving surgery margin assessment practice
audits.st: 2014 SSO/ASTRO consensus margin guidelines (no ink on tumour for invasive carcinoma)
audits.f: Overall positive margin rate 2.7%; 77.3% of cases had wider margins (>5mm); reoperation rate 1.9%; ipsilateral breast recurrence 1.7% at median 54.3 months follow-up.

audits.t: Abstract PO4-10-08: Building a standard methodology: Early Gynecologic Consultation and Bone Mass Density Examination in Breast Cancer Patients Receiving Endocrine Therapy
audits.tp: Gynaecological consultation and bone density monitoring on endocrine therapy
audits.st: Locally set criteria: gynaecological consultation triggered on starting tamoxifen; BMD examination triggered on starting an aromatase inhibitor
audits.f: Gynaecological consultation rate 22.4%; 6-month consultation rate for tamoxifen patients 42.9%; baseline BMD testing rate 30.6%
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team with lecture for collaborating doctors; standardised triggering criteria embedded in the ambulatory alarming system; tested via PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Gynaecological consultation rate rose to 40.4% (p=0.006); 6-month consultation rate for tamoxifen patients rose to 77.77% (p=0.005), median time to first consultation fell from 51 to 28 days; BMD testing rate rose to 48.3%

audits.t: Abstract PO5-11-01: Audit of multidisciplinary team meetings for improving breast cancer care
audits.tp: Multidisciplinary team meeting effectiveness for breast cancer care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 38.2% benign cases; pre-MDT plan modified in 31.4% of cases; new investigation advised in 34.7%; 79% feasible for breast conservation; average 7.5 days to decision.

audits.t: Abstract PS5-11-13: Patient navigation improves treatment compliance in women with breast cancer: A prospective observational audit from India
audits.tp: Treatment initiation timeliness in breast cancer
audits.st: Institutional benchmark: treatment planned within 21 days and initiated within 30 days of registration
audits.f: Default rate 34.4% (42/122); treatment initiation within 30 days achieved in 40.2% (49/122); treatment planning within 21 days in 41.8%
audits.c: Structured patient navigation (PN) programme with trained navigators
audits.r2: Default rate 18.2% (49/269, p=0.03); treatment initiation within 30 days 58.7% (158/269, p=0.009), a 46% relative improvement; planning within 21 days 43.8% (not significantly different, p=0.78)

audits.t: Serum Growth Hormone Measurements in Clinical Practice: An Audit of Performance from the UK National External Quality Assessment Scheme
audits.tp: External quality assessment of growth hormone assays
audits.st: UK National External Quality Assessment Scheme (NEQAS) for growth hormone testing
audits.f: Between-laboratory agreement for GH immunoassays worsened with newer methods; no numeric performance figures given.

audits.t: Management of Epilepsy among Children in the Gaza Strip: A Multicenter Clinical Audit
audits.st: NICE (2017) guidelines and AACC recommendations for epilepsy diagnosis, treatment and follow-up
audits.f: Overall adherence to audit standards was moderate; 77.4% (147) of records did not include seizure type, frequency and duration; drug therapy inconsistent with seizure type in 8.4% (16); investigations generally underutilised; marked variation between centres

audits.t: Abstract P100: An Interactive, Training-Based Data Audit Approach Improves Subsequent Data Validation in a Large State-Based Registry
audits.tp: Stroke registry data accuracy and abstractor training
audits.st: National Coverdell Stroke Registry data element definitions
audits.f: Mean variable-level discrepancy rate 11%; 20% of variables (10/51) had 'high' error rates.
audits.c: Interactive training-based site visit audits with re-abstraction of charts and written feedback to coordinators.
audits.r2: Mean discrepancy rate fell to 5% in 2008 and remained 5% in 2009 (p=0.006); proportion of 'high' discrepancy variables fell to 3% (2008) and 0% (2009), p=0.001.

audits.t: Abstract 18: Does Quality Improvement Training Add to Audit and Feedback for Inpatient Stroke Care Processes?
audits.tp: VTE prophylaxis and dysphagia screening in stroke care
audits.st: GWTG-Stroke quality indicators for DVT prophylaxis and dysphagia screening
audits.f: Pre-intervention DVT prophylaxis 85% (intervention) vs 90% (control); dysphagia screening 51% vs 37%.
audits.c: Quality improvement training programme plus QI feedback (intervention sites) vs QI feedback alone (control sites) in a cluster randomised trial.
audits.r2: Post-intervention DVT prophylaxis 90% (intervention) vs 94% (control), ratio of ORs 0.89 (p=0.75); dysphagia screening 56% vs 52%, ratio of ORs 0.67 (p=0.04), improving more in control sites.

audits.t: Internal Audit as a Quality Assurance Tool to Ensure Staff and Patient Safety During COVID-19 Pandemic
audits.st: CDC, WHO, Indian Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and All India Ophthalmological Society COVID-19 prevention protocols
audits.f: 100% staff compliance with PPE usage and hand hygiene, but 21 incidents of physical distancing not maintained; 100% compliance with facemask use, but 34.5% of patients wore masks improperly; thermal screening not performed at 6/53 (11.3%) observations, no thermal screener at 3/23 instances

audits.t: Beta-Interferon Use in Multiple Sclerosis: Audit of Practice in Grampian
audits.st: Current clinical guidelines for beta-interferon use in multiple sclerosis
audits.f: 137 patients treated (12.5% of local MS population); very few discontinued treatment; treatment found to be in line with current clinical guidelines.

audits.t: Four-Year Prospective Audit of Tonsillectomy Practice in Argyll and Clyde
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 76% discharged on first postoperative day; complication rate 1.33%; 3% readmitted (mostly secondary haemorrhage); prophylactic antibiotics used in 39% of cases.

audits.t: Prospective Audit of the Management of Head Injuries in a Small District General Hospital
audits.tp: Head injury CT scanning compliance with SIGN guidelines
audits.st: Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN, Sept 2000) recommendations on CT scanning for head injury
audits.f: 15 patients met CT criteria; 9 were scanned; only 1 of 15 scanned within the recommended 4-hour period.

audits.t: Audit of acute upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage: the effects of education and the introduction of a protocol.
audits.st: Local protocol for management of acute upper GI haemorrhage, supported by a teaching programme for House Officers; no external numeric target stated
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Introduction of a management protocol for acute upper GI haemorrhage and a teaching programme for House Officers
audits.r2: Results suggested a reduction in out-of-hours emergency endoscopies and the need for emergency surgery, alongside a policy of active endoscopic intervention

audits.t: An audit to assess the impact of a strategy to reduce inappropriate red cell transfusions at Honiara Hospital.
audits.st: Local blood transfusion committee standards for rational, safe, cost-effective blood use (target for 'group and hold' requests not numerically stated)
audits.f: Baseline rates of units crossmatched per admission and units transfused per 100 operations before the education strategy (not reported)
audits.c: Establishment of a blood transfusion committee and an education strategy to reduce inappropriate red cell transfusion
audits.r2: 29.7% reduction in units of blood crossmatched as a proportion of total admissions; 30.1% reduction in units transfused per 100 operations

audits.t: Audit of Flexible Nasoendoscope Decontamination: Clinical Efficacy and Cost Effectiveness
audits.st: UK Department of Health recommendation for automated washer decontamination of flexible nasoendoscopes
audits.f: Chlorine dioxide wipes: 2% (1/50) residual growth vs automated wash: 28% (14/50) (p<0.001); automated washer cheaper over 10 years.

audits.t: Fast Track Head and Neck Referrals Audit
audits.tp: Head and neck 2-week-wait cancer referral appropriateness
audits.st: NICE urgent referral guidelines; UK Department of Health 2-week cancer referral target
audits.f: 425 (95%) seen within 14 days, average wait 9 days; diagnostic yield for malignancy 6%; average symptom duration before referral over 6 months.

audits.t: Comprehensive Dynamic Airway Assessment: Audit of a Novel Technique to Improve Rates of Tracheostomy Decannulation
audits.tp: Tracheostomy decannulation rate improvement with a new airway assessment technique
audits.st: Conventional tracheostomy decannulation protocols using flexible nasendoscopy
audits.f: Using conventional management, 5 of 17 (31%) patients who failed initial decannulation were eventually decannulated with a standard approach.
audits.c: Introduction of the Comprehensive Dynamic Airway Assessment (CDAA) technique.
audits.r2: 6 of 8 (75%) patients undergoing CDAA were decannulated; a diagnosis for decannulation failure was made in the remaining 2.

audits.t: Audit of Patients Undergoing Thyroid Surgery in an Attempt to Improve the Standard of Care
audits.tp: Thyroid surgery documentation of nerve monitoring and vocal cord checks
audits.st: National Institute for Clinical Excellence (NICE) criteria for thyroid surgery care
audits.f: Haphazard postoperative calcium management; incomplete documentation of vocal cord checks and recurrent laryngeal nerve identification/testing.
audits.c: Recommendations and staff guidance, plus a revised protocol on calcium management.
audits.r2: Only 1 patient became hypocalcaemic postoperatively (managed per protocol); RLN identification, testing and monitoring, and pre/postoperative vocal cord checks documented in all patients.

audits.t: A Clinical Audit of the Outcome of Occupational Therapy Assessment and Negotiated Patient Goals in the Acute Setting
audits.tp: Occupational therapy assessment and goal-setting documentation
audits.st: Locally set standard combining the Modified Barthel Index with negotiated patient goal setting
audits.f: Baseline review of functional assessment and documentation process.
audits.c: Practice changed to meet the combined Modified Barthel Index and negotiated goal-setting standard.
audits.r2: Subsequent audit found reliability/validity of goal setting depended on therapists' ability to write specific, quantifiable goals; low disability levels found on discharge.

audits.t: How Successful are We at Getting our Clients Back to Work? The Results of an Audit
audits.st: Locally developed guidelines for assisting return to work
audits.f: Retrospective audit highlighted several areas where the return-to-work process had not been successful.
audits.c: New multiagency guidelines for return-to-work developed in 2000.

audits.t: An Audit of Occupational Therapy Outpatient Attendance
audits.tp: Occupational therapy outpatient attendance and referral procedures
audits.st: Locally set referral procedure standard for first appointment attendance
audits.f: Baseline attendance for first appointments before new referral procedures.
audits.r2: Improved attendance for first appointments in neuropsychiatry after new referral procedures were followed, though substantial drop-out from therapy continued.

audits.t: Elderly Fallers: A Baseline Audit of Admissions to a Day Hospital for Elderly People
audits.tp: Falls incidence among day hospital admissions for elderly people
audits.st: Locally agreed audit criteria developed by consensus following literature review
audits.f: 56 of 196 (29%) had fallen at least once; 73% had no apparent predisposing factor; 59% had increased social support after the fall.

audits.t: Audit of a Group Programme for Inpatients in an Acute Mental Health Setting
audits.tp: Ward occupational therapy group programme uptake
audits.st: not reported
