audits.r2: Patient contacts almost doubled and time from referral to first contact significantly reduced; ward nursing staff positive about changes.

audits.t: Clinical Audit of the Outcome of Individualised Occupational Therapy Goals
audits.st: Locally developed individualised outcome measure and audit system
audits.f: Positive outcome achieved in 88% of individual goals.
audits.c: Ongoing use of individualised outcome measure/audit system with documentation improvements.
audits.r2: Positive outcome achieved in 90% of individual goals.

audits.t: Assistive Devices: An Audit of Waiting Times
audits.st: Locally set target to minimise delays in assistive device supply
audits.f: Patients waited an average of 39 days for an assistive device.
audits.c: Fife Rheumatic Diseases Unit occupational therapists took on direct supply of consumables (previously via Fife Social Work Service).
audits.r2: Average waiting time reduced to 21 days, an improvement of 18 days.

audits.t: Introduction of a Mandatory Pre-Block Safety Checklist into a Regional Anaesthesia Block Room Service: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.tp: Mandatory pre-block safety checklist to prevent wrong-side nerve blocks
audits.st: Locally introduced mandatory pre-block ('stop before you block') safety checklist
audits.f: Checklist compliance 31%.
audits.c: Introduction of a mandatory pre-block safety checklist following a wrong-side block incident.
audits.r2: Checklist compliance rose to over 90%, with no negative effect on block efficacy, theatre efficiency, complications or patient satisfaction.

audits.t: Clinical and economic benefits of de-escalating stress ulcer prophylaxis therapy in the intensive care unit: A quality improvement study
audits.tp: Inappropriate continuation of stress ulcer prophylaxis at discharge
audits.st: Locally developed prescribing guideline for stress ulcer prophylaxis discontinuation
audits.f: 78 of 184 (42.4%) hospital survivors inappropriately continued on stress ulcer prophylaxis at discharge.
audits.c: Prescribing guideline, education programme and pharmacist oversight.
audits.r2: 11 of 143 (7.7%) inappropriately continued (OR 8.83, 95% CI 4.47-17.45, p<0.0001); C. difficile cases fell from 10 to 1.

audits.t: A multidisciplinary perioperative medicine clinic to improve high-risk patient outcomes: A service evaluation audit
audits.tp: Multidisciplinary perioperative medicine clinic for high-risk surgical patients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 2017 high-risk cohort: unplanned ICU admission 19%, 30-day mortality 13%, 30-day readmission 20%.
audits.c: Introduction of a multidisciplinary Comprehensive High-Risk Surgical Patient Clinic (Jan 2019-Mar 2020).
audits.r2: Unplanned ICU admission 8%, 30-day mortality 0%, 30-day readmission 0%; shorter postoperative stay (median 8 vs 10.5 days).

audits.t: Adverse Local Reactions to Amethocaine Cream—Audit and Case Reports
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Severe local adverse reactions to 4% amethocaine cream found to be rare (exact rate not stated); two case reports of local reactions described

audits.t: Tube Feeding Audit Reveals Hidden Costs and Risks of Current Practice
audits.tp: Tube feeding practice and cost audit
audits.st: Hang-time policy and safe tube feeding practice standards (unspecified source)
audits.f: 18-62% of formula wasted per patient per day; mean annual wasted formula cost $26,846 per facility; open systems required 14 min/patient/day vs 2 min for closed systems (extra $47,744/year); 33% of feedings required additional labour

audits.t: A comparative study of clinical and autopsy findings (Clinical audit) in 100 cases died of trauma
audits.tp: Clinical versus autopsy diagnosis discrepancy in trauma deaths
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Rational Use of Medicines: An Audit of Private Practitioners’ Prescription
audits.tp: Prescribing practice audit in private practice
audits.st: Standard prescribing norms for complete, rational prescriptions (unspecified source)
audits.f: Prescriptions lacked age/sex/diagnosis/dosage information; antibiotics most widely prescribed (37%); >65% of NSAIDs prescribed as fixed-dose combinations; polypharmacy (≥4 drugs) in 38.5%; no drugs prescribed by generic name; median cost per day ₹29.30

audits.t: Clinical Audit on Short Stay Emergency Medical Admission
audits.st: Appropriateness Evaluation Protocol
audits.f: 13/177 (7.3%) admissions considered inappropriate; assuming stays >24h were appropriate, overall inappropriate admission rate 0.67% (13/1930)

audits.t: Comparative Clinical, Microbiologic, and Economic Audit of the Use of Oral Ciprofloxacin and Parenteral Antimicrobials
audits.tp: Oral versus parenteral antimicrobial use audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Resolution occurred in 133 patients (79 oral, 54 parenteral); overall treatment cost $74.00 (oral) vs $305.59 (parenteral) per course (p<0.001)

audits.t: Effect of COVID-19 on High-risk Neonate Home Care Program: An Audit Study
audits.tp: High-risk neonate home care programme quality
audits.st: Researcher-made checklist across 7 areas of healthcare (no named national standard)
audits.f: Mean score for in-person 'conduction' 56.7 vs in-absentia 52.5; in-person 'education' 63.6 vs in-absentia 65.6; 53.2% of caregivers performed well, 33.5% poorly
audits.c: Shift from in-person to in-absentia (telephone) home care monitoring during the COVID-19 pandemic

audits.t: An Audit of 7000 Successive Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Referrals in Scotland
audits.tp: Child and adolescent psychiatry referral patterns audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Non-attendance rate 28%; average age at referral 10.6 years; boys 56% of referrals; conduct/mixed disorders 37% of diagnoses; improvement in 70% of children treated

audits.t: Audit of computer literacy and skills
audits.tp: Staff IT skills and training needs
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Most clerical staff but only about 33% of medical and nursing staff could use the current patient information system; 72% of staff interested in further IT training
audits.c: Local college arranged to run the CLAIT (Computer Literacy and Information Technology) course on hospital premises

audits.t: WITHDRAWN: Surveillance of Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: An Audit of Sonographer-Led Ultrasound and Radiologist-Led Computed Tomography Services
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: What are the most common reasons for return of ethics submissions? An audit of an Australian health service ethics committee
audits.tp: Reasons for ethics committee requests for further information
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 355 individual request elements analysed; mean 14.2 elements per first request letter; administrative errors most common (in 100% of submissions); Participant Information/Consent Form issues in 79%

audits.t: Improving documentation of side-effects discussions by doctors for newly initiated psychotropic medications in outpatient clinics: A single-centre quality-improvement project
audits.st: Singapore Medical Council Ethical Code and Ethical Guidelines / Modified Montgomery Test; local aim of 100% documentation within 12 months
audits.f: 40% of new cases had documented discussion of at least one side effect
audits.c: PDSA methodology; an IT documentation tool was adopted into the standard documentation template for new case assessments

audits.t: Implementation of criteria-based audit to reduce patient’s burdens and improve efficiency in hospital management
audits.tp: Criteria-based audit performance appraisal in hospital management
audits.st: Hospital-department two-level criteria-based audit (CBA) performance appraisal using six core indicators (2A4P), aligned to 3A grade hospital evaluation criteria
audits.f: Baseline 2A4P performance data (values not given in abstract)
audits.c: Implementation of a hospital-department two-level criteria-based audit (CBA) management performance appraisal model
audits.r2: Significant improvement (P<0.05 or P<0.001) in 2A4P data compared with 2016

audits.t: Treating Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-sectional Audit of Naturopathic Standards of Care Using the Naturopathic Patient Database
audits.tp: Type 2 diabetes management against ADA standards (naturopathic clinic)
audits.st: American Diabetes Association 2010 Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes
audits.f: Average audit score 55.5/90 across diagnosis, physical exam, laboratory tests and management categories graded 0-2

audits.t: An Audit of Lipid Management in Patients with Diabetes in an Academic Internal Medicine Practice
audits.st: Nationally accepted diabetes standards of care (LDL-C goal <100 mg/dL)
audits.f: 42% at LDL-C goal <100 mg/dL; 65% on a statin; 12% (24 patients) had high LDL-C (>130) but were not on lipid-lowering agents; 36% remained above goal despite statin use

audits.t: Albumin Audit Results and Guidelines for Use
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 60 adult patients received 1-69 units of albumin; surgical services prescribed 73%, medical 27%; common indication volume expansion (65%); pharmacy computer system identified only 63% of patients; up to $17,740/year (15%) of albumin administered went unbilled
audits.c: Development and approval of albumin use guidelines by the pharmacy and therapeutics committee following the audit

audits.t: Feasibility of an Audit System for Canadian Sonographers in Generalist Ultrasound
audits.st: Degree of agreement between sonographer technical impression and radiologist final report
audits.f: 75% (322/429) complete agreement (DoA1); 20% DoA2; 4% DoA3; 1% (5/429) significant discrepancy (DoA4)

audits.t: Collaborative diabetes virtual clinics – a service evaluation and clinical audit
audits.st: Local audit standard: 50% of cases with baseline HbA1c >=58 mmol/mol (7.5%) to achieve a clinically significant reduction of >=6 mmol/mol (0.4%)
audits.f: HbA1c reduced by 7 mmol/mol (0.46%) from 73 mmol/mol (8.79%) to 67 mmol/mol (8.32%), p=0.001; 85% of patients achieved an improvement in glycaemic control and 57% achieved a reduction of >=6 mmol/mol, exceeding the audit standard
audits.c: Diabetes virtual clinic enabling collaborative case discussion between the specialist and primary care teams

audits.t: Saskatoon Urban Hospital Frozen Plasma Utilization and Appropriateness Audit
audits.st: Ontario Clinical Practice Recommendations for the Use of Frozen Plasma
audits.f: 50.5% of adult plasma transfusions judged inappropriate; most common inappropriate indication was INR ≤1.5 (26.5%); among paediatric patients, 79.8% of transfusions were inappropriate
audits.c: Proposed implementation of local clinical practice guidelines, plasma order screening by the transfusion laboratory, or a plasma transfusion order set

audits.t: Quality of Oral Anticoagulation with Vitamin K Antagonists in 'Real-World' Patients: Lessons from a Six Years Audit Study
audits.tp: Time in therapeutic range for vitamin K antagonist anticoagulation
audits.st: Target time in therapeutic range (TTR) 70-80% for oral anticoagulation with vitamin K antagonists
audits.f: TTR 83% (Group 1, target INR 2-3), 74% (Group 2, target 2.5-3.5), 54% (Group 3, target 3-4)
audits.c: Increased time between INR measurements beyond the 4-8 week recall interval
audits.r2: TTR 72% (Group 1), 69% (Group 2), 60% (Group 3); TTR decreased in Groups 1 and 2 but increased in Group 3 versus the previous study (p<0.001)

audits.t: Substantial Variability in Platelet Transfusion Practice in a Patient-Level Audit of 56,204 Transfusions across 22 Hospitals
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: A quality improvement project to optimize VTE prophylaxis in surgical patients
audits.tp: VTE prophylaxis appropriateness in surgical patients
audits.st: Institutional/guideline-based VTE prophylaxis algorithm (agent and dosing by weight, renal function and VTE risk)
audits.f: 37.8% received guideline-concordant VTE prophylaxis; main causes of inappropriate prophylaxis were incorrect choice between pharmacological/non-pharmacological prophylaxis (22.4%), inappropriate agent selection by renal function (65.7%) and incorrect weight-based dosing (11.9%)
audits.c: Education sessions for surgical teams, weekly automated data extraction with manual chart audit and individualised feedback, and an EHR pop-up alert with embedded VTE prophylaxis algorithm
audits.r2: Appropriateness improved to 54.8% (p<0.0001); SPC charts showed sustained special cause variation from October 2024

audits.t: Less plasma, less drama: A quality improvement initiative to reduce inappropriate plasmatransfusions across community hospitals in the niagara region.
audits.st: Appropriate plasma transfusion defined as INR >1.7 and dose of 3-4 units in adults
audits.f: 42% of plasma transfusions in hospitalised adults were inappropriate
audits.c: Awareness campaign, enhanced audit and feedback, and an electronic Transfusion Medicine order set in the hospitals' EMR, tested via PDSA cycles from July 2024
audits.r2: 253 plasma units transfused over the study period; median monthly appropriate transfusion rates 90% (INR>1.7), 89% (dose>2 units) and 78% meeting both criteria; out-of-guideline requests screened by technologists fell by 15%

audits.t: A Transfusion Audit In An Ugandan Hospital
audits.tp: Blood transfusion practice audit in a resource-limited setting
audits.st: Expected transfusion practice standards for cross-matching, patient identification and documentation (unspecified source)

audits.t: Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) Usage and Appropriateness in Adult Medical in-Patients: A Retrospective Audit
audits.tp: Fresh frozen plasma appropriateness of use in medical inpatients

audits.t: Lung cancer multi-disciplinary team (MDT) decisions audit

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Provision of nonpharmacolocical treatment options for COPD patients in 13 European countries: Results from the European COPD audit

audits.t: Audit of intervention to improve educational experience in a respiratory medicine department
audits.tp: Junior doctor educational experience in respiratory department

audits.t: Audit on pleural procedure in UK district general hospital
audits.tp: Intercostal chest drain insertion training and practice

audits.t: Using quality indicators to monitor changes in adherence to clinical practice guidelines for treatment of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) of the breast.
audits.st: Interprovincial Delphi-derived quality indicators for DCIS management
audits.f: Axillary staging (axillary dissection) 20%; lower rates of radiation oncology referral, post-lumpectomy radiation and complete pathology reporting
audits.r2: Significant improvement in radiation oncology referral, post-lumpectomy radiation, and complete pathology reporting; axillary staging (sentinel node biopsy) rose to 73%; sentinel node biopsy rate considered unacceptably high

audits.t: Compliance to select quality measures in a non-QOPI subspecialty academic practice: A pilot quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: ASCO QOPI core and colorectal disease-specific quality measures (QOPI certification requires 72.62% core / 80% adjuvant)
audits.f: Average compliance with 17 QOPI measures 96%, 98%, 92% and 97% by month; only 48% of patients met all 17 measures
audits.c: Assignment of staff roles to meet defined quality measures prior to project start, with separate auditor review

audits.t: Timeliness of adjuvant chemotherapy (AT) for stage III adenocarcinoma of colon (CC): A measure of quality of care.
audits.tp: Time to adjuvant chemotherapy in colon cancer
audits.st: Clinical trial convention of adjuvant chemotherapy start within 8 weeks of surgery (no established standard time)
audits.f: Median time to start of adjuvant chemotherapy 60 days (range 12-145); 60% waited more than 8 weeks and 19% more than 12 weeks

audits.t: The rapid quality reporting system: Assessing and improving the quality of cancer care with a prospective clinical performance tracking and reporting system.
audits.tp: Breast and colon cancer NQF quality metric compliance
audits.st: National Quality Forum endorsed breast and colon cancer quality of care metrics
audits.f: Baseline compliance for the five measures prior to RQRS participation, lower in patients of other races versus white/black for several measures
audits.c: Implementation of the Rapid Quality Reporting System (RQRS) for prospective monitoring and reporting of compliance
audits.r2: Compliance rates increased significantly for all five measures, from a 16% increase (multi-agent chemotherapy) to 36% (hormone therapy); by 2010 racial difference persisted only for radiation after breast-conserving surgery

audits.t: Use of a community of practice (CoP) platform as a model in regional quality improvements in cancer surgery: The Ottawa model.
audits.tp: Community of practice model for cancer surgery quality
audits.st: Regionally agreed quality indicators and provincial standards for breast, colorectal and prostate cancer surgery
audits.f: Baseline compliance with provincial colon cancer surgery guidelines and prostate cancer surgical margin rate of 45%
audits.c: Community of Practice (CoP) model combining educational outreach, audit and feedback, and a regional registry across 9 hospitals
audits.r2: Regional pathway compliance 65-94%; colon cancer guideline compliance increased 20%; sentinel lymph node biopsy use in breast cancer rose to 60-77%/year; prostate cancer positive margin rate fell from 45% to 22%

audits.t: Effect of a gastrointestinal multidisciplinary clinic on the quality of pancreatic cancer care delivery at a community cancer center.
audits.tp: Multidisciplinary pancreatic cancer quality of care
audits.st: 43 composite quality measures proposed by a 2009 pancreatic cancer expert quality panel
audits.f: Complete guideline adherence in all 30 non-operative patients and 22 of 25 resected patients; overall compliance with all pancreatic cancer care guidelines 99.7%
audits.c: Multidisciplinary treatment planning conference plus clinic, with gastrointestinal nurse navigation

audits.t: Patient Preference and Contraindications in Measuring Quality of Care: What Do Administrative Data Miss?
audits.tp: Lung cancer care quality indicator adherence (VHA)
audits.st: VHA lung cancer-directed therapy quality indicators (6 measures)
audits.f: Adherence to quality indicators ranged from 81% (adjuvant chemotherapy) to 98% (curative resection); refusals 0-14% and contraindications 1-30% accounted for much of the apparent non-adherence

audits.t: Augmenting state cancer registry data for quality-of-care assessment: A Georgia-based application to evaluate receipt of adjuvant therapies for breast cancer and colorectal cancer.
audits.tp: Breast and colorectal cancer adjuvant therapy quality-of-care measurement
audits.st: National Quality Forum endorsed breast and colorectal cancer adjuvant therapy quality measures
audits.f: Stage III colon cancer patients meeting NQF standard for adjuvant chemotherapy: 75% (Medicaid), 92% (Kaiser), 92% (SHBP); breast cancer adjuvant chemotherapy standard met in 86%, 84%, 87% respectively; Medicare-linked patients had lower rates

audits.t: Time to adjuvant chemotherapy (AC) in stage III colon cancer at a community cancer center: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Time to adjuvant chemotherapy in colon cancer
audits.st: Clinical trial convention of adjuvant chemotherapy start within 56 days of surgery
audits.f: Median time to initiation of adjuvant chemotherapy 60 days (range 29-118); only 32% started within 56 days of surgery
audits.c: Educational programmes for referring surgeons on timely referral; pre-booking of central IV devices and colon cancer nurse navigators explored

audits.t: Effects of prospective review of medical oncology treatment plans (TPs) on quality of care, payer denial, and cost.
audits.tp: Prospective review of chemotherapy treatment plans for guideline compliance
audits.st: Recognised oncology guidelines (ASCO, NCI, ASTRO, NCCN) and registered clinical trials
audits.f: 89 treatment plans (44%) contained 92 unexpected variations of care; 12% presented documented safety issues; total net cost difference $304,055 for one cycle
audits.c: Prospective, platform-based review of chemotherapy treatment plans before care delivery, with peer-to-peer discussion for unresolved variances

audits.t: Resource and quality information provided by compliance with NCCN hereditary breast cancer guidelines.
audits.tp: NCCN compliance for genetic counselling and BRCA testing
audits.st: NCCN hereditary breast cancer guidelines for genetic risk assessment and testing
audits.f: Referral to genetic counsellor NCCN-compliant in 99% (671/675); recommendation for BRCA testing NCCN-compliant in 98% (170/174); 74% (128/174) of offered tests were completed

audits.t: Adherence to national quality guidelines for nodal staging and treatment of cutaneous melanoma.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence for lymph node staging in melanoma
audits.st: ASCO/SSO guidelines for lymph node surgery in T2/T3 cutaneous melanoma
audits.f: 75.3% underwent lymph node staging including sentinel lymph node biopsy; of node-positive patients, 73.4% underwent completion lymph node dissection

audits.t: A peer review quality assurance program for outpatient radiation treatments.
audits.tp: Radiation oncology peer review quality assurance
audits.st: Internal weekly peer review requirement for presentation of all definitive radiotherapy cases
audits.f: 8.2% of eligible patients not presented for peer review in 2007; changes recommended in 16.5% of presented cases
audits.c: Weekly multidisciplinary peer review conference (teleconferenced) reviewing radiotherapy plans, with documented QA notes
audits.r2: Missed presentations fell to 2.7%; changes recommended fell to 7.8% (both p<0.001)

audits.t: Standardizing chemotherapy education for quality improvement.
audits.st: Press Ganey Survey for Adult Oncology patient satisfaction scores
audits.f: Patient satisfaction 83.7% understanding what to expect during chemotherapy; 72.9% understanding how to manage side effects
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles: standardised teaching checklist, electronic patient calendars, and patient education assessment survey
audits.r2: Score for what to expect during chemotherapy rose to 92.1%; score for managing side effects rose to 91.9%

audits.t: Reduction in chemotherapy administered at the end of life (CAEOL) through quality improvement processes in a large community oncology clinic: The West Clinic experience.
audits.tp: Chemotherapy administered near end of life
audits.st: Clinic-wide goal of chemotherapy at end of life below 5% (14 days) and 10% (28 days) of death
audits.f: Baseline chemotherapy at end of life (2009-2010 cohort); 1st-line therapy accounted for high proportion of chemotherapy within 28 days of death in NSCLC (42.9%) and pancreatic cancer (68.4%)
audits.c: Distribution of practice-level results to physicians for review and discussion against the clinic-wide standard, with periodic re-evaluation
audits.r2: 14.5% reduction in chemotherapy at end of life within 14 days and 25% reduction within 28 days, meeting the clinic-wide standard

audits.t: Improving oncology quality through the implementation of evidence-based clinical pathways in a payer’s oncology network.
audits.tp: Clinical pathway adherence in oncology chemotherapy
audits.st: Compendium (evidence-based) and preferred clinical pathway adherence for six cancer diagnoses
audits.f: Baseline average compendium-based chemotherapy adherence rate across six cancer diagnoses
audits.c: Mandatory online chemotherapy prior-authorisation system capturing treatment plans and measuring pathway adherence, with quarterly feedback to practices
audits.r2: Statistically significant increase in the level of compendium-based chemotherapy treatment plans submitted, compared with baseline

audits.t: Enhancing your culture of safety and quality through practice accreditation.
audits.st: Third-party radiation oncology practice accreditation standards
audits.f: Internal audits at each of 20 sites identified instances of non-compliance with accreditation standards
audits.c: Education for non-compliant sites, site visits, and multidisciplinary review ahead of external accreditation survey
audits.r2: All 20 sites judged by the accrediting body to meet minimum quality and safety standards and were accredited

audits.t: Customization of electronic health record (EHR) to implement meaningful use for quality improvement (QI).
audits.tp: Meaningful Use compliance in oncology EHR
audits.st: CMS Meaningful Use Stage I criteria (20 criteria, 11 with measurable thresholds)
audits.f: All 20 Meaningful Use criteria met; average compliance for the 11 measurable criteria was 86.8% against an average threshold of 54.5%; $288,000 in incentive money collected
audits.c: Customisation of EHR workflow features to reduce provider documentation burden and audit data-collection compliance via reports

audits.t: Implementation of a statewide quality assessment program for rectal cancer.
audits.st: Literature-based rectal cancer surgery quality measures (lymph node yield, mesorectal excision, margin status, neoadjuvant therapy use, sphincter preservation)
audits.f: Adequate lymph node procurement (>=12) 75% (range 64-100% by hospital); mesorectal excision 76% (38-97%); positive margins 9% (0-17%); neoadjuvant therapy for stage II/III 94% (67-100%); sphincter preservation 86% (62-100%)

audits.t: Onco-fertility care in a children's hospital: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Oncofertility counselling and referral in paediatric oncology
audits.st: Standard of counselling on fertility risk and offering fertility preservation before gonadotoxic therapy
audits.f: Baseline survey: only 70% of patients/parents recalled receiving fertility counselling at diagnosis, and 50% of eligible patients were referred for fertility preservation
audits.c: Multidisciplinary team established a comprehensive risk-stratified fertility counselling and preservation protocol, published on a centre-wide policy repository, with a 24/7 oncofertility consult service

audits.t: Improving immunization (imm) rates among oncology patients and health care providers (HCP) through a partnership of continuing medical education (CME) and quality improvement (QI) in an NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center.
audits.tp: Immunisation rates among oncology patients and staff
audits.st: Regulatory immunisation requirements for patients and healthcare workers; Joint Commission 90% healthcare-worker vaccination goal by 2020
audits.f: 1,129 influenza vaccine doses given to patients; healthcare-worker vaccination rate 65%
audits.c: Multiplatform CME/QI education initiative (lectures, web content, point-of-care tools, visual cues, standardised order sets, vaccine computerised manager) for clinicians, patients and families
audits.r2: 1,838 influenza vaccine doses given (24% increase on prior season); healthcare-worker vaccination rate rose to 76%

audits.t: Assessment of quality improvement efforts by ASCO’s Quality Oncology Practice Initiative (QOPI) participants.
audits.st: ASCO QOPI/QOPI Certification Program measures and standards
audits.f: 96% of respondents reported that QOPI/QCP participation led to local QI efforts; core measures (57%) and symptom/toxicity management (48%) were the most common triggers

audits.t: Development of a new oncology quality metric: The rate of evidence-based adherence.
audits.st: Institutional benchmark of 80% adherence to evidence-based (NCCN/clinical trial based) chemotherapy protocols
audits.f: Institutional Rate of Evidence-Based Adherence (REBA) 0.86 (86%), exceeding the 80% benchmark (p<0.001); disease-group REBA ranged 0.50-0.95; provider REBA in breast group ranged 0.78-0.97

audits.t: Converting a clinical indicator on patient missed treatments into a functional quality improvement metric.
audits.st: American College of Radiology Radiation Oncology Practice Guideline requirement to review unplanned treatment interruptions
audits.f: Missed treatment rate 5-10% over 3 years
audits.c: EMR modification to record missed-treatment sub-categories (intended vs unintended, with 8 unintended reason categories) documented in real time by radiation therapists
audits.r2: Overall missed-treatment rate 8%; documentation compliance 100%; main reasons patient preference (14%), weather (14%), machine downtime (9%)

audits.t: Can protocol development improve breast cancer and breast surgery quality measures?
audits.tp: Breast cancer diagnosis and surgery quality measures
audits.st: Institutional standardised protocols for breast cancer diagnosis and surgical quality measures
audits.f: Pre-surgical needle biopsy 90%; diagnosis via needle biopsy 50%; sentinel lymph node biopsy 43%; specimen orientation 58%; image confirmation 86%; second operations 44%; re-excision for margins 30%
audits.c: Standardised institutional protocols, guidelines, checklists and policies across specialties for breast cancer management
audits.r2: Pre-surgical needle biopsy 96% (p=0.02); diagnosis via needle biopsy 87% (p=0.04); sentinel lymph node biopsy 68% (p<0.001); specimen orientation 88% (p<0.001); image confirmation 97% (p=0.01); second operations 26% (p=0.004); re-excision 14% (p=0.003)

audits.t: Developing symptom management quality improvement reports with data from a registry-based patient reported outcomes (PRO) collection method.
audits.st: Registry-based patient-reported outcome quality indicators for pain, fatigue and emotional distress management
audits.f: 20-45% of patients did not report discussing, or getting advice about, pain, fatigue or emotional distress with their healthcare team; centre-specific rates varied significantly

audits.t: An interdisciplinary model of collaboration between medical staff (MS), hospital quality improvement (QI), and continuing medical education (CME) departments to promote education and practice changes in the prevention of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in cancer patients (pts).
audits.tp: VTE prophylaxis order set compliance in oncology
audits.st: Institutional standardised VTE prophylaxis order sets
audits.f: Compliance with use of standardised VTE prophylaxis order sets 65%
audits.c: Multiplatform education (didactic lectures, visiting professorships, e-learning, FAQ emails, small groups) and standardised, service-tailored VTE prophylaxis order sets with visual cues
audits.r2: Compliance with standardised order sets improved to 95%

audits.t: Effect of intervention on a quality measure of pain management at Medstar Washington Cancer Institute.
audits.st: ASCO QOPI pain documentation indicator (aim >=90%)
audits.f: Documentation of plan of care for moderate/severe pain 70% (QOPI Fall 2011 round was 69% vs QOPI aggregate 79%)
audits.c: PDSA methodology: process map, cause-and-effect diagram, EHR trigger for pain score >=4, and clinician education
audits.r2: Pain documentation rate improved to 90.2%, meeting the >=90% goal

audits.t: Improving the quality of multidisciplinary care for head and neck cancer.
audits.tp: NCCN guideline adherence in head and neck cancer MDT
audits.st: NCCN head and neck cancer treatment guidelines
audits.f: Conference recommendations non-compliant with NCCN guidelines in 6.2% oropharyngeal, 13.4% oral cavity, 0.9% laryngeal, and 15.8% nasopharyngeal cancer patients

audits.t: Quality of care study in the surveillance of curable colon cancer.
audits.st: 2005 ASCO surveillance guidelines for stage II/III colon cancer (target 80% compliance)
audits.f: Overall compliance with early surveillance guidelines 55% for stage II and 83% for stage III patients; only 62% of high-risk stage II patients referred to medical oncology

audits.t: Adjuvant colon cancer care quality, risk, value, and level one data and guideline compliance among the elderly privately insured in southeastern USA.
audits.tp: NCCN adherence for adjuvant chemotherapy in elderly colon cancer patients
audits.st: 2012 revised NCCN guideline recommending omission of oxaliplatin from adjuvant chemotherapy for colon cancer patients over 70
audits.f: 69.2% (184/266) of adjuvant chemotherapy requests for patients aged 70+ still contained oxaliplatin; time period was not significantly associated with change in prescribing

audits.t: Establishing a system to monitor and evaluate the quality of cancer care in Japan.
audits.tp: National cancer care quality indicator monitoring (Japan)
audits.st: Nationally developed cancer care quality indicators (adjuvant therapy, lab/procedure/medication, supportive care)
audits.f: Adjuvant therapy QIs generally lower than supportive care QIs, e.g. 48.0% of stage III colorectal cancer patients received adjuvant chemotherapy within 8 postoperative weeks; 83.3% of invasive breast cancer patients received HER2 testing
audits.c: Claims data linked to hospital-based cancer registries, with feedback to hospitals via interactive webpages

audits.t: Quality indicators of end-of-life cancer care: What rate is right?
audits.st: Empiric top-decile benchmark rates for 5 end-of-life quality indicators (ED use, ICU admission, physician house calls, nursing visits, death in hospital)
audits.f: Benchmark rates: ED 34%, ICU 2%, physician house calls 34%, nursing visits 63%, death in hospital 38%; mean regional rates (except ICU) were uniformly worse than benchmarks even after adjustment

audits.t: Quality Oncology Practice Initiative (QOPI) participation as a means to physician engagement, performance improvement, and delivery of safe and high-quality cancer care.
audits.st: ASCO Quality Oncology Practice Initiative (QOPI) quality metrics
audits.f: Pain reporting 40.6%; emotional distress screening 37.3%; performance status documentation 42.6%; staging at diagnosis documented 74.6%, all lagging the QOPI aggregate
audits.c: Analysis of underperforming areas, followed by introduction of a standardised clinical note template in the EMR
audits.r2: Pain reporting improved to 61.2%; emotional distress to 42.8%; performance status documentation to 53.7%; staging documentation to 80.9%

audits.t: Five-year retrospective review of end-of-life care quality metrics in a large, multidisciplinary community oncology practice.
audits.tp: End-of-life care quality metrics (hospice, advance care planning)
audits.st: Internally identified end-of-life care quality metrics (advance care planning documentation, hospice enrolment, chemotherapy at end of life)
audits.f: Evidence of advance directive/POLST/code status documented in 36%; hospice enrolment at death 56%
audits.c: Communication skills training, whole-staff palliative care education, embedded palliative care at 2 sites, and a standardised advance care planning approach
audits.r2: Advance care planning documentation improved to 50% (p<0.001); hospice enrolment improved to 63% (p=0.003)

audits.t: Do newly diagnosed cancer patients require palliative care? An audit at a regional cancer center in India.
audits.tp: Symptom documentation for newly diagnosed cancer patients
audits.st: Expected documentation of distressing symptoms identified by patient-reported ESAS-r assessment
audits.f: Anxiety reported by 97.8% of patients but documented by physicians in only 3/87; depression reported by 89.9% but not documented in any; pain reported 86.5% and documented 83.1%

audits.t: Early integration of palliative care in patients with pancreatic cancer: A retrospective study for quality improvement.
audits.tp: Early palliative care integration in pancreatic cancer
audits.st: National Consensus Project / National Quality Framework domains for early palliative care integration
audits.f: Palliative care discussion documented in 35% (52/150) of records, mostly at disease progression; mean time from first visit to prognosis discussion 177 days and to palliative care consult 343 days

audits.t: Timing of adjuvant chemotherapy in stage III colon cancer as a measure of quality: Reasons for noncompliance.
audits.tp: Time to adjuvant chemotherapy in colon cancer
audits.st: American College of Surgeons quality measure: adjuvant chemotherapy for stage III colon cancer within 120 days of diagnosis
audits.f: 12.3% (15/122) of cases non-compliant with the 120-day measure; annual compliance averaged approximately 90%

audits.t: Quality improvement opportunities in prostatectomy care in a regional hospital-based urologic quality collaborative.
audits.st: Regional collaborative quality benchmarks for radical prostatectomy harms (positive margins, length of stay)
audits.f: Overall positive margin rate 18% (12-25% organ-confined, 0-75% pT3+ by hospital); length of stay exceeded 3 days in >10% of cases overall, up to 36% at one hospital

audits.t: Evaluation of spiritual needs assessments in oncology palliative care: Results of an improvement project.
audits.tp: Spiritual needs assessment documentation in palliative care
audits.st: National Quality Forum Measure #1647 (discussion of spiritual/religious concerns); National Consensus Project guidelines
audits.f: Documentation of spiritual/religious concerns 36%
audits.c: Iterative PDSA cycles: revised EHR templates, use of a web-based Quality Data Collection Tool, and monthly performance review with chaplaincy staff
audits.r2: Documentation of spiritual/religious concerns rose to 96%

audits.t: Timeline analysis of adjuvant therapy timing in colorectal cancer to improve adherence to the 120-day quality measure.
audits.tp: Time to adjuvant chemotherapy in colon cancer
audits.st: ASCO/ACS quality measure: adjuvant chemotherapy for stage III colon cancer within 120 days of diagnosis
audits.f: 13.1% (16/122) of cases were non-adherent; mean time to chemotherapy 159.5 days in non-adherent cases vs 68.7 days in adherent cases (p=2x10-6)

audits.t: A provider-based quality improvement intervention aimed at improving appropriateness of radiation therapy regimens for patients with advanced cancer and painful bone metastases.
audits.tp: Radiotherapy fractionation for painful bone metastases
audits.st: Guideline-recommended shorter-course radiotherapy regimens for painful bone metastases (RAND/UCLA appropriateness panel review)
audits.f: Less than 10 fractions used in 38% overall, 19% of uncomplicated bone metastases
audits.c: RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Panel review of guidelines, faculty presentation, and template-based point-of-care intervention led by a clinical champion
audits.r2: Less than 10 fractions used in 63% overall (p<0.001), 52% of uncomplicated bone metastases (p<0.001)

audits.t: Acute pain management in radiation oncology: Quality of care and the impact of an integrated palliative oncology service.
audits.tp: Acute pain management in radiation oncology consults
audits.st: NCCN Adult Cancer Pain guidelines (V2.2015) recommending analgesic assessment/titration for pain scale value >=4
audits.f: Among symptomatic patients, analgesic regimen assessed in 44.5% overall; among those with pain >=4, pain intervention occurred in 17.2%
audits.c: Implementation in 2011 of a dedicated palliative radiation oncology consultation service at one site
audits.r2: Dedicated palliative RO consultation associated with higher analgesic assessment (82.4% vs 47.7%, p=0.007) and higher pain intervention (31.2% vs 7.9%, p=0.012)

audits.t: A quality improvement approach to oncologist referrals for hospice care.
audits.tp: Hospice length of stay quality improvement
audits.st: Consensus target of hospice length of stay set by an Oncology Clinical Guidance Council (90 or 45 days), compared with NHPCO national median of 43 days
audits.f: Median hospice length of stay 19.7 days
audits.c: Feedback letters and charts to individual oncologists comparing their median hospice referral length of stay against council opinion and national data
audits.r2: Median hospice length of stay improved to 39.6 days

audits.t: Novel solution to achieve “80% by 2018” Two-Man colonoscopy performed by primary care physicians with expert back-up: Compliance and capacity without diluting quality.
audits.st: American Cancer Society '80% by 2018' colorectal cancer screening target
audits.f: Screening compliance well below the 80% target at baseline, with existing colonoscopists screening only about half of the eligible population
audits.c: Primary care physician-led 'two-man' colonoscopy with expert back-up, using patient navigators, to expand screening capacity
audits.r2: Compliance more than doubled and exceeded the 80% target; colorectal cancer incidence fell 83% and mortality fell 89%, with no loss of right-colon protection

audits.t: Improving the treatment of patients with low-risk neutropenic fever: A quality improvement project at the Cleveland Clinic Taussig Cancer Institute (TCI).
audits.tp: Outpatient management of low-risk neutropenic fever
audits.st: MASCC score-based guideline for safe outpatient management of low-risk neutropenic fever
audits.f: Historical average length of stay 6.2 days
audits.c: Provider education on MASCC score calculation, admission under observation with oral antibiotics for low-risk patients, and structured follow-up
audits.r2: Average length of stay fell to 3.3 days; 9/34 (26%) low-risk patients discharged within 24 hours; no deaths from neutropenic fever

audits.t: A multidisciplinary quality improvement project to improve the safety of oral chemotherapy in hospitalized patients.
audits.st: Institutional target of 75% of administered oral chemotherapy agents having an associated provider chemotherapy note
audits.f: 12.5% of oral chemotherapy administrations had an associated formal chemotherapy note
audits.c: Multidisciplinary standardisation of ordering, administration, documentation and education, with a REDCap-based automated weekly audit report
audits.r2: Chemotherapy notes present in 58% (June), 100% (July), 78% (August) and 93% (September) of audited administrations

audits.t: A novel auditing procedure for an oral chemotherapy process improvement project.
audits.st: Requirement for a provider-completed oral chemotherapy note before pharmacy dispensing
audits.f: Compliance with documentation requirement 58% in June
audits.c: REDCap-based auditing tool with automated follow-up surveys to non-adherent pharmacists, providing root-cause-tailored continuing education
audits.r2: Compliance rose to 100% (July), 78% (August) and 93% (September); no single pharmacist involved in more than one non-adherent case after targeted education

audits.t: A quality improvement project to increase compliance with indicated prechemotherapy pneumococcal vaccination.
audits.st: Guideline recommendation for pneumococcal (PCV13/PPSV23) vaccination of immunocompromised cancer patients
audits.f: Only 7 patients (6.4%) received pneumococcal vaccination through the clinic
audits.c: Physician education on guidelines and recruitment of clinic nurse practitioner to prescribe vaccine during chemotherapy teaching
audits.r2: 25 of 58 eligible patients (45.5%) vaccinated through the QI project; compliance improved by 39%

audits.t: Establishing achievable benchmarks for quality improvement in systemic therapy for early-stage breast cancer.
audits.tp: Systemic therapy quality indicators for breast cancer
audits.st: Previously established quality indicator panel for systemic therapy in early-stage breast cancer, benchmarked to top-decile institutions
audits.f: Many institutions fell considerably below the empiric top-decile benchmark for systemic therapy quality indicators

audits.t: The Dutch Upper GI Cancer Audit: 2011-2014.
audits.tp: National upper GI cancer surgery audit
audits.st: Predefined national quality measures for oesophageal and gastric cancer surgery (Dutch Upper GI Cancer Audit)
audits.f: 33% of oesophageal cancer patients started treatment within 5 weeks of diagnosis; adequate lymph node yield (>=15) 50% (oesophageal) and 48% (gastric); postoperative mortality 8.0% (gastric)
audits.c: Nationwide web-based registration providing weekly benchmarked feedback on process and outcome measures
audits.r2: 41% started treatment within 5 weeks; adequate lymph node yield rose to 73% (oesophageal) and 74% (gastric); postoperative mortality fell to 4.0% (gastric, p=0.020) and remained ~4% (oesophageal)

audits.t: Making steps to decrease emergency room visits in patients with cancer: Our experience after participating in the ASCO Quality Training Program.
audits.tp: Reducing emergency room visits in oncology patients
audits.st: Self-set QI target (30% reduction in ER visits) developed via the ASCO Quality Training Program
audits.f: 48% of oncology patient ER visits occurred during office hours; breast, haematology and GI malignancies were the main diagnoses using the ER
audits.c: Telephone triage protocol at a patient access centre, staff training, and patient education to contact the centre instead of using the ER
audits.r2: 60% decrease in the number of patients utilising the ER, exceeding the 30% reduction goal

audits.t: Ambulatory redesign: Strategies for quality improvement in patient care.
audits.tp: Ambulatory clinic lab turnaround time quality improvement
audits.st: National benchmarks for laboratory turnaround time and patient flow
audits.f: Baseline lab turnaround time defect rate; Press-Ganey mean satisfaction with physician wait time 81.7
audits.c: Multidisciplinary teams redesigned lab, rooming and scheduling processes and expanded the Advanced Practice Provider role
audits.r2: Lab turnaround time defect rate reduced by 52.3% (CBC) and 76.1% (CMP), both p<0.001; APP visit volume increased 81%; Press-Ganey satisfaction rose to 82.7

audits.t: Electronic operative reports to support quality improvement and patient-centered care.
audits.st: National standards (2007) for synoptic cancer surgery operative reports and 64 associated quality indicators
audits.f: Narrative operative reports provided inconsistent and incomplete information for patient care before national standards were available
audits.c: Transition from narrative to electronic synoptic reporting (ESP) for breast, colorectal, ovary, endometrial, lung, prostate and thyroid cancer surgery, based on disease-site expert panel consensus
audits.r2: Surgeons reported synoptic reports captured complete/essential content 89-96% of the time (50% more than narrative); completion time 5-15 minutes vs 5 days; transmission to charts within 1 hour in 91% of cases vs 30-90 days

audits.t: Update: Implementation of a multidisciplinary quality improvement initiative to improve molecular testing rates in advanced non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer.
audits.tp: Molecular testing rates in advanced non-small cell lung cancer
audits.st: Current guidelines recommending EGFR/ALK molecular testing in all advanced non-squamous NSCLC patients
audits.f: EGFR testing rate 43.2%; ALK testing rate 23.8%
audits.c: Lean six sigma initiative using multidisciplinary meetings for direct physician education and process/workflow enhancement, per the ACCC molecular testing framework
audits.r2: EGFR testing rate 81.1% (340/419), ALK testing rate 69.0% (289/419); both increases significant (p<0.00001), and testing rates were comparable or improved year-over-year

audits.t: The next generation of quality improvement at MSK: Turning chemotherapy process delays into chemo express.
audits.st: Internal target wait time reduction from 40 minutes to 15 minutes
audits.f: Retrospective review showed lab-related bottlenecks causing an average wait time of about 40 minutes
audits.c: 'ChemoExpress' programme: redefined lab parameters, pre-visit blood draws, nurse tele-clearance, and pre-mixing of drugs ahead of appointment
audits.r2: Average wait time for ChemoExpress participants was 9 minutes (76% less) versus 39 minutes for non-participants; patient satisfaction was high

audits.t: Implementing pregnancy screening prior to chemotherapy: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: ASCO QOPI standard for pregnancy screening of women of childbearing potential before chemotherapy
audits.f: 35% of women of childbearing potential screened before chemotherapy; medical oncology performed only 7% of screening; 48% of tests ordered within 14 days of treatment start
audits.c: Checkbox added to pre-chemotherapy checklist, with point-of-care pregnancy test in standing orders for eligible women
audits.r2: 30.6% (15/49) screened before chemotherapy; 84% of tests ordered by medical oncology, 64.2% within 14 days of treatment

audits.t: Patient distress assessment in a VA oncology clinic: A quality improvement project.
audits.st: 2012 ACS Commission on Cancer standard and NCCN guideline for distress screening
audits.f: NCCN Distress Thermometer completed at triage; mean distress score below 4 (mild) at most time points; number of problems reported decreased over serial visits
audits.c: Distress Thermometer administered at triage with physician follow-up on identified problems

audits.t: Integration of survivorship care plans into standard care: A quality improvement project.
audits.st: American College of Surgeons Commission on Cancer requirement for survivorship care plans after initial treatment
audits.f: Pre-SCP sociodemographic, quality-of-life, satisfaction and disease-knowledge baseline data collected
audits.c: Integration of Survivorship Care Plans into standard care for stage I-III breast and colon cancer patients
audits.r2: 100% of participants returned for follow-up (only 2, 4.8%, delayed); significant increase in disease knowledge (p<0.001); no significant change in quality-of-life or satisfaction scores

audits.t: A quality verification tool to assure complete pre-treatment electronic medical records (EMR) for patients undergoing radiation therapy.
audits.st: Institutional sentinel-item checklist for a complete pre-treatment radiation oncology medical record
audits.f: Variance rate from standard practice 16% on initial observation
audits.c: Electronic quality-verification spreadsheet completed at pre-treatment peer review, with tracking of deficiencies as a continuous quality improvement activity

audits.t: A quality improvement initiative to reduce low-value red blood cell transfusions in hospitalized oncology patients.
audits.tp: Red blood cell transfusion practice in oncology inpatients
audits.st: Standardised restrictive RBC transfusion algorithm (haemoglobin goal 7-8 g/dL) based on evidence review
audits.f: Low-value RBC transfusions occurred in 29.6% of transfusions overall (78.7% in patients with platelets >50K)
audits.c: Development and multifaceted education campaign for a standardised restrictive RBC transfusion algorithm
audits.r2: Low-value transfusions fell to 19.7% overall (p<0.001) and to 55.6% in the platelet >50K subgroup (p<0.001)

audits.t: Reducing invasive fungal infections in patients with acute myeloid leukemia receiving induction and re-induction chemotherapy at the University of Virginia Health System.
audits.tp: Antifungal prophylaxis for AML induction chemotherapy
audits.st: National average target of less than 10% invasive fungal infection rate in AML induction/re-induction chemotherapy
audits.f: Invasive fungal infection rate 19.7%, versus national average 8-10%
audits.c: Standardised clinical practice guideline for antifungal prophylaxis and staff education (developed via ASCO Quality Training Program PDSA cycles)
audits.r2: Invasive fungal infection rate fell to 11.7%

audits.t: Improving the quality of oncology fellows' clinical documentation.
audits.st: 34 institution-identified areas of importance for oncology clinical documentation
audits.f: Initial and follow-up notes reviewed against 34 documentation areas; verbal and written feedback given
audits.c: Verbal and written feedback to fellows on documentation areas identified as important
audits.r2: Documentation skills reported as successfully improved (detailed results in table)

audits.t: Driving quality improvement with public reporting: Use of imaging tests outside guidelines for early-stage breast cancer in Ontario.
audits.tp: Imaging overuse in early-stage breast cancer staging
audits.st: Choosing Wisely / staging guidelines recommending against distant-metastasis imaging in asymptomatic early-stage (stage I/II) breast cancer
audits.f: 75.1% of early-stage breast cancer patients received at least one imaging test for staging, far above the 5-10% expected to need testing
audits.c: Public reporting of imaging rates via Ontario's Cancer System Quality Index, with regional interventions planned
audits.r2: Imaging rate fell to 71.3%, with regional variation of 47-80% and no clear pattern

audits.t: Multidisciplinary cancer conferences as a forum for early identification of patients who can benefit from a palliative approach to care: INTEGRATE quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Early identification for palliative care at multidisciplinary cancer conferences
audits.st: UK Gold Standards Framework Surprise Question, used as a screening standard for early palliative care referral
audits.f: Baseline survey found over 50% of providers had no palliative care training
audits.c: Implementation of the Surprise Question at multidisciplinary cancer conferences (Lung, GI, CNS) with primary-level palliative care education (Pallium Canada LEAP Oncology) and standardised care pathway
audits.r2: 300 patients (27.6%) identified as potentially benefiting from a palliative approach; 100% of glioblastoma patients identified at the CNS site versus 19% at Lung and GI sites

audits.t: Addressing the risk of infertility in young women with breast cancer (BC): A quality improvement (QI) intervention.
audits.tp: Fertility preservation counselling in young breast cancer patients
audits.st: Standard of fertility risk counselling and fertility preservation referral for young women with cancer before systemic therapy
audits.f: Provider documentation form completed for 70% (56/80); of these, childbearing potential noted in 86%, treatment-related infertility risk discussed in 72%, and fertility goals assessed in 94%
audits.c: QI protocol requiring clinician assessment of childbearing potential, infertility risk and fertility goals, with a provider documentation form

audits.t: Bone marrow aspirate quality assessment.
audits.st: Institutional standard of adequate bone marrow aspirate specimen quality for pathological review
audits.f: 51.2% (22/43) of aspirates adequate
audits.c: Faculty-led educational seminar (1 Feb 2016) on bone marrow aspirate technique, following a Plan-Do-Study-Act approach
audits.r2: 54% (27/50) of aspirates adequate; fellow comfort performing the procedure alone rose to 93.3%

audits.t: Feasibility of capturing radiation oncology quality metrics in a large integrated oncology practice.
audits.tp: Radiation oncology quality metrics capture feasibility
audits.st: Bundle of radiation oncology quality metrics including US Oncology Breast Cancer XRT Pathways adherence
audits.f: Metrics data availability and compliance greater than 80% in all 52 sites
audits.c: Quarterly sampling and reporting of a standard metrics bundle across all sites, with attestation and later plan-concordance checks for pathways
audits.r2: Breast cancer pathway compliance fell when additional pathways (NSCLC, prostate, rectal, bone metastasis) were added, suggesting added complexity reduces performance

audits.t: Improving support for smoking cessation in medical oncology patients: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Smoking cessation referral in oncology patients
audits.st: Cancer Care Ontario provincially defined target of 20% smoking-cessation referral rate (Ottawa Model)
audits.f: Institutional baseline referral rate to a smoking cessation programme 8.5%
audits.c: 'Opt-out' referral process for recent/current smokers with staff and patient education (grand rounds, lecture, pamphlet)
audits.r2: Referral rate increased to 14.3%, short of the 20% target

audits.t: A tale of 2,000 charts: Measuring provider response to patient-reported outcome measures.
audits.tp: Chart audit of provider response to patient-reported symptom screening
audits.st: Cancer Care Ontario chart audit process for provider response to ESAS symptom screening
audits.f: Severe symptoms acknowledged 69.9%; pain acknowledgement 71.5%, assessment 67.7%, intervention 55.8%; depression/anxiety least likely to be acknowledged (44.5%/45.0%) or offered intervention (35.7%/36.6%)

audits.t: Quality of care during active surveillance in low-risk prostate cancer patients: A population-based approach.
audits.tp: Active surveillance guideline adherence in low-risk prostate cancer
audits.st: Adherence to clinical guidelines on active surveillance (AS) follow-up for low-risk prostate cancer, assessed via 25 proposed structure-process-outcome quality indicators
audits.f: 39% of low-risk prostate cancer patients received AS (88% managed by a urologist); only 43% of low-volume (≤ 3 positive cores) patients underwent AS; adherence of confirmatory biopsy with guidelines was 32%, better in higher-volume institutions, physicians, and cancer centres

audits.t: Quality improvement interventions to reduce chemotherapy dose-modification ordering errors at a large academic medical center.
audits.st: Local target: reduce unintended chemotherapy dose-escalation ordering errors per month by 50%
audits.f: Average 3.83 chemotherapy ordering errors per month (UCL=9.71, LCL=0)
audits.c: Revision of the nursing chemotherapy checklist at infusion workstations, and education of ordering providers/nurses on EHR functionality to display prior and future chemotherapy orders
audits.r2: Average errors reduced to 1.33 per month (UCL=4.97, LCL=0), a 65% reduction

audits.t: Improving start-up times in oncology clinical trials: An ASCO quality improvement project.
audits.st: Local target: decrease the longest activation timeline (IRB approval to activation) by 50% (6 weeks) by December 2018
audits.f: Average time from protocol receipt to trial activation was 33 weeks; IRB approval to activation was the longest step at 12 weeks
audits.c: Sponsor survey to identify logistical concerns earlier, email template for regulatory coordinators to request systems access early, and earlier scheduling of site initiation visits

audits.t: Automated quality control process for tracking appropriateness of antiemesis.
audits.st: ASCO Quality Oncology Practice Initiative (QOPI) measure 29 and the 2017 ASCO Clinical Practice Guideline Update for antiemetics
audits.f: 862/118/510 encounters were high/intermediate/low emetic risk; 1314/14/162 chemotherapy administrations received pass/fail/pass(-) respectively (88.1% pass); the 14 fails were mostly due to lack of steroid in high-risk regimens, and over-treatment (pass(-)) was mainly fosaprepitant use in low/intermediate risk regimens

audits.t: Using standardized electronic pathology data to identify practice variation, potential impact to patient outcomes, and quality improvement initiatives.
audits.tp: Synoptic cancer pathology practice variation indicators
audits.st: 48 indicators created from College of American Pathologists data standards and literature, covering breast, lung, colorectal, endometrial and prostate cancer (e.g. examining ≥12 lymph nodes in colorectal resections)
audits.f: Only one province met the ≥12 lymph node guideline in 90% of cases; Lynch syndrome screening ranged 0-70% of colorectal cancer patients ≤70 years and 10-40% of endometrial cancer cases

audits.t: Pathology quality improvement in British Columbia using performance measurement and knowledge mobilization.
audits.st: Local target: increase adoption of College of American Pathologists cancer checklist-based electronic synoptic reporting from 76% to 90%
audits.f: Adoption varied 11-94% across different laboratories; average adoption rate 76%
audits.c: Digitalised standardised synoptic reporting program interfaced with all five provincial laboratory information systems; comparative performance data reports shared with pathologists and communities of practice

audits.t: Preventing excess narcotic prescriptions in MIS urologic oncology discharges (PENN): A prospective cohort quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Opioid-sparing discharge analgesia after urologic cancer surgery
audits.st: Local target: reduce opioid prescribing at discharge following robotic urologic oncology surgery
audits.f: 100% of patients discharged on varying amounts of oxycodone (75-337.5 oral morphine milligram equivalents)
audits.c: Standard non-opioid analgesia pathway (gabapentin, acetaminophen, ketorolac) with escalation to tramadol then oxycodone as needed
audits.r2: 67.7% discharged without opioids, 24.4% with ten tramadol 50mg pills, 8.2% with ten oxycodone 5mg pills

audits.t: Improving quality care through it/analytics for team-based care interventions.
audits.tp: Identification of new oncology patients for team-based care interventions
audits.st: Local target for identifying new treatment patients for team-based interventions
audits.f: Only 51% of new patients were being identified prior to the intervention
audits.c: Plan-Do-Study-Act model to build an automated report using IT/data analytics to identify new treatment patients, validated for accuracy
audits.r2: Initial report validated at 93% identification accuracy, with a secondary 3-week look-back report to identify remaining patients; financial navigator out-of-pocket estimate calls sustained >94% YTD 2018 and social work assessments sustained 79% over 6 months

audits.t: Capturing discrete complete staging elements in EPIC for new and progressing breast (B) and prostate (P) cancer patients: A quality training program pilot.
audits.tp: Complete cancer staging documentation in EHR
audits.st: Local target for complete discrete staging element entry in EPIC EHR for new and progressing breast and prostate cancer patients
audits.f: Baseline enterprise-wide complete staging in EPIC was 6% for breast cancer and 3% for prostate cancer
audits.c: 12-week Quality Training Program pilot with PDSA cycles, staff training, doctor-level reports on missing staging elements sent from week 9
audits.r2: Complete staging for breast MO/surgeons rose to 20% and for prostate MO/urologists to 12%

audits.t: Integrating family caregiver identification into a gynecologic oncology practice: An ASCO quality training program project.
audits.tp: Family caregiver identification and documentation in cancer clinics
audits.st: ASCO Quality Training Program local target: identify and document primary caregivers for 85% of patients within 2 clinic visits of a gynaecological cancer diagnosis
audits.f: Chart review found only 19% of patients had a documented caregiver
audits.c: Eight successive PDSA cycles including protocol development, staff training, a dedicated EHR field, and staff champions
audits.r2: Caregiver identification rose to 25.3% by PDSA 2, dropped to 12.5% by PDSA 4, rose to 56% of new patients by PDSA 5, and stabilised at 57-60% over the last 6 weeks (288 caregivers documented in total)

audits.t: Family caregiver needs assessment in a gynecologic oncology practice: An ASCO quality training program project.
audits.tp: Family caregiver needs assessment in cancer clinics
audits.st: ASCO Quality Training Program local target: assess and intervene on the needs of 75% of gynaecological oncology family caregivers
audits.f: Caregiver needs assessment was 28% at baseline
audits.c: Eight PDSA cycles over 6 months: assessment/intervention protocol, CG tracking database, prioritisation of newly diagnosed/high-risk patients
audits.r2: By PDSA cycle 8, staff had assessed 58% and intervened on 50% of caregivers (up from 28% baseline)

audits.t: High-risk human papilloma virus testing in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma at a university-based cancer center: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: HPV testing rate in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
audits.st: American Society of Clinical Pathology guidelines on HPV testing relevance for treatment/follow-up in OPSCC
audits.f: HR HPV testing by p16 IHC was performed in 41.5% (42/101) of patients and not performed in 58.5% (59/101); 90.5% of those tested were HR HPV positive
audits.c: Corrective actions proposed via meetings with pathologists and otolaryngologists

audits.t: A quality improvement initiative for reducing morning hypoglycemia in children undergoing treatment for acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
audits.tp: Morning hypoglycaemia in children on acute lymphoblastic leukaemia therapy
audits.st: Local quality target to reduce hypoglycaemia rates in children undergoing ALL therapy
audits.f: About 10% of children with ALL developed hypoglycaemia monthly at each clinic (combined monthly average 9.4% of patients, with 6% of blood glucose samples showing hypoglycaemic episodes)
audits.c: Root cause analysis (fishbone/Pareto), hypoglycaemia educational brochure and knowledge assessment for caregivers, staff education sessions, across 4 PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Caregiver education uptake rose from 16.3% to 88% after PDSA cycle 4; average monthly patients with hypoglycaemia fell from 9.4% to 7.8% (17% reduction) and hypoglycaemic episodes fell from 6% to 4.2% (30% reduction)

audits.t: Improving quality of cancer care: Lessons learned from the journey towards QOPI Certification.
audits.st: ASCO Quality Oncology Practice Initiative (QOPI) Certification standards
audits.f: Initial two QOPI rounds scored lower than required for certification
audits.c: Multidisciplinary QOPI team, EHR training with super users, double-check record review system, weekly meetings, and new templates (chemotherapy treatment plan, end-of-treatment summary, consent documentation), over three PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Score exceeded the QOPI benchmark at 93%, leading to on-site certification visit in May 2018 and QOPI Certification in October 2018 (first in the Middle East and Asia)

audits.t: Increasing screening for latent tuberculosis in patients with hematologic malignancy: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Latent tuberculosis screening before systemic therapy for haematologic malignancy
audits.st: Local target: complete and document tuberculin skin tests (TBST) in ≥85% of patients starting systemic therapy for haematologic malignancy by Feb 2018
audits.f: 3/25 patients (12%) had documentation of prior TBST
audits.c: Order set, workflow process map and standard operating procedure; TBST added to a pharmacist-run “ready for treatment” checklist, developed via PDSA cycles, go-live 15 Aug 2018
audits.r2: 14/30 patients (47%) had documentation of TBST prior to starting systemic therapy; all 14 had negative TBSTs

audits.t: A trainee-led quality improvement project to improve rates of palliative care utilization in patients with advanced cancer.
audits.tp: Palliative care referral rates for advanced cancer
audits.st: ASCO guidelines recommending palliative care referral for patients with advanced or metastatic cancer; local target of 30% utilisation over 4 months
audits.f: Baseline palliative care utilisation 11.5% (5/43 patients)
audits.c: Single referral order set, single scheduler with bidirectional communication, focus groups with stakeholders, dissemination of process changes
audits.r2: Palliative care utilisation rose to 43% (27/62 patients); median time to evaluation improved from 23 days (range 10-60) to 12 days (range 6-19)

audits.t: Successful implementation of a quality improvement intervention towards a QOPI-compliant breast cancer center in Mexico.
audits.st: ASCO Quality Oncology Practice Initiative (QOPI) 84 breast cancer related metrics; local target 80% documentation of 13 identified achievable metrics
audits.f: 40/84 QOPI metrics met; of the 44 unmet, 13 were 'done/not documented' and 31 were 'not done/not documented'
audits.c: Multidisciplinary QI team, Microsoft Word medical record template, new 'first time visit' model, monthly PDSA cycles from August-December 2018
audits.r2: Surpassed the objective by the third PDSA cycle, reaching 95% cumulative compliance on the 13 targeted metrics

audits.t: Navigating oncology inpatient care from admission to discharge: A quality improvement study.
audits.st: Society of Hospital Medicine best practice recommendations for safe discharge planning
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Development of a comprehensive discharge navigator document in the EHR, initiated at admission and updated throughout the stay by providers and discharge coordinators
audits.r2: 100% compliance with utilising the navigator has been maintained since its inception

audits.t: Driving quality improvement: How clinical decision support can facilitate compliance with evidence-based pathways.
audits.tp: Clinical decision support compliance with evidence-based pathways
audits.st: Evidence-based treatment pathways (EBP) developed with physician input on efficacy, toxicity and value
audits.f: Individual oncologists reached the 75% compliance target less often before implementation (58% of physicians)
audits.c: Clinical decision support system (CDSS) embedded in the EHR to alter the choice architecture clinicians see when prescribing therapy
audits.r2: 72% of oncologists reached 75% compliance target after implementation of the CDSS tool (p<0.001), with significant improvement across the whole cohort and at individual practices

audits.t: Initial Experience with Cancer Guidelines Navigator, a tool to standardize and improve the quality of cancer care in Sub-Saharan Africa, at Ocean Road Cancer Institute in Tanzania.
audits.tp: Digital cancer treatment guideline navigator implementation
audits.st: NCCN Harmonized Guidelines for Sub-Saharan Africa
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Hospital-wide implementation of the IBM Cancer Guidelines Navigator (CGN) digital reference tool, with one week of staff training

audits.t: Real-world practice patterns and barriers to quality care in acute myeloid leukemia (AML).
audits.tp: Guideline-concordant care for acute myeloid leukaemia
audits.st: Guideline recommendations for individualised AML treatment selection based on performance status and targetable biomarkers
audits.f: 33.3% of patients with FLT3/IDH mutations (n=15) received low-dose cytarabine alone; 50% of patients with performance status 3+ (n=2) received intensive induction; low documented use of novel therapies and no documented use of FLT3/IDH inhibitors
audits.c: Audit-feedback sessions for teams to develop action plans (e.g. collaboration with hematopathologists, mutational status assessment, patient engagement)

audits.t: Real-world data and patient perspectives on quality care and maintenance therapy (MT) decision-making for recurrent ovarian cancer (ROC).
audits.tp: Guideline-concordant maintenance therapy decision-making in recurrent ovarian cancer
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines for maintenance therapy (MT) and shared decision-making in recurrent ovarian cancer
audits.f: Low utility of maintenance therapy documented; only 20% of patients reported MT was discussed as an option; HCPs answered correctly on BRCA-based patient selection (18%), response to prior chemo (49%) and line of therapy (46%)
audits.c: Audit-feedback sessions with action plans (guidance documents for therapy sequencing, patient education tools)

audits.t: Improving the referral rate of universal genetic counseling for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) at the Cleveland Clinic Taussig Cancer Center: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Genetic counselling referral rate for pancreatic cancer
audits.st: 2018 ASCO/NCCN guidelines recommending genetic counselling and germline testing for all pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients; local target 60% referral rate
audits.f: Baseline discussion rate 25% and referral rate 9%
audits.c: Three PDSA cycles: updated electronic order/tumour board template, physician education, and patient education with physician reinforcement
audits.r2: Discussion and referral rates improved to 55%/30% after PDSA1, 73%/33% after PDSA2, and 95%/58% after PDSA3

audits.t: Quality indicators of colorectal cancer care in a public healthcare institution in Uruguay: Results from a retrospective population-based study.
audits.st: 12 previously validated quality indicators for colorectal cancer care (4 diagnostic, 7 treatment, 1 surveillance)
audits.f: 10.1% diagnosed by screening; complete preoperative colonoscopy in 47%; CT-TAP scan in 64%; staging MRI for locally advanced rectal cancer in 63%; tumour-free margins in 97%; ≥12 lymph nodes examined in 68%; neoadjuvant CRT for rectal cancer in 79%; adjuvant chemo within 16 weeks for high-risk stage II/III colon cancer in 72.9%; postoperative CEA follow-up in 97%

audits.t: Care redesign of pelvic radiotherapy using Design Thinking: An enhanced quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Reduction of unplanned cone-beam CT in pelvic radiotherapy
audits.st: Local target: reduce incidence of unplanned CBCT from 21% to 9% over 5 months
audits.f: Baseline incidence of unplanned CBCT was 21%
audits.c: Design Thinking approach introducing a bladder ultrasound before CBCT to ensure adequate bladder filling
audits.r2: Incidence of unplanned CBCT decreased to 5.8% (13.3% mean reduction, statistically significant)

audits.t: State-wide quality improvement addressing overutilization of neurokinin-1 receptor antagonists.
audits.tp: Overuse of neurokinin-1 receptor antagonists (NK1-RA) in low/moderate emetic risk chemotherapy
audits.st: ASCO-QOPI/ABIM Choosing Wisely measure SMT28a; local target <30% overuse
audits.f: 23% of practices (32/43, 74% response rate) had a pre-populated order set for NK1-RA and/or olanzapine in moderate emetic regimens
audits.c: Baseline assessment, statewide CINV education, reporting of practice/state-level performance, and value-based reimbursement tied to measure performance
audits.r2: 48% of respondents (25/43, 54% response rate) had modified or were modifying their order sets after education

audits.t: Quality of timely adjuvant chemotherapy for veterans with colorectal cancer.
audits.tp: Timely adjuvant chemotherapy for colorectal cancer
audits.st: NCCN recommendation of adjuvant chemotherapy within 8 weeks of surgery for high-risk stage II/III colorectal cancer
audits.f: Among those treated, median time to treatment 50.5 days (IQR 40-64); 63% received chemotherapy within 8 weeks; timely treatment fell from 75% (2000-2004) to 62% (2005-2009) to 41% (2010-2015); including all eligible patients, timely treatment fell from 57% to 45% to 25% over the same periods

audits.t: Hospital-level quality indicators for kidney cancer surgery: A Veteran’s Affairs national health system validation of concept.
audits.tp: Hospital-level quality indicators for kidney cancer surgery
audits.st: Two previously validated process quality indicators: proportion of T1a tumours undergoing partial nephrectomy and T1-T2 tumours undergoing minimally invasive radical nephrectomy
audits.f: A compound quality score (CQS) identified 25, 33 and 38 hospitals with higher, lower, and average performance respectively

audits.t: A retrospective analysis and quality improvement education initiative to increase HPV vaccination rates in an inner city primary care clinic.
audits.st: CDC guidelines for HPV vaccination in persons aged 9-45
audits.f: Only 5.2% of those eligible received the total HPV vaccine dosage; 47.83% of residents did not inquire about/recommend HPV vaccination compared with 71.43% of attending physicians; only 27.7% of residents and 71.43% of attendings correctly identified updated guidelines
audits.c: Educational handout and lecture for residents/attendings on HPV vaccination guidelines
audits.r2: Follow-up survey found 100% of residents correctly identified the updated guidelines, risks, benefits and importance of shared decision-making, though 69.2% remained unaware HPV vaccination does not prevent progression of existing HPV-related disease

audits.t: Improving management of hypersensitivity reactions: A BC Cancer-Victoria quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: BC Cancer guidelines for managing hypersensitivity reactions (HSR), target <5% of doses
audits.f: Mean 11.27 HSR per month; 3.1% of doses; notes dictated 55%; physician attendance 57%
audits.c: Physician/nursing education sessions, daily huddles, pre-printed orders for reaction management and prophylaxis, modified clinic flow (PDSA cycles)
audits.r2: Mean 7.526 HSR per month; 1.9% of doses; notes dictated 64%; physician attendance 90%

audits.t: Recovery of a quality improvement project during the COVID pandemic.
audits.tp: Medication reconciliation documentation in ambulatory oncology
audits.st: Local target for documented best possible medication history (BPMH)/medication reconciliation (MedRec) for patients initiating systemic therapy
audits.f: Prior to COVID, initial QI achieved 16.7% and 3.9% increases in BPMH and MedRec completion respectively, but rates returned to baseline after COVID onset
audits.c: Four-phase Quality Implementation Framework: re-examination of the process, development of educational materials, role revisions, new dedicated clinical team, staged scale-up, educational outreach and clinical supervision
audits.r2: BPMH and MedRec completion rates improved across the successive implementation phases (exact figures given in table, not reported in text)

audits.t: Learnings from a multiphase, mixed-methods lung cancer quality initiative in U.S. community cancer centers.
audits.tp: Lung cancer care delivery quality initiative baseline evaluation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Site-specific QI solutions developed at a multidisciplinary workshop across five key areas: irAE management, biomarker testing, emergency visit management, clinical trial access, and smoking cessation

audits.t: National benchmarks and practice level variation on eight cross cutting quality measures.
audits.tp: National benchmarking of cross-cutting oncology quality measures
audits.st: Eight cross-cutting quality measures (including tobacco screening, performance status documentation, hospice admission, ED admission)
audits.f: Overall performance for measures where higher adherence reflects quality ranged 13.5%-77.3% (hospice admission to PS documented); for measures where lower is better, range was 11.4%-22.6% (hospice <3 days to ED admission)

audits.t: Genetic counseling and testing rates among community cancer programs for patients with breast cancer following site-directed quality improvement.
audits.tp: Genetic counselling and testing rates for breast/ovarian cancer
audits.st: NCCN guidelines recommending BRCA/ovarian gene testing for early-onset or metastatic HER2-negative breast cancer and genetically at-risk women
audits.f: 36% (658/1845) of women with HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer received genetic counselling pre-intervention; 57% (729/1284) with documented high-risk family history received GC
audits.c: Site-directed QI interventions ranging from testing eligibility education to a virtual genetic counselling clinic
audits.r2: 61% (1387/2267) received GC post-intervention; early-onset patients attended GC 83% of the time with 74% having genetic test results (92% before surgery); GC in those with documented high-risk family history rose to 85% (1485/1741, p<0.0001)

audits.t: Prophylactic anticoagulation in pancreatic adenocarcinoma patients: A single tertiary care center retrospective quality improvement project.
audits.tp: VTE prophylaxis using the Khorana score in pancreatic cancer
audits.st: Khorana score-based guidance for VTE primary prophylaxis in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
audits.f: Only 12 of 92 patients (13%) were on VTE prophylaxis; 26 patients (28.2%) developed a VTE event

audits.t: Quality indicators for glioblastoma treatment: An audit from a tertiary care cancer center in India.
audits.st: PRIME Quality Improvement study quality indicators for glioblastoma treatment
