audits.f: Quality metrics reported per indicator (detailed in table); 12-month overall survival 74.6% (95% CI 65.4-85.1%), progression-free survival 43.6% (95% CI 33.8-56.3%)

audits.t: Practice transformation at scale through a microsystems quality improvement (QI) approach.
audits.tp: Oncology practice transformation to value-based care performance
audits.st: Medicare Oncology Care Model (OCM) one-sided risk target (4% below benchmark)
audits.f: FCS was 5.8% above the OCM cost target; all 18 regions were above target; lung cancer was 2.5% over target
audits.c: Microsystems QI approach engaging physicians via sense-making models, sharing interpreted performance data, regional QI sessions targeting disease, utilisation, location and individual physicians
audits.r2: Performance improved to 0.3% above target in PP2/PP3, then below target by 0.9%, 0.8% and 0.75% in PP4-PP6; lung cancer improved to 2.1% under target by PP6; 11 of 19 regions were below target by PP6

audits.t: Outcomes of the BRCA quality improvement dissemination program in three health systems.
audits.tp: BRCA genetic referral, counselling and testing rates
audits.st: Guideline-recommended referral, genetic counselling (GC) and germline genetic testing (GT) for invasive epithelial ovarian/fallopian tube/primary peritoneal cancer and early-onset triple-negative breast cancer
audits.f: Baseline referral, GC and GT rates were lower than post-implementation at all 3 sites (exact baseline % given only in table)
audits.c: BRCA Quality Improvement Dissemination Program (BQIDP): virtual implementation facilitation including provider/patient education, case-finding alerts, streamlined referral/scheduling, infusion-suite genetic counselling
audits.r2: All clinics increased rates compared to baseline; statistically significant improvement in GC for ovarian cancer at all 3 sites and in referral/GT for TNBC at 2 of 3 sites

audits.t: Intraoperative quality metrics and association with survival following lung cancer resection.
audits.tp: Intra-operative quality metric adherence in lung cancer resection
audits.st: Five contemporary treatment guideline-based intra-operative quality metrics: timely surgery within 12 weeks, minimally invasive approach, lobectomy, adequate nodal sampling (≥10 nodes), negative margin
audits.f: Timely surgery achieved in 68.9%, minimally invasive approach in 41.4%, lobectomy in 71.1%, adequate nodal sampling in 34.1%, negative margin in 96.7%

audits.t: Outcomes from LDCT screening for lung cancer in an undeserved population: A quality initiative.
audits.tp: Follow-up compliance after LDCT lung cancer screening
audits.st: USPSTF low-dose CT lung cancer screening recommendation with LUNG-RADS-based follow-up
audits.f: Compliance with recommended follow-up imaging/biopsy was only 51.2% (95% CI 44.0-59.0); 15% of biopsies were malignant; resident survey found only 57% knew the recommended screening age and 47% the pack-year criteria
audits.c: Proposed plan: resident education on LDCT guidelines and a designated coordinator to call non-compliant patients (cites literature showing coordinators raised adherence from 22% to 66% elsewhere)

audits.t: Hepatitis B screening to reduce the risk of viral reactivation in gynecologic oncology patients receiving chemotherapy at a regional tertiary cancer center: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Hepatitis B screening before chemotherapy in gynaecologic oncology
audits.st: 2020 ASCO Provisional Clinical Opinion recommending universal HBV screening before systemic chemotherapy; local target 70% screening rate
audits.f: Median baseline HBV screening rate was 0%
audits.c: Provider education, standardisation of testing protocol, integration with clinical workflow, and biweekly feedback reports, via Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles
audits.r2: Physicians screening rose from 0% to 85%; monthly HBV screening rate rose from 0% to 72.2% by month 8, sustained for 4 months; overall 53% (175/330) of patients screened; anti-HBc reactive in 5 (2.9%)

audits.t: Oncology-hospitalist co-management: A model for efficient, high-quality care and education.
audits.st: Local business plan target: reduce length of stay by 0.25 days in the first year
audits.f: Traditional team (oncologist-led) served as comparator; specific baseline LOS not given in text
audits.c: Integration of internal medicine hospitalists as primary attending on an Intervention Team, with oncologists as consultants, using PDSA cycles reported at 3 months (PDSA1) and 6 months (PDSA2)
audits.r2: Intervention Team achieved a 1.0-day LOS reduction versus Traditional Team, cared for 29% higher patient volume, and improved early discharge rate without increasing readmissions

audits.t: Outcomes of a quality improvement project aimed at improving delivery of new anticancer drug education to nursing in an academic-community hybrid model.
audits.tp: Nurse comfort/education on new anticancer drugs
audits.st: Local target: increase nurses reporting comfort administering newer oncology drugs from 57% to ≥75%
audits.f: 57% of nurses reported being extremely/somewhat comfortable administering newer oncology drugs; 32% somewhat/very uncomfortable
audits.c: Pharmacy-driven 'At-A-Glance' education sheets made accessible on the intranet, nursing consideration sections added, monthly nursing/pharmacy huddles, over 2 PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Comfort level rose to ≥75%, sustained through PDSA cycle 2

audits.t: Quality care for patients with tenosynovial giant cell tumor: A multidisciplinary quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Multidisciplinary care coordination for tenosynovial giant cell tumour
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Audit-feedback sessions after a baseline survey (n=25) to develop action plans, followed by extended surveys/education to a nationwide audience (n=553)

audits.t: Quality initiative to improve lung cancer screening in a Veterans Affairs medical center.
audits.tp: Lung cancer screening enrolment and follow-up compliance
audits.st: National cancer roundtable-recommended lung cancer screening (LCS) follow-up timelines by Lung-RADS category (15 months for RADS 1/2, 8 months for RADS 3, 18 weeks for RADS 4)
audits.f: 54% of LDCTs performed through the formal LCS program; Lung-RADS 1/2 scans with appropriate follow-up 49% outside the programme
audits.c: Changed the radiology ordering menu to route providers through the Clinical Reminder System (CRS) enrolling patients in the LCS programme
audits.r2: 79% of LDCTs performed through the LCS programme (p<0.001); Lung-RADS 1/2 follow-up compliance was significantly better within the programme (70% vs 49%, p<0.001)

audits.t: Promoting prostate cancer screening equity: Findings from a quality improvement education initiative implemented in 3 sites.
audits.st: Prostate cancer screening guidelines with emphasis on higher risk in Black patients
audits.f: Baseline screening practices and provider surveys revealed gaps in awareness of risk factors and screening timing
audits.c: 12-week Quality Improvement Education (QIE) intervention with educational materials (Prostate Health Education Network) and an updated screening protocol
audits.r2: Table shows increased PC screening during the intervention phase, but limited sustainability post-intervention

audits.t: Reducing same-day cancellations of precious CT simulation slots: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Same-day cancellation of CT simulation appointments
audits.st: Local target: reduce same-day CT simulation (CTsim) cancellations from 15.5% to 10% within 6 months
audits.f: 33% of CTsim appointments were cancelled, of which 47% occurred on the same day (15.5% of all appointments)
audits.c: Workflow to assess patient preparation adequacy, screening phone call 2 days before appointment, and an information sheet on CTsim, developed via cause-and-effect diagram and PDSA cycles
audits.r2: Target achieved in month 4 and sustained for 2 further months; mean same-day cancellation rate was 5% in the last three months

audits.t: Assessment of quality improvement priorities to improve care delivery for patients with ovarian cancer.
audits.tp: Ovarian cancer care delivery quality self-assessment
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Single-center comparison of cancer genetics referral rates for patients with pancreatic cancer following implementation of a best practice advisory: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Cancer genetics referral rate for pancreatic cancer
audits.st: Guidelines recommending germline genetic testing and counselling for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
audits.f: Cancer genetics referral (CGR) offered to 24.3% (44/181) of eligible patients, with 88.6% accepting; germline testing was 90.9% of testing performed
audits.c: Implementation of an electronic health record physician best practice advisory (BPA) recommending a cancer genetics referral order for PDAC patients
audits.r2: CGR offered to 51.1% (23/45) of eligible patients, with 86.95% accepting; germline testing was 100% of testing performed

audits.t: EpiPen STAT: A quality improvement project for anaphylaxis management.
audits.tp: Timely EpiPen administration for chemotherapy anaphylaxis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 6 anaphylactic reactions to chemotherapy occurred between June 2000 and April 2021, with EpiPen delayed in all cases; nurses reported lack of confidence administering EpiPen
audits.c: Revised chemotherapy reaction guidelines, a reaction management algorithm, PRN-reaction orders, EpiPen training, and an adverse drug reaction kit, guided by the TRIP framework
audits.r2: Management algorithm followed in 50% of reactions; PRN-reaction orders available in 85% of cases; ADR kit used in all reactions; EpiPen given immediately in 2 of 4 anaphylactic reactions

audits.t: Screening for supportive care services in the neuro-oncology patient: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Symptom screening and supportive care referral in neuro-oncology
audits.st: NCCN recommendation for routine symptom screening and ASCO supportive care criteria for brain tumour patients
audits.f: Only 39% of patients were screened in-clinic and 8.7% of those qualifying were referred (39.3% ESAS completion)
audits.c: PDSA-guided improvement of Edmonton Symptom Assessment Scale (ESAS) use and reduction of barriers to supportive care referral
audits.r2: ESAS completion rose from 39.3% to 94.4%; referral among qualifying patients rose from 4.9% (5) to 10.7% (7)

audits.t: Building a learning network to accelerate improvement in pancreas cancer care and outcomes: Canopy Cancer Collective.
audits.tp: Learning health network for pancreatic cancer care improvement
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Learning health network model applying continuous QI, data-sharing, empowered interdisciplinary teams and stakeholder community, with IHI Model for Improvement training

audits.t: Outcomes of a quality improvement project integrating an EHR (electronic health record) for improved adverse drug reaction (ADR) communication at an adult outpatient cancer infusion center.
audits.tp: Adverse drug reaction communication in outpatient infusion
audits.st: Local target: 75% compliance with communication of infusion-related adverse drug reactions (ADRs) to ordering provider
audits.f: 41% compliance with communication of ADRs to ordering provider
audits.c: New EHR flowsheet section and smart phrase for ADR documentation, automated in-basket messaging to care team, alert prompting clinician acknowledgement, over 2 PDSA cycles (Jan 2021, June 2021)
audits.r2: 80% improvement in communication of ADRs to ordering providers and 35% increase in internal safety-system reporting of ADRs

audits.t: Quality of cancer family history taking in pediatric solid tumor patients.
audits.tp: Cancer family history documentation quality in paediatric solid tumours
audits.st: ASCO minimum family history quality metrics: 2-generation pedigree, patient ethnicity, cancer genetic testing results in relatives, cancer type/age/lineage for each relative with cancer
audits.f: Pediatric oncology providers (POPs) failed to document family history in 16% of patients (including 2 with pathogenic germline alterations) and missed first/second degree relatives with cancer in 36% of patients with such relatives; POPs met all 6 ASCO metrics in only 3% of cases versus 99% for genetic counsellors

audits.t: Advancing individualized care in advanced gastroesophageal cancers (GEC): A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Biomarker testing and guideline-concordant treatment in gastroesophageal cancer
audits.st: Evidence-based guidelines for biomarker testing (HER2, EGFR, FGFR, NTRK, MSI, TMB, PD-L1) in metastatic gastroesophageal cancer
audits.f: Providers reported testing for key biomarkers in ~55-65% of advanced GEC patients; correct identification of guideline-concordant treatment for stage IV oesophageal cancer was 48%
audits.c: Interdisciplinary audit and feedback (AF) sessions (n=24 HCPs) to develop clinic-specific action plans on HCP education, testing turnaround time, and clinical trial referral
audits.r2: Correct identification of guideline-concordant treatment rose to 72% post-AF; confidence using biomarkers for treatment decisions rose from 46% to 72% high/very high

audits.t: Understanding differences in the rates of BRCA/HRD testing and treatment in 1<sup>st</sup> line maintenance in patients with ovarian cancer treated by gynecologic oncologists compared to other providers: A quality initiative by Integra Connect (IC) PrecisionQ.
audits.tp: BRCA/HRD testing and maintenance therapy use in ovarian cancer
audits.st: Guideline-recommended BRCA/HRD testing and 1st-line maintenance therapy use in advanced ovarian cancer
audits.f: BRCA testing 81% at SCOA vs 75% elsewhere; HRD testing 60% vs 39% (p<0.01); 1st-line maintenance use 64% (SCOA, n=75) vs 50% (others, n=899, p<0.05)

audits.t: A multi-level system quality improvement project to reduce disparities in lung cancer screening: The Sylvester Lung Screening Project.
audits.tp: Disparities in lung cancer screening uptake
audits.st: Guideline-concordant annual low-dose CT lung cancer screening
audits.f: Baseline lung cancer screening completion rate was 20%
audits.c: Multi-level QI: EMR identification of eligible patients, patient navigation, expanded provider education, marketing campaign, interpreters, and full-time lung screening navigator
audits.r2: Screening exams increased 25% (from 20% to 25% of eligible patients); highest screening rate was among Hispanic patients (12%), then Black (8%), then non-Hispanic white (6%) patients

audits.t: Just ASK: A quality improvement project to enhance smoking assessment and treatment.
audits.tp: Smoking assessment and treatment (the 3As) in cancer care
audits.st: Clinical practice guidelines for the 3As (Ask, Advise, Assist) for smoking assessment and treatment in cancer care
audits.f: 90% of programmes reported routinely assessing smoking and 71% advising all current smokers to quit, but routine delivery of evidence-based cessation assistance (quitline, medication, counselling) was under 30% for all approaches
audits.c: Educational webinars, online resources, and 3 surveys (baseline, 6- and 12-month) as part of the national 'Just ASK' quality improvement project
audits.r2: Marked improvements reported in all quality indicators of the 3As at 12-month follow-up

audits.t: Unnecessary thrombophilia testing reduction: Quality improvement project.
audits.st: American Society of Hematology (ASH) recommendations against routine inpatient thrombophilia testing
audits.f: 33 of 310 patients (10%) underwent thrombophilia workup (175 tests); testing was more common in unprovoked VTE (29.3% vs 7.8%, p=0.0003); only 16% of tests were hematology-recommended, costing $34,083 outside recommendation
audits.c: Physician education on ASH recommendations via lectures, biweekly emails and educational posters
audits.r2: 21 of 191 patients (10.9%) underwent thrombophilia workup (78 tests); testing ordered outside hematology recommendation fell from 84% to 43%, saving $16,635 in the quarter

audits.t: A quality improvement initiative on the utility of the Oncotype DX breast cancer assay in a community hospital.
audits.tp: Guideline adherence to Oncotype DX-guided adjuvant chemotherapy decisions
audits.st: Guidelines for use of adjuvant chemotherapy based on Oncotype DX recurrence score (RS) risk category, with differing benefit by menopausal status
audits.f: 29.62% low risk, 56.79% intermediate, 13.5% high risk; 100% of high-risk patients received chemotherapy; only 7.4% of patients with RS 0-25 received chemotherapy; of 7 post-menopausal lymph-node positive patients with RS 0-25, only 1 received chemotherapy

audits.t: Towards the improvement of breast cancer management based on EUSOMA quality indicators: Insights from a 15-year institutional experience.
audits.tp: Breast cancer care compliance with EUSOMA quality indicators
audits.st: European Society of Breast Cancer Specialists (EUSOMA) quality indicators (2017 update)
audits.f: Of 34 EUSOMA QIs, 14 could be assessed; 6 reached the minimum EUSOMA standard (3/7 diagnosis, 2/3 surgical/locoregional treatment, 1/4 surgical/quality of life)

audits.t: Identifying and overcoming racial disparities in triple-negative breast cancer care: Insights from an equity-focused quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Racial disparities in triple-negative breast cancer care
audits.st: Equitable, timely, guideline-concordant care standards for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC)
audits.f: Mean time from diagnosis to treatment was 67 days for Black vs 37 days for Non-Black patients; documented treatment discussion 30%, risks/benefits discussion 58%
audits.c: Audit-feedback session with HCPs to prioritise improvements in individualised treatment decision-making
audits.r2: Documented discussions about treatment options rose to 59% and risks/benefits discussions to 64%; mean time to treatment improved for Black patients (67 to 44 days) and overall (53 to 42 days)

audits.t: Standardization of pregnancy screening prior to chemotherapy: A quality improvement project.
audits.st: NCCN and QOPI Certification program standards for documenting pregnancy status before first chemotherapy administration
audits.f: Baseline compliance with pregnancy testing within 7 days of starting chemotherapy was 17% (5/30)
audits.c: Institutional guideline for qualitative serum beta-hCG testing, educational email to staff, and an automated EHR nudge prompting guideline-concordant pregnancy testing
audits.r2: Compliance increased to an average of 76%, sustained over a 5-month period

audits.t: Advancing TNBC care in the community oncology practice: Insights from a quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Community oncology TNBC care quality improvement
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Top challenge reported was sequencing treatment across multiple therapy lines (33%); most difficulty managing gastrointestinal distress, cardiotoxicity and endocrinopathies (31% each)
audits.c: Audit/feedback educational sessions (n=150) leading to action plans on coordinated care, patient-centred supportive care, testing, adverse event management and standardised order sets

audits.t: Examining molecular testing practices and targeted therapy use in advanced/metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (mNSCLC): A quality improvement initiative across ten community cancer centers.
audits.tp: Molecular biomarker testing and targeted therapy use in metastatic NSCLC
audits.st: NCCN-recommended biomarker testing (9 biomarkers) for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer
audits.f: Fewer than half of HCPs reported regular testing for 4 of the 9 NCCN-recommended biomarkers; 52%/23% were somewhat/very-extremely likely to start treatment before receiving molecular results
audits.c: Interdisciplinary audit and feedback sessions (n=105 HCPs) with a targeted therapy toolkit developed with oncology/pathology experts
audits.r2: HCP confidence in biomarker testing rose from 72% to 92%; correct knowledge answers rose from 43% to 61% and competence answers from 29% to 54% post-intervention

audits.t: Patterns of actionable biomarker testing in lung cancer patients: Disparity or an opportunity for improvement.
audits.tp: Timely comprehensive molecular testing in non-small cell lung cancer
audits.st: Guideline recommendations for next-generation sequencing (NGS) molecular testing in newly diagnosed NSCLC
audits.f: 64.4% (125) had at least one molecular test; 18.6% had only PD-L1 testing; 17.0% had no immunohistochemical or molecular testing; median time from biopsy to results was 29 days
audits.c: Automatic reflex of confirmed NSCLC biopsy tissue for NGS, and a shift from individual molecular studies to comprehensive panels only
audits.r2: Median time from biopsy to molecular testing results decreased to 23 days; molecular testing rate increased to 100% in newly diagnosed NSCLC patients

audits.t: Promoting multidisciplinary care for patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC): Findings from a quality improvement initiative across two community cancer centers.
audits.tp: Multidisciplinary and patient-centred care for hepatocellular carcinoma
audits.st: Guideline recommendations for multidisciplinary coordination and patient-centred/shared decision-making care in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma
audits.f: 77% of HCPs estimated ≤25% of patients were evaluated for/referred to distress/behavioural health services; shared decision-making reported by only 24% of HCPs
audits.c: Interdisciplinary audit and feedback sessions with action plan implementation
audits.r2: Improvements shown in supportive care utilisation and documented HCP participation in shared decision-making post-intervention (exact figures given only in table)

audits.t: AI virtual patient navigation to promote re-engagement of U.S. inner city patients nonadherent with colonoscopy appointments: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: AI patient navigation for colonoscopy appointment re-engagement
audits.st: Local target: re-engage patients nonadherent with colonoscopy appointments
audits.f: 59% (1925/3276) of patients cancelled or did not show for colonoscopy; human patient navigator re-engagement led to 21% (410) completing colonoscopy
audits.c: AI-based virtual patient navigator (MyEleanor) calling nonadherent patients to discuss rescheduling, assess barriers, and offer live transfer to clinical staff
audits.r2: Colonoscopy completion rate for patients who did not show for their initial appointment nearly doubled from 10% to 19%; overall patient volume increased 36%

audits.t: NSQIP audit of enhanced recovery after surgery protocols for radical cystectomy.
audits.tp: ERAS protocol compliance audit for radical cystectomy
audits.st: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocol components for radical cystectomy
audits.f: 41% received ≤3 ERAS components, 39% received 4, 20% received 5; higher compliance associated with lower complication rates (OR 0.71-0.74), shorter length of stay, and better odds of optimal outcome (OR 1.68-1.97)

audits.t: Viral hepatitis screening in patients with early breast cancer receiving cancer therapy: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Hepatitis screening before breast cancer therapy
audits.st: ASCO guidelines recommending HBV and HCV screening before initiation of cancer therapy; local target ≥50% screening
audits.f: Historical HBV screening rate in patients receiving cancer therapy was around 29%
audits.c: Creation of a comprehensive HBV/HCV EMR order panel and an educational session for Breast Medical Oncology providers
audits.r2: 48% (105) received comprehensive HBV screening (63% at least one HBV test); 56% (122) screened for HCV; 40% (88) received both comprehensive HBV and HCV screening; EMR order panel used in 23% of patients

audits.t: Identifying and addressing real-world challenges to triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) care: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Community oncology TNBC care quality improvement
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Top challenges reported were treatment sequencing, care coordination/transitions, and patient-centred supportive care; ~40% used distress screening, QOL assessment and end-of-life counselling versus ~70% for nutrition/lifestyle/financial counselling
audits.c: Audit/feedback sessions (n=47 HCPs) leading to action plans on communication channels, treatment sequencing protocols, and workflow standardisation
audits.r2: Follow-up survey found 83% of clinics had improved follow-up/monitoring for adverse events and 67% reported more frequent shared decision-making

audits.t: Real-world multi-target stool DNA longitudinal adherence for colorectal cancer re-screening in a large, national population.
audits.tp: Adherence to repeat colorectal cancer stool DNA screening
audits.st: Recommended 3-year interval for multi-target stool DNA (mt-sDNA) colorectal cancer re-screening
audits.f: Overall repeat test completion rate was 83.6%, with average time to kit return 18.9 days; completion rates rose with age (81.6% at 45-49 years to 85% at 65-75 years)

audits.t: Multidisciplinary care for patients with gastroesophageal cancers (GEC): A quality improvement initiative in community cancer clinics.
audits.tp: Multidisciplinary care coordination for gastroesophageal cancer in community clinics
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Top challenges were interdisciplinary care coordination, patient-centred supportive care, and adverse event management; about one-third found AE recognition/management most challenging
audits.c: Audit/feedback sessions (n=70 HCPs) with action plans on streamlining surgical team communication, patient navigation, tumour board review, and AE education

audits.t: Oncologic outpatient specialty palliative care referral utilization: A single institution quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Outpatient specialty palliative care referral utilisation
audits.st: ASCO recommendation that late-stage/recurrent disease patients with 6-24 month prognosis receive specialty palliative care within 8 weeks of diagnosis
audits.f: 27% of referred patients did not schedule an appointment; median time from referral to appointment was 20 days (IQR 9-30); median time from referral to hospice enrolment was 66 days (IQR 22-164)

audits.t: Trainee-led quality improvement (QI) project examining PCP prophylaxis in patients on chronic, high-dose corticosteroids.
audits.tp: PCP prophylaxis in patients on chronic high-dose corticosteroids
audits.st: ASCO/IDSA consensus guidelines for Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) prophylaxis in patients on chronic high-dose corticosteroids (≥20mg prednisone equivalents daily for ≥1 month)
audits.f: Fewer than half of eligible patients (140, 47%) were prescribed appropriate PCP prophylaxis; no sociodemographic differences found between those prescribed and not prescribed prophylaxis

audits.t: Educating and empowering health care teams who present to the hospital to recognize and intervene on cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) in patients on bispecific t-cell engager therapy (BiTEs): A quality improvement study.
audits.tp: Education on cytokine release syndrome and ICANS recognition for BiTE therapy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average pre-survey knowledge score was 39% in the emergency department and 45% in the BMT department
audits.c: 15-minute educational presentation on CRS/ICANS recognition and management for emergency department and BMT unit staff
audits.r2: Post-intervention scores rose significantly to 66% in the emergency department (p=0.0001) and 68% in the BMT department (p=0.0006)

audits.t: Results of a quality improvement program to increase complete lung cancer biomarker testing rates by focusing on system, physician, and other factors associated with adverse health outcomes.
audits.tp: Complete biomarker testing in advanced lung cancer
audits.st: Standard of care for complete biomarker testing (CBT) in advanced lung adenocarcinoma
audits.f: Only 41% of patients received complete biomarker testing; when quantity not sufficient (QNS) required liquid biopsy, time from diagnosis to results averaged 42 days
audits.c: New workflow collecting both tissue and blood at biopsy, using a single reference lab that tests blood only when tissue is QNS, prioritising PD-L1 tissue testing
audits.r2: CBT increased by 39.6 percentage points to 80.6% post-intervention; time from diagnosis to complete liquid biopsy results decreased by 15.7 days to 27.2 days; CBT rates rose across all but one physician by an average of 55%; CBT increased 8% in females and patients with Medicare/Medicaid/underinsured status

audits.t: Quality of surveillance in patients with completely resected gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.
audits.st: CommNETs 2018 consensus surveillance guidelines for completely resected GEP-NETs
audits.f: Adherence to recommended surveillance investigations was 23% (20/87); 76% (66/87) had at least one test not recommended by the guidelines

audits.t: Enhancing lung cancer surgical quality: Insights from a national quality improvement collaborative.
audits.tp: Lung cancer resection lymph node sampling compliance
audits.st: ACS Commission on Cancer Operative Standard 5.8: sampling of at least 3 mediastinal and at least 1 hilar lymph node stations, goal hospital compliance ≥80%
audits.f: 144 hospitals (40.7%) achieved ≥80% compliance; median hospital-level compliance 67.8% (IQR 42.9-90)
audits.c: Participation in the Lung NODES national quality improvement collaborative: guided root cause analyses, educational webinars, peer-to-peer learning, and development/implementation of hospital-level strategies over 12 months
audits.r2: 238 hospitals (67.2%) achieved ≥80% compliance; median compliance 90.5% (IQR 70-100), p<0.001

audits.t: Improving germline genetic testing in pancreatic cancer: A quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Germline genetic testing in pancreatic cancer
audits.st: NCCN 2019 recommendation that all patients with exocrine pancreatic cancer receive germline testing
audits.f: 37.8% (14/37) completed testing, 8% incomplete, 54.05% not tested
audits.c: Clinic-initiated germline testing instead of genetic counselling referral, smart phrase for consent documentation, simplified forms to standardise gene panels, and a patient information booklet
audits.r2: 63.7% (51/80) completed testing, 3.75% incomplete, 32.5% not tested, p=0.015399; mean time to results improved from 168.94 to 77.68 days

audits.t: Strengthening multidisciplinary collaboration to enhance early-stage melanoma outcomes: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Guideline recommendations for adjuvant systemic treatment (immunotherapy/BRAF-targeted therapy) in stage II/III cutaneous melanoma
audits.f: only 32% of patient charts documented molecular testing despite 90% of HCPs reporting regular BRAF assessment; no documented first-line therapy for 49% of patients; only 24% of HCPs fully satisfied with multidisciplinary coordination
audits.c: Network-wide practice summit and action plans: reflex testing, individualised care plans, tumour board case reviews, improved multidisciplinary workflows
audits.r2: 100% of teams reported improved communication and collaboration; 43% of providers increased biomarker testing; 29% integrated tumour boards; 29% increased patient education and referrals

audits.t: Lung cancer screening for high-risk patients: A quality improvement initiative to improve guideline adherence in real-world primary care practices.
audits.st: USPSTF guidelines recommending low-dose CT for adults 50-80 years with a 20 pack-year smoking history
audits.f: only 41% of HCPs identified the correct guideline-recommended population; 37% unaware LDCT is the recommended modality; only 41% of high-risk patients referred for LDCT
audits.c: Point-of-care resource, cross-clinic educational sessions, and clinic-specific action plans integrating the resource into workflows
audits.r2: 46% used the point-of-care tool regularly; 89% developed/improved protocols to identify high-risk patients; 86% increased LDCT use/referral; 83% reported increased patient adherence to screening

audits.t: A quality improvement initiative to improve fertility counseling and referral procedures for cancer patients at a university cancer center.
audits.tp: Fertility counselling and referral documentation in cancer patients
audits.st: ASCO 2018 guideline on fertility counselling and referral for cancer patients aged 18-45
audits.f: 43.5% (40/92) had documented discussion of infertility risks; only 18.5% received referral for fertility counselling
audits.c: Patient education pamphlet, a Smart Phrase for documentation, a list of local fertility preservation clinics with urgent referral guidelines, and provider education resources

audits.t: Improving colorectal cancer screening rates in veterans: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.tp: Colorectal cancer screening in eligible patients
audits.st: USPSTF recommendation to screen for colorectal cancer in adults aged 45-75
audits.f: 46 (21%) had missed age-appropriate screening; pre-intervention screening rate 79%
audits.c: Mailed pamphlet, telephone and annual follow-up visit screening discussions, and ordering of appropriate testing for consenting patients
audits.r2: screening rate increased to 96%; of the 46 with missed screening, 28 completed colonoscopy, 8 completed FIT, and 10 declined

audits.t: Optimizing biomarker testing and targeted therapy integration in early-stage NSCLC: A quality improvement initiative at community oncology clinics.
audits.st: NCCN-recommended biomarker testing in early-stage non-small cell lung cancer
audits.f: fewer than half of patients received NCCN-recommended biomarker testing; EGFR documented in 42%, PD-L1 in 42%, ALK in 48% of charts
audits.c: Network-wide summit and action plans to streamline biomarker testing workflows, boost tumour board participation, and improve inter-specialty communication
audits.r2: 71% of HCPs reported increased tumour board use; 100% agreed clinic practice changes led to more patients receiving biomarker testing

audits.t: Accelerating answers: Impact of a quality improvement initiative for lung cancer pathology practices at the VA.
audits.tp: Lung cancer pathology sample turnaround time
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 9.8% of samples had insufficient quantity for FISH; turnaround time from biopsy to genetic data 26 days
audits.c: Whole-block cutting at time of biopsy (rather than step-by-step cutting) and replacing send-out testing with in-house next generation sequencing
audits.r2: insufficient FISH samples decreased to 4.2% (p<0.0001); turnaround time improved to 20 then 19 days (p<0.0001); time to first therapy in Stage IV patients reduced from 49 to 30 days (p<0.01)

audits.t: Implementation of a breast cancer survivorship needs assessment tool, an ASCO Quality Training Program initiative.
audits.st: 2015 ASCO Breast Cancer Survivorship Guidelines recommendation for needs assessment
audits.f: 116 (97%) had access to the electronic portal; survey response rate 37%, increasing to 51% with a second outreach
audits.c: Implementation of an electronic breast cancer survivorship needs assessment tool using process maps and PDSA methodology, with tailored follow-up resources from a community health worker

audits.t: Monitoring concordance with evidence-based guidelines in the treatment of stage I to IIIA lung cancer: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.st: Commission on Cancer Standard 7.2: in-depth analysis of cancer treatments for concordance with national evidence-based guidelines
audits.f: 81.6% were in concordance with evidence-based guidelines; only 2% received neoadjuvant therapy; of those eligible for systemic therapy, only 18.2% received it

audits.t: Early findings from a national quality improvement (QI) program to address disparities in bladder cancer (BLCA) care.
audits.tp: Disparities in guideline-concordant bladder cancer care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: only 1 of 3 programmes had processes to regularly assess disparities; only 1 felt it had adequate training or culturally appropriate educational materials
audits.c: Association of Cancer Care Centers quality improvement programme: in-person workshops using an impact-feasibility matrix to prioritise interventions and develop site-specific action plans

audits.t: Implementation of a telephone genetic screening program in breast cancer survivorship in the Bronx: A health care delivery quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Genetic testing uptake in breast cancer survivors
audits.st: not reported

audits.c: Provider education on accurate family history documentation via in-person lectures at quarterly staff meetings and informational pamphlets

audits.r2: screening rate increased to 42.5% (OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.35-3.17, p<0.001); FIT order rate rose from 27.1% to 70.3%; FIT completion rose from 15.6% to 35.8%

audits.f: 88% Graves' disease aetiology; treatment initiated within 6 hours in 82% of cases; 5 ventilated patients co-managed in ICU; one death within 3 days

audits.t: AUDIT ON ALDOSTERONE-TO-RENIN SAMPLING IN SCREENING FOR PRIMARY ALDOSTERONISM
audits.st: Clinical practice guideline indications for ARR sampling in primary aldosteronism screening
audits.f: 67.6% of ARR sampling was for hypertension onset <40 years, yielding only 3.3% positivity; ARR positive/indeterminate in 10.4% overall; 65.2% of positives confirmed primary hyperaldosteronism

audits.t: A CLINICAL AUDIT OF DIABETES CARE AMONG OLDER ADULTS ADMITTED TO MEDICAL WARDS
audits.tp: Inpatient glycaemic care guideline compliance audit
audits.st: Malaysia Endocrine and Metabolic Society inpatient glycaemic management guidelines (target ≥80% of readings 7.0-10.0mmol/L)
audits.f: Glycaemic target achieved in only 39% of patients; adherence to guidelines during IV insulin use poor (highest 40.6%); non-achievers had higher 30-day readmission (67.3% vs 32.7%) and inpatient mortality (69.2% vs 30.8%), not statistically significant

audits.t: PATIENTS’ OUTCOME AND COMPLIANCE IN OBESITY CLINIC HOSPITAL KAJANG – A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT OF WEIGHT LOSS INTERVENTIONS
audits.tp: Obesity clinic outcomes and compliance audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline BMI 44.47kg/m2, 37% with diabetes
audits.r2: 75.7% achieved ≥5% weight loss; mean weight reduction 2.997kg (p=0.012); BP, LDL and HbA1c changes not statistically significant; treatment adherence 75.7%, follow-up attendance 97.3%

audits.t: Audit of the quality of medical care as a way to improve the efficiency of medical organizations
audits.tp: Clinical audit methodology to improve efficiency of care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Making Audit Work
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Practice-Based Learning and Improvement: Improving Residents' Performance in Providing Preventive Care Through a Web-Based Chart Audit System
audits.tp: Resident preventive care screening chart audit tool
audits.st: US Preventive Services Task Force and American Diabetes Association disease prevention screening guidelines
audits.f: Resource description of a web-based self-assessment/chart audit tool; residents reported positive feedback but no aggregate compliance results with screening guidelines are given.

audits.t: UPDATED: A Signout Audit Tool to Address ACGME Milestones and Entrustable Professional Activities in Patient Handoffs
audits.st: ACGME internal medicine milestones / EPA #8 (manage transitions of care) as assessed by the UPDATED signout audit tool
audits.f: Only 13% of signouts audited received 'good' scores prior to implementation of the UPDATED tool/workshop.
audits.c: Workshop introducing the UPDATED audit tool (slide set, facilitator guide, paper-based audit tool and auditor training guide) for PGY-1 residents.
audits.r2: 73% of signouts received 'good' scores following implementation (p<0.001).

audits.t: IMPLEMENTATION OF CONCURRENT NURSING AUDIT: AN EXPERIENCE REPORT
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Describes feasibility and benefits of concurrent nursing audit implementation, including reduced time to bill health insurers and improved interaction between auditors and care teams.

audits.t: Intensive care unit audit: invasive procedure surveillance
audits.tp: Adherence to healthcare-associated infection prevention measures for invasive procedures
audits.st: Hospital Infection Control Commission (HICC) standardised prevention measures for invasive procedures
audits.f: For every 1,000 patients: 15 had catheter-related bloodstream infection and 6.85 had catheter-associated urinary tract infection.

audits.t: Audit of the workload in a maxillofacial and oral surgical unit in Johannesburg
audits.tp: Maxillofacial and oral surgery unit workload audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Male:female ratio 1.3:1, most patients in 3rd/4th decade; tooth extraction (impacted 3rd molar) most common; dentoalveolar surgery most common procedure followed by facial fracture treatment

audits.t: Management of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Diseases (COPD) Exacerbation. A Clinical Audit in Nasser Hospital, Gaza-Strip, Palestine
audits.st: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) 2015 guideline
audits.f: All received inhaled bronchodilators; 96.4% received systemic corticosteroids, 78.2% >40mg prednisolone daily, only 21.8% for the recommended 5 days; 92.7% had oxygen, 100% antibiotics; no patient received chest physiotherapy

audits.t: A Clinical Audit of Psychotropic Drug Use in a Nigerian Teaching Hospital
audits.tp: Psychotropic drug use and adverse effects audit
audits.st: WHO/INRUD core prescribing indicators and NICE guideline for psychotropic prescribing
audits.f: 31.6% reported at least one adverse effect (excessive salivation 13.5% most frequent); benzhexol most prescribed (27.0%); 73.1% prescribed by generic name; antibiotic co-prescription <30%; injection route 2%

audits.t: Health technology management: implementation and validation of an audit tool
audits.tp: Audit tool validation for medical equipment management
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Validation of an audit tool for health technology/medical equipment management: Cronbach alpha 0.90, Spearman correlation 0.88 among 12 expert reviewers; audit reports generated strengths/weaknesses for improvement.

audits.t: Audit of radiology request forms –“Are they adequately filled?”
audits.st: Implied completeness standard for adequate clinical information on radiology request forms
audits.f: Clinical diagnosis absent in 42% of forms and clinical details absent in 62%; age/sex missing in 35%; 46% signed by nursing staff rather than the referring physician; handwriting illegible in 20%.

audits.t: Obstetric audit of cesarean sections according to M. Robson classification criteria – the experience of St. Petersburg in 2020-2021
audits.st: WHO-recommended M. Robson 10-group classification system for monitoring/auditing caesarean section rates
audits.f: External audit of childbirth outcomes by Robson classification analysed determinants and frequency of caesarean section across obstetric organisations in St. Petersburg.

audits.t: Audit of quality of care in critical conditions in obstetrics (“near miss”)
audits.tp: Quality of care in obstetric near-miss cases
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Case management with severe out-patient form of pneumonia audit at the in-patient
audits.tp: Severe community-acquired pneumonia case management audit
audits.st: Quality indicators for case management of severe out-patient (community-acquired) pneumonia
audits.f: Initial antibacterial therapy did not meet modern recommendations in 70.6% of cases; IV antimicrobial injections used in under half; step-down therapy used in only 24%; clinical severity scaling not applied; pulse oximetry used in only 24.5%

audits.t: Addressing unplanned escalations of care to the trauma ICU
audits.st: Modified Early Warning Score (MEWS) protocol for early detection of deterioration
audits.f: Mean nurse-to-provider notification time 39.73 minutes
audits.c: Staff education on MEWS over six weeks, real-time feedback, integration of MEWS into electronic medical records (rapid cycle QI)
audits.r2: Mean notification time fell to 20.38 minutes (p<0.001); no statistically significant change in escalation rate (p=0.311)

audits.t: European Audit on Colorectal Cancer Treatment Outcome – The Next Step in Quality Assurance Initiated by the European Society of Surgical Oncology
audits.tp: European audit of colorectal cancer treatment outcomes
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Impact of implementing pre-Medical Emergency Team tier and digital Code Blue monitoring on cardiac arrest outcomes: A clinical audit at an Indian tertiary care center
audits.tp: Code Blue / cardiac arrest response audit
audits.st: Structured escalation (pre-MET/MET) and Code Blue resuscitation performance standards
audits.f: Return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) rate 37.5%; ward-specific ROSC 63.2%
audits.c: Implementation of pre-Medical Emergency Team (pre-MET) tier and a digital Code Blue performance-monitoring platform
audits.r2: ROSC improved to 56.5% overall, ward-specific ROSC to 85.7%; chest compression fraction improved; MET calls decreased as pre-MET calls increased (χ²=10.98, p=0.012)

audits.t: A clinical audit and confidential enquiry of caesarean section indications at rural tertiary health care centre
audits.st: WHO recommended caesarean section rate (15%) and NICE urgency-category classification
audits.f: Overall caesarean section rate 36.88%; NICE category I 22.62%, II 38.61%, III 28.37%, IV 10.40%; confidential enquiry found questionable indications in 26.17% (Cat I), 20.3% (Cat II), 23.17% (Cat III), 8.3% (Cat IV)

audits.t: An audit of drug package insert: a survey based study in India
audits.st: Schedule D (Sections 6.2 and 6.3) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945
audits.f: Posology/method of administration present in 97.3% and contra-indications in 93.2%; special precautions for storage in 77%; shelf life in only 33.8%.

audits.t: Prescription audit of outpatients in tertiary care government hospital
audits.tp: Prescription audit using WHO core indicators
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators
audits.f: 1910 drugs prescribed (1.91 drugs/prescription); 55% single-drug prescriptions; almost all drugs prescribed by generic name; ~95% doses specified in mg/ml.

audits.t: Drug utilization audit of antipsychotics using WHO methodology: recommendations for rational prescribing
audits.tp: Prescription audit using WHO core indicators
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators
audits.f: Monotherapy in 76%; atypical antipsychotics used more (89%) than typical (11%); olanzapine (31%) and risperidone (26%) most prescribed; 24% prescribed by generic name; 46% from National List of Essential Medicines 2015.

audits.t: The use of ATC/DDD WHO 2016 and Prescription audit study in the Dermatology OPD of a tertiary care hospital in Jharkhand
audits.tp: Prescription audit using WHO ATC/DDD indicators
audits.st: WHO 2016 ATC/DDD (defined daily dose) classification
audits.f: Prescriptions mostly rational; DDD/1000 patients/day for antifungals exceeded the WHO DDD, while antihistaminics were below the WHO DDD; polypharmacy evident.

audits.t: Prescription audit and drug utilization pattern in outpatients of psychiatry department of tertiary care teaching hospital: an observational study
audits.tp: Prescription audit using WHO core indicators
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators
audits.f: Depression most common diagnosis (32.6%); average 2.45±1.013 psychotropic drugs/patient; 99.98% oral formulations; only 28% prescribed by generic name; 29% from WHO's 18th essential medicines list.

audits.t: Prescription audit to evaluate the pattern and errors in a tertiary care hospital
audits.st: Standard prescription content requirements (prescriber/patient information, drug details, legibility, warnings)
audits.f: Patient information complete in 98.44%; prescriber information present in 88.75%; legibility 75%; generic drug use only 2.81%; overall completeness (drug name, dose, strength, route, frequency, duration, form) in 78.75%.

audits.t: Outpatient prescription audit in a tertiary care hospital at Puducherry
audits.tp: Prescription audit using WHO core indicators
audits.st: WHO core drug use prescribing indicators
audits.f: Average 2.74 drugs per prescription; antibiotics in 20.33% of prescriptions, injections in 0.16%; 83.13% prescribed by generic name and 87.9% from essential medicine list; antibiotic use higher in ENT (56.67%).

audits.t: Prescription audit of online booked outpatients for department of medicine and dermatology in a tertiary care hospital: a comparative observational study
audits.tp: Prescription audit using WHO core indicators
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators; target 100% adherence to National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM)
audits.f: Adherence to NLEM was 45% for medicine and 49% for dermatology, both below the 100% target; legibility was not a major concern.

audits.t: Audit of prescriptions from the department of general medicine based on the WHO core prescribing indicators at Sapthagiri hospital, Bangalore
audits.tp: Prescription audit using WHO core indicators
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators, compared with derived standard values
audits.f: Average 2.23±1.03 drugs per prescription; 23% had at least one generic-named drug; 25% contained an antibiotic; 31% contained an injection; only 57% of drugs from NLEM versus recommended 100%.

audits.t: Pharmacotherapeutic audit meetings as a tool of improving prescribing practices
audits.tp: Pharmacotherapeutic audit meetings to improve prescribing
audits.st: WHO/International Network for Rational Use of Drugs (INRUD) core prescribing/drug-use indicators
audits.f: Baseline prescribing screened using WHO/INRUD core indicators before pharmacotherapeutic audit meetings (PTAM).
audits.c: Pharmacotherapeutic audit meetings (PTAM) discussing WHO/INRUD indicator findings with prescribers.
audits.r2: After PTAM: antibiotic prescribing fell by 8.7% (95% CI 1.0-16.7%, p=0.02); generic-name prescribing rose by 10.9% (95% CI 5.6-16.2%, p<0.0001); EDL prescribing rose by 8.1% (95% CI 2.5-13.5%, p=0.0046); injectable use change not significant (0.7%, p=0.23).

audits.t: Prescription audit of patients in a teritiary care hospital
audits.tp: Prescription audit using WHO core indicators
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators (ideal recommended values)
audits.f: 16% of prescriptions had incomplete demographic details; 15% omitted diagnosis/had irrational combinations; antibiotics were 23.64% of prescriptions, much higher than the WHO-recommended ideal value.

audits.t: Increasing rates of cesarean section, an upcoming public health problem: an audit of cesarean section in a tertiary care center of North India based on Robson classification
audits.st: WHO/FIGO-recommended Robson 10-group classification system for monitoring caesarean section rates
audits.f: Overall caesarean rate 49.9%; Group 5 (previous section, singleton, cephalic, >=37 weeks) contributed the maximum caesarean rate (17.7%).

audits.t: Referrals revisited: a clinical audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Referral rate was 6.52%; 93.94% of referrals occurred during labour; main barriers were unavailability of 24-hour OT services, blood bank and ICU care.

audits.t: Audit of caesarean deliveries in a tertiary care hospital of northern Andhra Pradesh using modified Robson criteria
audits.st: Modified Robson criteria used to audit caesarean section rate and trends
audits.f: Significant increasing trend in groups 2B and 5C, and decreasing trend in 6C and 7C; commonest indications cephalo-pelvic disproportion (28%) and fetal distress (22%) in group 1.

audits.t: An audit of hysterectomies at a tertiary care teaching hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Most common age group 40-49 years (36.8%); commonest indication fibroid uterus (40%); hysterectomy considered justified in 98% based on postoperative histopathology, but 20 DUB, 5 CIN, 10 endometriosis and 3 chronic cervicitis cases could arguably have been managed conservatively.

audits.t: Classification of cesarean section through Robson criteria: an emerging concept to audit the increasing cesarean section rate
audits.st: Robson's 10-group classification system used to audit rising caesarean section rate
audits.f: Increased percentage of caesarean sections in groups 5 and 2, attributed partly to sedentary lifestyle and maternal request.

audits.t: Audit of caesarian deliveries in a tertiary care center, in rural Bangalore, India
audits.st: Robson's Ten-Group Classification System
audits.f: Overall caesarean section rate 46.7%; main contributors nulliparous spontaneous labour (group 1) and previous caesarean section (group 5); 52.1% of caesareans were in women unbooked or referred from peripheral facilities.

audits.t: Caesarean section audit in a tertiary hospital of North India using Robson’s classification
audits.st: WHO 2014 and FIGO 2016 recommend Robson's Ten-Group Classification System for monitoring caesarean section rate
audits.f: Overall caesarean section rate 28.24%; major contributors were group 5, followed by primigravidae in groups 1 and 2; increasing rate observed in groups 1, 2, 3 and 5.

audits.t: Robson ten groups classification system for caesarean section audit: are our operation theatre registers RTGC enabled?
audits.tp: Operation theatre register completeness for Robson classification
audits.st: Data fields required for Robson Ten-Group Classification System of caesarean audit
audits.f: Fetal presentation was the only factor clearly recorded for all 100 cases; labour onset (spontaneous/induced) was the least recorded observation; labour status at the time of caesarean section was also commonly missing.

audits.t: Classification of births according to Robson 10 group classification: an emerging concept to audit the increasing caesarean section rate
audits.st: WHO advises use of Robson's 10-group classification system to audit caesarean section rates and recommends CS rate not exceeding 15%
audits.f: Overall caesarean rate 38.48%; groups 5 and 2 contributed 62.4% of the total; groups 6 and 9 had 100% caesarean rates within their own group.

audits.t: Audit on maternal mortality in a tertiary care centre in India of 6 years, a retrospective analysis
audits.tp: Maternal death and severe morbidity review
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Maternal mortality ratio 915/100,000 live births; 42.7% of deaths in women aged 21-25; hypertensive disorders (12%), obstetric haemorrhage (11%), tuberculosis (11%) and hepatitis E (8%) were leading causes.

audits.t: Are we operating unnecessarily?: caesarean audit in a single unit of a private tertiary care hospital in North India
audits.st: Robson's Ten-Group Classification System
audits.f: Overall caesarean rate 46.88%; group 5 (previous LSCS, 33.9%) and group 2 (nulliparous >37 weeks induced, 26.3%) contributed most; commonest indications previous LSCS (38%) and fetal distress (19.2%).

audits.t: Analysing trends in caesarean sections at a tertiary care teaching hospital in South India: findings from a clinical audit using Robson criteria
audits.tp: Caesarean section trend audit using Robson criteria
audits.st: Robson ten-group classification system for caesarean sections
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An audit of caesarean section rate based on Robson’s ten group classification system
audits.st: Robson's Ten Group Classification System
audits.f: Overall caesarean section rate 46.88%; group 5 (previous LSCS) contributed 33.9% and group 2 (nulliparous induced) 26.3%; commonest indications previous LSCS (38%), fetal distress (19.2%) and meconium-stained liquor (13.7%).

audits.t: Changing trends in uterine rupture audit, from the Institute of obstetrics and gynecology, modern government maternity hospital, Osmania medical college
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 48/81 (59.25%) were scar ruptures; hysterectomy done in 53.08%; scar rupture rate in VBAC was 18/662 (2.71%); maternal mortality 3/81 (3.7%).

audits.t: An audit of the decision to delivery interval in emergency caesarean section and its effect on neonatal outcome
audits.st: RCOG/NICE emergency caesarean section categorisation: decision-to-delivery interval within 30 minutes (category 1) and within 75 minutes (category 2)
audits.f: Category 1: 113 (27.63%) cases, only 19.5% achieved DDI <30 minutes. Category 2: 126 (30.81%) cases, 93.65% achieved DDI <75 minutes. Category 3: 170 (41.56%) cases. Fetal distress was leading cause in categories 1 and 2; low Apgar significantly associated with DDI <30 minutes (p<0.0001).

audits.t: Re-staging surgery in endometrial cancer: an audit on its value
audits.tp: Completeness of surgical staging in endometrial cancer
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 10% of patients were upstaged by FIGO stage after completion surgery; 40% were upgraded by FIGO grade; recurrence rate 40% among those with incomplete initial staging.

audits.t: Hysterectomy for benign conditions in a tertiary care centre: a clinical audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Changing trends in the incidence of caesarean section after a district hospital became medical college teaching hospital at Karwar, a coastal city in Karnataka-an eleven years retrospective audit
audits.tp: Caesarean section rate against WHO obstetric care standards
audits.st: WHO guidelines for obstetric care, used as the standard against which caesarean section rate and maternal mortality were audited
audits.f: Caesarean proportion rose from 16.8% in 2007 to a peak of 51% in 2012, then fell to 23.5% by 2018 after protocol implementation; 99.9% of caesareans under spinal anaesthesia; one maternal death (2009).

audits.t: Analysis of caesarean sections using Robson’s classification system in a tertiary care centre in Northern India: an emerging concept to audit the increasing caesarean section rate
audits.st: Robson's Ten-Group Classification System
audits.f: Overall caesarean rate 46.12%; group 5 (previous caesarean) contributed 40.3% and group 2 (nulliparous induced/pre-labour) 29.2%; breech groups 6 and 7 had >90% caesarean rates.

audits.t: A clinical audit of hysteroscopy in a tertiary care teaching. What challenges did we face?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 12 diagnostic and 47 operative hysteroscopies; complications: media efflux/poor visualisation 17% (10), minor haemorrhage 15.1% (9), perforation 3.3% (2)

audits.t: Audit on the first obstetric ultrasound in a tertiary health facility in the Niger Delta and its implications for maternal foetal care
audits.tp: First obstetric ultrasound scan conformity to international norms
audits.st: International norms for content/performance of the first (dating) obstetric ultrasound scan, derived from literature review
audits.f: No guidelines or uniformity in conduct of first obstetric scans at RSUTH; appropriate biometric parameters used in only 28.19% of reports; chorionicity/amnionicity determination, anomaly scan and other screening elements were not performed.

audits.t: A clinical audit of Pap smear test for screening of premalignant and malignant cervical lesions
audits.tp: Pap smear screening uptake and findings audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 4.29% of gynaecology OPD attendees had a Pap smear done; 22% of those tested came for routine screening; 93% negative for intraepithelial lesion, 7% epithelial cell abnormality, 0% malignant

audits.t: Analyzing indications for caesarean delivery in a tertiary care facility in India by Robsons Ten Group Classification System: journey to reduce maternal mortality-audit caesarean rates: a prospective observational design
audits.st: Robson's Ten Group Classification System used to audit and standardise caesarean section indications
audits.f: 45.8% of women were in group 5; modifiable indications present in 60.2% of primary caesareans in group 5; postpartum haemorrhage, puerperal sepsis, postnatal anaemia and wound dehiscence significantly higher in group 5 (p<0.05).

audits.t: Audit of the first caesarean section in a reference hospital in the African environment
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Caesarean section found avoidable in 53 cases (18.9%) by expert opinion; probable fetal asphyxia was the leading indication overall (27.5%) and among avoidable cases (22.4%).

audits.t: Audit of caesarean deliveries in a tertiary care rural hospital of Bangalore, Karnataka, India
audits.st: WHO-adopted Robson classification system as the global standard for auditing caesarean section rates
audits.f: Highest proportion of caesarean deliveries among multigravidae (66.5%); group 3 (multiparous >37 weeks, spontaneous labour) accounted for 35% of caesareans.

audits.t: An audit of respectful maternity care during pregnancy and childbirth in a tertiary healthcare facility
audits.st: Respectful Maternity Care (RMC) principles (international standard), assessed via Birthplace Lab MADM, MOR and MIST scales
audits.f: High autonomy reported by 70.5% and high respect by 67.1% of women; mistreatment (mainly privacy breaches) reported by 6.7%; caesarean section rate 26.8%.

audits.t: Clinical audit on period of gestation at induction of labor in singleton low risk women at a tertiary care centre in South India: M. O. S. C. Medical College, Kolenchery
audits.tp: Gestation at induction of labour audit
audits.st: Guideline recommendation to induce singleton low-risk pregnancies at or after 39 weeks
audits.f: 77 women (56%) induced at or after 39 weeks; 60 women (44%) induced before 39 weeks

audits.t: Platelet audit: To weigh the rationality between requirement and uses in blood transfusion -
audits.st: Approved clinical guidelines for rational platelet transfusion use
audits.f: 10.9% group-nonspecific platelet transfusion; 31% inappropriate platelet transfusion; 1.99% wastage

audits.t: Prescription audit in outpatient department of a teaching hospital of North East, India
audits.tp: Prescription audit using WHO core indicators
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators, legibility and completeness checklist
audits.f: Only 50.90% of prescriptions were legible; average 2.64 drugs per prescription; 19.07% generic drugs; 52.86% from national essential drug list; signature section incomplete in 99.80%.

audits.t: Review of code blue system and audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average response time 1.58±0.96 minutes; survival rate higher in medical emergency group (46.15%) than cardio-respiratory arrest group (31.61%); initial success rate 35.2%, final success rate 34.6%.

audits.t: Analysis of intraoperative frozen section consultations and audit of accuracy: a two year experience in a tertiary care multispeciality hospital in India
audits.st: Comparison of intraoperative frozen section with final histopathology; international quality control statistics for frozen section accuracy used as benchmark
audits.f: Accuracy rate 97.17% (206/212 concordant), error rate 2.83% (6/212 discordant); most discordant cases were interpretation errors (83.33%)

audits.t: An audit on usage of fresh frozen plasma in a tertiary care hospital in north western part of India
audits.tp: Fresh frozen plasma usage appropriateness audit
audits.st: British Committee for Standards in Haematology (2004) and College of American Pathologists (1994) guidelines for FFP usage
audits.f: 29.48% of FFP transfusions reclassified as inappropriate, mostly due to lack of indication or inappropriate dose; most usage in Gastroenterology (41.75%) and CTVS (15.32%)

audits.t: An audit to analyze the three-week-wait pathway at department of otolaryngology, head and neck surgery, Sligo university hospital
audits.tp: Cancer pathway referral to treatment time
audits.st: Three-week wait pathway (patients seen by specialist within three weeks of GP referral)
audits.f: Average of 22 days from referral to being seen and average of 70 days between facility entry and completion of medical decision making; pathway judged effective with no significant delays

audits.t: An audit of hepatitis B vaccination status, knowledge and attitudes among healthcare professionals at northwest general hospital Peshawar
audits.tp: Hepatitis B vaccination status and knowledge audit (healthcare workers)
audits.st: Full 3-dose hepatitis B vaccination and up-to-date training for healthcare professionals
audits.f: 84.9% of HCPs reported being vaccinated but only 45.8% had received the full three doses; only 24.5% had participated in recent hepatitis B training despite high perceived exposure risk

audits.t: Evaluation of triple assessment performance against NICE breast cancer standards: a prospective breast clinic audit assessing guideline compliance and diagnostic outcomes in a rural hospital in Bangladesh
audits.tp: Breast cancer triple assessment pathway compliance audit
audits.st: NICE breast cancer diagnostic standards (triple assessment pathway)
audits.f: Compliance with clinical examination 87%, imaging 76%, histology 58%; overall pathway compliance 73%; malignancy in 39.5%, benign in 48.6%; mean referral-to-diagnosis time 24 days; inadequate diagnostic tools (p=0.032) and facilities (p=0.045) associated with lower compliance

audits.t: Prescription audit of tertiary care centre using world health organization core prescribing indicators: an observational study
audits.st: WHO/INRUD core prescribing indicators
audits.f: Average 5.84 drugs per prescription; 81.54% prescribed by generic name; antibiotics in 15.72% of encounters; injections in 1.81%

audits.t: Surgical audit of inguinal hernia surgery under local anaesthesia at a district hospital set up in central India
audits.tp: Local anaesthesia inguinal hernia repair outcomes
audits.st: Feasibility and reliability of local anaesthesia as routine practice for inguinal hernia surgery (audited against own outcome criteria: cost, satisfaction, complications)
audits.f: Mean operating time 70 minutes; mean recovery room stay 3.3 hours; intraoperative problems in 25% (30 patients); recurrence in 0.83% (1 patient) over mean follow-up of 3.6 months

audits.t: Facility-based evaluation of under-fives with diarrhoea in Cross River State, Nigeria: a clinical audit -
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of transfusion practices in pediatrics in a tertiary care hospital
audits.st: British Committee for Standards in Haematology guidelines for transfusion
audits.f: Overall appropriate use 58.33% (98/111); RBC most appropriately transfused (64.86%) vs platelets 42.85% and FFP 47.22%

audits.t: Study of the effect of pharmacotherapeutic audit meetings on prescription writing in a tertiary care center-an interventional study
audits.st: WHO/INRUD core prescribing and drug use indicators
audits.f: Prescriptions screened for rationality using WHO/INRUD indicators; index of rational drug prescribing calculated before intervention
audits.c: Pharmaco-therapeutic audit meetings (PTAM): prescriptions beyond acceptable limits discussed in regular meetings
audits.r2: Significant increase in generic-name prescribing (+10.5%, 95% CI 6.1-14.6%, p<0.0001); antibiotic prescribing change 3.4% (95% CI -1.7 to 9.4%, p=0.20, not significant); no significant change in injectable use or EDL prescribing

audits.t: A qualitative perinatal audit at a rural health facility in Eldoret, Kenya
audits.st: WHO ICD-10 perinatal mortality classification (ICD-PM)
audits.f: Perinatal death rate 11 per 1000 births; antepartum deaths from fetal growth problems, infection or unexplained causes (each 33.3%); neonatal deaths 47.1%, mostly low birth weight/prematurity

audits.t: Clinical audit: Awareness of bio medical waste (BMW) management among OT personnel
audits.tp: Biomedical waste management awareness audit (OT personnel)
audits.st: Recommended guidelines for biomedical waste segregation and disposal
audits.f: 85.2% had received formal BMW disposal training but knowledge was unsatisfactory; more than 40% of participants in each group (except OT technicians) did not know proper waste segregation

audits.t: Drug use evaluation and rational prescription audit of restricted antibiotics in tertiary care corporate hospital: An interventional study
audits.st: Local restricted antimicrobial policy

audits.t: A CRITICAL LITERATURE REVIEW AND AUDIT OF REAL WORLD DATA TO INFORM THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN MENTAL ILL-HEALTH AND TYPE-2 DIABETES FAVOURABLE PROGNOSIS
audits.tp: Mental ill-health and type 2 diabetes comorbidity
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: A CRITICAL REVIEW AND LOCAL AUDIT OF THE PREVALENCE OF MENTAL ILL-HEALTH IN HEART FAILURE PATIENTS
audits.tp: Mental ill-health prevalence in heart failure patients

audits.t: Study on Prescription Audit from a Rural Tertiary Care Hospital in North India
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators
audits.f: 100% had complete general patient details; 83.5% (167/200) had legible handwriting (68.5% easy, 20% difficult, 11.5% illegible); antibiotics prescribed in 51.5% (103/200)

audits.t: Study to Conduct Prescription Audit as per Objective Elements of NABH in Medical and Surgical Wards of a Tertiary Care Teaching Hospital
audits.tp: Prescription writing compliance with accreditation standards
audits.st: NABH (National Accreditation Board for Hospitals) objective elements for prescription writing
audits.f: 22% lacked patient ID numbers, 89% missed bed numbers, 95% omitted patient weight; 100% had at least one drug not in generic name; errors in strength (9%), route (20%), dose frequency (4%); allergy info absent in 65%; 32% lacked diet plan; drug-drug interactions in 26%

audits.t: A STUDY OF PRESCRIPTION AUDITING IN A TERTIARY CARE TEACHING HOSPITAL OF EASTERN INDIA
audits.tp: Prescription completeness and drug utilization pattern
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators
audits.f: Weight not written in 91.33%; inappropriate drugs in 52.99%; average 4.4 drugs/encounter; generic name prescribing only 20.99%; antibiotic prescribed in 28.89% of encounters; injection in 28.99%; drugs from essential drug list only 60.98%; overall illegibility 22.99%

audits.t: Thrombolysis in Acute Ischaemic Stroke: A Retrospective Audit of the Role of Alteplase in Hyperacute Stroke Management
audits.tp: Thrombolysis rates in acute ischaemic stroke
audits.st: not reported
