audits.t: A Report of Clinical Audit for Prevention and Improvement of Bedsore in Southwest Iran
audits.st: NICE guidelines for bedsore/pressure ulcer prevention
audits.f: Baseline assessment identified weakness points before intervention (pre-intervention values not separately quantified)
audits.c: Interventions implemented based on NICE guidelines following identification of weakness points
audits.r2: Increase in all studied variables after intervention: bedsore reduction (p=0.001), assessment within first 6 hours of hospitalization (p=0.008), assessment of external pressure (p=0.001), change of position (p=0.001), care standards (p=0.170), skin friction (p=0.001)

audits.t: A Prospective Antimicrobial Prescription Audit in the Inpatient Department of Pulmonology in a Tertiary Care Hospital
audits.st: Sanford Guide and GOLD guideline recommendations for antimicrobial use (no explicit numeric target stated)
audits.f: Irrational antibiotic use was high (53.41%); most common concomitant disorder was COPD (21.79%); most administered drug was ceftriaxone (20.51%); culture and sensitivity testing done in only 32.90% of cases; empirical therapy dominated over targeted therapy.

audits.t: De-Escalation of Broad-Spectrum Antibiotics After Relevant Culture Reports in Medical Ward Patients Audit from A Tertiary Care Hospital in South India
audits.st: Antimicrobial stewardship programme de-escalation practice
audits.f: Cefoperazone-sulbactam (32%) was commonly used empirical monotherapy; de-escalation rate after positive culture reports was 28%; serious clinical illness (36%) was most common reason for non-de-escalation; de-escalation not done in ~25% of eligible instances without proper justification

audits.t: Audit of Operative Notes and Documentation in a Surgical Unit of Tertiary Health Care Centre Karachi
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England 2014 Good Surgical Practice guidelines (20-parameter checklist)
audits.f: Patient identification, date/time of procedure, surgeon's name, operative procedure title and legibility were consistently documented across all records; nature of procedure, antibiotic prophylaxis and DVT prophylaxis were not recorded in any operative notes.

audits.t: An Audit of the Turnaround Time of Fixed Prosthodontics Cases in the Ceramic Laboratory
audits.tp: Turnaround time of fixed prosthodontics laboratory cases
audits.st: Local turnaround time standard for prosthodontics laboratory cases
audits.f: 57.8% of diagnostic wax-ups completed within 3 days; 100% of 1-unit crowns within 7 days; 94.4% of bridges within 14 days; significant association of turnaround time and case complexity for wax-ups and crowns (p<0.05)

audits.t: Key process and outcome indicators on quality and safety of care for critically ill pediatric patients according to international standard organization protocols: a four-year follow-up study
audits.tp: Quality and safety process/outcome indicators in PICU
audits.st: European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) quality/safety indicators, per ISO protocols
audits.f: 2017: Standardized Handover Procedure handwritten; mortality rate 24%; Standardized Mortality Ratio 1.42; no early readmissions; CRBSI rate 1.37:1000 catheter days
audits.c: Transition of Standardized Handover Procedure from handwritten to electronic form (2019-2020); implementation of OPDSA (Observe-Plan-Do-Study-Act) cycles
audits.r2: 2020: Handover procedure electronic with 100% compliance; mortality rate 16%; SMR 1.33; no early readmissions; CRBSI rate 1.39:1000 catheter days; unplanned extubation rate 5.72% (3.91:1000 ventilation days)

audits.t: Training Nursing Staff to Improve Diabetes Care for Long-Term Care Facility (LTCF) Residents
audits.tp: Diabetes care standardised orders in long-term care facility
audits.st: American Diabetes Association Guidelines (2017) for individualized HbA1c targets and T2DM management in LTCF residents
audits.f: Needs assessment identified deficiencies in evidence-based T2DM care provision
audits.c: Nurse education in-service training on diabetes standards (HbA1c, finger stick monitoring, eye exams, foot care) and use of standardized orders
audits.r2: APRN knowledge increased 60% to 100%, RNs 63% to 87%, LVNs 63% to 71%; of 22 charts, 13 HbA1c due and 12 ordered (92%); 1 renal panel due was ordered; all 5 urine albumin creatinine ratios ordered; ophthalmology/podiatry referrals not routinely ordered due to resistance

audits.t: 2033-P: Artificial Intelligence–Audited Protocol Adherence Is Strongly Associated with Shorter Length of Stay in Diabetic Ketoacidosis
audits.tp: DKA protocol adherence and length of stay
audits.st: Local DKA management protocol (first seven protocol decision points)
audits.f: Correct initial insulin dosing in 100%; prompt initiation in 89%; patients without prompt initiation had longer mean LOS (9.4 vs 3.7 days); complete adherence associated with mean LOS 1.7 days (n=25) vs 5.5 days with any deviation (n=57); adherence correlated with shorter LOS (r=-0.43)
audits.c: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based auditing tool used to retrospectively evaluate protocol adherence

audits.t: Hypoglycemia Unawareness Is Associated With Reduced Adherence to Therapeutic Decisions in Patients With Type 1 Diabetes: Evidence from a Clinical Audit
audits.tp: Adherence to therapeutic decisions in hypoglycemia unawareness
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: An audit of the DAFNE programme found 48% of those reporting impaired awareness of hypoglycemia (IAH) had reduced adherence to therapeutic decisions

audits.t: A Prospective Prescription Audit of Topical Corticosteroid usage at Skin OPD in a Tertiary Care Centre
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Eczema was the commonest indication (34%); betamethasone valerate was the most prescribed molecule (27%); potent corticosteroids most frequent group (46%); average 3-6 drugs per prescription in 82%; twice daily application advised in 73%; fingertip unit application mentioned in only 3% of prescriptions.

audits.t: Facility Based Audit of Maternal Near Miss, Maternal and Neonatal Mortality in a Tertiary Hospital, South-West Nigeria: One-Year Review
audits.st: MPDSR (Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response) review process
audits.f: Near-miss incidence ratio 70 per 1000 live births; maternal mortality ratio 1399 per 100000 live births; hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and sepsis caused 85.8% of maternal deaths; unbooked patients accounted for 83% of near-miss morbidity and 95% of mortality.

audits.t: Integrating population-wide laboratory testing data with physician audit-and-feedback reports to improve glycemic and cholesterol control among Ontarians with diabetes
audits.st: Glycaemic and lipid control thresholds used for physician audit-and-feedback reporting (HbA1c >9%, LDL >4 mmol/L)
audits.f: 70%, 64% and 59% of diabetes patients were tested for HbA1C, LDL and both, respectively; among 648,238 patients with both tests, 13% had HbA1C >9%, 4% had LDL >4 mmol/L and 0.8% exceeded both thresholds; physician-level median (IQR) exceeding thresholds was 12% (9-16%) for HbA1C and 4% (2-6%) for LDL, with significant between-physician variability.
audits.c: Integration of population-wide laboratory testing data (Ontario Laboratory Information System) with existing physician audit-and-feedback reports.

audits.t: Clinical Audit on Neonatal Care Unit Structure in Five Selected Governmental Hospitals of Addis Ababa, Ethiopia 2019
audits.tp: Neonatal care unit structure and equipment
audits.st: Standards for NICU structure/equipment (national/facility-based)
audits.f: Gandhi Memorial Hospital: NICU works as one case team, ~8,500 deliveries and ~2000 newborns admitted in 2018; St. Paul's Hospital/Millennium Medical College: NICU equipped with wall thermometer, O2 cylinder, arm pit thermometer, but equipment not per unit (one room with partition); room temperature 22-26°C matched the standard

audits.t: Caesarean Section Audit: The Use of the Robson’s Criteria in a Teaching Hospital with Limited Advanced Fetal Surveillance
audits.st: Robson's Ten-Group Classification System for caesarean section
audits.f: Caesarean section rate of 35.5%; Group 1 had highest contribution to CS rate, followed by Group 5; statistically significant relationship between booking status and Robson groups (p<0.001)

audits.t: Risk Factors for Neonatal Deaths: An Audit of Neonatal Care: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
audits.tp: Neonatal care indicator compliance and mortality risk factors
audits.st: Neonatal/antenatal care indicator standards (HIV PCR testing, ART prophylaxis, TB vaccination)
audits.f: Neonatal care indicators mostly good (>90%) except HIV status confirmation for exposed neonates (88.7%) and TB vaccination (69%); of 692 HIV-exposed live births, 92.4% had PCR tests, 95.9% had results available, 88.8% overall known PCR status; 91.7% of eligible neonates received ART prophylaxis; neonatal death rate 1.3% (7.5 per 1000 live births)

audits.t: REGIONAL FEATURES OF NEWBORN HEALTH (according to state and industry statistics, perinatal audit "MATRIX - BABIES")
audits.st: WHO 'MATRIX-BABIES' perinatal audit methodology
audits.f: Low birth weight rose 5.39% to 5.99% (OR 1.12, 95% CI 1.09-1.15, p<0.0001); prematurity rose 4.64% to 5.68% (OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.21-1.27, p<0.0001); sick newborn rate fell from 280.8 per mille to 196.9 per mille (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.65-0.67, p<0.0001)

audits.t: Audit on Completeness of Operative Notes Documentation at a Teaching Hospital in Lahore Pakistan
audits.st: Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority, Punjab Healthcare Commission and Royal College of Surgeons guidelines (standardised checklist)
audits.f: Date (94.1%) and time (92.6%) of procedure well documented but patient identification documented in only 13.8%; surgeon/assistant names (100%), operative finding (99.0%), doctor signature (97.0%), procedure name (96.6%), diagnosis (91.6%) and tissue details (90.1%) well documented; gaps in elective/emergency type (26.6% missing), prosthesis use (21.9%), extra procedure reason (17.7%), anticipated blood loss (15.8%), complications (9.4%) and DVT prophylaxis (3.4%).

audits.t: Audit of paediatric cardiac services in South Africa

audits.t: Multidisciplinary Relationship between Periodontology and Orthodontic Department: A Clinical Audit Study

audits.t: An Audit of Paediatric Dental Patient Assessment and Recall in Faculty of Dentistry UiTM Sungai Buloh

audits.f: Caries risk assessment not recorded in 58% of cases; baseline radiographs taken in 44.6%; among 145 cases with recorded caries risk assessment, 3-month recall attendance was 70%, 6-month 6.2%, and 1-year 6.7%.

audits.t: The Implementation of the Minimal Intervention Dentistry in the Undergraduate Dental Clinical Teaching: A Retrospective Audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Amalgam restorations decreased and composite restorations increased across cohorts (highest amalgam 9.6% in 2009/2014, highest composite 97.7% in 2011/2016); resin-bonded bridges (67.6%) were preferred over conventional bridges (32.4%); crowns (91.4%) dominated over onlays (8.6%).

audits.t: AUDIT SYSTEM FOR USAGE OF BLOOD PRODUCT IN SANGLAH GENERAL HOSPITAL DENPASAR BALI

audits.c: Development and dissemination of guidelines for blood product usage, followed by concurrent and prospective audit of blood requests

audits.t: Infection Prevention and Control Audit of a Tertiary-Level Care Hospital Hemodialysis Unit in the United Arab Emirates at Times of COVID-19 Pandemic - A Case Study
audits.tp: Haemodialysis unit infection prevention and control audit
audits.st: CDC haemodialysis unit infection prevention and control assessment tool (11 items)
audits.f: Majority of CDC IPC checklist items were applicable and largely followed at the study site; short-term improvements (additional staff training and competency assessment, educational posters displayed via unit television) were already acted upon at the time of the audit.
audits.c: Additional staff training/competency assessment, educational posters and videos, and more infection control certifications for nurses, recommended as further improvements.

audits.t: Assessment of molybdenum-99m content in 99Mo/Tc-99m Generator: A clinical audit at Cancer Hospital
audits.st: Internationally recommended molybdenum breakthrough limit of 0.15 μCi 99Mo per mCi 99mTc
audits.f: Mean molybdenum breakthrough 0.018±0.023 μCi 99Mo/mCi 99mTc (standard mean error 0.006%), below the internationally recommended limit

audits.t: An Audit of Patient Characteristics, Contributing Factors, and Outcomes of Patients Leaving against Medical Advice at Sheikh Khalifa Medical City Abu Dhabi
audits.st: SEHA clinical policy guideline on LAMA (Policy no. C-MD-GEN-01-024)

audits.t: Induction Chemotherapy: Hope or Hype in Head & Neck Cancer - An Audit from Institute of National Importance in Western Rajasthan & Review of Literature

audits.t: RESULTS OF THE FIRST STAGE OF CLINICAL AUDIT IN THE UROLOGY DEPARTMENTS OF HEALTH CARE FACILITIES IN LVIV
audits.tp: Patient satisfaction with urology inpatient care
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Audit of Bloemfontein Primary Healthcare Clinics' Emergency Preparedness
audits.tp: Primary care clinic emergency preparedness audit
audits.st: Provincial equipment list for primary healthcare clinic emergency preparedness
audits.f: Mean compliance was 45% for consumables (range 32-67%), 53% for equipment (range 46-63%) and 58% for medication (range 36-77%); no clinic achieved above 90% in any category; 6 clinics (38%) scored below 40% for consumables, 1 (6%) for equipment and 2 (13%) for medication.

audits.t: A Study of the Prescription Audit Conducted in a Tertiary Care Hospital
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators; hospital OPD/IPD prescription documentation parameters (capital letters, generic names, dose, route, frequency, duration, registration number, signature, etc.)

audits.t: Prescription Audit in a Paediatric Outpatient Department: A Crosssectional Study in Sub-district hospital
audits.st: WHO-recommended core prescribing indicators
audits.f: Average 2.44 drugs per prescription; generic name usage 78.41%; NLEM adherence 75.68%; antibiotics prescribed 23.33%; injections 3.33%; dosage documented 39.33%, frequency 12%, duration 56%, patient instructions 84%; prescriber identification absent in all cases

audits.t: Audit of clinical use of blood products in a tertiary care hospital
audits.tp: Audit of clinical blood product use
audits.st: Hospital transfusion appropriateness guideline (CTR, transfusion probability and transfusion index)
audits.f: 65.9% of blood transfusions were appropriate per guideline and 34% were inappropriate; CTR, transfusion probability and transfusion index all exceeded guideline values, indicating effective blood utilisation; mean haemoglobin improved significantly post-transfusion; 5% of transfusions had a reaction (fever/anaphylaxis).

audits.t: Effect of internal audit-guided intervention on quality indicators in the processing and reporting of complete hemogram
audits.tp: Internal audit of haemogram processing quality indicators
audits.st: ISO 15189 international standard for clinical laboratories
audits.f: Baseline turnaround time (TAT) was 130 minutes in Phase I.
audits.c: Audit-guided interventions and amendments to hemogram processing and reporting over 2 months following Phase I analysis of five quality parameters.
audits.r2: Sample rejection rate reduced by 54%; internal quality control results and z-scores for accuracy/precision improved; critical value entries increased nearly 3-fold; TAT increased slightly to 173 minutes.

audits.t: Median Door to Needle Antibiotic in Potential Febrile Neutropenic Patients in an Emergency Department of a University Metropolitan Tertiary Hospital in Barcelona (Spain): Results of an Initial Audit
audits.tp: Time to first antibiotic dose in febrile neutropenia

audits.f: Time to first antibiotic dose within 1 hour achieved in 9.6% (16) of cases; 69.3% (115) received first dose more than 2 hours after presentation, non-compliant with the febrile neutropenia protocol

audits.t: Clinical audit of prescribing practices in a tertiary care hospital: a cross - sectional analysis
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators
audits.f: Mean number of drugs per prescription was 3.8±1.2 (exceeding WHO recommendations); generic prescribing in 42%; antibiotics prescribed in 58% of encounters; injections in 22%; significant differences across departments (F=8.56, p<0.001).

audits.t: Prospective Observational Study of Antimicrobials Utilization Prescriptions Audit in Pediatric Patients at District General Hospital in Maharashtra
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators
audits.f: 72.30% received combination antimicrobial therapy (43.06% two-drug, 25.83% three-drug regimens); mean 2.08 drugs per patient; of 435 antimicrobials, 71.24% were injectable and 28.27% oral; amoxicillin-clavulanic acid was most prescribed (24.59%); irrational prescriptions by use, dose and frequency were 27.27%, 5.74% and 2.87% respectively.

audits.t: Explainable AI Framework for Evaluating Sepsis Management in Critical Care: A MIMIC-IV Implementation Study
audits.st: Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) 1-hour bundle
audits.f: Step-level compliance: lactate 35.3%, culture-before-antibiotic 20.8%, antibiotics 74.3%, fluids when indicated 31.8%, vasopressors when indicated 57.3%; overall all-steps compliance 2.0%, falling slightly under a strict lactate rule

audits.t: Completion of Electronic Medical Records in General Clinics at Yousif Engineer Health Centre in Bahrain–A Clinical Audit
audits.st: Completeness of SOAP note documentation in the I-SEHA electronic medical record system
audits.f: SOAP note fully complete in 1% (1), partially complete in 96% (142), incomplete in 3% (4); Subjective section complete 11%; Objective section complete 6% (69% incomplete); Assessment complete 96%; Plan complete 86%

audits.t: Screening And Management of Renal Impairment In Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus In Primary Health Care Of Royal Medical Services: A Clinical Audit
audits.st: Guideline-driven screening and management of renal impairment in type 2 diabetes (albuminuria, eGFR)

audits.t: Auditing of the phlebotomy system in medical laboratories in Port Sudan City, Sudan
audits.st: Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) venepuncture guidelines and local standard operating procedures

audits.t: Clinical Audit on Detection of Tuberculosis at Primary Health Care Corporation, Qatar
audits.st: not reported

audits.t: Appropriateness of Antimicrobial Therapy for Treatment of Acute Tonsillitis at Primary Care level in Qatar- Clinical Audit Report
audits.st: not reported

audits.c: An action plan was developed to improve compliance with appropriate antibiotic use in acute tonsillitis

audits.t: A Clinical Audit for Compliance on the Innovated Radiographic Technique at a Radiologic Unit
audits.st: Standard operating procedures for the innovated radiographic technique
audits.f: 20 of 30 participants (67%) complied with the innovated radiographic technique and 10 (33%) did not; the technique was effective in decreasing repeat X-ray exposure among users.

audits.t: A Clinical Audit on the Compliance of Ultrasound Users to the Standard Operating Procedure of Ultrasonography in a Private Radiologic Academy
audits.st: Standard operating procedures for ultrasonography
audits.f: Of 11 male participants, 7 were compliant and 3 non-compliant; of 12 female participants, 8 were compliant and 4 non-compliant; compliance was related to participants' skills and how the SOP was communicated.

audits.t: Audit of Neonatal Outcome in Tertiary Care Hospital.
audits.st: Aberdeen Obstetric classification of perinatal deaths
audits.f: Perinatal mortality rate was 27.14 per 1000 births and stillbirth rate 13.25 per 1000 births among 1627 deliveries with 43 perinatal deaths; antepartum haemorrhage, pregnancy-induced hypertension and anaemia were the commonest causes.

audits.t: AUDIT ON MEDICAL THORACOSCOPY IN PATIENTS WITH EXUDATIVE PLEURAL EFFUSION IN TERTIARY CARE HOSPITAL IN CENTRAL SRI LANKA
audits.st: British Thoracic Society guideline on thoracoscopy procedure
audits.f: Informed written consent obtained in over 94% of patients; pre-procedure chest CT performed in 50%; real-time ultrasound guidance used in 60%; no significant thoracoscopy-related complications; 95% received a definitive diagnosis (5% uncertain).
audits.c: Standard documentation templates introduced, real-time ultrasound integrated into the procedure, a protocol for safe sample transportation established, and small-gauge chest drains introduced to reduce discomfort.

audits.t: Geriatric Recovery and Enhancement Alliance in Trauma (GREAT) multidisciplinary quality improvement initiative: improving rates of successful resuscitation, rehabilitation and reintegration of geriatric trauma patients across the trauma spectrum of care
audits.st: Comparison with Alberta Trauma Registry and Trauma Quality Improvement Program (American College of Surgeons) control data
audits.f: Enrolment lowered the threshold for trauma team consults, increasing recognition of geriatric trauma; decreased average ISS scores and higher trauma consult rates were seen, but exact compliance figures were not given
audits.c: Creation of a geriatric trauma navigator role, standardized order sets, and screening tools (ISAR, CAM, Mini-Cog, PHQ-2, GDS-15, AUDIT-C, CNST, Clinical Frailty Scale) with monthly data review and quarterly PDSA changes

audits.t: Edmonton Zone triage project (EZ Triage)
audits.st: Canadian Triage Acuity Scale (CTAS)
audits.f: Automated screening had 100% sensitivity/specificity/accuracy for high- and low-acuity vital sign errors (κ=1, p<0.001), outperforming expert review; computer screening for pain errors: sensitivity 71.3%, specificity 96.7%, accuracy 96.27%; for SIRS-related errors expert screening (sensitivity 100%) outperformed computer screening (sensitivity 7.9%)
audits.c: Prior Edmonton Zone QI audits reduced high- and low-risk vital sign errors by 86% and 78% respectively; a Tableau dashboard using EPIC data and Python-based rule translation was then built to scale up the audit-and-feedback framework

audits.t: Audit of the Effect of Non-Nasal Specific Scoring On the Postoperative Snot22 Questionnaire

audits.t: An Audit on the implementation of administering Ondansetron in children with acute gastroenteritis and its effect on admission rate

audits.t: Lower Limb Amputee patients have comorbidities and risk of complications - Findings from a hospital audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Dysvascularity was the commonest cause of amputation (57.1%); one in six amputees were not haemodynamically stable and one-quarter had hypoglycaemia when stepped down; complications occurred in 71.4% (mainly decubitus ulcers, chest infections, delirium); median length of stay 44.5 days.

audits.t: World Health Organization (WHO) modified partogram fill audit at Matam Communal Medical Center
audits.st: WHO modified partograph performance standard
audits.f: Overall partograph use met the standard in more than 87.41% of cases; hourly rhythm and timing of acts notified/respected in 66.60%; progress of labour correctly notified in 28.72%; presentation level and fetal heart rate reported/respected in 28.78% and 85.96% respectively; method of labour onset notified/complied with in 95.7%

audits.t: Audit of compliance with Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis guidelines across medical and non-medical wards in a tertiary care hospital
audits.st: Hospital VTE prophylaxis policy aligned with NICE guidelines
audits.f: Compliance with VTE prophylaxis guidelines was 95% in medical wards versus 75% in non-medical wards

audits.t: Audit of oxygen therapy target saturation documentation and adherence to guidelines in hospitalized patients in a medical ward
audits.st: International guidelines for oxygen therapy target saturation ranges (88-92% for COPD, 94-98% for non-COPD)
audits.f: Target oxygen saturation was documented in 100% of patients; among COPD patients (n=20), 60% received oxygen within the 88-92% target range (40% over-oxygenated); among non-COPD patients (n=30), 85% received oxygen within the 94-98% target range (15% under-oxygenated).

audits.t: Audit of anaesthetic chart documentation in private hospitals in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, Nigeria
audits.st: Institutional requirement for complete anaesthetic chart documentation (no named external guideline)
audits.f: 300 (67.9%) of 442 surgeries had anaesthetic charts completed and 142 (32.1%) had none; of the 300 charts, 105 (35.0%) were correctly filled, 118 (39.3%) incompletely filled and 77 (25.7%) illegible; no significant association was found between chart availability and documentation quality (χ²=5.07, p=0.167).

audits.t: Audit of caesarean deliveries in ESUT Teaching Hospital (ESUTH) Enugu: A 3-year review
audits.st: WHO recommended caesarean section rate of 10-15%
audits.f: Caesarean section rate was 29.6% (against WHO's recommended 10-15%); 73.7% were booked patients, 26.3% unbooked; 59.2% emergency and 40.8% elective; major indications were previous caesarean (20.2%), hypertensive disease in pregnancy (14.6%) and poor progress of labour (11.4%); maternal complications included PPH (8.4%) and maternal death (0.5%); neonatal death rate 8.5%.

audits.t: An audit of caesarean section in a semi urban hospital in northern cross river state Nigeria utilizing the robson-10 criteria
audits.st: WHO Robson Ten Group Classification System for caesarean section
audits.f: 430 of 1402 women (30.7%) had a caesarean section; Robson group 3 contributed most to the overall rate (25.81%), followed by groups 1 (18.84%) and 4 (13.95%).

audits.t: Clinical audit on blood pressure measurement practices using the simple app in primary care institutions under the regional director of health services, Colombo, Sri Lanka
audits.st: National hypertension guidance and accepted blood pressure measurement principles
audits.f: Overall adherence 65.19% (1,809 components); cuff size, forearm support, mid-arm positioning and documentation each 99.5%; validated digital device used in 90.3%; smoking/exercise/coffee inquiry 0.5%; empty bladder inquiry 0.0%; two measurements from both arms 0.0%; back support 24.9%; 3-5 minute rest 51.9%; facility adherence ranged 53.07%-76.86%

audits.t: An audit on the management of patients with chronic hypoparathyroidism in a district general hospital in the UK
audits.st: UK national survey/guidelines for management of chronic hypoparathyroidism (2020)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: An audit on the management of hypophosphataemia on the wards in a district general hospital in the UK
audits.st: Prevailing UK guidelines for management of hypophosphataemia (not individually named)
audits.f: Parathyroid hormone, cortisol and 24-hour urinary phosphate testing were performed in only a small number of patients, but management of hypophosphataemia on the wards was found to be adequate in most cases in accordance with prevailing guidelines.

audits.t: What do the numbers say? - Introduction of the WHO ICD-PM classification and fetuses-at risk approach in perinatal audit, South India
audits.st: WHO ICD-PM classification and Three Delays model for perinatal death audit
audits.f: Perinatal mortality rate was 6.1 per 1000 births among booked cases and 21.32 per 1000 births among referred cases; fetal growth restriction caused 33.3% of antepartum deaths and prematurity caused 52% of neonatal deaths; hypertension was the single most common risk factor; peak gestational-age-specific mortality occurred at 30, 37 and 38 weeks for early-onset pre-eclampsia, severe fetal growth restriction and gestational diabetes respectively.

audits.t: CAN REFERRAL TO COMMUNITY-BASED EXERCISE PHYSIOLOGIST SERVICES REDUCE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT BURDEN? A CHART AUDIT

audits.f: 84% of patients presented with musculoskeletal conditions persisting a mean of 9.3 days; leg (34%), lower back (22%) and arm (16%) conditions were most common; physical activity advice was given to 17%; no patients were referred to exercise physiology services.

audits.t: A Descriptive View on Prescription audit of prescribing patterns in primary, secondary, tertiary healthcare facilities in India

audits.t: Maternal death audit- institutional based maternal death review in four major hospitals of Municipal Corporation of Delhi

audits.t: Effectiveness of Audit and Feedback in Improving the Quality of Operative Notes - A Retrospective Observational Study

audits.st: not reported

audits.t: ROLE OF CLINICAL PHARMACIST IN CLINICAL AUDIT AT DEPARTMENT OF GENERAL MEDICINE
audits.tp: Clinical pharmacist role in prescription audit

audits.c: A six-stage clinical audit cycle using a three-part checklist for t-PA drug injection, comparing intervention and control groups

audits.t: The IAEA/WHO TLD Audit Program. The results of the TLD postal dosimetry audits in the National Centre for Radiotherapy and Nuclear Medicine Department, Korle-Bu, Accra (1998 to 2012)
