audits.st: Target SpO2 91-95% in preterm neonates (per recent studies)
audits.f: SpO2 trend and ventilator settings recorded twice daily; results/compliance figures not given in supplied abstract text (truncated)

audits.t: An audit on the technique of collection of blood for culture at the National Hospital of Sri Lanka
audits.st: Standard technique for collection of blood for culture (written institutional instructions)
audits.f: 44/50 drawn after antibiotics started; 45/50 did not wash hands before collection; 37/50 wore sterile gloves; only 21/50 drew adequate blood volume; only 2/50 drew a second blood culture; 40/50 recapped syringes before disposal

audits.t: Clinical Audit on Record Keeping Standards at a Specialized Out-patient Child Psychiatry Service in Sri Lanka
audits.tp: Record keeping standards audit in child psychiatry
audits.st: Professional record-keeping standards (medico-legal)
audits.f: Confidentiality of record organisation and execution of management plan satisfactory; serious concerns identified in documentation of evaluation

audits.t: Compliance with World Health Organization Surgical Safety Checklist: A Clinical Audit
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist
audits.f: Checklists completed for 21 (22.1%) patients; sign-in 51.6%, sign-out 35.8%, time-out 22.1% compliance
audits.c: Staff awareness/educational programme on the WHO surgical safety checklist
audits.r2: Checklists completed in 79 (83.2%); sign-in 88.4%, sign-out 84.2%, time-out 87.4%; statistically significant improvement overall (p<0.001)

audits.t: A Clinical Audit on Management of Transfusion Reactions
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 65 (45.14%) of transfusion reaction cases were managed appropriately; commonest symptom urticaria followed by fever

audits.t: An Audit on Developmental Screening in Child Health Record from a Tertiary Care Centre in Western Province of Sri Lanka: Lost Opportunities for Early Intervention
audits.st: National guideline for Child Health Development Record documentation (General Circular 01-12-2020)
audits.f: Overall developmental milestone documentation completeness 67.6% by mothers, 51.8% by PHC workers; completeness declined from 82.0% at 2 months to 30.0% by age 5 years; referral documented for only 2 of 4 children with developmental problems (50%)

audits.t: Exploring Clinical Documentation Practices among Healthcare Staff: A Clinical Audit of National Hospital Galle, Sri Lanka
audits.st: Ministry of Health 2022 rules for bedhead ticket (BHT) documentation
audits.f: First page completeness good in 96%; continuation sheets good in only 2% (average in 82%); entries good completeness in 67%; signature at end of entry in only 1%; date recorded 73.5%, time recorded 64.3%

audits.t: A clinical audit on uptake of delayed cord clamping at caesarean sections
audits.tp: Delayed cord clamping uptake at caesarean section
audits.st: Guideline recommendations on delayed cord clamping (DCC)
audits.f: Only 34% of doctors practised DCC, 52% practised early cord clamping, 14% cord milking; 74% were aware of guideline recommendations; among non-adherent doctors, 69.44% were aware of the recommendation but still did not practise it, mainly due to belief in increased blood loss/surgical time

audits.t: Management of neonatal seizures developed after the first 24 hours of life: a clinical audit from a tertiary children’s hospital, Sri Lanka
audits.tp: Neonatal seizure management after first 24 hours of life
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Aetiology identified in only one third (n=9); EEG confirmation not performed; advanced neuroimaging not offered to most; recommended first-line medication given to 93%, but dose/route irregularities in 22%

audits.t: A clinical audit on febrile seizure management at the primary care unit of Lady Ridgeway Hospital for Children, Colombo
audits.st: Standard febrile seizure (FS) management guidelines
audits.f: Over-investigation in 65% of simple febrile seizures; 9.5% of eligible patients under-admitted; parental counselling inconsistent (verbal 32%, written 16%); epilepsy risk never discussed; inappropriate prescription of intermittent prophylaxis minimal

audits.t: An audit on the prescription and administration of ECT at NIMH, Sri Lanka
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists (UK) and Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists guidelines for ECT
audits.f: Only 50% of patients had a motor seizure >20 seconds; average energy dose increment 5% in subsequent ECTs; post-ECT assessment substandard in up to 78%; poor documentation of indication and inadequate monitoring of motor seizures

audits.t: Data quality of request forms for lumbar spine X-rays: A clinical audit form a tertiary care hospital in Sri Lanka
audits.tp: Lumbar spine X-ray request form data quality
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 13 (7.0%) failed to provide clinical history; 32 (17.3%) did not provide region of examination details; of those with history, 97.1% relevant, 2.9% had non-standard abbreviations

audits.t: Clinical audit on knowledge, practice and common mistakes in drug usage among psoriasis patients attending Dermatology Clinic at National Hospital Kandy
audits.tp: Psoriasis patient knowledge and drug usage errors
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Study identified a few common mistakes in drug usage among psoriasis patients
audits.c: Patient information leaflet and monitoring charts prepared to improve adherence and compliance

audits.t: An Audit on Near-Miss Events in Transfusion Medicine: The Experience of the Teaching Hospital in Northeastern Malaysia
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 178 near-miss events (0.40%) reported and analysed; mislabelled samples 66.3%, miscollected (WBIT) samples 33.7%; highest number of mislabelled samples from accident and emergency, miscollected from medical ward

audits.t: 2011 appropriate use criteria audit of an echocardiography lab in South Western Nigeria
audits.st: 2011 Appropriate Use Criteria (AUC) for transthoracic echocardiography
audits.f: Appropriate indications 41.4%, inappropriate 31.1%, uncertain 0.1%; 9.3% could not be classified; 18.1% had no indication

audits.t: La terapia a pressione negativa presso i reparti acuti dell’Ospedale Regionale di Mendrisio: risultati di un audit clinico/Negative pressure wound therapy in the acute care units of the Mendrisio Regional Hospital: results of a clinical audit
audits.tp: Negative pressure wound therapy use appropriateness
audits.st: Current scientific evidence on negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) indications
audits.f: Quantitative analysis of NPWT use compared with current scientific evidence to identify alignments and discrepancies in daily practice

audits.t: Multi-professional audit supports clinical governance in projecting and implementing a new stroke care area
audits.tp: Stroke unit setup clinical governance audit
audits.st: National and international stroke guidelines and Italian Regional Audit markers (Benjamin audit cycle)
audits.f: Baseline monitoring of diagnostic, clinical and therapeutic process markers during Stroke Unit set-up
audits.c: Structured multi-professional audit cycle guiding the design and implementation of the new Stroke Unit
audits.r2: High level of care achieved with significant improvement in most clinical, diagnostic and therapeutic parameters; only waiting times for ultrasound and prescription of oral anticoagulation required specific further improvement projects

audits.t: The discharge of patients with diabetes from Internal Medicine Units: a clinical audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean performance: home glycemic control instructions 41.6% (range 5.0-89.9); hypoglycemic treatment instructions 32.4% (range 0.0-92.1); insulin administration instructions 60.4% (range 56.5-100.0); nutritional advice 24.8% (range 25.4-76.6); ambulatory control referral 60.7% (range 65.6-100.0); HbA1c reported in discharge 40.6% (range 1.75-98.0); all levels below 70% acceptable threshold

audits.t: P104 | The appropriate recording of nursing procedures in an Italian Emergency Department: results of a nursing audit
audits.tp: Nursing procedure documentation audit in Emergency Department
audits.st: Panel of recommended nursing documentation items from international literature and Italian ED benchmarking
audits.f: Care activity procedures reported in nursing records in only 10% of cases; when conducted, registration incomplete in 93% of cases

audits.t: Asthma Care: An audit of asthma care in Khayelttsha Community Health Centre
audits.st: SA Pulmonology Society 1995 clinical guidelines for optimal assessment and management of asthma
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Obstacles faced in conducting a clinical audit in Botswana
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Medical records difficult to find, poor documentation when available, lack of local ICU admission criteria/guidelines causing inappropriate referrals, staff fear of being audited

audits.t: Quality of handover in the post-anaesthetic care unit at a quaternary children’s hospital in Cape Town, South Africa: A clinical audit
audits.st: Paediatric Anaesthesia Handover Checklist (26 mandatory verbal handover items)
audits.f: Handovers frequently incomplete; scores ranged 0/26 to 17/26 (65.38%); average score 5.54/26 (21.31%); intraoperative analgesia handed over in 76.36% of cases; sedative premedication reported in only 47.27%

audits.t: South African pilot study: End-to-end radiotherapy and medical physics dosimetry audits
audits.st: IAEA reference and end-to-end dosimetry audit methodology using a CIRS IMRT thorax phantom
audits.f: Photon beam reference dosimetry variations 0.5%-2.48%; electron beam variations up to 8.0%; end-to-end audit variations up to 7.1% between calculated and measured doses

audits.t: Community psychiatry: An audit of the services in southern Gauteng
audits.st: South Africa's mental health legislation and policies (objectives for community psychiatric care)
audits.f: Mean 2 new patients seen per doctor per clinic day (30 min each); mean 17 follow-up patients per doctor per day (8 min each); mean waiting time for new appointments 6 months; follow-up seen monthly by nurses, roughly 4-monthly by doctors; 1 in 5 patients on oral atypical antipsychotics; only 0.2% of users access psychologists/social workers/OTs where present

audits.t: An audit of non-urgent general adult referrals to Stikland State Psychiatric Facility
audits.st: National Department of Health recommendations for appropriate level of care referrals
audits.f: 58.3% of referrals from the private sector; 36.7% of referral letters gave no clear reason for referral; 41.7% gave no psychiatric diagnosis; 29.1% of patients referred without psychotropic medication started; 62.1% found to have a single Axis I diagnosis on assessment

audits.t: A dose audit of fluoroscopy examinations at Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital: Analysis of preliminary results
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Wide spread in radiation doses (skin dose and dose-area product) for a given examination type; weak correlation between skin dose and screening time (r=0.59); poor correlation between DAP and screening time (r=0.42)

audits.t: Multi-detector computed tomography radiation doses in the follow-up of paediatric neurosurgery patients in KwaZulu-Natal: A dosimetric audit
audits.tp: Paediatric neurosurgery follow-up CT radiation dose
audits.st: ALARA principle; comparison with reference/literature radiation dose values
audits.f: Highest median dose for intracranial abscess follow-up (1183 mGy cm) in 8-12 year age group; lowest for shunt follow-up (447 mGy cm); median DLP/ED/mAs comparable to literature but with broader distribution and higher upper limits

audits.t: Audit of medical records keeping at a Nigerian geriatric clinic
audits.st: Royal College of Physicians Health Informatics Unit generic standards for medical record keeping
audits.f: Only the third standard reached 50%; all other standards were at 0%
audits.r2: 100% increase (improvement) in standards 1, 3, 4 and 5, with a 10% increase in standard 2

audits.t: Audit of colonoscopy practice in Lagos University Teaching Hospital
audits.st: Standard colonoscopy key performance indicators (cecal intubation rate, withdrawal time, polyp detection rate)
audits.f: Cecal intubation rate 80.2%; polyp detection rate 7.4%; average withdrawal time 6 min 53 s; overall diagnostic yield 55.9%; bowel preparation excellent in 54.4%, adequate 28.2%, inadequate 17.4%; no adverse events

audits.t: Clinical audit of fresh frozen plasma usage in a Tertiary Care Hospital of Islamabad, Pakistan
audits.st: American College of Pathologists guidelines for use of fresh frozen plasma
audits.f: 460 FFP units requested, 278 issued; 73 units (52%) appropriately transfused, 67 units (48%) inappropriately transfused; most inappropriate use in Mother and Child Health Centre, Oncology, Emergency/Casualty; most appropriate use in thalassaemia centre, paediatric units, and medical ICU

audits.t: Quality audit of haematology laboratory: Challenges and opportunities
audits.st: NABL-specific quality indicators (13 common quality indicators) for haematology laboratories
audits.f: Most common error was clotted sample (0.04%), followed by sample misidentification (0.008%); monthly critical alerts showed a significant upward trend (P=0.045); redo rates showed no significant change over time

audits.t: Audit of quality indicators of cytology: An institutional study
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Cyto-histo correlation, non-conformities, turnaround time, repeats/redos, critical value, staining quality and revised report rate were evaluated; specific figures not stated in the abstract

audits.t: Prescription Audit of Out-Patients in Medicine Department of a Tertiary Care Government Hospital of Central India
audits.st: WHO core drug prescribing indicators
audits.f: Height and weight missing in all prescriptions; average 3.53 drugs per prescription; 92.97% prescribed by generic name; antimicrobial prevalence 8.26%; injectable drugs used in 1.74%

audits.t: The effect of cardiopulmonary resuscitation clinical audit on the patient survival in the emergency room
audits.st: Adib checklist for resuscitation steps, based on the Situation Stabilization Model
audits.f: Primary resuscitation success rate 6/35 (17.1%)
audits.c: 1-month educational programme for resuscitation staff based on identified weaknesses
audits.r2: Primary resuscitation success rate improved to 8/35 (22.9%), not statistically significant (P=0.47); mean scores on resuscitation skill steps improved significantly (P<0.001)

audits.t: Clinical audit on management of β-thalassemia major in Minia General Hospital
audits.st: UK Standards for the Clinical Care of Children with Thalassaemia
audits.f: Abdominal ultrasound performed in 93%, liver function 74%, serum ferritin 65%, hepatitis marker 57%, echocardiography 47%, growth assessment 43%; puberty assessment not performed; iron chelation used in 53% (deferasirox 38%, hydroxyurea 41%)

audits.t: Clinical audit of anticoagulant therapy with pregnancy
audits.st: RCOG (Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists) standards for anticoagulant therapy in pregnancy
audits.f: 174 cases (58%) agreed with RCOG guidelines; 126 cases (42%) did not agree with RCOG guidelines

audits.t: An audit of infection control practices in Central Sterile Supply Department in a Tertiary Care Hospital, Puducherry
audits.tp: Central Sterile Supply Department infection control practices
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Pretest results ranged from 20% to 100% among participants across various questions
audits.c: Training and teaching of staff on infection control practices
audits.r2: Posttest conducted after training showed 100% results among all participants

audits.t: Intraoperative cuff pressure measurements of endotracheal tubes in the operating theater: A prospective audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Auditory method used to estimate cuff pressure in 66.0% of patients, tactile in 18.3%; mean cuff pressure after induction 31.0 cmH2O (SD 16.4); higher BMI and smaller endotracheal tubes associated with higher cuff pressures

audits.t: Clinical audit of methotrexate therapy in psoriasis at a tertiary care teaching hospital in Western India
audits.st: Standard guidelines for monitoring methotrexate therapy in psoriasis (specific guideline body not named)
audits.f: Proper history/clinical assessment recorded in 83.3%; PASI>10 in 80%; baseline investigations (CBC, LFT, RFT) done in 100%; initial recommended low dose (2.5-5 mg/week) given in 20%; folic acid supplementation in 93.3%; 2-weekly CBC/LFT monitoring in 96.6%, RFT monitoring in only 53.3%; MTX tapered after 75% PASI reduction in 70%

audits.t: Clinical audit of radiofrequency electrocautery procedure at dermatology department of a tertiary care teaching center
audits.st: Standard guidelines for pre- and post-operative preparation for radiofrequency electrocautery (specific body not named)
audits.f: Counselling/explanation given in 100%; clean surroundings in 100%; injectable local anaesthetic used in 80%; electrode wiped between uses in 80%; aspirin use missed in history for 1 patient (3.33%) and keloidal tendency missed in 1 patient

audits.t: A prescription audit using the who core drug use indicators in a rural health training center of Pondicherry
audits.st: WHO core drug use prescribing indicators
audits.f: Generic drug names used in 89.67% of prescriptions; investigations ordered in 63.87%; follow-up advised in 54.19%; handwriting in capitals in 56.77%; doctor's registration number entered in 46.77%; history 98%, examination 99%, signature with name 96.12%

audits.t: Audit of blood bank services with emphasis on loss of workforce
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 226 units (5.76%) of blood and components prepared were discarded due to wastage, expiry or transfusion-transmitted infection

audits.t: Clinical audit on management of aplastic anemia at hematology unit of Assiut University Children Hospital
audits.st: British Committee for Standards in Hematology guideline (2015) for aplastic anaemia
audits.f: Management was compatible with BCSH 2015 guideline except for use of high-dose cyclosporine alone (no antithymocyte globulin availability) and no availability of stem cell transplantation

audits.t: Evaluation of appropriateness of red blood cell transfusions: A prospective audit at a tertiary care oncology centre
audits.st: Institutional guidelines for RBC transfusion
audits.f: 4413 RBC transfusion events analysed; 83% of transfusion events found appropriate; anaemia was the most common indication; appropriateness significantly higher in medical oncology than surgical oncology (P<0.05); highest and most significant appropriateness in operation theatres, most inappropriateness in daycare facility (P<0.05)

audits.t: Transfusion audit and targeted education as tools to improve clinical practice of fresh frozen plasma transfusions: An interventional study
audits.st: Evidence-based FFP transfusion practice (specific external guideline not named)
audits.f: 75.6% of FFP indications were definitely indicated (pre-intervention), out of 3281 units transfused
audits.c: Continuous education, one-to-one interactions, and hospital transfusion committee-mediated regulations
audits.r2: 81.8% of FFP requests were definitely indicated (post-intervention), out of 2480 units transfused; increase in definite indications was statistically significant

audits.t: Prospective audit of blood transfusion practices among nurses and role of education and intervention at a tertiary care hospital
audits.st: Hospital blood transfusion guidelines (specific body not named)
audits.f: Only 145 nurses scored 11-15 for knowledge/practice; transfusion order not written for 1 patient; consent noncompliance in 5 cases; blood request error 8%, sample labelling error 4%; sample labelling inappropriate in 2 patients; vitals/IV cannula check compliance 96%; crosscheck missing in 8% (nursing officers) and 30% (medical officers); transfusion initiation delayed for 7 patients
audits.c: Training of 243 nursing staff over 45 days (18 didactic lectures and 36 bedside classes)
audits.r2: All 243 (100%) nurses scored 11-15 for knowledge/practice; 100% compliance with transfusion orders; consent noncompliance reduced to 1 case; blood request and sample labelling errors reduced to 0%; vitals/IV cannula check compliance improved to 98%; crosscheck missing reduced to 0% (nursing) and 2% (medical officers); delay reduced to 2 patients

audits.t: Audit of clinical use of red blood cells in a tertiary care setting: An algorithmic approach!
audits.st: Algorithmic approach based on haemoglobin threshold (8 g%), symptoms, comorbidities and imminent blood loss
audits.f: 924 of 1024 transfusions (90.02%) were appropriate

audits.t: Critical audit of fresh frozen plasma transfusion practices in obstetric and gynecology departments in a tertiary care hospital – Where and what needs to be improved?
audits.st: British Committee for Standards in Haematology and College of American Pathologists FFP transfusion guidelines
audits.f: 901 FFP units issued; appropriate usage in 67%, inappropriate in 33%; bleeding related to surgery with deranged coagulation was the most common appropriate indication; severe anaemia was the most inappropriate indication

audits.t: An audit of clinical cases of dengue fever and the usage of platelets in such cases in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Hyderabad
audits.tp: Platelet transfusion use in dengue fever
audits.st: Platelet transfusion guidelines (specific body not named)
audits.f: 26% of cases developed haemorrhage; 84 single-donor and 340 random-donor platelet units used; 99% of product utilisation was within recommended guidelines; platelet count restored with single-unit transfusion in 72%; mortality rate 0.8%

audits.t: IJCM_203A: Referral Audit of the Public Healthcare system in Bhopal district of Madhya Pradesh
audits.st: WHO Referral Register Standards
audits.f: Out-referral registers were physically present in all facilities; reason for referral was mentioned in most facilities; back referral was not mentioned in most facilities

audits.t: IJCM_38A: Impact of perinatal death audit on healthcare delivery in two districts of Karnataka- A health system intervention research
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline documentation, reporting systems and infrastructure for perinatal death review were assessed as needing improvement, especially in Koppal district
audits.c: Design and implementation of a perinatal death (PND) audit system with an expert committee review
audits.r2: Significant improvement in documentation of care delivered (especially in Koppal); increase in PND reporting in the second half of the study; improved preventability assertion and reduced proportion of unclassified neonatal deaths; significant improvement in facility infrastructure

audits.t: IJCM_45A: Inter-district variation in preterm deaths identified by a perinatal death audit: a health system intervention research
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 119 preterm deaths analysed in DK and 97 in KPL; in-utero transfer was 81.5% in DK versus 11.3% in KPL; 22.6% of KPL babies died at home despite hospital delivery; risk factor documentation was poor in both districts; expert committee review increased preventability assertion from 7.5% to 11.7% in DK and 2% to 62.8% in KPL

audits.t: Optimising Pharmaceutical Dispensing Turnaround Time to the ICU: A Quality Improvement Study
audits.st: 45-minute pharmacy dispensing turnaround time standard; NABH MOM.6 standards
audits.f: Only 51.4% (36/70) met the 45-minute standard; average TAT 1 hour 4 minutes; largest delay at packing-to-dispatch stage (31 minutes)
audits.c: Lean Six Sigma-based strategies, Donabedian model and fishbone analysis used to identify and plan to address non-value-added delays (electronic verification, trolley bifurcation, optimised routing)

audits.t: Use of Messaging App in Reducing Outpatient Visits and Waiting Time for Re-prescription in a Tertiary Hospital Cardiology Clinic in Oman: An Audit
audits.st: Lean/Six Sigma value-stream mapping benchmarks (institutional QI project, no external clinical standard)
audits.f: Before intervention: total lead time ~109 minutes, value-added time ratio 17%
audits.c: Use of a messaging app between patients and pharmacy for monthly medication refill requests
audits.r2: After intervention: total lead time ~9 minutes, value-added ratio 80%; OPD walk-in visits reduced to 0 (100% reduction); app-based requests increased from 18% to 87% of dispensations; total waiting time reduced by 90%

audits.t: An Audit to Compare the Adherence of Housekeeping Practices to Kayakalp Standards in the Intensive Care Unit of a Tertiary Care Hospital
audits.tp: ICU housekeeping/cleaning compliance with Kayakalp standards
audits.st: Kayakalp initiative standards (Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, India, 2015) for cleanliness, hygiene and infection control
audits.f: Baseline compliance with cleaning/disinfection practices 50%
audits.c: Four PDSA cycles supported by root cause analysis (fishbone diagram) to improve housekeeping adherence
audits.r2: Compliance increased through PDSA cycles: 50% to 68%, then 87.5%, then 95%

audits.t: Blood transfusion reactions and institutional hemovigilance protocols: A 2-year retrospective single center audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Febrile nonhaemolytic reactions were the most common type (41.5%); only 37.5% of reactions were investigated; none were reported to the hospital blood transfusion/hemovigilance committee; one death recorded among cases

audits.t: A clinical audit to assess the adherence of the code blue team to advanced cardiac life support protocol and its effect on the patient outcome in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Kochi, Kerala
audits.tp: Code blue team adherence to ACLS protocol
audits.st: American Heart Association Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) guidelines
audits.f: ACLS protocol followed in 58.7% of resuscitations; most common deviation was use of inappropriate drugs; return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) attained in 53.3%, of whom 28.5% were discharged (P<0.05, significant association between adherence and ROSC)

audits.t: An Audit of Laboratory Requisition Forms for Coagulation Tests in the Hematology Laboratory of a Tertiary Care Center
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: None of the forms had all required information; clinician's department and unit documented on 99.8% each; clinician's name missing on 99.8% of forms; junior doctor's signature present on 94.1%; patient age present on 98.9%, sex on 99.9%

audits.t: An Audit of Prescription Forms of Patients from Obstetrics and Gynecology Clinics in Tertiary Care Hospitals: An exploratory study
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Name, age, date of consultation, sex and OPD registration number present in 100% (preprinted); legible handwriting in 93%; essential medicines available in dispensary in 77%; dosage clearly written in 85%; prescription signed and name legible/stamped in 87%; highest score 17/17, lowest 8/13

audits.t: Administrative Audit of Blood Transfusion Services in a Hemoglobinopathy-Endemic District of Central India: Implications for Clinical Practice
audits.st: Uniform regulatory standards for blood transfusion services (specific body not named)
audits.f: Significant inter-bank variability despite uniform regulatory standards; gaps included fragmented workflows, poor hemovigilance, inadequate counselling, donor dependency and weak continuity of care; most deficiencies were process-related rather than resource-related
audits.c: Limited pilot corrective interventions (administrative/workflow reforms) trialled

audits.t: Clinical audit on management of hypernatremia in the Gastroenterology Department of Assiut University Children Hospital
audits.tp: Hypernatraemia management in children with gastroenteritis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 220 cases of hypernatraemia identified among gastroenteritis admissions; supplied abstract text is truncated before management/compliance results

audits.t: Management of postcholecystectomy biliary injury in Assiut University Hospital clinical audit
audits.st: Biliary leakage/injury management guidelines (comparison for planning improvement)
audits.f: Most common presentation was bile leakage (46.66%), followed by jaundice (20%); open cholecystectomy caused biliary injury more often (73.33%) than laparoscopic (26.66%); minor leakage from cystic duct in 52% of cholangiograms

audits.t: Management of organophosphorus pesticide poisoning in Assiut University Children's Hospital: A clinical audit
audits.st: International guidelines for management of organophosphorus (OP) poisoning
audits.f: Plasma cholinesterase not done in 90% of cases; decontamination and atropinization done in most cases; 90% improved, 10% died

audits.t: Clinical audit on diagnosis of ascites in infants and children in Assiut University Children Hospital
audits.st: Tomar 2016 guidelines for diagnosis of ascites in children (no numeric target stated)
audits.f: No complete adherence to Tomar 2016 guidelines (not further quantified); 33 male, 27 female cases over a 1-year period

audits.t: Clinical audit of the management of pericarditis in children in a Tertiary Referral University Hospital in Egypt
audits.st: European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 2015 guidelines for pericarditis management
audits.f: ESC guidelines followed by a reasonable percentage of cases (not numerically quantified); outcomes: 46.6% improved, 30.0% recurrent pericarditis, 23.3% died

audits.t: Management of upper gastrointestinal bleeding in neonates admitted at Neonatal Intensive Care Unit of Assiut University Children's Hospital: A clinical audit
audits.st: Local adapted protocols for diagnosis and management of upper gastrointestinal bleeding in neonates
audits.f: History and examination fully recorded in 100%; investigations fully done in 100% except Apt-Downey test and upper endoscopy for ulcer evaluation (0%); two IV lines obtained in 18%; saline blood loss replacement in 96%; Foley catheter placement in shocked patients in 12%; epinephrine lavage in 37%; H2 blockers in 13%; PPIs in 46%; blood transfusion in 72%; plasma transfusion in 79%

audits.t: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis: a clinical audit
audits.tp: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis management guideline adherence
audits.st: 2011 American College of Rheumatology recommendations for treatment of juvenile idiopathic arthritis
audits.f: Rheumatoid factor done in 84% of cases; deficiencies found in data recording, laboratory (rheumatoid factor, ANA/anti-dsDNA) and radiological workup, nonpharmacological therapy and surgery not considered, and deficient regular follow-up of safety drug monitoring

audits.t: Clinical audit on management of pediatric urinary tract infection at Assiut University Children Hospital
audits.tp: Paediatric urinary tract infection management guideline adherence
audits.st: American Academy of Pediatrics and National Institute for Health and Care Excellence guidelines for UTI in children
audits.f: History and examination generally complete but neurological examination missing in 48% and genital examination missing in 51%; urine analysis missing in 17%, DMSA scan missing in 32%, VCUG missing in 28.8%; management complete except treatment of complications in the 2-18 year age group

audits.t: Clinical audit on infection control of catheter-related bloodstream infection in neonatal ICU
audits.st: Local infection control protocol for umbilical venous catheter insertion (before, during and after fixation)
audits.f: Infection control measures before fixation done 100%; during fixation defective in 100% (defective drape use and face mask use); after fixation 20% did not maintain sterile technique during dressing

audits.t: Clinical audit on medical treatment of infective endocarditis in Assiut University Children's Hospital
audits.tp: Paediatric infective endocarditis treatment guideline adherence
audits.st: American Heart Association (AHA) guidelines for treatment of infective endocarditis
audits.f: 76.7% received vancomycin per AHA-recommended dosing, 23.3% received ceftriaxone (not AHA-recommended as empirical agent); overall guideline adherence averaged 85.0%

audits.t: Evaluation of children with syncope: a clinical audit at Assiut University Children Hospital
audits.st: Institution's own protocol for management of syncopal attacks in children and adolescents (local standard)
audits.f: Institution successfully followed its recommended protocol for management of syncope (not numerically quantified)

audits.t: Clinical audit on management of hepatic encephalopathy in children admitted to Gastroenterology and Hepatology Unit of Assiut University Children Hospital
audits.tp: Paediatric hepatic encephalopathy management guideline adherence
audits.st: Local guideline protocol for hepatic encephalopathy management (based on international guidelines)
audits.f: History of drug intake not recorded in 23.15%, reversal of sleep rhythm not recorded in 17.3%, behavioural changes not recorded in 9.6%; fetor hepaticus recorded in 42.3%, asterixis in 36.5%, neurological examination in 91.2%; ICU admission and prophylactic endotracheal intubation not applied; oral branched-chain amino acids and rifaximin not given

audits.t: Audit of blood utilization in a tertiary care hospital: Our experience over a period of 2 years
audits.st: Cross-match to transfusion (C/T) ratio >2.5 taken as an indicator of excess cross-matching
audits.f: Maximum C/T ratio of 34.11 noted in Cardiology; only three departments (Artificial Kidney Dialysis, Paediatrics, Medical ICU) showed effective blood utilisation; minimum C/T ratio 1.34 in Artificial Kidney Dialysis

audits.t: Prospective audit of requisitions for transfusion at a rural tertiary care hospital in central India as a step to improve transfusion practices
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 10.75% of forms lacked demographic details, 14.58% lacked priority, 18.91% lacked blood group, 32.69% lacked indication, 24.23% lacked previous transfusion history, 23.47% lacked proper clinical history; more than 60% of forms not properly filled

audits.t: Prescription audit of the outpatient department of an ophthalmic tertiary care public sector hospital
audits.st: WHO drug prescription and usage indicators
audits.f: Patient identification details incomplete in 23% (missing name 1.28%, age 10.88%, gender 10.4%); dose/strength correctly mentioned in only 1.12% of prescriptions; route of administration missing in 2.72%; only 8.68% of 1543 drugs prescribed generically; average 2.47 drugs per patient; more than 5 drugs prescribed in only 4%

audits.t: Monitoring the adherence to an adapted evidence-based clinical practice guideline on antiemetics in 669 patients with cancer receiving 1451 chemotherapy doses at a University oncology center in Saudi Arabia
audits.tp: Antiemetic prophylaxis guideline adherence in chemotherapy
audits.st: Centre's adapted evidence-based clinical practice guideline (CPG) for antiemetics for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV)
audits.f: Nearly 48% of antiemetic prescriptions adhered to the adopted CPG; adherence was higher for moderate emetogenic agents (e.g. doxorubicin, ifosfamide) than for high emetogenic agents (e.g. cisplatin, cyclophosphamide >1500 mg/m2)

audits.t: Conversion of labour epidural analgesia to anaesthesia for emergency caesarean section: A retrospective audit
audits.tp: Labour epidural conversion to surgical anaesthesia
audits.st: Royal College of Anaesthetists (UK) recommended standards for epidural conversion failure rates
audits.f: Epidural analgesia was successful for surgical anaesthesia in 95.75% (4078/4259); overall failure rate was 4.25% (181/4259), which was within RCA-recommended standards; 1.71% needed supplemental sedation, 2.53% needed alternate techniques

audits.t: Incidence and Risk Factors of Peri-operative Hypothermia in Adults Undergoing Cancer Surgery – A Quality Improvement Audit
audits.st: Core temperature <35C and skin temperature <34C used as the definition of hypothermia
audits.f: Incidence of intraoperative hypothermia was 22%, postoperative hypothermia 8.7%; hypothermia associated with general anaesthesia and longer cavity surgery; patients with postoperative complications were 91% more likely to have had perioperative hypothermia; cavity surgery patients 2.3 times more likely to have intraoperative hypothermia than surface surgery patients

audits.t: Management of Cancer Pain – An Audit of 500 Patients at a Tertiary Care Cancer Center in India
audits.st: WHO analgesic ladder
audits.f: 81% had moderate-to-severe pain at first visit, reducing to 34% by 2nd visit and 28% by 3rd visit; neuropathic pain in 12%; sleep disturbance in 33%; tapentadol most common opioid at first visit (31%), morphine use increased to 45% by 3rd visit

audits.t: Outcome of hand hygiene audit in intensive care unit during COVID-19: An experience from a tertiary care centre
audits.tp: Hand hygiene compliance in intensive care
audits.st: World Health Organization hand hygiene audit tool (5 moments of hand hygiene)
audits.f: Differences found in hand hygiene adherence rate (HHAR) between healthcare worker professions (doctors, nurses, others), between genders, and across the WHO moments; exact percentages not stated in the abstract

audits.t: Impact of novel blood culture collection bundle to reduce blood culture contamination rates: An important continuous quality improvement indicator of laboratory medicine
audits.st: International standard of blood culture contamination rate <3%
audits.f: Baseline blood culture contamination rate was 17%
audits.c: Introduction of a novel blood culture collection (BCC) bundle (six steps for blood culture collection), active surveillance, root cause analysis of contaminated cultures, feedback to phlebotomists/nurses/doctors, and periodic/need-based onsite staff training
audits.r2: Contamination rate reduced from 17% to 4% over 18 months

audits.t: An audit of perioperative antibiotic prescriptions in patients undergoing clean surgeries and compliance with antibiotic policy in a tertiary hospital
audits.tp: Perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis compliance in clean surgery
audits.st: Institutional antibiotic policy for perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis in clean surgeries
audits.f: Compliance with timing of surgical prophylaxis was good (91%) and all patients received prophylaxis; broad-spectrum antibiotics used in almost 50% of cases with prolonged duration versus protocol; oral antibiotics continued at discharge in 72.7% (40/55); no increase in healthcare-associated infections

audits.t: An Audit of Antibiotic Prescribing Pattern Among Children in Emergency Settings of a Tertiary Medical College and Hospital
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing pattern in paediatric emergency
audits.st: WHO methodology for investigating drug use in a health facility
audits.f: Combination of three antibiotics prescribed in 8.8% of patients; 100% of antibiotics prescribed from the essential drug list; antimicrobials prescribed by generic name in 52%; broad-spectrum antibiotics 86.6%, narrow-spectrum 13.4%; ceftriaxone was the commonest antibiotic (43.3%), followed by amikacin (25.2%)

audits.t: An Audit on Orthodontic Referrals by Government Dental Officers in the Federal Territory of Labuan
audits.st: Ministry of Health Malaysia orthodontic referral guidelines, including Index of Orthodontic Treatment Need (IOTN) grading
audits.f: 71.4% of referral forms were complete (dental history most frequently missing, 22.1%); inaccurate IOTN scoring in 20.8% of cases; 27.3% of incisor classifications were incorrect; 90.9% of referrals met the MOH requirement for IOTN grades 4 or 5

audits.t: An audit of “Repeat” fine needle aspiration cytology procedures in a cytopathology laboratory—An important quality indicator
audits.tp: Repeat fine needle aspiration cytology rate
audits.st: Quality manager benchmark of 15% for repeat FNAC rate
audits.f: 39 of 303 FNACs (12.8%) were repeated, within the 15% benchmark; soft tissue lesions, predominantly lipomas, accounted for most (35.9%) repeats; principal reason was insufficient material from initial aspiration

audits.t: Prescription Audit for WHO Prescribing Indicators and Prescription Errors in a Tertiary Care Teaching Hospital
audits.st: WHO prescribing indicators
audits.f: 1451 errors found; 324 (22.3%) errors of omission and 145 (10.0%) errors of commission related to drugs; 982 (67.7%) errors of omission other than drug details; average 3.14 drugs per prescription; 28.72% prescribed by generic name; 34.0% prescribed antibiotics; 2.25% prescribed injectable drugs; all drugs from the National Essential Drug List

audits.t: Measure what you treasure! – A maternity dashboard
audits.tp: Maternity dashboard monitoring of quality indicators
audits.st: Locally agreed maternity unit standards for clinical activity, workforce, clinical outcome and complaints/risk indicators, benchmarked monthly with a traffic-light system
audits.f: Various clinical activity and clinical outcome (maternal and neonatal) indicators were audited and triaged monthly using traffic-light colours; specific pass/fail numbers not given in the abstract

audits.t: Clinical Audit of Radiographs Following Maxillofacial Injuries in Sultanah Nora Ismail Batu Pahat Hospital
audits.tp: Appropriateness and quality of maxillofacial trauma radiographs
audits.st: Guidance Notes for Dental Practitioners on Safe Use of X-ray Equipment (2001) for quality rating; Oxford Handbook Dental Patient Care 2nd Edition (2005) and Dental Update (2006) for appropriateness of radiograph type
audits.f: 151 of 221 radiographs (68.3%) were ordered inappropriately, 85.4% of inappropriate requests from A&E; on quality rating, only 26.7% were good quality, 36.2% acceptable, 37.1% poor

audits.t: Improving surgical antibiotic prophylaxis compliance: A tertiary hospital quality improvement study
audits.st: Institutional surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (SAP) standard operating procedures (six SAP SOP parameters)
audits.f: Only 58.75% received SAP within the recommended 30-60 minute pre-incision window (24.75% too early or later than 60-120 minutes); 83.25% received ceftriaxone instead of guideline-recommended first-line agents; documentation completeness was 49.5%
audits.c: Development of a Four-Pillar SAP Compliance Framework (process standardisation, capacity building, technology enablement, governance) informed by 26 key-informant interviews and root-cause analysis

audits.t: Audit of Anaesthesia Chart Completion at the University College Hospital, Ibadan
audits.st: Checklist based on variables from the currently used anaesthesia chart
audits.f: Mean chart completion 72.0% (SD 7.3); minimum score 33.3%, maximum 88.3%; 1 chart (0.6%) scored <50%, 125 (69.4%) scored 50-74.9%, 54 (30%) scored >=75%; demographic section best completed (91.2%), pre-operative section worst (55.9%), intra-operative section 68.7%

audits.t: Audit of Renal Allograft Biopsies Handled in a Nephropathology Unit in Kano, Nigeria
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 2 of 21 (10%) allograft biopsies were unrepresentative; all adequately fixed; 5 cores <1 cm with crush artefact; 7 cases had <7 glomeruli; 8 (42%) free of rejection, 58% positive for rejection nephropathy; turnaround time 2-3 working days in 81% of cases, up to 7 days in 11%

audits.t: A single-centre audit of request forms and the 2011 appropriate use criteria for transthoracic echocardiography
audits.st: 2011 Revised American College of Cardiology Foundation appropriate use criteria (AUC) for transthoracic echocardiography
audits.f: All 412 request forms had patient names; age missing in 22.6%, sex in 11.4%, address in 92.5%; 119 (28.9%) lacked indication and were unclassifiable by AUC; of the remainder, indications were appropriate in 259 (88.4%), inappropriate in 26 (8.9%), uncertain in 8 (2.7%)

audits.t: A prescription audit in the outpatient department of the national accreditation board for hospitals and healthcare providers and joint commission international approved super speciality hospital in the capital territory of India
audits.tp: Prescribing practice compliance with WHO core indicators
audits.st: World Health Organization core prescribing indicators format
audits.f: 67.59% (1149) of parameters were compliant, 21.65% (368) noncompliant, 10.76% (183) not applicable

audits.t: Audit of Lower Segment Cesarean Section Cases Based on Obstetric Care Standards in a Small Healthcare Facility
audits.st: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG) and National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) audit standards for elective lower segment caesarean section
audits.f: Consent documentation 100%, regional anaesthesia 96.97%, antacid/antiemetic prophylaxis 100%; umbilical cord pH testing only 36.36%; thromboprophylaxis compliance only 12.12%

audits.t: Prospective audit of transfusion utilization trends and transfusion practices at a rural tertiary care hospital in Central India
audits.st: Transfusion utilisation quality indicators (crossmatch-to-transfusion ratio, transfusion probability, transfusion index)
audits.f: 9907 of 12840 crossmatched units were transfused, 2573 not transfused; crossmatch-to-transfusion ratio 1.26, transfusion probability 79.38, transfusion index 0.79; 65 transfusion reactions occurred, only 27.69% (18) reported to the blood centre

audits.t: Prospective Audit of Colonoscopy Practice in a Lebanese University Hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall caecal intubation rate 99.99%; 70 snare polypectomies, 29 cold forceps excisions, 5 Argon Plasma Coagulations performed; most important post-procedural complication was chemical colitis in 2 cases
audits.c: Change in endoscope rinsing method following the audit findings

audits.t: Audit of Management of Immediate Postpartum Hemorrhages in Parakou (Benin)
audits.tp: Immediate postpartum haemorrhage management criteria-based audit
audits.st: 41 key criteria-based actions necessary for management of immediate postpartum haemorrhage (dysfunction defined as any action not meeting 85% of criteria)
audits.f: Frequency of IPPH in the unit was 8.07%; average dysfunction score was 9; dysfunctions registered at all stages of care, most affecting referral, emergency and hospitalisation

audits.t: Clinical Audit of Quality of Intrapartum Care in a State University Teaching Hospital, Enugu, Southeast, Nigeria
audits.st: Intrapartum care quality indicators (institutional/local standard)
audits.f: Maternal mortality ratio 292/100,000 live births (15 deaths); stillbirth rate 4.8% (256/5385); Apgar <7 at 5 minutes in 9.9%; neonatal ICU admission in 9.0%; postpartum haemorrhage >1000ml in 0.9% of women; eclampsia in 0.8%

audits.t: The Frequency of Antipsychotic Prescribing in Older People Mental Health Services: A Southern Health OPMH CRIS Audit
audits.tp: Antipsychotic prescribing adherence to NICE guidelines in older people
audits.st: NICE guidelines for antipsychotic prescribing in older people with mental health problems
audits.f: 84.6% of patients without comorbid psychotic illness were prescribed an antipsychotic, most commonly for agitation, psychotic symptoms, distress or aggression; dementia was the commonest diagnosis prescribed antipsychotics (40%); prescribing found to be in line with NICE guidelines

audits.t: Limiting Oxygen Therapy in the Neonatal ICU: A Quality Improvement Initiative
audits.tp: Target oxygen protocol compliance in neonatal ICU
audits.st: NICU's 4-pronged Target Oxygen Protocol (correct SpO2 alarm limits, Nellcor OxiMax pulse oximeter use, correct postmenstrual-age oxygen target saturation card display, oxygen blender FIO2 <10% above current support)
audits.f: Correct SpO2 alarm limits 86% (99/115), Nellcor use 91% (109/120), saturation card display 87% (101/116), FIO2 above respiratory support 79% (92/116)
audits.c: Switch from random to daily audits performed by respiratory therapists as part of their workflow, with staff education on oxygen strategies
audits.r2: Correct SpO2 alarm limits 76% (103/135, not improved), Nellcor use increased to 98% (133/135, p=0.02), saturation card display increased to 96% (130/135, p=0.007), FIO2 above respiratory support increased to 95% (128/134, p<0.001)

audits.t: Use of a Gestational Age Based Chart (Kempley Chart) for Optimal Endotracheal Tube Depth to Prevent Unplanned Extubation in Mechanically Ventilated Patients in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit
audits.tp: Endotracheal tube depth accuracy to prevent unplanned extubation
audits.st: National goal for neonatal unplanned extubations (UEs) of less than 1 per 100 ventilator days; Kempley gestational-age-based chart for optimal endotracheal tube (ETT) depth
audits.f: Baseline UE rate before Kempley chart implementation not numerically stated; approximately 80% of NICU UEs occurred in infants born at 28 weeks' gestation or less
audits.c: Use of PDSA cycles, fishbone diagrams and reliability bundles; education of NICU providers, nurses and respiratory therapists on the Kempley chart; discussion of ETT depth at multidisciplinary rounds at gestational milestones
audits.r2: Absolute number of unplanned extubations reduced by 50%; one-third of remaining UEs still had a prescribed ETT depth less than that predicted by the Kempley chart

audits.t: An Audit on Compliance of Surgical Time Out after a Decade of Implementation at an Academic Tertiary Care Hospital
audits.st: WHO surgical safety checklist / surgical time-out requirement, after a decade of implementation
audits.f: Time-out checklist employed in 45.7% of cases and fully completed in 26.7%; noncompliance associated with absence of staff members (OR=0.04, 95% CI 0.01-0.21, p<0.001) and lower primary surgeon involvement (p<0.001); no association with time of day (p=0.83) or surgical load

audits.t: Clinical Audit on the Provision of Diabetes Care in the Primary Care Setting by United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA)
audits.st: UNRWA technical instructions (TI) for diabetes care
audits.f: 2-hour postprandial glucose, serum cholesterol, serum creatinine and urine protein analysis records available in 94.7%, 96.4%, 91.4% and 87.5% respectively; annual fundoscopic eye examination recorded in 47.3%; only 28.2% had HbA1c <=7%; 55.5% and 28.2% had BP <=140/90 and <=130/80 mmHg respectively
audits.co: Gaza, West Bank, Jordan, Lebanon and Syria (Palestine refugees)

audits.t: Improving Clinical Documentation through Monthly Audits in Butare Teaching Hospital, Rwanda
audits.tp: Clinical documentation completeness and accreditation compliance
audits.st: COHSASA (Council for Health Service Accreditation of Southern Africa) hospital accreditation standards for clinical documentation
audits.f: Department clinical auditing completion rate 57% (pre-intervention); hospital-wide accreditation standards compliance rate for clinical documentation 27% (pre-intervention)
audits.c: Creation of a standardised, MS Excel-based clinical documentation auditing system with automated completion/compliance rate computation and monthly QI meeting feedback
audits.r2: Completion rate increased to 96% (post-intervention, p<0.000); accreditation compliance rate improved to 60% (p=0.000)

audits.t: Audit of Obstetric Outcome in Morbidly Obese Women at Great Western Hospital NHS Foundation Trust UK
audits.tp: Care of morbidly obese women in pregnancy
audits.st: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 72 'Care of Women with Obesity in Pregnancy'
audits.f: Prevalence of morbid obesity 3.45%; compliance with care was 92.67%; gestational hypertension was the commonest antenatal complication (9 cases), followed by gestational diabetes (7); 11 women had postpartum haemorrhage

audits.t: The Kenya surgical capacity study: An audit of surgical equipment/infrastructure in Level 4 public hospitals
audits.tp: Surgical equipment and infrastructure availability audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Intra-operative and anaesthesia equipment availability 44.5% and 47% respectively; general patient care supplies present in nearly 60% of facilities; running water in maternity wards 83.1%; sterilization equipment in about half (42.6-68.3%); generator backup 79.1%; on-site X-ray always available in only 35%; 52.6% obtained blood from a national/regional centre

audits.t: A 5-year Assessment of Negative Appendectomy Among Adolescents and Adults at a Tertiary Hospital: A Clinical Audit
audits.st: Acceptable negative appendectomy rate benchmark: 20% in females of reproductive age versus 10% in young males
audits.f: Negative appendectomy rate 7.5% overall (males 5.15%, females 12.0%), within the acceptable threshold; Alvarado score used in 41% (sensitivity 80%, specificity 22%, PPV 74%); CT and ultrasound each about 80% predictive of appendicitis.

audits.t: Audit report: Baseline health facility assessment of quality assurance for malaria diagnosis in existing government hospital laboratories in Sokoto State, Nigeria
audits.tp: Malaria diagnostic laboratory quality assurance audit
audits.st: WHO/NMEP EQA (External Quality Assurance) standardised assessment tool for malaria diagnosis
audits.f: Combined mRDT and microscopy used routinely at 17 (65.0%) laboratories, microscopy only at 7 (27.0%), mRDT only at 1 (3.8%); 16 (63.0%) facilities had staff trained in the past year; 23 (96.0%) had a functional microscope; none had a well-structured quality assurance/quality control procedure or SOPs

audits.t: Audit of head and neck fine needle aspiration cytology from a tertiary institution in south - west Nigeria
audits.tp: Head and neck fine needle aspiration cytology utilisation audit
audits.st: National Institute for Clinical Excellence (NICE) recommendations for FNAC use
audits.f: Anterior neck was the commonest site (47.4%); cervical lymph node swellings 19.6%; benign lesions 35%; 160 (5.7%) specimens inconclusive; no complications reported

audits.t: Prescription of Brain CT in Traumatic Brain Injury: A Prospective Audit in a Senegalese Level-2 Hospital (2024 – 2025)
audits.tp: Brain CT use in traumatic brain injury
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mechanism of injury reported in only 8.6% of cases; GCS documented in 1.9% and other neurological signs in 20.5%; initial loss of consciousness absent in 60.6%; 66.2% of scans were normal

audits.t: Clinical audit of operation notes at the Department of Surgery, Addis Ababa University
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England (RCSE) 2014 best practice guidelines for operation notes
audits.f: Operative findings, anaesthesia details, patient position and incision type documented >90% of the time; surgeons/assistants identified in >96% of notes; anaesthesia team identified in 88.5% (MIIH) vs 5.7% (TASH); gauze/instrument counts documented in 81.2% and 69.5%; closure technique described in 71.8% and 52.3%; no fields for antibiotic prophylaxis, DVT prophylaxis or estimated blood loss

audits.t: Audit clinique basé sur les critères sur les infections bactériennes néonatales dans l’unité de néonatologie du centre hospitalier universitaire départemental de Parakou
audits.tp: Neonatal bacterial infection management criteria-based audit
audits.st: Criteria-based clinical audit approach (ACBC) for management of confirmed neonatal bacterial infections
audits.f: Frequency of neonatal infection 45.96%; overall mortality 26.34%, with infection-attributable mortality 8.16% and case-fatality 4.67% (8/171); examination within 1 hour of admission in only 4.68%; maternal urogenital infection screening in 4%; blood culture requested in 5%; first antibiotic dose given within 1 hour of diagnosis in 29%; respiratory and temperature monitoring regular in 15% each

audits.t: Annual audit of haematology tests performed at a laboratory of a tertiary teaching hospital in Dar es salaam Tanzania
audits.st: MAMC specialised clinic and laboratory services guidelines (established turnaround time standards)
audits.f: 81.3% of orders were collected but only 21.3% of collected tests had results available in the Hospital Information System; none had Hb or CBC results available before consultation; half of Hb results and two-thirds of CBC results were within turnaround time target

audits.t: Measures of Function in Physical Therapy Assessment of Children with Cerebral Palsy: A Clinical Audit
audits.tp: Outcome measure use in cerebral palsy function assessment
audits.st: Current standards of assessment for function in children with cerebral palsy (using the Gross Motor Function Measure, GMFM)
audits.f: 18 of 96 charts (18.7%) met current assessment standards using GMFM; the remaining 78 (81.3%) used descriptive-type assessment (gait analysis 20.9%, ADL analysis 79.1%, functional muscle testing 44.2%, gross motor skills assessment 37.2%, advanced motor skills assessment 23.3%, balance assessment 4.7%, developmental milestone assessment 2.3%, self-adaptive measure 2.3%)

audits.t: Aphasia Rehabilitation Service Delivery in a Stroke Rehabilitation Unit in Australia: A Clinical Audit of Speech Pathology Practices
audits.tp: Aphasia rehabilitation service delivery guideline adherence
audits.st: National Stroke Foundation (NSF) Clinical Guidelines and Australasian Rehabilitation Outcomes Centre (AROC) benchmarks
audits.f: Patients admitted to inpatient rehabilitation at an average of 21 days post-stroke (2 days beyond the AROC benchmark); mean length of stay 60 days (vs AROC benchmark of 32.8 days); patients received an average of 4.25 hours of speech pathology therapy per week, more than twice the NSF minimum recommendation

audits.t: Identifying the Pathway to Conservative Pelvic Floor Physiotherapy in a Tertiary Public Hospital in Australia: A Retrospective Audit
audits.tp: Pelvic floor physiotherapy referral pathway audit
audits.st: Best practice guidelines mandating conservative physiotherapy as first-line management for incontinence/pelvic organ prolapse
audits.f: Only half (n=31, 49%) were referred on to physiotherapy; referral time from local provider to Gynaecology ranged 49-351 days (average 169.6 days); of the 31 referred to physiotherapy, 22 (70.9%) were referred on the day of Gynaecology consultation, others waited 2-126 days; of 31 not referred to physiotherapy, 18 (58%) proceeded directly to surgery

audits.t: Factors Contributing to Prolonged Total Ischemic Time in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Patients Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Quasi-Experimental Clinical Audit of In-Hospital Process Improvement
audits.tp: Total ischemic time in STEMI primary PCI
audits.st: Guideline-recommended reperfusion timelines for STEMI (prolonged total ischemic time [TIT] defined as >=360 minutes)
audits.f: Mean TIT 525.4 +/- 177.5 minutes; door-to-balloon time 108.8 +/- 28.1 minutes
audits.c: Audit-guided in-hospital process improvement: structured emergency triage, direct Cath-lab activation, deferral of non-essential administrative processes
audits.r2: Mean TIT decreased to 461.3 +/- 193.6 minutes (p<0.001); door-to-balloon time improved to 73.7 +/- 10.9 minutes (p<0.001); door-to-ECG and ECG-to-Cath-lab times also significantly reduced

audits.t: Clinical Audit on Hypoglycemic Symptoms in Type 2 Diabetic Patients
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 70 males and 80 females; mean age 58.95+/-5.67 years for patients with hypoglycaemic symptoms and 55.15+/-10.67 years for those without symptoms

audits.t: Secondary Heamorrhage After Cold Steel Tonsillectomy: An Audit Performed in Shalamar Hospital
audits.st: International standards for post-tonsillectomy secondary haemorrhage rates
audits.f: Secondary haemorrhage occurred in 7 patients (2%); significant age difference (P=0.01), lower incidence in under-18s (0.7%) vs over-18s (7.14%); rate slightly higher in males (2.6%) than females (1.31%)

audits.t: Adherence to Thromboprophylaxis Guidelines in Acutely ill and Immobilized patients: A Clinical Audit
audits.st: Thromboprophylaxis guidelines for acutely ill and immobilised patients
audits.f: 435 (72%) were high risk, 165 (28%) low risk; 345 (57.5%) received VTE prophylaxis (31.2% of high-risk, 26.4% of low-risk); 74 (12.3%) received both TED stockings and anticoagulation, 173 (28.6%) TED stockings alone, 101 (16.7%) anticoagulation alone

audits.t: Antibiotics prescription in the elderly across different clinical areas; A real-life clinical audit
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing safety in the elderly
audits.st: Local safety standard for antibiotic prescribing in patients over 85 years (appropriate antibiotic selection, documentation of indication and duration)
audits.f: Minimum compliance rate was 95% in each studied parameter overall; significant compromise in antibiotic prescription on non-geriatric wards and out of hours

audits.t: Blood Transfusion Audit in Tertiary Care Hospital Blood Bank
audits.st: Blood transfusion utilisation quality indicators (crossmatch and issue rates)
audits.f: 6374 units (45.43%) of crossmatched units were issued; of 5009 single-unit requests, only 1480 (29.54%) were utilised

audits.t: Prescription Audit: Observation and Outcome on Ideal Perspectives
audits.st: Criteria for an ideal/complete prescription
audits.f: Incomplete direction for drug use in 60%; missing prescriber registration number in 86%, the highest-frequency errors identified

audits.t: Effect of Audit and Feedback on the Documentation of Nursing Care Actions in a Tertiary Hospital in Southeastern Nigeria: A Quasi-Experimental Study
audits.st: Validated Nursing Action Audit Checklist (28 nursing care actions)
audits.f: 6 of 28 nursing care actions (21.4%) were adequately documented
audits.c: Structured nursing audit feedback intervention using the validated Nursing Action Audit Checklist
audits.r2: 24 of 28 nursing care actions (85.7%) were adequately documented (χ²=23.26, P<0.001; RR=5.50, 95% CI 2.17-13.91)

audits.t: A clinical audit report on quality of nursing documentation at Jigme dorji Wangchuck national referral Hospital, 2018
audits.st: D-catch tool for nursing documentation quality
audits.f: Quantitative completeness of nursing documentation (mean 3.4, SD 0.59) was higher than quality of documentation maintained (mean 2.8, SD 0.79); admission data and vital signs charting were documented better than nursing care process documentation

audits.t: Diagnosis and Management of Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy- A Retrospective Clinical Audit
audits.tp: Diagnosis and management of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
audits.st: Diagnostic criteria for intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (pruritus with serum bile acid >=10 micromol/L and/or ALT >30 U/L)
audits.f: Prevalence of ICP 0.18%; both SBA and liver enzymes elevated in 53.2%, SBA alone elevated in 42.6%; severe ICP in 17% (all had caesarean section) vs 44% caesarean section rate in mild ICP; repeat SBA performed in only 8.1% of those with normal initial SBA; postpartum follow-up observed in only 21.2%

audits.t: Audit of Caesarean Sections in a Single Centre: Analysis of its Frequency and Indications
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 2605 (57%) caesarean sections, 1970 (43%) vaginal deliveries; commonest indication was repeat caesarean section (22%) followed by fetal distress (21%)

audits.t: Nursing Care Audit Based on Nursing Process Model and Ensuring Patient Safety among Staff Nurses
audits.st: Nursing process model-based nursing audit checklist
audits.f: Rate of least compliance with nursing process indicators was 12.6, confirming most nursing care was not carried out per the nursing process model; overall compliance score differed significantly between BSc and GNM qualified nurses (P=0.04), including diagnosis (P=0.001), implementation (P=0.02) and evaluation (P=0.01) domains

audits.t: Enhancing Peripheral IV Cannula Management: A Clinical Audit on Optimal Replacement Time, Post-Insertion Documentation, and Rate of Superficial Phlebitis in Surgical Wards
audits.st: Local/institutional standard for optimal peripheral IV cannula replacement timing and post-insertion documentation
audits.f: Abstract text truncated in source; no numeric results available

audits.t: Comparative audit of induction of labour at Furness General Hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported (comparative audit described; no numeric results supplied in the available text)

audits.t: Management of tubal pregnancies - an audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported (audit of tubal pregnancy management mentioned; no numeric results supplied in the available text)

audits.t: Elective caesarean sections before 39 weeks - an audit
audits.st: NICE guidelines (April 2004): uncomplicated elective caesarean sections after 39 completed weeks
audits.f: not reported (audit asks whether the NICE standard is being met; no numeric results supplied in the available text)

audits.t: A secondary care retrospective clinical audit: assessing coronary angiography door-to-catheter times in acute coronary syndrome
audits.st: NICE guidance: angiography within 72 hours for high-risk (GRACE>3%) NSTEMI and late-presenting (>12 hours) STEMI
audits.f: Abstract text truncated in source; no numeric results available

audits.t: Audit of Pain Management at the Hospital
audits.st: not reported

audits.tp: Infection control compliance for mechanically ventilated patients
audits.st: International infection prevention guidelines, applied via a structured observational checklist
audits.f: High adherence for disposal of contaminated materials (90.1%), closed suction system use (85.2%), and head-of-bed elevation (83.1%); lower compliance for oral care (54.9%), aseptic suctioning (62.7%), and hand hygiene before patient contact (67.6%); overall 41.1% of nurses showed good compliance and 13.9% poor compliance

audits.t: Antimicrobial Audit and Stewardship Practices among Hospitalised Patients: A Retrospective Study
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 83.8% male; confirmed infection in 25%, predominantly Gram-negative (94.2%; E. coli 72.2%, Klebsiella pneumoniae 10.19%, Pseudomonas aeruginosa 5.8%). Cephalosporins most prescribed (89.7%). Only 41.5% of antibiotic prescriptions matched culture sensitivity reports; 58.5% were not culture-matched.

audits.t: Dental audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Clinical Audit of Gynecology Ward Shahida Islam Medical Complex, Lodhran: Evaluating Patient Care and Record Management
audits.tp: Gynaecology ward record and care quality
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 97% discharged, 1% left against medical advice, 1 death; provisional diagnosis documented in 94%; reports properly checked in 99%; documentation of progress notes 100%; essential drugs were available.

audits.t: Clinical Audit to Optimize Pre-Endoscopy Checklist in Patients Undergoing GI Endoscopy
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Prescription Audit of CKD Patients in Nephrology Department of a Tertiary Care Hospital: An Observational Prospective Study
audits.tp: Prescription pattern audit in chronic kidney disease
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Common comorbidities were diabetes (31%) and hypertension (27%); antibiotics were prescribed to all patients; drug interactions occurred in 28.7% of cases; prescription errors included dose (16%) and frequency (6.7%); only 4.7% lacked a doctor's signature

audits.t: Waiting Times for Cataract Surgery in a Dedicated Cataract Clinic: A Retrospective Audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median waiting time for all eyes was 113.5 days; first-eye surgery 109.0 days; second-eye surgery 134.5 days
audits.r2: Median waiting time for all eyes rose to 194.0 days (p=0.0002); first-eye surgery to 171.0 days (p=0.0175); second-eye surgery to 322.0 days (p=0.0008)

audits.t: A Multinational Audit of WHO Surgical Safety Checklist Adherence in Low-Resource Settings
audits.st: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (WHO SSC) adherence
audits.f: Perceived adverse event prevention reported in 77.1% of cases; perfect checklist adherence in only 4.1%; gaps in infection risk assessment (72.9%) and DVT prophylaxis (66.8%); adherence associated with perceived adverse event prevention (OR 6.40, 95% CI 1.91-39.9, p<0.001) but attenuated and non-significant after accounting for hospital clustering (OR 3.45, p=0.100, ICC=0.27).

audits.t: ASSESSING OUTCOMES OF CENTRAL VENOUS CATHETER INSERTION WITH AND WITHOUT ULTRASOUND GUIDANCE, FOLLOWED BY A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVE INTRODUCING MANDATORY ULTRASOUND USE IN A TERTIARY CARE HOSPITAL IN PAKISTAN
audits.st: International recommendation for ultrasound guidance during central venous catheter insertion
audits.f: Ultrasound-guided insertion was used in 18.7% (18/96); first-attempt success rate was 40.6% (39/96); overall complication rate was 19.8% (19/96)
audits.c: Mandatory ultrasound guidance policy, ensuring bedside ultrasound availability, and staff training in the general medicine ward
audits.r2: Ultrasound-guided insertion increased to 92.7% (76/82); first-attempt success improved to 72.0% (59/82); complication rate decreased to 6.1% (5/82)

audits.t: Clinical Audit of Denture Fabrication by Undergraduate Students: Error Frequency and its Association with Patient Demographics
audits.tp: Denture fabrication error rates in undergraduate training
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Most frequent error was occlusal interferences (64%) in the stability domain, and poor surface finishing (75.2%) in the esthetics domain; significant correlation found between tooth shade/shape selection and patient age (p<0.05)

audits.t: Clinical audit on monitoring of clinical and laboratory parameters in patient of acne taking oral isotretinoin
audits.st: Standard/set protocol requiring 100% of patients be counseled on liver function/lipid monitoring, contraception, and depressive symptoms
audits.f: 98% of patients were counseled for contraception; 70% had routine liver function test and fasting lipid profile monitoring; 37% were counseled for depressive symptoms, against a standard of 100% for all three components

audits.t: Clinical audit of National Institute of Clinical Excellence (NICE) Technology Appraisal Guidance (TAG) 81 and 82/Clinical Guidelines (CG57) on atopic eczema in children
audits.tp: Atopic eczema management compliance with NICE guidance
audits.st: NICE Technology Appraisal Guidance (TAG) 81 and 82 and Clinical Guideline CG57 for atopic eczema in children
audits.f: 100% of patients were treated with topical corticosteroids and 100% of cases were treated in accordance with NICE recommendations; the drug with lowest acquisition cost was prescribed in 62% (31/50) of cases; none of the 50 patients was prescribed tacrolimus or pimecrolimus

audits.t: Clinical audit: Baseline investigations for intramuscular meglumine antimoniate in cases of cutaneous leishmaniasis
audits.st: Local guidelines requiring baseline investigations before intramuscular meglumine antimoniate for cutaneous leishmaniasis
audits.f: Result showed 100% compliance with local guidelines in the analyzed cases

audits.t: Clinical audit: baseline Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) and Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) assessment of psoriasis patients
audits.tp: Baseline PASI and DLQI assessment in psoriasis
audits.st: Local guideline: 100% of patients with psoriasis should have baseline PASI and DLQI assessment
audits.f: Result showed 100% compliance with local guidelines in the analyzed cases

audits.t: Clinical audit on treatment of mucosal and multiple cutaneous leishmaniasis lesions with pentavalent systemic antimony
audits.tp: Treatment compliance for mucosal and multiple cutaneous leishmaniasis
audits.st: Local guidelines: 100% of patients with mucosal and multiple cutaneous leishmaniasis lesions should be treated with pentavalent systemic antimonials
audits.f: Result showed 100% compliance with local guidelines in the analyzed cases

audits.t: Departmental case notes audit: A quality assurance measure in a changing organizational climate
audits.st: Local guidelines: 100% standard for case note record keeping
audits.f: Result showed 75% compliance with local guidelines in the analyzed case sets

audits.t: Clinical audit on field services for maternal and newborn care in Sri Lanka
audits.st: National target of 98% coverage for postnatal visits within the first 5 days (Family Health Bureau standards)
audits.f: Coverage of postnatal visits within the first 5 days ranged from 72.8% to 77.6%, falling short of the national target of 98%; coverage during subsequent recommended periods was significantly lower

audits.t: Clinical Audit of Heparin Use in Rift Valley General Hospital, Nakuru County, Kenya
audits.st: Institutional performance threshold/standard for heparin use (no policies or guidelines existed locally)
audits.f: Overall clinical audit score was 60.6%, showing minimal compliance with the performance threshold/standard for heparin use; no policies, protocols or guidelines existed to guide heparin use; delayed or lack of heparin monitoring was observed; warfarin was introduced at least three days before stopping heparin in most patients

audits.t: A Project to Use Team Resources to Reduce the Rate of Central Catheter-Related Bloodstream Infection in Internal Medicine Intensive Care Unit
audits.st: CLABSI surveillance standards (2021 surveillance report benchmark)
audits.f: CLABSI density increased from 3.43% in the first quarter of 2021 to 5.63% by July
audits.c: Revised standard operating procedures, educational training, instructional videos, and implementation of the LINE@ digital audit platform

audits.t: Optimizing Heart Failure Management Development And Implementation Of A Standardized Discharge Checklist For Heart Failure Patients In A Tertiary Care Hospital In Pakistan
audits.st: European Society of Cardiology (ESC 2023) and NICE NG106 guidelines for heart failure management
audits.f: Documentation of HF type was 59.2%, NYHA class/LVEF 52.8%, complete GDMT prescription 40.8%, patient education documentation 31.2%, follow-up within 14 days 37.6%, and primary care communication 26.4%
audits.c: A standardized, evidence-based discharge checklist developed from ESC 2023 and NICE NG106 guidelines, piloted via a PDSA cycle with house officer and resident training
audits.r2: HF type documentation increased to 85.7%, NYHA class/LVEF to 82.1%, GDMT prescription to 67.8%, patient education to 60.7%, follow-up within 14 days to 78.5%, and primary care communication to 57.1%; 30-day readmission rate trended down from 33.6% to 25.0% (preliminary)

audits.t: Reducing Inappropriate Blood Transfusion in Stable CKD Anemia: Management Stewardship
audits.tp: Blood transfusion appropriateness in CKD anaemia
audits.st: Transfusion appropriateness criteria for stable CKD anaemia under a transfusion stewardship programme
audits.f: 80.0% of patients received blood transfusions, of which 33.3% (50) were considered inappropriate
audits.c: Transfusion stewardship programme comprising clinician education, audit and feedback, and electronic decision support tools
audits.r2: Inappropriate transfusions decreased significantly to 10.0% (15) (p<0.001); appropriate transfusions increased from 46.7% to 60.0%; average transfused units per patient declined from 2.5 +/- 0.9 to 2.1 +/- 0.7

audits.t: Prescribing patterns of low-dose aspirin during initial maternity appointments in relation to NICE guideline recommendations: findings from two clinical audits
audits.tp: Aspirin prophylaxis for hypertensive disorders in pregnancy
audits.st: NICE guideline NG133 for aspirin prophylaxis in moderate or high-risk pregnancy
audits.f: 5.6% of patients (15/266) meeting NG133 criteria for aspirin use remained untreated
audits.r2: Only 31 (63%) of the 49 patients meeting NG133 criteria were prescribed aspirin; 4.5% of the total cohort (13/299) remained untreated overall

audits.t: A Clinical Audit on Identification of Medication Errors in a Tertiary Care Hospital, Lahore
audits.st: National Accreditation Board of Hospitals (NABH) standards (no numeric target stated)

audits.t: An Audit to Evaluate the Etiologies and Preventability of Hyperkalemia in Inpatients: Focus on Modifiable Risk Factors and Medication-Related Triggers
audits.st: Institute for Safe Medication Practices (ISMP) preventability criteria
audits.f: 45.4% of hyperkalaemic episodes deemed preventable; medication-related triggers in 69.1% (ACE inhibitors 34.9%, potassium-sparing diuretics 26.3%); inadequate monitoring 68.1%; inappropriate drug use in renal impairment 49.3%; mortality 5.9%.

audits.t: Clinical Audit of Opioid and Non-Opioid Analgesic Prescribing in Cancer Pain Management at Hayatabad Medical Complex
audits.st: WHO guidelines for cancer pain management (WHO Analgesic Ladder)
audits.f: Opioids prescribed in 69.3% of cases (mainly morphine); non-opioids in 30.7%; appropriate analgesic selection per pain severity in 74.4%; deficiencies in breakthrough pain management (58.5%), laxative prescribing (46.1%), antiemetic prescribing (38.7%) and pain reassessment documentation (42.2%); adverse drug reactions in 29.6% (mainly constipation).

audits.t: Clinical Audit of Indications, Duration, and Documentation of Proton Pump Inhibitor Therapy in Hospitalized Patients
audits.st: Usual clinical treatment guidelines for PPI indication, duration and documentation (not named specifically)
audits.f: Most frequent indication was stress ulcer prophylaxis (40.8%); GERD 25.8%; no documented indication 13.4%; peptic ulcer disease 20.0%. Appropriate duration in 55%, prolonged treatment in 45%. Good documentation of indication in 62.5%, inadequate in 37.5%. Overall 50% of prescriptions judged appropriate.

audits.t: Quality of sepsis management in the Emergency Department at Goulburn Valley Health, Victoria, Australia: A Retrospective Audit
audits.tp: Sepsis management in the emergency department
audits.st: National sepsis benchmarks, local sepsis pathway and electronic Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG)
audits.f: Median time from triage to fluid resuscitation 51 minutes (IQR 32-91.5); median time to antimicrobial infusion 68 minutes (IQR 48-117); 59% received appropriate antimicrobial coverage, 41% did not.

audits.t: Audit of antenatal and delivery care at a midwife obstetric unit, South Africa
audits.st: National guidelines for antenatal and delivery care indicators
audits.f: Most antenatal and delivery care indicators had good compliance (>95%). Gaps: recording of Last Menstrual Period 78.5%, syphilis treatment at antenatal booking 72.7%, repeat syphilis test at 32 weeks 43.4%, completion of basic antenatal care checklist 46.3%; recording of neonate length/head circumference at delivery 76.5%; use of pain relief at delivery 5.4%.

audits.t: An audit of emergency admissions to the adult general surgery department at Pietersburg Hospital, Polokwane, Limpopo Province, South Africa, during an 8-month period in 2021
audits.tp: Emergency general surgery time to theatre
audits.st: Operation within 24 hours of decision for surgery (local benchmark)
audits.f: 61% managed non-operatively; of the 39% requiring surgery, only 24% had their operation within the first 24 hours, the remainder delayed owing to lack of theatre space and/or ICU bed.

audits.t: An audit on the preliminary results of endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography performed in the Limpopo Academic Complex, Polokwane, South Africa
audits.st: Local five-component quality grading of ERCP unit set-up (room set-up, equipment, fluoroscopy, sedation/analgesia, endoscopist/staff), grade 1 (very poor) to grade 5 (highly satisfactory)
