audits.f: Only 7 of 18 allocated theatre slots utilised; sedation and analgesia scored highest (mean grade 4); fluoroscopy scored lowest (mean grade 1.8).

audits.t: Initial management and investigations in acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: an audit
audits.tp: Initial management of acute exacerbation of COPD
audits.st: NICE CG101 for management of acute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD)
audits.f: Adequate ABG in 47.5% (19); CXR 97.5% (39); ECG 92.5% (37); FBC plus U&Es 95% (38); all pyrexial patients received blood cultures; documentation of theophylline use was poor and levels were not measured; compliance with air-driven nebuliser use uncertain due to insufficient documentation.

audits.t: Audit of the Aetiological Investigations Performed in Children with Sensorineural Hearing Loss At Salford
audits.st: British Association of Audiological Physicians protocol for aetiological investigation of sensorineural hearing loss
audits.f: All patients had thorough history and examination; 95% underwent imaging (MRI/CT); 80% received CMV testing; 75% underwent ECG testing; 60% received family hearing tests; only 35% had ophthalmology examinations and 25% underwent urine and genetic testing.

audits.t: Radiological protection in the Neonatal Intensive Care Units (NICUs): a retrospective and observational audit at two teaching hospitals
audits.st: Radiological protection principles for portable neonatal x-rays (beam restriction and shielding)
audits.f: In the observational survey (230 x-rays, 65 neonates, 57 shifts): unsatisfactory beam restriction in 90.1% of chest, 80% of abdomen, and 13% of chest/abdomen x-rays; protective shielding available but not commonly applied. In a linked retrospective review of 498 PACS images, only 17.5% had adequate beam restriction and 0.4% showed evidence of shielding.

audits.t: Audit Implementasi Clinical Pathway Diare Akut di Rumah Sakit Anak dan Bunda Harapan Kita Tahun 2016
audits.st: KARS (Komisi Akreditasi Rumah Sakit) national accreditation standard for clinical pathway implementation
audits.f: Completeness of clinical pathway form filling only 25%; no variation in laboratory examination, nutrition or nursing care, but 41% variation in additional drug use; length of stay 3.3 days.

audits.t: Clinical audit of computed tomography requisition form in a himalayan country, Nepal
audits.st: Completeness and legibility of CT requisition forms (local criteria)
audits.f: Clinical history present in 28%; clinical diagnosis in 64%; 44% of contrast-enhanced procedures requiring IV contrast lacked a renal function test report; last menstrual period was missing on all forms for women of reproductive age.

audits.t: Evaluation of pulmonary computed tomography angiography protocols: A multicenter audit in Togo
audits.st: Optimisation criteria for iodinated contrast media use and acquisition protocols in pulmonary CT angiography
audits.f: Mean injected iodinated contrast volume 67.08±14.21 ml; mean iodine dose 0.31±0.07 gI/kg; bolus test technique used in 75.28%; vascular enhancement insufficient in 7.87% of cases; no significant difference in insufficient enhancement between optimisation factors or between bolus test and bolus tracking.

audits.t: Surgical Operative Notes Compliance with the Standard Guidelines of the Royal College of Surgeons: A Retrospective Clinical Audit at a Tertiary Hospital in Bangalore, India
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons (RCS) of England guidelines for operative note documentation (19 parameters)
audits.f: Surgeon's name, diagnosis, intraoperative findings and procedure documented accurately in 100% of both 45 elective and 30 emergency cases; DVT prophylaxis documentation lower, in 22% (10/45) of elective and 13% (4/30) of emergency cases.

audits.t: An Audit of Antibiotic Usage among Neonates in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: A Prospective Observational Study
audits.tp: Antibiotic usage in the neonatal intensive care unit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Antimicrobials prescribed in 32% (322) of infants, most often for suspected sepsis (48%); amikacin used in 74%; cephalosporin in 8.9%; blood culture positivity 28%; antibiotics stopped after a negative culture in only 40% of infants.

audits.t: Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in Medical Intensive Care Unit: An Audit
audits.st: American Society of Haematology (ASH) guidelines for VTE prophylaxis, with risk assessment by Padua score and IMPROVE VTE RAM
audits.f: Formal risk assessment was not done in any patient; by Padua score 84.66% (149) were high risk but only 51% of these received prophylaxis; by IMPROVE VTE RAM 77.84% (137) were moderate/high risk but only 55.47% received prophylaxis; clinician judgement alone was less accurate (58.52%/64.20%) than either score.

audits.t: Reduction of Tunnelled Haemodialysis Catheters Related Infections by Intervention and Training: A 12 and 18-month Audit
audits.st: CDC/prevention core intervention (care bundle) for bloodstream infection reduction; KDOQI 2006 criteria to define CRBSI
audits.f: CRBSI incidence 2.58 per 1000 catheter days; median catheter use 132 days (IQR 71.25-202.25).
audits.c: CDC core intervention/care bundle for catheter-related bloodstream infection reduction incorporated into routine tunnelled catheter care
audits.r2: CRBSI incidence fell to 1.99 per 1000 catheter days; median catheter use increased to 149.5 days (IQR 83.5-294.5); organisms predominantly Gram-negative.

audits.t: Quality Audit Towards Improvement of Transfusion Services: An Institutional Assessment
audits.st: National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH) five compulsory quality indicators for transfusion services
audits.f: Mean transfusion reaction rate 0.18% (peak 0.9% in March 2020, none in several months); mean wastage rate 12.9% (max 21.7% in August 2020, min 7.2% in October 2020); mean turnaround time <30 minutes for emergency cases (27.11 min) and 140.9 minutes for routine cases.
audits.c: Root-cause analysis with corrective and preventive measures applied for deviations from the quality indicators, within the same monitoring period

audits.t: An Audit of the Length of Bone Marrow Trephine Biopsy in Adult Patients: A Cross-sectional Study
audits.st: WHO recommended minimum adequate trephine biopsy length ≥1.5 cm before processing
audits.f: 1042 (90.2%) biopsies met the ≥1.5 cm recommended length (Group A), 97 in Group B (1-1.4 cm), 16 in Group C (0.5-0.9 cm); longer biopsies associated with more conclusive diagnosis (p=0.02), though Groups A and B did not differ significantly (p=0.9).

audits.t: Completeness and Accessibility of Oral Cancer Discharge Summaries: A Retrospective Clinical Audit
audits.st: Local standardised 28-parameter discharge summary completeness checklist (patient identification, clinical history, treatment, discharge information, TNM staging)
audits.f: 54/93 (58%) discharge summaries were available in the institutional electronic system (DIAS); of these, 35.2% scored fully complete (28/28) and 31.5% scored 27/28; mean score 24.83±5.85; most frequently omitted items were the departmental stamp (42.6%) and TNM staging (40.7%).

audits.t: Clinical audit of Clostridium difficile management
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Management of Medical Records at the Surgical Department of a Tertiary Hospital in Blackpool, UK: Results of an Internal Audit
audits.st: Good Medical Practice and Good Surgical Practice guidelines for real-time, accurate, legible, comprehensive, honest, non-judgemental, up-to-date records
audits.f: not reported
audits.r2: Recording of patient ID, reviewing physician's name, examination findings, management plan and final NEWS all improved; reviewer name, date and management plan showed over 80% improvement, the rest ranged from 40-60%.

audits.t: An Analysis between Patient Demographics and Non-attendances in General Surgery Clinics at an NHS Trust: An Audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Non-attendance (DNA) rates correlated with age, gender, ethnicity, subspecialty and distance from hospital.

audits.t: Audit of Lymph Node Sampling in Colorectal Carcinoma Resections-implication for Prognosis and Management
audits.tp: Lymph node sampling adequacy in colorectal carcinoma
audits.st: Adequate lymph node yield (≥12 nodes) for colorectal cancer staging
audits.f: 62 (93.9%) reports commented on the search for lymph nodes; attached mesentery documented in 37.9%; lymph nodes present in 78.8% of specimens, of which 53.8% were tumour-positive; lymph node count ≥12 was significantly associated with finding tumour-positive nodes (p<0.05).

audits.t: Prescriptions Audit for Antibiotics among Outpatients in the Department of Periodontics
audits.tp: Antibiotic prescribing against essential medicines list
audits.st: WHO core drug use indicators and National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) 2015
audits.f: 614 of 849 patients received antibiotics; only 74.5% of antibiotics were from the NLEM 2015; amoxicillin+clavulanic acid commonest (61.2%, 87.80% of total cost of 146,669.82 INR); only 9.7% prescribed by generic name.

audits.t: Improving Alcohol Use Screening on A University Campus with AUDIT-C: A Reflective Practice Report
audits.st: WHO Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test-Concise (AUDIT-C) routine screening for alcohol use disorder
audits.f: Alcohol use disorder was not being routinely assessed before implementation of AUDIT-C screening.
audits.c: Implementation of routine AUDIT-C alcohol use screening at the university primary care centre
audits.r2: Statistically significant improvement in alcohol use disorder identification rates after implementation, chi-square X2(1, N=991)=42.97, p=.001.

audits.t: Comprehensive Death Audit Analysis from a Single District COVID Hospital in Madhya Pradesh, India
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 70 of 118 audited deaths were male; highest proportion (24.28%) in the 51-60 age group; comorbidities associated with increased mortality (42.37%); Remdesivir administered in 39.83% of cases; longer ICU stays linked to higher mortality.

audits.t: QUALITY OF NURSING RECORDS IN INTENSIVE CARE: EVALUATION THROUGH A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT
audits.tp: Nursing documentation quality in intensive care
audits.st: Local completeness criteria: Quality if Percentage of Completion (PoC) ≥80%; Incomplete ≤15%; Not Completed <5%; Incorrect 0%
audits.f: No records met all quality criteria; mean PoC was 46% Complete, 43% Incomplete, 10% Not Completed, 1% Incorrect.

audits.t: Clinical Audit of Ovulation Induction at Qena university and Qus Hospitals
audits.st: ACOG and NICE guidelines for ovulation induction
audits.f: Significant differences between hospitals in history, examination, male assessment and hormonal profile (p<0.001); letrozole more used at Qena, clomiphene citrate more used at Qus (p<0.001); infertility counselling, ovulation monitoring and anovulation assessment lacking at both; ovulation success (p=0.658) and pregnancy incidence (p=0.401) were similar between sites.

audits.t: An audit of maternal near-miss and mortality cases in a tertiary care rural teaching hospital in Eastern India: A 2-year retrospective analytical case–control study
audits.st: WHO maternal near-miss criteria
audits.f: Maternal mortality ratio 223 and near-miss ratio 501 per lakh live births; near-miss:mortality ratio 2.25; ICU admission in 2.1% of obstetric admissions; obstetric haemorrhage was the commonest near-miss cause (47.47%) and eclampsia/pre-eclampsia the commonest mortality cause (29.5%); 81.8% fulfilled near-miss criteria at admission, 4.5% were brought in dead.

audits.t: Medical Audit of Screening Mammography at a Tertiary Referral Hospital Using the 5th Edition of Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System
audits.st: Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS), 5th edition, medical audit metrics
audits.f: Cancer detection rate 4.6 per 1000; treating category 3 as positive versus negative changed positive predictive value by 1.3% (6.0% vs 7.3%) and recall rate by 1.3% (7.3% vs 6.0%); results were appropriate for the newly revised BI-RADS targets.

audits.t: Hand Hygiene Audit and Practices among Resident Doctors and Nursing Staff Working at Pediatric and Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: An Observational Study
audits.st: WHO hand hygiene practice recommendations
audits.f: 160/172 (93%) observations demonstrated hand hygiene practice; adequate performance in 69.4%; alcohol-based hand rub used more than soap; among 20 doctors and 24 nurses surveyed, 97% had received hand hygiene education in the past year and nearly 100% used alcohol rub consistently.

audits.t: A Prescription Audit Utilizing the World Health Organization Recommended Key Medication Use Indicators at a Tertiary Care Hospital, India
audits.tp: Prescription quality against WHO drug use indicators
audits.st: WHO core drug use indicators
audits.f: 67% of prescriptions used a generic name; 85.6% included the diagnosis; average 11.45 drugs per prescription; clinical examination mentioned in 53.8%; allergy history missing in 94%.

audits.t: Determinants of TB/HIV coinfection-related deaths audited using the TB death checklist from health facilities in Rwanda
audits.st: National TB Program TB death checklist/audit process
audits.f: 68.2% of death audit reports were for men; 70.6% of deaths were TB-related; smear-negative pulmonary TB (aOR 1.97, p=0.082), TB retreatment (aOR 2.03, p<0.007) and severe malnutrition (aOR 1.71, p=0.002) were associated with HIV coinfection.

audits.t: Can medical audit change electromyographic practice?
audits.tp: Variation in EMG practice across centres
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Baseline variation in number of examinations per patient and techniques used for polyneuropathy assessment.
audits.c: International collaboration and mutual influence among physicians through shared medical audit.
audits.r2: Clear change towards more uniform practice for F-wave and motor nerve studies; only minor changes for sensory nerve conduction and muscle studies; reduced use of time-consuming near-nerve sensory and quantitative muscle studies.

audits.t: Management of interstitial lung disease: an audit at a university teaching hospital in Saudi Arabia.
audits.tp: Management of interstitial lung disease against guidelines
audits.st: Published guidelines for management of interstitial lung disease
audits.f: A specific diagnosis was reached in 82/122 (67%) of cases; the undiagnosed third were older and less likely to receive immunosuppressive therapy, with a poorer prognosis; surgical lung biopsy was diagnostic in 98% of cases where performed.

audits.t: An audit of distribution and use of guidelines for management of head injury.
audits.tp: Head injury guideline dissemination and use
audits.st: Effective distribution and use of a head injury management guidelines card
audits.f: 131/163 (80%) responded; 103/131 (79%) aware of guidelines, 82/131 (63%) had possessed a card, only 36/82 (44%) acquired it in the induction pack; 98/107 (92%) found it useful, 89/110 (81%) referred to it
audits.c: Modified distribution of the guidelines card (wider display in departments and supply to A&E consultants)
audits.r2: 52/83 (63%) had received cards (no increase) but 71/83 (86%) were aware of the guidelines

audits.t: Impact of a national audit project on gynaecologists in Scotland.
audits.tp: Impact of national audit project on gynaecological practice
audits.st: Gynaecology Audit Project in Scotland (GAPS) recommendations for induced abortion, endometriosis and vulvar carcinoma care
audits.f: 90% response rate; 96% (109/113) recalled receiving feedback material; significant self-reported practice change in 7 of 12 specific elements of care
audits.c: National audit project feedback and recommendations circulated to gynaecologists
audits.r2: Over two-thirds of respondents said they had reconsidered or changed practice for induced abortion and endometriosis

audits.t: Telemedicine in support of peacekeeping operations overseas: an audit.
audits.tp: Telemedicine support for deployed military units
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 53 consults on 47 patients; telemedicine affected evacuation decisions 13/47 times with a net reduction of 9 evacuations; management changed in 30/47 cases

audits.t: A risk management audit: are we complying with the national guidelines for sedation by non-anaesthetists?
audits.tp: Sedation documentation compliance with national guidelines
audits.st: National guidelines for sedation by non-anaesthetists (documentation of consent, risk assessment, monitoring, oxygen use, discharge advice)
audits.f: Case note review before the form showed poor documentation of consent, risk assessment, monitoring, oxygen use and discharge advice
audits.c: Introduction of a preprinted post-sedation advice/audit form plus staff education
audits.r2: Use of the form significantly improved documentation of most parameters measured

audits.t: Suitability of breastfeeding facilities outside the home: an audit of baby change rooms in shopping centres.
audits.st: NMAA (Nursing Mothers' Association of Australia) Baby Care Room criteria (8 criteria)
audits.f: Only 48% of shopping centres had baby care rooms; only 43.7% of baby care rooms met all 8 NMAA criteria (kappa 0.52 for reliability)

audits.t: A quality assurance audit of a drug information service.
audits.tp: Quality of written drug information responses
audits.st: Internally developed criteria for quality of written drug information responses, informed by a survey of Canadian hospital DI centres
audits.f: Completeness of response rated 9.5/10 by users; impact on patient therapy rated lowest at 8.3/10; committee review found >90% compliance with criteria including literature correlation, documentation and conclusions.

audits.t: Audit on the degree of application of universal precautions in a haemodialysis unit.
audits.st: Universal (standard) precautions: hand washing and glove use
audits.f: Gloves used on only 18.7% of 364 opportunities; hand washing after patient contact on 32.4% of 273 opportunities; hand washing before an activity on only 3% of occasions

audits.t: Using clinical audit in practice: a pilot peer review project.
audits.tp: Peer review clinical audit in general dental practice
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Objective assessment of voice intervention: a clinical audit.
audits.st: Timescales for care episodes of dysphonic client groups, based on Lockhart et al. 1997 research findings
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Bleeding peptic ulcers: audit of eradication treatment for H pylori.
audits.tp: H. pylori testing and eradication in bleeding peptic ulcer
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 62% confirmed H. pylori positive (20% had no biopsies); eradication treatment given to 49/89 patients with an 81% eradication rate among those tested

audits.t: [Audit of the treatment of arterial hypertension in specialized consultation].
audits.tp: Blood pressure control in hypertension clinic
audits.st: Blood pressure control target of <140/90 mmHg
audits.f: Mean physician-measured BP fell from 179/107 to 148/91 mmHg and nurse-measured BP from 164/96 to 143/83 mmHg during follow-up; many patients remained above 140/90 mmHg target

audits.t: Adherence to standards of care and implications of body temperature measurement in trauma patients.
audits.tp: Body temperature recording in trauma patients
audits.st: Standard that trauma patients have body temperature recorded (source not stated)
audits.f: Temperature was recorded in only 40% of records, ranging 87-100.6F; 33% of patients had hypothermia (<=96.6F); a significant inverse relationship was found between temperature and Injury Severity Score.

audits.t: An audit of appropriate use of blood products in adult patients in a Venezuelan general university hospital.
audits.st: Pre-set criteria for appropriate use of blood products
audits.f: Appropriate use overall was 51.3% (72% Medicine, 36% Surgery, 56% Emergency, 47% Obstetrics); no department exceeded 80% appropriate use

audits.t: Meperidine utilization and compliance with Agency for Health Care Policy and Research guidelines in a tertiary care hospital.
audits.tp: Meperidine prescribing compliance with AHCPR guidelines
audits.st: Agency for Health Care Policy and Research (AHCPR) guidelines for meperidine use in acute and chronic cancer pain
audits.f: 124/157 (79.8%) of nonobstetric inpatients receiving meperidine were in conflict with AHCPR guidelines, most often for suboptimal dosing or treatment of chronic pain

audits.t: Management of sickness absence: a quality improvement study from Slovenia.
audits.st: Locally agreed standard for reducing cases causing problems for the sickness leave approval committee
audits.f: 44% of cases were reported by the committee of experts as causing problems
audits.c: Feedback to GPs, a guideline on record keeping and a guideline (AID) on processing medical documentation

audits.t: Day surgery: a post operative audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Almost half of patients could not be contacted by telephone at 24 hours; 7.1% had severe pain despite analgesics; 14.3% had wound care queries; 78.6% would undergo day surgery again

audits.t: A 2-year audit of perioperative mortality in Malaysian hospitals.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall crude mortality 0.34% (715 deaths in 211,354 surgeries); 62.52% of deaths occurred within 2 days of surgery and 85.87% were related to emergency procedures; shortfalls identified in critical care facilities, supervision, unnecessary surgery in moribund patients and inadequate preoperative optimisation.

audits.t: Audit of hysterectomies at the Aga Khan Hospital, Nairobi: justification of operative indications.
audits.st: Justification of hysterectomy indication by pathological confirmation
audits.f: Overall 86% justification rate (90.1% for confirmable diagnoses, 75.9% for non-confirmable diagnoses)

audits.t: An audit of the management of malaria in a Tanzanian district hospital.
audits.tp: Management of falciparum malaria in a district hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Chloroquine effective in 1128/1494 (79%) cases; 68 patients died (mostly under 5 years), 30 of them within 2 days of admission

audits.t: A prostatectomy audit: phase I--insights and questions.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Phase I of the audit aimed to define a minimum data set and data-collection tool and produced a tentative model forecasting post-operative stay

audits.t: Lessons to be learnt from a perinatal audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Fetal abnormality was the commonest cause of death (24%), followed by spontaneous prematurity (19%) and infection (11%); avoidable factors detected in 25% of all deaths

audits.t: Autopsy rate and a clinicopathological audit in an Australian metropolitan hospital--cause for concern?
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Autopsy rate declined from 47% to 19% at the index hospital between 1979 and 1989; major misdiagnoses found in 18/124 (14.5%) autopsies, relevant to management in 8 cases (6%)

audits.t: Audit of practice based cervical smear programme: completion of the cycle.
audits.st: Practice-based cervical screening coverage and effective abnormal-result management
audits.f: 2356/2767 (85.1%) had a test; coverage in women aged 20-25 was 45.8% (146/319)
audits.c: Changes to the screening programme made after analysing the first five years' data, including inviting women aged 20-25 to attend
audits.r2: 2498/2790 (89.5%) had a test; coverage in women aged 20-25 rose to 82.5% (282/342); referral for abnormalities requiring hospital review rose, especially in women aged 25-34 (44% to 70%)

audits.t: Audit exposes flawed blood sampling for "digoxin levels".
audits.tp: Blood sampling timing for digoxin level monitoring
audits.st: Appropriate blood sampling timing for digoxin levels defined as at least 6 hours after the last dose
audits.f: 9/22 requisitions with documented timing were inappropriate; among the 150 with estimated timing, 45 were inappropriate; premature sampling was associated with higher digoxin concentrations (1.6 nM vs 1.0 nM, p<0.001)

audits.t: An improved 'interim discharge letter' a successful outcome from audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: General practitioners were dissatisfied with the hospital's unstructured interim discharge letters, written by house officers shortly after discharge, with a separate copy of the discharge drug list.
audits.c: A new, structured form of interim discharge letter was introduced (including the discharge prescription), developed after discussing needs with general practitioners.
audits.r2: The new discharge letter was well received by hospital staff and general practitioners; paperwork for junior doctors was reduced by including the prescription in the letter; the layout was further modified in light of feedback.

audits.t: Perinatal mortality in Norway: experience with perinatal audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Perinatal mortality in 1989 was 7.8 per 1000 births; committees in every county make local guidelines and audit all perinatal deaths, focusing on avoidable and possibly avoidable factors and suboptimal care.

audits.t: The Mentakab Hypertension Project. Part IV--Hypertension care: is it adequate? A criterion-based audit of hypertension care in a hospital.
audits.st: Locally pre-defined criteria for adequate hypertension care (assessment, blood pressure control, investigation, side-effect surveillance, patient knowledge)
audits.f: Only 18% of patients had achieved adequate blood pressure control; assessment was inadequate; none screened for secondary causes though 16% had basic investigations, 5% had target-organ assessment, 2% were screened for other cardiovascular risk factors; only 5% had surveillance of drug side-effects; 45% demonstrated adequate knowledge of complications; non-drug treatment was not used.

audits.t: Gentamicin therapy: medical audit.
audits.st: Clinical indication criteria for gentamicin use (e.g. neonatal septicaemia, meningitis, serious staphylococcal infection, immunocompromise)
audits.f: Gentamicin use was considered indicated in 71 cases (62% under 1 year); all cultured bacteria were sensitive; 29 cases were prescribed gentamicin unnecessarily (bronchial asthma 7, bronchiolitis 6, gastroenteritis with dehydration 8); 9 patients developed gentamicin-related nephrotoxicity.

audits.t: Two stage audit of cerebrovascular and coronary heart disease risk factor recording: the effect of case finding and screening programmes.
audits.st: Recording of cardiovascular risk factors (blood pressure, smoking, alcohol, weight, height) in GP records
audits.f: Blood pressure was recorded in 68.0% of records; recording of smoking, alcohol and weight was lower.
audits.c: Case finding and screening programmes; practices with organised systems of data collection had higher recording levels
audits.r2: Mean level of recording of all risk factors increased between the two audits; increases in recording of smoking habit, alcohol consumption and weight were statistically significant.

audits.t: Experience with biliary audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: No mortality; duct exploration rate 17%; infection rate 8.6%; re-operation rate for retained bile duct stone 1.6%; bile culture positive in 66/278 (23.7%), most commonly coliforms and streptococci.
audits.c: Antibiotic policy changed as a result of the audit findings

audits.t: Was that hysterectomy really necessary? Audit of operative justification at the Aga Khan University Medical Centre, Karachi.
audits.st: Locally defined validation criteria for justifying hysterectomy (preoperative diagnosis verified by pathology, or defined validation criteria where no pathology expected)
audits.f: In 250 (66.5%) cases where pathology was expected, hysterectomy was justified if preoperative diagnosis was verified by pathology; in 126 (33.5%) cases validation criteria were used; justification rates were 83% recurrent uterine bleeding, 85% adenomyosis, 90% adnexal masses/endometrial carcinoma, 95% fibroids, 97% pelvic relaxation, 100% pregnancy catastrophe/endometriosis/chronic PID/premalignant disease; overall 92.0% of hysterectomies were justified.

audits.t: Audit of ranitidine administration in parenteral nutrient solutions.
audits.st: Locally developed criteria for justification, process indicators and outcome measures for ranitidine use in parenteral nutrition solutions
audits.f: No inappropriate uses of ranitidine were identified; patients with renal impairment tended to be underdosed; nasogastric aspirate pH testing was not performed in 17 of 22 patients who needed it; gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 2 patients who were not monitored for gastric pH and were underdosed.
audits.c: not reported (a programme to promote safe and effective use was being developed)

audits.t: Human albumin solutions: an audit of use in three major metropolitan hospitals. Subcommittee of the Victorian Drug Usage Advisory Committee.
audits.st: Australasian Society of Blood Transfusion recommendations for use of human albumin solutions
audits.f: 84% of forms were returned; the products were used for appropriate indications (e.g. hypovolaemia, hypoalbuminaemia) and not for inappropriate indications such as nutritional support or wound healing, but there was marked variation in usage level for a given indication between the three hospitals.

audits.t: Auditing the hospital care of dying patients.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Describes an audit tool for assessing hospital care of dying patients based on palliative/hospice care components, illustrated by an audit at one acute care hospital.

audits.t: Audit of outpatients: entering the loop.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: New referrals as a proportion of consultations varied from 15% to 34% across 10 clinics; source of referral and type of pain varied widely between clinics (e.g. GP referrals 22-78%, low back pain 10.8-55.2%) and could not be explained by referral pattern differences alone.

audits.t: The Cambridge Audit System in a service hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Benchmarking inadvertent perioperative hypothermia guidelines with the National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence.
audits.st: NICE guideline CG65 (April 2008) for prevention of inadvertent perioperative hypothermia
audits.f: Local practice guidelines largely matched NICE guidance except for the preoperative phase; baseline incidence of hypothermia was 1.5%.
audits.c: Preoperative phase steps added to local policy and procedures per NICE guidance and implemented immediately; follow-up audits every 3 months for 18 months to ensure compliance.
audits.r2: Follow-up audits showed the incidence of hypothermia fell from a previous 1.5% to 0.3%.

audits.t: An audit of adult tetanus immunity.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: A date of previous immunisation was recalled by 38% (49/129); immunisation was documented in 34% (44/129) of charts; of 22 patients with both a recall and documented date, 82% (18/22) had accurate recall; only 19% (25/129) kept written personal immunisation records.

audits.t: Audit of the activity of a same day ward.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported specific baseline figures; wide use of the ward across disciplines, one in five patients aged over 70.
audits.c: Increased use of discharge notes and follow-up arrangements by medical staff; preadmission visits by a community nurse.
audits.r2: Significant falls in complication and delayed discharge rates across the three audits (exact figures not reported).

audits.t: Use of peri-operative antibiotics in abdominal surgery: a criterion audit.
audits.st: Appropriate peri-operative antibiotic therapy (not further specified)
audits.f: 39% of patients received inappropriate antibiotic therapy

audits.t: Hydrotherapy management of low back pain: a quality improvement project.
audits.tp: Hydrotherapy management of low back pain
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Highly significant beneficial response to hydrotherapy in area of pain, pain intensity, range of motion and ability to perform activities of daily living (t(67)=9.2, p<0.001).
audits.c: Improved documentation, standardised assessment, re-worked hydrotherapy programme, and regular assessment of patients within planned time-frames

audits.t: Audit of investigation and follow-up of patients with raised monoclonal proteins.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 9% of monoclonal proteins detected were not followed up at all; a urine Bence-Jones test was not requested in 12% of those regularly followed up.

audits.t: Prospective audit of aminoglycoside usage in a general hospital with assessments of clinical processes and adverse clinical outcomes.
audits.st: Clinical and microbiological criteria for appropriate aminoglycoside prescribing and monitoring (not further specified)
audits.f: 85.6% of 278 documented prescriptions were appropriate; serum assays performed in 77.6% of 511 patients but uninterpretable in 52.6% of 3079 assayed cases; 5.6% received potentially toxic doses.

audits.t: A prospective audit of the use and costs of myelography in a regional neuroscience unit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Proportion of patients submitted to myelography ranged from 7% to 28% between consultants; median admission-to-request, request-to-myelography and myelography-to-discharge intervals were 0, 1 and 3 days.

audits.t: Rapid Ascent From Zero Quality to International Organization for Standardization Accreditation
audits.st: ISO accreditation standards, measured using the Stepwise Laboratory Quality Improvement Process Towards Accreditation (SLIPTA) audit tool
audits.f: Median compliance score 44%; the lowest-scoring laboratory (Hai Duong) entered at 28%.
audits.c: SLMTA (Strengthening Laboratory Management Toward Accreditation): a year-long, structured quality improvement curriculum including projects and mentorship.
audits.r2: Median scores rose from 44% to 78% compliance; Hai Duong rose from 28% to the highest score, 86%, and was accredited five months after completing the programme without additional external support.

audits.t: Intraoperative pathologic consultation. An audit of 1,000 recent consecutive cases.
audits.tp: Accuracy of intraoperative frozen section consultation
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Retrospective review of 1,000 consecutive intraoperative consultations assessing accuracy as a quality assurance exercise; indications and specimen types have changed over time.

audits.t: An audit of blood component therapy in a Canadian general teaching hospital.
audits.st: Predetermined criteria for appropriate use of packed red cells, fresh frozen plasma and albumin (source not stated)
audits.f: 88% of 520 red cell transfusion episodes appropriate; 90% of 106 FFP episodes appropriate; 64% of 187 albumin episodes appropriate.

audits.t: Prospective application of an implementation framework to improve postoperative nutrition care processes: Evaluation of a mixed methods implementation study
audits.st: ERAS (Enhanced Recovery After Surgery) postoperative diet guidelines
audits.f: A pre-implementation audit identified gaps in nutrition-related care practices against ERAS guidelines for older surgical patients (no overall pre-implementation percentage given).
audits.c: Facilitated implementation strategy guided by the i-PARIHS framework, comprising 17 discrete facilitation activities identified through qualitative interviews and field notes.
audits.r2: Early postoperative diet upgrade was well adopted (79%) and appropriate for 89% of patients; fidelity (protocol delivered as intended) was 59%; intervention-ward patients had higher adjusted odds of receiving early nutrition post-implementation (adjusted OR 6.5, 95% CI 1.9-22.4, P=0.01).

audits.t: Emerging evidence of the value of health assessments for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in the primary healthcare setting.
audits.tp: Indigenous health preventive care continuous quality improvement
audits.st: National guide to preventive health assessment for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people
audits.f: A structured continuous quality improvement (CQI) programme was shown to improve delivery of preventive health assessments and use of evidence-based guidelines (no single overall percentage given).
audits.c: Research-based continuous quality improvement (CQI) initiative involving clinical audits and systems assessments.

audits.t: Total parenteral nutrition: a four-year audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 147 patients discharged healthy (2 after home TPN); overall mortality 36% (53% in ICU patients); 74.8% of survivors showed improved nutritional status; metabolic complication rate 2.9%, catheter sepsis rate 3.6%.
audits.c: Changes made to protocols and staffing patterns, and improved patient selection

audits.t: Prospective-concurrent audits and medical consultation for platelet transfusions.
audits.st: Appropriate-use criteria for platelet concentrate transfusion, applied via mandatory pretransfusion review
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Prospective-concurrent audit and mandatory medical consultation/review of platelet transfusion requests
audits.r2: A 56 percent decrease in the use of platelet concentrates was associated with prospective-concurrent audits and medical consultation.

audits.t: An Improvement Effort to Optimize Electronically Generated Hospital Discharge Instructions.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Discharge delays due to hospital discharge instruction (HDI) errors averaged 3.4 per month; parents' rating of how understandable HDIs were averaged 2.35; only 9% of paediatric residents agreed the electronic discharge process was easy to use.
audits.c: Redesign of the electronic discharge navigator and HDI to address advance preparation, formatting, standard templates/language, and translation into non-English languages, using quality improvement methodology.
audits.r2: Discharge delays due to HDI errors decreased to a mean of 0.5 per month; parents' understandability ratings improved to 2.74 (P=.05); resident agreement that the process was easy to use increased to 67% (P<.001).

audits.t: Open access fibresigmoidoscopy: a comparative audit of efficacy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Diagnostic yield remained about 40% and was similar between open access and hospital-initiated procedures; referral was considered justified in 475 (88%) open access patients; yield was low (19.8%) in patients under 40 and with abdominal pain/constipation, but high (90-100%) for diarrhoea and rectal bleeding.

audits.t: Impact of nursing staff and patient education in improving inpatient heart failure care: a closed audit cycle.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: IAEA support to radiotherapy dosimetry
audits.st: IAEA/WHO reference dosimetry postal audit programme (5% acceptance limit)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Application of refined management in prevention and control of the coronavirus disease 2019 epidemic in non-isolated areas of a general hospital
audits.tp: COVID-19 infection prevention and control compliance
audits.st: Locally developed standards for COVID-19 prevention and control based on refined management theory
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Refined management: developed local prevention/control standards, systematic implementation of measures, 'gridding' audits, and communication supported by information technology.
audits.r2: Mask-wearing, epidemiological history screening and medical supplies disinfection rates were all 100%; accuracy of mask-wearing by patients/families was 73.79% and hand hygiene compliance was 40.78%; no hospital-acquired COVID-19 infections occurred among staff.

audits.t: Emergency laparotomy success – optimisation or triage?
audits.st: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA); Emergency Laparotomy Collaborative bundle (sepsis screening/antibiotics within 1 hour, theatre within 6 hours of decision, consultant-led care, goal-directed fluid therapy, ICU admission)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Provincial Door-to-Needle Improvement Initiative Results in Improved Patient Outcomes Across an Entire Population
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median door-to-needle time was 70.0 minutes (IQR 51-93).
audits.c: Provincial improvement collaborative: interdisciplinary teams at each stroke centre, 3 workshops and closing celebration, site visits, webinars, and data audit and feedback.
audits.r2: Median door-to-needle time reduced to 39.0 minutes (IQR 27-58), P<0.0001; discharge home from acute care increased from 45.6% to 59.5% (P<0.0001); median 90-day home time increased from 43.3 to 53.6 days (P=0.0015); in-hospital mortality decreased from 14.5% to 10.5% (P=0.0990).

audits.t: National variations in perioperative assessment and surgical management of Crohn’s disease: a multicentre study
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Patient Journey Champions: A project to facilitate delivery of effective board rounds for inpatients, aiding flow through the hospital
audits.st: Hospital standard operating procedure for board rounds
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Patient Journey Champion campaign: education sessions for junior doctors on board round structure, aiming to empower them to lead effective board rounds.
audits.r2: An improvement in the quality of board rounds compared with baseline was observed, along with a positive effect on length of stay on the acute admissions ward.

audits.t: Effect of data collection method on results of serum digoxin concentration audit.
audits.tp: Appropriateness of serum digoxin concentration testing
audits.st: Pharmacy and therapeutics committee-approved criteria for appropriate indication, sampling time and dose adjustment for serum digoxin concentration (SDC) testing
audits.f: Concurrent audit found 18.7% of SDCs were ordered without an appropriate indication, 16.4% were sampled at an incorrect time, and 8.2% did not result in dosage adjustment when indicated; significantly more SDCs met standards under concurrent audit than under retrospective chart-review audit.

audits.t: Patient and clinician national registry synergy to enhance quality improvement in United Kingdom IBD surgery – is there appetite?
audits.st: IBD Standards (key performance indicators defining high-quality IBD care)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Patients with Opioid Use Disorder and Chronic Pain: Improving Pain Assessment Documentation
audits.tp: Pain assessment documentation in opioid use disorder
audits.st: Standard of care: pain assessed and documented as a vital sign at each clinical encounter
audits.f: A baseline audit of patient charts found that pain assessment of patients diagnosed with opioid use disorder and chronic pain was not being documented consistently by providers (medical doctors and advanced practice nurses) or medical assistants.

audits.t: An audit of electroconvulsive therapy.
audits.tp: ECT practice compared with published guidelines
audits.st: Published guidelines for optimal use of electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)
audits.f: The audit identified several areas of clinical practice that did not comply with recommended standards for ECT (specific items not detailed in the abstract).

audits.t: Deimplementing Continuous Pulse Oximetry in Patients With Bronchiolitis-What Are We Waiting For?
audits.tp: Guideline-discordant continuous pulse oximetry in bronchiolitis
audits.st: National guidelines discouraging continuous pulse oximetry in mild-to-moderate bronchiolitis patients not receiving supplemental oxygen
audits.f: Guideline-discordant continuous pulse oximetry use at baseline was 53%.
audits.c: Audit and feedback, and educational outreach (traditional quality improvement strategies) to deimplement continuous pulse oximetry.
audits.r2: Use of guideline-discordant pulse oximetry declined from 53% to 23% during the study period compared with historical controls; the strategies were rated acceptable, appropriate, feasible and safe by clinicians and nurses, generally at 90% or more agreement.

audits.t: The impact of COVID‐19 on acute non‐invasive ventilation services: A case for change
audits.st: 2018 British Thoracic Society (BTS) quality standard: NIV within 60 minutes of the decision-making arterial blood gas (decision-to-mask time)
audits.f: Median decision-to-mask time 61 minutes (IQR 43-77); deaths 4 (4.8%); blood gas pH 7.34 (7.30-7.37); pCO2 8.59 (7.79-10.37).
audits.r2: 45.8% fewer patients received NIV; median decision-to-mask time increased to 132 minutes (IQR 65-179), p<0.0001; deaths 8 (17.8%), p=0.014, associated with lower blood gas pH 7.62 (6.53-9.17)/higher pCO2, p=0.019/p<0.001.

audits.t: Preventing Wrong Tooth Extraction
audits.st: Local best practice (LBP) for tooth extraction record-keeping, based on national guidelines and standards
audits.f: Retrospective audit of tooth extraction record-keeping identified deficiencies against local best practice (LBP).
audits.c: Computerised safety checklist compliant with LBP, comprising a pre-operative safety check, a pause to re-confirm the surgical site, and a post-operative record-keeping proforma, linked to record-keeping software, provided to 11 clinicians.
audits.r2: At week 10, 67% of records contained the computerised safety checklist, a 50% increase in overall compliance with LBP for tooth extraction compared with baseline.

audits.t: Reflections on opioid stewardship and the journey to improving intraoperative storage and handling
audits.tp: Opioid and controlled substance storage/disposal in the operating room
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Opioids and other controlled substances (e.g. ketamine, midazolam) were routinely left unattended on anaesthesia medication carts and disposed of in open bins, making theft/diversion a simple task (qualitative finding, no numeric percentage given).
audits.c: Safe Medication Practices Working Group formed (multidisciplinary); departmental rounds using a personal narrative to explain the 'why'; development of an opioid disposal container with holding rack permanently installed on anaesthesia medication carts.

audits.t: Notifying general practitioners about deaths in hospital: an audit.
audits.tp: Notification of GPs about hospital deaths
audits.st: Established method of immediate telephone notification of a patient's death in hospital, with a follow-up hospital letter
audits.f: An immediate telephone call took place in only 58% of cases and the hospital letter was sent within one week in only 49% of cases.
audits.c: Issue of a unit medical circular to hospital staff requesting more prompt notification
audits.r2: The proportions of prompt telephone notification (58%) and timely letters (49%) were unaltered by the issue of the unit medical circular.

audits.t: A comparison of a home parenteral nutrition service with the current European (ESPEN) guidelines on chronic intestinal failure in adults.
audits.tp: Home parenteral nutrition service guideline compliance
audits.st: European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism (ESPEN) 2016 and 2020 guidelines on chronic intestinal failure/home parenteral nutrition (183 recommendations)
audits.f: Overall compliance with the 2016 guideline recommendations was 80%; compliance with the 2020 guideline recommendations was 65%. 24 of the 2020 guideline's recommendations showed noncompliance, 15 of these due to absence of a nutrition support team and dedicated intestinal failure unit.

audits.t: Raising a colostomy--results of a prospective surgical audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Only 53 (48%) of patients saw a stomatherapist preoperatively (86% elective vs 15% urgent); tension of the colostomy caused complications in 29 cases (26%), including the only colostomy-related death; registrars with fewer than 5 colostomies were trained mainly by other registrars rather than consultants.

audits.t: #TheUglyTruth? A Qualitative Evaluation of Outcomes Photography on Instagram: Introducing the SEPIA Scoring System
audits.st: Standards for the Evaluation of Photographs In Aesthetics (SEPIA), a nine-point scoring system and grading scale
audits.f: Average score 4/9 (medium quality); approximately 40% of posts scored in the low-quality range; PRSS (Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery specialty/subspecialty) practitioners scored higher (4.5/9 v 3.1/9, P=0.002) and had fewer low-quality posts (22% v 54%, P=0.001) than non-PRSS providers; low-quality photographs most often seen with rhinoplasty (30% v 7%, P<0.00001) and lip filler (60% v 33%, P=0.0001).

audits.t: Surgical audit in a district general hospital: a stimulus for improving patient care.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 652 patients required operative treatment; 408 did not, most admitted with abdominal pain (179), with a final diagnosis made in only 76; 94 patients (8.9%) were admitted for more than three weeks, 42.5% of these because of poor home/social circumstances.

audits.t: Infection prevention and control in tertiary care hospitals of Bangladesh: results from WHO infection prevention and control assessment framework (IPCAF)
audits.tp: Infection prevention and control (IPC) level assessment
audits.st: WHO Infection Prevention and Control Assessment Framework (IPCAF)
audits.f: Median IPCAF score 355.0/800 (IQR 252.5-397.5); 73% of hospitals scored 'Basic' IPC level, 18% 'Intermediate'; around 90% lacked an active IPC monitoring and audit system; 64% had IPC orientation/training for new employees but only 30% had regular ongoing IPC training.

audits.t: The use of nasogastric tubes after abdominal surgery--a criteria audit.
audits.tp: Nasogastric tube use after abdominal surgery
audits.st: Locally defined criteria for appropriate nasogastric tube use and duration after gastrointestinal surgery
audits.f: 32.5% (65/200) of patients had a nasogastric tube inserted perioperatively; 20% vomited while the tube was in situ; there was poor correlation between aspirated fluid volume and timing of tube removal, suggesting tubes were inserted too often and left in situ too long.

audits.t: Audit of work at a medical centre for the homeless over one year.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Certain health problems were more common among the homeless than the general population, but the overall range resembled general practice; registration with GPs was much less common among the homeless, and a high proportion of hospital referrals did not lead to appropriate treatment.

audits.t: Thermal care for preterm infants in the delivery room has not been compromised since the routine adoption of delayed cord clamping in our unit
audits.tp: Delayed cord clamping and admission normothermia
audits.st: National Neonatal Audit Programme (NNAP) standard: 90% preterm admission normothermia; NNAP national average delayed cord clamping (DCC) rate 43.0%
audits.f: The unit's DCC rate for preterm infants was 12.1%, versus a national average of 43.0%, making it a negative outlier; DCC rate for infants <34 weeks was 32.4%.
audits.c: Quality improvement project led by a multidisciplinary team (neonatal, obstetric, anaesthetic, midwifery): new guideline, education sessions and poster resources to embed DCC into routine practice.
audits.r2: DCC rate for infants <34 weeks' gestation improved from 32.4% to 78.6% (p<0.01); admission normothermia was maintained at 89.2% versus a prior 90.5%, meeting the 90% NNAP standard via an established 'normothermia bundle'.

audits.t: A blood bank audit of elective gynaecological surgery: a case for group and antibody screen.
audits.tp: Blood cross-matching utilisation in gynaecological surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Routine cross-matching for the gynaecological procedures studied was found to be wasteful of blood bank resources, supporting adoption of group and antibody screen policies.

audits.t: Auditing the vascular surgical audit.
audits.tp: Vascular surgical audit methods and activity trends
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Endarterectomy (other than carotid) decreased, transluminal angioplasty was introduced, lumbar sympathectomies fell, and major amputations increased relative to arterial reconstructions; actual procedure numbers were generally similar to expected figures calculated from the Hospital In-patient Enquiry, the Lothian audit and the Vascular Surgical Society survey.

audits.t: Reducing Unnecessary Transfusions of RBCs in Inpatients Admitted Across Niagara Health Community Hospitals
audits.st: Choosing Wisely Canada guidelines: pre-transfusion haemoglobin ≤80 g/L (target >80% of requests) and single-unit transfusion (target >65%)
audits.f: Earlier retrospective audit found only 85% of requests met the pre-transfusion Hb ≤80 g/L criterion and 54% met the single-unit criterion.
audits.c: Repeated PDSA cycles: educational strategies, prospective transfusion medicine (TM) technologist-led screening of orders, and an RBC order set.
audits.r2: Appropriate RBC use based on pre-transfusion Hb was 90% (median 87% pre-, 90% post-screening); appropriate use based on single-unit transfusion improved to 71% (median 54%, 56%, 71% at pre-, post-technologist screening, and most recent periods).

audits.t: Evaluating the effectiveness of a process medical audit in a teaching general hospital.
audits.tp: Hypnotic drug prescribing and sleep monitoring
audits.st: Local audit committee recommendations for recording sleep graphs and appropriate hypnotic prescribing patterns
audits.f: The 1981 audit identified deficiencies in recording of sleep graphs and in physicians' hypnotic prescribing patterns, and produced two recommendations: more frequent nursing sleep-graph recording, and an educational programme to change prescribing patterns.
audits.c: Nursing instructed to record sleep graphs more often; an educational programme aimed at changing physicians' hypnotic prescribing patterns
audits.r2: Recording of sleep graphs improved as intended, but medical staff failed to change their prescribing patterns; oxazepam remained the preferred hypnotic.

audits.t: Restorative rectal resection: an audit of 220 cases.
audits.tp: Restorative rectal resection outcomes and antimicrobial prophylaxis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Operative mortality was 8.3% overall (3.5% under 70 years, 13% over 70); leakage at the colorectal suture line was an intractable problem, uninfluenced by anastomotic technique.
audits.r2: A statistically significant reduction in the anastomotic leak rate followed introduction of routine antimicrobial prophylaxis (numbers not given in the abstract).

audits.t: Perinatal mortality in a Swedish county 1973-1978. Time trends revealed by perinatal audit.
audits.tp: Perinatal mortality trends and avoidable deaths
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Perinatal mortality declined over the six-year period, coinciding with increased in utero transfer of infants (particularly low birth weight) to the specialised county hospital; the proportion of deaths classified as potentially avoidable decreased significantly.
audits.c: Increased rate of in utero transfer of at-risk infants to a specialised county hospital

audits.t: Improving early initiation and exclusive breastfeeding practice through PDSA framework: the experience at a private hospital in Tanzania
audits.st: Baby Friendly Hospital Initiative (BFHI) standard, 80% target
audits.f: Baseline early breastfeeding initiation was 22%; baseline exclusive breastfeeding rate was 45%.
audits.c: PDSA framework: hospital policy on breastfeeding and formula milk use, staff training on lactation management, antenatal education using breastfeeding videos, immediate skin-to-skin contact after caesarean birth, modified newborn feeding charts, daily lactation rounds, and monthly antenatal classes for high-risk women.
audits.r2: Early breastfeeding initiation improved from 22% to 84%; exclusive breastfeeding rate increased from 45% to 90%.

audits.t: The Intricacy of Setting Up a Service to Bridge the Gap in Skin Malignancy Treatment for the Frail Population
audits.tp: Electrochemotherapy service for skin malignancy in frail patients
audits.st: NICE-approved technique (electrochemotherapy)
audits.f: The pilot demonstrated clinical and economic benefits versus conventional surgical excision, with patients experiencing fewer complications, reduced wound care requirements, and faster recovery (no numeric comparison given).
audits.c: Streamlined workflows, simplified consent documentation, tailored patient information, structured care pathway, developed via close multidisciplinary collaboration (plastic surgeons, oncologists, pharmacists, nurses, administrative teams); ongoing quality improvement via regular multidisciplinary meetings, clinical audits and outcome tracking (patient-reported outcome measures).

audits.t: Criteria map audit of scorpion envenomation in the Negev, Israel.
audits.tp: Quality of care for scorpion envenomation
audits.st: Criteria map (algorithmic clinical criteria) for quality of care in scorpion envenomation, including antivenom sensitivity testing before treatment
audits.f: Testing for antivenom sensitivity was omitted in an unacceptably high 69% of cases, and its omission led to an allergic reaction in 4 of 40 cases (10%); inadequate treatment of 7 secondary clinical problems ranged from 29% (seizures) to 71% (hypertension), mean 46%; mortality was 1.2% and persistent morbidity was negligible.

audits.t: Audit of nebuliser use.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: All but one nebuliser was driven by 100% oxygen, though only 3 of 111 interviewees preferred air for patients with hypercapnia; water was used as diluent in 5 of 44 nebulisers in use; calculated nebulisation times ranged from 3.5 to 117 minutes.

audits.t: Person-centered falls prevention and management in neurological post-operative patients: a best practice implementation project.
audits.st: JBI (Joanna Briggs Institute) evidence-based audit criteria for falls prevention
audits.f: Baseline audit of fall management practices identified barriers to best practice (individual criterion baseline percentages not given, only post-implementation results).
audits.c: JBI Evidence Implementation Framework (seven-phase, pre/post-test audit methodology): barrier identification, tailored improvement strategies, Plan-Do-Study-Act cycle, democratic leadership approach, multidisciplinary interventions, and on-the-job nurse training.
audits.r2: Compliance rates for Criteria 1, 3, 5 and 10 increased to 100%; Criterion 2 to 90%, Criterion 4 to 93%, Criterion 6 to 95%, Criterion 7 to 95%, Criterion 8 to 88%, Criterion 9 to 88%, and Criterion 11 to 97%; fall incidence did not exceed 0.08%.

audits.t: Customizing infection prevention and control modules for combating healthcare-acquired infections in low-resource hospitals or resource-constrained healthcare settings: a local and global approach
audits.tp: Infection prevention and control (IPC) programme improvement
audits.st: WHO Infection Prevention and Control Assessment Framework (IPCAF); WHO IPC guidelines and care bundles (CAUTI, CLABSI, SSI, VAP)
audits.f: IPCAF median score 78%; hand hygiene compliance median 65%.
audits.c: Multicentre pre-post WHO-aligned IPC model: induction, HAI data collection, IPCAF baseline assessment, team formation, training, surveillance and audit protocols; intervention phase of comprehensive IPC training, virtual courses and IPC surveillance.
audits.r2: IPCAF median score improved to 97% (p=0.004); hand hygiene compliance improved to 88% (p=0.004); significant improvement in compliance with care bundles for CAUTI (p=0.016), CLABSI (p=0.004), SSI (p=0.010) and VAP (p=0.037).

audits.t: Toddler Track: Streamlining Developmental Assessments-A Retrospective Cohort Study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Average time from initial clinical session to diagnostic formulation was 116 days.
audits.c: Toddler Track Model (TTM): PDSA framework redesigning service delivery, triaging children aged 18 months-3 years 11 months into one of four streams with tailored allied health/paediatrician pathways.
audits.r2: Average time to diagnostic formulation decreased to 63 days (p<0.001); service-wide wait times declined by 61.5%, with 68% of the reduction estimated to be associated with TTM; diagnostic outcomes did not differ between cohorts.

audits.t: Medical audit used for estimation of optimum level of outpatient care.
audits.tp: Optimum level of outpatient medical care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Total agreement between expert committee members on optimum level of care was reached initially for 84% of visits and, after discussion, for 99%; a general practitioner was considered the optimum level of care for 76% of patients overall, and about 85% of those over 80.

audits.t: Is a community-based mastoid microsuction service feasible: the audit of a pilot project.
audits.tp: Feasibility of community-based mastoid microsuction service
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: During the pilot project it was possible to transfer long-term care of most mastoidectomy patients attending hospital ENT outpatients to the community microsuction service run by a GP.

audits.t: Quality assurance network in central Europe. External audit on output calibration for photon beams.
audits.st: Acceptance level of +/-3% for TLD intercomparison of photon beam output calibration.
audits.f: 100 of 129 beams (78%) were within the +/-3% limit; 11 beams showed deviations larger than +/-6%. Of 47 centres, 22 had not had external audit in the preceding 5 years; in these, 68% (34/50) of beams were within the acceptance level vs 84% (66/79) in the 25 previously audited centres.
audits.c: Rechecking of all beams in centres with deviations exceeding +/-3%, investigation and discussion of discrepancies with participants, and corrective action (including addressing inadequate equipment and insufficient physicist training).
audits.r2: Standard deviation of the distribution of results for all x and gamma beams decreased from SD 7.4% at the first check to SD 2.5% at the second check, showing improvement after corrective action.

audits.t: An audit of the early complications of turbinectomy.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Audit indicated an unacceptably high rate of significant haemorrhage after turbinectomy.
audits.c: Surgical technique changed to avoid damage to the main arterial supply of the turbinate.
audits.r2: Haemorrhage rate fell after the technique change, but one case of severe nasal crusting occurred, a complication not seen previously.

audits.t: The value of incorporating avoidable factors into perinatal audits.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Perinatal mortality rate 26/1,000 deliveries; avoidable factors present in 58% of perinatal deaths, chiefly labour management, obtaining syphilis results, and fetal weight estimation.

audits.t: Appropriateness of transfusions of red cells, platelets and fresh frozen plasma. An audit in a tertiary care teaching hospital.
audits.st: Criteria for transfusion appropriateness derived from a review of the current published literature.
audits.f: Inappropriateness rates: red cells 16% of episodes/10% of units (n=200 episodes); platelets 13%/11% (n=215); fresh frozen plasma 24%/16% (n=260), rising to 31%/21% when transfusions for thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura were excluded.

audits.t: A means of tying provision with need. Audit of pressure-relieving aids in community-based hospitals.
audits.st: Multidisciplinary team criteria for selecting pressure-relieving mattresses according to patients' clinical needs.
audits.f: Use of criteria led to appropriate mattress selection standardised to patients' individual clinical needs; nurses ensured pressure area care was prescribed, delivered and documented.

audits.t: Meningococcal disease in New Zealand: an audit of disease notification and contact management.
audits.tp: Meningococcal disease notification and contact management
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Retrospective questionnaire survey found considerable variation in practice for notification and contact management of meningococcal disease across the country, with deficiencies in follow-up, record keeping and communication.

audits.t: How to implement an audit to improve records.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Ward-based nursing documentation audit undertaken to improve the standard of nursing records.

audits.t: An audit of clinico-radiologic conferences.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 200 cases at 19 meetings audited (mean duration 44.8 min); 75 (37.5%) routine, 100 (50%) for radiologic assistance, 25 (12.5%) general interest; discussion of educational value occurred in 88 of 200 cases, taking 61.7% of meeting time.

audits.t: An audit of the quality of operation notes in two district general hospitals. Are we following Royal College guidelines?
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons guidelines on operation note content, referencing the 1992 NCEPOD report.
audits.f: Postoperative instructions absent in nearly two-thirds of notes; prosthesis serial numbers rarely recorded; about 70% of consultants' notes were illegible or the procedure could not be understood; trainees scored higher than consultants and emergency notes scored better than elective notes.

audits.t: An audit of the effect of a 24-hour emergency operating theatre in a district general hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Before the 24-hour emergency theatre, half of emergency operations were carried out between 10pm and 8am, with theatre availability rather than clinical need determining timing.
audits.c: Introduction of a 24-hour emergency operating theatre for General Surgery.
audits.r2: The proportion of emergency operations carried out overnight (10pm-8am) fell to a third after the 24-hour theatre was introduced.

audits.t: Intershift report: a quality improvement project.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Staff nurse complaints about length and quality of intershift report led to identification of current strengths and weaknesses.
audits.c: Recommendations for improving intershift report were implemented.
audits.r2: Periodic audits document the ongoing quality of intershift report; no numeric results reported.

audits.t: [Implementation of a hypertension protocol in a basic health area as a basis for a medical audit].
audits.tp: Hypertension management audit in primary care
audits.st: Local Arterial Hypertension procedure/protocol.
audits.f: 43% of hypertensive patients had pressure adequately monitored (95% CI 33.3-52.7), mean 4.86 checks/year; analytic blood controls 66%, urine controls 56%; minimal cardiovascular investigation in 34%; back-of-eye investigation 44%, ECGs 49%.

audits.t: The investigation of chest pain: audit and intervention.
audits.st: Testing patterns recommended by an expert panel for patients with chest pain.
audits.f: Excessive use of 'biochemistry test profiles' instead of targeted tests recommended by the expert panel; average 22.9 tests per admission.
audits.c: Practice guidelines based on the expert panel's recommendations were drawn up for the cardiology unit.
audits.r2: Average tests per admission fell to 9.7, a statistically significant decrease.

audits.t: A dosimetric quality audit of photon beams by the Belgian Hospital Physicist Association.
audits.st: Nederlandse Commissie voor Stralingsdosimetrie (NCS) code of practice for photon beams, using EORTC intercomparison methodology.
audits.f: In 13 cobalt beams and 24 high-energy X-ray beams (4-25 MV) across 16 centres: mean ratio of measured to stated dose was 0.999 (SD 0.010) for cobalt and 1.006 (SD 0.23) for X-ray beams under reference conditions, with delta of 0.042 (cobalt) and 0.084 (X-ray); mechanical checks showed some large deviations in digital displays.

audits.t: Closing the audit circle: effect of continuing audit on arthroscopic practice.
audits.st: Internal audit codes and a standard proforma used to record and code arthroscopic diagnoses; no external target stated.
audits.f: Baseline diagnostic clarity and accuracy, including for meniscal tear diagnosis, and accuracy of audit coding.
audits.c: Continuing audit process using the proforma and audit codes, with results fed back between periods.
audits.r2: Diagnostic accuracy and clarity improved, as did accuracy of audit coding; diagnostic accuracy for meniscal tears improved over the year.

audits.t: Acute laryngo-tracheo-bronchitis (croup): an audit of hospital practice.
audits.st: Current published literature recommendations for management of acute laryngo-tracheo-bronchitis (croup).
audits.f: Retrospective case note audit found inappropriate use of radiography and outmoded therapies, and increasing (lax) use of adrenaline and steroids over the preceding 4 years, with potential danger to patients.
audits.c: An agreed protocol taking into account current published recommendations was introduced following the audit.

audits.t: Comparative vascular audit using the POSSUM scoring system.
audits.st: POSSUM scoring system predicted mortality and morbidity, used to risk-adjust comparative outcomes.
audits.f: Unit A: 255 patients, operative mortality 9.4%, morbidity 37.3% (POSSUM-predicted mortality 10.2%, morbidity 38.4%). Unit B: 89 patients, operative mortality 20.2%, morbidity 47.2% (POSSUM-predicted mortality 20.2%, morbidity 50.6%). ROC analysis showed no significant difference between units once risk-adjusted.

audits.t: An audit of the preoperative investigation of surgical patients.
audits.st: Preset criteria for whether preoperative investigations were 'indicated' or 'not indicated'.
audits.f: 272 investigations performed on 117 patients; 66% of investigations (excluding ECGs) were available at the time of surgery; 53% of investigations were deemed indicated.
audits.c: Modified criteria for preoperative investigation distributed to house surgeons as guidance.
audits.r2: 308 investigations performed on 136 patients; 81% of investigations available at surgery (P<0.001); 90% deemed indicated (P<0.001); an estimated 94% of a maximum possible annual saving of 7080 pounds could be achieved by implementing the criteria.

audits.t: National audit of pre-employment assessment in the NHS.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: WHO-WHL Hypertension Management Audit Project.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Undiagnosed hypertension varied from 17% to 34% across centres; not more than 29% of treated hypertensive patients had attained normal blood pressure; diuretics were the most commonly prescribed drug class, followed by beta-blockers.

audits.t: [The benefits of auditing clinical histories. Our experience over 5 years].
audits.st: Locally agreed optimum standards (OS) for four quality indicators (internal communication/legibility/comprehensibility, external communication, manageability, and quality of the SOAP-recorded activity), agreed by the team using a nominal group technique.
audits.f: Legibility 88%, comprehensibility 62%, external communication 81%, manageability 53%, SOAP 62%.
audits.c: Periodic team meetings to analyse audit results and agree corrective activities.
audits.r2: Legibility rose to 96.5%, comprehensibility to 75.3%, external communication to 88.9%, manageability to 79.6% and SOAP to 82.5%, all reaching the optimum standards.

audits.t: [The auditing of the clinical histories of a health center].
audits.st: Quality control criteria for completeness of clinical record sections (no external named standard).
audits.f: Data card and follow-up sections correct in over 90% of records; weight and height correct in 25.75%; composite indicator showed 32.25% of records correct overall; results were better for patients over 44.

audits.t: Nasal catheters for oxygen administration. An audit of safety and patient comfort.
audits.tp: Nasal catheter oxygen delivery in recovery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Audit designed to assess feasibility of nasal catheters for oxygen delivery in the recovery room, based on oximetry (safety) and patient comfort; no numeric results given in the abstract.

audits.t: Continuous quality improvement for continuity of care.
audits.tp: Continuity of care in family practice
audits.st: Local CQI target for provider continuity of care (no external standard stated)
audits.f: Provider continuity level was 0.45
audits.c: CQI study team selected process improvements in the critical pathways influencing provider continuity, based on physician and patient surveys.
audits.r2: Provider continuity improved to 0.74, a 64% increase

audits.t: Patients' perception of the hysterosalpingogram: the initial stages of the audit cycle.
audits.tp: Patient information and anxiety before hysterosalpingogram
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: The majority of patients knew why the examination was performed, but only 50% had received an explanation of the technique before arrival; anxiety levels were high and time delays contributed to anxiety.

audits.t: Certifying the cause of death: an audit of wording inaccuracies.
audits.st: Notes for medical practitioners on the correct wording/formulation of causes of death on medical death certificates.
audits.f: One or more wording/formulation inaccuracies identified in 29% of cases; in 5.8% the inaccuracies were serious enough to warrant further action or enquiry by the Registrar of Births and Deaths, including referral to HM Coroner.

audits.t: [Auditing the performance of the physician facing patient alcohol consumption].
audits.tp: Alcohol consumption assessment in primary care
audits.st: Explicit normative criteria for assessing patients' alcohol consumption in primary care.
audits.f: 60% of patients were not asked about alcohol consumption; where asked, amount consumed was specified; excessive consumption recorded as a risk factor in 87%; liver profile requested in 62%; advice to reduce/stop given in all identified cases.

audits.t: Induction of labour with prostaglandin E2; a prospective audit.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Hyperstimulation in 3 patients (2.5%); failed induction in 6 (5%); nulliparous patients with an unfavourable cervix had an increased caesarean section rate (29%) and prolonged mean induction-to-delivery interval (27 hours).

audits.t: Breast disease and the general surgeon. II. Effect of audit on the referral of patients with breast problems.
audits.tp: Breast clinic referral and waiting time pathway
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 25% of new referrals were for breast problems; median waiting time 22 days; 80-85% of new patients did not need admission for an operation; 65% of operations performed were for carcinoma.
audits.c: Changes implemented following Study 1, including writing to patients and GPs with investigation results to speed diagnosis/treatment communication and reduce follow-up attendance.
audits.r2: Median waiting time fell from 22 to 10 days; no significant difference between studies in proportions of each investigation type performed; carcinoma diagnosis rate unchanged between studies.

audits.t: Medical audit based on computer-stored patient records exemplified with an audit of hypertension care.
audits.tp: Hypertension management audit in primary care
audits.st: Local hypertension care protocol, assessed via 30 database queries against computer-stored records.
audits.f: Deficiencies identified in management of hypertension, particularly in patient history taking and risk factor analysis.
audits.c: Introduction of a hypertension care protocol.
audits.r2: Minor improvements in recording, and an increased rate of well-treated hypertensive patients.

audits.t: Continuous quality improvement in a day ward.
audits.tp: Continuous quality improvement in day surgery ward
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: A continuous quality improvement programme in a surgical day ward identified targets through reviews and audits; issues resolved included ward clerks confirming admissions by phone and developing written pre-admission guidelines; no numeric results reported.

audits.t: A peer review programme to audit the management of hypertensive patients in family practices in Israel.
audits.tp: Hypertension management audit in primary care
audits.st: Blood pressure control threshold of 160/95 mmHg used to define uncontrolled hypertension.
audits.f: 46.8% of hypertensive patients were uncontrolled (BP >=160/95 mmHg) at the start of the study, from a total adult population of 4445 patients (15% hypertensive prevalence, range 8.5-24.6% by clinic).
audits.c: Self-audit and peer review programme for management of hypertension, with feedback to participating physicians throughout.
audits.r2: Percentage of uncontrolled hypertensives fell to 34.3% (P=0.01).

audits.t: Cerebrovascular accident patients: an interdisciplinary/multidisciplinary audit.
audits.st: Locally developed clinical standards for allied health professional intervention with CVA patients.
audits.f: Retrospective criteria audit of hospital files found written documentation by allied health professionals did not meet expected standards in all criteria, and varied between professions.

audits.t: An audit of the use of antifungal agents.
audits.st: Appropriateness of systemic antifungal therapy per authoritative literature standards
audits.f: 115 courses of antifungal treatment over 1481 days in 74 patients; therapy was unconventional in 26.9% of courses and 40.5% of regimens, mainly due to indication or duration not conforming to conventional practice.

audits.t: An audit of the management of malignant hypercalcaemia.
audits.st: Departmental protocol for pamidronate dosing by serum calcium level, target normocalcaemia
audits.f: 72% (54/75) achieved normocalcaemia within 5 days of a single pamidronate infusion; a further 13% after a second dose; 15% remained hypercalcaemic until death.

audits.t: [Audit of the management of postoperative pain].
audits.st: Correct opioid dosage and dosing interval for postoperative analgesia (internal standard, not further specified)
audits.f: Dosage was correct in 86.5% of cases; dosing interval was too long in 54.1% of prescriptions for at least one drug; incidence of severe pain was 46.4%, especially after abdominal, high urologic and back surgery.

audits.t: Audit of ward to theatre communication. December 1994-March 1995.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Author describes problems with incomplete patient checklists and handovers from ward to theatre causing wasted time; no numerical results given in the abstract.

audits.t: Audit of nutrition screening in patients with acute illness.
audits.st: Standard for nutritional screening and assessment of acutely ill patients (not further specified)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Staff training programme on nutritional assessment and management.
audits.r2: Significant improvement in nutritional management following the staff training programme

audits.t: Audit of pain after nasal surgery.
audits.tp: Nasal pack duration and postoperative pain
audits.st: New departmental standard of 2 hours for routine nasal packing (set as a result of this study)
audits.f: Mean pain score with packs in place fell from 3.4 (24h packing, n=39) to 1.16 (2h packing, n=33), P<0.001; on removal from 5.3 to 2.6, P<0.05; no postoperative haemorrhage in either group.
audits.c: Reduced routine nasal pack duration from 24 hours to 2 hours; departmental protocol changed accordingly.
audits.r2: Mean pain score 1.12 with packs in place and 2.36 on removal, not statistically different from the 2-hour group's earlier results.

audits.t: CHANGES IN THE USE OF EEG FOLLOWING CLINICAL AUDIT
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: EEG requests seemed inappropriate in more than one-quarter of cases.
audits.c: Presentation of the audit results to clinicians.
