audits.r2: There was a marked reduction in EEG requests, which were subsequently used in a more cost-effective and clinically appropriate way; there was also a reduction in the time taken to process requests.

audits.t: An audit of 319 deaths across four general practices.
audits.tp: Preventable factors in deaths in general practice
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Audit of all 319 deaths in the practices over one year; smoking was considered the leading contributory cause; preventable factors occurred in both primary and secondary care.

audits.t: An audit of the use of sphygmomanometers.
audits.st: British Hypertension Society recommendations on sphygmomanometer servicing and cuff use
audits.f: 22% had an aneroid sphygmomanometer only, 10% had a random zero device; 57% had obese cuffs and 46% had paediatric cuffs; 23.5% had never had their sphygmomanometer serviced (mean 5.75 years).

audits.t: A medical audit and patient survey of hysterectomies performed for menstrual disorders.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: No clinical abnormality postulated in 53% of cases; preoperative clinical and pathological diagnoses agreed in 59%; 13% required transfusion; 21% had a complication; 94% pleased they had the operation.

audits.t: Sotalol proarrhythmia: a report of five cases and an audit of the use of a sotalol in a teaching hospital.
audits.tp: Sotalol prescribing and dose adjustment for renal function
audits.st: Dose adjustment of sotalol according to creatinine clearance (Cockcroft and Gault equation)
audits.f: Sotalol prescribed predominantly for atrial arrhythmias (80%, paroxysmal AF 71%); dose was not appropriately adjusted for creatinine clearance.

audits.t: Routine nasal surgery: an audit of outpatient follow-up.
audits.tp: Outpatient follow-up after routine nasal surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 78.3% (72/92) of patients requested to return attended follow-up; 76.4% had a satisfactory result and needed no further treatment; 76% of those on discharge medication still complied without needing specialist help.

audits.t: Audit in pain clinics: changing the management of low-back and nerve-damage pain.
audits.tp: Management of chronic low back and nerve-damage pain in pain clinics
audits.st: Appropriate use of antidepressants, anticonvulsants and TENS for chronic low back/nerve-damage pain (evidence-based, not a single named guideline)
audits.f: Wide variation between clinics in use of antidepressant/anticonvulsant drugs and TENS for 1236 patients with low back and/or nerve-damage pain.
audits.c: Feedback of audit data to clinics, comparing practice between centres.
audits.r2: Large increases in the use of antidepressants, anticonvulsants and TENS were seen in the further 1791 patients assessed after feedback.

audits.t: Audit changes clinical practice! Impact on rate of justification of hysterectomy indication.
audits.st: Local validation criteria for justification of hysterectomy indication (pathology confirmation, or prerequisite diagnostic work-up where pathology not expected); no external target stated
audits.f: Justification rates lower than ongoing audit: 89% for indications not confirmable by pathology, 83% for recurrent uterine bleeding, 95% for leiomyoma; multiple indications used in 16% of cases
audits.c: Introduction of an ongoing prospective quality assurance/audit process for hysterectomy indications from January 1990
audits.r2: Overall justification rate 96% (97% where pathology could confirm indication, 93% where it could not); improved vs baseline for indications not confirmable by pathology (93% vs 89%, p<0.05), recurrent uterine bleeding (90% vs 83%, p<0.05) and leiomyoma (97% vs 95%, p<0.05); multiple indications used in only 10% of cases (vs 16%, p<0.05)

audits.t: Audit of vascular surgical workload: use of data for service development.
audits.tp: Vascular surgical workload vs recommended activity
audits.st: Published recommendations for consultant surgical workload (3.5 intermediate equivalent value operations per list)
audits.f: Mean 37.2 IEV operations/week performed vs 21 IEV/week expected from the recommended standard; mean 25.3 admissions/week; mean bed occupancy 23.3.

audits.t: The Ambulatory Care Medical Audit Demonstration Project. Research design.
audits.tp: Feasibility and effectiveness of ambulatory care quality assurance cycles
audits.st: Practitioner conformance to review criteria for eight patient-care guidelines (e.g. low haematocrit follow-up, cancer screening, high glucose follow-up, digoxin monitoring, urine culture follow-up, immunisation/screening, gastroenteritis and ear infection management)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Concurrent crossover design of quality assurance interventions applied to different guidelines in different practices.

audits.t: An audit of Merchiston Hospital respite service.
audits.tp: Use of an inpatient respite service for learning disability
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 26 patients received respite care; 73% had severe/profound handicap; 73% would need extra nursing care in hospital; bed occupancy was lower on weekdays than weekends.

audits.t: An audit of the clinical features and use of antimicrobials in adult diarrhoea.
audits.tp: Empirical antimicrobial use in adult diarrhoea
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Ciprofloxacin started empirically in 46% of gastroenteritis cases; of these 51% had a relevant pathogen isolated; NSGE patients were treated with ciprofloxacin as often as culture-positive patients.

audits.t: Audits of the treatment of genital warts: closing the feedback loop.
audits.st: Local guidelines for management of new patients with genital warts (introduced after the first audit)
audits.f: Treatment was unselective and poorly monitored; 44% of men still had warts at 3 months and 32% were still attending at 6 months; 38% of women still had warts at 3 months and 12% were still attending at 6 months.
audits.c: Guidelines devised for management of new genital warts patients, reducing first-line podophyllin use in favour of cryotherapy, trichloroacetic acid and podophyllotoxin.
audits.r2: 8% of men still had warts at 3 months and 3% were still attending at 6 months; 18% of women still had warts at 3 months and attendance at 6 months halved to 6%; mean clinic visits fell from 5 to 3 (men) and 9 to 6 (women).

audits.t: The introduction and auditing of a formal do not resuscitate policy.
audits.st: Local formal do not resuscitate (DNR) policy developed with legal, medical, nursing and ethical input
audits.f: 86% of deaths had a DNR order but only 26% were in accordance with the formal policy; 30% of the time there was no record of discussion with the patient or family.

audits.t: Should consultant surgeons see new or follow-up patients? A prospective audit of a change in clinic organisation.
audits.tp: Consultant vs trainee review of new and follow-up clinic patients
audits.st: Existing guideline recommending that consultants see all new patients (challenged by this audit's findings)
audits.f: Ratio of new to follow-up patients was 1:1.9.
audits.c: Clinic reorganised so supervised trainees assessed new patients and the consultant saw follow-up patients.
audits.r2: Follow-up patients reduced by 28% at six months; ratio of new to follow-up patients was 1:1.6 at four years; 59% of GPs would accept less consultant involvement with new patients; all trainees and 83% of nurses preferred the new arrangement.

audits.t: Auditing out-of-hours primary medical care.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Call rate 265 per 1000 patients/year; 63% resulted in a home visit; 15% of patients were referred to hospital; doctors classified 61% of calls as necessary and 29% as unnecessary.

audits.t: Audit of patient acceptance of nasal surgery as a day case procedure.
audits.tp: Patient acceptance of nasal surgery as day case
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 52% of patients would accept nasal surgery as a day case, rising to 67% with 2-hour pack removal (difference not statistically significant overall).

audits.t: Ten-year audit of arterial surgery from a district hospital.
audits.st: Internal standard of previously identified problem areas (haemorrhagic complications and outcomes for femoro-crural bypass grafts); no external target stated
audits.f: Femoro-crural bypass and haemorrhage were identified as problem areas; re-operation for postoperative bleeding 4.6%
audits.c: not reported (comparison of practice over time rather than a described discrete change)
audits.r2: Re-operation for postoperative bleeding fell to 2.2%; improved outcomes for aortic/iliac aneurysm repair and lower limb (especially crural) bypass grafts; arterial admissions rose 55.7% and operations 46.6%; aorto-iliac/aortofemoral bypasses done less often but with higher mortality and complications in more urgent, limb-threatened patients

audits.t: Impact of continuous quality improvement on selection of pacing mode and rate of complications in permanent pacing.
audits.tp: Pacemaker mode selection and implantation complications
audits.st: International pacing guidelines favouring physiological pacing; preset local standards for acceptable reasons to withhold physiological pacing and for complication rates
audits.f: Physiological pacing was not selected mainly for age (12.8% SND, 31.4% AV block) and technical problems/other disease; complication rate 16.2% (77/476), including atrial lead displacement 10.2% (19/186)
audits.c: Age alone was disregarded as a reason to withhold physiological pacing and VDD pacing was introduced; atrial screw-in leads and cephalic cut-down were encouraged to reduce complications
audits.r2: Standards for physiological pacing selection were fulfilled; complications fell significantly to 12/140 (8.6%) (P=0.03) compared with 77/476 in the earlier period

audits.t: An audit of theatre scrubrooms in a district general hospital.
audits.st: Baseline minimum design parameters for theatre scrubrooms (including minimum free floor space)
audits.f: Only one scrubroom met the minimum free floor space requirement; none complied with all baseline parameters; 60% of surveyed surgeons had to re-scrub because their hands became desterilised through insufficient scrubroom space

audits.t: Auditing prescription practice using explicit criteria and computerized drug benefit claims data.
audits.tp: Potentially inappropriate prescribing in the elderly
audits.st: Explicit criteria for appropriate prescribing in the elderly, applied to computerised drug benefit claims data
audits.f: 38% of elderly recipients of antidepressants, 19% of oral hypoglycaemics, 18% of sedative hypnotics and 13% of NSAIDs were classified as receiving a potentially inappropriate drug

audits.t: Avoidable deaths still occur after large bowel surgery. Scottish Audit of Surgical Mortality, Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh.
audits.tp: Avoidable deaths after large bowel surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Independent assessors found an adverse event in 78 deaths (42%); 26 deaths (14%) followed anastomotic leak; 43 deaths (23%) followed delayed surgery, diagnosis or recognition of complications; consultants operated on only half of ASA IV/V or reoperation patients.

audits.t: Changing urine testing protocols through audit.
audits.st: Appropriate use of ward-based urine screening (Multistix 10 SG) before sending samples for laboratory culture (local protocol)
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Introduction of ward-based urine screening test (Multistix 10 SG), with ongoing education and support for nursing staff.
audits.r2: 40% reduction in the number of culture-negative samples sent for laboratory testing

audits.t: Audit of the change of outcome of peptic ulcer disease following treatment of Helicobacter pylori.
audits.tp: Helicobacter pylori treatment and peptic ulcer outcome
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: H. pylori eradication as primary treatment rose from 24% of patients in 1991 to 79% in 1994; recurrence was 8% after documented eradication versus 43-57% in other groups; 9 of 453 patients required surgery.
audits.c: Increasing use of H. pylori eradication therapy by general practitioners over the study period.

audits.t: Audit of death certificates.
audits.tp: Accuracy and completeness of death certification
audits.st: Defined quality criteria for completeness and relevance of death certificate data
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of nutritional practice and knowledge.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Found areas for improvement, particularly in documentation of nutritional status and referral criteria for specialist help.
audits.c: An assessment sheet and nursing care plan were developed to assess malnutrition risk and provide a place to record nutrition-related information.

audits.t: Audit of changes in serum urea and electrolytes following peri-operative intravenous fluid therapy.
audits.tp: Perioperative fluid therapy and electrolyte monitoring
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 69.7% of patients had preoperative urea and electrolytes (U&Es) measured, 42.5% had both pre- and postoperative measurement; abnormal postoperative sodium rose from 13% preoperatively to 27.3%; elderly and emergency patients had more electrolyte disturbance.

audits.t: Variation in management of intermittent claudication by vascular surgeons in Scotland. Scottish Vascular Audit Group [corrected].
audits.tp: Variation in management of intermittent claudication
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Proportion of patients considered for conservative management varied 10-83% between consultants (mean 42%); for surgery the range was 4-68% (mean 37%); all differences between consultants were significant.

audits.t: [Medical auditing: procedures assessment in the women's integral health care program in the Vila Municipal Health Clinic, Pelotas, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil]
audits.tp: Women's integral health care programme procedures
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Women visited the clinic 3.5-4 times a year; 42.5% had a Pap smear in the previous three years; 19% had had a breast examination; blood pressure measurement was the most commonly recorded procedure.

audits.t: Can GPs audit their ability to detect psychological distress? One approach and some unresolved issues.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported
audits.c: Self-directed educational intervention: measurement of GP performance, data feedback, and review of selected videotaped consultations.

audits.t: Audit of ambulatory blood pressure monitoring in the diagnosis and management of hypertension in practice.
audits.tp: Value of ambulatory blood pressure monitoring
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Diagnosis of hypertension confirmed by ABPM in 70% of patients (86.3% using a lower cut-off); in 204 patients reviewed 5 years later, diastolic pressure fell from 100.6 to 85.7 mmHg with treatment, though 30% remained above 90 mmHg.

audits.t: The value of histological examination in the audit of hospital autopsies: a quantitative approach.
audits.tp: Value of histological examination in hospital autopsy
audits.st: Royal College of Pathologists guidelines for postmortem reports (1993)
audits.f: 70% of causes of death confirmed by macroscopic and histological examination; 61 clinical diagnoses were inconsistent with pathological findings; overall clinical sensitivity 54%, specificity 92%; a third of causes of death were unsuspected clinically.

audits.t: An audit of post-operative pain and nausea in day case surgery.
audits.tp: Postoperative pain and nausea in day case surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Initial audit found pain scores and nausea considered unacceptable; 8.6% of patients called their GP to visit at home postoperatively.
audits.c: Pre-operative piroxicam 20mg introduced in most patients to reduce postoperative pain.
audits.r2: Pain scores were reduced; only 0.9% (1/111) called their GP out, but nausea scores remained unchanged.

audits.t: Comparison of wound scoring methods for use in audit.
audits.st: Standard definitions of surgical wound infection (Centers for Disease Control, USA; National Prevalence Survey, UK)
audits.f: 325 wounds examined in 230 patients (88% followed up); ASEPSIS identified 13% of wounds as infected and a further 16.5% with disturbed healing.
audits.c: Surveillance results were fed back to surgeons after the first survey.
audits.r2: 559 wounds examined in 375 patients (97% followed up); no significant difference in infection rates found between the two surveys despite feedback.

audits.t: Audit of the management of spontaneous pneumothorax.
audits.st: British Thoracic Society guidelines for management of spontaneous pneumothorax
audits.f: Simple aspiration attempted in only 7 of 65 patients; intercostal chest drain clamping occurred in 12 of 50 cases, against guidance.

audits.t: Informacia o niektorych vysledkoch z Pilotnej studie projektu Ministerstva zdravotnictva SR. AUDIT diagnostickeho a terapeutickeho postupu u chorych s akutnymi koronarnymi syndromami
audits.tp: Diagnostic and therapeutic management of acute coronary syndromes
audits.st: National AUDIT project standards for management of acute myocardial infarction (details not given in abstract)
audits.f: Pilot study found several negative findings in the management of patients with acute myocardial infarction that could adversely affect prognosis or increase costs; specific figures not given in the available abstract.

audits.t: Auditing mortality from upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage: impact of a high dependency unit.
audits.tp: Mortality from upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage and high dependency care
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: A retrospective audit found mortality from upper GI haemorrhage above that reported from nearby centres; in the first prospective audit mortality was 9%.
audits.c: Establishment of a high dependency unit (HDU) and an agreed management protocol for upper GI haemorrhage.
audits.r2: Mortality in the second prospective audit (after HDU) was 10%, with a trend towards higher age and comorbidity; the HDU and protocol did not reduce mortality.

audits.t: Audit in practice: planning for discharge from hospital.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Efficacy of an EMS quality improvement program in improving documentation and performance.
audits.tp: EMS patient care report documentation and performance
audits.st: Local QI standards for documentation of six patient assessment parameters, appropriate treatment, protocol adherence and response/scene/transport times
audits.f: Response, scene and transport times were acceptable in more than 90% of cases at baseline; baseline documentation and performance figures used for comparison
audits.c: Quality improvement programme instituted in 1994 comprising prospective, concurrent and retrospective monthly random audits (~6% of patient care reports), with feedback to crews and CME sessions targeted at identified problems
audits.r2: Statistically significant improvements in documentation of patient assessment, protocol compliance, patient disposition, overall documentation, overall performance and need for further review; significant improvement in 13 of 19 parameters and goals met in 14, sustained over the two-year study period; response/scene/transport times remained acceptable in more than 90% of cases

audits.t: Hand lacerations. An audit of clinical examination.
audits.tp: Diagnostic accuracy of hand laceration examination
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Accident and emergency officers diagnosed only 64% of tendon divisions vs 84% for admitting hand surgeons; nerve injuries were diagnosed by 87% of A&E officers vs 94% of hand surgeons.

audits.t: Chart audit of inpatient treatment of schizophrenic patients: implications for development of coordinated care paths.
audits.st: Standard of care for inpatient schizophrenia treatment (used to develop a coordinated care path)
audits.f: Chart audit identified deficiencies in medical tests, master treatment planning, documentation of care, patient teaching and discharge planning.
audits.c: Development of a coordinated care path for schizophrenia based on the audit findings.

audits.t: Are abdominal radiographs still overutilized in the assessment of acute abdominal pain? A district general hospital audit.
audits.tp: Abdominal radiograph overutilisation in acute abdominal pain
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Plain film radiography performed in 55.8% (125/224) of patients but only 10.4% (13/125) were diagnostic; 62% of non-specific abdominal pain patients had radiographs; restricting to recommended indications would have reduced use to 20.5%.

audits.t: Effect of medical record audit and feedback on residents' compliance with preventive health care guidelines.
audits.tp: Residents' compliance with preventive health guidelines
audits.st: Preventive health care guidelines for tetanus immunisation, breast examination and rectal examination (audited interventions)
audits.f: Baseline compliance with audited preventive interventions prior to the audit-and-feedback programme (exact baseline figures not given in the abstract).
audits.c: Intensive audit-and-feedback programme of medical record audits with individualised feedback to residents, started in 1994.
audits.r2: Compliance rates for audited interventions (tetanus immunisation, breast examination, rectal examination) significantly improved, and compliance also rose for six of seven non-audited interventions.

audits.t: Auditing electroconvulsive therapy. The third cycle.
audits.st: Royal College of Psychiatrists' 2nd ECT handbook standards
audits.f: Only one-third of clinics met College standards; 16% of consultants attended weekly; 6% had sessional time for ECT duties; 59% had recommended machines and 7% still used outdated machines; only about one-third had clear junior doctor guidance policies.

audits.t: [Use of a medium and long chain triglyceride mixture for parenteral nutrition in a university hospital: results of an internal audit].
audits.tp: Use of a medium and long chain triglyceride mixture for parenteral nutrition
audits.st: Manufacturer indications and contraindications for a medium/long chain triglyceride parenteral nutrition emulsion
audits.f: Maximal recommended dose (per kg/day) was exceeded in 32% of patients; 11% had serious hepatic insufficiency, 38% had hypertriglyceridaemia; contraindications were present in 45% of cases despite indications otherwise being respected.

audits.t: Audit of patients on oral anticoagulants with International normalized ratios of eight or above.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 131 of 55,625 INRs (0.24%) were 8 or above; major cause was unsatisfactory dose loading during in-hospital initiation; major bleeding occurred in 12.9% of episodes with two fatalities; FFP and IV vitamin K were effective but not given in most major haemorrhage cases.

audits.t: The impact of audit in a district general hospital on post-operative nausea and vomiting after major gynaecological surgery.
audits.tp: Postoperative nausea and vomiting after major gynaecological surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: PONV incidence was as high as 71.5% at the start of the audit; compliance with antiemetic protocols was 41%.
audits.c: Departmental antiemetic policy adopted after corporate development and evaluation of five antiemetic policies.
audits.r2: PONV incidence fell to 51.7%; compliance with antiemetic protocols increased from 41% to 76% (P=0.002); significantly less PONV when a protocol was followed (P=0.002).

audits.t: THE DIFFICULTIES ENCOUNTERED IN COMPLETING AN AUDIT CYCLE IN A DISTRICT GENERAL HOSPITAL
audits.tp: Barriers to completing the audit cycle
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Autopsy audit in a teaching hospital in Nigeria--the Benin experience.
audits.st: Target autopsy ratio of at least 75% and clinico-pathological concordance well above 90% (authors' proposed targets)
audits.f: Autopsy ratio was 29% (179 of 612 deaths); concordance between clinical and autopsy diagnosis was 54% in the 143 analysed cases.

audits.t: Current management of acute leg ischaemia: results of an audit by the Vascular Surgical Society of Great Britain and Ireland.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Vascular surgical advice requested in 95% of 539 episodes; immediate embolectomy in 21%; at 30 days 70% of limbs were viable and 16% had been amputated; mortality rate 22%.

audits.t: [Quality in compliance and prescription of nursing treatment orders for injectable drugs].
audits.tp: Nursing treatment orders for injectable drugs
audits.st: Complete and correct nursing treatment order (NTO) prescribing (length of treatment, guidelines, allergy documentation)
audits.f: Compliance with NTOs was deficient for length of treatment (63.33%), length and guidelines together (58.00%), and allergy documentation (28.31%); 72.48% of prescriptions were difficult to justify.

audits.t: Improving musculoskeletal clinical skills teaching. A regionwide audit and intervention study.
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Response rate 71/150; factors identified as associated with a high quality score included the course being organised by a rheumatologist.
audits.c: Identified factors applied to the clinical skills course at one hospital.
audits.r2: Response rate 89/161; the standard of teaching was improved by applying the identified factors, though additional costs were incurred.

audits.t: Needlestick injury: Audit report of compliance with an American Nurse Association guideline in a private hospital, Sudan
audits.st: American Nurses Association (ANA) guideline for post-exposure assessment, prophylaxis and treatment following needlestick injury
audits.f: First aid: antiseptic sterilizer cleaning used by 60%, washing with soap and water by 40%; 57% of exposed workers reported their injuries; needle source identified in 73%; serological/virology screening for HBV/HCV/HIV unknown in 25%; rapid test not done by 43%; post-exposure prophylaxis started within 2 hours in only 23%.

audits.t: Audit of transfusion practice during burns surgery at the Red Cross War Memorial Children's Hospital
audits.tp: Blood transfusion practice in burns surgery
audits.st: Locally developed guideline based on haemoglobin level and extent of surgery for preoperative blood ordering
audits.f: Blood was ordered according to the guideline in 131/195 (67.2%) cases; excluding two poorly adherent 'group and screen only' categories, preoperative instructions were appropriate in 119/126 (94.4%) where the guideline was followed; blood was ordered preoperatively in 83/195 cases but used in only 50 (60.2%); of 33 unused cases, 23 were not in keeping with the guideline; surgery proceeded as planned in 162/195 (83.1%) cases.

audits.t: Guideline-based contouring and clinical audit systems
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of prophylactic antibiotic use in orthopaedic surgery in Mulago Hospital
audits.st: Standard practice for timing of prophylactic antibiotic administration in clean implant orthopaedic surgery (specific guideline not named)
audits.f: Antibiotics were not used in 17.3% of patients; over half of patients received the antibiotic after the skin incision had been made, at an average of about 11 minutes from incision

audits.t: The Way Residents Treat Patients with Decreased Level of Consciousness in the Emergency Department; a Clinical Audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Prevalence of arcuate foramen anomaly was 9.6% overall (10.34% in men, 7.93% in women) among adult patients undergoing lateral neck radiography in the emergency department

audits.t: Emergency trauma care in a tertiary centre in Lagos: A clinical audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Trauma resuscitation time averaged 112.73 minutes and was prolonged in 51.5% of cases; care was judged inadequate in 39.60% of cases; delay in blood transfusion (p=0.051) and treatment error (p=0.006) were most strongly associated with mortality (odds ratios 3 and 5 respectively); unexpected death rate was 60%; mean casualty ward length of stay was 106.85 hours; standardized mortality ratio was greater than 1

audits.t: The Canadian Head CT Rule; A Hospital Audit
audits.st: Canadian CT Head Rule (CCHR) for minor head injury (GCS 13-15)
audits.f: All 41 patients had a CT scan performed; only 14 would have required a CT scan had the CCHR been applied; positive findings in 7 of patients who qualified under the rule and 3 who did not, giving a 50% positive predictive value, 89% negative predictive value, 70% sensitivity and 75% specificity

audits.t: An audit of blood transfusion in elective neuro-surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 31% of patients undergoing neurosurgery required blood product transfusion; intracranial tumour surgery was associated with significantly higher blood loss and transfusion than other lesions (p<0.006); spinal surgery had the lowest transfusion rates; among intracranial tumours, meningiomas required the highest transfusion volumes (p<0.001); paediatric transfusion rates were similar to the whole group; single-unit transfusions accounted for 34% of all products transfused, and were more frequent in paediatric patients (22 of 45) and intracranial tumour patients (24 of 45)

audits.t: Cancellation of elective cases in pediatric surgery: An audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 189 of 2473 (7.64%) elective cases were cancelled on the scheduled date; main reasons: upper respiratory infection 30.68%, shortage of time 29%, medically unfit patients 15.34%, precedence of emergency cases 3.7%, non-availability of ventilator/ICU bed 4.7%, patient no-show 4.76%, non-availability of blood 4.2%, incomplete work-up 2.64%, administrative reasons 1.58%, patient not fasting 1.58%, unspecified 2.1%; 38.6% of causes were judged preventable

audits.t: La calidad de la atención al hombro doloroso: Audit clínico The quality of care in pain shoulder: A medical audit
audits.st: Locally developed quality indicators for history-taking, physical examination, diagnosis and treatment of non-surgical shoulder pain, based on systematic reviews of clinical trials, practice guidelines and expert review
audits.f: 76.3% of records failed to meet ≥4 of 10 history-taking quality criteria; 61.6% failed ≥3 of 10 physical examination criteria; 7.7% had no diagnosis recorded; 96.9% of 98 patients with subacromial impingement syndrome did not meet the criterion for timely anti-inflammatory treatment or infiltration, and 15.3% were not offered physiotherapy or programmed exercise within 4 weeks of diagnosis; 95.8% of 24 patients with rotator cuff tears were not referred for early surgical evaluation; 86.7% of 15 patients with adhesive capsulitis did not receive instructions for programmed exercise within the proposed timescale

audits.t: Five-year vascular audit from a district hospital
audits.tp: Vascular surgery complication and reoperation rates
audits.st: Acceptable standard of in-hospital surgical outcome for vascular procedures, judged in the absence of national comparative statistics
audits.f: 30% of patients had at least one complication, 14% required further surgery, and 9% died; below-knee bypass surgery had an unacceptably high rate of complications, reoperations and amputations; overall reoperation rate for postoperative bleeding was 5%, considered high

audits.t: PRO‐OSTEO Extend I study (improving osteoporosis management in the acute and rehabilitation settings): multicentre audit
audits.st: Local standard for osteoporosis assessment and treatment following minimal-trauma fracture, using a standard osteoporosis management form
audits.f: Osteoporosis assessment and treatment rates varied widely across sites; acute wards such as emergency departments provided no assessment or treatment
audits.c: Introduction of a standard osteoporosis management form enabling a pharmacist-driven approach to management
audits.r2: Uptake of the osteoporosis management form was negligible post-intervention; assessment and treatment remained inadequate; overall 2-year mortality was 7.4% following any fracture, rising to up to 33% following a hip or neck of femur fracture at some sites

audits.t: Patient dose audit of the most frequent radiographic examinations and the proposed local diagnostic reference levels in southwestern Nigeria: Imperative for dose optimisation
audits.st: Comparison of local diagnostic reference levels against established national diagnostic reference levels (NDRLs) in the UK, US, Slovenia, Italy and Brazil, for chest PA, pelvis AP, lumbar spine AP, skull AP, knee AP and hand AP radiography
audits.f: Local diagnostic reference levels ranged 1.78-3.01 mGy (chest PA), 2.71-2.84 (pelvis AP), 2.11-3.79 (lumbar spine AP), 3.93-8.79 (skull AP), 1.06-1.73 (knee AP) and 1.10-1.44 (hand AP); pelvis AP and lumbar spine AP entrance surface doses were lower than the UK NRPB-HPA 2010 review, while all other five examinations exceeded UK review doses; large dose variation was found among X-ray units even within the same centre

audits.t: A Structured Thematic Audit Analysis with Consensus Building Leads to Optimized Antibiotic Use and Clinical Decision Pathways.
audits.st: Institutional and literature-based standards for appropriate antibiotic choice, dose and duration by clinical syndrome, as part of an antimicrobial stewardship programme
audits.f: Baseline antibiotic consumption was DOT/100PD=78.2 with average length of therapy 6.2 days; non-infective elective surgery and closed fracture received a mean of 4.4 and 5.6 days of antibiotics respectively, judged unnecessary; no institutional antibiotic protocol existed for open fractures
audits.c: A 1-month intervention phase of real-time prospective audit and feedback with treating-team liaison, followed by a department-wide consensus meeting that agreed an antibiotic protocol for open fractures (maximum 72 hours or until wound closure) and other optimisation points, adopted into institutional antibiotic guidelines
audits.r2: Post-intervention antibiotic consumption and the proportion of justified antibiotic use (choice, dose, duration) were compared with baseline; specific post-intervention figures were not given in the text

audits.t: An Audit of Nausea and Vomiting in a Post Anaesthetic Care Unit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of Anaesthetic Chart Documentation in Major Orthopaedic Surgery
audits.st: Local standard for completeness of documentation on the anaesthetic chart for elective orthopaedic anaesthesia
audits.f: Documentation of most variables was generally good, but blood loss and urinary output were poorly documented
audits.c: Email and verbal reminder sent to anaesthetic colleagues ahead of a second data collection
audits.r2: Average improvement of 5.7% in data documentation across variables (range -2.7% to +24.7%); blood loss and urinary output remained poorly documented

audits.t: The Construction of a Clinical Audit to Evaluate the Prevalence of Uncontrolled or Untreated Hypertension among an Adult Population Presenting to Pre-assessment Prior to Major Orthopaedic Surgery
audits.st: Local audit standards for detection and management of uncontrolled or untreated hypertension at pre-assessment prior to major orthopaedic surgery (specific numeric target not given in this text)
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Prospective audit of major amputations for peripheral vascular disease
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 114 above-knee, 45 below-knee and 3 through-knee amputations; 30-day mortality was 14% (22 patients), rising to 29% (47) at 9 months; 57 patients (35%) were rehabilitated with a prosthesis (30 above-knee, 27 below-knee); mobility with prosthesis was better or maintained in 24, worse by one grade in 17, and worse by two or more grades in 16; 58 patients (36%) were unsuitable for a prosthesis (4 due to stump problems, the rest due to co-morbidity); mean hospital stay after amputation was 37 days in survivors; only 42% of prosthesis recipients (15% of the total) maintained or improved their mobility

audits.t: Pre‐audit survey of documentation of invasive procedures in paediatric anaesthesia
audits.tp: Consent documentation for paediatric invasive procedures
audits.st: Royal College guidelines requiring written evidence that use of special/invasive techniques (e.g. epidurals, regional blocks, invasive monitoring, blood transfusion) has been discussed with the child (when appropriate) and parents
audits.f: Case mix: ENT 37%, Plastic Surgery 28%, General Surgery 24%, Orthopaedic and Oral Surgery 11%; a consultant was present for 98% of anaesthetics; documentation of who was present at the pre-operative discussion was absent in 82% (60/73); of the 62 records with invasive procedures, 83.5% had the procedure documented pre-operatively but only 11% (7/62) recorded the procedure being specifically discussed with the child; 50% (2/4) of caudals lacked documentation of discussion, 14% (7/48) of suppositories were given without record of verbal consent, and 31% (5/16) of local anaesthetic techniques were performed without documentation of discussion

audits.t: DEXA for Females Aged 65+ at an OBGYN Resident Clinic in Hawaii: A Chart Audit on Compliance for Osteoporosis Screening [13I]
audits.st: USPSTF recommendation that women aged 65 and older without previous known fractures or secondary causes of osteoporosis be screened with DEXA
audits.f: 92% (80/87) were offered DEXA screening and 87% (76/87) underwent the test; of the 11 untested, 4 were offered screening and refused, 2 refused outright, 2 declined while awaiting insurance coverage, 4 presented for problem visits and 3 had no charted explanation; no difference by race (p=0.8) or insurance type (p=0.5); OBGYNs and primary care providers ordered equal numbers of scans (38/76 each, p=1.0)

audits.t: Informed consent for orthopaedic surgery: a prospective audit
audits.st: Local standard for adequacy of the informed consent process for elective orthopaedic surgery (patient information and satisfaction)
audits.f: Patients were often given incomplete information about their management (exact figures not reported); despite this, patients felt the level of information given was appropriate and allowed them to make an informed decision

audits.t: Audit: efficiency of fast‐tracking hip fractures from accident and emergency
audits.st: Local fast-track pathway standard for transfer of hip fracture patients from accident and emergency to orthopaedic wards
audits.f: Several deficiencies were identified in the implementation of the fast-track pathway (specific figures not reported)

audits.t: Clinical audit and the implementation of the Ottawa Ankle Rules
audits.st: Ottawa Ankle Rules for determining the need for X-ray in ankle/foot injury
audits.f: 128 of 150 patients (85%) received an X-ray; 16 of 128 X-rays (12.5%) showed a fracture
audits.c: Education of every doctor working in A&E using a hand-out giving the Ottawa Ankle Rules
audits.r2: 83 of 150 patients (55%) received an X-ray, a significant reduction (p<0.001); 17 of 83 X-rays (20%) showed a fracture, an increase that was not statistically significant

audits.t: An audit of lost X‐ray films on orthopaedic and trauma wards
audits.st: Local quality standard for minimising X-ray film loss and retrieval time on orthopaedic and trauma wards
audits.f: 16 patients' X-ray films were lost; 15 (93%) had been stored in anonymous polythene packets; only 5 (31%) were found within half an hour, with a mean of 67 minutes' working time spent locating each film
audits.c: Recognition of why and where films were being lost
audits.r2: The number of losses was reduced after the cause and location of losses were identified (specific figures not reported)

audits.t: Dual‐energy CT for occult pelvic fractures: An audit and roc analysis
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 84 of 178 patients (47%) had acute fractures; dual-energy CT (DECT) sensitivity was 99% and specificity 100%; ROC analysis showed the area under the curve increased from radiograph to conventional CT to DECT for all observers; the difference between conventional CT and DECT was statistically significant for all observers where metal implants were not present

audits.t: PR25 SOFT TISSUE COVERAGE IN LOWER LIMB TRAUMA – ANNUAL AUDIT FROM A TERTIARY RECONSTRUCTIVE SURGERY UNIT IN INDIA
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 95% of cases were two-wheeler traffic accidents; site distribution: leg 39, foot 14, leg and foot 16, thigh/leg/foot 3; 8 cases Gustilo IIIB and 7 IIIC; 42 flaps performed (gastrocnemius 4, soleus 7, reverse sural 7, cross leg 2, fasciocutaneous 5, perforator-based local 3, latissimus dorsi 7, gracilis 6, lateral thigh 1); timing of intervention: immediate 12%, early (<1 week) 36%, delayed (>1 week) 52%; complications: minor wound infection 12, major wound infection 8 (3 clostridial), partial flap loss 6, loss of skin graft over flap/donor site 5, acute renal failure 1; amputations: above-knee 4, below-knee 2

audits.t: Fracture incidence after liver transplantation: results of a 10 year audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean follow-up 61.4 months; 5.6% of patients had a fracture history pre-transplant; incident clinical fractures post-transplant occurred in 15 (3.5%) of patients, most commonly at the spine; median time from transplant to fracture was 26 months (range 2-83)
audits.c: Introduction of a bone management protocol, including lower-dose prednisolone for immunosuppression and bone protective therapy for high-risk patients

audits.t: PMO-260 Bone protection is under used in IBD patients: data from the 3rd round UK IBD audit
audits.st: British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guidelines: calcium and vitamin D supplementation when systemic steroids are needed, and co-administration of bisphosphonates with steroids for patients over 65 or with known osteoporosis/osteopenia
audits.f: Bone protective agents were given to 66.2% (1443/2181) of ulcerative colitis (UC) patients discharged on steroids versus 58.7% (1022/1742) of Crohn's disease (CD) patients (p=0.021); among 600 CD outpatients prescribed steroids for over 3 months, 67.3% (404/600) also received bone protection, not significantly different from CD inpatient care (p=0.07); 22.2% (132/600) of these CD outpatients had a DEXA scan

audits.t: WED 240 An audit of unplanned admissions in myasthenia gravis patients
audits.st: Muscular Dystrophy UK (MDUK) national audit of unplanned admissions in neuromuscular patients (2012 and 2017 rounds), benchmarking the preventable admission rate
audits.f: 60 unplanned admissions were identified among 240 patients; only 22 (37%) were judged potentially avoidable, compared with MDUK national data of 68.7% (2012) and 59.4% (2017); causes included myasthenia relapse (8), severe myasthenia on dual immunosuppression (8), pneumonia in elderly comorbid patients (9), anxiety-related (2), and falls/fracture despite appropriate bone protection (3)

audits.t: An Audit of Referrals to Occupational Therapy for Older Adults attending an Accident and Emergency Department
audits.tp: Occupational therapy referrals in the emergency department
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean age of referred patients was 80 years; the majority were female and living alone; the most common presenting problem was a fall, with a resulting fracture in half of the patients; occupational therapy input was estimated to save admissions equivalent to two hospital beds each year of the audit

audits.t: Total Hip Replacement: An Audit of the Provision and Use of Equipment
audits.st: Local standard that all total hip replacement patients will be provided with a 'hip pack' (raised toilet seat, helping hand, long-handled shoe horn, sock/tights aid) prior to discharge, for use 6-12 weeks postoperatively, based on James (1992) guidelines
audits.f: 85% (63/74) response rate; the equipment was highly valued by patients and usage duration varied, with many items still in use 6 months postoperatively; 93% (51/55) of respondents said they would have purchased at least one hip pack item; the standards were nearly but not fully met

audits.t: Retrospective Audit of Blood Transfusion and Comparison with Haemoglobin Concentration in Patients Undergoing Elective Primary and Revision Lower Limb Arthroplasty
audits.tp: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Overall transfusion incidence was 16.0%; in primary arthroplasty 11% (9.8% for total knee replacement, 13.5% for total hip replacement) and in revision surgery 44.4% (27.3% for revision knee replacement, 56.3% for revision hip replacement); a preoperative haemoglobin threshold of 120 g/l divided patients into high and low transfusion risk groups (47.7% transfusion incidence at or below threshold versus 7.2% above it)

audits.t: Audit on Treatment and Recovery of Ankle Sprain
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 35.3% had mild, 19.6% moderate and 15.2% severe ankle sprain; only 48% of the moderate group were given more than 3 days of medical leave compared with 71% (mild) and 76% (severe); 81 patients (58%) and 70 patients (50%) were captured at the 2-week and 6-week telephone follow-up respectively; the moderate severity group fared worse with higher functional limitation and secondary consultation rates, more evident at 6 weeks

audits.t: International benchmarking of 500 admissions with a fractured hip in Australia using the Standard Audit of Hip Fractures in Europe and the Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network
audits.st: Standard Audit of Hip Fractures in Europe (SAHFE) proforma, benchmarked against the Scottish Hip Fracture Audit (2004 and 2006) and Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN) standards
audits.f: The audit detected long emergency department door-to-operating theatre times and a high re-operation rate compared with the Scottish Hip Fracture Audit benchmarks (specific percentages not reported)

audits.t: Development Of a Patellofemoral Instability Compendium for Assessment and Treatment (PFI-CAT): A Multisite Chart Audit
audits.st: PFI-CAT (Patellofemoral Instability Compendium for Assessment and Treatment), 43 demographic, subjective, physical exam and imaging parameters developed by the PRiSM Patellofemoral Research Interest Group from literature review
audits.f: Six variables (laterality, range of motion, varus/valgus laxity, lateral patellar glide, skeletal maturity, and one other) were documented in all patient charts, though methods for assessing range of motion, palpation, laxity and glide were inconsistent; plain radiographs and MRI were included in the assessment of all 50 patients; documentation consistency of other PFI-CAT components ranged from 0% to 96% of records; trochlear dysplasia was not recorded in 18% of patients

audits.t: The UK Foot and Ankle COVID-19 National (FAlCoN) Audit – Regional Variations in COVID-19 Infection and National Foot and Ankle Surgical Activity
audits.tp: COVID-19 impact on foot and ankle surgical activity
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 0.53% (35/6644) of operated patients contracted COVID-19; infection rate was highest during lockdown (2.11%, n=16) and lowest post-lockdown (0.16%, n=3); overall activity during lockdown fell to 24.44% of pre-lockdown levels; elective surgery fell most, to 1.73% during lockdown, recovering to 10.72% post-lockdown; national peak infection rate was 1.37%, occurring in the final week of lockdown; the highest regional COVID-19 rate was in South East England (3.21%)

audits.t: The UK Foot and Ankle COVID-19 National Audit – Rate of COVID-19 Infection and 30 Day Mortality in Foot and Ankle Surgery in the UK
audits.tp: COVID-19 mortality in foot and ankle surgery
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 0.52% (35/6644) contracted COVID-19; overall 30-day all-cause mortality was 0.41%, but 25.71% (9/35) among patients who contracted COVID-19, rising to 75% (3/4) in diabetic foot surgery patients; adjusted odds ratio for mortality with COVID-19 infection was 11.71 (95% CI 1.55-88.74, p=0.017); there was no difference in surgical complications or infection rates before or after lockdown, or by COVID-19 status; post-lockdown infection rate was 0.15% with no COVID-19 deaths

audits.t: Rate of COVID-19 Infection and 30 Day Mortality Between Blue and Green (Dedicated COVID-19 Safe) Pathways: Results From the UK Foot and Ankle COVID-19 National-Audit
audits.st: Designation of a dedicated COVID-19-free 'green' surgical pathway versus a standard 'blue' pathway, evaluated for reduction in perioperative COVID-19 infection
audits.f: In phase 1 there was no significant difference in perioperative COVID-19 infection rate between blue and green pathways in the pre-lockdown (p=.109), lockdown (p=.923) or post-lockdown (p=.577) periods
audits.c: Continued and refined implementation of the dedicated COVID-19-free 'green' pathway into phase 2 of the audit
audits.r2: In phase 2 there was a significant reduction in perioperative infection rate with the green pathway in both the pre-lockdown period (p<.001) and lockdown period (odds ratio 0.077, p<.001); across both phases combined the infection rate was 1.07% (69/6470) on the blue pathway versus 0.21% (9/4280) on the green pathway, a five-fold overall reduction and a 13-fold reduction in phase 2; there was no significant difference in COVID-19 related mortality between pathways

audits.t: UK Foot and Ankle Thrombo-Embolism Audit (UK-FATE): A Multicentre Prospective Study of Venous Thromboembolism in Foot and Ankle Surgery
audits.st: UK-wide variation in thromboprophylaxis threshold and provision for foot and ankle surgery and Achilles tendon rupture; no single named national standard, audited against 90-day symptomatic VTE incidence
audits.f: 95 VTE events overall (0.86%); cohort split trauma 51.72% (5571), diabetic surgery 3.78% (415), elective 45.18% (4962); diabetic foot disease surgery had the highest VTE rates (below-knee amputation 5.3%, acute foot debridement 2.6%); Achilles tendon rupture had the highest trauma VTE rate (3.7%); elective procedures were generally <1% VTE except elective tendon procedures (1.1%); factors significantly associated with VTE included prophylaxis stopped more than 1 day pre-surgery (p=.027), non-compliance with prophylaxis (p=.001), post-surgical infection (p=.005), and comorbidities asthma (p=.014), cancer (p=.014), dementia (p=.001), diabetes (p=.005), stroke (p<0.001) and recent long-distance travel (p=.048); highest VTE rate was with Apixaban (4.9%); most common agents were Enoxaparin (27.19%) and Dalteparin (20.38%); no evidence that mechanical prophylaxis reduced VTE

audits.t: Providing a One-Stop Hip Clinic for High Risk Babies: A District General Hospital Audit and Evaluation of the First 200 Patients
audits.st: UK developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) screening programme for high-risk neonates
audits.f: not reported (abstract text supplied is truncated before numerical results are given)

audits.t: Post-Anticoagulation Cessation D-Dimer Testing and VTE Recurrence in Real-World Australian Audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: D-dimer was tested in 189 of 1024 patients (18.5%) within 90 days of anticoagulation cessation; abnormal post-cessation D-dimer (>500) was found in 72 patients (37.9%), of whom 25 were restarted on anticoagulation, with 1 recurrence on low-dose apixaban and 1 recurrence after later cessation; the highest recurrence risk was in patients with D-dimer >1000 (relative risk 7.38); a positive post-cessation D-dimer was associated with a relative risk of recurrence of 4.21 in provoked VTE and 4.09 in isolated distal DVT subgroups

audits.t: Frozen Plasma Transfusion Practices in Ontario-an Electronic Audit at Five Tertiary Care Hospitals to Inform a Knowledge Translation Strategy to Reduce Inappropriate Plasma Transfusions
audits.st: Published guidelines on appropriate plasma (frozen plasma) transfusion, based on INR threshold, bleeding status and dose; provincial benchmark of approximately 50% inappropriate use
audits.f: not reported (this text describes a planned audit protocol; prior provincial audits and preliminary Ontario Blood Utilization Data Strategy (ONBUDS) data suggested about 50% of plasma transfused in Ontario is inappropriate, but this study's own results are not given in the supplied text)

audits.t: Emergency Blood Supply Planning: A Statewide Prospective Audit To Determine the Potential Benefits of Triaging Red Cells during a Critical Shortage.
audits.tp: Emergency red cell supply triage planning
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 3% of tagged red cell units were not transfused; major clinical categories of use were haematology (17%), gastroenterology (11%), orthopaedic surgery (9%), non-haematological oncology (6%), gastrointestinal surgery (6%), cardiothoracic surgery (5%), obstetrics/gynaecology (5%), urology (3%), trauma (3%) and paediatrics (2%), with miscellaneous indications and anaemia not otherwise specified making up 10% and 22%; urgency of transfusion was acute (<1h) in 18%, urgent (1-24h) in 43%, semi-urgent (24h-1 week) in 33% and non-urgent in 4%; of units supporting perioperative bleeding (34%), only a quarter of procedures were elective and urgency of surgery was not stated in 15%; only 38% of transfused units could have been deferred more than 24 hours, and only 9% of total units were allocated to potentially deferrable elective surgery

audits.t: Quality-of-care provided to prostate cancer (PC) patients for prevention and treatment of osteoporosis-induced by androgen deprivation therapy (ADT): Results of a chart audit.
audits.tp: Bone health monitoring during androgen deprivation therapy
audits.st: Canadian guidelines for bone health screening, prevention and treatment (calcium and vitamin D intake, BMD testing, fracture risk assessment using the CAROC tool, and bisphosphonate use) in men on androgen deprivation therapy for prostate cancer
audits.f: 56 (83.6%) were on continuous ADT and 11 (16.4%) intermittent, for a mean duration of 27.4±30.7 months; 19.4% had a BMD scan before starting ADT and 50.7% during the first year; 55.2% were taking less than 1000 mg calcium daily and 26.9% more than 1200 mg; 22.4% had taken vitamin D for 3 months or more, of whom 81.8% had a vitamin D level ≥75 nmol/L; using the CAROC tool, 10-year fracture risk was moderate in 41.8% (28) and high in 13.4% (9); 71.4% of sedentary patients were advised to increase exercise or referred to a formal exercise programme; of those not taking appropriate calcium (70%, 39) or vitamin D (39.2%, 24), 100% were recommended to adjust their intake to guideline levels; all patients with high fracture risk were recommended bisphosphonates

audits.t: A retrospective file audit of preoperative anaemia in patients referred to an anaesthesiology clinic before elective orthopaedic surgery
audits.tp: Preoperative anaemia screening in joint replacement
audits.st: International patient blood management standards for investigation and correction of preoperative anaemia before elective surgery (anaemia threshold 13 g/dL)
audits.f: 44 patients (25%, 95% CI 19-32%) had preoperative anaemia, median haemoglobin 12.25 g/dL (IQR 11.2-12.7); mean age 63.3±10.0 years; 34% were booked for knee arthroplasty and 55% for hip replacement; no diagnostic workup was done for the anaemia; only 15 of 44 anaemic patients (34%) received any treatment; 18 anaemic patients (41%) received perioperative red cell transfusion, of whom 8 (44%) developed postoperative sepsis, and 5 remained anaemic postoperatively

audits.t: Vitamin D: prescription audit in tertiary health care centre
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Vitamin D prescribing was highest in the orthopaedic department (22% of that department's prescriptions), compared with 4.6% in medicine, 1.5% in dermatology and 0.8% in psychiatry; vitamin D prescribed in combination with calcium occurred in 52% of orthopaedics prescriptions, 7% of medicine and 10% of obstetrics and gynaecology

audits.t: Audit of fresh frozen plasma usage, prospective study: a report from department of immunohematology and transfusion medicine, government medical college Jammu, Jammu and Kashmir, India
audits.st: Fresh frozen plasma (FFP) transfusion guidelines of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), India
audits.f: 66.44% of FFP use was appropriate and 33.56% inappropriate according to DGHS guidelines; units were issued to ICU (15%, 122), paediatrics (12.87%, 104), emergency/GI bleed (12.25%, 99), obstetrics (6.8%, 55), orthopaedics (6.18%, 50), road traffic accident patients (4.45%, 36), hepatic failure (4.20%, 34), cardiothoracic and vascular surgery (3.09%, 25), oncology (2.97%, 24), snake bite (2.47%, 20), dengue (1.23%, 10) and haemophilia (1.11%, 9); the indication was unknown for 27.38% of units

audits.t: Audit & analysis of cancelled elective operations of surgical patients at Mankweng Hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 540 of 2812 elective operations were cancelled, an overall cancellation rate of 19.2%; top reasons were prolonged operative time (31.3%), poor preparation (24.6%) and emergencies (22.8%); the highest departmental cancellation rate was in paediatric surgery (27%) and the lowest in gynaecology (6.9%)

audits.t: Making the birth experience safer for everybody audit to determine knowledge retention in shoulder dystocia training: 2014 - 2015
audits.st: PROMPT 2 (PRactical Obstetric Multi-Professional Training) shoulder dystocia skills competency standard for multidisciplinary team retention
audits.f: Clinicians demonstrated 3 shoulder dystocia skills before PROMPT training was delivered on the same day; baseline performance figures were not quantified in the text
audits.c: PROMPT 2 shoulder dystocia training delivered to the multidisciplinary, multicultural team
audits.r2: A post-audit of the same 3 skills after a year showed statistically significant knowledge retention (2-sample t-test and Chi-square, p<0.05 for correct versus incorrect performance); PROMPT training was associated with reductions in brachial plexus injury, hypoxic ischaemic encephalopathy and term neonatal unit admissions

audits.t: Evolution of Surgical Antibiotic Prophylaxis: A Prospective Audit of Practice Change at Government Medical College & Hospital, Purnea, Bihar, India
audits.st: WHO AWaRe classification and surgical antibiotic prophylaxis guideline concordance (correct antibiotic choice, administration within 60 minutes pre-incision, appropriate intraoperative redosing, and discontinuation within 24 hours)
audits.f: Correct antibiotic choice 45.2%; administration within 60 minutes pre-incision 54.8%; appropriate intraoperative redosing 33.3% of indicated cases; discontinuation within 24 hours 25.8%; complete guideline concordance 22.6%; mean prophylaxis duration 3.15±1.83 days; WHO AWaRe Access regimen use 45.2%; 30-day surgical site infection (SSI) 19.4%; postoperative length of stay 5.43±1.93 days
audits.c: Continuous audit and feedback with stewardship-focused standardisation of surgical antibiotic prophylaxis, shifting practice toward narrower-spectrum cefazolin-based regimens
audits.r2: Correct antibiotic choice improved to 76.5% (p=0.012); administration within 60 minutes to 85.3% (p=0.013); appropriate redosing to 80.0% (p=0.043); discontinuation within 24 hours to 67.6% (p=0.001); complete guideline concordance to 64.7% (p=0.001); mean prophylaxis duration fell to 1.31±0.91 days (p<0.001); WHO AWaRe Access use rose to 85.3% (p=0.001); 30-day SSI fell to 5.9% (not statistically significant, p=0.138); postoperative length of stay was 4.41±1.32 days (p=0.018)

audits.t: Audit on induction time delays in operating room at Kibogora District Hospital: A quality improvement project
audits.st: Local quality indicator defining a delay of induction of anaesthesia as more than 30 minutes between the previous patient leaving theatre and the next patient's induction
audits.f: 24.8% of surgeries had delays in induction of anaesthesia versus 75.2% without delay; 48.6% of delays were due to hospital issues, 40.0% due to anaesthesia provision issues, and 5.7% each due to surgery-related and patient-related issues

audits.t: Minimally invasive surgery for lesser toe deformity: a clinical audit of a proposed treatment algorithm
audits.tp: Minimally invasive lesser toe deformity surgery outcomes
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Mean pre-operative Visual Analogue Pain (VAS) score was 3.95 (median 5.00); post-operative VAS scores improved to 0.23 at 6 weeks and 0.43 at 12 weeks, a statistically significant improvement (Mann-Whitney U test, p<0.05)

audits.t: An Audit of Orthopaedic Operative Notes : Do we Need Improvement?
audits.st: Local guidance on content and legibility of orthopaedic operation notes (no numeric target stated)
audits.f: Generally good standard overall but important information was missing in some cases and a high proportion of notes had illegible sections (exact numbers not reported)
audits.c: Proposed a computerised pro forma for writing operation notes, training for resident doctors, and placement of aide memoires throughout the operating theatre complex

audits.t: A Retrospective Audit of Indwelling Urinary Catheter Practices in Primary Hip Fracture Patients at Fiona Stanley Hospital
audits.tp: Urinary catheter use in hip fracture patients
audits.st: Standard practice for pre-operative indwelling urinary catheter (IDC) use in hip fracture patients, balancing prevention of postoperative bladder dysfunction against catheter-associated urinary tract infection risk
audits.f: not reported

audits.t: Audit of Prescribing Practices to Evaluate Rational Use of Medicines in the OPD of Orthopaedics in a Private Medical College Hospital
audits.st: WHO core prescribing indicators for rational use of medicines
audits.f: Average number of drugs per encounter was 3.78; no drug was prescribed by generic name; an antibiotic was prescribed in 6.67% and an injection in 3.33% of encounters; only 4.32% of drugs were from the national Essential Drug List; an NSAID was prescribed in 97%, an antiulcerant in 97.33%, and a calcium preparation in 67.33% of encounters

audits.t: Reasons and appropriate measures to circumvent cancellation of elective surgical cases: A clinical audit of a government teaching hospital
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 1207 of 7316 (16.49%) scheduled elective surgical cases were cancelled on the day of surgery; highest cancellation rate in orthopaedics (6.84%) followed by general surgery (5.41%); main reasons for cancellation: patient medically unfit 599 (49.6%), inadequate operation theatre time 274 (22.7%), equipment failure 207 (17.2%), patients not attending 127 (10.5%)

audits.t: Radiofrequency Denervation of the Lumbar Zygapophysial Joints: 10-Year Prospective Clinical Audit
audits.tp: Radiofrequency denervation outcomes for chronic low back pain
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Of 174 patients with complete data (35 lost to follow-up or with incomplete data), 55 (31.6%) experienced no benefit from radiofrequency denervation, while 119 (68.4%) had good (>50%) to excellent (>80%) pain relief lasting from 6 to 24 months

audits.t: SHORT TERM AUDIT OF OUTCOMES OF CHILDREN WITH NEURAL TUBE DEFECT REPAIR IN A TERTIARY CARE CENTER
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: Median age at admission 30 days (range 2-270); 42 (70%) male, 18 (30%) female; median swelling size 5cm (2-11cm); locations: cervical 4 (6.66%), upper thoracic 1 (1.66%), dorso-lumbar 11 (18.33%), lumbar 22 (36.66%), lumbosacral 19 (31.66%), sacral 3 (5%); preoperative lower limb weakness in 22 (36.66%); neurogenic bladder/bowel with bilateral CTEV in 8 (13.33%); preoperative CSF discharge in 10 (16.66%); preoperative hydrocephalus in 15 (25%); Arnold Chiari malformation in 18 (30%); postoperatively, wound infection in 19 (31.66%), CSF leak in 10 (16.66%), new neurological deficit in 11 (18.33%), and new hydrocephalus in 9 (15%); ventriculo-peritoneal shunt placed in 22 (36.66%); median postoperative stay 10 days (4-28); readmission in 17 (28.33%); 2 (3.33%) deaths from sepsis and aspiration pneumonia

audits.t: Two years audit of Ponseti technique for the management of clubfoot: Challenges encountered in a developing country
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: At 24-month follow-up, 20 patients (71.4%) showed no recurrence of deformity, 1 patient (3.6%) showed recurrence (associated with brace non-compliance and successfully retreated with repeat casting), and 7 patients (25%) were not available for follow-up; recurrence was significantly more likely in patients non-compliant with the brace

audits.t: Adherence to referral pathway of hip fractures: A clinical audit
audits.st: King's College Hospital hip fracture imaging referral pathway, based on NICE guidance for cost-effective imaging of suspected hip fracture
audits.f: 21.4% of hip fractures identified via plain radiography; where radiographs were negative, MRI was suggested in 75% of cases but only 19.6% underwent CT or MRI to exclude occult fracture; only 6% of X-ray negative patients had an MRI; surgical intervention occurred within 48 hours in 67.8% of patients

audits.t: Audit of perioperative management of patients with fracture neck of femur
audits.st: AAGBI (Association of Anaesthetists of Great Britain and Ireland) safety guidelines for perioperative management of fracture neck of femur, including surgery within 48 hours of admission and thromboprophylaxis
audits.f: Only 4 of 41 patients (11%) had surgery within the recommended 48 hours; 50% had surgery only after 7-8 days; none of the patients received thromboprophylaxis despite current guidelines; one patient died of a probable acute coronary event or pulmonary embolism

audits.t: Clinical Audit of Hip Fracture Management in Elderly Patients (Aged 70 Years and Above): A Focus on Improving Standards of Care
audits.st: Evidence-based orthogeriatric hip fracture care standards covering time to surgery, pain assessment, comorbidity optimisation, BMD evaluation and fall risk assessment (specific source guideline not stated)
audits.f: Only 52% underwent surgery within 48 hours, 31% within 72 hours, and 17% beyond 72 hours; BMD assessment performed in 0% of patients; fall risk assessment documented in 0% of cases; comorbidities present in 84% (20% one, 64% two or more); all 86 patients received analgesics on admission but formal pain documentation was inconsistent

audits.t: A Local Clinical Audit on Osteoporosis Prevention and Management in Sudanese Patients Treated with Long Term Oral Glucocorticoids for Rheumatic Diseases in a Military Tertiary Hospital in West Khartoum
audits.tp: Osteoporosis prevention in long-term steroid use
audits.st: NICE and ACR guidelines for osteoporosis/fragility fracture prevention in patients on oral glucocorticoids for 3 months or more; audit standard: 50% of eligible patients appropriately managed
audits.f: The centre failed to meet the audit standard of 50% of eligible patients being appropriately managed for osteoporosis/fragility fracture according to NICE and ACR guidelines (exact percentage not reported)

audits.t: Usage of Therapeutic Offloading In Diabetic Foot- A Clinical Audit
audits.st: not reported
audits.f: 34 patients received offloading; 88.24% had diabetic foot ulcer as the indication; 82.35% received simple offloading (Amit Jain's offloading system was commonest); only 5.88% had total contact cast

audits.t: Improving integration and care through clinical audit: The Irish Hip Fracture Database
audits.st: Irish Hip Fracture Database national care standards for hip fracture management (e.g. time to admission to orthopaedic ward, time to surgery, geriatrician review, mobilisation, secondary prevention)
audits.f: 2015 report captured 2962 hip fracture patients (81% of national cases): 70% female, over 55% aged 80 or older; 10% admitted to a specialist orthopaedic ward within 4 hours; 74% received surgery within 48 hours; 15% seen pre-operatively by a geriatrician; 73% mobilised the day of or after surgery; 4% developed a pressure ulcer; mean length of stay 20 days; 30% discharged directly home

audits.t: A Clinical Audit on Appropriateness of Intravenous Fluid Prescribing Practices in Hospitalized Adult Inpatients: Evaluating Compliance with National Guidelines
audits.st: NICE CG174 guidelines on intravenous fluid therapy in adults
audits.f: 48% of IV fluid prescriptions were fully compliant with NICE CG174, 35% partially compliant and 17% non-compliant; initial assessment documented in 70% and ongoing reassessment in 49%; General Medicine had highest compliance (55%) and Orthopaedics the lowest (38%); Normal Saline was the most frequently prescribed fluid (65%)

audits.t: Audit clinique des pratiques radiologiques des traumatismes maxillo-faciaux à l’Hôpital Central de Yaoundé
audits.st: 2023 American College of Radiology (ACR) criteria for maxillofacial trauma imaging
audits.f: CT was the main imaging modality (86.4%); imaging requests compliant with ACR 2023 recommendations in 75.5% of cases; no CT scan had slice thickness ≤0.62 mm; all CT scans included axial images with sagittal, coronal and 3D reconstructions; radiation dose below 4 mSv in 96.5%; precise fracture description in 71.2% of reports, evaluation of fracture relationships with adjacent structures in 90.9%, and overall report completeness in 76%; overall 53% of examinations were fully compliant with ACR criteria

audits.t: Rolling audit on the quality of discharge summary in TU Teaching Hospital
audits.st: Modified Van Walraven et al. (1999) criteria for discharge summary completeness, plus admission/discharge dates and follow-up instructions, and completeness of the hospital's printed discharge summary form
audits.f: Department of Gynaecology had the best discharge summaries; Department of Orthopaedics had the poorest inclusion of criteria
audits.c: Recommendations from the earlier audit aimed at improving discharge summary completeness
audits.r2: Department of ENT and Head and Neck Surgery (HNS) had the best discharge summaries by modified Van Walraven criteria; Department of Orthopaedics had the least inclusion of criteria; ENT and HNS had the highest number of almost completely filled forms (>90%); Department of Medicine had the least properly filled forms

audits.t: Antibiotic Prophylaxis Practices in Orthopedic Surgeries: A Public Health Audit of Guideline Adherence
audits.st: International guidelines on antibiotic prophylaxis for orthopaedic surgery (antibiotic choice, timing, dose, route and duration)
audits.f: Full guideline adherence in 24.3% of cases; correct timing in 58.1% and correct duration in 29.1%; ceftriaxone was the most commonly used antibiotic (48.0%), cefazolin in 15.5%; overall surgical site infection (SSI) rate 8.8% (2.8% in the adherent group vs 10.7% in the non-adherent group, OR 4.17, 95% CI 0.52-33.3, p=0.18)

audits.t: Trauma Care Transitions: A Clinical Audit in a Pakistani Tertiary Care Teaching Hospital
audits.st: Royal College of Surgeons of England advice on safe trauma handovers (minimum dataset: patient name, date of birth, location, responsible consultant, resuscitation plan, current diagnosis, operational issues including ICU bed availability, and results of pending investigations); local target 80% (raised to 95% for re-audit)
audits.f: Handover standard was very unsatisfactory: date of admission 42%, responsible consultant name 28%, patient condition at handover 47%, patient name 66%, operational issues 61%, results of pending investigations 76% — all below the expected 80% standard
audits.c: Implementation of an electronic handover proforma
audits.r2: Only one criterion, results of pending investigations (84%), fell below the 95% standard; the electronic proforma was used in 100% of cases and all other criteria met or exceeded the standard

audits.t: NICE GUIDELINES ON PREOPERATIVE TESTS IN ELECTIVE ENT SURGERY: A PROSPECTIVE AUDIT
audits.st: NICE guidance on preoperative testing before elective surgery
audits.f: 154 patients attended QEH (which did not refer to NICE guidelines) and 115 attended WRH (which had NICE guidance sheets available); non-compliance with NICE guidelines was 34.4% at QEH versus 23.5% at WRH; most unnecessary investigations were in ASA I-II patients (90.4% at QEH, 81.3% at WRH); only 3 abnormal results were found at WRH (none affecting the planned operation) and none at QEH
